title: Synergistic evolution and trade-off mechanisms of ecosystem services in coal-grain composite areas a 23-year spatiotemporal analysis of mining subsidence impacts and reclamation strategies
abstract: In eastern China, where grain production and coal mining coexist, mining-induced subsidence is reshaping ecosystem services (ES) in the coal–grain composite areas (CGCA). Understanding the dynamic trade-offs and synergies among ES is crucial for sustainable land management. This study developed a 23-year (2001–2023) assessment framework for five ES—food production (FP), water conservation (WC), soil conservation (SC), oxygen release (OR), and climate regulation (CR)—using multi-source datasets. Subsidence-induced waterlogged areas (SIWAs) were delineated using the LandTrendr algorithm, ES were quantified with biophysical models, and their interactions were assessed via time-series analysis and structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that while all five ES increased overall, SIWAs expanded 2.54 times, with over 70 % of these areas showing FP declines. Targeted reclamation, such as Yellow River sediment filling, drove localized FP surges (up to 465.40 %) but also triggered severe trade-offs, with sharp declines in SC (−950.11 %), WC (−22.75 %), and CR (−41.86 %). PLS-SEM revealed strong, region-specific linkages, from pronounced FP–CR synergies (β = 0.971) to significant FP–WC trade-offs (β = −0.461). A novel dynamic equivalence factor adjustment framework (DEFAF), which integrates spatiotemporal changes, improved ES valuation accuracy. This mechanism-informed framework provides a scientific basis for balancing ecosystem services in mining landscapes and offers actionable guidance for adaptive reclamation policies.

title: Can OECD countries lead the green transition? Leveraging green innovation, trade openness, information globalization and financial depth for environmental sustainability
abstract: In an era marked by mounting climate challenges and rising global environmental consciousness, the urgency for sustainable economic transitions has never been greater. This study explores the heterogeneous impacts of green innovation (GRIO), trade openness (TROP), information globalization (INGN), and financial depth (FNDH) on environmental outcomes in OECD countries from 1994 to 2023. To capture environmental sustainability (ES), this study employs carbon dioxide emissions (COXE) as a widely recognized proxy, since reductions in CO2 emissions represent a fundamental pathway toward sustainability goals. Recognizing the limitations of existing literature that often focuses on country-specific or linear models, we employ Panel Quantile Regression (PQR) to uncover nuanced relationships across different levels of emissions. Both first-generation and advanced second-generation econometric approaches are applied to ensure robustness. The findings reveal that GRIO significantly reduces COXE across almost all quantiles (10th to 90th), confirming its central role in supporting sustainability transitions. TROP also exerts a strong mitigating influence on COXE across quantiles, though with varying intensity. Interestingly, the effect of INGN is asymmetric, reducing COXE significantly at lower and middle quantiles (10th to 50th) but becoming weaker at higher emission levels, suggesting diminishing marginal gains in advanced economies. FNDH shows limited influence, with a predominantly negative effect only at the lower quantile—20th quantile. Moreover, economic growth (GRPC) significantly increases COXE in the middle and higher quantiles (50th to 90th), while foreign direct investment (FINT) reduces emissions in the lower and middle quantiles (20th to 50th). By capturing distributional effects and nonlinearities, this study provides novel insights into how different structural drivers influence COXE, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on climate mitigation and sustainable economic transitions in advanced economies.

title: Toward climate-resilient supply chains: Analyzing the impact and mechanisms of physical climate risks on supply chain network in China’s listed companies
abstract: Existing studies have predominantly concentrated on supply chain disruptions caused by individual climate risks and its subsequent propagation, with limited in-depth analysis of the specific impacts on supply chain network traffic. Our study innovatively examines these impacts by considering multiple physical climate risks simultaneously, including floods, earthquakes, extreme temperatures, and storms. Utilizing a dataset of Chinese A-share listed companies spanning over two decades (2001–2022), we employ a novel combination of directed minimum spanning tree and fixed-effects regression methods for empirical analysis. The results show that spatially, supply chain core hubs are alarmingly concentrated in high-risk areas; urban clusters with multi-core complex supply chain structures exhibit stronger resilience. Temporally, an increase in natural disaster frequency coincides with a decline in supply chain net flow. Regression analysis confirms that physical climate risks significantly and negatively impact supply chain net flow (β=−22.4465, p<0.01). This primarily disrupts supply chains by weakening transportation capacities, increasing short-term financial pressure on enterprises, and restricting their comprehensive financing capabilities. Finally, we recommend that governments enhance infrastructure development in disaster-prone areas and subsidize corporate technological transformation to improve supply chain resilience. Meanwhile, enterprises can effectively counter physical climate risks by optimizing network layouts and establishing contingency financing mechanisms.

title: Synergistic effects of spatial urban form on PM2.5 concentration and urban heat islands: A multi-scale explanatory machine learning
abstract: Urban form significantly influences environmental challenges, such as fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration and the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. However, few studies have explored the synergistic effects of urban form's spatial configuration on PM2.5 concentration and UHI prediction, with most overlooking spatial autocorrelation in their analyses. This study calculates four built-up landscape pattern metrics, alongside built-up volume, built-up surface, and 2D and 3D greenery, to investigate their effects at various scales on PM2.5 concentration and UHI intensity in Vilnius, Lithuania. Using an explanatory machine learning method, we identified non-linear relationships between contributing factors and their impact on PM2.5 concentration and UHI, while accounting for spatial autocorrelation. Our findings reveal the consistent prominence of the largest patch index (LPI), percentage of landscape (PLAND), and built-up volume in prediction models, although their relative importance varies across scales. LPI is strongly associated with UHI, while built-up volume and PLAND are more influential in predicting PM2.5 at finer resolutions. Two-way interactions among leading variables indicate that high values of LPI or PLAND, combined with high built-up volume, are associated with increased PM2.5 concentration and UHI levels. Furthermore, areas with high tree cover height (TCH) and high built-up volume in urban canyons restrict airflow, exacerbating pollutant accumulation and increasing PM2.5 concentration.

title: Evaluating technical soil derived from lithium mica residue: Integrating soil quality and life cycle assessment for functional performance and environmental sustainability
abstract: The large-scale accumulation of Lithium Mica Residue (LMR) poses environmental challenges, requiring sustainable utilization beyond conventional disposal or limited reuse. Constructing technical soil from LMR shows promise but lacks comprehensive design, quality assessment, and environmental evaluation frameworks. This study developed LMR-based technical soil by blending industrial and agricultural wastes to explore the performance mechanisms and identify key indicators through analyses of physicochemical properties, maize seedling growth, and microbial communities. A statistical Soil Quality Index (SQI) analysis indicated that optimal formulations could be obtained. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) demonstrated notable environmental advantages under the optimal formulations-particularly in reducing carbon emissions and land use-against landfilling and cement use. Overall, transforming LMR into technical soil represents a promising and comparatively sustainable utilization strategy, with the integrated design-SQI-LCA framework providing a rigorous methodology to evaluate, optimize, and advance waste-derived soil substitutes for broader environmental applications.

title: On-demand thermal regulation and water harvesting via liquid metal-infused bio-inspired microchannel architectures
abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting in humid regions demands textiles that balance efficient moisture capture with desirable thermal gradients, a challenge complicated by liquid metal (LM) integration. The incorporation of LMs like EGaIn into textiles presents distinct challenges: controlling the conductive fluid's stability, ensuring reliable encapsulation within flexible fiber matrices, and sustaining functionality under both mechanical stress and thermal cycling, particularly in moisture-rich environments. To address the challenges of extreme weather and water scarcity, we introduce a novel biofabric featuring a liquid metal-integrated, multichannel nanofiber structure. Fabricated via multi-fluid electrospinning, this design securely encapsulates EGaIn particles within hollow PLA nanofibers, creating a stable, lychee-inspired rough surface that achieves rapid photothermal response (53.6 % efficiency) without leakage. Co-integration of phase change materials (PCMs) and biomimetic hollow channels enables exceptional energy storage (89.7 J/g) and minimizes radiative heat loss. The fabric further demonstrates efficient atmospheric water harvesting (6.00 g/g), adaptable PCM tuning via physical blending, and robust durability (85.3 J/g after cycling). This multifunctional textile overcomes key barriers of LM-integration to pioneer effective thermal management and rapid water sorption-desorption, standing at the forefront of smart fabric innovation for extreme environments.

title: An integrated DPSIR-TOPSIS modeling approach for assessing and predicting coastal wetland ecological security: A case study of Haikou, China
abstract: Coastal wetlands (CWs) provide critical ecosystem services but are increasingly threatened by rapid urban expansion and industrial restructuring. These pressures highlight the need for an improved assessment of the ecological security (ES) of CWs, yet the existing approaches lack the integrated frameworks for a comprehensive evaluation. This study addresses that gap by developing an integrated assessment framework that combines the driving-pressure-state-impact-response (DPSIR) model with the technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (TOPSIS) analysis to evaluate the ES of Haikou's CWs. The framework integrates multi-source data and ecological process indicators (ecosystem services, landscape ecology, socioeconomics, and climate factors) to analyze spatiotemporal changes from 1990 to 2023 and employs a grey model (GM (1,1)) to project the trends through 2030. The results indicate substantial wetland loss (34.67 km2) and fragmentation due to urban expansion, corresponding to an initial decline in ES. The ecological security index (ESI) of the driving and state layers increased by 0.0277 and 0.4621, respectively, while the indicators of pressure, impact, and response layers showed a general downward trend. Among them, the pressure dimension decreased by 79.46 %. The ESI followed a decline-stagnation-recovery trajectory with a notable rebound by 2023 (reaching 0.4586), which indicated a delayed ecological response to management interventions. Spatially, the low ES areas extend from the urban periphery to the core wetland areas driven by urban encroachment and intensified agriculture. If current protection policies stand, the ESI are projected to rebound to approximately 0.5183 by 2030. Overall, the DPSIR-TOPSIS framework effectively captures the complex socio-ecological dynamics in ES. This integrated framework offers a practical reference for sustainable urban planning and wetland conservation in rapidly urbanizing coastal regions.

title: Deep insights into the effects of polystyrene nanoplastics on methanogenic microbial communities in food waste anaerobic digestion under meso-thermophilic temperatures
abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NP) from improper plastic disposal can enter the anaerobic digestion (AD) process with food waste (FW), potentially impacting AD performance. This study investigates the effect of PS-NP on FW AD at meso-thermophilic temperature (45 °C). Exposure to 0.1 and 1 g L−1 PS-NP had no significant impact on the AD process, but 2 g L−1 caused a significant decrease in methane production, organic matter accumulation, and system acidification. However, the inhibitory effect was alleviated after day 12. Microbial composition analysis revealed a shift in the core microbial community, with Methanosarcina, Defluviitoga, Proteiniphilum, and Tepidimicrobium as dominant taxa. Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses indicated that PS-NP exposure did not disrupt methane metabolism pathways, but inhibited AD by reducing the transcription of functional genes. Notably, acetoclastic methanogenesis (AM) was impaired, as transcription of ackA and pta increased while cdh decreased. Conversely, genes involved in the reverse Wood-Ljungdahl (WL), glycine cleavage system (GCS), and methylotrophic methanogenesis (MM) pathways were significantly upregulated. These findings suggest that PS-NP exposure shifts methane production from AM to syntrophic acetate oxidation (SAO) and hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis (HM), coupled with MM. This study provides new insights into the impacts of PS-NP on AD performance under meso-thermophilic conditions.

title: Structure–solubility relationships of CO2-soluble surfactants for in-situ foaming in enhanced oil recovery and CO2 sequestration
abstract: In-situ foaming using green hydrocarbon-based CO2-soluble surfactants offers a promising approach for enhancing oil recovery and geological CO2 sequestration. Compared to water-based foams, this strategy enables deep transport of surfactants via supercritical CO2, facilitating in-situ foam formation and increasing CO2 storage through formation water consumption. However, low surfactant solubility in supercritical CO2 remains a key challenge. This study introduces a static equilibrium sampling method to directly measure surfactant solubility under various temperature–pressure conditions, overcoming the limitations of traditional cloud point methods. The novelty of this method lies in its coupling of static sampling with a sensitive, IFT-based quantification technique, which is particularly suited for non-chromophoric surfactants. Validation against vapor–liquid equilibrium data confirms a deviation within 5 %. The solubility of 11 surfactants—including nine DFQ variants and two commercial references—is systematically assessed from 10 to 26 MPa and 35–65 °C. The primary contribution of this work is the establishment of the first systematic structure-solubility relationship for this class of surfactants. Structure–solubility analysis reveals that solubility decreases with increasing PO/EO group numbers and alkyl chain lengths but increases with branching and higher PO/EO ratios. DFQ-4 exhibits the highest solubility among all synthesized surfactants, reaching 0.382 wt% at 50 °C and 26 MPa, significantly surpassing commercial NP-15. Its foam performance is tested in brine (60,000 mg L−1) at 0.4 wt% under 10–50 MPa and 35–65 °C. The foam volume reaches a maximum of 88 mL at 35 °C and 30 MPa, and declines with increasing temperature. Foam stability, assessed through drainage half-life measurements, exceeds 110 min under 35 °C and 50 MPa. These findings confirm DFQ-4's strong compatibility with CO2 and suitability for in-situ foam generation. This work provides design principles for next-generation CO2-soluble surfactants and establishes a robust methodology for structure–performance evaluation under reservoir conditions.

title: Enhancing nutrients recovery from source-separated urine through a novel bioelectrically assisted forward osmosis coupled with gas permeation membrane system: reaction kinetics and mechanisms
abstract: Effective nutrient recovery from source-separated urine is essential for sustainable resource management and water pollution control. In this study, we developed an innovative bioelectrically assisted forward osmosis coupled with a gas-permeation membrane system (BFGS) to simultaneously recover nitrogen and phosphorus from urine. The BFGS substantially improved nutrient recovery efficiency, achieving 80.44 % nitrogen and 99.92 % phosphorus recovery. Relative to a control system without an electric field, the electric field accelerated the kinetics of nitrogen and phosphorus recovery by factors of 1.25 and 1.22, respectively. Electronic equilibrium analysis revealed that the BFGS achieved optimal electronic balance, facilitating efficient oxygen reduction reaction and minimizing electronic losses. Partial least squares path modeling further identified electric field–assisted forward osmosis as the primary driver of nutrient recovery. Mechanism exploration disclosed that the BFGS enabled simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus recovery by inducing ion migration by the electric field while exploiting the reverse salt flux of the FO membrane. This work offers novel insights into nutrient recovery using the BFGS and highlights its remarkable efficiency and feasibility for sustainable management of source-separated urine.

title: Harnessing policy synergies to decarbonize China's light-duty passenger vehicle fleet
abstract: Many studies have evaluated single-policy measures for decarbonizing China's light-duty passenger vehicle fleet, but few have systematically addressed policy interactions. Using a dynamic fleet-based life cycle greenhouse gas emission model, we assess six major policies under 1152 scenarios. We find that accounting for synergies increases mitigation potential by up to 19.3 Gt CO2 eq, raising the number of scenarios consistent with the 2 °C pathway from 3 to 449. The strongest synergies arise from the joint acceleration of vehicle electrification, lightweighting, and power sector decarbonization, while rigid demand-side restrictions tend to reduce overall effectiveness. These results underscore the importance of coordinated policy portfolios. We recommend prioritizing technology-driven strategies and complementing them with flexible demand-side measures to maximize mitigation outcomes.

title: Advanced multi-functional biomass aerogel for enhanced acoustic absorption and flame retardant
abstract: With the increasing demands for safety and environmental protection in the construction field, there is an urgent need for multifunctional green materials that are mechanically robust, noise-reducing, and fire-resistant. Aerogels made from natural biomasses such as cellulose are eco-friendly. However, they are limited by the antagonistic effects between various performance parameters, making it difficult to improve mechanical, acoustic, and flame-retardant properties simultaneously. To address this issue, a kapok fiber-gelatin-based composite aerogel (KGMP) is prepared. The aerogel is made from delignified kapok fiber, magnesium hydroxide, and phytic acid-modified magnesium hydroxide, crosslinked with gelatin. The effects of gelatin concentration, phytic acid-modified magnesium hydroxide concentration, and cavity depth on the acoustic is investigated. The aerogel not only exhibits good sound absorption, but also has compressive strength and flame resistance. These features make the aerogel meet safety requirements and provide new insights for the development of green multifunctional materials.

title: An innovative deep learning surrogate for watershed pollutant-carbon synergistic optimization
abstract: Current watershed management lacks a synergistic consideration of the three objectives of water quality, economic costs, and carbon emissions, while developing a computationally efficient surrogate model for water environments that also captures spatial structure is absent in optimization studies. This study addresses this gap by developing a Graph Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (GC-LSTM) network surrogate model for water environments. The model is based on inputs and outputs from mechanistic watershed models. We integrated this model into a multi-objective optimization framework to analyze the synergistic effects of watershed environment regulation measures on pollution control and carbon mitigation. The proposed framework was applied to the Dianchi watershed, a typical plateau lake watershed in Southwest China. Results show that the GC-LSTM model achieved R2and NSE values above 0.9, demonstrating strong generalizability and reliability as a surrogate for mechanistic models. The model reduced simulation runtime from 504 seconds to just 1.6 seconds per instance, a 315-fold improvement in computational efficiency. Within the three-dimensional (water quality-carbon emissions-economic costs) optimization framework, pollutant concentration entering the lake was reduced by 33.5 %, and carbon emissions by 12.5 % relative to current conditions. A comparative analysis with conventional two-dimensional optimization (water quality-economic costs) revealed that the two-dimensional approach favors solutions with reduced implementation scales for watershed constructive regulation measures. This leads to increased reliance on inter-basin water transfers and external wastewater discharges, suggesting that neglecting carbon emissions incentivizes solutions prioritizing external measures over in-situ watershed improvements. The developed GC-LSTM-based co-optimization methodology can spatially configure regulation measures—optimizing their type, scale, and geographic placement—to simultaneously enhance watershed water quality and mitigate carbon emissions, thereby advancing “dual carbon” goals.

title: Enhanced flotation upgrading of high-ash fine waste coal with a novel compound collector: High-value and clean utilization of waste
abstract: The enhance flotation upgrading of high-ash fine waste coal (HFWC) is urgent, as the low economic value and environmental risks from direct disposal necessitate a clean and efficient separation technique. In this work, HFWC was upgraded to a high-value coking coal product via flotation using a novel compound collector, H708, thereby achieving goals in both waste utilization and clean production. The H708 collector significantly improved the flotation performance of the HFWC, producing a clean coal concentrate with an ash content of 12.25 %, a 52.79 % yield, and 71.40 % combustible recovery at a dosage of 1000 g/t. FTIR and GC/MS analyses confirmed the main components of H708 to be hydrocarbons, esters, and hydroxyl-containing species. The flotation mechanism was investigated through measurements of Zeta potential, wrapping angle, and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) force analysis. These measurements confirmed that H708 selectively enhances low-density coal flotation by promoting stronger interactions with coal's oxygen-containing groups and increasing hydrophobicity. Meanwhile, it boosts the electrostatic repulsion between coal and kaolinite, effectively suppressing clay coating and hetero-coagulation to achieve high combustible recovery and low ash content. A simplified economic analysis indicates the potential for a substantial annual net profit, estimated at $41.52 million. This work demonstrates that the application of H708 in HFWC flotation is efficient, economical, and offers promising industrial application prospects.

title: Electrochemical detection and electro-Fenton degradation of fipronil via Fe/Ni-BTC/MS-derived NiFe2O4@C core-shell catalyst
abstract: The core-shell material NiFe2O4@C, prepared from a maize straw-derived metal-organic framework (MOF) precursor of Fe/Ni-BTC/MS, was developed for the simultaneous detection and degradation of trace fipronil in water bodies. This material exhibited ultra-sensitive detection performance with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.901 fmol L−1 and a linear range from 10−12 to 10−4 mol L−1 for fipronil, where the detection mechanism was attributed to the specific capture of fipronil molecules by Ni3+/Fe2+ bimetallic sites; it simultaneously demonstrated efficient degradation capability, achieving complete mineralization of 10 mg L−1 fipronil within 60 min with a rate constant of 0.0702 min−1, which was dominated by •OH radicals, as verified by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), whose generation relied on the continuous activation of H2O2 through Fe2+/Fe3+and Ni2+/Ni3+ valence cycling. Meanwhile, combining experimental methods and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the electron migration pathways and structural properties of NiFe2O4@C were explored systematically. This strategy was confirmed to provide an integrated detection-degradation solution for pesticide pollution control.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of distribution characteristics and sensitivity of soil organic carbon in typical soils of China
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is a vital component of the terrestrial ecosystem carbon cycle, reducing global warming and promoting plant nutrition, with its changes greatly impacting the global carbon balance and climate change. Recent studies show that different soil types have different abilities to store carbon under the influence of climate, topography, vegetation, and human activities. This study investigates five typical soil types in China (dark brown soil, aeolian soil, alpine meadow soil, red soil, and yellow soil), utilizing an open-access SOC density database and relevant literature to collect SOC density data from 2004 to 2023. Using the Random Forest (RF) model, the SOC density of the 0–20 cm soil layer from 2000 to 2023 was examined to reveal its changes over time and location and influencing factors. The study integrated SOC data from 2000 to 2023 with environmental factors, including climate, topography, vegetation, and soil properties. We found that SOC density across the five soil types ranks as follows: dark brown soil (8.75 kg/m 2 ) > alpine meadow soil (6.59 kg/m 2 ) > yellow soil (5.81 kg/m 2 ) > red soil (4.57 kg/m 2 ) > aeolian soil (2.47 kg/m 2 ). The carbon storage capacity of these soil types is influenced by factors like climate, vegetation, and soil properties. Furthermore, SHAP analysis revealed how each soil type responds differently to these factors. Based on these findings, we propose strategies for managing soil carbon storage. For different soil types, we recommend measures like restoring plant cover, using conservation tillage, and increasing tree planting to boost carbon storage and align with the dual carbon goals of China to tackle climate change. • A database of SOC for five typical soil types in China from 2015 to 2023(Manually collected). • Significant differences in carbon storage capacity among five typical soils. • The key factors influencing the carbon storage capacity of five typical soil types in China were quantified. • Revealed the threshold effects of key factors on the carbon sequestration capacity of five typical soil.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of PM2.5 components in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and its surrounding areas during the heating seasons from 2018 to 2023
abstract: To mitigate the severe PM2.5 pollution, China established the National Atmospheric Particulate Chemical-Speciation-Network (NAPCSN) in 2016 and has been implementing more strict clean air policies since 2018. In this study, based on the data from the NAPCSN, we analyzed the spatiotemporal characteristics of PM2.5 chemical components in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region and its surrounding areas of China during the heating seasons (November 15-March 15) from 2018 to 2023. The results showed that PM2.5 and its chemical components exhibited distinct stage characteristics during the 2018-2023 heating seasons. From 2018 to 2020, a significant decline phase occurred, during which PM2.5 concentrations decreased by 27.4% and its components by 17.2%-58.4%, driven by targeted emission reductions of pollutants such as PM2.5, SO2, and NOx implemented under the Three-Year Action Plan for Winning the Blue Sky Battle. From 2021 to 2023, a slight fluctuation phase was observed, characterized by PM2.5 concentrations ranging from 63 to 66 mu g/m3 with minor interannual variations, the composition of components remaining largely stable, and component concentrations showing small declines or localized rebounds. These patterns likely reflected the diminishing marginal potential for emission reductions and unfavorable meteorological conditions. Notably, the disproportionate decreases across PM2.5 components led to a growing dominance of secondary aerosols, with nitrate (NO3-) emerging as a particularly significant contributor. NO3- and organic matter (OM) emerged as the dominant components, indicating that future mitigation efforts should focus more on the generation of secondary PM2.5. Additionally, PM2.5 chemical components exhibited distinct monthly variations largely due to changes in emission sources and meteorological conditions. For instance, elevated NO3- concentrations were observed in December and January, when NOx levels were high and relative humidity (RH) was elevated. OM was primarily influenced by secondary transformation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), with concentration peaks occurring in November and March. Furthermore, although PM2.5 pollution in the BTH region and its surrounding areas exhibited regional characteristics, significant differences in pollution sources were still observed across different cities. Further analysis reveals that changes in PM2.5 and its major components were closely aligned with the significant reductions in emissions of key pollutants such as PM, NOx, and SO2. Therefore, the improvement in air quality in the BTH region and its surrounding areas is primarily driven by anthropogenic emission reductions. This study provides essential information for optimizing future pollution prevention and control strategies.

title: Transitioning to a circular economy for plastics with an artist in residence (TRACE-P)
abstract: Methods for science communication about the harms caused by plastic wastes have been ineffective in stimulating change. This study assessed if combining intergenerational influence and the skills of creative artists enables enhanced communication of scientific/engineering principles to the public (the COM-ART concept), with a focus on plastic wastes and its consequences. It involved discussions between a university artist-in-residence and specialist academics/professionals, creation/exhibition of artwork, and an associated social survey. The study demonstrated that the COM-ART concept has considerable potential as an approach to improve scientific communication and stimulate change based on scientific evidence. Results showed the artwork was successful in: i) educating people about sources and impacts of plastic pollution ii) creating an emotional response from viewers iii) encouraging people to reduce their plastic usage and question the impact of their lifestyles on the environment.

title: Non-conventional thermal treatment of organic hazardous waste: Conversion to high-energy materials via molten sucrose system
abstract: Based on the rapid detonation reaction between sucrose and potassium chlorate, we propose a method for modifying distillation residues from chemical pesticides using molten sucrose as a reaction matrix, thereby enhancing their detonation performance. Within the molten sucrose medium, sugar radical-driven dehydration condensation reactions, coupled with azetidine ring-opening and rearrangement, generate functional groups such as C ≡ N, N-C=O, and N-H. Concurrently, this process promotes substitution or cleavage of halogenated CF3/C–Cl groups. Two primary products are formed: C25H25F3N2O and C34H22Cl2N2O2. Structural and electronic characterisation reveals both exhibits layered hollow crystal structures. C25H25F3N2O forms a regular layered cavity lattice featuring strong charge polarisation, intra-layer C–H···O/N hydrogen bonds, and interconnected π channels, facilitating ordered charge and energy transport. C34H22Cl2N2O2, however, is governed by halogen-mediated interactions and local positive potentials, rendering C–Cl bonds susceptible to cleavage. This generates Cl· radicals that accelerate KClO3 decomposition; C–F/CF3 charge rearrangement or bond cleavage induces azetidine ring-opening and strain energy release; Thermal cracking of C ≡ N and N-C=O generates nitrogen-containing free radicals and promotes electron transfer, while N–H groups form hydrogen bonds at the interface between the modified product and KClO3, enhancing electron-proton coupling. The resulting rapid radical generation, interfacial charge complementarity, and layered crystal topology significantly reduce the detonation initiation energy barrier, substantially enhancing detonation velocity and energy output. The molten sugar bath effectively improves the energy density, material composition, and structure of various low-calorific-value organic hazardous wastes, laying a solid foundation for pioneering new pathways in the synergistic treatment and resource recovery of organic hazardous wastes using energetic materials.

title: Toward industry 5.0: Quantum-biological synergistic mechanisms for lithium battery recycling through multiscale optimization
abstract: The transition to sustainable industrial systems requires innovative approaches that combine advanced technologies with circular economy principles. This study proposes a novel smart circularity framework for Industry 5.0 that enables cross-industry collaboration, creating an integrated network for lithium battery recycling. Our approach combines the structured production methods from the steel industry, circular material flow patterns from the paper industry, and specific lithium recycling requirements to develop a bio-inspired architecture enhanced by quantum principles. Through advanced modeling and control systems, we demonstrate how quantum-inspired mechanisms can optimize material flow interactions and improve recycling efficiency through biological self-regulation principles. Key contributions include: 1) Cross-industry synergy: Quantum-based coherence measures enhance material recovery in different production systems; 2) Integrated governance: A three-level framework combining quantum-assisted carbon tracking, biological processing, and adaptive control improves system stability; 3) Industry 5.0 integration: Combining digital twins with biological-quantum feedback makes recycling an inherent system function. Case studies confirm that our approach significantly improves collection, recovery, and reuse performance, providing scalable solutions for regenerative economies that extend beyond battery recycling. Based on the robustness analysis and simulation-reality gap assessment, this study further proposes a systematic optimization pathway to bridge the gap between theoretical simulations and practical applications in lithium recovery.

title: AI-driven energy and environmental control for sustainable space farming under altered gravity
abstract: Space controlled environment agriculture (SpaCEA) offers promising solutions for sustainable life support in closed environments but require careful balancing of energy use and resource efficiency. In this study, we use computational modeling and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate key performance metrics–oxygen production, carbon dioxide scrubbing, water recycling, food production, and energy consumption–of SpaCEA under two decision-making strategies: a resource-focused strategy and an energy-focused strategy. Specifically, we develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based environmental regulation system to effectively manage supplemental CO2, lighting, and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) in SpaCEA. The DRL system streamlines resource production and consumption in SpaCEA using only basic environmental information like bulk CO2/O2 concentration, air temperature and humidity, without requiring detailed knowledge of the biological plant's photosynthetic, respiration and transpiration rates as well as leaf surface/canopy conditions. We simulate the SpaCEA performance for a 7-day growing period (referenced to Earth time) across four environments with varying gravity levels: Earth (1g), Mars (0.38g), the Moon (0.16g), and the International Space Station (0g). Our results show that the energy-focused strategy consistently reduces power consumption by up to 21 % but at the expense of lower oxygen output and food yield. In contrast, the resource-focused policy improves critical life support outputs with at least 40 % oxygen production, 63 % carbon dioxide removal, 40 % water recycling and 9 % food production (dry weight) over the energy-focused policy, while increasing energy demand. Furthermore, under optimized environmental regulation using both policies, the impact of gravity on resource consumption and production in SpaCEA is minimized. These findings highlight trade-offs between energy efficiency and biosystem productivity and demonstrate the potential of DRL-based control for enabling mission-specific optimization strategies for long-duration space habitation.

title: Understanding the complexities of mustard intercropping: Inferences based on land suitability and farmers’ choices in a paddy-dominated cropping system of eastern India
abstract: Mustard is often used as an intercrop in many cropping systems across the world. India is globally one of the chief producers of oilseeds and mustard oil. However, a primary hindrance of mustard production is that the productivity is comparatively lower than other oilseeds producing countries. Reasons for low crop yield and production of mustard in India include natural barriers due to soil, topography and climate; farmers' lack of knowledge, etc. In the domain of sustainable agriculture, it is well recognized that agricultural productivity is affected by numerous factors including land suitability, infrastructure and farmers' awareness. However, studies integrating all such factors in a single platform are absent, especially in the Indian context. This study has, therefore, been conducted with an objective of ascertaining the present status and possible complexities of mustard farming in eastern India by integrating diverse aspects of land suitability, production and farmers’ choices. First, the general and the mustard-specific land suitability were assessed using the Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), which included the multi-criteria analysis of a host of topographic, climatic and pedologic variables. This was validated by the available productivity data for mustard crop with the help of a bivariate scatter plot. Results reveal that eastern part of the district coinciding with Barind tract, offers excellent prospects for mustard cultivation. However, participatory resource appraisal with the farmers reveals that they are sometimes reluctant to cultivate this crop. Primary reasons suggested by them include high weeding cost, absence of proper oil mills and irrigation facilities which can be used during the dry season, as well as low market prices. Furthermore, the farmers are not aware about the prevalence of a Minimum Support Price for this crop. It is expected that the outcomes and recommendations obtained from this study may help the policy makers in adopting a sustainable guideline for expanding the scope and purview of mustard cultivation in different regions of eastern India.

title: Molten Li/Na/K ternary carbonate salt pyrolysis of biomass: A facile approach for co-production of porous biochar, CO-enriched syngas, and high-selectivity bio-oil
abstract: This study aims to systematically investigate the effects of temperature and molten carbonate salts on the formation and regulation of pyrolysis products, pine sawdust pyrolysis in molten Li2CO3-Na2CO3-K2CO3 ternary salt was examined using a fixed-bed reactor. The results indicated that high-concentration of alkali cations and CO32− anions in molten salts significantly altered reaction pathways and product distributions compared to conventional pyrolysis. Alkali cations promoted charring reactions, with increased O retention in biochar leading to higher yields with lower aromaticity. Their strong catalytic effect on primary pyrolysis and secondary cracking resulted in a substantial reduction in bio-oil yield. At 500 °C, enhanced ring-opening of sugar units, along with dehydrogenation, decarboxylation, and WGS reactions, produced an anhydrosugar-free bio-oil, accompanied by increased H2 and CO2 formation in non-condensable gas. Increasing temperature strengthened alkali cation-induced deoxygenation and cracking of bio-oil, yielding a bio-oil enriched in phenols and aromatic hydrocarbons. Concurrently, CO32− anions in molten salts acted as activators, etching the char surface to create pores while generating CO, particularly at high temperatures (e.g., 800–900 °C). A highly porous biochar (BET surface area of 971.28 m2/g) and an extremely high non-condensable gas yield (147.33 wt%) were obtained at 900 °C, with CO + H2 accounting for 82.51 vol%. The biochar produced at 800 °C (800MPY) exhibited a superior CO2 adsorption capacity of 4.5 mmol/g (@ 0 °C, 1 bar). This study demonstrates that molten carbonate salt pyrolysis of biomass enables one-step co-production of porous biochar, CO-enriched syngas, and high-selectivity bio-oil, highlighting its potential for high-value biomass utilization.

title: The impact of digital-intelligent policy synergy on corporate green transformation: A perspective based on new-quality productive forces
abstract: Against the backdrop of “dual carbon”, the synergy between digitalization and intelligentization policies is of vital importance, as it not only promotes the comprehensive green transformation of society and economy but also facilitates sustainable development of enterprises. This paper constructs a quasi-natural experiment based on the combination of the “Broadband China Strategy” and “Smart City Construction” as digital intelligence policy (DIP). By utilizing data of Chinese listed companies, it empirically verifies the role of this policy in corporate green transformation (CGT) and its potential transmission paths. The findings are as follows: First, the implementation of DIP, centered on digital development and intelligent upgrading, directly contributes to CGT. Second, DIP not only directly exerts a dual-driven effect on promoting CGT but also indirectly drives CGT through enhancing technological productivity, green productivity, and digital productivity. Third, the effect of DIP is closely associated with geographical location, corporate characteristics, and industry attributes. Enterprises in eastern regions, small-scale enterprises, and heavy-pollution enterprises can all gain more CGT dividends from the collaborative drive of DIP. Further research reveals that when the distance to surrounding cities is 200, 300, and 400 km, DIP exhibits spatial spillover effects on the promotion of CGT, though such spillover effects decrease as the geographic distance increases. This research offers valuable insights for building a digitally advanced and technologically strong nation in the current era, while also promoting the sustainable growth of enterprises.

title: Ecoregion certification and housing green premium: Evidence from the “National Ecological Civilization Construction Demonstration Zone”
abstract: This study uses China's National Ecological Civilization Construction Demonstration Zone (NECCDZ) policy as a quasi-natural experiment to examine the impact of eco-region certification on housing markets. Employing a difference-in-differences framework with second-hand housing price data from 2231 districts and counties between 2014 and 2022, we find that county-level certification increases prices by 2.4 %–6.0 %, with results robust across multiple estimation methods. The effect operates through two mechanisms. First, certification provides a credible signal of local environmental quality and long-term ecological commitment. Second, it incentivizes local governments to improve environmental conditions, enhancing air quality and greening. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect is stronger in urbanized areas with higher public environmental awareness, but weaker in rural and resource-dependent regions. These findings suggest that eco-region certification can effectively align market incentives with environmental governance, highlighting its potential as a tool for promoting sustainable urban development.

title: Climate policy, financial constraints and firm greenwashing behaviors: Evidence from China
abstract: This study investigates the causal effects of climate policy on greenwashing behavior among financially constrained firms in China. By exploiting the staggered implementation of the Low-Carbon City Pilot policy as an exogenous shock and using cash flow sensitivity of investment as a proxy for financial constraints, a staggered difference-in-difference-in-differences estimation reveals that firms under greater financial pressure exhibit a significantly higher tendency toward greenwashing practices in low-carbon pilot cities. An underlying mechanism is that stricter climate policies are associated with higher non-compliance costs and greater financial distress, particularly for firms with limited financial resources in low-carbon pilot cities, thereby intensifying greenwashing incentives. Furthermore, the observed effects are more pronounced among firms with lower information disclosure quality, non-state-owned firms, and firms operating in industries with lower competition intensity. This study contributes to the existing literature on climate policy by moving beyond its well-documented positive effects on firm's environmental performance to highlight unintended consequences for financially constrained firms. It also provides timely policy implications for central regulators seeking to curb ESG-related misleading practice.

title: From signals to actions: Understanding sustainable fashion consumption through a multisource signalling mechanism—evidence from China
abstract: The increasingly severe environmental impact of the fashion industry is a critical issue that demands immediate attention, and sustainable development presents a viable and promising approach for addressing it. However, researchers still lack a systematic explanation of how individuals make sustainable choices when influenced by multiple sources of signals. In this study, we investigated the problem from a micro-level perspective, focusing on consumers' purchasing behaviour to generate novel holistic insights and support the sustainable transformation of the fashion industry. To systematically examine the driving mechanisms of sustainable fashion purchasing behaviour, we integrated signalling theory and stimulus–organism–response theory, employing a sequential mixed-methods design for the empirical investigation. In the qualitative research phase, we developed research hypotheses and a conceptual model through an extensive literature review and qualitative interviews. Subsequently, in the quantitative phase, we collected survey data to empirically test the hypothesised pathways within the model. The empirical results showed that four categories of signals—environmental concern, recyclability, green innovation, and social participation—can indirectly promote consumers’ sustainable fashion purchasing behaviour by stimulating their perceptions of economic, green, and social values. In this article, we present a signal–value–action mechanism framework for uncovering how signals from different sources jointly guide green consumption tendencies through the synergistic interplay of multidimensional values. Simultaneously, we offer strategic recommendations to support the practical implementation of green principles and assist the fashion industry in achieving a sustainable transition.

title: A novel TpAQ-COF/ZnS/ZnIn2S4 ternary photocatalyst with double Z-scheme heterostructure for visible light photocatalytic degradation of 2,4-dichlorophenol
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) represent a class of crystalline polymers whose structure is built from covalent bonds, which have a porous structure and good light trapping ability. However, the carrier mobility of COFs is low, resulting in a high electron hole recombination rate. Before practical application, it is usually modified by constructing a heterojunction. In this paper, TpAQ-COF/ZnS/ZnIn2S4 (TZI) double Z-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts are prepared by the solvothermal method to grow ZnIn2S4 and ZnS on 1,3,5-triformyl phloroglucinol (Tp) and 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (AQ) COF (TpAQ-COF). Under simulated sunlight, TZI-2 (mass ratio of TpAQ-COF: ZnS: ZnIn2S4 is 1:2:1) has the best removal rate of 30 mg L−1 2,4-dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP) within 70 min, and the removal rate is 90.3 %. The 2,4-DCP removal rate by TZI-2 declined by just 10.8 % after five consecutive cycles, showing excellent stability. The enhancement of photocatalytic efficiency in TZI-2 can be attributed to the fact that the high specific surface area of TpAQ-COF provides rich adsorption sites to enhance the adsorption capacity of the photocatalyst for pollutants. In addition, the double Z-scheme charge transfer mechanism between TpAQ-COF, ZnS and ZnIn2S4 also promotes charge separation and migration, inhibits the recombination of photo-generated electron hole pairs, and improves the redox ability of the photocatalyst. This design shows promise for treating refractory chlorinated organic pollutants.

title: Eco-friendly power generation process using Allam cycle and cryogenic carbon capture for biogas upgrading
abstract: The growing energy demand has led to increased fossil fuel consumption in the power generation sector, thereby intensifying concerns over environmental degradation. Accordingly, various economic strategies and research initiatives have been directed toward bioenergy as a viable alternative. This study investigates a biogas-based power generation system by evaluating its energy efficiency, environmental impact, and economic feasibility in conjunction with various renewable energy sources. To upgrade biogas, a cryogenic desublimation process is employed, utilizing cold energy recovered from an air separation unit. The resulting biomethane and oxygen are subsequently fed into the Allam cycle, a regenerative Brayton cycle, for high-efficiency power generation. The overall energy efficiency of the proposed process ranges from 44.33 % to 54.15 %, depending on the share of renewable electricity utilized. The integrated desublimation and oxy-fuel combustion system achieves a high carbon capture rate, recovering 99.78 % of the carbon originally contained in the biogas. When various renewable energy sources are considered, the process yields negative carbon emissions, ranging from −740.45 gCO2eq/kW to −471.51 gCO2eq/kW. A conventional techno-economic analysis determined a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of $95.3/MWh, primarily driven by the high biogas cost of $12.8/MMBtu. In particular, at a biogas price of $16/MMBtu, the LCOE remains within the range of $81.6/MWh to $120.0/MWh on average, even when the variability of renewable energy sources is additionally considered. In addition to its environmental advantages, the proposed process is compatible with existing oxy-fuel combustion facilities, suggesting its potential as a substitute for current fossil-fuel-based power generation systems.

title: Tailored biochar amendments enhance cadmium immobilization via microbial community modulation and soil biotransformation processes
abstract: Biochar is increasingly applied to remediate cadmium (Cd)-contaminated soils, yet the microbial mechanisms by which biochar governs Cd speciation remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we evaluated three structurally and chemically distinct biochars—Juglans regia, Flaveria bidentis, and Spartina alterniflora—applied at 1 %, 3 %, and 5 % to coastal saline–alkali soil to elucidate how biochar-driven microbiome reassembly contributes to Cd immobilization. Biochar amendments significantly reshaped bacterial and fungal diversity, with bacterial communities showing greater sensitivity to salinity- and nutrient-mediated stresses. The low-ash J. regia biochar enhanced α-diversity and microhabitat quality, fostering stable functional guilds that supported predictable Cd biotransformation. In contrast, high-ash, ion-releasing F. bidentis and S. alterniflora biochars intensified osmotic and stoichiometric pressures, promoting deterministic assembly and enriching stress-tolerant, Cd-resistant taxa despite reduced overall diversity. Across treatments, biochar was associated with shifts toward microbial taxa predicted to encode pathways related to extracellular polymeric substance production, siderophore biosynthesis, and biofilm formation, which are potentially linked to Cd chelation and detoxification. KEGG-based predictions further revealed strengthened pathways related to lipid biosynthesis, membrane reinforcement, and stress resilience, indicating functional reprogramming of microbial metabolism under Cd exposure. Cd fractionation analyses confirmed substantial reductions in bioavailable Cd following amendment. Collectively, these results demonstrate that tailored feedstock selection can strategically couple biochar's physicochemical properties with microbiome-mediated detoxification to optimize Cd remediation in saline–alkali soils.

title: Exploring the synergistic effects of the effectiveness of carbon governance policy instruments
abstract: The Chinese government emphasizes the importance of achieving ecofriendly growth. It has employed various types of carbon governance policy instruments (CGPIs), striving to transition from a high-emission, high-pollution economic development model to a more sustainable one. To investigate the practical effectiveness of CGPIs in China from 2016 to 2022, this study employs content analysis to quantify the cumulative effectiveness of seven categories of CGPIs, applies necessary condition analysis (NCA) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify complex causal recipes of CGPI effectiveness on carbon productivity (CP). The study finds that: (1) the cumulative effectiveness of all types of CGPIs has continuously increased, although the number of policies has not followed the same trend; (2) no individual CGPI constitutes a necessary condition for achieving high-level CP; and (3) five feasible and representative paths of CGPIs are identified that consistently lead to high -level CP in the context of China. Only direct supply and property rights trading instruments can be effective solely; other CGPIs require complementary implementation. From a configurational perspective, this study contributes to policy instrument literature and provides practical implications for policymakers to enhance and refine the existing structure of CGPIs.

title: The power of play: Exploring the impact of self-directed and social-priented gamification on low-carbon engagement
abstract: During the escalating global climate crisis, green gamification design has been recognized as an innovative approach to promote users' low-carbon engagement. However, empirical research exploring how different design directions influence user engagement—particularly from the perspective of subject‒object interaction—remains limited. To address this gap, this study integrates the rational decision-making framework of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with the dynamic trigger mechanism of the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM) to investigate how self-directed and social-oriented green gamification designs impact users' low-carbon engagement. Drawing on survey data from users of Ant Forest on Alipay, one of China's leading online payment platforms, the proposed research model was tested using structural equation modeling. The results indicate that both self-directed and social-oriented green gamification designs significantly enhance users' low-carbon engagement, with self-directed exerting a notably stronger effect. Furthermore, subjective norms and perceived behavioral control partially mediate the effect of self-directed green gamification design on users' low-carbon engagement. In contrast, the social-oriented design fails to activate these mediating pathways effectively due to the absence of intrinsic value support. This research offers new insights into the role of green gamification in promoting low-carbon engagement and provides a theoretical foundation for platform design, policy development, and the advancement of cross-sector carbon credit systems.

title: Social globalisation and environmental sustainability: An analysis on ASEAN countries
abstract: This study examines the impact of social globalization on carbon emissions in ASEAN-9 countries and analyzes how this relationship is shaped by economic growth, renewable energy consumption, and natural resource rents. ASEAN countries provide a significant sample for assessing the environmental sustainability effects of globalization due to their rapidly increasing economic integration and diverse environmental dynamics over the 1990–2021 period. The study applies Powell's non-additive fixed effects quantile regression method to analyze the environmental effects of social globalization across different emission levels. The results indicate that social globalization positively influences carbon emissions, with a more pronounced effect in nations exhibiting moderate to high emission levels. Although per capita GDP correlates with increased emissions, the utilization of renewable energy significantly mitigates carbon emissions, especially in nations with elevated emission rates. Moreover, natural resource rents are associated with heightened carbon emissions; however, a clear causal relationship between resource rents and carbon emissions is not established, indicating that the environmental impacts of resource reliance may be mediated by indirect mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that the efficacy of renewable energy in mitigating carbon emissions is contingent upon national energy policy, infrastructural investments, and technology progress. Although renewable energy is essential for reducing emissions, sustained reductions necessitate augmented investment in clean energy technology. The findings underscore the necessity for increased expenditures in renewable energy, enhanced management of the environmental repercussions of social globalization, and the establishment of sustainable natural resource policy in ASEAN nations.

title: Valorization of partially combusted wood fly ash with nano-silica as low-impact alternative to coal fly ash in cementitious composites
abstract: The declining availability of coal fly ash (CFA) due to the phasing out of coal-fired power plants has created an urgent demand for alternative supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) in sustainable concrete construction. This study aims to effectively recycle wood fly ash (WFA), a by-product from wood biomass combustion, as an SCM for greener construction practices. While WFA has demonstrated promising potential, its partially burnt nature negatively impacts mechanical properties due to the presence of porous biochars. This study explores the valorization of WFA as a low-carbon SCM through the addition of a small dosage of nano-silica (NS) to mitigate these drawbacks. Ternary-blended cementitious composites were prepared by replacing cement with 15 % and 30 % WFA, combined with 3 % NS, to evaluate fresh, mechanical, durability, and microstructural properties. The results were compared with composites made of commercially available classes C and F CFA. It was observed that although NS addition negatively affected the fresh properties, it greatly enhanced the mechanical properties, chloride resistance, water absorption, and freeze-thaw durability of the WFA-modified composites. The improved freeze-thaw resistance can potentially extend the service life, thereby enhancing environmental compatibility. The mix having 15 % WFA and 3 % NS outperformed the control one in both mechanical and durability aspects, indicating that a low-level NS replacement can effectively mitigate the drawbacks of partially combusted WFA. Overall, CFAs demonstrated better performance than WFA at the 30 % level. • Wood fly ash possesses good pozzolanic properties. • Nano-silica improves the strength and durability of wood fly ash-based composites. • The mix with 15 % wood fly ash and 3 % nano-silica outperforms the control one. • Overall, coal fly ash demonstrates better performance than wood fly ash.

title: Optimal allocation of the water and land resources based on water-carbon-food-ecology trade-off and synergy in concentrated agricultural planting areas
abstract: Optimizing the spatial allocation of water and land resources under water–carbon–food–ecology (WCFE) trade-offs is a key challenge in concentrated agricultural regions. In this study, we establish the WCFE-SLOpt model, which advances previous approaches by integrating multi-objective resource allocation with spatial layout optimization. Compared with conventional allocation models, WCFE-SLOpt explicitly enhances ecological connectivity, reduces land conversion costs, and balances economic, ecological, and carbon objectives. The model was applied in 11 subregions of Western Jilin Province in China under varying resource conditions. The results demonstrate that the coupled model effectively coordinates multiple optimization objectives and dynamically adjusts land use based on resource constraints. Under an economic-priority strategy, irrigation water use decreased by 2.98 %–15.97 %. Under a carbon-priority strategy, maize cultivation increased by 7 % and carbon sequestration increased by approximately 2.97 × 109 kg. The synergistic optimization strategy involved minor adjustments to planting structures, reducing irrigation water use by 4.58 %–16.86 %, increasing carbon sequestration by 2.86 %. Finally, the ecological connectivity increased by 0.03 %–0.14 %.

title: Mapping circular economy product and material flows in healthcare: A visual taxonomy
abstract: The healthcare sector contributes substantially to environmental pollution, affecting ecosystems and public health. Circular economy (CE) strategies offer potential solutions, but existing frameworks provide limited guidance for healthcare, overlooking factors such as infection control, decontamination, and staff workload. We developed the Circular Healthcare Flows visual , a taxonomy of CE strategies for medical devices, using observations in sterilization departments, recycling facilities, and manufacturing plants; 21 expert interviews; and a systematic review of 1104 studies (68 full-text reviews). Additional stakeholder feedback validated and refined the taxonomy. The taxonomy identifies 13 CE strategies—refuse, replace, rethink, reduce, reuse, maintain, repair, refurbish, remanufacture, repurpose, recycle, renew, and recover—and organizes them in a healthcare-specific framework. Iterative feedback ensured that the taxonomy is clear, practically applicable, and addresses sector-specific regulatory, clinical, and operational constraints. The Circular Healthcare Flows visual provides a practical tool to standardize terminology and guide the implementation of CE strategies in healthcare. By offering conceptual structure and actionable guidance, it supports informed decision-making, facilitates collaboration among stakeholders, and encourages consistent application of circular strategies across the sector. IJzenbrandt was partially funded by Erasmus University Rotterdam and the Health and Technology Convergence Alliance of TU Delft, Erasmus MC, and Erasmus University Rotterdam. Hoveling was funded through the DiCE project (EU grant agreement no. 101060184). Opinions expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect those of the EU or REA.

title: Evaluating spatial heterogeneity and suitability patterns for soybean cultivation in Heilongjiang: A productivity-oriented approach
abstract: Soybean is not only a vital food and oil crop but also an essential nitrogen-fixing plant that contributes to environmental sustainability. In China, however, soybean production is heavily dependent on imports. Despite national efforts to expand soybean cultivation to increase planting area and yield, current research has yet to comprehensively assess soybean suitability based on yield potential. To fill in this gap, this study focuses on Heilongjiang Province, the primary soybean-producing region in China. A grid-scale soybean yield prediction model was developed by integrating remote sensing vegetation indices across phenological stages with the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and Random Forest (RF) methods. Spatial autocorrelation, combined with a MaxEnt model incorporating environmental and anthropogenic factors, was then used to identify high-yield areas and map soybean suitability zones, based on which potential reductions in carbon emissions were estimated. The results indicate that the RF model achieved higher prediction accuracy, and incorporating the temporal dynamics of vegetation indices during the filling seeds and senescence stages further improved yield prediction, reducing the RMSE by 9.8 % compared with models using only static indices. The land suitability for high-yield soybean in Heilongjiang is primarily determined by the temperature of the wettest quarter, isothermality, elevation, and precipitation of the warmest month. The extremely suitable area covered 28,617.4 km2, accounting for 6.3 % of the province's area, and was predominantly located in the Sanjiang and Songnen Plains, where suitable habitats and high-yield hotspots exhibited substantial spatial overlap. However, in 2021, only 65.3 % of soybean cultivation occurred within these suitable zones, highlighting a notable mismatch between resource endowments and actual planting patterns. These findings highlight the need for targeted soybean expansion in ecologically suitable areas and provide scientific support for optimizing land use and advancing sustainable agricultural development.

title: Comparative assessment of biochar reactor technologies for biomass conversion: Design, performance, and application suitability
abstract: The effectiveness of biochar for ecological restoration, toxicity remediation and carbon sequestration are fundamentally dependent on the biochar production technology. This review provides a systematic comparison of thermochemical conversion techniques such as pyrolysis (slow, rotary kiln, auger-based), gasification (downdraft and fluidized bed) and hydrothermal carbonization (HTC). Key performance metrics such as temperature profile, residence time, emissions regulation, and scalability are evaluated alongside critical biochar qualities such as surface area, porosity, fixed carbon content, cation exchange capacity, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon. Priority has been given to aligning the biochar produced from each reactor with their respective environmental applications based on the biochar functions, such as nutrient retention, pH adjustment, and carbon fixation. The reactor performances have been summarized in context with production capacity, capital cost, and other variables related to system selection. The review uniquely integrates technical, environmental, and agronomic factors to propose a decision framework that aligns biochar production technologies with appropriate feedstocks, logistical settings, and long-term sustainability goals. In conclusion, this interdisciplinary approach fills a gap in literature by linking reactor engineering with functional outcomes in land management and climate resilience.

title: Labor price distortion and carbon emission performance: The role of technological progress bias in China
abstract: Carbon intensity and per capita carbon emissions are key indicators of carbon emission performance, but the connection between factor price distortion and these indicators remains unclear. Utilizing panel data from 284 cities covering the years 2006–2020 in China, this study investigates how labor price distortions affect carbon intensity and per capita carbon emissions. By employing Stochastic Frontier Analysis to measure technological progress bias, the research further explores its moderating role in these relationships. The results show that: (1) For every unit increase in labor price distortion, carbon intensity decreases by 2.1 %, but at the cost of a 7.8 % increase in per capita carbon emissions. (2) A one-unit increase in labor price distortion reduces the energy-capital ratio by 2.4 %, driving down carbon intensity; Conversely, it raises the energy-labor ratio by 8.5 %, leading to higher per capita carbon emissions. (3) When technological progress is biased toward energy, the suppressive effect of labor price distortions on carbon intensity diminishes by at least 2.7 %, while their stimulating impact on per capita carbon emissions increases by at least 4.8 %. This study not only explains the phenomenon of declining carbon intensity and rising per capita carbon emissions in China, but also advances research on labor price distortion's effects from the dimensions of factor structure and carbon emission performance.

title: Complex network analysis of water scarcity risk propagation in the Yellow River Basin under the quality–quantity–environmental flow requirement (QQE) framework
abstract: Poor water quality and ecological function maintenance can exacerbate regional water scarcity, potentially leading to economic losses. This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of the impact of water scarcity risk on the supply chain network in the Yellow River Basin (YRB) under different scenarios, using the quantity-quality-environmental flow requirement (QQE) framework. We found that neglecting pollution control and ecological function maintenance will severely underestimate regional water scarcity. When ecological health is maintained at a moderately protective flow level (equivalent to 60 % of mean annual runoff), local water scarcity risk (LWSR) increases significantly compared to the scenario considering only water quantity. Further raising the environmental flow requirement to a fully protective level (100 % of runoff) leads to an even greater escalation of risk. In addition, this study integrates the multi-regional input–output (MRIO) model to construct a multilayer complex network that tracks the critical sectors and pathways for virtual water scarcity risk (VWSR) transmission. The results indicate that poor water quality and ecological function maintenance have expanded the potential economic losses due to water scarcity within the intra-provincial supply chain. For the inter-provincial supply chain, not only have the VWSR transmission scales increased, but the hotspots and transmission patterns have also changed, leading to higher transmission efficiency of VWSR. This has reduced the overall resilience of the YRB supply chain to risks. Our study emphasizes that pollution control and ecological protection are also crucial components in mitigating water scarcity.

title: Transition from grazing to indoor feeding elevates the risks of antibiotic resistance gene transmission in Tibetan sheep
abstract: The shift toward intensive livestock farming on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) has raised biosecurity concerns regarding the spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) through animal waste. In this study, ARGs dynamics in Tibetan sheep are examined under three dietary systems: grazing, total mixed ration (TMR) indoor feeding, and flaxseed-supplemented TMR. Fecal ARG abundance in the indoor groups (TMR and flaxseed-TMR) increased 8.8- and 9.7-fold, respectively, compared with that in the grazing group (P < 0.01), dominated by aminoglycoside (APH(3′)-IIIa), MLS (cfr(E), lsa(B), lnu(C)), and tetracycline (tet(W), tet(O)) resistance genes. Metagenomic analysis revealed Lachnospiraceae may be as the primary ARGs host, which was significantly enriched in the indoor groups (14.6 % and 15.7 % in groups I and L, respectively, and 9.0 % in group G). Lachnospiraceae was positively correlated (P < 0.05) with intestinal metabolites associated with stress responses: pro-inflammatory agents (4-phenylbutyric acid, stercobilin) and repair mediators (urocanic acid/5-hydroxyindole-3-acetic acid/indole-3-acetic acid). Redundancy analysis attributed 42 % of the ARGs variation to the combined effects of changes in microbial metabolism, suggesting that dietary stress leads to changes in microbial community structure and that some amino acid metabolites that cause intestinal inflammation promote the enrichment of Lachnospiraceae. On the one hand, Lachnospiraceae serve as potential reservoirs of resistance genes and mobile genetic elements (MGEs), leading to increased abundance of resistance genes. On the other hand, increased abundance of MGEs can also promote horizontal transfer of resistance genes. These findings reveal a critical trade-off between livestock productivity and the risk of antibiotic resistance in plateau ecosystems. Sustainable strategies, such as cyclical grazing (alternating pasture-indoor feeding) or microbiome-stabilized feed formulations, are proposed to maintain agricultural production while mitigating biosecurity threats.

title: Cross-cutting scenarios for air pollution reduction and carbon mitigation in heavy-duty trucks
abstract: Globally, the road freight sector, particularly heavy-duty trucks (HDTs), has represented a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and air pollutants, challenging international climate and health goals. While technological fixes have been common, a comprehensive assessment of cross-cutting strategies integrating technological, regulatory, and demand-side measures (e.g., Avoid-Shift-Improve, or A-S-I) has remained a critical research gap, especially regarding regional synergies and equity. This study addressed this gap by developing interdisciplinary scenarios for China's HDTs. It employed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) deep learning model to forecast HDT populations, and then designed and evaluated 12 cross-cutting A-S-I scenarios for 2020–2060. The results revealed that promoting zero-emission trucks produced the most significant cumulative reductions in criteria air pollutants and carbon emissions. However, enhancing emission standards generated the largest cumulative reductions in air pollutants, with NOx reductions reaching up to 110 Tg, which was 36 % higher than the reductions in the zero-emission truck scenario. In combined scenarios, “technology” achieved the highest CO/CO2 reductions, while “regulation” delivered the most substantial HC, PM2.5, and NOx reductions and exhibited the lowest Gini coefficient, indicating high equity. The analysis concluded that economically developed eastern regions should focus on demand-side and information measures, while central and western regions should prioritize traffic management, technological advancements, and economic initiatives. Future efforts should incorporate regionally-tailored measures to maximize synergies.

title: Clean valorization of lignin via radical-enhanced photoelectric collaborative selective cleavage of C–C bonds using a P-doped hollow porous electrocatalyst
abstract: Developing green technologies for converting abundant lignin biomass into valuable chemicals is a cornerstone of cleaner production and a circular bioeconomy. This study addresses this goal by constructing a photoelectric collaborative system for the selective cleavage of lignin's recalcitrant C–C bonds, a strategy reliant on the powerful combination of Cβ• and •OOH radicals. In this work, a hollow spherical P-doped CuO composite electrocatalyst had been firstly prepared by hard template method. The morphology of the hollow porous structure, the abundant oxygen vacancy and the P-doped regulated adsorption type all contributed to the efficient production of •OOH. With the photoelectric collaborative system, 2-phenoxy-1-phenylethanol (pp-ol) conversion rates increased by absolute margins of 8.44 % and 52.04 %, while total product yields rose by 125.65 % and 26.04 % compared to single photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, respectively. Beside combining •OOH and Cβ• to produce the path of pp-ol, 1O2 and •O2− were also involved in pp-ol conversion. By elucidating the catalyst's structure-performance relationship and demonstrating outstanding synergistic effects, this research provides new insights and a viable green pathway for the high-value valorization of lignin.

title: Exploring global synergies in agricultural mitigation and adaptation: an integrated perspective on agriculture carbon emission and production efficiency
abstract: Agriculture faces the dual challenge of adapting to climate change while mitigating its environmental footprint, yet current assessments often lack integrated and dynamic perspectives. This study proposes an efficiency-based framework using agricultural production efficiency (APE) and agricultural carbon efficiency (ACE) to respectively represent adaptive and mitigative capacity. We develop a dynamic union frontier directional distance function (DUDDF) to evaluate 174 countries (2001–2022) and classify them into four synergy types based on period efficiency changes: mitigation-adaptation synergy (MAS), adaptation-dominant trade-off (ADT), Mitigation-Dominant trade-off (MDT), and ineffective/non-synergy (INS). The results reveal significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global agricultural climate performance. Oceania maintains high synergy, while Europe shows systemic decline. The proportion of MAS countries increased from 47.7 % to 58.6 % across four periods, whereas INS countries decreased from 14.9 % to 5.7 %. Transition pathway analysis further identifies three typical patterns: a shift from MDT to MAS or ADT, a transition from INS to ADT and then to MAS, and high persistence among MAS countries. Theoretically, this study integrates efficiency and synergy concepts within a production-theoretic framework that accommodates technological heterogeneity. Practically, it provides a state-contingent diagnostic tool for targeting policies and suggests integrating APE/ACE into NDC monitoring systems to help countries achieve durable mitigation-adaptation synergy without compromising food security.

title: Young consumers' attitudes toward selecting green delivery option of ready-to-eat food products: a case of West Bengal, India using extended theory of planned behaviour model
