title: The green performance of major economies within global green value chains: A 20-year review
abstract: Global value chains (GVCs) are central to both economic integration and the redistribution of environmental burdens. However, existing studies have largely focused on single-dimensional metrics, either economic value added or environmental footprints, failing to provide an integrated assessment of green performance. This gap limits our understanding of genuine trade benefits in an environmentally constrained world. To bridge this gap, this study develops a novel framework for decomposing global green value chains (GGVCs) based on environmentally extended multi-regional input–output (EMRIO) model, to assess the evolution of green value added (GVA) across 19 major economies from 2000 to 2020. The analysis reveals that the gap in the green production and exports level between developed and developing economies has largely narrowed in the past 20 years with their disproportionate strides in enhancing environmental sustainability, while developed economies continue to capture a higner share of GVA by externalizing environmental burdens through trade. GVCs trade production dominates the GVA that is generated by the production of trade products. Substantial heterogeneity emerges across economies, with resource- and technology-intensive economies capturing the higher levels of real green trade gains. For most economies, changes in the economic scale are the main driving factors of changes in GVA, and the effects of green technology and input‒output technology are also important factors that cannot be ignored. The study contributes empirical novelty by quantifying green gains along value chains over two decades, and it underscores the urgent need for policies that align trade benefits with environmental responsibilities. Our results inform international just transition and suggest that green upgrading of GVCs is pivotal for achieving equitable and sustainable low-carbon transitions.

title: Mild extraction of PdAg precious metal components and efficient recovery of Al2O3 supports from spent acetylene hydrogenation catalyst
abstract: Addressing the challenges of simultaneously extracting Pd and Ag components from spent acetylene hydrogenation catalysts, severe structural damage to the Al2O3 supports, and high wastewater discharge, here, we propose a “hydrochloric acid–ammonium chloride–ammonia” (HCl–NH4Cl–NH3) complexation system that enables efficient extraction of PdAg leaching alongside recovery of the Al2O3 supports. The leaching rates of Pd and Ag exhibit an increasing trend with rising concentrations of HCl, NH4Cl, and NH3, the increase of reaction temperature, and the extension of reaction time. Nevertheless, excessively high HCl concentration, overly elevated reaction temperature, and unduly prolonged reaction time caused some damage to the structure of the alumina support and reduce its mechanical strength. Under optimized conditions (0.2 M HCl, 1.0 M NH4Cl, 120 °C, 6 h, 5 wt% ammonia), the PdAg components were efficiently leached while effectively preserving the crystal phase and pore structure of the Al2O3 beads. The leaching rates of Pd and Ag reached 95.6 % and 94.4 %, respectively; and the recovered Al2O3 beads have a pore diameter of 30.8 nm, a specific pore volume of 0.244 mL g−1, a specific surface area of 29.2 m2/g, and a crushing strength of 53.2 N, corresponding to retention rates of 95.2 %, 96.0 %, 100.2 %, and 98.6 %, respectively. The HCl–NH4Cl–NH3 complexation system, combined with cyclic washing, shows advantages of low cost, mild extraction conditions, and reduced wastewater discharge, which keeps to the principles of green development.

title: An integrated renewable system for brackish water to achieve zero liquid discharge with nitrate reduction
abstract: Water scarcity is a growing global concern, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions where brackish groundwater is increasingly used as a freshwater source. However, the desalination of such sources faces major challenges, notably the generation of saline brine and the presence of nitrate contamination due to agricultural and urban activities. This study presents a novel zero liquid discharge process integrated with biological denitrification to enable sustainable treatment of brines derived from brackish water reverse osmosis. The system combines membrane technologies, thermal concentration, atmospheric evaporation, and crystallization, all powered by renewable energy sources based on photovoltaic and biomass. Three process configurations are experimentally evaluated under real operating conditions in a southeastern Spain case study. The highest water recovery, 87.9% with respect to the incoming brine from a brackish water reverse osmosis, was associated with an energy cost of 26.7 kWh/m 3 freshwater. Extending the operating hours of the atmospheric technologies led to a reduction in total energy consumption, 11.8 kWh/m 3 freshwater; however, the water recovery dropped to 84.8% as a result of increased atmospheric evaporation. Moreover, bypassing the thermal technologies leads to a further reduction in total energy cost to 5.5 kWh/m 3 recovered water, but increased the system’s dependence on ambient conditions, with a water recovery of 83.6%. In general, this work demonstrates the feasibility of an integrated, flexible, and site-adaptable zero liquid discharge approach for brackish water desalination that addresses both nitrate removal and brine minimization within a sustainable framework.

title: Risk identification and prediction of corporate low-carbon transition via multi-agent reinforcement learning: Using OpenEI and CDP database
abstract: This work identifies and predicts the multi-dimensional risks faced by enterprises during the low-carbon transition process, thus improving the scientific nature of risk management and the targeted nature of policy interventions. Based on this, the work implements an integrated model combining multi-agent reinforcement learning with causal inference. The data used includes the multi-source heterogeneous data from the Open Energy Information platform and the Carbon Disclosure Project database. The potential transformation failure issues may arise in the enterprises under the influence of factors such as insufficient carbon disclosure, delayed policy response, and weak governance structures. To address these issues, the work designs behavior mechanisms for three types of agents: enterprises, governments, and investors. It establishes a risk evolution simulation system and uses causal graphs and the Causal Forest algorithm to identify key causal paths. This work focuses on solving the following problems: (1) How to model the dynamic game behavior between enterprises and the policy environment for risk prediction; (2) How to identify deep mechanism variables for risk formation through causal inference; (3) How to achieve integrated modeling of risk identification, mechanism explanation, and intervention evaluation. Experimental comparisons with models such as Deep Causal Forest and Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning are made. The results demonstrate that the optimized model outperforms others in prediction accuracy, stability, and interpretability. With a sample size of 3,000, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0.882, an Area Under Curve value of 0.957, and a precision of 0.854, significantly outperforming existing models. Furthermore, causal tracing results show that carbon disclosure quality, corporate governance capability, and policy intensity are the three core causal risk variables. Among them, the average causal effect of carbon disclosure scores is −0.164, indicating high intervention potential. Therefore, this work provides theoretical innovation and technical pathways for risk identification and prediction in corporate low-carbon transition, and offers significant reference value and practical implications for green governance and corporate strategic decision-making.

title: Transport, logistics, and emergent technology within the circular economy
abstract: The paper reviews various important topics at the nexus of the themes of the special issue Transport, Logistics, and Emergent Technology within the Circular Economy. An overview of the articles and directions for research are also presented.

title: Outstanding self-healing ability of weathered asphalts endowed with deeply degraded tire rubber
abstract: The decline in the self-healing capability of aged asphalt leads to the deterioration of pavement. Incorporating tire rubber into asphalt both enhances the self-healing ability of aged asphalt and provides a sustainable solution to the growing accumulation of waste tires. In this study, deeply degraded tire rubber (DR) containing a high content of liquid rubber was used as a modifier to evaluate the self-healing ability of aged asphalt. The effects of DR on the physical, chemical, and rheological properties of the modified asphalt during weathering were investigated. Dynamic mechanical analyzer, dynamic shear rheometer, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, fluorescence microscope, gel permeation chromatography and toluene solubility analysis were used to explore the self-healing ability and aging mechanism. The self-healing mechanisms were analyzed through wetting and molecular diffusion. The results revealed that DR increased the surface energy and enhanced the molecular segment mobility, thus significantly enhancing the self-healing efficiency (from 72.9 % to 100.9 % at 25 °C) of modified asphalt, concurrently reducing the initial self-healing temperature (from 30 to −10 °C). Fluorescence microscopy indicated that the DR modified asphalt retained its network structure. Rheological properties (lower complex modulus) and toluene solubility tests of aged samples demonstrated that DR delayed asphalt aging through a degradation-recombination process during weathering. Moreover, the degradation of rubber and hardening of asphalt synergistically modulated the viscoelastic behavior of the composite modified asphalt. Understanding the self-healing behavior of tire rubber in the modified asphalt during weathering is of great significance for improving pavement service life.

title: Silica-structured lignin biochar engineered via pyrolysis for multifunctional remediation of Cd-contaminated soils
abstract: Soil cadmium (Cd) pollution poses a serious threat to food security and ecosystem health. Silicon (Si)-modified biochar shows great promise for remediation; however, the critical influence of the timing of Si introduction (whether during hydrothermal or pyrolysis synthesis) on Si speciation, stability, and interactions within soil-plant systems has been largely overlooked. This study systematically compares two preparation methods: introducing silicon during hydrothermal (HPC-Si@HT) or pyrolysis (HPC-Si@PY) stages. Comprehensive characterization revealed that HPC-Si@PY formed a stable amorphous silica structure, yielding a significantly higher Cd2+ adsorption capacity (315.53 mg/g) than HPC-Si@HT, primarily via ion exchange and C-Si complexation. In contrast, HPC-Si@HT, with lower stability, relied on complexation and precipitation. Pot experiments confirmed the remarkable remediation efficacy of HPC-Si@PY: it reduced exchangeable Cd by 26.1 % while increasing residual Cd by 143.3 % through silicon-driven precipitation and pH modulation. Furthermore, HPC-Si@PY enhances soil multifunctionality by improving nutrient cycling and enriching Cd-resistant microbes. For Pakchoi, HPC-Si@PY increases biomass by 81.67 % and reduces Cd accumulation by 68.96 % through integrated mechanisms of rhizosphere immobilization, antioxidant activation, and silicon-mediated deposition. The limited performance of HPC-Si@HT underscores the fundamental importance of incorporating silicon during the pyrolysis stage to create stable, reactive amorphous silica structures. These findings establish crucial design principles for engineering effective silicon-biochar that enable superior cross-scale remediation of Cd-contaminated environments.

title: Seasonal response greenhouse gas accounting model supporting regionalized carbon reduction in wastewater treatment plants
abstract: Greenhouse gas mitigation in wastewater treatment plants is imperative under global climate change. However, existing greenhouse gas estimation models lack seasonal adaptability and high-resolution data integration, obscuring spatiotemporal emission heterogeneity and hindering climate-specific strategies. To address these limitations, a seasonal-responsive greenhouse gas accounting framework was developed, incorporating temperature-sensitive emission factors and multi-temporal datasets to holistically quantify process-wide emissions. To validate the model's seasonal responsiveness, greenhouse gas emission accounting was conducted specifically for wastewater treatment plants in cold regions. The findings revealed marked seasonal disparities in emissions, with winter greenhouse gas intensity surging by 26.24 %. Compared to traditional carbon accounting models, the proposed model applied to high-temporal-resolution datasets exhibits significantly enhanced sensitivity to seasonal fluctuations. Leveraging the regional emission patterns derived from the seasonal-responsive model, a region-tailored near-zero-carbon framework was developed to achieve substantial carbon offset potential without compromising treatment efficacy. By bridging seasonal emission dynamics with greenhouse gas reduction imperatives, this work provides scalable strategies for transforming wastewater treatment plants into energy-efficient systems, advancing global climate governance objectives.

title: Integrated processing of ionic liquid recovery with clean hydrogen production via electrodialysis in biorefinery
abstract: Ionic liquids have caught wide attention in biorefinery due to a few unique characteristics. The efficient and fast recycling of ionic liquids is necessary before their scale-up application in practical biorefinery. The feasibility of integrated ionic liquid recovery with clean hydrogen production has rarely been studied. Electrodialysis has been verified valid in the recovery of different ionic liquids after biomass processing, which could also be used for clean hydrogen production. Thus the integrated recovery of ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate (EmimAc) with clean hydrogen production after biomass pretreatment was studied based on an electrodialysis unit, which could selectively transfer Emim+ with Ac− from diluted compartment to concentrated compartment and realize the hydrogen evolution reaction of H+ on the cathode. The recovery ratio of EmimAc, transfer rate of Emim+ and specific energy consumption for EmimAc recovery reached 98.7 %, 598.2 mmol/(m2·min) and 7.385 mol/kw·h. The production rate of H2 and Faraday efficiency approached 670.76 mmol/(m2·min) and 97.1 %. The operational stability of electrodialysis and recycling performance of regenerated EmimAc were both testified for 5 cycles without showing obvious reduction. The calculated recovery cost for EmimAc was less than 0.5 % of its purchasing price. Results of this research provided a new insight for the system design of cleaner processing of ionic liquid recovery with H2 production in biorefinery.

title: Resilient planning and operational management of renewable-integrated hydrogen refueling stations with multiple storage units under delivery delays
abstract: The large-scale deployment of hydrogen-powered transportation requires economically viable and operationally resilient control strategies for hydrogen refueling stations (HRSs) operating under renewable variability, dynamic hydrogen demand, and logistics-induced delivery delays associated with fueling hydrogen mobility. To address this, this study develops a relaxation-based model predictive control (RMPC) framework for a renewable-integrated HRS equipped with heterogeneous hydrogen storage units, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and dual participation in hydrogen and electricity markets. The system architecture incorporates high-pressure tanks dedicated to distinct fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) classes, along with auxiliary buffer and backup tanks that enable inter-storage routing and enhance flexibility in meeting demand. Hydrogen procurement from external markets is scheduled through the backup tank, providing temporal decoupling between uncertain deliveries and refueling requirements. Based on time-dependent concave delay functions, a logistics-aware delivery delay model is introduced to capture time-varying lead times arising from routing constraints, fleet availability, and congestion. This battery-hydrogen co-optimization strategy enhances operational flexibility and resilience, effectively decoupling on-site hydrogen supply from short-term market volatility and demand fluctuations. A convex relaxation approach addresses the complexity of binary tank-switching decisions, nonlinear dynamics, and inter-market coordination, while maintaining real-time scheduling capability. The proposed RMPC is assessed under idealized and delay-affected market conditions to establish bounds on service continuity and operating cost. In particular, coupling BESSs with hydrogen storage improves station resilience and economic feasibility. The proposed approach yields a significant economic advantage over conventional controllers, with simulations indicating up to a 57% increase in profit when using multi-day predictive optimization, while the HRS achieves 98% refueling availability and reduces energy costs by approximately 15% relative to baseline operation. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to enable robust, cost-effective, and scalable operation of next-generation hydrogen refueling infrastructure.

title: The evolving structure of emissions in the transition to renewable electricity systems
abstract: Deep decarbonization of national energy systems requires high percentages of renewable electricity supply and significant electrification of transport and heat. As the proportion of renewable electricity supply increases, operational emissions will gradually decrease, making embodied emissions a more important component of the total emissions of these future electricity systems. Embodied emissions from electricity systems remain largely overlooked in existing energy and climate policy frameworks that prioritise operational emissions. Life cycle assessment (LCA) provides a systematic approach to evaluating both the operational and embodied emissions from these electricity systems. However, systematic LCA studies of future highly renewable electricity systems are scarce, and previous studies have omitted emissions associated with distribution and transmission infrastructure. To address these gaps, this study applies scenario-based LCA modelling to six future decarbonization scenarios for the New Zealand national electricity system, including a scenario that achieves 100 % renewable supply by 2045. Comparative analysis of two periods (2020–2035 vs. 2036–2050) shows operational and maintenance emissions drop from 85 % to 60 % of total life cycle emissions, while the share of embodied emissions more than doubles. Mitigation priorities should therefore shift from reducing fossil fuel use to improving and decarbonizing renewable energy technologies as their share grows. Including embodied emissions results in all five scenarios exceeding the electricity sector's allocated carbon budget by around 2037. The framework and findings in this study are applicable to other countries pursuing deep decarbonization of their energy system.

title: Recent heat wave across the Yunnan-Guizhou plateau and its impact on alpine lakes
abstract: Lakes are integral components of the global terrestrial ecosystem, with lake water temperature serving as a key parameter influencing the physical and biogeochemical processes within lake systems. In recent years, however, the intensification of global warming has significantly impacted lake water temperatures, resulting in a range of environmental consequences, including the increased frequency and intensity of algal blooms (ABs). This study focused on the Yunnan-Guizhou (YG) Plateau, a region sensitive to climate change, as the research area. The warming trends of the whole area were analyzed since the establishment of 234 meteorological stations. The trends in land surface water temperature (LSWT) and the ABs risk in 14 plateau lakes over the past 25 years were assessed using MODIS land surface temperature dataset, water quality monitoring data, and key climatic parameters, an evaluation framework was developed using machine learning algorithms (random forest, RF) and logistic regression (LR) models. The main findings of this study are as follows: 1. The YG Plateau has undergone significant warming since 1960 (0.20 °C/10a), with the most rapid temperature increase occurring after 2000 (0.37 °C/10a) and 2023 recorded as the warmest year on record; 2. All 14 lakes in the region have exhibited significant warming, although the rate of increase in LSWT is lower than that of the surrounding air temperature (0.26 °C/10a lower); 3. The ABs risk range is influenced by the lakes' water quality characteristics, all lakes have shown a significant increase in higher risk levels of ABs over the past 25 years. This study aims to provide a scientific basis for the development of climate change adaptation strategies and holds practical significance for the management of local aquatic environments.

title: Buildings as active nodes: Studying the effect of retrofitting and distributed energy resources
abstract: This study investigates the combined impact of building retrofitting and distributed energy resource (DER) deployment on the efficiency and stability of urban low-voltage distribution networks. A synthetic residential district was developed using a bottom-up approach, aggregating dynamically simulated building energy profiles and mapping them to feeder nodes. Two models were used: a steady-state investment optimization model to size photovoltaics (PV) and battery systems under net billing, and a detailed dynamic simulation to assess power flows and voltage regulation. This enables a spatially resolved analysis linking building-level demand, district energy planning, and grid dynamics. Results show that retrofitting reduces total electricity demand by 32.7 %, heating loads by over 50 %, and peak load from 201 kW to 113 kW. Aggregated PV-battery systems are more cost-effective than decentralized installations. In the decentralized setup, weighted self-consumption rates reached 46.2 % and 56.1 % in the reference and renovated cases, while the aggregated configuration achieved 51.2 % and 60.2 %, respectively, with shorter payback periods (∼6.4 years vs. 7.4–9.9 years). Despite the shared use of resources, electricity imports per building decreased under aggregation, reflecting higher autonomy; for instance, imports in unrenovated apartments dropped by 10.7 %, while the allocated CAPEX share declined from 4085 € to 3730 € (−8.7 %) due to more efficient system sizing and economies of scale. Dynamic simulations showed that Q/V control reduced RMS voltage deviation by 10.7 %, variability by 16.7 %, and ensured 100 % compliance with voltage limits. The proposed framework demonstrates the benefits of coordinated retrofitting and DER aggregation in enabling cost-effective decarbonization, improved self-consumption, and enhanced power system resilience.

title: Construction and optimization of wetland ecological networks integrating subjective–objective integrated weighting and scale effects: A case study of the Wuhan metropolitan area
abstract: Wetlands are essential components of ecosystems, providing key ecological services such as water regulation, habitat support, and climate moderation. They also serve as critical ecological infrastructure for regional sustainable development. However, rapid urbanization has led to significant wetland loss and reduced connectivity, disrupting species migration routes, shrinking habitats, degrading biodiversity, and intensifying environmental pollution. Traditional single-scale ecological network construction methods are insufficient to address the complexity of these challenges. This study proposes a multi-scale wetland ecological network framework by identifying ecological sources at three spatial levels, constructing a resistance system through subject-object integrated weighting, and incorporating the cross-scale effects of corridors. Ecological corridors were then generated using Circuitscape and spatial overlay analysis. Results reveal that: (1) landscape patterns reveal a shrinkage of core patches and a loss of connectivity-relevant areas, with core patch coverage decreasing from 81.34 % in municipal districts to 30.57 % in main urban areas. Ecological sources are primarily concentrated along major rivers and lakes in the central metropolitan area; (2) resistance factors vary by scale, but land use and distance from higher-level corridors consistently hinder connectivity; (3) the integrated network forms dense corridors in southern Wuhan, eastern Xiantao, and southeastern Huangshi, while the northern region remains fragmented; and (4) the multi-scale wetland ecological network significantly enhances the network structure compared to the single scale model, while highly matching the distribution of target species and ecological policies. Innovations lie in integrating subjective-objective weighting for resistance factors, incorporating cross-scale interactions, and applying these advances to the construction of a multi-scale wetland ecological network. This framework provides practical guidance for cross-jurisdictional wetland planning, spatial optimization, and the transition from passive restoration to resilience-based conservation.

title: Sustainable and mechanically robust fully bio-based aerogels with leaf-inspired structure for multifunctional air filtration
abstract: Air pollution from intensive livestock farms threatens human health, animal welfare, and ecosystem sustainability. Most existing air filters are unable to achieve efficient purification of particulate matter (PM), ammonia (NH3), and bacteria simultaneously. Inspired by the dust-proof property of natural leaves, this study proposes a biomimetic design strategy based on a cross-scale mechanism to fabricate high-performance air filters. Using silk fibroin (SF) as the matrix and loofah sponge (LS) as the three-dimensional scaffold, the hydrogen bond network and pore structure of the aerogel were regulated by carboxymethyl chitosan (CMC) and gelatin (GT). The SF/CMC/GT/LS (SCGL) composite aerogel with biomimetic leaf structure was successfully synthesized. The biomimetic structure endows the SCGL aerogel to exhibit the characteristics of low density, mechanical robustness, and low pressure drop. Component synergy enables aerogel multifunctional filtration performance, including efficient PM interception (>99.43 %), NH3 adsorption capacity (239.60 cm3/g) and antibacterial efficacy (>84.26 %). Simultaneously, the SCGL aerogel demonstrates biodegradability and negligible environmental impact. This work provides a simple, efficient, and eco-friendly biomimetic strategy for air purification, advancing agricultural efficiency and environmental sustainability.

title: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of a biobased solvent-driven lignocellulosic biomass refinery
abstract: Conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to fuels is one of promising pathways to tackle the emerging fossil fuels depletion and environmental pollution issues. Within the biorefining supply chain, pretreatment is a critical step in fractionating cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin for downstream utilization. While biobased green solvents pretreatment shows great promise for efficient biomass fractionation under mild conditions, its industrial feasibility remains uncertain due to the lack of comprehensive analysis at the system level. This study evaluates the industrial feasibility of employing dimethyl isosorbide (DMI) as a representative biobased green solvent within a scalable, closed-loop biorefinery process for the efficient fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass. Here, strategies to enhance lignin recovery and DMI recycling were developed and optimized guided by techno-economic assessment and life cycle assessment assisted with process simulation. The MSP of ethanol produced by designed conceptional biorefinery is estimated to $1169.7/t with a GWP of −0.431 kg CO2 eq./kg when solid loading of pretreatment reaches 20 % and biomass used for heat and electricity. In addition, two alternative value-added products, 2,3-BDO and high purity DMI, are simulated with MSPs of $1567.4/t and $1731.5/t with GWPs of −0.257 kg CO2 eq./kg and 1.06 kg CO2 eq./kg, respectively, lower than reported values. This work provides an example for evaluation-guided experimental optimization, accelerating the transition to carbon-neutral biorefining systems.

title: Equilibrium analysis of certification programmes for energy-saving products: Specification-based vs. contribution-based
abstract: External certifications are credible signals of product qualities, enhancing consumers’ valuation of energy-saving products. We study two certification programmes: specification-based certification, which requires products to meet a threshold energy efficiency level, and contribution-based certification, which requires firms to share a portion of profit with stakeholders. We demonstrate the theoretical equivalence of contribution-based certification to a price regulation scheme, where the price cap decreases with energy consumption. This finding provides a clear prospect for implementation using existing regulatory tools. Both programmes reduce energy use as requirements become stricter. We identify a key trade-off that represents the significance of our research: under equal firm profit, specification-based certification leads to lower energy consumption, while contribution-based certification yields greater sales, higher consumer surplus, and improved social welfare. We further examine three extensions: (1) switching the contribution baseline from profit to revenue lowers firm profit, (2) specification-based certification can mitigate rebound effects whereas contribution-based certification may not, and (3) both improve system-wide energy efficiency, though the efficiency is not monotonic in certification stringency.

title: Improving lithium extraction from claystone: Maximizing efficiency and sustainability with integrated beneficiation and sulfuric acid leaching
abstract: Sedimentary claystones in Nevada are a new type of resource for lithium. However, the large presence of carbonate gangue minerals impose a significant processing challenge because these carbonates not only increase sulfuric acid consumption during leaching but also lead to the generation of carbon dioxide. Therefore, understanding the potential of carbonate removal and its subsequent impact on downstream leaching constitutes a significant knowledge gap meriting further investigations. In this study, a smectite claystone was beneficiated using an enhanced gravity separation technique to remove its carbonate content, and subsequently leached using sulfuric acid. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to study the effects of acid concentration, leaching temperature and time, and solid-liquid ratio on the lithium extraction from the beneficiated claystone. The results showed that the optimum beneficiation was able to reject most of the calcite, with 86 % of calcium removed while recovering 91 % of the lithium. Leaching of the beneficiated claystone yielded a high lithium recovery of 89.18 % at conditions of 1.31 M acid concentration, temperature of 80 °C, time of 1.93 h, and 26 % solid-liquid. Furthermore, incorporating the beneficiation stage reduces the acid consumption from 106 g/g lithium to 23 g/g lithium, and the emission of carbon dioxide from 4.26E-01 kg CO2eq/g lithium to 1.51E-01 kg CO2eq/g lithium. The findings show the significance of prior beneficiation in enhancing leaching efficiency and mitigating environmental impacts, thereby providing understandings to address the previously identified knowledge gap.

title: Multi-objective optimization of crop distribution in arid agriculture: From water-carbon-food nexus perspective
abstract: Crop planting is high consumer of water and energy resources and a major contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions (GHG). Expanding demand for food increases dependence on these resources, which in turn leads to water scarcity and increased GHG emissions. To address these challenges, optimization models were developed based on resource nexus. This study incorporates water and carbon footprints into an optimization framework for agricultural planting structures in arid regions, integrating Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) with Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), aiming to achieve optimal water conservation, greenhouse gas emission reduction, and improved grain production. The findings reveal that variations in agricultural inputs and management practices result in a higher carbon footprint per unit of production for cotton than for maize and wheat by 38.8 % and 56.4 %, respectively. The agricultural water footprint in arid regions is predominantly composed of blue water, with spatial heterogeneity driven by regional climatic differences. Carbon emission intensity, agricultural economic development levels, and water resource utilization efficiency were identified as the major drivers of the increase in water and carbon footprints in Xinjiang over the past 20 years. By reallocating sown areas of major crops to establish an optimal planting configuration, reducing arid agricultural carbon emissions by 11.4 % and curbing blue water usage by 12.6 %. The results provide a scientific basis and feasible solutions for achieving efficient resource use and environmental protection in arid farming systems while ensuring food security.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of CO2 and CH4 fluxes in China's mariculture ponds: Application of a biogeochemical model
abstract: Assessing greenhouse gas emissions from mariculture pond systems is crucial for understanding the aquaculture industry's impact on global climate. This study developed a process-based biogeochemical model for marine aquaculture ponds (Greenhouse Gas Model for Marine Aquaculture Ponds, GHG-MAP) that parameterizes the system's biogeochemical processes. These include sediment carbon dynamics under high organic loading, the metabolism of cultured organisms, and the regulatory effects of management measures (e.g., feeding, water exchange, and aeration) on the system's carbon cycle. The model was used to analyze the spatiotemporal patterns of CO 2 and CH 4 emissions from different farming modes and to assess the global warming contribution of China's mariculture pond systems. Results show a high consistency between simulated and measured CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes (CO 2 : NSE = 0.59, R 2 = 0.79, RRMSE = 9.62 %; CH 4 : NSE = 0.93, R 2 = 0.96, RRMSE = 3.51 %). Greenhouse gas emissions from China's mariculture ponds exhibit a "southern source, northern sink" pattern. Southern Monoculture Earthen Ponds had the highest emissions (29.61 Tg CO 2 -eq/yr), while northern Extensive Lagoon Earthen Ponds acted as a net carbon sink (−0.84 Tg CO 2 -eq/yr). From 1978 to 2023, these ponds cumulatively emitted 552.77 Tg of CO 2 and 39.36 Tg of CH 4 , resulting in a 0.35 ± 0.13 mK contribution to global average temperature increase and offsetting approximately 4.13 % of China's terrestrial ecosystem carbon sink based on warming potential. Emission growth exhibited distinct phases, initially driven primarily by area expansion, and later more influenced by aquaculture intensification. Shellfish polyculture with lower CH 4 emission potential represents a feasible pathway for greenhouse gas reduction in China's mariculture industry.

title: Vehicular VOC speciation dynamics under China's progressive emission standards: Mechanistic drivers from real-time monitoring
abstract: Vehicle emissions are a key source of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in Chinese cities, requiring urgent cuts to combat ozone and secondary organic aerosol pollution. VOC emissions from vehicle exhaust are influenced by multiple factors, with driving conditions being one of the most critical one. In this study, two online instruments—a proton transfer reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry (PTR-ToF-MS) and an ion-molecular reaction mass spectrometry (IMR-MS)—were employed in parallel to monitor second-scale VOC components emissions from vehicles with varying emission standards and fuel types under different driving conditions. Results revealed a 98.3 % reduction in total VOC emissions of gasoline vehicles (GVs) from China I to VI standards, compared to 87.8 % for diesel vehicles (DVs) from China III to V standards. GVs across emission standards concentrated high emission-rate zones under high-acceleration conditions (>0.5 m/s2), while DVs primarily triggered emission peaks at higher speeds (>7 m/s). Vehicle specific power, a comprehensive indicator reflecting engine load, revealed distinct compositional differences with higher proportions of alkanes and aromatics from GVs and greater fractions of alkenes and oxygenated VOCs from DVs. This indicates that the dynamic emission profiles are influenced by fuel type and the interplay between engine load conditions and combustion completeness across driving conditions. The results in this study elucidate the underlying mechanistic drivers of VOC component emissions under different driving conditions and shed light on directions for further mitigation of VOC emissions from vehicle exhaust.

title: Optimisation of agrivoltaic systems within the water-energy-food nexus
abstract: Agrivoltaic (APV) systems enable the co-production of food and solar energy, yet their optimal design depends on complex interactions among climate, crops, and policy frameworks. This study introduces a multi-objective optimisation framework that integrates multi-year crop rotation, diverse APV configurations (vertical, one-axis tracking, overhead), and explicit national regulatory constraints across three European countries: Sweden, Germany, and Italy. The model couples photovoltaic (PV) and crop-growth simulations to evaluate trade-offs across the water–energy–food (WEF) nexus. Results show that both climate and regulation strongly shape feasible system geometries. Under Swedish subsidy limits (≤10 % land occupation), one-axis tracking systems achieved total land equivalent ratios (LERs) around 1.25 and water savings near 10 %. Under German yield-retention rules (≥66 %), overhead systems achieved LER around 1.36 and strong economic returns. While under Italian ministerial constraints combined with best practices, feasible designs emerged only in the enhanced WEF scenario (accounting for crop adaptation), achieving LER up to 1.66 with water-use reductions approaching 20 %. These outcomes demonstrate that applying identical policy thresholds across different climates can suppress overall sustainability performance, highlighting the need for climate- and crop-sensitive APV policy frameworks to unlock their full WEF potential. • Multi-year APV optimisation finds optimal row spacing of 5–10 m across Europe. • Strict policy thresholds might leads to unfeasible APV configurations. • Crop yield adaptation enables feasible APV designs under strict policies. • Optimal configuration reaches LER = 1.66 and NPV approaching €3 million in Italy.

title: Cleaner production of net-negative emissions via integrated Biogas–LNG multigeneration system: 5E analysis, LCA, and artificial intelligence-driven optimization
abstract: The study introduces a novel multigeneration system powered by sorghum-fermented biogas and enhanced with LNG cold recovery, a gas turbine, an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), and a thermally integrated carbon capture unit. The system is designed to simultaneously generate electricity, heating, cooling, and captured CO2 while achieving net-negative emissions. Integrated multigeneration systems are crucial for meeting global energy demands and environmental concerns, but conventional configurations frequently suffer from limited fuel flexibility, high CO2 emissions, and inefficient energy integration. In order to assess system performance, a thorough 5E (energy, exergy, economic, environmental, and emergy) analyses and a life cycle assessment (LCA) were conducted. Parametric studies revealed the effects of turbine inlet temperature, ORC pressure, LNG pressure, and LNG rate. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network precisely predicted important metrics (R2 = 0.999), and multi-objective optimization (SPEA-II) was used to balance cost, efficiency, and sustainability. In order to achieve −386 kg/h net CO2 emissions, the system produced 5240 kW of net power, 52.19 % energy efficiency, 40.59 % exergy efficiency, and 65.81 % CO2 removal. Economic analysis showed a net present value of 14.19 M$, levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.29 $/kWh, and payback period of 5.91 years. A total product unit cost of 23.11 $/GJ, exergy efficiency of 43.8 %, and LCOE as low as 0.228 $/kWh were obtained from optimization scenarios. For carbon reduction and sustainable energy production, this system provides a scalable solution.

title: Photocatalytic fuel cell based on highly conductive pathways for norfloxacin removal in mariculture wastewater and simultaneous electricity generation
abstract: Antibiotic contamination in mariculture wastewater urgently requires effective remediation. Seawater's natural conductivity facilitates photocatalytic fuel cell (PFC) deployment for meeting this challenge. In this study, the ZnSe/ZnO/Ti core-shell nanorod array photoanode was successfully prepared, which was assembled with carbon cloth (CC) cathode to build the PFC system for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation and simultaneous electricity generation in mariculture wastewater. Experimental results demonstrated that the introduction of the ZnSe shell effectively enhanced the light harvesting capability and formed interfacial electric field at the heterojunction interface, promoting charge transfer performance. The ohmic resistance was the limiting factor for PFC performance enhancement. The Ti plate effectively reduced ohmic resistance, enhanced ion migration rates, and maximized the efficiency of interfacial reactions. The heterojunction, nanorod array, and Ti current collector formed high-conductivity pathways for the rapid directional transport of both charge carriers and electrolyte ions, reducing the resistance of the PFC and significantly enhancing its performance. The PFC system exhibited superior degradation performance with 94.42 % removal of NOR in 120 min. The simultaneous electric energy output of ZnSe/ZnO/Ti-15 was 2.46 mW/cm2, which was 2.48 and 2.2 times higher than those of the ZnO/Ti and ZnSe/ZnO/FTO systems, respectively. Moreover, the abundant Cl− in mariculture wastewater acted as supporting electrolyte while also generating Cl•, ClO• radicals, thereby further facilitating degradation. This study provided new insights for the performance improvement of PFC and the resource utilization treatment of marine aquaculture wastewater.

title: Development of green low-carbon denitrogenation process for EAF- reaction behavior and industrial performance of Ar-CH4 injection via hollow electrode
abstract: Reducing nitrogen content in electric arc furnace molten steel is crucial for enhancing product quality and advancing green manufacturing. This study proposed a low-carbon denitrogenation method, in which hydrogen plasma was generated by injecting an Ar-CH4 mixed gas through a hollow electrode to promote nitrogen removal via the 3H + [N] = NH3 reaction. Thermodynamic calculations using Factsage 8.1 software confirmed the reaction's feasibility at standard steelmaking temperatures. Systematic laboratory experiments demonstrated over 90 % nitrogen removal from molten steel, with efficiency increasing as the CH4 proportion increased. At a 60 % CH4 ratio, nitrogen content was successfully decreased from 180.19 ppm to 28.39 ppm within 600 s. Real-time flue gas analysis revealed a correlated increase in NH3 concentration, thereby validating the reaction mechanism. Industrial trials in a 115 t Quantum EAF further verified the process's effectiveness: operating at a total gas flow rate of 5000 Nl/min and 60 % CH4 ratio reduced nitrogen content from 58.5 ppm to 47.8 ppm while decreasing smelting costs by 0.737 RMB/t and reducing CO2 emissions by 3.49 kg/t. This technology provides a practical and cost-effective solution for low-carbon steelmaking, supporting the development goals of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality.”

title: Research on water-energy-carbon consumption and emission situation and nexus in iron and steel industry
abstract: The iron and steel industry's (ISI) intensive consumption of energy and water, coupled with its high emissions, exacerbates resource scarcity and environmental degradation. Consequently, exploring the water-energy-carbon nexus (WECN) is crucial for the sustainable development of the industrial sector. This study develops a framework for the WECN in the ISI, uses balance degree (BD) to assess ISI' consumption and emissions, explores the interrelationships between water-energy, energy-water, energy-carbon and water-carbon, and constructs a synergistic development index (SDI) to evaluate the sector's synergistic situation. The results indicate that the case enterprise consumed 134.9 m3 of water and 561.4 kgce of energy per ton of crude steel, while generating approximately 1.7 tCO2. The BD analysis indicates high energy consumption in ironmaking (IM) and cold-rolling (CR), excessive water use in hot-rolling (HR) and CR, high carbon emissions in coking (CO) and sintering (SI), and severe imbalance between resource consumption and emissions in steelmaking (SM). IM and SM are at a low level of synergy and have high potential for energy conservation and emission reduction. This research provides an important foundation for policy-making and achieving sustainable development in the ISI.

title: Evaluation of floating photovoltaic deployment potential and associated environmental benefits on China's lakes and reservoirs
abstract: Floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems represent a promising pathway for expanding renewable electricity generation in China without competing for limited land resources. Drawing on the China-LERL dataset, this study evaluates 3051 lakes and 2194 reservoirs larger than 0.1 km2 under 5 %–30 % surface coverage scenarios, including a 15 % cooling gain. The results indicated that lakes contribute approximately 70 % of national FPV potential, with western provinces such as Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, and Qinghai each exceeding 100,000 GWh of electricity generation, saving over 1200 hm3 of water and avoiding 734 Mt of CO2 emissions. Reservoirs, accounting for roughly 30 % of the total, provide more balanced geographic distribution and strengthen energy security in the east. A dual strategy combining lake-based deployment in arid regions with reservoir-based expansion in populated areas can enhance renewable generation, conserve water, and reduce emissions, supporting China's sustainable energy transition.

title: Resilience assessment and optimization of ecological networks under multi-scenario disturbances: A 40-year analysis in Northwest China’s agro-pastoral transition zone
abstract: Accelerating climate change and intensifying human activities are reshaping the resilience of ecological networks, especially in arid and semi-arid agro-pastoral transition zones where ecosystems remain highly disturbance-sensitive. Long-term resilience dynamics in northwestern China’s agro-pastoral ecotone (1985–2023) were analyzed by constructing ecological networks using an integrated “importance-sensitivity-connectivity” framework combined with self-organizing map neural networks and circuit theory. Five disturbance scenarios were applied to assess temporal resilience trajectories and identify effective optimization strategies. Three key findings emerged. First, resilience exhibited a distinct U-shaped evolution across three phases: initial stability (1985–2000), mid-term fluctuation (2000–2015), and restabilization (2015–2023), closely mirroring major policy transitions. Second, resilience responses were disturbance-specific, indicating differentiated adaptive capacities. Networks remained robust under random attacks but vulnerable to targeted disturbances, while resistance to overgrazing improved most substantially under long-term grazing management. Third, optimization strategies exhibited scenario-dependent thresholds with paradoxical effects: source expansion enhanced sensitivity-based resilience by 14.68% but reduced overgrazing resilience by 10.25%; corridor optimization peaked at 0.1–0.2 addition ratios before triggering negative returns. These results support a spatial–temporal-functional framework to guide disturbance-specific strategies across management zones, clarifying mechanisms shaping resilience evolution in arid ecosystems and providing a transferable basis for precision ecological engineering and resilience-oriented land management globally.

title: A framework for the sustainability evaluation of smart and connected products concepts during early product design
abstract: The integration of electronic components into physical products to enable advanced data-driven functionalities has led to the emergence of Smart Connected Products (SCP). Due to their complex hybrid nature, SCP can have both positive and negative impacts on the environmental, economic and social pillars. They can thus pose ambiguous sustainability challenges. Recognizing that a product's sustainability impact is in part determined during the early design phases, this study proposes a framework to evaluate the sustainability impacts of SCP concepts after their generation in the creative design stages. The framework objective is to provide a structured and accessible method to select the relevant concepts to consider for the subsequent phase of the design process. Thus, the framework comprises three successive steps: (1) formalizing generated concepts into a common format, (2) evaluating them with regard to 18 sustainability indicators and (3) ranking them based on their scores. The proposed set of 18 actionable indicators was established on the basis of a systematic literature review. The framework scientific robustness and utility were validated through expert interviews. Results highlight the framework's relevance, transparency, and applicability within the SCP domain, though limitations were noted in its exhaustiveness and adaptability to other domains. Regarding the usability of the framework, it was validated through a design workshop. Results demonstrated that the framework was appreciated by the participants and they were satisfied by its outcomes. However, its directive structure seemed to hinder immersion in the evaluation task.

title: Airborne microplastics in China: Assessing urbanization, weather factors and policy implications from the nationwide study
abstract: This study presents the first nationwide assessment of atmospheric microplastics in China that systematically investigates the sources, distribution patterns, and governing factors of atmospheric microplastics across China through an integrated approach combining: year-round monitoring of both deposited (DAMPs) and suspended atmospheric microplastics (SAMPs) in Ningbo, and nationwide analysis of DAMPs data from 30 cities. Results showed an average DAMP flux of 473.9 ± 349.3 items m −2 d −1 and SAMP concentration of 0.15 ± 0.08 items m −3 in Ningbo, with an inverse seasonal relationship between SAMPs and DAMPs and a washout ratio of (1.02 ± 0.42) × 10 6 confirming rainfall's crucial role in microplastic removal. Multivariate analysis identified precipitation, temperature, and wind speed as key environmental drivers, while socioeconomic factors including population and GDP per capita strongly influenced spatial distribution of DAMPs. Nationwide analysis of 30 cities also established robust correlations between deposition fluxes and socioeconomic indicators. Based on this strong statistical relationship we developed the first predictive model for China, estimating total annual deposition at 1745 ± 619 tonnes, with wealthier coastal regions exhibiting 2.3–5.1 times higher fluxes than inland/less-urban areas. These findings quantify the coupled influence of meteorological and anthropogenic drivers on atmospheric microplastic pollution. This assessment provides a scientific basis for targeted mitigation, suggesting prioritized stormwater management in high-deposition coastal megacities and enhanced waste infrastructure in developing inland regions to address emission sources. • First nationwide study quantifies atmospheric microplastic deposition across 30 Chinese cities. • Rainfall-driven seasonal inversion: SAMPs decrease as DAMPs increase with precipitation. • Urban GDP and population density strongly correlate with coastal microplastic fluxes. • Prioritize mitigation in high-GDP coastal zones with 2.3–5.1 times higher deposition.

title: Dynamic suitability site selection and policy pathway for decommissioned photovoltaic recycling in China: Integrating spherical fuzzy sets and dynamic computable general equilibrium model
abstract: Driven by global energy transition and Sustainable Development Goals, photovoltaic (PV) capacity has expanded rapidly. However, this growth has simultaneously created formidable challenges in managing decommissioned PV recycling. This study constructs a latitude-longitude level spatiotemporal database of China's decommissioned PV by 2040 using a geographic information system. Thereby clarifies the spatiotemporal distribution of decommissioned PV to establish a research foundation for subsequent studies. Improved integrated multi-machine learning models predict key indicators to enhance assessment precision. Based on this, it dynamically evaluates recycling site suitability across four phases from 2028 to 2040. An integrated model supports this evaluation: Spherical Fuzzy Set (SFS) handles uncertainty; Analytic hierarchy process and Criteria importance through intercriteria correlation determine subjective and objective weights, fused via game theory combination weight method; SFS-Multi-attribute based analytic compromise quantifies suitability. A dynamic computable general equilibrium model assesses the impacts of Research and Development (R&D) subsidy policies from 2020 to 2050 for the decommissioned PV industry on energy structure, carbon emissions, and economic growth. Results reveal that decommissioned PV exhibits a west-to-east shift, with northwest regions dominated by large-scale centralized PV and east regions by distributed PV. Suitability is shaped by transportation and economy beyond decommissioned volume. The score difference between the points in the dynamic assessment and those in the static assessment is 1.4 %. R&D subsidies demonstrate diminishing marginal returns when increased beyond 20 % of baseline levels, with optimal effectiveness at moderate levels. This study contributes to advancing the sustainable production and management of decommissioned PV on a global scale.

title: Early-stage sustainability assessment of greywater treatment with Moringa oleifera seed extract and biochar
abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a significant challenge in much of the Global South, especially in rural areas where greywater treatment infrastructure is lacking. This study presents an early-stage sustainability assessment of a novel system that utilises biochar and Moringa oleifera seed extracts to treat greywater in rural Kenyan households. The proposed solution combines local biochar, a by-product of wood gasification cookstoves, and powdered Moringa oleifera seed cake, a residue from local agroforestry activities. The presented assessment applied a qualitative approach that integrates life cycle, circular bioeconomy, and sustainable sanitation principles. The key sustainability opportunities involved in the assessed system include improved human health and hygiene, the carbon sequestration potential of biochar, greywater reuse, and efficient use of local biomass resources. However, the system also involves risks related to filter media disposal, nutrient loss and system maintenance. The analysis highlights the trade-offs between using Moringa oleifera seed cake for water purification and animal feed. Moreover, the early-stage assessment identifies the need for pilot trials, participatory design and data collection to develop future life cycle analyses and implementation strategies. This integrated approach provides a sound basis for the sustainable development of natural greywater treatment systems that meet the goals of a circular bioeconomy. • A qualitative sustainability assessment method for bio-based water treatment. • Life cycle impact, circular bioeconomy and sustainable sanitation combined. • The assessment identified a major uncertainty linked to filter disposal.

title: Environmental impacts and benefits of vertical greenery systems in humid subtropical climate: A comprehensive life cycle perspective
abstract: In a context where the urgency for sustainability and renewable energy is undeniable, adopting vertical vegetation systems in urban buildings has emerged as a promising strategy for mitigating environmental impacts. However, despite the apparent benefits, continuous innovation is still needed to optimize these green solutions. In this drive for progress, this study investigates the efficiency of using recyclable materials in constructing green walls, analyzing the sustainability of this system through a life cycle analysis. Three rooms with similar characteristics and solar orientation were selected for analysis, differing only in the shading system: living wall (plants in recycled pots made of liquid packaging board), green façade (metal structure trellises), and control room (no vegetation). The shading potential of each system was assessed by measuring environmental variables, including indoor and outdoor air temperature, indoor and outdoor surface temperature, globe temperature, and indoor relative humidity. The results indicated that the vertical vegetation systems could effectively reduce the buildings' temperature. In summer, the living wall recorded a reduction of up to 9.2 °C and the green façade, a difference of up to 6.5 °C compared to the control room, demonstrating the effectiveness of these systems. Vertical vegetation systems, especially living walls with recycled materials, have effectively reduced energy and resources, mitigating environmental impacts in several categories. The natural shading provided by these systems has contributed significantly to energy savings and improved air quality by absorbing CO2 and other pollutants, thus promoting a more sustainable future. By examining the feasibility and performance of these recycled materials, the study contributes to developing more eco-friendly alternatives for creating vertical vegetation in urban areas. This approach benefits the urban environment and promotes more responsible and resource-conscious practices, aligning with modern cities' sustainability and resilience goals.

title: Environmental and economic impacts of using brewers spent grains for animal feed and anaerobic digestion
abstract: Over 130,000 tonnes of brewer's spent grains are generated annually in the UK. Most brewer's spent grains are utilised as a low-carbon animal feed, although anaerobic digestion provides economic benefits, through generating heat, energy, and biofertilizer. This study addresses a research gap by comparing both the economic and environmental impacts of using brewer's spent grains for animal feed versus anaerobic digestion. Specifically, it explores replacing brewer's spent grains-derived cattle feed with either high-carbon soya or UK-grown field beans, including dietary implications on methane generation and indirect land use change. Life Cycle Assessment and Life Cycle Costing were used to evaluate the environmental and economic impacts of utilising all brewer's spent grains generated in the UK for anaerobic digestion, as opposed to feeding cattle. Anaerobically digesting brewer's spent grains and using soya feed to replace brewer's spent grains as a cattle feed increased greenhouse gases by 39 Kt of CO 2 eq, while a field bean diet reduced emissions by 27 Kt of CO 2 eq. Additionally, the brewer's spent grain cattle diet required 6 and 8 thousand hectares less land than the field beans and soya diets respectively. However, anaerobic digestion of brewer's spent grains proved more profitable, offering an annual net economic benefit of £16 million. Thus, policy mechanisms such as an eventual ban could be introduced in order to phase out use of imported soya as an animal feed in the UK. Moreover, additional consultancy support, or interest free loans could be provided to facilitate breweries incorporating onsite anaerobic digestion.

title: Towards cleaner production of methyl glycolate: Techno-economic-environmental optimization via hybrid physics-machine learning modeling
abstract: The transition to sustainable chemical manufacturing requires a balance among technical feasibility, economic viability, and environmental impact. This challenge is particularly evident in the dimethyl oxalate to methyl glycolate (DTMG) process, a promising route for producing a key monomer of biodegradable polymers. To address these, this study develops a hybrid physics-machine learning framework for multi-objective optimization (HyMeO) of the DTMG process. It seamlessly integrates the strengths of process simulation, automated machine learning, and natural heuristic algorithms. A high-fidelity dataset of 1058 operational scenarios is generated via rigorous process simulation. Eight machine learning models are developed and automatically optimized, with the deep neural network model demonstrating the best performance (R2 > 0.96). The Shapley additive explains and partial dependency analyses are conducted to unveil the internal prediction mechanism of this model, which reveal that the distillate-to-feed ratio of the MG refining column and the hydrogen flowrate are the most influential factors governing the trade-offs between economic and environmental objectives. The preferred model coupled with the genetic algorithm to maximize exergy efficiency while minimizing production cost and CO2 emission of the DTMG process. The optimal solution achieves an 8.82 % increase in exergy efficiency, an 8.91 % cost reduction, and a 0.31 % decrease in CO2 emissions. Therefore, the proposed HyMeO framework can effectively reconcile the trade-offs among economic, technical, and environmental objectives in the DTMG process, providing a generalizable methodology for the sustainable intensification of chemical processes.

title: Interfacial behavior and mechanistic insights into CGAs-mediated remediation of crude oil-contaminated sludge
abstract: Oily sludge, laden with hazardous constituents, poses a significant risk to both human health and ecological integrity. Colloidal Gas Aphrons (CGAs) were prepared and optimized using a binary surfactant system composed of sodium dodecyl benzene sulfonate (SDBS) and rhamnolipid (RL). Findings revealed that the RL/SDBS composite system markedly augmented the stability of CGAs. Maximal synergistic interaction emerged under an equal proportion between components, resulting in minimized surface and interfacial tension and achieving an oil removal efficiency of 95.1 %. The corresponding CGAs displayed a mean particle diameter of 66.03 μm, approximately a 50 % reduction relative to monocomponent systems. The interfacial area increased by 115 %, corresponding to an approximate 9 % improvement in oil removal efficiency. With a mean particle size, the collision likelihood between CGAs and oily sludge was quantified at 29.73 %. CGAs facilitate the effective detachment and migration of crude oil from the solid matrix of oily sludge via van der Waals interactions. The detached oil compounds tended to accumulate on the surface of CGAs. Following the adsorption of crude oil, CGAs exhibited intensified fluorescence within the liquid film, and their thickness expanded from 14.38 μm to 23.24 μm, signifying that CGAs enabled the solubilization of crude oil driven by hydrophobic interactions. This research established a practical foundation for the efficient oil removal application of CGAs in the remediation of oil-contaminated sludge, while offering theoretical insights into the interfacial behavior within complex multiphase systems.

title: GenX triggers concentration-dependent photosynthetic inhibition and defense strategy shifts in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) seedlings
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), a widely used alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid, has been increasingly detected in agricultural soils. However, its phytotoxic mechanisms at environmentally relevant concentrations remain poorly understood. In this study, the phytotoxicity of GenX at environmentally realistic concentrations (0.1–100 ng g−1) in wheat seedlings was systematically investigated using physiological and multi-omics (proteomic and metabolomic) analyses. GenX exposure led to insufficient activation of superoxide dismutase, resulting in persistent superoxide anion accumulation and specific oxidative stress that ultimately impaired photosynthetic efficiency and osmoregulatory capacity. In response, an antioxidant defense network involving peroxidase, glutathione, and proline was activated. Multi-omics analyses revealed that GenX-induced remodeling of amino acid metabolism enhanced reactive oxygen species scavenging and nitrogen homeostasis. Molecular evidence indicated that GenX caused concentration-dependent cellular damage and stress responses. As exposure levels increased, damage to the photosynthetic system progressed from functional impairment to structural disruption: at 0.1 ng g−1, GenX primarily reduced light-harvesting efficiency by suppressing chlorophyll biosynthesis and destabilizing photosystem II, whereas higher levels caused structural damage to the photosynthetic apparatus and inhibited electron transport, thereby hindering carbon fixation. Defense mechanisms also shifted from protein translation to epigenetic regulation with increasing GenX concentration. This study provides the first comprehensive elucidation of the toxicity pathway of GenX in wheat at environmentally relevant concentrations, offering crucial mechanistic insights for ecological risk assessment and advancing understanding of the phytotoxicity of emerging substitute pollutants.

title: Engineering phytic acid-modified Zr-based 2D MOF nanoflowers for selective detection and efficient removal of uranium ions
abstract: Uranium contamination has caused a serious threat to the environment and human health due to its chemical toxicity and radiological hazards. Developing materials for sensitive detection and efficient removal of U(VI) is essential for the advancement of nuclear energy. Herein, ZrCl4 and 1,3,5-tri(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene (H3BTB)/2′-amino-5'-(4-carboxyphenyl)-[1,1':3′,1″-terphenyl]-4,4″-dicarboxylic acid (H3BTB-NH2) were used to prepare Zr-BTB (ZB) and Zr-BTB-NH2 (ZBN). Subsequently, post-synthetic modification with phytic acid (PA) was performed to obtain PA-modified ZB and ZBN, denoted Zr-BTB-PA (ZBP) and Zr-BTB-NH2-PA (ZBNP), respectively, for the selective detection and removal of U(VI). Compared with ZB and ZBN, the adsorption capacity of ZBP and ZBNP for U(VI) was significantly increased, and the theoretical maximum adsorption capacity of ZBNP for U(VI) was 254.45 mg/g. More importantly, ZBNP demonstrated outstanding adsorption selectivity for U(VI) in simulated seawater. The distribution coefficient (Kd) reached 3.65 × 104 mL/g, which is attributed to the synergistic interactions between the amino/phosphate groups in ZBNP and U(VI). Furthermore, the ZBNP exhibited a well-calibrated linear relationship between fluorescence intensity and U(VI) concentrations, and the correlation coefficient reached 0.989. Moreover, ZBNP exhibited selective fluorescence responses to U(VI) in the presence of competing metal ions. This study presents a novel dual-functional material that possesses significant potential for real-time monitoring and removal of U(VI).

title: From bamboo biomass to geopolymer binders: Valorizing SiO2 and K2O-rich residual ashes for the low-carbon construction
abstract: Global cement production is projected to exceed (4.6–5.0) × 1012 kg yr−1 by 2050, reinforcing the urgency of developing clinker-free binders to reduce the construction sector's ∼40 % share of CO2 emissions. This study presents a novel valorization pathway for Dendrocalamus asper bamboo residues, leaves, and inner/outer culm sawdusts, as dual-function sources of reactive SiO2 and K2O for alkali-activated (geopolymer) binders. After optimized calcination at 630 °C, the ashes were characterized by PSD, XRF, XRD, TG–DSC/DTA, SEM–EDS, FTIR, and solid-state NMR. Leaves ash showed a unimodal PSD (∼80 μm), high amorphous SiO2 (76.9 wt %), and strong calcium uptake, confirming its high pozzolanic reactivity. Culm ashes were bimodal (10–700 μm), crystalline-rich, and enriched in K2O (up to 40.3 wt %) and P2O5 (14.5 wt %), suggesting complementary alkaline and fluxing functions. In the fresh state, bamboo-ash-based geopolymer pastes exhibited moderate workability (flow = 215 mm, viscosity ≈ 28 cP) and cohesive behavior favorable for precast applications, while the reference mix (pyrogenic-silica activator) showed lower viscosity and higher spread (240 mm). Upon curing, the bamboo-leaves-ash geopolymer achieved 16.7 MPa compressive strength, forming aluminosilicate networks structurally comparable to those synthesized with commercial waterglass, as evidenced by 29Si/27Al MAS-NMR, the first direct spectroscopic validation of bamboo-ash-derived activators. This proof of concept demonstrates that bamboo residues can supply both reactive silica and alkalis for geopolymerization, advancing circular, region-specific strategies for low-carbon construction.

title: Forward osmosis to concentrate coconut water and impact of ultrafiltration Pre-treatment: Insights into membrane fouling
abstract: Coconut water is a widely consumed healthy beverage due to its nutritional benefits, and demand for packaged products is steadily increasing. Traditional concentration methods, particularly thermal processes, can compromise quality and are energy-intensive. Forward osmosis (FO) offers a promising nonthermal alternative with lower energy requirements and reduced transportation costs. This study investigates FO-based concentration of coconut water, focusing on fouling behavior and performance under ultrafiltration pre-treatment (UFPT) and constant osmotic pressure (COP) operation to increase the volumetric concentration factor (VCF). The results show that UFPT enhanced water flux by up to 50 % at 1 M NaCl and 25–30 % at 4 M NaCl compared to untreated feed, while the VCF increased by 50 % with UFPT. COP operation helps maintain a higher water flux for longer durations, enabling a higher VCF than the conventional FO mode. Thermal and fouling analyses identified critical VCF points where gel layer formation caused a sharp decline in flux. These findings offer new insights into optimizing FO-based juice concentration, providing a sustainable, and energy-efficient approach that enhances product quality and advances nonthermal beverage processing.

title: Cobalt encapsulated doping via framework solvation of MIL-88A for anchoring peroxymonosulfate to generate surface-bound radicals
abstract: Stable binding and activation of peroxy species in Fenton-like reactions are the central challenge. Herein, the solvation properties of MIL-88 A were exploited for surface cobalt doping, applying in peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation for sulfamethazine removal. Initially, the electrostatic attraction-driven binding of PMS activated by cobalt sites consistently generates surface-bound SO4•− and O2•−. This surface catalysis as well as the identification of reactive oxygen species was effectively determined by correlation analysis. Besides, the spectroscopic and probe experiments demonstrate synergistic interactions between cobalt and inert iron in the original node, enriching the catalytic pathway and reactive species generation. Compared with one-pot introduction, the solvation doping method makes the modified MIL-88 A surface more catalytically active and effectively reduces the cost of preparing membrane filtration reactor. In addition, competitive experimental studies monitored the effect of surface microenvironment on PMS catalysis. This work provides new insights into the activation behavior of PMS at bimetallic sites, while promoting the application of MOFs in Fenton-like systems for cost-saving and efficiency enhancement.

title: New strategies for synergistic inhibition of mild steel corrosion by dual-functionalized chitosan: Film formation and Fe2+ adsorption
abstract: Steel corrosion is a critical issue impacting the durability and sustainability of concrete structures. To address this challenge, eco-friendly chitosan derivative inhibitors, ferulic acid modified chitosan (CTS-FA) and ferulic acid and cysteine modified chitosan (CTS-FA-Cys), were designed and synthesized using a dual-functionalization strategy to enhance both spontaneous surface film formation and Fe2+ adsorption for effective corrosion inhibition. Based on experiments and theoretical calculations, their corrosion inhibition performance and mechanisms were systematically evaluated. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that both CTS-FA and CTS-FA-Cys significantly improved the corrosion resistance of steel in simulated concrete pore solution containing 3.5 % NaCl (SCPS-NaCl, pH ≈ 12.5), especially for CTS-FA-Cys, achieving a maximum inhibition efficiency of 95.97 % at 500 mg/L. During immersion for 168–1176 h, the inhibition efficiency of CTS-FA-Cys remained at 83.63–92.35 %, demonstrating superior durability and stability compared to unmodified chitosan (91.28–92.65 % within 12–168 h). Theoretical calculations revealed that both inhibitors formed an adsorption film on the Fe (110) surface by donating electrons to the empty d-orbitals of Fe and forming covalent bonds. Adsorption experiments revealed that both inhibitors effectively adsorbed Fe2+, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 60.12 mg/g (CTS-FA-Cys), and their adsorption behaviors followed the pseudo-second-order (PSO) kinetics and Langmuir isothermal adsorption model. This study aims to provide novel strategies for prolonging the durability of reinforced concrete through innovative design and synthesis of inhibitors with a dual inhibition mechanism.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity of environmental sustainability in China: A strong sustainability assessment integrating planetary boundaries and environmental footprints
abstract: Human activities are causing escalating environmental crises, making sustainable development a paramount global challenge. This research introduces a comprehensive and integrated framework to assess the environmental sustainability of China's provinces over time and across regions. By adapting the global ‘Planetary Boundaries'(PBs) concept to create local, science-based targets, we measured each province's consumption-based footprint for four key elements: carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and water (W). Specifically, environmental footprints quantify consumption-based anthropogenic pressures, whereas the downscaled PBs thresholds define the safe biophysical limits. We then evaluated these footprints against the safe environmental limits. Our findings from 2007 to 2017 reveal that China's national carbon, phosphorus, and water footprints grew, while the nitrogen footprint showed a decline. Spatially, we found stark regional disparities, with northern provinces bearing much heavier environmental loads. The assessment shows that most provinces have breached the safe limits for C, N, and P, creating a distinct “high-north, low-south” pressure pattern. The risk of water unsustainability was particularly acute in northwestern provinces. Crucially, no province managed to stay within the safe thresholds for all four elements simultaneously. To address these challenges, we classified provinces into high-, medium-, and low-risk zones and formulated tailored policy recommendations. This study provides vital data-driven support for China's sustainability goals and offers a scalable analytical framework for other nations facing similar regional environmental challenges.

title: Systematic inter-plant carbon integration through emission-optimal design of robust carbon dioxide reuse networks
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) reuse networks can play a crucial role in reducing CO2 emission by connecting CO2 supplies with demands. In this paper, an optimization-based approach to the synthesis of emission-optimal CO2 networks is proposed. The novelty lies in accounting for process uncertainties through a robust optimization approach such that the network is guaranteed to remain feasible under concentration and flow disturbances. This is achieved by considering a flexible (or robust) design framework in a superstructure optimization algorithm. The optimization objective is fresh CO2 minimization subject to supply concentration uncertainties and constraints such as CO2 purity thresholds and a desired emission reduction for the supplies, according for environmental regulations. Also, a two-tier optimization framework is proposed to minimize unused CO2 emission to the atmosphere along with the fresh CO2 minimization. This allows for detecting multiple design solutions that can possibly minimize both fresh CO2 consumption and total CO2 emission, thereby further reducing the overall environmental impact. Case studies demonstrate that optimal networks yield significant reduction in the fresh CO2 consumption (over 80%) and CO2 emission, with certain cases achieving even zero source emission. Moreover, the emission-optimal design guarantees the network feasibility over the entire uncertainty range. It is shown that in a real operation involving disturbances, this benefit may come at even a lower fresh CO2 usage than a network designed without uncertainty considerations. This work highlights the potential for carbon reuse networks in advancing sustainability and environmental friendliness of industrial parks.

title: Explainable machine learning for predicting compressive strength of rubberized concrete: SHAP interpretation, lifecycle assessment, and design recommendations
abstract: The study explores dataset preparation, machine learning (ML) model training, interpretation, and life cycle assessment (LCA) to predict and enhance the performance and sustainability of rubberized concrete.
