A large dataset comprising 1209 collected samples with nine input features was used to train and evaluate six machine learning models. Among the six models, the Light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) model achieved the highest prediction accuracy on the testing dataset, with an R 2 value exceeding 0.96, a MAPE of 8.31 %, a MAE of 2.36 MPa, and a RMSE of 3.25 MPa. The SHAP algorithm was used to interpret predictions and identify key factors influencing compressive strength. Rubber content and water-to-cement ratio reduced strength, while longer curing time, more superplasticizer, higher fine aggregate content, and a greater silica fume-to-cement ratio improved it. Coarse aggregate, crumb rubber size, and cement content had minimal impact. Optimal performance was achieved with: Rubber content <55.92 kg/m 3 , w/c ratio <0.4, curing time >26 days, superplasticizer >3.7 kg/m 3 , fine aggregate >642 kg/m 3 , and silica fume/cement ratio >2.5 %. LCA results show that, although rubberized concrete offers no clear advantage over conventional concrete in cost, carbon, or energy, the lower strength and higher superplasticizer use of rubberized concrete lead to greater strength-normalized impacts, and therefore its value lies more in waste recycling and toughness than in strength-based sustainability. The unique advantage of this research lies in the development of a ML-LCA integration framework that synthetically balances performance prediction and sustainability assessment of rubberized concrete, with delivering actionable mix design recommendations, identifying key and low-impact variables, and revealing trade-offs among strength, cost, and environmental performance.

title: Chronic C-S-Fe defense dominance over nutrient removal in nanoplastics-exposed constructed wetlands: persistent feoA as the core biomarker
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) face intensifying threats from nanoplastics (NPs). While existing evidence confirmed NPs impaired pollutant removal by disrupting microbial metabolism, critical knowledge gaps persist regarding how acute metabolic disturbances escalate into sustained functional impairment through self-sustaining cycles, and what strategies can effectively detect and disrupt such cycles. This study bridged this critical gap by examining how NPs reprogrammed interconnected biogeochemical networks during stress phases. Initially, microbial communities in CWs efficiently coupled C-N-P metabolism within a robust network, achieving high removal efficiencies of 92.23 % for total nitrogen (TN) and 90.13 % for total phosphorus (TP). However, prolonged NPs exposure (>90 days of operation) triggered a decisive metabolic shift toward a prioritized C-S-Fe defense module, with feoA identified as the top biomarker confirming Fe-centered defense via random forest. This redirected carbon flux into S-dependent glutathione biosynthesis and Fe-mediated antioxidant pathways while simultaneously suppressing N/P cycling investment. Consequently, microbial networks fragmented, sharply reducing TN (55.48 %) and TP (49.01 %) removal efficiencies. While partial C-N-P reintegration occurred during stabilization >150 days of operation), restoring TN removal efficiency to 73.53 %, the persistent topological dominance of the C-S-Fe defense module signals a chronic, defensive resource allocation strategy. Critically, the sustained primacy of feoA established its potential as a definitive biosensor for ecosystem dysfunction. Future development of cost-efficient assays targeting this biomarker could enable early detection of metabolic compromise and trigger tiered interventions, shifting environmental management from reactive pollution control to proactive functional governance to prevent chronic degradation.

title: Green sustainability of chelating agents used in cadmium-contaminated soil washing remediation: experimental validation and life cycle assessment
abstract: Despite the prevalence of soil washing as a soil remediation technique, there is a lack of comprehensive guidance on the selection of washing agents in the context of green and sustainable remediation. Therefore, the three most used chelating agents, including ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), glutamic acid N, N-diacetic acid (GLDA), and citric acid (CA), were evaluated in terms of cadmium (Cd) removal efficiencies, impacts on the soil environment, and life cycle assessment (LCA). The findings demonstrated that whereas CA had a lower removal efficiency of 48.4 %, GLDA could reach a similar removal efficiency of up to 68.8 % as EDTA. Compared with the control group (deionized water washing), the three chelating agents can significantly increase soil nutrients. Following EDTA washing, available nitrogen (AN), available phosphorus (AP), and available potassium (AK) increased by 10–15 %, 36–83 %, and 42–54 %, respectively. The application of GLDA resulted in an increase of 18 % in AN, 13–77 % in AP, and 36–83 % in AK. After CA washing, AN, AP, and AK increased by 3 %–15 %, 13–37 %, and 36–129 %. However, EDTA had the strongest inhibitory effect on urease, which was 56.8 %–69.3 %. The activity of sucrase was all enhanced by all three chelating agents, with an increase of 0.8–1.2 times. After 90 days of natural soil restoration, the soil properties tend to stabilize, where the enzyme activity of the GLDA-washed soil recovered to be closer to the initial value. The results of soil planting showed that all the remediated soil had a positive effect on the germination rate of cabbage. Notably, GLDA washing promoted root length more significantly, increasing it by 9.56 %–10.22 %. Based on LCA, the environmental impact of the production process of the three chelating agents and the environmental impact of the final washing process were CA > EDTA > GLDA. In summary, GLDA is a more suitable green chelating agent for this soil. This study will provide reference and comprehensive evaluation methods for selecting suitable chelators for future chemical remediation while balancing the effectiveness and green sustainability of soil remediation methods.

title: Multi-criteria optimization of methanol-based energy systems in ports using PMPEF-TOPSIS: A path to sustainable and efficient operations
abstract: Ports are strategic, energy-intensive nodes in global logistics, and decarbonization pressures are driving the need for low-carbon, infrastructure-compatible solutions. Methanol offers a technically practical pathway due to its liquid form, established handling compatibility, and lower emission potential relative to conventional fuels. This study presents the first structured comparative evaluation of methanol-based port power systems across thermochemical, electrochemical, and hydrogen-carrier routes. A new multi-criteria decision-making model, the Port Methanol Power System Evaluation Framework–TOPSIS (PMPEF-TOPSIS), is developed to assess feasibility across technical, economic, environmental, and regulatory dimensions. The TOPSIS results indicate substantial differentiation in criterion influence. Technological Innovation (1.000) and Environmental Impact (0.941) exhibit the highest proximity to the ideal solution, followed by Cost Efficiency (0.735), demonstrating that technology advancement and emissions performance remain the primary leverage points for methanol system feasibility. Performance in Dynamic Scenarios (0.000) and Economic Feasibility (0.382) ranked lowest, highlighting current limitations in operational robustness and macro-economic resilience. Electrochemical conversion ranked first among the alternatives (0.73), indicating the strongest overall suitability for port deployment. This framework offers a robust basis for strategic prioritisation and investment sequencing in port energy transition planning.

title: Balancing reality, meaning, and play for water governance transformation: A triadic game design perspective on the Aquaconnect serious game
abstract: Serious games are increasingly used to engage stakeholders with complex social-ecological challenges and to support transformative learning. Their effectiveness depends on achieving a careful balance between play, reality, and meaning, ensuring that games are not only engaging and enjoyable (play), but also credible in their representation of real-world systems (reality), and capable of producing reflective, actionable insights (meaning). This study evaluates the design and performance of a serious game on future water supply in drought-prone regions of the Netherlands. The game translates Termeer et al. (2024)'s three governance transformation pathways: big plans, small wins, and rule change, into interactive decision options with actor-specific risks and interdependencies. By embedding governance theory directly within gameplay, the game enables players to experience and negotiate the tensions, trade-offs, and uncertainties inherent in transformation processes. While previous water-domain games have sought to reconcile play, reality, and meaning, few have systematically documented the iterative design and evaluation processes needed to sustain this balance. Guided by Triadic game design, the development process advanced through iterative cycles, each aimed at maintaining a productive balance of the three elements. The study makes two key contributions. First, it provides a concrete operationalisation of governance transformation pathways within game mechanics. Second, it provides a structured and empirically grounded assessment of balancing play, reality, and meaning in serious game design, serving as a guide for others. Together, these contributions enhance the methodological rigour and practical relevance of serious games as instruments for transformative water governance and other sustainability transitions.

title: Water–energy–food nexus in a multi-product biomass supply chain
authors: Mauro Antonio da Silva Sá Ravagnani
abstract: Brazil faces persistent undernutrition and increasing resource pressures across its agricultural, food, and bioenergy sectors. Existing Water–Energy–Food nexus models rarely integrate nutritional security as a primary optimization objective, which limits their relevance for sustainable development policy. This study addresses this gap by optimizing the Brazilian agri-food and bioenergy supply chain through a multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that simultaneously incorporates social (food security), environmental, and economic objectives. The formulation explicitly links food distribution to nutritional density, redirecting flows toward states with the highest vulnerability. As a result, undernutrition decreases sharply, reaching near-zero values in the most effective scenarios. For example, Maranhão declines from 2.59 % to 0.0014 % and Pará from 2.16 % to 0.0011 %, with reductions exceeding 90 % in several northern and northeastern regions. Economically, the most efficient configurations achieve annual net profits of up to USD 13.89 million per year. Simultaneously, the valorization of agro-industrial residues for biofuel production reduces dependence on fossil fuels and strengthens the circular bioeconomy. By incorporating indicators of water use, energy consumption, CO2 emissions, and economic value generation, the model demonstrates that it is possible to satisfy a significant share of food and energy demand without overexploiting natural resources. Overall, this research provides an integrated decision-support framework for policymakers and planners to balance nutritional equity, energy transition, and environmental resilience, advancing the Water–Energy–Food nexus toward actionable sustainability solutions.

title: Rational design of Pt-Ti electrodes for accelerated ammonia removal and metabolic steering towards N2 mitigation by Oceanimonas sp. in microbial electrochemical systems
abstract: Efficient and sustainable removal of ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) from wastewaters is crucial due to its toxicity and environmental implications. While biological methods show promise, their effectiveness can be hindered in challenging conditions, often resulting in the unwanted nitrous oxide (N2O). This study focuses on enhancing NH3-N removal efficiency through the application of microbial electrochemical technologies (METs) using Oceanimonas sp., a halophiolic bacterium sourced from saline-alkaline soil. By applying optimal electrical stimulation at 0.6 V with a platinum (Pt) electrode, we achieved an NH3-N removal efficiency of 78.18 %, significantly surpassing control treatments. Transcriptomic analyses indicated that this improvement was linked to the upregulation of key genes (glnA, gltB, gltD) involved in ammonia assimilation. However, the Pt stimulation also led to partial denitrification, resulting in the generation of the greenhouse gas N2O. To optimize the nitrogen conversion pathway while minimizing byproducts, we developed a novel tandem electrode strategy. This approach consists of a "Pt first" stage to maximize initial NH3-N remove, followed by a "Ti optimization" stage. This functional transition is supported by the upregulation of upstream denitrification genes (napA/B, nirK, norB) and resulted in a dramatic reduction of N2O emissions by over 78.56 % compared to the Pt-only treatment, suggesting enhanced beneficial electron supply from the electrode. This research provides critical mechanistic insights into electrochemically stimulated ammonia metabolism and demonstrates the Pt-Ti tandem strategy as an approach for achieving high removal rates with sophisticated metabolic control to minimize byproducts.

title: Exploring socio-psychological factors driving adoption of renewable energy products
abstract: This research addresses the socio-psychological factors influencing consumer intentions to adopt renewable energy (RE) products within Malaysia, an emerging market context. Building upon the established Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study proposes an enhanced model by integrating two crucial constructs: green trust and attitudinal ambivalence (AA). This integration addresses a critical gap in existing TPB applications, which often overlook the role of trust formation and attitudinal conflict under the conditions of risk, uncertainty, and social pressure. These conditions are often characteristic of emerging RE markets. Data is collected via a cross-sectional online survey distributed across Malaysian consumer groups and LinkedIn over 3 months ( N = 435). The conceptual model is tested using Structural Equation Modeling. The key findings demonstrate that green trust operates as a necessary antecedent, preceding the formation of a positive environmental attitude toward RE adoption. Furthermore, AA is confirmed as a significant predictor of behavioral intention. Traditional TPB constructs, such as subjective norms, are not significant, and perceived behavioral control has negligible effects. By explicitly modeling consumer trust issues and conflicting feelings, this updated framework offers a more accurate and better-performing explanation of consumer adoption decisions in uncertain markets. The findings provide practitioners and policymakers with a refined, theoretically sound model for designing interventions to accelerate RE adoption in similar emerging economies.

title: Heat mitigation effects of urban parks and gardens on surrounding areas in hot, arid environments: A case study of Shiraz
abstract: Urban green spaces represent a highly effective strategy for mitigating elevated air temperatures and reducing the intensity of the urban heat island (UHI) effect. Existing research on the cooling effects of urban parks and gardens has been relatively limited, often relying on two-dimensional analyses and remote sensing methodologies. This study aims to address this gap by utilizing local weather station data, conducting three-dimensional analyses, and employing Envi-met simulations to investigate the role of urban parks and gardens in alleviating urban heat. The primary objective of this research is to examine the thermal conditions of urban green spaces and their contributions to mitigating the magnitude of the UHI within urban canyons surrounding these green spaces in Shiraz, Iran. The methods used in this study include field measurement, and simulation using ENVI-met. The simulation results demonstrated that the urban green space geometry in Shiraz had a cooling effect of about 5 °C. The cooling impact was extended to the surrounding areas (up to 140 m away). It was also found that the percentage of pavement was directly related to the increase of air temperature in surrounding urban canyons. Additionally, studying the orientation of urban canyons around the examined urban green spaces demonstrated that better thermal conditions are achieved by moving further west, ultimately reducing the intensity of UHI. Furthermore, examination of the thermal conditions of the study sites indicated that the average value of Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) in Shiraz in summer lays within the range of extreme heat stress (47.8 °C).

title: Sustainable ethylene production: A life cycle perspective on oil, coal, and natural gas derived industrial pathways in China
abstract: Under stringent Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction (ECER) policies, a comprehensive evaluation of the environmental and economic performance of ethylene production technologies has become an imperative. This study assessed five predominant industrial ethylene production pathways, including three petroleum-based (OTE), one coal-based (CMTE), and one natural gas-based (NETE), using integrated life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle cost (LCC) analysis, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions accounting. Results indicated that the NETE route exhibited the lowest environmental impact, representing only 21.4 % of that associated with CMTE. Coal-derived methanol constituted the primary environmental burden in CMTE, significantly affecting primary energy consumption, CO2 emissions, industrial water use, and VOC releases. GHG analysis revealed that CMTE had the highest emissions, reaching 8298.58 kg CO2 eq per ton of ethylene, allocated almost equally between ethylene (45.3 %) and propylene (44.2 %). The three OTE routes followed in GHG emissions, with ethylene responsible for 32–37 % of CO2 eq. In contrast, NETE exhibited substantially lower emissions at only 1374.52 kg CO2 eq, with 77.4 % assigned to ethylene. Economically, NETE achieved the lowest total cost (internal and external costs), approximately 55.8 % lower than OTE routes. The analysis further revealed distinct regional disparities in ethylene production and GHG emissions across China, with high emissions in the central region attributable to CMTE dominance and elevated emissions along the eastern coast resulting from the prevalence of OTE routes. This spatially explicit assessment provided a foundation for developing region decarbonization strategies for the ethylene industry.

title: Enhancing rockfall barrier performance using waste used car tyres: A step towards sustainable civil engineering
abstract: Rockfall events pose a significant threat to infrastructure in hilly regions, necessitating robust and cost-effective mitigation strategies. This study initially evaluates the performance of traditional energy-absorbing material EPS-11 foam in enhancing the impact resistance of reinforced concrete rockfall barriers. A finite element model of a double-anchored rockfall barrier subjected to a high-velocity impact (25 m/s) from 1 m, diameter spherical rock was developed using Abaqus/Explicit. To explore sustainable alternatives, used car tyres were then investigated as hyperelastic energy-absorbing layers. The tyres were modelled using the Arruda-Boyce hyperelastic model. Three different configurations were examined: unprotected barrier (control), single tyre layer, and double staggered tyre layers. An additional energy absorption analysis showed that the double-layer staggered configuration exhibited higher internal energy dissipation (EVDDEN), indicating its superior ability to redirect and absorb impact energy through the tyre layers. Simulation results revealed that tyre layers significantly outperformed EPS foam in reducing peak deformation and vertical settlement. Compared to the unprotected case, single and double tyre layers reduced peak deformation by 16.08 % and 51.16 %, and vertical settlement by 10.90 % and 48.79 %, respectively. Further, supplementary impact velocity simulations (15–30 m/s) confirmed that the double-layer system maintained its effectiveness under increasing velocities, with peak performance observed at 25 m/s. Crack propagation and energy transfer to the structure were also notably mitigated with tyre protection. These findings highlight the potential of recycled tyres as a low-cost, sustainable, and highly effective alternative for improving rockfall protection systems.

title: Open-source manufacturing of polypropylene replacements for peat cups in vertical farming: improvements in life cycle embodied energy, greenhouse gas emissions, labor and operational costs
abstract: Peat-based planting cups, widely used in horticulture, contribute to significant environmental degradation due to peatland destruction. This study introduces an open-source, low-cost method for converting polypropylene (PP) cups into planting containers using a modified 3D printer equipped with a hot knife for automated hole punching. The system enables precise, repeatable modifications that support plant growth through improved drainage and aeration. Experimental validation showed that modified PP cups support comparable crop yields to peat cups, with only a slight reduction offset by substantial economic and environmental benefits. Peat cups, which must be replaced after every growing cycle, impose higher long-term economic costs. For relatively low-value kale, despite higher experimental yields the net profit advantage of peat cups was only 2.2 % over the agrivoltaic agrotunnel system lifetime. In contrast, relatively high-value spring mix experimentally cultivated in PP cups generated higher profit from the first year onward for a total of $5.3 million in the same system. Life cycle assessment revealed that, per use, peat cups have approximately 4.5 times higher carbon footprint and 35 % greater energy consumption than single-use PP cups. When reused over their lifetime of 250 cycles, PP cups reduce total material demand by ∼98 % and lower lifetime energy and carbon impacts by up to 59 % and 77 %, respectively. Even under unfavorable dishwashing scenarios, environmental impacts of reusable PP cups remain 44–53 % lower than peat. This approach offers a scalable, sustainable alternative for peat cups in vertical farming of controlled environment agriculture.

title: Electrokinetic dual-cathode permeable reactive barrier system: Efficient Cr(VI) removal and Cr(III)/Fe(III) resource recovery from contaminated soil
abstract: Conventional electrokinetic (EK) remediation of Cr(VI)-contaminated soil faces considerable challenges, including extreme pH gradients, inadequate total chromium (TCr) removal efficiency, challenges in Cr(III) recovery, and the risk of causing secondary pollution. Here, this study proposes a novel electrokinetic dual-cathode permeable reactive barrier (PRB) system integrated with membrane separation. The following key advancements have been made: the dual-cathode design in combination with an AEM is effective in blocking Cr(III) back-migration. The removal rates of Cr(VI) and TCr were 98.17 % and 93.8 %, respectively. Dynamic electrolyte circulation maintained the soil pH (5.33–7.87) in a near-neutral state, thereby effectively suppressing the focusing effect. The optimized PRB filler ratio (zero-valent iron to sand = 1:5) reduced material costs. This configuration enabled the targeted enrichment and recovery of Cr(III) and Fe(III) in secondary cathode chamber (Cathode 2), with recovery rates of 33.97 % and 10.67 %, respectively. This technology provides an environmentally benign solution for efficient remediation and resource recovery from Cr(VI)-contaminated soils.

title: Cradle-to-gate assessment and optimization of sustainable geopolymer concrete
abstract: Geopolymer concrete (GPC) is a sustainable alternative to Portland cement concrete by eliminating Portland cement. However, using alkaline activators compromises the sustainability of GPC. This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of the cradle-to-gate life cycle cost, carbon footprint, and energy consumption of 2304 GPC mixtures which represent the state-of-the-art dataset, aiming to establish a holistic understanding of the impacts of GPC design parameters on mechanical and sustainability performance. The cost-benefit characteristics of solid wastes are considered, and strength-normalized sustainability parameters are discussed. Results reveal that the formulation of GPC plays critical roles in mechanical and sustainability metrics. Inappropriate use of alkaline activators and solid wastes can largely compromise both mechanical strength and sustainability metrics, lower than their Portland cement counterparts. Based on the large dataset, this paper identifies the appropriate upper and lower bounds for various ingredients to guide the design of GPC for balanced mechanical strength and sustainability metrics.

title: Identification of drought-flood abrupt alternation thresholds triggering vegetation loss
abstract: Frequent drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) events significantly threaten vegetation carbon sequestration and ecosystem stability. Previous studies have primarily focused on the impacts of individual extreme events, with limited attention to the complex effects of DFAA sequences on vegetation. In this study, we identified DFAA events using the short-cycle drought-flood abrupt alternation index (SDFAI), and estimated vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) via the Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model. Furthermore, we developed a copula-based conditional probability framework to determine the DFAA intensity thresholds that trigger vegetation loss and to quantify the drought-to-flood (DTF) and flood-to-drought (FTD) thresholds in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River Basin (MLRYRB). The results reveal that: (1) DTF and FTD events occur 22–26 times on average, with moderate intensity being most prevalent. Hotspots include western Hunan, southern Anhui, and southern Jiangsu. (2) Vegetation growth is relatively good, with NPP increasing at 2.82 gC·m−2·a−1. High NPP values cluster in southern Shaanxi and northwestern Hubei, while lower values appear in central Hubei, southern Jiangsu, and southern Anhui. (3) Vegetation NPP exhibits similar response patterns to DTF and FTD events, with the likelihood of vegetation loss increasing as the intensity of DFAA increases. NPP is highly sensitive to DFAA events, with the threshold intensities for DTF and FTD that trigger vegetation loss being relatively low, respectively ranging from 1 to 1.8 and −2.1 to 1, with area proportions reaching 73.75 % and 80.35 %, respectively. Vegetation in southern Anhui, northern Hubei, and southern Shaanxi resists DTF events more effectively, whereas central-northern Hunan and western Jiangxi vegetation shows higher FTD resistance. Among driving factors, vapor pressure deficit (VPD) most significantly influences DFAA-related vegetation loss thresholds. This study advances understanding of vegetation responses to DFAA events in the MLRYRB and supports strategies for maintaining regional vegetation health and enhancing carbon sequestration capacity.

title: Improving the performance of green office buildings in mainland China through facility management under the "dual carbon" goals
abstract: This study examines how facility management (FM), influenced by national policy and technological advancements, can enhance the carbon reduction capacity (CRC) of green office buildings in mainland China. Addressing a significant research gap, it examines the operational phase of green buildings, often neglected in traditional design-focused evaluations. A novel theoretical framework, Integrated Technology Acceptance and Policy Change Theory (I-TAM-PCT), is introduced to analyze the institutional and technological drivers of FM effectiveness. A hybrid analytical method, Entropy-TOPSIS–Machine Learning (ET-ML), is applied to 203 survey responses and nine expert interviews. A composite index, the Integrated Carbon Reduction Performance Index (ICRPI), was developed using 16 dimensions from policy and technology indicators. Among eight evaluated algorithms, Gradient Boosting achieved the highest accuracy (0.89), with SHAP analysis indicating that policy incentives, responsiveness, and Digital Twin-based FM (DTFM) features, especially real-time consumption monitoring and predictive optimization, are the most significant factors in enhancing CRC. Notably, buildings implementing DTFM showed an average CRC improvement of 18.4 % compared to non-adopters. By integrating a multi-level policy–technology framework with a reliable computational model, this study advances both theoretical understanding and practical approaches for carbon-neutral building operations. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers and practitioners in China and other developing economies pursuing low-carbon growth through intelligent FM.

title: Predicting the emergence of the EV industry: A product space analysis across regions and firms
abstract: The automotive industry is undergoing a profound transformation, driven by the electrification of powertrains, the rise of software-defined vehicles, and the adoption of circular economy concepts. These trends are increasingly blurring the boundaries between the automotive sector and other industries. The pace of adaptation to electrification varies considerably between regions and firms. Unlike internal combustion engine (ICE) production, where mechanical capabilities dominated, competitiveness in electric vehicle (EV) production increasingly depends on expertise in electronics, batteries, and software. This study investigates whether and how firms' ability to leverage cross-industry diversification contributes to their competitive advantage in this evolving landscape. We develop a country-level product space covering all industries, and an industry-specific product space covering over 900 automotive components. This allows us to identify clusters of parts which are exported together, revealing shared manufacturing capabilities. Closeness centrality in the country-level product space, rather than simple proximity, is a strong predictor of where new comparative advantages are likely to emerge. First, we examine this relationship across all industrial sectors to establish general patterns of path dependency, diversification and capability formation. Then, we focus specifically on the electric vehicle (EV) transition. It is argued that new strengths in vehicles and aluminium products in the EU will generate 5 and 4.6 times more EV-specific strengths, respectively, than other EV-relevant sectors over the next decade. In contrast, these sectors are expected to generate only 1.6 and 4.5 new strengths, respectively, in already diversified China. However, a different pattern emerges when these country-level results are compared to the firm-level product space. Countries such as South Korea, China, the US and Canada show the greatest potential for diversification into EV-related products. Established producers in the EU are likely to come under pressure. These findings suggest that the success of the automotive transformation will depend on the ability of regions to mobilize existing industrial capabilities, particularly in related sectors such as machinery and electronic equipment.

title: Microenvironments outweigh mobility in PM2.5 exposure inequality: A case study of Beijing commuters
abstract: PM2.5 exposure poses significant public health risks by contributing to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. Traditional static PM2.5 exposure assessments, which focus on residential or workplace locations, overlook human mobility and microenvironmental variations, leading to biased estimates. To address this, we developed the Microenvironment-bAsed Dynamic Exposure (MADE) framework to assess PM2.5 exposures for Beijing commuters. Using mobile phone signaling data and fuzzy mathematics, we simulated spatiotemporal behaviors across residential, occupational, commuting, and other microenvironments. The MADE framework integrates geographic PM2.5 variations and indoor-outdoor concentration differences, achieving precise, large-scale exposure estimates. The mean PM2.5 exposure estimated by the MADE framework (40.82 μg/m3) is 6.9 % lower than that estimated by the static model (43.86 μg/m3). The PM2.5 exposure concentrations present a geographic pattern of being higher in the south and lower in the north, which is consistent with the static model but with smaller values. The reductions in exposure concentrations for individuals living in southern areas with high PM2.5 concentrations are slightly greater than for those living in northern areas with low PM2.5 concentrations. Differences in indoor-outdoor concentrations are the primary drivers of disparities, challenging the notion that geographic variations in PM2.5 concentrations dominate exposure inequality. Commuting, owing to its limited time proportion, contributes minimally to overall exposure. These findings correct overestimations in static models and highlight the need to incorporate indoor environmental complexity and diverse population activities for accurate exposure assessments. By addressing these factors, the MADE framework advances environmental justice and informs equitable public health policies.

title: Can Technology make a paradigm shift in sustainable tourism: Augmented Reality a path towards sustainable tourism
abstract: Tourism impacts a destination's environment, economy, and society, acting as a double-edged sword. Though it is a good source of revenue generation, it has an immense impact on the carbon footprint also. Developing and promoting sustainable practices will be a panacea to minimize the negative impacts that could be caused by technological advancements. Technological breakthroughs such as Augmented Reality (AR) apps can help operationalize sustainability in the tourism industry by creating a virtual environment for travelers, cutting down on energy consumption, which is otherwise at its peak. Despite the rising interest in sustainable tourism, little research has examined influence of AR on sustainable tourism beyond initial adoption. Drawing on Affordance Theory and Transaction Cost Theory, this research examines if sustainable tourism behaviour facilitate continued usage intention for AP travel apps. This research also examines antecedents of continued usage of AR travel applications (apps) that motivate environment-conscious tourists to use the app for all their decisions. Data was collected through a survey of 566 travelers and sustainability-oriented users. Empirical results show that Perceived Augmentation Quality is positively related with Sustainable Tourism (β = 0.281, SE = 0.046, p < 0.001), and Sustainable Tourism significantly influences Continuance Usage of AR applications (β = 0.139, SE = 0.067, p < 0.05). Also, Novelty Seeking is a good predictor of sustainable tourism behaviors (β = 0.291, p < 0.001), reflecting the fact that tourists prefer new, low-impact holiday activities. Empirical findings evince that perceived augmented reality, experiential authenticity, novelty seeking and frugality consciousness significantly impact sustainable tourism while using an AR mobile App, thereby enabling responsible tourism. This research contributes to theory by extending the affordance lens to usage of AR in sustainability contexts, and practice by yielding actionable advice for for App marketers to provide digital solutions for tourists and boost sustainable practices by motivating travelers to protect the environment during leisure activities.

title: Dual-atom-site photocatalysts enhanced CO2 reduction coupled with benzylamine oxidation
abstract: Solar-driven artificial photosynthesis via CO2 reduction represents a promising method for generating renewable feedstock in a sustainable manner. However, CO2 activation is very demanding and the separation of undesired O2 as by-product is challenging. Promoting the oxidation of organic substances by consuming photo-generated holes can effectively prevent O2 production, improving energy conversion, product selectivity and separation. In this study, we report a photosensitizer-functionalized (tris(2,2′-bipyridyl)ruthenium, PS) dual-atom-site [Ru(C10N2H4)2Cl2]H4[Ru2Cl2(CH3COO)4]·H2O (PS-Ru2) photocatalyst that promotes the conversion of CO2 to CO with the photooxidation of benzylamine to liquid benzylidenebenzylamine, enabling facile separation without additional photosensitizers or sacrificial agents in a single redox cycle. This is the first reported dual-atom-site photocatalytic system to promote an artificial photosynthetic CO2 reduction coupled with benzylamine oxidation, delivering high activity, selectivity and separability. Modification of the photosensitizer resulted in an eleven-fold increase in yield, representing a significant advancement in catalytic CO2 photoreduction. The findings of this study establish a novel dual-atom-site catalyst design strategy that facilitates dual-functional artificial photosynthesis, enabling by-product reuse with improved performance.

title: Coordinating net-zero: Organizational learning as a meta-capability in carbon-intensive Indian firms
abstract: Despite rising net-zero commitments, many carbon-intensive firms struggle to translate ambition into change in everyday work. This study examines how organizational learning operates as a coordination meta-capability linking strategic net-zero intent to operational transformation. Using Gioia-style grounded theorizing, we analyse 25 semi-structured, multi-level interviews from five large Indian firms in the energy, oil and gas, steel, cement, and automotive sectors. We inductively identify four micro-foundations and six cross-cutting learning routines that together constitute organizational learning as a coordination system. We then introduced capability fluency and proposed a Distribution–Reflexivity–Integration (D-R-I) rubric to operationalize the quality of this system. The rubric assesses how widely routines are deployed, whether periodic reviews trigger within-cycle changes, and how tightly micro-foundations are linked. Two firms in our sample exhibit high capability fluency, two moderate, and one low. Variation in net-zero learning stems less from the presence of routines than from their D–R–I quality and the strength of coupling mechanisms. We further translate the Dynamic Capabilities View into a measurable, auditable architecture, offering a simple D–R–I rubric, count-based indicators, and a learning maturity roadmap that provides managers and policymakers with concrete diagnostics and low-cost design options for integrating net-zero into day-to-day decisions in emerging economies.

title: Green manure incorporation as a solution to synergistically improve crop yields and soil organic carbon sequestration
abstract: Planting and incorporating green manure has been widely used worldwide due to the benefits of improving soil quality and crop yields. However, a comprehensive assessment of the effects of planting and incorporating green manures on soil properties and crop production is still lacking. Here we conducted a meta-analysis to determine the effects of green manure planting and incorporation on soil nitrate-N leaching, soil water, soil properties, SOC sequestration, and crop yield in wheat, maize, rice, and tobacco. Results showed that planting and incorporating green manure reduced soil nitrate-N leaching during its growing season by 44 %, and reduced the soil water storage in the 0–200 cm soil layers before sowing and at harvest of the following crop by 11 % and 5 %, respectively. Incorporating green manure increased soil total nitrogen, soil available phosphorus, soil available potassium, and SOC sequestration rate by 13 %, 8 %, 8 %, and 64 % in the 0–20 cm soil layer, respectively. As a result, green manure incorporation increased the mean yield of the following season by 12 %, with maize yields significantly higher than those of rice and tobacco. Over the past six decades, the area harvested for green manure has increased substantially worldwide, playing an important role in sustainable crop production. Scientific management of green manure will therefore be a key strategy to achieve a win-win situation for both food security and environmental protection.

title: The digital divide and hog industry: The impact of digital technology levels on the sustainability of the hog industry in China
abstract: The hog industry is vital for food security and global protein supply, yet it faces challenges in achieving sustainability due to environmental issues and inefficiencies in production processes. The rapid growth of the digital economy provides new opportunities for transforming traditional industries, including the hog sector, by enhancing efficiency, optimizing resource use, and reducing environmental impacts. This study aims to explore the relationship between digital technology and the sustainable development of the hog industry, this study employing the Entropy Weight and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method to construct two comprehensive indices: the Digital Technology Level (DTL) index and the Sustainable Hog Industry (SHI) index. Using a two-way fixed effects model, this study analyzes the impact of DTL on SHI and identifies key findings. From 2012 to 2021, DTL in China showed a continuous upward trend, increasing from 0.091 to 0.176 nationally, while SHI rose slowly from 0.269 to 0.295. However, significant regional disparities remain, with developed eastern regions such as Tianjin and Beijing achieving both high DTL and SHI, while central and western regions lag behind. DTL is found to be a key driver of SHI, with a significantly positive correlation across all models. However, the digital divide weakens the positive effects of digital technology in underdeveloped areas, hindering sustainable development. To address these challenges, this study proposes narrowing the digital divide, enhancing digital technology applicability in different regions, and fostering regional collaboration. These findings provide valuable insights for promoting the sustainable transformation of the hog industry through digital technologies.

title: Seaweeds as a nature-based solution to mitigate nutrient and carbon emissions from shrimp farming (Penaeus vannamei) under current and future climate conditions
abstract: Economically important agarophyte seaweeds have proven to be excellent biofilters for mitigating excess nutrients from shrimp farming. However, the effects of warming on their bioremediation capacity have been little explored, which is concerning given the current context of climate change. Thus, this study evaluated the performance of the agarophytes Gracilaria caudata and Gracilaria birdiae as biofilters for mitigating excess nutrients and carbon produced by shrimp cultivation (Penaeus vannamei) in an outdoor integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) experiment using two recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS): one at ambient temperature (ambient-RAS) and the other under elevated temperature (warmed-RAS). Shrimp in the ambient-RAS exhibited relative growth rates (RGRs) ranging from 0.25 % to 3.24 % day−1, with final weights increasing from 11.6 g to 18.4 g. In the warmed-RAS, RGRs ranged from 0.31 % to 1.97 % day−1, with final weights increasing from 11.4 g to 16.2 g. No significant differences in shrimp productivity were observed between treatments. In seaweed cultivation of the ambient-RAS, NO3− concentrations decreased by 7–39 %, NH4+ by 4–33 %, and PO43− by 1–18 %. In the warmed-RAS, reductions were 8–31 % for NO3−, 5–21.5 % for NH4+, and 1–17 % for PO43−. Warming did not significantly affect biofiltration efficiency. Seaweeds cultivated in RAS exhibited increasing content of nitrogen, phosphorus, and phycobiliproteins over time, confirming nutrient uptake. CO2 concentrations in seaweed cultivation were reduced by 38 % under ambient conditions and by 27 % under elevated temperature. In the IMTA experiment, seaweeds stored from 8 to 12.4 g C m−2 in their dry biomass. Gracilaria caudata exhibited better performance under elevated temperature compared to G. birdiae. Our findings support the feasibility of implementing IMTA in shrimp farms as a sustainable strategy for cleaner shrimp production. In addition to environmental benefits, seaweed cultivation in IMTA can generate social and economic gains through the production of agar, organic fertilizers, natural pigments, and carbon credits.

title: Industry heterogeneity of environmental, social, and governance performance, impact mechanisms and trend forecasts - Evidence from big data and machine learning analysis
abstract: This paper aims to delve into the industry-specific heterogeneity of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance among Chinese listed companies by employing a comprehensive research design that integrates descriptive statistics with analysis of variance (ANOVA), time series modeling, correlation analysis, cluster analysis. Through an in-depth examination of 188,006 ESG score records from Chinese listed companies spanning from 2009 to the first quarter of 2024, the study reveals that financial services and insurance sectors generally exhibit higher ESG scores, whereas traditional manufacturing industries lag in ESG performance, facing more significant environmental and social challenges. ANOVA results indicate highly significant differences across industries in terms of E, S, G, and composite ESG scores. Time trend forecasting based on Prophet model time series analysis suggests that ESG scores for Chinese listed companies will continue to rise over the next few years but with fluctuations, providing crucial forward-looking decision support for enterprises and policymakers. Correlation analysis reveals generally weak interconnections among the E, S, and G dimensions, with the strongest (though modest) association observed between environmental and social scores, suggesting limited cross-dimensional spillover effects. Cluster analysis segments companies into five groups with similar ESG characteristics, revealing significant variations in ESG performance among these clusters.

title: Multi-objective optimization framework for enhancing the sustainability and resilience of green-grey infrastructure: A perspective incorporating the impact of pipeline siltation on flood simulation
abstract: The renovation of green-grey infrastructure is increasingly recognized for its role in mitigating urban flood risks and promoting environmental sustainability related to surface infiltration and drainage systems. Despite extensive research on decision-making for optimization, enhancing sustainability and resilience considering instantaneous infiltration capacity and the impact of pipe network siltation remains under-explored. To address this gap, a modified function for the infiltration capacity of the permeable underlying surface considering the influence of pipeline siltation was constructed by integrating the seepage control equation of the storage box and the quantification method of the infiltration model. Then, combining the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation based on improved entropy weight and correlation coefficient (IEC-CRITIC), multi-channel preprocessing long short-term memory network and weighted time embedding Transformer (MPLSTM-WTET), a hydraulic model and flood simulation approach that took into account the impact of the calibrated infiltration parameters and the equivalent siltation degree/length of the drainage pipeline network was formulated. On this basis, a combined multi-objective optimization decision-making model for the renovation of green-grey infrastructure (i.e., environmental sustainability, flood resilience, flood loss, inundated area and renovation cost) was proposed based on generational distance and distributed adaptive genetic algorithm (GD-DAGA). The results indicated that the introduced equivalent siltation degree of pipe network and the determination method of instantaneous infiltration capacity can significantly improve the prediction accuracy of flood simulation (91.4 % and 82.9 % for prediction of inundation depth and inundation area). Simultaneously, generation distance and distributed adaptive genetic algorithm overcome the problems of premature convergence and distortion of local optimal solutions, thereby enhancing the performance of multi-objective optimization of green-grey infrastructure renovation in terms of environmental sustainability, flood resilience, flood loss, inundated area and renovation cost. Consequently, this framework can provide novel insights into the application of redundancy strategies for the renovation and planning of sustainable urban green-grey infrastructure management.

title: Optimization of rumen function for decreasing enteric methane: A conceptual framework
abstract: Livestock contribute to 32 % of methane production from the agriculture sector. To limit global warming to under 1.5 °C, it is imperative to decrease methane emissions. While various approaches have been investigated, two strategies are receiving particular attention at present: a) additives that inhibit methane-producing enzymes (e.g. 3-Nitrooxypropanol and seaweeds), and b) rumen microbial ecosystem modifiers (e.g. probiotics and plant secondary metabolites). However, the potential of rumen fermentation optimization towards enteric methane reduction has been underexplored and rarely discussed. This report quantifies decrease in enteric methane and increase in microbial mass production achievable through optimized rumen fermentation. The estimates are derived from: (a) substrate requirements for short-chain fatty acid production according to Wolin's stoichiometry of carbohydrate fermentation, (b) ATP generated during these conversions, and (c) variations in microbial mass synthesis efficiency with ATP utilization. The results suggest a reduction of 30–35 % enteric methane and doubling of microbial mass production. The advantages of optimizing rumen fermentation over the approaches using the inhibitors and phytogenic compounds, e.g. enhanced animal productivity and farmers' income; reduced nitrogen excretion; and enhanced animal health, welfare and immunity are presented. Furthermore, the narrative presented is that optimization of rumen fermentation is a pre-requisite for eliciting higher effects of other approaches and must not be neglected. Triple-gains of higher livestock productivity, reduced enteric methane and greater profitability can be achieved sustainably through this approach.

title: Modulation of reservoir surface wettability by CO2 injection: A molecular simulation perspective
abstract: Reservoir surface wettability plays a crucial role in governing the efficiency of CO2-EOR and concurrent geological carbon storage. However, previous studies have mostly focused on CO2-water-rock or oil-water-rock systems, with few studies revealing the modulation of reservoir surface wettability by CO2 injection and its underlying micro-mechanisms under CO2/oil miscible conditions. This study employed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate how CO2 injection modulates reservoir surface wettability under miscible flooding conditions, and to examine the microscopic interfacial interactions among CO2/octane, water, and silica. In addition, the influence of the reservoir surface hydroxylation degree and water coverage on CO2 flooding was further investigated. Results indicated that CO2 injection significantly affected the surface wettability, with the underlying mechanism strongly dependent on surface chemistry. On hydroxyl surfaces, CO2 and water exhibited co-adsorption, while CO2 and octane showed strong competitive adsorption. Thus, CO2 enhanced oil recovery and carbon storage without significantly altering wettability. On non-hydroxyl surfaces, CO2 competed with both water and octane, enhanced hydrophobicity and increased the water contact angle by ∼33.3° (26.3%). Further analysis indicated that surface water coverage determined the effectiveness of CO2 flooding. On non-hydroxyl surfaces, CO2 flooding was effective at low surface water coverage, but became detrimental to oil recovery when the coverage exceeded 60%. To bridge engineering application, we proposed an upscaling ΔP criterion that relates composition-dependent adsorption to reservoir-scale oil adsorption, and provided an illustrative calculation. This study provides a theoretical basis for modulating surface wettability and optimizing injection strategies during CO2 flooding in unconventional reservoirs.

title: Coordination and management of multiple energy-water microgrids based on a fuzzy predictive control strategy
abstract: This paper presents an energy-water management system for coordinating multiple energy-water microgrids connected to the main electrical grid, a drinking water network, and access to groundwater from an aquifer. The structure of the proposed energy-water management system is a two-level hierarchical control system composed of local-level controllers for each microgrid and a supervisor-level controller for multiple microgrids. At the supervisor level, a novel model that describes multiple interconnected energy-water microgrids is proposed, which includes the information of electrical demand, renewable generation, and water consumption predicted by fuzzy models, the known dynamics of the different electric and water components from previous works, and a new capability of bidirectional sharing of the local water resource among the microgrids. Thanks to the inclusion of this bidirectional water sharing feature, the proposed control strategy can be used to manage and coordinate multiple energy-water microgrids, considering a sustainable use of the shared aquifer. A simulation for three interconnected energy-water microgrids is carried out to validate these proposals, comparing its results with a scenario where each microgrid is operated locally without coordination. The results show that the proposed coordinated controller achieves a sustainable use of groundwater and promotes cooperation between microgrids, decreasing groundwater use by 5.69% with respect to the case without coordination.

title: Cascade biorefining of tobacco waste: co-production of aroma extracts, photo-fermentation biohydrogen, and biogas
abstract: The co-production technology of aroma extraction, photo-fermentation biohydrogen production (PFHP) and biogas can greatly enhance energy conversion efficiency of tobacco waste. This study was carried out to detect the aroma components, the liquid-phase and gas-phase properties of the co-production of biohydrogen and biogas. Meanwhile, the kinetic characteristics of both PFHP and biogas production were analyzed using the Gompertz equation. At a substrate concentration of 27.04 g VS/L (35 g/L), the hydrogen yield and methane yield obtained in the experiment were 189 mL H2/g VS (146.13 mL/g) and 260 mL CH4/g VS (200.94 mL/g), respectively. The maximum light conversion efficiency of PFHP was 52.01 %. The findings can not only reduce the harm of tobacco waste to the environment but also establish a biorefining protocol for high-value resource recovery.

title: Sustainable alkaline cements with different Ca contents for stabilisation of copper mine tailings
abstract: The sustainable management of mine tailings is a growing challenge for the mining sector, with substantial environmental risks and long-term storage costs. This study explores the valorisation of copper mine tailings through the production of alkali-activated mortars (AAMs) using low-calcium fly ash and high-calcium blast furnace slag as precursors. A five-level Central Composite Design within the Response Surface Methodology framework was applied to optimise three key mix parameters: precursor/solid ratio, activator/precursor ratio, and sodium silicate/hydroxide ratio. Uniaxial compressive strength testing was supported by microstructural analyses (Scanning Electron Microscopy, Energy-Dispersive Spectroscopy, X-Ray Diffraction, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy) to correlate strength with gel composition and morphology. Optimal slag-based mixes achieved compressive strengths up to 15 MPa, driven by C-(A)-S-H and N-(C)-A-S-H gel formation, whereas ash-based systems reached 12 MPa, with performance strongly dependent on silicate/hydroxide ratio and N-A-S-H gel development. Response Surface modelling accurately predicted compressive strenght (R 2 > 0.87) and identified precursor chemistry as a key determinant of activator efficiency. These results demonstrate the feasibility of designing high-performance, tailings-based AAM, while reducing reliance on Portland cement, contributing to circular economy goals through CO 2 emission reduction and industrial waste reuse. A screening LCA indicates 0.24–0.37 kg CO 2 e kg −1 of paste for optimised mixes, 56–71 % lower than an OPC benchmark under declared assumptions. The work is framed as a screening-level optimisation and comparison (FA vs BFS) with explicit model limits and microstructural corroboration. The findings provide a robust optimisation approach for tailoring sustainable binder systems to diverse tailings chemistries. • Alkali-activated binders stabilise copper tailings using FA and BFS. • Precursor fraction and activator chemistry control early-age strength. • Inline figures and model diagnostics (incl. parity plots) improve clarity. • XRD, FTIR and SEM-EDS evidence support gel formation mechanisms. • Ambient validation, durability and leaching tests defined as next steps.

title: A gas–liquid entrainment scrubber for fine silica dust control in an ore-crushing workshop: Industrial field testing and integrated assessment
abstract: Wet scrubbers are the main technology for controlling fine particulate matter (PM) in workplaces. However, their effectiveness is often limited by intermittent dust escape, unquantified scrubbing liquid turbidity effects, and non-integrated performance metrics; these deficiencies result in suboptimal efficiency, high energy consumption, empirically-based blowdown scheduling, and hindered objective comparison across technologies. To address these issues, we developed a novel gas-liquid entrainment scrubber (GLES). The efficacy of the GLES in respirable silica dust removal was systematically evaluated through field tests, with a quantitative assessment of the effects of liquid level, gas flow velocity, inlet dust concentration, and scrubbing liquid turbidity on purification efficiency. Furthermore, we proposed a comprehensive performance metric, namely the wet scrubber comprehensive quality factor (WSCQF), which integrates purification efficiency, specific energy consumption, and dust wettability. Results show that the GLES achieved peak purification efficiencies of 99.90 %, 99.83 %, 99.49 %, 98.39 %, and 95.48 % for total suspended particles (TSP), PM with aerodynamic diameters ≤10 μm (PM10), ≤4 μm (PM4), ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5), and ≤1 μm (PM1), respectively. According to the WSCQF, the GLES outperformed other scrubbers by a factor of 1.44–4.59. A significant inverse correlation between purification efficiency and turbidity was observed, with greater sensitivity for smaller dust size fractions. This study not only provides a systematic theoretical framework and technical solution for performance enhancement and precise operation of wet scrubbers but also offers a novel and universal tool for benchmarking and optimizing such systems, thereby contributing to the advancement of cleaner production practices.

title: Investigating spatial-temporal patterns of the important disruptions associated with China's LNG shipping network
abstract: Maritime shipping serves as the primary mode of transporting liquefied natural gas (LNG) due to the significant regional disparities of LNG distribution. However, the shipping industry is subject to various disruptions. In this study, disruptions associated with China's LNG import shipping network are investigated. For this purpose, the data is first collected to understand the disruptions during 2015–2024. To evaluate the disruption information, the collected disruption information is mathematically processed by developing a data-driven particle swarm optimization and back propagation neural network (PSO-BP) algorithm. The various disruption information is input into the input layer, and through the calculation of the hidden layer and output layer of the BP neural network, which is aggregated into a comprehensive value. Then, the comprehensive disruption value is geographically and visually presented with the application of ArcGIS. Additionally, the key disruption aspects are identified by developing an obstacle degree model. Finally, the results are described from three aspects: temporal changes, spatial distribution, and key disruption aspects. More importantly, the disturbed level of the network is compared and analyzed before and after the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The results of this study provide practical insights that can help decision-makers promote the development of the LNG shipping network.

title: Strength enhancement and microstructural observation of cement-stabilized calcareous sand by optimizing the preparation process
abstract: Although calcareous sand is utilized in select marine infrastructure, its high porosity and inherent particle crushability fundamentally limit structural integrity under operational loads, necessitating effective stabilization strategies. Cement stabilization, valued for its maturity and mechanical stability in sandy soils, may cause environmental issues when cement is excessively applied to reinforce calcareous sand. This study optimizes the preparation process of cemented calcareous sand to enhance its mechanical properties without increasing cement content. The incorporation of nano-silica further strengthens the shear resistance by the improvement of cement reactivity and microstructural densification. Macroscopic mechanical properties were systematically evaluated through consolidated drained triaxial tests. Micromorphological features were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) quantitatively analyzed the evolution of pore architecture within the microstructure. Results demonstrated that specimens prepared by the pre-wetting method exhibit significantly enhanced shear strength compared to traditional approaches, particularly under lower curing ages and effective confining pressures. Interestingly, the pre-wetting method enhances cohesion by 43.9 % compared to traditional methods, while having a relatively small effect on the friction angle. Mechanistically, the pre-wetting method enhances cementation by simultaneously promoting cementitious hydrates and strengthening the interfacial transition zone (ITZ). This process yields a densified microstructure with optimized pore architecture, where quantitative MIP analysis confirms a 6.2 % reduction in large capillary pores, thereby enhancing cohesive properties. Life cycle assessment (LCA) further demonstrates that this pre-wetting optimization approach achieves sustainable development goals while maintaining cost-effectiveness. It provides an eco-friendly strategy to enhance calcareous sand stabilization while reducing cement dependency.

title: Unlocking the synergistic advantages of Sponge city initiative: A hybrid life-cycle assessment of industrial stimulation effect and water-carbon co-benefits
abstract: Sponge City aims to improve urban resilience through sustainable water management. With China aiming for 80 % urban area coverage by 2030, this study examines its industrial stimulation effects and water-carbon co-benefits, including water resource recovery, water pollution reduction, and carbon emission mitigation. A Hybrid Life-Cycle Assessment (HLCA) utilizing a semi-closed input-output model was constructed based on inputs derived from official statistics, industry standards and technical guidelines. Results indicate strong industrial stimulation multiples of 6 and 6.2 during construction and operation phases. Yet, construction contributes significantly negative impacts (9–30 % of the national total), while operation yields smaller impacts (0.3–0.4 % of the national total). Sectoral analysis indicates that agriculture and forestry drive water use, labour drives pollution, and electricity sector dominates carbon emissions. Net benefits arise in operation, with payback periods of no more than 44, 3, and 39 years for water resource recovery, pollution reduction, and carbon mitigation. This study concludes that Sponge City offers a distinct overall advantage: unlike traditional infrastructure which fails to offset negative water-carbon impacts, it achieves a net positive outcome within its service life, even under the stringent, all-inclusive accounting of the semi-closed HLCA model. These findings provide policy recommendations to optimize Sponge City's water-carbon co-benefits and guide global adoption.

title: CoFe@NiFe-LDH/CC bifunctional electrode: Mechanism and reactive oxygen species generation in the synergistic anodic oxidation and electro-Fenton processes
abstract: Electrochemical advanced oxidation processes show great promise for water purification, yet the development of efficient bifunctional electrodes remains a pressing challenge. In this work, a CoFe@NiFe-LDH/CC electrode was strategically fabricated via hydrothermal synthesis and electrodeposition, integrating anodic oxidation and electro-Fenton capabilities. The three-dimensional layered double hydroxide architecture enhances pollutant adsorption and expedites electron transport, thereby promoting reactive oxygen species generation. Unlike conventional systems dominated by hydroxyl radicals, this system predominantly generates singlet oxygen and superoxide radicals, enabling robust degradation performance across a wide pH range. Under neutral conditions, over 90 % of moxifloxacin was degraded within 60 min, demonstrating excellent stability. Density functional theory calculations revealed the ROS attack sites, while toxicity assessments confirmed the environmental safety of the degradation intermediates. This study offers valuable insights into the rational design of bifunctional electrodes for high-efficiency wastewater treatment.

title: Full-chain analysis of biogas-to-hydrogen (BTH) process: Integrating advanced catalysis, multi-scale process modeling and techno-economic analysis for industrial implementation
abstract: The biogas-to-hydrogen (BTH) process has emerged as a promising pathway toward carbon neutrality due to its closed-loop carbon characteristics and process compatibility advantages. To systematically investigate an efficient green hydrogen (H2) production system from biogas, the optimal performances of different biogas steam reforming (SMR) catalysts were explored, and the most suitable water gas shift (WGS) catalyst under real SMR tail gas conditions was screened in this study. Aspen Plus was used to simulate and evaluate the H2 production efficiency and economic viability of the entire BTH process. Experimental results demonstrate that the selected SMR catalyst achieves near-complete biogas conversion, yielding syngas with the highest H2 content. The optimal WGS catalyst maintains low methane (CH4) content while producing H2-rich gas. Aspen process simulation reveals excellent agreement with experimental data, with deviations within ±5 %. At a processing capacity of 1000 m3/h biogas, the system demonstrates high CH4 conversion, H2 yield, and H2 purity. Economic analysis indicates a competitive H2 production cost of 1.28 USD/kgH2, demonstrating this BTH system offers potential advantages in both H2 production efficiency and economic viability, while also delivering significant environmental benefits.

title: Awakening “sleepy” data: Can public data openness promote enterprises to achieve an “economic-environmental” win-win situation?
abstract: As a key measure to unlock the value of data elements, public data openness (PDO) provides essential data support and information reference to enterprises, and its impact on corporate operational practices warrants close attention. Based on the data of Chinese A-share listed companies in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2009 to 2023, this article uses a multi-period difference-in-differences model to empirically examine the impact of PDO on corporate sustainable development performance. The results reveal that PDO can significantly improve corporate sustainable development performance, promoting enterprises to achieve an “economic-environmental” win-win situation. The mechanism analysis indicates that this positive impact is generated through the information effect and innovation effect. The heterogeneity analysis shows that PDO improves economic performance more significantly in private enterprises and competitive industries, while improving environmental performance more significantly in low-environmental regulation areas and heavily polluting enterprises. The extended analysis reports that PDO shows significant spillover effects at both geographic and industry levels, which can promote the improvement of corporate sustainable development performance more widely. Our research not only provides new insights into the practical impact of PDO in China, but also provides valuable references for promoting the sustainable development of other economies with similar institutional backgrounds.

title: Decarbonizing the U.S. aluminum ecosystem using a dynamic material flow simulation framework
abstract: Aluminum is essential to clean energy technologies yet remains a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Decarbonizing the aluminum industry requires insight into material flows and interactions between decarbonization pathways. This study holistically analyzes the U.S. aluminum industry and its GHG emissions through system modeling and simulation. An object-oriented system model is developed to digitally represent the U.S. aluminum supply chain, enabling the generation of consumption-driven material flows and the assessment of GHG emissions from both domestic production and imported feedstocks. A range of decarbonization pathways was applied to U.S. domestic activities and evaluated over 2020–2050. To assess their interactions and combined impacts under uncertainty, strategy portfolios were evaluated within a design-of-experiments framework using stochastic simulation. Improving post-consumer scrap recyclability most significantly reduces total emissions by lowering carbon-intensive primary metal imports, while green hydrogen offers the greatest reduction in domestic emissions. Improving manufacturing yield efficiency markedly reduces both domestic and import emissions but also diminishes the effectiveness of other domestic measures. In contrast, pathways such as electrification and grid decarbonization act synergistically, amplifying their overall impact. A combined strategy—integrating grid decarbonization, alternative fuels, inert anodes, and enhanced material efficiency—could reduce annual GHG emissions from the U.S. aluminum supply chain by up to 90.9 % (or 42.8 % when accounting for imports) by 2050 relative to 2020. This study introduces a model-based paradigm to support strategic decarbonization planning at the supply-chain level, which can be readily adapted to other energy-intensive industries and regional contexts.

title: An automated and intelligent monitoring system for shield tunneling muck evaluation integrating multimodal data
abstract: This study presents a systematic framework for real-time monitoring and evaluation of excavated muck during shield tunneling, enhancing construction safety and efficiency while minimizing environmental impact. By integrating multimodal data from LiDAR, machine vision, and infrared spectroscopy, the system enables precise measurement of muck volume and moisture content. An enhanced optical flow-based method is designed to monitor the conveyor belt's operational status using high-resolution machine vision images, which simultaneously activates the LiDAR and spectroscopy subsystems for data acquisition. A Point-PN++ segmentation network is then applied to distinguish muck from the conveyor belt in laser point clouds, while an AE-ICP algorithm is developed to calibrate belt speed variations. Furthermore, a triangular cumulative cross-section method enables precise muck volume measurement under varying conditions. Moisture content is assessed using a PLS-SVR-based infrared spectroscopy method, which also calibrates volume measurements and supports evaluation of water inrush risks. Experimental results demonstrate a muck volume measurement accuracy of 95 % and moisture content estimation accuracy of 92 %, with results provided within 10 s. Overall, the proposed intelligent system contributes to automation, resource efficiency, and safety in shield tunnel construction.

title: Natural fiber-supramolecular hydrogel evaporator strategy for efficient solar desalination to produce freshwater
abstract: Hydrogel-based solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIWE) provides a sustainable water purification strategy with significant application value for freshwater resource acquisition. Here we propose a hydrogen bond enhanced supramolecular hydrogel (PEG-Imidazolidinyl Urea, PMI) integrated with natural balsa wood fibers and modified carbon nanotubes (CNU) for desalination of seawater and wastewater. The integration strategy of PMI and balsa enabled CNU@PMI-balsa achieved an evaporation rate of 3.45 ± 0.08 kg m−2·h−1 under one sun irradiation and showed high removal efficiencies (>95 %) for salt ions, dyes, antibiotics, and herbicides. PMI-balsa achieved efficient water transport and reduced evaporation enthalpy by hydrophilic effect of NH2 and self-assembly strategy of hydrogen bond and NaOH/Urea-functionalized carbon-nanotubes (CNU) enhanced hydrophily, dispersion and thermal management capability. The CNU@PMI-balsa system exhibited an evaporation rate of 33.77 kg m−2 d−1 and 32.47 kg m−2 d−1 after 30 d in seawater and wastewater treatment. The techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) corroborated the cost advantage of CNU@PMI-balsa and provided the optimization synthesis and application strategies. This study establishes an efficient water purification process combining natural fibers with supramolecular material to achieve sustainable purification technique of wastewater.

title: Advancing circular economy through chain of custody models: Insights into mass balance approach applications
abstract: As the concept of the circular economy gains increasing attraction, industries need to adopt more sustainable feedstock options. The mass balance approach (MBA), as a chain of custody model developed based on the academic principle of mass balance (MB), is recognized as an effective sustainable development tool and has been increasingly implemented across various sectors. This paper reviews MB and MBA applications to summarize their contributions to a sustainable transition. The findings show these approaches are vital for tracking and reducing emissions, ensuring ethical sourcing in sectors like agriculture, and integrating certified recycled or bio-based feedstocks. The scale of adoption is substantial, with tens of thousands of entities participating in major certification schemes globally. The measurable advantages are significant, including documented carbon footprint reductions of up to 90% for certain circular materials and the commercialization of new product lines with up to 80% certified sustainable content. MBA has been accelerating the circular economy by leveraging existing large-scale infrastructure. This pragmatic approach avoids the high capital cost of building segregated supply chains, offering an economically viable pathway for industries to scale up sustainable practices. Furthermore, this paper investigates challenges to MBA promotion, including implementation complexities, inconsistent definitions, and criticisms on its transparency. To overcome these, we propose three key strategies: (1) refining standards through harmonized definitions to ensure credibility; (2) increasing transparency by effectively communicating traceability information to build consumer trust; and (3) broadening the application’s scope to cover the full product lifecycle. These strategies are synthesized into a novel implementation framework to provide a structured roadmap, maximizing MBA’s potential to facilitate a sustainable industrial transformation.

title: Corporate purpose, regulation, innovation and performance: An empirical examination of French purpose-driven bylaws companies
abstract: In the contemporary volatile economic environment, companies are increasingly prioritizing societal objectives, focusing on the concept of purpose, which has attracted growing academic interest. Simultaneously, firms are encouraged to innovate across multiple dimensions to achieve greater financial performance. This paper investigates French purpose-driven bylaws companies (PBCs) as leading candidates for observing the effect of the dual approach—combining innovation efforts with commitment to purpose—on financial performance. Using a unique dataset of French PBCs and comparable industry peers from 2015 to 2021, we explore the relationship between innovation, purpose bylaws and financial performance. Our results indicate that French PBCs outperform their industry counterparts, particularly when firms maintain a continuous commitment to innovation both before and after the adoption of purpose-driven bylaws. However, companies that fail to renew their commitment to innovation following their transition to PBC status experience a decline in this performance advantage. • Purpose-driven bylaws companies outperform peers on financial performance. • Purpose bylaws with continuous innovation boost firm's profitability and accountability. • Innovation drop after adopting purpose bylaws harms financial outcomes. • Managers should favor innovation continuity when adopting purpose bylaws.

title: Research on the urban carbon reduction effect and impact mechanism of regional collaborative innovation: An quasi-natural experiment based on the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor in the Yangtze River Delta
abstract: Regional collaborative innovation plays a significant role in the low-carbon transformation of cities and the shaping of new industrial patterns. Based on the analytical framework of the STIRPAT model, this study takes the construction of the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor in the Yangtze River Delta as a quasi-natural experiment.
