It employs the difference-in-differences (DID) method to empirically examine the effect of regional collaborative innovation on urban carbon emission reduction, and incorporates a mediation effect model to further clarify the pathways and transmission mechanisms through which regional collaborative innovation influences urban carbon emissions. The results reveal a significant spatiotemporal dynamic correlation between the implementation of the collaborative innovation strategy and the reduction in urban carbon emission intensity, with the effect being particularly pronounced in interprovincial adjacent areas. Empirical analysis demonstrates that regional collaborative innovation significantly contributes to urban carbon emission reduction. This conclusion remains robust after controlling for parallel trends and conducting a series of robustness tests, including PSM-DID and placebo tests. Comparatively, the carbon reduction effects of interregional collaborative innovation are more prominent in interprovincial neighboring cities, higher-tier cities, cities with low carbon emission intensity, and resource-based cities, as opposed to average cities. Moreover, the policy dividends of regional collaborative innovation exhibit a certain degree of lag and transformation period, and the effects display a significantly increasing marginal trend over time. Mechanism analysis indicates that regional collaborative innovation primarily promotes urban carbon emission reduction through four key pathways: infrastructure improvement and upgrading, industrial structure transformation, market integration, and the innovation and diffusion of green technologies.

title: The impact of substituting animal with plant protein foods in adults’ self-selected diets on environmental, nutritional, and health outcomes: A systematic review of modelling studies
abstract: A growing body of evidence supports the shift towards plant-based diets to improve environmental sustainability and human health. However, less is known about the extent to which benefits can be achieved through simple food substitutions and potential synergies and trade-offs that occur when plant protein foods displace animal-sourced foods. We aimed to conduct a systematic review of studies that modelled replacements of animal with plant protein foods in self-selected diets on environmental, nutritional, and health outcomes. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and EMBASE in April 2024 (updated in November 2025). Eligible studies reported on diet-related environmental impacts, percentage of the population meeting recommendations for nutrients of concern or to limit, or disease burden outcomes from modelled substitutions of meat or dairy with plant protein foods in self-selected diets. Eighteen studies were included (16 of the 2662 articles retrieved from the original search and 2 additional studies from the updated search). Five studies reported outcomes across multiple domains, and the rest for one domain. Replacing red and processed meat with plant protein foods led to the greatest share of reductions in environmental impacts, while also modestly improving nutrient intakes and preventing deaths. Dairy substitutions reduced intakes of saturated fat, but also calcium and vitamin A, and depending on whether replacement foods were fortified, iodine and vitamin D. Improvements to health outcomes in the dairy scenarios were attributed solely to increases in plant protein foods. Simple substitutions of animal with plant protein foods, particularly red and processed meat, promote healthier and more sustainable diets, but policies to facilitate dietary change must address potential pitfalls for nutrients of public health concern, depending on the types of animal-sourced foods replaced. CRD42024536095. • Food substitutions are a strategy to improve human and planetary health. • Co-benefits from substituting red and processed meat with plant protein foods. • Trade-offs with calcium and vitamin A when dairy is replaced with plant protein foods. • Nutritional outcomes depend on whether replacement foods are fortified. • Policy makers should facilitate dietary change while mitigating potential trade-offs.

title: Water loss and return flows matter for water stress mitigation in China
abstract: Water is withdrawn, lost, consumed, polluted, returned, treated, reused, and traded between regions within the societal water cycle due to human activities, contributing to regional water stress. In this research, we aim to examine the impacts of the societal water cycle on water resources and explore strategies for reducing water stress in China. The results show that most provinces in China suffer from water quantity and quality stress. However, there is a significant potential to reduce water quantity stress by 36–79 % through reducing water loss and return flows. The return flows and water loss in the virtual export forms could be avoided to reduce virtual water export-induced quantity stress by 39–89 %. Agriculture and households’ return flows contribute 61–98 % to provincial water quality stress in China. The five sectors with the greatest potential to mitigate water quantity and quality stress are identified for each province, which could reduce quantity stress by 22–75 % and quality stress by 23–76 %. • Majority provinces in China suffer from both water quantity and quality stress • System thinking of societal water cycle is necessary for water stress assessment and mitigation • Water loss and return flows contribute to 36–79 % of water quantity stress • Agriculture and households' return flows contribute 61–98 % to provincial water quality stress • The top five sectors could mitigate quantity stress by 22–75 % and quality stress by 23–76 %

title: Crafting advantageous root traits by combining root restriction and dry-wet circulation to enhance rhizosphere effect and pollutant removal in constructed wetlands
abstract: Crafting advantageous root traits to fully develop plant potential for pollutant removal in constructed wetlands provides a plant metabolism-based enhancement strategy that requires no energy input. At the pilot scale, this study combined root restriction with dry-wet circulation (DWC) after plant transplanting to craft the advantageous root traits and elucidated the underlying mechanism. Furthermore, the enhancement of the crafted root traits on the rhizosphere effect and pollutant removal was verified during the subsequent normal operation. Root restriction doubled the root-to-shoot ratio, tripled root aerenchyma, and reduced root diameter by half. Based on these changes, moderate DWC (substrate water holding capacity of 50 %–100 %) enhanced photosynthesis and root respiration while also readjusting the indoleacetic acid-to-zeatin riboside ratio between root and shoot. These changes triggered a cascade of morphological responses, including a 40.6 %, 66.7 %, 52.6 %, and 10.4 %–21.6 % increase in root biomass, root active absorption area, root branching frequency, and root aerenchyma, respectively, and an approximately 50 % reduction in root diameter. Building on the nearly twofold increase in radial oxygen loss induced by root restriction, these advantageous traits further tripled and doubled radial oxygen loss and root exudation rate, respectively, and recruited more functional bacteria with stronger potential function. Consequently, the volumetric removal efficiencies of COD, NH4+-N, TN, and TP increased by 55.6 %, 13.3 %, 30.0 %, and 32.9 % on average, respectively, and the effluent met the latest environmental standards. These results demonstrate a novel plant-based, environmentally friendly enhancement strategy and establish a rapid approach to fully exploit the underutilized plant potential for pollutant removal.

title: Synergizing artificial neural networks with SSP-RCP scenarios: Long-Term projection of residential electricity demand in China under climate-economic interactions
abstract: Amid escalating climate challenges, understanding the compound effects of economic and climatic drivers on residential electricity demand has become critical for sustainable energy planning. This study develops an integrated modeling framework combining econometric analysis with machine learning to forecast China's residential electricity consumption through 2100. Utilizing provincial-level panel data (2001–2019), we first employ fixed-effects regression to identify significant predictors. The results reveal that both economic variables (including per capita GDP [PGDP] and tertiary industry share [TIS]) and climatic variables (including Cooling/Heating Degree Days [CDD/HDD] and CO2 emissions [CO2]) exhibit statistically significant effects. These determinants are subsequently integrated into an artificial neural network (ANN) architecture enhanced with scenario analysis combining Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) and Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP). Our ANN-SSP-RCP hybrid integration reduces RMSE by 13.16 %–26.83 % versus traditional models by capturing nonlinear climate-economic dynamics. Key projections reveal: (1) Under deep decarbonization scenarios (2020–2060, compared to RCP4.5 and RCP8.5), early-stage decarbonization (RCP2.6) triggers a demand rebound of 1.51 %–2.39 % due to large-scale electrification; (2) By 2100, the impact of climate factors on China's residential electricity demand is 2.7 times greater than the impact of socioeconomic factors; (3) By 2100, residential electricity consumption in the high emissions scenario will be 100 billion kWh higher than in the low emissions scenario. The framework informs adaptive policies for grid resilience, regional energy-sharing, and rebound-effect mitigation, advancing China's dual-carbon targets amid climate-economy synergies across different development trajectories.

title: Thermodynamic and economic analysis of aluminum-water reaction systems for power generation and energy storage
abstract: Efficient, carbon-free chemical energy storage and power generation can be achieved via aluminum-water reactions coupled with renewable-powered aluminum regeneration. However, systematic integration strategies for the synergistic use of thermal and hydrogen energy in aluminum-water systems are still lacking, along with comprehensive studies on the coupling between reaction parameters, power cycle configurations, operating conditions, and overall economic viability. This study developed and evaluated multiple direct and indirect power generation systems using high-temperature catalyst-free reactions as both hydrogen and heat sources. A thermodynamic modeling framework was established to examine the coupling mechanisms between reaction heat, hydrogen utilization, and power cycles, including Rankine and supercritical carbon dioxide systems. A new metric, unit aluminum power output, was proposed to link aluminum consumption with electricity generation, and the effects of reaction conditions, system design, and operating parameters on efficiency and resource use were systematically analyzed. Among the systems evaluated, the indirect configuration using a secondary reheats and recompression supercritical carbon dioxide cycle achieved the best performance, with a generation efficiency of 54.74 % and a specific output of 126.19 W h·mol−1 Al. Reaction temperature, pressure, and water-to-aluminum ratio significantly influenced energy output, showing threshold characteristics. The key supercritical carbon dioxide parameters such as turbine inlet temperature, outlet pressure (8–10 MPa), and compressor inlet temperature were also identified as performance-sensitive. Sensitivity analysis revealed that electrolysis energy use, aluminum loss, and electricity prices critically affected efficiency and cost, enabling coal-comparable electricity prices under optimal conditions. This work provided theoretical and technical guidance for developing scalable, low-carbon aluminum-fueled storage systems.

title: Effects of architectural spatial design on bacterial and fungal diversity and pathogenic potential in student dormitories under hot-humid climates
abstract: Student dormitories in hot-humid climates are prone to microbial contamination due to high humidity, inadequate ventilation, and overcrowding. However, the influence of spatial design factors on microbial diversity, assembly mechanisms, and pathogenicity in distinct functional areas remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the diversity, assembly mechanisms, and potential pathogenicity of bacterial and fungal communities at the toilets (WC) and the indoor floors (WL) in student dormitories in Shenzhen, China. The results showed that WC exhibited higher bacterial α-diversity but lower fungal α-diversity than WL, with significant β-diversity partitioning. Spatial design parameters (balcony dimensions and area) shaped the diversity of bacterial and fungal communities, with additional direct modulation and indirect alteration of microbial communities via the mediation of wind speed (Va) and PM2.5. Fungal communities were more stable than bacterial communities, and the cooperative interactions of microbial communities in WC were more pronounced than in WL. Bacterial assembly was stochastic (wider niche widths), whereas fungal assembly followed a balanced stochastic-deterministic partitioning. Notably, the abundance of potential fungal pathogens significantly exceeded that of bacteria, highlighting fungi-mediated health risks as a previously underestimated concern. Spatial design factors strongly influenced potential pathogenic taxa, underscoring their paramount importance in healthy building design. This study provides a framework linking architectural design to microbial dynamics, advocating for pathogen surveillance and design-driven interventions to mitigate exposure risks in crowded residential ecosystems.

title: Can Digital Product Passports become the next-generation eco-label? Analyzing consumer preferences for labeling using Digital Product Passports
abstract: Digital product passports (DPPs) create a QR-enabled disclosure system that traces a product's carbon footprint and post-consumer recycling pathways and are emerging as a next-generation eco-labeling mechanism for circular economies. While recent studies have focused on the supplier-oriented design frameworks of DPPs, there is a lack of research focusing on consumer preferences and their willingness to pay. To close this gap, this study conducts a consumer preference analysis targeting 500 adults in Korea and applies a Hierarchical Bayesian model to estimate the utilities for five key attributes: “scope of applicable industry”, “life cycle information”, “sustainability information,” “information management entity,” and “monthly usage fee.” The results show that consumers prioritize lifecycle and sustainability information, with “recyclability” yielding the highest marginal willingness to pay (MWTP) at KRW 285 (USD 0.19) per month. Furthermore, scenario analysis revealed that an optimal configuration can increase acceptance by approximately 30 %. These findings highlights the potential of the DPP to serve as a transformative eco-labeling mechanism that can enhance transparency, strengthen consumer trust, and accelerate the transition toward a circular economy. By identifying consumer-valued attributes such as recyclability and governance, this study offers policymakers concrete guidance for designing socially acceptable and environmentally effective DPP frameworks.

title: Analysis of modular construction challenges in the UK via a fuzzy DEMATEL-ANP approach
abstract: Modular construction (MC) represents a key innovation in the transition toward more industrialized and technologically advanced construction practices. It offers significant improvements in productivity, construction speed, and environmental performance compared to conventional building methods. However, its adoption in the UK remains limited, mainly due to persistent labour shortages, regulatory complexities, and insufficient demand. This slow uptake contrasts with the method's recognized benefits, highlighting the need for a more structured analysis of underlying barriers. Acknowledging the central role designers play in shaping MC implementation, this study investigates the barriers to modular construction from the designer's perspective. Ten critical barriers were identified through a comprehensive literature review and validated via semi-structured interviews. To evaluate both their relative importance and causal interdependencies under uncertainty, an integrated Fuzzy DEMATEL–ANP method was employed. Traditional barrier assessment approaches assume independence among barriers and fail to capture complex interdependencies. This integrated method addresses these limitations by combining fuzzy set theory to handle linguistic ambiguity, DEMATEL to reveal cause-effect relationships, and ANP to quantify priorities under interdependent conditions. Subsequently, an inner dependence matrix was constructed to capture the internal relationships among barriers, while an ANP-based weight analysis was employed to quantify the relative priority of each barrier. The analysis revealed that demand, supply, technical and regulatory barriers function as key driving barriers in the UK context, while process, quality, and knowledge barriers act as dependent constraints shaped by key drivers. These findings provide a strategic foundation for targeting high-impact interventions to support more effective modular construction adoption.

title: Environmental benefits of virtual sampling for garment production
abstract: The digitization of sample preparation processes, known as virtual sampling, offers a promising solution to reduce the environmental footprint of garment manufacturing. In the traditional physical sampling process, producing multiple prototypes for each design, sending them to buyers for approval, and repeating these steps in case of design changes cause significant environmental impacts. Virtual sampling, which uses 3D modeling software to visualize garments, provides a viable alternative to minimize these negative effects. This study aimed to evaluate the environmental benefits of virtual sample preparation compared to conventional physical sampling. A comparative Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was conducted using GaBi 10.7 software, based on real factory data from four different garment models. Replacing physical sampling with virtual sampling reduced the global warming potential, human toxicity, and primary energy demand by approximately 85–90 %, and water consumption by 86–91 %, depending on the garment type. Virtual sampling also shortened sample preparation time by up to 73 %. A sensitivity analysis assessed the effect of ±10 % variations in electricity consumption for energy-intensive processes, indicating that Global Warming Potential values were more sensitive to electricity use in virtual sample preparation. Overall, this study provides one of the first quantitative, factory-based LCA comparisons of virtual and traditional sampling, offering novel insights into digital transformation and sustainability in the apparel industry.

title: Circular economy as governmentality and postcolonial discourse in Indonesian telecom companies
abstract: The global challenge of electronic waste has made the circular economy an increasingly prominent sustainability agenda, yet its meanings and practices remain contested. Telecommunications, a sector generating significant e-waste and driving rapid digitalisation, provides a revealing context for exploring these tensions. In Indonesia—the largest digital market in Southeast Asia with weak formal recycling systems and rising regulatory pressures—the stakes of circular economy adoption are particularly urgent. This paper critically examines how the circular economy is constructed and mobilised within Indonesia's telecommunications sector. Based on 28 semi-structured interviews with managers, regulators, consultants, academics, and NGO representatives, the study employs thematic analysis guided by Foucault's concept of governmentality and postcolonial critique. The findings reveal three dynamics: circular economy as a disciplinary technology that responsibilises consumers and regulators; circular economy as an imported discourse that marginalises indigenous practices and reinforces dependency; and circular economy as entangled with digital expansion, legitimising extractivism under the guise of sustainability. By conceptualising circular economy in telecoms as governance, dependency, and digital extractivism, this study advances new understanding of how sustainability agendas are translated in emerging economies. It introduces a new discourse that repositions Indonesia as a lens for theorising the global politics of circular economy, moving debates beyond barriers and efficiency toward power, responsibility, and inequality.

title: Effects of aerosol and cloud on global gross primary productivity
abstract: The aerosol and cloud have been shown to influence the gross primary productivity (GPP) in terrestrial ecosystems. The common methods are physical and vegetation process models, which are restricted only to the surrounding area of study. To overcome these geographical and scalar limitations, we establish several machine learning models to assess the effect of aerosol optical depth (AOD) and cloud optical depth (COD) on GPP. Results showed that LightGBM performed better than other models, and contribution uncertainty (CU) is less than 15 % for 81.7 % AOD and 80.5 % COD. Both AOD and COD demonstrated an inhibitory effect on GPP (ΔGPPAOD: 3.46 g C/m2, ΔGPPCOD : 14.96 g C/m2), largely dispersed in the Congo Basin, North America, and Southeast Asia. Analysis of extensive data revealed two critical thresholds for ΔGPP response to AOD/COD gradients. The first threshold marks the transition from low suppression to diffuse fertilization enhancement, other indicates the return to suppression under heavy loading. Comparing the threshold for different plant types revealed that Forests with high canopy structures and farmland types with high leaf area index have a stronger positive regulatory capacity for AOD, while shrubs are more sensitive. For most vegetation, the inhibitory effect of COD on GPP is more significant and stronger than that of AOD. The results of this study help to understand the impact mechanisms of AOD and COD on the terrestrial carbon cycle.

title: Toward carbon neutrality? legitimizing carbon-neutral disengagement in agri-food organizations
abstract: The aim of this article is to analyze the perceptions held by business leaders in the agri-food sector with regard to carbon neutrality pledges, and how these leaders justify their organizations' lack of commitment or relative passivity in this area. The results of a qualitative study carried out by using semi-structured interviews with 34 business leaders show that—despite the strategic importance of climate issues, the vulnerability of the agri-food sector to climate risks and growing institutional pressure to reduce and offset greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions—most respondents remain skeptical or even distrustful of the relevance and credibility of carbon neutrality targets. The findings show a core tension between recognizing the importance of the principle of carbon neutrality and adopting specific, measurable and short-term commitments. The rationalizations used to legitimize the absence of a clear commitment to reduce, measure and offset these organizations’ carbon footprint revolve around five main neutralization techniques: navigating resources and strategic constraints, claiming to engage in exemplary organizational practices, debunking carbon neutrality principles, tackling measurement challenges and ambiguities, and scapegoating large emitters. This study contributes to the literature on corporate carbon neutrality commitments, on impression management strategies and neutralization techniques, and on sustainability performance measurement and organizational accountability on climate issues. • Agri-food leaders are skeptical of the credibility of carbon neutrality targets. • Agri-food leaders are open to the principle of carbon neutrality. • Agri-food leaders criticize the integration of the principle of carbon neutrality. • Neutralization techniques are used to legitimize the absence of climate targets.

title: Changing global vegetation-climate interactions constrain photosynthesis in the 21st century
abstract: Photosynthesis drives life on the Earth and it is essential to examine the response of terrestrial ecosystems to climate change. This study investigates the changing vegetation-climate interactions and the response of global photosynthesis to it in the current (2000–2021) and future climate scenarios (until 2100). The study finds temperature (T, 31 %) as the dominant driver of global photosynthesis, followed by soil moisture (SM, 26 %), precipitation (P, 23.4 %) and downward shortwave radiation flux (DSRF, 19.5 %) as suggested by Random Forest (RF). Across biomes and land covers, T controls photosynthesis in forests (36.4 %), croplands (35 %), and temperate (36.1 %) and cold (29.7 %) biomes, but P in grasses (35.5 %), and tropical (26.8 %) and arid (27 %) biomes. Photosynthesis has causal feedbacks with SM (croplands), P (forests, tropical and temperate), and T (temperate and cold); reveals Granger Causality that goes beyond correlations as it indicates directional effects. Water availability (SM, 5 %; P, 2.4 %) has strengthened its control on the global photosynthesis, and weakened the influence of T (−4.4 %) in recent decade (2010–2019) from its previous (2000–2009). The enhanced Solar-Induced Fluorescence (SIF, 4.2 %), Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI, 2.8 %) and Fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FPAR, 0.8 %) confirm the “Greening Earth”, as also attested by the positive cumulative growth rate (FPAR, 1.2 % CGR). Greening is intensified in croplands (1.7 % CGR), arid (1.6 % CGR) and temperate (1.4 % CGR) biomes, and forests (0.4 % CGR); conversely, slowdown/reversed in grasses (−4.1 % CGR), and tropical (−1.8 % CGR) and cold (−0.2 % CGR) biomes. Greening is projected to continue until the end of the century (2090–2100), predominantly in the cold (45.9 %) and arid (31.6 %) biomes. Future greening can expedite the hydrological cycle and strengthen land-atmosphere coupling. This calls for effective utilisation of land resources, judicial management of green cover and climate adaptation policies to attain sustainability in a warmer and drier world with an unprecedented human population rise.

title: Response of organic matter decomposition and nitrogen transformation in surface sediment to Hyriopsis cumingii bioturbation
abstract: Aquaculture sediments, the gathering place of residual organic waste, potentially represent an endogenous water pollution threat. To address these issues, Hyriopsis cumingii, a benthic filter-feeding shellfish was chosen to study its bioturbation on sediment organic matters (OM) decomposition and nitrogen transformation. The results demonstrated that H. cumingii enhanced the sediment metabolic capacity as the emissions of CO2 increased significantly in 90-day incubation. The total nitrogen (TN) in the H. cumingii treatment decreased significantly at the 60th and 90th days. The sediment metabolites including lipids, organic acids and nucleosides in the H. cumingii treatment were higher though no significant differences of the total organic carbon (TOC) between treatment and control were found at the 90th days. The enzyme activities of α-glucosidase, acid protease, and peroxidase increased gradually along with the incubation, and significantly higher levels were observed in the H. cumingii treatment. The abundance of genes involved in OM decomposition (e.g. hisC, ilvE, serC, glk, pfkA, pyk, gltA, IDH1/2, pflD, FDH and acyP) and nitrogen transformation (e.g. ureC, narG, nirS, norB, nosZ, napA, nasA, amoA, hao and nxrB), as well as the microbial community's diversity and interactions were significantly higher in H. cumingii treatment. Proteobacteria especially Rhodocyclaceae, Flavobacteriaceae of Bacteroidota and Verrucomicrobiota were the primary mediators in OM decomposition and nitrogen transformation. A species affiliated to Lacibacter genus, was the keystone in H. cumingii treatment, carried multiple OM decomposition and nitrogen transformation genes. The functional genes and microbes were positively correlated with ORP, enzymatic activities and metabolites of organic acids and organic oxygen compounds. PLS-PM analysis showed that H. cumingii bioturbation had significant direct and indirect positive effects on promoting OM decomposition and nitrogen transformation. This study provides evidence that H. cumingii bioturbation were ecological benefits by preventing the accumulation of OM and promoting nitrogen cycling in aquaculture sediment.

title: Cascading effects of microplastic-pollutant co-exposure in coastal wetland soil-plant-microbe systems: Mitigation potential through nutrient management
abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly threatened by microplastics (MPs) and co-occurring contaminants, however, their combined ecological impacts remain poorly understood. In this study, we examined the interactions between a representative microplastome (MPE) and two widespread pollutants—tris(2-chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP) and oxytetracycline (OTC)—in wetland soil–plant systems. Our findings revealed that co-exposure to MPE and TCPP significantly enhanced plant biomass, soil organic matter (SOM), and microbial diversity, while also stabilizing microbial co-occurrence networks. In contrast, exposure to OTC alone or in combination with MPE increased soil salinity, lowered pH, and reduced SOM, resulting in microbial community disruption and the lowest observed levels of ecosystem multifunctionality. Random forest analysis and structural equation modeling identified total carbon (TC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), SOM, and soil catalase activity (S-CAT) as key drivers of multifunctionality, with soil fertility exerting the strongest direct and indirect influences through plant–microbe feedback mechanisms. Moreover, greater plant diversity was associated with increased microbial network complexity and functionality. Collectively, these results underscore the cascading effects of co-contamination and suggest that enhancing soil nutrient management may help mitigate wetland ecosystem degradation.

title: Soil cadmium contamination facilitates the invasion of invasive weeds through enhanced herbivore resistance and competitive ability over congeneric species
abstract: Certain invasive plant species, such as Alternanthera philoxeroides and Wedelia trilobata, have been reported to accumulate trace metals in their tissues (the elemental defense hypothesis). We hypothesized that such metal pollution enhances herbivory resistance in these metal-accumulating invasive plants, giving them a competitive advantage over native species by serving as a defence mechanism against herbivory. To test this, we compared the growth and herbivore feeding preferences of the invasive species (A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata) and their native congeners (A. sessilis and W. chinensis) under both monoculture and mixed culture conditions, with and without cadmium (Cd) contamination in the soil. We found that the invasive plant species A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata had higher superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and peroxidase activities than their native counterparts, while native plant species A. sessilis and W. chinensis had significantly higher levels of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), malondialdehyde (MDA), and hydroxyl ions (O2 •–) in their leaves and roots, respectively, following Cd toxicity. Invasive A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata plants were also shown to be more resistant to Cd stress and to accumulate more Cd in their roots, stems, and leaves than A. sessilis and W. chinensis. In comparison to native A. sessilis and W. chinensis, invading plant species A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata become more resistant to Spodoptera litura herbivory after being exposed to Cd. Competition studies showed that, with or without herbivore pressures, Cd stress significantly boosted A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata competitive advantage over A. sessilis and W. chinesis. Cadmium contamination reduced soil enzyme activities, with invasive species and mixed cultures showing greater resilience than natives, highlighting their potential for phytoremediation. Our results thus demonstrate that both A. philoxeroides and W. trilobata are able to employ Cd-triggered defenses to support colonization, even under S. litura infestation, in Cd-contaminated soil.

title: Photo-responsive imprinted cellulose nanocrystalline aerogels for selective terbium recovery and controlled desorption
abstract: Conventional adsorbents have the bottleneck of struggling to balance adsorption and desorption efficiencies, adsorbents with high selectivity tend to require high energy consumption for desorption and are prone to secondary pollution. The development of sustainable adsorbents with high selective adsorption performance and eco-friendly regeneration is essential. In this work, cellulose nanocrystalline imprinted aerogels (SP-IA) with smart-responsive properties were synthesized by using aminated cellulose nanocrystals as the substrate, incorporating methoxy-spiropyran as the photo-responsive monomer, and applying ion-imprinting and freeze-drying techniques. The ligand structures formed by incorporating diglycolic anhydride synergistically interacted with methoxy-spiropyran, improving the capture efficiency of SP-IA for terbium ions. Under the condition of pH 5.0, SP-IA had the optimum adsorption capacity of up to 74.10 mg g−1. SP-IA showed excellent specific recognition of terbium ions in the complex rare earth solution with separation constant as high as 2382 mL g−1. The green desorption of SP-IA can be realized by switching the illumination condition from UV to visible light. The desorption rate of SP-IA was over 87 %, and the decrease in adsorption capacity after five cycles was significantly smaller than that of other aerogels, maintaining approximately 86 % of initial value. The selective capture and harmless release of terbium ions from SP-IA could be realized by switching between UV and visible light, respectively. The responsive aerogel broadens the potential application of responsive adsorbents for recovery of rare earth elements from e-waste leachate.

title: Heavy metal removal efficiency in tailings through washing: Prediction and optimization
abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) released from mine tailings pose persistent threats to ecosystems and human health, making effective tailings management essential for achieving cleaner production in the mining industry. Tailings washing is an effective method to mitigate the risks of HM pollution associated with tailings; however, experimental evaluation of removal efficiency is often complex, time-consuming, and may cause secondary pollution. This study established a machine learning framework to rapidly and accurately predict HM removal efficiency through tailings washing. The optimized categorical boosting (CatBoost) model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.799 on the testing dataset. The validated CatBoost model could identity the optimal washing scheme from a grid space of 98,560 combinations, guiding real-world tailings washing strategies. Model interpretation indicated that washing conditions played a dominant role in determining removal efficiency, with a cumulative importance of 40.128 %. A threshold effect was observed at pH = 5.9, below which more acidic conditions enhanced HM removal. Structural equation modeling further clarified the direct and indirect causal pathways influencing removal efficiency. Moreover, a user-friendly web interface was developed to make model prediction and optimization readily available online. Overall, this study proposed a robust and interpretable decision-support tool that provides scientific guidance for tailings management and HM pollution control, contributing to resource sustainability and the protection of human health.

title: Toward supply-side decarbonization: Integrating low-carbon trade, resilience, and cross-border synergies in Singapore's energy transition case study
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality necessitates a paradigm shift in energy system design, emphasizing sustainable import–export mechanisms, diversified energy portfolios, and reduced dependency on fossil-based natural gas. This research proposes a self-sustaining, and adaptive import-export optimization framework tailored to Singapore's 2035 energy transition objectives as a case study. The framework integrates a probabilistic AI-driven forecasting model to capture the stochastic mix-energy generation and demand patterns, and temporal price volatility across multiple uncertain trade and operational scenarios, enabling resilient and economically efficient planning. A decentralized transmission–distribution network is developed to evaluate the operational impacts of diverse energy-mix configurations, particularly renewable and hydrogen imports, on system reliability, supply-side management, emissions, and profitability. An integrated techno-economic–environmental assessment module quantifies trade-offs between cost, emission intensity, and energy security, providing actionable insights for policy formulation and infrastructure investment. The forecasting demonstrates strong performance, with climate change uncertainty incorporated across more than 50 % of transformer model variables. The optimal import-export trading platform achieves the lowest emission intensity at 3211.97 kgCO2/km, reduces occupational risk with transportation, and significantly lowers dependence on fossil fuels. The evaluation confirms substantial strategic value in large-scale hydrogen integration, contributing 110.94 × 106 SGD by converting fossil-derived pathways into sustainable energy carriers along with renewables. This enhanced peak load management flexibility and improved system-wide sustainability metrics. This foundational pathway positions Singapore as a regional nexus for renewable and hydrogen-based energy exchange, enabling a resilient, low-carbon, and economically robust energy future.

title: Simplifying thermal pretreatment of lithium iron phosphate cells: Benefits of whole-cell processing without inert atmospheres
abstract: The rapid growth of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries challenges recycling due to their lower material value, making capital and operational cost reduction essential. Current flowsheets rely heavily on thermal treatment under inert atmospheres, which drives cost through complex sealed reactor design requirements, inert gas consumption, and high energy input. This study demonstrates a simplified alternative: thermally treating whole LFP cells in an open rotary kiln. The cell casing acted as a passive barrier, providing an inert micro-environment that limits oxidation. Furthermore, the in-situ volatilization and combustion of electrolyte and separator provided a source of heating for the process. Under best conditions (650 °C, 15 min), 78 % LFP and 69 % graphite were recovered into black mass (<0.3 mm), with limited Cu (3 %) and Al (<1 %) reporting to fines, achieving a black mass of comparable composition to the one obtained through inert atmosphere methods (68.6 % LFP, 30.6 % C, 0.2 % Al, 0.6 % Cu). XRD confirmed preservation of LiFePO 4 , whereas uncased comparative runs oxidized to Li 3 Fe 2 (PO 4 ) 3 . The resulting black mass was compatible with flotation, yielding 96 % LFP grade in underflow and 73 % graphite grade in overflow. This work provides evidence that thermal treatment of whole cells in air can achieve comparable performance to inert atmosphere flowsheets with significantly lower process complexity, supporting the development of more scalable and economically viable industrial LFP recycling systems. • Whole-cell feedstock provides heating and isolation enabling usage of reactors as rotary kilns operated under open atmosphere conditions. • Thermal runaway reactions provide sufficient heat to remove PVDF preparing materials for mechanical separation and flotation. • Casings prevent material oxidation, preserving LFP phase and low Cu and Al content in black mass. • Flotation of the black mass achieved >85 % LFP recovery at >96 % grade and ∼90 % graphite recovery at 74 % grade.

title: Kinetic mechanism of CO2-coal/rock dissolution and mineralization under temperature and pressure constraints in mined-out area: Implications for pore network reconstruction and carbon storage safety
abstract: CO2 geological sequestration constitutes a critical negative emission technology reserve for addressing carbon emissions in coal industries. Decommissioned subsurface voids, with their substantial storage capacity and controllable engineering conditions, emerge as ideal geological reservoirs for carbon storage that combine scalability and safety advantages. This investigation employed a self-developed hydrogeochemical reaction simulation apparatus to systematically conduct CO2-water-coal/rock interaction experiments under controlled thermobaric conditions (25 °C, 45 °C; 0.5–2.5 MPa). The study quantitatively analyzed elemental release-migration patterns and aqueous phase ion concentration evolution pre- and post-reaction, investigated mineralogical phase transitions and pore architecture modifications in mined-out area environments, and elucidated the coupled mechanisms of mineral dissolution-carbonization, elemental migration, and secondary mineral precipitation. Key findings reveal: (1) Hyperbaric conditions significantly enhance CO2 dissolution and acidification-driven mineral dissolution, while elevated temperature initially inhibits CO2 solubility but subsequently promotes carbonate precipitation through Ca2+/Mg2+ liberation, demonstrating thermobaric co-regulation of dissolution-precipitation equilibria; (2) Low-activation-energy carbonate minerals (calcite: 12.4 kJ/mol, dolomite: 36.16 kJ/mol) dominate short-term dissolution processes, whereas silicate phases (e.g., kaolinite) govern long-term reservoir stability through dissolution-reprecipitation transformations; (3) CO2-fluid-rock interactions induce distinct pore structure evolution-coal matrices exhibit macropore volume expansion (+5.98 % maximum) due to initial microporous dominance (39.42 %), while rock strata demonstrate staged porosity differentiation from carbonate dissolution-secondary precipitation; (4) Mined-out area storage optimization requires dual consideration of reservoir-caprock characteristics: reservoir design should balance short-term dissolution-enhanced porosity with long-term mineralization stabilization, while caprock selection favors silicate-rich formations achieving pore sealing through hydration-induced swelling. This research establishes fundamental theoretical and experimental frameworks for safe and efficient CO2 sequestration in abandoned mine voids by revealing the dissolution-mineralization dynamics governing reservoir integrity.

title: Sustainable self-healing asphalt mixture with microcapsules: self-healing behavior and indicators analysis
abstract: The intrinsic self-healing capacity of asphalt pavement is insufficient to effectively heal the cracks. This study investigated the effect of microcapsules on the self-healing performance of asphalt mixtures. A computer tomography (CT) scan was used to analyze the distribution of microcapsules in asphalt mixture with different mixing methods. Additionally, the impact of microcapsules on mechanical properties of asphalt mixture was assessed. The semi-circular bending (SCB) damage-healing test and overlay tester (OT) fatigue-healing test were conducted to evaluate the self-healing capacity, and a two-way ANOVA was performed to determine the significance of various healing indicators. Eventually, the Life-cycle analysis was adopted. Results revealed that dry mixing method achieved a more uniform distribution of microcapsules. Addition of microcapsules below 0.8 % was found to be acceptable for mechanical properties. The self-healing of asphalt mixture was increased significantly with microcapsules dosage, ranging between 40 % and 80 % (1 % ∼ 9 % provided by the microcapsules). The fracture energy-based indicator outperformed the strength-based indicator in the SCB test, while the load-cycle curve-based indicator showed promise in the OT test, though these preliminary findings require further validation under broader conditions. The presence of microcapsules caused slightly influence on the environment.

title: Assessing the impact of crop–livestock integration on food security: Evidence from the Huang–Huai–Hai region of China
abstract: Building a circular agricultural system that couples crop and livestock production can mitigate environmental problems caused by excessive fertilizer use and large-scale manure discharge while improving the resource recovery of agricultural wastes, thereby delivering both ecological and economic benefits. This study measures the level of crop–livestock integration (CLI) in the Huang–Huai–Hai region of China from 2010 to 2023 and empirically examines its impact on food security using two-way fixed effects models, mediation models, and instrumental variable approaches. The results demonstrate a stable and significant positive relationship between CLI and food security, mainly through three mechanisms: enhanced resource allocation, reduced environmental emissions, and improved agricultural income. Spatial heterogeneity analysis further shows that the enabling effect of CLI on food security is particularly strong in areas with relatively weak economic foundations but favorable agricultural production conditions. Based on these findings, this study proposes targeted policy recommendations to strengthen food security through the advancement of CLI.

title: Optimal planning of charging stations considering electric vehicles’ temporal-spatial charging scheduling
abstract: In recent years, the increasing demand for electric vehicle (EV) charging has put forward higher requirements for constructing electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs). The EVCS planning is a problem of high complexity of power grid and transportation system integration, which can simultaneously consider the reasonability of EVs’ charging scheduling and the interests of multiple stakeholders. This paper proposes an optimal capacity planning method for EVCSs, considering the demands of participants, including EV users, charging station operators, power distribution systems, and transportation networks. Moreover, the temporal and spatial charging scheduling characteristics of EVs are properly modeled in the proposed method, which accurately reflects the relationship between the EV charging behaviors and the operation state of the coupled power-transportation system. The established optimization model is transformed into a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem by the polyhedral approximation method based on “ε-relaxed” and the equivalent substitution method. Finally, the proposed planning method in this paper is validated through simulation in an urban area with a coupled power-transportation system. Compared to planning methods that only consider single-dimensional charging scheduling, the proposed method can balance the interests of multiple stakeholders and has significant economic benefits.

title: Evaluating cap-and-trade and green subsidies in promoting green investments for capital-constrained manufacturers with environmentally aware consumers
abstract: In alignment with the 2050 net-zero CO2 emissions goal outlined in the Paris Agreement, this study proposes a decision-making model to optimize green technology investments for reducing carbon emissions. To evaluate its practical implementation, we examine the role of government intervention through the provision of optimal subsidies for green technology investment. To address this issue, we developed a profit-maximizing, multi-period model that integrates strategic and tactical decisions of a capital-constrained manufacturing company operating under a cap-and-trade (C&T) system. The proposed framework effectively predicts and adapts to consumer behavior by balancing the trade-off between lost demand due to a high carbon footprint and the costs of green technology investment. However, in practice, green investment decisions – particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)- are often constrained by limited initial capital. As a result, integrating financial decision-making into the framework is crucial for enabling these firms to achieve long-term sustainability. A series of numerical examples evaluate the influence of consumer green awareness and environmental policy interventions on capital constrained firms' profitability and environmental performance. The findings show that firms are more likely to adopt sustainable practices when these actions align with their financial interests. This underscores the critical role of both governmental and corporate efforts in raising consumer awareness about sustainability. Our results also reveal under which environmental policies sustainability can be profitable.

title: Organosilicon mitigates cadmium toxicity and accumulation in rice (Oryza sativa L.): Tripartite synergistic mechanisms of apoplastic barrier reinforcement, vacuolar compartmentalization, and antioxidant defense activation
abstract: Organosilicon exhibits exceptional potential for reducing cadmium (Cd) uptake and accumulation in crops, owing to its molecular structure-endowed high membrane permeability and biocompatibility. However, the current understanding of the mechanisms by which organosilicon mitigates Cd toxicity in rice remains fragmented. We combined controlled hydroponic experiments and foliar organosilicon-sprayed field trials, integrating physiological, biochemical, transcriptomic, histochemical, and in vitro simulation analyses to clarify the underlying mechanisms. Results demonstrated that organosilicon reduces Cd uptake and accumulation and mitigates its toxicity through a synergistic triple mechanism: by reinforcing the root apoplastic barrier via enhanced lignification and suberization, by promoting vacuolar Cd compartmentalization in leaves, and by activating the plant defense system via potentiated glutathione-dependent antioxidant and glyoxalase pathways. Field trials revealed that foliar organosilicon application reduced Cd concentration in rice grains by 48.89 %–52.87 %, decreased Cd-associated health risks by 56.76 %–57.87 %, increased rice yield by 9.26 %–9.98 %, and enhanced grain nutritional quality. This study is the first to unveil the synergistic triple mechanism through which organosilicon mitigates rice Cd toxicity and accumulation. Given its low cost and high efficiency, this approach provides a practical and cost-effective strategy for using silicon-based materials in heavy metal-contaminated agricultural lands.

title: One-pot, synthesis-free tannin-furfuryl alcohol-phytic acid adhesive: A scalable bio-based alternative to formaldehyde resins with ultra-high flame retardancy, exceptional water resistance and life-cycle benefits
abstract: Sustainability and health concerns are driving the wood industry to seek green, bio-based adhesives. Herein, a synthesis-free and entirely bio-based adhesive, composed of tannin, furfuryl alcohol (FA) and phytic acid (PA), that delivers exceptional bonding strength and ultra-high flame retardancy is reported. PA moderates the acid-catalyzed polymerization of FA due to PA's sterically demanding and hydrogen-bonded architecture, preventing “violent polymerization” while simultaneously integrating into the network through co-reactions with tannin and its own self-polymerization. Three-layer and seven-layer fast-growing poplar plywood bonded with the TF-P adhesive achieved shear strengths of 1.54 MPa and 1.94 MPa, respectively, surpassing the China National Standard GB/T 9846–2015 requirement for exterior-grade plywood type I (≥0.7 MPa) and matching commercial phenolic resin (∼1.4 MPa). Additionally, the TF-P adhesive has demonstrated great potential for bamboo bonding, achieving a lap shear strength of 3.60 MPa in bamboo lap specimens after a boiling water treatment. The limiting oxygen index (58.6 %) and cone calorimetry (pHRR = 24.73 kW/m2, THR = 26.96 MJ/m2) indicate superior flame-retardant performance of TF-P adhesive, relying solely on the inherent properties of the raw materials. Additionally, life cycle assessment (LCA) analysis indicates that TF-P adhesive has a lower environmental impact compared to urea-formaldehyde, melamine-formaldehyde, and phenolic resin. Given its excellent water resistance, simple preparation, and sources from renewable raw materials, it holds significant potential to replace classical formaldehyde-based resin adhesives.

title: Bridging the industrial carbon divide: a techno-economic framework for carbon capture pathways in the cement sector of emerging economies
abstract: The cement industry is one of the largest stationary CO2 emitters, yet systematic assessments of capture pathways remain scarce in the developing economies. This study establishes a comprehensive techno-economic framework that integrates bias-corrected Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) with Levelized Cost of CO2 Capture (LCOC) modeling to evaluate thirteen post-combustion capture technologies in cement production systems. Using Nepal as a representative case, the framework benchmarks technologies based on energy use, cost, and technological readiness while quantifying break-even carbon-credit thresholds required for economic feasibility. Results indicate that advanced amines and Monoethanolamine (MEA)-based systems achieve full technical efficiency with competitive capture costs of $8 to $20 per ton of CO2, while pressure swing adsorption (PSA) offers a low-cost, scalable alternative. Calcium looping demonstrates strong retrofit potential but requires thermal integration to offset its energy penalty. A phased carbon capture roadmap (2026–2036) is proposed, aligning carbon pricing incentives ($25 to $35 per ton of CO2) with pilot-scale deployment of the most promising capture options and outlining planning-level options for subsequent CO2 utilization and storage, including mineral carbonation, concrete curing, and synthetic material production. The results provide actionable guidance for designing carbon capture strategies under capital and policy constraints. Furthermore, the framework offers a transferable tool for informing broader CCUS planning and circular carbon management in the Global South.

title: The positive effects of refluxing thermophilic compost materials on composting at low temperatures: insight into the large-scale composting experiments
abstract: The inhibition of microbial activity under low temperature conditions poses a major challenge for composting start-up in cold regions. Field-scale rapid start-up technologies for low temperature composting remain limited. This study employed a combined strategy involving the reflux of 20 % thermophilic compost materials (>50 °C) and microbial inoculation. This method achieved multiple positive effects: (1) increased initial pile temperature by 10 °C, reducing the temperature limitations for microbial activity; (2) enhanced nutrient salt contents and humic precursor substances, with SO42− and PO43− levels increasing by 48.23–66.15 % and humus-like components rising by 25.23 %, providing both essential nutrients and humic precursors to create a dual favorable environment that promotes microbial growth and humification; (3) stimulated the proliferation of beneficial microorganisms, such as Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, Actinobacteriota, and Proteobacteria, which are efficient organic matter degraders. As a result, the onset of the thermophilic period was advanced by 16 days, accelerating composting start-up and improving efficiency. Furthermore, this strategy reduced greenhouse gas emissions, with CH4 and N2O emissions decreasing by 32.54 % and 62.3 %, respectively. This study reveals the mechanisms of refluxing thermophilic compost materials through physical (heat transfer), chemical (nutrient enrichment), and biological (microbial community enhancement) dimensions. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for optimizing composting in low temperature conditions and offer a low-carbon pathway for agricultural waste treatment.

title: Spatial-temporal evolution and driving factors of urban resilience based on SCE framework and PCA-RF algorithm——A case study of Beijing
abstract: To reveal the temporal and spatial evolution law and driving factors of Beijing's urban resilience, an urban resilience evaluation framework was constructed from the perspective of service-connectivity-environment. The urban resilience indexes of Beijing in 2010, 2015, and 2020 were obtained by principal component analysis-random forest algorithm. Their temporal and spatial evolution was explored by using the kernel density estimation method. The geographic detector analyzes the importance and interaction of Beijing's urban resilience's driving factors. Conclusion: (1) The combined principal component analysis-random forest assessment model has a solid ability to deal with large data sets and has high fitting accuracy. (2) Regarding time evolution, Beijing's urban resilience exhibits a fluctuating upward trajectory with time, with growing disparities in regional resilience becoming evident. (3) Regarding spatial evolution, the spatial expansion of service resilience in Beijing is the most obvious, and the resilience index shows an upward trend. The spatial expansion of connected resilience is relatively gentle, and the resilience index first increases and then decreases. Environmental resilience is the highest, showing a steady upward trend. (4) Regarding driving factors, slope, and NDVI are the most potent driving forces for Beijing's urban flexibility, and the interaction between slope and tertiary industry is the strongest. The proportion of water bodies and PM2.5 concentration have strengthened the driving force of resilience, while the traffic network density has weakened the driving force of resilience. This study provides a scientific basis for further improving Beijing's urban resilience layout.

title: Degradation of organic refractory contaminants by phosphate buffer activated peroxymonosulfate: The overlooked roles of oxygen reactive species
abstract: Phosphate was generally applied as a buffer and its effect as a common water constituent has been extensively investigated in peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-contained advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), although its role remains controversial. In this study, it was surprisingly found that phosphate buffer solution (PBS) was readily to activate PMS at initial pH (pH0) of 7.0 and 8.0 with different activation pathways, and satisfactory removal efficiencies (≥95 %) were achieved for all nine target organic refractory compounds (ORCs) especially at pH0 8.0, thus the catalytic contribution of PBS might be underestimated. Typical quenching methods, electron spin resonance (ESR) spectrum and density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated that HPO42− and H2PO4− could effectively break the O-O bond of PMS, leading to the formation of different active radicals (i.e., sulfate radical, singlet oxygen, etc.) in the PBS/PMS system. The probable degradation pathway was elucidated. The toxicity of the intermediates was predicted and the biotoxicity of the treated solution was monitored. In addition, the PBS/PMS system could be well reused and maintained strong resistance and tolerance to most common inorganic ions (Cl−, NO3−, PO43− and SO42−) and natural organic matter (NOM). Overall, this work provides a promising metal-free PMS technique, highlights the overlooked roles of oxygen reactive species, and thereby deepens our understanding of PBS/PMS process in water purification.

title: Mechanisms of AMF-mediated correlation between nutrient uptake and soil micropatterns in sugar beet plants under rotational and continuous cropping soil environments
abstract: Continuous cropping limits the sustainability of sugar beet cultivation, and as an important soil-plant symbiotic microorganism, the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can significantly mitigate crop growth stress. This study utilises sugar beet as the subject of investigation, employing physiological and biochemical indices alongside amplicon sequencing technology to analyse the regulatory mechanisms of AMF inoculation on the growth, soil physicochemical properties, and rhizosphere microbial communities of sugar beet in continuous cropping. The findings indicate that AMF enhanced plant nutrient uptake through the mycelial network and significantly increased biomass. Inoculation of AMF improves soil structure; pH is increased by 0.3–0.5; the mycelial network further activates phosphorus, promotes nitrogen transport, and improves soil nutrient use efficiency. AMF also enhances soil extracellular enzyme activity, with phosphatase activity elevated by 35.2 %–42.7 % across all treatment groups. Amplicon sequencing data indicate that AMF treatment enhances the diversity of rhizosphere microorganisms, diminishes the prevalence of harmful bacteria, elevates the fraction of beneficial bacteria such as Proteobacteria and Actinobacteria, and stabilizes the microbial ecological network. PLS-PM analysis shows that AMF improves the adaptability of sugar beet to the soil environment and promotes nitrogen partitioning capability by elevating soil enzyme activity and nutrient efficiency. The experiment proves that AMF can effectively mitigate the continuous cropping disorder in sugar beet, which provides a theoretical basis for the utilisation of AMF in sugar beet farming. Subsequent research should investigate the impacts of various bacterial strains and their interactions with the soil, refine application methods, and advance the environmentally sustainable farming of sugar beet.

title: Sustainable MXene-mediated in-situ ZnO/cellulose composites via green fabrication with enhanced mechanical durability, antimicrobial activity, and EMI shielding performance
abstract: The development of multifunctional composite films integrating robust mechanical strength, potent antibacterial activity, and efficient electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding is critical for advancing next-generation smart materials. Herein, the rational engineering of CEL@ZnO/MXene composite films was achieved by the in-situ growth of ZnO nanoparticles on cellulose substrates and by synergistically harnessing the unique physicochemical attributes of ZnO and two-dimensional MXene nanosheets. This interfacially engineered and network-reinforced structure endowed the CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film with superior mechanical properties, including a tensile strength of 32.5 MPa, a Young's modulus of 2.35 GPa, and an elongation at break of 1.87% achieving a balanced integration of strength, stiffness, and flexibility. In addition, the CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film exhibited potent bioactive functionality by achieving antibacterial efficiencies of 86.2% against Escherichia coli, 89.4% against Staphylococcus aureus, and antioxidant activity exceeding 80%, which in turn mitigates bacterial proliferation and oxidative stress. Furthermore, the obtained CEL@ZnO/MXene 5:5 composite film exhibits an EMI shielding property of 38.67 dB across the X-band (8.2–12.4 GHz) with reflection coefficients consistently above 0.8, indicating stable properties dominated by surface reflection complemented by controlled absorption. This study highlights the extensive application potential of the composite films in antibacterial protection, environmental safety, and electronic equipment shielding due to combined advantages in mechanical robustness, effective antibacterial activity, and electromagnetic interference shielding.

title: Designing resilient remanufacturing strategies: A probabilistic framework for uncertainty-aware decision making
abstract: Remanufacturing is a vital strategy for advancing sustainability and resource efficiency across diverse industries. However, developing effective remanufacturing plans remains challenging due to inherent uncertainties, such as varying conditions of returned products and fluctuating market demands. Previous studies have a limitation in reflecting these uncertainties, as they rely on deterministic inputs in optimization models. This study proposes a new framework—referred to as Probabilistic Green Profit Design (PrGPD) model—that explicitly incorporates uncertainties into remanufacturing optimization. The model assigns probability density functions to key parameters based on expert knowledge and empirical data, enabling stochastic analysis through synthetic data generation. Furthermore, the framework identifies critical factors affecting remanufacturing outcomes by analyzing constraint activities under varying conditions. The proposed approach was validated through a case study involving a recreational boat engine. The results showed that improvements in the quality of disassembled parts directly enhance both profitability and carbon reduction, justifying the targeted investments in Design for Remanufacturing (DfR), early-return programs, and quality inspection systems. Additionally, the analysis revealed that profit margins remain stable across different market conditions, indicating that green profit opportunities are robust even under demand fluctuations. Overall, this research develops a practical and adaptable decision-support tool for remanufacturing businesses, providing more resilient strategies than traditional deterministic approaches.

title: Does ecological product protection compensation have a green effect? Empirical evidence based on the value accounting of ecological products in key ecological functional areas of the Yellow River Basin
abstract: The construction of ecological civilization is a core national strategy for sustainable development in China, and realizing ecological product value is a critical foundation. Using 2010–2023 panel data for the Yellow River Basin and 30m grid-level land-use data, this study measures ecological product value via an integrated framework combining market valuation and equivalence factor methods, and constructs a multidimensional ecological compensation model to assess regional compensation capacity across ecological, economic, and social dimensions. A two-stage system generalized method of moments (SYS-GMM) model is then employed to examine how compensation capacity affects ecological product value realization. Results show that stronger compensation capacity significantly promotes value realization and remains robust across multiple tests; the effects are heterogeneous across hydrological zones, development stages, and urban–rural integration levels. Mechanism analysis identifies new-quality productivity as the main transmission channel, while the digital economy and green finance strengthen the compensation effect; additional evidence from super-efficiency epsilon-based measure (Super-EBM) estimations and multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) analyses indicates improved spatiotemporal efficiency and positive impacts of pilot policies. These findings provide empirical support for optimizing ecological product compensation frameworks and advancing sustainable value transformation in ecologically sensitive regions.

title: Electromagnetic one-pot fabrication of flexible monolithic catalysts with boosted oxygen vacancies for enhanced VOCs oxidation
abstract: Practical purification devices for the complete degradation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in industrial exhaust gases typically employ monolithic catalysts due to their advantages in reducing gas resistance and enhancing efficiency. Fe cotton serves as a potential support material for such catalysts owing to its excellent thermal conductivity and the inherent flexibility of its velvet structure. Its superior thermal conductivity ensures uniform heat distribution during catalytic reactions. At the same time, the unique velvet architecture facilitates the homogeneous loading of active components on the surface and significantly reduces the risk of active component detachment. To fully leverage these advantages, this study introduces an electromagnetic induction dry quenching (EMIQ) technique that in-situ loads non-noble metal active sites onto Fe cotton via Joule heating induced by a high-frequency magnetic field. This universal method compresses the catalyst synthesis cycle from days to minutes and precisely controls the dispersion state and loading of active species (e.g., Co 3 O 4 nanoparticles) by tuning the precursor concentration (e.g., 0.05–0.20 mol/L Co solution) and quenching cycles (1–4 times). The optimized 0.10-Co/Fe-2 catalyst achieves a 50 % toluene conversion at 300 °C under traditional resistance heating, with excellent stability. Characterization results reveal that the rapid heating process induced by electromagnetic induction dry quenching (EMIQ) promotes the formation of defect structures (e.g., oxygen vacancies) on the material surface and strengthens the electronic metal-support interaction (EMSI) between Co and Fe, significantly enhancing the redox activity and oxygen adsorption capacity of the catalyst. This work provides a new strategy for the scalable preparation of high-performance VOCs degradation catalysts.

title: Dynamic modeling of consumer behavior in sustainable food markets
abstract: Organic food markets face a persistent problem of delivering reliable availability and acceptable profitability while meeting strict limits on waste and greenhouse emissions. This research develops a continuous time behavior to operations framework that links consumer choice, shaped by health concerns, label credibility, price salience, and product visibility, to service level inventory control for perishable goods while jointly determining pricing, replenishment, and marketing policies. The methodology employs risk aware optimization to guard against adverse demand and supply conditions, establishes rigorous performance guarantees, and assesses policy effectiveness through simulations calibrated to settings representative of California and India. The results indicate that maintaining target service levels and on-shelf availability strengthens reputation, reduces price sensitivity, speeds switching to organic products, and enables coordinated pricing, marketing, and replenishment to raise profit while meeting waste and emission limits; the profit-environment trade-off is well behaved, yielding practical rules for prices and steady stock levels. The framework abstracts from individual-level heterogeneity and uses stylized costs, so it requires local calibration and would benefit from multi-product extensions and field studies; in practice, it offers clear levers-service targets, focused marketing, and disciplined pricing-to grow organic adoption with safeguards. The contribution is a unified, easy-to-apply behavior-to-operations framework with mathematical guarantees that links consumer psychology to operational control under sustainability guardrails, providing actionable guidance for managers and policymakers.

title: Unraveling greenhouse gas accumulation and emission characteristics of partial and full nitrification-denitrification in anaerobic/aerobic/anoxic municipal wastewater treatment systems
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from biological nutrient removal in municipal wastewater treatment arise from multiple operational phases, yet the spatiotemporal patterns across gas-liquid phases remain poorly resolved. This study quantified gaseous and dissolved N2O, CH4 and CO2 in two parallel sequencing batch reactors (SBRs) inoculated with partial and full nitrification-denitrification (PND and FND) sludge, treating identical municipal wastewater under an anaerobic/aerobic/anoxic operation mode. Results showed that the anaerobic phase was dominated by CH4 release, with transient dissolved N2O (dN2O) generated after mixing being nearly completely reduced and both systems exhibiting strong N2O reduction capacity. The aerobic phase was characterized by CO2 release, while CH4 was mainly stripped at aeration onset. The average N2O emission rate in PND-SBR was 1.3 times that of FND-SBR. In the anoxic phase, N2O dominated GHG emissions, with PND-SBR releasing 3.5-fold more N2O than FND-SBR. dN2O in PND-SBR increased from 0.17 ± 0.07 mg-N/L to 0.23 ± 0.08 mg-N/L, whereas FND-SBR exhibited notable N2O reduction capacity, with effluent dN2O decreasing to 0.01 mg-N/L. Overall, the carbon-equivalent emissions of PND-SBR were 1.7 times those of FND-SBR. Metagenomic analysis revealed that Dechloromonas, enriched in FND-SBR, harbored nosZ genes typically associated with high N2O affinity, suggesting a potential role in enhanced N2O reduction. Moreover, higher abundance of CH4 oxidation genes in FND-SBR contributed to its slightly lower CH4 emissions. These findings advance understanding of phase-specific GHG dynamics in PND/FND systems under the AOA mode and provide actionable insights for targeted GHG monitoring and process optimization toward sustainable wastewater treatment.

title: Simultaneously reducing carbon emissions and endogenous pollutants release: a novel CaO2 composite-induced in-situ microbial community reconfiguration
abstract: In response to the mutual promotion of water eutrophication and greenhouse effect, a composite CaO2 (CCM) which slowly releases O2 and induces CH4 oxidation was developed in this study. Unlike exogenous microbial addition, CCM reshaped the native microbial community, enriching indigenous methane oxidizers for a more stable and cost-effective solution. The results indicated the domain-limiting effect of CCM ensured a long-lasting O2 release, prolonging the release duration by 2.6-fold versus powdered CaO2. Optimal effect was achieved at the CCM dosage of 150 g m−2, which reduced the NH4+-N, PO43−-P, and COD in the overlying water by 88.74 %, 89.01 %, and 81.45 %, and decreased the global warming potential by 83.99 %. The oxidation property and dissolution products of CCM inhibited methanogenic archaea proliferation, while increased methanotrophic bacteria abundance, CH4 monooxygenase activity, Proteobacterial pmoA in surface sediments and M. nitroreducens mcrA in middle sediments. By reducing greenhouse gas production and promoting CH4 oxidation, the CCM established a three-dimensional metabolic network of “surface aerobic oxidation, middle anaerobic oxidation, and deep heterotrophic metabolism”, which could provide new ideas for carbon reduction and ecological restoration in slow-flow water.

title: Petrophysical responses to different CO2 injection methods in shale: Insights from flow and geological sequestration
abstract: CO2 injection into shale integrates resource exploration with carbon sequestration. Prior investigations have relied predominantly on crushed samples or CO2-brine mixtures to study long-term geochemical interactions during soaking. Consequently, the essential mechanisms governing the evolution of flow capacity and microstructure across different injection methods remain poorly understood under realistic formation conditions. This study employs nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and multiple characterization techniques to investigate the microscopic mechanisms of flow evolution and sequestration efficacy across different CO2 injection methods under actual formation conditions. Quantitative criteria are established to evaluate the contributions of distinct processes, and the influences of key factors and their interactions are systematically analyzed. Furthermore, a prediction model with multifactor coupling is constructed based on correlation analysis. The results show that CO2 soaking under thermodynamic equilibrium transitions from physical to chemical control as pressure increases. At low pressure, limited particle migration rises blockage risks in micropores in zones above 0.06 mD. Elevated pressure enhances elastic energy, improving flow capacity by 100–200 % in zones below 0.06 mD despite increased macropore blockage risks. Conversely, CO2 flooding remains physically controlled by pressure gradients. Low pressure causes sharp flow decline due to particle blockage in narrow pore-throats, while increased pressure promotes high-speed CO2 flow, reducing flow capacity by 7.79 %–50.48 % but increasing CO2 gas column height by 1.67 %–18.32 %. For engineering practice, CO2 flooding should be avoided in high-permeability, low-porosity formations under low pressure. Instead, during the middle-to-late stages, massive flooding in ankerite-rich zones is recommended to couple capillary and mineralization trapping.

title: Life cycle assessment of a food waste-based biorefinery: From production of biopolymers to fabrication of advanced nanofibre masks
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to a surge in mask consumption, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives.Despite pandemic restrictions easing, mask consumption remains significantly higher than pre-pandemic levelsdue to increased public awareness. In this regard, this study presents a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA)of an innovative biorefinery framework that converts food waste (FW) into biopolymers, specifically polylacticacid (PLA) and poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV), for the production of nanofibre facemasks. The analysis reveals that the environmental profile of FW-derived biopolymers is influenced by theallocation method. Under the primary mass allocation method, PLA and PHBV show GWPs of − 1.32 and 1.32 kg CO2 eq/kg, respectively. The results for PLA range from 0.18 to 2.29 kg CO2 eq/kg across economic and energyallocation, while PHBV ranges from − 0.62 to 0.24 kg CO2 eq/kg, underscoring the methodological sensitivity.When these polymers are electrospun into medical textiles, the resulting nanofibre masks show a reduction of23.8 % in global warming potential compared to conventional surgical masks, along with significant improvements in toxicity-related categories. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identifies key environmental hotspots andsuggests optimisation strategies. Uncertainty analysis confirms the robustness of the environmental benefitsdespite variations in parameters. Overall, this research demonstrates the potential of waste-based biorefinerysystems to mitigate the environmental impact of personal protective equipment.

title: An advanced fuzzy based multi-layered decision-making system for sustainable carbon emission reduction strategy selection in steel industry
abstract: The steel industry generates close to 8% of global carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, releasing about 1.85 tons of CO2 for every ton of steel produced. Tackling this challenge requires decision-support tools that can handle uncertainty and balance competing criteria. This work introduces a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) model that combines Interval-Valued Bipolar Fuzzy Soft Sets (IVBFSS), the Logarithmic Percentage Change-Driven Objective Weighting method (LOPCOW), and an enhanced COBRA ranking procedure.
