While many studies have evaluated their environmental benefits, most assessments assume that all bike trips equally contribute to carbon emission reduction, overlooking differences in trip purposes. In particular, leisure riding, which does not substitute motorized transport, can lead to overestimations of bike-sharing's carbon reduction. This limitation becomes even more critical under large-scale disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, which significantly reshaped urban mobility patterns. To address this gap, this study proposes a refined framework that distinguishes emission-reduction riding (ER-riding) from leisure riding and develops a hybrid method combining the threshold approach and nested logit model to more accurately estimate BSS carbon emission reduction. With the proposed methodology framework, we perform a comparative spatiotemporal analysis to investigate the impact of the COVID-19 on carbon emission reduction and its recovery before, during, and after the COVID-19 in New York, Washington, and Chicago. Results show that the pandemic significantly disrupted the carbon emission reduction of bike-sharing, with recovery patterns varying across cities. New York demonstrated the strongest resilience, with its emission reduction levels in 2021 surpassing those of the pre-pandemic period in 2019.This resilience may be attributed to the expansion of its BSS infrastructure, as well as a higher proportion of private transport replacement compared to public transport. These findings highlight that Washington and Chicago could enhance their bike-sharing carbon benefits by learning from New York's system. Overall, this study enhances the understanding of bike-sharing's environmental role in multimodal transport and highlights the need for resilient systems to sustain carbon emission reductions under external shocks.

title: Prospective life cycle assessment of the Spanish electricity mix (2023–2050): Interrelation between climate change, water footprint, and costs
abstract: In response to the climate emergency, the European Union (EU) launched the “Fit for 55” package in 2023, aiming to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by 55 % in 2030 and achieve climate neutrality in 2050, including targets like increasing the share of renewable energy to 42.5 %. This study evaluates the environmental and economic performance of Spain's primary electricity generation technologies in the context of the EU's 2030 climate objectives and the national energy strategy. Using life cycle assessment (LCA), it quantifies the global warming potential (GWP), water scarcity impacts, and costs associated with wind, hydropower, solar thermal, photovoltaic, coal, combined cycle and nuclear power. Results indicate that coal and combined cycle technologies present the highest GWP and costs. As it could be anticipated, hydropower exhibits the highest water footprint. Wind energy shows the most favourable balance across the three categories, followed by solar technologies. The prospective analysis of the 2030 and 2050 scenarios shows that the planned transition would progressively reduce the electricity mix's fossil GWP by over 50 % and its water footprint by approximately 25 % by 2050 compared to 2023 levels. These findings support Spain's current energy transition path, though they suggest reconsideration of the planned nuclear phase-out given its relative performance in the triangle of the three assessed categories. Further LCA studies focusing on water scarcity are recommended to broaden the existing literature and therefore strengthen decision-making.

title: A data-driven approach to mapping global commodity-specific mining land-use
abstract: Mineral extraction is a key driver of environmental change globally, yet geospatial data on mining operations remains fragmented and incomplete across data sources. Datasets with complementary information, such as mining project inventories (points) and satellite-derived land use (polygons), are often disconnected due to spatial mismatches and the complex distribution of infrastructures, such as open pits, tailings, and processing facilities, which are frequently scattered. Integrating these geographic features is critical for enhancing mining data availability and leveraging data complementarity, thereby advancing the understanding of mining impacts globally. This study proposes a scalable approach to link heterogeneous mining datasets and demonstrates its applicability by quantifying the global mine land associated with specific commodities. The new approach introduces data-driven mine clusters , grouping geographic features through hierarchical clustering with locally optimised distance thresholds. This method enables associating information from inventory data with land-use polygons covering mine infrastructure derived from satellite data. To test the approach, data from various sources were integrated. The resulting integrated dataset covers over 145,000 km 2 and offers the most comprehensive overview of global mine land use linked to mineral commodities. Validation of the clusters against expert-labelled mines shows a high level of agreement, with 95 % of the clusters sharing at least one primary commodity. Results revealed that coal (22.5 %) and gold (21.1 %) dominate global mining land footprints. 26.8 % of the area could not be assigned to a commodity. This methodology provides a reproducible approach to enhancing the integration of spatial data on mining activities, supporting more robust global assessments of mining impacts. • New approach to link satellite-derived mine land-use and mine operation data. • Unsupervised clustering reduces subjectivity and increases the linking accuracy. • Integrated data sources reveal a total of 145,738.1 km 2 of extractive land globally. • Coal and gold each account for over 21% of global mine land area. • 26.8% of mining land could not be linked to a specific commodity.

title: Higher tier estimation of ammonia emissions from synthetic nitrogen fertilizers in emission inventories: data collation, methodology and analysis
abstract: Synthetic fertilizers are a key source of ammonia (NH 3 ) emissions globally and national emission inventories are an essential element of international agreements aimed at reducing these emissions. Here an analysis of published measurements of NH 3 emission from synthetic fertilizer found that emissions were primarily determined by the experimental approach, the chemical composition of the fertilizer, environmental variables and the method of application. Measurements made using wind tunnels, semi-open chambers and the micrometeorological method produced similar results whereas those made with closed or ventilated chambers, Dräger tubes or 15 N were lower. Measurements made outdoors were lower than those made in the laboratory. The most important factors determining the NH 3 emissions were the method of application, the chemical composition of the fertilizer and, for fertilizers not based on solid forms of urea, the soil pH. National inventory compilers normally take account of these factors but are encouraged to use more detailed methodologies. Here we present a range of statistical models that would allow inventory compilers to also take into account application rate, air temperature, rainfall and soil clay content. However, to take advantage of these models would require the availability of additional, good quality input data. The conditional R 2 of the models developed accounted for 44–55 % of the variance in NH 3 emission measurements but the marginal R 2 only 19–27 %. We recommend further investigation into the source of the low marginal R 2 and, in particular, into the differences caused by the use of the different measurement methods.

title: Zero-valent metal enhanced BN/TiO2 photodegrades PFOA via regulating the Mott-Schottky Junction
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose significant risks to both ecosystems and human health, necessitating the development of effective remediation techniques for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in aquatic environments. We engineered Mott-Schottky heterojunctions by depositing Pt0 onto BN/TiO2, which promotes electron transfer from TiO2 to Pt, facilitates spatial separation of charge carriers, and substantially inhibits recombination processes. The incorporation of Pt modification extends the photoresponse range spectrum from 400 to 600 nm, narrows the bandgap from 3.0 to 2.8 eV, and markedly improves PFOA degradation under UVC (3 times higher degradation rate, 1.6 times higher defluorination rate) and UVA (1.6 times higher degradation rate, 2.8 times higher defluorination rate). Through comprehensive systematic material characterization and energy band analyses, the role of the Schottky junction was elucidated, thereby providing a strategic framework for rationalizing materials aimed at efficient aqueous PFOA remediation. This work not only advances the fundamental understanding of Mott-Schottky junctions in PFAS remediation but also provides valuable insights for the rational design of efficient photocatalysts toward PFAS degradation.

title: Biochar addition reduces soil greenhouse gas fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Biochar addition is gradually recognized as a nature-based solution for mitigating greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes from soils. However, its overall climatic benefits remain unclear due to the high heterogeneity and complexity of ecosystem types, biochar properties, and experimental conditions. We provide a comprehensive global meta-analysis that integrates 13,523 paired observations from 59 studies to evaluate the overall effect of biochar addition on soil carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems. Our results reveal that biochar addition notably promoted soil CO2 and CH4 fluxes by 2.2 % and 12.4 %, respectively, but reduced N2O fluxes by 17.9 %, culminating in a net reduction of 3.3 % in the combined 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) derived from soil greenhouse gas fluxes. The stable mitigation effect on N2O fluxes was mainly attributed to improved soil aeration, increased pH, adsorption of inorganic nitrogen, and the suppression of nitrification and denitrification processes. Interestingly, the positive effect of biochar addition on soil CO2 fluxes was primarily observed in the pot and incubation experiments, whereas a negative effect was noted in the field. This difference was mainly caused by the duration of the experiment. The former is usually short-term, during which CO2 fluxes are enhanced, but the latter has a relatively longer period, with the efflux effect gradually decreasing. Soil CH4 fluxes increased in forests in response to biochar addition, which contributed to the formation of an anaerobic environment and a supply of substrate for methanogens from the increase in soil moisture and organic carbon. Our results suggest that biochar with high-temperature pyrolysis, high carbon content, and fine particles exhibits greater mitigation capacity in warm and humid environments. This work emphasizes the notable potential of biochar in improving soil physicochemical properties and reducing GHG fluxes, offering a helpful reference for clean and sustainable production.

title: Biochar's impact on carbon sequestration and yield-scaled global warming potential in China: A machine learning-enhanced meta-analysis
abstract: Biochar has shown strong potential to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, yet most meta-analyses have examined isolated factors, overlooking the interactive effects of climate, soil, and management on agricultural productivity and environmental sustainability. This study integrated meta-analysis with machine learning (ML) to quantify biochar's effects on GHG emission, soil organic carbon (SOC), and yield-scaled global warming potential (GWP). A total of 1207 paired observations from 64 field studies conducted in China (2000–2024) were analysed. Biochar application significantly increased crop yield by 5 % and SOC by 34 %, while reducing NO emissions by 25 %, resulting in a 25 % decrease in yield-scaled GWP. Weakly alkaline biochar was most effective in reducing CO emissions in alkaline soils and CH emissions in acidic to neutral soils ( p < 0.05). Low C/N ratio biochar significantly decreased CO and CH emissions across soils with varying C/N ratios. Machine learning models identified biochar pH, application rate, soil pH, and soil C/N ratio as the primary determinants of these effects. CO emission responses were positively correlated with biochar application rate and negatively correlated with soil pH and C/N ratio ( p < 0.05), whereas CH emissions were positively regulated by soil pH, soil C/N ratio, and biochar pH. Pathway analysis indicated that biochar pH indirectly reduced CO emissions through enhanced SOC, while soil pH and C/N ratio directly influenced CH dynamics ( p < 0.05). Overall, this study demonstrates biochar's potential to enhance crop productivity while mitigating GHG emissions, providing a scientific basis for its application in carbon-neutral agroecosystems development.

title: Integrating system dynamics and machine learning to establish the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus of aquavoltaics
abstract: Traditional aquaculture faces growing challenges from climate change, including rising water temperatures, reduced water availability, and declining yields. This study explores aquavoltaic systems—integrating aquaculture with solar panels—as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution. We used clam farming at the Mariculture Research Center Taihsi Station in Yunlin County, Taiwan, as a case study. Within the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus framework, we applied system dynamics (SD) modeling enhanced by a hybrid machine learning approach. By combining the genetic algorithm (GA) and the backpropagation neural network (BPNN), we improved the accuracy and reliability of SD models, simulating real-world conditions using in-situ monitoring datasets to promote sustainability, resource use efficiency, and policy coherence in aquaculture. Results show that 40 % solar panel shading reduced water temperatures by 2.5 °C, improved water use efficiency by 30 %, and generated renewable energy to offset emissions. Although clam yields declined by 27 %, solar power compensated for production losses, creating an economically viable system. Further optimization identified 45 % shading as ideal, preserving 70 % of yields while maximizing energy output. This study offers valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders, showcasing aquavoltaics as a scalable framework for balancing food production, renewable energy generation, and climate adaptation—advancing sustainable aquaculture in Taiwan and beyond.

title: Nighttime lights-based downscaling for high-resolution electricity mapping: Insights into consumption, efficiency and footprint for sustainable energy management
abstract: Electricity consumption is a key indicator of urbanization and sustainability, yet its fine-scale spatiotemporal patterns remain insufficiently explored. Nighttime lights are a widely recognized remote sensing proxy for human activities. They offer great potential to downscale and map electricity consumption at high resolution. This study develops a grid-based downscaling model that integrates nighttime lights with socioeconomic data to generate annual 1 km resolution maps of electricity consumption in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA). The model demonstrates high accuracy and robustness across two decades. Results indicate that electricity consumption increased more than fivefold, evolving from a single-core to a multi-core pattern in GBA from 2000 to 2020. Linkages among Guangzhou, Foshan, Shenzhen, and Dongguan strengthened, with Foshan and Dongguan driving westward expansion. Efficiency improved overall, diffusing from the eastern to the western bank, while inter-city gaps narrowed. This pattern reflects spillover driven by industrial upgrading in eastern cities through industrial linkage extension, factor mobility, and regional collaborative innovation. The footprint expanded from the Guangzhou-Shenzhen core to Zhongshan and Huizhou, shaped by population and industrial migration. These findings reveal pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity in electricity consumption-efficiency-footprint, and highlight the uneven dynamics of energy demand across an urban agglomeration. By providing a comprehensive grid-level assessment of electricity consumption and its implications, this research advances the use of nighttime lights for urban energy mapping and offers transferable insights for sustainable electricity planning in other rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Effects of clean energy equipment manufacturing industry's growth on carbon emission in China: An analysis based on emission-offsetting effect
abstract: The rapid development of China's clean energy equipment manufacturing industry (CEEMI) exerts a dual impact on carbon emission: generating emission at the production while achieving emission abatement at the consumption through substitution of traditional energy sources. Based on provincial panel data from China spanning 2011 to 2023, this article specified a simplified STIRPAT (Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence and Technology) model. By isolating the elasticity coefficients of production and usage, this article quantitatively measured the net “offsetting effect” of clean energy equipment, incorporating mechanism variables such as Global Value Chain (GVC) participation, GVC position, and technological progress. The findings reveal: (1) An increase of one unit in output from China's CEEMI offsets 30.72 % of carbon emission. (2) The effectiveness of this “offsetting effect” depends on regional industrial development levels, product technology maturity, and the co-located cluster of production and consumption. Growth in the CEEMI significantly inhibits carbon emission in eastern regions, whereas western regions, despite their resource endowment advantages, exhibit no significant emission-offsetting effect. (3) Enhanced GVC participation and technological progress drive carbon emission reduction. (4) A decline in GVC position indicates that the industry currently faces a “low-end lock-in” dilemma, yet this does not significantly affect the “offsetting effect”, as domestic technological progress plays a more significant role. This study provides a policy foundation for giving full play to the promotion role of CEEMI in China's carbon emission reduction.

title: Role of energy consumption, gross capital formation, and urbanization in determining economic growth in Spain: Evidence from non-parametric methods
abstract: This study explores the relationship between urbanization, energy consumption, and gross capital formation, while accounting for the roles of foreign direct investment (FDI) on economic growth using annual time-frequency data from 1970 to 2024 in Spain. This study leverages time-frequency domain by capturing short- and long-time dynamics, such as the Wavelet Coherent analysis and Wavelet Granger Causality (WGC). The results show urbanization has a direct causal impact on foreign direct investment, which aligns with the urbanization-induced FDI growth. Similarly, economic growth also exhibits causation on capital formation, as proposed by GCF, reflecting Spain's reliance on energy use to sustain investment. The Wavelet Granger Causality approach revealed that another vital channel is the causality from energy consumption (EC) to gross capital formation (GCF), reflecting Spain's heavy reliance on energy use to sustain investment during periods of industrial expansion, particularly the construction boom of the 1990s and early 2000s, when energy-intensive sectors played a central role in driving capital accumulation. The results call for a shift from Spain's historical reliance on energy-intensive, construction-driven, and externally financed growth toward a model centered on renewable energy adoption, energy-efficient investment, sustainable urban transformation, and enhanced domestic investment capacity.

title: Speciation of N, P, K nutrient elements and heavy metals in sewage sludge char produced from a pilot-scale thermal carbonization device and its utilization in soil amendment
abstract: Municipal sewage sludge is featured by both pollution risks and resource attributes. However, existing collaborative disposal technologies suffer from several inevitable defects including heavy metal residues, pollutants control, and limited nutrients utilization. Nevertheless, thermal carbonization technology offers several advantages for resource recovery and utilization by converting sewage sludge into high value-added biochar. To clarify its potential of sewage sludge char (SSC) utilization in soil amendment, this work aimed to comparatively analyze the speciation of N, P, K nutrients and heavy metals in dried sewage sludge (DSS), and SSC produced from a pilot-scale thermal carbonization device. The results showed that the total nutrient element in SSC was increased to 10.02 % (as the form of N + P2O5+K2O), in comparison with DSS. Specifically, total N element in SSC accounted for 3.68 %, and its speciation shifted towards more stable pyridine/pyrrole-N. Total P element increased to 4.11 %, primarily existing as the form of biologically-available inorganic-P. Total K element was slightly decreased to 0.58 % but the relative proportion of available-K content was increased. Moreover, pilot-scale thermal carbonization process also showed a satisfactory fixation effect on heavy metal elements, and it promoted the transformation into oxidizable and residual form with a lower leaching risk level. Critically, with SSC improving soil structure and nutrient content (e.g., N, P, K, and organic matter), maize pot experiments further confirmed its promoting effect on plant growth, including accelerated germination, increased plant height and root/stem biomass. This pilot-scale thermal carbonization method provided a cleaner utilization paradigm for municipal sewage sludge valorization.

title: Long-term scenarios for climate adaptation of cotton crops in China, considering multidimensional biophysical and socio-economic scenario analysis
abstract: Climate change is fundamentally reshaping agricultural land suitability, with profound implications for water use, carbon emissions, and crop productivity. Understanding the long-term drivers of climate on the planting suitability of arable land and exploring multi-sectoral coordinated response solutions for the climate-agriculture-society system are essential for mitigating and adapting to climate change. This study develops a multidimensional framework to assess climate adaptation scenarios for cotton−one of the world's most important cash crops−in China from 1960 to 2100. Integrating species distribution modeling with socio-economic scenario analysis, we identify three key findings: (1) Historical cotton's highly suitable areas has shifted northward (+166 km) and to higher elevations (+47 m average) due to changing climate-soil-topography interactions; (2) While climatic suitability determines land potential, actual planting decisions are still mainly driven by economic returns, coordinating to local production management level; (3) Sustainable adaptation requires balancing biophysical suitability with production efficiency and circular economy practices. This study emphasizes not only the climate impact on agricultural land use changes but also reveals the synergistic mechanisms between climatic suitability, socio-economic, and production factors, that inform targeted land-use planning. Based on these findings, we recommend that future agricultural policies prioritize climate-smart land-use zoning, support adaptive infrastructure development in emerging suitable regions, and provide economic incentives to guide planting structure optimization under climate change scenarios. These insights play a crucial role in optimizing climate-smart farming structures, promoting agricultural adaptation and mitigation of climate change, and realize the sustainable and cleaner production under climate change.

title: Internet use and public acceptance of nuclear energy: Evidence from China
abstract: As nuclear power projects remain controversial in many countries worldwide, it is crucial to understand the determinants of public acceptance of nuclear energy. This study attempts to explore the relationship between Internet use and an individual's willingness to accept (WTA) compensation for the construction of nuclear power plants. Based on data from the Chinese General Social Survey, instrumental variable estimates reveal a significant and negative correlation between Internet use and WTA. Further analyses show that Internet use improves individuals' knowledge of nuclear energy and reduces their safety-related risk perception, thus leading to a lower WTA. Meanwhile, Internet use increases individuals' environmental-related risk perception, which is negatively correlated with WTA. These findings provide several implications for policymakers designing nuclear policy in the digital age.

title: Improving the multi-temporal dissolved oxygen estimation using statistically enhanced remote sensing proxies in data-scarce, optically complex inland water
abstract: Monitoring optically inactive water quality (WQ) parameters, such as dissolved oxygen (DO), through remote sensing presents a significant challenge due to their lack of spectral signatures. Traditional in-situ methods provide only point measurements with limited spatial coverage. This study introduces a novel remote sensing framework for spatially continuous, multi-temporal dissolved oxygen (DO) estimation in inland water bodies. The framework is demonstrated on the river Ganga in Varanasi, India. The approach leverages satellite-derived normalised Water Surface Temperature (n-WST) and Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) as key proxies. Symbolic Regression (SR) was selected for its modelling efficacy with limited datasets and ability to generate interpretable mathematical relationships. The SR model achieved Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 17.44 % on the test dataset of February 5, 2025, and MAPE of 18.12 % when applied to satellite data of November 26, 2025, demonstrating robust multi-temporal generalization. Trained on the dataset of November 26, 2025, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Regressor (SVR) exhibited MAPE (%) values of 21.26 and 26.43 respectively on the test dataset. Satellite based seasonal analysis revealed DO variability from 6.32 ppm during summer to 9.06 ppm in winter. The framework emphasized the importance of thermodynamic control through inverse DO-temperature relationships over positively correlated association between DO and chlorophyll-a while capturing spatial-temporal heterogeneity. By coupling interpretable machine learning with remote sensing proxies, the framework addresses data scarcity and lack of spectral signature of certain WQ parameters, offering a scalable and effective framework for monitoring WQ parameters using satellite data.

title: Interfacial engineering of amyloid nanocomposites for eco-friendly and high-efficacy herbicide delivery
abstract: To address the critical issue of pesticide loss (up to ∼60 % of applied pesticides) caused by splash, rebound, and rain-induced runoff, which contaminates groundwater and poses risks to human health and the environment, this study presents a novel interfacial engineering strategy to enhance herbicide droplet deposition and adhesion on (super)hydrophobic leaf surfaces. This strategy utilizes the interfacial assembly of amyloid-like protein/laponite (PTB/LAP) nanocomposites to create stable oil-in-water (O/W) nanoemulsions with strong foliar affinity. Specifically, bovine serum albumin (BSA) is first adsorbed onto laponite (LAP) surfaces via hydrogen bonding; subsequent introduction of tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) reduces BSA's disulfide bonds, triggering in situ amyloid-like aggregation of surface-bound BSA (PTB) to form PTB/LAP nanocomposites. These nanocomposites significantly enhance interfacial activity, reducing aqueous surface tension to ∼36 mN/m, and form elastic-dominated interfacial networks with excellent mechanical strength. The resulting PTB/LAP nanoemulsion remains stable (mean droplet size ∼250 nm, polydispersity index <0.2) for over 180 days. It exhibits rapid, nanosecond-scale anchoring on leaf cuticles, yielding a 3.6-times higher retention rate than BSA/LAP emulsions under simulated heavy rainfall (150 mm per day). At an equal dosage of 2,4-D isooctyl ester, the nanoemulsion achieves 96.9 % efficacy against shepherd's purse, 2.2 times higher than conventional emulsifiable concentrates (ECs), which only achieve ∼43.5 % efficacy. Furthermore, the PTB/LAP nanoemulsion demonstrates exceptional biocompatibility, with 100 % survival of non-target land snails after 120 h and no significant cytotoxicity or genotoxicity in CHL cell assays. This work provides an eco-friendly, scalable platform for improving pesticide efficiency, reducing environmental contamination, and advancing sustainable agriculture.

title: Thermochemical conversion of sunn hemp biomass and mixed plastic waste via co-liquefaction
abstract: Global interest has surged in the co-liquefaction of oxygen-rich lignocellulosic biomass with hydrogen-rich plastic into oil, a valuable precursor for biofuel and biomaterial. This study investigates the co-liquefaction of modelled mixed plastic waste with sunn hemp ( Crotalaria juncea ) biomass (SHB) for oil production. Initially, SHB was co-liquefied with polyethylene terephthalate (PET) under varying conditions, including temperature (300–340 °C), residence time (30–90 min), and biomass-to-plastic ratio (1:2–2:1), to optimise the process using Response Surface Methodology. The predicted optimal conditions at 324 °C, a 1:2 biomass-to-plastic ratio, and a 30 min residence time yielded a maximum theoretical oil output of 57.79 wt%. Under these conditions, experimental validation resulted in an oil yield of 55.73 ± 1.11 wt% (close to the predicted 57.79 wt%), demonstrating a positive synergistic effect. The co-liquefaction of SHB with binary and ternary plastic mixtures produced oil yields of 22–62 wt%. Notably, the SHB + PET + flexible polyurethane (PUF) (58.33 wt%) and SHB + PET + PUF + rigid polyurethane (62.36 wt%) combinations achieved the highest yields, exhibiting corresponding higher heating values of 27.18 and 27.63 MJ/kg, respectively. Co-liquefaction also improved oil yields from lower-performing plastics such as polypropylene, polystyrene, and low-density polyethylene. Polyurethane (PU) co-liquefaction improved overall process efficiency via enhanced oil, carbon, and energy recovery compared to pure SHB processing. Detailed characterisation indicated that PU-derived nitrogen-containing compounds enhanced oil formation through increased heteroatomic reactivity. Finally, co-liquefaction of lignocellulosic biomass with mixed plastic waste offers a more viable approach for waste valorisation than relying on sorting, paving the way for energy and carbon recovery.

title: Comparative assessment of manual and UAV-based deep learning approaches for beach litter
abstract: Since the 1980s, marine litter has increasingly accumulated on global coastlines. Traditional monitoring methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and face significant challenges in consistently detecting small or partially buried litter, which has driven the need for intelligent, data-driven approaches. This study proposes an optimized UAV-deep learning framework to address these challenges. We selected two typical coastal regions in Guangdong Province, China: Donghai Island (Zhanjiang) and Daya Bay (Huizhou). At these sites, a high-resolution dataset consisting of 6300 UAV images through aerial photography and manual annotation. An enhanced YOLOv8 model with Gold-YOLO-inspired feature extraction and fusion was developed and trained on this dataset. The optimized model achieved 96.50 % precision, 87.00 % recall, 91.50 % F1-score, and 89.80 % mAP@0.5, markedly outperforming baseline YOLO variants and traditional manual methods in both accuracy and efficiency. Field validation at 12 sampling sites showed that the system improves operational efficiency by 75 %, completing surveys in hours instead of days. Environmental assessment using the Clean Coast Index (CCI), Plastic Abundance Index (PAI), and Hazardous Litter Index (HLI) revealed that plastics account for 85 % of all detected litter. The proposed UAV-deep learning framework enables rapid, accurate, and cost-efficient large-scale beach litter monitoring, providing coastal managers with a practical tool for data-driven environmental management and pollution control. It paves the way for integration with automated cleanup systems and long-term ecological risk assessment, contributing to global marine plastic pollution mitigation.

title: Environmental assessment of anaerobic digestion within net-zero and policy-aligned AFOLU sector futures
abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is promoted to decarbonise agriculture while providing renewable energy and improved manure management. This study assesses the technical feasibility and environmental performance of large- and small-scale AD deployment within the agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU) sector in Ireland to 2050. The national GOBLIN land-balance model was used with detailed feedstock allocation and a life cycle assessment (LCA) model (LCAD 2.0), simulating 160 AFOLU configurations and analysing 14 policy-relevant scenarios in detail. First, only high-ambition AFOLU pathways that substantially reduce beef cattle numbers and reallocate spared grassland to silage and bioenergy crops can reliably supply sufficient feedstock to meet Ireland's 5.7 TWh yr −1 biomethane target; incremental policy pathways offer limited AD expansion and modest emission reductions. Second, large-scale plants deliver the strongest national climate benefits and lowest normalised environmental burdens, whereas widespread deployment of silage-dominated small-scale plants could increase environmental burdens. Third, the net contribution of AD to national climate goals is highly sensitive to how AFOLU transitions, land-sparing strategies, and AD configurations are combined. Overall, optimum AD deployment is contingent on ambitious AFOLU restructuring and carefully targeted technology choices. Land use and AD strategies should be aligned to include targeted incentives for digestion of manure from priority livestock regions, silage or bioenergy crop production in regions spared from livestock and support for high-performing AD configurations. Strategic policy support will be essential to ensure that biomethane expansion contributes to climate neutrality and circular bioeconomy objectives.

title: Synergistic pyrolysis of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste for phosphorus recovery and release from wastewater: A multi-fold resource utilization strategy
abstract: Addressing the dual challenges of waste disposal and the phosphorus resource crisis, the development of cost-effective and sustainable adsorbents for phosphorus recovery through the utilization of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste is of great significance. Herein, an effective strategy was presented for synthesizing Ca/Mg biochar composites by integrating concentrated seawater and agricultural waste through a co-precipitation and low temperature carbonization (400 °C), aimed at phosphorus recovery and release. The introduction of 3.0 mol/L KOH during preparation increased the specific surface area, optimized the pore structure, and promoted the co-precipitation of Ca/Mg from concentrated seawater into the biomass framework, providing more active sites. Characterization results confirmed the mesoporous structure and the presence of surface-loaded metal species in all three Ca/Mg-modified biochar composites. The adsorption of phosphorus by the Ca/Mg biochar composites produced from three types of agricultural waste was well-described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm models, recording a maximum adsorption capacity of 138.192 mg/g. This suggested that the biochar preparation strategy possessed considerable universality, yielding biochar with consistent physicochemical properties and phosphorus adsorption performance. The characterization and analysis further reveal that the primary adsorption mechanisms include electrostatic attraction, chemical precipitation, and ligand exchange. Significantly, excessive Ca/Mg in individual biochar composites group (CBC-K) inhibited Mung beans germination and growth, whereas phosphorus-saturated Ca/Mg biochar composites group (P-CBC-K) still promoted crops growth due to the formation of calcium- and magnesium-containing phosphorus compounds, resulting in a 2.64-fold increase in fresh biomass compared to CBC-K group. This study enables the simultaneous phosphorus removal and recovery, along with the harmless treatment of concentrated seawater and agricultural waste, thus achieving a multi-fold resource utilization.

title: Multiple enhanced PMF framework addressing ambient processing and factor allocation for VOC source apportionment
abstract: Volatile organic compound (VOC) pollution control is a key driver of the sustainable improvement in air quality. As one of the most commonly used approaches for linking emissions with ambient pollution, Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) model exhibits limitations due to its neglect of ambient processing and reliance on subjective factor allocation. This study developed multiple enhanced PMF framework. By incorporating corrections for photochemical losses and secondary formations, the Initial Number PMF (IN-PMF) addressed gaps between the observed and initial concentrations. On this basis, the Initial Number and Dispersion Normalized PMF (IN-DN-PMF) was developed to exclude atmospheric dilution. Triaxial characteristic species ratios screened from extensive emission tests were raised to constrain all models, enabling precise apportionment of highly collinear mobile sources. Taking a typical corridor city in China as a case study, the IN-PMF model traced contributions of active species across sources and corrected underestimation of emission intensities. The IN-DN-PMF model provided a spatial distribution of local VOC emissions more closely aligned with actual source locations, while reducing the influence of wind-direction relative to sources. Improvements were most pronounced for gasoline vehicles due to the high emissions of active substances and strong mobility. The traditional PMF underestimated the contribution of gasoline vehicles during pollution episodes by 28.58 % due to photochemical reactions, and by 44.70 % when both photochemistry and dilution were considered. These biases indicate that the traditional model could weaken the importance of vehicle emissions, underscoring the value of the enhanced PMF approach for reliable pollution governance and policy formulations.

title: Staged pyrolysis of corn cob to improve the production of glycolaldehyde, acetic acid, and acetol
abstract: During high-temperature fast pyrolysis, cellulose and hemicellulose undergo simultaneous pyrolysis with partially overlap decomposition temperature ranges, resulting in the concurrent release of abundant molecular fragments/intermediates. The coexistence of these active intermediates readily induces side reactions like polymerization, which inhibits the formation of small molecules (e.g., glycolaldehyde and acetol). Pre-releasing the products of either component is a viable strategy to alleviate this overlap inhibition effect. Given that hemicellulose has a lower decomposition temperature than cellulose, staged pyrolysis is implemented by leveraging this temperature difference. The staged pyrolysis was divided into two sateges, first at 290, 320, or 350 °C to release hemicellulosic derivatives, and then at 600 °C. The results indicated that higher first-stage temperature significantly reduced the inhibition effect, enhancing the production of small molecules (C1-C5), including hydrogen storage molecules. However, extending the first-stage residence time detrimentally decreased the hydrogen storage molecules production, excluding acetic acid. Conversely, a longer second-stage residence time improved the yield of both small molecules and hydrogen storage compounds. Ultimately, staged pyrolysis yielded the highest amount of small molecules (C1-C5) and hydrogen storage molecules when firstly pyrolysis of corn cob at 350 °C with 0.5 min, and subsequently at 600 °C for 0.5 min (350-0.5 + 600-0.5). Direct pyrolysis of cellulose-corn cob blends to test the effectiveness of attenuating the overlap inhibition effect. This discovery has implications for optimizing pyrolysis efficiency and designing reactors for future applications.

title: Quantifying transport contributions and diagnosing ozone formation sensitivity: An integrated approach using machine learning with high-resolution gridded data and backward trajectories
abstract: Regional transport of air pollutants poses a serious challenge to tropospheric ozone (O3) pollution control. Although recent study has combined machine learning and backward trajectories to quantify the contribution of transport, the accuracy of these models has been limited due to the use of average transport times. Therefore, this study integrates high-resolution pollutant concentration data with machine learning and backward trajectories (XGBoost-Traj-Grid), significantly improving the model's simulation performance. The Mangdang Mountain, located at a high-altitude background site on the southeast coast of China, exhibits daily minimum values as high as 80.00 μg⋅m−3, and the difference between daily maximum and minimum values of only 9.14 μg⋅m−3. The XGBoost-Traj-Grid model identified the top five features with the largest contribution to O3 at this site as nitrogen dioxide (NO2), fine particulate matter, coarse particulate matter, relative humidity, and O3 concentration corresponding to a backward trajectory of −3 h. The positive relationship between NO2 and O3 shown in the dependence plot, together with the high HCHO/NO2 ratios observed in OMI satellite data, provides strong evidence that O3 production at this site is NOx-limited. The transport has a predominant role in Mangdang Mountain, with the contribution of transport increasing from 46 % to 56.5 % after meteorological normalization., The contribution of direct O3 transport has always been the largest among the various transport components, with 34.9 % and 32.4 % respectively before and after the meteorological impact. This study indicates that the control of O3 at high-altitude background sites requires joint prevention and control measures. The XGBoost-Traj-Grid model can not only quantify regional transport contributions but also identify O3 formation sensitivity, providing a basis for ozone management.

title: Pilot-scale ultrasonic agglomeration of flue gas particulates for reduced energy consumption during industrial gas cleaning
abstract: Waste-to-energy (WTE) is a widely adopted and effective approach for waste reduction and energy recovery. However, flue gas generated during WTE processes must be treated prior to discharge, and the removal of high concentrations of ultrafine particles at elevated temperatures remains an energy-intensive challenge. Acoustic agglomeration (AA), particularly when implemented using ultrasonic waves, offers a promising method to reduce energy consumption by promoting the coagulation of fine particles into larger aggregates that can be more readily captured with lower energy input. To date, most studies on AA have been confined to laboratory-scale systems or low-temperature conditions, with limited validation at the pilot or industrial scale. In this study, AA was successfully applied in a pilot-scale particle removal system at an operational WTE facility. Particle removal efficiency, bag filter pressure drop and energy consumption were systematically quantified to evaluate performance. The results demonstrate substantial energy savings of up to 36.8 % in the purge system, along with a modest 1.3 % reduction in draft fan energy consumption. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents one of the first applications of AA in a full-scale operational WTE facility, providing valuable insights into the feasibility of AA for industrial deployment and guiding future research and optimization efforts.

title: Global synthesis of agricultural practices on crop yield, soil organic carbon and greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Low-carbon agricultural practice is crucial for reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, without compromising crop yield. However, consensus on which practices were certain to deliver positive outcomes remains limited. Synthesizing global meta-analysis evidence (covering 81 first-order meta-studies and 275 paired observations), this study identified different agricultural practices effects of crop yield, SOC content and GHG emission caused through secondary use of meta-analysis data on the topics. Results showed that crop rotation, film mulch, new crop variety and various fertilizer management strategies significantly increased crop yield (up to 62 %); crop rotation, conservation tillage, deep tillage, biochar addition, organic fertilizer addition, cover crop, straw management significantly increased SOC content (up to 34.30 %); the CH4 emission were effectively reduced by new crop variety, deep fertilization, enhanced-efficiency fertilizer and non-flooding irrigation, while N2O emission declined with reduced nitrogen fertilizer and herbicide application. Among all practices evaluated, rice-animal co-culture emerged as one of the most consistently beneficial strategies in paddy field, increasing crop yield by 2.48 %, enhancing SOC by 10.03 %, and reducing CH4 emissions by −36.30 %. Biochar was the most beneficial strategies in unspecified land use pattern that could increase crop yield and SOC (12.79 %, 32.71 %), decrease GHG emission (−8.68 % to −6.22 %). By quantifying weighted effect sizes for paddy, upland, and mixed cropland systems, this synthesis offered a clear evidence base for designing low-carbon farming systems.

title: Air-source high-temperature heat pump systems for zero-carbon parks: Performance and application
abstract: In the pursuit of global carbon neutrality, zero-carbon industrial parks urgently require efficient and low-emission technologies for high-temperature heat supply. This study investigates an air-source high-temperature heat pump (ASHTHP) system by establishing a cascade cycle model and validating its performance through both laboratory tests and field operation in a pharmaceutical park. Results indicate that system efficiency rises with ambient temperature: under a 125 °C supply condition, the coefficient of performance (COP) increased from 1.35 at −20 °C to approximately 1.85 at 35 °C. In contrast, raising the supply temperature led to a decline in efficiency. The deviation between simulations and experiments was within 5 %, confirming the accuracy of the model. Field operation further demonstrated stable delivery of 115 °C steam with an average COP of 2.1, meeting the continuous high-temperature demand of pharmaceutical production. Economic and environmental analyses highlighted the advantages of ASHTHP over conventional boilers. Compared with coal-fired boilers, CO2 emissions were reduced by 35 %. Under conventional electricity supply, annual operating costs were 10 % lower than gas-fired boilers and more than 30 % lower than electric boilers. When coupled with renewable electricity, costs further decreased by 38 %, while near-zero emissions were achieved. Overall, the ASHTHP system combines high efficiency with strong decarbonization potential for high-temperature applications in zero-carbon parks, demonstrating both engineering feasibility and significant potential for large-scale deployment. These results provide a practical pathway toward the development of zero-carbon industrial parks.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and enhancement potential of global water retention: Insights from a water balance-geographical detector framework
abstract: Water retention is one of the essential ecosystem service functions, playing a critical role in maintaining regional ecological security and the sustainable development of water resources. This study, based on the principle of water balance and employing the optimal parameters-based geographical detector, revealed the spatiotemporal patterns of global water retention from 1991 to 2019, identified the main driving factors, and proposed a method for assessing water retention potential. The results indicate that tropical regions represent the core zones of global water retention, whereas arid and semi-arid areas exhibit pronounced declining trends in water retention. Autumn and winter represent the peak periods of retention, while spring and summer correspond to risk periods. Precipitation is the primary factor influencing the spatial variability of water retention, and it exhibits a significant nonlinear-enhance interaction with evapotranspiration, jointly shaping the spatial pattern of water retention. Globally, the potential for increasing water retention is predominantly at medium to high levels, with most regions having room for enhancement, and South America showing the greatest potential. This study provides a critical theoretical foundation and data support for the scientific enhancement of water retention in the future and offers valuable reference for the formulation of sustainable water resource management and ecological conservation policies.

title: Techno-economic modeling and carbon footprint analysis of electrodialysis technology for ammonium ion recovery
abstract: Electrodialysis is a promising technology for ammonium ion recovery, but its techno-economic performance has not been comprehensively explored. This paper presents a process-based techno-economic model and detailed analysis to simulate ammonium ion recovery using electrodialysis stacks, incorporating cell resistance associated with spacer shadow effect, membrane resistance, and electrode rinse solution. The total recovery costs of electrodialysis technology is systematically analyzed by considering costs associated with capital investments, maintenance, energy consumption, replacement, insurance, and labor. The effects of various operating conditions, including feed concentration, dilute concentration, feed flow rate, channel height, and current density, on total recovery costs are also analyzed. The benchmarking results show that electrodialysis achieves lower total recovery costs of $2.63/kg NH 4 + and greenhouse gas emissions of 2.29 kg CO 2 eq/kg NH 4 + compared to the baseline air stripping technology, highlighting electrodialysis as a promising cost-effective and sustainable approach for ammonium ion recovery. • A techno-economic model for ammonium recovery using electrodialysis is proposed. • Reducing energy use significantly enhances electrodialysis economic performance. • Electrodialysis lowers total recovery costs by 65 % compared to air stripping. • Electrodialysis shows economic feasibility for pilot-scale ammonium recovery.

title: Hybrid PVT-PVSFs powered desalination system with phase change material thermal energy storage: Dynamic simulation in an actual weather condition for sustainable off-grid freshwater production
abstract: The growing demand for freshwater in rural and off-grid communities highlights the need for sustainable desalination systems that operate independently of fossil fuels and unstable grid electricity. This study investigates a hybrid solar-powered desalination unit that integrates a photovoltaic–thermal collector with perforated V-shaped fins, a water-based phase change material (PCM) thermal storage tank, and a two-stage reverse osmosis (RO) system. A coupled simulation framework combining computational fluid dynamics, dynamic thermal modeling, and RO process software was developed to evaluate thermal, electrical, and water production performance under realistic weather conditions in Tangshan, China. Results show that the hybrid collector reduced average photovoltaic cell temperature by 14.8 %, lowering the peak temperature by 12.7 °C and enhancing electrical efficiency by 7 %. The PCM tank with 50 kg of storage material increased stored energy by 27.7 % and stabilized outlet temperature. Thermal preheating reduced RO feed pressure by 0.7–1.0 % and decreased the specific energy consumption from 5.086 to 4.831 kWh/m3, a 5.0 % saving. Unlike previous solar RO systems that focus primarily on either PV cooling or thermal storage in isolation, the present work uniquely combines PVT-PVSFs active thermal management, PCM-based energy buffering, and two-stage membrane desalination in a single integrated platform evaluated through multi-physics simulation using ANSYS Fluent, Python, and Toray RO software. The results demonstrate a viable and economically competitive approach for decentralized, emission-free desalination, achieving a water cost of approximately 3 USD/m3 and a payback period of 5.3–7.4 years in solar-rich regions.

title: Mechanistic insights into microbial and metabolomic responses in PAHs-contaminated soil derived from a coal gasification site
abstract: Microbial remediation offers a promising in situ solution for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs)-contaminated soils at coal gasification sites, where these persistent pollutants cause long-term ecological risks. However, the mechanistic links between microbial metabolic processes, community dynamics, and degradation efficiency under realistic remediation conditions remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a large-scale soil column experiment evaluated an integrated bioremediation approach combining bacterial consortium inoculation, nutrient supplementation, and intermittent bio-ventilation (BA treatment). The BA treatment significantly accelerated the degradation of PAHs in soil, particularly high-concentration PAHs such as naphthalene (NAP), phenanthrene (PHE), pyrene (PYR) and benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), and resulted in pronounced changes in differential metabolites (DEMs), with notable enrichment of key transformation intermediates such as pyrene-1,6-dione and phenanthrene-1,2-oxide. KEGG pathway analysis indicated significant enrichment in xenobiotic biodegradation, amino acid metabolism, and lipid metabolism pathways, reflecting microbial functional expression associated with pollutant breakdown and cellular metabolic activity. Simultaneously, BA treatment enhanced dehydrogenase and fluorescein diacetate hydrolase activities while also increasing available phosphorus, which were strongly correlated with PAHs removal and metabolite profiles. Mantel tests and co-occurrence network analyses revealed strong linkages among microbial genera, PAHs, DEMs and soil biochemical properties, highlighting synergistic interactions underlying degradation. Specific bacterial genera exhibited close associations with PAH-related metabolites, suggesting functional contributions to pollutant transformation. Overall, the enhanced microbial treatment not only promoted PAHs removal but also altered soil metabolic profiles and biochemical activity, providing evidence of synergistic microbe–metabolite interactions that contribute to efficient bioremediation.

title: Inhibition effect of coating cement on the sticking behavior of pellets in hydrogen-based shaft furnace direct reduction
abstract: The sticking behavior of reduced pellets directly influences gas distribution, burden descent smoothness, and continuous operational stability in the shaft furnace. Coating a small amount of inhibitor on the pellet surface is currently a simple, low-cost, and effective method under the given raw material and process conditions. Therefore, based on the atmospheric conditions of a hydrogen-based shaft furnace in China, this study investigates the sticking behavior of pellets and its inhibition mechanism using various types of coating agents and different coating dosages. The results show that the reduction sticking behavior of pellets is aggravated with the increase of reduction temperature and reduction time, among which reduction temperature plays a decisive role. Combined with SEM-EDS detection and analysis, it is determined that the formation of low-melting-point eutectic phases initially induces high-temperature sticking, while the subsequent emergence of highly lamellar reactive metallic iron in the later reduction stage constitutes the primary cause of pellet sticking in hydrogen-based shaft furnaces. To mitigate these issues, small amounts of different cementitious materials are coated on the pellet surface before reduction. It is found that P.O 32.5 slag Portland cement and P.O 42.5 ordinary Portland cement have significant inhibitory effects on the reduction sticking phenomenon, while silica fume has a poor effect, which is directly related to the composition of coating agents. Compared with Fe2+ ions, Ca2+ ions in CaO-based coatings are more likely to migrate to iron vacancies during wüstite reduction, thereby altering the formation structure of nascent iron, reducing the activity of freshly formed metallic iron, and further significantly lowering the reduction sticking strength and sticking index (SI) of pellets. SiO2-based coating can also inhibit sticking, but the low-melting-point fayalite phase formed by the reaction of SiO2 with FeO reduces the inhibitory effect. The SI decreases with increasing coating dosage. When the reduction temperature does not exceed 1000 °C, a coating amount of 3 kg per ton of pellets can meet the inhibition requirements. In the future, either selecting coating agents with high CaO and MgO content or adding small amounts of CaO and MgO to cement can enhance the inhibition effectiveness of the coating.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and resilience optimization of urban ecological networks: A case study of the Xiong'an New Area
abstract: Ecological networks (ENs) are critical for enhancing urban ecological resilience and mitigating the impacts of natural hazards by sustaining biodiversity and ecosystem services. However, previous studies often rely on proxy indicators or composite indices to assess resilience, with limited attention to the dynamic resilience of ENs under future land use scenarios. This study proposes an integrated framework to trace the spatiotemporal evolution of ENs and assess their resilience dynamics. Taking the Xiong'an New Area (XNA) as a case study, land use patterns in 2035 were simulated under natural development scenario (NDS) and planning conservation scenario (PCS) using the patch-generating land use simulation (PLUS) model. Circuit theory was then applied to construct ENs and evaluate their resilience from 2005 to 2035 via complex network analysis. Results showed that the establishment of the XNA reversed the declining trends in both ecological land area and EN resilience. Under the PCS, ecological land was 120.24 % greater than under NDS. EN resilience values ranged from 0.85 to 1.20 between 2005 and 2035, with PCS (1.15) surpassing NDS (0.99) in 2035. The Baiyangdian wetland, a key ecological hub with the highest node importance, plays a vital role in the XNA but its overreliance increases network vulnerability. Accordingly, integrated strategies for protection and restoration were provided to strengthen urban ecological resilience, leading to an 18.97 % improvement in network resilience. The proposed framework provides a reproducible pathway to identify network resilience variations and design resilience-oriented spatial strategies, offering valuable insights for urban green infrastructure and sustainable land use planning.

title: A comprehensive well-to-wheel assessment of different sport utility vehicle powertrain-fuel combinations in European countries focusing on climate change indicators.
abstract: Decarbonizing road transport is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality. This study presents a comprehensive Well-to-Wheel analysis of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from 26 powertrain-fuel combinations for passenger cars in Europe. The analysis considers both upstream (Well-to-Tank) and tailpipe (Tank-to-Wheel) emissions, using real-world fuel consumption data from similar sport utility vehicles (SUVs) across five powertrains. The results show that battery electric vehicles (BEVs) powered by renewable electricity achieve the lowest GHG emissions, with 97 to almost 100 % savings compared to fossil fuel counterparts. Fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) running on hydrogen from waste wood gasification and diesel internal combustion engine vehicles (DICI) using e-diesel from wind electricity also demonstrate significant emissions reductions. The study highlights the importance of regionalized solutions and a combination of decarbonization options to achieve substantial GHG emissions reductions in road transport. A broader environmental assessment is also considered, encompassing the vehicle's life cycle within the system boundary. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and researchers, emphasizing the need for a holistic approach to decarbonize road transport. By considering the complexity of powertrain-fuel combinations and regional energy systems, this study informs the development of effective strategies to mitigate GHG emissions from road transport and support a low-carbon transportation sector. • Climate change impact of 5 powertrains and 16 fuels: 26 combos for SUV crossovers. • Sensitivity analysis per European countries: 27, and one for the EU27 area. • Well-to-Wheel of BEVs with renewable electricity achieve more than 97 % GHG savings. • Only 5 countries: LT, DK, FI, FR, SE; could produce e-fuels with GHG savings.

title: Assessing microbial internal drivers of nitrogen–cycle functional potential in lakeside wetlands: insights from random forest modelling and co-occurrence network analyses
abstract: Environmental factors are widely assumed to influence nitrogen (N) cycle processes in lakeside wetlands. However, recent studies suggested that shifts in environmental conditions do not consistently correspond to proportional changes in N–functional potential. To elucidate the contributions of different drivers, multiple influences, including environmental factors, microbial diversity, functional microbial genera, and gene abundance, were examined by integrating a random forest model (RFM), variation partitioning analysis (VPA), network co-occurrence analysis, and structural equation modeling (SEM). Almost 66 % of functional genes in RFM analysis exhibited a preferable R2 fit over 0.6. VPA analysis revealed that functional microbial genes (55.1 %) and genera (35.1 %) accounted for over 90 % of the explanatory contribution rate, surpassing environmental influences (4.3 %) and diversity indices (5.4 %). Network co-occurrence demonstrated that denitrification genes (norB/C/D/E; napA) formed central connective nodes in the network linked to nitrogen-cycle functional potential, and functional genera–gene linkages were closely aligned with variations in N-functional potential. SEM results further revealed that environmental factors did not exhibit a significant direct association with functional genes; instead, their effects were mediated indirectly through the restructuring of microbial community composition. Under long-term hydrological and nutrient fluctuations, microbial communities exhibited internal co-occurrence networks that were associated with N–cycle functional potential. Recognizing these internally structured microbial associations provides new insight into microbial contributions to N–cycle functional potential and may guide the design strategies of sustainable lakeside wetland restoration.

title: The impact of turbulence induced by spur dikes on the spatial carbon metabolism patterns of epilithic biofilms
abstract: Epilithic biofilms serve as critical microbial engines in global river carbon cycling. Understanding carbon metabolism in these "microbial skins" is essential for enhancing rivers' potential as terrestrial carbon sinks. The widespread construction of spur dikes has substantially altered local hydrodynamic conditions, yet how turbulence induced by these structures reshapes biofilm carbon fixation and degradation processes remains poorly understood, representing a key frontier question in freshwater microbial ecology. To address this knowledge gap, this study investigated a multi-spur dike section of the Beijiang River in China, employing metagenomics to elucidate turbulence impacts on epilithic biofilm carbon metabolism. Results revealed that spur dikes altered hydrodynamic conditions across the river section, with turbulent kinetic energy (0.0018 ± 0.001 m/s) and intensity (0.029 ± 0.01 m/s) significantly increasing at dike heads. At high-turbulence dike heads, autotrophic microorganisms proliferated and adapted by secreting extracellular polymers and reducing metabolic rates. Efficient carbon fixation was achieved through the cross-feeding-mediated Arnon-Buchanan cycle and Calvin cycle, resulting in 1.33-fold higher biofilm organic carbon accumulation compared to dike tails. Conversely, low-turbulence dike tails exhibited higher chemical oxygen demand, providing abundant carbon sources for heterotrophic microorganisms, which significantly enhanced carbon degradation activity through augmented capabilities for degrading starch, cellulose, and aromatic compounds. This study demonstrates that spur-dike-induced turbulence drives differentiation in microbial community structure and function, establishing a distinct spatial pattern characterized by "autotrophic carbon fixation" at dike heads and "heterotrophic degradation" at dike tails.

title: Optimized crystallization and thermal treatment for high-purity calcium fluoride recovery from fluoride-containing wastewater
abstract: Industrial semiconductor wastewater contains extremely high fluoride concentrations, yet conventional treatments often produce low-purity calcium fluoride (CaF2) sludge. This study establishes an optimized crystallization process combined with thermal treatment to recover high-purity CaF2 directly from real wastewater. Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) suspension was used as the calcium source, and the [Ca2+]/[F−] ratio was systematically adjusted to determine optimal conditions. At the optimal ratio of 0.39 under alkaline conditions (pH 10), fluoride removal reached 98 %, yielding products with 99 wt% CaF2 purity. X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterization revealed that drying at 105 °C retained chemically bound water, leading to amorphous CaF2 formation (2.17 wt%). Meanwhile, thermal treatment at 400 °C effectively addressed these limitations through dehydration and recrystallization, reducing amorphous content to 1.10 wt%. The recovered CaF2 exceeded acid-grade CaF2 concentrate requirements (>97 wt%), demonstrating that hazardous wastewater can be upcycled into a stable, high-value mineral resource. These results highlight the importance of thermal treatment in producing CaF2 with crystallographic quality suitable for industrial reuse.

title: Hydrothermal carbon-based sulfate-reducing bioagent for enhanced sulfate reduction and acidification mitigation in oligotrophic environments
abstract: Sulfate reduction via sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a key strategy for mitigating acidification in acid mine drainage (AMD). However, SRB are limited by low acid tolerance and reliance on external carbon sources, leading to inefficient sulfate reduction under strongly acidic and nutrient-deficient conditions. To address these challenges, we developed a hydrothermal carbon (HC)-based SRB bioagent and investigated its dual role as a microbial carrier and an intrinsic carbon source. Among the HC materials synthesized under different conditions, the sample prepared at 220 °C for 3 h exhibited the highest performance and was selected for further study. In nutrient-deficient environments, the HC-SRB bioagent significantly enhanced sulfate reduction, lowering sulfate concentrations from 1100 to 730 mg L−1, while free SRB showed negligible activity. The bioagent also increased system pH from 5.3 to 6.5, compared with 5.6 for free SRB. This improvement is attributed to the dual function of HC, which provides a protective microenvironment and continuously releases bioavailable carbon to support SRB growth. Importantly, the HC-SRB bioagent maintained stable sulfate reduction after five consecutive reuse cycles, achieving sulfate reduction efficiencies of up to 99 %. Overall, our results demonstrate that HC-SRB bioagents effectively overcome the main limitations of conventional SRB under acidic and carbon-limited conditions, offering a sustainable and green approach for AMD treatment.

title: How do national wetland parks promote corporate green innovation? Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
abstract: Climate change driven by carbon emissions poses a grave threat to the sustainable development of human societies and economies. Most existing studies focus on traditional environmental regulation tools such as pollution fees and carbon taxes, while giving little attention to whether national wetland parks serve as an important driver of corporate green innovation. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2024, this paper empirically investigates how China's national wetland parks affects corporate green innovation. The results show that China's national wetland parks strengthen corporate green innovation, and this effect proves to be persistent over time. Mechanism analysis shows that China's national wetland parks foster corporate green innovation by improving corporate ESG performance and expanding their environmental investments. Heterogeneity analysis shows that China's national wetland parks have a stronger effect on corporate green innovation among non-state-owned and non-high-pollution firms than among state-owned and high-pollution firms. Our findings provide actionable guidance for the Chinese government on how to design and implement wetland-park policies that more effectively stimulate corporate green innovation.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of an efficient green methanol production system based on biomass gasification and carbon capture
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing demand for renewable energy and escalating environmental pressures from fossil resources, developing efficient, low-emission biomass conversion technologies has become a crucial direction for optimizing the energy structure. This study developed an innovative integrated poly-generation system for the co-production of energy and chemicals from biomass resources. This system synergistically couples biomass gasification, high-efficiency steam-organic Rankine dual-cycle power generation, cryogenic distillation, carbon dioxide capture, and methanol synthesis, achieving coordinated utilization of biomass energy and carbon resources. Key operating parameters were optimized through comprehensive process simulations, thermodynamic assessments, and sensitivity analyses. Under optimized configuration, the system achieved an overall energy efficiency of 71.83 %. The economic evaluation reveals a dynamic payback period of 4.44 years and a net present value of US$118.14 million, underscoring the strong investment feasibility of this project. Life cycle assessment based on multiple intermediate point categories and damage endpoints indicates that feedstocks dominate resource consumption and ecotoxicity indicators. At the same time, the methanol production stage contributes the most to human health, ecological quality, climate change, and resource consumption, accounting for 41–87 % of the total. This study provides a systematic solution for the efficient and clean utilization of biomass, offering important technical references for the future regionalized production of low-carbon fuels and chemicals.

title: Energy efficiency and carbon emission reduction of fly ash vacuum insulation boards: A coupled thermal modeling and lifecycle assessment
abstract: This study develops a fly ash-based composite insulation (FAHM-MF) to balance building performance and carbon reduction. It quantifies the impact of fiber volume fraction (Vfibre) and vacuum conditions on pore structure parameters. Increasing Vfibre reduces porosity (φ), fractal dimension (D), and regularizes pore structure, but lowers connectivity (Cconn), affecting thermal conductivity (λ). Vacuum conditions enhance λ through low φ. The pore structure complexity coefficient (k2) is the most sensitive parameter to λ (sensitivity 79.28 %), with ±2SE fluctuations resulting in a ±8.2 % change. Sensitivities of the vacuum correction coefficient (k3) and fiber reinforcement factor (β) are lower at ±3 % and ±1.5 %, respectively. Lifecycle assessment shows FAHM-MF buildings reduce carbon emissions by 10.2 % (464.85 tons CO2) compared to EPS. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that grid emission factors (sensitivity 0.96) cause ΔCO2 fluctuations of ±28.75 % with ±30 % variation, and reduce the emission-reduction potential in coal-powered regions by more than 20 %. Extending building lifespan to 60 years improves ΔCO2 by 17.7 %. This framework optimizes the use of building materials and supports sustainable development.

title: Effects of absorbent physical properties on microscale hydrodynamics in structured packing for CO2 capture and new correlations for interfacial area and liquid holdup
abstract: Chemical absorption using structured packing columns is an economical and efficient technology for mitigating CO2 emissions. The fluid dynamics and gas-liquid mass transfer behaviors within such packings are remarkably affected by solvent properties and geometric features (such as perforations on the corrugated sheets). However, the explicit representation of perforations in three-dimensional simulations and their impact on the microscale hydrodynamics of different solvents remain insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed a computational domain comprising 2 × 4 Representative Elementary Units of 250.Y structured packing, with full geometrical resolution of the perforations. Gas-liquid two-phase flow simulations were conducted using the Volume of Fluid method. The investigation systematically examined the effects of solvent properties (characterized by Kapitza number), surface wettability, and flow rate on flow patterns, interfacial area, and liquid holdup. The results demonstrate that perforations promote rivulet separation, droplet formation, and periodic renewal of gas-liquid interface. A lower Kapitza number stabilizes rivulet flow and enhances wettability. Notably, for perforated sheets, the wetted area is smaller than the interfacial area, which contrasts with the behavior observed in non-perforated sheets. The dependence of interfacial area on contact angle (γ) exhibited two distinct regimes: in Region I (γ > 30°), the area shows weak sensitivity to γ, while in Region II (γ ≤ 30°), it increases markedly as γ decreases. Finally, modified correlations were developed to enable more accurate prediction of liquid holdup and interfacial area in perforated packings. These correlations can facilitate improved column design and operational optimization, thereby contributing to cleaner industrial production and carbon emission reduction.

title: Engineered microbial consortium enhances tomato salt tolerance through rhizosphere modulation for sustainable crop production
abstract: Salinity stress in agricultural soils severely inhibits crop growth and jeopardizes global food security. This study involved the construction of an ACC deaminase-engineered bacterium, BL-EF, which was combined with multifunctional Enterobacter cloacae Rs-2 and injected into potted tomato plants experiencing salt stress. Eight parallel treatments were established to investigate the optimal compounding ratio by altering the proportions of the two bacterial complexes. The morphological indicators of plants inoculated with the optimal ratio of the bacterial consortium were monitored, revealing that the compounded bacteria enhanced the seedling metrics of plant length (69.45 %), fresh weight (81.26 %), dry weight (176.41 %), and stem diameter (16.61 %). Moreover, the bacterial consortium enhanced the levels of photosynthetic pigments, peroxidase activity, and osmoregulatory chemicals in the plants. Furthermore, soil nutrient availability and enzyme activity in the rhizosphere were significantly enhanced. Additionally, the bacterial consortium altered the composition of the rhizosphere microbial community. The potential synergistic mechanism of these two bacteria may be attributed to their salt tolerance and enhancement capabilities, the optimization of the rhizosphere microenvironment, and the establishment of novel ecological niches within the rhizosphere. This study underscores the potential of BL-EF as a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium and the prospective applications of this bacterial consortium.

title: Unlocking the potential of pyrite by mechanochemistry ball mill for efficient heterogeneous Fenton degradation of florfenicol
abstract: Ball milling of pyrite significantly improves the degradation of florfenicol (FLO) by activated H2O2, extending the effective pH range. After 5 h of ball milling, FeS2bm can degrade more than 95 % of FLO in the pH range of 3–9 at 0.1 g/L dosing with 2 mM H2O2, and the performance is approximately 70 times higher (as kobs) than that of raw pyrite. The ball milling process renews the pyrite surface, reducing the percentage of oxidized iron sulfide species by 44.18 % and 12.05 %, respectively, while decreasing particle size and creating a rough, porous surface. The total dissolved Fe ions of FeS2bm increased by 16.6 times and H+ production by 7.1 times, concurrently, the Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling was enhanced. The ·OH produced by the activation of H2O2 by dissolved Fe2+ is the primary contributor to FLO degradation. LC/MS analysis confirmed the complete degradation of FLO. FeS2bm/H2O2 system demonstrated excellent durability and the capacity to degrade various antibiotics, using air as the ball milling atmosphere or switching to natural pyrite as the raw material had no significant effect on the properties of the ball-milled material. Overall, these findings offer valuable insights into the engineering of ball-milled pyrite for enhanced H2O2 degradation of antibiotics.

title: Carbon-digital interplay in industry risk spillovers: Analyzing spatiotemporal dynamics and network topology for adaptive governance
abstract: Advancing low-carbon and digital transformation represents two major global challenges of the era. Carbon regulation and digital transformation jointly pressure and empower industries, yet prior studies mostly examine their effects separately and neglect how their interaction reshapes multi-regional and multi-sectoral risk spillovers, being an issue of both theoretical and practical importance that remains underexplored.
