A synergistic amplification of pollution occurs when the livestock-fishery share exceeds 60 % whereas increasing the tertiary share above 45 % induces systematic load reductions through structural transformation. (3) The watershed displays pronounced spatial heterogeneityalong a gradient of production core, crop-livestock transition, ecologically sensitivity, and ecological barrier, rendering uniform pollicies ineffective. Based on these insights, a novel Threshold constraint-Zoning synergy-Phasing progression (TZP) spatial governance framework is proposed. Conceived as an integrative methodology, it bridges mechanistic diagnosis with actionable management by systematically coupling diagnostic thresholds, spatial zoning, and phased progression to enable adaptive, targeted governance. This framework formulates differentiated strategies tailored to four functional zones and outlines a three-stage implementation pathway: initial breakthroughs in sensitive zone (2025–2027), watershed-wide industry-technology synergy as the core phase (2028–2030), and a vision for ecological transformation across the entire basin (2031–2035). Multi-scenario simulations confirm that this pathway can achieve a sustained reduction in total nitrogen load of approximately 25.6 % without compromising food security. This study provides both a concrete governance blueprint for the Danjiangkou Reservoir and a replicable scientific paradigm, the integrated diagnosis-threshold-zoning-timing approach, thereby offering a practical pathway for similar basins globally to synergistically advance Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger) and Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation).

title: Navigating the maritime energy transition: a narrative analysis of Nordic short-sea shipping companies
abstract: The central focus of this study is to offer a micro-level examination of how Nordic short-sea shipping company representatives describe their role within the energy transition. We employed narrative analysis on RoPax/RoRo, a segment of short-sea shipping, company representatives to elucidate how elite interviewees narrate challenges and barriers to transitioning to low-emission fuels. The analysis revealed tensions related to the energy transition, namely concerns about IMO and EU policies not supporting technological change, technological and infrastructural limitations of transitioning, and the struggle to engage customers with the energy transition. Additionally, interviewees illustrated their knowledge of different decarbonization options, including the technical and commercial feasibility of different fuel options, alongside commenting on their involvement in the current policy environment. Interviewees expressed that their customers, both cargo and passenger, were unwilling to pay for the energy transition, many arguing that the customer should pay for the transition costs. Industry representatives could narrate their visions and pathway to their company's 2035 targets, but their narration of how to reach 2050 goals indicated a limited ability to only storify the sector's potential future accomplishments, but not how their company would reach the same targets. Nordic RoPax/RoRo Managers and C-level executives may have the drive or interest for transitioning to low-carbon fuels, but the lack of alignment with infrastructure, policy making that aligns with current technological know-how, cultural, users, and markets, and distribution systems makes transitioning a wicked problem.

title: An integrated framework for synergistic multi-element, cross-media pollution control in organic solid waste treatment system
abstract: Organic-waste treatment processes redistribute carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur across air, water, and soil, creating cross-media risks from uncontrolled losses that single-medium controls miss. However, elemental fluxes traverse multi-stage units with feedbacks and leakage, forming an interconnected, path-dependent network where amplification pathways and cross-media trade-offs remain unresolved. We develop an integrated three-module framework for synergistic pollution control of unintended CNPS releases. First, we cast the treatment system as a directed process network and model elemental flows as multi-stage cross-media fluxes. Second, we identify key cross-media control nodes using a chain-level hubness indicator from weighted and current-flow betweenness, and calculate cross-media emission efficiencies to quantify medium-specific outputs. Third, to flag chains where pathway amplification and outlet intensity co-occur, we non-compensatorily couple hubness with efficiency into a composite hotspot, and use ridge-regularized partial correlations to rank composite risk for co-control. This framework is applied to the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, covering 61 multi-stage chains (30 for crop straw, 10 for livestock manure, and 21 for kitchen waste). Rankings are robust to ±5% edge-weight perturbations, with anaerobic digestion as a backbone node. Chain mapping yields two archetypes: multi-node trunks and single-bottleneck short routes. Cross-media efficiencies are stable, with carbon and sulfur predominantly to air, nitrogen to water, and phosphorus to soil. Highest composite-risk chains are C20 (straw: AD-biogas power-digestate landfilling), L1 (manure: open anaerobic lagoon), and K12 (kitchen waste: whole-substrate AD-biogas power). Findings prioritize gas capture and cleaning, liquid polishing, and monitored containment, providing a generalizable route to multi-element cross-media control.

title: Retraction notice to “A fully decentralized home energy management system for efficient energy management and photovoltaic with battery energy storage system sizing for grid connected home microgrid” [J. Clean. Product. 514 (2025) 145768]

title: Expanding carbon pricing boundaries and the EU CBAM: insights into China and India
abstract: Implemented alongside the EU Emissions Trading System revision, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) requires importers of selected energy-intensive commodities to purchase certificates reflecting the EU carbon price. Designed to prevent carbon leakage and incentivise cleaner industrial production, CBAM has sparked heated academic and political debate, raising questions about its economic and environmental effectiveness and its interaction with emerging carbon pricing regimes outside the EU. This paper examines how the evolution of carbon pricing in China and India, two major emitters and key trading partners of the EU, could influence the effects of CBAM through its exemption mechanism, shaping prospects for international climate policy alignment. It further provides an ex-ante assessment of CBAM's impacts under its legislated design, including its sectoral scope, implementation timeline, and the phase-out of free allowances in the EU ETS. The analysis applies FIDELIO, a global, multi-sectoral, recursively dynamic general equilibrium model, to quantify impacts on trade, production, and emissions. Results show that CBAM has limited aggregate macroeconomic and environmental effects but induces significant structural changes within the EU in highly energy-intensive sectors, including substitution from imports of carbon-intensive goods toward relatively cleaner production and emerging intra-EU disparities. When China and India implement stronger carbon pricing, CBAM's trade impacts diminish, yet cross-country asymmetries between major trading partners persist. Overall, the findings highlight CBAM's modest direct effects but underline its potential to act as a lever for greater international ambition in climate policies.

title: Carbon footprints of recycling straw waste into building materials: A life cycle assessment (LCA) study
abstract: A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to evaluate the carbon footprint and resource efficiency of recycling straw waste into building materials. Three straw valorization pathways—straw resin-bonded particleboard (SRBP), straw cement-bonded particleboard (SCBP), and straw-based supplementary cementitious material (SCM)—were assessed and compared with the prevailing practice of straw open burning (SOB). Environmental and economic performance was evaluated in terms of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, global warming potential (GWP), non-renewable energy consumption, resource expenditure, and cost–carbon synergy indices. The assessment adopts a dual-dimensional framework, combining horizontal comparison among straw management scenarios with vertical benchmarking against conventional wood-based particleboards. Methodological novelty is further achieved by integrating a cost–carbon synergy index with a one-million-iteration Monte Carlo simulation to jointly quantify economic–environmental performance and uncertainty, and by grounding the analysis in region-specific industrial data from Jilin Province to support policy-relevant conclusions. Results show that SCM exhibits the lowest carbon footprint (273.18 kg CO2eq per ton of straw), whereas SOB produces the highest emissions (2834.80 kg CO2eq/t). Relative to conventional wood-based boards, SRBP and SCBP reduce GHG emissions by 9.90 % and 4.53 %, respectively, while lowering non-renewable energy demand by up to 3.08 % and 14.88 %. SCM achieves the largest emission mitigation potential, with a unit abatement cost of 0.072 CNY per kg CO2eq, substantially below representative social carbon cost thresholds, whereas SRBP and SCBP achieve positive cost–carbon synergy without direct fiscal support. Sensitivity analysis identifies transportation distance and molding electricity as dominant GWP drivers, and Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of scenario ranking under parameter uncertainty. Overall, SRBP and SCBP offer economically viable pathways with synergistic emission reductions, while SCM provides substantial climate benefits through deep emission mitigation. These findings support targeted promotion of straw-based particleboards and the development of carbon-trading mechanisms for SCM, alongside logistics optimization and process-level emission reduction strategies.

title: Can the urban environmental resilience facilitate the sustainable development of the coastal city: evidence from China
abstract: The United Nations' 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development emphasizes conserving marine resources, making sustainable ocean economies a global priority. Coastal cities, critical hubs for marine-terrestrial systems, face dual pressures: driving growth and managing climate risks. This research examines how urban environmental resilience facilitates the sustainable marine economic development of coastal cities. Using data from 51 Chinese coastal cities spanning 2007 to 2022, the research constructs multidimensional indices for Marine Economy-Society Comprehensive Benefit Index and Environmental Resilience. To analyze the relationships, a two-way fixed-effects model is utilized. The analysis reveals that environmental resilience enhances the sustainable marine economic development, and with the mediating role of Foreign Direct Investment. Results demonstrate a nonlinear threshold effect: resilience significantly boosts sustainability in medium-resilience cities but yields diminishing returns in high-resilience regions. Regional heterogeneity is evident, with southern cities benefiting more due to export-oriented economies and disaster exposure, while northern cities face structural constraints. By integrating environmental and sustainable metrics, this research offers new insights into the resilience-sustainability linkages, enriches coastal studies with threshold and mediation frameworks, and provides actionable foundations for policymakers to tailor development strategies to local capacities.

title: Improving the performance of recycled EN 45500: a sustainable approach through heat treatment optimization
abstract: This study investigates the performance and environmental impact of a 100% recycled EN 45500 aluminum alloy subjected to T6 heat treatment, using its primary counterpart as a benchmark. Both alloys were produced by gravity die casting under controlled laboratory conditions and subsequently characterized from a microstructural and mechanical standpoint. The recycled alloy exhibited a higher iron content, promoting the formation of Fe-based intermetallic compounds, which increased defect density and reduced ductility compared to the primary alloy. Heat treatment parameters were optimized to balance mechanical performance with energy efficiency. Tensile testing revealed that the recycled alloy achieved mechanical properties comparable to those of the peak-aged primary alloy when aged at 160 °C for 4.5 h, a less energy-intensive condition than the 180 °C for 4.5 h required by the primary alloy. The environmental impact analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in carbon footprint, from 19.6 kgCO 2 eq /kgAl for the primary alloy to 2.47 kgCO 2 eq /kgAl for the recycled one. For 100% recycled EN 45500 alloy, the heat treatment, including solution treatment and aging, accounted for 92.3% of CO 2 eq emissions, underscoring the relevance of heat treatment optimization. Overaging tests demonstrated that the recycled EN 45500 retained copper-driven thermal stability. Overall, the findings highlight the capability of recycled aluminum to meet both mechanical performance and sustainability requirements to produce advanced automotive applications.

title: Enhanced sludge anaerobic digestion by voltage-driven electron transfer of humic acids
abstract: Sludge anaerobic digestion (AD) is often constrained by inefficient extracellular electron transfer (EET), which limits syntrophic metabolism and methane production. Humic acids (HAs), naturally occurring redox-active organic matter, can mediate EET as soluble electron shuttles, but their heterogeneous structures lead to inconsistent activity and even electron competition with microbes. Here, a voltage-driven regulation strategy was developed to enhance the electroactivity of HAs and thereby improve AD performance. Results showed that at the applied voltage of 0.6 V, the electron transfer capacity of HAs increased by 164.0%, transforming them into “super electron shuttles”. Further semi-continuous AD experiments demonstrated that voltage-driven HAs increased methane production by 60.4% and refractory organic removal by 51.5%, while maintaining stability under a high organic loading rate of 10 kg/m3.d. The AD system electrochemical characterization and microbial community analyses revealed that voltage-driven HAs selectively enriched syntrophic VFAs oxidizing and electroactive bacteria, forming a “super electron transfer network” that raised system conductivity by 275.2%. Mechanistic verification via co-culture and electrode insulation experiments proved that applied voltage disrupted HAs’ weak molecular interactions, reduced molecular weight, and exposed quinone-type groups. This structural evolution increased electron storage capacity and accelerated the redox cycling between electrodes and microbes. Collectively, these findings reveal a novel bioelectrochemical pathway for activating the latent electroactivity of HAs, highlighting a promising strategy for efficient waste treatment.

title: Fast water purification through sea cucumber-inspired hierarchical network
abstract: Sustainable utilization of micro-polluted water sources presents a viable strategy to address water scarcity in underdeveloped regions. However, conventional membrane technologies, despite their precision engineering, face limitations due to high costs, mechanical fragility, and poor performance in complex water matrices. To address these issues, this study proposes a biomimetic hierarchical network, self-sustaining, easily deployable, and cost-effective for decentralized water treatment, designed to achieve efficient organic pollutant removal while maintaining high permeability. Inspired by sea cucumbers, the network integrates a precisely-tailored nanochannel layer on microchannel walls and leverages peroxymonosulfate as an artificial enzyme mimic. Such a cascaded network mimics optimized synergistic partitioning of the sea cucumber gut. Macroscopic lateral pressure gradient drives in-situ separation of organic pollutants and natural organic matter at the nanochannel surface. These contaminants are then mineralized by reactive species generated from peroxymonosulfate activation via Co2MnO4-based functional materials. This “artificial sea cucumber” system enables efficient water purification under low-pressure conditions, providing a cost-effective and eco-friendly solution for decentralized water treatment scenarios.

title: Techno-enviro-economic evaluation of using recycled concrete aggregate in asphalt mixtures: A life cycle assessment and multi-criteria decision-making framework
abstract: The mechanical performance criterion has been widely used to evaluate the feasibility of preparing asphalt mixtures with recycled concrete aggregates (RCAs) for pavement construction. However, the reliability of these investigations in the asphalt pavement industry should be further modified by considering the techno-economic feasibility and environmental impact dimensions. Hence, a framework combining life cycle assessment (LCA) and production costs was proposed to assess the replacement of natural aggregate (NA) with RCA for hot mix asphalt (HMA) production. Four alternatives were suggested: scenario#1 (control) used 100% NA with construction waste (CW) disposal into open sites; scenarios#2 and #3 replaced 30% of NA by RCA derived from two types of CWs: normal-and high-strength concrete (25 MPa; 60 MPa), respectively; scenario#4 modified RCA using waste cooking oil residue (WCOR) pretreatment. A multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) model was developed to assign scores to the LCA environmental indicators (SimaPro 9.6.0), functional properties, and cost criterion. Scenarios#3 and #4 exhibited mechanical properties comparable to the control mix, probably attributed to enhanced surface characteristics, better binder adhesion, denser structure, and reduced micropores. Scenario#4 reduced global warming potential by 13%, lowered costs by 0.14 US$/ton, and achieved the highest MCDM score (0.78) compared with the control (scenario#1). Using WCOR for RCA-asphalt pretreatment would reduce the demand for asphalt binder, avoiding bitumen-related environmental pollution and modifying manufacturing costs. Because this scenario also fulfilled multiple sustainable development goals, further studies would upgrade the proposed AHP-TOPSIS framework by considering other pretreatment methods, the shadow price of pollution reduction, and organic-based binder material.

title: Moving to sustainable servitization: categorisation and analysis of underlying approaches
abstract: As rising environmental concerns create the need to embed sustainability more centrally into business propositions, the emerging research on sustainable servitization is looking into the possibility for manufacturing companies to combine service-led growth with the generation of environmental value. Existing characterisations, however, interpret sustainable servitization as a generic strategy, failing to recognise the heterogeneity of approaches that it may encompass. This paper develops a taxonomy that – based on service orientation (lifecycle management or operational efficiency) and business model scheme (ownership-based or access-based) – classifies manufacturers' approaches to sustainable servitization into four distinct categories, which differ fundamentally in their sustainability tactics and underlying resource requirements. We also investigate how these categories resonate with practice by analysing the cases of three manufacturers of industrial equipment that have embarked on a sustainable servitization journey. By proposing our taxonomy and unpacking each of the four approaches, we provide granular insights into what it takes for a manufacturer to integrate a sustainability perspective into its servitization strategy. This granular analysis is important as it adds depth and nuance to the understanding of sustainable servitization implementation, which would otherwise be overly simplistic and inaccurate. We also identify that resource requirements and customers’ strong focus on economic benefits may introduce core rigidities and act as barriers to the widespread adoption of certain approaches. For managers, the study may help think through how to enhance and evolve service businesses in ways that contribute to environmental sustainability, and what resources to activate to support a sustainable servitization orientation over time. • Lack of conceptual clarity concerning the heterogeneity of manufacturers' approaches to sustainable servitization. • Four categories of approaches based on service orientation and business model scheme. • Different resource-saving tactics and, thus, different resource requirements. • Resource requirements and customer expectations as core rigidities hampering the adoption of certain approaches. • Guidance to develop a sustainable servitization orientation and activate the necessary resources.

title: Reuse processes for construction materials in a municipal building sector - a scoping literature review
abstract: According to the European Green Deal, increasing the reuse of building materials is recognised as a key measure for reducing emissions and contributing to climate neutrality by 2050. The public sector and municipalities play significant roles and have numerous opportunities to guide planning, construction, and maintenance processes. This paper reviews state-of-the-art research on building material reuse, covering deconstruction to construction, with a focus on the municipal building sector. This study builds on a scoping literature review using PRISMA-ScR, covering literature up to 2024. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 93 articles were identified. Data were analysed and categorised to investigate publication trends in the circular economy (CE) within the municipal building sector. The results indicate a rising trend in publications to date, representing a global pattern, although the majority originate from Western European countries. CE in the built environment is widely addressed through various models, methods, and location-specific case studies. Few studies examine the reuse of existing buildings and processes for utilising current structures, as well as their integration into new projects. There is a noticeable gap in research on establishing these practices as future models, particularly in their management and logistical aspects. Additionally, the study highlights a significant lack of literature on the reuse of building materials in municipal contexts, with municipalities serving as project leaders. The findings reveal critical opportunities to promote CE practices in the municipal building sector and enhance the reuse process. These insights can guide public policy development, improve reuse efficiency, and foster sustainable management of construction materials. Future research should focus on logistical development, governance structures, and stakeholder collaborations to effectively implement CE in the municipal building sector.

title: Advancing reservoir water quality management by a depth-specific approach integrating Bayesian optimization and machine learning algorithms
abstract: A pioneering depth-specific water quality management method was developed and evaluated at Oman's largest and most strategic dam. Unlike conventional models that depend on costly deep-water sampling, this study introduces a novel surface-to-depth inference framework. We demonstrate a framework where surface measurements of water quality variables (WQVs) combined with geographical coordinates (latitude and longitude) were used to estimate dissolved oxygen (DO) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) at two intake-relevant depths within the reservoir. This novel method uses Bayesian optimization and four machine learning (ML) algorithms: Regression Trees (RT), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Ensemble of Trees (ET). The WQVs were comprehensively monitored at twenty sampling stations across the Wadi Dayqah reservoir, with measurements restricted to a maximum depth of 35 m. At depths of 20 and 25 m, which correspond to the installation locations of the inlet pipes, a stepwise regression analysis was conducted to identify the principal variables affecting DO and Chl-a. The performance of the GPR model in estimating Chl-a and DO at both depths was enhanced by reducing the number of input variables. For DO at a depth of 20 m, the GPR model yielded an R-squared value of 0.88, an RMSE of 0.105, and an MAE of 0.070. Additionally, it demonstrated the highest level of accuracy in estimating Chl-a at the same depth, as supported by its R-squared value of 0.95 and the smallest RMSE value of 0.059. This study serves as a single-reservoir proof-of-concept; generalization of the proposed method requires further validation on additional water bodies with different morphometric characteristics. In addressing reservoir water quality concerns, the outcomes of this study may offer a fresh perspective on implementing water quality management strategies and interventions.

title: A moderated mediation model of sustainable fashion purchase
abstract: Although numerous studies have explored sustainable fashion consumption, most have focused on individual demographic, psychological, or contextual factors in isolation. Limited research has integrated these dimensions to explain how they jointly shape consumer behavior, particularly in the Asian context. This study addresses this gap by examining sustainable fashion purchasing behavior among Hong Kong sustainable fashion consumers using a comprehensive model that integrates the Knowledge-Attitude-Behavior (KAB) model with demographic factors and two contextual variables, namely perceived consequence and product availability. An online survey of 545 respondents was conducted, and the data were analyzed using hierarchical regression and moderated mediation analysis techniques. The results indicated that knowledge, attitude, product availability, age, income, and education were significantly associated with sustainable fashion purchasing behavior. While attitude statistically mediated the association between knowledge on behavior, perceived consequence moderated the attitude-behavior relationship. Within the moderated mediation framework, this study provides insights into how psychological and contextual factors interact to shape sustainable fashion purchasing behavior among sustainable fashion consumers in Hong Kong. The findings underscore the importance of context-specific interventions, such as public education campaigns, improved access to sustainable fashion alternatives, and effective communication, as potentially relevant strategies for promoting sustainable fashion in Hong Kong.

title: Measurement and source analysis of carbon-factor-biased technological progress in China
abstract: Against the backdrop of China's “dual-carbon” targets—peaking emissions by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2060—clarifying the carbon-factor bias of technological progress is crucial. Building on the measurement of the “shadow price of carbon,” which reflects the potential price associated with its scarcity and optimal allocation, this study applies a translog cost function (which characterizes the relationship between production factors and costs) and integrates state-space modeling (depicting the evolution of dynamic systems) to examine the evolution and sources of carbon factor-biased technological progress in China from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal three key insights. First, at the national level, technological progress shows a clear transition from carbon-factor using to carbon-factor saving. Second, across the eight major comprehensive economic zones, distinct regional patterns emerge: in the eastern coastal region, technological progress consistently favors carbon saving, while in the northeast it fluctuates substantially. The remaining six zones follow an evolutionary trajectory in which early technological advances were carbon-factor using but gradually shifted toward carbon-factor saving. Third, the sources of technological progress exhibit differentiated dynamics. Independent research and development has steadily strengthened its carbon-saving effect. Export spillovers briefly rebounded toward carbon use in 2018–2019 but have since shifted decisively toward carbon saving. Import spillovers are predominantly carbon-saving, though with intermittent fluctuations. In contrast, foreign direct investment spillovers historically leaned toward carbon use but are trending toward neutrality over time. Overall, the study uncovers the multi-source drivers and regional heterogeneity of carbon-biased technological progress. These findings provide a scientific basis for formulating differentiated technology policies and for precisely steering low-carbon technological trajectories.

title: Spatiotemporal associations between tourism development and ecosystem service value in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River urban agglomeration and implications for regional regulation
abstract: Global ecosystems are increasingly subjected to intensified human interventions, particularly those associated with tourism activities. As a resource-dependent industry, tourism development (TD) exerts complex and multidimensional impacts on regional ecosystem service value (ESV). This study examines the effects of TD on ESV in the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration (MRYRUA) from 2005 to 2023. A three-tier analytical framework integrating measurement, interaction analysis, and management is constructed. Specifically, a Bayesian Random Effects Regression Model and Interactive Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (IGTWR) are employed to reveal spatiotemporal dynamics and interaction mechanisms. The main findings are as follows: (1) TD in the MRYRUA exhibits pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, forming a core-periphery structure centered on provincial capital cities. The coordination degree of TD evolved through three stages: “low level-rapid improvement-stable optimization”; (2) During the study period, regional ESV declined by 3.16%, displaying a distinct spatial pattern characterized by “higher values in the west and lower values in the east”; (3) TD exerts multidimensional impacts on ESV. Positive interaction effects are observed between road mileage (RM) and the number of star-rated hotels (SRH), between total tourism revenue (TTR) and road passenger transport volume (RPTV), and between the number of tourism employees (NTE) and the proportion of tertiary-sector income (PTR-TSI%). In contrast, negative interaction effects are identified between tourism spatial density (TSD) and RPTV, as well as between tourism revenue as a share of GDP (TTR-GDP%) and RPTV; (4) Based on a static–dynamic integrated zoning approach, six ecological management types are identified. Among them, 14.3% of cities are classified as ecological-tourism critical zones, 17.9% require enhanced ecosystem restoration, and 21.4% require ecological-tourism reconstruction. Overall, this study provides empirical evidence from a rapidly urbanizing region in China and offers scientific support for balancing tourism development and ecological conservation, with important implications for regions facing similar coordination challenges.

title: A wind energy-biomass-coal synergistic system for producing multiple products based on the carbon and nitrogen cycles and its optimization
abstract: A novel clean-chemical production system was introduced to integrate agricultural and industrial processes, utilizing renewable electricity from biomass and wind sources. This system establishes a closed carbon-nitrogen cycle centered on the production of methanol, ethanol, and urea, providing an innovative approach to resource utilization and carbon dioxide mitigation. The configuration comprises a coal and a biomass gasification unit, a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer (PEME), and a nitrogen reduction reaction solid oxide electrolyzer (NRR SOEL) with water. The interactions among these units are optimized to reduce energy losses. A comprehensive analysis was performed to evaluate the system's thermodynamic, economic, and environmental performance. The water footprint of biomass production emerges as a critical determinant affecting both industrial and agricultural carbon-nitrogen cycles. The study examines the impact of varying operating parameters on overall system performance, demonstrating that direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) operate most efficiently at lower temperatures when the current density is low. Multi-objective optimization was conducted to maximize exergy efficiency, minimize the sum unit cost of products (SUCP), and reduce the unit carbon footprint (UCF) using parametric analysis. The optimized system achieves an exergy efficiency of 53.59%, exceeding the average value of 37.6%. Furthermore, the system attains an SUCP of 32.43 $/GJ and a UCF of 0.72 kg/kWh, demonstrating strong energy y and environmental performance.

title: Green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system: conceptual design and parallel multi-objective optimization based on entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis
abstract: Conventional coal-to-chemicals processes suffer from a fundamental hydrogen-to-carbon (H/C) imbalance between carbon-rich coal feedstocks and hydrogen-rich target products. In the context of the global energy crisis and climate change, integrating green hydrogen is a promising approach to adjust the H/C ratio and reduce carbon emissions. A novel green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system is proposed to achieve deep decarbonization and process diversification in the coal-to-chemicals processes. A precise system model is developed in Aspen Plus by combining embedded Fortran subroutines with built-in modules to enable accurate process simulation and entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis. Multi-objective optimization targeting the total entropy generation rate (S˙g), annual energy costs (Cu), and net present value (NPV) is performed using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) in MATLAB for the proposed system. A Parallel optimization framework is proposed to improve computational efficiency. For the proposed system, optimization is completed in 6.5 h, with both the population size and the maximum generation set to 150. The NPV improves by 27.69% after optimization, while S˙g and Cu decrease by 1.42% and 0.11%, respectively, and the carbon utilization rate reaches 99.50%. This study enables advances in decarbonization and diversification in coal-to-chemical processes while providing a robust parallel-optimization framework for complex systems established in Aspen Plus.

title: Mapping carbon flows and future trajectories in China's textile sector
abstract: Rapid textile industry expansion contributes substantially to global carbon emissions, yet critical gaps persist in empirical data, embodied carbon transfer, and long-term decarbonization pathways. This study develops a “Diagnostic-Tracing-Predictive” framework to evaluate the industry's carbon dynamic. Direct CO2 emissions and driving factors are quantified by energy coefficient method, Tapio decoupling analysis, and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI). Embodied carbon flows are traced via environmentally extended multi-regional input-output (EE-MRIO) model and Structural Decomposition Analysis (SDA). The LEAP model simulates multi-scenario decarbonization pathways through 2040. Results indicate a 62.4 Mt emission increase (2003–2022), primarily driven by electricity consumption (72.1%). The sector transitioned from weak (2003–2007) to strong decoupling (2007–2019), followed by fluctuations during 2019–2022. Economic growth was the dominant emission driver, whereas energy intensity served as primary mitigator. Regarding trade flows, embodied carbon in China's textile trade fell from 14.07 Mt in 2012 to 9.69 Mt in 2017. A “production concentration and consumption dispersion” pattern emerged, shifting emissions from eastern coastal to western inland regions. Notably, 73.3% of provinces acted as net carbon exporters in the textile sector, while the proportion in the apparel sector was 73.3%, 76.7% and 66.7% in 2012, 2015 and 2017. Intensity reductions and structural shifts suppressed emissions by 70.4%. Finally, scenario projections suggest that the Technological Progress scenario-integrating clean energy and efficiency innovations-could achieve a 70.5% decrease in emissions by 2040 compared to business-as-usual baseline. These findings provide a framework for designing policy-technology synergies to advance the industry's low-carbon transition.

title: Spatial disparities and policy implications of urban-ecosystem coupling: A case study from the southern China
abstract: Rapid urbanization has intensified ecological degradation and health risks, posing significant challenges to sustainable development, particularly in fast-growing regions. Understanding the spatiotemporal coupling between urban systems and ecosystems is essential for effective spatial planning and environmental management. This study examines the spatiotemporal interaction between urbanization and ecosystem health in the Guangdong section of the pearl river basin from 2000 to 2020. We developed spatial adaptive indices to represent urbanization and landscape health, incorporating diverse indicators through a geographically weighted integration method. A coordination model was applied to assess the degree of alignment between urban growth and ecological performance. Our results reveal a clear pattern of regional divergence: while core cities experienced rapid urban growth and ecological decline in the early 2000s, signs of ecological recovery have emerged in recent years, especially in peripheral areas. The coordination between urbanization and ecosystem health remained unstable in densely built-up zones but improved in transitional regions. Despite external pressures, internal ecological components showed stable synergy, suggesting latent resilience within the system. These findings underscore the need for differentiated, spatially aware planning strategies that align urban development with ecological preservation. The framework introduced in this study provides a practical tool for identifying high-priority areas for policy intervention, supporting more balanced and sustainable development in urbanizing river basins.

title: Evaluation of dual water supply systems using seawater for toilet flushing: Techno-economic and environmental aspects
abstract: Multiple coastal regions worldwide are challenged by limited access to freshwater resources. However, advanced water supply systems can prevent water scarcity and maintain water security in these regions but require identifying potential unconventional sources. A dual water supply system, consisting of two distribution networks conveying freshwater for potable water supply and preliminary treated seawater for toilet flushing, would significantly decrease energy consumption by displacing the demand for desalinated water. This study examined the techno-economic and environmental performance of dual water supply systems in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, compared to the conventional system using multi-stage flash (MSF) or reverse osmosis (RO) desalination, based on hydraulic performance. Despite the dual scenarios consisting of two networks, the excavation was only 14.8% higher compared to the conventional scenario, due to the reduced sizes of the pipelines. A life cycle cost revealed that the dual water supply system using MSF desalination (DWS-MSF) over a 40-year design period generated the highest profit with a net present value (NPV) of $48.4 million and an internal rate of return of 17.4%. The NPV of all scenarios was significantly affected when total revenue and population density were varied by 10% and 50% in a sensitivity analysis. A life cycle assessment determined the environmental impacts of the proposed systems, where the dual water supply system with RO desalination (DWS-RO) was the most sustainable, with a total single score of 136.9. An eco-efficiency analysis demonstrated that the DWS-RO scenario was the most eco-efficient, followed by the DWS-MSF scenario.

title: LSTM-CNN-CBAM-based prediction of NOx emissions with zonal control strategies for flexible peak-load NOx reduction in CFB coal-fired units
abstract: Under deep low-load operating conditions, NOx emissions from circulating fluidized bed (CFB) boilers exhibit pronounced fluctuations, making stable control increasingly challenging. To enhance emission regulation performance, this study first employs the Maximal Information Coefficient, Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to quantify the correlations and time-lag characteristics between operating parameters and NOx emissions, based on which the dataset is reconstructed to better represent combustion dynamics. A hybrid deep learning model integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is then developed to predict NOx formation under various coal-feeding and air-distribution configurations, and its generalization capability is evaluated. The proposed LSTM-CNN-CBAM model achieved superior prediction accuracy (RMSE = 4.30 mg/Nm3), outperforming baseline models like LSTM and LSTM-CNN, and demonstrates a significant advantage over a state-of-the-art Temporal Convolutional Network. Subsequently, an Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III)–based multi-objective optimization framework is established to achieve coordinated optimization of NOx emissions, boiler efficiency, and total coal consumption. For a 350 MW CFB boiler operating at 150 MW (42% load), the optimization results show that 139 Pareto-optimal solutions are obtained under the constraints of NOx ≤30 mg/Nm3 and boiler efficiency ≥87%. Among these solutions, one configuration reduces total coal consumption by 16.6% while maintaining the same efficiency as the historical operation. The optimized strategy features front-wall air staging, rear-wall oxygen-lean conditions, and a differentiated coal-feeding pattern characterized by “lower distribution in the middle and higher levels on both sides,” effectively suppressing NOx formation in the high-temperature core region. Overall, the integration of advanced predictive modeling and evolutionary optimization significantly enhances NOx control accuracy and operational efficiency under low-load conditions, offering a promising pathway for intelligent emission regulation in coal-fired power plants.

title: Balancing market integrity and industrial decarbonization: A GMCR-based strategic conflict resolution framework
abstract: The Carbon Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) is an essential policy tool for promoting corporate efforts to reduce carbon emissions. However, its successful implementation depends heavily on the decarbonization actions of stakeholders involved in carbon markets. Understanding and analyzing the decision-making processes and dynamic interactions among these stakeholders is a complex task. To this end, we propose a novel analytical framework that combines game theory with the Graph Model for Conflict Resolution (GMCR), enabling a thorough analysis of stakeholders’ evolving decision-making behaviors. Additionally, this framework sheds light on how changes in stakeholders’ preferences affect the effectiveness of policies and the stability of the market. The key findings reveal: (1) significant dynamic interdependence among the preferences of the government, emission entities, and verification agencies; (2) decarbonization behaviors demonstrate responsiveness to the level of regulatory stringency for specific stakeholders; and (3) the government encounters greater difficulties in effectively supervising verification agencies compared to emission entities. These insights offer valuable guidance for policymakers aiming to optimize market mechanisms, enhance regulatory frameworks, and support corporate transitions toward clean technologies.

title: Can membrane aerated biofilm reactor (MABR) realize more efficient simultaneous partial nitrification and denitrification than conventional biofilm under low COD/N?
abstract: Simultaneous nitrification and denitrification (SND) is an efficient nitrogen-removal process, yet its application in low COD/N wastewater is limited in conventional co-diffusion biofilms due to carbon source waste and microbial competition. Membrane aerated biofilm reactors (MABR) could theoretically realize more efficient SND by employing counter-diffusion biofilms to separate oxygen and carbon sources. However, the SND efficiencies were not satisfactory in previous publications, possibly because excessive aeration and uncontrolled nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) growth increased the demand for carbon sources. Herein, three MABRs using oxygen-affinity PP-PDMS membranes were operated with an extremely low aeration pressure (0.6 kPa) to initiate SND in high-strength nitrogen wastewater (200 mg/L NH4+-N) with low COD/N (R1: 2; R2: 3; R3: 4). A stable simultaneous partial nitrification and denitrification (SPND) was established in R2 and R3 (TN removal of 73.8% and 79.8%, respectively), which was higher than the reported co-diffusion biofilms. Increased COD/N did not significantly enhance nitrogen removal once SPND was established. Microbiological analysis indicated that ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and archaea (AOA) both contributed to nitrification, and NOB were incompletely suppressed. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and mass transfer calculation revealed that carbon sources inhibited NOB and enhanced oxygen transfer by increasing the oxygen concentration gradient. However, nitrate accumulation and COD waste still occurred and led to a gap between MABR and single denitrification because of the unavoidably high oxygen at the membrane-biofilm interface. Overall, counter-diffusion biofilms outperformed co-diffusion biofilms in TN removal, but entire SPND was still hard to be attained.

title: Effects of biochemical component interactions on molecular transformations in bio-oil during microwave-assisted pyrolysis of protein-rich biomass
abstract: In this study, the interactions between the primary biochemical components of protein-rich biomass (proteins (P), carbohydrates (C) and lipids (L)) and their effects on molecular transformations in bio-oil during microwave-assisted pyrolysis were systematically investigated via pyrolysis of model compounds at different temperatures (400, 600, and 800 °C). Then, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) were employed to analyze the light and heavy components in bio-oil, respectively. Results revealed that over 58 wt% of oxygen was released as gas, while the interactions promoted nitrogen migration into bio-oil. Maximum bio-oil yield and nitrogen content occurred at 600 °C. Moreover, nitrogen-containing compounds (NCCs) dominated the light components (49.67–72.70 area%), with N2-3 species prevalent in the heavy components (33.81–50.20%). Heavy oxygen-containing compounds primarily comprised species with two to five oxygen atoms (76.25–83.47%). Notably, N-heterocycles were abundant in all the bio-oils, with distinct dominant formation pathways in different groups: in P, they mainly originated from deoxygenation of dipeptides formed by amino acid condensation; in PC, from Maillard reactions between carbonyl and amino compounds; and in PL, from amide cyclization. At 800 °C, the heavy components in PC and PL bio-oils exhibited higher unsaturation and aromaticity than those of P bio-oil, attributed to ring-opening of N-heterocycles in P and formation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in PC and PL. This study provides new insights into the molecular transformation mechanisms of bio-oil, thereby advancing the high-value and eco-friendly utilization of protein-rich biomass.

title: Green manure reduces global agricultural carbon footprint by enhancing soil organic carbon stocks: Evidence from global meta-analysis and machine learning assessment
abstract: Green manure (GM) has strategic value in the context of sustainable agriculture and climate change. However, few studies have analyzed the effects of GM on regulating the carbon footprint (CF) through the dynamic coupling of soil organic carbon (SOC) and greenhouse gases (GHG) using the meta-analysis method, and there have also been insufficient assessments of the potential reductions of global emissions based on changes in CF. Thus, by combining global meta-analysis and machine learning predictions, we demonstrated that while GM increases CH4 and N2O emissions by 22.05% and 2.94% respectively, it significantly enhances SOC stocks by 9.59%. This increase in SOC effectively offsets the carbon cost of GHG emissions, reducing the total carbon emissions by 33.37% and CF by 36.23%. Machine learning predictions indicate that GM can reduce the global CF by 42.18%, with notable crop-specific and spatial heterogeneity, where the response is most pronounced in wheat systems (63.30%), weaker in rice systems (19.94%), and negative feedback may occur in regions with high soil fertility. These findings provide a theoretical basis for developing precise carbon management strategies using GM as a global paradigm.

title: Catalytic co-pyrolysis-hydrogenation of lignin and polyolefin waste into biofuels: A comparative energy–environment–economy analysis of hydrogen sourcing strategies
abstract: During the fermentation of lignocellulosic biomass for biofuel, enzymatic hydrolysis lignin (EHL), a byproduct rich in aromatic ring structures, is generated in substantial quantities. Currently, most EHL is directly combusted or co-fired in boilers, resulting in environmental pollution and resource wastage. In this study, EHL and polyolefin waste were co-pyrolyzed to produce bio-oil, which was subsequently upgraded via catalytic hydrogenation to obtain high-quality biofuel. Based on our own experimental data, three H2 supply strategies (designated as Case 1 to 3) were simulated to optimize biofuel production from the co-pyrolysis-derived bio-oil: Case 1 utilized commercially purchased H2, Case 2 employed H2 produced via natural gas reforming, and Case 3 utilized H2 generated through partial reforming of the bio-oil itself. The systems were comparatively analyzed through three complementary methodologies‒life cycle assessment, exergy analysis, and techno-economic assessment‒implemented using eBalance, Aspen Plus, and custom calculations, respectively. Results revealed that Case 3 achieved the lowest biofuel production cost ($0.026 MJ−1) along with the highest exergy efficiency (42.56%), whereas Case 1 demonstrated the lowest environmental impact. Sensitivity analysis based on Monte Carlo simulations identified critical variables related to feedstock characteristics and resource inputs. Multi-criteria analysis was performed by normalizing energy, environmental, and economic indicators. The comprehensive evaluation indexes (CEIs) were calculated by assigning equal weight to energy utilization, environmental impact, and biofuel cost. The resulting CEIs for Case 1, Case 2, and Case 3 were 0.185, 0.231, and 0.172, respectively. The strategy of partial bio-oil reforming for H2 production in Case 3 demonstrates strong application potential.

title: Coordination regulation of non-radical high-valent cobalt-oxo species for simultaneous removal of antibiotics and antibiotics resistance bacteria
abstract: Reactive species regulation is a promising method for organic contaminant decontamination enhancement in advanced oxidation processes, while the regulation strategies and mechanisms through catalyst design still need to be further investigated. In this study, cobalt-doped boron nitride (CoBN) with a Co-N3 coordination structure was successfully prepared via a one-step calcination method, where the optimal parameters were determined as the molar ratio of boric acid to melamine of 2:1, calcination temperature of 700 °C, and cobalt loading of 0.20 wt%. The existence of boron vacancies was confirmed by electron paramagnetic resonance characterization. Using the typical antibiotic of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) as the target pollutant, CoBN demonstrated effective activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS), and the system achieved total SMX removal within 15 min. Mechanistic studies revealed that CoBN and PMS generated high-valent cobalt-oxo species (Co(IV)=O) through a two-electron transfer pathway, which contributed 85% to SMX removal. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrated that the energy required for Co-N3 sites to generate Co(IV)=O with PMS was significantly lower than that required for radical formation. The toxicity of SMX degradation intermediates identified was reduced compared to its parent compound, confirming the ecological safety of this system. Meanwhile, CoBN/PMS system exhibited excellent performance in simultaneous removal of antibiotics and antibiotics resistance bacteria (ARBs), and showed satisfactory potential for practical application as well. This study provides new insights into the precise regulation of reactive species and the efficient treatment of emerging contaminants in water.

title: Metal removal and valorization using Dactylococcopsis salina 16Som2: Insights into metal binding properties and catalytic activity of metal-enriched biomass
abstract: This study explores the dual potential of the cyanobacterium Dactylococcopsis salina for heavy metal removal and its application as a sustainable catalyst. Focusing on the biosorption of Cu(II), Ni(II), and Zn(II), we employed advanced analytical techniques, including SEM-EDX, FT-IR, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy, to elucidate the metal-binding patterns in both cellular and soluble fractions of the cyanobacterium. Cu(II) exhibits the highest biosorption affinity, accumulating in the cellular and soluble fractions at 3.7% and 7.0% (w/w), respectively. Our findings reveal distinct binding preferences for each metal ion, with coordination modes predominantly involving mixed (O,N)-(Cl,S) ligands. The (O,N):(Cl,S) ratio varied significantly based on the metal type, the biosorbent fraction, and the presence of multiple metals, with a ratio close to 0.5 and 0.75 for Cu(II) (fourfold coordinated) in the soluble and cellular fraction, respectively; a ratio close to 0.5, that decreases to 0 when more than one metal is present in the solution for Zn(II) (fourfold coordinated) in both fractions; and a ratio of 1 for Ni(II) (exclusively bonded to O/N in sixfold coordination). The type of biosorbed metal plays a critical role in the determination of catalytic performances: in borylation reactions of α,β-unsaturated chalcones with bis(pinacolato)diboron, Cu(II)- and multimetal-enriched biosorbents demonstrated outstanding catalytic activity (up to 94% conversion efficiency), whereas Zn(II)-enriched samples delivered modest performance. This study thus establishes a direct link between metal-binding chemistry of cyanobacteria-based biosorbents and catalytic functionality, paving the way for tailored catalyst design. By integrating metal remediation and catalyst development, these results contribute to the advancement of cleaner production strategies through resource recovery and waste valorization. Highlights • Cyanobacteria can efficiently remove heavy metals from contaminated waters. • Cyanobacteria have potential as green catalysts in pharmaceutical applications. • Their dual-purpose application reflects circular economy principles. • A detailed atomistic characterization of metal-organic interaction is provided.

title: Towards fossil-free ethylene: ex-ante techno-economic comparison of three alternative processes at low technology readiness levels
abstract: Ethylene production processes using alternative carbon sources like biomass or CO 2 could have great potential for the olefins industry. Comparing the benefits and pitfalls of different process routes is challenging due to the vastly different feedstocks and key conversion technologies involved. Here, we performed an ex-ante techno-economic and environmental assessment to explore potential trade-offs of three low technology readiness level ethylene production processes. The three routes were: 1) biobased syngas fermentation to ethanol followed by ethanol dehydration, 2) direct electrochemical conversion of CO 2 , and 3) indirect CO 2 and H 2 O electrolysis to form syngas followed by a Fischer-Tropsch step. This study found three main takeaways. Firstly, the biobased route significantly outperforms the direct and indirect routes in terms of techno-economic and carbon footprint performance. Secondly, the electrolyzer unit is the main factor limiting the techno-economic performance of the direct and indirect cases, reemphasizing the need for continued technological advancements and cost reductions by researchers in this domain. Finally, the indirect plant design, incorporating two electrolyzers and a Fischer-Tropsch step, is not techno-economically feasible for ethylene production, underscoring the need for further research on Fischer-Tropsch plant designs to advance the replacement of traditional fossil-based refineries.

title: Fenton-derived iron for reversible self-assembly of alginate network: A sustainable strategy for simultaneous antibiotic degradation and microplastic removal
abstract: The concurrent presence of antibiotics and microplastics (MPs) in aquatic environments poses a significant treatment challenge, as conventional approaches largely adhere to a “remove-and-dispose” framework. Herein, we present a sustainable strategy that repurposes iron by-products from Fenton reactions to create functional coordination centers for managing MPs. The newly developed Alginate-Fenton Smart Sequestration (AFSS) system utilizes in-situ generated Fe3+, which is usually considered waste from Fenton process, to cross-link sodium alginate and form a 3D network for effective encapsulation of MPs without the need for additional chemicals. The incorporated reversibility, achieved through biocompatible ascorbic acid, enables the controlled release of MPs, with recovery efficiencies reaching 86% under ambient conditions. The AFSS system demonstrated consistent performance in diverse environmental waters, efficiently degrading antibiotic and maintaining the removal of multiple types of MPs at over 97%. This work establishes a sustainable approach in which residual iron is transformed into a reusable resource for capturing and recovering MPs, thereby advancing water treatment towards circular resource management.

title: Normal pressure transforming kaolinite-rich soil into sodalite for Cd-contaminated soil remediation
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) soil contamination poses a particularly acute threat to public health. While synthetic zeolites have shown promise in immobilizing Cd, their widespread application is hindered by high material costs, energy-intensive synthesis, and reliance on high-pressure reactors. To date, no study has reported the successful transformation of natural kaolinite-rich soil into sodalite zeolite under normal pressure conditions. This study bridges that critical gap by developing a novel, low-cost, and energy-efficient route to synthesize sodalite from kaolinite-rich soil using only a household electric cooker at ambient pressure. Superior to the conventional high-pressure hydrothermal route, it offers significant advantages in terms of material costs, equipment expenses, synthesis efficiency, and energy consumption. Remarkably, this soil-derived sodalite demonstrates exceptional Cd-contaminated soil remediation efficacy. With only 0.3 % sodalite additions (w/w), the proportion of exchangeable Cd species in the soil decreases from 43.2 % to 22.6 %, converting into Fe-Mn oxide-bound and residual forms, effectively diminishing Cd's mobility. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Cd2+ is primarily locked into the framework of sodalite through ion exchange reactions and partially captured on the surface via chemisorption effects. In the state of Cd adsorption saturation, the contribution ratios of ion exchange and chemisorption by sodalite are approximately 78.7% and 21.3%, respectively. Overall, this study develops an innovative normal-pressure sodalite synthesis route using natural soil and further reveals the huge potential of soil resources for zeolite synthesis and contaminated soil remediation.

title: Implementing circular economy and zero-waste strategies in a multipurpose port terminal: Indicator-based evidence from Colombia
abstract: Maritime ports are increasingly expected to reduce waste and resource externalities while expanding throughput. This study reports indicator-based evidence from Palermo Sociedad Portuaria (PSP), a multipurpose terminal in Colombia, showing how circular economy (CE) and Zero-Waste (ZW) strategies can be operationalized using routinely collected registers. Based on 2024 segregation logs, total waste generation reached 1,320,519 kg, dominated by “special wastes”, particularly sweepings (881,560 kg) and residual wood (437,590 kg), with big bags (20,430 kg) as a smaller but material stream. To translate these dominant flows into actionable control points, the program combines: (i) a PDCA-anchored residual-wood sub-method (standardized coefficients, registers, and checklists) to enable traceable monitoring; (ii) a tiered mass-based indicator set distinguishing high-value circular diversion from compliance-driven regulated treatment; and (iii) a 27-measure portfolio mapped to the 9R framework and aggregated into 3R headline groups. The portfolio distribution equals 63% reduction, 22% reuse/repair, and 15% recycling by action counts (weighted: 58%, 27%, 15%). The case delivers a replicable, low-cost toolkit, classification taxonomy, mass-flow indicators, and PDCA routines, that supports prevention-oriented decision-making and progressive benchmarking for multipurpose terminals under rapid growth conditions.

title: Enhancing airworthiness compliance of measurement system for aircraft non-volatile particulate matter emissions and its suitability to sustainable aviation fuel application
abstract: The non-volatile particulate matter (nvPM) emitted by aircraft engines poses significant environmental and health challenges, prompting strict international airworthiness standards. However, previous studies have not sufficiently quantified system-level measurement errors, often directly applying commercial instruments designed for conventional aviation fuel (CAF) to Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAFs). Given that SAF particles exhibit distinct characteristics, including smaller sizes, more concentrated distributions, and unique morphologies, the applicability of existing nvPM measurement systems requires rigorous evaluation. This study comprehensively evaluates the error sources across the dilution, transport, and measurement stages of the measurement chain and proposes compliance enhancement methods, including background pollution purification, instrument calibration, and a particle size distribution (PSD)-based loss correction model. These strategies reduced the uncertainty of the DF1 dilution factor by 73.8% and the relative error of the Condensation Particle Counter (CPC) to 2.124%. Additionally, a PSD-based fitting correction was developed to address penetration losses, achieving a correlation coefficient (R2) exceeding 0.95. Experimental validation using RP-3 and HEFA-SAF demonstrated that these methods effectively improved measurement repeatability and accuracy, reducing the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of the Emission Index (EI) by over 50% and the measurement error by 24%. Notably, the study confirms that SAF exhibits significantly different microscopic characteristics compared to traditional fuel, showing a reduction in peak particle size by approximately 50%, a decrease in number concentration by one order of magnitude, and a more uniform size distribution indicated by reduced Geometric Mean Diameter (GMD) and Geometric Standard Deviation (GSD). However, under high thrust conditions, the higher proportion of ultrafine particles in SAF emissions increases sensitivity to transport losses, highlighting the necessity of expanding the CPC detection limit in future standards and adopting a unified loss correction model based on full particle size spectra. This work provides a validated framework for improving the accuracy of nvPM measurements and supports the integration of PSD into airworthiness certification.

title: Resilient biomass-based CHP system design under uncertainty and customer demand prioritization
abstract: A biomass-supported combined heat and power system (bCHP) has the potential to play a key role in supporting rural and remote communities by providing an alternative power supply during natural disasters. However, the success of such systems depends on how reliably the biomass supply system is designed to support high-priority users (e.g., hospitals, shelters) under both normal and extreme weather conditions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a two-stage stochastic programming model that captures the design and management of a reliable bCHP system under customer demand uncertainty and priority. To solve the model in realistic-sized test instances, we have developed a customized solution technique, namely, Sample Average Approximation enhanced with trust-region cutting planes within a Lagrangian decomposition approach, and tested the performance of this technique in several coastal counties in rural Mississippi. Experimental results provide important insights, both in terms of managing and designing a bCHP supply system as well as the solution efficacy solve such a large-scale model. For instance, results indicate that prioritizing the high-need customers (e.g., hospitals and schools) can reliably increase the demand satisfaction rate in our testing region by nearly 20% while decreasing the power interruption time without significantly compromising the overall network feasibility. Additionally, on average, the proposed customized technique solves a range of practically sized problems nearly 71% faster than the commercial solvers.

title: Digital product passports for cleaner production: Economic evidence from producers and consumers in the fashion industry
abstract: The shift towards sustainable production and consumption presents a critical global challenge, particularly in resource-intensive sectors such as textiles. This study explores the role of the Digital Product Passport (DPP) in enhancing transparency, promoting sustainable consumption, and supporting circular economy practices. Integrating multi-criteria analyses from industry experts with a consumer survey ( n = 415), the research examines producer priorities for circularity adoption and consumer perceptions of digital labelling, sustainability, and willingness to pay. The findings reveal that, while traditional factors such as aesthetics and price remain influential, consumers show strong interest in DPP-enabled transparency and a marked willingness to pay a premium for digitally labelled products. For producers, the DPP functions as a strategic instrument for traceability, lifecycle management, and regulatory compliance. Spanning both domains, the DPP addresses information asymmetries and fosters trust, underscoring its potential to align corporate sustainability strategies with consumer expectations. Offering empirical insights into adoption, perceived benefits, and behavioural effects, the study positions the DPP as a key enabler of informed, responsible, and sustainable fashion consumption. • Information on supply chain traceability is a determining factor. • Raw materials play a decisive role in fashion sustainability. • Sustainable practices do not strongly influence fashion purchases. • The DPP provides consumers with a sense of confidence. • Consumers value DPP and show higher willingness to pay.

title: Coal-to-aromatics process with integrated propane dehydrogenation technology: Benefit analysis and life cycle assessment
abstract: In the momentum of reducing CO2 emission of coal to aromatics (CTA) process, a novel integrated coal-to-aromatics process (CO2-ODHP-CTA) has been proposed. This innovative process combines CO2 utilization with propane dehydrogenation to produce propylene, aiming to identify the optimal pathway for simultaneous CO2 reduction and utilization in conventional CTA processes. By integrating propane dehydrogenation technology, this process enhances feedstock and energy efficiency while simultaneously reducing CO2 emissions. Based on process simulation data, we conducted a techno-economic analysis and environmental assessment of the proposed process, comparing it with the conventional coal-to-aromatics process. The results indicate that the CO2-ODHP-CTA process offers significant techno-economic advantages, with improvements in carbon utilization, hydrogen utilization, and energy efficiency of 28.36%, 68.96%, and 7.61%, respectively, compared to the CTA process. Additionally, the production cost is reduced by 3.08% relative to the CTA process. Additionally, the life cycle assessment results demonstrate the significant environmental advantages of the CO2-ODHP-CTA process. Its global warming potential (GWP) has been reduced to 4.67 kg CO2·kg−1, representing a 49.74% decrease compared to the CTA process. Thus, the proposed process provides a promising way to efficiently utilize CO2 and improve the techno-economic performance of the coal to aromatics industry.

title: Estimating marine atmospheric PM2.5 over the Bohai Sea: Spatiotemporal dynamics under policy transition in China's emission reduction
abstract: Marine regions are increasingly influenced by atmospheric PM2.5 (fine particulate matter), posing significant challenges to ecological sustainability and air quality management. However, limited observational coverage continues to hinder comprehensive assessments of marine pollution dynamics. This study develops a deep neural network model (PM2.5-DNN) to estimate PM2.5 concentrations over the Bohai Sea during 2015–2023, integrating aerosol optical depth, meteorological reanalysis, and temporal indicators. Compared with reanalysis products and Community Multiscale Air Quality model (CMAQ) simulations, the PM2.5-DNN achieved notably higher accuracy (mean fractional bias ≤22.43%, mean fractional error ≤50.93%), enabling robust spatiotemporal evaluations of marine atmospheric PM2.5. The results reveal two distinct stages in response to China's evolving emission reduction strategies. During the end-of-pipe control phase (2015–2017), PM2.5 concentrations over the Bohai Sea declined rapidly (0.39 μg/(m3·month)), accompanied by a marked contraction in the spatiotemporal extent of high PM2.5 concentration episodes (HPCEs). From 2018 to 2023, as end-of-pipe measures reached a technical and economic bottleneck, PM2.5 levels entered a slower decline phase (0.14 μg/(m3·month)). In this period, emission mitigation shifted toward structural and source-oriented controls, effectively suppressing emissions and continuously reducing HPCEs frequency. These findings highlight the effectiveness and evolving nature of China's clean air actions, emphasizing that long-term structural emission reductions yield more sustainable outcomes than short-term end-of-pipe interventions. These results are currently focused on the Bohai Sea, and the framework could be further expanded to include multi-pollutant estimation for broader applicability. The study provides data-driven evidence to support cleaner production strategies and sustainable air quality governance in East Asian coastal regions.

title: Circular economy for social welfare in European NUTS 2 regions: Evaluation of circular strategies and income differences
abstract: This study advances the understanding of circular economy practices by offering a multidimensional assessment of their social welfare impacts across European NUTS 2 regions. It distinguishes between material recycling and energy recovery while accounting for heterogeneity along the income distribution. We examine the institutional hypothesis that circular economies foster inclusive green development by enhancing income and quality of life, particularly among lower-income groups through new market opportunities in circular niches. Using machine learning for feature selection and ranking, together with Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QREG) that incorporates fixed effects and location and scale shifts, we analyze 323 regions over the period 2010–2022. The results indicate that material recycling significantly improves disposable income and reduces social deprivation, with stronger positive effects at lower income quantiles, whereas energy recovery is associated with more limited or adverse outcomes. The findings illustrate how specific circular economy practices translate into differentiated welfare outcomes and provide guidance for regionally tailored green transition policies.

title: Enhanced and sustainable extraction of acetic acid from wastewater using a novel ternary deep eutectic solvent
abstract: Acetic acid is an irreplaceable raw material for the synthesis of key chemicals. However, its production is accompanied by the generation of large volumes of acidic wastewater, posing a significant environmental challenge. The strong polarity of acetic acid and water complicates its separation. The present study examines the effectiveness of binary and ternary deep eutectic solvents (DESs) in extracting acetic acid. A novel ternary DES composed of tri-n-butyl phosphate (TBP), tri-n-octylphosphine oxide (TOPO), and 1-Octanol was successfully synthesized and characterized using spectroscopic techniques. The ternary DES exhibited significantly higher extraction efficiency (up to 73.18 %) than the binary DES (TBP-1-Octanol), underscoring the synergistic effect of the third component. Cyclic extraction experiments demonstrated excellent recyclability, with a single-cycle efficiency loss of less than 2 % after six cycles. Molecular dynamics simulations further elucidated the extraction mechanism. This DES minimizes energy input and solvent emissions, thereby offering a low-energy, low-waste, and environmentally compatible alternative to conventional organic solvents.

title: UCO provides greater carbon reduction potential than plant oils across diverse biodiesel production technologies
abstract: Existing studies typically examine either feedstock choice or production technology, leaving a gap in comprehensive assessments of biodiesel carbon emissions. This study examines the carbon emissions of biodiesel products manufactured from diverse feedstocks and technologies across 21 factories. A life cycle assessment (LCA) is conducted using both mass allocation and energy allocation methods. Most of the carbon emissions of crude palm oil (CPO) and soybean oil (SBO) biodiesel stem from the land use changes (LUC), planting, and oil extraction processes. When system boundaries and allocation methods are kept consistent, feedstock choice causes much larger variations in carbon intensity than the choice of production technology. Recommendations for reducing the carbon emissions of biodiesel include employing ecologically friendly biomass energy, coupling used cooking oil (UCO) and UCO biodiesel production processes, and promoting UCO as feedstock. Substituting CPO or SBO with UCO results in more than a 60% life cycle carbon emissions reduction due to the absence of the mentioned LUC, planting, and oil extraction processes. Selecting an appropriate allocation method has a critical impact on the LCA outcome. Additionally, the carbon emissions of the UCO biodiesel and used hydrodeoxygenating vegetable oil (HVO) biodiesel are 4.11-24.15 g CO2 eq/MJ and 6.54-10.18 g CO2 eq/MJ respectively. The LCA results of UCO and HVO biodiesel are mainly affected by energy and raw material consumption during the collecting and production processes. Deploying UCO as a feedstock for biodiesel can contribute to energy security, generating employment opportunities, and mitigating the environmental burden.

title: From micro-pixels to macro-performance: An explainable machine learning framework for xanthan gum-stabilized expansive soils via AI-assisted trainable weka segmentation
abstract: The transition from carbon-intensive soil stabilizers (cement, lime) to sustainable biopolymers is stalled by a knowledge gap: the lack of quantifiable links between the co-evolution of micro-scale gel structures and pore-network geometry and their collective impact on long-term macro performance. To bridge this gap, this study establishes a “Micro-Pixels to Macro-Performance” framework for Xanthan Gum (XG)-stabilized expansive soils, integrating AI-assisted Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS) with explainable machine learning. High-resolution SEM images were segmented into gel and pore phases via TWS to extract phase-specific features—including fractal dimension (FD), skeletal connectivity, texture entropy, surface roughness and morphology—to quantify the gel-pore interplay across XG dosages (0.5–5%) and aging durations (7–365 days). Results identify gel-phase FD as a magnification-invariant proxy (5–200kx) for material stability, exhibiting robust correlations with Unconfined Compressive Strength, soaked California Bearing Ratio, Swell percent, and compression index. Random Forest and SHAP analyses identify gel-phase FD and Junctions as the primary drivers of strength, outweighing passive pore-filling effects. The study defines a quantifiable “microstructural maturity threshold” at 1.5% dosage and 28–60 days, where the network achieves a structural percolation state (FD > 1.75, Junctions >1700). Validated on an independent expansive soil dataset, these indices offer a transferable tool for sustainable earthworks. Optimized 1.5% XG treatment achieves up to an 84.2% reduction in embodied carbon and a superior Strength-to-Carbon Index (30.4–101.4). By maintaining a lower embodied energy (220.5 MJ/ton), this framework establishes a robust Energy-Efficiency-Carbon nexus, providing a precision-engineered pathway toward cleaner, circular geotechnical practices.

title: Analyzing the phosphorus flow characteristics in China's food system over the past two decades
abstract: Phosphorus (P) is indispensable for global food production, yet its overuse has transgressed planetary boundaries, jeopardizing food security and environmental sustainability. This study quantified P flows and phosphorus use efficiency (PUE) in China's food production-consumption system for over the past two decades and identified the primary drivers of PUE dynamics. Total P input increased from 7.6 to 10.9 Tg yr−1, mainly due to fertilizer application in crop production, while P output rose from 2.6 to 3.3 Tg yr−1.
