Despite a 47.0% increase in P recycling-largely through manure and crop residue reuse-the recycling rate remained relatively stable (60.7-61.5%). Among subsystems, food processing showed the highest PUE (75.2%), and aquaculture the lowest (8.4%). Principal component analysis revealed straw utilization efficiency and post-consumption waste recovery as key PUE determinants. Scenario analysis suggests circular strategies could reduce future P losses by 14.6% by 2050. Low PUE in aquaculture and high animal manure losses indicate the need for integrated management, improved recycling, and infrastructure upgrades. Urban-rural disparities and economic influences underscore the importance of policy support and environmental education. Enhancing urban wastewater treatment offers a substantial reduction in P losses. These findings provide guidance for targeted interventions to maximize P recycling, reduce fertilizer demand, and mitigate environmental impacts.

title: Renewable energy transition in sub-Saharan Africa: Opportunity for wind energy in Djibouti
abstract: Djibouti is an excellent example of a sub-Saharan African nation that struggles to provide the energy required for national demands and no doubt renewable energy has enormous potential here. Djibouti recently launched its first wind farm project in the Ghoubet location. It includes 17 turbines, each with a rating of 3.465 MW and a total capacity of 58.9 MW, directly employing large commercial-scale wind technology. However, due to the untested market and hostile conditions, Djibouti should initially adopt a phased approach to wind pilot projects, utilising wind turbines with smaller capacities, similar to those observed in Ethiopia and Kenya. This study selects two distinct wind turbine designs with smaller capacities—the Nordex N43/600 kW and the Fuhrlander FL MD77/1500 kW—in order to assess the technical and economic feasibility of a 6 MW wind pilot project at the Ghoubet location. Wind data from a meteorological station at the Ghoubet site, taken in 2004 at 10-min intervals, is used in this study. According to the findings, the Ghoubet site offers a suitable class 7 wind regime, with an average power density of 483.8 W/m 2 at a hub height of 10 m, 876.5 W/m 2 at 40 m, 964.1 W/m 2 at 50 m, and 1298 W/m 2 at 100 m, demonstrating that the Ghoubet site is a viable location with considerable wind resource potential suitable for a wind farm. It is observed that ten Nordex N43/600 kW wind turbines, with a capacity factor of 40.8%, can produce 21,462,398 kWh of power annually, while FL MD77/1500 kW due to its larger capacity (57%), produces an annual electricity of 29,596,728 kWh/year. The proposed two turbine types result in a levelized cost of energy ranging from 0.0223/kWh (N43) to 0.0240/kWh (FL MD77). When compared to other installations worldwide, this is highly competitive. Ultimately, it is possible that the wind pilot project will save 13,500 to 19,000 metric tonnes of CO 2 annually if it is implemented.

title: Characteristics and techno-economic analysis of nickel-cobalt-manganese composite oxides produced by the flame synthesis method
abstract: Currently, the lithium-ion battery cathodes are primarily manufactured through the hydroxide precursors by the wet chemistry methods, such as sol-gel, co-precipitation. Alternatively, the oxide precursors of nickel-cobalt-manganese (NixCoyMn(1-x-y)Om, NCMO) produced by the flame synthesis (FS) method offer improved tap density, increased reactivity as well as reduced environmental impact for the manufacturing of next-generation lithium-ion battery cathodes. Yet, the phase composition of the NCMO oxide precursors by FS remains unclear, and the economic and energy assessments also remain uncertain, preventing the wide application of the FS-synthesized cathodes. In the present study, a flat-flame burner with a uniform temperature field was developed to synthesize a variety of NCMO precursors through the FS method, including NCMO523, NCMO622, NCMO811, and NCMO900. The phase compositions of these oxide precursors were characterized, and the chemical formulas were determined as Ni0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O1.2, Ni0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O1.15, Ni0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O1.1, and Ni0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O1.05, respectively. Based on the experimentally-determined phase compositions, the thermodynamic analysis and techno-economic modeling were performed to evaluate economic viability of the FS-synthesized NCMOs. Technical analysis revealed that, comparing to the conventional co-precipitation method, the FS method was able to reduce water consumption by 60% and decrease CO2 emissions by 45%. Economic analysis showed that the FS method offered substantial advantages for producing high-nickel NCMO precursors. Specifically, the minimum production selling price (MPSP) of NCMO811 and NCMO900 were 14.0 $/kg, and 14.3 $/kg, respectively, which were 5.4% and 8.9% lower than those of the hydroxide precursor counterparts. Sensitivity analysis showed that the raw material prices were the most significant factor, with a 25% reduction in input costs lowering the MPSP of NCMOs to 9.0-11.1 $/kg. Overall, the present study indicates that FS is a promising method for producing oxide precursors for lithium-ion battery cathodes. These findings establish FS as a scalable, low-carbon manufacturing solution, which favors greatly the global circular economy and climate neutrality.

title: Bridging policies and practice: Integrated pathways for cleaner urban air and climate co-benefits from road transport
abstract: An integrated assessment of Road Transport Emission Reduction Policies (RTERPs) is presented for Vijayawada, India, combining hierarchical top-down policy pathways with a high-resolution bottom-up framework for vehicular emissions and energy demand. The approach quantifies tailpipe and non-exhaust emissions, indirect CO2 from electricity use, and spatial pollution patterns under Business-as-Usual (BAU) and Alternative (ALT) scenarios for 2025 and 2030. Coordinated RTERPs, including stringent emission standards, cleaner fuels, accelerated adoption of electric and hybrid vehicles, end-of-life vehicle phase-outs, and a targeted Low-Emission Zone (LEZ) along National Highway-16, collectively achieve substantial reductions in PM10, NO2, CO and hydrocarbons. Direct CO2 and black carbon (BC) emissions also decline, producing strong climate and public health co-benefits, while spatially resolved emissions highlight priority road corridors for mitigation interventions. The analysis reveals important energy-emission trade-offs: although electrification reduces petroleum consumption and tailpipe pollution, increased electricity demand (32 GWh/year in 2025; 235 GWh/year in 2030) may generate up to 186,000 tonnes of indirect CO2 in a city with coal-dominated grids. These findings underscore the importance of integrating transport electrification with renewable energy expansion, battery circularity, and supply chain resilience to mitigate upstream emission leakage. The combined modelling framework offers a novel pathway for city-scale decarbonisation, advancing SDG 3.9 (reduced pollution-related health impacts), SDG 7 (clean energy integration), SDG 11.2/11.6 (sustainable and low-impact urban mobility) and SDG 13.2 (climate-responsive planning). Municipal agencies, state transport authorities and power-sector planners can utilise these insights to design coherent policy packages that balance air-quality gains, climate goals, energy sustainability and equitable mobility transitions.

title: Biochar-mediated regulation of gaseous emissions and microbial community during the whole vermicomposting process
abstract: Incorporating biochar into vermicomposting has been verified effective in mitigating gaseous emissions. However, existing research is focused on a single biochar particle size, neglecting the pre-composting phase gas emissions and particle size-dependent responses of earthworm gut microbiota to gaseous emissions. This study explored the effects of biochar particle size (0.05 mm, 0.50–3.35 mm and 3.35–8.00 mm) and dosage (5% and 10%, w/w) on gaseous emission during pre-composting and vermicomposting, as well as underlying mechanisms. The results demonstrated that fine-particle biochar (0.05 mm) applied at a high dosage of 10% (10%SBC) was the most effective in mitigating gaseous emissions during both pre-composting and vermicomposting, reducing total emissions by 40.28% for ammonia, 42.63% for nitrous oxide, and 63.39% for methane. This was accompanied by improved organic matter degradation and nitrogen preservation, with the germination index peaking at 204.11%. The addition of biochar not only achieved gases reduction through adsorption but also altered the potential core microorganism abundance associated with gaseous emissions, including Anaerolinea, Devosia and Gemmatimonas in substrate, and Haliangium, norank_o_Microtrichales and Bacillus in earthworm gut. This type of biochar markedly downregulated mcrA, nirS, and nirK gene abundances while upregulating pmoA-amoA and nosZ, thereby mitigating methane, nitrous oxide, and ammonia emissions. Likewise, it stimulated earthworm reproduction and increased the abundance of Bacillus, potentially contributing to higher carbon dioxide emissions. In conclusion, applying 10% fine-particle biochar effectively reduces methane emissions and nitrogen losses while enhancing compost maturity throughout the vermicomposting process. These findings offer practical guidance for the application of biochar in vermicomposting systems.

title: Regional inequality and labor transitions in China's low-carbon power shift
abstract: The global transition towards renewable energy sources is accelerating, driven by the imperative to address climate change and achieve sustainable development. This paper conducts a comprehensive assessment of the social and economic impacts of transitioning towards carbon neutrality in China's electric power sector, with a particular focus on regional heterogeneity and technological change. This research proposes a power system operations framework that optimizes power generation structure until 2050, as well as evaluating changes in generation costs, and employ a multi-regional input-output (MRIO) model coupled with structural path analyses to track employment impacts and the root causes of employment transfer across sectors and regions over time. Key findings of our study highlight that although the national average power generation cost is projected to rise from 0.366 CNY/kWh in 2020 to 0.43 CNY/kWh by 2050, there exist significant regional disparities driven by differences in energy mix, fuel reliance, and technological structure. The transition toward renewable energy is also producing significant labor market shifts. Nationally, the electricity sector's upstream and direct employment is projected to expand by 1.99 million jobs from 2020 to 2050, with indirect employment in upstream sectors (e.g., coal mining, finance, and services) contributing 1.04 million jobs. While some provinces, such as Guangdong, Sichuan, and Fujian, experience sustained employment growth, others like Shanxi and Shandong show a “peak-then-decline” pattern. Moreover, employment creation is shifting from direct, resource-based effects to complex, multi-layered, and inter-regional pathways driven by manufacturing and service-oriented linkages. These findings emphasize the importance of a just and regionally differentiated energy transition policy, particularly in mitigating the employment risks faced by coal-dependent regions.

title: Comparison of greenhouse gas emission reductions in wood-based plastics production in Japan
abstract: The Japanese government aims to produce and promote 2 million tons of bioplastics by 2030. With 25.05 million hectares of forests, Japan has significant potential to utilize wood as a feedstock for large-scale bioplastic production. In this study, we assessed the sustainability of bioplastics produced from wood in Japan, while focusing on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and the long-term carbon neutrality associated with forest management. Life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted across four scenarios, considering different feedstocks: conventional petroleum (S0), woodchips (S1), woodchips and hydrogen (S2), and captured CO 2 and photovoltaic-produced hydrogen (S3), with S1–S3 being alternative scenarios. A forest management model was employed to ensure a sustainable wood supply and estimate the long-term carbon balance of forest management for bioplastic production. Compared to conventional S0, the alternative scenarios S1 and S2 exhibit higher emissions of 0.68 and 0.60 t CO 2 -eq/t-bioplastics, while scenario S3 emits less 0.72 t CO 2 -eq/t-bioplastic. S1 and S2 were projected to achieve carbon neutrality under the constraint of forest management, with S2 reaching it around 10 years earlier. However, producing 2 million tons of bioplastics domestically is impractical, given the limited artificial cedar forests. Overall, this study presents novel insights into GHG emission reduction within the context of bioplastic production in Japan.

title: Mechanism of efficient selective separation and purification of Cu, In, and Ga in the deep eutectic solvents system
abstract: Conventional CIGS recycling primarily employs acid-base leaching methods. Since In and Ga in the leachate both belong to group IIIA elements with similar ionic radii and charge densities, the traditional process suffers from poor environmental friendliness and a high co-extraction rate of them. Based on the green and sustainable leaching properties of deep eutectic solvent (DES), this work developed a roasting-leaching process that not only allows for the simultaneous recovery of all elements from CIGS but also enables their effective separation. Through systematic experimental optimization, the key process parameters of DES, including solvent composition ratio, temperature, and leaching time, were accurately determined. Combined with leaching kinetics studies, the rate-controlling steps and interfacial reaction mechanisms were revealed. A multi-stage extraction-stripping coupling process was designed to achieve the deep separation of Cu, In, and Ga. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations were employed to decipher the leaching mechanism of DES and the mechanism of selective extraction within it. High-purity products, including CuO (99.36%), In2O3 (99.59%), Ga2O3 (99.43%), and SeO2, were successfully obtained through precipitation and calcination treatments. Moreover, the developed technique achieved high recovery efficiencies of 98.43% for Cu, 99.26% for In, 100% for Se, and 98.23% for Ga. Ultimately, a life cycle assessment revealed that the entire process is environmentally friendly, efficient, and sustainable. The advantages of this work over conventional methods include: (1) enhanced leaching efficiency, (2) highly selective separation of Cu, In and Ga, (3) the sustainable and environmentally benign nature of the DES.

title: Synergistically enhanced foam dust suppressant based on Polyvinyl alcohol acetal crosslinking and hydrogen bond adsorption
abstract: To address the issue of coal dust in mining production, a novel foam dust-suppression material was developed in this study by leveraging the synergistic effect of glutaraldehyde (GA)-induced polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) self-crosslinking and the hydrogen-bond association network formed with sodium lignosulfonate (LS). The results show that the acetal reaction can consume the hydroxyl group on PVA and enhance water resistance of the polymer. The “stiff-tough balance” interpenetrating network with GA as the bridge improves the mechanical properties of the material, the average surface hardness is as high as 78 HA, and the dust suppression efficiency of 10 min wind erosion and rain resistance test is more than 96 %. The anionic nature of aliphatic alcohol polyoxyethylene ether sodium sulfate (AES) synergizes with the sulfonic acid groups of LS, which significantly improves the wettability and foam properties. This study will provide a practical and feasible new scheme for the application of PVA in foam dust suppression.

title: An automated pavement maintenance decision-making optimization model for sustainability of performance, cost and environment
abstract: Existing pavement maintenance decision-making optimization models lack connectivity and sustainability when solving two adjacent short planning period plans; the solved long planning period plan does not pay attention to the maintenance plans of the previous years of the planning period. Currently, there is no method that comprehensively considers both the short-term and long-term development of pavement when solving maintenance plans in a single step. To solve these problems, this study proposed a three-stage cyclic pavement maintenance decision-making optimization model. This model improved the first stage of a two-stage optimization algorithm and introduced time-level optimization using a sliding planning period. The model includes segment-level optimization, network-level optimization, and time-level optimization. The model was solved for one case using backtracking algorithm and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The results show that the improvement of segment-level optimization can increase the alternative paths of network-level optimization and improve the model's ability to find the optimal; Compared with the existing two-stage model, the effect of maintenance plan solved in one go by this model is similar to that of the maintenance plans for the long and short planning periods solved separately by the existing model, and can comprehensively consider the short-term and long-term development of the pavement at one go. Overall, the model realizes the sustainability of pavement performance, cost and environment in pavement maintenance decision-making optimization, providing a more reasonable automated pavement maintenance decision-making optimization model for pavement management system.

title: Multi-objective supply chain optimization for cost reduction and environmental sustainability in porcelain manufacturing
abstract:
Purpose
The porcelain manufacturing industry faces the critical challenge of balancing cost efficiency with rising environmental concerns and growing consumer demand for health-conscious products. Although multi-objective optimization (MOO) offers a potential solution, many existing models fail to integrate product quality, explicitly compare production methods, and are rarely validated with real-world data. This study addresses these gaps by developing an MOO model to simultaneously minimize total costs, reduce environmental impact, and maximize the delivery of health-compliant products within a porcelain supply chain.
Design/methodology
A multi-objective Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is developed to optimize strategic and tactical decisions, including raw material procurement, selection between traditional (M1) and sustainable (M2) production methods, production scheduling, inventory control, and multi-period distribution planning. The model is implemented and solved using the ε-constraint method within the GAMS (General Algebraic Modeling System) environment. Its validity and practical relevance are demonstrated through a comprehensive real-world case study of an Iranian porcelain manufacturer (the “Taqdis Brand”), based on detailed operational data.
Findings
The results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively identifies an optimal solution, achieving balanced performance across all objectives with an aggregated score of 0.397. Critically, the sustainable production method (M2) is chosen exclusively, yielding a total cost of 19,906,710, an environmental impact of 759,100, and the delivery of 1586 health-compliant units. This result indicates that shifting to sustainable practices can significantly reduce ecological footprint (by an estimated 20–30% per industry benchmarks) without prohibitive cost increases, while successfully maintaining product quality.

title: Integrated techno-economic and environmental assessment of lithium-ion battery recycling in Chile
abstract: The rapid global expansion of electric vehicles (EVs) is a key pillar of transport decarbonization but also intensifies pressures on critical material supply, battery manufacturing, and end-of-life (EOL) waste management. While lithium-ion battery (LIB) recycling has been widely studied, most existing assessments focus on mature markets and rely on deterministic approaches, limiting their applicability to emerging economies under uncertainty. This study develops an integrated framework to evaluate the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of a circular LIB value chain. The framework combines a hybrid EV adoption forecast, Weibull-based EOL battery estimation, chemistry-resolved mass balance, and techno-economic and environmental simulation using the EverBatt platform, complemented by Monte Carlo risk analysis. The methodology is applied to Chile as a representative case of an emerging EV market. Results indicate rapid EV adoption, reaching 50% market share by 2036 and generating more than 80 kt of EOL batteries annually by 2045. Hydrometallurgical recycling reduces the production cost of NMC 811 cells by approximately 46% and lowers cost volatility by 37%. Environmental benefits include reductions of 24.4% in fossil fuel use, 78% in sulfur oxide emissions, and 22.3% in greenhouse gas emissions, at the expense of increased water consumption. The proposed 80 kt yr−1 facility shows robust financial performance, with median NPV between $589 and $653 million and IRR of 56–69%. The framework provides a transferable tool to support investment and policy decisions toward circular and low-carbon battery value chains.

title: Coupled evaluation of the pros and cons of fluorochemical industry for sustainable development
abstract: The fluorochemical industry, critical for advanced technologies like lithium-ion batteries and aerospace materials, emits emerging pollutants such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and fluorinated gases (F-gases), which pose severe environmental and health risks despite global regulations. In this study, we proposed a coupled evaluation to evaluate the pros and cons (trade-offs) between environmental impacts and socio-economic benefits of fluorochemical industry. The co-emission dynamics of PFAS and F-gases were examined across the fluorochemical industrial chain—upstream (fluorspar mining), midstream (refrigerants, fluoropolymers), and downstream (applications). A novel co-monitoring framework was established to better promote the monitoring efforts. Stakeholder analysis highlights ongoing debates between scientists, industry leaders, and policymakers over balancing economic benefits with environmental responsibility. Through sentiment analysis we mapped impacts fluorochemical industry to 28 targets of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), results highlighted that the fluorochemical market bolsters SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, Infrastructure) through innovations while exacerbates SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) challenges, underscoring the need for enhanced emission controls. This study provides actionable policy recommendations, advocating targeted restrictions and global cooperation to balance economic growth with environmental sustainability, offering a transformative approach to managing fluorochemical industry impacts.

title: Sustained polyhydroxyalkanoate recovery from fermentative food wastewater in a one-stage mixed microbial culture system under aerobic dynamic discharge strategy: Effects of organic loading rate and substrate composition
abstract: In this study, a one-stage mixed microbial culture (MMC) system coupling Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA)-accumulating microbial proliferation and PHA production was developed under the aerobic dynamic discharge strategy for PHA recovery from fermentative food wastewater. The system achieved rapid start-up at an organic loading rate (OLR) of 4.5 g COD/L/d). As OLR increased to 6.0 g COD/L/d, the PHA content reached 0.64 g PHA/g VSS, with 20.4% of the organic flux directed toward PHA synthesis. The combined density-selective and substrate-limiting pressures continuously washed out non-PHA-accumulating microbes and enriched PHA-accumulating microbes such as Gemmobacter (24.3%) and Microbacterium (16.9%). Long-term operation at this OLR did not reduce PHA content in the sludge. However, this operation stimulated extracellular polymeric substance secretion by PHA-accumulating microbes, leading to non-filamentous bulking and sludge loss. As the substrate composition shifted from short-chain volatile fatty acids to medium-chain caproate, the system first exhibited a metabolic lag stage. After this lag, the functional genes encoding long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase and enoyl-CoA hydratase were predicted to be enriched, leading to a reconfiguration of the PHA synthesis pathway from PHBV to PHH production. This metabolic shift was accompanied by the enrichment of Millisia and Rhodobacter. The PHA polymers recovered during the stable phase exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, highlighting their potential as bioplastic materials. These results provide new insights into the response of a one-stage MMC system to various operational conditions for sustained PHA production.

title: Integrated microwave pretreatment and bioelectrochemical system for sustainable biodegradation of low-density polyethylene waste
abstract: Plastic waste, particularly low-density polyethylene (LDPE), remains highly persistent in the environment due to its chemically stable and hydrophobic structure, resulting in extremely limited biodegradability. Although microwave-assisted oxidation and bioelectrochemical systems (BESs) have individually shown potential to enhance polymer degradation, their combined application for accelerating anaerobic LDPE biodegradation has not yet been explored. In this study, we developed a novel integrated system that couples microwave pretreatment with bioelectrochemical stimulation to overcome the intrinsic recalcitrance of LDPE. Microwave irradiation induced surface oxidation and structural modification, improving microbial accessibility, while electroactive biofilms enhanced microbial metabolism and promoted further breakdown of the polymer. The integrated system achieved an 11.7% LDPE weight loss and 100 mL of biogas production over 45 days—significantly outperforming microwave-only pretreatment (6.7%) and electrochemical stimulation alone (0.31%), thereby confirming a distinct synergistic effect. FT-IR, SEM, and microbial community analyses verified the formation of oxidized functional groups and the enrichment of electroactive, plastic-degrading taxa under combined treatment conditions. Overall, this study provides the first empirical evidence that microwave-induced modifications can enhance BES-driven anaerobic plastic degradation. The proposed integrated strategy offers an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable technology for managing persistent plastic waste, supporting future development of cleaner production and circular resource recovery systems.

title: 3D-printed fish-scale dam-like structured photothermal evaporators based on thiol-ene click chemistry for solar-driven freshwater production and salt recovery
abstract: Solar-driven interface evaporation technology provides a new solution for industrial wastewater treatment. The aim of this study is to combine 3D printing technology with thiol click chemistry reaction to accurately manufacture five fish scale dam-shaped evaporators within 40 min and successfully integrate carbon materials into the printed structure, giving it excellent photothermal performance. The evaporator utilizes pentaerythritol tetra (3-mercaptopropionate) (PEGDA) and polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PETMP) to construct a porous polymer network via thiol-ene click chemistry and carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs-COOH) as photothermal material. Inspired by the multi-layered structure of fish scale dams to enhance light scattering and reflection, prolong the residence time of water on the surface of photothermal materials, and utilize gradient structure to generate the Marangoni effect, achieving cross-scale coupling of solar energy utilization and fluid regulation, significantly improving evaporation efficiency. Under one solar intensity condition, the evaporation rate of the evaporator is 1.704 kg m−2 h−1, and the photothermal conversion efficiency is 88.93%. It can stably treat water containing different salinities and other various wastewater purification circumstances. The collected water meets relevant drinking water standards. When treating high-salinity printing and dyeing wastewater, the salt collection rate is 0.1742 kg m−2 h−1, and the water collection rate is 0.72 kg m−2 h−1. This biomimetic photothermal evaporator provides an efficient and sustainable solution for the purification of high-salinity wastewater and industrial wastewater.

title: Decarbonizing fossil-to-chemicals conversion: reliable real-time optimization under coupled chemical and carbon capture dynamics
abstract: Decarbonizing fossil-to-chemicals conversion—by enabling reliable real-time optimization under coupled chemical and carbon capture dynamics—provides a critical pathway for refinery-scale decarbonization. Integrated crude oil catalytic cracking (COCC) and post-combustion carbon capture (PCC) systems can achieve over 90% CO2 reduction, but their full potential is limited by surrogate models that learn spurious correlations, leading to unstable operation and inefficient energy coordination in green energy integration architectures. In COCC-PCC, changes in carbon capture conditions should not influence cracking yields, yet standard Deep Neural Network (DNN) erroneously learn such non-causal relationships due to violated process topology. This work addresses this barrier in refinery green transition by proposing a Causal Structure-Constrained Cascade Neural Network (CSCNN). CSCNN addressed the knowledge gap in reliable optimization for energy integrated systems by embedding directed graph constraints to ensure decisions align with material conservation laws, unlike conventional methods that treat process variables statistically. CSCNN eliminates non-causal interactions, enhances interpretability, and facilitates reliable multi-objective optimization. Applied to COCC-PCC, CSCNN reduces optimization time from 2 to 3 h to under 1 min, increasing propylene yield by 6.7%, and achieving CO2 purity of 99.9%. This approach redefines how energy integration systems can be optimized under uncertainty, ensuring that AI-driven decisions support—not compromise—the reliability and sustainability of green refinery transitions.

title: Comparing greenhouse gas emission accounting tools for organic dairy stakeholders
abstract: Dairy farms have established net-zero goals to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the U.S. requiring accounting of GHG predictions to assess progress. Tools such as Cool Farm Tool (CFT) and COMET-Farm are available to estimate farm-level GHGs, but the outputs from these calculators have not been evaluated for organic dairies. This study compares GHG estimates from 14 organic dairy farm scenarios using CFT, COMET-Farm, and a partial life cycle assessment (LCA) model in four regions of the U.S. Multiple data adjustments were required to compare GHGs from these different accounting tools. Intensities of GHGs are greater for CFT while the LCA and COMET-Farm produce similar results (CFT: 0.97–1.77, LCA: 0.84–1.50, COMET-Farm: 0.83–1.60 kg CO 2 -eq/kg of fat and protein corrected milk (FPCM)). Enteric methane (CH 4 ) accounts for 42–69% of GHGs for all tools and scenarios. Manure management CH 4 and crop production nitrous oxide (N 2 O) constitute the next most prominent sources of GHGs after enteric CH 4 contributing 1–23% and 4–18%, respectively. Crop production GHGs are primarily from manure application N 2 O emissions and are higher in scenarios with greater land use. COMET-Farm is not an LCA tool and does not account for GHGs from materials produced off-farm or express results per functional unit, thus limiting applicability to larger reporting needs. Although the three tools generally agree on trends in enteric CH 4 emissions, estimates can differ by up to 26%, and discrepancies in manure-related emission estimates are even larger. As a result, the estimated impact of a mitigation practice can vary considerably across tools, even when the same practice is evaluated.

title: CO2-activated supplementary cementitious materials: Microstructural densification, mechanical enhancement, and life cycle assessment of carbonated mortars
abstract: Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) contributes about 7-8% of the world's carbon dioxide emission which necessitates the development of low-carbon high-performance cement alternatives. The cement and concrete industry have high potential to minimize the emissions by substituting cement in part with supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) including Fly Ash (FA), Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag S), and Limestone Powder (LP). Nevertheless, the low reactivity of these materials at early age is a key gap in knowledge. The present study fills a critical knowledge gap through a scientific study of the synergistic impact of SCM's carbonation pretreatment combined with accelerated carbonation curing, a two-step method employed to enhance reactivity, strength, and CO2 sequestration of blended mortar. FA, S, and LP were pretreated at 0.5 bar for 3 h and blended with OPC at 15-30% replacement, with the subsequent curing at 0 to 5 h CO2 exposure. Results revealed that the carbonation pretreatment transformed Ca-bearing phases into finely dispersed CaCO3, enhanced particle reactivity. Moreover, 3 h carbonation curing yielded optimal mechanical performance, increasing dry density by 1-5% and compressive strength by 7-12%, while reducing water absorption by 5-8%. In contrast, the 5-h carbonation duration achieved the maximum CO2 sequestration. Furthermore, microstructural analyses (XRD, TGA–DTG, SEM) confirmed portlandite consumption, carbonate formation, and matrix densification. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) demonstrated up to 27% lower Global Warming Potential (GWP) compared to OPC mortar. Hence, the results establish carbonation pretreatment coupled with CO2 curing as an effective pathway to produce low-carbon, high-performance cementitious materials suitable for sustainable construction.

title: Enhanced immobilization of heavy metals in cement using functionalized chitosan: Leaching reduction and performance improvement
abstract: Cement products derived from co-disposal in cement kilns have a high content of heavy metal ions (HMs). Long-term environmental exposure risks the leaching of HMs, causing secondary pollution. In this study, aminothiourea combined with tetraethylenepentamine modified chitosan material (ATC) was synthesized and incorporated into cement to immobilize HMs (Zn2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+). The effects of ATC on HMs-containing cement and the stability of HMs within the matrix were systematically examined. Adsorption experiments confirmed the superior capacity and stability of ATC for Zn2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ uptake under acidic conditions. XPS analysis further indicated that the adsorption mainly involved complexation between HMs and the functional groups (hydroxyl, amino, and thiourea) on the modified chitosan. Furthermore, measurements after 28 days of curing showed more than a 20% reduction in the leaching concentrations of Zn2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+. Adding ATC reduces the proportion of HMs in exchangeable (Q1), carbonate-bound (Q2), and iron/manganese oxide-bound (Q3) states, increases the organically-bound (Q4) proportion, and thus stabilizes HMs in the cement. Mechanical tests showed that ATC increased the compressive strength of HMs-containing mortar by 29.0% and 20.2% at 3d and 7d, respectively. This improvement stems from ATC adsorbing HMs, thereby mitigating their retardation of early cement hydration. XRD patterns and hydration heat results demonstrated that ATC alleviates the early hydration delay and promotes the formation of early hydration products.

title: A multiscale study on the molecular mechanisms of surfactants that enhance the wettability of coal dust and the efficiency of droplet coagulation
abstract: Surfactants are widely applied in mine dust control; however, the intrinsic mechanism by which microscopic physicochemical properties determine macroscopic wetting performance remains not fully elucidated, limiting the rational design of high-efficiency reagents. To address this, this study employs a multi-scale approach integrating macroscale experiments, mesoscale dust-droplet collision modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to systematically reveal the wetting performance differences and multiscale mechanisms of four typical surfactants: SDS, AES, APG, and DTAB. Macroscale experiments, including surface tension measurements and spray-based dust suppression tests, established the wetting performance order as SDS > AES > APG > DTAB. Mesoscale collision simulations elucidated how droplet physicochemical properties, velocity, and size govern the encapsulation and wetting efficiency of coal dust. Molecular simulations quantitatively revealed the intrinsic correlation between wettability and the interfacial hydration layer structure and hydrogen bond network. Critically, we identified that the intensity and spatial distribution of the electrostatic potential extrema within the hydrophilic head group region are the key determinants of the capacity and quantity of water molecule adsorption. These findings not only clarify the cross-scale mechanisms of coal dust wetting but also provide a crucial theoretical basis for shifting from traditional empirical trial-and-error to the rational screening and design of surfactants based on electronic properties.

title: How carbon emissions shape sustainable investment returns: Evidence from a quantile-on-quantile analysis
abstract: This study examines the nexus between carbon emissions and sustainable investment returns in the United States, specifically clean energy equity, green bonds, ESG equity, and ESG bonds. By introducing a novel quantile-on-quantile correlation (QQC) approach, as well as, applying the quantile-on-quantile Granger causality (QQGC) method, using daily data over the period from 2019 to 2025. The results show that the relationship between carbon emissions and sustainable asset returns is concentrated in the tails of the return distributions rather than around average performance. For clean energy and ESG equities, emissions are strongly associated with both downside and upside extremes, indicating heightened risk during adverse conditions alongside opportunities for exceptional gains. In contrast, ESG and green bond returns exhibit weaker and asset-specific tail dependence. Causality results further indicate that low-to-moderate emission levels predict increased downside risks across asset classes, whereas extreme emission states forecast strong positive outcomes in the upper tails of equity returns. Overall, the findings suggest that carbon emissions function simultaneously as a source of systemic tail risk and a signal of transition-related investment opportunities, underscoring the importance of distribution-sensitive risk management and carbon-aware portfolio strategies in sustainable finance.

title: Modeling rebate-based strategies for circular construction material sourcing policy development
abstract: A major barrier to circular construction practice at scale is the disconnect between materials recovered from deconstruction and their reintegration into new building projects. This paper investigates how economic and social drivers, such as financial incentives and risk perception, can be modeled to inform policies promoting the adoption of salvaged building materials. A rebate-based incentive is tested using the Integrated Material Sourcing (IMS) Framework to evaluate how financial incentives influence the uptake of salvaged materials in new construction projects. The IMS model was tested on a designed fourplex building, where the flooring demand of four residential units was used to simulate sourcing decisions. The model optimizes material selection by factoring in cost, embodied energy, and perceived risk, while also introducing a rebate incentive in which cost-matching subsidies are offered for salvaged materials. The results show that rebates can substantially increase the uptake of salvaged materials, but their effectiveness diminishes under conditions of high-risk aversion, in which case mandates might be a more effective policy tool. This study highlights the lack of downstream policies for reintroducing salvaged materials and demonstrates a model that can guide decision makers in tailoring strategies to support circularity in construction.

title: MSME sustainable performance in India's circular economy: Networks, innovation, and institutional enablers
abstract: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are central to circular economy transitions but often lack resources and coherent institutional support. Drawing on the resource-based view, dynamic capability logic, and institutional theory, this study examines how collaborative network engagement and sustainable innovation capability shape MSME sustainable performance, and how these relationships are conditioned by access to green finance and the regulatory environment. Survey data from 418 Indian MSMEs were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings indicate that collaborative network activities and sustainable innovation power have great positive influence on sustainable performance. The moderation analysis indicates that access to green finance enhances performance influence of working on collaborative network engagement but surprisingly lowers the influence of sustainable innovation capability thus a discrepancy persists among the prevailing green finance interventions and MSME innovation processes. Regulatory pressure and support, on the contrary, enhance the advantages of both collaborative networks and innovation capacity. The research develops theoretical integration within resource-based, dynamic capability and institutional approaches, and presents practical implications on the part of policymakers, financial institutions and managers who aim to develop congruent regulatory and financial facilitation that maximizes MSME role in circular and sustainable development.

title: Integrated environmental and economic efficiency assessment of lithium extraction processes in China: An LCA-TCM-DEA framework
abstract: With the rapid growth of lithium demand across diverse resources and extraction technologies, developing environmentally sustainable and economically viable pathways is crucial for ensuring long-term supply security. Previous studies have often focused on individual processes or resource types, with inconsistent assessment conventions that limit cross-comparability. An integrated framework combining life cycle assessment (LCA), a technical-economic cost model (TCM), and data envelopment analysis (DEA) is developed using China-based industrial inventories and key cost parameters. A unified functional unit and system boundary are defined to ensure cross-process comparability across environmental, economic, and integrated efficiency dimensions. Results indicate: (1) Environmental performance: it was found that the adsorption-chemical precipitation process exhibits the lowest impacts. Along lepidolite routes, impacts are driven primarily by acid and alkali reagents, whereas brine routes are dominated by electricity use. (2) Economic performance: sulfate roasting process achieves the highest profitability under current market conditions and is highly dependent on byproduct valorization, whereas brine routes are generally less profitable. (3) Integrated efficiency: adsorption-chemical precipitation and sulfate roasting lie on the efficiency frontier, while other processes achieve lower scores. Therefore, a differentiated pathway is recommended: prioritize sulfate roasting to secure near term supply, fast-track adsorption-chemical precipitation to bankable economics before scaling, and confine sulfuric-acid leaching to upgrades with strict caps on new capacity.

title: Asphalt-rubber interaction in crumb rubber modified asphalt: a review
abstract: This paper reviews asphalt-rubber interactions from macroscopic, microscopic, and molecular perspectives, and discusses solutions for high viscosity and poor storage stability in crumb rubber-modified asphalt (CRMA). Crumb rubber (CR) interacts with asphalt through swelling and degradation, where swelling is a physical process that enhances high- and low-temperature performance, while degradation is a chemical process that generally reduces high-temperature resistance but improves low-temperature properties. The dominant interaction influencing CRMA performance is determined by CR characteristics, asphalt composition, and CRMA production conditions. The basket drainage method and molecular simulations provide insights into the affinity between CR and asphalt components. Strategies to reduce viscosity or improve storage stability include production control, warm mix additives, oil pre-soaking, CR devulcanization, grafting, and polymer additives. These methods either accelerate swelling or promote degradation, affecting viscosity, stability, and thermomechanical performance. Developing kinetic models for CR swelling and degradation, linking them to performance, and identifying consistent solutions for viscosity reduction and stability improvement are crucial for advancing CRMA application from recycled tires for sustainable infrastructure.

title: Ultrasonic-assisted water washing dechlorination modified coal-based activated carbon and its adsorption performance for dyes
abstract: Shaerhu coal is an ideal raw material for the preparation of high-performance activated carbon due to its high carbon content, excellent reactivity, and low sulfur content. However, its high chlorine content will produce polluting gases during the preparation of activated carbon, aggravate equipment corrosion and affect product performance. This study employs liquid-phase thermal conduction coupled with an ultrasonic intensification field as an external driving enhancement method, assisting the leaching agent in overcoming traditional mass transfer limitations, thereby achieving efficient and clean removal of chlorine from high-chlorine coal. It investigated the influence mechanisms of coal sample particle size, washing environment, and ultrasonic intensity on the removal efficiency of chlorine in high-chlorine coal. The results indicated that the ultrasonic-assisted water washing method achieved the best removal efficiency of 98.51% of the chlorine in the coal with particle size less than 0.50 mm under the optimized conditions of ultrasound power of 120 W, solid-liquid ratio of 3 g/100 mL, washing temperature of 60 °C, and washing time of 120 s. The activated carbon prepared after dechlorination showed excellent adsorption performance for methylene blue, and the adsorption rate was 99.91%, which was 12.63% higher than that before dechlorination. The modification process deeply removed the chlorine-containing components present in the precursor material, unblocked the surface pore channels, increased the specific surface area, and provided more active sites for the adsorption of methylene blue. This study proposes a novel approach for the removal of chlorine from multi-particle size high-chlorine coal, verifies the feasibility of preparing high-performance activated carbon from high-chlorine coal for the removal of methylene blue.

title: The potential of mixotrophic denitrification for N2O mitigation: Insights from the perspective of electron distribution
abstract: Mixotrophic denitrification (MDN) has emerged as a promising nitrogen removal technology for wastewater treatment plants, due to its low carbon source costs and minimal sulfate discharge. While denitrification is recognized as effective in reducing N2O emissions, the specific mitigation potential of MDN remains unclear. This study investigated the N2O mitigation capacity and electron distribution of MDN, revealing its significant potential and strong resistance to shock load for N2O mitigation. The maximum N2O-N reduction rate observed was 519.7 mg N/(gVSS × h), significantly surpassing the maximum NO2−-N reduction rate (101.3 mg N/(gVSS × h)), underscoring the effectiveness of MDN in mitigating N2O emissions. Despite electron competition from nitrogen oxides inhibiting the N2O-N reduction rate, MDN maintained a higher N2O-N consumption rate than production. Notably, MDN exhibited stable N2O mitigation performance via electron distribution toward N2O reductase. It shows no statistically significant shift change under a 50% reduction in organic carbon or sulfur supply. Additionally, optimal performance, with maximum nitrogen removal efficiency and superior N2O reduction potential, were achieved at a COD/N ratio of 2.5 and an S/N ratio of 4.6. Economically, this strategy reduced dosing costs of chemical input costs by 26% compared to heterotrophic denitrification. Overall, this study provides fundamental insights into electron flow during MDN, demonstrating its significant potential for N2O mitigation under tested conditions and offering a theoretical basis for future development of efficient N2O mitigation strategies.

title: Topography and rural settlement control the evolution of sloping cropland toward diversity—evidence from the Three Gorges Reservoir Area over half a century
abstract: Sloping cultivated land serves as a critical agricultural resource in mountainous areas, and its transformation and management are vital for food security and sustainable development. This study employs the Caotangxi watershed in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area as a case study, establishing a theoretical framework to examine the dynamic evolution of sloping cultivated land from 1965 to 2023. Key findings include: (1) A significant reduction in sloping cultivated land area over the study period; (2) Sloping cultivated land located at high altitudes, on steep slopes, and far from rural settlements was mostly converted to woodland, grassland, or abandoned slope cultivated land, while land at low altitudes, on gentle slopes, and near settlements was primarily transformed into economic fruit forests; (3) Three distinct evolution patterns were identified: eco-economic synergy, abandonment-restoration alternation, and ecology-dominated transformation. The study indicates that the transformation of sloping cultivated land is driven jointly by policies, topography, and rural settlements. Policy direction determines the necessity of transformation, while topography and settlement distribution constrain policy implementation, thereby influencing transformation pathways and the spatial differentiation of agricultural landscapes. This research provides scientific insights for ecological conservation and agricultural development in similar mountainous regions.

title: Process parameter optimization for greenhouse gas mitigation during green-waste composting and mechanistic insights from microbe–environment networks in treatments with contrasting outcomes
abstract: Green waste (GW) is one of the fastest-growing fractions of urban solid waste, and aerobic composting offers a sustainable pathway for its valorization. However, greenhouse gases (GHGs) emissions remain a critical environmental challenge. In this study, we applied a three-factor, three-level orthogonal design to evaluate the interactive effects of particle size, feedstock ratio, and aeration rate on compost maturity, nutrient retention, and GHG mitigation. The treatment with a 15 mm particle size, a 3:1 feedstock ratio (GW:chicken manure), and an aeration rate of 0.4 L min−1·kg−1 (CT4) achieved the best overall performance. Compared with other treatments, CT4 reduced CO2, N2O, and CH4 emissions by 4.07%, 53.07%, and 20.89%, respectively, resulting in a 46.94% decrease in total global warming potential (GWP), while ensuring high compost quality. Orthogonal and correlation analyses identified particle size as the dominant factor controlling GHG fluxes: medium particles were associated with reduced CO2 and N2O emissions, whereas larger particles were more effective in suppressing CH4 emissions. Microbial functional predictions and co-occurrence network analysis revealed that CT3 exhibited intensified carbon and nitrogen metabolism, forming complex microbe–environment feedback loops that amplified GHGs emissions. In contrast, CT4 maintained moderate metabolic activity and a simplified microbial network, with GHG emissions primarily regulated by the internal metabolic balance and showing only a single association with Sphingobacterium. These findings clarify how process parameters shape microbial network structure and function, providing mechanistic insights and guidance for the optimizing low-carbon, high-efficiency GW composting.

title: Performance and emission assessment of biogenic syngas -hydrogen blends for internal combustion engines
abstract: The growing need for sustainable energy solutions is accelerating the search for alternative fuels for internal combustion engines (ICEs), with hydrogen and pyrolysis-derived gases emerging as promising candidates. This study explores the potential of syngas produced from biogenic waste, enriched with different proportions of hydrogen, as a fuel for ICEs. Experiments were conducted on a turbocharged four-cylinder direct injection (DI) engine adapted for hydrogen operation to evaluate a range of pyrolysis gas-hydrogen blends. To ensure accurate and repeatable testing, a custom-built gas mixer was developed and validated to dynamically control the fuel composition during operation. The investigation focused on combustion behaviour, thermal efficiency, and emissions characteristics for blends containing 30-100% hydrogen by volume in the intake mixture, using lambda sweep and load-cut tests. Results indicate that mixtures with higher hydrogen content have superior thermal efficiency and combustion stability, a phenomenon that can be attributed to the favorable properties of hydrogen, including its high flame speed and wide flammability limits. Results also indicate that reducing the hydrogen fraction prolongs combustion duration and increases cyclic variability, while NOx emissions decrease due to lower peak temperatures. This study highlights key challenges associated with low-calorific fuel blends, particularly regarding ignition stability and limited energy density, for which the engine demonstrated robust adaptability across a wide range of compositions. This flexibility is of critical importance for the practical implementation of decentralized combined heat and power systems, where the composition of fuel may vary.

title: Circularity assessment of power electronic converters: manual disassembly, bill of material, circularity indicators and actionable guidelines
abstract: Power electronics are essential for the energy transition, supporting renewable integration, electrified transport, and efficient industrial systems. However, their growing deployment raises environmental concerns linked to the use of scarce materials, difficult-to-disassemble product architectures, and insufficient end-of-life strategies, factors which contribute to the global increase in electronic waste. As the core functional units of power electronic systems, power electronic converters (PECs) play a central role in determining these environmental outcomes. This study evaluates the circularity of two PECs. The methodology combined complete disassembly and desoldering, bill of material development, and the calculation of four indicators: Product Circularity Index (PCI), Reparability Index (RI), Recyclability (Rcyc), and Recoverability (Rcov). The results indicate that disassembly and desoldering of the two PECs, 37 and 78 steps, 71 and 88 min, respectively, require a high degree of manual effort, representing a significant barrier to practical and economically viable end-of-life recovery. Circularity was consistently low for PCI (0.21 and 0.20), Rcyc (0.21 and 0.16), and Rcov (0.21 and 0.17), while RI values were moderate (0.62 and 0.64), suggesting some potential for life extension through repair. Based on these findings, eight design guidelines are proposed to improve disassembly, reparability, and recovery. This study underscores how product design directly affects circularity outcomes in PECs, reinforcing the need to integrate circular economy principles in the development and management of PECs. • Integrated circularity assessment performed on two real power electronic converters. • Manual disassembly and desoldering revealed major circularity barriers. • Circularity performance of power converters remains very limited. • Eight actionable circular design guidelines are proposed to improve sustainability.

title: A fast and accurate multi-user load forecasting method based on coupled traditional neural networks and a time-series large model
abstract: Accurate and efficient individual load forecasting for building clusters is essential for smart grid operation and urban energy management, enabling optimal demand-side control and efficient integration of renewable energy sources. However, balancing prediction accuracy, generalization capability, and computational cost remains a significant challenge in practical applications. Inspired by recent advances in large models for vision and language tasks, this study proposes a novel multi-user load forecasting model that combines convolutional neural networks with a large time series model (CNN_Timer). The model adopts a dual-layer architecture to capture both shared and user-specific consumption patterns, enabling fast and robust predictions of multiple users with diverse characteristics. The performance of the proposed CNN_Timer model is evaluated using real-world hourly load data from multiple users and compared against benchmark models, including LSTM, XGBoost, pre-trained Timer, and fine-tuned Timer. Results show that CNN_Timer can realize the multi-user load prediction with high accuracy very quickly. It achieves the highest proportion of users with relative errors below 20% across MAPE, WAPE, and NRMSE, while improving median accuracy by 5.5%–51.5%. The training time is 26–75 times speed-up over benchmarks, with only up to 11.6 s for 30 users. To provide practical guidance for application, impacts of input length, training dataset size, and model update frequency are examined. It shows that using 4–7 days of input history, 25–30 days of training data, and an update interval of around 12 days offers an optimal balance between performance and efficiency. The proposed hybrid CNN_Timer model provides an effective alternative for large-scale regional user forecasting and supporting smart energy management of urban energy systems.

title: Sustainable lightweight composite nanofibers: efficient control of electromagnetic pollution
abstract: Electromagnetic pollution constitutes an emerging environmental and health threat, and the escalation is driving the search for sustainable and efficient mitigation technologies. This study presents an environmentally friendly and scalable solution through the design of composite nanofibers for effective electromagnetic pollution control. Utilizing the energy-efficient and industrially compatible solution blow spinning (SBS) technique, we successfully constructed a three-dimensional porous network within carbon fibers by integrating SiO2 nanoparticles and in-situ pyrolyzed Co@BCN nanotubes. The design not only features SiO2 as a dielectric modulator that optimizes impedance matching, but also induces abundant heterointerfaces with the carbon matrix and Co@BCN nanotubes, significantly enhancing interfacial polarization loss. The optimal material achieves a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −70.3 dB at a thickness of 1.8 mm and an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.2 GHz at a thickness of 2.3 mm, significantly reducing material usage and promoting lightweight design. The study demonstrates that high performance and environmental sustainability can be synergized, providing a new pathway for developing next-generation green electromagnetic protection materials that align with the goals of sustainable industrial development.

title: Beyond the average: understanding the heterogeneity of environmental impacts of green coffee in Brazil and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: Coffee production provides income for millions of families, but it also leads to many social-ecological challenges. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) studies of coffee show that most greenhouse gas emissions occur at the preproduction and production stages. In general, different coffee LCA studies lead to different results, which highly depend on the production practices, set system boundaries, selected methods, and impact categories. There is a need for more primary, transparent, regional and site-specific data covering different environmental impact categories to feed into coffee LCA studies. In this study, we assessed the environmental impacts of producing green coffee based on primary data of five case studies in Brazil and four case studies in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), covering a total of 60 farms. We considered the impact categories global warming, acidification, eutrophication, land use, water use, ecotoxicity, and carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic human toxicity. Our findings revealed that the environmental impacts of producing green coffee vary widely, even more so than reported in the literature. In this study, we have found that this variability is not only the result of differences in production and management practices but also depends on varying yields. In the DRC in particular, climate-induced yield variability accounted for more variance in our LCA results than differences between farms, countries, or case studies. Further research should focus on incorporating climate change and yield scenarios into LCA studies more effectively to improve our understanding of the different sources of variability in LCA results. • LCAs based on primary data from a very large sample of 60 coffee farms. • One of the first empirical LCA studies of coffee production in Sub-Saharan Africa. • Current coffee LCAs probably underestimate environmental impacts. • Climate change increases the uncertainty of LCA results for agriculture.

title: The dual role of microplastics in anaerobic digestion of food waste: Enhancing hydrolysis but inhibiting methanogenesis via biofilm-mediated microbial community succession
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) like polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) are pervasive in food waste (FW), yet the mechanisms through which they influence anaerobic digestion (AD) remain elusive, particularly regarding how they alter microbial metabolic pathways at different concentrations. This study investigated the concentration-dependent effects (0.05 to 5% total solids (TS)) of PET and PVC MPs on microbial ecology and process performance in FW anaerobic digestion. MPs significantly enhanced cumulative methane production by 15.38% (PET-5% TS) and 15.78% (PVC-0.5% TS), while high-dose PVC (5% TS) diminished this stimulatory effect. Although MPs accelerated hydrolysis, evidenced by hydrolysis efficiency of starch and bovine serum albumin were both significantly higher than in CK (p < 0.01), both acidification and methanogenesis were inhibited. Metagenomic analysis revealed that MPs enriched hydrolytic bacteria (e.g., Anaerolineae) but suppressed hydrogenotrophic methanogens (e.g., Methanobacteriaceae) and key methanogenic enzymatic pathways, with coenzyme M biosynthesis declining by 6.71%. Notably, MPs promoted robust biofilm formation, selectively enriching hydrolytic and acidogenic bacteria (Bacillus, Lachnospiraceae) and fungi (Aspergillus, Penicillium) in the plastisphere. These biofilms exhibited upregulated metabolic functions, including phosphotransferase systems (increased by 107.61%) and carbohydrate degradation, creating localized microenvironments that favor hydrolysis over methanogenesis. The results demonstrate the dual role of food waste-derived MPs in anaerobic digestion and highlight the critical function of biofilms in shaping process efficiency and microbial community dynamics.

title: Exploring next-generation PFAS-free TPX membranes fabricated via solubility-guided strategy for saline water treatment by membrane distillation
abstract: Direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) with saline water feed has emerged as a highly promising strategy to mitigate the escalating global drinking water crisis. Yet, heavy reliance on conventional membranes such as polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and poly (tetrafluoroethylene) (PTFE) is increasingly unsustainable, as their association with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) poses severe, long-term risks to both environmental safety and human health. To address these pressing challenges, the present study develops PFAS-free membranes from poly(4-methylpentene-1) (TPX), offering a sustainable and safe alternative for desalination applications. TPX membranes were systematically optimized through the Structure-Property-Performance (SPP) framework, with Hansen Solubility Parameters (HSP) guiding rational selection of casting conditions. Leveraging the HSP-SPP relationship, suitable co-solvents including dioxane, N-methyl-2- pyrrolidone (NMP), and dimethylformamide (DMF) were selected in combination with cyclohexane as primary solvent to precisely control membrane morphology and performance. In addition, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) was incorporated as an additive to tailor membrane hydrophobicity. The membranes were characterized by viscosity, overall porosity, morphology, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and hydrophobicity. The DCMD desalination performance of membranes was evaluated, showing that an optimized TPX membrane prepared with dioxane as co-solvent achieved highest permeate flux (5.89 ± 0.62 kg m−2 h −1) and excellent salt rejection exceeding 99.8%, outperforming all other tested membranes. Long-term performance comparisons with commercial PTFE membranes highlight potential of the fabricated TPX membrane for high salt rejection efficiency. This study delivers key insights into the design and optimization of TPX membranes for DCMD, emphasizing their potential in desalination. Future research should focus on further enhancing permeate flux.

title: Green interaction on online platforms and its role in enhancing corporate ESG performance: A dual green innovation chain mediation effect
abstract: Green interaction on online platforms is reshaping corporate ESG responsibility and advancing green transformation in capital markets. Yet prior research often relies on coarse quantity-based proxies and rarely explains how external stakeholder pressure translates into sustained ESG-oriented action through sequential internal innovation. Using inquiry-and-reply records from official exchange-hosted platforms and a panel of Chinese A-share manufacturing firms listed on the Shenzhen and Shanghai Stock Exchanges (2010–2023), this study combines Python-based text measures with an instrumental-variables strategy and moderation tests to estimate the effect of green interaction on ESG performance. Models incorporate rich firm controls and fixed effects, and findings remain robust to alternative ESG ratings and interaction measures. Results show that investor–firm green interaction significantly improves ESG performance. Mediation evidence indicates a chain mechanism via dual green innovation: green management innovation facilitates subsequent green technological innovation, which together transmit the effect to ESG outcomes. The effect is stronger for firms in regions with stricter environmental regulation, those facing higher reputational pressure, and those with stable institutional investors. These findings inform policymakers and managers on leveraging platform-based engagement to enhance ESG performance and provide guidance for retail investors to promote corporate green transition and sustainable development.

title: Process for resource-based preparation of soda ash from waste sodium sulfate based on double displacement reaction: Optimization using response surface methodology
abstract: With the growing emphasis on green chemistry and sustainable development, the resource utilization of waste salt has garnered significant attention. The production of soda ash from waste sodium sulfate presents a viable and sustainable pathway for the green transformation of the chemical industry. Current studies on this production method primarily focuses on single-factor effects on product purity, often overlooking the critical synergistic or antagonistic interactions between key process parameters. To address the aforementioned issues, this study systematically investigated the key factors and their interactions using response surface methodology. The process began with a pretreatment stage that effectively removed total organic carbon and color, while also adsorbing organic impurities such as heterocycles, anilines, ketones, phenols, and long-chain alkanes. For the soda ash synthesis via the double decomposition reaction of the pretreated waste sodium sulfate, single-factor experiments and response surface methodology optimization established the following optimal conditions: a reaction time of 1.96 h, a reaction temperature of 39 °C, and a material mass ratio of 1.284 (m (ammonium bicarbonate): m (sodium sulfate)). Under these conditions, the maximum soda ash purity of 99.35% was achieved. Furthermore, a binary regression model was developed for the process, with predictions showing excellent agreement with experimental data, confirming its reliability and practical utility. Additionally, the kinetics of the double decomposition reaction were determined by fitting a pseudo-second-order kinetic model in combination with the Arrhenius equation, and the resulting expression is as follows. 1/tlnβ0−Xβ01−X−βX/t=exp−69475/RT+4.3637×10−16. Through this waste-salt valorization pathway, not only can the accumulation of industrial waste sodium sulfate and associated environmental pollution risks be effectively reduced, the production cost per ton of sodium carbonate can be reduced by approximately 600 RMB, yielding significant sustainable economic benefits and providing strong support for advancing a green and low-carbon economy.

title: Regional differences in the relationship between New Quality Productivity and development quality in China, 2011–2023
abstract: Under tightening resource and environmental constraints and growing pressures for structural adjustment, New Quality Productivity (NQP) has become an increasingly relevant lens for analyzing regional upgrading and green transformation. Using panel data for 31 provinces in China from 2011 to 2023, this study constructs a composite NQP index that reflects technological innovation, production efficiency, and the foundations of green development, and systematically evaluates its relationship with High-quality development (HQD) as well as the underlying mechanisms. A two-way fixed effects model, mediation analysis, and regional heterogeneity tests are applied, together with a Coupling coordination degree (CCD) framework to examine the joint evolution of the two systems. The results show that (1) NQP is negatively associated with HQD, suggesting that under intensified green regulation and accumulating adjustment pressures, productivity gains may not be fully absorbed by existing structural conditions; (2) industrial structure upgrading acts as an inhibitory mediator, indicating that structural transitions may involve short term adjustment burdens; (3) the negative association displays a marked regional gradient, with weaker effects in eastern provinces and stronger effects in central, western, and resource dependent regions; and (4) consistent with this pattern, CCD results reveal an overall improvement in coordination but greater volatility in central and western regions, reflecting heterogeneous constraints in institutional absorption and structural adaptation. Overall, the results can be interpreted as being consistent with a transitional situation in which technological progress may temporarily outpace structural absorption, thereby enriching our understanding of the interaction between productivity transformation and development quality under green transition conditions, and informing region-specific structural upgrading strategies.

title: Can clean heating policy promote the development of green economy?
abstract: The core of green economic development lies in striking a balance ecological conservation. To explore whether the clean heating pilot policy (CHPP) effectively promotes green economic development, this study examines northern Chinese cities using a DID model to test the CHPP's impact on green growth. Findings reveal that the CHPP stimulates green economic development, with this conclusion remaining robust across a series of stability tests. Mechanism tests indicate that the clean CHPP positively impacts green economic development by driving green technological innovation. Heterogeneity tests further reveal that the clean CHPP more effectively promotes urban green economic development in non-resource-based cities and those with higher digital economic development levels. However, in the sample of cities with lower levels of technological concentration, the CHPP fails to produce a significant effect on promoting green economic development. By doing so, this study addresses a notable gap in the literature, as existing research on clean heating policies has largely emphasized environmental and health outcomes while paying limited attention to their economic effects and underlying transmission mechanisms. This study enriches the research on evaluating the effects of the CHPP, providing empirical evidence and practical references for governments to optimize clean heating policy designs and advance high-quality green economic development.

title: Sustainable self-healing concrete using industrial by-products: A multi-objective optimization strategy minimizing resource and experimental consumption
abstract: The construction sector's immense carbon footprint, largely from cement production, necessitates the resource-efficient utilization of industrial by-products. However, balancing and optimizing the mechanical and self-healing properties between resource recovery of industrial byproducts and composite building materials presents a significant challenge currently facing the industry. This study systematically evaluates the independent and combined effects of six mineral and chemical admixtures (fly ash, silica fume, ground granulated blast furnace slag, sodium silicate, sodium bicarbonate, and calcium nitrate) on compressive strength and self-healing capacity. A unified testing protocol, Taguchi L27 orthogonal array, and an improved response surface methodology (RSM) were integrated to optimize mix proportions and minimize experimental cost. 5-fold cross-validation confirmed the improved RSM's accuracy in predicting 28-day compressive strength. Results highlight the dual role of GGBS: replacing 30% of cement with GGBS maximizes strength gain, achieving a 16.7% increase compared to the conventional composite. While a 60% replacement optimizes crack width healing and strength recovery, achieving 651.7% and 248.3% improvements respectively compared to conventional composite. Additionally, incorporating 0.34% sodium silicate and 0.68% calcium nitrate effectively enhances internal crack healing and water absorption recovery, achieving a 149.5% improvement compared to the conventional composite, but having minor effects on compressive strength. The synergistic interactions among admixtures provide a scientific basis for designing high performance self-healing concrete (SHC) with balanced mechanical and healing properties. Additionally, this work establishes a waste-valorizing and experiment-minimizing paradigm, demonstrating that the improved RSM model offers a reliable tool for optimizing composite cementitious materials, substantially reducing experimental workload and guiding practical applications, and directly contributing to cleaner concrete production and sustainable infrastructure development.

title: Influence modeling analysis of blockchain incorporation in emerging economies for achieving sustainable development goals and net-zero carbon emissions: Implication of sustainable healthcare supply chains in Bangladesh
abstract: Blockchain technology plays a key role for enhancing the transparency, efficiency, and sustainability of healthcare supply chains in emerging economies such as Bangladesh. However, its implementation faces substantial challenges due to institutional, technological, and socio-cultural barriers. This study employs the GINA modeling technique to evaluate the impact of eleven key barriers of blockchain adoption in sustainable healthcare supply chains. Using expert opinions from 76 professionals in the relevant sector, the influence modeling identifies Institutional Regulatory Uncertainty (IRU) as the most critical barrier, with a total influence score of 0.196, followed by Data Privacy and Security Concerns (DPC) at 0.189, and Lack of Cooperation among Supply Chain Partners (LCS) at 0.187. These three factors emerge as the most notable systemic obstacles across critical, ideal, and typical modeling scenarios. Among the barriers assessed in the critical scenario, IRU had the strongest systemic influence, with DPC and LCS following behind. The findings suggest that addressing these top three barriers could mitigate majority of systemic resistance to blockchain adoption. These insights offer valuable guidance for policymakers and healthcare leaders aiming to integrate blockchain technology in alignment with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and net-zero carbon targets. For developing economies, this alignment may enhance the resilience of healthcare supply chains by improving equity, access and long-term sustainability. Furthermore, this study aids complex decision making in data scarce contexts that contribute to the application of novel GINA method.

title: Understanding surgeons’ preference for reusable surgical materials in laparoscopic surgery: A global cross-sectional survey
abstract: Making surgical practice more sustainable can substantially reduce healthcare's environmental impact, for example by adopting reusable surgical materials. However, a gap exists between surgeons' beliefs about the necessity to reduce this environmental impact and their adoption of reusable materials. This study examines psychological factors explaining surgeons' preference for reusable surgical materials in laparoscopic cholecystectomy, to inform strategies promoting sustainable practice. Secondary analyses were conducted using global survey data from 594 surgeons (M age =45 years; 70.7% male) in 75 countries.
