Results showed that for trocars and surgical drapes, core explanatory variables for choosing reusable over disposable items are beliefs about personal responsibility for reducing surgical practice's environmental impact, whether changing towards sustainable surgical practice is perceived to be worth the strain on healthcare, and perceived collegial support. Preference for reusable clip applicators is statistically predicted by belief in surgical practice's need to reduce environmental impact, with other relevant variables varying by subsample. Preference for reusable gowns is predicted by beliefs about the need to reduce environmental impact, whether sustainable change is worth the strain, and perceived collegial support. Bayesian analysis showed extreme evidence for all models. These results provide stakeholders with concrete starting points to further examine interventions aimed at promoting sustainable surgical practice. In conclusion, strengthening perceived collegial support for change towards sustainable surgical practice could be a viable general strategy to strengthen surgeons' preference for reusable surgical materials. However, the relative importance of psychological factors differs by material, suggesting interventions tailored to specific materials will be most effective. • Survey study on surgeons' preference for reusable surgical materials. • Focus on psychological predictors of preference in laparoscopic surgery. • Materials studied are trocars, clip applicators, drapes, and gowns. • Responsibility and social norms are key psychological factors. • Material-specific interventions may best promote reusable material use.

title: Green photocatalytic conversion of CO2 to renewable fuel over Ag/Cu-TiO2/g-PAN nanofibers under solar irradiation
abstract: While semiconductor-based photocatalysis presents a promising avenue for CO2 reduction, the application of conventional TiO2 is restricted by its limited light absorption, short photogenerated charge carrier lifetime, and poor CO2 adsorption capability. To overcome these constraints, we constructed multifunctional Ag/Cu-TiO2/graphitic-phase polyacrylonitrile (g-PAN) composites. In this system, g-PAN functions as a robust support for Ag/Cu nanoparticle-loaded TiO2 fibers synthesized via electrospinning and heat treatment. UV–Vis NIR DRS analysis reveals synergistic light harvesting where the localized surface plasmon resonance of Ag/Cu nanoparticles extends absorption into the near-infrared and g-PAN doubles the intensity by trapping photons within nanocavities. Beyond these optical benefits, g-PAN enhances CO2 adsorption and accelerates charge transfer. Consequently, the Ag/Cu-TiO2/g-PAN composite achieves a CO evolution rate of 11.82 mmol/g/h under simulated solar irradiation, representing a twice increase compared to the Ag/Cu-TiO2 counterpart. As evidenced by Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy and instantaneous photocurrent response, g-PAN acts as an electronic bridge that significantly reduces the resistance to photogenerated charge migration. This study provides novel insights into designing highly efficient composite photocatalysts for sustainable CO2 conversion, contributing to the advancement of cleaner production and green technologies.

title: Multi-objective optimization of operation conditions by smart proxy model for geological CO2 storage design in an over-pressured aquifer in the Ulleung Basin
abstract: This study aims to optimize the geological CO 2 storage (GCS) design in the D structure in the East Sea using a Smart Proxy Model (SPM). Analyzing the geomechanical stability of the overpressured aquifer, it was found that the pore pressure in the fault plane must be maintained below the current pressure value. Assuming that two existing wells were repurposed as an injection well and a relief well, Feature Engineering was adopted to derive new parameters for training the SPM with a reduced number of simulation runs. The optimization was conducted to maximize cumulative CO 2 injection and minimize brine production, considering several design parameters, including pre-relief period, the selection of pre-existing wells, and perforation intervals. The model exhibited high predictive accuracy in blind testing, with higher R 2 than 90%. 14 optimal solutions and the Pareto front were obtained by employing the SPM in the NSGA-II algorithm. As a result, the lowest cumulative CO 2 injection and brine production are 3.89 Mt and 5.12 Mt, respectively, while the largest CO 2 injection and brine production are 33.9 Mt and 59.7 Mt, respectively. In addition, it was found that the optimal perforation intervals strongly depend on both the operation conditions and reservoir characteristics. Therefore, the perforation intervals of the injection and relief wells should be optimized when a relief well design is incorporated into a GCS process. Although this study is specific to the D structure, the proposed ML-based optimization framework incorporating geomechanical risks can be adapted to other geological formations for GCS designs.

title: Energy-saving performance of formation sailing strategies for amphibious vehicles: A hydrodynamic and energy perspective
abstract: Amphibious vehicles, crucial for modern maritime transportation, face significant challenges due to their high energy consumption and resistance in water. This study investigates an operational strategy—formation sailing—as a viable approach to enhance their energy efficiency, leveraging hydrodynamic interactions for energy conservation. From a coupled hydrodynamic and energy perspective, the energy-saving performance of two typical amphibious vehicles has been numerically evaluated: a high-speed small unmanned vehicle (SAUV) and a low-speed medium transport vehicle (MATV). A high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model, based on the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations, is developed to simulate the complex wave-interference phenomena within formations. Both line and V-shaped formations are examined under rated and maximum speed conditions. The results demonstrate that energy is effectively transmitted through wave systems, leading to significant energy-saving gains for following vehicles. Specifically, the SAUV formation achieved up to a 29.9% reduction in total effective power at 7 m/s, while the MATV formation maintained over 15% energy savings across a wide range of spacings. The study elucidates the underlying hydrodynamic mechanisms—wave riding and wave cancellation—that govern these energy transfers. However, these energy gains can be accompanied by lateral forces and moments, posing stability challenges. This work provides both theoretical insights and practical strategies for achieving substantial energy conservation and emission reduction in amphibious vehicle operations, contributing to the development of greener transportation systems.

title: Towards a circular bioeconomy: A bi-criteria site level decision support for potential cluster nodes exemplified by hydrogen production in Baden-Württemberg
abstract: Fostering a local and circular bioeconomy is expected to result in increased resilience and decreased environmental impacts. By converting biobased residuals into valuable products, biowaste-to-X (B2X) technologies are enablers of such value creation. However, as biowaste is characterized by limited availability, its use must be optimized based on local supply and demand. This article presents a site level optimization model for the design of regional bioeconomic cluster nodes based on economic and ecological key performance indicators. Decisions concern the capacity of feasible technology combinations to be installed and transport of biomass from supply regions and products to demanding locations respectively. As B2X technologies are currently an emergent research field, the model is extendable to allow the consideration of future technology developments. Furthermore, framework conditions of the system under consideration are adjustable to enable a location- and time-independent application. The work addresses research, private investors, companies and municipalities, planning to install B2X facilities on a specified property to establish a cost-efficient local circular bioeconomy. The model is validated with the use case of hydrogen production. This includes B2X- but also conventional technologies to prevent dogmatic decisions and enable the identification of an optimum based on two dimensions of sustainability. Case studies with two companies in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, exemplify that specific framework conditions are necessary to turn biobased hydrogen production with carbon capture and storage into a favorable technology-combination. A sensitivity analysis outlines the costs for water, electricity, biomass, and workers, as well as the selling price for hydrogen and carbon removal certificates as pivotal parameters. • Presentation of a transferable and extensible model for optimizing local biobased supply chains. • The model is designed as a single facility location planning with capacity and flow optimization. • Decisions include. o the selection of the best suiting technology combination, including its scale o the annual production volume o the yearly mass of transported biomass from supply regions o the yearly mass of transported goods to demand locations o the yearly amount of captured CO 2 either transported to demand locations or a carbon dioxide storage facility • Consideration of economic (net present value) and ecological parameters (cumulated GHG emissions) • The model was tested in the context of the use case of bio-based hydrogen production and through two case studies of potential production sites in Baden-Württemberg. • Parameterization of the model and input data enables a variable, in terms of time and location universal application of the model

title: Valorization of aluminum-silica-based industrial solid waste to high quality ceramic proppants: waste sources and design strategies
abstract: As the industrial economy continues to grow, the accumulation of industrial solid waste has increased significantly, consuming large land areas and posing serious threats to ecosystems. In response to the growing emphasis on green production, the comprehensive utilization of industrial solid waste has become critically important. Simultaneously, high-grade bauxite—a key raw material for ceramic proppants used in oil and gas field development—is experiencing increasing scarcity. Certain industrial solid wastes are rich in Al 2 O 3 and SiO 2 and have a chemical composition similar to that of high-grade bauxite, presenting promising opportunities for the production of ceramic proppants. This review focuses on the state-of-the-art methods for preparing ceramic proppants from aluminum-silica-based industrial solid waste (ASISW). First, the potential for utilizing ASISW in ceramic proppant manufacturing is evaluated. Second, the suitability of ASISW for this purpose is analyzed. Next, the current status of commercializing waste-based ceramic proppants is assessed. Finally, the existing challenges and future research directions are discussed. This research not only promotes the efficient utilization of industrial waste and contributes to environmental sustainability but also reduces production costs for ceramic proppants, providing a novel technical pathway for their manufacturing. • Potential of ASISW for ceramic proppant preparation is analyzed. • Current utilization status of ASISW in proppant preparation is reviewed. • Pros and cons of different types of ASISW for proppant preparation are compared. • Current status of commercial production of waste-based proppants is summarized. • Existing challenges and future work opportunities are discussed.

title: Integrating indigenous petroleum-degrading bacteria into soil washing for enhanced remediation efficiency
abstract: Soil washing is an efficient and cost-effective approach for remediating petroleum-contaminated soils; however, the role of indigenous microorganisms has often been overlooked. In this study, indigenous bacterial communities from five petroleum-contaminated oilfield soils were characterized, and petroleum-degrading strains from the same soils were screened, cultivated, and reintroduced to enhance the performance of ex-situ soil washing. The optimal conditions for petroleum removal were predicted by response surface methodology (RSM), which suggested a 32% (v/v) bacterial inoculum and 75% of soil particles larger than 0.02 mm. Experimental validation confirmed that these conditions resulted in the highest petroleum removal efficiency, further demonstrating the reliability of the RSM model. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that soils from the Xinjiang (XJ), Liaohe (LH), and Changqing (CQ) oilfields, which showed superior remediation, shared higher operational taxonomic unit (OTU) similarity. Functional prediction based on cluster of orthologous groups (COG) analysis indicated that microbial proteins involved in hydrocarbon transport and degradation were more abundant in these soils. A glass-etched micro-model test confirmed that the addition of indigenous Sphingomonas sp. enhanced pollutant desorption and removal. Overall, this study highlights the crucial role of native microbial communities in soil washing and offers a sustainable approach for the remediation of petroleum-contaminated soils.

title: Sustainable aquafeed? The devil is in the detail
abstract: Aquaculture is essential to meet the increasing demand for nutritious seafood. Aquafeed input represents most of the environmental impact and production cost, formulations consist of a combination of marine and plant-based ingredients. Driven by economic and sustainability incentives there has been a shift from marine ingredients towards plant-based ingredients, and smaller inclusions of (fish) by-products and novel feed ingredients. We applied Index Decomposition Analysis to assess the changing environmental impact from 2000 to 2020 for the European (European Economic Area (EEA) + United Kingdom (UK)) aquaculture industry. In this period the total production of the main produced species in Europe grew from 1.15 million metric tonnes (MMT) in 2000 to 2.17 MMT in 2020. On an industry level we find a substantial increase in Global warming (314%), Land use (594%), Water consumption (236%), Marine eutrophication (630%) and Freshwater eutrophication (468%), while Wild Fish Use was reduced by 13%. Considering an efficiency metric per kg fish produced, Wild fish use was reduced by 59% while Global warming (103%), Land use (336%), Water consumption (65%), Marine eutrophication (285%) and Freshwater eutrophication (167%) increased substantially. These changes are mostly attributed to the substitution of marine ingredients by plant-based ingredients shifting pressures from marine to terrestrial impacts. While by-product utilisation for marine ingredients contributed to a lower reliance on marine ingredients without significant trade-offs. We demonstrate that use of two terrestrial ingredients, soy protein concentrate, and rapeseed oil, have had a disproportionate and detrimental impact on the environmental footprint, emphasising the need for comprehensive and consistent sustainability assessments of aquafeed and aquaculture production.

title: Gas-solid-liquid three-phase interface modulated ROS generation over a floatable S,N-CaZn2(BO3)2 for enhanced water disinfection
abstract: Effective water disinfection is essential for mitigating the global burden of waterborne pathogens, and advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) leveraging reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as ·O2− have emerged as a promising photocatalytic strategy to achieve microbial inactivation without harmful by-products. However, the efficiency of the photocatalytic reduction of O2 is severely limited by the inherently low solubility and diffusion coefficient of O2 in aqueous solutions. To address this, we developed a gas–liquid–solid three-phase system using a floating composite sponge (S,N-CaZn2(BO3)2@Sponge) that directly utilizes abundant atmospheric O2 for ·O2− generation. Under visible light irradiation, the composited sponge achieved a 100% antibacterial rate against streptomycin-resistant Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus within 60 minutes-1.3 times faster than the powdered system, which required 80 min. It maintained 100% sterilization against streptomycin-resistant E. coli for 4 continuous hours and eliminated real water microorganisms within 60 min, underscoring its strong potential for practical water disinfection. By facilitating the dynamic mass transfer of O2, this floating design effectively overcomes the mass-transfer limitations inherent in conventional powdered systems. Additionally, the built-in electric field generated by S,N-CZBO accelerates electron–hole separation and migration, substantially boosting ROS production. This study proposes a floating composite sponge that simultaneously enhances ROS generation and antibacterial performance while eliminating catalyst-recovery issues, offering a novel strategy for water disinfection application.

title: Alternating magnetic field-augmented solar evaporation in 3D magnetic porous architectures for enhanced interfacial water evaporation
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation is considered a promising technology to water scarcity due to its sustainability, low cost, and environmental friendliness. However, its development is limited by the low and unstable heat flux of sunlight, calling for new technologies to boost evaporation rates. Herein, we propose a magnetothermal-assisted solar evaporation strategy that utilizes distributed renewable electricity for magnetothermal conversion to enhance solar-to-thermal efficiency. A cobalt-based metal-organic framework (Co-MOF) was synthesized and loaded onto wood pulp sponge, followed by high-temperature carbonization to form a 3D magnetic porous carbon evaporator with excellent photothermal and magnetothermal performance. Under combined solar irradiation and an alternating magnetic field, a high temperature of 100.1 °C was achieved, and the evaporation rate reached 8.65 kg m−2·h−1, which nearly twice that of solar-only evaporation. This enhancement is attributed to the synergistic effects of Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance and magnetic hysteresis loss, which jointly promote efficient thermal conversion. Additionally, the evaporator demonstrates excellent desalination and wastewater treatment performance, with over 99.9% removal efficiency and excellent resistance to salt accumulation. This research establishes a recyclable-derived, AMF-augmented solar interfacial evaporation paradigm that enables non-contact, quantifiable magnetothermal–photothermal synergy with robust salt management, thereby offering a scalable route toward high-throughput seawater desalination and clean-water production.

title: Efficient recovery of high-purity 2D flaky R-FePO4 from lithium extraction slag leachate via solvent extraction and chemical precipitation
abstract: The recycling of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries (LFPs) has enormous market potential and great significance for environmental protection and sustainable development. Notably, lithium extraction slag (LES) recovery is a critical link in the full-process recycling of spent LFPs, while existing technologies are often limited by low impurity separation efficiency, poor environmental compatibility, or high costs. Herein, this study innovatively integrated solvent extraction with LES recovery and proposed a method for efficient impurity separation and preparation of high-purity 2D flaky regenerated iron phosphate (R-FePO4). Three extractant systems were evaluated for purifying LES leachate, and TBP-kerosene was identified as the optimal extractant composition with corresponding optimal operating conditions determined. Fe and P could be co-extracted, and under conditions of 80% TBP volume fraction (φTBP = 80%), 60 s extraction time, and initial phase ratio R = 3, their single-stage extraction efficiencies reached approximately 99.20% and 38.50%, respectively, with excellent impurity separation performance. After cascaded extraction, the maximum extraction efficiencies of Fe and P reached 100% and 82.60%, respectively. McCabe-Thiele diagrams for Fe and P were constructed to determine the theoretical number of stripping stages. After three-stage countercurrent stripping, the maximum mass concentrations of Fe and P in the stripping solution reached 29.20 and 17.23 g L−1, respectively, while contents of impurities (Al, Ni, Co, Mn, Cu, Ti) remained extremely low. HCl and R-FePO4 were recovered from the stripping solution via evaporation and chemical precipitation, respectively. XRD, FT-IR, SEM, and EDS characterizations verified that the product was 2D flaky FePO4. Chemical titration and ICP-OES analysis showed the Fe/P molar ratio of R-FePO4 was 0.969, and its impurity content met requirements of multiple standards simultaneously. Collectively, these results confirm the successful recovery of high-purity 2D flaky R-FePO4 from LES via this method, with the comprehensive recovery rates of Fe and P reaching nearly 100%. Cyclic performance tests of the extractant demonstrate its excellent regenerative performance. The economic and environmental performance of the proposed process was evaluated, revealing its enormous industrial application potential. Eventually, a novel technical process is provided for the LES recycling industry to achieve maximum resource utilization.

title: Optimization of cropping structures in mega-city food systems for integrated water-saving, energy efficiency, and low-carbon goals: Evidence from the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region
abstract: As China advances its “dual carbon” goals and food security strategy, its food system faces growing challenges from resource constraints and environmental pressures. In view of the current lack of research on the systematic optimization of crop planting structure at the regional scale under the coordinated control of water resources, energy consumption and carbon emissions, this paper constructs a comprehensive optimization framework for the goal of “water saving - energy saving - low carbon". Taking the planting structure of rice, wheat, and corn as decision variables, and incorporating constraints of water security, land security, and food security, the model is applied to the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region using historical data from 2000 to 2022. The results indicate that, during this period, the region's blue water footprint, energy consumption, and carbon emissions from grain production all showed a fluctuating downward trend. Among the crops, corn demonstrated the highest adaptability to regional water conditions and the most efficient use of resources. After optimization, the blue water footprint could be reduced by 2.987 billion m3, energy consumption by 189,500 tons of standard coal, and carbon emissions by an equivalent 678,800 tons. Although optimal planting structures vary across sub-regions, the overall trend points toward reduced wheat and increased corn cultivation. This framework provides a novel approach to crop structure optimization under multi-resource constraints and offers practical guidance for advancing sustainable agriculture and food security in metropolitan regions.

title: Photothermal metal organic framework@wood evaporator with honeycomb structure for efficient solar-driven freshwater and high-value chemical production
abstract: Solar-driven water evaporation and photocatalysis are promising and sustainable strategies for alleviating global freshwater shortages and energy crises. Wood-based solar evaporators attract considerable interest for their eco-friendliness, low cost, and inherent porous structure. However, their practical application is often hindered by limited light absorption, poor salt resistance, and inefficient water transport. Herein, a new interfacial array-structured wood evaporator modified with metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is designed. Hydrophilic MOFs are anchored within the lamellar pores of wood via an in-situ growth strategy, forming a MOF-wood hybrid network that significantly reduces the energy required for water evaporation while increasing the water transport rate. The interfacial array structure enhances light absorption and facilitates salt solubilization backflow. Furthermore, covalently grafted ferrocene molecules serve as core functional units with highly efficient photothermal conversion and rapid electron transfer capabilities, constructing an efficient bifunctional platform for photothermal evaporation-catalysis. The prepared evaporator delivers an exceptional evaporation rate of 2.62 kg m−2 h−1 under one sun while simultaneously achieving a 99.65% yield of cis-stilbene in photothermal catalytic reactions. The evaporator also exhibits outstanding cyclic stability, superior salt resistance, and broad applicability across diverse aqueous environments. The present study provides new insights into the construction of a synergistically enhanced solar-driven energy-resource integration system.

title: Do customer climate risk perceptions promote green innovation along the supply chain?
abstract: Climate risk perceptions are increasingly influencing corporate behavior, yet their impact on green innovation along the supply chain remains insufficiently understood. We combine customer–supplier links among Chinese listed firms with a BERT-based measure of customer firms' climate-risk perceptions constructed from annual reports. We find that higher customer climate risk perceptions are associated with subsequent increases in supplier green innovation. Mechanism evidence indicates that the effect operates through customers’ market power, technology spillovers, and financial support. The effect is stronger when suppliers have greater digital capability and environmental expertise, and when customers exhibit stronger ESG performance and higher information transparency. Dynamic analyses reveal that short-run responses attenuate over time, whereas persistent signaling sustains innovation momentum. Overall, the results suggest that customer climate-risk perceptions strengthen market-based supply-chain governance and bias technical change toward greener trajectories.

title: Fair scheduling efficiency benchmarking for sustainability in heterogeneous hydropower systems
abstract: Achieving fair efficiency comparisons among hydropower stations with vastly different hardware remains a key barrier to improving sustainability in clean energy production. This study proposes a novel hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) framework that integrates the Weighted Maintenance Object (WMO) theory to quantify comparable “strength values.” This “strength value” standardization neutralizes bias in key performance indicators-such as the Water Consumption Rate (WCR) and Spilled Hydropower (SH)—that arises from inherent infrastructural differences. We construct a dual-category indicator system that captures both efficiency metrics and hardware characteristics. Our approach combines objective, data-driven weighting with an enhanced decision-making algorithm to resolve the traditional ambiguities in ranking. Applied to 37 stations across seven river basins in Southwest China, our framework demonstrates that high-efficiency stations consistently minimize water consumption and spillage while maximizing energy output. Seasonal analysis reveals that efficiency is generally higher in wet seasons. Furthermore, our method demonstrates superior robustness and discriminative ability to conventional MCDM approaches. This research provides operators and policymakers with a robust and fair framework for performance assessment, advancing sustainable hydropower operations through targeted improvements in resource efficiency and cleaner energy production.

title: Can coffee silverskin be a suitable substrate for biogas production and odour impact mitigation of digestate?
abstract: Coffee silverskin (CS), the main by-product generated during coffee roasting in consuming countries, remains largely underutilized despite its high organic content. This study evaluates its suitability as a substrate for anaerobic digestion by determining its biochemical methane potential (BMP) and assessing its influence on digestate odour emissions. Laboratory-scale BMP tests were conducted under mesophilic conditions (40 °C) using an inoculum from a full-scale biogas plant. Results showed a cumulative methane yield of 112.33 ± 61.33 L CH 4 ·kg −1 VS and a biogas production of 254.07 ± 135.87 L kg −1 VS, with an average methane content of 45.4%. These values indicate a moderate methanogenic potential, limited by the high lignin fraction and low C/N ratio of CS, suggesting its preferential use in co-digestion with carbon-rich substrates. Odour impact was assessed using both an electronic nose and dynamic olfactometry. The addition of CS temporarily altered volatile compound fingerprints during digestion but did not lead to substantial improvements in perceived odour quality. Although odour concentration increased in treated samples, hedonic tone differences were minimal. Overall, the results highlight that while CS is not an optimal standalone substrate, its integration into co-digestion strategies could support renewable energy production and enhance the circularity of the coffee supply chain.

title: Evaluating wave energy solutions for coastal Food-Energy-Water-Carbon (FEWC) nexus
abstract: Freshwater and food shortages, combined with increasing soil salinity, are forecasted as critical challenges of this century. To address these issues and enhance resilience in coastal areas, this study models an ocean wave-powered Food-Energy-Water-Carbon (FEWC) Nexus system and evaluates its feasibility with economic and environmental indices. Freshwater is produced through Reverse Osmosis (RO) seawater desalination directly powered by ocean wave energy, which is then used to reclaim saline soil and irrigate crops. An integrated optimization framework is developed to evaluate the system's impacts on food security, as well as its environmental and economic aspects. Key parameters, such as the size of the Wave Energy Converter (WEC) array and local crop distribution, are optimized within the framework. A case study in Virginia, USA, demonstrates the significant potential of this system. The optimization results and sensitivity analysis highlight that the application of wave-powered desalination and appropriate organization of farming can simultaneously boost local agricultural economic revenue and enhance resilience against climatic challenges.

title: Explainable machine learning and life cycle assessment for sustainable design of fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete
abstract: Conventional asphalt concrete has a limited lifespan due to cracking, deformation, and environmental degradation, driving the development of fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete (FRAC). However, key gaps remain in current data-driven FRAC studies due to small and homogeneous datasets, “black-box” machine learning models, and trade-offs between mechanical-sustainable performance, failing to provide a transparent understanding of features governing FRAC behaviors. This paper proposes a framework integrating explainable artificial intelligence and life cycle assessment (LCA) to advance mechanical and sustainable design of FRAC. A dataset of 2490 laboratory samples covers 15 input features and 3 mechanical outputs. Eight machine learning models, along with a voting ensemble strategy, were optimized using Genetic algorithm for hyperparameter tuning. The optimized voting ensemble achieved an average prediction performance of R 2 = 0.87, RMSE = 1.09, MAPE = 11.96%, and MAE = 0.60 across the three mechanical targets, indicating robust and reliable predictive capability. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and linear non-gaussian acyclic causal inference quantified global/local feature impacts and pairwise interactions. LCA evaluated economic and environmental impacts and derived strength-normalized sustainability metrics. Finally, an interactive graphic user interface platform was developed for predictions, SHAP interpretations, and LCA outcomes. This data-driven approach establishes a paradigm for intelligent FRAC design, harmonizing mechanical performance with sustainability. • A dataset of 2490 laboratory samples was constructed for fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete. • The dataset comprises 15 design parameters as inputs and 3 mechanical properties as outputs. • 9 machine learning models were optimized using genetic algorithm for hyperparameter tuning. • The SHAP algorithm and causal inference were used to interpret optimal predictions. • A life cycle assessment was conducted to evaluate cost, carbon footprint, and energy efficiency.

title: Selective molecular oxygen activation via electron transfer modulation in nZVI/TpPa-1 for doxycycline hydrochloride degradation
abstract: Nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI) demonstrates significant potential for environmental remediation through molecular oxygen activation and subsequent generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) for the degradation of organic pollutants. However, inefficient oxygen conversion due to competing side reactions and rapid passivation greatly limits its practical application. This study developed a porous TpPa-1 covalent organic framework-supported nanoscale zero-valent iron composite (nZVI/TpPa-1) through liquid-phase in situ reduction, which significantly enhanced molecular oxygen activation for efficient doxycycline hydrochloride (DOX-H) degradation under ambient conditions. The crystalline framework of TpPa-1 precisely modulated the reactive interfaces of nZVI, where spatially confined pores prevented nZVI aggregation while the π-conjugated structure promoted selective electron transfer from Fe0 to oxygen, thereby suppressing the reductive removal of pollutants mediated by direct electron transfer. TpPa-1 with a porous crystal structure provides controlled anchors for nZVI particles as well as the reaction sites for both O2 and DOX-H. The results showed that the nZVI/TpPa-1 achieved 98.02% DOX-H removal within 20 min, representing a 5-fold enhancement over bare nZVI. Mechanistic investigations through EPR spectroscopy and radical quenching experiments identified that •O2− played the dominant role, while •OH and 1O2 played secondary roles in DOX-H degradation, sustained by surface-bound Fe2+/Fe3+ redox cycling. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis further elucidated the degradation pathway of DOX-H. This work provides a promising strategy for the design of COFs-metal hybrid catalysts that simultaneously address the intrinsic limitations of molecular oxygen activation and enable energy-efficient remediation of antibiotic-contaminated water.

title: Edible plates from wheat bran and blackcurrant pomace: A multidisciplinary approach to by-product valorization
abstract: This study developed biodegradable, edible plates (EP; plural EPs) using wheat bran (WB 67–90%) and blackcurrant pomace (BP 3–10%) as sustainable plastic alternatives. Eleven formulations were tested with additives: stabilizers (chitosan, levan, xanthan), plasticizers (glycerol, lactic acid), crosslinking agents (citric acid, lecithin), and film-forming agents (gluten, gelatin). EPs with WB (67–80%) and BP (4–5%), plus gluten or xanthan and lactic acid, showed high fracture strength (148.7–235.2 N) and low water/oil absorption. SEM showed dense, compact structures; in contrast, >8% BP and 10% apple puree were associated with a less uniform, more defect-prone structure with visible void-like regions. All EPs had safe levels of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural. Functional compounds were present, including tocopherols, tocotrienols, alkylresorcinols, anthocyanins, and fiber. Sensory analysis highlighted EPs 21.2 and 25.1 as the most favorable in structure, taste, and visual appeal. These findings show that combining food by-products with targeted bio-additives can yield sustainable, nutritious, and consumer-acceptable EPs, supporting win-win-win environmental, nutritional, and industrial sustainability goals.

title: Characteristics of n-heptane conversion by microwave liquid plasma for C2 hydrocarbons production:Effect of reactant volume and pressure
abstract: C2 hydrocarbons are critical intermediates in the energy and chemical industries. Plasma technology offers a promising route for converting liquid hydrocarbons into these high-value products. In this work, a regulation mechanism for converting n-heptane into C2 hydrocarbons via microwave liquid-phase discharge was established. Specifically, the interplay between reactant volume, system pressure, and discharge characteristics was investigated. Results show that reactant volume acts as a critical geometric factor regulating bubble dynamics, with an optimal C2 hydrocarbon concentration of 42.2% achieved at a reactant volume of 80 mL. Additionally, system pressure was found to significantly affect production performance. The study reveals that a decrease in system pressure reduces plasma density and increases electron temperature, driving a shift in reaction pathways from radical recombination to β-scission, which favors C2 hydrocarbon formation. This work elucidates the intrinsic coupling between operating parameters and discharge behavior, providing a theoretical basis for the precise control and scalable design of high-selectivity C2 production systems.

title: Sustainable mobility in cities: Benchmarking level of service for shared micro-mobility services
abstract: In order to adopt sustainable practices in cities, public bicycle-sharing systems (PBSS) and e-bike/scooter-sharing systems (EBSS) are gaining momentum across the globe. However, inconsistent service quality leads to reduced user satisfaction and a decrease in the proportion of users of these shared micro-mobility services. Moreover, the lack of a structured performance evaluation framework hinders efforts to monitor, improve, and scale these systems effectively. This study proposes a comprehensive level of service (LOS) framework to benchmark the performance of different quantitative and qualitative attributes of shared micro-mobility services based on user-centric evaluation. LOS thresholds (A-E) are derived using the method of successive intervals for quantitative attributes, and a combination of ordered probit modeling with fuzzy c-means clustering for qualitative attributes. The study is conducted in two urban Indian cities, where face-to-face intercept surveys are conducted to collect user satisfaction data on various service quality attributes. A heterogeneity in the threshold values of LOS for PBSS and EBSS becomes apparent. Furthermore, the current LOS for each attribute of PBSS and EBSS in the two cities is exhibited, mostly having LOS B or C. The varying performances of PBSS and EBSS highlight the associated key challenges, such as higher operational delays, insufficiently charged electric bicycles and e-bikes, poor docking station design, etc. The proposed LOS framework offers scalable and quantitative tools for benchmarking the current service quality of shared micro-mobility services, allowing policymakers and operators to quantify the impact of service improvements over time.

title: Material and carbon intensity of offshore wind foundations for sustainable infrastructure
abstract: Offshore wind is central to global decarbonisation, yet the lifecycle impacts of turbine foundations remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a systematic comparative framework to assess seven foundation types (i.e., monopile, jacket, tripod, gravity-based, semi-submersible, tension-leg platform, and spar) using data from 62 projects. We integrate material intensity, regional carbon factors, operational lifespans, and capacity factors to estimate embodied carbon emissions per unit of installed capacity and per unit of electricity generated. The life cycle inventory is compiled across key upstream and project stages, including material production (steel and cement) and end-of-life management. The analysis highlights a core design duality: steel-dominant foundations are typically more recyclable and support higher end-of-life recovery, while concrete-intensive foundations can be harder to recycle yet may offer longer technical lifetimes, creating trade-offs in lifecycle carbon intensity. Fixed-bottom foundations exhibit the lowest carbon intensities, averaging 2.2–2.5 gCO 2 /kWh over a 25-year lifespan, with gravity-based foundations achieving 1.2 gCO 2 /kWh when operating for 50 years. Floating designs show higher values, ranging from 4.7–6.4 gCO 2 /kWh over 25 years, though longer lifespans can reduce it to 2.4–3.2 gCO 2 /kWh. Adoption of sustainable manufacturing practices, including low-carbon steel and green cement, could cut foundation-related carbon emissions by 66 % to 76 %. At the terawatt scale of planned offshore deployment by 2050, foundation design, material choices, and end-of-life strategies will be decisive in ensuring offshore wind aligns with global net-zero targets. • Comparative assessment of seven offshore wind foundation types across fixed and floating designs. • Data-driven lifecycle framework integrating material intensity, lifespan, and capacity factors. • Fixed foundations emit 2.2–2.5 gCO 2 /kWh over 25 years; gravity-based reach 1.2 gCO 2 /kWh at 50 years. • Floating foundations emit 4.7–6.4 gCO 2 /kWh over 25 years, falling to 2.4–3.2 gCO 2 /kWh at 50 years. • Sustainable materials reduce embodied CO 2 emissions by 66%–76%, highlighting foundation industries’ role.

title: Can computing infrastructure unlock enterprise carbon lock-in? Evidence from National Supercomputing Centers
abstract: Against the backdrop of China's “dual-carbon” strategy and the accelerated development of the digital economy, enterprises commonly face persistent transition inertia arising from production structures, technological trajectories, governance arrangements, and social constraints. Whether computing infrastructure (CI) can serve as an effective “unlocker” remains to be empirically verified. Based on panel data of 821 A-share listed enterprises across 172 prefecture-level cities in China from 2008 to 2022, this paper treats the establishment of National Supercomputing Centers (NSCs) as a quasi-natural experiment. We construct multidimensional enterprise-level carbon lock-in (CLI) indexes and employ the Callaway and Sant’Anna difference-in-differences approach (CSDID) together with double debiased machine learning (DDML) to systematically evaluate the impact of CI on enterprise carbon lock-in and its underlying mechanisms. The results show that NSC construction significantly reduces enterprise CLI on average, and this conclusion remains robust across a battery of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis reveals that NSCs indirectly alleviate enterprise carbon lock-in by increasing government science and technology expenditure and improving enterprise profitability efficiency, while education expenditure exhibits an inhibitory effect during the sample period. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that CI generates a pronounced unlocking effect in non–high-carbon and non–high-water-intensity industries, whereas in high-carbon industries it may reinforce existing path dependence, highlighting its pronounced “double-edged sword” effect.

title: A dynamic micro-macro-economic model to assess water charging policies
abstract: This paper presents an integrated and dynamic coupling of micro- and macro-economic models for water resources management. As compared to conventional static micro-macro-economic coupling designs, the dynamic coupling produces time-variant assessments of endogenous (e.g., dynamics and impacts of capital accumulation) and exogenous variables (e.g., impacts of policy shifts or market trends over time). Methods are illustrated with an application to the Castile and León Region in Spain, where we: 1) assess the performance of two hypothetical water charging policies (one-time charge adjustment v. Incremental charges), and 2) compare the simulation results obtained with the proposed dynamic coupling to those obtained using two conventional static models. A key finding is that simulations under the dynamic coupling attribute lower effectiveness to water charges in reducing water use over time: 47% and -24% (dynamic coupling) water use change at the beginning and end of the simulation period vs. -46% (static coupling). Additionally, an incremental water charge has a greater economic impact than a one-time adjustment, resulting in a peak profit reduction of -8.9% compared to -5.9% under the one-time charge. Our results highlight the relevance of accounting for dynamic micro-macro-economic dynamic feedback in water policy design.

title: An index to measure SDG-aligned sustainable performance: A developing country perspective
abstract: Existing sustainability assessment tools are often unsuitable for smallholder farmers in developing countries, where resource constraints and economic pressures outweigh environmental and social considerations. This study develops and validates an SDG-aligned index that operationalizes Cleaner Production (CP) at the farm level to measure the sustainable performance of smallholder dairy farmers in Sri Lanka. Drawing on triple bottom line (TBL) and sustainable supplier development (SSD) concepts, we test a conceptual model using survey data from 324 farmers. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) estimates construct weights that are translated into a transparent 0–1000 scoring system. The index comprises five dimensions—farmer capability (FC), farmer–processor relationship (FPR), and farmer economic (ES), social (SS), and environmental (EnvS) sustainability. Results show FC is the strongest contributor (236 points), while ES lags (170 points). By embedding CP principles—resource efficiency, waste minimization and circularity, and pollution prevention—the index enables processors to classify farmers, tailor interventions, and integrate verified outcomes into sustainability reporting. The framework contributes to SSD and CP practice, offers a replicable, low-burden measurement tool for agri-food supply chains, and outlines a tiered linkage to life-cycle assessment and carbon accounting for sector dashboards. The paper's primary contribution is methodological and practical: it operationalizes established TBL, SSD, and CP perspectives into an empirically weighted (0–1000) tool for smallholder supplier management and SDG reporting. • Developed a 0–1000 index for smallholder dairy farmer sustainability. • Index integrates enablers, TBL outcomes, Cleaner Production principles. • Validated with PLS-SEM using data from 324 Sri Lankan dairy farmers. • Farmer capability is the strongest contributor, economic sustainability lags. • Tool supports SDG reporting and scaling sustainability in agri-food chains.

title: Bridging China's energy and mineral system: Evaluating the risk of domestic supply shortages for critical raw materials in the context of China's energy transition
abstract: Achieving the goal of “net zero emissions” requires accelerating the transformation of the energy system to more clean, green and low-carbon, which means shifting from a fossil fuel-intensive traditional energy system to a material-intensive renewable energy system. In this transition, it is important to quantify the demand for critical minerals/raw materials as well as the domestic supply. This paper combined dynamic material flow analysis methods and Hubbert-peak model to identify possible bottlenecks and supply shortage risks between future demand and geological availability of critical raw materials in the period 2021-2060 driven by China's “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals”. Evaluating 22 critical minerals across 16 technology scenarios, we identify: 12 materials at extremely high risk of domestic supply shortage (cumulative demand > reserves by 2050): Ag, Al, Cr, Cu, Ni, Cd, In, Se, Te, Li, Co, Pt; 3 at high risk (cumulative demand > reserves by 2060): Fe, Ge, Dy; 2 at medium risk (annual demand > production capacity): Mn, Ga. Recycling reduces risks for Al, Fe, Mn, Li, Dy, and Ge (down to medium or low risks), but cannot resolve deficits for Cr, Co, Pt, and scattered metals (Cd, Se, In, Te). Electric vehicles emerge as the technology with the largest variety of required materials, reliant on 17/22 minerals (notably Li, Co, Ni for batteries), 13 of which are classified as extremely high or high-risk minerals. This study provides a methodological framework to assess mineral supply risks, supporting China's energy transition security and global critical mineral supply chain stability.

title: On the social implications of technological processes: Towards hybrid social life cycle analysis (H-SLCA)
abstract: Recent approaches to hybrid life-cycle analysis (H-LCA) and social life-cycle analysis (SLCA) converge in common aims to develop methods for assessing the social dimensions of technological processes, with particular attention to the conditions affecting the provision and reproduction of labor. In this paper, we explore ‘hybrid social life-cycle analysis’ (H-SLCA), an integrated approach combining process-based SLCA with economy-wide social accounting to assess environmental and social impacts of particular technological processes in their interactions with the wider economy. To do so, we modify the numerical example with which Suh (2004) introduced the input-output based H-LCA to build a proof of concept for H-SLCA. The resulting model exploits the compatibilities in the computational structures of process-based LCA, the input-output model and social accounting matrices to include labor provision, income generation, and household consumption in the characterization of both the foreground system and the background economy. Thus defined, hybrid-SLCA computes impacts in those social variables while also producing estimates for environmental impacts higher than those obtained with H-LCA. This is because the social accounting matrix is more comprehensive than the input-output table. The model for H-SLCA is sufficiently flexible to potentially include additional social dimensions relevant to SLCA (human rights, safety, gender, etc.) when represented quantitatively. Finally, we suggest that this richer representation of production technologies is compatible with understandings of technology in the wider social sciences. As such, H-SLCA can be a basis for multidisciplinary collaboration between researchers interested in technological processes from either quantitative or qualitative orientations.

title: Rock attitude regulates the growth traits and soil‒water conservation functions of lithophytic mosses by modulating the microenvironment
abstract: Rocky desertification expansion and ecological degradation are prominent issues in karst regions, arising from the combined effects of carbonate bedrock fragility and human disturbance. Traditional management approaches are constrained by high costs and limited adaptability. While lithophytic mosses, as pioneer colonists on bare rocks, deliver critical soil-water conservation functions, their growth dynamics and functional responses to microenvironments remain inadequately understood. This study systematically investigated the cascading mechanisms linking rock attitude, microenvironment, moss growth, and soil-water conservation across different land-use types (cropland, grassland, orchard), rock orientations (east, south, west, north, up), and vertical positions (top, middle, bottom) in a typical karst area. Results revealed that rock attitude significantly drove moss growth and functional differentiation: north-facing, slopes <40°, and rock bottoms supported optimal moss thickness (11.81 mm), biomass (5.51 × 103 kg hm−2), water-holding (54.18 × 103 kg hm−2), and soil stabilization capacity (12.56 × 103 kg hm−2). Moss performance was superior in orchards, exhibiting 3.2 times the water retention of croplands and 2.3 times the soil stabilization of grasslands. Higher humidity favored moss growth, and critical microenvironmental thresholds were identified: chlorophyll a+b (0.59 mg g−1) and water-holding rate (861.42%) peaked under >50% relative humidity and 30–50% full sunlight, whereas high irradiance coupled with low humidity suppressed growth. A chain effect was evident: rock attitude governs the microclimate and hydro-nutrient conditions, which in turn regulate moss growth and its consequent soil-water conservation functions, with land use acting as a key external driver. This work establishes theoretical foundation and practical strategies for moss cultivation and restoration in karst regions.

title: An integrated hot air-microwave drying strategy for lignite: Achieving enhanced efficiency and CO2 reduction potential
abstract: Lignite drying continues to be majorly hindered by high energy consumption and low efficiency. A laboratory-scale combined hot air–microwave drying system integrating convective and dielectric heating was developed to address these limitations and thus enhance performance. Drying characteristics and energy efficiency were systematically evaluated. Zhaotong lignite contained abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and a well-developed mesoporous structure, which facilitated significant moisture retention, with a maximum bound water content of 0.600 g/g. Its initial activation energy (40.30 kJ/mol) resulted in slow drying kinetics during the initial drying stage. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed system significantly outperformed conventional hot-air drying, achieving a 16.1-fold increase (Drying rate, DR) under optimized conditions (microwave power: 500 W; microwave intervention: 25 min). The maximum exergy evaporation efficiency (ηex,evp) reached 27.02%, while specific energy consumption (SEC) decreased from 26.60 to 6.45 kJ/g (a four-fold reduction). Four key indicators: average drying rate (‾DR), average exergy evaporation efficiency (‾ηex,evp), SEC, irreversible exergy loss (ηex,loss) were integrated into an energy efficiency factor (EEF), and process conditions were optimized using response surface methodology (RSM). Experimental validation confirmed the optimal EEF and demonstrated a 75% reduction in CO2 emissions, achieving a balance between drying kinetics and energy utilization. This study provides a novel energy-efficient drying strategy for lignite, leveraging the synergistic effects of hot-air and microwave heating. The findings have practical implications for optimizing industrial drying processes, reducing carbon emissions, and enhancing the sustainability of coal-based energy systems.

title: Metabolomics-guided sustainable enhancement of disease-susceptible rice using Fe3O4 nanoparticles: From molecular mechanisms to cleaner production
abstract: Conventional rice production through excessive chemical inputs violates cleaner production principles, with disease-susceptible varieties requiring 40% more agrochemicals while experiencing 10-30% yield losses. This study investigates Fe3O4 nanoparticles as a potential cleaner production technology for sustainable rice enhancement through precision metabolic intervention. Applying 0.5 mg/L magnetite nanoparticles (5 nm) to rice achieved remarkable growth promotion: 193.44% shoot height enhancement and 74% root elongation using 50% less iron than conventional FeCl3, representing substantial improvements in nutrient utilization efficiency compared to traditional fertilizers. Metabolomics analysis (2085 metabolites) revealed mechanisms enabling this efficiency transformation: biphasic metabolic reprogramming from anabolic activation (0-48h) to defense priming (48-72h) avoided growth-defense trade-offs, while coordinated hormone regulation maximized resource utilization. The narrow optimal concentration (0.5 mg/L) demonstrates precision delivery advantages, eliminating wasteful over-application common in conventional approaches. Twenty metabolic pathways showed coordinated reorganization, enabling multifunctional benefits from single intervention. Unlike conventional fertilizers causing nutrient runoff and soil degradation, nanoparticles provide controlled release with potential for reduced environmental contamination. These findings establish nanotechnology-enabled approaches as potentially viable for sustainable rice production, offering pathways to while enhancing productivity. The demonstrated 50% reduction in iron requirements combined with growth enhancement provides molecular foundations for future assessment of Fe3O4 nanoparticles in sustainable rice production systems, directly supporting efforts toward responsible agricultural production and food security.

title: Tourism's curved path to global renewable energy growth
abstract: This study offers what appears to be the first systematic assessment of how tourism dynamics shape the trajectory of renewable energy use across 155 economies between 2003 and 2022. Using several complementary identification strategies, we uncover a non-linear association between tourism activity and renewable energy uptake. Specifically, the estimates indicate a U-shaped pattern: initial increases in tourism tend to restrain renewable energy consumption, whereas more advanced stages of tourism development are associated with accelerated adoption of renewables. The mechanisms we explore suggest that the curvature of this relationship is sensitive to international capital flows. Overall FDI inflows reinforce the U-shaped response, while greenfield investment and exposure to climate-related risks temper its strength. Additional analyses indicate that tourism affects renewable energy indirectly through shifts in industrial composition, gains in green productivity, and improvements in energy security. The results indicate that the role of tourism in the low-carbon transition is contingent on its stage of development and the broader investment environment. These insights underscore the importance of supporting a stable tourism sector while fostering conditions that promote renewable energy growth.

title: Process design and techno-economic evaluation of hydrogen production from microalgae conversion in molten salts
abstract: Hydrogen production from microalgae represents a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel-based methods. However, conventional thermochemical routes face challenges such as inadequate hydrogen yield/purity and persistent tar formation. This study proposes a novel integrated process for hydrogen production by thermochemical conversion of microalgae in molten hydroxide, which uniquely incorporates critical yet understudied ash removal and salt regeneration units. A rigorous, experimentally validated Aspen Plus model was developed to simulate the entire process. Operating at 750 °C with a microalgae feed rate of 1000 kg/h, the process produces 110.5 kg/h (equivalent to 30 mmol/g ash-free feedstock) of high-purity hydrogen (99.99%) with an energy conversion efficiency of 41.67%, which can be elevated to 46.57% by optimizing the ash removal strategy. Techno-economic analysis indicates a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of 35.07 CNY/kg, making it competitive among advanced thermochemical routes for microalgae conversion. Sensitivity analysis identifies feedstock cost as the most influential parameter. The LCOH can be significantly reduced to 15.45 CNY/kg when microalgae are priced at lignocellulosic biomass levels, which outperforms methane reforming/cracking with CO2 capture. These findings confirm the techno-economic viability of the molten hydroxide technology, highlighting the crucial role of feedstock sourcing and operation optimization in accelerating the commercial implementation.

title: Sustainable transformation in furniture manufacturing: The impact of green supply chain management in China
abstract: In the pursuit of sustainable business practices, this study explores the critical nexus of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) and its profound impact on the environmental performance within China's vibrant furniture industry. A gap exists in the literature on the influence of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) in this sector. To address this, we use multiple linear regression analysis to examine the interaction between enterprise strategic positioning, institutional environmental stewardship, and government supervision in shaping GSCM effectiveness. Our findings unveil the most influential factors, providing actionable insights that resonate with manufacturers and policymakers alike. This research not only bridges the gap in the current literature by introducing a novel methodology tailored to the furniture industry but also paves the way for a more sustainable and responsible furniture industry, underscoring the urgent need for strategic environmental stewardship in today's competitive landscape.

title: Global fine-scale assessment of the technical and economic potential of solar photovoltaic power using Google Earth Engine
abstract: The large-scale combustion of fossil fuels and the associated greenhouse gas emissions are considered the primary contributors to global warming. Accelerating the deployment of solar photovoltaics (PV) is therefore essential; however, global-scale assessments of areas where PV is both technically feasible and economically viable remain limited. Here, we present the first 1 km-resolution, pixel-level global assessment of the technical and economic potential of PV and construct an 11-year (2013-2023) affordability dataset that tracks how declining capital costs reshape siting opportunities. Using Google Earth Engine to integrate multi-source rasters with annually updated total installation costs and national electricity prices, we first estimate technically developable potential by applying a comprehensive set of physical and land-use constraints. We then apply two transparent economic filters to delineate economically developable land: (i) a payback period ≤15 years and (ii) a straight-line distance ≤50 km to the nearest road and settlement. Our results are as follows: (i) Technical potential reaches 12.96 × 103 PWh yr−1 (87.96 % of resource potential), whereas economically developable potential totals 4.99 × 103 PWh yr−1 (33.86 %)-enough to satisfy global electricity demand more than 170 times; (ii) areas with payback periods ≤15 years increased from 24.69 % of land in 2013 to 75.13 % in 2023; (iii) analysis of 93,257 existing PV plants reveals that 19.36 % of actual installations occupy farmland, underscoring land-use and food-security trade-offs and the need for agrivoltaic (AV) solutions. These findings provide an open and reproducible basis for prioritizing grid expansion, financing, and AV policies to accelerate PV deployment while safeguarding food and ecological security.

title: Exergy-based sustainability assessment of an agro-tourism-ecological system in a typical coffee-growing village: A ternary diagram analysis of sewage treatment optimization
abstract: Amid growing development demands and environmental pressures, enhancing the sustainability of integrated agro-tourism-ecological systems has become a pressing need. Using exergy analysis, this study assesses the 15-year (2009-2024) performance of Xinzhai Village, a representative coffee-growing community in Yunnan, China. Ternary diagrams are applied to compare system dynamics between the original state and a scenario optimized for sewage recycling. The results demonstrate that (1) the original scenario exhibited high exergy loss with minimal efficiency improvements, as indicated by only 17.05% and 27.55% reductions in Investment-Yield Ratio (IYR) and Non-renewable Yield Ratio (NRYR), respectively; (2) optimizing sewage treatment with threshold recycling significantly enhanced system performance, achieving a 50.63% reduction in IYR, 74.93% reduction in System Transformity (STr), and 55.92% reduction in NRYR by 2024; (3) the Ecosystem Resource-Yield Ratio (ERYR) in the optimized scenario remained consistently higher (44.70% in 2024 vs. 13.80% in the original scenario) despite a temporal decline, confirming improved ecological-economic synergy. And (4) ternary diagrams clearly illustrated the system's transition from linear to circular resource use, with phase points converging toward high-efficiency, low-dependence regions. In conclusion, integrating sewage recycling into rural development is a key strategy for enhancing energy efficiency and reducing environmental loads. This study recommends prioritizing decentralized wastewater treatment and reclaimed water reuse to support sustainable agro-tourism development in similar regions.

title: Docking the boat: Realizing boat-to-grid for recreational vessels through collaborative business model innovation
abstract: Boat-to-grid (B2G) has the potential to reduce the barriers for the electrification of the recreational boating sector and support the adoption of renewable energy sources. Despite considerable environmental benefits, such as reductions in noise and heavy metal emissions, technological and economic challenges hinder widespread adoption of B2G. Drawing on prior research and a case study from the Swedish recreational boating sector, this paper identifies key obstacles and enablers for B2G business models. The study shows how B2G can be realized during the four phases of the boating year and identifies core and peripheral actors with their specific challenges. Five general themes of barriers are identified: battery and infrastructure costs, uncertainty about the leadership and the future of electrification, system and technological barriers, access to insurance, and a lack of commonly recognized and attractive business models. For policymakers, the paper points to the potential benefits of policy support associated with knowledge development and improved industry coordination.

title: Decarbonizing concrete with biochar:Insights from life cycle sustainability assessment
abstract: Currently, substituting cement with biochar in cementitious composites has drawn considerable attention within the scientific community. The use of biochar produced from municipal solid waste offers a promising approach to improve concrete performance while promoting a circular economy and a sustainable management approach. However, most of the studies on biochar-enhanced concrete focused on mechanical properties; life cycle sustainability assessments (social, economic, and environmental) of biochar in the life cycle have not been addressed. This paper presents an integrated life cycle sustainability assessment that combines economic, social, and environmental impacts to evaluate municipal solid waste biochar-enhanced concrete in comparison with conventional concrete. A multi-criterial decision-making framework employing the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution was used to identify the most sustainable mix design. The result shows that replacing 5 wt% of cement with MSW-derived biochar increases compressive strength from 43.3 MPa to 45.5 MPa and lowers the global warming potential by about 5 wt%, without significant cost variation. The multi-criteria decision analysis confirmed that a 5 wt% of the biochar mix concrete represent the optimal alternative, achieving the best balance among the economic, social, and environmental indicators. Social impact showed the largest improvement: health-related damage, expressed in terms of societal willingness to pay to avoid these effects, decreased from an estimated USD 6487 for conventional concrete to USD 3538 for biochar-enhanced concrete. When the three sustainability pillars were integrated, the social life cycle assessment accounted 99.9 wt% of the total sustainability gap, emphasizing the dominant role of social factors. Overall, biochar produced from municipal solid waste not only enhances concrete performance but also supports waste valorization and circular economy objectives. Future research should address the long-term durability and large-scale applicability of biochar derived from municipal solid waste based concrete systems.

title: Recycling brick powder and recycled concrete powder in geopolymers: hydration kinetics, microstructure and mechanical properties
abstract: Understanding the hydration behavior of recycled brick powder (BP) and recycled concrete powder (CP) in geopolymers is crucial for their efficient utilization. The novelty of this study is that it combines isothermal calorimetry and low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR) to reveal the effects of BP and CP on the early (within 72 h) hydration kinetics of metakaolin (MK)-based geopolymers, and further investigates their influence on microstructural and mechanical properties. The results demonstrated that partial replacement of MK with BP or CP reduced the hydration degree of MK-based geopolymers up to 72 h while enhancing nucleation and growth rates. CP-containing geopolymers showed improved early-stage (up to 4 h) hydration degree through additional Calcium-Aluminate-Silicate-Hydrate (C–A–S–H) formation, however, their 28-day compressive strength decreased 5.9% to 67.9% compared to MK100. BP-containing geopolymers exhibited greater gel content development between 3 and 28 days owing to higher soluble Si4+ and Al3+ content in BP than CP. At 28 days, the geopolymer with 10% BP replacement showed reduced porosity, optimized pore size distribution, and a 3.2% increase in compressive strength compared to the MK100. In contrast, higher BP replacements (20–50%) led to compressive strength reductions ranging from 3.6% to 65.5% relative to MK100.

title: Integrating carbon-susceptibility risks into multi-zone green infrastructure prioritization for carbon-related ecosystem service conservation
abstract: Intensified human activities in urban agglomerations threaten regional carbon sinks and ecosystem services (ESs), making green infrastructure (GI) configuration critical for protecting carbon-associated benefits and achieving carbon neutrality. However, the interactions between carbon sinks and related ESs have received insufficient attention, carbon-emission risks are still inadequately quantified, and integrating them into GI spatial planning remains challenging. This study developed a new GI optimization framework for synergistically protecting carbon sinks and carbon-related ESs that integrates carbon-susceptibility risks (CSRs), then applied it to the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. A pressure–sensitivity–resilience (PSR) system was employed to assess multidimensional CSRs, which served as spatial cost constraints in GI optimization. The framework incorporated synergies and trade-offs between carbon sinks and both carbon-related and non-carbon-related ESs, coordinated their protection targets across management zones, and used the Marxan with Zones model to determine multi-zone GI solutions. Comparative analyses were conducted under four scenario combinations to illustrate the influence of incorporating CSRs and synergies on GI optimization solutions. The results indicate that synergistic protection of carbon sinks and carbon-related ESs is more efficient than targeting single features, reducing potential conflicts with non-carbon-related ESs. Integrating CSRs allowed for effective spatial prioritization among management zones. These findings support our conclusions that compatible conservation of carbon sinks and carbon-synergistic ESs, as well as consideration of CSRs, are essential for GI network optimization under carbon-neutrality goals. The proposed framework offers practical guidance for implementing GI networks in global urban agglomerations, supporting flexible conservation management under multiple objectives and risk threats.

title: Enhancing sustainability in electric vehicle reverse logistics from an open innovation perspective using fermatean fuzzy risk analysis
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) highlights the need for sustainable reverse logistics ecosystems to manage end-of-life batteries. These ecosystems involve diverse stakeholders with conflicting interests, making risk management critical for environmental and economic sustainability. This study identifies key stakeholders in EV Reverse Logistics Ecosystems (EVRLEs), evaluates their interrelationships, and prioritizes risks using a novel fuzzy-based method. The proposed method integrates interval-valued Fermatean fuzzy sets (IVFFSs) with the Matrix of Alliances and Conflicts: Tactics, Objectives and Recommendations (MACTOR) method to address uncertainty and analyze stakeholder influence and risk dynamics. Findings reveal government agencies as the most dominant stakeholder, while manufacturers, suppliers, and innovation partners are key stakeholders under market and regulatory constraints. Dominated stakeholders, including recycling centers and logistics providers, operate in upstream flows, whereas EV users, universities, and research institutions have limited influence. Environmental, financial, and safety risks require coordinated stakeholder engagement. Sensitivity and comparative analyses confirm the stability of the results and the consistency of the proposed method. The study supports policymakers and industry practitioners in enhancing collaboration, regulatory alignment, and open innovation in EV battery reverse logistics.

title: How to deliver mega-scale investment in climate infrastructure
abstract: Meeting global climate goals will require an estimated USD $136-275 trillion in investments by 2050, yet current capital flows fall well short of this need. This paper examines how the world's largest long-term investors, with the support of government and industry players, can help bridge this financing gap by scaling up climate infrastructure investments. Although these investors collectively manage USD $128 trillion in assets and have investment horizons wellsuited for large-scale climate projects, their involvement remains limited due to a structural gap in the capital marketplace. Through a series of semi-structured interviews with global asset owners, this study identified five critical criteria for improving collaboration and fostering scalable investment models: governance and control, transparency and reporting, aligned interests, thirdparty partnerships, and collaborative platforms. Addressing these criteria can help asset owners reduce risks, improve coordination, and unlock new investment opportunities in climate infrastructure. These findings also underscore the need for innovative, direct investment models that enhance collaboration and better align private capital with global climate goals.

title: Insights into structure-performance relationship and adsorption mechanism of amine-functionalized silicon-based adsorbents for high-efficiency CO2 capture
abstract: Amine-functionalized solid CO2 adsorbents show great promise as the next-generation materials for carbon capture; however, a comprehensive multidimensional evaluation of their CO2 adsorption performance remains insufficient. This study systematically evaluates the CO2 capture performance of amine-functionalized adsorbents. By loading TEPA, PEHA, and PEI onto mesoporous silica supports with different pore sizes, a three-dimensional assessment framework covering CO2 adsorption capacity, kinetics, and amine efficiency was established. Results show a volcano-shaped trend between amine loading and adsorption capacity; however, the loading corresponding to the maximum capacity does not deliver optimal overall performance, as kinetics and efficiency are considerably compromised at that point. The best-performing adsorbents generally exhibit amine loadings occupying about 40–50% of the support's pore volume, with CO2 adsorption capacities exceeding 2 mmol/g. Mechanistic studies reveal that lower loadings favor carbamate formation, whereas higher loadings promote carbamic acid dimers, which cross-link via hydrogen bonding, hinder mass transfer, and reduce adsorption rate and amine efficiency. This work provides theoretical insights and practical design strategies for developing high-performance solid amine adsorbents.

title: Novel insight into the investigation of CO2 capture performance of secondary amines based on quantum chemical calculations coupled with machine learning methods
abstract: Chemical absorption based on organic amines is currently one of the most promising carbon capture technologies. Among them, secondary amine absorbents have attracted significant attention because of the balance between reactivity and regeneration energy consumption. However, given the wide variety of secondary amines, the key properties influencing their CO2 capture performance remain unclear. This study investigated the structure-activity relationship between the structure of secondary amines and their CO2 reaction heat using a research methodology encompassing “quantum chemical analysis, data-driven feature screening, and in-depth quantification of core features.” Through quantum chemical analysis of eight typical secondary amine molecules, 24 quantum chemical descriptors were obtained. A Bayesian noise enhancement strategy was employed to address the limitations imposed by small sample sizes, and the contribution of various descriptors to their properties was systematically analyzed using random forest and XGBoost ensemble learning methods. The results revealed strong correlations between the SCPA charge of nitrogen atoms, local electrostatic potential (ESP), condensed local nucleophilicity index (CLNI), and orbital-weighted dual descriptor (OW DD) in secondary amine molecules and the CO2 reaction heat. Moreover, the random forest and XGBoost models achieved high accuracies with R2 values of 0.960 and 0.926, respectively. Additionally, this study utilized a gradient boosting decision tree model to perform regression fitting analysis between key molecular descriptors and CO2 reaction heat, achieving an R2 value of 0.996. This study employed machine learning approaches to investigate the extent of influence exerted by multidimensional chemical descriptors on the CO2 capture performance of secondary amines, thereby offering a novel perspective for an in-depth understanding of the CO2 capture performance of organic amines.

title: Experimental analysis and system design of a novel autothermal moderate-temperature chemical looping hydrogen production process with steam enhancement
abstract: Hydrogen is recognized as a clean and versatile energy carrier critical to global decarbonization. Among various production routes, steam methane reforming (SMR) dominates but suffers from high energy consumption, catalyst degradation, and substantial CO2 emissions. Chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) process has emerged as a promising alternative for its inherent CO2 capture and autothermal potential. In conventional CLHP, CH4 complete oxidation to CO2 is required for effective CO2 separation, necessitating high temperatures, limiting H2 yield, and causing significant irreversible energy losses.
