This offers a mutually reinforcing cycle of exploration and exploitation that can equip firms to meet contemporary challenges and institutional demands effectively to cope against the twin transition. Our study contributes with a four-phase process model for understanding the organisational change management processes required for the twin transition in project-based settings. Most existing research on absorptive capacity focuses on either organisational or industry-level dynamics, our study examines the loci of absorptive capacity (e.g., by examining firm and project boundaries) in a highly complex, project-driven industry such as construction. • This paper seeks to improve the understanding of the twin transition in construction project-based firms. • Helps project-driven industries to develop well-structured development processes for navigating organisational change. • Potential absorptive capacity (acquisition and assimilation of knowledge) takes place mainly in firm boundaries. • Realised absorptive capacity (transformation and exploitation) takes place mainly in the boundaries of projects they deliver.

title: A bi-objective optimization model for task scheduling in human-robot collaboration considering maintenance operations and energy consumption under uncertainty
abstract: This research unveils a unique integrated scheduling problem within an automated, multi-floor vertical farming tower, which acts as a viable urban agriculture solution for promoting sustainable food production. To this end, a bi-objective optimization model is formulated to simultaneously schedule four essential elements in the system, which consists of automated elevators, transport robots, human-assisted robots, and human workers, along with the maintenance tasks of automated elevators. In this regard, the first objective function minimizes the total completion time of operations, while the second one minimizes the total energy consumption of transport robots. Furthermore, this research encompasses all aspects of agricultural operations, namely planting, cultivation, and harvesting, to ensure that the proposed model is as maximally applicable as possible. In this context, a wide array of precedence, synchronization, and non-interference constraints are incorporated to offer a comprehensive strategy for addressing transportation and production challenges. In addition, the set-induced robust optimization approach is applied to manage the uncertainties linked to the processing times of production agents, the efficiency of transport robots, and their travel times. Ultimately, a detailed numerical analysis is conducted to evaluate the validity and applicability of the developed model and uncertainty approach. The computational analysis shows that increasing the number of transport robots by 30% causes a 37% reduction in the total completion time. In addition, a 50% enhancement in the efficiency of the transport robots leads to a 12% reduction in total completion time, along with a 10% decrease in energy consumption. What is more, the incorporation of safety requirements leads to an approximate increase of 4% in the total completion time.

title: Pollution haven or path to decarbonization? Assessing the co-control of pollution and carbon in China's industrial trade
abstract: Pollutants and carbon emissions share common origins, generating substantial synergies for integrated mitigation. Despite growing scholarly recognition of these synergies across multiple scales, their trade-driven co-reduction—particularly within industrial interregional trade networks—remains underexplored. In this study, we develop an Integrated Assessment Framework for Trade-driven Pollutants and Carbon Co-reduction (IAF-TPC), which integrates an environmentally extended multi-regional input-output (EE-MRIO) model, cross-elasticity (ELS) coefficient, and theoretical emission reduction metric. This framework systematically evaluates the theoretical emission reduction induced by China's interprovincial industrial trade, delineates the synergy degree between PR and CM, and identifies industrial subsectors contributing to synergistic outcomes. Results indicate that: (1) Hebei and Inner Mongolia function not only as major exporters of outsourced embodied carbon and air pollutants but also as primary contributors to emission reductions. Their principal outsourcing flows and mitigation contributions are directed toward Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Guangdong. (2) Synergy analysis reveals that most industrial subsectoral and interprovincial transfer pathways exhibit limited synergy. Strong synergy dominated by pollution reduction is concentrated in outsourcing transfer pathways from Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Inner Mongolia, whereas strong synergy dominated by carbon reduction is distributed in outsourcing transfer pathways from clean-energy-rich regions like Southwest China. (3) Pathways from western manufacturing sector more easily achieve carbon-reduction dominated synergy, while those from central-eastern mining sector and power and heating supply sector tend toward pollution-reduction dominated synergy. This study elucidates the mechanism of pollution transfer-responsibility mismatch and offers a critical foundation for designing differentiated and province-specific responsibility allocation mechanisms within China's industrial sector.

title: Dissolved oxygen abrupt variation and its hydrodynamic-based adjustability: phenomena identification, prediction model, and adaptive regulation strategies
abstract: Abrupt fluctuations in dissolved oxygen (DO) can pose severe ecological risks, yet their short-term dynamics and driving mechanisms remain poorly understood. Especially in the water diversion-based hydroproject, frequent gate operations induce hydrodynamic perturbations, but it also provides a manipulative way for DO variations. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on fixed thresholds or single-indicator assessments of DO, this study develops a novel framework combining abrupt variation scenario classification, machine-learning modeling, and probabilistic control analysis to elucidate how hydrodynamic disturbances drive DO abrupt shift events. Four DO abrupt variation scenarios were defined via first-order difference and quartile thresholds. Using hydrodynamic variables and their lagged terms as inputs, an XGBoost multi-class classification model was trained to identify these scenarios, achieving overall accuracies of 63.0% ∼79.1% across four representative monitoring stations in the longest water diversion project in the world, the South-to-North Water Diversion Project of China. Feature importance analysis revealed that gate opening degree and flow rate contributed 15.34% and 11.63%, respectively, to scenario discrimination, highlighting the dominant drivers of DO transitions. One-dimensional and two-dimensional probabilistic response analyses further revealed spatial heterogeneity in DO sensitivity to hydrodynamic regulation, with distinct control potentials for strong increase versus weak increase scenarios. An enhanced feedback strategy then quantified optimal regulation paths for shifting DO from high-risk to recovery scenarios, yielding up to a 17.81% increase in target-scenario probability while minimizing control cost. These findings demonstrate that coupling data-driven modeling with precise hydrodynamic interventions offers a robust tool for mitigating DO instability in engineered water systems.

title: Wildfire fuel-reduction biomass for remote energy: Small-scale combined heat and power feasibility and strategic implications for British Columbia's bioeconomy
abstract: Wildfire fuel-reduction treatments in British Columbia (BC) generate large volumes of underutilized biomass. This study assesses the technical suitability and supply chain economics of using biomass from thinning and surface fuel reduction for small-scale combined heat and power (CHP) systems. Biomass availability, including non-delimbed and delimbed energy wood, residues, and surface woody debris, was evaluated in a 12-ha forest stand in the interior of BC, Canada. Woodchip quality was analyzed for particle size distribution, ash content, moisture content, and bulk density. Supply chain costs were estimated for multiple recovery methods, machinery scales, and chipping locations, considering specific treatment options. Results showed that one year of natural air drying enabled non-delimbed and delimbed energy wood to meet CHP system requirements for particle size and ash content, whereas residues and woody debris required targeted post-processing. Supply chain costs ranged from $175-426 per oven-dry tonne, driven primarily by transportation distance and treatment intensity. These findings demonstrate that fuel-reduction biomass can support small-scale CHP system operations when feedstock is locally sourced and of sufficient quality. Integrating energy production with higher-value product streams may provide a practical approach to cost-effective biomass utilization while contributing to wildfire risk mitigation, local energy security, and the regional bioeconomy. This study offers a transferable framework for evaluating operational feasibility and supply chain design in other fire-prone regions. • Selected fuel-reduction biomass can serve as feedstock for small bioenergy systems. • One-year natural drying significantly reduced biomass moisture and fine particle content. • Supply chain costs ranged from $175 to $426 per oven-dry tonne across evaluated scenarios. • For short distance biomass recovery, chipping at the delivery site resulted in lower overall costs than roadside chipping.

title: Successional agroforestry systems enhance environmental sustainability in cacao production: Evidence from a long-term trial
abstract: Cacao is a strategic crop in many tropical countries, but achieving a balance between productivity, sustainability, and food security represents a complex challenge. This study presents a robust, multidimensional evaluation of five cacao production systems that integrates the energy–water–emissions–food (EWEF) nexus framework with life cycle assessment (LCA) and nutritional functional units to assess long-term environmental sustainability. Based on a 12-year dataset (2010–2021) from a long-term trial, the analysis spans from the establishment of the plots to their maturity. The systems include full-sun monocultures and agroforestry under organic and conventional management, and a successional agroforest, i. e., a highly diverse and dense system without external inputs. Monocultures, especially conventional ones, achieved higher cacao yields (between 1.77 and 2.22 times) but worse environmental outcomes (between −2.5% and −94%). In contrast, agroforestry systems produced 5.2 times more food (cacao and associated crops) per hectare, improving resource use efficiency in terms of energy (3.6 times more efficient) and using less water per kilogram of total food produced (−96%). Additionally, nutritional quality indicators reached higher values in relation to water and energy use in agroforestry systems (4 to 14 times higher), mainly in the successional one. Compared with monocultures, agroforestry systems had lower environmental impacts across most of the analyzed categories, during both the young (2010–2016) and the mature phase (2017–2021). Organic management did not systematically report lower environmental impacts for all categories and functional units analyzed. Our findings indicate that successional agroforests combine efficient resource use with high nutritional quality, and achieve similar cacao yields to those of conventional and organic agroforestry systems. Overall, this study supports the potential of diversified agroforestry systems—especially successional agroforestry—to advance food security and sustainability goals in cacao production. • Analysis of the environmental and productive performance of different cacao systems. • Monocultures achieve higher cocoa yields (+40%) but less food per hectare (−81%). • Agroforests have lower impacts in the young and mature phases (between −2.5 and −96%). • Highest efficient resource use and nutritional quality in successional agroforests. • Differences between organic and conventional farming are inconclusive.

title: Water-carbon intensity transition driven by the inter-basin water transfer project: spatiotemporal patterns and attribution analysis
abstract: Inter-basin water transfer (IBWT) projects are increasingly implemented to mitigate regional water shortages and support socioeconomic development. However, researches about the impacts of IBWT on the coupled water-carbon systems in both water-receiving area and water-source area remain limited. The indicator of water-carbon intensity (WCI) is proposed to assess the coupled impacts of IBWT on water-carbon systems. Taking the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Transfer Project (MR-SNWTP) in China as a case study, we employed a counterfactual trend comparison and Difference-in-Differences strategy to investigate its impacts on water use, carbon emissions, and WCI, and applied the LMDI decomposition to investigate the driving factors of WCI. Results indicated that: (1) The MR-SNWTP increased total water use in the water-receiving area in the early post-transfer years, while suppressing industrial and domestic water use in the water-source area. Total carbon emissions continued to rise during the pre-transfer period but stabilized during the post-transfer period in the water-receiving area. (2) The WCI exhibited a significant upward trend in the water-receiving area during the pre-transfer period, whereas it remained relatively stable during the post-transfer period. Economic water productivity (EWP) served as a positive driver of WCI, while energy intensity (EI) and energy structure (ES) exerted negative impacts. (3) The MR-SNWTP effectively stabilized the upward trend of WCI observed during the pre-transfer period by enhancing water availability and promoting low-carbon industrial transformation in the water-receiving area. Our study offers new empirical evidence on how large-scale IBWT projects influence the water-carbon nexus, providing guidance for integrated water and carbon management for sustainable development.

title: Design optimization in the spindle structure of a multi-blade rip saw machine to improve cut surface quality and minimize wood waste
abstract: This study presents the structural optimization of the main shaft support structure in a multi-blade rip saw machine. The optimization aims to enhance cutting speed and precision while minimizing weight, manufacturing costs, wood waste, energy consumption, and carbon emissions. The optimization involved numerical simulation and performance analysis across multiple design iterations evaluated in terms of weight, displacement (horizontal and vertical), and natural frequencies. The optimized design incorporates a thickened full-perimeter jacket reinforcement covering 50% of the cantilever beam length. This design achieves a balanced reduction in machine weight alongside improved stiffness, dynamic performance, and stress redistribution. Specifically, the optimized design shows 6% reduction in the structural weight of the rip saw machine with natural frequencies increasing by 23% to 28%. Life cycle assessment of the optimized design demonstrates significant environmental benefits including reduced transportation emissions, minimized wood waste, and decreased energy consumption from sanding operations. Overall, the optimized design is projected to reduce carbon emissions by approximately 920,000 metric tons of CO2 annually, equivalent to the sequestration potential of approximately 41 million trees. These findings underscore the environmental and operational benefits of structural optimization of industrial multi-blade rip saw machines.

title: Synergistic optimization of computing-power-cooling-heat multi-energy flow: Integrating flexible data centers and district heating networks
abstract: Mining flexible and reliable resources on both energy consumption side and during transmission process to match the fluctuations of renewable energy sources can reduce system capacity requirements and enhance operational performance. However, a major challenge lies in the seamless coordination and real-time management of diverse energy flows. This study presents a holistic framework that coordinates computing-power-cold-heat multi-energy flows across data centers, integrated energy systems, and district heating networks, enabling chained optimization and system-wide synergistic operation. This synergy is achieved by establishing a closed-loop energy flow where the flexibility of data center computing loads and the virtual thermal storage of the heating network are coordinated to balance multi-energy supply and demand dynamically. By leveraging them, the approach establishes a closed-loop energy chain that not only enhances renewable energy integration and waste heat recovery but also enables real-time balancing of electricity, cold, and heat demands. A double-layer optimization method is proposed to co-optimize system design and operation of the chained system. The outer layer configures components’ capacities, while the inner layer schedules computing workloads, temperature regulation of networks, and multi-energy flows, resolving configuration-operation interdependencies. A case study validates the proposed methods through comparing three cases. The simulation results demonstrate that the scheme with the flexibilities of data center and heating networks achieves a 19% reduction in total cost and a 32% decrease in carbon emission costs compared to the baseline without workload shifting and heat storage in heating networks, significantly enhancing renewable integration and operational flexibility.

title: Policy-driven distinct dust pollution patterns in a super-large magnesite mining area: Spatiotemporal analysis integrating satellite remote sensing and CALPUFF model
abstract: As global industrialization accelerates, increasing concern regarding health impacts on living environments has positioned air quality at the forefront of research. Dust pollution is particularly severe in open-pit mining areas, primarily due to the methods of open-pit extraction and processing. This study investigates dust dispersion driven by both anthropogenic and natural factors, employing multi-temporal aerosol optical depth (AOD) analysis, particle size distributions, and a comprehensive air quality model that incorporates plume dynamics (CALPUFF) modeling. Concentrating on Haicheng-Dashiqiao area in China, the world's largest magnesite mining area, this paper examines spatiotemporal variations in the atmospheric environment. (1) Over the past two decades, magnesite mining intensity rose from 9.17 in 2014 to 17.09 in 2024 (peaking at 28.98 in 2022). Despite this increase, AOD levels during 2014-2024 remained below those of 2001-2014, largely due to the implementation of effective pollution control policies. AOD hotspots remained concentrated within mining boundaries, consistently exceeding levels observed in surrounding non-mining regions. (2) The dust pollutants above the magnesite mining area are characterized primarily by large-sized particles, which differ significantly from those found in non-mining areas. This distinction in particle size is particularly pronounced during the summer months. (3) The PM/TSP transport fields simulated by CALPUFF align closely with the spatial patterns of satellite-derived AOD. Among the influencing factors, wind direction is the most significant, capable of transporting pollutants from the mining area up to approximately 40 km away. Furthermore, the dilution effect of spring winds on AOD is more pronounced than that observed in summer.

title: The impact of carbon emissions on financial performance: A case study of global semiconductor chip manufacturers and equipment suppliers
abstract: The semiconductor industry, pivotal to global technological advancement and economic growth, faces escalating environmental challenges as its carbon emissions are projected to rise by 8% annually. This study examines the relationship between carbon emissions and financial performance within the global semiconductor manufacturing and equipment ecosystem, focusing on chip manufacturers and equipment suppliers. Utilizing data from 34 leading companies (2019–2022), we analyze the impact of narrowly defined total carbon emissions (ΔTN_CE) and Scope 3 emissions (ΔS3_CE) on return on assets (ROA). Our findings reveal a significant negative correlation between ΔTN_CE and ROA for chip manufacturers, indicating that emission reductions align with improved financial outcomes. Conversely, ΔS3_CE shows a positive association with ROA in this segment, reflecting nascent stages of Scope 3 management and market responses. Equipment suppliers exhibit no statistically significant links between emissions and financial performance. The study underscores the critical role of value chain collaboration—particularly with upstream suppliers, responsible for 20–30% of emissions—to achieve decarbonization. The study proposes that targeted carbon strategies, supported by policy and cross-industry partnerships, can reconcile environmental and economic goals in this high-growth sector.

title: Evaluation of bio-oil fractions from woody biomass pyrolysis as precursors for bio-binder in anode manufacture
abstract: To reduce the environmental impact of the aluminium industry, this study evaluates various bio-oil fractions as precursors to synthesize bio-binder, which is a potential sustainable alternative to coal tar pitch. Bio-oil fractions, including unfiltered and filtered bio-oils, and their aqueous and organic fractions, were investigated. The bio-oil and bio-binder samples were extensively characterized in terms of physicochemical properties and toxicological assessment. The evaluation demonstrates that the organic bio-oil fraction exhibits higher carbon content, greater aromaticity degree, and improved thermal stability. Toxicity assessment reveals that filtration effectively reduces the toxic risk associated with the bio-oil. The bio-binder derived from the organic fraction possesses a higher carbon content of 74.5 wt.%, a viscosity of 4.84 Pa·s, and superior thermal and oxidative stabilities, compared to other bio-oil fractions. The green anode made of filtered organic fraction shows comparable apparent density and electrical resistivity to that made of commercial binder. The findings suggest that the filtered bio-oil organic fraction is a promising precursor for bio-binder synthesis, with properties approaching those of coal tar pitch. This study introduces comprehensive perspectives and methodologies for selecting and tuning bio-oil as a sustainable alternative for the carbon anode production in the aluminium industry.

title: Comparative life cycle assessment of one-step and two-step injection molding compounding for manufacturing recycled glass fiber/polypropylene composites
abstract: Despite advances in fiber-reinforced polymer recycling, few studies have assessed the environmental impacts of manufacturing processes and their compatibility with recycled composites. This study presents a comparative Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of a conventional compounding plus granulation and injection molding process, and an innovative one-step injection molding compounding (IMC) for the cleaner production of composites using virgin and recycled polypropylene reinforced with mechanically recycled glass fibers. Two LCA perspectives, manufacturing and component, differ in functional unit, system boundaries, and material modelling. The manufacturing perspective evaluates cradle-to-grave processing impacts per geometrically identical item, while the component perspective includes raw material acquisition and end-of-life treatment of the component compared at equal tensile strength. Both perspectives show that IMC reduces environmental impacts across all 16 EF3.1 impact categories for all material combinations. Infrastructure and energy use are major contributors in the manufacturing perspective, while manufacturing accounts for roughly half of total impacts in the component perspective considering a passive use phase. Results are sensitive to processing waste and mass variations based on process-induced differences in composite quality. The strength-based equivalence applied here is simplified and should be adapted for industrial design contexts. Material modelling approaches, the zero-burden approach or the Circular Footprint Formula, influence virgin polypropylene impacts but provide comparable results for recycled materials. This deviation from previous findings may be case-specific, highlighting uncertainties in the formula's parameters, which require region- and market-specific evaluation. The study also discusses implications of IMC's low technological readiness and experimental setup, providing insights for other assessments considering scale effects. • Recycled materials from post-industrial organosheet and post-consumer packaging waste. • LCA methodological choices from manufacturing and component perspectives. • Reduction of environmental impacts due to one-step injection molding compounding. • Further research on specific field of application and industrial upscaling required.

title: A novel sensor layout method and deep learning model: leakage source term estimation for natural gas station sites
abstract: Accurate and efficient source term estimation (STE) is essential for ensuring the safe operation of natural gas facilities in the event of hazardous gas leakage. A well-designed sensor deployment, as the foundation of STE, directly affects the accuracy of source term estimation methods. Existing sensor placement methods are often limited to specific operating conditions and rely on prior information about the leakage source, making them impractical for real-world STE applications. Furthermore, traditional STE methods suffer from poor real-time performance and are difficult to adapt to dynamic leakage scenarios. This paper proposes a novel sensor optimization deployment method based on information entropy theory, designed to be applicable under multi-objective operating conditions. The proposed method employs a hybrid algorithm combining genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) to minimize the objective function, enabling optimal sensor placement under multiple wind direction conditions. Building on this foundation, the CEEMDAN algorithm is employed to denoise and reconstruct the sensor's noisy data. A fused model combining a bidirectional temporal convolutional network and a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiTCN-BiGRU) is then constructed to achieve high-precision estimation of the leak source term. Compared with traditional sensor deployment strategies, the optimized configuration improves the accuracy of source location estimation in STE methods by 24.5%, while reducing the estimation error of leak intensity by 87.3%. In terms of the STE model, the proposed CEEMDAN-BiTCN-BiGRU model achieves a leak intensity estimation accuracy of 99.90%, representing a 6.5% improvement in source location accuracy over the best-performing conventional model. These results demonstrate that the proposed sensor optimization approach and CEEMDAN-BiTCN-BiGRU model hold promise for applications in gas leak source term estimation.

title: Identifying active nitrate-assimilating bacteria that alleviate secondary salinization in facility soil driven by carbon source availability
abstract: Eliminating nitrate is a prerequisite for remediating secondary salinization in facility soils. Nitrate immobilization via microbial assimilation can effectively remove excess soil nitrate, which is regulated by carbon amendments. However, active nitrate-assimilating taxa and their responses to carbon source amendments remain unclear. 15N-labeled nitrate tracing of secondary salinized soil amended with different carbon sources (control, glucose, xylan, cellulose, wheat straw, corncob, wood flour, and cow dung) revealed that glucose and xylan amendments resulted in the most rapid and pronounced increase in gross nitrate immobilization rate (162.29- and 175.29-fold increases vs. control within 7 days), followed by cellulose (26.84-fold) and corncob amendments (18.68-fold). Nitrate depletion showed similar trends, with significantly lower residual NO3−-N under glucose/xylan amendments. Additionally, these two amendments also resulted in higher nitrate loss and N2O emissions. 15N-DNA-based stable isotope probing (SIP) revealed unique nitrate-assimilating communities under high-immobilization carbon sources. Specifically, unclassified Halomonas and Photobacterium dominated under glucose/xylan amendments, whereas unclassified Cellvibrio and Streptomyces thrived under cellulose and corncob amendments, respectively. Path analysis revealed that the primary factor affecting the immobilization rate was the community-level ribosomal RNA operon (rrn) copy number of nitrate-assimilating bacteria, with its effect surpassing diversity index, community composition, and assimilation gene abundance. Carbon source availability indices, including initial dissolved organic carbon and MC source (CO2 efflux), indirectly increased nitrate immobilization rate by stimulating rrn copy number and assimilation gene abundance. This study identified nitrate-assimilating bacteria and revealed the community-level rrn copy number as a critical functional trait driving nitrate immobilization in secondary salinized soil.

title: Closing the loop on nanoplastic pollution: A 3D printed coral-like adsorbent enabling cyclic adsorption and ice-crystal catalytic degradation for waste minimization
abstract: Nanoplastics obtained from the decomposition of plastics have received extensive attention from researchers worldwide because of their wide distribution and potential hazards to human health. In this study, based on the bionic principle of coral predation mechanism, an efficient adsorbent with a three-dimensional bionic structure was proposed, and the degradation behaviour of polystyrene (PS) nanoparticles (≤500 nm) under extrusion at the interface between the adsorbent surface and ice crystals was investigated. The composite adsorbent with bionic coral structure (3DGPC) was prepared by combining the composite of polyethyleneimine (PEI) and carbon nanotubes (CNT) with graphene oxide (GO) in a certain ratio (PEI: CNT: GO = 1:2:4), which had an adsorption capacity of 199.66 mg/g and a capture efficiency of up to 96% for the nanoplastics in the water. The adsorption mechanism was investigated with the help of XPS and DFT calculations, and the adsorption process was dominated by electrostatic and chemical bonding interactions between nanoplastics and adsorbents. The presence of anions in the actual water also affects the capture efficiency of nanoplastics by 3DGPC due to the competitive adsorption effect. Under the simulated freezing conditions in the extreme cold zone, the reactive oxygen species generated during the extrusion and squeezing of nanoplastics at the interface between the surface of the 3DGPC material and ice crystals can further promote the degradation of nanoplastics, and the adsorbent still maintains more than 80% of adsorption efficiency after five freeze-thaw cycles, and the degradation-regeneration at the interface of the ice crystals maintains the adsorption capacity of the material. Therefore, this study combines bionic structures with 3D printing and applies it for the first time to a special scenario of synergistic degradation of nanoplastics at the ice crystal interface.

title: Unveiling the triple roles of carbonyl groups in carbon nitride for enhanced solar-driven peroxymonosulfate activation towards efficient water decontamination
abstract: Photocatalytic peroxymonosulfate (PC-PMS) activation is a promising yet challenging strategy for wastewater purification, particularly in metal-free systems plagued by sluggish charge kinetics and ill-defined active sites. Herein, we engineered carbonyl (C=O) bridged graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) to achieve rapid sulfamethoxazole (SMX) degradation in a PC-PMS system and unravelled structure-activity relationships. Combined experimental and theoretical calculations unveil the tripartite functionality of the C=O groups, which enhances the separation of photogenerated charge carriers via an in-plane S-scheme homojunction during photocatalysis, serves as robust active sites for PMS activation to generate singlet oxygen (1O2) in the dark heterogeneous catalysis, and reduces the intersystem crossing barrier to sustain 1O2 production through an energy-transfer pathway across the entire process. Such a threefold synergetic effect advanced 96.8% SMX removal in 90 min and complete removal of SMX in real pharmaceutical wastewater within 60 min. Furthermore, the SMX degradation pathway and intermediate toxicity were further elucidated. This work provides valuable insights for designing advanced metal-free PC-PMS catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: Urea-tailored biochar activated peroxydisulfate for carbazole degradation: An electron transfer process from in-plane to out-of-plane
abstract: Carbazole (CBZ) is a ubiquitous and toxic N-heterocyclic contaminant in water and soil, posing substantial environmental risks. Current remediation strategies for CBZ struggle with low efficiency, high energy consumption, or strict operational conditions, making persulfate-based advanced oxidation a promising alternative. Herein, we synthesized a series of urea-tailored biochars (UBCs) via low-temperature co-pyrolysis. Among them, UBC5 featuring an extremely high N content (21.4%) showed optimal peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation for CBZ degradation. The UBC5/PDS system achieved ∼90% CBZ removal within 1 h across pH 3-9, and exhibited strong resistance to inorganic anions (Cl−, SO42−, H2PO4−) and humic acid. Furthermore, the system effectively degraded CBZ in soil (71-82% within 1 h), with residual concentrations falling below safety thresholds for industrial land after 12 h. Quenching experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance, and electrochemical analyses revealed a non-radical degradation pathway: UBC5-PDS∗ mediated electron transfer, with a minor contribution from 1O2. Characterizations and density functional theory calculations elucidated a unique “in-plane to out-of-plane electron transfer” mechanism. The degradation intermediates exhibited reduced toxicity, with negligible adverse effects on soybean growth. Notably, UBC5 has lower production cost ($9.52 kg−1) and carbon emissions (18.38 kg CO2 e kg−1) than typical activators. This study provides new insight for the design of carbon-based persulfate activators and an efficient, sustainable approach for the remediation of CBZ-contaminated water and soil.

title: Enhanced SO2F2 degradation via Fe2O3-based catalyst coupled with DBD plasma
abstract: SO2F2 gas is widely used in pest control and garden insect management because of its powerful diffusion and penetration capability. However, it is a potent greenhouse gas. Therefore, its degradation treatment can help mitigate atmospheric pollution. This study investigated the effect of Fe2O3 synergized with dielectric barrier discharge plasma on the degradation of SO2F2 through the density functional theory (DFT) analysis of the mutual reaction between Fe2O3 (001) surfaces and SO2F2. Results indicated that Fe2O3 effectively promoted the decomposition of SO2F2 and improved the distribution of degradation products, facilitating the conversion of SO2F2 into manageable SO2. At an applied power of 110 W, destruction and removal efficiency (DRE) and energy yield (EY) reached 91% and 7.6 g/kWh, respectively, with SO2 selectivity in the products reaching 54%. The degradation products of SO2F2 mainly included SO2, SOF2, and SOF4, with additional absorption peaks corresponding to SF6 and SiF4 being detected. DFT simulations revealed that on the Fe2O3 (001) surface, SO2F2 experienced the cleavage of two S–F bonds to form SO2, whereas released Fe atoms formed stable Fe–F bonds with surface Fe sites. This work provides theoretical and experimental insights into the efficient and environmentally benign degradation of SO2F2.

title: Impact of digital infrastructure on the income of rural residents: Empirical evidence from China
abstract: This study explores the impact of digital infrastructure on the income of rural residents in China's old revolutionary base areas, using panel data from 914 counties between 2010 and 2022. Taking the Broadband China Policy (BCP) as a quasi-natural experiment, a time-varying difference-in-differences model is employed to identify the policy's effects and mechanisms. The results reveal that digital infrastructure significantly increases rural residents' income by enhancing government fiscal capacity and promoting social informatization. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the income-boosting effects are more pronounced in regions with low broadband access density and high agricultural machinery endowment, indicating that both digital access and production factor complementarities shape policy effectiveness. Furthermore, spatial econometric analysis confirms positive spillover effects, suggesting that digital infrastructure construction in one region can promote income growth in economically adjacent areas. The findings highlight digital infrastructure as a critical driver of inclusive rural development, providing valuable policy implications for narrowing the digital divide, fostering synergistic integration of digital and traditional assets, and achieving coordinated regional prosperity in underdeveloped areas.

title: Hydrogen evolution behavior and morphology regulation of electrowinning of iron in acidic sulfate system
abstract: In response to the global transition towards low-carbon and potentially zero-carbon industries, the steel sector can feasibly transition from carbon-based to electrically-driven processes. Electrowinning of iron represents a cutting-edge, low-carbon process technology characterized by ease of regulation and high energy efficiency. Within an acidic system, the electrowinning of iron cathodes is subject to competitive reactions. The hydrogen evolution side reaction can adversely affect the current efficiency of iron deposition and compromise the uniformity of the deposition layer at the electrode interface, posing challenges to the production of high-quality iron products. Given the insufficient understanding of the hydrogen evolution reaction and bubble formation during electrowinning of iron in acidic environments, this study investigates the impact of these phenomena on the morphology of electrowinning of iron. It investigates the impact of these processes on the morphology of electrowinning of iron, confirming that the “evolution - growth - coalescence - desorption” sequence of hydrogen bubbles contributes to the development of pores and other defects in the deposited layer, ultimately leading to the initiation and propagation of microcracks. In response to these challenges, the paper proposes three regulatory strategies for low-temperature electrowinning of iron. By adjusting the temperature or employing surface sandblasting, the escape of bubbles can be enhanced. Modifying the current deposition mode can improve the morphology of the deposited layer, thereby mitigating the issue of cracking during electrowinning of iron. This research is significant for advancing stable low-temperature electrowinning of iron, particularly advocating for the combined application of the three proposed methods.

title: Ni/Biochar-catalyzed biomass gasification for process-compatible NOx reduction in cement pre-calciner: pathways and mechanisms
abstract: In-situ reductant generation within the cement pre-calciner is a critical requirement for achieving process-compatible denitrification (de-NOx), as it supplies H2 and CO to enhance established NH3-SNCR pathways or enable direct NOx reduction. However, conventional biomass gasification under flue gas conditions suffers from low gas yield and poor reductant selectivity, resulting in limited de-NOx efficiency and high reliance on ammonia. Herein, we address this upstream bottleneck by developing Ni catalysts supported on waste-derived activated carbon (Ni/AC) featuring highly dispersed Ni clusters and strong metal–support interactions. Under representative pre-calciner conditions, Ni/AC-catalyzed biomass gasification exhibited a 21-fold enhancement in total gas yield (from 198 mL/g to 4237 mL/g), increased H2 and CO selectivity from 40% to 95%, and suppressed CO2 formation from 54% to only 3%, while demonstrating high adaptability to diverse biomass feedstocks. Mechanistically, highly dispersed Ni sites promote sequential H2O dissociation into ·OH and ·H radicals, lowering the activation barriers for aromatic tar conversion (modeled by toluene) by 0.54 and 1.09 eV for C–H and C–C bond cleavage, respectively, thereby promoting deep tar cracking. Meanwhile, CO2 tends to activate on Ni sites and then break the C=O bond, providing an alternative pathway for CO formation. These insights capture the dominant reaction trends governing reductant formation on Ni surfaces. Overall, this work demonstrates the efficient and selective generation of reductants via catalytic biomass gasification in cement flue gas, laying the scientific foundation for process-compatible de-NOx during clinker production.

title: Digital vs traditional: the impact of different disaster knowledge promotion paths on farmers' disaster preparedness
abstract: Digital technology, with its wide accessibility, real-time interactivity and efficient information dissemination capabilities, has opened up a brand-new path for the popularization and transmission of disaster risk knowledge. The digital promotion of disaster prevention knowledge obtained, exchanged and internalized through the Internet has been deeply integrated into the traditional knowledge promotion system dominated by the government, shaping the behavioral logic of farmers in disaster preparedness. Using the Logit model and 685 household questionnaires from flood-threatened areas in Sichuan Province, China, this study explored the effects of digital and traditional disaster prevention knowledge promotion methods on farmers' disaster preparedness behavior. It is found that: (1) Traditional knowledge promotion can significantly improve farmers' disaster preparedness behavior, and digital knowledge promotion can also significantly improve farmers' disaster preparedness behavior. The conclusions are still valid after considering sample self-selection and robustness test. (2) Both the traditional and the digital promotion strategies can significantly improve catastrophe avoidance behavior when they are utilized concurrently, with digital strategies exhibiting a stronger marginal effect. (3) The two extension methods have a substitution effect on farmers' disaster preparedness behavior, indicating that farmers' reliance on one type of promotion method will weaken the behavioral promoting effect of the other type. Therefore, to further strengthen the effectiveness of disaster prevention and management, this paper proposes to optimize traditional disaster prevention publicity strategies, advocate farmers to adopt digital learning approaches, and build an interactive online and offline disaster prevention knowledge dissemination system.

title: Quantifying transboundary ecosystem services flows to inform ecological compensation in the China-Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor
abstract: Transboundary sustainability challenges increasingly require integrated evaluations of ecosystem service (ES) interdependencies to support equitable and efficient resource governance. Yet, current frameworks remain constrained by static, local-scale accounting, overlooking the tele-coupled dynamics of cross-border flows in rapidly integrating economic zones. Bridging this gap, we propose a novel methodology that couples the spatial quantification of biophysical flows with socio-economic valuation. We analyze the tele-coupled flows of four critical ES—food, freshwater, carbon sequestration and recreation—across the China-Indochina Peninsula Economic Corridor (CIPEC). Our approach transcends conventional mapping by monetizing these flows, thereby establishing a rigorous foundation for transnational ecological compensation (EC). We reveal significant spatial mismatches between ES supply and demand among participating nations. The results show that Myanmar, endowed with abundant natural resources, acts as the primary ES supplier in the CIPEC, with a total surplus valued at USD$20.31 billion, whereas Thailand is a main beneficiary, facing deficits in freshwater and carbon sequestration services valued at USD$1.20 billion and USD$20.00 billion, respectively. The strongest tele-coupling effects were observed for recreational and food services between Singapore and Malaysia (79.68% and 48.76%, respectively), and for freshwater and carbon sequestration between Yunnan Province, China and Myanmar (18.14%), and Myanmar and Thailand (33.17%). These findings provide a strategic tool for shifting from siloed national management to cooperative regional governance, offering precise quantitative evidence to design equitable cross-border payment schemes. Ultimately, this study contributes to cleaner production strategies by elucidating how optimizing transboundary resource allocation can align environmental liabilities with entitlements, thereby enhancing regional resilience and socio-ecological sustainability.

title: MgAlFe-layered double hydroxides/carbon nitride photocatalysts for nitrogen oxides abatement: enhancing visible light driven performance while minimizing reliance on critical raw materials
abstract: The development of effective and sustainable photocatalysts for air pollution abatement is critical to address both environmental and resource security challenges. In this work, novel MgAlFe layered double hydroxides were synthesised. These materials were combined with graphitic carbon nitride to form heterostructured photocatalysts (MAF/CN) for nitrogen oxides removal under visible light. Partial substitution of Al 3+ with Fe 3+ enhanced visible-light absorption and photocatalytic activity. Notably, the best performance was achieved for the formulation with the lowest Mg:M 3+ ratio (Mg 2 Al 0.25 Fe 0.75 ). The reduced consumption of Mg 2+ and Al 3+ , both of which are considered critical raw materials, aligns with the European Union's objectives on resource efficiency and sustainability. The optimized composite (MAF/CN-5) exhibited a remarkable visible light nitrogen oxide removal efficiency (E NO ≈ 60 %) and complete selectivity (S = 100 %). Electron paramagnetic resonance and radical scavenger studies suggested the operation of a Z-scheme mechanism involving the generation of hydroxyl and superoxide radicals and effective suppression of charge carrier recombination. These photocatalysts also demonstrated excellent stability over multiple cycles. Overall, the Mg 2 Al 0.25 Fe 0.75 /g-C 3 N 4 system represents a promising, low-cost, and critical raw materials-conscious solution for solar-driven nitrogen oxides abatement. The material shows clear potential for real-world application in urban air purification. • Fe 3+ substitution promotes the visible-light activity of MgAl LDHs. • Optimized Mg 2 Al 0.25 Fe 0.75 photocatalyst reduces the use of CRM by 25 %. • Mg 2 Al 0.25 Fe 0.75 /g-C 3 N 4 composite removes 60 % NO under visible light. • Photocatalyst shows 100 % selectivity and long-term stability. • Z-scheme mechanism governs .•OH and •O 2 ˉ radicals formation

title: Self-cleaning nanofiber membrane for efficient oil-water separation and dye degradation
abstract: Conventional hydrophobic membranes often suffer from fouling accumulation due to the absence of effective self-cleaning mechanisms, thereby hindering their long-term operational stability and recyclability. In this study, a polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based composite nanofiber membrane with a hierarchical micro-nano surface structure was fabricated by combining the in-situ growth of TiO with an optimization of octadecyltrimethoxysilane (OTMS) coating morphology. Benefiting from the unique hierarchical morphology of micron-scale flower clusters and nano-protrusions, coupled with the synergistic effect of photocatalyst TiO and the superhydrophobic layer OTMS, the resulting nanofiber membrane (PAN/TiO/OTMS) exhibited outstanding dual-functional properties of superhydrophobicity (water contact angle >154°, sliding angle <5°) and photocatalytic activity (a degradation efficiency of 99 % for methylene blue within 150 min). Moreover, the PAN/TiO/OTMS nanofiber membrane demonstrated favorable demulsification capability in water-in-oil emulsions, with an oil permeation flux of 2388 L m·h and a water separation efficiency of 99.9 %. More importantly, owing to dual self-cleaning mechanisms of physical superhydrophobicity and chemical photocatalysis, the as-prepared PAN/TiO/OTMS exhibited a favorable antifouling and regeneration performance, demonstrating the oil flux recovery above 83 % and the irreversible fouling ratio below 17 % after multiple operation cycles. This study offers a practical strategy for the rational development of advanced membranes that integrate synergistic physical and chemical self-cleaning properties.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution of trade-off/synergy relationships and bundles in ecosystem services in Fujian, China: An integrated PLUS-InVEST-SOM framework
abstract: Coastal regions in developing economies increasingly face trade-offs between ecosystem services (ESs) provision and urban expansion, while scenario-based projections of ESs remain limited. This study integrated the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS), Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST), and machine-learning approaches to quantify five ESs—water yield (WY), soil retention (SEC), carbon storage (CS), habitat quality (HQ), and phosphorus emission (PE)—under natural development (ND), economic development (ED), and ecological protection (EP) scenarios in Fujian, China, during 2030–2060. Key findings are as follows: (1) Model validation demonstrated high predictive accuracy (Kappa = 0.86; Figure of Merit = 0.40). ND and ED scenarios resulted in approximately 7.5% forest loss, whereas the EP scenario preserved 99.17% of existing forest cover. (2) Temporal analysis revealed divergent ESs dynamics: CS and HQ decreased by 2.4% and 4.4%, respectively, while WY, SEC, and PE increased concurrently with urban expansion. Conversely, the EP scenario exhibited marginal increases in WY (0.03%), SEC (0.01%), and CS (0.71%), while PE and HQ remained stable. Spatial correlation analysis identified seven synergistic relationships among WY, SEC, HQ, and CS, and three trade-off relationships involving PE. (3) Ecosystem service bundles (ESBs) were classified into four distinct types. ND and ED scenarios substantially restructured ESBs, whereas the EP scenario maintained structural stability and high service diversity. (4) ESBs under the ND and ED scenarios exhibited alternating dominance of climatic, topographic, and socio-economic drivers, whereas the EP scenario fostered stable ESBs configurations through topography–climate synergies. Overall, this study provides robust scientific support for cross-scale governance aimed at achieving regional ecological–economic equilibrium.

title: Research on the spatio-temporal evolution and influencing factors of the coupling coordination among climate risk, new energy resilience and economic growth
abstract: Driven by China's dual objectives of green economic transformation and carbon neutrality, investigating the synergistic relationship among climate risk, new energy resilience, and economic growth holds significant strategic importance. Taking 30 Chinese provinces as the research subjects, this study constructs a three-dimensional system evaluation index framework for "climate risk – new energy resilience – economic growth". By comprehensively applying the coupling coordination degree model, spatial autocorrelation model, and Beta regression model, it reveals the spatio-temporal evolution patterns and influencing factors of the three-dimensional system's coupling coordination degree from 2011 to 2023. Findings indicate: (1) The coupling coordination degree of the three-dimensional system across the 30 provinces first declined before fluctuating upwards during the study period; (2) The spatial pattern exhibited a "higher in the east, lower in the west" distribution. Over time, regions with high coupling coordination gradually expanded from eastern provinces like Guangdong and Jiangsu towards central and western provinces such as Xinjiang and Qinghai, with the three-dimensional system demonstrating significant positive spatial correlation; (3) Beta regression model results indicate that climate policy uncertainty exerts a significant negative impact on the development of three-dimensional system coupling coordination, while the level of new energy infrastructure development exerts a significant positive impact. Policy recommendations are proposed based on these findings to accelerate the sound coordinated development of the three-dimensional system.

title: Aluminum-doped carbon anodes derived from denim waste for high-performance microbial fuel cells: Electrochemical enhancement and life-cycle sustainability
abstract: This study proposes a cleaner production pathway for simultaneous wastewater treatment and energy recovery by converting denim textile waste into high-performance anodes for microbial fuel cells (MFCs). Waste cloth was coated with carboxymethyl cellulose, cross-linked with aluminum sulfate, and subsequently carbonized to produce a three-dimensional aluminum-doped carbon anode. In this approach, aluminum ions serve as both a carbonization catalyst and a biocompatible dopant, enhancing the development of graphitic structure, surface area, and electrical conductivity without adversely affecting electroactive microorganisms. The optimized anode carbonized at 800 °C exhibited a high specific surface area of 539 m2 g−1 and promoted effective biofilm formation and extracellular electron transfer. When deployed in single-chamber MFCs treating sugarcane wastewater, this anode achieved an open-circuit voltage of 760 ± 8.6 mV and a maximum power density of 1174 ± 9.8 mW m−2, corresponding to a 5.4-fold increase relative to commercial carbon felt. Improved electrochemical performance was coupled with enhanced wastewater treatment efficiency, achieving 65% chemical oxygen demand and 74% biochemical oxygen demand removal. Life cycle assessment, conducted using a functional unit of 1 Wh of electricity generated, revealed substantially lower environmental impacts across climate change, human toxicity, ecotoxicity, and resource depletion categories compared with conventional carbon felt anodes. By integrating textile waste valorization, energy-efficient electrode fabrication, and bio-electrochemical wastewater treatment, this work demonstrates a scalable, easy-to-design, and environmentally favorable route toward cleaner energy and circular resource management.

title: Dynamic distribution of heavy metal fractions in European soils during 2009–2018: spatiotemporal modeling
abstract: Soils in the European Union (EU) are widely contaminated with heavy metals (HMs) due to intensified industrial and agricultural activities. Although the EU has released maps of total concentrations for 11 soil HMs, comprehensive knowledge of HM fractions is essential for accurate risk assessment. In this study, we compiled global database encompassing 27,756 data points from 199 studies on HMs. After systematic data processing and model hyperparameter tuning, the established optimized extra tree model achieved an R2 of 0.81 on the test dataset. The spatiotemporal distribution of the exchangeable fraction of the six prevalent HMs across the EU in 2009, 2015, and 2018 (0.05° resolution) was mapped using this extra tree model. Chromium (Cr) exhibited the highest percentage of the exchangeable fraction among the six HMs, averaging 27.57% in the three investigated years. From 2009 to 2018, the exchangeable fraction of Cr fluctuated, with an initial decrease and a subsequent increase, which was primarily due to changes in soil properties. To quantify the effects of HMs on crops, a normalized HM risk indicator was defined using HM content, the percentage of the exchangeable fraction, and crop yield. Using this indicator, the potential influence of Cr on wheat was assessed as a case study, revealing a persistently high risk around central Europe. Our model effectively elucidated the dynamic trends of HM fractions and quantified the associated risks to crops. These results provide critical insights into risk assessment, thus supporting targeted governance strategies and informing rational crop distribution planning.

title: Multifunctional interfacial material for integrated energy-carbon-cost optimization in unconventional petroleum development: A techno-economic-environmental analysis
abstract: Unconventional petroleum development faces a critical challenge in balancing energy output, carbon emissions, and economic viability. This study introduces a novel multifunctional interfacial material that integrates the roles of multiple chemical agents (demulsification, viscosity reduction, corrosion inhibition, and displacement enhancement) into a single molecular architecture. We develop a dynamic techno-economic-environmental model that simulates the full upstream supply chain from extraction to refinery intake, using oil sands bitumen as a case study. The model translates material performance into process variables, enabling a system-level assessment of energy use, carbon emissions, and operational costs. Compared to conventional water and chemical flooding, the multifunctional material reduces energy consumption by 65.7% and 50.7%, carbon emissions by 56.9% and 38.1%, and costs by 19.2% and 10.2%, while increasing oil production by 31% and 12%, respectively. These results demonstrate that molecularly integrated materials can effectively reconcile the energy-carbon-economics trilemma, offering a scalable pathway toward low-carbon and cost-effective unconventional resource development.

title: A novel biopolyurethane foam synthesized from Pterocarya stenoptera seed oil and polyethylene glycol and its efficient application for oil-water separation
authors: Davina Chloe De La Victoire Magni
abstract: Polyurethane foam (PUF) is widely used across industrial sectors due to its lightweight structure and tunable mechanical properties; however, its conventional synthesis depends heavily on petroleum-based polyols. Developing renewable and sustainable polyols is therefore essential for advancing green polyurethane technology. Herein, we report a novel biopolyurethane foam (POPUF) synthesized from Pterocarya stenoptera seed oil via a thiol-ene photo-click reaction. The P. stenoptera seed oil polyol (POP) exhibited a hydroxyl value of 119 mg KOH·g−1 under optimized conditions (12 h reaction time, 4:1 M ratio of mercaptoethanol to C=C). Substitution of polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG-400) with POP yielded foams with adjustable pore morphology and improved physicochemical performance. At 15 wt% POP addition, POPUF displayed a reduced pore size (172 ± 30 μm), increased density (138.6 kg m−3), and higher water uptake (4.20 g g−1). Thermal analyses confirmed enhanced crosslinking, greater ester content, and increased soft-segment flexibility, contributing to superior thermal stability. TiO2 nanoparticles and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) were sequentially deposited onto POPUF to impart selective wettability for separation applications. The modified foam demonstrated rapid adsorption kinetics (<30 s), solvent uptakes up to 21.45 g g−1, excellent recyclability (>94% retention after 20 cycles), and outstanding oil-water separation efficiency (>98.3% under static and gravity-driven conditions). This study demonstrates an efficient and sustainable approach for converting underutilized seed oil into a high-performance bio-based polyurethane foam, offering a promising pathway toward renewable polymeric materials for environmental and separation applications.

title: A comparative life cycle assessment of coal-tar pitch-based and bio-pitch-based carbon anode production for sustainable aluminium
abstract: The carbon anodes used in aluminium production are conventionally produced using coal-tar pitch (CTP), a fossil-based binder associated with greenhouse gas emissions and harmful pollutants such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. These emissions contribute to climate change, human health impacts, and other environmental effects. To support global decarbonization goals and meet growing aluminium demand sustainably, the industry is exploring renewable sources of carbon. Bio-pitch (BP), a biomass-based binder, has been proposed as an alternative for CTP to produce anodes. Although BP has shown promise at the laboratory scale, its environmental performance must be evaluated before industrial adoption. This study presents a comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) of CTP- and BP-based anode production. The research builds upon an initial LCA of CTP-based anode production, which identified the environmental impacts of anode production processes. The evaluation uses the ReCiPe midpoint method in the openLCA software with the Ecoinvent database. Results indicate that replacing CTP with BP reduces CO 2 emissions by 15 % per t anode. When anode consumption in electrolysis cells is included, CO 2 emissions per t Al decrease by 8 %. Sensitivity analysis shows that increasing the coking value of BP from (30 to 50) % further decreases anode-related CO 2 emissions by 10% relative to CTP-based anodes. A second sensitivity scenario demonstrates that BP remains environmentally advantageous even if net carbon consumption increases by 7 kg/t Al. The study also identifies reductions in human toxicity impacts and fossil energy resource use, alongside an expected increase in land use due to biomass sourcing.

title: Developing an ‘evolution’ understanding of the multi-level alignment in regional sustainability transition: insight from Baotou, China
abstract: Existing studies have acknowledged that alignment among multilevel (landscape, regime, and niche) elements is crucial for regional sustainability transitions. Through examining the PV (photovoltaic)-led transition in Baotou, China, this research demonstrates that multilevel alignment is operated through the evolution of a regime underpinned by agency-structure interplay. Herein, the regime of a region functions as a selective mechanism that enters a path-creation status to develop new functions, through promoting agencies for developing and diffusing niches, thereby adapting to emerging landscape dynamics. Following this line, this research further reveals that the local state plays a key role in shaping the agency-selective mechanism by performing place-based leadership to orchestrate and align different stakeholders into collective agencies. These findings provide a new explanation, based on agency-structure interplay, of the dynamism regime in transition studies beyond previous structure- and actor-oriented perspectives, as well as enlarge existing knowledge of the hybrid actor played by the local state in shaping transition pathways.

title: Varying weight aggregation framework for assessing the perceived digital-supported resilience in EV-LIB Supply Chain Concerning Dual Reference Points
abstract: In the booming age of electric vehicles (EV), a stable and robust lithium-ion battery (LIB) supply chain is vital for electric vehicle manufacturers (EVM) to maintain consistent production. To enhance the resilience of the EV-LIB supply chains, many EVMs are implementing digital transformation, which can help them to realize digital operation functions, such as supplier’s dynamic evaluation, real-time production monitoring and adjustment, automatic inventory optimization, and precise sales prediction. To accurately evaluate the digital-supported resilience (DSR) of the EV-LIB supply chain, dual reference points are considered in EVM’s perceived DSR as benchmarks, such as the main competitor’s and industrial service resilience levels. This study provides a novel aggregation method concerning dual reference points with varying dominance to assess EVM’s perceived DSR. In particular, the definition of DSR and the set of potential appraisal indicators are introduced. The standardization process for calculating DSR is proposed according to different quality characteristics. Additionally, the psychological perceptions induced by external reference points are calculated according to prospect theory, in which EVM’s optimistic preferences on reference points are explored. Furthermore, varying weighting methods related to the changing optimistic preferences are designed to describe EVM’s dynamic attitudes on external reference points. Finally, the case of a digital supply chain is conducted to demonstrate its feasibility and effectiveness, in which the dominance of external reference points is dynamically varying. Research conclusions of the study can assist the EVM in selecting resilience KPIs, choosing suitable innovation modes, determining proper benchmarks, and confirming the dynamical dominance of external references.

title: Transformation of organic matter in swine wastewater treatment via an artificially enhanced stratification system
abstract: In this study, a full-scale artificially enhanced stratification system (AESS), composed of horizontal and vertical units constructed from inexpensive, readily available industrial materials, was applied for swine wastewater treatment at an intensive pig farm (∼5000 finishers) in Guang'an, Sichuan, China. Operating at HRT 163 days and OLR 0.2 kg COD/m3·day, the AESS achieved average removal efficiencies of 98.8 ± 1.3% for COD, 99.5 ± 0.8% for SS, 98.3 ± 1.7% for TN, 98.6 ± 1.7% for NH3–N, and 98.4 ± 1.7% for TP over nine months. Despite 97.3% DOC removal, high influent COD (7256–88,081 mg/L) left substantial residual DOM. To investigate the potential transformation mechanism, we employed Excitation-Emission Matrix Parallel Factor (EEM-PARAFAC) to monitor the compositional and fluorescent characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) across key process stages (CK, T2, T4) and at various vertical depths (surface, middle, bottom) in Treatment Pool-2. The results demonstrated that the treatment process preferentially removed protein-like components, while microbial activity led to the accumulation of humic-like substances and a significant increase in humification. Vertical profiling revealed that the bottom layer served as a sink for stable humus, in contrast to the surface layer. Seasonal observations further indicated that summer conditions promoted the production of fresh organic matter, whereas winter conditions enhanced humus stability. Collectively, this multi-angle analysis confirms that the AESS achieves efficient removal and transformation by immobilizing DOM within its layered artificial structure. These findings provide a foundation for the technology and present a scalable, carbon-neutral framework for the treatment of intensive livestock wastewater.

title: Fabricating polyphosphonic acid-based ion exchanger with spatially symmetric structure for efficient removal of uranium
abstract: Effective elimination of uranium (VI) from wastewater is critical to environmental remediation. Herein, a novel polyphosphonic acid-based ion exchanger PDVA/SiO2 with spatially symmetric structure was designed and fabricated, and its adsorption behavior towards uranium in pH 4 solution was investigated at both mg/L and μg/L concentration levels using batch and column experiments respectively. The adsorbent could rapidly recognize and complex with uranium and reach adsorption equilibrium within 5 min, with the adsorption efficiencies of uranium in pure water, tap water, lake water and seawater were about 99.9%, 98.7%, 96.5% and 71.5% respectively. Uranium could be consistently and efficiently removed using a column separation device, with the concentrations in the purified solution less than 30 μg/L. The adsorption mechanism was dominated by ion exchange between UO22+ and H+ (in P–OH). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated that the complex formed by the phosphate group with bi-deprotonated binding to UO22+ possessed higher stability, and the binding process was accompanied by charge transfer and energy reduction.

title: Differentiated carbon emission patterns and multi-scenario low carbon transition pathways of classified Chinese cities
abstract: Cities are facing highly heterogeneous low-carbon transformation pressures. However, existing studies often classify cities using territorial emissions or traditional socio-economic indicators, ignoring the role of cities in intercity supply chains and providing limited support for differentiated pathways. This study establishes a city classification that jointly reflects the carbon responsibility externality and internal mitigation capacity by combining cities' positions in the carbon transfer network with their economic structures. We use the self-organizing map and K-means clustering for classification and then apply a unified analysis framework, including emission phases identification, Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index decomposition based on production and consumption, and multi-scenario pathway projections. The results show that 55% of Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities are still in the growing carbon emissions phase. Traditional Carbon-Supporting Cities and High-Carbon-Resource Output Cities have higher carbon intensity and energy intensity and only 14.58% of the latter show a decreasing emission trend. 49% of emissions of the wealthiest cities are generated from outsourced production, generating 21%-25% of value-added for less affluent cities. In Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities, industrial structure and energy efficiency effectively offset the emission growth from consumption. The carbon reduction potential of High-Carbon-Resource Output Cities can offset 30% of Low-Carbon Leading Hub Cities’ consumption-related emissions. Traditional Carbon-Supporting Cities face stronger emission growth pressure, with carbon peaking delayed to after 2035 in the high-carbon scenario. This study provides theoretical and practical insights for low-carbon urban development and differentiated carbon peaking strategies.

title: Synthesis and application of a novel selective detoxification agent to enhance cellulosic ethanol production
abstract: Environmental pollution and energy crises have accelerated the development of rice straw-based cellulosic ethanol. However, ferulic acid (FA) which predominantly acts as a fermentation inhibitor produced by alkaline pretreatment processes of rice straw feedstock may substantially compromise bioethanol production efficiency. In this study, a novel molecularly imprinted adsorbent (AEPA250@MIPs) was synthesized using enzymatic hydrolysis residue as a matrix to selectively separate FA. Density Functional Theory (DFT) identified 2-MEA as the optimal functional monomer. AEPA250@MIPs exhibited excellent selective adsorption performance, with a distribution coefficient (Kd) exceeding 2.67 in competitive adsorption experiments, representing a significant improvement compared to conventional adsorbents. In simulated fermentation systems, AEPA250@MIPs achieves a 16.6% enhancement in ethanol production yield. Microporous diffusion, hydrogen bonding, and π-π interactions were identified as key mechanisms for selective adsorption. Compared to previous studies, AEPA250@MIPs achieved higher selectivity and reduced glucose loss. This work provides a promising solution to enhance alkaline hydrolysate detoxification and improves the efficiency of bioethanol production.

title: Magnetic biochar-immobilized enzymatic systems for bioremediation of penicillin G sodium in antibiotic-laden fermentation residues: Removal efficiency, degradation mechanism, and ecological safety
abstract: Developing an efficient method to remove the high concentration of residual penicillin G sodium (PGNa) from penicillin fermentation residue (PFR) is of great significance for safeguarding human and animal health. In this study, the scaled-up production of PGNa-degrading enzymes was achieved for the first time using a 5 L stirred-tank reactor, reaching an enzyme activity of 1288.09 U/mL. Comparison of different treatments including strain SQW1, biochar SAMB, free enzymes, and immobilized enzymes SAMB-E showed that SAMB-E exhibited the best PGNa removal performance, achieving a 98.72% removal rate within 120 min using only 0.1 g of immobilized enzymes. The biological effects of PGNa degradation intermediates were evaluated using the disk diffusion method and ECOSAR software, and the results indicated that these intermediates exhibited no significant antibacterial activity and generally low ecological toxicity. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that SAMB-E treatment increased microbial α-diversity while reducing the abundance of most high-risk antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In addition, LC–MS analysis demonstrated that PGNa was primarily degraded by immobilized enzymes through enzymatic hydrolysis followed by subsequent biotransformation reactions, ultimately yielding low-toxicity products. This study is the first to apply immobilized enzymes for the removal of PGNa from PFR, providing a novel, cost-effective, and highly efficient approach for mitigating PGNa contamination. The treated fermentation residue also shows great potential for high-value utilization of hazardous waste.

title: Effects of recycled rubber crumbs on the maintenance behavior of a new composite ballast bed
abstract: The huge number of waste rubber tires in existence can cause serious environmental pollution, and the recycling of discarded tires in ballast beds is of paramount importance. This is the first detailed investigation of tamping maintenance for a composite rubber-ballast bed, with the aim of mitigating tamping-induced damage and enhancing maintenance effects. A numerical model of a composite rubber–ballast bed model was established, and tamping maintenance was simulated. The effects of recycled rubber crumbs on the maintenance behaviors of composite rubber–ballast beds were studied with this model. The results indicated that adding rubber crumbs could substantially mitigate the mechanical response and improve the mechanical state of a composite rubber–ballast bed. Balancing the damage and maintenance effects caused by tamping, rubber crumb contents of 15% and 20% and a diameter of 20 mm were recommended. This research could greatly facilitate the application of recycled rubber tires in ballasted tracks.

title: Photocatalytic and antimicrobial efficacy of CO2 capture photocatalytic material for environmental applications
abstract: Urban air pollution and the high carbon footprint of construction materials pose significant environmental challenges. To address these issues, this study evaluates a novel TiO2-SiO2-based photocatalytic material that integrates CO2 capture via carbonation curing with advanced environmental purification. Distinct from conventional cementitious carriers where natural carbonation often induces pore blockage and activity loss, TSC utilizes controlled carbonation curing to permanently sequester CO2. This process constructively generates a stable, porous carbonate-silica matrix that ensures sustained reactant accessibility and efficient photocatalysis. Its NOx degradation performance was systematically optimized under varying gas flow rates, light intensities, and humidity levels. Model-based simulations for Hong Kong indicated a theoretical kinetic potential for NOx removal reaching 100% under peak UV conditions. While demonstrating robust climate adaptability, these results reflect a kinetic overcapacity relative to pollutant flux rather than absolute environmental clearance. Furthermore, TSC exhibited superior antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Chlorella, attributed to enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. By integrating carbon sequestration, air purification, and biofouling resistance, TSC emerges as a holistic, sustainable solution for resilient urban infrastructure.

title: Machine learning for imbalanced WWTP energy consumption data in China: A spatially informed resampling framework with region-specific driver analysis
abstract: Growing concerns over energy consumption in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) have highlighted the need for more accurate and reliable predictive tools. While machine learning offers promising solutions, its effectiveness is often limited by spatial imbalance in real-world WWTP operational data. To address this, we developed a spatially informed resampling framework using a Relative Local Deviation Weight (RLDW) function to guide sample selection, combined with Cross-Resampling Generalization Testing (CRGT) to evaluate model robustness across different resampling strategies. We applied this framework to operational data from 2256 WWTPs in China, testing multiple machine learning models under various resampling scenarios. Independent test-set evaluation demonstrated robust predictive performance (R2 = 0.9403; MSE = 0.0058), while five-fold cross-validation indicated high internal consistency of the optimal model (average R2 = 0.9974; MSE = 0.0039). CRGT further confirmed the robustness and generalization of this model across heterogeneous and imbalanced data. To explore regional heterogeneity, SHAP analysis was applied to WWTPs grouped by geographic region. Results indicate that the key drivers of energy consumption vary spatially: treatment capacity dominates in southern provinces, whereas influent BOD5 and TN exert greater influence in northern regions. By integrating spatial imbalance handling with region-specific interpretability, this study advances machine learning applications for energy-efficient wastewater management and provides actionable insights to inform regionally targeted environmental policies.

title: Understanding key factors driving circularity in plastic systems through material flow analysis: Findings from Portugal
abstract: This article presents a structured approach integrating Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and circularity indicators to assess key factors affecting material circularity, illustrated through a Material Flow Analysis of plastic flows in Portugal. The study follows material flows from polymer production to post-consumption treatment, measures circularity indicators across various system boundaries. A sensitivity analysis is performed to evaluate the effects of specific variables on circularity. Results highlight the limited circularity of plastics in Portugal, with a recycling rate of only 17% and a Material Circularity Indicator of 20.9%. The analysis highlights key areas for improvement: increasing production efficiency, boosting the fraction collected for recycling, and raising the fraction of product feedstock derived from recycled materials.
