This work provides critical insights for standardized design and scalable deployment of electrochemical reactors for wastewater phosphorus recovery.

title: Manufacturers’ adoption of industrial symbiosis under carbon taxation: Environmental performance and the role of green technology
abstract: A carbon tax incentivizes manufacturers to adopt low-carbon strategies. Industrial symbiosis (IS) is widely advocated to enhance waste reduction and resource efficiency. This study examines the economic feasibility and environmental performance of IS under carbon taxation. We develop a game-theoretic model with an upstream waste-generating manufacturer and a downstream waste-utilizing manufacturer, analyzing three scenarios: traditional manufacturing, IS only, and IS combined with upstream green technology. The analysis derives thresholds showing that IS adoption depends jointly on fixed investment costs, cost-sharing arrangements, and upstream production costs. Importantly, IS does not necessarily reduce carbon emissions, as output expansion induced by cost savings may offset environmental benefits. The adoption of green technology stabilizes waste supply, improves carbon efficiency, and enlarges the parameter region in which IS is both economically viable and environmentally effective. Carbon taxes influence IS adoption differently across upstream production costs: moderate rates encourage adoption among intermediate-cost manufacturers, whereas excessive taxes can discourage participation. Higher taxes reduce emissions but may lower social welfare in certain cost ranges. Overall, IS combined with green technology under well-designed carbon taxes enhances both environmental and economic outcomes.

title: Ultrasonication-assisted MXene/CdS photocatalysts for biomass-derived H2 production: Performance optimization and life cycle assessment
abstract: Transitioning toward sustainable energy systems requires H2 production routes that are both efficient and environmentally responsible. In this work, biomass-based photocatalytic H2 production was systematically investigated by integrating catalyst synthesis optimization with environmental assessment. A CdS-based photocatalyst modified with Ti3C2Tx MXene was synthesized via an ultrasound-assisted approach, and the effects of ultrasonication conditions, catalyst loading, and reaction temperature on photocatalytic performance were evaluated. Under optimized conditions, the MXene/CdS photocatalyst achieved a H2 production rate of 16.212 mmol g−1·h−1 with good cycling stability. To assess the environmental implications of different experimental strategies and operating conditions, a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment was conducted and complemented by outdoor photocatalytic tests under natural sunlight. The results indicate that moderate ultrasonication, appropriate catalyst dosage, and optimized reaction temperature can effectively reduce environmental burdens. Variations in solar availability further influence environmental performance, highlighting the combined importance of process optimization and realistic operating conditions. Overall, this study demonstrates that coupling photocatalytic performance optimization with environmental assessment provides a more comprehensive understanding of the opportunities and limitations of biomass-based H2 production.

title: Cleaner production–oriented design of cemented foam backfill with high strength, low cost, and low carbon emissions: A TabPFN-based multi-objective optimization framework
abstract: – Cleaner production of cemented foam backfill (CFB) is critical for sustainable mining, as mixture design simultaneously affects mechanical performance, material consumption, and carbon emissions. However, the nonlinear interactions among composition, foaming parameters, and curing conditions make conventional trial-and-error design inefficient and resource-intensive. This study develops a cleaner production-oriented prediction–optimization framework for sustainable CFB design by integrating a pretrained Transformer-based Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) with multi-objective optimization. Unlike conventional machine learning models requiring iterative training and extensive hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN enables robust inference under small-data conditions. SHAP analysis is employed to interpret key physicochemical drivers of strength development and ensure physical consistency. The predictive model is coupled with NSGA-II to simultaneously maximize unconfined compressive strength while minimizing cost and carbon emissions. The resulting Pareto front reveals explicit trade-offs among mechanical, economic, and environmental objectives, providing diversified mixture solutions under varying engineering requirements. Compared with empirical design approaches, the proposed framework enables coordinated improvement in strength with reduced cost and carbon footprint. This study demonstrates the feasibility of pretrained transformer inference for sustainable backfill systems and provides a practical decision-support tool for low-carbon mine backfill design.

title: Valorisation of anaerobic digestate: Environmental life cycle assessment of anaerobic digestate value chain in the UK with a digestate treatment technology
abstract: Digestate, a by-product from anaerobic digestion (AD), presents challenges for direct land application due to potential contamination of pathogens and large volumes requiring transportation, necessitating further treatments. This study applies life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology to evaluate the environmental impacts of introducing a digestate treatment technology, developed by the project NOMAD (Novel Organic recovery using Mobile Advanced Technology), to a UK AD plant. The technology includes a solid-liquid separation, membrane filtering, antibiotic removal, and nutrient recovery processes, enabling the extraction of concentrated nutrients and water from digestate. Three scenarios were assessed: a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario based on current UK AD practices; a resource recovery (RR) scenario representing the technology at pilot scale; and an upscaled scenario reflecting full-scale deployment. Results show, generally, that the pilot technology brings insignificant changes to the BAU case, whereas the upscaled technology reduces environmental impacts from 7% to 85% across selected impact categories; however, the upscaled scenario exhibits 16% and 24% higher impacts in particulate matter formation potential (PMFP) and terrestrial acidification potential (TAP), respectively, due to NH3 emissions from field applications. All established scenarios demonstrate environmental advantages over mineral fertiliser use. This study underscores the potential of the advanced digestate treatment technology for a UK food waste AD value chain and provides insight for nutrient recovery from digestate to circularity from the environmental impact point of view.

title: Strategic valorization of biogenic CO2 from kraft pulp mills
abstract: Kraft pulp and paper mills, significant sources of biogenic CO 2 emissions, offer a promising opportunity for carbon capture and valorization. This study develops a framework for assessment of the combined implementation of carbon capture and methanol production through CO 2 hydrogenation, using biogenic emissions from kraft pulp mills, assessing both technical and economic viability. Canada has the opportunity to capture approximately 22.2 million tonnes of biogenic CO 2 annually from these mills, with capture costs ranging from $62 to $104 per tonne. Sensitivity analysis reveals the process's sensitivity to capital costs, internal rate of return (IRR), and utility costs, while Monte Carlo simulations indicate cost uncertainties of $76.54 ± 5.60 per tonne. Furthermore, the study extends to methanol synthesis using the captured CO 2 and a SMR-CCS-based hydrogen, examining two production pathways: decentralized construction of methanol plants near individual mills and centralized plants with CO 2 transported via pipelines. The captured CO 2 could be converted into approximately 15.6 million tonnes of methanol annually. Production costs range from $642 to $751 per tonne in the decentralized pathway and $650 to $700 per tonne in the centralized, both competitive with the market price of $722 per tonne. Hydrogen costs drive over 69% of production expenses, with Monte Carlo simulations showing production cost uncertainties of $678.50 ± 59.86 per tonne. These findings demonstrate the economic feasibility of carbon capture and methanol production from kraft pulp mills and present a transferable framework that can be applied to other regions by substituting Canadian-specific inputs with locally relevant data for biogenic CO 2 utilization.

title: Recovery of fluoride toward sustainable integrated circuit manufacturing: Quantifying water–energy–carbon–fluorine footprints in China
abstract: Integrated circuit (IC) industry in the world faces unprecedented environmental challenges like carbon neutrality, and China is serving as a critical manufacturing hub in this global supply chain. However, fluorinated chemicals used in IC manufacturing and discharged to wastewater systems remain underexamined in environmental assessments. This study integrates life cycle assessment, material flow analysis, PROMETHEE II, and support vector machine-based Sobol analysis to evaluate water, energy, carbon, and fluorine (WECF) footprints across IC manufacturing, fluorine-containing wastewater double membrane treatment, and sludge recycling in a representative Chinese IC plant. The results showed that chemical vapor deposition accounted for the highest energy consumption and contributed over 30% of greenhouse gas emissions, primarily due to the intensive energy required for managing fluorinated chemicals. Although most fluorine enters the wastewater system, sludge recycling serves as a highly effective pathway for recovery of approximately 32% of the total fluorine. Moreover, sludge recycling and double membrane treatment showed better WECF footprint performance than manufacturing processes. Furthermore, fluorinated chemicals and energy consumption emerged as the most interactive inputs, which demonstrates that the mitigation of fluorine would significantly increase the energy and carbon footprints. Scenario analysis showed that substituting fluorinated chemical inputs and optimizing steam use could cut fluorine and carbon footprint by up to 65% and 30%, respectively. These findings indicate that achieving sustainable IC manufacturing requires a transition from isolated energy efficiency measures to comprehensive management of WECF nexus, alongside the development of low-fluorine manufacturing alternatives.

title: Performance analysis and life cycle assessment of a carbon capture system integrating solar and methane power generation and cooling in a 1,000 MW ultra-supercritical coal-fired power unit
abstract: To promote cleaner and more sustainable production in large-scale coal-fired power generation, this study proposes a novel integrated carbon capture system that combines solar-assisted feedwater heating and a methane-based power generation and refrigeration subsystem with a 1000 MW ultra-supercritical coal-fired unit, referred to as USCU-MS-CCS. The proposed configuration aims to mitigate the high energy penalty of post-combustion carbon capture by enhancing low-grade waste heat cascade utilization and reducing high-quality steam extraction. A comprehensive thermo-economic analysis and cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) are conducted to evaluate the performance of the reference USCU, the conventional USCU-CCS, and the proposed USCU-MS-CCS systems. Compared with the USCU-CCS configuration, the USCU-MS-CCS increases net power output by 74.64 MW, improves power generation efficiency by 3.60%, and reduces coal consumption by 48.2 g/(kW·h). Owing to effective waste heat recovery and solar-assisted integration, the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) and the cost of CO2 removal (COR) are reduced by 7.4% and 17.14%, respectively. Life cycle results indicate that carbon capture enables significant mitigation of climate impacts, with global warming potential (GWP) reductions of 66.97% for USCU-CCS and 69.13% for USCU-MS-CCS relative to the reference system. Parametric and sensitivity analyses further reveal the effects of main steam pressure, methane operating conditions, CO2 capture rate, operational lifetime, and solar irradiance on system performance and environmental impacts. Overall, the USCU-MS-CCS provides a viable and scalable pathway for reducing energy losses, fuel consumption, and carbon emissions in coal-fired power generation under stringent carbon reduction targets.

title: Environmental and social sustainability assessment of a circular process for the valorisation of sewage sludge ash and mining by-products into bio-based fertilisers
abstract: Phosphorus (P) recovery from sewage sludge ash (SSA) represents an interesting solution to P supply concerns. While techno-economic assessments show promising outcomes, the environmental and social performance of these recovery processes remains insufficiently explored, hindering the market uptake of recovered P in bio-based fertilisers. This work investigates the environmental impacts of producing four commercial granular fertilisers representative of the Italian fertilizer market in 2024 (i.e., ENERGEO CV, ENERGEO CV TOP, LITHOZINC and PHEOSCOR). Furthermore, a social hotspot analysis (SHA) was conducted to account for the social implications of raw materials supply (e.g., P, Mg, S, Ca, Cl) in fertiliser manufacturing. Impacts were evaluated for a Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario, in which fertilisers are based on mineral P (i.e., phosphorite), and a Circular Economy scenario (CE), in which phosphorite is partially replaced with P recovered from SSA via wet chemical extraction and co-precipitated with calcium hydroxide or low-grade magnesium oxide mining by-product (LG-MgO). Raw material supply covered from 56% to 98% of total environmental impacts across all fertilisers, except for ENERGEO CV – BAU and ENERGEO CV TOP – BAU, where core processes were the main contributors to specific sub-categories. LITHOZINC – CE and PHEOSCOR – CE showed similar or enhanced performances compared to the corresponding BAU formulations, indicating potential benefits in employing LG-MgO as precipitant. The supply chains of raw materials exhibited a medium-high social risk in the assessed categories, with Egyptian phosphorite extraction posing the greatest concerns for workers and local communities, and the innovative solution potentially improving the social performance of the fertiliser manufacturing process. • Raw material supply covered 55% – 98% of total environmental impacts. • LG-MgO-based formulations improved environmental performance in CE scenario. • Raw material supply showed medium-high social risk in the assessed categories. • CE solution potentially improves the social performance of fertiliser manufacturing.

title: Dynamic light environments, rather than shading ratios, determine rice yield and quality in agrivoltaic systems
abstract: Agrivoltaic (AV) systems offer a promising pathway to co-produce food and renewable electricity, yet rice paddies remain a challenging case because yield maintenance is strictly required in Japan. This study evaluated three AV panel architectures implemented at three commercial paddy sites in Japan over three consecutive growing seasons (2022–2024). High-frequency measurements of photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) at canopy level were used to quantify both seasonal cumulative light availability and short-term fluctuation characteristics. The relationships between PPFD dynamics and yield components were examined using factorial analysis and linear mixed-effects modeling, and a robust threshold analysis was conducted to identify the relative cumulative PPFD requirement for maintaining rice yield. Grain quality was assessed in 2024, and land-use efficiency and revenue robustness were evaluated using the Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) and sensitivity analyses incorporating both technical (meteorological and PV performance) and market uncertainties. Across sites, AV plots showed yield reductions relative to paired open-field controls (three-year means: 33.6% at Sakata, 20.6% at Higashine, and 31.6% at Yonezawa). Yield losses were consistently associated with reduced panicle number, while greater short-term PPFD variability was linked to larger yield penalties even under comparable cumulative PPFD. Maintaining ≥80% yield corresponded to a relative cumulative PPFD threshold of 76.5% (95% CI: 71.6–79.9%) of ambient conditions. Grain quality changes suggested potential market-grade risks; however, electricity revenue improved total revenue and buffered income under plausible rice price penalties and electricity price uncertainty during the FIT period. Overall, the results indicate that dynamic PPFD delivery—beyond the nominal shading ratio—provides decision-relevant insight for AV design and policy frameworks aiming to maintain rice productivity while securing economic resilience.

title: Galaxolide triggers trophic cascades from microbes to fish: Community sensitivity and molecular insights reveal underestimated ecological risks
abstract: The synthetic musk Galaxolide (HHCB) is a ubiquitous pollutant detected in diverse environmental matrices and biota globally. While its toxicity to individual species is documented, ecosystem-level impacts remain unclear. This study evaluated HHCB's ecological effects across multiple biological levels in an aquatic microcosm, focusing on sensitive community thresholds and molecular perturbations. After 28 days of HHCB exposure (0–62.5 μg/L), the community-level no-observed-effect concentration (NOECcommunity) was 0.5 μg/L. This is lower than most species-specific no-observed-effect concentrations (NOECs), indicating heightened ecological sensitivity at the community level. At 62.5 μg/L, microbial diversity declined significantly, with Proteobacteria (56.2%) and Actinobacteriota (14.88%) emerging as key taxa for network stability. Transcriptomic analysis of Danio rerio at 0.5 μg/L suggested potential endocrine disruption, despite unchanged thyroid hormone levels. Multilevel modeling indicated two potential trophic linkages: (1) reduced Chlorella vulgaris was associated with impaired energy transfer to Daphnia magna and lower D. rerio triiodothyronine (T3); and (2) microbial facilitation was linked to competitive dominance of Tetradesmus obliquus over Navicula cryptotenella and altered D. rerio thyroxine (T4). These findings demonstrate HHCB's multilevel effects, highlighting the potential value of integrating community and molecular endpoints into environmental risk assessment, while noting that extrapolation to natural ecosystems requires further validation.

title: Defining socio-climate-energy zones based on photovoltaic potential to support new standards for eliminating energy poverty in Chile
abstract: Countries are facing contexts of high climatic and socio-spatial heterogeneity, where integrated territorial diagnostics to address energy poverty are essential. This research aims to evaluate the extent to which the current thermal zoning in Chile can discriminate among variables related to residential electricity consumption, photovoltaic generation potential, and poverty at the communal scale. Therefore, a replicable methodology has been designed and tested to build a socio-climate-energy zoning. 343 communes have been analyzed, combining information on residential electricity consumption, annual photovoltaic generation potential, and the number of people in poverty to examine their behavior according to the current thermal zoning. The contrast between zones is evaluated by descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and difference tests. The results show that current thermal zoning, by itself, discriminates among the socio-energy variables considered to a limited extent, including variables such as annual electricity consumption. Subsequently, the generation/consumption relationship is stratified into three ranges, and poverty is stratified into quartiles, creating 12 categories. This new classification allows building socio-climate-energy zoning as an alternative to the current thermal zoning, enabling the identification of vulnerable areas, the planning of photovoltaic energy programs, and, in general, the prioritization of interventions that integrate social vulnerability with local electricity generation and consumption. The association between the two dimensions is contrasted using Pearson's Chi-square test, and the results are represented cartographically. Overall, the proposed framework provides an operational tool for territorial energy planning and the design of differentiated policies, with the potential to adapt to other regions of the Global South.

title: Synchronous mechanochemical remediation of petroleum-contaminated soil and attapulgite-biochar composite for enhanced Cr(VI) removal from water
abstract: Mechanochemical (MC) remediation offers a promising green strategy for the treatment of petroleum-contaminated soil (PCS) and the valorization of remediated soil into functional materials. This study achieved efficient PCS remediation under solvent-free conditions via ball milling, attaining a total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) removal rate of 92.11% under optimized parameters. Simultaneously, PCS and attapulgite (ATP) were co-ground to prepare a carbon-mineral composite material (BCM). The obtained materials (BCS, ball-milled ATP (BATP) and BCM) were systematically evaluated for aqueous Cr(VI) adsorption. Results showed that BCM exhibited superior adsorption performance, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 94.196 mg g−1 at 298 K. Meanwhile, BCM demonstrated outstanding stability and reusability, with removal efficiency decreasing by only 4.19% after five adsorption-desorption cycles. The adsorption process followed pseudo-second-order kinetics, primarily involving chemical adsorption, and is spontaneously endothermic. Mechanism studies and simulations reveal that Cr(VI) removal is primarily achieved through redox and complexation dominate. This work demonstrates that MC not only enables efficient remediation of PCS but also converts it into a high-performance, environmentally benign adsorbent for Cr(VI)-laden wastewater, providing a sustainable “treating-waste-with-waste” strategy for simultaneous soil restoration and water purification.

title: Self-healing behavior of asphalt binder with Nano-SiC controlled-release microcapsules under microwave irradiation
abstract: Controlled-release microcapsules containing regenerant have attracted considerable attention for improving the self-healing performance of asphalt binder. This study investigates the self-repairing behavior of asphalt incorporating nano-SiC controlled-release microcapsules under microwave irradiation. Fatigue-heal-fatigue tests using a dynamic shear rheometer (DSR) were conducted to evaluate the self-repairing performance, and a response surface methodology was employed to determine the optimal combination of influencing factors. Furthermore, a prediction model for self-healing behavior was established based on a two-stage healing kinetics. Finally, the self-healing mechanism was elucidated through a combination of fluorescence microscopy (FM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Results show that the incorporation of controlled-release microcapsules markedly improves the healing efficiency of asphalt binder under microwave irradiation. Optimization of microwave parameters and microcapsule content further enhances the healing efficiency. Microscopic observations indicate that controlled-release microcapsules effectively fill microcracks under short-term microwave irradiation. Simulation results demonstrate that the rejuvenator-modified asphalt model exhibits lower solubility parameters and higher mean square displacement (MSD) than the base asphalt model. Moreover, this difference becomes more pronounced with increasing temperature, indicating that the enhanced self-healing performance results from the synergistic effect of microwave-induced heating and regenerant diffusion. This study elucidates the self-healing behavior of controlled-release microcapsules across multiple scales, providing a theoretical foundation for their practical application in asphalt pavements and contributing to improved pavement durability and sustainability.

title: Leading or misleading? The role of firms' ESG performance in banks' green credit granting decisions
abstract: This study examines whether corporate ESG performance serves as a valid signal for green credit allocation in China's banking sector. However, despite growing attention to ESG and sustainable finance, existing research offers limited evidence on whether ESG disclosure reliably guides banks' green lending decisions, particularly with respect to both the scale and structure of green credit. Furthermore, the credibility of ESG as a signaling mechanism remains under-explored in contexts where greenwashing is prevalent. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms spanning 2012–2020, we investigate how ESG disclosure affects the scale and structure of green credit granted by banks. We apply fixed-effects panel regression and an instrumental variable approach to address endogeneity concerns. Results show that a one-point improvement in ESG rating is associated with a 0.02 increase in green credit volume and a 0.019% decrease in the share of green credit within total bank lending—indicating a “crowding-out effect,” where green credit expands more slowly than overall credit. Further analysis reveals that the ESG-credit relationship is more pronounced in green-credit-restricted industries. We also find that ESG performance improves green credit access through three mechanisms: enhanced information transparency, reduced firm risk, and higher firm productivity. However, the impact of ESG performance on actual energy conservation depends on the degree of greenwashing—defined as the strategic overstatement of environmental commitment in ESG disclosures. Only firms with low greenwashing show meaningful reductions in energy and emission intensity. These findings suggest that while ESG disclosure facilitates green credit, its effectiveness is undermined by unverifiable reporting. Policymakers should improve ESG reporting standards and penalize misleading disclosures. Banks should enhance post-loan monitoring to ensure credit funds are used for truly green purposes.

title: Improved method for evaluating wave energy flux and its applicability research
abstract: Accurate wave energy assessment is crucial to the selection of wave energy hotspots. However, wave energy assessments typically adopt the simplified wave energy assessment formula, which is acceptable for assessing wave energy flux in deep waters. Still, the evaluation error increases rapidly when applied in shallow waters. For this reason, this study proposed a wave energy evaluation formula that is more suitable for shallow waters by introducing the explicit approximation form of the wave dispersion equation. On this basis, the formula is further improved to obtain a general wave energy flux formula more suitable for various water depths. By applying the formula to Rizhao sea area and comparing it to the wave energy flux calculated by wave spectrum integration, it is found that the formula has high accuracy in various water depths. Furthermore, by analyzing the influence of different wave energy flux formulas on the captured power evaluation, and analyzing the reasons for its error, it is found that the general wave energy flux formula proposed in this study can provide more accurate wave energy assessment at various water depths, and provide a reference for the design and selection of wave energy converters in deep waters.

title: Generation of nitrogen-containing compounds by cellulose nitrogen-rich pyrolysis under CO2/N2 atmosphere: Influence mechanism of different catalysts
abstract: This study investigates nitrogen-rich catalytic pyrolysis of cellulose in an N2/CO2 atmosphere, focusing on the synergistic effects of catalysts and CO2 on bio-oil composition. The results show that catalyst acidity governs product selectivity, markedly enhancing high-value nitrogen-containing compounds while suppressing carbonyl species. Among the catalysts tested, Al-MCM-41 exhibited the strongest promotion of nitrogen-containing compounds, increasing their relative content from 22.24% (without catalyst) to 88.83%. HZSM-5, Mo2C, and γ-Al2O3 favored the formation of furans, esters, and sugars, whereas CO2 facilitated biomass decomposition and altered product distribution. In addition, catalysts significantly regulated nitrogen heterocycles, increasing pyridine, pyrrole, and nitrile contents. Biochars obtained with HZSM-5 and Al-MCM-41 showed abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, indicating improved pore structure development. These findings demonstrate an effective catalytic strategy for the selective conversion of biomass into high-value nitrogen compounds.

title: Life cycle assessment of coir geotextiles for sustainable infrastructure applications
abstract: Recent years have witnessed a surge in demand for sustainable infrastructure materials, prompting increased scrutiny of natural fiber-based geotextiles as alternatives to synthetic counterparts. This study evaluates the environmental performance of coir geotextiles, derived from coconut husk fibers, through a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) using SimaPro v. 9.3.03, with inventory data sourced from Ecoinvent 3.7.1 and primary data from coir manufacturing facilities in India. The objective is to quantify the environmental impacts of 1 kg of woven coir geotextile (700 g/m2 density) and compare it with synthetic geotextiles, focusing on 18 environmental impact categories. Results indicate that the manufacturing phase, particularly weaving, dominates environmental impacts, contributing ≈75% of global warming (GW) (1.17E−01 kg CO2 eq out of 1.64E kg CO2 eq), driven by fossil fuel-based electricity. Sensitivity analysis shows ±5% electricity variation significantly affects fossil resource scarcity and GW. Scenario analysis reveals renewable energy, especially hydropower, reduces impacts by 10%–50%. A comparative analysis of the three largest copra-producing countries reveals distinct environmental impact profiles: Indonesia experiences higher impacts primarily due to resource-intensive coconut cultivation; India’s footprint is driven by its manufacturing processes; while the Philippines shows a more balanced profile, benefiting from the use of renewable energy. Compared to synthetic geotextiles, coir exhibits lower GW (≈ 34%–40% reduction) and toxicity burdens, largely due to its biodegradability, which eliminates energy-intensive disposal. These findings align coir geotextiles with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, 12, and 13, underscoring their potential as eco-friendly materials for erosion control and slope stabilization in tropical regions.

title: Indirect household electricity consumption in Korea: A regional analysis using energy-extended input–output and structural decomposition methods
abstract: Households, as primary agents of consumption, play a major role in electricity use and greenhouse gas emissions through the production of the goods and services that satisfy their needs. Understanding how household consumption patterns influence electricity use is therefore increasingly important. This study investigates the indirect electricity consumption driven by household demands across Korean regions from 2005 to 2020, using an energy-extended input-output framework based on inter-regional input-output tables. Structural decomposition analysis is then applied to identify the main factors driving changes in indirect electricity use over the study period. The results highlight four key findings. First, indirect electricity consumption accounts for a substantial share of total electricity use attributable to households, ranging from 66.3% to 68.1%. Second, the service sector is the largest contributor, responsible for nearly half of indirect electricity use, with a larger share in non-metropolitan regions due to higher electricity intensity. Third, the inter-regional structure reveals substantial spillovers and spatial decoupling: electricity embodied in metropolitan household consumption is realized disproportionately in electricity-intensive producer provinces. Fourth, although electricity intensity decreased, these improvements were insufficient to offset rising consumption, and household downsizing further increased indirect electricity demand. Overall, these findings underscore the need for policies that explicitly address indirect household electricity consumption and its inter-regional spillover pathways while accounting for regional and demographic differences.

title: Enhancing thermal insulation with cellulose acetate-based composites: Impact of environmentally-friendly binders on performance and durability
abstract: This study investigates the potential of cellulose acetate (CA) derived from recycled cigarette butts for developing cementitious composites, by evaluating its compatibility with three different binders: Ordinary Portland Cement CEM I 52.5 N, and two low-carbon binders, the pozzolanic Naturat and the Natural Prompt Cement, for non-loadbearing or self-supporting applications. While previous studies have explored the recycling of cigarette butt derived materials and the use of bio-based or low-carbon binders in construction, comparative investigations combining recycled CA fibers with different binders and assessing both their thermal and durability related performance remain limited. This study addresses this knowledge gap through a comprehensive comparative analysis of different binder types. Building upon the authors' previous research that characterized CA and investigated its effects on mortar properties, this research explores an innovative recycling approach that mitigates waste without promoting smoking. The optimised formulations achieved over 80% CA by dry volume in all composites. A novel laboratory manufacturing method was developed, involving compaction at 0.1 MPa across three layers followed by immediate demoulding, producing lightweight cementitious composites with densities

title: Source-specific risks of heavy metals in urban–agricultural soils and implications for human health in a liver cancer high-incidence area of Central China
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in urban–agricultural soils poses significant ecological and human health challenges, especially in regions with high disease incidence. This study provides an integrated assessment of soil heavy metals in Xiangfu District, Kaifeng—a liver cancer high-risk area in Central China—to evaluate contamination levels, spatial variability, ecological risk, and human health implications. Eleven heavy metals (As, Ba, Cr, Cu, Fe, Hg, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, and Zn) were analyzed using geostatistical and multi-index approaches. The Nemerow integrated pollution index, geo-accumulation index, and potential ecological risk index were applied to characterize contamination intensity and risk levels. The APCS–MLR (Absolute Principal Component Score coupled with Multiple Linear Regression) model was employed to identify major pollution sources, while Monte Carlo simulation quantified uncertainty in probabilistic health risk assessment. Results revealed that Hg exhibited the highest spatial variability and ecological risk, while Mn was identified as the dominant contributor to carcinogenic risk in children. The findings highlight the critical influence of industrial and agricultural activities on soil contamination and demonstrate the value of combining source apportionment and risk modeling for management decision-making. This study provides a scientific basis for targeted pollution control, ecological protection, and public health management in high-risk urban–agricultural environments.

title: Slag and fly ash in low-carbon concrete do not justify retaining blast furnaces and coal power: Evidence from Japan
abstract: The cement and concrete industry is increasingly turning to blast furnace slag and fly ash to decarbonize its products, mainly as clinker substitutes or as mineral admixtures capable of binding CO 2 . However, the efficacy of this strategy in reducing system-wide emissions across concrete, steel, and electricity production remains unclear. Using Japan as a case study, this study shows that although slag and fly ash can reduce CO 2 emissions within the concrete sector, sustaining blast furnaces and coal-fired power plants to secure these by-products ultimately increases system-wide emissions across three sectors. Retaining them would be defensible only when both blast furnaces and coal-fired power plants achieve deep decarbonization, on the order of ∼90% emission reduction. Otherwise, dependence on these by-products risks locking in emission-intensive infrastructure and undermining system-wide decarbonization. These findings indicate that while slag and fly ash should be fully utilized, their role must be transitional; securing their supply alone does not justify retaining blast furnaces or coal-fired power plants.

title: Impact mechanisms and spatial heterogeneity of blue–green infrastructure on carbon sequestration in Jinan, China
abstract: Global carbon emissions have jeopardized the sustainable development of ecosystems and human society by exacerbating ecological crises. As a key nature-based solution, blue-green infrastructure (BGI) has attracted increasing attention for its relationship between landscape pattern and carbon sequestration. Taking Jinan City in China as a case study, this research aimed to reveal the impact mechanism and spatial heterogeneity of BGI landscape patterns on carbon sequestration by integrating multi-scale grid analysis, geographically weighted regression (GWR) model based on principal component analysis (PCA), and explainable machine learning approaches. The results showed that: 1) the core BGI area of Jinan was distributed in an outer-ring concentric pattern, with large patches in the north and fragmented small ones in the south; 2) the 5km × 5 km grid was identified as the optimal scale for capturing BGI landscape patterns and carbon sequestration, with the correlation strength ordered as aggregation index, area index, shape index, density index, and diversity index; 3) at the township administrative unit, F1(Complexity/diversity) enhanced carbon sequestration in southern and southeastern mountainous - agroforestry transition zones toward the southwestern suburban areas; F2(Scale/connectivity) increased northward, peaking in the northern ecological core dominated by forest and grassland; and 4) MESH and LPI emerged as the dominant positive drivers of carbon sequestration, with evident nonlinear interactions among the indices. These findings provide theoretical and practical guidance for optimizing BGI landscape patterns and enhancing carbon sink capacity, offering a scientific reference for climate-resilient planning and carbon management in cities worldwide.

title: Digital technology empowering ESG governance: How does supply chain digitalization affect corporate ESG greenwashing?
abstract: Amidst the global climate pollution and environmental crisis, corporate ESG greenwashing severely impedes sustainable development processes such as industry-wide green transformation and carbon reduction. Supply chain digitalization, through its provision of end-to-end transparent oversight, may prove a crucial means of inhibiting corporate ESG greenwashing practices. This research uses the DID model to empirically analyse the impact of supply chain digitalization on ESG greenwashing among Chinese A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2023. The findings indicate that supply chain digitalization can inhibit corporate ESG greenwashing. Mediating effects reveal that supply chain digitalization inhibits ESG greenwashing through two pathways: enhancing corporate innovation capability and marketisation levels. Moderating effects suggest that external oversight effectively amplifies supply chain digitalization's inhibitory effect on ESG greenwashing, whereas external incentives weaken this effect. Heterogeneity tests demonstrate that this inhibiting effect is significant especially in state-owned, eastern China and western China, non-overseas-background executive corporate entities. This study provides a novel perspective on enhancing corporate ESG governance through supply chain digitalization, while also offering significant policy implications for advancing supply chain digital applications and corporate sustainability.

title: Constructing green and low-carbon Co-C3N5 with highly dispersed active sites to promote Co2+/Co3+ cycling for efficient PMS activation: Performance, mechanism, and life cycle assessment
abstract: Constructing catalysts with highly dispersed active sites in a photocatalytic-peroxymonosulfate (PMS) system is crucial for the efficient removal of chlortetracycline (CTC) from water. In this study, Co-C3N5 (n%) with abundant and highly dispersed active sites was synthesized by liquid-phase mixing followed by one-step calcination, achieving in situ doping of varying proportions of Co(NO3)2·6H2O into the C3N5 lattice with minimal energy consumption. The Co-C3N5(50%)/PMS/Vis system achieved a CTC degradation rate of nearly 95% within 5 min and the final mineralization rate of approximately 50%. Furthermore, the solution approached neutral conditions after reaction in real water matrices, benefiting aquatic ecological balance and demonstrating substantial progress toward practical photocatalyst implementation. After five cycles of treatment, the degradation efficiency remained above 85% with no cobalt leaching, demonstrating good reusability and stability. 1O2, h+, and O2·- were identified as the primary active species in the degradation process. The Co2+/Co3+ cycle continuously activates PMS, while the highly dispersed Co active sites enable rapid and efficient degradation. Based on LC-MS analysis and T.E.S.T assessment, three degradation pathways of CTC were proposed, and the intermediates were demonstrated to be non-toxic. Moreover, using Chlorella as an ecological indicator, Co-C3N5 effectively reduce the aquatic toxicity of CTC. Finally, a life cycle assessment (LCA) shows that Co-C3N5 outperforms other emerging photocatalysts as a low-carbon option. This green, low-carbon, and environmentally benign photocatalyst offers a sustainable solution for translating laboratory research to practical antibiotic remediation in industrial applications.

title: From Energy–Exergy optimization to improved economic and environmental performance in sustainable urea production: A comparative study of gray, blue, and green processes
abstract: With the growing global population, food demand is projected to rise significantly, leading to increased urea consumption. Therefore, sustainable urea synthesis pathways are essential to address both food security and climate change. In this study, gray, blue, and green urea production processes were systematically designed, optimized and comparatively analyzed. To identify the key process variables, both local sensitivity analysis (LSA) and global sensitivity analysis (GSA) were conducted. Subsequently, multi-objective optimization (MOO) was performed to improve the economic and environmental performance of each process. A comprehensive 4E (Energy, Exergy, Economic, Environmental) assessment was followed, including energy consumption (EnC), exergy destruction (ExD), levelized cost of urea (LCOU), and greenhouse gas emissions (GHGe). The energy–exergy–based MOO enabled reductions of 3.60 % in LCOU and 6.82 % in GHGe for the gray process. The EnC and ExD results showed a consistent trend: Gray < Blue < Green. In contrast to EnC, the reforming and urea synthesis sections were identified as the dominant contributors in terms of ExD. Meanwhile, the LCOU ($/t-Urea) followed the same trend as ExD: Gray (309.10) < Blue (325.99) < Green (498.46). In contrast, GHGe (tCO2-eq/t-Urea) exhibited the opposite trend: Gray (1.06) > Blue (0.90) > Green (0.66). Therefore, policy support is important to facilitate the transition toward sustainable urea production processes. For instance, under a carbon tax of $60/tCO2, the LCOU of the blue process becomes lower than that of the gray process. Furthermore, when the price of a renewable energy certificate (REC) exceeds $30/REC, the green process can achieve greater economic competitiveness over the gray and blue processes.

title: Material flows in the UK wood system: reducing import dependency and emissions through circular economy
abstract: The United Kingdom imports over twice its domestic wood harvest, creating severe exposure to geopolitical supply risks. This study presents a material flow analysis quantifying the potential of circular economy interventions to reduce import dependency as well as emissions. We show that in 2018, the UK imported 67% of wood and 64% of paper products, with domestic recycling rates at just 20% and 28%. Scenario modelling demonstrates that combining increased forest productivity, onshoring recycling, and landfill elimination raises the domestic paper recycling rate to 61% and reduces import dependency to 48% (wood) and 33% (paper), while generating 30.9 PJ of energy. Furthermore, substituting imported biomass with the additional energy reduces emissions by up to 5.5 Mt CO 2 eq, assuming carbon is taken up by the forest again, whilst halving wood import dependency to 32%. Our findings show the circular economy can simultaneously deliver decarbonization and geopolitical benefits through reduced import dependency.

title: Impact of oxygenated biofuels dopant on soot and PAH formation in laminar flames: Experimental and theoretical insights
abstract: Combustion-derived soot is a hazardous contributor to air pollution and poses significant health risks. n-decane and methyl butanoate (MB) are key constituents of diesel and biodiesel fuels, respectively. This study examines how varying MB concentrations (0-80%) affect soot formation in n-decane laminar diffusion flames to explore ways to reduce these harmful emissions. The concentrations of soot, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and hydroxyl radical (OH) were measured using laser-induced incandescence (LII) and laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) techniques. Results show that increasing MB concentration decreases OH, PAHs and soot concentrations, indicating that MB weakens combustion intensity and inhibits PAH and soot formation. A chemical reaction mechanism comprising 225 species and 1,321 reactions was developed and validated for n-decane, MB, and PAHs against literature data on ignition delay times, laminar flame velocities, and major specises. Chemical kinetic analysis revealed that increasing MB reduces aromatic hydrocarbon mole fractions. Rate of production (ROP) and sensitivity analyses for A1 (benzene), a key PAH precursor for soot formation, indicate that A1 is primarily formed through the sequential combination of C3 and smaller chain radicals produced during fuel pyrolysis. However, the addition of MB results in the generation of significant amounts of CO and CO2, which reduces the formation of key soot precursor radicals (e.g., C2H2, C2H4, C3H3), thereby reducing soot formation. These findings provide insights into the impact of oxygenated fuel additives on soot formation, offering potential applications for optimizing fuel formulations to reduce soot emissions.

title: Can a discount save the planet? Evidence from the field on sustainable food choices
abstract: Reducing meat consumption is a key strategy to lower the carbon footprint of food systems, yet real-world adoption of sustainable dietary alternatives remains limited. This study investigates how price-based incentives can promote sustainable food choices in a hedonistic, high-emissions consumption setting: a large European music festival. We conducted an incentivized field study at a music festival, targeting attendees who intended to purchase a beef burger and offering them the option to switch to a vegetarian alternative at varying rebate levels. The results show that, on average, a 38% discount (equivalent to €7.10) is required to induce a switch, though 11% of participants refuse to switch even at the maximum discount. We find that switching is significantly associated with gender and sustainability attitudes at the festival, but not with intoxication or sustainability attitudes at home. Using these findings, we estimate that pricing the vegetarian burger at €7.29 (a 43% discount relative to beef) would be necessary to meet the festival's carbon emissions target of 0.75 kg CO 2 e per meal. These results show that even though some consumers with intentions to buy the high-emitting food are sensitive to price rebates, at the aggregate, the rebates need to be very high to obtain a substantial effect. This provides actionable insights for professionals with a focus on designing cost-effective interventions to promote sustainable consumption in leisure and public environments. • A field experiment with 212 real consumers at a major music festival reveals how price influences sustainable food choices. • On average, a 38% discount (€4.30) is required for beef-intending consumers to switch to a vegetarian burger. • 11% of consumers refuse to switch even at a 71% discount, suggesting deep-rooted preferences or identity-based barriers. • Achieving the festival's climate goal (0.75 kg CO 2 e per meal) requires an estimated 83% vegetarian share and a burger price of €7.29 for the vegetarian option. • Female participants and those with stronger festival-specific sustainability attitudes required significantly lower incentives to switch.

title: Circular economy outcomes in EU countries: The impact of manufacturing sectors and the moderating effects of investment, employment and trade
abstract: Countries in the European Union are transitioning from a linear to a more circular economy as they progress towards sustainable development. Drawing on knowledge-based theories, the importance of the manufacturing sector is examined in the context of these circular economy transitions. Using a fixed-effects moderated regression analysis on a panel dataset comprising European Union (EU) countries from 2010 to 2021, the analysis reveals that EU countries with a higher manufacturing base have improved circular economy outcomes. Furthermore, the findings indicate that contingent factors—including private investment in circular economy initiatives, employment in circular economy activities, and trade freedom—positively moderate the relationship between a country's manufacturing base and its circular economy outcomes. Empirical, theoretical and policy implications of these findings are discussed for the circular economy literature and future research directions are outlined.

title: Evaluating the impact of extreme climate events on crop yields under future climate scenarios
abstract: Climate change and associated extreme climate events, such as drought, heavy precipitation, and heatwaves, present challenges to crop yields and global food security. However, the critical thresholds of associated dominant extreme events remain unclear, and so does the manner in which these events may influence future agricultural risks. This work develops a novel, data-driven, framework for assessing climate-induced crop yield risks and for evaluating the role of extreme climate events on the yields of major crops. The evaluation is made using an explainable LightGBM prediction model based on historical yield and climate data. The model elucidates key climate events driving yield variability and identifies their critical thresholds at which they negatively impact crop yield. Non-climatic factors are controlled to isolate climate-driven yield variability. This paper's framework is applied to evaluate the role that extreme climatic events might have on crop yields at the district (Landkreis) level in Germany relying on data from 2001 to 2020 across the growing season. This study projects future spatiotemporal exposure risks to crop yields induced by extreme climate events and their critical thresholds under two carbon emission scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) from 2025 to 2100 in the study region. Our results indicate that meteorological drought and extreme high temperature are the dominant climate stressors threatening spring-sown or summer crop yields, while grain maize, oats, and summer barley are particular sensitive to short-term, intense drought events. In contrast, sugar beet is principally affected by long-term water deficits, as indicated by average meteorological drought conditions, and relies on consistent water availability throughout the growing season. Spatiotemporal exposure analysis reveals crop-specific vulnerability patterns: for instance, potato yields face exposure probabilities of up to 90%, whereas sugar beet shows the lowest risk, albeit with a twofold increase under higher emissions. This work's findings provide actionable insights for precision yield estimation, early warning systems, and adaptation strategies to mitigate climate impacts on food security.

title: Attribution analysis of spatial differentiation in green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency based on geographical detector and random forest models: A case study of the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Green and low-carbon transition and development represents a global issue encompassing economic, social and environmental dimensions. To objectively assess the efficiency of this transition, this study establishes an evaluation index system from input-output perspectives of economy, resources and society, focusing on 108 prefecture-level cities along the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Through trend surface analysis and spatial autocorrelation methods, we investigate the spatio-temporal characteristics of green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency during 2011–2022. The geographical detector method integrated with random forest model is employed to identify driving factors. The main result are as follows: (1) Distinct spatial disparities in transition efficiency across the economic belt, with an overall upward trend despite suboptimal efficiency levels. Regional clusters demonstrate intensified agglomeration patterns, exhibiting a “high-east-west, low-central” spatial configuration. (2) Spatial positive correlations show increasing trends, with local spatial clusters predominantly manifesting as high-high or low-low agglomerations. (3) Dynamic variations in factor explanatory power across study years, with enhanced combined effects through factor interactions. Notably, the top three determinants, industrial development level, urban development level, and social consumption level exhibit nonlinear relationships with transition efficiency, while the nature of these relationships varies. This research provides empirical evidence for understanding regional transition mechanisms and offers decision-making support for formulating differentiated green development strategies.

title: Quantify resource footprint transfers through interprovincial agricultural trade in China: Visible flows and hidden impacts
abstract: Agricultural trade contributes to regional food security while mediating resource transfers across regions. However, the impact of agricultural trade on resource footprints at the subnational scale remains poorly quantified. This study quantifies the magnitude and impact of resource footprint transfers through agricultural trade at the provincial scale in China for 2020. The results show that resource footprint transfers are equivalent to 55%, 65%, and 51% of China's total agricultural land, nitrogen and phosphorus footprints, respectively and involve all provinces within the footprint transfer network. The distribution of footprint transfers is highly heterogeneous, with five northern provinces contributing around 50% of domestic exports, while Guangdong, the largest importer in southern China, accounts for ∼10% of total imports. Notably, nearly 50% of the footprint transfers originate from international imports, benefiting China by shifting resource burdens abroad. Moreover, the results indicate that agricultural trade reduces China's land, nitrogen, and phosphorus footprints by 34%, 37%, and 18%, respectively. However, interprovincial trade alone yields significantly lower resource-saving efficiencies of 5.6%, 5.1% and 1.4% for land, nitrogen, and phosphorus, respectively. This inefficiency is accompanied by a resource burden shift from developed provinces to less developed regions, exacerbating environmental inequity. Finally, we identified specific trade links (e.g., rice trade from Heilongjiang to Hebei) and product-province categories (e.g., maize for Inner Mongolia) with high potential to improve the resource efficiency of the trading system. This study provides a scientific basis for formulating region-specific policies to address the resource inefficiencies and environmental inequalities embedded in China's interprovincial agricultural trade.

title: Fully passive siphon-driven salt removal surpassing diffusion limits in solar distillation
abstract: Salt accumulation is a key bottleneck in solar- and waste-heat driven passive distillation systems, where evaporation inevitably leads to salt buildup that compromises long-term performance. Here, the first evaporation-driven siphon architecture enabling fully passive and autonomous salt removal from a porous evaporator is introduced. The device operates in a fully passive manner, relying solely on evaporation-induced hydraulic head differences. The system functions without external energy, active control, or moving parts. An analytical model, developed through the electric–hydraulic analogy, predicts both the transient evolution of evaporation-induced hydraulic head difference and the frequency of self-triggered rinsing cycles, and is validated experimentally under controlled conditions. A case study shows that the system generates hydraulic head differences exceeding 1.5 cm and triggers multiple rinsing events within hours. Parametric analysis reveals that geometry and hydraulic resistance of the porous evaporator strongly influence performance, and that a simple topological modification – introducing a localized high-resistance segment – further boosts hydraulic head buildup. Compared to state-of-the-art passive strategies limited by diffusion, the siphon-driven mechanism achieves over an order-of-magnitude faster salt removal, restoring seawater-level salinity within three hours. These results establish a new paradigm in solar distillation, providing a scalable strategy compatible with meter-scale evaporators and capable of drastically reducing maintenance requirements for robust salt management in evaporation-driven applications, e.g. desalination, particularly suited to off-grid and resource-limited environments. • Fully passive siphon removes salt from porous solar evaporators autonomously. • Evaporation-driven hydraulic head triggers self-sustained rinsing cycles. • Validated analytical model predicts hydraulic head and rinsing frequency. • Evaporator salinity restored to seawater levels within 3 h. • Salt removal >10× faster than diffusion-limited passive methods.

title: Advancing polyhydroxybutyrate-co-polyhydroxyvalerate (PHBV) production from coconut coir pith waste: An intensified and targeted approach for sustainable bioconversion through enzymatic hydrolysis
abstract: The extensive use and indiscriminate disposal of petroleum-derived, non-biodegradable plastics have created an urgent global environmental and health crisis. Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV), a microbial co-biopolymer, represents a promising alternative due to its favorable mechanical and thermal properties. However, its large-scale production is hindered by higher costs than those of conventional plastics. This study establishes an integrated and cost-effective strategy for PHBV production from low-cost coconut coir pith (CCP) hydrolysate using Brevibacillus invocatus MTCC 9039. Sequential alkaline H2O2 pretreatment of CCP resulted in a 67.94% lignin reduction and a 58.46% increase in cellulose content. An intensified fed-batch enzymatic hydrolysis of cellulose-enriched CCP at 15% (w/w) solid loading (5% + 4% + 3% + 2% + 1%) under an intermediate enzyme addition condition, supported by RSM-based pre-optimization, ultrasonication-enhanced enzyme–substrate interaction, and ultrafiltration-based enzyme recycling, yielded 99.74 g/L reducing sugars with a 66.49% conversion efficiency. Utilizing the diluted form of CCP hydrolysate at 30 g/L glucose in combination with 50% (v/v) mineral salt medium, achieved a 66.36% PHB accumulation yield. A fed-batch fermentation strategy with optimized sodium propionate supplementation at 0.2% (w/v) and stepwise CCP hydrolysate feeding at 30 g/L glucose at 72, 96, and 120 h yielded maximum biomass and PHBV titers of 17.76 g/L and 13.6 g/L, respectively. FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed the structural identity of the biopolymer. Overall, this work demonstrates a robust, low-cost, and scalable bioprocess utilizing lignocellulosic waste for efficient PHBV production, advancing the development of sustainable bioplastics.

title: A contribution to Urban Mining Potential through a probability-of-conformity-based indicator for optimizing reuse of cut concrete slabs
abstract: Reusing concrete slab elements offers a promising urban mining strategy to reduce the environmental footprint of constructions. Cast-in-place concrete slabs represent a particularly large resource, yet their reuse is complicated by uncertainties regarding geometry, load-bearing capacity, serviceability, and fire resistance. To capture these uncertainties, this paper introduces the Urban Mining Potential (UMP) as a novel environmental indicator quantifying the expected CO 2 savings from reusing urban mining slabs compared to conventional construction. The UMP is defined by combining process-related efforts with probabilities of conformity (PoCs), which reflect the likelihood that urban mining slabs meet technical requirements of new structures. A recursive optimization algorithm is developed to solve the two-dimensional knapsack problem of cutting monolithic slabs into urban mining slabs, efficiently identifying cutting patterns that maximize the UMP. Sensitivity analyses assess the influence of the PoCs and material testing. Results from four case studies show that incorporating PoCs increases the UMP by at least 30% (5th percentile), while material testing of concrete cover significantly improves outcomes; in contrast, testing of compressive strength and reinforcement yield strength has only minor effects. The proposed methodology provides a probabilistic, optimization-based framework to maximize environmental benefits of concrete slab reuse, advancing urban mining as a viable business model for CO 2 reduction, resource efficiency, and waste minimization.

title: Selective separation of bismuth from high-acid copper electrolytes: design of highly stable antimony-based adsorbent and investigation of strong adsorption mechanisms
abstract: Bismuth (Bi) in high-acid copper electrolytes (HACEs) substantially impairs copper electrolytic refining and cathode copper quality while being a critical strategic metal. Selective separation of Bi from HACEs enables electrolyte purification and Bi resource recovery. Although antimony (Sb)-based purifiers have shown promise as green HACE purification materials, they suffer from high self-dissolution losses, poor selectivity for Bi, and complex synthesis processes. In this study, a highly stable amorphous mesoporous Sb2O5 adsorbent (specific surface area: 109.6 m2/g) was synthesized via a facile one-step water bath method. The adsorbent exhibited exceptional resistance to interference from Cu, As, and H2SO4, thereby enabling effective and selective Bi separation. Under optimal conditions, the adsorbent selectively removed 91.79% of Bi from industrial HACEs to 0.05 g/L— thereby fully meeting the electrolyte purification requirements—with a dissolution loss of only 0.33%. Thermodynamic and kinetic analyses revealed that the adsorption process followed the Langmuir isotherm and a pseudo-second-order kinetic model, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 88.50 mg/g. Mechanistic investigations revealed a multistage chemisorption process: electrostatic attraction caused Bi3+/BiO+ to aggregate on the surface of the adsorbent, coordination with the Sb-OH active sites on secondary particles on the adsorbent surface, and finally, localized crystal rearrangement for stable Bi fixation. The Bi-loaded adsorbent achieved Bi separation and recovery through chloride desorption and simultaneously enabled adsorbent regeneration, maintaining a Bi removal rate of more than 80% over five purification cycles. This study provides a promising strategy for the HACE purification and Bi resource recovery.

title: Sustainable glucose meters: Circular economy insights from integrated life cycle assessment and material composition analysis
abstract: Continuous glucose meters (CGMs) are increasingly used for diabetes management but raise environmental concerns due to short product lifetimes and materials-intensive designs. This study evaluates the potential of applying circular economy (CE) strategies to reduce the environmental impacts of CGMs. Our approach uses an integrated environmental assessment which combines life cycle assessment (LCA) with product-scale material composition analysis (MCA), informed by material flow analysis (MFA) principles. Three commercially available CGMs were assessed and compared with a conventional finger-prick glucose meter as a baseline. Two CE scenarios were modelled: (i) a modular design, in which the applicator and transmitter were redesigned as reusable components with extended lifetimes while allowing single-use needle replacement, and (ii) material substitution, where polycarbonate components and packaging were replaced with lower-impact alternatives. Across all case studies, the CE scenarios reduced combined product and packaging material use by 54–84% and climate change impacts by up to 66.5% relative to the extant (non-circular) baseline. The modular design scenario delivered the greatest environmental benefit by extending the functional lifespan of key components. Packaging and electronic components were thus identified as dominant environmental hotspots, indicating priorities for future redesign. Overall, the results demonstrate that CE-oriented redesign can substantially improve the environmental sustainability of CGMs without compromising functionality and highlight the value of integrating material composition mapping with LCA to support sustainability-driven medical device design.

title: Optimal capacity configuration of the wind-solar-hydrogen multi-energy system for green data computing centers: An integrated AI forecasting and improved multi-objective optimization approach
abstract: The explosive growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing has triggered an unprecedented global demand for computing power, pushing the energy consumption and carbon footprint of Data Computing Centers (DCCs) to critical levels. Clean energy supply systems are crucial for supporting their sustainable development. This study innovatively integrates concentrated solar power (CSP) and hydrogen storage into the multi-energy system for DCCs, constructing a deep-coupled wind-solar-hydrogen multi-energy complementary system (MCES) tailored to the load coupling characteristics of DCCs. An integrated KOA-ITransformer-BiLSTM model is developed to predict wind-solar output, and Latin hypercube sampling combined with scenario reduction is adopted to characterize and mitigate system uncertainty. A multi-objective optimization model is further established to minimize economic expenditure and carbon emissions while enhancing energy utilization. The study improves the NSGA-III algorithm by adding an NDX-SBX crossover operator to achieve a better solution set. Finally, the optimal capacity configuration is chosen using a multi-attribute decision-making approach. Findings indicate that the optimized wind-solar-hydrogen system demonstrates strong economic and environmental performance for a DCC in Hami, Xinjiang. The optimal configuration achieves 100% energy utilization efficiency, with an annual cost of 7.65 million CNY and annual carbon emissions of 678.25 tons. Compared with the unoptimized scheme, carbon emissions are reduced by over 15%, and both energy efficiency and economic performance are improved. The findings offer practical guidance for advancing low-carbon energy transitions and sustainable development in DCCs and other high-demand campuses.

title: A practical way to reduce slag entrainment during ladle teeming: Regular cleaning of ladle outlet adherents
abstract: In the final stage of ladle teeming, slag entrainment caused by drain sinks degrades molten steel cleanliness and reduces metal yield. Actual ladle outlets often experience clogging and protrusion formation. A water model of a 300-ton ladle was established to study the effect of outlet structure on the critical drainage height for slag entrainment, with varied outlet configurations.​ The results indicated that, for a constant outlet taper, the critical drainage height increased by 27.0% from 21.6 to 27.43 mm as the upper diameter of the discharge cone decreased from 50 to 30 mm; for a fixed lower diameter, it rose slightly by 2.56% from 27.43 to 28.13 mm as the upper diameter was reduced from 30 to 18 mm​ A modified theoretical model, distinguishing between the upper diameter of the discharge cone and the outlet diameter of the nozzle, was developed to explain this trend, which contradicted traditional theoretical models. Furthermore, in the water model, the critical drainage height rose significantly by 86.9% from 28.13 to 52.57 mm as the protrusion height increased from 0 to 30 mm​ Industrial application confirmed that ladle outlet clogging led to a significant increase in residual molten steel, while systematic cleaning of the ladle outlet effectively reduced this residual molten steel. Therefore, it was recommended to regularly clean adherents from the ladle outlet and maintain the integrity of the outlet structure. This practice would help improve metal yield and molten steel cleanliness, thereby advancing cleaner production in steelmaking processes.

title: Decoupled greening and vegetation resilience in the arid Tarim River mainstream and its driving mechanisms
abstract: Vegetation resilience reflects the capacity of ecosystems to withstand and recover from disturbances. However, current research on greenness trends has predominantly focused on changes in vegetation cover or biomass, with limited attention to resilience dynamics and their underlying drivers. Using the arid Tarim River mainstream as a case study, this study quantified vegetation resilience based on the first-order autoregressive coefficient (AR(1)) derived from kNDVI time series during 2000–2020, and identified the environmental drivers of greening and resilience change using random forest models. Results show that the region exhibited significant (p < 0.05) overall greening, yet 51.1% of the area showed a significant (p < 0.05) decline in resilience, and 45.2% of greening areas simultaneously experienced resilience loss, most prominently in the upper and middle reaches. Attribution analysis indicated that greening was dominated by increased surface soil moisture, whereas resilience loss was primarily driven by deep groundwater depletion, with thresholds favorable for greening and resilience maintenance identified as soil moisture trend >0.0005 m3 m−3 yr−1 and groundwater storage anomaly trend > −7.3151 mm yr−1, respectively. Ecological water conveyance improved resilience within the core zones of the lower reaches, but the benefits were spatially constrained, motivating a shift from linear conveyance to spatially distributed delivery with resilience-based zoning and rotational scheduling. Overall, greening does not necessarily imply enhanced resilience, underscoring the value of integrating resilience metrics into future arid ecosystem management.

title: Sustainable hydrogen production from biogas under operational variability: Feed forecasting with a rolling horizon scheduling strategy
abstract: Hydrogen production from biogas is strongly affected by upstream feedstock variability and market fluctuations, creating challenges for efficient and sustainable production planning. This study proposes a digital scheduling framework for hydrogen production via combined steam and CO2 reforming (CSCR), integrating feed forecasting, surrogate modeling, and rolling horizon optimization to enable adaptive operation and support future operational planning under variable conditions. First, detailed process simulations of the integrated CSCR system were conducted to generate technical, economic, and environmental performance data over a wide range of operating conditions. A deep neural network–based surrogate model was then developed to represent the nonlinear behavior of the process with low computational cost. Forecasts of feed biogas CH4 concentration were generated using a gated recurrent unit (GRU) model over a seven-day horizon. Rolling horizon (RH) optimization was employed in a multi-step scheduling scheme to determine optimal daily operating parameters within predefined bounds, aiming to meet hydrogen demand while adapting to predicted feed variability and market fluctuations. The results showed that the GRU model provided accurate forecasts (R2 = 0.9411), enabling advanced estimation of feed biogas composition. Informed by these forecasts, the RH approach allowed flexible adjustment of the CSCR operating parameters, leading to increased hydrogen production, reductions in net CO2-equivalent emissions of up to 1470 kgCO2/day, and improvements in cumulative profit of up to 47% compared with fixed scheduling over the seven-day horizon. Overall, the proposed scheduling approach effectively coordinates production with feedstock and operational fluctuations, enhancing adaptability and supporting sustainable hydrogen production planning.

title: Optimization of binary binder blends for aqueous-based slurries of SiOx/C for next-generation lithium-ion batteries
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy solutions has highlighted the crucial role of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) in the global energy transition. However, the conventional use of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binders combined with toxic solvents like N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), in the LIBs manufacturing process, poses environmental and cost concerns. In this study, three different water-soluble polysaccharides, sodium alginate, tragacanth gum, and carrageenan, are investigated as suitable binders for silicon/graphite composite anodes. The three single polysaccharide binders are initially screened through rheological and electrochemical analyses to ensure compatibility with slurry processing, electrode and cell manufacturing. From the pre-screening, sodium alginate emerges as the most promising candidate, demonstrating favourable rheological properties and electrochemical stability. To further improve electrode mechanical properties and long-term electrochemical performances, sodium alginate is mixed with lithiated polyacrylic acid in binary mixtures with a total binder content of 3 wt%. The optimal formulation, 2 LiPAA :1 ALG , exhibits enhanced cycling stability and higher specific capacity retention compared to single-binder systems. Statistical analysis confirms the significant influence of binder mixture composition, highlighting the complementary mechanical and electrochemical roles of ALG and LiPAA. In comparison with previously reported crosslinked or grafted binder systems that require chemical modification, this approach uses a simple physical mixing strategy, improving the electrochemical behaviour, preserving processability. Overall, the results demonstrate that rationally designed combinations of natural and synthetic water-soluble binders offer a viable strategy to balance mechanical integrity, sustainability, and electrochemical performance, providing valuable insights for the development of next-generation LIB anodes. • k-carrageenan excluded due to poor coating and gel-like behaviour. • ALG and LiPAA mixture improves both cycling and manufacturability. • 2 LiPAA :1 ALG formulation outperforms single-binder systems. • LiPAA improves ICE while ALG ensures long-term cycling stability. • Statistical analysis confirms LiPAA boosts initial capacity.

title: Digital transformation and sustainable industrialization: the role of dynamic digital capabilities and continuous auditing as digital governance
abstract: This study examines the role of digital transformation in promoting sustainable industrialization in resource-limited manufacturing and the functioning of continuous auditing within this framework. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and digital governance, we develop a model of three digital dynamic capabilities (sensing, capturing, and transforming) that drive digital transformation. We also look at how these capabilities, along with continuous auditing, affect sustainable industrialization in Jordanian industrial companies. We use PLS-SEM to analyze survey data from 580 managers across 69 companies. The findings indicate that digital sensing (β = 0.46) and digital transformation capability (β = 0.36) have the most potent effects on digital transformation (R2 = 0.66). In contrast, digital capture (β = 0.09) has a more negligible yet notable effect. Digital transformation significantly enhances sustainable industrialization (β = 0.71, R2 = 0.78), with continuous auditing exerting a notable direct effect (β = 0.58). In contrast, the interaction between digital transformation and continuous auditing is not statistically significant (β = −0.27, p > 0.30), suggesting that, in this context, continuous auditing primarily serves as an independent governance layer rather than a moderating factor. The research situates the outcomes of sustainable industrialization within an information-governance framework. It helps managers and policymakers determine how to integrate digital investments, continuous auditing, and industrial sustainability under resource and regulatory constraints.

title: Optimization and simulation-based comparative performance analysis of Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) treatment in Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) and covered lagoon system: Insights from industrial applications
abstract: This study presents the first simulation-based comparison of CSTR and covered lagoon for biogas production from palm oil mill effluent (POME) using anaerobic digestion (AD), integrating simulation, optimization, and economic evaluation.
