However, backfilled gangue is commonly exposed to mine-water seepage, which can restructure pore networks and surface chemistry, thereby enhancing low-temperature oxidation and increasing self-heating risk-posing challenges to cleaner backfill practices. In this study, mine-water evolution was simulated by percolating backfilled coal gangue with pure water (neutral stage), an HCl solution adjusted to pH 3.5 (acidification stage), and a 0.05 M FeCl3 solution at pH 3.5 (Fe3+-rich stage) for 3 and 7 days. Pore structure, mineral assemblage and functional groups were characterized using BET, XRD, FTIR and TG, while low-temperature oxidation was evaluated through programmed heating coupled with gas analysis (O2 consumption, CO release and CO/CO2 ratios). Seepage typically augmented the accessible surface area and pore volume, which in turn facilitated mass transfer. Water treatment primarily removed soluble salts, producing only a modest increase in oxidation activity. Acidic seepage accelerated the dissolution of acid-sensitive minerals, improved pore connectivity, and increased oxygen-containing functional groups, leading to higher O2 consumption and CO generation than water treatment. FeCl3 seepage produced the strongest activation, promoting transformations of reactive minerals and generating Fe-O-associated reactive sites, resulting in the highest O2 consumption rate and CO release. Among all treatments, the 7-day FeCl3-treated sample exhibited the strongest self-heating propensity. Overall, the evolution of mine water toward acidic and Fe3+-rich conditions drives coal-gangue backfill to a highly porous and chemically reactive state. Effective management of mine-water acidification and Fe3+ enrichment, combined with monitoring of O2 consumption and CO release, can support cleaner and safer coal-gangue backfill operations.

title: Removal of PFAS and 1,2,4-TCB from firefighting-contaminated sites by iron-modified biochar microspheres loaded with microbes
abstract: The co-contamination of PFAS and 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene (1,2,4-TCB) in fire fighting-contaminated sites has long been an overlooked issue, posing potential toxicity risks to ecosystems and human health. The combined use of biochar adsorption and biodegradation has garnered significant attention in the field of organic pollutant removal. However, the sustained removal performance of the composite system toward sites co-contaminated with PFAS and 1,2,4-TCB, as well as its effects on soil microbial communities, remain to be systematically investigated. This study developed an iron-modified biochar sphere coupled microbial consortium system (Fe/BCM-DB) for degradation. A 180-day remediation experiment was conducted at different profiles of a PFAS and 1,2,4-TCB co-contaminated site under pilot-scale conditions. The study investigated the sustained remediation effects of composite systems on co-contaminated sites, the underlying removal mechanisms, and the response of microbial communities. The removal of pollutants by Fe/BCM-DB involves two core mechanisms: adsorption and biodegradation. The research results indicate that the maximum removal rates achieved across different profiles were 98.42% for PFOS, 93.14% for PFOA, 46.57% for PFHxA, 32.81% for PFBS, 28.73% for PFBA, and 90.84% for 1,2,4-TCB. The diversity of the soil microbial community increased significantly after remediation, providing core biological support for the gradual restoration of its ecological functions. Fe/BCM-DB effectively remediates sites co-contaminated with PFAS and 1,2,4-TCB, representing a promising approach to remediation.

title: Influence of biochar feedstock and particle size on cementitious composites incorporating biochar as a partial cement replacement
abstract: This study investigates the potential of biochar as a sustainable partial replacement for cement in cementitious composites, aiming to reduce embodied carbon while maintaining or improving material performance. Biochars derived from rice husk, softwood, and hardwood were examined across three particle size ranges (<38 μm, 53–149 μm, and 149–300 μm). A comprehensive characterization was performed to assess their elemental composition, crystalline structure, surface morphology, functional groups, and porosity. Cementitious composites incorporating 5% and 10% biochar by weight of cement were prepared and evaluated in terms of compressive strength, hydration behavior, and thermal conductivity. A cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment was conducted considering cement production, biochar processing, and pyrolysis operations; upstream biomass cultivation and harvesting, long-distance transportation, construction, use phase, and end-of-life stages were excluded. Results show that influence of biochar on performance is highly dependent on feedstock type and particle size. Compressive strength results demonstrated that mortars incorporating rice husk biochar maintained up to 97% of the control strength, whereas hardwood and softwood biochars led to reductions of up to 32% and 47%, respectively, particularly at finer particle sizes and higher dosages. Among the biochars evaluated, rice husk biochar produced at approximately 550 °C and ground to a particle size range of 53–149 μm achieved the greatest reduction in thermal conductivity, with values up to 54% lower than the control mixture at a 10% cement replacement level. In addition, life cycle assessment revealed that rice husk biochar offered the most favorable balance between mechanical performance and environmental impact, achieving up to 33% reduction in global warming potential. The results demonstrate that biochar–cement composites offer practical potential for energy-efficient and low-carbon construction applications, particularly in non-structural and semi-structural elements where reduced thermal conductivity and environmental impact are prioritized.

title: Pathways for clean and low-carbon transition in coal-rich countries: A coal-based integrated energy system scheme featuring co-production of cooling, heating, power and chemicals
abstract: The clean and low-carbon utilization of coal resources is a crucial aspect of energy transition for coal-rich countries. A substantial amount of CO2 generated from conventional coal utilization patterns can be effectively utilized by producing green hydrogen from renewable energy, providing a pathway to both carbon mitigation and efficient resource utilization. Furthermore, integrated energy systems represent an effective option for realizing synergistic complementarity and proximity absorption of heterogeneous energy sources. Therefore, a coal-based integrated energy system was devised. The CO2 from coal combustion is combined with hydrogen from renewable energy to synthesize methanol and methane. Methane is then combusted to supply external energy, while methanol simultaneously enables chemical carbon sequestration and can be sold as a byproduct, thereby achieving efficient and low-carbon utilization of the resources. The feasibility and operational performance of the system were further analyzed. The system can simultaneously achieve the clean and low-carbon utilization of coal and enable the joint supply of multiple energy products. The life-cycle carbon emission factors for power, heating, and cooling are 488.38 g/kWh, 49.61 kg/GJ, and 66.15 kg/GJ, respectively, and the system achieves net-zero emissions for methanol production, demonstrating its prominent carbon mitigation capability. The levelized cost of energy of the system is 154.52 $/MWh. Furthermore, the influence of technological development and energy policies on system evolution was discussed, with the levelized cost of energy projected to fall to 82.01 $/MWh by 2050. This study supports the low-carbon energy transition in coal-rich countries and provides a new perspective for the clean and low-carbon utilization of regional coal resources.

title: Superstructure optimization of sustainable formic acid synthesis from hydrogen and carbon dioxide: a scenario-based approach
abstract: CO2 capture and utilization to produce formic acid (FA) as a hydrogen carrier offers a promising route for climate mitigation. As a complement to previous studies on CO2 and H2-based formic acid synthesis, this study adopts a superstructure-based approach to evaluate alternative process pathways for sustainable production, considering the availability of diverse feedstocks, CO2 capture technologies, and H2 production technologies. The superstructure is optimized under various economic, environmental, and policy scenarios using a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model implemented in GAMS software. Results show that under the economic scenario (scenario-1), the optimized pathway result in an LCOF of USD 555/t FA and net emissions of 3.26 t CO2-eq/t FA. For the environmental scenario (scenario-2), the LCOF is USD 890/t FA with significantly reduced net emissions of 0.22 t CO2-eq/t FA. Scenario-3, which balances cost and emissions, increases the LCOF by about 10% but reduces net emissions by more than 66% relative to scenario-1. To transition toward cleaner FA production, policy scenarios were explored. In the short term scenario (scenario-4), the USD 70/t CO2-eq carbon tax causes the superstructure to choose a cleaner pathway, reducing net emissions to 0.8 t CO2-eq/t FA. In the long-term scenario (scenario-5), learning-induced capital cost reductions in low-carbon technologies lead to a pathway with net emissions of 0.24 t CO2-eq/t FA and a 26.8% lower LCOF than scenario-2. Overall, these findings show that combining emission-reduction policies with technological development can accelerate the transition to sustainable FA production and enhance its economic competitiveness.

title: Corporate governance-based financial performance analysis: A decision support system for identification of top-performing industry benchmarks
abstract: This study aims to evaluate corporate governance-based financial performance by integrating governance mechanisms with financial metrics, moving beyond analyses that rely solely on financial indicators. A decision support system (DSS) is developed using a hybrid Continuous Pythagorean Fuzzy (CPF)–Criteria Importance through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC)–Weighted Euclidean Distance-Based Approach (WEDBA). The method simultaneously incorporates quantitative and qualitative parameters and assigns expert influence based on experience and risk-taking propensity. Subjective and objective weighting approaches are combined: CPF sets are employed for subjective weighting, while the CRITIC method is used to determine objective criterion weights. The WEDBA method calculates companies’ corporate governance-based financial performance levels. The approach is applied to ten food and beverage companies operating in Turkey. Among sixteen corporate governance-based financial performance criteria, “Return on Equity” emerges as the most influential, with independent board members, board size, and female board representation also demonstrating significant importance. Within the sample, Türk Tuborg is identified as the top-performing company. The reliability and robustness of the results are confirmed through sensitivity and comparative analyses. The study presents a novel hybrid MCDM framework that integrates expert judgment and quantitative data within a Continuous Pythagorean fuzzy context, offering a practical DSS for assessing corporate governance-driven financial performance. The findings provide actionable insights for corporate managers and policymakers seeking to enhance governance practices and financial outcomes in sector-specific contexts.

title: Fluorine-free and sustainable synthesis of Ti3C2Tx MXene via chelation-assisted alkaline etching for environmental sensing and photothermal applications
abstract: Two-dimensional MXene nanosheets have attracted extensive attention due to their exceptional physicochemical properties. However, the conventional synthesis of MXenes relies heavily on hazardous fluoride-based etchants, causing severe environmental and safety risks. Herein, we report a clean, fluorine-free, and sustainable strategy for synthesizing oxygen-terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene (Ff-Ti3C2Tx) via a novel chelation-assisted alkaline etching approach. By synergistically combining tetramethylammonium hydroxide with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, we successfully overcome the intrinsic aluminum-passivation bottleneck that severely restricts the etching efficiency of conventional pure alkaline systems. This dual-agent chelation system not only enables the controlled and efficient delamination of Ti3AlC2 into monolayer Ti3C2Tx nanosheets under extremely mild conditions but also delivers a record-high yield of 40%, representing a 60% improvement over existing fluorine-free methods. The resulting Ff-Ti3C2Tx exhibits a highly hydrophilic, oxygen-rich surface (–OH, –O), which inherently enhances its electrochemical activity and light-harvesting performance. As an environmental sensor, it achieves ultrasensitive detection of p-nitrophenol with a low detection limit of 0.055 μM and a high sensitivity of 3.16 μA μM−1 cm−2. Moreover, Ff-Ti3C2Tx demonstrates exceptional near-infrared photothermal performance, with a mass extinction coefficient of 21.8 L g−1 cm−1 at 808 nm and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 42.1%. This work provides a scalable, environmentally benign, and high-yielding pathway for fluorine-free production of MXene and establishes Ff-Ti3C2Tx as a versatile platform for next-generation environmental monitoring and sustainable energy applications.

title: Application of novel eco-friendly membranes prepared with recycled high-impact polystyrene to municipal wastewater treatment
abstract: In the frame of circular economy, plastic wastes could be used for producing eco-friendly membranes. Specifically, in this work, recycled high impact polystyrene (HIPS), whose world production reached 3.2 million metric tons in 2024, has been used for the manufacture of microporous membranes by the nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) method. Three different polymer concentrations were tested (20, 25 and 30% w/w) in the manufacture of the membranes. Two different lab scale plants with a dead-end cell and a cross-flow module, respectively, were used. The manufactured membranes were applied for the for the filtration of samples from effluents from secondary and primary treatments of a municipal wastewater treatment plant, which has not been reported previously in the bibliography, being a scientific novelty. Results with the dead-end cell drove to the selection of the membranes made with 20% of HIPS with and without thermal post-treatment. In the tests with secondary effluents, these membranes yielded permeates with enough quality to be reused in agriculture in terms of turbidity and microbial analysis (0 coliforms forming units of E. coli and turbidity lower than 1 NTU), fully comparable with those provided by commercial membranes. The membrane made with 20% of recycled HIPS with thermal post-treatment achieved chemical oxygen demand and turbidity removal efficiencies higher than 35 and 90%, respectively, in the application to primary effluent. Most of the membrane fouling was reversible.

title: Mechanical and thermal performance of 3D printed fired bricks incorporating algae-based biomass for sustainable construction
abstract: This study explores the potential of seaweed as a bio-based pore-forming agent in the context of 3D printed clay bricks, with the objective of developing masonry units that are both lightweight and more thermally efficient. The formulations were developed by varying the algae content and particle size: fine particles (FP) were incorporated at 2–8% (by mass) and coarse particles (CP) at 2.5–5%. Following the firing process at 1050 °C, there was an observed increase in porosity from 3.30% (C-0A) to 10.48% (C-8A). This resulted in a significant decrease in thermal conductivity from 0.47 to 0.30 W/m.K, as well as a 13% reduction in bulk density. From a mechanical standpoint, the increase in porosity leads to a reduction in stiffness and strength. However, it is noteworthy that all formulations exhibit a compressive strength of at least 21 MPa. A microstructural analysis by X-Ray nano-tomography reveals that FP promotes more homogeneous porosity, resulting in a more favorable insulation/strength compromise. Conversely, CP generates localized defects and more pronounced mechanical degradation without additional thermal gain. The findings of this study establish quantitative relationships between porosity, conductivity, and strength, which are useful for optimizing 3D printed fired bricks. However, further research is necessary to validate its industrial deployment, including studies on bending, freeze-thaw durability, and life cycle assessment (LCA).

title: The synergistic effect of dual value chain participation on pollution and carbon reduction: A provincial-level analysis in China based on the MIROT-ICIO framework
abstract: Even as the pace of globalization moderates, clarifying how national value chains (NVCs) and global value chains (GVCs) shape environmental performance remains central to climate governance. Using an MRIOT-ICIO framework and panel data for 30 Chinese provinces (2000-2022), this paper examines how dual participation in GVCs and NVCs affects pollution-carbon reduction synergy (SPCR). Empirical results show that: (1) GVC participation exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with SPCR, whereas NVC participation demonstrates a consistent positive linear effect. (2) Regional innovation capacity acts as a critical threshold condition: once the S&T fiscal expenditure share exceeds an empirically identified benchmark of 13.26, the SPCR payoffs from both NVC and GVC participation become significantly positive and strengthen thereafter. (3) Dual participation yields a statistically supported but intensity-dependent synergy, defined by the cross-partial derivative of SPCR with respect to NVC and GVC participation on the estimated response surface. Within the observed range of participation, complementarity is confined to a well-defined region where NVC participation is sufficiently developed and GVC participation remains moderate, underscoring that the SPCR performance of dual participation is governed by threshold conditions and intensity-dependent interactions. These findings provide new insights into the pursuit of sustainable development in interconnected economies.

title: Water-resistant adhesives from bio-inspired mineral networks for the sustainable valorization of petroleum waste
abstract: Poly (olefin-alt-sodium maleate) (OSM) is a water-based formaldehyde-free adhesive, produced via alkaline hydrolysis of Poly (olefin-alt-maleic anhydride) (OMA) utilizing petroleum byproducts. This study was inspired by the anionic-cationic-hydrophobic interplay of biological fluid condensates to construct a ternary composite adhesive system based on the Agglomeration-curing-network reform tripartite mechanism: an anionic resin (OSM) and cationic resin polyamidoamine-epichlorohydrin (PAE) as the dual-network adhesion matrix; Palygorskite clay was introduced in-situ as the hydrophobic phase, and a mechanical reinforcement framework was constructed using organic-inorganic hybrid effects. This strategy simplified the preparation process and enabled efficient cross-linking and curing under a mild temperature of 120 °C and pressure of 1 MPa. The resulting plywood exhibited remarkable dry (2.24 MPa) and wet bonding strengths (1.54 MPa), which were nearly triple the values of previously reported materials. These values were equivalent to the strength of commercially available phenolic resins and far exceeded the requirements of Class II plywood (GB/T 17657–2022). The adhesive simultaneously displayed excellent pre-pressing capability and final bonding performance across different substrates, highlighting its broad applicability. This bio-inspired strategy resolves the long-standing trade-off between eco-friendliness (water-based, formaldehyde-free) and performance (moisture resistance, mild curing) of adhesives for various wood composites.

title: AlF3 synthesized by leaching-mixture calcination process from spent cathode carbon
abstract: Spent cathode carbon (SCC) is classified as an industrial hazardous waste due to its extraction toxicity. Meanwhile, SCC contains abundant fluorine-aluminum resources, with significant utilization value. Owing to product quality, cost, and safety, the current process for recovering aluminum fluoride (AlF3) from SCC urgently requires improvement. This research developed a novel leaching-mixture calcination technology for AlF3 synthesis and investigated the effects of various factors on the leaching and calcination process. The results showed that the total leaching rate of F from SCC reached 99.48% by AlCl3-NaOH leaching. After the Al-F in filtrates precipitated as aluminum hydroxyfluoride hydrate (Al2(OH)2.76F3.24·H2O, AHF), AlF3 was synthesized by AHF-NH4F mixture calcination, with AHF-to-NH4F mass ratio of 1:1 at 500 °C for 60 min, achieving the purity of 93.60%. At high temperatures, NH4F can combine with the hydroxyl groups in AHF and convert into the fluoroaluminates of (NH4)3AlF6 and NH4AlF4, which subsequently decompose into AlF3, while the Al2O3 from AHF decomposition continues to react with NH4F or generated HF to promote AlF3 formation in the system. This process demonstrates the potential of SCC for application and achieves AlF3 recycling.

title: Recycling-and-disassembly collaborative scheduling in remanufacturing system with routing and disassembly line balancing consideration
abstract: Research on the recycling and disassembly of end-of-life (EOL) products has garnered escalating academic and industrial attention. Specifically, vehicle routing and product pickup scheduling decisions dictate the batch arrival time and quantity of EOL products at disassembly facilities, while precedence-constrained disassembly task scheduling decisions dominate the rationality of task allocation and the efficiency of workstation utilization. This inherent temporal-resource coupling effect significantly amplifies the complexity of integrated decision-making, since the multidimensional routing and disassembly decisions are highly interdependent and thus pose formidable challenges to coordinated optimization. There, this study introduces the Recycling-and-Disassembly Collaborative Scheduling Problem (RD-CSP), which unifies recycling routing and disassembly line scheduling within a single framework to jointly optimize both stages. And a bi-objective mathematical model is formulated to minimize total operational cost and total synchronization delay. To solve the RD-CSP, a Q-learning-guided variable neighborhood hybrid evolutionary algorithm (QVHEA) is developed. In the QVHEA, a three-layer encoding scheme is designed to represent the coupled routing and disassembly decisions. Then, a Q-learning-driven variable neighborhood search module is proposed to adaptively select among six problem-tailored neighborhood operators, balancing search diversification and intensification. Extensive experiments across a wide range of instance scales demonstrate that QVHEA outperforms several representative state-of-the-art algorithms, while statistical tests and ablation analyses further validate its effectiveness and key design components. Overall, this study establishes an integrated modeling framework for coordinated recycling routing and disassembly line scheduling and provides decision-support and managerial implications for improving cross-stage synchronization and resource utilization in recycling and remanufacturing operations.

title: Economic behaviors of generation companies at higher penetration of renewables under different market concentrations
abstract: Increased penetration of renewables has posed a significant influence on the wholesale electricity market. For markets with a limited number of large generation companies, such as China, the manner in which bidding strategies for these companies could impact system operation and pricing has not been investigated. This paper proposes a market gaming model to explore such impact. The model is based on a bi-level optimization problem to simulate the interaction between bidding strategies for generation companies and market clearing processes for system operators. A dynamic-gradient, active-set algorithm is developed to obtain an analytical solution for the proposed model. The model is applied to several regional power systems using real-world data. Results indicate that generation companies, under higher market concentration (less generation companies), have the incentive to withhold their available renewable generation in the bidding process to maximize revenue: renewables can be effectively curtailed with no physical constraint binding, at a high degree of market concentration under elevated renewable penetrations. With one generation company owning renewables, saturation occurs at 19% with 2 generation companies and curtailment starts at 50% with 12. When all have renewables, no saturation occurs even at 80% penetration. The issue would be mitigated by increasing the number of generation companies (lowering market concentration) and distributing the renewable capacities more evenly among these generation companies. The results could provide important input for the ongoing, trillion-dollar scale, power market reform in China.

title: Modeling time-resolved emission characteristics of VOCs from asphalt binder under thermal exposure
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted during asphalt pavement construction are an important yet insufficiently quantified source of urban air pollution due to the lack of time-resolved emission models. This study develops a physically interpretable emission rate model to describe the nonlinear temporal evolution of VOCs release from asphalt binders under film-state thermal exposure. The model captures both early rapid release and subsequent decay and provides a closed-form solution for cumulative emission estimation. Laboratory experiments conducted at 120-180 °C were used for model calibration and validation. Predicted cumulative emissions showed excellent agreement with measurements (R2 ≥ 0.985) for both neat and SBS-modified binders. The model requires only time and temperature as inputs, enabling practical application in emission factor development, exposure assessment, and life-cycle environmental evaluation of pavement construction. This work provides a scalable and physically grounded framework for quantifying asphalt-based VOCs emissions.

title: Incision geometry as a controlling parameter for cleaner oleoresin harvesting: wound recovery dynamics and resource efficiency in Pinus roxburghii
abstract: The cleaner production of bio-based materials requires extraction technologies that minimize biological damage while maintaining long-term resource productivity. Oleoresin tapping in pine forests represents a repeated biomass extraction process in which incision design strongly influences recovery efficiency and cumulative yield. This study evaluates the role of incision geometry as a cleaner production lever in oleoresin harvesting by comparing Borehole and Rill tapping methods in Pinus roxburghii under different chemical stimulation regimes and application intervals. Wound recovery was assessed one year after tapping using callus formation and percentage wound occlusion as indicators of biological disturbance and recovery efficiency. Borehole incisions exhibited substantially higher healing rates than Rill blazes, with incision geometry explaining the largest proportion of variation in wound recovery (η2 ≈ 0.78), however, this estimate is derived from pooled interval-wise models under field constraints and should be interpreted as an approximate indicator of relative effect size rather than a precise global partition. Near-complete wound closure (up to 96.25%) was achieved under localized incision Borehole tapping, whereas Rill incisions showed persistently low healing irrespective of treatment. Excessive stimulation frequency impeded recovery, indicating that chemical intensity cannot compensate for unfavourable incision geometry. Anatomical observations confirmed effective compartmentalization and localized cambial regeneration in Borehole wounds. The results demonstrate that appropriate incision design can support low-damage oleoresin extraction by enhancing recovery efficiency and reducing immediate biological disturbance, while suggesting potential for improved long-term bioresource productivity that requires confirmation through multi-year studies.

title: Life cycle assessment of carbonated recycled concrete fine products
abstract: Carbonation of recycled concrete fines (RCF) offers a dual benefit of CO2 sequestration and construction waste recycling. However, systematic assessments of the environmental and the economic performance of RCF remain limited. A “cradle-to-gate” life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to compare the environmental impact of two production methods for concrete blocks, namely (1) conventional casting of concrete blocks incorporating 30% RCF, and (2) compaction combined with CO2 curing of concrete blocks made of 100% RCF. Compared with blocks made of 100% Portland cement, both methods resulted in a significant reduction in CO2 emissions (27.68-100.75%, including net-negative emissions), energy consumption (19.61-67.38%), and production cost (8.95-30.47%). The preparation and transportation of raw materials, particularly recycled concrete fines and aggregates, have contribute the most to both environmental impact and total cost. CO2 curing enabled compacted blocks to achieve the lowest LCA indicator, with a net-negative emission of −1.50 kg CO2/t. However, longer CO2 curing to reach higher carbonation degree, particularly when using commercially supplied CO2, significantly increased the overall CO2 emissions, energy demand, and cost.

title: Endogenous organic matter of anaerobic sludge as a recyclable carbon source for anammox process: in situ enrichment and ingredient differences
abstract: Securing sufficient organic carbon is a critical challenge for sustainable nitrogen removal from wastewater, with external carbon sources (e.g., sodium acetate, >300 USD per ton) contributing ∼20% of direct operational costs. This study evaluated the feasibility of using partial endogenous organic matter (EOM) derived from wastewater sludge as a recyclable carbon source for biological nitrogen removal. Two lab-scale reactors were operated for 150 days with in situ addition of nitrate (NO3−) or nitrite (NO2−) to differentiate their oxidative properties to selectively enrich partial EOM and the associated microbial consortia. Results indicated that partial EOM accounted for ∼70% of the total EOM, while the anammox process contributed to ∼20% removal of the endogenous released NH4+. 15N isotope tracing results confirmed that anammox accounted for 5.7% of total nitrogen removal. GC–MS analysis identified n-hexane as a key component of the partial EOM. These findings demonstrate that partial EOM from sludge can be harnessed as an economical and recyclable carbon source, offering a sustainable pathway for sludge recycling and enhancing biological nitrogen removal in wastewater treatment systems.

title: Are Italian farms achieving water-use efficiency in agriculture? Meta-frontier DEA analysis of efficiency gaps and farm-level disparities
abstract: An analysis of irrigation efficiency in Italy is essential to manage increasing water scarcity while sustaining agricultural productivity and informing targeted policy interventions. Using Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data for 2018–2023 (700 farms across seven types of farming), we implement a two-step DEA framework (DEA–Tobit) with meta-frontier decomposition to estimate water-use efficiency (WUE), implied water-saving potentials, and technology gaps, and to examine farm- and context-specific determinants of WUE. Results indicate low average WUE and substantial heterogeneity across types of farming: horticulture shows the highest efficiency, whereas grazing livestock and mixed crop–livestock farms perform worst. Meta-frontier results reveal that inefficiencies reflect both technological shortfalls and managerial inefficiencies, with permanent crops exhibiting the largest technology gap. Tobit estimates suggest that higher water prices and micro-irrigation adoption are positively associated with WUE, while smaller economic scale and southern location correlate negatively. Overall, the findings support policy mixes combining demand-side instruments (e.g., volumetric pricing) with targeted technology diffusion and capacity building—particularly in water-stressed southern areas—and provide empirically grounded benchmarks for future modelling, scenario analysis, and policy design to improve agricultural water productivity.

title: Wet milled municipal solid waste incineration fly ash: reagent free immobilization of heavy metals and evaluation as a low carbon supplementary cementitious material
abstract: The immobilization of heavy metals in municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) fly ash is a critical prerequisite for its safe disposal and resource utilization. Current heavy metal stabilization of MSWI fly ash typically relies on the addition of chelating agents, which not only incurs high costs but also restricts subsequent resource utilization. In this study, ettringite was successfully induced in MSWI fly ash through wet ball milling within a short treatment duration of 2 h and without the addition of any chemical reagents. By comparing the effects of water soaking, alkali soaking, and wet milling pretreatments on the physicochemical properties of MSWI fly ash, the specific reaction products responsible for immobilizing each heavy metal species were identified. The results showed that wet milling for 2 h induced the reprecipitation of calcium, sulfur, and aluminum, released from calcium sulfate and feldspar in the MSWI fly ash, under inherently alkaline conditions, forming precipitates dominated by ettringite with minor C-S-H/C-A-S-H, and effectively immobilizing specific heavy metals. A comparison with the C-S-H/C-A-S-H precipitates generated during alkali soaking revealed that heavy metal immobilization in MSWI fly ash is selective: Hg, Cd, Cr, and Pb preferentially stabilize within the ettringite, whereas As tends to be incorporated into C-S-H/C-A-S-H gels. The superior performance of wet ball milling was attributed to its ability to fracture particles and activate the aluminosilicate structure, leading to the highest Ca(OH)2 consumption and accelerated leaching of Ca, Si, and Al species. Overall, this work presents a reagent-free approach for heavy metal stabilization, improving MSWI fly ash utilization as a low carbon binder and offering a new direction toward zero-waste, sustainable urban development.

title: Toward a carbon-neutral and stable forest supply chain: A spatiotemporal log yard allocation model via multi-objective optimization
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality while ensuring a stable timber supply represents a critical challenge for sustainable forest management, particularly in regions with fragmented forest ownership and unbalanced age structures. While previous studies have addressed individual optimization components, the lack of spatially coordinated logistics infrastructure often leads to supply instability and inefficient forest utilization. Consequently, an integrated framework that simultaneously considers spatiotemporal allocation, long-term forest dynamics, and multi-dimensional sustainability objectives remains absent. To bridge this gap, a multi-objective optimization framework was developed for strategic log yard allocation in the Nishikawa region, Japan. A novel flow model is developed that simulates directional timber movement based on terrain and road network conditions to systematically identify candidate sites. This model is integrated with stand aggregation and harvesting scheduling to optimize economic efficiency, environmental performance, and supply stability using NSGA-II over 30- and 60-year horizons. Results show transportation costs are reduced by nearly 20%. Regarding environmental impact, a positive annual CO2 balance is maintained at 6632 t/year for the 30-year horizon and 7701 t/year for the 60-year horizon. Furthermore, daily supply stability consistently exceeds 90% for both periods, with the 60-year horizon demonstrating superior outcomes in balancing carbon sequestration and timber reliability. This research advances forest operations by integrating spatiotemporal dynamics with multi-objective optimization in a unified framework. Practically, it provides actionable strategies for forest managers to establish regional circular bioeconomy systems, directly contributing to Sustainable Development Goals and national carbon neutrality targets.

title: Geospatial machine learning for benzene estimation in an environmentally disadvantaged area: Snapshot air quality assessment of Joppa community, Dallas, Texas
abstract: The Joppa Community in Dallas, Texas, is located in a heavily polluted area which poses substantial health risks to local residents. Surrounded by dense industrial zones, the community potentially faces worsening health issues, exacerbating environmental and social disparities. These conditions underscore the urgent need for targeted environmental interventions to assess ambient air quality concerns. The present study aimed to estimate benzene, identified as a hazardous pollutant, in the environmentally disadvantaged community of Joppa. An integrated approach combining geospatial-based methods with advanced machine learning algorithms was utilized to develop a stacking ensemble learning model for benzene estimation. Rapid measurements of benzene and meteorological factors were conducted to provide a snapshot of air quality in the study area. Potential predictors contributing to benzene emissions were also gathered and processed using geospatial-based approaches. Several machine-learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), and CatBoost (CB), were developed and subsequently integrated to establish a stacking ensemble learning model. Validation procedures were conducted to ensure model reliability. The result found that the proposed model accounts for approximately 96.3% of the spatial variability in benzene levels (R2 = 0.963, RMSE = 0.023 ppb). Several key predictors contributing to benzene were identified, including developed intensity area, residential activities, temperature, and traffics. Further, spatial analytics revealed that benzene levels were elevated in asphalt plants adjacent to residential areas. This study provided preliminary insights into localized air quality concerns, emphasizing the need for continued investigation and increased attention to pollution-related health risks by relevant authorities.

title: Constrained aggregated approach for charging station using federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
abstract: With the rising demand for Electric Vehicles (EVs), a coordinated Demand Response (DR) enabled framework is required to maintain grid stability and optimize energy consumption. Optimizing the charging demand at the Charging Station (CS) by managing resources is key to effective energy management. In this paper, we propose the Federated Learning Constrained Deep Reinforcement Learning (FLCDRL) framework, where each station acts as a local agent to optimize the schedule by following a local safety layer and periodically updates the central aggregator for the updated global schedule. For pricing, dynamic, market-driven coordination between agents is developed for energy bids and flexibility responses from/to the station and the Distributed System Operator (DSO) levels. Furthermore, the feeder voltages are managed by the safety layer in the Reinforcement Learning (RL) model, enabling the local agent to learn autonomously and contribute to global consensus through a voltage-balancing policy. Simulation results demonstrate that the federated TD3 agent effectively shifts EV demands to off-peak hours, minimizing operational costs while maintaining grid security. The proposed privacy-preserving framework validates multi-station EV charging scheduling, improving State of Charge (SOC) satisfaction by approximately 8.3% compared to other methods while preserving voltage limits and ensuring fair provisioning across different scenarios. It exhibits robustness and fair allocation by utilising unmet, Time Of Use (TOU), and federated model comparisons, ensuring compliance with SOC demand by EVs. The future framework focuses on uncertainty-aware coordination with Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and dynamic pricing mechanisms for resilient operation.

title: Palladium recovery from wastewater using electric field-enhanced ultrafiltration assisted with polyethyleneimine and electro-decomplexation/electrodeposition
abstract: Palladium (Pd), a precious metal with extensive industrial applications, poses challenges of environmental risks and resource loss when it is present in wastewater. An integrated process combining polyethyleneimine (PEI) complexation capture, electric field-enhanced ultrafiltration, and electrochemical recovery for the efficient recovery of Pd from aqueous solutions was developed. Through polyelectrolyte-surfactant aggregates (PSAs), conductometric titration, and spectroscopic analysis, the optimal complexation ratio between the amine moiety of PEI and Pd2+ was determined to be 4:1. The process achieved a Pd2+ removal efficiency of 98.3% at pH 5 and maintained a high efficiency of approximately 70% even under strongly acidic conditions (e.g., pH 1). In multi-metal systems, PEI exhibited the highest selectivity toward Pd2+ among the tested metal ions. This preferential removal is attributed to the stronger coordination affinity between Pd2+ and the amine functional groups of PEI. To mitigate membrane fouling, the application of a +0.4 V voltage was found to effectively suppress surface deposition and flux decay. Furthermore, when treating a real-world acidic electroless plating wastewater (pH ≈ 2.1), adjusting the PEI dosage under a +0.4 V voltage still achieved approximately 76% Pd2+ removal. Optimal performance, i.e., up to 91.1% Pd recovery, in the final electrochemical recovery step was achieved at a constant current density of 20 A/m2 using an acidic chloride system (pH 1, HCl) with a graphite cathode. This is attributed to the synergistic effect of protonation, Cl− complex with Pd and chlorine oxidation due to the high concentration of H+ and Cl− in the PEI-Pd electrolyte, which promotes the dissociation of the PEI-Pd complex and facilitates the reductive deposition of Pd. An initial economic assessment based on a lab-scale case study calculated the direct operating cost to be approximately $6.83 per gram of recovered Pd, confirming the strong economic potential of this integrated approach.

title: Framework integrating supplier-level social and environmental risk assessment with global supply-chain tracing and impact analysis for early-stage supplier selection
abstract: Global supply-chains continually struggle to align supplier practices with ESG targets. Raising awareness encourages OEMs to adopt sustainable materials, introducing new suppliers into the supply-chain. In practice, early-stage supplier selection—defined here as the pre-contractual and early onboarding phase before full audits and longitudinal performance data are available— often lacks reliable ways to identify both direct supplier risks as well as indirect upstream-tier impacts due to limited data, fragmented indicators, and inconsistent governance standards. This gap is acute in industries with complex, multi-tier networks such as automotive manufacturing. This gap is addressed by proposing a novel framework, Probabilistic Interaction-Driven Social Impact Assessment (PID-SIA), which translates limited self-assessment data into probabilistic performance distributions, incorporates interdependencies through an Interaction Adjustment Model, and flags inconsistencies using an Early Warning Index. The method is integrated with a streamlined Multi-Regional Input-Output (MRIO)-based hotspot analysis that quantifies indirect sustainability risks across global tiers, hence providing a dual-perspective diagnosis. Application to a Spanish wood-based vegan-leather supplier classifies the supplier as moderate risk at the direct level, while integrated supplier–supply-chain assessment yields an overall risk score of 50.6/100, driven by upstream governance and sourcing hotspots in China, India, and Italy, linking localized supplier data to global supply-chain exposures. By integrating probabilistic scoring with multi-regional tracing, the framework enhances early-stage decision-making, supports targeted supplier evaluation and selection, and provides actionable pathways toward sustainable supply-chains. The approach advances social and environmental measurement, offering a reproducible foundation for broader validation in future studies.

title: Substitutes or complements? How industrial symbiosis and intermediaries relate to the adoption of circular economy practices in SMEs
abstract: Industrial symbiosis and circular-economy intermediaries are both regarded as meso-level enablers of the adoption of circular practices, yet their interaction remains poorly understood. This study examines whether these mechanisms function as complements or substitutes in their association with circular-economy adoption and firm performance among SMEs. We combine firm-level survey data from 4550 SMEs across the 27 European Union member states plus the UK with a novel dataset on country-sector presence, comprising 42 operational industrial symbiosis networks and 40 circular-economy-oriented intermediaries. Using multi-group path analysis, we find that the presence of intermediaries is positively associated with circular-economy adoption only in contexts without an industrial symbiosis network, whereas their influence in IS-present contexts is negligible. Performance gains from circular economy adoption are statistically indistinguishable between contexts with and without industrial symbiosis, suggesting that strong intermediary support can offset the absence of network infrastructure. These findings challenge assumptions of unconditional complementarity between meso-level enablers and are consistent with a diminishing marginal role of intermediation where symbiotic infrastructures are already in place. The results imply that targeted investment in intermediaries may help foster the uptake of the circular economy in IS-absent contexts. At the same time, in IS-present contexts, resources may be better directed toward deepening exchanges and enhancing shared infrastructure. For policy, the findings suggest prioritizing intermediary capacity-building where IS networks are absent, while complementing IS-present contexts with actions that deepen exchanges and shared infrastructure rather than duplicating brokerage functions.

title: Recyclable thermoset polyurethane adhesives based on thermoreversible DA-adducts for wood and metal substrates
abstract: Designing recyclable high-performance thermoset adhesives remains a key challenge in sustainable materials science. In this work, a series of partially biobased, highly crosslinked polyurethane networks were synthesized incorporating varying amounts of a trifunctional Diels-Alder (DA) adduct as thermoreversible crosslinks to enable recyclability. Thermal and rheological analyses confirmed their recycling potential via retro-DA bond dissociation. However, at elevated temperatures required for reprocessing, undesired side reactions (maleimide homopolymerization) led to irreversible crosslinking. To address this issue, a radical scavenger, p -benzoquinone, was incorporated into the formulations to suppress free-radical side reactions, effectively extending the operational recycling window by 15 to 20 °C. The resulting DA-based polyurethanes exhibit robust mechanical performance (flexural modulus up to 3.1 GPa) and excellent adhesion to both untreated metal and wood substrates, with lap-shear strengths of 4.1 MPa on metal and 1.6 MPa on wood. Multiple debonding/rebonding cycles demonstrated high joint integrity, with failure occurring predominantly within the adhesive layer (cohesive failure), indicating strong interfacial adhesion. These findings highlight a promising strategy to balance the end-of-life reusability in thermoset adhesive systems within the constraints imposed by the high glass transition temperatura associated with enhanced structural performance, thereby contributing to improved value retention in polymer-based bonding technologies.

title: Federated reinforcement learning-based dynamic hosting domain for electric vehicles charging management in distribution networks with renewable energy resources
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and electric vehicles (EVs) introduces considerable uncertainty into distribution networks, where renewable intermittency and uncoordinated charging can cause voltage violations, congestion, and reduced hosting capability. Conventional static assessment methods, based on fixed operating assumptions, fail to capture the spatiotemporal interactions induced by renewable variability and aggregated charging demand under network constraints. To address these challenges, this study proposes a dynamic hosting domain (DHD) framework based on reinforcement learning. The DHD defines the time-varying feasible region of system states, providing a quantitative representation of admissible operating boundaries with explicit physical safety guarantees. It adapts to spatiotemporal charging variations and incorporates a margin-based index for hosting capacity evaluation. A station-level delay perception model is embedded into the reward design to account for aggregated service-quality constraints as macroscopic economic feedback, discouraging excessive charging postponement while preserving operational feasibility at the system level. Furthermore, a federated reinforcement learning architecture based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) enables collaborative policy learning among multiple charging stations without raw data sharing, thereby enhancing scalability, privacy preservation, and spatiotemporal coordination under non-IID conditions. Case studies on renewable-integrated distribution networks demonstrate faster convergence, enhanced voltage stability, and lower operational costs compared with benchmarks. The proposed DHD framework offers a unified pathway for secure, efficient, and behavior-aware EV charging management in renewable-energy-integrated systems.

title: Seasonal dynamics of aqueous phase from hydrothermal carbonization of waste activated sludge: Unraveling composition, ecological risks, and resource opportunities
abstract: Waste activated sludge (WAS), a major by-product of municipal wastewater treatment, is valorized via hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) to produce carbonization liquid (CL), a key resource-oriented product. However, the linkages between seasonal WAS property variations and CL composition remain unclear, restricting in-depth understanding of CL's environmental risks and safe resource recovery. This study explored the impacts of summer–winter WAS variations on CL composition, clarified substrate-driven CL formation patterns, evaluated CL's biological effects on plants, aquatic organisms, and anaerobic microbes, defined safety thresholds, and proposed targeted graded treatment strategies. Results showed winter CL (WCL) contained 428 organic species (enriched in phenols and N-heterocyclic compounds) with high ecological risks (Potential Ecological Risk Index = 583.43; Pollution Loading Index = 6.56), a safe concentration ≤1% (v/v) for wheat root growth and anaerobic microbes, and a 96 h-LC50 of 9.69 mg/L for zebrafish embryos. Summer CL (SCL) had significantly lower toxic organic content (phenol content = 33% of WCL), high nutrient bioavailability, and low ecological risk compared with WCL. An integrated framework linking seasonal variations, WAS composition, CL properties, and ecological risk effects was established, with graded strategies: precise toxic control for WCL and simplified high-proportion utilization for SCL. This study fills the research gap of seasonal substrate impacts on HTC-derived CL, providing scientific support for CL's risk management and safe resource recovery.

title: Sustainable management of plateau mountainous urban agglomerations based on the ecosystem services supply-demand balance: Application of scale and threshold effects
abstract: Applying ecosystem services (ES) supply-demand balance thresholds effectively supports the refinement of urban agglomerations and multiscale spatial governance. This study takes the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration (CYUA) as the study zone and constructs a research framework of “clustering zoning-threshold-spatial management”. First, we quantify six ES supply-demand balance and classify spatial ES supply-demand bundles (ESDRBs), which are subsequently mapped and zoned. Next, we apply XGBoost and constraint line models to identify the principal drivers of ES supply-demand balance and to estimate interaction thresholds among these drivers. Finally, multi-scale spatial zoning management is implemented based on the threshold. The results show that: (1) Based on the functional characteristics and distribution features of the five ESDRBs at three scales, the CYUA is divided into ecological improvement zones, comprehensive ecological conservation zones, composite functional zones, ecological restoration zones, and urban core zones. (2) Across three scales, nighttime light intensity, population density, and distance to building land are identified as the principal drivers of ES supply-demand balance. Changes in scale do not change the direction of the effects exerted by these drivers on ES supply-demand balance; however, the threshold values associated with balance responses differ markedly among scales. (3) Regarding zoning management, the grid scale requires refined, localized interventions, whereas township and county scale management should prioritize alignment with administrative responsibilities and governance functions. Therefore, to sustain the long-term ES supply-demand balance in urban agglomerations, we propose threshold informed, targeted multiscale spatial management strategies that provide a scientific basis for sustainable urbanagglomeration management.

title: Life-cycle carbon footprints of rural toilet systems in China: Hotspot diagnosis and mitigation pathways
abstract: China’s rural toilet reform has advanced rapidly, yet the life-cycle carbon footprints of typical systems remain insufficiently quantified. In this study, each toilet system was partitioned into four functional modules, and the carbon emissions during construction and operation were evaluated using IPCC emission-factor methods. During construction, emissions from the toilet facility module dominate (64.05–76.35%), mainly due to carbon-intensive materials such as sintered fly-ash bricks and cement mortar, followed by transport (19.6–26.2%). Structural light-weighting and prefabrication can reduce construction emissions by up to 55.96%. During operation, CH4 and N2O from sanitation treatment account for 45.40–88.89% of operation-phase emissions. Notably, resource recovery in the eco-environmental module offsets 10.66–53.67%, turning the centralized treatment system from a net carbon source (315.03 kg CO2-eq/unit) into a net carbon sink (−23.25 kg CO2-eq/unit). This study proposes module-level optimization and resource-recovery strategies to support low-carbon toilet design in developing regions.

title: Electro-activation of peroxymonosulfate for degradation of doxycycline using Cu-activated carbon fiber recovered from Cu-containing wastewater
abstract: Excessive discharge of copper-containing electroplating wastewater and the widespread misuse of antibiotics pose serious risks to human health and the environment. Herein, an innovative electrochemical closed-loop system was proposed, in which copper-loaded activated carbon fibers (Cu-ACF) were recovered via electrodeposition from Cu-containing wastewater and subsequently employed as cathode to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for doxycycline (DOX) degradation. At an applied potential of −1.1 V, the Cu2+ deposition capacity reached 729.9 mg⋅g−1. Copper species were mainly present as Cu2+ together with Cu0/Cu+ species on the ACF surface, providing active sites for electron transfer and enhancing PMS activation. Under optimal conditions, more than 95% of DOX was removed within 60 min, exhibiting a pseudo-first-order rate constant about twice that of blank ACF. Cu-ACF1 also showed good reusability, retaining 85.1% removal efficiency after five cycles. Electrochemical analyses demonstrated that Cu-ACF exhibited enhanced catalytic current response and interfacial activity compared to blank ACF, favoring PMS activation. Multiple reactive oxygen species were identified in the system, with •O2− identified as the dominant contributor, while 1O2 from a non-radical pathway served as the secondary species. In addition, DOX can be degraded via three pathways, generating 19 intermediate products, most of which exhibit low toxicity. This work provides a sustainable strategy that simultaneously enables copper recovery and efficient antibiotic removal, offering dual benefits for resource recycling and environmental protection.

title: The impact of intelligent development in manufacturing on carbon emissions: Evidence from China
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence(AI) is profoundly reshaping firms' development patterns and transformation pathways. Based on data on China's A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2011 to 2022, this research employs fixed-effects ordinary least squares (FE-OLS), instrumental variable methods, and a difference-in-differences model (DID) to examine the impact of intelligent development in manufacturing on carbon emissions. The study reveals that intelligent development in manufacturing enterprises significantly reduces carbon emissions, particularly demonstrating more pronounced effects in state-owned enterprises (SOEs), large enterprises, high-tech firms, non-strategic emerging industries (non-SEIs), and heavily polluting enterprises. Mechanism analysis indicates that intelligent development contributes to emission reduction through facilitating green technological innovation (GTI) and streamlining resource allocation efficiency. This research enriches the literature on intelligent manufacturing's environmental impacts and provides empirical insights that have policy implications for advancing intelligent transformation and fostering low-carbon growth within the manufacturing industry.

title: The cloud has wires: Toward circular governance of smart grids
abstract: Smart grids are widely promoted as efficient, low-carbon solutions for energy transitions, yet their governance often treats digital infrastructure as immaterial and uniformly beneficial. This obscures the material, temporal, and justice dimensions that shape real-world outcomes. We introduce Circular Grid Governance (CGG), a framework that integrates circular-economy principles, lifecycle thinking, and energy justice, and apply it to Sweden's smart-grid development. Organized around three analytical layers (material–temporal, social, institutional), we compare 26 consultant reports with 19 interviews across public, private, and research sectors. Consultant reports emphasize digital optimization and system efficiency, while practitioners foreground mineral dependencies, depreciation-driven asset turnover, digital exclusion, and fragmented coordination. Two central governance priorities emerge. First, lifecycle synchronization: aligning regulatory, financial, and technical lifetimes to avoid premature replacement of still-functional assets. Second, equity- and circularity-by-design: embedding affordability, access, procedural safeguards, and circular requirements into rules, procurement, and program design from the outset. We identify actionable governance levers, including depreciation reform, circular procurement and reuse certification, and renter-inclusive participation. CGG offers a practical lens for steering digital energy transitions toward material durability, social inclusion, and institutional integration. Grounded in Swedish evidence, the framework is advanced as an adaptable heuristic for other digitalizing infrastructures. • Introduction of Circular Grid Governance framework for sustainable smart energy systems. • Integration of circular economy, lifecycle, and energy justice frameworks. • Reveals material, temporal, and equity gaps in Swedish smart-grid governance. • Proposes lifecycle synchronization and circular procurement reforms. • Offers actionable levers for durable, inclusive digital energy transitions

title: Network-enabled dynamic modeling unveils divergent land-carbon futures and governance pathways in a megaregion
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality in rapidly urbanizing megaregions is critically dependent on land use dynamics. However, conventional assessments, often reliant on static carbon coefficients, fail to capture the dynamic feedback and complex interactions within the land-carbon system, leading to significant policy blind spots. Here, we introduce a novel modeling framework that dynamically couples future land use simulation with process-based carbon sequestration and stochastic emission projections under multiple SSP-RCP scenarios. In addition, we integrate Ecological Network Analysis (ENA) to quantify the hidden flow chains and utility relationships between land types that govern the system's carbon metabolism. Applied to China's Pearl River Delta, our results uncover a persistent and dominant “ecological → cropland → construction" land transition pathway, which creates unidirectional carbon flow chains leading to substantial carbon loss. A key finding is a projected precipitous decline in regional carbon sequestration capacity post-2040, driven by ecological land degradation and forest aging, which could severely undermine long-term carbon neutrality goals. ENA further reveals that the land system is dominated by competitive and exploitative relationships, with urban expansion in core cities making them entrenched net carbon sources. Conversely, peripheral cities, serving as the region's ecological backbone, retain over 80% of the regional carbon sequestration. Our analysis demonstrates that the integration of dynamic simulation with ENA provides an unprecedented lens to diagnose the structural and relational drivers of carbon metabolism. This framework offers a generalizable tool for unraveling the complex land-carbon nexus in other urbanizing regions worldwide.

title: From molecular ferroptosis to ecosystem recovery: A metal-driven temporal ecological switch as a hidden node of wetland resilience
abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has been widely studied in biomedical contexts but remains poorly understood as an ecological process. Here, we identify ferroptosis as a threshold-mediated ecological switch that governs stability and functional transitions in wetland ecosystems. Using an integrated experimental framework combining molecular assays, metagenomics, and functional analyses, we discovered a critical Fe2+ threshold (18.53 mg L−1) that initiated ferroptosis-specific oxidative damage within earthworm gut microbiota. This molecular activation triggered the depletion of Geobacter and expansion of Desulfovibrio, disrupting electron-transfer networks and nitrogen removal performance. Through multi-omics and network analyses, we identified a progressive ferroptosis trajectory that advances through trigger, execution, and recovery stages. This process featured glutathione suppression, enhanced iron and sulfur coupling, and decreased microbial modularity. Breakpoint regression and machine-learning validation confirmed that Fe2+ accumulation acts as the initiating driver, ferroptosis as the mechanistic mediator, and microbial dysfunction as the proximate cause of ecosystem instability. Collectively, our findings establish ferroptosis as a metal-induced, cross-scale transition mechanism that links molecular oxidative stress to community restructuring and ecosystem functional collapse. This study provides a mechanistic framework for predicting and managing threshold-driven regime shifts in metal-stressed ecological systems.

title: Design-for-Disassembly Principles for Apartment Blocks – Experimental Design in a Finnish Housing Project
abstract: Researchers in the building sector are discussing design-for-disassembly as a concept to reduce the environmental impact of the construction sector in the long term. The term design-for-disassembly refers to practices used in new construction to increase the likelihood of the reuse of building components in the end-of-life phase. Academia and practice have suggested guidelines or principles for design-for-disassembly, while there is little knowledge of their practical implications. Based on the guidelines in the literature, this study focuses on developing tangible architectural and structural planning solutions and assessing their potential to improve the reuse potential of a building. The study uses the research-by-design approach in a case study when modifying an existing design of a Finnish apartment building in collaboration with the client. The indicators of reuse potential tested and developed in this study are reuse rate, simplicity, and standardization. The result shows that avoiding architectural and structural planning solutions that require monolithic structures, designing divergent functions as independent systems, and centralizing shafts for building services are effective ways to create conditions for maximizing reuse, simplicity, and standardization in load-bearing structures. These practices caused no significant limitations to architectural and structural planning. Further research is needed to develop comprehensive and practical DfD performance metrics, apply them in different contexts, test and validate reversible structural joints, implement design-for-disassembly principles in exterior walls, and analyze the economic feasibility of the concept.

title: A dynamic dissolution non-equilibrium mass transfer model for simulating CO2 migration in groundwater and its application in CO2-EOR project
abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) geological sequestration can mitigate emission effective but risks leakage of CO2 into shallow groundwater system. Consequently, timely monitoring of CO2 leakage into shallow groundwater is imperative. Due to the absence of accurate groundwater migration simulation to address leaked CO2 dispersion in groundwater driven by complex hydrogeological processes and hydrodynamic forces, it is a challenge to design a least-cost optimal monitoring scheme for ensuring environmental safety of shallow groundwater. This study presents a non-equilibrium mass transfer model based on dynamic dissolution process for simulating CO2 migration in shallow groundwater. The model is developed by formulating dynamic dissolution mass transfer coefficient equation, coupled with mass and momentum conservation equations for gas-liquid two-phase flow. An enhanced non-equilibrium dissolution mass transfer model solver (nEqMTFoam) is implemented within OpenFOAM platform, enabling efficient solution algorithm of the model. The simulation model can effectively reflect the influence mechanism of non-equilibrium dissolution process on CO2 migration under complex hydrodynamic conditions in shallow groundwater. Application to a CO2-EOR (CO2-Enhanced Oil Recovery) case study at SINOPEC Shengli Oilfield demonstrates that the model is capable of predicting spatial distributions of both gas phase and dissolved-phase CO2 in shallow groundwater to provide a robust decision support for design of shallow groundwater monitoring system.

title: Optimization of reversible solid oxide fuel cells for enhanced dual-mode operation: a multi-objective approach using NSGA-II algorithm
abstract: Reversible solid oxide fuel cells (rSOCs) enable bidirectional power-to-fuel and fuel-to-power conversion, making them a promising technology for renewable energy storage and grid regulation. However, most existing studies rely on single-objective or single-parameter optimization approaches, which are insufficient to capture the coupled effects of multiple operating parameters on dual-mode performance. To addresse this limitation, a dual-mode steady-state rSOC operation model was developed based on the Aspen Plus simulation platform. Orthogonal experimental design combined with analysis of variance was employed to identify the key decision variables influencing system performance. Meanwhile, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was then employed to simultaneously optimize the total active area of the stack and overall system efficiency, generating a set of Pareto-optimal solutions. The results demonstrate a strong coupling between rSOC performance and operating conditions. In SOFC mode, increasing the H2 concentration from 50% to 70% expands the optimal stack area from 1.1 m2 to 1.52 m2 and improves system efficiency from 52.5% to 66.4%. Moreover, coordinated adjustment of key decision variables enables high-performance operation across both SOFC and SOEC modes. This work advances the application of multi-objective optimization in rSOC systems and provides theoretical insights for enhancing their dual-mode performance.

title: Leapfrogging inequality? Navigating a pathway to cleaner energy in rural Ghana
abstract: Despite progress toward SDG7, many people in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) are projected to remain without access to clean energy by 2030 unless drastic measures are taken. Existing studies have largely focused on technological innovation in the Global North, producing a techno-centric bias that overlooks the complexities of energy access in non-Western contexts. This study addresses this gap by examining energy transitions in rural Ghana through the Political Ecology framework for Sustainable Energy Transition (PESET)—an integrated analytical model that synthesises energy justice, political ecology, and inclusive innovation. It provides novel empirical insights into how context-specific factors influence clean energy adoption and reinforce existing inequalities. Through a reflexive thematic analysis of 43 qualitative key informant interviews, the study reveals the multidimensional nature of energy transitions and challenges dominant techno-centric paradigms by demonstrating how structural inequalities and power asymmetries shape participation, access, and outcomes in the transition process. The analysis identifies four adoption barriers (cost, availability, behavioural resistance, and limited awareness), four forms of exclusion (process, consumption, impact, and structural), and three dimensions of energy injustice (distributive, recognition, and procedural) that intersect to constrain a sustainable transition. Building on these insights, the study proposes a holistic pathway to support a more equitable and sustainable energy transition, offering actionable policy guidance and contributing to progress toward SDG7 in rural Ghana. • Context-specific strategies are vital for a sustainable energy transition in SSA. • Technology-focused transitions risk reinforcing existing marginalisations • Current transition efforts in rural Ghana are marked by injustices and exclusions. • Governance, financial and regulatory realignments are vital for equitable transition. • Multi-level actors play significant role in transition processes and outcomes.

title: Greenwashing and firm performance in an emerging market: Short-term gains vs long-term risks
authors: Ana Beatriz Lopes de Sousa Jabbour
abstract: Amid increasing institutional pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, many firms have adopted sustainability-related communications without concrete actions, which can lead to perceived greenwashing. Taking into account this situation, this study extends the literature on greenwashing and neo-institutional theory by developing and testing a comprehensive model that examines both the antecedents and consequences of corporate greenwashing behavior in an emerging market. This study examines key antecedents of perceived greenwashing, namely: environmental attitude, environmental knowledge, stakeholder pressures and information asymmetry, as well as the implications for firms’ performance. Survey data from 268 managers of Kompas100-listed firms on the Stock Exchange of Indonesia were analyzed using partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM). The results show that environmental attitude and knowledge reduce perceived greenwashing, while stakeholder pressures and information asymmetry increase its likelihood. Notably, perceived greenwashing positively affects economic, environmental, and social performance in the short term. This study emphasizes the importance of highlighting the contextual setting of the research because emerging markets have institutional differences compared with developed economies.

title: Exploring UK consumer perceptions and willingness to adopt alternative wine packaging
abstract: Glass bottles are the dominant packaging format in the global wine industry yet are consistently recognised as a significant environmental burden due to their energy intensive production and contribution to transport emissions. Using alternative packaging mediums can significantly decrease the environmental impacts associated with wine packaging. Despite environmental advantages, consumer acceptance remains low. This study explores the attitudes of a UK sample towards alternative wine packaging. Despite the UK's status as one of the largest global wine-importing nations, its consumer base remains underexplored. An online survey targeting UK-based wine consumers (n = 153) assessed willingness to adopt alternative packaging and explored key factors influencing acceptance. Analyses identified four significant predictors of willingness: sustainability and price ratings increased likelihood of acceptance, while male gender and supermarket users were associated with resistance. Cluster analysis found willing participants were driven by environmental concern and price sensitivity. Amongst unwilling respondents, resistance varied between strong traditional preferences and unfamiliarity with alternatives. Re-evaluation prompts found 36.2–46.8% of resistant participants were open to reconsidering their stance under certain conditions, particularly lower environmental impact and cost. Results show 69.3% of respondents in this UK sample are willing to purchase wine in alternative packaging in stark contrast to results produced in wine producing regions. Findings suggest that the wine culture among this UK sample is less deeply embedded in traditional and cultural aspects of wine consumption, positioning it more favourably for the adoption of alternative packaging. • UK consumers show 69.3% willingness to adopt alternative wine packaging. • Sustainability and price strongly increase willingness to adopt new formats. • Male consumers and supermarket shoppers show lower acceptance of alternatives. • Cluster analysis reveals diverse motivations among willing and unwilling consumers. • UK's commercially driven wine culture supports higher acceptance of packaging innovation.

title: Tracking the pattern of material metabolism and environmental impacts of phosphogypsum utilization in China
abstract: The widespread use of fertilizers has led to the accumulation of large quantities of phosphogypsum (PG). Under the global consensus on circular economy and low-carbon development, the resource utilization of PG can replace the extraction of primary resources, and achieve synergetic benefits across multiple objectives. This study explores issues such as unclear baseline data, unknown material metabolism patterns, and insufficient environmental impact assessment (EIA) in solid waste management. A precise calculation model for PG generation based on the principles of physicochemical reactions has been established. The resource utilization rate in southwestern regions, represented by Guizhou, has risen annually yet remains comparatively low overall. Conversely, eastern cities such as Tongling have achieved over 100% utilization of PG, gradually addressing historical solid waste accumulations. From a full life cycle perspective, production of cement retarders from PG incurs the highest fossil resource consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. The manufacture of paper-faced gypsum boards poses the greatest human toxicity risk, while acid production coupled with cement manufacturing exerts the most significant toxic impact on acidification and aquatic ecosystems. The material metabolism and EIA framework, covering the entire production-utilization chain, can serve as a reference for the refined management of single-type solid wastes. The conclusions can provide methodological and data support for the global management of PG.

title: Enhanced bioremediation performance of Mn(Ⅱ) contamination in acidic wastewater by immobilized composite fungi on biochar
abstract: The treatment of manganese in acidic wastewater, such as acid mine drainage, remains a challenge due to the inefficiency of biological processes under extreme acidity. This study developed an immobilized system by encapsulating a composite of acid-tolerant fungi (Aspergillus sp. MF1 and Penicillium sp. MF3) within a sodium alginate and sesame straw biochar matrix (SC-CF). Under optimized conditions (2% sodium alginate (SA), 3.5% biochar (BC), 25% inoculum), SC-CF achieved 83.65% removal of Mn(II) from an initial solution of 50 mg/L at pH 3.0 within 7 days. The immobilized system initiated rapid Mn(II) removal two days earlier and reached completion faster than the free fungi. This enhanced performance was linked to a shift in fungal metabolism: SC-CF secreted markedly lower levels of organic acids (citric, oxalic, malic) and produced substantially more ammonium, coinciding with a rise in the environmental pH. Mechanistic investigations indicated that Mn(II) was sequestered primarily in the cell wall fraction and transformed into more stable chemical species, including oxalate-bound forms. This work demonstrates that the SA-biochar immobilization platform enhances fungal remediation of Mn(II) not merely by physical protection, but by creating a microenvironment that promotes a metabolically favorable shift, which is associated with more efficient Mn(II) removal. This work provides an efficient and sustainable strategy for acidic heavy metal remediation through the valorization of agricultural waste, and deepens the understanding of microbial metabolic Modulation via functional immobilization.
