title: Multifunctional additive-driven efficient critical metal recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries via all-solid-state subcritical process
abstract: The sustainable recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is crucial for ensuring resource security and minimizing environmental impact. To address this challenge, we developed an innovative all-solid-state (ASS) subcritical process using FeCl2·4H2O as a multifunctional reaction mediator. This method achieves near-quantitative recovery of valuable metals (99.9%) from LiNixCoyMnzO2 (NCM) cathode materials. In our process, spent NCM are directly mixed with solid FeCl2·4H2O and heated under controlled subcritical conditions. This initiates a rapid structural breakdown of the cathode material, facilitated by a synergistic redox reaction involving Fe2+ and in-situ generated HCl. As a result, the valuable metals are efficiently leached out in just 10 min, using an ultra-low amount of water (low liquid-solid ratio). Mechanistic investigations reveal a dual activation pathway: thermal hydrolysis of Fe2+ generating proton flux for lattice protonation, and chloride-assisted electron transfer inducing transition metal reduction. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations quantitatively demonstrate the synergistic effect of different components of FeCl2⋅4H2O in destabilizing the NCM lattice framework. This closed-loop process exhibits exceptional sustainability metrics, including zero acid consumption, significant energy reduction, and substantially reduced aqueous emissions. The methodology establishes a techno-economically viable paradigm for next-generation green battery recycling infrastructures.

title: Synergistic electrocatalytic-biological degradation of Ni-EDTA in a baffled three-dimensional reactor: Performance optimization and mechanism analysis
abstract: Ni-ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (Ni-EDTA) complexes pose significant challenges for sustainable wastewater treatment due to their stability and resistance to conventional removal methods. This study develops an integrated baffled three-dimensional electro-biological coupling reactor (BTD-EBR) as a sustainable solution for Ni-EDTA wastewater treatment, aligning with cleaner production principles by synergizing energy-efficient electrocatalysis with biological processes. The system synergized electrocatalysis (0.35 mA/cm2) with spatially segregated aerobic (•OH-mediated decomplexation) and anaerobic (Trichococcus-dominated biodegradation) zones, achieving removal efficiencies of 69.71% (Ni-EDTA), 93.76% (chemical oxygen demand, COD), and 94.43% (ammonium nitrogen, NH4+-N), outperforming controls (current density, CD = 0) by 56.25%, 13.50%, and 19.11%, respectively. Mechanistic analysis revealed aerobic zones contributed 34–46% efficiency via •OH/active chlorine oxidation, while anaerobic zones achieved 47–58% COD removal through hydrolysis. Compared to conventional Fenton processes, the BTD-EBR demonstrated 45% lower global warming potential (GWP), 70% sludge reduction, and operational cost savings of ¥1.5 perton. Microbial analysis revealed enrichment of Trichococcus, Nitrospira, and Hydrogenophaga, with metabolic pathways (e.g., citrate cycle, environmental metabolism) critical for Ni-EDTA breakdown. Electrochemical processes destabilized Ni-EDTA, while biofilms enhanced biosorption and biodegradation. This work provides a scalable, energy-efficient solution for refractory metal-organic wastewater treatment, aligning with circular economy principles.

title: Modified bentonite-catalyzed oxidation of typical odorous substances in wastewater: comparison of H2O2 and ClO2 systems and mechanism study
abstract: In recent years, industrial emissions and waste treatment have increasingly contributed to organic odour pollution, necessitating efficient degradation technologies for typical odorous substances like dimethyl disulfide, trichloroethylene, and p-xylene. This study innovatively employs acid- and iron-modified bentonite (Fe-H-Bent) as a catalyst to enhance the oxidation performance of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and chlorine dioxide (ClO2) systems, addressing the limitations of low oxidant utilization in conventional methods. By comparing degradation efficiencies, the Fe-H-Bent + ClO2 system demonstrated superior removal rates (99% for DMDS, 91% for TCE, and 87% for p-xylene under optimal conditions: catalyst-to-oxidant ratio of 1:2, 40 °C, pH = 3), attributed to its enhanced redox potential and catalytic active sites. Mechanistic investigations, combined with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and Fukui function calculations, revealed a dual oxidation pathway: hydroxyl radical (·OH)-mediated attack on methyl-adjacent sites of p-xylene and ClO2-driven electron transfer reactions on para-methyl positions, forming intermediates like 2,5-dimethylphenol and alkyl radicals. This work highlights the synergy between modified bentonite and ClO2, offering a novel, efficient strategy for odorous substance removal in wastewater treatment, with theoretical insights into radical- and electron-transfer co-oxidation mechanisms.

title: How does novel energy governance nurture Europe's energy transition and environmental safety? A long-difference and dose-response modeling approach
abstract: Encompassing both legislative design and executive implementation, energy governance has become a key instrument for accelerating the energy transition and strengthening environmental protection. This study investigates whether and how governance effectiveness influences Europe's energy transition and environmental outcomes, with a particular focus on their time-varying relationship. Employing the long-difference framework and dose-response function to address heterogeneity and endogeneity, the analysis reveals that stronger legislative and executive governance is associated with increased renewable energy capacity and reduced CO 2 emissions. However, these effects weaken or reverse during a medium-run transition phase, pointing to a nonlinear governance–outcome relationship. Likewise economic growth exhibits a nonlinear association with environmental degradation consistent with the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis. The findings collectively underscore our central argument that governance effectiveness exerts a nonlinear influence on the energy transition and that successful outcomes depend not only on the existence of legal frameworks but also, and more critically, on the credibility of their implementation. Strengthening both the legislative and executive dimensions of governance is, therefore, essential for advancing a low-carbon growth pathway in Europe.

title: Social sustainability competencies: a globally informed reference framework integrating non-Western and Western expert perspectives across all continents
abstract: Sustainability challenges, such as inequality and climate change, are urgent and intricate. Meaningful responses require deliberate and comprehensive preparation that aligns with both the nature and magnitude of these challenges. Recognizing the importance of identifying and fostering sustainability competencies to address complex sustainability challenges, scholars have increasingly explored these competencies, with a primary focus on multidimensional sustainability. While these efforts mark important progress, significant limitations remain in the existing literature. These include a predominant focus on Eurocentric contexts and expert perspectives, as well as the limited exploration of the social dimension of sustainability. The first limitation restricts the global relevance of competencies. Meanwhile, the underrepresentation of the social dimension hinders a deeper understanding of interrelationships among sustainability dimensions. We address these widely recognized limitations by involving experts from diverse sustainability fields and contexts of all continents in a two-round Delphi study, drawn from 52 and 48 countries, respectively. Through this comprehensive approach, we identified ten globally relevant and interdependent competencies, including systems thinking, social equity, and social activism competencies, relevant to promoting social sustainability. We also integrated the competencies into a unified framework. Based on diverse global voices, the study identifies competencies relevant across socioeconomic, cultural, and political contexts, expanding sustainability competencies literature on a global scale. By framing the often-overlooked concept of social sustainability through a competence lens, the study enriches discourse on interdependencies among sustainability dimensions. Additionally, it offers policy insights for global sustainability and contributes to initiatives including corporate social responsibility and education for sustainable development.

title: Recycled copper and V2G accelerate carbon neutrality in China: Decoupling power and passenger vehicle sectors from copper constraints
abstract: The power and passenger vehicle sectors are critical to the energy transition. Under carbon neutrality targets, the energy transition in these two sectors is heavily dependent on stable supply of copper. However, the existing copper supply may serve as a critical constraint. This study integrates Dynamic Material Flow Analysis and linear programming model to quantify the impacts of copper constraints on carbon mitigation in power and passenger vehicle sectors during 2023-2060, and further assess the carbon mitigation potentials of enhancing recycling and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) adoption. The results show that: 1) China's energy transition in the power and passenger vehicle sectors will generate a cumulative copper supply shortage of 21.9 Mt; 2) Copper constraints significantly curb renewable energy and new energy vehicle (NEV) deployment, resulting in carbon emissions of 2.99 Gt in 2060, exceeding carbon neutrality targets by 16.2%; 3) improved and aggressive recycling will achieve reductions of 11.7% and 13.3% in 2060 compared to the current recycling level; 4) V2G deployment drives progressive emission reductions, approximately achieving an emissions mitigation of 1.5%∼6.2% in 2060; 5) The carbon neutrality targets for these two sectors can be achieved through the synergy between enhanced recycling and V2G: greatly improving copper recycling efficiency combined with a V2G penetration rate exceeding 65% alleviates copper scarcity and closes the resulting carbon emissions gap relative to the Carbon Neutrality Scenario.

title: Corporate responses to the carbon border adjustment mechanism: Impacts, policy interactions, and strategic pathways
abstract: This study examines how the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) affects export-oriented manufacturing firms in Taiwan and shapes their strategic responses toward decarbonization and cleaner production. As CBAM is scheduled to impose carbon charges on selected imports from 2026, carbon-intensive industries—particularly steel, aluminum, cement, and fertilizers—are expected to face rising compliance costs and increasing pressure to adjust production and investment decisions. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study integrates focus group discussions with a structured questionnaire survey and applies the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to analyze firm-level decision-making under multiple criteria. A total of 32 valid responses were collected from Taiwanese firms with actual exports to the European Union. The results indicate that firms place the greatest emphasis on carbon reduction effectiveness, followed by policy support, while cost considerations rank third. This pattern suggests that firms are increasingly willing to pursue structural decarbonization and cleaner production strategies when supported by clear and credible policy incentives. In terms of strategic preferences, firms prioritize direct payment of CBAM charges as a short-term compliance strategy, while mitigation-oriented options—such as participation in domestic decarbonization projects combined with preferential carbon pricing—emerge as viable medium-term alternatives. Overall, these findings provide practical insights into how carbon border measures influence firm-level production strategies and highlight the importance of aligning domestic carbon pricing and policy support mechanisms to facilitate industrial transition toward cleaner production.

title: Predicting and interpreting the effects of steel slag amendment on soil acidification across diverse agricultural conditions
abstract: Soil acidification poses a significant challenge to global agricultural sustainability, while steel slag (SS), as an alkaline industrial by-product, is regarded as a potentially efficient soil amendment. However, existing studies on the application of SS for mitigating soil acidification remain largely confined to regional field trials, lacking quantitative tools capable of efficiently predicting amendment effectiveness and systematically elucidating the underlying mechanisms. This study compiled 211 field experimental records on soil amendment using SS, covering broad gradients in SS properties, soil characteristics, and agronomic scenarios. A machine learning model was constructed to predict the effect of SS amendment on soil acidification, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.929. The results indicate that the application of SS amendment increased soil pH by an average of 1.671. Application rate, initial soil pH, and soil particle size were identified as the primary numerical features influencing improvement effect, with a cumulative importance of 53.813%. A threshold effect was observed at pH = 5.0, below which soils exhibited more pronounced improvements. The results also highlight the trade-off between improvement effect and economic input, as well as the importance of supplementary application to maintain regulatory effects. Overall, this study provides an interpretable and readily accessible decision-support tool for soil management, while offering a methodological and empirical basis for the resourceful utilization of industrial by-products.

title: Revisiting emergy algebra: The cross-looping problem in emergy accounting on systems networks
abstract: Emergy accounting relies on tracing available energy contributions through systems networks using a special set of rules to handle features such as splits, co-products and feedbacks, collectively known as emergy algebra. This algebra has been subject to diverse interpretations and is not always applied consistently in the literature, with important consequences for reported emergy values. This study provides a fundamental examination of two accounting approaches in systems with splits and cycling: the standard emergy algebra and an alternative procedure also referred to as the network method. We describe a phenomenon that seems to have gone unnoticed thus far. This phenomenon, which we term the cross-looping effect, arises from different choices in system partitioning and feedback allocation and significantly affects standard emergy algebra computations. It leads to undesirable and arbitrary variations in computed emergy flows, even though these variations correspond to no real differences in resource use or system performance. In contrast, the alternative emergy algebra is inherently robust to this effect. Through analytical examples and generalisation to an arbitrary number of subsystems, we demonstrate that the results of standard emergy algebra approach those of the alternative method only in a certain limiting case. Overall, our findings expose a limitation of the standard interpretation of the emergy accounting rules when applied to systems featuring recycling, feedbacks or complex network structures and support the use of the alternative emergy algebra in such cases, thereby contributing to more reliable emergy-based sustainability assessments and to a clearer theoretical understanding of emergy computations on networks.

title: Release and reprecipitation of phosphorus during peroxymonosulfate-based sludge disintegration
abstract: Phosphorus recovery from waste activated sludge is essential for sustainable resource management. Peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based oxidation is a promising technique for sludge disintegration and phosphorus release, yet the transformation pathways during disintegration remain poorly understood. This study achieves high phosphorus release efficiency and reveals phosphorus release–reprecipitation process during the treatment. At a PMS dosage of 0.6 mmol/g total suspended solids, concentrations of PO43− and total dissolved phosphorus in sludge supernatant reached a maximum of 99.82 and 107.75 mg/L, enhanced by 99.84% and 112.36% after sludge disintegration. However, a decrease of phosphorus concentration in the sludge supernatant after reaching the peak was observed due to reprecipitation. By combining Visual MINTEQ software simulations with the Standards, Measurements and Testing sequential extraction of solid-phase phosphorus, we confirmed the framework of release-reprecipitation and revealed the dominance shift of reprecipitation between Al3+ and Fe3+. The results revealed that phosphorus reprecipitated with metal ions released by sludge disintegration in supernatant, forming non-apatite inorganic phosphorus dominated by variscite and strengite. When the PMS dosage was within 0.4 mmol/g TSS, Al3+ dominated the reprecipitation process, thereby limiting the release of phosphorus. As the PMS dosage increased to 0.6 mmol/g TSS, Al3+ exhibited a decrease in its reprecipitation effect and Fe3+ replaced Al3+ as the dominant metal ion of reprecipitation, leading to further phosphorus release. The results demonstrate that balancing the release and precipitation of phosphorus can promote efficient phosphorus recovery, providing a critical theoretical foundation for phosphorus resource recovery from sludge.

title: The awareness-action gap in sustainable development: faculty perceptions and practices in Palestinian higher education
abstract: Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable development through teaching, research, and community engagement. Universities play an important role in preparing graduates capable of addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. However, existing research on sustainability in higher education has focused largely on institutions in politically stable and economically advantaged countries. This geographical concentration leaves limited understanding of how sustainability is taught and implemented in contexts affected by prolonged conflict and resource scarcity. Addressing this gap, the present study investigates professors’ perceptions, practices, and challenges related to integrating sustainable development and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals into academic work in Palestinian higher education. The study aims to examine whether faculty awareness of sustainability concepts is reflected in teaching and research practices and to identify institutional conditions that influence implementation. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed. A validated online questionnaire was distributed to full-time faculty members at public universities in the West Bank, producing a final sample of 388 respondents representing a range of academic disciplines. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, and one-way analysis of variance. The findings reveal an awareness–action gap. Although approximately 75% of respondents reported high awareness of the importance of sustainable development, extensive integration was reported by only 28% in teaching and 25% in research. Significant differences were observed by gender, discipline, and professional experience. The results indicate that sustainability approaches developed in stable higher education systems may require adaptation in conflict-affected contexts. The study highlights the importance of faculty development initiatives, institutional incentives, and curricular support to strengthen sustainability education in Palestinian universities.

title: Comparative life cycle assessment of an overhead agrivoltaic system: Environmental impacts and methodological insights
abstract: Agrivoltaic systems have been identified by the European Union as a key strategy to enable the utility-scale deployment of photovoltaic (PV) systems needed to achieve complete decarbonization of the European energy system by 2050, while simultaneously reducing land-use conflicts. This study addresses the environmental sustainability of such systems by conducting a life cycle assessment (LCA) in compliance with ISO 14040/14044 standards. The assessment focuses on an overhead agrivoltaic system (characterized by PV modules mounted above cultivated crops), primarily intended for electricity generation, and compares it to a conventional system consisting of a ground-mounted PV system (reference PV system). The functional unit is defined as 1 kWh of alternating current electricity delivered into the grid, and system boundaries follow a cradle-to-grave approach. The results reveal that the agrivoltaic system provides significant advantages in land-use efficiency, reducing land-use impact by 95% and increasing land-use efficiency use by 46%, compared to the reference PV system. However, it also shows slightly higher environmental impacts in categories such as resource use, minerals and metals (14%) and climate change (12%). The increase in resource use is due to the larger material requirements of elevated structures, while in climate change impact is partly attributed to reduced crop yields under partial PV modules shading. Despite the slightly higher climate impact, the specific emissions per kWh remain very low (16.8 gCO 2 eq/kWh), confirming the potential of agrivoltaic systems to contribute to energy decarbonization while optimizing land use. Nevertheless, the study suggests that strategic crop selection, i.e. shade-tolerant crops capable of benefiting from the microclimatic conditions under PV modules, can enhance agrivoltaic performance and mitigate environmental trade-offs in a wide range of impact categories, including climate change, allowing agrivoltaic systems to perform as well as or even better than conventional ground-mounted PV systems. Beyond these results, the study contributes to the methodological advancement of LCA applied to agrivoltaic systems. It outlines how to clearly define the primary function, select a coherent functional unit, and resolve multifunctionality in line with ISO 14040/14044. This work represents one of the first ISO-compliant LCAs of agrivoltaic systems, providing robust insights to support their future sustainable expansion.

title: How can public procurement foster sustainability along global supply chains? A systematic and critical review
abstract: Public administrations across the globe are increasingly adopting sustainable public procurement (SPP), as their substantial expenditures are expected to orient their potential suppliers towards sustainability. However, the existing research on SPP is fragmented across disciplines, lacking a comprehensive understanding and conceptualization of its effects on the suppliers, along their supply chains. To address this gap, we conduct a systematic literature review of 49 empirical peer-reviewed articles exploring how and under which circumstances SPP practices can foster sustainability in Global Supply Chains (GSCs). The resulting conceptual framework illustrates the relationship between public procurement and sustainability in GSCs, along with influencing factors. Our findings reveal that intra-organizational and inter-organizational SPP practices indirectly influence GSC sustainability performance. Moreover, the study highlights the indirect influence of institutional distance between buyers and suppliers’ environments on GSC sustainability performance. Finally, various endogenous and exogenous factors are identified that directly influence the effectiveness of SPP and global sustainable supply chain management practices. The study stands out as the first to conceptualize the interplay of context-specific differences and factors influencing SPP effectiveness beyond the direct supplier, along supply chains. It underscores the potential for public buyers to influence firms' SSCM through SPP practices, contingent on internal capacities and external regulatory support. While firms, in turn, shall strategically select multi-tier SSCM practices based on environmental contexts and be aware of the effects of their pressures on lower-tiers suppliers to meet sustainability requirements effectively.

title: Environmental and cost trade-offs uncertainty in ecodesign: a new approach to communicate life cycle impacts
abstract: Ecodesign involves significant uncertainty, especially at early design stages, when information is scarce, and multiple assessment criteria must be considered simultaneously. Such uncertainty can lead to misleading conclusions when comparing potential ecodesign alternatives. Stochastic Multi-Attribute Analysis (SMAA) can help address this challenge by propagating uncertainty in Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA) indicators and other criteria through Monte Carlo simulation, providing a robust decision-support framework. This article proposes an ecodesign decision-support approach to communicate trade-offs between environmental and cost dimensions under uncertainty. The environmental weight threshold quantifies the minimum weight that must be assigned to the environmental dimension for a given ecodesign alternative to be preferred over a business-as-usual situation. The proposed decision-support approach is applied to an ecodesign case study of a nutraceutical bottle made of high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The results show that a future bottle made of 30 % recycled polymer from post-hospital waste is the ecodesign alternative with the largest potential to replace the current HDPE bottle. The additive aggregation model and PROMETHEE multicriteria methods are compared, showing that the environmental weight threshold is method-agnostic. The case study also demonstrates that the proposed approach avoids the sensitivity of SMAA's traditional rank acceptability index regarding hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical weighting, and can support choices concerning the development of more competitive products with lower environmental impacts.

title: Coordinating carbon and pollution reduction with human settlements in Chinese cities: A key step toward achieving sustainable development goals
abstract: China's rapid urbanization has raised living standards but also intensified environmental pollution, traffic congestion, and housing shortages that threaten human settlements (HS). Coordinating carbon and pollution reduction (CPR) with HS improvement is therefore critical to high-quality green urban development. However, existing studies largely examine CPR and HS separately, with limited attention to whether coordinated emission reduction improves human settlements at the city scale. Most city-level research also focuses mainly on spatial heterogeneity, while giving little attention to intercity networks and directional information flows. To address these gaps, this study uses data from 280 prefecture-level cities to build an integrated framework that combines coupling coordination and spatial association. Separate indicator systems are constructed to quantify CPR and HS, a modified coupling coordination degree model is used to gauge their interdependence, and social network analysis is applied to map spatial linkages within and between the two systems. Results show that (1) both CPR coordinated-development level and HS quality improved over time, with CPR exhibiting a south-high, north-low pattern and HS showing a coastal-high, inland-low pattern; (2) the CPR-HS coupling coordination relationship displayed pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and both coupling degree and coupling coordination degree increased overall with fluctuations, shifting from maladjustment toward coordination, although the overall coordination level remained moderate; and (3) CPR and HS networks showed clear modularity and tightly connected regional structures, while the HS network became slightly denser over time. Cross-system information flows, however, remained weak, with CPR→HS spillovers slightly stronger than HS→CPR. This study integrates urban system coupling with spatial diffusion theory and provides evidence to guide place-specific and cross-regional green governance strategies, thereby promoting sustainable development.

title: Nanoplastic-driven microbial communication breakdown weakens biogeochemical resilience in constructed wetland ecosystems
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) are increasingly detected in constructed wetlands (CWs), yet we still lack a mechanistic understanding of how nanoscale contaminants disrupt microbial communication and thereby destabilize coupled C-N-P-S cycling. Here, we address this gap by integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, metabolic network reconstruction, and multi-model causal inference to elucidate how NPs perturb cross-habitat microbial cooperation. We demonstrate that NPs do not merely alter community structure; they fundamentally rewire microbial regulatory architecture by (i) inducing sustained oxidative stress that diverts ATP and reducing equivalents toward cellular defense, and (ii) degrading or adsorbing quorum-sensing molecules (AI-2, AHLs), which suppresses key signal synthases (luxS, cqsA) and breaking down interspecies coordination. This coupled oxidative and signaling disruption collapses metabolic complementarity between rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere communities, leading to spatial decoupling of nitrogen redox transformations, enhanced phosphorus immobilization, and divergence in carbon fluxes. Through integrated PLSR-RF-SEM modeling, we identify dsrA/dsrB, nosZ, phoA/pstC, and luxS as previously unrecognized regulatory “control points'’ that mechanistically link nanoscale perturbation to ecosystem-scale functional decline. Our findings reveal an emergent mechanism-NP-induced oxidative-informational collapse-through which anthropogenic nanoparticles erode the self-organizing capacity of wetland microbiomes, providing a predictive basis for assessing plastic-driven biogeochemical vulnerability.

title: Mechanisms driving the effects of tetramethylammonium hydroxide on the operation of anaerobic baffled-Anammox reactor: Nitrogen removal, sludge characteristics, and microbial community
abstract: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH) is a common toxic pollutant in microelectronics wastewater and creates challenges for environmental governance. This study evaluated the effects of different TMAH concentrations on the nitrogen removal performance and microbial ecology of an anaerobic baffled reactor-Anammox (ABR-Anammox) coupled system. The results showed that at a low TMAH concentration (≤25 mg/L), the system maintained NH4+-N and NO2−-N removal rates above 80%. At a high TMAH concentration (50 mg/L), nitrogen removal performance dropped to below 60%. Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) and Three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy (3D-EEM) analyses revealed that TMAH stress altered the composition and structure of extracellular polymers (EPS) in sludge. Within the EPS, the proportion of α-helix in the protein secondary structure decreased from 25% to 13%, and the proportion of β-sheet increased from 34% to 40%. A microbial community analysis indicated that the abundance of the core ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Candidatus Brocadia decreased from 28.34% to 10.30%. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that TMAH inhibited the expression of the electron transport chain (i.e., atpA decreased by 38.4%), the tricarboxylic acid cycle (i.e., key genes decreased by 31-49%), and denitrifying-related genes (i.e., narG decreased by 54.8%). This weakened the energy metabolism and denitrification pathways at the molecular level. This study reveals the concentration-dependent inhibition mechanism of TMAH on the ABR-Anammox system, providing a theoretical basis for the biological treatment process of industrial wastewater containing TMAH.

title: Kinetic modelling of continuous biomass liquefaction for biopolyols and bio-based polyurethane synthesis
abstract: Overconsumption of fossil fuels has led to detrimental effects on the environment, underscoring the need to shift industrial processes towards the adoption of renewable sources. Biomass is valorised in thermochemical conversion for sustainable fuels and chemicals production. This work aims to construct robust kinetic models to predict process performance in the liquefaction of different biomasses to obtain biopolyols, green compounds used in bio-based polyurethane synthesis. The models were developed in Aspen Plus adopting power-law kinetics, achieving good agreement with experimental data, with errors below 15%. The model validation for batch liquefaction of municipal solid waste resulted in bio-oil yields of 33.7, 46.3 and 58.8 wt%, at 300, 325 and 350 °C respectively, with errors of 11.1% at 325 °C and only 0.17% at 350 °C. About microalgae liquefaction, theoretical bio-oil yields of 16.7, 21.1, 26.4 wt% were found at 180, 200, and 225 °C, respectively, with errors of 1.2, 0.5 and 2.7%. Model validation of sewage sludge batch liquefaction achieved less than 10% errors on products flow rates and excellent agreement with experimental biopolyols yields: 65.0 wt% from solvent glycerol (0.04% error), 49.1 wt% from sewage sludge (0.1% error). The present work provides the first simulations of continuous solvothermal liquefaction for waste biomass conversion into biopolyols, optimising the pilot plant design for the company Ecorbio Ltd. Through sensitivity analysis, this novel study identifies optimal reactor temperatures and dimensions to reduce energy demand and enhance biopolyols yield for bio-based polyurethane production.

title: Energy yield and water resource utilization in Chlorella pyrenoidosa under saline-alkali stress: An integrated physiological, ionomic, and transcriptomic approach
abstract: Saline-alkali water is increasingly recognized as a promising alternative resource for microalgal cultivation. However, it remains unclear which ion-homeostasis constraints most directly limit growth and are linked to metabolic reprogramming under combined saline-alkali (SA) stress. Here, Chlorella pyrenoidosa was exposed to a gradient of saline-alkali stress established by NaCl and a Na2CO3/NaHCO3 mixture, and its physiological, biochemical, ionomic, and transcriptomic responses were analyzed to identify the key physiological constraints underlying saline-alkali adaptation. Notably, intracellular Mg2+ levels were strongly associated with biomass and cell density, and 2 × Mg2+ enrichment under high irradiance during saline-alkali stress increased biomass by 20.6% and gross energy output by 61.8%, indicating that Mg2+ bioavailability is a practical lever for improving cultivation performance under saline–alkali conditions. Saline–alkali stress markedly suppressed growth yet promoted carbon reallocation toward carbohydrates and lipids, thereby strengthening the strain's potential contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with the highest contributions observed for SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy, 56.2%) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger, 19.1%). Ionomic profiling revealed marked Na+ accumulation accompanied by substantial K+ depletion and elevated intracellular Ca2+, suggesting disruption of Na+/K+ homeostasis and potential activation of Ca2+-mediated stress signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified candidate genes associated with membrane/transport functions, energy metabolism, and redox regulation, supporting a “survival-over-growth” strategy that redirects carbon flux to starch/sucrose and lipid synthesis while repressing proliferation-related processes (e.g., DNA replication). These findings provide a practical basis for optimizing microalgal cultivation strategies to enhance biomass and energy production in saline-alkali water.

title: Short term economic outcomes associated with ecological sustainability practices among small and medium scale agricultural producers in Chile
abstract: Ecological sustainability practices have become central to debates on agricultural systems and climate resilience, yet evidence on their short-term economic implications for small- and medium-scale producers remains fragmented. This question is consequential because household livelihood security hinges on income cycles that rarely align with the temporal horizons of ecological processes. Existing research emphasizes the agronomic and environmental benefits of sustainable practices, but offers limited insight into how operational and systemic interventions are associated with income outcomes under heterogeneous production and market structures. This study examines whether ecological sustainability practices are associated with short-term income positioning within agricultural systems and how these associations vary across practices with distinct ecological functions. Using microdata from 57,439 agricultural units in the 2021 Chilean Agricultural Census, this study estimates a generalized partial proportional-odds model that preserves the ordinal structure of income while capturing threshold-specific effects. The results reveal consistent upward associations between operational practices and higher income categories. Organic fertilizers, organic matter, and erosion control increase the probability of belonging to the highest income category by 4.8, 2.4, and 1.5 percentage points, respectively. By contrast, conservation areas reduce that probability by 1.7 percent points, while reforestation lowers the probability of belonging to the upper-middle income category by 3.7 percent points. Structural activities and market channels exert substantially stronger effects: agro-industrial commercialization increases the probability of reaching the highest income category by 15 percentage points. These findings show that ecological sustainability practices are associated with differentiated economic pathways and clarify the conditions under which they align with or strain short-term livelihood dynamics.

title: Efficient removal of ibuprofen and ketoprofen from aqueous solutions using ZIF-8: A comparative study of two synthesis technique
abstract: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as ibuprofen and ketoprofen, are widely used however pose environmental challenges due to their poor solubility and persistence in aquatic systems. This study presents a novel approach employing Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) for the simultaneous removal of NSAIDs from aqueous solutions. ZIF-8 was fabricated using a Y-type micromixer (Y-ZIF-8), which exhibited superior properties compared to conventional batch reactor method (B-ZIF-8), including higher specific surface area (1362.57 m 2 /g) and smaller particle size (100–200 nm). Adsorption experiments showed significantly improved removal efficiencies for Y-ZIF-8, with maximum Langmuir adsorption capacities reaching 154.36 mg/g for ibuprofen and 108.72 mg/g for ketoprofen, compared to 108.73 mg/g and 77.49 mg/g, respectively, for B-ZIF-8. The adsorption performance was evaluated under varying pH conditions, with optimal removal observed between pH 5 and 9, driven by electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and π-π stacking. Kinetic and isotherm studies revealed that the pseudo-second-order and Sips models best described the adsorption process, indicating chemisorption and heterogeneous surface interactions. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided molecular-level insights into the adsorption mechanism, highlighting the dominance of π-π stacking. Y-ZIF-8 demonstrated high efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and scalability for NSAID removal, with potential applications in advanced pharmaceutical wastewater treatment and drug delivery systems.

title: Green synthesis of dual cobalt active sites confined in mesoporous carbon for the ultrafast water decontamination
abstract: Nanoconfinement effect could significantly accelerate the transformation of organics, yet the construction of catalytic centers in the confined space was still challenging. Herein, a green synthesis strategy was explored to confine dual cobalt active sites, i.e., cobalt nanoparticles (Co NPs) as well as single atom sites (Co-N3) in ordered mesoporous carbon. The synergistic effect between Co NPs and Co-N3 performed exceptional catalytic activity and stability. Remarkably high degradation rate constants (0.586−3.81 min−1) were achieved for diverse organics (e.g., sulfadiazine SDZ, bisphenol A BPA, benzoic acid BA), surpassing most reported cobalt-based catalysts. Though multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS) were identified, the dominant ROS was largely depended on the organic compound. Specifically, the electron-rich organics with low ionization potential (IP) and high highest occupied molecular orbital (EHOMO) were preferentially oxidized through the direct electron-transfer mechanism driven by the nonradical high potential complexes (PMS*). Geometric confinement minimized cobalt leaching and enhanced durability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed Co-N3 sites modulated neighboring Co NPs, synergistically strengthening PMS adsorption (energy decreased from −1.859 eV to −2.508 eV) and inducing significant PMS distortion via stretching. The upward shift of the d-band center (−1.452 eV to −1.443 eV) further confirmed the electronic regulation. This work provides an innovative strategy for designing high-performance and stable cobalt-based catalyst.

title: Highly efficient recovery of gold by selective sulfide reduction from chlorine leachate
abstract: Addressing supply shortages and escalating prices, hydrometallurgical recovery of gold from electronic waste has become crucial for sustainable resource utilization. This study proposed a strategy for green and highly efficient recovery of gold by sulfide reduction from chlorine leachate. Under the optimized conditions (pH = 0.2, 293 K, [S]/[Au] molar ratio = 2, 30 min), experiments demonstrate that gold recovery exceeds 99.88 %, and subsequent nitric acid pickling yielded pure gold (>99.99 wt %). Characterization analysis shows that the product is composed of elemental sulfur and gold rather than traditional gold sulfide. The calculated results elucidate a distinct fifth step sequential reduction pathway for gold sulfidation, in contrast to the conventional two step mechanism. Sulfide ions are partially hydrolyzed to form H2S, which gradually replaces chloride ions to form Au2S3, further decomposes into Au2S, and finally forms gold and sulfur. Elevated temperature accelerates mass diffusion, while impurities undergo chemisorption onto the gold surface but can be readily removed by acid pickling. This work elucidates a novel reduction pathway and provides an efficient, low cost, and environmentally benign route for gold recovery from hydrometallurgy chlorine leachate.

title: Cost–benefit comparison of steel slag co-utilization and carbon capture, utilization and storage pathways for cement industry decarbonization: Evidence from China
abstract: Process emissions from clinker production make the cement industry difficult to decarbonize, highlighting the need for cost-effective mitigation pathways. Steel slag co-utilization and carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) are promising options, yet their comparative performance under real industrial clustering conditions remains unclear. This study aims to compare these two pathways for cement industry decarbonization in Hebei Province, China. A life-cycle cost comparison framework was developed by integrating a multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for optimizing steel slag flows between steel mills and cement plants with a CO2 source-sink matching model for evaluating CCUS deployment over a 30-year horizon. Results show that steel slag co-utilization provides a lower-cost mitigation option for plants located in steel-cement clusters, with abatement costs ranging from 292.75 to 840.60 CNY/tCO2 and cumulative emission reductions of 102 million tons CO2. CCUS performance varies substantially by storage type. Oil and gas reservoir storage can achieve negative abatement costs, while saline aquifer storage ranges from 338.65 to 507.94 CNY per ton of CO2 and yields cumulative reductions of 1266 million tons. Among the 46 cement plants assessed, 32.6% are better suited to steel slag co-utilization, 60.9% should prioritize CCUS deployment, and 6.5% are suitable for a hybrid pathway. The findings reveal the two pathways’ distinct mechanisms and spatial patterns and support more effective decarbonization planning for the cement industry.

title: Micromechanical properties of geopolymers with carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) and carbon nanohorns (CNH): A multiscale indentation and clustering analysis approach
abstract: This study investigates the effect of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) and carbon nanohorns (CNHs) on the micromechanical properties of metakaolin-based geopolymer composites (MKGC) through multiscale indentation analysis. Samples with 0%, 0.2%, 0.5%, and 1.0% nanomaterial content were cured at 20 °C and 60 °C for 7 days. Micro- and nanoindentation measurements were performed to assess the mechanical heterogeneity, supported by K-means clustering analysis. The analysis aimed at comprehending how nanoscale reinforcements influence local mechanical properties, while guiding the design of advanced geopolymers for thermoelectrical and piezoelectrical applications. The highest Vickers hardness (HV) occurred at 0.2% MWCNT, cured at 20 °C (38.2 kgf/mm 2 ), with no further improvement at higher contents. For CNH-reinforced samples, the highest HV was observed at 0.5% CNH (39.7 kgf/mm 2 at 20 °C). Nanoindentation results revealed high mechanical heterogeneity, with instrumented hardness (HIT) ranging from 0.75 to 1.1 GPa and Young's modulus (ER) from 9.55 to 12.06 GPa, both exhibiting large standard deviations. K-means clustering analysis successfully distinguished geopolymer matrix regions from nanomaterial-affected regions, but reinforcement effects were not always clearly observed. These findings highlight the importance of increasing indentation density, improving dispersion strategies, and applying advanced data analysis techniques to tailor nanocomposite performance for multifunctional construction materials.

title: Exploring the carbon footprint of time-series prediction models
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly. Nevertheless, its pursuit of precision through large-scale computation (“red AI”) raises concerns about sustainability. While recent advances in machine learning have significantly improved forecasting performance, existing research predominantly focuses on accuracy, largely overlooking the associated environmental costs. This omission is particularly problematic in high-frequency financial forecasting, where continuous model training and inference can generate substantial carbon emissions. To address this gap, we propose a dual-dimensional evaluation framework that jointly assesses predictive performance and carbon emissions. Using 1-min intervals of Bitcoin data and controlled experiments across model architectures (XGBoost, LSTM, and Transformer), hardware configurations, data volumes, and learning strategies, we provide a systematic analysis of the accuracy–emissions trade-off. The results suggest that when considering accuracy and emissions jointly, LSTM is the most effective choice. Notably, the configuration employing the four-step prediction for one step, which was trained on 80,000 samples, demonstrated the best performance, combining high accuracy with moderate carbon cost. This work challenges two common assumptions: that larger datasets do not necessarily improve accuracy and that high-performance graphics processing units are not consistently superior, as lightweight models can perform more efficiently on general-purpose hardware. Together, these findings extend research on sustainable AI by highlighting trade-offs between accuracy and ecological effects. Overall, this research advances the understanding of “green AI” by emphasising the ecological effects of algorithmic design. This work underscores the importance of integrating environmental considerations into AI practice and incorporating green development into AI ethics, enabling more energy-conscious and sustainable AI systems.

title: Aqueous carbonated coal fly ash enhancing soil organic matter stability with implications for carbon storage and soil amelioration
abstract: Utilizing coal fly ash (CFA) for soil amelioration offers a dual benefit: waste management and agricultural improvement. Soil organic matter (SOM) could help prevent the release of inherent toxic substances from the CFA. However, SOM is inherently unstable and can be easily degraded by microbes without protection. To address this, CFA was activated via aqueous carbonation to enhance the interaction between CFA and SOM. The carbonation formed a cation-rich layer on CFA surface, increasing the specific surface area and positive charge. These changes in CFA surface properties strengthened the binding between humic acid (HA, as a representative of SOM) and carbonated CFA (C-CFA), significantly reducing carbon loss caused by microbial degradation and water erosion. Furthermore, HA + C-CFA complexes were applied as soil ameliorators. Leaching experiments demonstrated that cadmium (Cd, used as a representative toxic substance) was immobilized in the following order: CFA < C-CFA < HA < HA + CFA < HA + C-CFA-5 (weakly carbonated) < HA + C-CFA-60 (highly carbonated). Additionally, phosphorus (P) bioavailability improved with HA + C-CFA treatments. These results indicate a synergistic effect between CFA carbonation and HA complexation, reducing heavy metal toxicity and enhancing fertilizer use efficiency. Additionally, pot experiments revealed that HA + C-CFA complexes significantly inhibited Cd accumulation in Chinese cabbage (Brassica campestris L.) while promoting plant growth in contaminated soils. These systematic studies, from revealing the molecular mechanisms underlying the enhanced binding between HA and C-CFA to applying HA + C-CFA complexes in plant cultivation, highlight the critical role of C-CFA in carbon storage and offer important implications for soil amelioration.

title: In-situ reinforcement of construction and demolition waste deposits using an intelligent penetration-type gas–vibration compaction and carbon sequestration system driven by the Brazil Nut Effect
abstract: Given the high generation and inadequate disposal of construction and demolition waste (C&DW), it is often improperly used as subgrade or foundation fill, posing risks of engineering failures and environmental hazards. To achieve both resource recovery and carbon reduction, this study proposes and develops a penetration-type gas–vibration compaction and carbon sequestration (PGCCS) method, integrating the “layering → grouting → carbon storage” concept and associated technique. This method combines physical and chemical processes: it first induces the “Brazil Nut Effect” to achieve particle stratification and densification, and then applies slurry injection with CO2 pressurized grouting to trigger MgO–CO2 mineralization, forming a dense carbonate “slurry-cap” that suppresses leaching and dust emission. This study is based on a large-scale C&DW landfill remediation project, combining in-situ experiments with a cradle-to-gate carbon footprint assessment and cost evaluation. Results show that under optimized gas–vibration excitation the C&DW structure transformed from a disordered structure to a stratified configuration, with coarse particles decreasing progressively with depth, accompanied by a 20–30% increase in shear wave velocity (to 272–313 m/s) and a reduction in wetting-induced collapsible settlement from ∼85.0 mm to 1.1 mm. Combined carbon footprint and cost analyses reveal a net global warming potential (GWP) of ∼57.65 kg CO2e/m3 with ∼7.4 kg CO2/m3 sequestered through MgO–CO2 mineralization, at a cost of only 21.3%–33.2% of conventional methods. The PGCCS method shows strong potential for in-situ remediation and reuse of thick, heterogeneous C&DW deposits, offering both mechanistic insight and a scalable technical pathway for carbon-neutral infrastructure.

title: Assessing the effectiveness of diverse climate change mitigation technologies on carbon emissions: insights from 243 OECD Regions
abstract: Evaluating climate change mitigation technologies during peak carbon emission phases is crucial for understanding the impact of technological innovation on reducing emissions. Drawing on OECD data, there was a noticeable upward trend in the number of environment-related patent applications during the peak plateau period 2000–2008. However, a significant disparity in patent distribution among regions is evident, with the top 10% of regions accounting for nearly 60% of total patents. This study analyzes data from 243 OECD regions to examine how different mitigation technologies impact carbon emissions. Results show strong time-lag effects and spatial spillovers, as well as heterogeneity in technological effectiveness. Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology demonstrates particularly strong potential, with a regression coefficient nearly twice that of other technologies. In contrast, energy-, buildings-, and transportation-related technologies show diminished effects due to potential rebound effects. Further mechanism analysis suggests that transportation-related technologies may potentially achieve this indirectly, at least in part, by improving energy utilization efficiency and adjusting industrial structure. Hence, enhancing investment in research and development for technological innovation, especially in CCS technology, becomes imperative for countries aiming to effectively mitigate their carbon emission peak levels. The full paper is available at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2026.148383

title: Assessing green synergy efficiency to advance sustainable development goals: A multi-objective collaborative efficiency analysis framework
abstract: Achieving global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and promoting green and low-carbon development have become the key to addressing global climate change. From an input-output perspective, a multi-objective synergistic efficiency analysis framework was constructed, and a corresponding evaluation indicator system was established based on the SDGs. Using panel data from Jiangsu Coastal Economic Belt (JCEB) from 2005 to 2022, a comprehensive measurement and empirical analysis of the regional Green Synergistic Efficiency (GSE) was conducted. Moreover, the dynamic evolution characteristics, regional differences and influencing factors of GSE was further investigated using Kernel density estimation, Dagum-Gini coefficient, Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression model. Results indicate that the GSE of the JCEB was generally at a medium efficiency level from 2005 to 2022, showing a fluctuating growth trend, with an average increase of 80.27%. Spatially, it evolves from a pattern of high in the middle and low in the north and south to a balanced distribution across the entire region. Furthermore, analysis of dynamic evolution characteristics reveals a decline in absolute differences between county-level units, the emergence of a multi-peak pattern in fluctuations and discernible polarization. Meanwhile, the Gini coefficient showed a fluctuating downward trend during the study period, with inter-group differences among administrative region types contributing more significantly to GSE. Finally, foreign trade, government regulation, financial development, technological innovation and ecological endowment promote GSE. However, industrial structure, population density, socio-economic activities and land use structure show the opposite effect.

title: AI-enhanced design of carbon capture and utilization networks using surrogate-based superstructure optimization
abstract: Carbon neutrality requires efficient, cost-effective carbon capture and utilization (CCU) pathways. Superstructure optimization enables the systematic evaluation of alternative CCU pathways and identification of the most cost-effective and environmentally sustainable configurations. However, existing superstructure optimization approaches are limited by fixed process parameters, reducing model accuracy and flexibility in evaluating novel CCU supply chains. Therefore, this study aims to develop a surrogate-integrated superstructure optimization framework to design CCU supply chains that maximize economic returns and minimize greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The proposed model employed a detailed two-level, block-based structure design that captures process-level nonlinearities through artificial neural network-based surrogate models, with a particular focus on methanol synthesis. Environmental and economic trade-offs were examined across 10–90% GHG reduction targets, showing that the surrogate-based approach allows more flexible and realistic optimization than traditional fixed-parameter models. The findings indicate that surrogate-based optimization sustained or improved profitability while enabling more sustainable carbon and energy pathways. This study offers valuable insights to guide the strategic deployment of CCU technologies in global net-zero transition efforts.

title: Pyro-gasification of olive pomace pellets for renewable hydrogen production: experimental data-driven techno-economic analysis
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable energy solutions has intensified research into renewable hydrogen production from biomass. This study investigates the pyro-gasification of olive pomace pellets, i.e. a by-product of the olive oil industry, to generate hydrogen through an integrated thermochemical process. Experimental tests were conducted at 900 °C in a rotary kiln reactor across varying equivalence ratios (ER) ranging from 0 (pyrolysis) to 0.28 (gasification). The resulting syngas compositions were used as inputs for process simulations in Aspen Hysys, where a data-driven modelling approach enabled the integration of experimental reactor outputs into the wider plant-scale assessment, encompassing steam methane reforming, water-gas shift reactions, and hydrogen purification via pressure swing adsorption. Results demonstrated that increasing the ER reduced char yields and tar content while enhancing syngas production. However, a non-monotonic trend in hydrogen output was observed, with the highest annual production (around 512.8 tons/year) and maximum thermochemical efficiency of 47.3% achieved at ER = 0.1. At this condition, the levelized cost of hydrogen was minimized to 16.30 €/kg, reflecting an optimal balance between partial oxidation and gasification reactions. Sensitivity analysis further revealed that reformer temperature significantly influences hydrogen yield, plateauing beyond 850 °C. Overall, the findings confirm that olive pomace pyro-gasification, under controlled oxidant supply, constitutes a technically and economically viable route for renewable hydrogen production. This work provides a robust foundation for scaling up biomass-based hydrogen systems and supports the valorisation of agro-industrial residues within a circular bioeconomy framework.

title: Advancing secondary raw material flows through cleaner production: integrating mechanical recycling and eco-design of post-industrial textile waste
abstract: The transition towards a circular textile economy requires approaches that simultaneously address material recovery, design for recyclability, and product durability. However, these dimensions are often addressed independently in the existing literature, resulting in limited operational integration between recycling processes and product design decisions. This study proposes an integrated engineering–design methodology that combines mechanical recycling of post-industrial polyester–cotton cutting waste with eco-design strategies aimed at enabling circular and resource-efficient garment production under realistic industrial conditions. The approach encompasses waste characterisation, optimisation of fibre opening parameters, yarn and fabric production incorporating 30% recycled content, and the development of a functional capsule collection guided by design for disassembly and recyclability principles. The optimisation of the mechanical recycling process improved fibre length by up to 28% relative to baseline opening conditions, enabling the production of yarns with tenacity values in the range of 15 - 16 cN/tex, approaching industrial reference values for comparable yarns counts. Fabric production using the optimised yarn demonstrated that mechanically recycled fibres can be incorporated into structurally stable woven fabrics within conventional spinning and weaving infrastructure. Beyond material performance, eco-design principles were applied to minimise mixed components, support durability-oriented design choices, including long-lasting aesthetic design and repair-friendly garment construction, while maintaining recyclability and facilitating future recycling. The study therefore demonstrates how process-level constraints of mechanical recycling can be translated into practical garment construction rules that support circularity. Environmental implications are discussed as screening-level estimates derived from literature-based assumptions. Under these assumptions, diverting 1 tonne of cutting waste from incineration to mechanical recycling may potentially avoid approximately 2.4 t CO 2 -eq emissions and save 8–10 m 3 of water, although a full scenario-based life cycle assessment remains necessary to confirm these impacts. Overall, the results indicate that mechanical recycling optimisation and eco-design can function as complementary levers to operationalising circular textile production, while highlighting technical trade-offs and industrial constrains that require further validation.

title: Incorporating finite-element simulation and complex networks to optimize ecological networks: A case study on karst regions in China
abstract: Ecological networks (ENs) were vital maintaining regional ecological security and enhancing ecosystem services. This study introduces a collaborative optimization framework integrating mechanical and complex network analyses to enhance EN connectivity and robustness. By coupling stress identification with network structural reconfiguration, the framework enables targeted local risk mitigation while simultaneously enhancing global connectivity and robustness. This framework involved: (1) identifying the EN in a typical karst region; (2) introducing finite-element simulation to achieve risk assessment and optimization of the EN; (3) analyzing the EN from a topological perspective and validating the results optimized by finite-element simulation; (4) integrating topological features and stress conditions to propose strategies for ecological restoration. A typical karst region in Southwest China, characterized by severe rocky desertification, ecological fragility, and fragmented habitats under strong human disturbance, was selected as a case study to evaluate the framework's feasibility. Traditional EN studies often overlook corridor stability under external disturbances. To overcome this limitation and achieve a more physically grounded risk assessment, this study introduced finite-element simulation into EN research. The finite-element simulation from mechanical engineering was introduced to transform ecological corridors into three-dimensional mechanical models. In addition, landscape pattern indices were mapped to material properties, and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and road network density defined dynamic loads, quantifying corridor stress distribution and identifying high-risk fracture zones. Furthermore, a weighted undirected topological network was constructed based on complex networks to analyze node centrality and clustering characteristics, revealing the spatial imbalance and connectivity vulnerability of the EN. Then, collaborative optimization was achieved by adding stepping stones, resulting in a maximum 14.5% reduction in corridor stress and an increase in natural connectivity from 0.340 to 0.368, indicating improved network robustness. This study offered precise decision-making support for enhancing landscape connectivity and construct ENs.

title: Antibacterial and conductive silk fabrics coated with polydopamine and polypyrrole preserving wearability
abstract: Silk fabric coated with conductive materials can be a desirable substrate for flexible and wearable electronic textiles. However, the preparation of conductive and antibacterial wearable silk fabrics by a simple method is still a great challenge. In this paper, conductive and antimicrobial silk fabrics (SF-PDA-Cl-PPy) were prepared by coating with polydopamine (PDA) followed by a chlorination treatment and coating with polypyrrole (PPy). Silk fabrics were functionalized with a PDA coating followed by chlorination to introduce antimicrobial activity, and a subsequent PPy coating was applied to confer electrical conductivity. In addition, the PDA layer acted as a protective interfacial coating, alleviating the severe loss of mechanical strength that silk fabrics would otherwise suffer during chlorination. The SF-PDA-Cl-PPy fabric exhibited good antibacterial property and could inactivate over 98% of both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. The SF-PDA-Cl-PPy fabric exhibited good specific capacitance (895 mF/cm2 at 10 mA/cm2), with a capacitance retention of 58.37% after 1000 cycles. Importantly, the SF-PDA-Cl-PPy fabric could be used to monitor the movement of fingers. This research suggests a facile method for preparing functional silk fabrics with antibacterial and conductive properties, which could find potential application in the field of flexible wearable electronic devices.

title: Thermoeconomic optimization of a novel solar-driven hybrid system integrating MSF, M-Cycle, and ORC for water, cooling, and power co-production
abstract: To address the concurrent global challenges of freshwater scarcity and growing energy demand, this study introduces an advanced hybrid system capable of simultaneous freshwater generation, space cooling, and power production. The proposed system synergistically integrates a Multi-Stage Flash (MSF) desalination unit, an indirect evaporative cooling mechanism based on the Maisotsenko Cycle (M-Cycle), an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC), and parabolic trough solar collectors (PTCs). Within the system, the M-Cycle cools ambient air, which is then used to pre-cool the saline water before it enters the MSF unit, thereby enhancing evaporation potential. Simultaneously, thermal energy harvested by the solar collectors is transferred via a closed-loop heat transfer fluid to support both the MSF and ORC subsystems. Exergy analysis and thermodynamic modeling indicate that the proposed configuration increases the gain output ratio (GOR) to 1.32 and enhances freshwater production by 22.8% relative to a conventional MSF system. Incorporation of the M-Cycle provides a net cooling capacity of 39,755 Btu/h (11.65 kW, 3.31 TR), sufficient to meet the cooling demand of approximately 50 m2 of conditioned office space under hot–arid design criteria. Following multi-objective optimization, the total annual cost (TAC) of this innovative water–cooling–power tri-generation system is estimated at 15.0066 million USD/year. To determine the most effective operational regime, a multi-objective optimization was conducted using the TOPSIS decision-making method. Results confirm that factors such as air flow rate, inlet saline water temperature, and operating pressure significantly influence thermal efficiency, exergy destruction, and economic performance. This integrated solution presents a viable and sustainable approach for arid and semi-arid regions, enabling efficient resource utilization while addressing the interconnected demands of water and energy.

title: Systematic design and optimization of integrated CCUS systems for methane and methanol production
abstract: High costs and uncertainties regarding CO2 reduction efficacy remain major barriers to implementing large-scale CCUS (CO2 capture, utilization, and storage) systems. This study presents a systematic framework for designing integrated CCUS systems that combine multiple CO2 sequestration and utilization processes to produce synthetic fuels, enabling efficient removal of CO2 emissions from stationary industrial sources. Within this framework, process simulations were conducted to generate mass and heat balances, which were combined with key evaluation parameters (e.g., market prices and carbon tax) to construct a comprehensive data platform. These data served as inputs to a nonlinear optimization model incorporating indicators of both economic performance and potential CO2 reduction (PCR). A cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment was employed to account for all direct and indirect CO2 emissions, reductions, and avoidances in the formulation of the PCR indicator. The framework was applied to design an integrated CCUS system capturing 82.2 ton/h of CO2 from a Japanese biomass power plant for methanation, methanol synthesis and geological storage. The optimization results demonstrate that the framework effectively determines the optimal distribution of captured CO2 under varying carbon tax and hydrogen input conditions, enabling development of economically viable and carbon-efficient integrated CCUS systems. For systems utilizing over 30% of captured CO2 for methane production, break-even is only achieved when hydrogen cost drops below $2/kg and carbon tax exceeds $250/ton. Overall, the framework can serve as a strategic tool for supporting CCUS implementation under evolving market and policy conditions.

title: Sustainable valorization of limonitic laterite via phosphoric acid leaching: Selective recovery of nickel and cobalt with Co-production of iron phosphate under atmospheric conditions
abstract: A novel and sustainable atmospheric leaching process using phosphoric acid was developed for the selective recovery of nickel and cobalt from limonitic laterite, with simultaneous conversion of iron into an iron phosphate co-product. Systematic process optimization achieved exceptional metal selectivity, with leaching efficiencies of 97.22% for Ni and 90.88% for Co, while effectively suppressing iron dissolution to merely 1.26%. Through integrated X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of the iron phosphate-rich residue, the underlying mechanism was elucidated: goethite dissolution releases structurally incorporated Ni2+ and Co2+ ions, while the liberated Fe3+ reacts with PO43− from the acid to precipitate as FePO4·2H2O. This precipitation drives a self-reinforcing mechanism by lowering aqueous Fe3+ concentration, further promoting goethite dissolution and acid dissociation. Solvent extraction using HBL110 confirmed efficient recovery of Ni and Co from the leachate. Preliminary hydrometallurgical refining of the residue via sulfuric acid dissolution and ammonia precipitation demonstrated the partial removal of key impurities (Si, Ca, Mg, Ni, Mn) from the iron phosphate product. This work presents a clean, low-energy pathway for the integrated valorization of limonitic laterite, aligning with circular economy principles by enabling selective critical metal extraction and iron by-product synthesis under mild conditions, though further purification of the iron phosphate phase is recommended to enhance overall process sustainability.

title: A novel composite building envelope integrating phase change material gypsum boards and gravity heat pipes: experimental and numerical investigation
abstract: Phase change material (PCM) gypsum boards help balance intermittent solar supply with building heating needs but face practical limitations: passive systems have low heat transfer efficiency, while active systems are complex and costly. Conversely, gravity heat pipes (GHP) efficiently deliver solar heat indoors but, when paired with traditional building materials, lack sufficient thermal storage, resulting in large temperature swings. Furthermore, existing research on combining GHP with building materials is largely simulation-based and lacks systematic real-building validation. To address these issues, this study developed a novel envelope integrating PCM gypsum boards with GHP. Three full-scale experimental huts (PCM-GHP, PCM, reference) were built and tested under passive and active modes. A numerical model was developed and validated to simulate the envelope's long-term performance over the heating season. Experimental results show that, compared to reference hut, the PCM-GHP hut under passive mode drastically improved thermal comfort, reducing the daily integrated discomfort degree of cold (IDDCday) by 98.7% (sunny) and 51.8% (cloudy). Under active mode, it achieved over 30% energy and cost savings, whereas the PCM hut showed savings below 2%. Heating-season simulation confirmed its long-term efficacy, demonstrating a 32.7% reduction in passive mode IDDCday and 36.8% energy savings in active mode compared to the reference hut. Techno-economic analysis indicates a dynamic payback period of 18.6 years for PCM-GHP hut, with significant potential for cost reduction in future large-scale application. This novel envelope offers a promising pathway to clean heating in northern regions, contributing to energy conservation and the achievement of the “Dual-Carbon” goals.

title: Evaluation of sustainable healthcare waste disposal techniques via an interval-valued p,q-rung orthopair fuzzy framework
abstract: Selecting the most sustainable healthcare waste disposal technique is a significant yet complex multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) issue that requires weighing conflicting sustainability criteria and evaluating the pros and cons of alternative disposal methods. However, existing MCDM frameworks often face methodological challenges, including uncertainty arising from subjective judgments, imprecise data, and interdependencies among criteria. To bridge these gaps, this research proposes a novel integrated MCDM framework combining Logarithmic Percentage Change-Driven Objective Weighting (LOPCOW), Step-Wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA), and Alternative Prioritization and Assessment System (ALPAS) under interval-valued (IV) p,q-rung orthopair fuzzy sets (ROFSs) for the first time. The IV-p,q-ROF LOPCOW and IV-p,q-ROF SWARA methods are used to determine the objectivity and subjectivity of criterion weights, while IV-p,q-ROF ALPAS is applied to rank the alternatives. Thus, the IV-p,q-ROF LOPCOW-SWARA-ALPAS framework enables efficient processing of ambiguous information, balanced weighting of subjective and objective criteria, and the calculation of a combined utility value for each alternative based on the ideal and anti-ideal solutions, thereby indicating the model's contributions. The most sustainable healthcare waste-disposal technique is selected based on 12 criteria that address the triple bottom line of sustainability among five non-incineration disposal techniques. The results indicate that occupational health and safety is the most critical criterion, followed by cost-effectiveness and energy efficiency. Furthermore, autoclaving is the most sustainable disposal technique, followed by microwave treatment and plasma pyrolysis. The proposed framework provides practical guidance for policymakers and healthcare decision-makers in addressing the complexities of sustainable healthcare waste management.

title: Long-term evaluation of pollution dynamics in West Lake Taihu, China: Enhanced WQI and TLI models for improved accuracy and management relevance
abstract: Accurately assessing water quality and eutrophication remains a critical challenge in global lake pollution management. Traditional models, such as the Water Quality Index (WQI) and Trophic Level Index (TLI), often rely on expert judgment and outdated guidelines, limiting their adaptability to evolving pollution conditions. This study proposes a novel, reproducible, and comprehensive evaluation framework by integrating Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Factor Analysis (FA) for linear weighting of parameters, using Random Forest (RF) for non-linear validation of weight rankings, and performing consistency checks through exceedance rate and algal density (AD) for management association. West Lake Taihu (WTH), the largest natural pretreatment reservoir of Lake Taihu, was selected as the case study for assessing long-term (2008–2023) pollution dynamics. Results showed that total phosphorus (TP) and total nitrogen (TN) were the dominant factors influencing both water quality and eutrophication, replacing traditional dissolved oxygen (DO) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a). RF and exceedance rate analyses confirmed TP (22.71%) and TN (18.11%) as the primary contributors to WQI, with exceedance rates >80%, while DO showed little influence (<9%) and an exceedance rate below 5%. For TLI, TN and TP contributed 27.02% and 22.67%, while Chl-a exhibited lower contribution (22.28%) and a distinct temporal mismatch. From 2008 to 2023, WQI increased by 27.25% and TLI decreased by 22.70%, indicating substantial improvements in both water quality and eutrophication. However, persistent seasonal and spatial differences disrupted WQI-TLI consistency in spatiotemporal trends. The enhanced WQI model provided more realistic assessments by reducing the influence of stable parameters and emphasizing frequently exceeding ones. The modified TLI model improved the identification of eutrophic zones and periods, enhancing the model's targeting ability and correlating more strongly with AD. Both models also showed higher consistency with external RF outputs, improving their reliability and management applicability. This study demonstrates that the integrated framework, combining data-driven PCA/FA, RF validation and management-related indicators check, significantly outperforms traditional approaches by enhancing accuracy, management relevance, and adaptability for contemporary lake pollution management. It proposes a robust, transferable framework for dynamic freshwater ecosystem management.

title: Exploring an ideal post-consumer plastic waste collection technique for sustainable waste management using a Type 2 neutrosophic number methodology
abstract: The escalating production of post-consumer plastic waste (PCPW) necessitates the selection of the proper PCPW collection methods (PCPWCMs) to mitigate the detrimental effects of this waste on sustainability.
