HANWs served as the reinforcing framework, while the MgCl2-modified biochar matrix provided abundant adsorption sites, synergistically boosting mechanical strength and adsorption capacity. The optimized HBA exhibited 47% higher compressive strength than conventional biochar aerogels and a notable Ni(II) adsorption capacity of 300.65 mg/g, which is 4 times more effective than conventional biochar. Comprehensive characterization confirmed Ni(II) adsorption on HBA follows a synergistic physicochemical process involving ion exchange, surface complexation, surface sedimentation, electrostatic interaction, and pore diffusion. The HANW-reinforced porous architecture not only sustains this multi-mechanistic pathway but also preserves high mass-transfer efficiency and structural stability during successive adsorption cycles. HBA further exhibited strong selectivity toward Ni(II) under competitive conditions, achieving 99.7% simultaneous removal of Ni in actual electroplating wastewater. The reinforced-concrete-like architecture offers new insights for the design of durable, recyclable, and scalable materials for heavy-metal-contaminated wastewater remediation.

title: Towards sustainable consumption? Professional discourses and institutional material arrangements
abstract: Over the past century, global carbon emissions have surged alongside increasing consumption levels, with food, mobility, and housing accounting for the majority of consumption-related emissions. This paper investigates how professional actors discursively frame sustainable consumption in a Danish context, where consumption emissions are particularly high, and sustainability is widely recognized as a priority across businesses, policymakers, and civil society. Drawing on seven focus groups with 52 professional actors from key organizations - including major companies, public authorities, NGOs, and grassroot organizations - the study examines how professional discourses and institutional material arrangements shape and constrain consumption. Our findings show that sustainability is discursively institutionalized across food, mobility, and housing sectors, however with significant variations in terms of how change is perceived. Three discourses are identified: 1) a market discourse centered on economic competitiveness and consumer demand; 2) a system change discourse centered on sufficiency, reductions, and redefinitions of the good life; and 3) a governance mediation discourse centered on experimentation, pragmatism, and political feasibility. These discourses shape how professional actors position themselves in relation to sustainability and how they contribute to the reproduction or destabilization of existing institutional material arrangements that frame consumption patterns. The paper highlights the need for regulatory interventions, experimental projects, and active citizen participation to disrupt unsustainable institutional material arrangements. Strengthening grassroots initiatives through economic, legal, and institutional support can enable systemic change, and a rethinking of governance structures can help unlock pathways toward more sustainable consumption and production. • We apply the concept of institutional material arrangements (IMAs). • IMAs both constrain and enable sustainable consumption and production. • Professional discourses reproduce and destabilize IMAs. • Three key discourses are identified cutting across food, mobility and housing. • Reveals tensions between market logics and sufficiency-oriented change.

title: From maleic to succinic acid: Electrochemical reduction as a game-changer for green electro-refinery schemes
authors: Suelya da S. Mendonça de Paiva
abstract: The selective conversion of maleic acid (MA) to succinic acid (SA) is traditionally achieved by high-pressure catalytic hydrogenation. This route requires external hydrogen and significant energy input. Electrochemical reduction offers a viable alternative. It enables MA-to-SA conversion under ambient conditions and allows mechanistic control through electrode selection and current density. Cyclic voltammetry shows direct electron-transfer reduction of MA and SA on Cu electrodes. Ni displays negligible activity toward MA. Polarization studies indicate that Cu favors MA reduction, whereas Ni accelerates SA reduction. These trends highlight the influence of molecular structure on electrode–substrate interactions. Bulk electrolysis yields selective MA-to-SA conversion with Faradaic efficiencies up to 96 %. High electron-transfer rates are essential to suppress competing pathways. Stability tests reveal that SA undergoes over-reduction at high current densities, particularly on Ni. This finding emphasizes the need to balance productivity with product preservation. Complementary hydrogenation experiments broaden the valorization scope. Residence time and hydrogen availability govern selectivity, ranging from partially hydrogenated intermediates to deeply hydrogenated volatiles. Overall, the results support a dual-path electro-refinery strategy for sustainable SA production. The approach integrates mild electroreduction with controlled deep hydrogenation. It offers a scalable and low-carbon route for incorporating dicarboxylic acids into next-generation chemical and fuel manufacturing. • Copper enables efficient electrochemical reduction of maleic to succinic acid. • Nickel shows negligible activity for MA but favors SA kinetics under polarization. • Bulk electrolysis achieves high Faradaic efficiency under mild operating conditions. • Current density strongly governs selectivity and prevents undesired over-reduction. • Hydrogenation expands valorization, tuning products via residence time and H 2 supply.

title: Integrated process analysis of hydrogen-carbon complementarity between the coke dust high-temperature gasification and coke oven gas to methanol
abstract: Coke dust, a fine particulate solid waste from coke dry-quenching, is currently underutilized, primarily stockpiled or used as low-grade fuel. To address this challenge and enhance resource efficiency, we propose a novel integrated process (HG-CGTM) that couples high-temperature gasification of coke dust with conventional coke oven gas to methanol (CGTM) production. This design leverages hydrogen-carbon complementarity by introducing carbon-rich syngas from coke dust gasification to balance the hydrogen-rich coke oven gas, thereby optimizing the stoichiometry for methanol synthesis. The process was simulated using Aspen Plus and validated against pilot-scale gasification experiments. Comprehensive techno-economic analysis shows that the HG-CGTM process increases hydrogen, energy, and exergy utilization efficiencies by 41.4%, 21.8%, and 21.9%, respectively, compared to the conventional CGTM route. Although the total capital investment and production cost are higher, the integrated process achieves a 16.6% reduction in unit methanol cost and superior profitability, with an internal rate of return of 30.4%. This work demonstrates a viable pathway for high-value utilization of solid wastes, contributing to circular economy and sustainable chemical production.

title: Operationalizing the dual circular hierarchy for post-disaster reconstruction: Two focused comments on Shevchenko et al.
abstract: Shevchenko et al. advance circular reconstruction by linking a dual hierarchy of value recovery and circular rebuilding to the notion of a “circularity potential” indicator. I support this agenda and offer two focused comments. First, the hierarchy would benefit from a crisis-aware decision logic to guide choices under conditions of urgency. Second, the circularity-potential concept would become more useful in practice if expressed through a transparent and auditable calculation. Together, these additions would strengthen the operational value of the framework for post-disaster reconstruction in Ukraine and beyond.

title: Inequality-based compensation for environmental burden transfers in crop trade to promote responsible crop production and consumption
abstract: Crop trade helps reconcile the spatial mismatch between arable land and population, yet it induces regional environmental-economic inequality (REEI). How to guide economic compensation from crop-importing to -producing regions for shifting environmental burdens based on quantified REEI remains insufficiently understood. Life cycle assessment is applied to quantify the multiple environmental impacts of staple-crop production in China. Building on a province-level trade network for disaggregated crops, the REEI driven by trade-induced transfers of environmental burdens and value added is measured to derive responsibility shares for the transferred environmental burdens between trading regions. Integrating responsibility shares with external costs of these burdens entails to establish an interprovincial economic compensation network. Crop trade-driven damage to human health and ecosystems accounts for 26.1% and 25.8% of their respective totals induced by crop production. Over 90% of provincial trading pairs have REEI values in the range of 0–0.5, whereas two pairs show markedly higher values above 1. Rice-related compensation dominates (54.8%), with smaller shares for wheat and maize, and payments flow mainly from Guangdong, Zhejiang, and Sichuan to Heilongjiang, Jiangsu, and Anhui. Compensation payments are designed to fund mitigation measures in crop production, and our findings support transition of crop production and consumption towards responsibility and sustainability.

title: Microalgae growth in reclaimed wastewater treatment plants: an unneglectable water security issue
abstract: Algae not only play a crucial role in carbon sequestration and reduction, but also act as the initiator of water quality deterioration and eutrophication. To date, rare studies have focused on the presence, abundance of microalgae and bacterial - microalgal interactions in reclaimed wastewater treatment plants (RWWTPs). In this study, the bacterial and microalgal community compositions, as well as bacterial - microalgal interactions were investigated in three typical RWWTPs in different seasons. Results showed that not only bacteria but also microalgae were contained in the RWWTP influent, with microalgae exhibiting temporal variations in community. Microalgae, mainly including Bacillariophyta, Cyanobacteria and Chlorophyta existed widely in three RWWTPs. The community compositions of microalgae and bacteria varied with process types, operation parameters, seasons and environmental conditions, etc. Correlation analysis showed that Bacillariophyta, Cyanobacteria and Chlorophyta were commonly positively correlated with Acidobacteriota, Myxococcota, Nitrospirota and Planctomycetota, while Cyanobacteria and Chlorophyta were negatively correlated with Patescibacteria. Notably, Cyclotella, Fragilaria and Synechococcus were detected in RWWTP effluent, which may indicate potential environmental risks such as harmful algal blooms. These results highlight the importance of focusing more on microalgal growth and control in RWWTP monitoring. Moreover, the detection of microalgae in RWWTP and their distribution characteristics across different treatment units suggest the potential feasibility of applying bacterial-microalgal symbiotic system in practical wastewater treatment.

title: Energy-efficient drying of LiFePO4 electrodes via residence time optimization: A temperature and thickness-dependent study
abstract: Electrode drying is the most energy-intensive and the second most time-consuming process in lithium-ion battery manufacturing. Current research mainly focuses on mechanistic analysis and simulations of the drying process, with limited experimental validation. Furthermore, studies investigating the impact of extended drying time (residence time) on electrode performance remain scarce. This study selects electrodes with two thicknesses (100 and 200 μm), dried under two temperature conditions (80 °C and 120 °C) to compare their performance through residence time extension. Results show that at 80 °C, extended residence time improves electrode morphology (reduced cracks, uniform binder distribution and grains) and electrochemical performance, particularly for thick electrodes. In contrast, at 120 °C, prolonged residence time offers marginal benefits and may even reduce cell capacity. Furthermore, the distribution patterns of the three drying stages across varying temperatures and electrode thicknesses is established, and the incremental energy consumption associated with prolonged drying time was quantified. The findings hope to provide a theoretical basis for balancing energy consumption and electrode quality in industrial production, suggesting tailored residence time based on electrode characteristic, drying temperature and Industrial needs.

title: Predicting increased diffuse nitrogen loss from compound extreme precipitations and pollution risk assessment
abstract: The temporal variations of diffuse nitrogen (N) pollution in watersheds primarily depends on the intensity and patterns of precipitation. There remains a gap in clarifying the impacts of compound extreme climates on N loss and quantifying the probability of future high-precipitation impacts on diffuse pollution. Using a well-calibrated hydrological model, copula function, and climate projections under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios (SSPs), the contribution of combined drought/heatwave and heavy precipitation events (DP/HP) on N losses and the risk of diffuse pollution have been assessed and predicted in the upper and middle Wei River Basin (UMWB), which is a new and more refined perspective for assessing the effects of extreme climate. The frequency of single extreme precipitation (EP) events would decrease in the future, while compound DP and HP events are anticipated to increase by 0.18–0.23 and 1.2–4.3 days. During far future period, organic nitrogen (Org-N) loss is projected to increase by 80-180 g/ha, with HP events driving 57%-93% of this increase. The increase in nitrate nitrogen (NO3-N) induced by compound HP events would contribute 40%–52% of the total increase under SSP8.5. The pollution risk assessment based on SWAT-copula method showed that the probabilities of Org-N loss in top 20% would increase by 3.9%, 3.9%, and 4.5% under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 when precipitation was in top 1%. The risk of NO3-N pollution would be higher when precipitation was in top 1% and 5%, especially in cropland. Our results suggested that future climate change will increase nitrogen loss and pollution risks, highlighting the importance and urgency of understanding watershed diffuse pollution responses to compound extreme climates for sustainable nutrient management interventions.

title: Integrated sustainability assessment of hydroponic, aeroponic, and geoponic systems for Acorus calamus cultivation: A life cycle and techno-economic analysis
abstract: Sustainable cultivation systems are increasingly required to reduce environmental impacts and improve resource efficiency in agricultural production. This study conducted a comparative life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis of three cultivation systems, hydroponics, aeroponics, and geoponics, to evaluate their environmental, engineering, and economic performance. Environmental indicators showed that soilless systems significantly reduced several impact categories relative to geoponics. Total carbon emissions per total load output were reduced to 59.18% in hydroponics and 58.96% in aeroponics, compared with the 100% baseline in geoponics. Water depletion potential was also markedly lower in hydroponics (25%) and aeroponics (10%) than in geoponics, indicating higher water-use efficiency. Resource consumption followed a similar trend, with material resource use reduced to 77.31% in hydroponics and 60.79% in aeroponics relative to geoponics. Human toxicity potential was lowest in aeroponics (16.77%), followed by hydroponics (38.40%), while geoponics showed the highest impact. Economic analysis revealed substantial differences among systems. Hydroponics generated the highest gross benefit (592.47 K USD) and net return (490.26 K USD) per production cycle, followed by aeroponics (515.94 K USD gross benefit; 195.50 K USD net return) and geoponics (165.04 K USD gross benefit; 93.77 K USD net return). Sensitivity analysis indicated that lighting electricity was the most influential parameter, where a ±20% change produced the largest variation in carbon footprint, energy demand, and net profit. Overall, hydroponics demonstrated the most balanced sustainability and economic performance, while aeroponics showed superior water-use efficiency but higher energy sensitivity.

title: Hydrogen internal combustion engine CHP in decentralized energy systems: Towards TEA-LCA in an open-source framework
abstract: Hydrogen-based decentralized energy systems (H 2 -DES) are gaining prominence as potential solutions for local decarbonization of heat and power supply. This paper presents a life cycle assessment (LCA) of a H 2 -DES using an internal combustion engine for combined heat and power (ICE-CHP), grounded on a techno-economic analysis (TEA) model implemented in OpenModelica. The study addresses the relative underexploration of H 2 -ICE-CHP technologies in the LCA literature, offering a comprehensive analysis based on real hourly demand data of buildings in Offenburg (Germany), a municipality involved in the Franco-German Interreg CO2InnO project. Scenarios families were developed with varying configurations and dimensioning (PV, wind, battery, H 2 storage). The results of the TEA model were interfaced with the Brightway2 framework for LCA through custom Python-based routines and manual implementation. Monte Carlo simulations and global sensitivity analysis were conducted in the Activity-Browser software to evaluate uncertainty and parameter influence. Results show that impacts are strongly dependent of the scenario family and selected system boundaries. The H 2 sub-system components showed modest impacts to climate change but not in other environmental categories, while PV significantly affected environmental assessment overall, depending on excess electricity consideration. These findings highlight the necessity of careful system design and boundary comparison in policy and environmental reporting. This work also contributes methodologically towards the development of an open-source TEA-LCA workflow. While still requiring manual data adaptations, it forms the foundation for future automation efforts. The approach offers actionable insights for local policymakers and researchers aiming for transparent, reproducible, and multi-criteria sustainability assessments of H 2 -DES.

title: Performance-efficiency trade-off for multiple reagent dosage regulation using lightweight deep reinforcement learning in full-scale drinking water treatment plant
abstract: Reagent dosing process is critical for drinking water treatment plants (DWTPs) to provide safe water, while its traditional regulation suffers from delayed responses to water quality fluctuations, excessive reagent cost and unstable effluent quality due to reliance on perceptual experience. Data-driven machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches have emerged to address these issues, but have overlooked the trade-off between performance and efficiency in previous applications and failed to autonomously explore optimal dosage strategies beyond historical patterns, hindering the edge deployment and cost reduction desired by DWTPs. Here, a lightweight deep reinforcement learning (LDRL) approach that integrates pre-trained DL-based prediction and RL-based optimization was developed and deployed into the proposed intelligent reagent dosage regulation framework. The comprehensive analysis regarding the performance-efficiency of state-of-the-art (SOTA) ML/DL models across different architectures identified the Transformer architecture to be well-suited for DWTP process modeling and demonstrate that the enhanced temporal concentration improved performance rather than data scale. The proposed LDRL approach reduced reagent dosages by 17.16-46.92%, avoided dosage volatility by 38.46-52.86%, while maintaining effluent turbidity of 0.06-0.14 NTU and residual Al of 0.03-0.12 mg/L during the field deployment in a full-scale DWTP. These results provide a robust and transferable data-driven framework for intelligent reagent dosage regulation in DWTPs.

title: A novel model to assess the hydrogen storage capacity in depleted gas reservoirs considering dynamic geo-bio-chemical reactions
abstract: Depleted gas reservoirs are widely recognized as promising candidates for large-scale, long-duration underground hydrogen storage due to their low cost, substantial capacity, and well-characterized geology. However, hydrogen's high reactivity introduces complex geo-bio-chemical interactions with residual hydrocarbons, minerals, and indigenous microorganisms, potentially causing hydrogen loss, impurity generation (e.g., H2S), and pore-space blockage. These processes are often overlooked in existing simulators, which typically focus on transport and mineral reactions while neglecting microbial effects. To address this gap, this study develops a three-dimensional, two-phase, multi-component simulator that explicitly couples dynamic geo-bio-chemical processes, incorporating a double-Monod microbial growth model to quantify microbial impacts on reservoir properties and hydrogen loss. A dynamic numerical model, calibrated with real reservoir data, is applied to multiple operational scenarios, including seasonal cycling and long-term storage. Results show that longer injection–production intervals significantly enhance reservoir energy recovery and hydrogen recovery efficiency. In particular, a five-year cycle limits hydrogen loss to below 1% over ten years and achieves a recovery ratio of 91.4%, outperforming seasonal strategies. These findings confirm the strong potential of depleted gas reservoirs for strategic hydrogen storage and suggest that longer operational cycles should be prioritized, with implications for capacity evaluation and evidence-based site selection in support of the energy transition.

title: Integrating catalytic performance and life cycle assessment for a γ-valerolactone biorefinery design from biomass
abstract: γ-Valerolactone (GVL) is a renewable platform molecule with applications as a greener solvent and fuel additive. This study couples catalytic experiments, process simulation, and cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) to guide lower-impact GVL production from lignocellulosic residues via levulinic acid (LA) hydrogenation. Vapor-phase continuous tests over Cu–Ni/SiO 2 catalysts used LA diluted in isopropanol (IPA) with H 2 co-feed; under these conditions, IPA acts as a solvent and contributes as a hydrogen donor alongside molecular H 2 through transfer-hydrogenation pathways, improving conversion and stability versus IPA-free operation. The best formulation (6Cu–14Ni/SiO 2 ) sustained 79% average LA conversion and 91% GVL selectivity over 50 h. Experimental results parameterized an Aspen Plus model to generate mass and energy requirements for an attributional LCA with selective system expansion (functional unit: 1 kg GVL) across three Colombian residues. Baseline impacts (9.30 ± 1.55 –11.37 ± 2.14 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 GVL) were dominated by fossil IPA and process heat. Switching to bio-based IPA, green H 2 , and renewable heat reduced impacts by up to 87%. Sensitivity analysis showed a near-linear dependency of impacts on LA conversion (SR > 0.9), highlighting catalytic efficiency as the primary lever for environmental improvement. Overall, coupling catalytic performance with LCA enables early identification of hotspots and supports low-carbon design choices for bio-based chemical production. • Integrating LCA into biorefinery design supports low-carbon chemical pathways. • LA hydrogenation over CuNi/SiO 2 can deliver relevant GVL yields over time. • LCA identifies isopropanol and fossil heat as main environmental hotspots. • Green routes reduce climate impact by up to 87% and eutrophication by 96%. • Sensitivity analysis identified LA conversion as the dominant environmental driver.

title: Carbon intensity assessment and fuel pathway optimization under the international maritime Organization's new regulations
abstract: Stringent climate targets under the International Maritime Organization's (IMO) revised greenhouse gas strategy are propelling the shipping sector from operational efficiency toward fuel-based decarbonization. The energy efficiency operational indicator (EEOI) and GHG fuel intensity (GFI) are core metrics for tracking the sector's contribution to the Paris Agreement. Using a scalable voyage-based emissions model (VoySEIM), this study quantifies EEOI and GFI across multiple scales and develops a cost-optimization framework to evaluate fuel transition pathways for existing fleets under varying policy incentives. Fleet-wide EEOI declines to 10.73 g CO2/t·nmile in 2021, meeting IMO targets, while the 2022 global average GFI remains at 93.65 CO2eq/MJ, above the 2008 baseline, highlighting the urgent need for accelerated fuel-side mitigation and targeted policy support. Optimization results demonstrate strong policy dependence of transition pathways. Low ZNZ rewards (<150 USD/tCO2eq) favor electro-fuel substitution without engine retrofits, whereas higher rewards shift the cost-optimal strategy toward ammonia, the preferred long-term option for existing fleets. Increasing incentives mainly affects absolute cumulative compliance costs while leaving the relative ranking of pathways largely unchanged. These findings underscore the importance of stable lifecycle-based incentives for fuel transition and support IMO policy and fleet decarbonization planning.

title: Corrigendum to “Assessing microbial internal drivers of nitrogen–cycle functional potential in lakeside wetlands: insights from random forest modelling and co-occurrence network analyses” [J. Clean. Prod. 541 (2026) 147519]

title: Drivers and barriers of transformation towards a sustainable food system in Warsaw
abstract: Despite the growing body of research on sustainable food systems (SFSs), empirical and locally grounded studies examining the drivers and barriers of urban food system (FS) transformation in Central and Eastern European cities remain limited, particularly from the dual perspectives of citizens and organized initiatives. Urban SFSs have significant potential to improve both public and planetary health. Therefore, this study aims to identify the drivers and barriers to a SFS in Warsaw from the perspectives of households and transition initiatives, following the SysOrg project framework. Data were collected using a mixed-methods approach, combining a household survey (HHS) (N = 449) and semi-structured interviews (SSI) with local initiatives (N = 5), across three key dimensions: sustainable and healthy diets, organic food and farming, and food waste reduction. The results indicate that all three domains share common barriers, including budgetary constraints, limited awareness and knowledge, insufficient institutional support, and data gaps, with outcomes significantly influenced by gender, age, income, and education. Key drivers identified include awareness-raising, improved availability and infrastructure, and policy support, particularly at the municipal level. The findings highlight the interconnectedness of the three project perspectives—diet (D), organic food and farming (O), and food waste (W)—and identify critical leverage points for sustainable transformation, such as targeted policies and incentives, green public procurement, education, and supportive food infrastructure. This study addresses the existing knowledge gap in urban FS research and provides actionable insights for policymakers, municipalities, and local initiatives in Warsaw. Furthermore, it serves as a preliminary resource for other European cities engaged in the development of food policies, particularly for less-explored municipalities in the field of SFS that share similar dynamics with the Polish capital, such as those within the Visegrad Group.

title: Research on the decision-making of green and high-quality agricultural product production at the front end of the industrial chain: From the perspective of cooperation between cooperatives and farmers
abstract: Green agricultural production is an inevitable trend in the development of modern agriculture, and it is also the key to achieving sustainable development of the ecological environment and ensuring the quality and safety of agricultural products. However, how to encourage farmers and cooperatives at the front end of the industrial chain to adopt green production behavior is the core challenge faced in promoting green agricultural development. Therefore, this article aims to explore the evolutionary trend of green production behavior strategy choices of farmers and cooperatives under the influence of different levels of government green subsidies and market green demand, and provide corresponding suggestions and countermeasures for the government. Based on the cost-benefit theory, this article constructs a decision-making model for the production behavior of green and high-quality agricultural products, and uses NetLogo for strategy evolution simulation analysis. The simulation results show that both market green demand and government green subsidies have a significant positive effect on the green production behavior of farmers and cooperatives. The impact of market green demand on the green production behavior of farmers and cooperatives has a lag in the initial stage, but it has a strong sustainability, as it is transformed from external driving forces into sustained endogenous driving forces. Government green subsidies have a significant impact on farmers' green production behavior in the initial stage, but the system may exhibit weaker sustainability as time progresses, and the impact effect in the later stage is slightly weak.

title: Sediment-mediated coupling of hyporheic exchange and land use drives macroinvertebrate community structure
abstract: Macroinvertebrates are among the most sensitive and informative biological indicators of river ecosystem health, yet the environmental mechanisms shaping their distribution remain unclear in human-impacted watersheds. The respective and combined contributions of catchment land-use and hyporheic exchange are poorly quantified, despite their complementary roles in regulating water quality and benthic habitat. In this study, 15 sites in the Weihe River Basin were surveyed during autumn 2023 to examine spatial patterns of land use and hyporheic exchange flux (Qv) and their links with macroinvertebrate communities and water physicochemical parameters. A causal framework based on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) guided the integration of Variance Partitioning Analysis (VPA), Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to quantify independent and joint effects and to identify pathways shaping community composition. A total of 53 macroinvertebrate species (1,354 individuals) were identified. The community was dominated by pollution-tolerant taxa (55% relative abundance), with Chironomidae as the most abundant group (700 individuals). VPA indicated that land use and Qv contributed 20.07% and 4.95% to community variation, respectively. Although water physicochemical parameters explained the largest proportion (26.57%), the combined effects of these three drivers accounted for 64.5% of the total variation. GAMs further quantified the relative contributions of these drivers to the Shannon Diversity Index (SDI) and the Hilsenhoff Biotic Index (HBI). Water quality, land use, and Qv explained 56.0%, 47.2%, and 7.6% of SDI variation, and 60.2%, 55.6%, and 6.3% of HBI variation, respectively, together accounting for over 86.25% of the total variance, indicating that multi-factor interactions exert a stronger influence on macroinvertebrate communities than individual factors. SEM demonstrated that both land use and Qv indirectly influenced macroinvertebrate assemblages through modifications of key water physicochemical variables (p < 0.05), particularly TDS, DO, and TOC. In addition, land-use changes regulated Qv via sediment particle-size feedbacks (p < 0.001), with farmland expansion increasing coarse sediment inputs and promoting Qv, whereas forest and grassland cover stabilized riverbed substrates and reduced Qv. Overall, the results uncover a sediment-governed cascade in which land-use patterns reshape Qv and water-quality conditions, ultimately organizing macroinvertebrate community structure. Clarifying this cross-scale pathway provides a more coherent scientific basis for watershed management, underscoring that maintaining riverine ecological integrity requires coordinated actions on landscape configuration and sediment regimes to indirectly moderate subsurface hydrological conditions.

title: Unveiling the ESG performance and green innovation: The moderating roles of business climate and executive green cognition
abstract: This study extends institutional theory and upper echelons theory by examining how internal and external factors jointly influence corporate green innovation. It investigates the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings and green innovation, focusing on the moderating roles of business climate and executive green cognition. Drawing on panel data from Chinese listed firms in the CSMAR and CNRDS databases, combined with provincial business climate data from the “Evaluation of Doing Business in Chinese Provinces 2023” report, this study covers 870 firm-year observations over 2018–2021 and applies fixed-effects ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models to investigate the primary and moderated relationships, along with robustness tests and heterogeneity analyses. The analysis incorporates a range of external factors—including market dynamics, government support policies, legal and regulatory frameworks, and prevailing cultural norms—alongside internal firm-level factors, notably executives' awareness of and commitment to environmental issues. The results show that higher ESG ratings significantly promote green innovation, aligning with institutional theory that firms adopt socially endorsed practices to meet stakeholder expectations. However, the governance environment and executive green cognition unexpectedly weaken this positive relationship. For example, firms with high ESG ratings may initially emphasize compliance-driven strategies, delaying green innovation. Over time, as ESG practices are integrated, green innovation becomes a key growth driver, particularly for firms with low profitability and high operational risks. These findings highlight the need to balance compliance with innovation incentives, offering insights for policymakers and stakeholders to promote sustainability transitions.

title: Sustainable titanium-tannic acid metal-phenolic network for aqueous Vanadium(V) removal: performance, mechanism, and practical potential
abstract: Vanadium (V) contamination in aquatic environments represents an escalating environmental and public health concern, highlighting the urgent required for sustainable, efficient, and biocompatible remediation strategies; however, the development of such solutions remains technically challenging. A titanium-tannic acid-based metal-phenolic network (Ti-TA MPN) adsorbent with a distinctive networked, porous, and amorphous structure was developed through an environmentally benign self-assembly process in the present work, and its V(V) adsorption performance and mechanism were systematically investigated through batch adsorption experiments and advanced analytical techniques. The pore structure and surface area of Ti-TA MPN were tunable with the molar ratio of Ti to tannic acid (Ti/TA), ranging from 5:1 to 25:1. Among the synthesized materials, Ti-TA (25), corresponding to a Ti/TA ratio of 25, showed a specific surface area of 223.3 m2 g−1 and achieved a maximum V(V) adsorption capacity of 60.84 mg g−1 at neutral pH 7, with adsorption behavior fitting the pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm models. The V(V) removal efficiency is pH-sensitive, an acidic environment is more favorable, and the removal process was enhanced in the presence of divalent cations (Ca2+ and Mg2+) but inhibited by PO43− and F−. The primary mechanisms controlling V(V) adsorption involve surface coordination, electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and divalent cationic bridging. Notably, the adsorbent effectively decreased V(V) concentrations in both river water and acid mine drainage to below regulatory limits. Furthermore, life cycle and techno-economic evaluations affirm its environmental sustainability and economic feasibility, highlighting its practical promise for V-contaminated water treatment.

title: Do green innovation subsidies deliver everywhere? Evidence from environmental patenting in EU regions
abstract: The mobilization of public funding to promote green innovation is becoming increasingly central to governmental agendas, as it is widely regarded as essential for tackling climate change and sustaining long-term economic competitiveness. Yet, systematic analyses of how different instruments interact in contributing to these goals and what effects they produce across different territorial contexts remain limited. To address this gap, the paper investigates how EU green research and innovation (R&I) subsidies influence environmental patenting patterns across European regions, using a Double/Debiased Machine Learning framework based on post-double-selection LASSO. More specifically, the analysis focuses on two major funding instruments: Cohesion Policy and the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation (Horizon). The findings show that both programmes had a positive conditional effect on regional green patent growth between 2013 and 2021. However, the results also point to partial substitutability between the two instruments, as the marginal return of one funding source decreases with the intensity of the other. This suggests the presence of diminishing returns rather than a zero-sum dynamic. Moreover, these conditional effects are not uniform across regions. The heterogeneity analysis indicates that positive outcomes are largely concentrated in more developed and innovation-intensive regions, whereas less developed and innovative regions showed no significant patenting response to either instrument during the period analyzed. Sectoral composition further moderates these dynamics. Overall, these findings suggest that the effectiveness of green innovation subsidies depends critically on regional absorptive capacity, highlighting the need for appropriate enabling conditions to be in place.

title: Leveraging industrial symbiosis benefits from multi-source heavy metal hazardous waste co-reutilization with industry kilns for anthropogenic metal recovery: Methods and applications
abstract: Driven by growing anthropogenic metal demand, heavy-metal-chlorine-containing hazardous waste treatment in China has shifted from simple detoxification to resource recovery. In this context, symbiotic co-processing with metal-rich industrial residues in existing furnaces is gaining increasing attention. This approach exploits high-temperature metallurgical conditions to recover volatile metals from hazardous waste while stabilizing residual components. Yet tools to assess technological benefits and optimize regional industrial symbiosis networks are still lacking. This study develops a bottom-up optimization framework that links micro-level technological feasibility with macro-level policy scenarios to support industrial symbiosis between the hazardous waste and industrial sectors. The framework integrates material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, techno-economic assessment, multi-objective optimization, and scenario analysis, and is demonstrated through a case study of co-processing incineration fly ash and blast furnace slag in China. Results indicates that, compared with standalone blast furnace ash treatment, co-processing with fly ash enhances zinc and lead recovery by 14-23%, yielding carbon benefits of 317.10-411.5 kg CO2eq/ton, as well as economic benefits of 577.4-673.2 yuan per ton. Furthermore, under the optimal adjacent-province symbiosis scenario, scaling this practice nationally would yield a one-third increase in both total co-processing capacity and carbon benefits, compared to the business-as-usual scenario limited to within-province symbiosis. While promising, these macro-level improvements are accompanied by increased waste transport risk. This study provides a practical, reality-grounded planning tool for hazardous-waste industrial symbiosis networks in developing countries, addressing the growing reutilization demand for hazardous waste.

title: The role of repair in the circular economy: Enhancing sustainability assessment through an integrated emergy - LCA framework
abstract: The rapid growth of electronic waste highlights the need for strategies that extend product lifespans and lessen environmental pressures. This study develops an integrated Emergy - LCA framework, combining Emergy Synthesis (EmA) and Life Cycle Assessment, to evaluate smartphone repair sustainability within a circular economy context. By linking donor-side and receiver-side perspectives, the approach captures both the environmental investment embodied in products and the impacts throughout their life cycle. Using a representative smartphone model, the analysis focuses on display replacement and examines how extending lifespan affects environmental performance. Results show that repair preserves about 80.86% of the embodied environmental investment, with an emergy efficiency (ηrep) of 0.24. LCA findings consistently show reductions in impacts across categories such as climate change, resource depletion, and water use. Importantly, the findings reveal that sustainability benefits strongly depend on the duration of post-repair use, with non-linear improvements as lifespan increases. The study advances current research by applying an integrated EmA-LCA approach to repair processes and demonstrating that repair effectiveness depends not only on the intervention but also on continued product use. These results reinforce repair as a key strategy for improving resource efficiency and support policies and design practices that promote longer product lifespans.

title: Multi-objective planning of renewable power-to-ammonia system under wind-solar resource-deficit events: Hybrid scenario generation and value-at-risk
abstract: Renewable power-to-ammonia (RePtA) plants face economic challenges due to wind-solar resource intermittency and deficit episodes. To address this, this study proposes a multi-objective stochastic programming framework that integrates hybrid scenario generation (normal and deficit scenarios), Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), and supply reliability indicators. To make reliability interpretable from an engineering perspective, this paper defines and operationalizes a set of ammonia-specific supply indices that quantify the frequency, magnitude, and severity of production shortages. The model endogenously incorporates oxygen co-product revenue and carbon emission reduction benefits, and yields Pareto frontiers of economic–reliability trade-offs. A case study indicates that oxygen sales and carbon emission reduction materially improve economics and reduce tail risk, with revenue offsetting 12%–17% of the levelized cost of ammonia. Scenario analysis reveals pronounced reliability degradation under deficits: relative to normal scenarios, the expected duration of production loss rises from single-digit hours to 60 h and the unserved ammonia mass increases from 10 t to 200 t in severe deficit scenarios, while the instantaneous shortage ratio is capped at 46% by process constraints. The expected annual profit increases nearly linearly with the carbon price and reaches a break-even point at about 142 CNY/t-CO2. This work provides a reproducible methodological framework for risk-aware and reliable RePtA planning, quantifying how carbon policy, by-product monetization, and storage coordination jointly improve both economics and supply security.

title: Can photovoltaic retrofit redefine heritage value? Practical and theoretical evidence from meta-analysis and multi-criteria evaluation of 133 international case studies over 35 years
abstract: This paper investigates the role of photovoltaic (PV) systems in accelerating the energy transition of built heritage through the comparative analysis of 133 international case studies realized between 1991 and 2026. Covering a wide range of climatic zones, regulatory frameworks, building functions, and heritage protection levels, the study adopts a mixed-method research framework that integrates archival analysis, policy review, technological assessment, quantitative energy evaluation, and critical architectural interpretation. The case studies enable the identification of performance patterns, temporal trends, and critical innovation thresholds, offering an evidence-based understanding of how aesthetic, technical, and energy performance goals negotiated in practice the trade-offs between decarbonization policies, technological feasibility, cultural values, product innovation, and social acceptance of PV adoption in historical environments. From a regulatory perspective, 47% of the analyzed buildings are formally listed, while others are subject to indirect heritage constraints, demonstrating that PV integration is not confined to weakly protected contexts. Case studies span from the 14th to the 20th century, and PV adoption is most frequent in residential, religious, office, and rural buildings, while cultural, educational, and institutional uses confirm the growing penetration of PV systems into public and highly symbolic building types. Crystalline silicon cells dominate due to reliability and availability, while glass-glass, frameless, and chromatically treated panels emerge after 2018 as enablers of higher architectural and energy integration. The PV fraction covering annual primary energy consumption ranges from approximately 10% to 149%, with a mean value of 60.7% and a median of 58.5%. More than 42% of the cases achieve coverage above 50%, while 21% reach full or surplus energy balance (≥100%). The temporal analysis identifies three evolutionary phases: experimental applications (1991-2001), visually subordinate and concealed solutions driven by conservative guidelines and early EU directives (2002-2017), and context-sensitive architectural integration (2018-2026) aligned with higher energy targets and technological maturation. Building on these findings, a data-driven design taxonomy was structured around emerging retrofit paradigms ( concealment, mimicry, transparency, and expression ) as guidance to inform future policy strategies, technological development, decision-making and design practices. This approach challenges and reinterprets the traditional principles of “ authenticity ” and “ reversibility ” from architectural conservation, adapting them to the language and design logic of PV retrofit. • Dataset of 133 international cases on photovoltaic retrofit of heritage buildings. • Cross-disciplinary framework balancing heritage, technological and energy measures. • Photovoltaic design taxonomy derived from real-world implementations.

title: Arsenic recovery by UV/sulfite/iodide system: Dual roles of carbonate/bicarbonate
abstract: Advanced reduction processes (ARPs), which produce hydrated electrons (eaq−) and hydrogen radicals (H•), are promising for arsenic resource recovery. However, its effectiveness in carbonate-rich systems is unclear because carbonate and bicarbonate effects on reduction efficiency and speciation remain understood. To clarify the underlying molecular mechanisms, this research examined the effects of carbonate and bicarbonate on the efficiency of removing arsenic (As) and reactive species distribution in the UV/sulfite/iodide system. The results indicate that both carbonate and bicarbonate alter the system pH, thereby affecting arsenic reduction efficiency. Moreover, under specific experimental conditions, both ions shift the recovery product from As(0) toward As2O3. The available evidence suggests that the effects of carbonate and bicarbonate are not identical and may involve distinct dominant pathways under the examined conditions. Carbonate-derived CO32− may react with •OH to form CO3•-, which is proposed to abstract hydrogen from HAsO42− and generate AsO43−; the latter may then be more readily reduced by eaq−, thereby facilitating the conversion of As(V) to As(III). Subsequently, the pH increase induced by carbonate inhibits the further reduction of As(III) to As(0). As for bicarbonate, high concentrations directly quench eaq− and suppress the reduction of As(III) to As(0). In contrast, low concentrations of bicarbonate may act as hydrogen donors, promoting H• formation and establishing a cooperative eaq−/H• reduction pathway that facilitates arsenic reduction, although the calculated barrier differences are most evident for the initial reduction step. Overall, these findings provide a basis for understanding arsenic remediation and resource recovery in carbonate-containing water matrices.

title: Simulation of coupled thermal decomposition, mass transfer, component transformation and pressure evolution during sintering of engineering spoil-based ceramsite
abstract: With accelerating urbanization, the generation of discarded soil remains extremely high, posing issues related to resource wastage and environmental pollution. Transforming discarded soil into sintered products such as masonry, bricks, and ceramsite is an effective strategy for its efficient resource utilization. However, discarded soil has a notably complex composition, and the unsteady decomposition of multiple components during sintering tends to induce abnormal pressure, subsequently resulting in structural damage to the products. Taking engineering spoil-sintered ceramsite as the research focus, this study ascertained the key reactions during sintering, including moisture evaporation, mineral dehydration, organic matter decomposition, and carbonate decomposition, via XRF/XRD compositional analysis and TG-DTG analyses. Building on these findings, a "thermal decomposition-mass transfer-component transformation-pressure evolution" multiphysical field coupling model was established. After the key parameters were estimated using the Nelder-Mead algorithm and the least squares method, the maximum deviation between the model's predicted values and the experimental TG curve is 1.29%, while that with the DTG curve is 6.91%, demonstrating satisfactory accuracy. By systematically investigating the intrinsic coupling mechanisms among decomposition temperature, gas evolution, and pressure variation, this study reveals that ceramsite is at high risk of damage in the temperature ranges corresponding to mineral dehydration and carbonate decomposition; the internal pressure of ceramsite presents a center-high and edge-low distribution pattern; and convection serves as the dominant mechanism for gas transport. Through examining the pressure response characteristics of ceramsite under varying sizes, permeabilities, and heating rates, the key factors for sintered product preparation and process control were defined. A precise slow-heating strategy tailored to the decomposition peak temperature ranges was proposed, which ensures that the peak internal pressure of ceramsite stays within the safety threshold while substantially reducing the preparation cycle, thereby providing theoretical and technical support for the efficient engineering-scale production of engineering spoil-sintered ceramsite.

title: A novel natural thermal-cooling cycle treatment for hemp fibers degumming
abstract: Hemp fiber is a renewable, lightweight, eco-friendly material. To meet the application requirements, the degumming treatment is necessary prior to its use. Traditional degumming methods often suffer from high costs and heavy pollution, which impedes the hemp industry's sustainability. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel green degumming method: natural thermal-cooling cycle treatment (NTCT). It utilizes thermal shock from alternating cold-heat cycles to break the fiber-resin interface. Combined with mechanical processing, this achieves separation of the two components, resulting in degummed fibers. Characterization of mechanical properties and microstructure of NTCT-degummed hemp fibers confirmed that the optimal degumming efficiency was achieved at 30 days of NTCT (The temperature differential of approximately 10 °C was maintained during the NTCT). At this optimal stage, the process achieved a peak mass loss of 13.47‰, indicating effective gum removal. Crucially, the fibers successfully retained robust structural integrity, with the tensile strength slightly increasing from 485 MPa (untreated) to 490 MPa. Additionally, NTCT significantly reduced volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions by 82%, meeting the safety requirements for high-value applications. In stark contrast to traditional chemical degumming methods that heavily rely on harsh alkalis and generate toxic wastewater, this process leverages natural climate conditions, requires absolutely no chemical reagents, and simplifies workflows. It effectively addresses the high pollution and cost issues associated with traditional methods, offering an innovative and highly promising green processing solution for hemp fibers.

title: Generating seamless hourly XCO2 maps over Asia: A CatBoost modeling approach integrating FY-4A GIIRS and OCO-2/3 (2021-2022)
abstract: As global climate change intensifies, accurate characterization of the spatiotemporal distribution of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide (XCO2) is essential for advancing climate change research and improving understanding of regional carbon sources and sinks. However, existing XCO2 datasets lack sufficient temporal resolution for continuous regional monitoring because of the revisit frequency of polar-orbiting satellites. To address this, we obtained a seamless, hourly XCO2 dataset over Asia (2021-2022) by combining high-spatial-resolution OCO-2/3 and high-temporal-resolution radiance from the Geostationary Interferometric Infrared Sounder (GIIRS) on the geostationary satellite FY-4A using a CatBoost model. The model demonstrated robust performance in random-sample validation (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 1.06 ppm) and 10-fold cross-validation (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 1.06 ppm). Comparison with TCCON ground-based observations showed reasonable agreement (R2 = 0.74, RMSE = 0.98 ppm). The predicted dataset also shows high consistency with existing daily-averaged products. Notably, this dataset captures the diurnal variability of XCO2, revealing fine-scale temporal variations that conventional daily-averaged products cannot resolve. Moreover, a case study of the Beijing Winter Olympics revealed strong correlations between XCO2 and criteria air pollutants, suggesting that carbon-pollution control could be coordinated. By leveraging GIIRS thermal infrared channels, this dataset extends XCO2 monitoring beyond the daytime constraints of shortwave infrared sensors and shows potential for round-the-clock observation, thereby providing a scientific basis for refined emission-reduction assessments.

title: Waste activated sludge derived biopolymer amelioration for desert sand: Impact on moisture retention, vegetation growth and microbial community
abstract: Extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are complex, high molecular-weight polymer mixtures secreted by microorganisms involved in organic matter degradation during the activated sludge wastewater treatment process. In this study, EPS extracted from wasted activated sludge (WAS) was used as a material to assess improvement in moisture retention and fertility of desert sand. Compared to untreated sand (30.87%), the water retention capacity of sand treated with 0.1% EPS increased to 75.51%, representing approximately 2.4 times enhancement. Pot experiments revealed that EPS addition promoted ryegrass growth: plant height increased up to 93.70%, shoot fresh weight increased up to 304.36%, and chlorophyll content increased up to 94.68% relative to the CK group. Metabolomics analysis indicated that EPS induced pronounced metabolic changes in ryegrass root exudates, with 44 shared DEMs (38.26%) identified between the two comparison groups. EPS addition significantly enriched Glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway, facilitating rapid cell division and improving antioxidant defense mechanisms. The dominant microbial genera of 0.1% EPS group were Stutzerimonas (12.75%) and Pseudomonas (10.87%), which are popular soil probiotics that participate in the nitrogen cycle. The yield of EPS extracted from WAS achieved 0.25 kg EPS/kg SS. Moreover, the economic evaluation results indicate that the EPS extraction cost in this study was 0.58 USD/kg EPS, which is substantially lower than the current market price of Xanthan gum (1.50-4.00 USD/kg). In general, the present study suggested that EPS extracted from WAS could be applied as a potential sand amelioration agent for improving moisture retention and fertility of desert sand.

title: From monitoring to scenario-based predictive planning: What-If rollouts for a commercial broiler-house microclimate
abstract: Commercial broiler production is increasingly operated as sensor-informed process in which ventilation-related actions shape indoor air quality, thermal stability, and operational efficiency. A persistent gap is that many analytics pipelines stop at point forecasting or single-variable alerts, while deployment decisions are made in discrete multi-hour windows and must be reliable across flock episodes and seasonal drift. This study develops a decision-scale framework for scenario-based predictive planning in one commercial broiler house, aiming to reduce high-ammonia exposure time without incurring disproportionate thermal penalties or excessive control effort. Operational records from one commercial broiler house were organized into four consecutive production cycles (306 days; 7344 hourly observations) and transformed into 6-h decision blocks. Season-adaptive, quantile-based thresholds were used to derive an operational RiskState label from thermal load and ammonia, while an interpretable Adaptive Agro-Environmental Efficiency Index (AAEEI) combined thermal burden, air-quality burden, and control burden into bounded efficiency score. RiskState identification was learned using a bagged-tree classifier and evaluated with leave-one-cycle-out testing to reflect strict episode-level transfer. A multi-output neural surrogate was trained for 6-h-ahead forecasting of ammonia (NH3_next6h), indoor–outdoor temperature gradient (dT_next6h), and AAEEI_next6h, enabling multi-step what-if rollouts under hypothetical inlet interventions. Cycle-wise evaluation showed high accuracy can coexist with modest class-balanced performance, highlighting the importance of macro-averaged sensitivity for risk prevention. Short-horizon forecasts provided useable fidelity for coupled endpoints, and rollout experiments revealed regime-dependent trade-offs where ammonia reductions may be offset by thermal-gradient penalties and reduced efficiency. A MATLAB dashboard was developed as an output to translate forecasts and rollouts into an auditable what-if scenario for practical decision support.

title: The mineral constraint: Energy transition under supply chain bottlenecks and greenflation
abstract: The global decarbonization agenda tacitly assumes a perfectly elastic supply of green capital, overlooking the physical rigidities of the upstream mineral supply chain. This paper develops a Supply-Chain DSGE model that endogenizes Kydland-Prescott style Time-to-Build delays to quantify the macroeconomic transmission of “The Mineral Constraint.” We identify a perverse general equilibrium mechanism termed the “Mineral Drag”: due to the gross complementarity between capital and mineral inputs, a positive green demand shock triggers a 42% spike in the shadow price of minerals, causing realized green output to paradoxically contract in the transition's initial phase. Calibrated to recent empirical elasticities, the model implies a cumulative gross macroeconomic welfare cost equivalent to 4.2% of lifetime consumption, alongside the emergence of structural stagflation. We demonstrate that this supply-side bottleneck breaks the “divine coincidence” of monetary policy, suggesting that strict inflation targeting exacerbates welfare losses. Optimal policy requires “looking through” transient greenflation and pivoting from demand-side subsidies to supply-side coordination.

title: Assessing low-carbon hydrogen feedstock deployment for refinery hydroprocessors in renewable-constrained regions using a scenario-based TEA-LCA framework
abstract: With tightening global climate policies, petroleum refineries face increasing pressure to transition toward cleaner technologies. However, the existing literature overlooks the unique challenges faced by regions with limited renewable resources, such as South Korea, Japan, and Central Europe, which must depend on imported clean fuels. To address this gap, this paper develops an integrated techno-economic and life cycle assessment framework that evaluates three low-carbon hydrogen pathways—domestic blue hydrogen and imported blue and green ammonia—for Korean refinery hydroprocessing units from 2025 to 2035. The framework estimates the CO2 avoidance cost under three scenario-based policy conditions: (1) Minimal Adoption, representing weak incentives and slow technological development; (2) Blue Bridge, supporting blue hydrogen-based decarbonization; and (3) Green Transition, reflecting ambitious climate policies and rapid deployment of green hydrogen. The findings indicate that domestic blue hydrogen achieves the lowest CO2 avoidance cost ($190/t CO2) with total emission reduction of 997 kt/y. In contrast, imported green ammonia exhibits the highest cost ($745/t CO2) and lower emission reduction. The analysis shows that this performance gap can be narrowed by incorporating photovoltaic waste recycling (38.4% cost reduction) and captured CO2 valorization (40.5% cost reduction). Scenario analysis reveals that, under the Blue Bridge scenario, both blue hydrogen pathways attain CO2 avoidance costs below $100/t CO2 by 2032, whereas the Green Transition scenario reduces green hydrogen CO2 avoidance cost to $163/t CO2 by 2035. Overall, the results highlight that while blue hydrogen offers a cost-effective near-term decarbonization pathway, accelerated deployment of green hydrogen is necessary to offset the technological and environmental limitations inherent to fossil-based hydrogen systems.

title: Global water scarcity assessment integrating quantity and quality across multiple spatiotemporal scales
abstract: Water scarcity is a growing global challenge, influenced by both water availability and quality. Conventional assessments often focus on water quantity alone and operate at a single spatiotemporal resolution, overlooking not only the critical role of water quality in determining resource usability but also the substantial sensitivity of scarcity estimates to spatial and temporal scale. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of water scarcity by integrating both quantity and quality across multiple spatial (from grid cell to basin) and temporal (annual, seasonal, monthly) scales from 2000 to 2019. Under the combined water quantity and quality scheme (WSqua + WSpol), severe scarcity overwhelmingly dominates at coarser spatial resolutions, affecting approximately 75% of first-order basins, 70% of second-order basins, and 65% of third-order basins. Even at the grid cell scale, nearly 50% of cells face severe scarcity, with the exposed population exceeding 5000 million during peak periods. In contrast, quantity-only assessments (WSqua) yield much lower exposure at the first-order basin scale (about 2000 million people), rising to nearly 5000 million at the grid cell scale, while moderate and significant scarcity become more prominent. The inclusion of water quality constraints significantly increases both the extent and severity of water scarcity, particularly at coarser scales, and identifies much larger areas and populations at risk compared to assessments based solely on water quantity. As spatial resolution increases, the difference between the two assessment approaches diminishes. Water quality constraints further amplify the imbalance between water availability and demand, particularly at finer spatial scales and during the growing season. Overall, these findings highlight the substantial impact of water quality on water scarcity risk and population exposure, emphasizing the necessity of high-resolution, integrated assessments to inform effective water resource management and policy.

title: Eco-friendly plant-enzyme-induced mineralization coatings for corrosion protection of low-carbon steel
abstract: This study presents an eco-friendly approach for corrosion protection of low-carbon steel using plant enzyme-induced mineralization. Soybean urease (crude or purified) catalyzes CaCO3 precipitation into organic-inorganic hybrid coatings, greatly enhancing corrosion resistance. The enzyme-mediated process involves urease catalyzing urea hydrolysis, which increases the local alkalinity of the solution, promoting the binding of Ca2+ and carbonate ions, and facilitating CaCO3 mineral deposition. The resulting mineral layer provides a dense inorganic barrier, effectively blocking corrosion agents, while the organic components in the coating act as a cementing phase, enhancing the cohesion and adhesion of the coating, thereby improving its durability. Electrochemical tests, including electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization, demonstrate that the mineralized coatings significantly improve corrosion resistance. The CSU-induced coating exhibits the most effective suppression of anodic and cathodic currents, followed by the purified soybean urease-derived coating, both of which perform markedly better than the uncoated steel. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveal that crude urease-based coatings form larger, cemented biogenic microspheres, while purified urease-based coatings consist of finer, denser calcite crystals. This plant-enzyme-mediated mineralization strategy offers a green, controllable, and scalable alternative to microbial-based corrosion protection methods, with significant potential for sustainable manufacturing and green material development in the field of environmentally friendly corrosion protection.

title: A machine learning framework for discovering carbon-peaking pathways: Coordinated optimization of 3D urban form and microclimate to regulate building carbon emissions
abstract: Rapid urbanization leads the building sector to embrace a strategic role in energy conservation and carbon reduction. While the urban 3D compact form influences building carbon emissions by modulating the microclimate, existing studies lack a systematic quantification of the “form–microclimate–carbon emissions” pathway and effective spatial optimization strategies. This study developed a 1-km gridded database of urban 3D compact form indicators (NVCI), Urban Heat Accumulation (UHA), and building energy consumption carbon emissions (BECCE) from 1995 to 2020 in Xiamen. A Bayesian-parameter-convolution-optimized Random Forest model (RFBPC) was proposed to analyze the pathway. The results showed that (1) the RFBPC model consistently demonstrated superior performance over RF and XGBoost across all test cases, with testing R2 values reaching as high as 0.993 (vs. 0.879 for RF) and RMSE reductions of up to 75% (from 0.583 °C to 0.144 °C); (2) UHA exhibited a significant mediating effect between NVCI and BECCE, accounting for 13.88% of the variation in BECCE; (3) the optimal compactness transition path was identified using a geographical detector, showing that shifting NVCI from Level 5 (high compactness) to Level 2 (low compactness) could yield BECCE reduction of 401.74 kg per grid unit; and (4) scenario projections indicated that such compactness optimization could advance the building sector's carbon peak in Xiamen by 2.56 years. This study provides a quantifiable and actionable modeling framework and planning reference for coastal cities to achieve carbon-peak goals.

title: Sustainable catalyst design: Magnesia slag-doped MS-LDHs fabricated via pulsed laser trapping for efficient and green Cr(VI) adsorption
abstract: Silicon thermal process magnesium slag, a primary byproduct of the Pidgeon process for magnesium production, generates over 1,080,000 metric tons annually worldwide. Although the Basel Convention has categorized waste slag from non-ferrous metal smelting as a significant controlled solid waste, a considerable quantity of magnesium slag continues to be disposed of in landfills globally. This practice not only inflicts severe environmental damage but also squanders valuable metal resources contained within hazardous waste magnesium slag. In this study, we successfully synthesized MS-LDH nanosheet materials as adsorbents utilizing hazardous waste magnesium slag through a chemical branch hydrothermal synthesis method. Owing to their abundant active chemical adsorption sites, these materials demonstrated outstanding removal performance for the typical heavy metal ion Cr(VI), achieving an adsorption capacity as high as 193.4 mg g−1. They attract significant attention due to their potential to remove heavy metal ions from wastewater. Within 60 min, the residual Cr(VI) concentration can be reduced to the μg·L−1 level, thereby meeting World Health Organization standards. Atomic-scale characterization and calculations based on density functional theory, coupled with reinterpretation through the lens of molecular dynamics, have revealed the microscopic mechanisms of Cr(VI) adsorption by MS-LDH nanosheets. This method presents an efficient and valuable recycling strategy for managing hazardous waste magnesium slag.

title: Assessment of the environmental impact of using a robot for underground mining of mineral resources - results of the ROBOMINERS project
abstract: The revolution in automation and robotics is a fact today. The ROBOMINERS project is moving in this direction. The aim of the project is to develop a small mining robot that will be able to explore hard-to-reach deposits completely autonomously. Currently, tests of the robot's locomotion in the mine, as well as mineralogical, geophysical sensors and production tools have been successfully completed. Since it is generally accepted that replacing humans with robots is economically justified, in the article asks whether there is also a justification for the impact on the environment. For this purpose, a variant environmental impact assessment (EIA) of the use of the robot in a mining environment was carried out. The three variants differed in the degree of development of the facility, geological structure and depth of occurrence. Compared to a conventional underground mine, the robot will be much more environmentally friendly. It will deliver only the richest ore to the surface, which will result in several times less waste. Surface destruction, noise emission and environmental pollution will be irrelevant to existing forms of land development. European legislation is included, which is constantly aimed at protecting the heritage that is our planet. The provisions of the laws of the European Union and its selected members were analysed: Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Portugal. The assumption is that the robot could replace the construction of an underground mine, which always has a significant impact on the environment. The result is very optimistic and at this stage of work it may open new opportunities for sustainable mining in Europe and around the world.

title: Carbon- and lifecycle-aware tariff design for solar-battery prosumers: A mean-field modeling framework for cleaner electricity production
abstract: Rooftop solar paired with behind-the-meter storage can either reduce or shift environmental burdens, depending on how tariffs reward charging, discharging, and exports. This study examines when decentralized prosumer battery operation aligns with decarbonization and lifecycle resource efficiency in a California-calibrated mean-field modeling framework. The model combines reflected battery-state dynamics, hourly carbon intensity, and a convex battery-wear proxy, and it distinguishes posted residential tariffs from a scenario-specific dynamic settlement adder. Flat-rate and time-of-use cases therefore follow exogenous posted tariffs, while endogenous load feedback appears only in a stylized dynamic-settlement scenario used to diagnose congestion feedback. We evaluate six policy scenarios using daily attributable CO 2 emissions, integrated battery-wear proxy, electricity-bill savings, and duck-curve metrics. Conventional time-of-use pricing increases emissions by 3.2% relative to the flat-rate benchmark because low off-peak prices synchronize charging in high-carbon nighttime hours. Carbon-intensity pricing reduces emissions by 22.1% but raises modeled battery wear by 2.1%. Combining carbon-intensity pricing with a lifecycle-preserving incentive delivers the strongest joint outcome in the base calibration: emissions fall by 24.6%, the integrated wear proxy falls by 13.6%, and electricity-bill savings reach $2.78 per prosumer-day. Carbon-aligned tariffs shift charging toward lower-emission hours, while lifecycle incentives moderate excessive cycling. In this calibration, the strongest joint emissions–wear outcome requires carbon-aligned tariffs together with lifecycle-preserving incentives.

title: A transformer-reinforcement learning framework integrating acoustic thermometry for multi-pollutant prediction and control in a full-scale WtE plant in China
abstract: Accurate prediction and control of pollutant emissions remain a major challenge in waste-to-energy (WtE) systems due to strong thermal fluctuations and complex fuel heterogeneity. This study develops an integrated framework coupling acoustic thermometry (ATM) with deep learning and reinforcement learning to achieve sustainable and resource-efficient incineration operation. A Transformer-based model was constructed to process multimodal operational data, including high-resolution ATM features, for real-time prediction of PCDD/Fs, NOx, and HCl emissions across full operational conditions. Incorporating ATM substantially enhanced predictive performance, increasing R2 values to 0.86, 0.64, and 0.59 for PCDD/Fs, NOx, and HCl, respectively, and reducing MAE to 0.0029 ng I-TEQ/Nm3, 7.6 mg/Nm3, and 0.21 mg/Nm3. Feature-importance analysis identified ATM as a dominant contributor, especially for NOx. Coupling the predictor with a Deep Q-Network enabled real-time optimization of SNCR, air distribution, and grate feed, achieving 71%, 33%, and 40% emission reductions for PCDD/Fs, NOx, and HCl, respectively. Moreover, ammonia consumption decreased by ∼10%, yielding both environmental and economic benefits. The proposed framework enhances emission control and reagent efficiency, contributing to cleaner production and circular sustainability in WtE operations.

title: Heatwaves intensify microplastic-driven greenhouse gas emissions from soil by modulating microbial abundance
abstract: As global warming intensifies, heatwaves are occurring more frequently, while microplastic (MP) levels in soil continue to rise. The combined stress of heatwaves and MPs could significantly impact soil ecosystem health. In this study, we simulated heatwave conditions and incubated soil with conventional polyethylene (PE) and biodegradable polybutylene succinate (PBS) MPs for 60 days. The results demonstrate that the combined effects of heat and MPs promoted soil greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, primarily regulated by changes in the abundance of dominant soil microbial populations. The impact of heat and MPs on soil properties and microbial community structure was more pronounced under high-temperature conditions. Specifically, the combination of heat and MPs significantly reduced cellulase and urease activities but increased sulfatase activity. These changes altered soil dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and microbial diversity, and significantly impacted microbial functional genes involved in critical ecosystem processes, particularly carbon fixation and degradation, nitrogen cycling, and phosphorus cycling. The potential of MPs to enhance soil CO2 and CH4 emissions under heatwave conditions underscores the need to assess the environmental risks of plastic residues in agricultural soils.

title: Achieving system-level decoupling in intensive agriculture via zoning-based cleaner production strategies: Insights from the Huang-Huai-Hai plain
abstract: Achieving high agricultural productivity without exacerbating climate change remains a major challenge. Comprehensive regional assessments of the yield–soil carbon–emission nexus are still limited. This gap obscures the “green paradox” of high-input farming, in which carbon sequestration benefits can be accompanied by rising nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. To quantify these hidden dynamics, we integrated multi-source datasets from 2000 to 2023 within a validated DNDC-Random Forest (DNDC-RF) framework. Compared with a standalone DNDC model, this hybrid framework enables more efficient regional-scale simulation, while compared with purely data-driven machine learning models, it retains process-based constraints on crop growth and biogeochemical cycling, thereby improving the simulation of the yield–soil carbon–emission nexus. Consequently, we successfully mapped the spatiotemporal synergies and trade-offs across China's Huang-Huai-Hai Plain. Our pixel-level quadrant analysis reveals an overarching baseline synergy across 68.8% of the region, where management-driven biomass gains have translated into a robust soil organic carbon (SOC) sink. Crucially, phase-based evaluations unveil a dynamic decadal shift: as regional soils approach carbon saturation, this SOC synergistic footprint predictably contracted from 83.2% (2000–2010) to 62.0% (2011–2023). Despite maintaining a regional net greenhouse gas (GHG) sink, a critical “hidden” environmental penalty persists, with 51.0% of high-yield croplands functioning as severe N2O emission hotspots. Machine-learning-driven attribution unequivocally identifies synthetic nitrogen application as the overwhelming engine dictating 73.4% of these N2O fluxes, whereas SOC accrual is governed by a bipartite climate-management equilibrium. In these areas, productivity gains remain coupled with reactive nitrogen losses. Consequently, N2O accumulation remains a key bottleneck to deeper system-level decoupling.
