In this work, various multilayer AlCrBN/AlCrN coatings (AlCrBN sublayers alternately deposited with AlCrN sublayers with bilayer numbers of 1, 5, 10, and 20, denoted as T1, T5, T10, and T20, respectively) were fabricated by cathodic arc ion plating to investigate the relationship between their microstructures and high-speed dry cutting performance of titanium alloys. Results showed that the multilayer architecture significantly improved coating adhesion (Lc2 up to 71 N) and impact fatigue resistance compared with the monolayer coating. The T10 coating exhibited the lowest wear rate (1.21 ± 0.11 × 10−16 m3 N−1m−1) and a reduced friction coefficient (0.38 ± 0.02) at room temperature, whereas T20 retained superior hardness after post-annealing. High-speed dry cutting (HSDC) tests (without cutting fluid) showed that the T10 multilayer coating presented the best comprehensive cutting performance, TEM analysis of the worn rake face of the T10 coated insert further confirmed the superior structural stability of the coating. This was attributed to its optimal adhesive strength of 71 N (Lc2), excellent impact fatigue resistance, strong interfacial enhancement effect and the ability to maintain the structural integrity under thermo-mechanical loading.

title: Visualization approach on the industrial hydrogen-enriched blast furnace for low-carbon ironmaking
abstract: Injecting hydrogen from the tuyere of the blast furnace (BF) is one of the most viable green-steel innovations for traditional BF ironmaking. However, the black box characteristic of the BF complicates the direct assessment of hydrogen's impact on fossil fuel replacement and the intricate events occurring within the furnace. This study employed a novel 2-D digital twin technology for an industrial hydrogen-enriched BF, establishing a coke-ore layered structure that facilitated distinct chemical reactions in the two solid layers of the BF shaft, while enabling the mixing of the two-phase solids throughout their descent. Based on the mathematical model considering mass and heat transfers, and chemical reactions, the impact of hydrogen content on the physical and chemical alterations was examined. The calculation domain covers the industrial scale region of BF from the lower throat to the bosh. The final results indicate that as the quantity of hydrogen injection increases from 0 to 40 and 100 m3/thm, (1) the carbon emissions decrease by 7.5 and 31.6 kg/thm, respectively; (2) The reduction of hematite accelerates by 19.98% and 25.61%, respectively; (3) The reduction of magnetite (Fe3O4→FeO) surpasses its production (Fe2O3→Fe3O4) during the same period, and the reduction of magnetite totally accelerates by 4.21% and 5.07%, respectively; (4) The wustite generates (Fe3O4→FeO) more than it consumes (FeO→Fe) simultaneously, resulting in a 65.71% and 99.92% deceleration in reduction, along with an enhancement of 4.43% and 9.68% in iron production, respectively; (5) The coke consumption at the shaft does not follow the expected trend of monotonic attenuation with the increase of hydrogen injection’ due to the complicated competition reactions in furnace. In conclusion, this research presents a digital and visual methodology for understanding and improving the hydrogen-enriched low-carbon ironmaking process.

title: Evaluation and optimization of water-land intermodal transportation routes of engineering spoil
abstract: The off-site transportation of engineering spoil faces multi challenges, i.e., high transportation cost, tight schedule, traffic safety hazards, and environmental pressures. The water-land intermodal transportation is an effective way to tackle with these challenges, especially in areas with well-developed waterway network. However, there is limited scientific standards and methods to comprehensively evaluate the existing water-land intermodal routes and optimize the inferior routes. Existing research had limited focus on the related aspects, including the evaluation indicator system, optimization model, and optimization algorithm. Therefore, this study proposed an AHP based evaluation model consisting of eight evaluation indicators to assess the performance of the intermodal routes of engineering spoil. In the proposed indicator system, a dynamic indicator, i.e., road congestion level, was novelly proposed to be estimated by random forest algorithm. Then, a multi-objective optimization model considering cost, comprehensive transportation performance and carbon emission, was established based on NSGA-II, aiming to optimize the inferior route(s). Through a case study in Guangzhou, the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation and optimization model was verified. Nine water-land intermodal routes were evaluated. Then, the worst-performing route was optimized through the proposed multi-objective optimization model. A Pareto front containing 24 solutions was obtained by NSGA-II. Compared with the original route, the optimization solutions have achieved significant improvements in cost (45.96% less), comprehensive transportation performance (33.92% better), and carbon emission (59.60% less). Theoretically, the proposed evaluation and optimization model provided methodological contribution to the related research field by integrating the strengths of AHP and NSGA-II. In practical, this study addressed the challenges of current urban C&D waste transportation in cost, efficiency, safety, and environmental impact.

title: Research on remote sensing ecological index prediction based on deep learning—Taking the application of long short-term memory neural network in Yili prefecture as an example
abstract: Ecological monitoring is often limited by the lag in post-event assessment, while predicting future ecological conditions is crucial for proactive environmental management. Therefore, we developed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to predict the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for the study area in 2025 and employed the Shapley Additive Interpretation (SHAP) method to explain the relative contributions of natural and anthropogenic factors. Studies show that drastic land-use change reduces prediction accuracy; therefore, we introduced a regional correction mechanism based on Bayesian conjugate priors to integrate land-use information into the deep learning prediction. This method was applied to the Ili region of Xinjiang, China, and performed well compared to measured data from 2020. Furthermore, its predicted regional average index for 2025 is consistent with the persistence indicated by the Hurst index. The study shows that ecological foundation and precipitation are the main positive drivers of future ecological quality, while high temperatures, soil drought, and intensive urbanization and grazing activities will reduce ecological quality. The results of the global bivariate Moran's index indicate a spatial correlation between land use change intensity and model residuals; areas with greater change are more likely to be adjacent to areas with larger prediction biases. Furthermore, we introduced a confidence parameter to measure the relative confidence between prior and predicted values and determined the optimal setting for balancing goodness of fit and robustness. Our research not only improves the model's predictive accuracy in areas of rapid land use transition, but also integrates spatial planning with ecological prediction. The findings support policymakers in anticipating multiple possible ecological outcomes when developing different regional planning pathways.

title: On the dynamics of the municipal separate waste collection: The case of Italy
abstract: The transition toward circular economy targets requires effective monitoring of waste-management performance at the level where services are actually organized and financed. This paper analyzes the dynamics of separate source collection of municipal waste across Italian municipalities over the period 2012–2021. Using a novel panel dataset covering nearly 7000 municipalities, we estimate β-convergence models to assess whether municipalities with lower initial levels of separate collection tend to improve more rapidly over time. The empirical analysis combines panel regressions with fixed effects and a set of structural controls capturing socio-economic characteristics, financial resources devoted to waste management, and technical efficiency in service provision. The results indicate the presence of conditional convergence in separate source collection. While unconditional convergence and conditional convergence with no fixed effects are estimated to be relatively slow, the speed of adjustment increases substantially once municipality-specific characteristics are taken into account. This finding suggests that municipalities adjust relatively quickly toward municipality specific steady states, reflecting persistent structural differences in local waste-management conditions. Additional results show that higher technical efficiency and greater per-capita expenditure on waste management are associated with faster improvements in collection performance. From a policy perspective the results of our analysis, faster speed of convergence than previously documented and the importance of unobserved characteristics at the municipal level, provide evidence of more persistent dynamics that may call for place based intervention.

title: From barriers to better work: Strategic insights on barriers to job quality for web-based gig workers
abstract: The web-based gig work (WGW) provides flexible employment opportunities and access to the global markets. However, several barriers obstruct gig workers' job quality. Existing literature inadequately examines the interconnected nature of WGW and offers limited understanding of platform strategies and regulatory environment. This study addresses these gaps by developing a hierarchical model of job quality barriers to demonstrate their interrelationships and interdependencies in WGW. A mixed-method approach is implemented in three phases, integrating expert insights through focus group discussions, fuzzy Delphi method, and FISM–MICMAC analysis. This investigation led to the selection of the twenty-one barriers, structured into an eight-level hierarchical model. The regulatory gaps, platform capitalism, and algorithmic domination were found to be the fundamental barriers that drive and reinforce the dependent barriers, including work-life imbalance, technostress, insecurity and emotional challenges. Findings offer insights for advancing research and theory in WGW. These insights can help regulators, platforms and clients understand barriers to ensuring job quality and strategically address these barriers for developing sustainable platform strategies and effective regulatory environment.

title: The limits of “Win–Win” transitions: Understanding tensions between resource nationalism and just transitions
abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) underpin clean energy and defense technologies, and recovering REEs from coal-related wastes is widely cast as a “win–win” that advances resource security, energy transitions, remediation, and regional development. Using a framework of the four tenets of energy justice (procedural, recognitional, distributional, and restorative justice), this paper interrogates the “win-win” claim by examining how resource nationalism and just transitions interact in U.S. efforts to extract REEs from coal ash, tailings, and acid mine drainage. Existing scholarship treats resource nationalism and just transitions as analytically separate. This paper addresses that gap by synthesizing both literatures and using a case study of rare earth element (REE) extraction from mining waste to examine their tensions in practice. Using a qualitative case study design, the analysis draws on 22 semi-structured interviews with expert stakeholders across government, academia, industry, and civil society. Findings show that national security and competitiveness concerns strongly shape research agendas and early implementation decisions, often privileging state-led priorities over community participation and transparency. Stakeholders identify risks that costs and environmental burdens will fall disproportionately on local communities and that site selection will prioritize economic viability over restorative justice needs. The study shows justice outcomes depend on explicit policy design. • Resource nationalism shapes REE extraction decisions across the innovation cycle. • Resource nationalism does not inherently conflict with just transition goals. • Tensions emerge across procedural, recognitional, distributional, and restorative justice. • Win–win outcomes require policy design to constrain nationalist priorities. • Competing narratives create risks of climate obstruction.

title: Nano-biochar enhances energy taxis of Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and the bio-utilization of minerals and Cr(VI)
abstract: Nano-biochar (NBC) is recognized as an effective mediator for microbial extracellular electron transfer (EET). However, its specific role in regulating microbial energy taxis toward insoluble minerals and toxic soluble electron acceptors remains unexplored. In this study, it was demonstrated through swim plate and capillary assays that NBC effectively mediated the tactic response of Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 toward ferrihydrite (Fh) and hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Among the tested variants, NBC pyrolyzed at 600 °C (NBC600) exhibited the optimal mediating efficacy. Its abundant redox-active quinone groups facilitated the bacterial energy taxis, expanding the migration area diameter (at 50 mg/L) by 1.3 to 1.6 times compared to other variants. Furthermore, for the soluble Cr(VI), energy taxis represented a dynamic metabolic trade-off. While 1.0 mg/L Cr(VI) suppressed migration by 75.3% compared to 0.1 mg/L due to cytotoxicity, NBC addition alleviated this stress primarily through physical sequestration. This intervention improved the energetic cost-benefit balance, restoring migration by 226.3% and boosting cellular ATP production by 25.7%. NBC therefore dynamically facilitates microbial energy taxis, offering a mechanism to support the survival of electroactive bacteria in contaminated environments.

title: Enhancing sustainability in zinc electrowinning: Pre-oxidation modification of Pb-Ag electrodes for improved performance and reduced energy consumption
abstract: Conventional Pb-Ag anodes for zinc electrowinning suffer from high oxygen evolution overpotentials and severe galvanic corrosion. To address this, an innovative pre-oxidation strategy was developed that electrochemically modifies Pb-1wt.%Ag alloys in a Pb(II)-NaOH solution (0.1 mol/L Pb(II), 3 mol/L NaOH, 35 °C), constructing a multi-component PbO/α-PbO2/Ag interfacial layer. This seed layer directs in-situ formation of a hybrid β/α-PbO2 coating during operation, with XRD/SEM-EDS confirming Ag doping expands β-PbO2 (110) interplanar spacing by 0.02 Å – an unignorable enhancer of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. Electrochemical evaluations, including cyclic voltammetry (CV), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and Tafel analyses demonstrate that the modified PbOn@Pb-Ag electrodes exhibit enhanced catalytic activity (335 mV reduction in OER overpotential) and corrosion resistance (96.3% lower corrosion rate (3.35 vs. 89.77 mm/a)). During zinc electrodeposition, the modified electrode demonstrated a 100 mV reduction in tank voltage compared to the conventional Pb-Ag anode. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a hybrid β-PbO2 and α-PbO2 layer, which offers superior catalytic and corrosion-resistant properties. These findings suggest that this surface modification technique not only improves electrode performance but also contributes to energy efficiency and sustainability in zinc electrowinning operations, aligning with the principles of cleaner production.

title: Advancing industrial-scale biogas production through cassava processing integration: From process water recovery to optimized multi-substrate digestion
abstract: Cassava processing industries generate substantial organic waste contributing to underutilized biomass streams that compromise energy efficiency in agricultural production systems. Cassava (Manihot esculenta) wastewater typically contains 8000–20,000 mg/L COD, whereas solid residues, such as peels and onggok, contain 15–50% total solids and a C/N ratio of 25–35, making them as highly suitable substrates for biogas production. This study introduces an integrated biogas production strategy that transforms cassava waste into a valuable energy resource through advanced multi-substrate anaerobic digestion (AD) and optimized parameters control. The system was implemented in three identical digesters (30 m diameter × 16 m height each) with total production rate of 72,000 Nm3/day. A closed-loop water management system was also implemented by recycling starch-rich process water to the digesters, simultaneously reducing freshwater consumption and increasing organic loading rate for enhanced biogas production. Stable anaerobic process conditions were observed at total alkalinity capacity (TAC) when ranged from 1850 to 3535 mg CaCO3/L, volatile organic acids (FOS)-to-TAC ratio up to 0.24, and pH between 6.83 and 7.57, which corresponded to controlled VFA accumulation and consistent methane production. By integrating diverse cassava fractions including starch, meal, fiber, and solid waste, methane content was significantly enhanced from 53.98 to 61.74%, compared to single-substrate digestion. Outlier removal using Z-score approach retained 62.4% of industrial-scale data, ensuring that subsequent analysis for optimization modeling was based on representative and reliable observations. Employing Response Surface Methodology (RSM), the multi-substrate approach optimized methane production, achieving a peak methane content of 62.39% under precisely controlled conditions (FOS 365 mg HAc/L, TAC 2771 mg CaCO3/L). Model validation through ANOVA confirmed RSM regression terms were statistically significant (F-value: 105.14, p-value <0.0001, R2 = 0.9563) with an overall desirability score of 0.801, indicating strong predictive reliability. The improved resource management system coupled with optimized multi-substrate AD and its significant methane quality improvements signal a promising pathway towards sustainable and decarbonized industrial energy systems.

title: Climate dynamics and air quality interactions: Machine learning analysis of diurnal temperature range drivers in three major Bangladesh cities
abstract: Satellite-derived land surface temperature diurnal range (LST-DTR), computed as the difference between MODIS daytime and nighttime LST, acts as a meaningful proxy for surface radiative dynamics in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study employed three machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Decision Tree) integrated with SHAP importance analysis to quantify the impacts of black carbon (BC), PM2.5, aerosol, and albedo on LST-DTR across three major Bangladesh cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi. Satellite-derived MODIS and MERRA-2 data (2001-2023) were analyzed using 5-fold cross-validation, yielding moderate yet stable model performance (R2 = 0.35-0.43; RMSE = 2.04-2.51). SHAP analysis showed BC as the dominant predictor in all three cities (SHAP importance: 0.94-1.59), highlighting its key role in urban land surface thermal dynamics through radiative absorption and surface albedo modification. Albedo emerged as a key secondary factor (0.30–1.27), ranking highest in Rajshahi, where it nearly matched BC, while Aerosols ranked second in Dhaka and Chattogram (0.27–0.94), and PM2.5 had the weakest influence (0.08-0.35). The dominance of BC over PM2.5 in LST-DTR modulation suggests that current air quality policies, which primarily focus on particulate matter, may overlook the most critical driver of urban land-surface thermal variability. The study provides evidence for targeted actions: encouraging diesel particulate filters, updating kiln technology, urban greening with high-albedo vegetation in fast-growing zones, and cool roofing with reflective materials. These findings inform evidence-based environmental policies for sustainable urban development in rapidly expanding South Asian cities.

title: A framework for assessing material Circularity: Integrating key performance indicators across the building life cycle
abstract: Material Circularity (MC) is increasingly recognised as a critical strategy for reducing resource depletion, minimising construction and demolition waste, and promoting sustainable practices in the built environment. Effective assessment of MC requires integration across the Building Life Cycle (BLC), with Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) providing measurable insights into material selection, design strategies, sourcing, construction, use, and end-of-life processes. Despite growing interest, current literature lacks a comprehensive, stage-specific framework linking MC criteria and KPIs, leaving practitioners with limited tools to operationalise circularity across all BLC stages. Thus, this study aimed to develop a framework for assessing MC across the stages of the BLC. Under an interpretivist philosophy, using a qualitative choice, the Delphi technique was applied over three rounds with 21, 18 and 17 experts respectively, followed by code-based content analysis to refine criteria and ensure practical applicability. The study identified six BLC stages: Design, Material Sourcing, Construction, Use, End-of-Life, and Beyond-the-Life, and established 10 Main Criteria with 32 Sub-Criteria linked to 40 KPIs. Key findings include reframing material specification as circular material selection, introducing adaptive reuse and closing cycles as new main criteria, and aligning KPIs such as recoverability, predictive maintenance, and supplier engagement to lifecycle stages. The proposed framework enables stage-wise evaluation of circular practices, supports data-driven decision-making, and enhances accountability in MC implementation. This study contributes to the industry by offering a practical assessment tool, to academia by advancing lifecycle-integrated MC evaluation, and to society by promoting sustainable resource flows, reducing material waste, and supporting environmentally responsible construction. • Framework links MC criteria and KPIs across six Building Life Cycle stages. • Delphi method with experts refines 10 criteria, 32 sub-criteria, and 40 KPIs. • Introduces adaptive reuse and closing cycles as new MC assessment criteria. • Supports stage wise evaluation for measurable and accountable MC practices. • Framework offers scalable applicability beyond Sri Lanka to other contexts.

title: Optimizing water-nitrogen management mitigates GHG emissions: microbial mediation across soil oxic and hypoxic interfaces
abstract: Over half of soil organic carbon and nitrogen are stored in subsoils deeper than 20 cm, and water-nitrogen management would stimulate the conversion of these buried nutrients into greenhouse gases (GHGs). Microorganisms are pivotal drivers underlying GHG conversion process, however, the specific microbial mechanism in soil profile remains unclear. Here, we conducted a field investigation and field experiment to investigate microbiome-driven effects on GHGs across soil oxic and hypoxic layers under the optimized water-nitrogen management, including irrigation regime (water-saving irrigation vs. flooding irrigation), irrigation water (aquaculture water vs. fresh water), and fertilizer dosage (reduced vs. traditional). Results showed that optimizing water-nitrogen management reduced nitrogen input and irrigation water volume by 3.7% and 17.6%, and effectively mitigated soil methane, carbon dioxide, and nitrous oxide by 52.1 ± 11.3%, 16.2 ± 6.2%, and 17.4 ± 5.4%, respectively. The optimized management improved soil oxidation-reduction potential and carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, and further downregulated microbial factors promoting GHGs. Specifically, optimizing water-nitrogen management preserved soil bacterial diversity, but the relative abundance of taxa associated with GHG-related functions was reduced by 1.5% in oxic layer and 56.7% in hypoxic layer. Moreover, optimizing water-nitrogen management resulted in reduced complexity and interspecies competition within bacterial networks in oxic layer and keystone networks in hypoxic layer. For microbial functions, genes associated with GHG production significantly decreased by 11.1%∼35.1% in hypoxic layer, and the related enzyme activities decreased by 11.4%∼27.6% in oxic layer and 16.2%∼40.1% in hypoxic layer. Noticeably, the specific microbial driving mechanisms on GHGs varied with soil layers. In the oxic layer, bacterial diversity, co-occurrence patterns, and enzyme activities promoted GHG emissions, whereas in the hypoxic layer, keystone taxa and microbial functional genes related to GHGs played a dominant role. Overall, our findings emphasized the importance of optimizing water-nitrogen management in regulating soil microbial traits and mitigating GHG emissions.

title: A green approach to photocatalysis: Silk-sericin-exfoliated MoS2 modified silk fabric for degradation of doxorubicin and textile wastewater
abstract: The treatment of pharmaceutical pollutants and textile wastewater has become increasingly important because these contaminants persist in the environment and pose risks to ecosystems and human health. Recently, photocatalysis has surfaced as a compelling strategy to address this critical issue. However, most photocatalytic systems rely on suspended powder catalysts that are difficult to recover and are often evaluated in simplified model solutions, thereby limiting their practical application. Furthermore, sustainable methods for incorporating photocatalysts into reusable, biodegradable substrates are underinvestigated. This study presents a novel biopolymer-based nanocomposite, silk fabric modified with molybdenum disulfide (silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric) as a scalable and environmentally sustainable alternative. This composite demonstrates potential as a photocatalytic agent for degrading both textile effluents and pharmaceutical substances, exemplified by the antineoplastic drug doxorubicin hydrochloride (DOX.HCl). Under optimal conditions, the silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric composite efficiently degrades DOX.HCl (94.32%) in just 30 min and degraded textile effluent (99.4%) within 90 min using advanced oxidation process (AOPs). The impacts of catalyst dosage, pollutant concentration, and oxidant level were investigated, and the system exhibited pseudo-first-order kinetics. To assess its practical application, the photocatalyst was evaluated in the presence of wastewater components, including dissolved salts, competing inorganic ions, and organic surfactants. These conditions slowed the reaction rate, but the catalyst maintained a clear and consistent degradation trend, suggesting high tolerance to matrix interference and suitability for real-world effluent conditions. We further examined the impact of scavengers on the degradation rate and determined that superoxide radicals (O2•-) primarily govern the degradation capacity, while hydroxyl radicals(•OH) serve as the principal pathway-controlling reactive oxygen species (ROS). This study shows that the silk-sericin/MoS2-coated fabric is a robust photocatalytic platform capable of addressing pharmaceutical contaminants and complex textile wastewater.

title: Mechanism of deep and selective sulfate removal from high-concentration CaCl2 solutions via porous interfacial deposition on calcium-modified carbon
abstract: Sulfate accumulation in industrial effluents severely impairs the production of high-quality calcium chloride (CaCl2), a high-value product with strong market adaptability whose economic benefits can well offset sulfate removal costs. Developing sulfate-selective adsorbents for high-concentration chloride systems remains a technical bottleneck, and herein, a calcium-modified porous biomass composite (ACCA) was synthesized via mechanochemical planetary ball-milling to address CaO agglomeration and poor stability. FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, TGA, and XPS confirmed ACCA has a well-developed porous structure with abundant Ca–O, C=O, and O–H groups. Calcium ions, as the intrinsic component of CaCl2 brine, were used as the core to enhance the positive interfacial charge of ACCA without introducing exogenous impurities, ensuring the purity of treated brine for high-quality CaCl2 preparation. ACCA achieved 84.874% sulfate removal in real 38∼40% CaCl2 brine, with highly dispersed Ca2+ capturing SO42− via electrostatic and complexation interactions against high-concentration Cl− interference. Kinetic, isotherm, TGA, and point-of-zero-charge (PZC ∼12.33) analyses confirmed that sulfate removal was dominated by chemical adsorption on a heterogeneous surface, which overcomes the high ionic-strength inhibition of traditional ion exchange and is suitable for continuous industrial processes. Post-adsorption studies confirmed the key role of Ca-O groups in sulfate binding, and the low solubility of CaSO4 in high-concentration CaCl2 brine synergized with adsorption to reduce sulfate levels. Raman spectroscopy and XPS clarified sulfate speciation (free ions/ion pairs) in the high-chloride system, shedding light on the removal mechanism. This work develops a high-performance ACCA for deep desulfurization of industrial CaCl2 brines and proposes a novel porous interfacial deposition strategy integrating solubility-controlled precipitation and targeted chemical adsorption, providing a feasible technical solution for deep sulfate removal and high-quality CaCl2 recovery from high-concentration chloride brines.

title: Mechanistic controls of soil organic matter content, water content and bulk density on soil screening levels: A VOC-focused evidence from contaminated sites in Jiangxi Province, China
abstract: China's new national soil screening levels (CSSLs) provide unified benchmarks, but the risks posed by local volatile organic compounds (VOCs) may require regional adaptation. Analyzing 4043 soil samples from Jiangxi Province in China, we evaluated 16 pollutants with concentrations exceeding the CSSLs. The application of region-specific soil parameters revealed substantial intra-provincial variation in the derived screening levels for VOCs. These discrepancies reached up to 533%, suggesting that even greater diversity likely exists at the national level. Mechanistic evaluations identified soil organic matter (fom), water content (Pws), and bulk density (ρb) as the dominant controls on VOC vapor intrusion. Crucially, we reveal that relying on the composite parameter of water-saturated porosity (θws) obscures the non-linear interactions between its independent driving factors, Pws and ρb. While Pws consistently suppresses exposure by restricting both gas-phase partitioning and effective diffusion, higher ρb exerts a dual role-initially promoting partitioning but ultimately physically impeding diffusion. Their effects are highly interdependent; increased ρb amplifies the suppressive impact of Pws on exposure levels. Furthermore, a clear mechanistic hierarchy emerges where strong sorption in high-fom soils effectively masks the physical impacts of Pws and ρb fluctuations, and high-Pws environments overshadow the effects of ρb. These findings provide a scientific basis for establishing a tiered national policy framework to optimize soil quality governance. We recommend combining conservative national baselines with region-specific soil screening levels, wherein fom serves as a mandatory baseline indicator, while the separate measurement of Pws and ρb should be prioritized in high-risk, low-fom areas. This approach provides a resource-efficient, scientific foundation for advancing environmental standardization in China and other geographically diverse nations.

title: Reverse solar interfacial evaporation for high salinity wastewater zero liquid discharge
abstract: The treatment of high salinity wastewater remains a major environmental challenge. Zero liquid discharge (ZLD) technology represents a promising solution; however, its large-scale application is hindered by high energy consumption and secondary environmental pollution during evaporation crystallization. This research proposes a novel strategy for ZLD based on advanced reverse solar interfacial evaporation. The proposed method separated the crystallization interface from the photothermal interface, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of salt crystallization on solar absorption, and the salt crystallization antiscalant was introduced to disrupt uniform nucleation of crystallization precursors and delay their precipitation. Experimental results demonstrated that salt crystals formed at the crystallization interface exert negligible influence on photothermal performance. The formation of micro-meniscuses liquid film between hydrophilic cotton fibers enhances Marangoni effect, improving evaporation efficiency and promoting NaCl crystallization at fiber tips. The composite antiscalant MDC220 could delay crystal nucleation, modify NaCl crystal morphology, boost crystallization efficiency during the initial stages of ZLD process. However, during continuous evaporation, pre-nucleated crystals may become encapsulated and overgrown by newly formed NaCl crystals, leading to salt layer clogging and reduced efficiency in later stages. These findings highlight the substantial potential of proposed reverse solar interfacial evaporation design and crystallization control strategy as a low-cost, energy-efficient, and sustainable solution for achieving ZLD in high salinity wastewater treatment.

title: Mapping biomass availability in China: Bridging theoretical potential to practical utilization through sustainability and cost analysis
abstract: Biomass holds significant promise for advancing China's goals in carbon neutrality and energy security. However, its sustainable use is constrained by logistical feasibility, economic barriers, and competition from alternative uses. Here, a systematic, spatially explicit assessment of agricultural residues, forestry residues, and livestock manure in China from 2000 to 2020 is presented, with biomass categorized into theoretical, collectible, and sustainable potentials at 1 km spatial resolution. Integrating statistical, spatial, and cost analyses, the assessment indicates that although China's annual theoretical biomass availability reaches 32.8 EJ yr−1, only about 25% (8.2 EJ yr−1) can be sustainably exploited for energy production due to collection constraints and competing uses. Sustainable biomass is concentrated in Northeast China, the North China Plain, and the Sichuan Basin, indicating strategic areas for bioenergy deployment. From 2000 to 2020, increases in theoretical biomass were jointly driven by intensity change (44.0%) and land-use change (56.0%), whereas the increase in sustainable biomass was influenced most strongly by rising availability (45.6%). Supply cost modelling reveals a steep marginal cost effect, with only 9.6% of sustainable biomass economically available below 30 $/t, but 72.9% becoming available at 40 $/t Our study presents a high-resolution, cost-informed framework for biomass use planning, highlighting key regions for strategic bioenergy deployment. These findings support the implementation of targeted policies and infrastructure investments to enhance the role of biomass in China's low-carbon transition.

title: Application research on indirect evaporative cooling systems with groundwater pre-cooling for multi-climate zone data centers
abstract: The ongoing surge in digital services has pushed data center (DC) energy demand to new heights, with cooling systems accounting for a dominant share and making sustainable cooling a pressing priority. Indirect evaporative cooling (IEC) is recognized as a promising sustainable solution. Although return air pre-cooling concepts have been previously explored, the specific integration of stable, low-temperature groundwater as a pre-cooling medium for IEC systems, and a systematic assessment of its cross-climatic applicability, remains insufficiently investigated. This paper investigates a system configuration that integrates groundwater pre-cooling with an IEC system, referred to as a Server Room Return Air Pre-cooling Type Indirect Evaporative Cooling (SERAP-IEC) system. Here, using a thermodynamic and energy consumption model established for a DC configuration based on an actual project, we evaluated system performance across five representative Chinese climate zones. The Simcenter Amesim platform simulated the pre-cooling finned-tube heat exchanger, and hourly annual energy analyses were conducted using Python. We found that the SERAP-IEC system can elevate climate switching thresholds by 3 °C–6 °C versus conventional IEC, potentially reducing annual high-energy hybrid mode operation by up to 22% in Xi'an and eliminating such operation in Kunming under simulated conditions. Total annual cooling energy consumption decreased by up to 15.05% in Xi'an, with a corresponding estimated Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) reduction of 0.01–0.03. These results further indicate that the system may contribute to significant annual CO2 emission reductions (estimated 1358.64 tons/year in Xi'an) and could decrease Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) by up to 71.57% in mild climates.

title: Impacts of artificial intelligence on urban carbon emission efficiency in China: A comparative analysis of geographic and network spillovers
abstract: As the digital economy reshapes production and governance, understanding whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to urban green transformation is critical for achieving carbon-neutrality goals. Existing studies mainly emphasize spillovers driven by geographic proximity, while paying limited attention to cross-regional transmission through innovation networks. Using panel data for 281 Chinese cities from 2000 to 2023, we construct a green innovation network-based spatial weight matrix from inter-city co-applied green patents and estimate the direct and spillover effects of AI on carbon emission efficiency (CEE) within a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). We further apply Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) to characterize spatio-temporal heterogeneity. (1) We find that both AI-related intelligentization and CEE increase steadily over time, exhibiting a persistent “high in the southeast and low in the northwest” spatial pattern; meanwhile, China's green innovation network evolves from a single-core diffusion structure toward a more polycentric configuration. (2) The robot-based proxy for AI-related intelligentization is positively associated with local CEE and generates significant spillovers. Proximity-based spillovers follow an inverted-U distance-decay pattern (peaking at approximately 300 km), while network-based spillovers strengthen and persist in the long run. (3) Mechanism analyses suggest that industrial upgrading and improvements in energy-use efficiency are key channels linking AI-related intelligentization to higher CEE. (4) The estimated effects are spatially heterogeneous, with the Hu Huanyong Line marking distinct regimes of AI-enabled decarbonization. Overall, this study provides network-based evidence on the environmental implications of AI-related intelligentization and offers policy insights for reducing administrative fragmentation and fostering coordinated low-carbon governance that integrates physical geography with virtual innovation networks.

title: Assessing the ecological performance of China's new-type urbanization policy: Quasi-experimental evidence on biodiversity co-benefits
abstract: While existing research generally views urbanization as a threat to biodiversity, this study presents contrary findings based on China's quasi-natural experiment in new-type urbanization. Utilizing county-level panel data and bird observation records from China between 2012 and 2022, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences approach for causal identification. The results indicate that the new-type urbanization policy has increased the average number of bird species in pilot areas by 4.691, representing a 40.1% improvement relative to pre-policy levels. This effect is attributed to overall improvements in habitat quality, specifically through enhanced regional ecological environmental conditions, expanded green infrastructure, and optimized industrial spatial layouts. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the policy impact is most significant in regions with lower baseline biodiversity, in the northwestern segment of the Hu Huanyong Line with smaller population density, and in municipal districts. Extended analyses reveal three important characteristics: economically, the policy promotes industrial structural transformation from agriculture to industry; ecologically, biodiversity improvements stem from genuine local habitat enhancement rather than spatial redistribution of species, as evidenced by significant increases in Resident and Migratory Birds but not Passage Migrants; spatially, the policy generates significant positive spillover effects on neighboring regions that strengthen with geographic distance. This study substantiates the ecological benefits of human-oriented urbanization and provides empirical evidence and policy insights from China for biodiversity conservation in the context of global urbanization.

title: Fluorinated-MXene-enabled self-powered nanofiber membrane for synchronous fog harvesting and atmospheric pollution monitoring
abstract: Atmospheric fog harvesting presents a promising strategy for alleviating water scarcity. However, the collected water is often contaminated by airborne pollutants during fog formation and transport. Real-time monitoring of these pollutants is essential to ensure the safe utilization of harvested water resources. This work presents an intelligent nanofiber membrane capable of both fog harvesting and real-time, self-powered water quality monitoring. The membrane is composed of fluorinated MXene (F-MXene) functionalized poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) nanofibers. Surface grafting-induced fluorination of MXene enhances its electronegativity and environmental stability. As a functional filler, F-MXene enables significantly enhanced triboelectric outputs with excellent stability under high-humidity and corrosive conditions. Furthermore, in-situ polymerization of polydopamine creates well-defined hydrophilic patterns on the membrane surface, endowing it with efficient fog collection capability. The movement of harvested droplets across this heterogeneous-wettability surface generates a solid-liquid contact electrification effect, producing electrical signals that serve as a self-powered sensor for real-time environmental monitoring. This sensor can detect fog flow velocity, acidity, volatile organic compounds, and PM2.5 based on their distinct charge transfer characteristics with the membrane. The developed intelligent nanofiber membrane establishes an autonomous platform that synergistically integrates atmospheric water resource utilization and self-powered environmental sensing, promising to promote the development of intelligent ecosystems.

title: Structural resilience evolution and vulnerability assessment of the global supply network for key raw materials of new energy batteries
abstract: The global energy transition is reshaping the industrial landscape, with the new energy battery industry playing a strategic role in supporting energy restructuring and carbon neutrality. Its sustainable development faces challenges, including unstable upstream supply and limited system resilience. Lithium, cobalt, and nickel are critical raw materials, and their supply stability is essential for the industry's growth. Based on international trade data from 2010 to 2024, global supply networks for these materials (Critical Battery Materials Supply Network [CBMSN]) are constructed to examine their structural evolution, resilience, and vulnerability. Structural patterns and long-term evolutionary trajectories are analyzed using topological metrics, including transmissivity, clustering, hierarchical structure, and matching. The ability of the network to maintain functionality during the shock, buffering, and recovery phases is quantified using a multidimensional network structural resilience (NSR) index. Multiple attack strategies are employed to simulate network performance degradation, revealing the vulnerability patterns of each material supply network. A comprehensive centrality ranking algorithm is applied to identify core nodes by integrating multiple centrality metrics with network performance information, thereby providing a decision-making basis for enhancing network resilience and managing risks. The results show significant differences in resilience mechanisms: the lithium supply network is highly centralized, with resilience driven by restoration potential and high sensitivity to core-node disturbances; the cobalt supply network exhibits a complex structure that balances core-node dependence and multi-node redundancy, reflecting both vulnerability and robustness; the nickel supply network is multi-centered and regionally coordinated, with strong overall structural robustness. Sensitivity analysis confirms the robustness of NSR to weight and input data perturbations, and the material-specific differences remain significant and comparable. These findings indicate that CBMSN vulnerability and resilience are jointly determined by network structure, core-node layout, and material properties, providing quantitative insights and strategic guidance for managing global critical raw material supplies.

title: A multifunctional Mn-CuBi2O4/rGO nanocomposite for integrated interfacial solar thermal desalination and visible light pollutant degradation
abstract: The growing global concern about water contamination demands the development of sustainable, efficient water purification technologies. In this work, a multifunctional Mn-CuBi2O4/rGO nanocomposite was synthesized to perform interfacial solar thermal water evaporation and photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants. The dual functional properties of Mn-CuBi2O4/rGO nanocomposite were due to broadband photothermal properties of rGO to promote the efficient steam generation under sunlight, while the Mn-CuBi2O4 nanorods catalyzed the visible light-driven photodegradation of organic contaminants such as Rhodamine B. The nanocomposite Mn-CBO/rGO exhibited 98 % photodegradation within 80 min, compared to the individual material under one-sun illumination. Similarly, the membrane of Mn-CBO/rGO/CG exhibited rapid and continuous water evaporation, with an evaporation rate of 1.92 kg·m−2·h−1, and maintained a continuous water evaporation rate from 3 % to 20 % of salt addition. Furthermore, the membrane showed over 99 % removal efficiency for methylene blue, crystal violet, Congo red, and diclofenac sodium, and maintained a consistent evaporation rate in the presence of these organic pollutants. More importantly, the membrane removed over 99 % of the salts (Na+, K+, Mg2+, and Ca2+). However, the membrane showed excellent long-term stability towards organic and inorganic pollutants. This work demonstrated the synergistic benefits of combining photothermal and photocatalytic mechanisms in a single nanocomposite, offering a scalable, energy-efficient solution for addressing both water desalination and pollutant removal, and advancing the development of solar-assisted water purification technologies.

title: ESG investment and oxy-combustion technology adoption for ocean ecosystem, seawater pollution reduction and climate commitment
abstract: The study inquires the influence of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investment and oxy-combustion technology inclusion on seawater pollution reduction, ocean ecosystem preservation and climate commitment acquisition in terms of net-zero carbon emission. The study explored ten major cities of Guangdong province of China that are located along the coasts based on empirical data from 2001 to 2024. This research tested historical data, and the findings evidenced that (a) ESG investment has a significant influence on seawater pollution reduction. (b) ESG investment has a significant role in ensuring net-zero carbon emissions in fulfilling climate commitments. (c) It is found that the use of oxy-combustion system technology increases efficiency and diminishes pollutant emissions of seawater. For that, gross tree cover area around beaches and green agricultural yield in Guangdong province needs to increase. The results showed that city-economic density, infrastructure level, green innovation, and public awareness of seawater pollution play a significant role. The recommendations for policymakers to advance the scale and reachability of investment flows effectively for seawater ecological improvement. A city-level pollution reduction benchmark is missing in Guangdong province, requiring more work from practitioners.

title: Quantifying future post-demolition concrete in Germany: A multi-model projection until 2080
abstract: To meet climate targets, the environmental impacts of concrete production must be reduced, particularly those associated with cement manufacture. While recycled aggregates primarily contribute to resource conservation, secondary cementitious materials derived from recycling offer direct CO 2 mitigation potential. Post-demolition concrete (PDC) represents a critical secondary resource for both substitution pathways. Reliable projections for future availability are therefore essential for climate-oriented material and circular construction strategies. This study aims to quantify and spatially resolve future availability of PDC in Germany at district level until 2080. A novel multi-model approach is applied, integrating concrete waste statistics, material stocks modelling of buildings and infrastructure, and historical concrete production data. Findings based on the production-based approach indicate that by 2040 approximately 50 million tons of PDC will become available as a secondary raw material, with the highest volumes concentrated in urban regions such as Hamburg and Berlin. Despite its considerable recycling potential, PDC is currently predominantly landfilled or used in low-value applications, indicating substantial underutilization. In parallel, landfill capacity is decreasing, while certain primary raw materials required for concrete production face increasing supply constraints. The projected PDC volumes provide a quantitative basis for assessing future substitution potentials in concrete production. Under the assumption of 35% replacement of primary aggregate and 30% substitution of Portland cement, the annual production of recycled concrete could reach up to 165 million tons annually by 2080. Overall, the results highlight the strategic relevance of PDC for advancing circular material cycles, reducing CO 2 emissions, and mitigating pressure on primary resources.

title: Barriers to sustainability engagement – Evidence from dual universities
abstract: Dual universities integrate theory and practice into their organizational structure and study design. Due to the inclusion of additional stakeholders and perspectives, dual universities may face unique challenges and opportunities when implementing sustainability. This study, based on a survey of stakeholders at a well-established dual university in Germany, examines barriers to sustainability engagement within the context of dual studies. Qualitative content analysis and quantitative correlation analysis reveal a consistent and comprehensive approach by stakeholders toward sustainability. The results indicate a generally high commitment to sustainability on the part of stakeholders. At the same time, the findings show that the intensive study model and the involvement of multiple stakeholders may create additional constraints when it comes to sustainability engagement. Time restrictions and competing priorities appear particularly pronounced in the dual university context. The analysis also reveals a high degree of consistency in how different stakeholder groups perceive sustainability barriers. Based on these findings, the study highlights the importance of developing a sustainability-informed vision and establishing dedicated organizational structures and responsibilities to support sustainability implementation in dual universities.

title: Sustainable design of a gelatin-sodium alginate aerogel for immobilizing bacterial consortia: A synergistic bioremediation strategy against marine oil spills
abstract: Microbial remediation offers an eco-friendly alternative for marine oil spill response, yet field efficacy is limited by insufficient indigenous degrader populations and poor environmental resilience of free bacterial cells in harsh marine conditions. To overcome this challenge, we developed a greenly synthesized, crosslinker-free gelatin-sodium alginate aerogel (GSAA) as an immobilization carrier for an optimized hydrocarbon-degrading consortium (Enterobacter sp. A and Bacillus paramycoides B). The GSAA carrier achieved an exceptional bacterial loading capacity of 9.66 × 1011 CFU/g through a fully green fabrication route. In simulated marine systems, the immobilized system attained 76.76–79.42% oil removal, significantly surpassing free cells and promoting the degradation of persistent hydrocarbons, including long-chain alkanes (C26–C34) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. When introduced into native seawater microbiomes, oil removal rose to 88.38–89.96%, revealing functional synergies between the bio-augmented strains and indigenous communities. Microbial profiling confirmed enrichment of hydrocarbon-degrading taxa (Proteobacteria and Firmicutes) and successful ecological integration. This work presents a carrier-enabled immobilization strategy that aligns with cleaner production goals by avoiding toxic crosslinkers, employing biodegradable matrices, and leveraging microbial cooperation, delivering a sustainable and scalable pathway for marine petroleum remediation.

title: From wastewater to soil improver: Assessing the risks and quality of wastewater resource recovery products
abstract: • Framework to assess quality, health, and environmental risks in resource recovery. • Extensive monitoring shows high level of compliance with EU and Norwegian standards. • Pathogens and heavy metals pose low health risks in crops with soil improver use. • Cumulative risk evaluation conducted for one-time application of 168 contaminants. • Long-term analysis shows slight heavy metal accumulation, highlighting future risks.

title: Longterm dynamics of plastisphere succession and polymer degradation mechanisms in marine environments: A 12-month in-situ study with machine learning applications
abstract: The escalating global crisis of marine plastic pollution underscores the urgent need to investigate longterm weathering mechanisms and associated ecological risks under environmental conditions. In this study, a 12-month in-situ exposure experiment was conducted in a subtropical marine environment to systematically elucidate the degradation dynamics of polypropylene (PP) and polylactic acid (PLA) and their interactions with microbial communities. Results demonstrate polymer-specific aging patterns and biofilm-enhanced risks, revealing that cyanobacteria (harmful algal bloom initiators) preferentially colonize persistent PP (12–15% abundance) over biodegradable PLA (0.22–0.26%). The persistence of PP in the environment enables stable cyanobacterial biofilms to act as longterm dispersal vectors for algal bloom initiation. In contrast, PLA surfaces were enriched with hydrolytic bacteria (e.g., Firmicutes), and this colonization was associated with enhanced mass loss and secondary microplastic formation. Furthermore, seasonal variations exerted limited control over dominant plastisphere taxa, with microbial communities on homogeneous plastics converging over time. Polymer type dominated plastisphere assembly, followed by exposure duration and physical form. Moreover, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN)-based machine learning (ML) model was developed to predict the weathering degree of plastics, achieving a highly reliable accuracy of 85.3 ± 0.8% by extracting image features of the weathered plastic surface, offering a novel paradigm for longterm ecological risk assessment. This work indicates that the short-term experiments are insufficient for predicting the fate of plastics and highlights the necessity of integrating multimodal data into extended observational frameworks and direct measures of microbial activity to evaluate ecological risks more accurately.

title: Dynamics and risks of urban road microplastics under climate stress
abstract: Urban development and the associated traffic expansion have increased microplastic sources, making roads critical zones for microplastic (MP) accumulation and transport. However, the mechanisms of MP accumulation and migration on roads, particularly under climate stress that intensifies high-temperature and heavy-rainfall events, remain poorly understood. This study investigated main roads located in the urban core of Nanjing, by collecting road dust before rainfall and stormwater runoff during rainfall. MPs were detected in all samples, with fibers, polyethylene, and polypropylene comprising about 83% of the total. Road surface temperature showed a strong positive correlation with MPs abundance, suggesting that high temperatures promote material aging and tire wear, thereby increasing MP generation. Midblock sections and intersections of roads exhibited higher MP concentrations in runoff than flat areas, indicating that slope and road layout affect their transport. Small particles below 1 mm accounted for 88% of MPs in runoff compared with 80% in road dust, indicating size-selective movement. These findings reveal the correlations between microplastic pollution and climate stress: high temperature enhances MP generation, and rainfall accelerates MP transport. Such interactions raise both the abundance and mobility of MPs on roads. Consequently, the ecological risk associated with rainfall-transported MPs (Polymer Risk Index: 55.75–102.28) was substantially higher than that of dust-deposited MPs (31.77–54.92), elevating the risk level from “moderate” to “considerable”. This study highlights a climate-driven mechanism in which heat intensifies MP generation and rainfall enhances the transport, together amplifying the abundance and environmental risk of MP on urban roads under climate stress.

title: Towards cleaner aquaculture: assessing the environmental performance of meagre (Argyrosomus regius) fed with insect meal (Hermetia illucens)
abstract: • Life Cycle Assessment of meagre fed with insect meal as fishmeal replacement. • Moderate insect meal inclusion (10-20%) improves several environmental impacts. • High inclusion (30%) reduces feed impacts but worsen performance of fish. • Results highlight trade-offs and the need for optimized aquafeed formulations.

title: Centennial evolution and driving mechanisms of the Baiyangdian Wetland: A multi-source data reconstruction and interpretable machine learning approach
abstract: Over the past century, the Baiyangdian Wetland, the largest shallow lake in the North China Plain, has undergone profound transformations driven by intensified hydraulic engineering and land-use changes. However, a quantitative, centennial-scale reconstruction linking historical hydrological baselines to contemporary anthropogenic impacts remains lacking. By integrating multi-source historical maps (1930s–1950s) and long-term remote-sensing imagery (1975–2025), this study achieves a continuous reconstruction of landscape-pattern dynamics over nearly a century. We employed landscape metrics, standard deviational ellipse (SDE) analysis, and an interpretable machine-learning framework (XGBoost–SHAP) to reveal the evolutionary trajectories and underlying drivers of wetland degradation. The results show a net wetland loss of 48.5% since the natural baseline of the 1930s. A critical “hydrological isolation” period (1975–1985) was identified, during which the construction of upstream dams led to a 94.5% collapse in open-water coverage. Although recent ecological water replenishment has restored water surface area to 131.46 km2 by 2025, aquatic vegetation continues to degrade, revealing a severe “structural imbalance”. Landscape metrics indicate a shift from “natural integrity” to “engineering-driven fragmentation,” with patch density rising sharply. SHAP analysis identifies cropland expansion as the dominant persistent negative driver, synergizing with low-lying topography, while built-up land has emerged as a major pressure interacting with potential evapotranspiration since the 1980s. Overall, this study reveals a multi-stage centennial response of the Baiyangdian Wetland characterized by “natural variability agricultural exploitation urbanization ecological restoration” and provides a scientific basis for sustainable wetland management and for coordinating human–land relationships in territorial spatial planning.

title: Scalable multiscale design of sustainable cellulose films with strength-toughness synergy
abstract: Cellulose nanofiber (CNF)-based bioplastics are promising sustainable materials; however, their inherent brittleness limits practical applications. Here, we present a multistage, low-damage sequential pretreatment strategy that integrates PFI beating, enzymatic hydrolysis, and carboxymethylation, combined with low-energy shearing to construct micro-nanofibers in a low-energy and additive-free process. This method synergistically regulates directional delamination of the S1 layer on the surface of cellulose fibers, enzymatic disentanglement, and electrostatic repulsion, integrating nanofibers (79.33 wt%, ∼5 nm width) and microfibers (20.67 wt%, ∼6.39 μm width) across multiple scales, while preserving the cellulose I crystalline structure (73.16 % crystallinity). Distinct from conventional micro-nanofiber blends, this work introduces abundant transitional submicron fibers that alleviate stress concentrations and suppress structural failure arising from large-scale disparities. As a result, the films achieve concurrent enhancements in strength and toughness, exhibiting a tensile strength of 189.55 MPa, a fracture strain of 34.85 %, and a tensile toughness of 39.11 MJ/m3, which is eight times higher than that of traditional CNF films. Furthermore, the toughening mechanism of multiscale fibers during tensile deformation is systematically elucidated through SEM fracture characterization, finite element analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Overall, this multiscale structural design significantly improves the mechanical performance of sustainable cellulose-based films, broadening their potential in high-toughness applications as sustainable alternatives.

title: Investigating the effects of artificial intelligence on pro-environmental knowledge orchestration and green product innovation: empirical insights from medical equipment suppliers
abstract: With science and technology advancing, artificial intelligence has become an indispensable part of green product innovation for medical equipment suppliers. However, existing research mainly focuses on the impact of artificial intelligence on green innovation from the perspectives of policy influence and economic benefits, while the micro-mechanisms of artificial intelligence on corporate green product innovation remain unclear. Based on the knowledge-based view, this paper constructs a theoretical model about artificial intelligence, pro-environmental knowledge orchestration, managerial environmental concern, and green product innovation. The study conducts empirical analysis using survey data from 302 Chinese medical equipment suppliers. The results show that artificial intelligence application boosts green product innovation by promoting pro-environmental knowledge orchestration. Managerial environmental concern positively moderates the mediation role of pro-environmental knowledge orchestration. This paper innovatively reveals the internal influence mechanism of artificial intelligence applications and green product innovation, expands the application of knowledge-based perspective theory in green product innovation, and enriches the research on boundary conditions of artificial intelligence applications.

title: Unveiling the energy implications of automated driving: Evidence from real-world data
abstract: • Quantification of the energy cost of automated driving. • Real-world experiments with an SAE Level 3 automated vehicle. • Automated driving increases fuel consumption by ∼10% under tested conditions. • Energy efficiency should be considered in automation policies.

title: Sustainability Window (SuWi) method for integrated multidimensional analysis
abstract: The article “Determining the potential global sustainability outcomes of three Business-as-Usual scenarios 2016–2050 from a Doughnut model perspective”, by Dr. Jason Philips, published in the Journal of Cleaner Production (Vol. 519, 2025, Article 145965), presents an interpretation of the Sustainability Window (SuWi) method that contains conceptual inaccuracies and methodological misrepresentations. This Letter to the Editor aims to clarify the theoretical underpinnings and methodological structure of the SuWi framework in order to support its consistent and accurate use in sustainability assessments. The Sustainability Window (SuWi) approach is a quantitative framework for assessing sustainable development by simultaneously integrating economic output, environmental pressure, and social welfare. The core objective is to determine whether economic production, measured by GDP, remains within sustainability boundaries defined and measured by environmental and socio-economic indicators. The social and environmental dimensions of the analysis are linked to the economic output (GDP) of the system using productivity metrics—environmental stress productivity of GDP and social welfare productivity of GDP—to define the maximum level of GDP not to exceed the environmental sustainability threshold, measured with environmental indicators, and the minimum level of GDP to guarantee social sustainability, measured with socio-economic indicators. Both the relative and absolute sustainability criteria derived from Planetary Boundaries and the Sustainable Development Goals can be used in the SuWi analysis. The SuWi method provides tools to address unsustainability through targeted policy pathways, including reducing environmental intensity via technological and structural change, or improving the social welfare productivity of economic activity. The quantitative results of the analysis can be used for constructing an Integrated SuWi Doughnut model to enable policymakers to identify specific sustainability gaps and design interventions that align economic development with both environmental safety and social justice.

title: First-principles modeling and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production using high ash content coal and biomass
abstract: This study investigates the techno-economic feasibility of producing hydrogen via synergistic co-gasification of coal refuse and biomass. Plant configurations are proposed and their first-principles process models are developed for feeds with following coal refuse: biomass ratios −1:0, 4:1, 3:1, and 0:1. Due to considerably high ash content, gasification of coal refuse is challenging and inefficient. Column flotation is used to deash coal refuse before gasification. Considering distributed hydrogen production plant (50 MWe), it is observed that the coal refuse: biomass ratio of 3:1 yields the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of $2.510/kg due to reduced operating costs, while the biomass-only case yields the highest LCOH of $2.718/kg. Sensitivity analyses show strong dependence of LCOH on biomass price, plant capacity, CO2 taxation, and gasifier capital cost. Considering centralized plant of 500 MWe capacity, LCOH decreases below $2/kg due to economies of scale, while additional cost-reduction scenarios, such as lower biomass prices, valorization of slag, reduced electricity costs, and optimized gasifier costs, further decrease LCOH to as low as $0.793–$1.023/kg. The study demonstrates the importance of feedstock optimization, capital and operating cost minimization, and plant scaling in achieving competitive hydrogen production costs by using coal refuse and biomass.

title: Closing the LCA data gap: Early prediction of injection moulding energy consumption
abstract: • Forecasts injection-moulding energy consumption for mould and machine selection. • Combines short cell-level measurements with a parsimonious estimation model. • Use early-known descriptors to deliver comparable and normalised SEC metrics. • Operationalises energy coefficients as matrices to support energy baselines. • Contributes to theory and practice on specific energy consumption.

title: A bilevel approach for sustainable warehouses location with inventory decisions
abstract: Growing environmental concerns have placed increasing pressure on supply chains to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while maintaining economic efficiency. However, strategic and operational decisions in sustainable supply chains are often optimized separately, despite their strong interdependence and combined impact on environmental performance. This paper addresses this gap by integrating strategic and operational decisions within a sustainable supply chain framework aimed at reducing GHG emissions. Strategic decisions are handled by a higher-level decision-maker (leader) and involve locating warehouses to satisfy the demand of a set of customers, with the objective of minimizing environmental pollution generated by delivery, order placement, and inventory processes. Operational decisions are managed by a lower-level decision-maker (follower), who focuses on inventory management and minimizes traditional economic costs. This hierarchized decision-making structure is modeled using a bilevel programming approach, resulting in a single-objective problem with multiple independent nonlinear follower problems, which poses significant computational challenges. To obtain high-quality solutions within reasonable computational times, two component-based metaheuristic algorithms are proposed. The first metaheuristic combines four commonly used and effective components for solving bilevel problems: random solution generation, solution recombination, random modification, and competition among solution sets. The second metaheuristic enhances this framework by incorporating a local search procedure at each iteration to further improve newly generated solutions. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is assessed by comparing their solutions with those obtained from an exact approach when instance sizes allow. Robustness is further demonstrated through computational experiments on a benchmark set of instances, showing good solution stability and low computational times. Finally, the proposed approach is applied to a realistic case study from the Mexican steel industry, where a sensitivity analysis provides valuable managerial insights and reveals several counterintuitive results.

title: Visual and quantitative insight into formation characteristics and sealing effect of CO2 hydrate cap in porous media with fracture channel
abstract: Leakage following carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration has been a significant worldwide concern. Previous studies have demonstrated that the formation of hydrate cap is able to prevent CO2 leakage. However, fracture channels are extensively developed and commonly present within porous media but hardly considered. This study employed magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) visualization technique to investigate the whole dynamic process of CO2 leakage in porous media with channels of four inner diameters (0, 200, 450 and 1000 μm) at 277.15 K, 3 MPa condition. The presence of fracture channels significantly facilitates gas-water flow, decreasing the efficiency of water-CO2 displacement by 0.62% to 4.91%, and reduced the breakthrough pressure of pore water flowed through the hydrate-bearing zone. The hydrate cap can form in porous media even with 1000 μm fracture caused by the CO2 hydrate formation, and it can withstand the overpressure caused by CO2 accumulation of at least 7.0 MPa. In addition, a method for determining the sealing interface and CO2 sequestration volume based on pressure changes of sequestrate CO2 was proposed, with an error of 0.1%∼0.92%. Hydrate cap would be broken through caused by pressure decrease, and the breakthrough pressure decreased exponentially with increasing channel size. These findings provide significant experimental evidence and theoretical understanding on CO2 leakage evolution after sequestration, especially in porous media with fracture channel.

title: Life extension of lithium-ion batteries using bidirectional pulse current: Focusing on amplitude
abstract: Under vehicle-to-grid (V2G) scenarios, the frequent charge-discharge behavior of on-board power batteries significantly increases ampere-hour (Ah) throughput and equivalent cycle numbers, thereby severely affecting internal electrochemical kinetics and degradation mechanisms, posing severe challenges to the battery lifespan. Bidirectional pulse current (BPC) charging and discharging, as a typical mid-to-high-frequency bidirectional energy interaction technology in V2G applications, demonstrates great potential in mitigating battery capacity loss. The amplitude of BPC plays an important regulatory role in both external characteristic parameters and internal degradation mechanisms of lithium-ion batteries, ultimately determining the life extension effectiveness. Building on this, the optimal amplitude parameter for BPC-based battery life extension method was identified, and the findings were further validated through degradation mechanism analysis. Specifically, an amplitude optimization experiment using the control variable method demonstrated that applying BPC regulation within the amplitude window of 0.1 C–0.7 C during calendar storage effectively reduced battery capacity loss. Within the experimental amplitude window, the capacity loss followed an upward-opening parabolic trend with respect to BPC amplitude, reaching a minimum at 0.5 C. This minimum corresponded to the optimal life extension effect of BPC, which increased calendar life by 11.05% and cycle life by 141.91% compared to the battery under conventional calendar storage. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses combining electrothermal characteristics, incremental capacity analysis, and voltage curve reconstruction revealed that a BPC amplitude of 0.5 C effectively suppressed internal resistance growth and exhibited the strongest inhibition effect on the loss of lithium-ion inventory (LLI), while achieving optimal life extension without incurring thermal damage from excessive temperature rise. These findings provide valuable insights for overcoming battery lifespan limitations in V2G applications and enhancing energy system scheduling efficiency.

title: Full cost accounting for biomethane from high-concentration organic wastewater
abstract: Utilizing high-concentration organic wastewater for biomethane production is a promising coupling pathway for wastewater treatment and energy transition, yet the cost implications of this strategy remain unclear. Here we develop a holistic framework that integrates both internal economic and external environmental costs to address this by designing four scenarios relative to the reference of distillery wastewater with a chemical oxygen demand concentration of 61 kg/m3. The findings reveal that, external environmental costs account for 16.7%–45.6% of the total, primarily due to health damage caused by SO2 emissions and the ecological impacts of NH3-N emissions. The policy mix of process-based improvements and energy restructuring can reduce total costs by 10%–15%, while increasing biomethane yield by 15%–21%. Additionally, within a carbon price range of 40-100 CNY/tCO2, all alternative scenarios exhibit negative green premium relative to the high-carbon baseline scenario S0 (upflow anaerobic sludge blanket + high-pressure water scrubber + thermal power), ranging from −0.68 to −1.29 CNY/m3, suggesting that low-carbon technologies become cost-competitive if environmental costs are internalized. Further, targeted subsidies can effectively alleviate cost burdens, bringing scenario S3 (expanded granular sludge bed + pressure swing adsorption + biogas power generation) to market parity after subsidies and thereby enhancing stakeholder acceptance of environmental cost internalization. Our study illustrates the interactions among different process combinations and their impacts on biomethane production costs and environmental impacts, enhancing the realism of decision-making support for high-concentration organic wastewater resource utilization.

title: Scope of the environmental corporate social responsibility of firms
abstract: This paper analyzes whether firms specialize in specific dimensions of environmental corporate social responsibility (ECSR). We assume that ECSR includes firms' investment in emission reductions and analyze whether environmental concerns should also be incorporated into production decisions. Firms' choices depend on both the extent of their environmental concern and the existence of strategic interaction between governments. In a single country setting, where no strategic interaction between governments arises, firms do not consider ECSR in their production decisions in equilibrium, resulting in a narrow scope of ECSR. However, this result may change when strategic interaction between governments is present. In this case, when environmental concern is low, firms incorporate ECSR into both production and emission reduction decisions, leading to a broad ECSR scope. By contrast, when environmental concern is high, firms choose a narrow scope. Thus, the strategic behavior between governments increases the likelihood that firms adopt a broad ECSR compared to the single country case. From a welfare perspective, joint social welfare is maximized when firms adopt a narrow ECSR in both national and international settings. Therefore, in international markets, alignment between firms' strategies and government objectives arises only when firms display a sufficiently high level of environmental concern, highlighting the importance of policies that shape firms’ environmental incentives.

title: Environmental regulation and asymmetric firm entry: Evidence from China
abstract: How environmental regulation affects market entry during the green transition may depend not only on average compliance costs, but also on how those costs interact with ownership-linked institutional asymmetries. Using a text-based regulation index and a Bartik-style shift-share instrument for 285 Chinese cities from 2000 to 2023, we examine how environmental regulation reshapes firm entry across ownership types.
