We find that stricter regulation is associated with lower private entry but a more muted, and in some cases positive, response of State-Owned Enterprise (SOE) entry, pointing to an ownership-asymmetric reallocation of market opportunities. The mechanism evidence is most consistent with two channels. First, regulation appears to tighten compliance-related financing constraints for private firms, making entry more difficult for firms with weaker access to external capital. Second, the state-sector response is more consistent with policy-linked demand and stronger insulation from policy uncertainty than with a uniform cost shock across firms. At the aggregate level, the results are consistent with a pattern in which regulation coincides with higher output but weaker market dynamism. Overall, the findings suggest that in a dual-track economy, environmental policy may undermine the dynamism of the green transition if competitive neutrality is not preserved.

title: Recovery of rare earth elements from phosphogypsum: A laboratory and pilot study
abstract: To date, a substantial body of experimental and theoretical knowledge concerning the extraction of rare earth elements (REEs) from phosphogypsum has been accumulated, as evidenced by comprehensive contemporary reviews. The principal challenges associated with phosphogypsum processing stem from its inherently low REE content, necessitating large-scale facilities. Furthermore, while leaching efficiency typically increases with elevated solid-to-liquid ratios and higher concentrations of leaching agents, these conditions concurrently generate voluminous, highly mineralized effluents, the management of which must be integrated into broader waste treatment strategies. Given the magnitude of apatite concentrate processing operations, phosphogypsum remains a prospective resource for REE recovery. The present study analyzes numerous aspects, encompassing both strictly scientific considerations and engineering constraints that impede progress toward the development of a cost-effective, integrated technology for phosphogypsum processing. Using thermodynamic modeling software, the equilibrium speciation of REE ionic forms in phosphogypsum leach liquors and the influence of F− and PO443− thereon were established. It is recommended to maintain the PO443− concentration at no more than approximately 0.4 mmol/L and the F− concentration at no more than approximately 0.5 mmol/L. Considering the specifics of the main processing stage - the sorptive leaching of REEs - the purification step to remove fluorine and phosphorus is recommended to be carried out using a weak base anion exchange resin within a resin-in-pulp process configuration. The conditions of the pilot-scale process, including a leach liquor-to-phosphogypsum (PG) ratio of 5, a pH of the resulting suspension between 1.4 and 1.6, and a flow rate of 8 L/h for the sulfonic acid cation-exchange resin (C-150), enabled a stable (cycle-to-cycle) REE recovery rate of approximately 70–80%. The subsequent processing stages - desorption, regeneration, and REE concentrate precipitation - allowed for the identification of technical constraints associated with the cyclic use of the desorption liquor (NH4NO3, 500 g/L) and led to the recommendation to introduce a stage for producing chemically precipitated calcium carbonate (chalk) from the desorption liquor following REE precipitation. The isolation of purified gypsum and its conversion into a gypsum binder, the concentration of F− and PO443− into a separate product, and the production of high-purity chemically precipitated chalk have significantly enhanced the project's quality in terms of both environmental sustainability and commercial viability.

title: Innovations in arid land salinization management: Xinjiang's evolving paradigm for saline-alkali land governance
abstract: • Systematic review of saline-alkali land management in Xinjiang. • Drip irrigation is the core of saline-alkali land management. • Quantitatively analyze the global suitability of the governance model.

title: Climate change impacts on micro-hydropower sustainability in remote off-grid communities
abstract: Increasing climate variability threatens the sustainability of micro-hydropower plants (MHPPs) in remote off-grid communities that depend on stable river flows. We developed and applied a simple, observation-based framework to assess future electricity-generation variability and power-outage risk, using Ciptagelar village in mountainous West Java, Indonesia, as a case study. Locally observed meteorological and hydrological data were integrated with a hydrological model and statistically generated rainfall scenarios to simulate future river discharge under climate change. Results indicate that projected climate change will reduce dry-season river discharge, leading to declines in annual electricity generation and substantial increases in outage days toward the late twenty-first century. While generation decreases were broadly similar across the four MHPPs examined, outage risk varied markedly with turbine type and site characteristics, with the propeller-turbine MHPP proving considerably more vulnerable to climate-induced low-flow conditions than those using cross-flow turbines under the specific site configurations examined. A hypothetical turbine-replacement analysis further revealed a critical paradox in MHPP design: switching from a propeller to a cross-flow turbine yielded little change in total annual energy generation but substantially reduced outage duration, demonstrating that maximizing energy output or efficiency does not necessarily ensure a reliable electricity supply. Qualitative interviews showed that expanding electricity use supports communication, household appliances, and tourism, suggesting that climate-driven increases in outages may have cascading impacts on livelihoods and well-being. Despite methodological limitations, the proposed framework offers a transparent and transferable tool for first-order climate-impact assessment and adaptation planning in data-scarce mountainous regions and similar off-grid rural settings worldwide.

title: Overlooked spectral matching-Enabled sulfoxide wastewater valorization and in situ pollutant elimination
abstract: Organic pollutant treatment is transitioning from a linear remove-and-discharge model to a circular paradigm centered on resource recovery. Here, various heterogeneous systems were constructed, first demonstrating a novel valorization of sulfoxides, where they function to enhance in-situ H2O2 photosynthesis. Using methyl phenyl sulfoxide (PMSO), we observed 1.38-10.34 folds H2O2 yield, with pyromellitic diimide/PMSO in visible light (Vis) responsive system showing optimal performance (5.34×). Spectral analysis revealed PMSO's matching characteristic, showing effective decomposition under UV-B (λ ≤ 300 nm) while maintaining stability under Vis (λ > 400 nm), achieving simultaneous valorization and contaminant removal across diurnal cycles. Micro mechanism investigations established PMSO as an electron-transfer mediator rather than a hole scavenger in systems with valence bands below +1.63 eV. The -S=O group mediates interfacial electron redistribution through a donor-acceptor pathway while functioning as a Brønsted acid to facilitate proton supply, synergistically promoting proton-coupled electron transfer for H2O2 production. A prototype day-night device was constructed for continuous solar-driven H2O2 production and subsequent UV-activated pollutant removal, achieving near-complete elimination (>98%) of both the parent sulfoxide and co-contaminants in 1 L batch cycles. This work presents an integrated valorization-elimination strategy, offering a novel design principle for wastewater-specific treatment systems based on contaminant intrinsic properties.

title: Operationalizing collaborations between universities and municipalities for place-based sustainability transitions
abstract: Even though many cities and regions pledge to become more sustainable and/or carbon neutral, actionable platforms that would enable the needed place-based transformation are not yet in place. In this study, we argue that successful university-municipality collaborations can play a key role in accelerating the uptake of sustainability innovations, with direct benefits for the region. We propose pathways that include operational mechanisms for universities and municipalities to co-develop institutional capacity for local/regional sustainability transitions. The study explores how higher education institutions that have developed relevant sustainability competencies, succeeded in connecting to local processes of sustainability transitions. We pursue the following research question—- Under which contexts could higher education institutions (HEIs) productively contribute to sustainability transitions locally or regionally, and how could such a mandate become institutionalized within universities that choose to do so? In the selected case studies, we identify multiple entry points for regions to tap into university sustainability competencies, capabilities and skillsets. Based on our findings, we initially propose university-region collaborations in methodological integration of cross-disciplinary research in sustainability planning and transdisciplinary practice. Next we recommend institutionalizing university-municipality engagement and configure specific operational mechanisms to make the engagement actionable and effective. Finally, we outline potential benefits and opportunities for the region, including impacts on sustainability transitions or specific sustainable development goals. The study contributes to research on (i) concepts of smart specialization for sustainable development, (ii) theoretical models of higher education institutions, and (iii) policy frameworks that envision universities as key contributors to regional sustainability innovation and sustainability transitions.

title: Hydrogen sulfide treatment and hydrogen production through commercial deployment of green sulfur bacteria: A life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis perspective
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) treatment and removal is a necessary step in natural gas processing and biogas upgrading with thermochemical systems such as the Claus process serving as the most common method of H2S treatment and sulfur recovery. However, several naturally occurring biological processes are also capable of removing H2S from sour gases at high efficiencies while avoiding sulfur dioxide formation and operating at lower temperatures and anoxic conditions. In this study, green sulfur bacteria (GSB) are evaluated as a potential commercial scale sour gas treatment system through process modeling, techno-economic analysis, and life cycle assessment. Two configurations are assessed here: (1) a single-strain GSB system producing elemental sulfur and (2) a consortium system coupling GSB with sulfur-reducing bacteria to produce hydrogen via the nitrogenase enzymatic pathway. The single-strain system was found to have a positive internal rate of return (IRR) of 17% and a net present value (NPV) of ∼$1,000,000 while producing elemental sulfur with a carbon intensity between 1.43 and 1.63 kg CO2-eq/kg S depending on allocation method. The hydrogen producing consortium system was found to have a negative NPV and faced economic challenges with organic substrate requirements and gas separation costs. The system resulted in a hydrogen carbon intensity between 2.98 and 6.63 kg CO2-eq/kg H2. Overall, this work demonstrates that green sulfur bacteria could be an economically and environmentally promising commercial scale alternative to H2S treatment and sulfur production, while also quantifying realistic bounds on hydrogen production via biological sulfur cycling.

title: Microstructure and durability analysis of fiber reinforced alkali-activated slag composites containing waste steel pig and marble dust
abstract: This study develops alkali-activated slag composites incorporating WSP, 0-100 wt% as aggregate replacement and polypropylene fiber (PPF, 0-1.5 vol%) for ductility enhancement, targeting sustainable construction materials with reduced carbon footprint. Tests included; flow diameter, compressive/flexural strength, oven-dry density, water absorption, apparent porosity, sorptivity, elevated temperature (250-750 °C), freeze-thaw cycling (150 cycles), sulfate (Na2SO4) and acid (H2SO4) exposure, with SEM microstructural analysis. Mechanical characterization revealed that 100% WSP replacement achieved 29.29 MPa compressive strength at 28 days, representing a 108% increase over the WSP free control, attributed to optimized particle packing density and enhanced interfacial bonding. PPF incorporation increased flexural strength by 20-40% and energy absorption capacity by 3-8 times through crack bridging mechanisms, with 1.5% dosage proving optimal. Durability assessments demonstrated exceptional freeze-thaw resistance, with high WSP formulations exhibiting less than 20% strength loss after 150 cycles. Notably, 100% WSP specimens demonstrated apparent sulfate resistance with 46% strength increase relative to 28-day values, though continued alkali activation may contribute to this gain, contrasting with degradation observed at intermediate replacements. Microstructural analysis confirmed dense C-(A)-S-H gel formation and reduced porosity (7.97%) in high performance formulations. Preliminary life cycle assessment indicates 80.3% reduction in cradle to gate carbon footprint (58 vs. 295 kg CO2-eq/m3) and 86.9% reduction in carbon intensity per unit strength compared to Portland cement systems. These findings validate the integrated utilization of industrial by products as a viable pathway for developing high-performance, environmentally sustainable construction materials within circular economy principles.

title: Environmental determinants and spatial patterns of soil antibiotic resistance gene diversity across Europe using interpretable geographically weighted machine learning
abstract: The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in soils poses significant threats to ecosystems and public health. Their diversity is associated with a complex interplay of environmental factors and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity. However, the spatial patterns and key associated factors remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, ARGs data from the topsoil of 649 sites across Europe, obtained from the 2018 Land Use/Cover Area frame statistical Survey (LUCAS, 2018), were used to develop an interpretable geographically weighted machine learning model. The model was used to quantify the relative importance of environmental factors associated with soil ARG diversity and to characterize spatial distribution patterns. The results indicate that by incorporating spatial heterogeneity in ARG diversity is associated with improved model performance, with geographically weighted machine learning models outperform conventional machine learning models. In particular, the geographically weighted extreme gradient boosting (GW-XGBoost) model achieved a higher R 2 and lower RMSE than the other models, with the test set R 2 improving by 22.3% compared to XGBoost. Soil pH showed the highest relative importance, accounting for 41.3%, with lower ARG diversity observed under neutral to alkaline conditions (pH > 6.7). Both pH and precipitation showed strong direct associations with ARG diversity, whereas land cover, temperature, and elevation were associated with ARG diversity through indirect pathways related to soil properties. Spatial mapping revealed higher ARG diversity in northern Europe, particularly Sweden and Finland, and lower ARG diversity in southern regions, including Spain and Italy. This study characterizes the environmental factors associated with soil ARG diversity and their spatial patterns, providing a scientific basis for soil management and public health protection, and offering a useful reference for modeling in environmental studies.

title: Sustainable coordination of polygeneration energy-water systems with reverse osmosis for cleaner production
abstract: This work puts forward Polygeneration energy systems (PGESs) framework capable of maximizing economic operation of integrated energy networks under uncertainty. The system uses sustainable generation technologies (e.g., solar power and wind energy), with conventional units like combined heat and power (CHP), gas boilers, electric boilers, and a reverse osmosis (RO) unit for producing water. A mathematical model is formulated for ensuring fulfillment of multi-energy demand electricity, gas, thermal, and water through cost minimization via energy allocation strategies. The model incorporates dynamic pricing, component limitations, as well as energy balance equations. In particular, decision regularized gradient learning (DRGL) has been developed for adaptive scheduling of PGES to obtain optimal operation and minimized costs. By training multi-layers neural networks (MLNNs), the DRGL agent aims to find optimal policy by interacting with the environment. In this framework, the weights of MLNNs are updated so that it maximizes a reward function which is selected based on the objective function of PGES. Simulation over a 24-h period establishes dynamic coordination between energy generation, demand fulfillment, as well as resource utilization, with grid dependency being minimized. Obtained findings also indicate CHP as a key thermal as well as electric resource due to its two-way output potential, with a big contribution from reverse osmosis in fulfilling water demand. The framework enables future smart energy systems with cost-effective, flexible, and robust functioning.

title: Identifying opportunities for repurposing decommissioned wind turbine blades in bus station design: A product attribute-based method
abstract: Wind turbine blades exhibit performance advantages over conventional metals, such as a high strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance, yet complex multi-layered structures and resistance to natural degradation of their composite materials hinder effective recycling. Repurposing blades offers a sustainable approach compared to landfilling, incineration, and low-value recycling practices. Accordingly, examples of blade repurposing are available, but there is a lack of systematic approaches. This paper proposes an attribute-based method to identify potential similarities between decommissioned product segments and target components, demonstrated through wind turbine blades and bus stations. As semi-open infrastructures exposed to outdoor environmental conditions, bus stations impose specific material performance requirements such as weather resistance, structural strength, and durability. Each product component is modeled as a vector of distinct attributes, forming matrices that link components with attributes across bus stations and wind turbine blades. Attributes are classified into three categories: inherent, developed, and image. The design potential of using specific components of blades in a bus station is identified by mapping component similarity in a matrix. This method enables the identification of non-obvious repurposing opportunities, avoids the problem that the original function of the components does not apply to the new application, and enriches the design possibilities of a green bus station.

title: Modeling and analysis of synthetic liquid fuel production from CO2 and nuclear energy using methanol-to-diesel process
abstract: Synthetic fuels produced from CO2 and electricity—so-called electrofuels (e-fuels)—are drop-in blendstocks for petroleum fuels. Nuclear energy is an attractive energy source for e-fuel production because it is able to provide steady heat and power with low carbon footprint. We modeled and evaluated the cost and environmental footprint of e-fuel production in the distillate range (jet fuel and diesel) for three nuclear power scales—100, 500, and 1000 MWe—via methanol and olefins intermediates leveraging commercial or high technology readiness level (TRL) processes. Compared to the commonly studied e-fuels from the Fischer-Tropsch process that often has a distillate yield of <70%, with the rest being low-value naphtha, the proposed process via a methanol intermediate increases the product selectivity, yielding 96% distillate and only 4% naphtha. The modeled process has a carbon conversion ratio of 98%, and a process energy efficiency of 56% relative to the total equivalent nuclear electricity input. The e-fuel plant economics and GHG emissions were estimated by considering CO2 collected from ethanol plants adjacent to nuclear power plants. The estimated minimum fuel selling price (MFSP) of e-fuel is in the range of $5.5-$8.9/gal depending on e-fuel plant scale, electricity cost, and CO2 transportation distance. The corresponding e-fuels life cycle GHG emissions are estimated to be in the range of 5-6 gCO2e/MJ of liquid fuel using the R&D Greenhouse gases, Regulated Emissions, and Energy use in Technologies (R&D GREET) model.

title: Integrating stimulation and CO2 storage in natural gas hydrate reservoirs: visualization of CO2-foam fracturing and hydrate self-sealing
abstract: Natural gas hydrate reservoirs (NGHRs) have long faced production bottlenecks because of low permeability and weak cementation, while conventional hydraulic fracturing is constrained by severe leakoff and viscous dissipation. Using a visual sapphire reactor, this study for the first time achieved in-situ visualization of CO2-foam fracturing in NGHRs, capturing fracture initiation, propagation, and closure. We elucidated the leakoff-control and fracture-creation mechanisms under coupled hydro-thermo-geomechanical conditions. The process is synergistically governed by transient overpressure, the Jamin effect, and near-fracture CO2-hydrate self-sealing, which suppresses leakoff and improves fracture-creation efficiency. Fracture response was strongly dependent on the hydrate-bearing sediment (HBS) type: fine-grained HBS (silt and clayey silt) produced larger, more stable fractures than medium sand HBS. At 2 MPa vertical stress, fracture length in clayey silt was 2.74 times that in medium sand and 1.70 times that in silt, while fracture area was 8.60 and 1.84 times larger, respectively. Higher hydrate saturation enhanced fracturing effectiveness, shifting fracture geometry from a single horizontal fracture to a T-shaped configuration with vertical branches. Low vertical stress favored vertically connected networks, whereas high vertical stress stabilized wide horizontal fractures. Among operating parameters, higher initial fracturing pressure and an optimized liquid volume fraction enlarged fracture geometry. Overall, CO2-foam fracturing offers a route to coupled natural gas hydrate production and CCUS by combining mechanical stimulation with hydrate-mediated leakoff control.

title: Coupling virtual and physical water optimization: a bi-level stochastic model for basin water scarcity mitigation
abstract: Virtual water trade planning magnifies the scope of regional water resources utilization, and becomes a burgeoning strategic choice for water management. In this study, a bi-level stochastic model coupling virtual and physical water optimization (BS-VPWO) is designed for quantifying the effects of virtual water trade on water trading as well as optimizing decisions for conjunctive management of physical-virtual water systems. BS-VPWO integrates water resources assessment with hydrological simulation, physical water trading modeling coupled with virtual water trade, and interval stochastic bi-level programming (ISBP) technique. Virtual water export and import processes as well as water right initial allocation and reallocation are elaborated in BS-VPWO framework. A case study of Dagu River Basin with water shortage, East China, is conducted for application of BS-VPWO. The impacts of virtual water trade on water system and spatial heterogeneity of basin's water shortage are quantified through mechanism analysis. The optimal virtual water trade scheme is also identified. Results reveal that coupling virtual and physical water optimization can increase system efficiency by [0.35, 0.45]% and benefits by [5.01, 5.03]%, meanwhile decrease basin's water shortage volume. This study discloses the driving forces of virtual water trade in physical water right trading and water resources management systems. It also examines virtual water trade decisions to alleviate water scarcity and enhance utilization efficiency in virtual water-exporting basins.

title: Deficit irrigation combined with wolfberry-alfalfa intercropping enhances soil carbon sequestration in saline-alkali soils: A soil microenvironment-driven perspective
abstract: To address agricultural green development and carbon neutrality goals, saline-alkali land remediation urgently requires a shift toward ecologically intensive pathways, but field strategies that synergistically enhance soil quality and carbon sink function in saline-alkali soils via water-saving irrigation and intercropping remain limited, particularly from the soil microenvironment driver perspective. This 4-year field study, using barren land (BL) as control, examined the effects of water management (rainfed (R) and deficit irrigation (D)) and planting patterns (wolfberry monoculture (W), alfalfa monoculture (A), and wolfberry-alfalfa intercropping (WA)) on soil amelioration, carbon turnover, and carbon sink function in saline-alkali land. Results showed that deficit-irrigated wolfberry-alfalfa intercropping (DWA) significantly improved soil water content, reduced surface soil pH and salt accumulation, and increased enzyme activities (alkaline phosphatase (ALP), catalase (CAT), urease (UE), and β-glucosidase (β-GC)) as well as organic carbon fractions (SOC, MBC, ROOC, and DOC) and their proportions. Compared with BL, DWA increased the carbon pool management index (CPMI) by 179.46–241.57 and enhanced carbon pool quality in the 30–40 cm soil layer. Deficit irrigation, relative to rainfed conditions, increased ecosystem respiration (ER) and gross ecosystem productivity (GEP), with DWA showing net carbon uptake. Partial least squares path modeling indicated that water management and planting patterns mainly enhanced soil carbon pool quality and carbon sink function indirectly by regulating organic carbon fractions and enzyme activities. In summary, DWA created a favorable crop root-zone microenvironment, simultaneously achieving water saving, salt suppression, soil improvement, and carbon sink enhancement, providing scientific reference for low-carbon agriculture development in saline-alkali lands of arid and semi-arid regions.

title: Biochar amendment improves rice seedling quality and mitigates greenhouse gas emissions for cleaner seedling production
abstract: This study investigated the effects of biochar addition on rice seedling quality, medium physicochemical properties, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions during the seedling stage. The ultimate goal was to develop a low-carbon nursery technology to support sustainable rice production. Two rice varieties, japonica ‘Nanhuaijing 5' (JR) and indica hybrid ‘Lianliangyou 9312' (IR), were cultivated under four substrate treatments: a basal layer of seedling mat topped with a 1:1 (mass ratio) mixture of nutrient soil and commercial seedling substrate amended with biochar at 0%, 4%, 8%, and 12% (w/w). Seedling growth, medium physicochemical and biological properties, GHG fluxes (CH4 and N2O), and microbial functional gene expression were analyzed at 7, 14, and 21 days after sowing (DAS). The results indicated that moderate biochar application (4%–8%) significantly enhanced seedling morphological and physiological traits, including plant height, dry matter accumulation, and antioxidant enzyme activities. Biochar also improved seedling medium properties, including electrical conductivity (EC), pH, and nutrient retention. Importantly, CH4 and N2O emission fluxes and cumulative emissions were significantly reduced, with the 8% biochar treatment showing the most pronounced mitigation effect. These improvements were associated with better medium aeration, moisture regulation, and modulated microbial activity. Furthermore, biochar amendment influenced key microbial functional genes involved in CH4 and N2O metabolism, including mcrA, amoA, nirK, nirS, and nosZ, supporting its role in regulating GHG emissions. The findings demonstrate that optimal biochar addition (e.g., 8%) can simultaneously enhance rice seedling quality while reducing GHG emissions during the seedling period, offering a sustainable, low-carbon strategy for green rice seedling production within a cleaner agricultural framework.

title: G2I-En predictions of indoor PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 exposure in child-specific microenvironments: Bridging the gap between low-cost sensors and mechanistic understanding in highly-polluted regions
abstract: Indoor air quality (IAQ) critically influences children's health and development; however, predictive models tailored to child-specific household environments remain underdeveloped. This study applied a GeoAI-to-Indoor Environment model to predict PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 concentrations in bedrooms and living rooms of 86 children in Tainan, Taiwan, a high-pollution region. We recruited households during both warm and cold seasons (April 2021–December 2023), installed low-cost sensors at children's breathing height, and integrated building characteristics and activity patterns through household surveys. The proposed model achieved adjusted R2 values exceeding 0.87 across particle size fractions and microenvironments. Bayesian Monte Carlo and SHapley Additive exPlanations sensitivity analyses identified outdoor PM2.5 as the most influential predictor (>50%), while human activities and building characteristics collectively explained 25–36% of indoor PM variation. Notably, PM level measured from the living room averaged 20% higher than bedrooms, driven primarily by proximity to kitchens and higher air exchange rates. This study advances the application of machine learning in environmental health research by providing a scalable and interpretable framework for indoor PM prediction. It offers a robust scientific foundation for air pollution control strategies, strengthens exposure assessment in epidemiological studies, and delivers evidence-based recommendations for providing actionable evidence for IAQ interventions and improving IAQ in child-specific households within highly-polluted areas.

title: Performance assessment of waste-to-energy and green hydrogen synergy in a chemical park using a minimalist LCCN-coupled model
abstract: The decarbonization of industrial steam supply remains a critical challenge for achieving net-zero pathways. This study develops an integrated assessment framework to evaluate the techno-economic and environmental performance of waste-to-energy (WTE) and hydrogen co-firing hybrids in a chemical park context. By coupling mass–energy–carbon balances, synthetic steam load generation, and scenario-based optimization, the analysis explores the role of WTE share and hydrogen co-firing rate in shaping both CI and the Levelized cost of heat (LCOH). Results reveal that while pure WTE setups maintain economic competitiveness, their potential for emission reduction is constrained by the fossil content of municipal solid waste. In contrast, high hydrogen-blending scenarios deliver the lowest operational carbon intensity (CI) (gate-to-gate, Scope 1–2) at substantially higher cost. All CI results are reported on a gate-to-gate basis (Scope 1–2); upstream emissions from hydrogen production (Scope 3) are excluded from the core model but are examined via a sensitivity check in the Discussion. Crucially, the study identifies that a moderate hydrogen blend (10%) offers the optimal cost-carbon balance, securing meaningful emission reductions with a manageable cost increase. Pareto frontiers and uncertainty simulations further underscore these trade-offs, highlighting the pivotal role of WTE efficiency. This study contributes a novel hybrid assessment linking waste valorisation and hydrogen utilization, providing actionable insights for policymakers on optimizing WTE–hydrogen synergies.

title: A laboratory evaluation of enhanced stabilization of dredged heavy metal-contaminated coastal sediments using a green biochar-metakaolin-sodium silicate composite: Performance, mechanisms, and applications
abstract: Ecotoxic heavy metals including Pb, Cr (VI), Hg, and Ni, together with elevated micronutrient metals such as Zn and Cu, exceed Class II marine sediment quality thresholds in some coastal sediments and threaten wetland ecosystems and coastal infrastructure, highlighting the need for sustainable stabilization technologies. This study introduces GBMSS, a green biochar metakaolin sodium silicate composite, to improve the solidification and stabilization of dredged heavy metal-contaminated coastal sediments by reducing leachability and enhancing engineering properties. The experimental framework evaluates stabilization performance under oxic conditions, simulating the typical geochemical environment encountered during the dredging, handling, and land-based staging of sediments. At a 2% dosage relative to sediment dry weight and with 7-day curing, GBMSS showed improved short-term performance compared with conventional stabilizers in controlled laboratory tests, including higher unconfined compressive strength (up to 1.92 MPa) and improved solidification uniformity. GBMSS modified sediment composition by reducing clay fractions and increasing silt-sized particles in the tested samples. Microscopic analyses and BCR sequential extraction indicated the formation of silicon-aluminum-based geopolymer products and stable mineral phases, which effectively sequestered heavy metals into the residual fraction (F4). For instance, Pb leaching concentrations were significantly reduced from 46.78 mg/L to 0.10 mg/L, remaining well below TCLP and SPLP regulatory thresholds. The synergistic action of biochar, metakaolin, and sodium silicate promotes geopolymer formation and lattice-level encapsulation, providing high thermodynamic stability to the immobilized metals. While this study establishes a robust engineering foundation for the beneficial reuse of dredged materials, all conclusions are limited to the tested short-term laboratory evaluation under oxic conditions. Dedicated validation under reducing or hypoxic and microbially active marine conditions is required for applications involving long-term in situ subaqueous burial. Future work will assess microbial compatibility and evaluate long-term metal speciation under dynamic coastal redox regimes.

title: Pd/TiO2 oxygen-vacancy photocatalysts on tapered optical fibers: Enhanced light harvesting for antibiotic degradation
abstract: Tapered optical fibers (TOFs) enable efficient light–catalyst coupling via evanescent-field concentration, yet their potential for photocatalytic antibiotic degradation remains underexploited. Here, Pd/TiO2-Ov nanorods were uniformly coated on TOFs to activate persulfate (PS) under UV evanescent-field irradiation. The TOF-Pd/TiO2-Ov-PS system achieved a sulfadiazine (SDZ) degradation rate of 37.9 mg g−1·min−1, 38-fold higher than conventional UV/PS (1 mg g−1·min−1). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman, and surface photovoltage (SPV) measurements collectively confirmed that oxygen vacancies (Ov) and Pd sites synergistically promoted photoinduced electron transfer from TiO2 to Pd. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and radical scavenging experiments further confirmed the synergistic contributions of direct h+ oxidation and •OH/SO4•− in situ generation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed an upshifted d-band centre of Pd/TiO2-Ov toward the Fermi level, enhancing PS adsorption and activation. The system delivered >98% SDZ removal in ultrapure water, tap water, and domestic sewage and maintained >99% efficiency against norfloxacin (NOR) and tetracycline (TET), attesting to its broad-spectrum capacity. This work establishes evanescent-field-driven photocatalysis as a robust platform for antibiotic wastewater remediation.

title: Decadal progress and provincial disparities: How did China's WEEE recycling fund policy refine regional resource-environmental performance?
abstract: As the world's fastest-growing waste stream, waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) poses urgent sustainability challenges. China's WEEE Recycling Fund Policy (WRFP), launched in 2012, has formalized recycling for the 4 + 1 appliances covered by the WRFP through audited dismantling channels. This study develops a spatiotemporal evaluation framework to quantify WRFP's 2013–2023 performance across provinces by integrating resource recovery value and carbon reduction into resource-environmental performance assessment. Results show that formal recycling generated RMB 12.8 billion in resource recovery value and reduced cumulative carbon emissions by 31.4 million tons, while also revealing significant regional disparities. Eastern provinces contribute 63.7% of total resource value but require production optimization, whereas western regions show stronger needs for infrastructure expansion. Provincial Malmquist analysis demonstrates 9.2% annual efficiency growth driven exclusively by technological progress, indicating that insufficient industrial scale remains a major constraint. Tobit regression further indicates that rapid growth in household appliance ownership may reduce recycling efficiency under uneven recycling infrastructure. By integrating resource recovery value, carbon reduction, and efficiency change within a unified spatiotemporal framework, this study not only quantifies provincial disparities in WRFP performance, but also establishes a more comprehensive basis for long-term policy evaluation and regional policy refinement.

title: Characteristics of pore structure evolution of ferrite-rich sulfoaluminate cement grouting materials under seawater corrosive environment
abstract: The evolution of pore structure in grouting materials under seawater corrosion critically governs their long-term durability and anchorage performance. This study employed accelerated seawater immersion tests on ferrite-rich sulfoaluminate cement (FCSA-1) grouting material, with X-ray diffraction (XRD) and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) analyses quantifying hydration phase alterations and pore structures evolution under varying corrosion salt concentrations and corrosion ages. The results revealed that the primary expansion products were ettringite and Friedel's salt, with their formation showing a positive correlation to increases in seawater salt concentration. Both corrosion age and salt concentration governed dual damage mechanisms: low concentration or early age led to a filling effect, while high concentration induced crystallization pressure damage, and longer corrosion age resulted in expansion cracks and overfilling. Additionally, the fractal dimension increased with both salt concentration and corrosion age, following a V-shaped distribution, with the turning point influenced by the salt concentration. The pore evolution mechanism varied at different corrosion depths. Corrosion dissolution dominated the degradation at the outer surface (1-4 mm), while a delayed diffusion plugging response was observed at deeper layers (19-23 mm). Furthermore, the porosity followed a logarithmic trend as the salt concentration increased. Based on fractal theory, a fractal permeability model incorporating porosity, fractal dimension, and pore size was developed to better synthesize the structural characteristics of the pores.

title: Pricing strategies on ride-hailing platforms: The role of carbon point reward program for electric vehicle services
abstract: To reduce carbon emissions, ride-hailing platforms have introduced electric vehicle (EV) services. Platforms have two pricing strategy choices between gasoline vehicles (GS) and EV services: Uniform pricing and differentiated pricing (DP). Additionally, to increase the EV demand, the platform implements a carbon point reward (CPR) program, which affects pricing strategy choices and further affects carbon emissions. In this paper, we develop a game-theoretic model with the platform as the leader and consumers and drivers as the followers to examine how pricing strategies and the CPR program impact stakeholders (consumers, drivers, and a platform) and the environment. The results show that the platform always prefers the DP strategy. And when the environmental impact of one trip (EI) is moderate and range anxiety is small or the EI is small, the DP strategy can achieve a win-win-win situation for the platform, the environment, and EV drivers if the number of consumers without a coupon is large and the economic value of carbon points is small. Furthermore, when the economic value of carbon points is small, the CPR program may increase the platform's profits while exacerbating total environmental impacts under the DP strategy. Therefore, this study provides valuable insights for ride-hailing platforms to optimize pricing strategies and promote green travel.

title: The impact of new energy demonstration city policy on energy transition under multi-stakeholder collaboration: Evidence from double machine learning
abstract: The collaborative governance of multiple stakeholders is pivotal to achieving the simultaneous enhancement of energy efficiency and reduction of energy intensity. Based on city-level observations in China over the 2006–2022 period, this study applies double machine learning to explore the causal influence of the New Energy Demonstration City policy on energy transition and its underlying channels. Empirical findings indicate that the policy generates a notably favorable impact on energy saving and efficiency improvement. Further analysis of the mechanism by which policies affect energy transition indicates that government governance, corporate response, and public participation are key factors driving local energy transition. Heterogeneity analysis indicates substantial variation in the policy's effectiveness across regions with different industrial bases, resource endowments, and levels of green financial development. Spatial econometric results highlight the positive spatial spillover effects of the policy, as pilot cities facilitate energy efficiency improvements in neighboring areas through demonstration effects. However, the policy exacerbates energy intensity in surrounding regions. Moreover, under the geographic decay theory, the spatial spillover effects on energy efficiency exhibit a distance boundary of 200–500 km. This study provides critical insights for global urban energy transition pathways.

title: Process design and performance evaluation of an integrated co-electrolysis-based power-to-liquid process using AVEVA process simulation
abstract: Carbon recycling through an integrated co-electrolysis (co-SOEC) and Fischer–Tropsch (FT) synthesis-based power-to-liquid (PtL) process is a critical decarbonizing technology for producing sustainable fuels. Nevertheless, intermittent renewable power generation affects not only co-SOEC operation but also the heat management of the overall co-SOEC–FT synthesis process. To address this, this work aimed to develop a general flowsheet model of the integrated PtL process using AVEVA Process Simulation tools to rapidly identify feasible operation windows under steady-state and dynamic conditions. The stack voltage, predicted by three-dimensional numerical simulations of co-SOEC, assisted in enhancing the accuracy of the developed process model. Steady-state simulations indicated a PtL efficiency of approximately 57% following efficient heat utilization between the co-SOEC system and highly exothermic FT reactor. To ensure the durability of the co-SOEC stack during dynamic operation, process control strategies tailored to stack temperature and reactant utilization were explored. The relative deviation (RD) from the desired setpoints was approximately ±2% throughout the temperature control period, demonstrating the ability of the control system to prevent large temperature differences within the stack. Lastly, the dynamic characteristics of the PtL plant were examined under fluctuating renewable energy. The RD values for the flow and stack temperature controllers were within ±1% and ±2%, respectively, during the dynamic period. The proposed control scheme maintained a PtL efficiency of 56–60% throughout the 24-h test period. While the current process model employs a simplified FT reaction model, future research will focus on incorporating more detailed reactor-scale kinetics to improve predictive capability.

title: Theoretical model development and performance analysis of magnetic heat-assisted multi-stage solar stills for water production
abstract: Multi-stage solar stills improve energy efficiency by recycling condensation latent heat; however, conventional designs are limited by fluctuating solar irradiation and boundary heat losses, resulting in a restricted effective stage number and performance saturation. Here, we propose a photothermal-magnetothermal dual-input magnetic heat-assisted multi-stage solar still (MHMSS), in which a magnetic porous carbon film acts as an integrated energy-conversion layer, generating heat under both solar irradiation and an alternating magnetic field. A comprehensive multi-stage heat and mass transfer model is developed to predict and optimize distillation performance, showing good agreement with experiments, with relative deviations of 3.77%-5.14% for evaporation rate and 2.10%-4.29% for glass-sheet outlet temperature. The system exhibits upstream-dominated water production with diminishing returns as the stage number increases, while heat dissipation through the top wall and sidewalls primarily limits the effective working stages. Parametric analysis indicates that reducing the chamber height H enhances latent heat recovery, although excessively small gaps risk condensate contamination; an optimal H of 0.4 cm is recommended by balancing efficiency and water quality. Increasing the evaporation-surface radius R and sidewall thickness t further suppresses heat losses, and the phase-change driving force can be substantially strengthened by regulating the magnetothermal input. At a total input power of 2130 W m−2, the total efficiency (ηtot) and recoverable efficiency (ηrec) reach 335.29% and 283.82%, respectively, with an evaporation rate of 10.91 kg m−2 h−1. This research demonstrates the synergistic coupling of regulated magnetothermal heating with multi-stage latent heat cascading, supported by a unified theoretical framework that quantitatively elucidates the effects of stage configuration, structural optimization, and operating conditions, providing theoretical insight into the design of high-performance multi-stage solar stills for water production.

title: Sustainability frontiers and environmental impact assessment of the future European power system
abstract: • Framework combining eTIMES-EU, prospective LCA and AESA. • 392 scenarios to quantify co-benefits and trade-offs among environmental categories. • Identifies priority impact categories with high transgression and limited trade-offs.

title: Towards a state-of-art co-utilization for multiple solid wastes by integrating deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Achieving a sustainable balance among resource, environmental, and economic performance constitutes a core challenge in the optimization of multiple solid wastes co-utilization facilities. However, efforts in multi-objective-based evaluation methods are insufficient. Drawing inspiration from the robust decision-making and optimization capabilities of reinforcement learning, this study constructs an improved algorithm-deep reinforcement learning-based non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-III (DRL-NSGAIII) -to address this challenge. As a case study, a multiple solid wastes co-utilization facility in China has been chosen to demonstrate the applicability of the developed methodological framework. Results indicate that the DRL-NSGAIII achieved a significant improvement in the hypervolume indicator (+40.15%) and a reduction in the inverted generational distance indicator (-21.85%) compared with NSGA III. The algorithm demonstrates high stability in maintaining solution diversity and convergence performance, confirming its effectiveness in solving complex multi-objective optimization problems. Four representative pathways were selected from the Pareto optimal solution set and compared with traditional disposal modes. The results indicate that the existing synergistic disposal mode performs best in terms of environmental impact and energy consumption, with improvements of 150.7% and 98.15%, respectively. Under the optimization mode, economic benefits can be maximized, achieving an improvement of 92.2%. The balanced development pathway represents a “sustainable development” strategy that achieves a favorable compromise among the three objectives. While delivering significant environmental benefits and strong economic returns, it maintains resource consumption at a relatively reasonable level. The proposed algorithm provides a more efficient and intelligent decision-support tool for the multi-objective optimization of co-utilization paths for solid waste.

title: Green ammonia: A techno-economic supply chain optimization
abstract: Green ammonia is emerging as a strategic intermediary within green energy supply chains, serving effectively as both industrial commodity and hydrogen carrier. This study provides a techno-economic analysis of green ammonia supply chains, compares cost-effective procurement strategies from global production to European consumers, and evaluates ammonia alongside alternative hydrogen carriers. Therefore, a global Well-to-Border import pricing model was coupled with a spatially explicit Border-to-Consumer optimization to complement import prices with inland distribution costs into supply costs across heterogeneous consumer locations. Gaseous hydrogen consistently remains the most economical import option for Europe, though ammonia holds a narrowing cost advantage over liquid hydrogen (from 16 % in 2030 to 10 % by 2040). Competitive ammonia suppliers, notably Morocco, the United States, and the United Arab Emirates, benefit from low renewable energy costs, with marginal costs reaching 123 €/MWh for ammonia, 137 €/MWh for liquid hydrogen and 84 €/MWh for gaseous hydrogen in 2040. Optimal transport modes vary by consumer demand and distance: trucks are ideal for low demands at all distances, rail for medium ranges, and pipelines for high-demand scenarios. By 2040, ammonia will primarily serve direct-use applications, as hydrogen consumers increasingly shift to direct hydrogen supplies. Policymakers should prioritize pipeline infrastructure for hydrogen distribution, cautiously invest in ammonia's short-to medium-term infrastructure advantages, and limit long-term reliance on ammonia as a hydrogen carrier to mitigate stranded asset risks.

title: Production of green inventory in EU metropolitan regions: The roles of collaboration networks and knowledge networks
abstract: Promoting the production of green inventory has been widely acknowledged as a key factor in mitigating climate change and carbon emissions. As a special case of complex knowledge, green inventory is more likely to be developed through collaborative efforts that creatively (re)combine a wide range of diverse technologies. In other words, the production of green inventory requires regions to be well-positioned in both collaboration and knowledge (re)combination networks. Using patent data on green inventory in EU metropolitan regions, this paper examines the impact of regions' network positions in both interregional collaboration and knowledge combination networks on regions’ technological productivity and complexity in the green domain. Our findings indicate that regions with higher productivity tend to possess more interregional channels, hold greater brokering power in collaboration networks, and benefit from more intensively combined knowledge elements with lower risk in knowledge networks. Meanwhile, regions with higher technological complexity need a certain degree of disconnectedness and closure in collaboration networks, and benefit more from unexplored knowledge combinations with higher risks in knowledge networks. Furthermore, some policy recommendations are provided based on the results.

title: The nonlinear link between AI and energy poverty: Empirical evidence from global data
abstract: Despite the burgeoning literature on artificial intelligence (AI) and sustainable development, cross-country panel research on AI and energy poverty has predominantly assumed a linear association, potentially obscuring stage-dependent dynamics. We examine whether this relationship is instead nonlinear, using a balanced panel of 64 countries from 2000 to 2019. Employing two-way fixed effects and system GMM estimations with Lind and Mehlum U-shape tests, we document a robust inverted U-shaped relationship: industrial-robot adoption is initially associated with higher energy poverty at low penetration levels but with alleviation beyond a critical threshold of approximately 358 industrial robots per million employees. Heterogeneity analysis shows that countries with stronger human capital and institutional quality exhibit flatter inverted-U curves; they are buffered from both the early adverse phase and the subsequent alleviation phase, while maintaining consistently lower energy poverty levels across the AI distribution. Mechanism tests provide suggestive evidence for two supply-side channels, namely energy efficiency enhancement and renewable energy transition. Results are robust to alternative measures, Bartik IV, and spatial lag models. Estimates should be interpreted as robust conditional associations rather than identified causal effects, and they primarily characterize middle- and high-income economies undergoing industrial transformation, with limited applicability to Sub-Saharan Africa. We organize the findings through an interpretive framework labelled the “conditional curse-remedy transformation”.

title: Corrigendum to “On the social implications of technological processes: Towards hybrid social life cycle analysis (H-SLCA)” [J. Clean. Prod. 547 (2026) 147806]
abstract: exclude

title: A comparative study on fuel properties of products from hydrothermal carbonization and pyrolysis of microalgae
abstract: To achieve efficient utilization of microalgae from eutrophic water bodies, this study conducted low-temperature pyrolysis and hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) using Chlorella vulgaris as feedstock, and systematically compared the effects of the two processes on product properties. The physicochemical properties, structural characteristics, combustion performance, and nitrogen transformation behaviors of biochars and their organic extracts were comprehensively characterized by elemental analysis, FTIR, XPS, XRD, N2 adsorption, and GC-MS. The results showed that the yield of organic extract from hydrochar reached 26.34%, markedly higher than that from pyrochar (18.02%), while pyrolysis favored solid char production with a yield of 57.29%. The subcritical water medium promoted the formation of hydrochar with more developed porosity, abundant aliphatic chains and oxygen-containing functional groups, whereas pyrolysis tended to form a dense aromatic carbon framework (Lc = 0.86 nm, d002 = 0.37 nm). In terms of fuel performance, hydrochar had a higher HHV (31.96 MJ/kg) than pyrochar (26.91 MJ/kg), whereas pyrochar exhibited a higher comprehensive combustion index, corresponding to superior combustion stability. Fundamental differences existed in nitrogen transformation pathways: during HTC, proteins were hydrolyzed into amino acids, which were converted to pyrrolic nitrogen and immobilized in the char skeleton; whereas pyrolysis induced in situ cyclization of nitrogen-containing intermediates, gradually forming pyridinic and quaternary nitrogen incorporated into the aromatic carbon structure. Although both organic extracts exhibited high HHVs (37.71–39.61 MJ/kg), their high nitrogen content (4.56–10.11 wt%) may pose a risk of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions when used as fuel, necessitating subsequent upgrading treatment.

title: Valorization of spent hops: a techno-economic analysis of bioactive extract production using conventional solvent and supercritical fluid extraction methods
abstract: • Spent hops retain valuable bioactive compounds suitable for valorization. • Ethanol and supercritical CO 2 extraction were compared by techno-economic analysis. • Supercritical CO 2 extraction yielded extracts with higher antioxidant activity. • Valorization of defatted biomass improved the economic performance of SFE. • Supercritical CO 2 extraction showed superior profitability.

title: Water–energy–carbon coupling index assessment of aeration control and techno-economic analysis of hybrid renewable energy for wastewater treatment plant
abstract: • Developed a Water–Energy–Carbon Coupling Index (WECCI) framework integrating aeration control and renewable energy. • Quantified trade-offs between water quality, energy efficiency, and GHG emissions in WWTPs. • Identified low-DO/high-NH 3 -N regions as GHG emission hotspots using mixed-effects modeling. • Demonstrated robust scenario optimization using WECCI–TOPSIS under diverse policy priorities. • Proposed techno-economic hybrid renewable energy configurations achieving up to 30.1% energy self-sufficiency.

title: Satellite reconstruction of offshore wind turbine development processes in mainland China: Spatiotemporal patterns, installed capacity, and carbon reduction implications
abstract: Offshore wind power (OWP) has become an important pathway for mainland China to promote low-carbon energy transition and decarbonize its power system under the “dual-carbon” targets. To better understand the development process of OWP in mainland China and assess its contribution to global climate change mitigation, this study develops a Two-stage Offshore wind turbine (OWT) Identification Framework (TOIF) based on remote sensing. By integrating Random Forest (RF) pre-classification and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) refinement, the TOIF reconstructed a 15-year (2010–2024) OWT distribution dataset with an OWT identification accuracy of 0.9775. Based on scattering features derived from Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, the hub heights of all identified OWTs were estimated and subsequently translated into the installed capacity of offshore wind farms (OWFs) using an empirical hub height–rated power relationship. Combined with grid emission factors and life-cycle emission factors, the resulting electricity generation was used to quantify the net carbon mitigation of the OWP sector. Results showed that by 2024, a total of 7236 OWTs had been installed along the coast of mainland China, with 71.6% of the installed capacity concentrated in the 3–6 MW range. Over the past 15 years, cumulative installed capacity reached approximately 37855 MW (empirical variation range: 33810-41900 MW), with Jiangsu and Guangdong provinces accounting for 30.7% and 27.3%, respectively. Spatially, OWT construction has evolved from early nearshore sites (typically <10 m deep and <15 km offshore before 2015) to a deployment across <40 m water depths and <30 km offshore distances, with provinces such as Jiangsu and Guangdong extending into the 30–60 km range. The year 2021 marked a major expansion in OWP development, with 2659 turbines installed and more than 13397 MW of new capacity added. Based on the total installed capacity, mainland China's OWP sector is estimated to achieve an annual carbon reduction of approximately 50–67 Mt in 2024. This study may serve as a reference for monitoring OWP deployment and evaluating carbon mitigation potential in coastal regions worldwide.

title: Industrial-scale production of ceramic interlocking pavers with flat glass waste: Mechanical performance, life cycle assessment and eco-efficiency
abstract: • Industrial-scale production of ceramic pavers with 15 wt% flat glass waste. • Compressive and flexural strengths increased by 42.5% and 70%, respectively. • Glass waste acts as a fluxing agent, enhancing densification and pore closure. • Eco-efficiency analysis shows a 25% reduction in carbon intensity per MPa. • Diverting glass from landfills yields net benefits in human toxicity.

title: Valorization of phosphogypsum and municipal sludge into functional ceramic filter for closing the loop in the phosphorus chemical industry: A sustainable "waste-treats-waste" strategy
abstract: Targeting the "resource misallocation" of phosphogypsum (PG) pollution, this study proposes a sustainable "waste-treats-waste" strategy. By synergistically valorizing PG and municipal sludge, the phosphogypsum ceramic filter (PGC) was developed for the adsorptive treatment of phosphogypsum leachate (PGL). Specifically, PGC was fabricated via a two-stage thermal process (400 °C pre-calcination and 1000 °C co-sintering) using an optimal mass ratio of PG, sludge, and bentonite (4:4:2), wherein the sludge synergistically acted as a pore-forming agent. The optimized PGC exhibited robust mechanical strength (1.51 MPa) and satisfactory adsorption capacities (4.06 mg/g for phosphate, 1.61 mg/g for fluoride), validating its stability in dynamic filtration. To decouple the "black-box" mechanisms, a cross-scale verification framework was constructed. At the hydrodynamic level, the Wakao-Funazkri model revealed that hydraulic shear physically thinned the stagnant liquid film, effectively eliminating external mass transfer barriers. At the meso-scale, an interpretable Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR) model (R2 > 0.97) was developed to quantitatively optimize process parameters of flow rate, filtration time and filter bed height. Microscopically, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated an intrinsic "adsorption-induced crystallization" mechanism, where surface Ca sites chemically anchor pollutants via strong orbital hybridization, inducing the growth of thermodynamically stable Ca3(PO4)2 and CaF2 phases to ensure secure immobilization. Life cycle cost assessment confirmed an ultra-low production cost of ∼$0.16 USD/kg. These reconfigure the PG valorization pathway, achieving the "Zero-waste" goal and transitioning toward a green closed-loop circular system for the phosphorus chemical industry.

title: A case study of R-corporation Eco-design internal system development
abstract: Recently, the quality gap in environmentally friendly products between large South Korean enterprises and advanced foreign companies has been notably narrowing. However, the quality of Green Products from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in South Korea remains comparatively low. This study specifically examines R-corporation, a medium-sized enterprise, which currently produces Green Products of lower quality than those of advanced competitors. To address this, an environmental assessment of R-corporation's current situation was conducted. Based on benchmarking advanced enterprises, a comprehensive Eco-strategy, detailed Guidelines, an Eco Tool, and an optimized Eco Process were developed and implemented. This approach, integrating principles of Eco-design, is expected to bring about significant positive effects within the Green Product industries. Furthermore, this initiative is anticipated to serve as a valuable case study, demonstrating how South Korean SMEs can enhance the global competitiveness of their environmentally friendly products.

title: Designing an optimised carbon capture and utilization network for sustainable e-methane production
abstract: • Carbon Capture and Utilization converts green H2 and industrial CO2 to e-fuels. • CO2 capture and H2 production rates were optimised in a novel e-methane network. • Optimisation combines breakeven costs with life cycle environmental impacts. • Optimising both costs and environmental impacts increases e-fuel costs by only 2%.

title: Clean and efficient utilization of high-iron bauxite by reductive digestion based on structural modification
abstract: As the conventional Bayer process is the predominant method for alumina production from high-iron bauxite, its inherent inefficiency in iron recovery leads to substantial resource wastage and significant red mud discharge. To realize the comprehensive utilization of high-iron bauxite a novel structural modification-induced reductive digestion strategy was proposed to simultaneously enhance the alumina extraction and magnetize the iron minerals by generating reducing organics for following magnetic separation. The effects of key activation and digestion parameters on reductive digestion performance were investigated, and the associated kinetics and reaction mechanisms were elucidated. Elevated reductive digestion temperature and appropriate triethanolamine addition significantly promote both alumina digestion and iron recovery, whereas excessive activation temperature or duration leads to over-decomposition of polyethylene glycol. Under the optimized conditions, the alumina digestion efficiency reaches 96.96%, the TFe content in the iron concentrate attains 61.22% and the iron recovery efficiency reaches 91.99%. This work provides an effective and integrated strategy for the co-recovery of valuable metals from high-iron bauxite while minimizing red mud generation, offering a practical route toward more sustainable alumina production.

title: Food waste homogenizes anaerobic digestion performance across heterogeneous waste activated sludge through multi-scale metabolic convergence
abstract: Waste activated sludge (WAS) heterogeneity poses critical challenges for anaerobic digestion (AD), with organic matter variations causing substantial performance instability. This study demonstrates that food waste (FW) co-digestion acts as a “performance equalizer”, reducing methane yield variability from 22.6 to 8.8% across three heterogeneous WAS sources through multi-scale homogenization mechanisms. FW supplementation increased methane yields by 44.2–62.7% while narrowing VFA composition disparities from 16.8 to 4.6%. Mechanistic investigations revealed a hierarchical convergence cascade: (1) substrate-level compensation: FW-derived carbohydrates enhanced soluble substrates by 1.07-1.89-fold, with greatest augmentation in originally substrate-deficient systems; (2) microbial functional convergence: selective enrichment of identical functional guilds (Prevotella_7: 80.4-260.6%; Bathyarchaeia: 2.1-95.6%) established uniform hydrolytic-methanogenic capacities; (3) network reorganization: positive correlations increased from 60.8-63.2% to 69.7-80.2%, with convergent keystone species (Limosilactobacillus) coordinating syntrophic cooperation; and (4) metabolic pathway standardization: coordinated upregulation of acetate biosynthesis (ackA: 8.8-33.6%), methanogenesis (cdhC: 1.2-5.5-fold), and electron transfer genes (ribE: 22.4-67.6%) homogenized biochemical activity. This work provides mechanistic insights into achieving stable bioenergy recovery from heterogeneous WAS streams and practical guidance for implementing robust FW-WAS co-digestion systems in full-scale WWTPs.

title: Configurational product life-cycle management (PLM) for sustainability: Embedding carbon-aware decision rules in product design
abstract: Industrial firms face a dual challenge: delivering highly customized products while meeting ambitious decarbonisation targets. Although product configurators accelerate variant definition and quoting, sustainability metrics are rarely integrated into configuration logic, leaving life-cycle impacts unaddressed at the point of design choice. This paper asks: How can sustainability objectives be embedded as executable decision logic within product configurators? We introduce integrated configurational PLM, a governance approach that embeds life-cycle carbon metrics directly into configurator rule systems, linking configuration logic, PLM traceability, and module-level LCA data. Empirically, we combine a multi-firm field study with a quasi-experimental digital twin to evaluate how carbon-aware rules influence configuration outcomes. Across 1000 synthetic orders, sustainability-aware rules reduce embodied (A1–A3) emissions by 10–20% and increase module reuse by 15–25%, with a modest increase in processing time (+18%). Monte Carlo analysis indicates that these effects remain robust under realistic LCA uncertainty. The findings demonstrate that configurators can evolve from feasibility tools into multi-criteria decision systems that operationalize carbon-aware design. The paper contributes (i) a mechanism for embedding sustainability into configurator rule logic, (ii) empirical evidence of its impact on variant outcomes, and (iii) design principles for integrating and governing LCA data within PLM-enabled configuration environments.

title: Study on the interaction mechanisms of urban flood risk driving factors based on explainable machine learning: A human-centered assessment framework
abstract: Flood risk is shaped by the complex coupling of natural and human factors, and its scientific assessment is essential for reducing economic losses and enhancing urban resilience. However, incorporating nonlinear relationships, spatial heterogeneity, and dynamic population responses into flood-risk assessment remains challenging. In this study, an integrated people-centered assessment framework was developed by combining multi-source big data, RF–GeoShapley, and spatial statistical analysis. Hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and adaptability were systematically integrated to characterize flood risk from the perspective of spatiotemporal patterns, factor interactions, and population mobility responses. By introducing GeoShapley, this study identified the dominant factors affecting mobility responses under heavy rainfall and quantified their global contributions, nonlinear effects, and spatial interactions, thereby improving the interpretability of flood-risk assessment and reducing the subjectivity of weight allocation. The driving mechanisms of mobility responses were further examined at the functional-zone scale to support differentiated risk management. Using Jingdezhen City as a case study, the results show that flood risk exhibits significant spatial clustering and corridor-like extension. High-risk areas are concentrated in the central urban area, built-up areas along the Changjiang River, and the northern study area. Spatial location, housing price, rainfall intensity, and service accessibility make substantial contributions to explaining population mobility responses, with evident nonlinear, threshold, and spatially conditional effects. Residential areas, public administration and service areas, and industrial areas show more prominent risk structures, while dominant risk factors differ across functional zones. This study provides an interpretable approach for people-centered urban flood-risk assessment and targeted governance.

title: Innovation quality trade-offs in transport decarbonization: Evidence from EU environmental regulation and national resilience
abstract: This study examines how European Union (EU) transport-environment regulation shapes innovation quality across 14 major economies over 1998–2021. While prior studies have focused primarily on patent quantity, three gaps remain: quality–quantity trade-offs are empirically underspecified, mechanisms of differential national resilience are unclear, and instrument-specific long-run quality effects are poorly understood. Analyzing 43 policies and 147,832 patents classified under the Y02T10 Cooperative Patent Classification code for greenhouse gas-reducing road transportation technologies, we measure innovation quality using the Regulatory Quality-Adjusted Innovation Index (RQAI), which integrates forward citation impact, SciBERT-based semantic novelty, and Bayesian-weighted economic value. Results from exposure-weighted difference-in-differences and distributed lag models show that stricter regulatory exposure significantly increases patent quantities while degrading average innovation quality, which we term the regulatory "Quality Trap." The effect varies systematically by instrument type, with command-and-control regulation producing the largest and most persistent quality declines, while informational instruments generate positive long-run effects. Cross-national heterogeneity is substantial; the United Kingdom demonstrates greater resilience than its Group of Seven (G7) peers, consistent with stronger knowledge network centrality and dynamic capabilities. These findings refine the Porter Hypothesis by demonstrating that quantity-based patent metrics can obscure divergent quality trajectories and provide instrument-specific implications for sustaining transformative green innovation during decarbonization.

title: Integrated biodiversity, ecosystem services, and ecological connectivity for conservation effectiveness: Evidence from the Yuanjiang-Lixianjiang River basin, China
abstract: Global biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation have emerged as core challenges to sustainable human development, with establishing a well-connected, comprehensive global protected area system being an international consensus. River basins, as key biodiversity hotspots and hubs of ecosystem service provision, are critical for advancing global conservation goals. However, existing protected area planning lacks consideration of ecological connectivity and thus fails to meet the demands of preserving river basin ecosystem integrity. To address this gap, we proposed an optimized approach for river basin protected areas integrating biodiversity, ecosystem services, and ecological connectivity, using the Yuanjiang-Lixianjiang River Basin (YLRB) as a case study. We first assessed suitable habitats for 12 flora and fauna species, 4 ecosystem services, and their correlations; then identified key ecological pinch points between existing protected areas; next delineated priority conservation areas (PCA) via systematic conservation planning, overlaying these with pinch points to map integrated PCA and conservation gaps; finally, potential protected areas were determined based on gap priority and spatial clustering. Results showed: (1) a weak positive correlation between biodiversity and ecosystem services; (2) 10312.98 km2 (16.92%) of first priority and 11877.21 km2 (19.49%) of second priority conservation gaps; (3) 10963.53 km2 (17.99%) of highly aggregated potential protected areas. The optimized protected area expanded from 5953.65 km2 (9.77%) to 16917.18 km2 (27.76%), markedly improving conservation effectiveness. We further proposed hierarchical management and OECM-based supplementary protection for the YLRB. This approach addresses traditional planning limitations and provides a pathway for functional, connected river basin protected area networks.

title: Valorization of waste tire pyrolysis residues in sustainable asphalt pavements: Anti-UV mechanisms and eco-efficiency assessment
abstract: The valorization of waste materials in road engineering is pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality. This study investigates the potential of pyrolytic carbon black (PCB) derived from waste tires for developing anti-UV aging asphalt and elucidates the chemo-morphological evolution and eco-efficiency of the modified binder during long-term aging. PCB-modified asphalt (PCBMA) with a dosage of 10 wt% was prepared and subjected to accelerated indoor UV aging for up to 20 days. The performance evolution was evaluated via a comprehensive framework integrating microscopic characterization, macroscopic rheology, and environmental assessment, with base asphalt (BA) serving as the benchmark. Results indicate that the carbonaceous skeleton and inorganic ash (ZnO/ZnS) within PCB not only construct a physical shielding layer but also drive the migration of light components to the surface via a diffusion gradient. This process leads to the formation of an iridescent oil film, which functions as a dynamic oxygen barrier while maintaining surface hydrophobicity. The failure temperature increment of PCBMA was only one-third of that for BA, and its LAS fatigue life was extended by an order of magnitude. Furthermore, the asphalt matrix achieved a heavy metal immobilization efficiency exceeding 99.9%. Even under acid rain conditions, the leaching concentrations of toxic elements remained far below the Class II limit values for surface water. The annualized carbon footprint and production costs of PCBMA were significantly lower than those of BA. This research elucidates the synergistic anti-UV aging mechanism of PCBMA at the binder level, highlighting its potential as a sustainable modifier and laying a preliminary foundation for its future application in long-term durable asphalt infrastructure.

title: Integrated dynamic, regulatory, and economic assessment of onboard carbon capture systems
abstract: The decarbonization of maritime transport is a key objective of IMO greenhouse gas strategy, requiring reductions in CO 2 emissions. Carbon Capture Systems (CCS) offer a promising onboard mitigation solution; however, most existing assessments rely on steady-state assumptions and fail to capture ship operations variability. Also, Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) evaluation methods do not fully reflect operational impact of CCS, including changes in net emissions and transport capacity. To address this gap, this study develops a novel integrated dynamic framework combining real operational data with physics-based models of engines and chemical absorption-based carbon capture. The framework simulates CCS performance under time-varying conditions, develops an enhanced CII evaluation method, and performs techno-economic analysis, including sensitivity analysis of key parameters. The framework was applied to a container ship emitting 63,547 tCO 2 annually, with 42.65 GWh of recoverable waste heat, evaluating four exhaust-integration scenarios and design capacities of 2–16 t/h. CO 2 avoidance increased from 19% at 2 t/h to 74% at 16 t/h when all engines were integrated, while fuel penalties increased from 2.2% to 15.5%. CCS reduced CII from 5.1 gCO 2 /t·nm (without CCS) to 1.44 gCO 2 /t·nm (16 t/h configuration), achieving A-ratings across all scenarios. Considering technical, regulatory, spatial, and economic performance, the integrated optimal configuration is 10 t/h, capturing from all exhaust sources, achieving 70.1% CO 2 avoidance, sustaining IMO A-rating compliance, displacing 242 TEU (1.62% of capacity), and a CO 2 avoidance cost of 171.5 $/tCO 2 . The results indicate that CCS delivers substantial emission reductions while maintaining regulatory compliance and economic and spatial feasibility.

title: Environmental burdens eclipse economic gains: China's negative net benefit in global solar trade
abstract: Global photovoltaic (PV) supply chains, while accelerating energy transition, are reshaping climate governance through environmental cost transfers.
