The results demonstrate that, the maximum fluctuation range of the energy consumption loss was 41.49%, the maximum fluctuation range of the heat consumption of power generation was 7.32%, with a variation of 564.30 kJ/kW·h, and the maximum fluctuation range of the net standard coal consumption rate was 7.58%, with a variation of 22.80 g/kW·h. The maximum fluctuation range of carbon emissions resulting from electricity consumption was 17.93%, and the maximum fluctuation range of carbon emissions resulting from energy consumption was 70.21%. This study can provide a reference for the energy conservation and carbon reduction optimization design of municipal multi-source organic solid waste co-firing coupled with a power generation hybrid energy system.

title: Optimizing dual sourcing and transportation strategies for sustainable flower supply chains: A stochastic model with application to Sian flowers
abstract: The global floriculture industry faces critical sustainability challenges with air freight generating 3.5 kg CO2 per dozen roses—8-10 times higher than ocean alternatives. This research develops a novel dual-sourcing optimization framework that strategically allocates flower shipments between air and ocean transportation while balancing carbon footprint reduction with product quality preservation. Using stochastic mixed-integer programming, we model demand uncertainty, product deterioration, and environmental costs. Applied to Sian Flowers—a Kenyan exporter—our model demonstrates how strategic modal allocation can reduce emissions by 43.3% while increasing costs by only 2.4% through optimal 58% air freight allocation. Sensitivity analyses reveal carbon taxation thresholds at $45/ton CO2-eq trigger significant modal shifts. The study contributes to sustainable perishable supply chain literature by quantifying tradeoffs between environmental impact and operational feasibility, providing actionable insights for floriculture managers implementing resilient decarbonization strategies.

title: Redox-active Fe2O3 as a catalyst for humic substance synthesis in composting: Linking iron biogeochemistry with carbon stabilization
abstract: Humification is a key process affecting compost maturity and carbon stabilization, but the mechanisms by which iron oxide regulates humic substance (HS) formation in different composting substrates remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the process-level responses through which Fe2O3 influences HS formation and carbon stabilization in two contrasting composting systems, fruit-vegetable waste (FW) and chicken manure (CM). Composting experiments were conducted with Fe2O3 additions of 0.5% and 1%, and changes in physicochemical properties, humic precursors, iron speciation, microbial community composition, and carbon transformation were systematically analyzed. The results showed that Fe2O3 significantly enhanced organic matter (OM) degradation and HS accumulation, with final HS contents increasing by 9.8% in FW1% and 9.3% in CM1% compared with their respective controls. Fe2O3 addition was also associated with increased Fe3+/Fe2+ transformation, higher Fep levels, shifts in microbial community succession, and enhanced conversion of labile organics into more stable humified fractions. Overall, the responses to Fe2O3 were substrate-dependent, with FW and CM showing different patterns of precursor turnover, microbial succession, and iron-related transformation. These findings suggest that Fe2O3 may contribute to compost humification through coupled iron transformation, microbial regulation, and carbon stabilization, providing process-level insight into the role of iron oxides in organic waste valorization.

title: A graph-based C-BOM framework integrating multi-view xBOM data for efficient product carbon footprint assessment
abstract: Efficient Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) assessment is critical for manufacturing enterprises to enhance core competitiveness and meet regulatory requirements. The Bill of Materials (BOM) contains comprehensive enterprise data covering the entire product life cycle, serving as a key foundation for PCF assessment. However, traditional BOM frameworks suffer from data silos and a lack of carbon-related attributes, thus failing to support reliable PCF assessment and cross-system data integration. In this research, a Carbon-Bill of Materials (C-BOM) framework was proposed to integrate multi-view data for precise carbon source management. In this work, the carbon-related information across life-cycle stages was systematically organized by establishing a mapping model that links carbon flows with enterprise business activities. To tackle multi-source heterogeneous data issues, a unified C-BOM data model was constructed using a graph-based transformation algorithm, converting disparate data into a consistent, carbon-enriched representation. A case study on a telecommunications die-cast enclosure with 23 C-BOM items was conducted to validate the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the C-BOM framework effectively resolves data heterogeneity and enables accurate carbon accounting. This approach provides manufacturing enterprises with a scalable solution for optimizing product life-cycle low-carbon management and achieving regulatory compliance.

title: A multi-scale adaptive graph convolution-based carbon price prediction model
abstract: Carbon price prediction is crucial for improving carbon market efficiency and supporting climate policy implementation. To address the limitations of existing models in capturing multiscale temporal dependencies and inter-variable relationships, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Adaptive Graph Convolution Network (CETPNet). Integrating Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), adaptive graph learning, temporal-frequency dual-domain graph convolution, and interactive convolution, CETPNet effectively captures periodic features, cross-scale nonlinear dependencies, and the fusion of local and global information. Experiments were conducted on daily carbon price data (2015–2024) from three representative Chinese carbon pilot markets (Guangdong, Hubei, and Shanghai). The results indicate that: (1) CETPNet outperforms mainstream models (DLinear, Transformer, Autoformer, MAGNN, and MSGNet), reducing MAE by 15.6% and RMSE by 13.3% compared with the optimal baseline MSGNet; (2) ablation studies confirm that adaptive graph convolution plays a critical role, and its removal increases MAE and RMSE by 106.6% and 89.4%, respectively; (3) scale-specific adjacency learning overcomes the limitations of shared adjacency matrices in modeling scale-specific dependencies. Overall, CETPNet exhibits strong multi-scale learning and generalization capabilities, providing technical support for carbon price discovery.

title: Collaborative optimization of thermal safety and interphase stability of sodium-ion batteries based on ethoxy (pentafluoro) cyclotriphosphazene additive
abstract: The conventional electrolytes are highly flammable and it is a key factor leading to the thermal runaway of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Ethoxy (pentafluoro) cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN) is recognized as a good electrolyte additive for SIBs. In this study, the evolution of electrochemical performance and safety performance are systematically revealed by controlling the concentration of PFPN. The results show that the addition of 5 vol% PFPN can not only achieve an ideal flame retardancy but also maintain a good electrochemical performance. Na‖NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) coin cells using the electrolyte with 5 vol% PFPN shows good electrochemical compatibility and low interface impedance. When the addition of PFPN reached 7 vol%, the fire risk was further reduced, but the reversible capacity of the cells decreased rapidly. Quantitative thermal-safety evaluation of electrolyte, electrolyte/electrode mixture and full cell by PFPN addition is carried out. Key parameters obtained from the cone calorimeter test indicate that 5 vol% PFPN can effectively delay the ignition time, reduce the peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (HRR) of electrolyte. Meanwhile, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) tests reveal that PFPN can effectively suppress the thermal decomposition of electrolyte, the mixture of electrolyte with NFM at 0% SOC, the mixture of electrolyte with Na metal anode, and the full cell at 0% SOC, but its inhibition effect is limited for the mixture of electrolyte with NFM at 100% SOC and the full cell system at 100% SOC due to the violent exothermic reaction between the electrolyte and highly desodiated NFM with high oxidizing reactivity.

title: Resource-toxicity tradeoffs for cleaner production of battery-grade lithium carbonate via attention-enhanced LCA
abstract: Traditional life cycle assessment (LCA) fails to capture the critical tradeoffs between strategic resource dissipation and solid waste-specific toxicological risks in battery-grade lithium carbonate (BGLC) production, causing incomplete and biased cleaner production decision-making in the lithium battery industry. This study proposes a novel attention mechanism-enhanced LCA framework, integrating emerging indicators for lithium depletion potential (Li-DPEM) and thallium/beryllium toxic hazard potentials (Tl-THPE, Be-THPE). Multiple BGLC production pathways (lepidolite-based S1, spodumene-based S2, waste LiFePO4 recycling S3) were systematically analyzed to reveal insights obscured by traditional LCA. Traditional LCA results show that S1 presents the highest burden in traditional impact categories (e.g., GWP100, and HTPnc). In contrast, the proposed innovative framework realizes a significant restructuring of the environmental impact profiles for primary ore-based pathways. The environmental impact gap between S1 and S2 is substantially narrowed from over 400 times under the traditional framework to 64.68%, which is mainly attributed to the massive lithium loss in spodumene smelting slag (Li-DPEM: 0.255 kg LCE). Meanwhile, S1 exhibits markedly higher specific toxic risks (Tl-THPE: 0.00314 kg 1,4-DCB-eq; Be-THPE: 0.08 kg 1,4-DCB-eq), which are rarely captured by traditional LCA. The comprehensive evaluation guided by the attention mechanism conclusively identifies S3 as the most sustainable cleaner production pathway, with the overall impact index reduced by 25.5% (S1) and 14.4% (S2), respectively. This framework reveals the multiple advantages of waste LiFePO4 recycling in reducing fossil fuel dependence, avoiding secondary release of highly toxic elements, and mitigating ecological impacts from primary ore mining, strongly supporting the development of circular economy in the battery industry. This study not only provides a methodological advance for more adaptive and accurate LCA to address emerging environmental challenges, but also offers quantitative scientific support for cleaner production process optimization and circular economy strategy formulation in the lithium battery industry.

title: The robot revolution's green footprint: A threshold analysis of industrial robots and carbon emissions
abstract: As primary instruments of intelligent automation, industrial robots sit at the intersection of digitalization and decarbonization. Their environmental implications, however, are not straightforward, especially when total carbon emissions rather than emission intensity are considered. To examine this issue, this study uses a country-industry panel covering 33 countries and 15 harmonized industry groups. The linear specifications use the full 2000-2020 sample, while the non-linear analysis relies on a strongly balanced 2000-2018 panel to meet the requirements of the dynamic threshold model. The results show that industrial robot adoption is associated with lower carbon intensity, and this association remains stable across endogeneity treatments and sensitivity checks. For total emissions, the estimated relationship is non-linear: robot density identifies an empirical inflection point of approximately 2.149 robots per 1000 workers. Above this level, the marginal association between robot adoption and total emissions becomes more favorable, suggesting that the technique effect strengthens only after automation reaches sufficient intensity. The channel results further indicate that robots are linked to lower emission intensity through changes in factor allocation and production efficiency. By identifying where and when robot adoption is more likely to support decarbonization, the study offers a more cautious empirical basis for aligning intelligent manufacturing with climate policy.

title: Income-segmented intention-to-adoption pathways for organic food in Lima, Peru: A survey-informed system dynamics analysis
abstract: Organic food uptake in unequal urban markets often remains below stated consumer interest, especially among lower-income groups. This matters for sustainable consumption and cleaner production because broader demand is one condition under which more sustainable food systems can move beyond niche markets. This study presents a survey-informed, scenario-based System Dynamics analysis of income-segmented intention-to-adoption pathways for organic food in Lima, Peru. Drawing on an archived survey of 509 valid millennial respondents and segment-specific weights derived through the Analytic Hierarchy Process, the model tests five mechanism-specific scenario families across segments D, C, and A-B over a 30-month horizon: social influence, subsidy-based reductions in economic effort, their joint dynamic activation, knowledge of benefits and environmental awareness, and ethical-value activation. The results are clearly segmented. The largest end-of-horizon improvement appears in segment D when affordability relief and social reinforcement operate jointly (ΔP = 0.123), followed by social influence alone (ΔP = 0.087) and subsidy-based relief (ΔP = 0.051). Knowledge of benefits and environmental awareness in segment C produces a more modest gain (ΔP = 0.012), while ethical-value activation in segment A-B provides bounded directional evidence (ΔP = 0.020). These findings suggest that intention-to-adoption pathways under urban inequality are better understood as dynamic, non-additive, and segment-specific than as the outcome of a single common driver. All results should be read as scenario-based evidence on differentiated modeled pathways, not as direct observation or external validation of real purchasing behavior.

title: The spatial impact of pixel scale PM2.5 driven by policy dissemination. New evidence from a super urban agglomeration
abstract: Accurately quantifying the effectiveness of air pollution control policies is critical for the regional mitigation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5). However, most existing assessments are confined to the urban scale, thereby overlooking the fine-grained spatial impacts of policy implementation. This study integrated the 1 km-resolution PM2.5 dataset from the Multiple Air Pollutants (MuAP) with PM2.5 control policies across the Greater Bay Area (GBA) to quantitatively analyze the nonlinear relationship between the two at the 1 km pixel scale. We processed and counted the number of PM2.5 control policies, and quantitatively scored the quality of each policy based on Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Deepseek. We use the quartile segmentation method applied to population data to reasonably distinguish the entire GBA and main urban region for multidimensional difference analysis. At the urban scale, through the K-means clustering and Pearson correlation analysis, it was found that the PM2.5 concentration difference (time lag scenario) was significantly positively correlated with the quantity and quality of policies (best scenario R = 0.691, p < 0.01). At the pixel scale, the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model was utilized to construct a robust multi-factor nonlinear relationship (0.86 ≤ R2 ≤ 0.88) effectively fitted between PM2.5 and the quantity and quality of PM2.5 control policies. Further, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework was used to analyze the nonlinear spatial heterogeneity between multi-dimensional factors and the quantity and quality of PM2.5 control policies. Crucially, our findings also clarified that PM2.5 concentration changes between cities can be affected and propagated through the diffusion and dissemination of policies across different cities. This research provides new analytical paths and key insights for promoting environmental policy assessment, air quality evolution modeling, and health risk assessment.

title: Resilience formation mechanism and policy simulation of drone industrial innovation ecosystems: A system dynamics approach
abstract: The rapid development of the low-altitude economy is significantly propelled by the drone industry, a key pillar of its sustainable high-quality growth. However, the industry faces multiple external risks, including technology blockades and restrictions, talent shortages and brain drain, and declining public acceptance, which lead to its systemic vulnerabilities. Therefore, achieving strategic sustainable development goals through policy measures represents a critical challenge. Adopting a system dynamics approach, this study constructs a model of the industrial innovation ecosystem, incorporating enterprises, universities, research institutions, government bodies, investors, and the public. The model integrates four dimensions of resilience—diversity, evolvability, mobility, and buffering, to simulate the resilience under external shocks of varying intensities and recovery strategies. Findings indicate: (1) Resilience formation involves highly complex system coupling and dynamic feedback; (2) Different types and intensities of shocks have distinct effects on resilience. Technology blockades and restrictions are the most disruptive, particularly in scenarios involving abrupt or multiple shocks; (3) While single policy tools offer targeted benefits in specific contexts, they are insufficient for fully restoring system resilience; (4) Combined policy tools perform significantly better than single measures, demonstrating a synergistic structure led by supply-side initiatives, supported by demand-side measures, and facilitated by environmental-side coordination. This approach substantially improves the system's resilience to multiple shocks. This study not only enriches the theory of innovation ecosystem resilience but also offers a theoretical and methodological foundation for governments to formulate differentiated policies, optimize resource allocation, and build a highly resilient drone innovation ecosystem.

title: Facilitating group consensus for offshore oil and gas decommissioning options: An improved similarity-based model
abstract: The decommissioning of offshore oil and gas (O&G) infrastructure is a complex process that requires balancing diverse priorities of decision-makers (DMs) across various criteria. While multi-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM) methods have been used for evaluating decommissioning options, it is challenging to determine the final option when DMs hesitate among several evaluation values. This study proposes an improved similarity-based model to facilitate this decision-making process. It integrates hesitant fuzzy numbers (HFNs) to capture DMs hesitation during evaluation. This model employs objective weighting mechanisms, using the Louvain community algorithm for DMs weights and linear programming technique for the multidimensional analysis of preference (LINMAP) method for criteria weights. A comprehensive evaluation framework is constructed to thoroughly assess decommissioning options. The model is validated through a real-world case, as results match the actual decommissioning decision. The research findings highlight the model's strengths in modeling DMs hesitation, reducing subjective bias, and balancing conflicting decommissioning criteria. The primary contributions are: (1) an improved similarity-based model framework for MCGDM problems; (2) integration of HFNs in offshore O&G decommissioning projects; (3) objective weights of DMs and criteria using the Louvain community algorithm and LINMAP method; and (4) a systematic criteria system designed for offshore O&G decommissioning requirements.

title: Rapid nickel extraction from saprolitic laterite based on synergistic effects between mechanochemical activation and nitric acid
abstract: The shift to clean energy is driving a surging demand for the extraction of battery metals like nickel and cobalt from laterite ores. Atmospheric acid leaching offers mild operating conditions and straightforward process control; however, its practical application often suffers from long leaching durations and limited extraction. This study optimized the nitric acid atmospheric leaching of saprolitic laterite using the response surface methodology. The optimized conditions were 228 g L−1 HNO3, 96 °C, 100 min, and a liquid-to-solid ratio of 5.9:1 mL g−1, under which Ni and Mg extractions reached 94.82% and 94.05%, respectively. Four mechanochemical activation pretreatments on leaching performance were subsequently evaluated, with HNO3-assisted ball milling demonstrating the greatest enhancement. During ball milling, mechanochemical activation transformed the serpentine structure into a more reactive amorphous phase, while H3O+ and NO3− altered serpentine surface properties and reactivity, contributing to the disruption of inert plane, reduced particle size, and improved wettability. The reaction mechanism was further explored by first-principles calculation and molecular dynamics simulation. The synergistic effects between mechanochemical activation and HNO3 significantly reduced the required leaching conditions, shortened the leaching duration from 100 min to 30 min, increased Ni extraction to 98.2%, and improved slurry filterability. This work develops a facile and effective method for enhanced Ni extraction from saprolitic laterite, paving the way for greener and more efficient processing of laterites and other silicate minerals.

title: Mapping business ecosystems using AI: A case study on energy transition
abstract: This study explores the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for mapping business ecosystems, particularly in the context of the energy transition, a phenomenon of global significance that requires the interaction of multiple industries, nations, technologies, innovations, and regulatory frameworks. An AI-driven method is introduced to process large-scale textual data and construct business ecosystems as social networks. By analyzing datasets from academic papers, online news, regulatory documents, and a combined dataset, the scalability and accuracy of these ecosystems were assessed. The validity of the method was tested through an expert survey involving 90 professionals across 9 countries, multiple industries, and diverse roles. Regression analysis revealed a statistically significant relationship between network centrality scores and expert assessments, demonstrating the robustness of the method. The combined dataset provided the highest model fit but required significant computational effort. In contrast, academic papers offered a more efficient and interpretable alternative, achieving similar accuracy with significantly lower processing demands and noise. The findings suggest that AI-driven methods can standardize, automate, and enhance real-world ecosystem mapping, reducing analyst subjectivity and improving scalability. This type of mapping is useful in both theory and practice because it enables scholars and decision-makers to identify structural dependencies, coordination patterns, and bottlenecks that may not be visible through manual analysis, thereby informing strategic positioning, diversification, scenario planning, and policy design. Future research should explore alternative AI models and validation methods, higher levels of functional aggregation, and longitudinal analyses to advance the study of energy ecosystems.

title: Biogas production from Co-digestion of chicken litter, swine manure, and whey: A comparative study of batch and semi-continuous regimes
abstract: This study investigates the anaerobic co-digestion of agro-industrial residues, specifically chicken litter, swine manure, and whey, as a sustainable approach for managing waste and generating renewable energy. The improper disposal of agricultural by-products can lead to soil and water contamination, along with increased greenhouse gas emissions. Anaerobic digestion represents an effective alternative by converting organic residues into biogas and nutrient-rich biofertilizers, thereby contributing to both environmental and economic sustainability. The research compares co-digestion performance under batch and semi-continuous operating conditions, emphasizing the role of solid–liquid fraction separation. Batch experiments showed that co-digestion improves biogas production relative to mono-digestion, and that separating the solid fraction further enhances gas yield. Kinetic modeling (Modified Gompertz, Cone, and BPK) confirmed this synergy, showing enhanced hydrolysis efficiency and higher maximum methane production rates in the co-digestion mixtures. A 20 L pilot-scale semi-continuous reactor was operated through two distinct cycles to evaluate process performance under different Organic Loading Rates. During the first cycle (150 days), with swine manure as the main substrate, the highest biogas production was achieved at an OLR of 1.00 kgVS·m−3·d−1, resulting in volumetric and specific methane productions of 3.58 LN·gVS−1·d−1 and 2.47 LN·gVS−1·d−1, respectively. In the second cycle (140 days), where chicken litter and whey were used as feedstock, the maximum biogas yield occurred at an OLR of 1.50 kgVS·m−3·d−1, producing 2.70 LN·gVS−1·d−1 of biogas and 1.88 LN·gVS−1·d−1 of methane. Overall, the results offer practical insights for developing anaerobic digestion systems at larger scales, promoting efficient waste utilization and the advancement of sustainable bioenergy technologies.

title: High-pressure de-sublimation for enhanced cryogenic CO2 capture in LNG production from natural gas with high CO2 content
abstract: The growing exploitation of natural gas with high CO2 content poses significant challenges to the liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry. In particular, the conventional amine-based purification process incurs substantial energy consumption for CO2 removal, which escalates non-linearly with the CO2 concentration in feed gas. This high energy consumption severely undermines the process's economic viability and environmental footprint, necessitating the development of more efficient CO2 capture technologies. Cryogenic techniques have potential advantages over chemical absorption for this aspect, but the existing low-pressure de-sublimation process significantly increases the energy demand of liquefaction. To address this issue, this study innovatively proposes cryogenic CO2 capture by supercritical pressure de-sublimation, and the core innovation is pressure-synchronous operation of the capture and liquefaction units. This design achieves dual energy-saving advantages: it significantly enhances cooling heat transfer efficiency and, crucially, eliminates the latent heat consumption for subsequent methane liquefaction. System simulations demonstrate that this approach reduces the specific energy consumption for LNG production to 0.9183 kWh/kg LNG, achieving a 15.4% reduction compared to a benchmark low-pressure de-sublimation system of equivalent configuration. This enhancement contributes to an increase of 7.3 percentage points in the overall exergy efficiency of the system. Due to the reduction in power consumption, the power consumption of the refrigeration cycles and purchase cost of the compressors are significantly reduced, resulting in a cost reduction from 113.5 to 98.8 $/t LNG. Compared with established technologies such as chemical absorption and membrane separation reported in the literature, the specific energy consumption is reduced by 16.0% to 55.6%. The proposed high-pressure de-sublimation process shows considerable promise for advanced CO2 capture, thereby enabling a pathway to cleaner LNG production.

title: Not all mining is equal: The impact of lithium production technology on land, water, and emissions footprints through 2040
abstract: As electrification accelerates, global lithium demand is rising. Lithium production pathways—hard rock mining, brine evaporation, and direct lithium extraction (DLE)—exhibit distinct land, water, and greenhouse gas footprints. We analyze how adoption of DLE, an emerging extraction technology, could reshape these impacts through 2040 under three global supply scenarios. Using Benchmark Mineral Intelligence 2024 supply projections, we constructed a business-as-usual (BAU), a moderately aggressive DLE, and an aggressive DLE scenario. The amount of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE; a standard measure that expresses lithium content across different compounds in terms of lithium carbonate) produced each year was constant across scenarios. We mapped footprints of operational hard-rock mines and evaporation facilities and combined these with literature-derived impact factors (CO 2 emissions and freshwater consumption per ton of LCE) and representative DLE facility data to estimate future land use, freshwater consumption, and CO 2 emissions. Under BAU, hard rock and evaporation have similar current footprints (∼300 km 2 ) and together add ∼600 km 2 by 2040, while DLE's facility footprint is minimal (50 km 2 added under BAU). Shifting to DLE (moderate/aggressive scenarios) could avoid 141–381 km 2 of land conversion (20-50% reduction), reduce total freshwater use by ∼11% −32%, and lower CO 2 emissions by ∼9%-44%, respectively. Deployment of DLE technologies offers a technically plausible pathway to substantially reduce the land, water, and climate footprints of lithium supply, though realized benefits will depend strongly on DLE technology choice, site reinjection practices, energy sources, and the rate at which DLE can scale and displace other lithium production pathways.

title: Bridging the biophysical gap of Water-Energy-Carbon nexus in agricultural systems: A unified emergy-based framework for evaluating regenerative and demand-side interventions
abstract: The transition to sustainable agriculture requires navigating the complex trade-offs within the Water-Energy-Carbon nexus, especially as decentralized renewable energy reshapes the temporal and spatial dynamics of resource availability. However, current assessments often face the incommensurability challenge, where environmental costs (user-side) and ecological contributions (donor-side) are evaluated in isolated metrics, ignoring the potential of agricultural infrastructure to act as a functional buffer for the energy transition. This paper proposes a unified emergy-based framework to bridge this gap, moving beyond a conventional burden-oriented nexus evaluation toward an biosphere-work-oriented valuation logic. By introducing a phasic assessment approach, we capture the temporal dynamics of agricultural metabolism, redefining irrigation not merely as a resource sink but as a “virtual energy storage” component capable of synchronizing demand with renewable power profiles. Emergy, introduced by the ecologist H.T. Odum, is a measure of the biosphere's work in support of resource generation over time and spatial scales. Beyond standard accounting, we define two novel emergy-based indicators: the System-Wide Net Carbon Emergy Balance (USNCEB) to evaluate the shift from carbon load to ecological regulation service, and the Renewable Resource Substitution Emergy Efficiency (ƞRRSEE) to quantify the multiplier effect of the technological nexus. We applied this framework to a comparative case study of an integrated solar-wind-drip irrigation system versus conventional fossil-based farming across diverse intensive agricultural scenarios (China and Argentina). Results reveal a fundamental metabolic shift: the integrated system increases the renewable emergy share to ∼55%-70% and drastically reduces the Environmental Loading Ratio. The USNCEB shifts from a negative ecological debt to a positive value, confirming that the system functions as a net climate regulator rather than a passive emitter. Furthermore, an ƞRRSEE > 1.0 demonstrates a positive synergy, where the renewable infrastructure investment unlocks biophysical savings (fossil fuel and water) that exceed its own embodied cost. Our findings suggest that by aligning agronomic flexibility with precision resource management, agricultural systems can achieve a triple win of water productivity, decarbonization, and grid resilience. The study establishes emergy synthesis as a vital tool for revealing the donor-side value of low-carbon technologies, advocating for policy shifts from linear input subsidies to integrated payments for ecological regulation services.

title: Thermomechanically-beneficiated waste concrete fines as binder in 3D-printing concrete formulation
abstract: Excessive reliance on high cement content to achieve printability in 3D-printed concrete (3DPC) increases its carbon footprint. This study evaluates the potential of thermomechanically-beneficiated waste concrete fines (WCF) as an extender to maximise the binder substitution. A series of 3DPC mixes were prepared by replacing limestone calcined clay (LC2) with uncarbonated (UWCF) and carbonated (CWCF) waste concrete fines at 30%, 50%, and 100% levels, while ordinary portland cement (OPC) was replaced at a 30% level. Rheological characterisation, including the determination of the static and dynamic yield stresses, plastic viscosity, thixotropy and structuration rates, was conducted. Printability was assessed by extrusion pressure, layer deformation and surface defect spacing during the fabrication of 1 m-high hollow cylinders. Carbonated WCF (CWCF) improved rheological performance by reducing water demand, plastic viscosity, and yield stresses, leading to lower extrusion pressure and enhanced printability. Mixes incorporating 30% CWCF in OPC or LC2 systems outperformed reference mix (RefMix), achieving smoother extrusion (defect spacing >15 cm), stable buildability, and minimal deformation (<7%) at reduced extrusion pressure (112.5 kPa). In contrast, uncarbonated WCF (UWCF) increased viscosity and extrusion resistance (up to 235.8 kPa), resulting in poor printability at higher replacement levels. Under the investigated conditions, CWCF replacement levels of 30–50% provided a balanced performance in terms of printability and compressive strength. From a sustainability perspective, CWCF incorporation reduced binder-level carbon emissions. Specifically, a 30% CWCF replacement level achieved up to a 36% reduction in carbon footprint relative to RefMix through a combined effect of CO2 sequestration and partial replacement of conventional binders.

title: Modelling the performance of emerging last-mile modes in 90 European pedestrian zones
abstract: This article compares the operational performance and sustainability of drones, autonomous delivery robots (ADRs), and electric cargo e-bikes through a simulation framework developed for pedestrian zones in 90 European cities. For each city, 200 parcels were assigned to evaluate mode-specific routing, energy use, cost, and service performance. Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) was used to incorporate stakeholder perspectives. E-bikes combine the lowest energy demand with the low unit cost. ADRs offer the quietest, most space-efficient ground operation, halving drone energy use while matching bike cost, though their pedestrian speed lengthens service time. Drones deliver the shortest point-to-point travel time, 6–11 % quicker than bikes, but at higher externalities. Stakeholder-weighted MCDA scores average 0.83 for bikes, 0.61 for ADRs and 0.18 for drones, placing each mode first in one core attribute: overall sustainability (bike), low-impact night delivery (ADR) and urgent response (drone). The findings suggest policy mixes that fund cargo-bike infrastructure for routine flows, license ADR fleets for quiet off-peak distribution, and reserve drones for time-critical or topographically constrained drops. Such differentiated deployment can support decarbonisation, protect pedestrian comfort and maintain service quality in Europe's historic urban cores.

title: Energy efficiency-oriented R&D effectiveness in türkiye: A fourier-based analysis of renewable energy use, energy prices, energy imports, and foreign direct investment
abstract: This study examines the determinants of energy efficiency–related R&D effectiveness (RDEFF) in Türkiye over the period 1990–2022. The analysis investigates the associations between energy prices, energy imports, renewable energy use, and foreign direct investment within an output-oriented framework that measures R&D effectiveness based on energy-saving outcomes per unit of R&D input. Fourier-based econometric methods are employed to account for potential structural breaks in the long-run relationships. The results indicate distinct short- and long-run patterns. Energy prices are positively associated with RDEFF in both the short and long run. Energy imports are consistently negatively associated with RDEFF across all specifications. Renewable energy use shows no statistically significant short-run relationship, while it is positively associated with RDEFF in the long run. Similarly, foreign direct investment is statistically insignificant in the short run but shows a positive long-run association. Overall, the findings suggest that RDEFF is related to macroeconomic conditions such as price signals, external energy dependence, and investment flows within a multi-factor long-run framework. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between short- and long-run relationships in an aggregate time-series context with structural breaks.

title: Associations between urban 5D morphology and thermal environments: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and socioeconomic interaction across Chinese prefecture-level cities
abstract: While optimizing the multidimensional built environment is increasingly advocated to address urban heat islands (UHI), current research predominantly relies on static, dimensionally fragmented evaluations at narrow spatial scales. Crucially, comprehensive evidence regarding how morphological associations dynamically evolve across heterogeneous baseline climates, socio-economic contexts, and distinct urbanization phases remain underexplored. Addressing these multidimensional gaps, we construct a decadal panel dataset (2011–2020) evaluating UHII across 325 Chinese prefecture-level cities by applying the unified 5D framework. Using explainable machine learning, we systematically decode morphological elements' nonlinear associations and their interactive patterns with overarching socio-environmental covariates. Results demonstrate these morphological associations are profoundly context-dependent, revealing the limitations of one-size-fits-all planning assumptions. First, background climate significantly contextualizes spatial thermal patterns; Notably, high-density development transitions from exhibiting a strong escalating thermal trajectory in arid regions to manifesting relatively lower thermal associations within specific density thresholds in wet zones. Second, morphological patterns exhibit strict stage dependency. As cities evolve from rapid physical expansion to refined stock optimization, structural layouts like polycentricity correlate with lower thermal loads, whereas background densification increasingly aligns with a weakened association between fragmented green spaces and relatively lower thermal predictions. Furthermore, socioeconomic contexts systematically define these boundaries: economic affluence emerges as a statistical condition correlating with compact development's environmental potential, while hyper-urbanization corresponds to weakened macro-ecological buffering and indicates that extreme spatial connectivity correlates with elevated thermal risks. Ultimately, drawing from a comprehensive suite of findings, this study advances framework integration and scale innovation, providing context-resolved evidence that supports a shift from universal targets toward localized, stage-calibrated, and socioeconomically aligned precision planning.

title: Thermophilic/hyperthermophilic stage as component of temperature-phased anaerobic digestion or pretreatment of mesophilic digestion to enhance bio-methanation of oily food waste?
abstract: Anaerobic digestion of oily food waste is subject to inhibition of long chain fatty acids, key intermediates of lipid degradation. Given enhanced mass transfer during pre-digestion at elevated temperatures, thermophilic/hyperthermophilic stages in two configurations were evaluated: as integrated components of temperature-phased anaerobic digestion (TPAD) and as pretreatment units for mesophilic digestion (MD). When integrated into TPAD, these stages improved process stability and effluent quality but did not elevate methane yields relative to single-stage MD. Used as pretreatment, they effectively alleviated high-loading inhibition, driving substantial increase in methane yield by approximately 30.0%. Pretreatment contributed to high-quality biogas with a methane content of approximately 75.0%, enabling the total system to achieve a net profit increase of 10.0-20.0%. Thermophilic pretreatment was optimal for moderate-lipid substrate. Hyperthermophilic pretreatment showed superior lipid conversion capacity and mesophilic archaea preservation for high-lipid feedstock. Hyperthermophilic pre-digestion was more competitive in maintaining archaea survival under high-lipid loading. Future work should focus on enhancing hyperthermophilic lipid tolerance and hybrid stage integration.

title: Spatiotemporal degradation of coastal ecosystem services in mainland China: A land-sea integrated assessment
abstract: The coastal zone is a critical land-sea interface essential for ecological security and regional sustainable development. Existing ecosystem service assessments often fail to integrate terrestrial and marine subsystems and may overlook gradual hidden ecological degradation, resulting in fragmented understanding of coastal ecosystem dynamics. To address this gap, we constructed a Land-Sea Integrated Assessment framework to quantitatively evaluate the ecosystem services of Mainland China's Coastal Zone (CCZ) from 2000 to 2020, and introduced the Magnitude of Change in the Ecosystem Service Index (MC-ESI) to quantify the relative change in ESI and identify hidden ecological degradation hotspots. The results showed that: (1) the ESI of the CCZ remained relatively stable and exhibited a “first decrease then increase” trend during 2000–2020, while 55.97% of the CCZ experienced declining ESI values and the area proportion of Good and Excellent ecosystem-service grades continuously decreased, revealing widespread hidden ecological degradation under long-term anthropogenic disturbance; (2) spatially, ecosystem services exhibited pronounced patterns of “South strong–North weak” and “north improvement versus south degradation”, with the average terrestrial ESI decreasing continuously by approximately 2% (2.50 to 2.45), whereas marine ESI rebounded by approximately 6% from 1.51 in 2010 to 1.60 in 2020, highlighting the important buffering role of marine ecosystems; (3) terrestrial ecosystem-service degradation was primarily driven by anthropogenic factors such as land-use changes and nighttime lights, whereas marine ecosystem stability depended mainly on nonlinear synergistic interactions among oceanographic factors including temperature, salinity, and distance to the coastline. This study highlights the importance of integrated land-sea ecosystem assessment for revealing hidden ecological degradation and understanding spatially heterogeneous coastal ecosystem dynamics. The proposed framework provides a scientific basis for adaptive coastal governance and spatially differentiated land–sea coordinated conservation under increasing urbanization and climate change pressures.

title: Using interpretable machine learning method to predict children's fluoride exposure health risks based on routine water quality data: An empirical study in the Huaihe River Basin, China
abstract: Fluoride exposure in surface water is a persistent public health concern worldwide. Current approaches still face challenges in continuous assessment and timely warning of fluoride-related health risks. To address this limitation, this study used the Huaihe River Basin in China as a case study. Monthly water quality data from 377 monitoring stations collected between January 2021 and September 2025 were employed to develop an exposure-oriented assessment framework. The framework predicted children's fluoride health risks using routinely monitored physicochemical water quality parameters. The study first systematically analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution of fluoride in the basin. Health risk values were evaluated for adult males, adult females, and children. Four machine learning models were constructed and compared for predictive performance. These models included Light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), multilayer perceptron, decision tree, and extreme learning machine. The optimal model was combined with the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method to identify key influencing factors. Results indicated that fluoride concentrations exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity, fluoride concentrations ranged from 0.003 to 2.26 mg/L. Health risks follow the order of children (13.75%) > adult females (0.24%) > adult males (0.05%). The LightGBM model achieved the highest predictive performance, with an overall accuracy of 90.7%, outperforming the other models. SHAP analysis identified five-day biochemical oxygen demand, total nitrogen, ammonia nitrogen as key indicators influencing the prediction of fluoride health risks in children. This study demonstrates that reliable prediction of children's fluoride health risks can be achieved using routine monitoring data. The framework provides a feasible tool for early screening and preventive interventions for regional fluoride exposure.

title: Novel dual-cone hydrocyclone for efficient recovery of micron-sized catalyst: Turbulence suppression and separation enhancement
abstract: Micrometer-sized catalyst particles are essential in numerous green chemical processes, yet their efficient recovery from wastewater remains a major challenge for resource conservation and environmental protection. Discharge of these particles causes significant economic loss and poses serious risks to aquatic ecosystems. Conventional single-cone hydrocyclones suffer from flow field instability and high turbulence intensity, severely limiting their ability to recover fine catalyst particles. This study introduces a novel dual-cone micro-hydrocyclone that optimizes internal flow field distribution through strategic cone section modification, thereby suppressing turbulence and enhancing separation efficiency. A comprehensive investigation combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, particle image velocimetry (PIV), and experimental validation was conducted across four hydrocyclone configurations. The CFD and PIV results showed excellent agreement, confirming that the dual-cone structure effectively reduces turbulence intensity in the main separation zone, increases tangential velocity, and stabilizes axial velocity profiles. These flow-field improvements lead to more stable particle trajectories, weaker fine-particle escape, and enhanced underflow enrichment. Under the tested optimal condition, the Type II hydrocyclone achieved a TS-1 catalyst recovery efficiency of 90.4%, reduced the overflow solids concentration to below the industrial requirement, and improved the concentration performance of the underflow. The proposed dual-cone hydrocyclone provides a chemical-free, compact, and energy-efficient strategy for recovering high-value micron-sized catalysts from industrial wastewater. This work offers mechanistic guidance for hydrocyclone structural design and supports cleaner catalyst recycling in sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Moisture-regulated pad dyeing of cotton fabrics: mechanistic insights into water migration and energy-efficient fixation
abstract: Reducing water and energy consumption in cotton dyeing is essential for cleaner textile production. In reactive dyeing of cotton fabrics, improving dye fixation while reducing water, salt, and energy consumption remains an important challenge for cleaner production. In this study, a moisture-regulated pad dyeing strategy was investigated. A rapid and non-destructive method for measuring fabric moisture content was established and combined with time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance (TD-NMR) to characterize internal moisture migration during pre-drying. The results showed that during pre-drying, water migration and moisture loss were accompanied by substantial removal of free water and gradual contraction of the internal pores within cotton fibers, while the remaining moisture mainly existed as loosely and strongly bound water within the fibers. On this basis, the effects of fixation temperature, humidity, and time were systematically investigated to identify the matching rule between pre-drying moisture content and fixation temperature and humidity conditions. Under practical fixation conditions, complete removal of free water did not further improve dye fixation. Instead, dye fixation was mainly governed by the matching between residual moisture content and fixation temperature and humidity conditions. By appropriately matching pre-drying moisture levels with fixation environments, dye fixation exceeding 90% were achieved. Compared with conventional pad-steam dyeing, the optimized moisture-regulated fixation process reduced electric energy consumption and steam usage by up to 53.57% and 42.73%, respectively. This study provides mechanistic insight into moisture-regulated dye fixation and offers a practical optimization strategy for cleaner cotton dyeing.

title: Collaborative modeling and multi-objective optimization of integrated energy systems with diverse energy storage and flexible hydrogen regulation
abstract: Driven by the “Dual Carbon” strategy and the transformation of energy systems, integrated energy systems (IESs) have become a key pathway for improving energy efficiency and enabling multi-energy synergy. To address strong multi-energy coupling, complex operation, and high-dimensional optimization, this study develops a deeply integrated IES architecture incorporating diverse energy production, conversion, and storage technologies. A laddered carbon trading mechanism is introduced to internalize emission costs, while a flexible hydrogen-blended gas strategy and a two-stage power-to-gas model enhance system flexibility and resilience. In addition, Monte Carlo simulation is employed to characterize the stochastic behavior of electric and hydrogen vehicles. To solve the resulting multi-objective optimization problem, a feedback-driven bi-level collaborative optimization framework is proposed, along with a novel multi-objective k-means optimizer (MOKO) integrating shift-based density estimation, fitness allocation, and enhanced archive strategies. The model is solved using Gurobi in combination with MOKO. Results demonstrate that coordinated multi-energy storage significantly improves system performance. Compared with benchmark system 1, the proposed method reduces economic cost by 25.89%, improves energy efficiency by 4.32%, and decreases pollutant emissions by 96.28%. Compared with benchmark system 2, it achieves a 5.36% performance improvement and a 99.09% enhancement in environmental indicators. Furthermore, after obtaining the optimal solutions and conducting benchmark comparisons, a post-analysis is performed, including multi-parameter sensitivity analysis and multi-scenario Monte Carlo-based load uncertainty analysis, to further evaluate system robustness under parameter variations and stochastic load conditions. The proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for low-carbon, flexible, and efficient IESs operation.

title: Assessing container glass production decarbonization through amine scrubbing, calcium looping and electrification: a comparative techno-economic analysis
abstract: This study performs a techno-economic assessment of decarbonization pathways for container glass production. A reference glass plant with a capacity of 250 t/day is modelled in Aspen Plus, implementing an end-fired regenerative furnace. Three alternative and decarbonized configurations are explored: (i) post-combustion CO 2 capture via calcium looping (Case 1), (ii) CO 2 absorption using monoethanolamine solvents (Case 2), (iii) system electrification through a modular approach involving two cold top vertical melting furnaces of 140 t/day each (Case 3). The energy, environmental and economic performances of the processes are compared aiming at identifying the most promising solutions for sector decarbonization in the short and long terms. Carbon capture by calcium looping cycles significantly increases energy consumption (from 7.5 to 10.1 GJ/t glass ), whereas MEA scrubbing results in a moderate increase (7.9 GJ/t glass ) due to extensive heat recovery for solvent regeneration. The fully electric configuration drastically reduces natural gas consumption but increases electricity demand (from 1.24 to 3.8 GJ/t glass ). All options reduce direct CO 2 emissions by more than 76% compared with the reference case. In a medium-term scenario, MEA scrubbing emerges as the most economically competitive option under current energy prices and CO 2 tax of 100 €/t CO2 , with a cost penalty of only 18 €/t glass . In contrast, full electrification could achieve economic attractiveness in a long-term scenario, involving higher natural gas prices, lower electricity costs and higher carbon tax.

title: Beyond performance-cost trade-off: Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC) incorporating ultra-high-volume coal gangue wastes
abstract: Coal gangue (CG) is a bulk solid waste with an urgent need for high-value utilization. To promote its sustainable upcycling, this study successfully developed Engineered/Strain-hardening Geopolymer Composites (EGC/SHGC) with an ultra-high tensile ductility of 8.4% using 100% coal gangue aggregates (CGA) and 60% calcined coal gangue (CCG) precursors under a low fiber dosage of 1.2%. Results showed that replacing fine silica sand with CGA increased tensile ductility by 17.9%, and the increment of CCG/fly ash replacement ratio from 0% to 60% further raised the value by 27.3%. From X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric analysis, Brunauer-Emmett-Teller, microhardness, and X-ray computed tomography test results, the role of CGA as “additional flaws” was demonstrated, thereby lowering cracking strength while enhancing tensile ductility of EGC. Meanwhile, with increasing CCG contents, although the reaction degree of precursors increased, the microhardness of gel regions decreased whereas the average paste microhardness almost remained unchanged, resulting in enhanced strain-hardening potential while maintaining the tensile strength of EGC. The proposed ultra-high-volume CG waste substitution strategy achieved a synergy between cost reduction and tensile performance enhancement in EGC, offering a promising pathway for the application of CG-based EGC in sustainable and resilient infrastructure.

title: Integrated bioprocessing of garlic peel waste: Dual valorization through prodigiosin production using Serratia marcescens NITDPER1 and sustainable nanocarbon dots synthesis
abstract: Agricultural peels are the ecological burden that is of immense environmental concern in today's world. One of such wastes, produced in tons, is the outer skin of garlic (Allium sativum), which remains dumped, only leading to landfill issues and soil contamination. Looking into the lignocellulosic content of these peels, the objective of the present study was to utilize it as a bacterial growth matrix for producing prodigiosin through solid state fermentation (SSF) using ligninolytic Serratia marcescens NITDPER1 and subsequently converting it into a cellulose-rich mass to generate carbon dots (CDs). At the lab scale, the highest prodigiosin yield was 60.35 ± 2.3 mg/g at 36 h, with a maximum production of 55.22 ± 3.1 mg/g at 48 h in scale-up. Analysis of garlic peels (GPs) after pigment extraction unleashed 32.7% relative lignin degradation and 26.3% cellulose enrichment compared to the initial content, respectively. Analysis of GPs after SSF, through FESEM, FT-IR, and XRD, confirmed the structural changes in the substrate due to bacterial action. The cellulose-rich fraction after pigment recovery was successfully converted into high-value CDs, which revealed a broad peak at 340 nm in the UV-Vis scan, excitation-emission peaks at 380 nm and 470 nm, respectively, in the fluorescence spectra, particle size of 2.5 nm, and characteristic peaks in FT-IR, revealing successful production. The produced CDs were found to be non-toxic in haemolytic assay and immobilization studies on Daphnia magna. This study showed efficient prodigiosin production using GPs along with ligninolysis, turning it into cellulose-rich biomass for further valorization into biocompatible CDs.

title: End-of-life biodegradation and enzymatic hydrolysis kinetics of regenerated cellulose soft electronics: Influence of silver nanowires, silver ions, and substrate composition
abstract: The rapid growth of electronic devices use has intensified concerns over electronic waste, emphasizing the need for biodegradable alternatives that align with cleaner production and circular economy principles. Regenerated cellulose films (RCFs) are renewable substrates with demonstrated biodegradability, but the environmental compatibility of complete electronic devices remains uncertain when additives and conductive materials are incorporated. Here, we investigate the end-of-life behavior of RCF-based soft electronics with screen-printed silver nanowires (AgNWs), combining ISO 14851 closed-bottle respirometry aquatic biodegradation with controlled enzymatic hydrolysis. Biodegradation profiles were quantitatively evaluated using the Gompertz model, which confirmed that glycerol and PEGDE (Poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) modifications enhanced microbial mineralization of RCFs, while the addition of AgNWs slightly lowered the average ultimate extent of biodegradation; however, the cellulose films remained biodegradable, generally reaching more than 60% extent of biodegradation within 28 days. Enzymatic hydrolysis kinetics were fitted with the Chrastil model, revealing diffusion-limited behavior in crystalline microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) and higher accessibility in amorphous RCFs. Comparative assays showed strong inhibition by ionic silver, particularly in MCC, where the product concentration decreased by up to 50%. In contrast, RCFs maintained high hydrolysis yields (78–84%) and only slight reductions in hydrolysis rates. Visual analysis indicated in situ reduction of silver ions into metallic nanoparticles, with color variations attributed to nanoparticle aggregation and substrate crystallinity. Overall, RCF-based devices incorporating screen-printed AgNWs remained biodegradable, though overall biodegradation performance depended on silver form and coverage. By integrating mechanistic insights, kinetic modeling, and standardized biodegradation metrics, this work highlights how additives and conductive materials influence cellulose degradation and provides a framework for assessing the environmental fate of biodegradable soft electronics, supporting circular end-of-life management.

title: Compatibility assessment and comprehensive evaluation model for co-production of natural gas hydrate and shallow gas
abstract: Natural gas hydrate is regarded as a strategic unconventional energy resource with enormous global reserves. Co-production of gas hydrate and shallow gas represents a promising approach for advancing the industrial development of gas hydrate resources. However, significant differences in reservoir properties between hydrate-bearing sediments and shallow gas reservoirs cause mutual interference during production, affecting energy recovery performance. The quantitative impact of these differences on co-production remains poorly understood, presenting challenges in evaluating compatibility. In this study, a numerical simulation model for hydrate–shallow gas co-production was developed to systematically examine the effects of reservoir properties on production performance. A compatibility evaluation method was further proposed to assess co-production feasibility under different reservoir conditions. The results indicated that production performance increased with the flow capacity and reserves of the shallow gas layer, as well as the permeability, thickness, and porosity of the hydrate-bearing layer, while exhibiting a parabolic relationship with hydrate saturation. A compatibility index integrating productivity contribution and recovery factor was introduced to quantify compatibility windows of key reservoir parameters. The permeability ratio (ppe) and thickness ratio (pth) exhibited logarithmic growth, with co-production windows defined by ppe > 1.07 and pth > 3.68. In contrast, the saturation ratio (psa) and porosity ratio (ppo) showed parabolic and exponential relationships, with ranges of 2.13 < psa < 5.50 and ppo > 4.09. A comprehensive compatibility evaluation model was developed and validated using a large-scale co-production experimental system, providing a practical tool for evaluating co-production compatibility and contributing to the efficient development of unconventional gas energy resources.

title: Uncovering the interaction between surface water heavy metal pollution and industry-induced pressures in Chinese cities
abstract: Heavy metals in surface waters are major pollutants that pose substantial threats to aquatic ecosystems and public health, with industrial activities representing a primary source. However, the industry-source contribution to heavy metal contamination in surface waters remains insufficiently characterized. This study focuses on five priority heavy metal(loid)s, including arsenic, mercury, cadmium, chromium, and lead, developing an integrated assessment framework to disentangle the relationships between aggregated surface water heavy metal pollution levels and industry-driven pollution pressure. A case study was conducted using data from 336 Chinese cities during 2020–2023. Over the study period, the composite pollution level and industry-driven pollution pressure of heavy metals in surface waters generally declined. Nonetheless, their relationships were complex and spatially heterogeneous, exhibiting a hyperbolic relationship between overall intensity and interaction patterns. To further explore the driving mechanisms, we conducted a machine learning analysis incorporating the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework. The results indicate that industrial sectors such as non-ferrous metal processing, chemical manufacturing, ferrous metal processing, leather tanning, and metal products manufacturing play prominent roles in explaining the heavy metal pollution levels in surface water. Non-industrial pollution sources, hydrological conditions, and inter-city spatial relationships also showed high importance among the model features.

title: Sufficiency in principle and practice: An operational definition and typology
abstract: Sufficiency is emerging as a necessary concept as safe and just Earth system boundaries are increasingly transgressed, yet its definition and operationalisation remain fragmented. In this paper, we provide an operational definition for the concept, defining sufficiency as a state of enoughness that avoids both deficiency and excess in relation to fair social and ecological limits. Then, we develop a typology for the classification and analysis of practical sufficiency measures through a theory-informed content analysis of 1,101 proposed measures drawn from three diverse datasets. The resulting typology identifies five distinct types of sufficiency measures: quantitative, qualitative, use, sharing, and steering. To demonstrate the applicability of our typology, we test it against 33 policies presented in the “Sufficiency Manifesto” for the European Union, classifying policies based on the sufficiency measure type and whether they targeted the household, private, or public sector. Our analysis shows that all five types of sufficiency measures were present, though unevenly, with sharing measures least represented. This demonstrates how the typology can reveal patterns or gaps in current approaches and highlight opportunities for more comprehensive strategies. By developing an operational definition of sufficiency, clarifying its implications in both principle and practice, and offering a typological tool for analysing sufficiency measures across sectors and scales, this study advances the conceptual foundations and operationalisation of sufficiency, providing an empirically grounded framework for its systematic application.

title: Electrolysis with ultrafiltration membrane as a pretreatment for seawater desalination
abstract: The work explores the feasibility of applying membrane electrolysis incorporated with a low-cost ultrafiltration (UF) membrane as an alternative seawater pretreatment process. For the first time, this study evaluates the potential of replacing anolyte Na 2 SO 4 with seawater in both UF membrane electrolysis chamber, eliminating chemical anolyte requirement, paving the way for a chemical-free pretreatment. Likewise, the novel approach of incorporating activated carbon (AC) submerged in the electrolysis chamber as a supplementary flow electrode material is examined. The combination of dual chamber seawater UF membrane electrolysis incorporated with AC removed up to 99% of Ca 2+ and Mg 2+ , while also efficiently removing boron and bromide. Dispersed AC provides high-surface-area adsorption sites and functions as a network of conductive micro-electrodes. This adsorption-electrochemical interaction synergy enabled 60% boron removal in the catholyte, against 38% without AC. AC also improved anode-side bromide oxidation, attaining 99.5% removal while inhibiting the chlorine evolution reaction (CER), increasing selectivity and overall process efficiency. Operating at a reduced current density of 4 mA cm −2 resulted in comparable seawater ion removal efficiency within 5 h as that at 8 mA cm −2 , with 51% lower energy consumption. Also, Ca and Mg can be recovered as Ca(OH) 2 and Mg(OH) 2 , providing a low-carbon route to raw limestone mining for cement feedstock production. These findings establish that AC-assisted UF membrane electrolysis as an alternative low chemical and scalable pretreatment platform for seawater pretreatment.

title: Integrative design process for structural optimization: A life cycle assessment-driven approach for sustainable office building design
abstract: This study explores the integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) within the sustainable construction of office buildings, focusing on a case study in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with relevance to national sustainability strategies. Using a cradle-to-grave LCA framework for structural components, environmental impacts associated with material production, construction, use, and end-of-life phases were evaluated, while operational energy (B6) was assumed to be identical across all design alternatives and therefore excluded from the comparative LCA model to isolate the environmental impacts of structural system optimization. The functional unit was defined as the provision of 10,400 m2 of gross floor area of an office building over a 60-year service life, and environmental impacts were assessed using the CML life cycle impact assessment method. The baseline design, featuring a conventional reinforced concrete structural system, was optimized through multiple iterations, including the adoption of functionally equivalent and optimized steel structural systems, the use of high-strength steel, and the incorporation of supplementary cementitious materials such as fly ash. The results show that transitioning from reinforced concrete to the optimized steel-based solution reduced Global Warming Potential (GWP) by approximately 26%, alongside notable reductions in Acidification Potential (AP), Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), and non-renewable energy consumption. Prefabrication of steel components contributed to reduced construction-phase waste, while material-efficient structural design and recycled steel content further enhanced environmental performance. The integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM) tools with LCA methodologies proved instrumental in enabling iterative design optimizations and informed decision-making. This research demonstrates the value of integrating LCA in the early design process to achieve meaningful environmental improvements. By addressing key impact categories, such as GWP, AP, and Eutrophication Potential (EP), the study demonstrates how iterative optimization and material innovations can significantly lower a building's environmental footprint. The sensitivity analysis further shows the substantial environmental benefits of optimizing steel usage and increasing recycled content. Adjustments in steel quantities by ±10% and variations in recycled content from 0% to 70% revealed significant fluctuations in GWP, with the highest reductions observed in designs utilizing high-recycled-content steel. These findings offer a replicable LCA-driven design workflow for evaluating and optimizing structural systems in sustainable construction, while acknowledging that quantitative outcomes are case and context specific. The outcomes contribute to advancing sustainable urban development and support global efforts to mitigate climate change through environmentally responsible construction.

title: Manure and sewage dominate nitrate sources in runoff from key headwaters area in China
abstract: Effective riverine nitrogen pollution control necessitates the accurate quantification of nitrate (NO3−) sources. In this study, water quality monitoring, ion analysis, and environmental isotope tracers (δ2H-H2O, δ18O-H2O, δ15N-NO3-, δ18O-NO3-) were coupled with the Bayesian mixing model (MixSIAR) to apportion riverine NO3− contributions from four potential sources in the Dan River Basin, which is the headwater region of China's South-to-North Water Diversion Project. The results revealed that nitrate concentrations fluctuated between 1.20 and 5.51 mg/L, with significant seasonal variation (P < 0.05). Isotopic values ranged from 0.70‰ to 13.53‰ for δ15N-NO3- (mean = 6.70‰) and from −5.02 to 3.25‰ for δ18O-NO3- (mean = −0.40‰). Isotopic data demonstrated that during the wet and dry seasons, NO3− was primarily derived from the conservative mixture of multiple sources, with limited influence from biological removal processes. MixSIAR analysis revealed manure and sewage (M&S) as the primary nitrate source, accounting for 67.6% of the nitrate in the dry season and 46.1% in the wet season. Meanwhile, chemical fertilizer (CF) accounted for 16.1% and 34.8% of the nitrate in the dry and wet season, respectively. Atmospheric precipitation (AP) contributed the least (0.8% in dry season, 1.1% in wet season). Uncertainty and sensitivity analyses revealed relatively high uncertainties for M&S, CF, and soil organic nitrogen (SON) (uncertainty index (UI90) = 0.299–0.534), with the δ15N isotopic signature of M&S exerting the strongest influence on source apportionment results. Overall, the study provides critical insights to help local authorities develop evidence-based pollution control and sustainable water resource strategies for the region.

title: Integrating circularity and lifecycle assessment for building renovation: A multicycle framework
abstract: There exist different circularity indicators and lifecycle assessment (LCA) methodologies to calculate resource efficiency and environmental impacts of the building sector. But they largely operate within single-lifecycle boundaries and lack a consistent approach for assessing material across multiple lifecycles in existing buildings. This study addresses this gap by adapting the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI) assessment approach for the renovation of buildings (MCI RENO ), which accounts for successive lifecycles of the materials generated from the renovation. The MCI RENO is integrated with the Circular Footprint Formula (CFF) to provide a methodological operational unified framework for evaluating circularity and environmental impacts. Using a systematic selection process, seven end-of-life-cycle allocation methodologies were compared to identify the CFF's point of integration with MCI RENO . In the framework, the MCI RENO incorporates extended lifetimes and reuse potential, while CFF allocates environmental burdens and credits across multiple loops using standardized factors. The framework is validated with an empirical example of façade brick using seven scenarios and probabilistic uncertainty analysis of key parameters. The analyses reveal that material recoverability drives the degree of circularity and is sensitive towards varying scenarios. Similarly, environmental outcomes remain scenario-dependent and primarily driven by avoided virgin material production. The combined results are sensitive to contextual and scenario-specific assumptions. The approach offers a structured framework to jointly evaluate multicycle circularity and environmental impacts of inert materials. Future research across heterogeneous materials and renovation complexity can strengthen the robustness of the proposed framework.

title: Linking land cover changes to carbon storage in Hunan Province, China: Insights from multi-task learning
abstract: Long-term land cover dynamics are a key regulator of regional carbon storage, yet most assessments still rely on a few temporal snapshots and therefore overlook how land transitions unfold over time. Here we reconstruct annual land cover in Hunan Province, China, from 1990 to 2023 using a multi-task deep learning framework, and combine it with climate-corrected carbon accounting, driver attribution and future scenario simulation. Although total carbon storage increased from 2122.74 Mt in 1990 to 2209.98 Mt in 2023 in Hunan, this net gain masked pronounced spatial heterogeneity and distinct carbon responses to land cover transition frequency and pathways. Trajectory analysis further showed that different change frequencies and transition pathways produced distinct carbon consequences, with return-type pathways tending toward near-neutral responses and directional pathways leading to clearer carbon gains or losses. The dominant drivers of carbon storage were also not stationary, with vegetation condition prevailing in 2000 and 2020, whereas population density became most important in 2010. Interactions among vegetation condition, topography, and population density mainly shaped spatial heterogeneity in carbon storage. Historical-trend simulation further indicates that regional carbon storage growth may decelerate sharply by 2030, with only a marginal increase of 1.35 Mt relative to 2020. These findings are particularly concerning because the potential to offset the carbon costs of continued urban expansion through land conversion alone may be increasingly limited, making the protection of existing high-carbon ecological spaces more urgent.

title: Hybrid fiber-reinforced shield muck-slag-based engineered geopolymer composites: multiscale thermomechanical behavior and sustainability assessment
abstract: Engineered geopolymer composite (EGC) is a sustainable fiber-reinforced cementitious composite, with an excellent cracking-control ability and superior tensile strain capacity. However, the insufficient supply of conventional geopolymer materials and the low melting point of commonly used fibers (i.e. polyvinyl alcohol and polyethylene fibers), restrict the wide engineering application of EGC in high-temperature environments. In this study, a novel hybrid fiber-reinforced shield muck-slag-based engineered geopolymer composite (SS-EGC) was proposed, a series of tests were performed to explore the influence of hybrid fibers on the multiscale thermomechanical behavior of SS-EGC. Results indicate that the synergistic enhancement mechanisms of hybrid fibers for SS-EGC at elevated temperatures can be ascribed to the release of vapor-driven pore pressure through channels left by melted PE fibers and the post-thermal residual strength of refractory fibers. SS-EGC (P1S1) containing 1 vol% PE fibers and 1 vol% steel fibers maintains the highest integrated residual strength index (IRSI) values across the entire temperature range. Meanwhile, SS-EGC (P1S1) exhibits the best heat resistance at 800 °C, its compressive, flexural, and tensile strengths increase by 34.4 %, 28.3 %, and 140.0 %, respectively, compared to the SS-EGC(P2) with 2 vol% PE fibers. In addition, the carbon emission, embodied energy, and cost of SS-EGCs decreases by 19.6 %∼25.0 %, 15.2 %∼27.1 %, and 8.9 %∼21.1 % compared to the M45-ECC.

title: Optimizing CO2 absorption and desorption in water-based nanofluids: Predictive modeling and analysis of multifactor interactions
abstract: Nanofluids have emerged as a promising medium for efficient carbon capture, with water serving as an ideal base fluid due to its sustainability and low cost. However, the performance of water-based nanofluids is governed by multiple operational and material factors, making systematic optimization challenging. Additionally, the interactions between these factors and their influence on carbon dioxide (CO2) absorption and desorption remain inadequately explored, despite being critical for practical system design. This study systematically evaluates and optimizes the CO2 absorption and desorption performance of deionized water (DIW) enhanced by Fe3O4, SiO2, TiO2, and ZnO nanoparticles in a bubble flask. Experiments were conducted following a Box-Behnken Design (BBD), considering nanoparticle concentration, inlet gas flow rate, inlet orifice diameter, and nanoparticle type. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to develop predictive models and analyze factor interactions. Results demonstrated that interactions among factors significantly influence CO2 absorption and desorption. After optimization, the maximum CO2 absorption amount increased by 54.47%, 42.46%, 35.42%, and 180.89% for Fe3O4-, SiO2-, TiO2-, and ZnO-DIW nanofluids, respectively, compared to pure DIW. Meanwhile, the CO2 desorption efficiency was enhanced by up to 29.42%. The significant enhancement in capture performance, together with nanoparticle recyclability and the low-temperature regeneration capability of water, indicates that this optimization approach not only improves process efficiency but also provides a feasible route to reduce material consumption and regeneration energy.
