These findings underscore the potential of simple oxide nanofluids to advance environmentally sustainable carbon capture systems, offering guidance for process optimization and scale-up.

title: Completing the puzzle of aged microplastics towards microalgae at environmental concentration: effects of polymer type, size, aging method, and aging duration
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) could substantially impair microalgal growth. However, existing experiences were mostly based on pristine MPs under non-environmental concentrations. Fewer studies considered aged MPs, yet polymer type, aging method, and aging duration were never simultaneously concerned, regardless of MPs concentration. This study firstly investigated the effects of 1000 μg/L 1∼100 μm pristine polyamide (PA), polyethylene (PE), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) on Chlorella sorokiniana, with 10 μm MP displaying minimum impact among all polymers. Afterwards, 10 μm MP were aged via multiple methods (UV, heat, biofilm coating) and durations (30 d, 60 d), and aged PVC displayed most variation both morphologically and infrared spectroscopically. Microalgal impairment by aged MPs comparing with pristine MPs ranked PVC > PA > PE, while 30-d bio-aged MPs enhanced microalgal growth among all polymers. Influence of aging method was UV > heat > biofilm for PVC and PA, with microalgal growth inhibition being respectively up to 19% and 13% comparing with pristine MPs. Influence of aging duration was more observable for PVC, while 60-d UV-aged PA particularly displayed severe photosystem II damage (by 34%). Microalgal growth properties among various PE exposure displayed insignificant differences except for intracellular biochemical composition under 60-d aged PE. Influenced by MPs morphology and microalgal stratified extracellular biochemical profiles, aged and pristine PA as well as PVC displayed limited differences in nutrients removal, while 60-d UV- and bio-aged PE significantly enhanced nutrients removal. This study innovatively unveiled that, impact of environmental concentration aged MPs towards microalgae was most determined by polymer type, then aging method, and least aging duration.

title: Sustainability assessment of advanced calcium looping solutions for the decarbonization of the iron and steel industry
abstract: Achieving the 1.5°C climate target by 2050 requires urgent action in the steelmaking sector, as it contributes by about 7% to global CO 2 emissions. With Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) routes representing 30% of global production, their decarbonization is critical to sector-wide emission reductions. The current study evaluates the environmental implications of an EAF equipped with a Calcium Looping (CaL) based carbon capture unit via Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology. The environmental analysis follows a cradle-to-gate approach and it is conducted using the ReCiPe 2016 assessment method. Four distinct CaL configurations featuring variations such as intermediate solid storage and/or calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH) 2 , injection were investigated, each assessed under two alternative CO 2 transportation scenarios: T1 – onshore pipeline followed by offshore shipping, and T2 – onshore truck transportation followed by offshore shipping. The findings suggest more than 63% Global Warming Potential (GWP) reduction in the advanced CaL configurations as against standard strategies, primarily due to Ca(OH) 2 injection (i.e., enhanced CO 2 capture efficiency) and CO 2 purification unit (CPU) vent gas recirculation. However, these improvements are offset by higher impacts in Fossil Depletion Potential (FDP), Mineral Depletion Potential (MDP), Photochemical Oxidant Formation Potential ecosystem (POFP ecosystem ), Photochemical Oxidant Formation Potential human health (POFP human-health ), Stratospheric Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), and Terrestrial Ecotoxicity Potential (TETP). Of the two CO 2 transportation pathways, T1 and T2 show similar values in five indicators (i.e., Freshwater Ecotoxicity Potential – FETP, Freshwater Eutrophication Potential – FEP, Human Toxicity Potential cancer – HTP cancer , MDP, and HTP non-cancer ), yet T1 outperforms T2 in terms of GWP, FDP, POFP ecosystem , POFP human-health , ODP, and TETP. Of all scenarios, the advanced CaL configuration with two intermediate storage tanks coupled with T1 exhibits the best overall environmental performance. A detailed analysis reveals that the CO 2 transportation contributes around 16.8 kg CO2 eq. /t CO2 captured , emphasizing the importance of developing alternative transport strategies to reduce associated emissions.

title: Multi-source carbon emission monitoring and certification for carbon-neutral industrial parks
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-source carbon emission monitoring and certification framework for carbon-neutral industrial parks that addresses critical limitations in existing assessment approaches. To overcome boundary elasticity, temporal resolution constraints, and monitoring accuracy challenges that plague current certification standards, we develop a spatially explicit diffusion model based on modified three-dimensional Brownian motion processes governed by Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution principles, incorporating meteorological drift coefficients and establishing probabilistic relationships between emission sources and monitoring points through noncentral chi-squared distributions. The framework deploys a network of cylindrical monitoring zones with real-time carbon concentration measurements, coupled with inverse modeling techniques that simultaneously estimate individual source emission rates through constrained optimization of linear equation systems relating observed concentration differences to predicted molecular arrival patterns. We introduce Daily Carbon Emissions (DCE) as an operational metric enabling continuous rather than annual assessment, incorporating both absolute emission thresholds and carbon density indicators normalized by industrial output value. Implementation of this scheme demonstrates its capability to identify emission rates across multiple sources and quantify total daily emissions, enabling systematic comparison against proposed certification criteria. The integrated approach transforms discrete monitoring observations into continuous emission estimates while providing a comprehensive solution to boundary inconsistency, temporal coarseness, and verification accuracy limitations that currently undermine credible carbon-neutral park certification. This framework enables continuous verification for carbon-neutral park operation, as demonstrated for a combustion based or electricity dominated industrial park under the studied monitoring layout and meteorological conditions.

title: Intergenerational inequality and its mitigation scheme of carbon pricing policy under China's dual carbon goals
abstract: As China advances toward its dual-carbon goals, carbon pricing is recognized as a core policy instrument. However, the intergenerational distribution of its welfare impacts and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, potentially leading to intergenerational inequity. This study constructs a framework to evaluate the intergenerational effects, including a CGE model that disaggregates the household and labor sectors by age group and a Theil index to quantify inequity. By simulating different carbon pricing policies over the period 2021-2060, we find that intergenerational factors are the primary source of inequality in welfare losses, accounting for more than 90% of the total. Carbon pricing drives intergenerational inequality through both age effects and period effects, with the former indicating greater losses for younger households and the latter indicating heavier burdens on future households. Further, we design an inequality mitigation scheme based on carbon revenue recycling, combining intratemporal redistribution and intertemporal allocation. The simulation using the NDRC scenario demonstrates the effectiveness of our scheme, showing a 49.06% reduction in intergenerational inequality. The findings provide policy insights to alleviate unequal social impacts of carbon reduction and facilitate a just transition.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell systems accelerate decarbonization of urban buildings in China
abstract: Through an active transition to clean energy, China's power sector has achieved substantial emissions reductions. However, owing to regional disparities in geography and energy structure, carbon emissions from the building sector remain high. This study proposes a strategy for the large-scale deployment of distributed solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) systems to accelerate decarbonization in urban buildings. High-carbon energy sources are progressively replaced by natural-gas-fueled SOFC CCHP systems, while enabling their coexistence with low- and zero-carbon energy. A novel provincial planning model focusing on long-term economic feasibility is developed to optimize installed capacity for every deployment period, as well as efficiency and emission upgrade pathway in the subsequent operating period. Comparative analysis with the business-as-usual scenario shows that the deployment schemes in different provinces exhibit distinct regional characteristics. This transitional strategy reduces carbon emissions in the urban building sector across 31 provinces by 25.5%-53.6%. Although the strategy yields a total net benefit of approximately $73.46 billion, it is not suitable for all provinces. Pilot projects should be prioritized in provinces with both high economic returns and significant mitigation potential, such as Xinjiang, Hubei, Chongqing, Sichuan, and Gansu. This work provides an economically viable pathway to accelerate decarbonization in the building sector, supporting China's ambitious carbon neutrality goals.

title: Chemical-free lithium separation from high-salinity brines using model-informed and machine learning-optimized multi-column zwitterionic chromatography
abstract: Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technologies often struggle to produce high-purity lithium salts from high-salinity brines, as current approaches require chemical-based elution, regeneration, and precipitation steps, resulting in significant environmental footprints. A novel salt fractionation approach using carboxybetaine resin, known as zwitterionic chromatography (ZIC), has demonstrated that lithium ions can be separated from divalent cations under high-salinity conditions using only water as eluent, with no regeneration required. To enable continuous and scalable deployment of this approach, we developed a chemical-free Multi-column Zwitterionic Chromatography (MZC) process and its theoretical and process models. To predict and optimize this nontraditional separation system, we introduced a novel anti-Langmuir isotherm, and the isotherm parameters were estimated through a machine learning-driven optimization based on artificial neural network ensembles with numerical feasibility assessment. Using machine learning-driven optimization, the MZC process achieved 98.0% lithium recovery, 99.5 % Li/(Li + Mg + Ca) purity, a 31.3% productivity increase, and a 33% reduction in water use compared to batch operation. The proposed MZC process enables lithium separation at $0.6–1.2 kg−1 Li, with costs dominated by resin manufacturing, while offering lower separation costs and carbon footprint compared with conventional carbonation. Overall, these findings position the MZC process as an effective polishing step within scalable and sustainable lithium production pipelines.

title: Organic amendment-induced enzyme activation regulates microbial nutrient limitation and soil multifunctionality under arsenic stress
abstract: Arsenic (As) pollution severely impairs soil ecological functions, disrupts microbial nutrient cycling and declines soil multifunctionality. Although organic materials aid soil remediation, exogenous organic carbon (Exogenous-OC) alleviates arsenic-induced soil functional degradation remains poorly understood. This 120-day microcosm experiment explored how Exogenous-OC structural complexity regulates soil ecological functions under As stress. Multiple indicators including nutrient availability (DOC, available N and P), activities of C-, N-, and P-acquiring enzymes, microbial biomass (MBC, MBN, MBP), microbial carbon and nitrogen use efficiency (CUE, NUE), and basal respiration. After 120 days, the addition of Exogenous-OC increased the soil multifunctionality index by 3.0–43.8%. In contrast, As addition reduced the index by 7.6–22.3% in oxalate and amylum treatments but increased it by 3.5–18.0% in the glucose and xylan treatments, depending on the OC source. Early soil multifunctionality was mainly governed by MBC, basal respiration and ammonium content, whereas β-1,4-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity, total enzyme activity index (TEI) and organic matter decomposition dominated in the later stage. Moreover, elevated As levels increased microbial carbon limitation after 120 days. However, this effect was mitigated by Exogenous-OC addition, particularly when the carbon had greater structural complexity, as revealed by ecoenzymatic stoichiometry. Notably, glucose, xylan, and carboxymethylcellulose shifted the effect of As on TEI from inhibition to stimulation. This study demonstrates that OC structural complexity strongly modulates microbial nutrient limitation and soil multifunctionality under As stress. Glucose, xylan and carboxymethylcellulose are promising amendments for targeted remediation, offering theoretical support and practical guidance for the ecological restoration of arsenic-contaminated soils.

title: Fine allocation of agricultural water resources at “Region-Grid” coupled-scale based on water rights management
abstract: Confronted with accelerating global water scarcity and intensifying pressures on food security, the pursuit of precise and resource-efficient agricultural water allocation has become a critical condition for sustainable development. This study integrates geographic information techniques supported by remote sensing, multi-objective game theory and a bilevel optimization framework to build a county scale and grid scale agricultural water rights allocation model that operates through a dynamic optimize and verify loop. The model introduces an iterative feedback mechanism that links macro scale and micro scale processes, thereby overcoming the limitations of single scale water rights trading and enabling precise allocation together with dynamic cross scale coordination of agricultural water resources. Applied to the black soil region of Northeast China, the model substantially improves allocation performance during 2005 to 2022 by eliminating excess allocation at the grid scale. It achieves water savings of 23.82%-38.06% of total available water resources, corresponding to 8.55 × 109 to 1.78 × 1010 m3, and increases the number of supply and demand balanced grids by 1.014 × 105 to 2.074 × 105. The analysis further identifies pronounced spatial differences in regional water rights trading. The Sanjiang Plain and the central and western agricultural core zones in Northeast China function as major receiving areas, whereas the humid southeastern zone and the northwestern ecological zone act as primary supplying regions. This configuration produces a new allocation pattern centered on Heilongjiang and eastern Inner Mongolia, where post trade water availability increases by approximately 2.83 × 109 and 1.83 × 109 m3, respectively. The scale coupling approach developed in this study provides a new pathway to resolve structural imbalances in agricultural water resource distribution.

title: Circular economy-oriented catalysis: Waste PET plastics-derived Co-N5 single-atom catalysts for sustainable pollutants removal via non-radical electron transfer
abstract: The growing environmental burden of plastic waste and antibiotic contamination demands scalable solutions. Accordingly, this study valorizes waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into asymmetric Co-N5 single-atom catalysts (Co-SA/NPC) through a multi-step protocol: molten salt carbonization, Zn/Co bimetallic coordination, and N-doped pyrolysis. The resulting catalyst features atomically dispersed Co sites within a hierarchically porous carbon matrix, demonstrating exceptional peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation capability. Specifically, the system achieves 83.2% tetracycline (TC) removal within 20 min with a kobs of 0.096 min−1, while maintaining over 80% efficiency across a broad pH range of 3 to 11 and under high ionic strength conditions, thus establishing a laboratory foundation for future practical water treatment applications. Mechanistic investigation via DFT calculations reveals that the asymmetric Co-N5 configuration induces a 1.34 eV downshift in the d-band center. This electronic modulation optimizes electron transfer kinetics and elongates the O-O bond in PMS. Consistent with this, experimental analyses (electron paramagnetic resonance, electrochemistry) confirm a dominant non-radical electron transfer pathway. This mechanism confers tolerance to radical scavengers and enables selective oxidation of electron-rich contaminants. Furthermore, to demonstrate practical utility, a fabricated Co-SA/NPC/PVDF composite membrane module achieved stable contaminant removal (>72 h continuous operation) when tested in diverse real water matrices. Beyond performance, techno-economic analysis based on a laboratory-scale levelized cost model shows that the total levelized production cost of the as-prepared Co-SA/NPC catalyst is approximately 40,222 $/kg, with electricity consumption identified as the primary cost contributor for catalyst production (accounting for 86.43% of the total cost), a cost structure consistent with the industry benchmark of similar persulfate-based advanced oxidation processes. Concurrently, the toxicity assessment indicates >80% detoxification of TC degradation intermediates, with negligible mutagenicity and bioaccumulation risks identified. Collectively, this work integrates valorization of plastic waste and atomic-scale catalytic engineering, thereby providing an industrially viable blueprint for sustainable environmental remediation under a waste-treats-waste paradigm.

title: Decoding the effect of SO2 on CO2 capture: A combined Ab initio molecular dynamics and spectroscopic approach
abstract: SO2 co-absorption can impair amine-based CO2 capture, but its molecular impact on CO2–amine reaction pathways remain unclear. Here, AIMD-metadynamics, in situ Raman spectroscopy, quantitative 13C NMR, and dynamic desorption measurements were combined to clarify how SO2 perturbs aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) chemistry. The free-energy surfaces show that SO2 increases the barrier for proton transfer from the zwitterionic intermediate to carbamate, while lowering the reverse carbamate-to-zwitterion barrier, indicating inhibited carbamate formation and reduced carbamate stability. AIMD trajectories further reveal enhanced amine protonation and weakened MEA–CO2 association under SO2 loading. These predictions are validated experimentally: Raman and 13C NMR spectra show decreased MEACOO− signals and increased MEAH+/HCO3− contributions during CO2/SO2 co-absorption. Dynamic desorption tests further demonstrate earlier CO2 release but a lower total desorbed amount after SO2 loading. These results identify SO2-induced proton-transfer inhibition, carbamate destabilization, and amine protonation as key mechanisms governing the loss of CO2 capture–regeneration performance.

title: Sustainable growth capacity and growth alignment: The roles of ESG performance and cost stickiness
abstract: This study examines how environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and cost stickiness are associated with firms’ sustainable growth rate (SGR) by distinguishing between growth capacity and growth alignment. Using an unbalanced panel of non-financial firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand from 2014 to 2024, the analysis employs firm fixed-effects models with weighted least squares and autocorrelation adjustments to address heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and dynamic growth behavior. The results show that cost stickiness is positively and significantly associated with SGR across all specifications (β = 0.0028, p < 0.001), suggesting that retaining organizational resources may strengthen long-term growth capacity and resilience. However, cost stickiness is also positively and significantly associated with GAP (β = 0.0469, p < 0.001), indicating that rigid cost structures may reduce operational flexibility and increase growth misalignment. In contrast, ESG performance is negatively and significantly associated with SGR (β = −0.0002, p < 0.001) and does not exhibit a consistent relationship with GAP, suggesting that ESG engagement reallocates resources toward long-term sustainability objectives, particularly environmental investment and compliance commitments rather than aggressive short-term expansion. Economically, a one-standard-deviation increase in cost stickiness is associated with approximately a 0.26 percentage-point increase in SGR, whereas a one-standard-deviation increase in ESG performance corresponds to an approximate 0.28 percentage-point reduction in SGR, relative to a mean SGR of 6.8%. The ESG pillar decomposition further reveals that the environmental dimension primarily drives the negative ESG–SGR relationship, while the social dimension is negatively associated with GAP, suggesting improved growth alignment. Thus, cost retention appears to strengthen sustainable growth capacity while increasing growth misalignment, whereas ESG engagement is associated with more disciplined growth without materially increasing misalignment. These findings contribute to the sustainable growth literature by integrating the resource-based view and stakeholder theory within a dual-dimensional framework of growth capacity and growth alignment. The study highlights that sustainable growth should be evaluated not only in terms of growth magnitude, but also in terms of how closely realized growth aligns with internally sustainable capacity. The findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal, and future research may further explore these relationships using causal identification strategies and cross-country evidence.

title: Enhancing microbial oils production from food waste-derived short-chain fatty acids via gas-permeable membrane nitrogen recovery
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids-rich fermentation liquids from food waste acidogenic fermentation contain high nitrogen concentrations that hinder lipid accumulation in yeast. Thus, achieving high carbon/nitrogen (C/N) ratio remains a key challenge for the valorization of fermentation liquors for microbial oils production. This work demonstrates the integration of nitrogen recovery using a gas-permeable membrane (GPM) with lipid production by oleaginous yeast. This nitrogen recovery from the fermentation liquids increased the C/N in fermentation broths, thereby boosting lipid accumulation. Specifically, GPM was able to recover 97 % of ammoniacal nitrogen in fermentation liquids, doubling the C/N and increasing lipid content by 2-3-fold in shake flask cultivations. Scaling up the process to a lab-scale bioreactor further increased lipid accumulation, reaching up to 30 % w/w lipids (4-fold increase) due to more controlled operational conditions. The study also evaluated the ability of Yarrowia lipolytica to metabolize organic and inorganic nitrogen sources, which is important to understand how the C/N influences microbial oils production. Although Y. lipolytica showed a preference for inorganic nitrogen ( i.e. , ammonium sulfate), bovine serum albumin was also consumed, though at approximately half the consumption rate. Overall, these finding prove that nitrogen recovery via GPM is an effective strategy to increase the C/N of fermentation liquids and promote lipid accumulation in yeast, therefore contributing to the development of an integrated waste-to-resource system within a circular economy framework.

title: Evaluating the sustainability of Montado farm's pastures: Insights from emergy and nitrogen footprint assessments of pastures with reduced productivity
abstract: The Montado ecosystem, a Mediterranean agro-silvo-pastoral system, plays a vital role in sustainable livestock production, yet faces increasing challenges from climate variability and pasture productivity decline. This study evaluates the sustainability of two Montado farms integrating cattle and sheep production by applying emergy and nitrogen footprint assessment under three different pasture productivity scenarios. Emergy indicators highlight the reliance on external resources during droughts, while nitrogen (N) footprint analysis underscores the potential environmental costs of maintaining livestock productivity under such conditions. Results indicate that cattle production is more emergy-efficient under regular pasture productivity, whereas sheep production consistently exhibits lower N losses and lower sensitivity to pasture decline. Integrating emergy and N footprint assessments reveals that increasing reliance on external feed to compensate for pasture reduction leads to higher resource dependence and N losses, particularly in cattle systems. These findings support management strategies that prioritize pasture-based feeding, promote legume-rich pastures to enhance N efficiency, and encourage mixed sheep–cattle systems as a means to buffer sustainability trade-offs under increasing climatic variability.

title: Exploring necessary and sufficient values in driving consumers’ willingness to pay premiums and purchase intentions for green food
abstract: Amidst myriad sustainable challenges associated with food consumption, green food is gaining prominence. Despite the growing importance, the green food market is at its nascent stage. Understanding consumption value perceptions to effectively stimulate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intention for green food has become ubiquitous in consumer research. Using the well-established theoretical lens-the theory of consumption value, the present study aims to get a comprehensive understanding of multidimensional consumption values impacting WTP and green food choice behaviour. Unlike the existing research, predominantly focused on sufficient value, the study applies a dual-methodological approach that integrates both sufficiency (should have) and necessity (must-have) perspectives. Data were collected from individuals aged 18 and above living in India (n = 340). Structural equation modelling (SEM) was applied to identify the values influencing WTP and purchase intention for green food. By incorporating necessary condition analysis (NCA), the study identifies the necessary values indispensable to achieving the outcome related to WTP and green food purchase intention. Results indicate that all of the proposed consumption values - functional, social, epistemic, health and environmental-significantly influence consumers' WTP from both “sufficiency” and “necessary” perspectives, whereas these value perceptions, except environmental value, are either ‘sufficient’ or ‘necessary' for the choice outcome related to green food purchase intention. The most critical influencing factor is environmental value, as it shows consistent influence on WTP and PI from both perspectives, sufficiency and necessity. Enhancement of environmental values significantly enhances WTP and, thereby, PI for green food. This study adds new depths to the existing understandings of the value propositions of green food to effectively stimulate the value-based positioning of green food products in the Indian context.

title: Labor and education factors' empirical enlightenment on environmental-economic decoupling: Evidence from China
abstract: Labor, as the foundation of economic activities, influences low-carbon economy through factor inputs. China's educational system is undergoing a transition from quantitative expansion to qualitative improvement, shaped by the interplay between policy regulation and social demand. This paper delves into the roles played by labor and education factors in the decoupling of economic growth from CO2 emissions in China from 2000 to 2023. Results show that: (1) The decoupling process of China can be specifically divided into four phases comprising five decoupling statuses: weak decoupling (WD), expansive coupling (EC), weak decoupling (WD), strong decoupling (SD) and weak decoupling (WD). (2) Labor productivity (DLD), educational density (DPK) and educational scale (DK) constitute the primary determinants of decoupling. This underscores a nonlinear relationship where human capital initially exacerbates CO2 emissions during industrialization, yet subsequently fosters cleaner growth through the expansion of skill-intensive sectors. (3) The impact of demographic dividend (DDD) on decoupling has remained at a low level, indicating that quality rather than quantity serves as the high-quality input driving low-carbon economic development. It is imperative to integrate the enhancement of educational quality and workforce capacity building into the core strategy of national low-carbon development. Specifically, optimize the allocation of educational resources and shift fiscal investment from a broad-based approach to a targeted investment model; reduce institutional transaction costs and promote the spatially optimal allocation of highly skilled talents; and drive the digital and intelligent transformation to unleash the ‘multiplier effect’ generated by the synergy between digital technologies and high-quality human capital.

title: Tracking the carbon footprint of the iron and steel industry along the supply chain: From the urban agglomeration level
abstract: The cross-city carbon footprint (CF) transmission and structural evolution of ISI at the urban agglomeration scale are firstly quantified from both production- and consumption-driven perspectives. Using an environmental extended multi-regional input-output (EE-MRIO) model and structural path analysis (SPA), the CF spatial evolution and the supply-chain transmission of ISI at the urban agglomeration level were first traced. From 2012 to 2017, the total CF increased by 29%, accompanied by structural shift from dispersed multi-point pattern to a core-periphery configuration dominated by key production cities such as Anshan, Benxi and Yingkou, indicating the central role in interregional CF transfer. Upstream CF were primarily driven by energy-intensive sectors, especially electricity and heat supply, coking, and coal mining, reflecting a transition from local resource dependence to cross-regional energy-system dependence. Notably in 2017, external energy inputs from the HCM induced about 12.4 MtCO2 to CF growth. Downstream demand expanded from intraregional construction and manufacturing to major regions such as the YRD and BTH. From 2018 to 2023, the driving factors and evolutionary simulation show the improvements in energy intensity and structure partly offset CF, but industrial expansion and final demand remains the dominant driver of CF growth. Without structural adjustment, demand growth will continuously reinforce CF along existing supply chain paths. These results reveal a CF structural mechanism of ISI, provide differentiated implications for urban agglomerations: traditional industrial regions should prioritize reducing upstream energy and material dependence, emerging industrial regions should focus on restructuring and technological upgrading, while consumption-oriented regions should address embodied CF through demand-side measures.

title: Closed-loop recycling of End-of-Life tires via devulcanized rubber: Life Cycle Assessment and circularity evaluation with durability trade-offs
abstract: More than 3 million tons of End-of-Life Tires (ELTs) are generated annually in Europe, with 91–95% currently managed through down-cycling processes for energy or material recovery. An Italian consortium has recently developed a closed-loop recycling process that enables the use of ELTs for producing new heavy-transportation tires. The baseline formulation has been validated through large-scale road testing, demonstrating performance comparable to traditional tires. This study evaluates the environmental performance and circularity of tread compounds incorporating devulcanized elastomer obtained from ELTs. Using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI), four formulations were assessed: a traditional virgin compound and three containing 20%, 30%, and 50% recycled elastomer (20R–80V, 30R–70V, and 50R–50V, respectively, where R and V indicate recycled and virgin rubber content). The LCA results show that natural rubber is the main contributor to the environmental impacts, accounting for more than half of the burdens in most categories. Partial substitution with devulcanized elastomer leads to consistent impact reductions, with global warming potential decreasing by 13% in the validated 20R–80V formulation. Higher recycled-content formulations offer greater potential benefits; however, sensitivity analysis highlights that these benefits strongly depend on durability. Reductions in performance can significantly offset the environmental gains, indicating that durability represents a critical threshold parameter. The circularity assessment further confirms the advantages of both material substitution and recycling pathways: the MCI increases from 0.46 for a virgin tread sent to energy recovery, to 0.73 when recycled, and up to 0.79 when devulcanized elastomer is incorporated. Overall, devulcanized elastomer can effectively improve both environmental performance and circularity, provided that adequate durability is maintained.

title: Artificial intelligence model-based high-accuracy estimation of global PM2.5 concentrations using gap-filled aerosol optical depth
abstract: Fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter smaller than 2.5 μm (PM2.5) exerts significant impacts on public health and the environment, yet high-precision estimation of global PM2.5 concentrations remains challenging. Aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieved from satellite observations is commonly employed for PM2.5 estimation; however, missing AOD data can lead to substantial biases, thereby necessitating effective gap-filling approaches. In this study, we proposed a two-stage modeling framework to achieve high-precision PM2.5 estimation by filling AOD gaps. During model selection, twelve artificial intelligence (AI) models were compared using ten-fold cross-validation, integrating hourly multi-platform ground-based PM2.5 observations, meteorological variables, and population density data to estimate monthly global PM2.5 concentrations from 2019 to 2021. The results indicated that the Random Forest (RF) model outperformed other models in both AOD gap-filling and PM2.5 estimation, with cross-validation R2 values of 0.835 and 0.851, respectively. The proposed model achieved 100% AOD gap-filling while maintaining high accuracy, with an R2 of 0.721 against AERONET validation. The global PM2.5 estimations exhibited high accuracy, with monthly validation R2 values ranging from 0.75 to 0.90, and spatial-scale validation R2 values between 0.75 and 0.85. From 2019 to 2021, global PM2.5 concentrations showed an overall declining trend, albeit with pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity: PM2.5 in highly urbanized regions was predominantly driven by anthropogenic activities, whereas that in less urbanized regions was largely influenced by natural factors. Among all influencing factors, AOD has the greatest impact on PM2.5, whereas PD has the least impact. The proposed framework provides important insights into the formation mechanisms of PM2.5 and offers substantial value for improving the quality of global PM2.5 datasets.

title: High-performance and recyclable HKUST-1-derived CuxO/Steel electrode for electrocatalytic dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid
abstract: Haloacetic acids (HAAs) are the second most prevalent disinfection by-products (DBPs) in drinking water and significantly contribute to the overall DBPs carcinogenic risk owing to their persistence and established carcinogenic mechanisms. This study focuses on the development of high-efficiency HKUST-1-derived CuxO/Steel(St) composite electrodes for the electrolytic dechlorination of trichloroacetic acid (TCAA), showcasing a novel approach for mitigating such contaminants. The low-temperature carbonization of HKUST-1 yielded CuxO-derived carbon materials, which were used to modify three low-cost electrodes (stainless St, Fe, and Cu), resulting in a novel CuxO/St composite electrode. This electrode exhibited a superior TCAA reduction efficiency due to its optimal material characteristics and electrode configuration. Electrocatalytic performance studies revealed positive correlations between TCAA removal rates and current density/electrode loading, and a negative correlation with solution pH. The CuxO/St-based composite electrode demonstrates efficient dechlorination of TCAA while maintaining high stability over five consecutive cycles. Quenching experiments identified the key active species, atomic H∗ and Cu ions, which facilitated a dual dechlorination pathway through both direct electron transfer and H∗-mediated indirect reduction. The developed HKUST-1-derived CuxO/St composite electrodes provide a recyclable electrocatalytic solution for the end-of-pipe treatment of DBPs in drinking water.

title: Local climatic effects and their spatiotemporal dynamics in subtropical stable forests
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying climate change and anthropogenic activities, forests serve as crucial regulators of local climate. However, their stability and thermal environmental effects face increasing perturbation. Elucidating local forest climatic effects and stability is essential for informing regional forest management and enhancing ecosystem services. Using multi-source remote sensing data, this study systematically investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of stable forests in subtropical China from 2001 to 2023. Furthermore, it quantifies the evolution of their local land surface temperature (LST) regulation across annual mean, seasonal, and diurnal dimensions. The study found the following: 1) Landscape dynamics. Compared to 2000–2010, the bidirectional conversion between forest and cropland increased approximately seven-fold during 2010–2023. The areal proportion of stable forests decreased from 98% to 89%, exhibiting characteristics of fragmentation. 2) Local LST regulation effects. Annually, stable forest coverage was positively correlated with local LST, particularly during the daytime. However, this warming effect attenuated over time. Seasonally, the correlation between stable forest cover and local LST displayed distinct patterns: a predominantly negative association in spring; a persistently positive but attenuated relationship in summer; diurnally divergent responses in autumn; and a synergistic correlation during both day and night in winter. 3) Patch size thresholds. Large patches (>20 km2) exhibited superior thermal regulatory capacity and spatiotemporal stability, offering significant cooling benefits particularly in winter. Conversely, small patches (<10 km2) were susceptible to interference from the surrounding environment, resulting in greater thermal fluctuation. 4) Local LST regulation effects of continuous stable forests. Distinct seasonal differences were observed, primarily characterized by warming during the growing season and cooling during the dormant period.

title: WSF-Bench: A regime-aware benchmarking framework for sustainable monitoring of wood-related production and trade systems
abstract: Short-horizon forecasting is increasingly important for cleaner-production and resilience-oriented monitoring in forest-based value chains, where production capacity, trade flows, and procurement decisions can change rapidly under structural disruption. However, existing forecasting studies in wood-related sectors are mostly application-specific and rarely test whether model rankings remain stable across production and trade tasks, official-data coverage constraints, and pre-shock, shock, and post-shock regimes. This study develops WSF-Bench, a regime-aware benchmarking framework for monthly monitoring of wood-related production and trade systems in Europe. The framework uses Eurostat short-term industrial production indices for wood products and furniture manufacturing, Comext wooden-furniture export and import data, and annual forestry-related anchors to evaluate one-step-ahead forecasts for 12 production countries and 8 trade countries over 2005–2024. Rather than imposing a single artificial country panel, WSF-Bench constructs task-specific balanced panels and compares Seasonal Naïve, ETS, pooled LightGBM, and a focused recurrent challenger under common chronological split rules. Forecast accuracy is evaluated primarily with MASE and interpreted together with execution validity, so that fallback predictions are not treated as equivalent to valid pooled LightGBM runs. The results show a clear production–trade asymmetry. In production, pooled LightGBM provides large gains in stable pre-pandemic windows, but this advantage weakens under later regimes, where ETS remains competitive and some nominal LightGBM wins depend on fallback handling. In trade, pooled LightGBM achieves the lowest error for both exports and imports across all regime windows, and this ranking is not overturned by the recurrent challenger. These findings indicate that, under structural change, the preferred monitoring architecture depends on which segment of the wood value chain is being monitored: strong classical models remain indispensable for production monitoring, whereas pooled LightGBM provides more consistent and execution-valid support for trade monitoring.

title: A novel three-stage modification method for enhancing the performance of rubber concrete: Shear-embedding of nanoparticles, heat treatment, and gel-based surface reconstruction of waste rubber particles
abstract: Utilizing waste rubber particles (WRP) to produce rubber concrete serves as an effective approach for solid waste recycling and enhancing concrete functionality. This material not only consumes a large amount of waste rubber but also imparts excellent toughness, acid and alkali resistance, and shock-absorption properties to concrete, demonstrating significant potential for specialized engineering applications such as hydraulic and military construction. However, the low density, low elastic modulus, surface impurities, and hydrophobicity of WRP lead to particle flotation, stress concentration, and weak interfacial bonding, causing the strength of rubber concrete to drop significantly. Although numerous studies have attempted to address these issues, existing methods often lack systematicity and fail to provide comprehensive and synergistic solutions targeting the multiple causes of mechanical performance degradation in rubber concrete. This paper proposes a novel and systematic three-stage pretreatment method for WRP, which reconstructs the surface structure of WRP. In the first stage, nano-silica is embedded into the internal structure of WRP via supercritical CO2-assisted shearing. The second stage involves high-temperature stirring pretreatment to achieve surface cleaning of WRP. In the third stage, tetraethyl orthosilicate at varying concentrations is used as a precursor to in-situ grow nano-silica on the surface of WRP. The results demonstrate that after the three-stage pretreatment, the density of WRP increases by up to 9.38%, the elastic modulus improves by up to 29.16%, and the water contact angle decreases by a maximum of 25.38%, while the particle flotation during concrete preparation is significantly mitigated. The nano-silica-coated WRP can participate in cement hydration, strengthening the interfacial transition zone. Compared with rubber concrete prepared using untreated WRP, the modified material exhibits significantly enhanced mechanical properties, which first improve and then stabilize with increasing tetraethyl orthosilicate concentration. When WRP pretreated with 8 wt% tetraethyl orthosilicate (relative to WRP mass) is used, the resulting rubber concrete shows a 65.1% increase in 28-day cubic compressive strength and a 75.9% improvement in tensile strength.

title: Recycling of vanadium-extraction tailings by controllable aluminothermic reduction process
abstract: Vanadium-extraction tailings (VET) are solid waste residues generated during the vanadium extraction. In the present study, a controllable aluminothermic reduction strategy was developed to upcycle VET into value-added products via two selectable routes. Specifically, route 1 represents the selective reduction of Fe followed by alkaline purification to obtain Ti-rich slag, whereas route 2 represents the deep reduction of both Fe and Ti to produce FeTi alloy. The feasibility of reducing the Fe- and Ti-bearing components in VET under high-temperature conditions, as well as the reaction priority, was evaluated through thermodynamic analysis. Reduction experiments at different temperatures were carried out, and the reaction mechanism of the aluminothermic reduction process of VET was examined. The optimum process conditions for the selective reduction route and the deep reduction route of VET were studied. The results showed that, at 950 °C for 60 min under Ar protection, tuning the Al ratio enabled selective or deep reduction of VET. In route 1, a Ti-rich slag with 63.27% TiO2 was obtained, with Fe and Ti recoveries of 83.78% and 96.58%, respectively. In route 2, supplementing TiO2 to raise the feed TiO2 content to 60.85% produced a FeTi40B alloy containing 40.9% Ti, with Fe and Ti recoveries of 81.31% and 51.56%, respectively. The lower Ti recovery in route 2 was attributed to thermodynamic constraints and micro-encapsulation within an Al2O3-based matrix. This method provides a tunable and cleaner route for the value-added utilization of VET.

title: Operational cost impacts of tertiary treatment in wastewater treatment plants: An inverse optimization approach
abstract: Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are critical infrastructure in urban water management. However, their operation entails substantial costs that must be accurately assessed to support informed policy and regulatory decision-making. Directive (EU) 2024/3019 introduces more stringent nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) removal requirements for WWTPs, with potentially significant economic implications. This study develops and applies a novel methodological framework to estimate the increase in operational expenditure (OPEX) required for WWTPs to comply with these new standards while preserving their existing techno-economic efficiency. The proposed framework is based on inverse data envelopment analysis and enables the quantification of plant-specific compliance costs. An empirical application to 74 Spanish WWTPs reveals substantial heterogeneity in both current efficiency levels and the additional OPEX required to meet regulatory targets. On average, compliance with Directive (EU) 2024/3019 increases total OPEX by 25.9%, corresponding to an average increase of approximately 0.134 €/m 3 , although cost impacts vary widely across facilities and are not systematically related to plant size or baseline efficiency. While most WWTPs can achieve the required N and P removal levels without efficiency losses, the largest fully efficient plants face structural constraints that limit further performance improvements. Overall, the proposed framework provides a transferable, plant-level tool to support ex-ante regulatory impact assessments and informed investment and tariff decisions under evolving environmental policy frameworks.

title: Assessment of cost and environmental impacts of single point incremental forming and deep drawing for a range of production volumes
abstract: Sheet metal forming is crucial for producing lightweight, durable components. Single-point incremental forming (SPIF) presents an alternative to deep drawing (DD), but its use remains limited due to insufficient analysis of its pre- and post-forming stages. This study compares the cost of goods sold (COGS) and environmental impacts of SPIF and DD for an asymmetric battery cell casing at various production volumes. It utilizes the manufacturing process design (MPD) and life cycle assessment (LCA) methods to assess all stages needed to produce a part. SPIF shows higher costs and impacts at 1000 parts/year due to longer forming times. Global warming potential (GWP) is similar at 1000–2000 parts/year, after which the impacts of SPIF outweigh those of DD. Sensitivity analysis highlights blank handling as a significant cost driver above 500 parts per year. Process improvements would reduce cycle times, equipment use, and environmental impacts, increasing the competitiveness of SPIF.

title: A practical framework for evaluating phosphorus redistribution after dewatering in tailings dry disposal
abstract: Reliable evaluation of dewatered tailings is important for dry stacking, storage management, and downstream utilization, yet it is often inferred from the size–bulk composition relationship established during classification. Whether this classification-stage relationship remains valid after dewatering has rarely been tested directly. In a phosphorus-bearing iron tailings dry-disposal system, we examined whether downstream bulk composition could still be explained by particle size alone after dewatering. Hydrocyclone underflow (S1) and overflow (S2) were used to define a classification-stage baseline, and the dewatered inner sample (S3b) was evaluated against this baseline using Dv,50 and XRF bulk composition. A deviation index (DIP) was then used to determine whether the measured downstream composition matched the reference value defined by the classification-stage trend. P2O5 showed a clear positive deviation after dewatering, whereas Fe2O3, SiO2, and Al2O3 remained close to zero (|DIP| < 0.02). ToF-SIMS detected similar PO2−/PO3− signals in S3a and S3b, suggesting that the bulk deviation was not accompanied by a comparable change in surface phosphorus-bearing signals. The deviation was therefore more consistent with particle redistribution within the dewatered bed under the studied process condition. Under the conditions considered here, the proposed framework provides a practical post-dewatering basis for judging dewatered tailings for dry stacking, storage, handling, and utilization screening.

title: Toward green and sustainable pad-dyeing of polyester: a microcapsule-enabled low-water and recyclable process
abstract: This study proposes and systematically validates a microcapsule-enabled pad-dyeing strategy for polyester (PET), aiming to establish an industrially viable pathway for efficient coloration with reduced water consumption and wastewater discharge. Waterborne polyurethane disperse dye microcapsules (DWPUMC) were prepared through a self-emulsifying polymerization method and applied in a pad-dyeing process to regulate dye release during thermal treatment. The prepared microcapsules exhibited particle sizes mainly distributed between 2 and 6 μm, with encapsulation efficiencies reaching 86.25% for DB60-WPUMC and 89.87% for DO30-WPUMC. The WPU shell showed significant melt-softening behavior within the temperature range of 130-180 °C, enabling controlled dye release and formation of a polyurethane film on the fiber surface during baking. Compared with conventional pad-dyeing systems, the DWPUMC-based process achieved comparable dyeing depth (K/S values) without the use of conventional dispersants or leveling agents, while maintaining excellent washing and rubbing fastness, reaching grade 5 after soap washing and reduction washing. In addition, the dye bath could be effectively reused after simple centrifugal filtration, which significantly reduced the pollutant load of the dyeing effluent. These results demonstrate that the proposed microcapsule-enabled dyeing strategy provides a feasible route toward cleaner polyester dyeing with reduced auxiliary chemicals and improved wastewater recyclability.

title: Partial oxidation for blue hydrogen production: Techno-economic assessment of low-temperature carbon capture technologies
abstract: Hydrogen produced by partial oxidation (POx) integrated with carbon capture systems (CCS) remains critically underexplored compared to steam methane reforming (SMR), despite its inherent advantages of higher natural gas conversion and reduced external heating requirements. This study fills that gap by presenting the first comprehensive environmental and techno-economic assessment of POx coupled with cryogenic carbon capture (CCC) and amine-based absorption (ABS) at capture rates of 95% and 98%, at a production scale of 600 MWth. Six hydrogen production configurations are evaluated: a baseline SMR, unabated POx, and four POx-CCS variants (POx-CCC-95, POx-CCC-98, POx-ABS-95, POx-ABS-98) not previously assessed together in the literature. Performance is benchmarked across net efficiency, specific CO 2 emissions, capital and operating costs, levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH), cost of CO 2 avoided (CCA), and investment payback periods. Our findings reveal, for the first time, that POx-CCC integrated systems show higher efficiency (∼59%) than amine-based CCS (∼55–56%). Integrating CCS cuts emissions from 93.91 gCO 2 eq/MJ (H 2 ) in unabated POx to 18.66–21.20 gCO 2 eq/MJ (H 2 ) for CCC and 27.34–29.12 gCO 2 eq/MJ (H 2 ) for amine-based, with only CCC (at 98% capture rate) meeting the UK Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard, a regulatory threshold not previously evaluated in this technology context. We further demonstrate that CCS integration increases the LCOH by 13–20% relative to unabated POx. Sensitivity analysis identifies natural-gas price as the main driver of LCOH, while plant cost most strongly affects CCA. Meanwhile, increasing carbon price reduces the CCA across all CCS cases.

title: Framework for assessing sustainability from an organizational perspective in early chemical product and process design
abstract: This work presents a framework for sustainability assessment during the early design stages of chemical products and processes from an organizational perspective by incorporating prioritization factors. The framework follows a progressive approach, beginning with a set of sustainability principles at a strategic level. These are gradually translated into specific criteria, providing guidance for designers when comparing different alternatives, which are subsequently evaluated through indicators, calculated based on specific system properties or operating conditions. This hierarchical approach helps information transfer from the strategic to the operational level, where technical design occurs, allowing the designers to align engineering decisions with the organization's sustainability objectives. The framework is applied in four stages: i) definition of principles and criteria according to organizational priorities; ii) identification of alternatives and information gathering; iii) assessment of alternatives through a multicriteria decision analysis method (MCDA); and iv) Decision-making. Two case studies are presented: the selection of a chemical route to produce a chemical product (i.e. ethyl acetate) and the design of structured product (i.e. cosmetic) containing it. In this case, the MCDA was conducted by using MAUT method. Utility functions were defined considering the meaning of the indicators, as interpreted through principles from the organizational context. The proposed methodology could be further used in the design of products and processes for different industries.

title: The balance of complexation and decomposition determines the sequestration behaviors of heavy metals from acidic wastewater by chelating captures
abstract: Traditional treatment technologies are ineffective in the recovery of metal resources from acidic wastewater in complexed and polymerized states, leading to significant waste generation and severe contamination. This research investigated the sequestration behaviors of heavy metals, and proposed a direct recovery of them from acidic wastewater. Observations indicate that‌ secondary-amine-derived dithiocarbamate (DTC) captures exhibited rapid decomposition within 1 min even at 1.0 mmol L−1 [H+] of mild acidity. In comparison, primary-amine and hybrid-amine-derived DTC captures underwent immediate self-precipitation and yielded dense white precipitates in acid, causing significantly lower decomposition percentage relative to the secondary-amine-derived captures. But very surprisingly, the selected four capture agents demonstrated high capacities to sequester over 99% of Cu, Ni, and 90.5% of Cd, exhibiting remarkable effectiveness in the recovery of heavy metals (HMs) even at 400 mmol L−1 [H+] of strong acidity. The complexation rates of the captures with HMs were found to exceed their decomposition rates by ten to hundreds of times. Evidently, the significantly faster kinetic rate associated with DTC–HM complexation, in comparison to DTC decomposition, exerted a predominant influence on the sequestration behaviors of the three typical HMs by the four distinct capture agents in an acidic environment. The in situ-formed DTC–HM complexes exhibited remarkable acid stability, which was significantly enhanced upon aging. Multi-scale characterizations (FTIR, SEM-EDS, and XPS) were employed to examine the molecular environments, structural, and morphological shifts facilitating a more profound understanding of the mechanism by which HMs are sequestered by the capture agents from an acidic environment.

title: Digital content for environmental change: The roles of credibility, usefulness, entertainment, and emotions in driving pro-environmental behaviours across education level
abstract: Digital message content is widely used to promote pro-environmental behaviour, yet limited understanding remains regarding how such content translates into behavioural willingness across heterogeneous audiences. Grounded in the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), this study examines how source credibility and entertainment cues influence perceived usefulness and emotional evocation, which subsequently shape pro-environmental behavioural willingness, with education level as a moderator. Data were collected from 400 Indonesian social media users exposed to short-form environmental content by the Pandawara Group and analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Multi-Group Analysis (MGA). The results reveal distinct education-based processing routes. Among higher-educated users, both source credibility and entertainment influence willingness indirectly through emotional evocation. In contrast, among lower-educated users, entertainment exerts a direct effect on willingness. MGA further shows that the effects of source credibility on perceived usefulness and emotional evocation are stronger for lower-educated audiences. Notably, the influence of entertainment on perceived usefulness and emotional evocation diverges across groups—positive for higher- but negative for lower-educated users. These findings offer theoretical contributions and practical guidance for designing sustainability messages across diverse educational background.

title: Compliance over performance in sustainable public procurement? Evidence from regulatory reforms in Slovakia
abstract: Public procurement has evolved into a strategic lever for environmental and social sustainability, moving beyond its traditional administrative role. However, the transformative potential of these policies is often constrained by an institutional culture of "safety", where risk-averse officials prioritise procedural compliance over long-term strategic value. This study investigates how regulatory volatility shapes the adoption of Sustainable Public Procurement (SPP) in below-threshold contracts—a market segment largely outside the scope of EU directives and underexplored in the literature. Focusing on the Slovak Republic, characterised by extreme legislative instability, the study exploits two contrasting national reforms — the 2022 Formalisation and the 2024 Simplification — to identify the impact of regulatory design on SPP uptake. The study contributes by jointly examining environmental and socially responsible criteria, leveraging national-level data that capture sustainability across all procurement stages, and providing causal evidence of asymmetric regulatory effects. Utilising a difference-in-differences design, the analysis draws on over 30,000 tender calls from 2020 to 2024. Findings reveal that stricter rules led to a decline in SPP adoption, particularly suppressing socially responsible criteria. The 2024 simplification facilitated a recovery, primarily fostering environmental requirements. Moreover, decentralised regional and local authorities emerge as primary drivers of SPP, though they remain vulnerable to procedural friction. Achieving sustainable goals requires moving beyond rigid, "one-size-fits-all" regulations toward designs that reduce transaction costs and empower officials to prioritise strategic sustainability over formal compliance.

title: A numerical model for quantifying the hydrological performance of clogged permeable brick pavement based on pilot-scale experiments
abstract: Over extended service periods, particulate matter (PM) progressively accumulates on the surface and within the internal pore structure of permeable brick pavement (PBP), leading to pronounced deterioration of hydraulic permeability. However, the infiltration-runoff process of PBP is unduly simplified by hydrological and hydraulic models like SWMM, which are unable to explain the dynamic quantitative relationships among the parameters throughout the clogging evolution. In this study, through pilot-scale experiments, the evolution of PBP clogging was revealed, and based on empirical parameterization, a multi-scenario numerical model (MS-NM) was proposed. The results indicate that the clogging progression of PBP can be classified into three distinct stages: rapid clogging, transition, and stabilization. As PM load increases, the permeability coefficient shows a quadratic decay. The relationship between accumulated PM wash-off load and cumulative runoff volume is well described by an exponential saturation growth model. After integrated maintenance comprising routine sweeping, high-pressure washing, and negative-pressure suction, the permeability of PBP increased by 91.25%. This indicates that regular maintenance is necessary to extend the lifespan of PBP. Unlike the LID module in SWMM, which uses a rough generalization of infiltration, MS-NM can perform staged runoff simulations dependent on clogging state. Under experimental conditions, the MS-NM can well describe the infiltration-runoff process of PBP, with an R2 range of 0.68–0.95 and an Ens range of 0.70–0.95. These findings provide an efficient computational alternative for evaluating the staged hydrological parameters of PBP.

title: Guiding sustainable waste management: LCA-based evaluation of trade-offs in high-quality recycling of paper and board from lightweight packaging waste
abstract: The expanding global market of fiber-based composite packaging and rising recycling targets necessitate high-quality recycling routes, which involve the reutilization of fibers in comparable applications. As existing treatment routes for paper and board (PB) from German lightweight packaging waste are limited to thermal recovery and low-quality recycling abroad, a novel process for high-quality recycling has been developed. This raises the question: Can high-quality recycling in Germany enhance recycling rates while simultaneously reducing environmental impacts compared with existing treatment routes? To address this question, we conducted a comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) with the functional unit “Treatment of 1 ton PB”. Analyzed scenarios were incineration, low-quality recycling abroad and novel high- and low-quality domestic recycling processes. We used primary data from technical assessments to establish a comprehensive model foundation for our study. Our results indicate that the main contributors to global warming potential (GWP), cumulative energy demand (CED), land occupation potential (LOP), and water consumption potential (WCP) are transport, stock preparation, and thermal treatment across all scenarios. For high-quality recycling, GWP decreased from 148 to 93 kg CO 2 -Eq/t compared with recycling abroad but increased compared with incineration with 51 kg CO 2 -Eq/t. CED and LOP decreased from −483 to −2,533 MJ-Eq/t and from −83 to −156 m 2 ∗a crop-Eq/t, respectively, when comparing high-quality recycling with recycling abroad. No significant differences were found for WCP. These findings provide essential guidance for developing circular economy strategies and legal frameworks by highlighting the importance of LCA in minimizing trade-offs and burden shifting in waste management.

title: Valorization of allelochemical-rich olive pomace: Comprehensive effect microbial nutrient release and ursolic acid-enhanced uptake improve crop growth and quality
abstract: Biomass can be recycled into organic fertilizers, but allelochemicals in some residues restrict their safe use. Using olive pomace (OP) as an example, we prepared an Olive Pomace Microbial Organic Fertilizer (OPMOF) through microbial fermentation. Pot experiments showed that, compared with a commercial organic fertilizer applied at the same rate, OPMOF increased Brassica chinensis yield by 27.5%. Effective microorganisms enhanced soil available nutrients and crop quality, and increased gram-negative bacteria, generating more C 12 -AHL to promote lateral root development. Importantly, this study demonstrated the concentration-dependent physiological effects of ursolic acid (UA) in OPMOF and provided evidence for these effects: low UA upregulated the expression of root respiratory-chain genes, was associated with enhanced ATP synthesis, and improved nutrient uptake in multiple crops, whereas high UA inhibited growth. However, the in situ interaction between microbial activity and UA effects remains to be experimentally verified. Overall, this study provides a promising strategy for the high-value utilization of allelochemical-rich agricultural wastes and highlights the potential of allelochemicals in developing plant growth-promoting products.

title: A perspective on the role of multi-criteria decision-making in assessing the sustainability of alternative shipping fuels
abstract: According to the fourth “International Maritime Organization greenhouse gas study”, the combustion of fossil fuels such as heavy fuel oil in the shipping sector was responsible for 2.9% of global anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions in 2018. These emissions can potentially be reduced through alternative fuels with low or zero-carbon footprints. Of issue, however, is the high financial investment and lead in time for development of facilities to produce these fuels, and the assessment of which of the fuel systems should be prioritised. Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods can aid decision-makers in comparing alternative fuels from technical and sustainability perspectives. MCDM provides methodologies to deal with multiple, often conflicting, criteria with varying degrees of importance. This paper provides a perspective on the use of the MCDM methods for comparing alternative shipping fuels. The work indicates that: 1) future research must use Life Cycle Assessment for a more holistic approach to assessing the environmental impact of each fuel; 2) process simulation software can be used to develop the data required for comparing different fuel production pathways; 3) objective weighting methods can be used more in future research; 4) input from port stakeholders must be considered in future research; and 5) to generate a robust comparison, infrastructural requirements must be considered.

title: From barns to atmosphere: Pakistan's livestock manure-derived NH3, N2O, and CH4 emissions (1961–2022) and cleaner production pathways
abstract: Pakistan's expanding livestock sector has led to increased gas emissions from manure management, with implications for both climate change and air quality. This study uses the only available long-term national baseline (FAOSTAT Tier-1 inventory data) to conduct a strategic analysis for 1961–2022 of ammonia (NH3), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) from livestock manure. Results revealed a substantial increase in emissions over the past six decades. In 2022, livestock manure emitted 1066.4 kilo tonnes (kt) of NH3, 433.8 kt of CH4, and 130.9 kt N2O, contributing 47.5 million tonnes (Mt) CO2e (CH4 + N2O). Emissions are primarily attributed to ruminants (buffalo and cattle account for ∼61% of CO2e), while goats were the leading source of NH3 emissions (28%). Spatially, we overlay provincial emission hotspots (primarily Punjab and Sindh) with maps of high PM2.5 exposure and extreme heat hazard to identify regions of co-location that may warrant prioritization. These overlays serve as a screening layer and do not quantify PM2.5 formation, exposure, or health impacts; likewise, heat-risk implications are qualitative. Uncertainties from Tier-1 factors are significant, underscoring the need for Tier-2 updates. This analysis leverages the national baseline to identify and prioritize cleaner-production strategies (e.g., covered storage, anaerobic digestion, and low-loss field application) that can potentially deliver co-benefits for air quality, near-term climate, and nutrient efficiency in high-priority regions.

title: Synergistic acid–sodium bisulfite pretreatment of banana straw for enhancing cellulose utilization: A comprehensive physicochemical and multivariate mechanism analysis
abstract: Banana straw (BS), a lignocellulosic residue abundant in tropical regions, represents a valuable resource for sustainable agricultural development when efficiently processed. Acid–sodium bisulfite pretreatment (ABP) was investigated for its impact on BS cellulose utilization. Response surface methodology with Box–Behnken design optimized ABP parameters to 150 °C, 1% H2SO4 (w/v), 12% NaHSO3 (w/w), 40 min, and solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:12. Compared with the sole sulfuric acid pretreatment (SSAP), the optimized ABP improved enzymatic hydrolysis, yielding 1.35-fold higher conversion rate of cellulose (CRC) and 1.37-fold greater yield of reducing sugars (YRS). Comprehensive analyses of the structural, physicochemical, and cellulose crystalline properties of BS elucidated the mechanisms underlying hemicellulose/lignin removal and cellulose exposure during pretreatment. Multivariate correlation analysis of 17 variables revealed relatively positive associations between enzymatic efficiency and cellulose recovery rate (CR), crystallinity index of cellulose (CrI), Congo red dye adsorption (CR ads.), and sulfonic acid content (SAC) (|r| > 0.8). NaHSO3 concentration showed positive associations with lignin removal rate (LR), SAC and CR ads., and corresponded to a decreased C/O ratio. Temperature was positively associated with hemicellulose removal rate (HR) and YRS, though temperatures above 150 °C were linked to reduced LR. H2SO4 concentration showed an association with HR but exhibited limited relationship with enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency. These observed trends suggest that ABP could serve as an effective strategy for enhancing lignocellulosic biomass utilization from agricultural residues, though given the relative sample size, these correlations should be interpreted as indicative of associations rather than definitive causal relationships.

title: Enhancing treatment performance for agricultural runoff in ecological ditches through synergistic effects of denitrifying phosphate-accumulating bacteria and natural/synthetic media
abstract: Agricultural non-point source pollution threatens aquatic ecosystems worldwide, and ecological ditches (EDs) offer a promising remediation approach. This study enhanced conventional EDs by adding functional media (volcanic rock, synthetic polyethylene, walnut shell and their ternary mixture). Bioaugmentation was further applied by inoculating a denitrifying phosphate-accumulating strain Pseudomonas sp. DWP1. Over six months, EDs amended with walnut shell or mixed media and inoculated with DWP1 achieved high removal of NO3−-N (up to 91.8%), NH4+-N (up to 86.1%), total nitrogen (TN, up to 85.4%), total phosphorus (TP, up to 73.1%), and total organic carbon (TOC, up to 90.2%), outperforming the control. When nutrient loading increased during the last three months, a second inoculation restored performance. Microbial analysis showed greater DWP1 retention in biofilms on walnut shell and mixed media (3.5–5.7 × 105 copies g−1) than on other media (4.4–9.9 × 104 copies g−1). In addition, denitrifying genera such as Pseudomonas, Thauera and Dechloromonas were enriched, implying strong viability of DWP1 strain in EDs. Individual-based biofilm modeling indicated that initial DWP1 dominance shifted to conventional anoxic heterotrophic denitrifiers via resource competition. Batch cultivation identified an optimal C/N/P ratio of 2.5:1:0.05 for DWP1 growth, yielding maximum biomass concentration and near complete nutrient consumption. Overall, the combination of walnut shell or mixed media with low-frequency DWP1 inoculation (e.g., once every three months) offers a cost-effective, scalable upgrade for EDs treating agricultural runoff.

title: Sustainable pre-reduced sinter production: Recycling carbon-bearing dust and reducing CO2 emissions
abstract: The iron and steel industry faces challenges in recycling solid waste and reducing carbon emissions. This study introduces a composite agglomeration process for producing pre-reduced sinter, enabling the use of carbon-bearing dust and preparing a low-carbon blast furnace burden. Investigations into the high-temperature mineralization mechanism show that controlling CaO levels in both the raw sintering matrix and the pellets enables liquid-phase bonding and the matrix's encapsulation of the pellets. This results in a dense shell and a high-porosity core. This structure not only prevents re-oxidation of the internally pre-reduced pellets but also improves the mechanical strength of the sinter. Semi-industrial tests demonstrate enhanced sintering performance and 4.49 kg t−1 in fuel savings, with sintering and ironmaking processes saving 22.93 kg of coke and reducing CO2 emissions by 71.46 kg per ton of sinter. With low equipment costs and simple operation, this approach shows strong potential for industrial application.

title: Designing low-carbon lithium carbonate production: An ex-ante life cycle assessment of CO2-Based precipitation pathways
abstract: Lithium carbonate (Li2CO3) is a critical precursor for lithium-ion batteries, yet its production remains chemically intensive and environmentally burdensome. While CO2-based precipitation has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional Na2CO3-based routes, yet its environmental performance has not been fully assessed. This study presents a comparative ex-ante life cycle assessment of four Li2CO3 precipitation pathways, Na2CO3-based, NaOH/CO2-based, direct CO2-based, and ultrasound-assisted CO2-based, using primary experimental data scaled to a 1000 L industrial process via a transparent scale-up framework. Baseline GWP ranges from 53.10 to 60.40 kg CO2-eq per kg Li2CO3, with the ultrasound-assisted CO2 route achieving the lowest impact (12% lower than the highest-impact NaOH/CO2-based route), driven mainly by its higher lithium yield rather than precipitation chemistry. Ethanol used in product washing dominates most impact categories (80-92% of total GWP), while CO2 supply, KCl, and the precipitation reagents (Na2CO3 or NaOH) act as secondary contributors. This dominance reflects not only the intrinsic environmental burden of ethanol production but also the harmonised modelling choice to apply a uniform washing requirement across all routes, which amplifies ethanol's contribution relative to other inputs. Scenario analysis indicates that single-lever decarbonisation (low-carbon CO2 or fermentation-derived ethanol alone) achieves only modest reductions, while combined substitution achieves up to 17% reduction, particularly in the CO2-based and ultrasound-assisted routes. Prioritising high-efficiency ethanol recovery, low-carbon ethanol and CO2 sourcing, and integrated process design emerge, within this gate-to-gate assessment, as the most influential levers for reducing the environmental footprint of the Li2CO3 precipitation stage under the modelled conditions.

title: Strategic role of integrated agricultural systems in alleviating land-use competition and accelerating climate mitigation
abstract: Integrated and agroforestry systems (IS/AS) are increasingly recognised as pivotal pathways to reconcile agricultural productivity, ecosystem services, and climate mitigation. This study assesses the system-level contribution of IS/AS to land-use dynamics and greenhouse gas mitigation in Brazil using the Brazilian Land Use and Energy System (BLUES) integrated assessment model (IAM). Distinct from previous global assessments, we developed and explicitly represented eleven region-specific IS/AS production systems – two Integration-Livestock-Forest (ILF) systems, five Integration-Crop-Livestock (ICL) systems, two Integration-Crop-Livestock-Native Forest (ICLFn) systems and two Integration-Crop-Livestock-Commercial Forestry (eucalyptus/pine) systems – to capture heterogeneous productivity, input intensity, and carbon dynamics across diverse biomes. Our findings demonstrate that IS/AS are not only economically viable but also strategically superior to conventional practices, with their large-scale deployment primarily driven by their systemic expansion potential rather than marginal costs. Under 1.5°C-consistent scenarios, IS/AS substantially abate agricultural emissions, particularly methane (22 MtCO 2 e) and nitrous oxide (35 MtCO 2 e), while accelerating carbon sequestration in soils and biomass (15 MtCO 2 e). Crucially, their adoption alleviates land-use competition by minimising the need for extensive industrial carbon capture and storage (CCS), reforestation and pasture recovery – reductions of 86, 216 and 439 MtCO 2 e, respectively – thereby securing food and bioenergy production. These results underscore the role of IS/AS as foundational structural components of sustainable land-use strategies, providing a benchmark for climate policy in nations with extensive degraded agricultural landscapes.

title: Measurement of competitive water-use pressure across multi-regional sectors in China: A perspective considering economic-benefits
abstract: Globally, persistent mismatches between water supply and demand, coupled with imbalanced water-use structures, have led to marked intersectoral competitive water-use patterns across regions. Quantifying competitive water-use pressure from an economic-benefit perspective is essential for optimizing allocation and supporting sustainable development.
