This study proposes a generalizable cross-regional and cross-sectoral method for quantifying competitive water-use pressure and applies it in an empirical case in China. The competitive water pressure index (CWPI) is calculated using a multi-regional input-output (MRIO) model coupled with water resources, and its coupling relationship with the water-use economic benefits (WUEB) is examined. A geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) model identifies key CWPI drivers. The results indicate that: (a) Most sectors are characterized by elevated competitive water-use pressure, whereas agricultural sectors consistently report the highest CWPI values nationwide. (b) Among cross-regional water-use sectors, the “low CWPI-low WUEB” condition occurs most frequently (113 instances), whereas the favorable “low CWPI-high WUEB” condition is the least common. (c) Total water supply serves as the primary mitigating factor for competitive water-use pressure, although Ningxia shows a positive regression coefficient (1.2234). WUEB exerts positive effects, while negative influences are concentrated in the southwestern mountainous areas and the arid to semi-arid regions of northwestern China. Factors related to agricultural, industrial, ecological, and domestic water use exhibit an overall spatial pattern characterized by “high values in the northeast, low values in the southwest, and a single negative value in Ningxia.” These findings offer a scientific basis for region-specific water allocation and advance the development of coordinated, cross-regional water-resource management.

title: Environmental and thermo-economic assessment of industrial heat recovery retrofits with integrated waste heat and multiple utility systems
abstract: Retrofitting industrial heat recovery systems is a key pathway toward low-carbon and resource-efficient manufacturing. Integrating waste heat recovery (WR) with multiple utility (MU) networks can significantly improve energy efficiency, but also creates strong coupling between process heat recovery, waste heat utilisation, and utility allocation. However, existing approaches often address these elements separately or sequentially, limiting the ability to identify optimal system-level retrofit solutions. This study aims to develop a system-level optimisation framework to resolve trade-offs between waste heat recovery and multiple utility integration in industrial retrofit. The framework allows for (i) modifying existing exchangers, (ii) installing new process-to-process units to enhance heat recovery, (iii) integrating waste heat recovery systems for generating high-pressure steam, low-pressure steam, and hot water, and (iv) incorporating optimal utilisation of multiple utilities. The framework is validated through two large-scale industrial case studies. In Case 1, WR and MU integration reduce utility cost to 9.8E+06 $/y (64.6% below the original design) and GHG emissions from 1.7E+08 to 1.2E+08 kg/y CO 2 (30.3% reduction), with hot water generation contributing 82.7% of savings. In Case 2, the same strategy achieves a 45.6% GHG reduction relative to the baseline and lowers operation costs by 28.9%. This work provides a practical, system-level retrofit framework to support sustainable production and low-carbon transition in industrial processes.

title: Firm-level evaluation of the environmental Kuznets curve: thresholds in cross-sectional data from small, medium and mid-sized enterprises
abstract: In a context of insufficient global regulation, a substantial proportion of firms set voluntary greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets. This study draws on a new dataset of about 1000 GHG Protocol-compliant assessments from a thousand Europe and US-based small and medium enterprises and mid-sized firms between 2019 and 2024 to investigate how emissions metrics compare across as companies grow and consolidate their productivity. Moving beyond the conflicting environmental Kuznets curve evidence and the traditional focus on large enterprises, we uncover a new, untheorized link between emissions and firm productivity. Using competing polynomial and threshold regression models, and addressing endogeneity, selection bias and omitted variable bias by relying on Granger causality, Hausman instruments, poststratification, Oster sensitivity tests and split sample testing, we establish that contrary to the classic inverted U shape of the EKC, corporate emissions and emissions intensities do not show a clear turning point but instead stabilize once over a critical threshold in revenue per employee. We find raising productivity can halve per revenue intensities despite simultaneous fourfold and twofold surges in absolute and per-employee emissions. This structural influence of financial productivity challenges the fairness of corporate net-zero targets that assume comparable baseline intensities across firms.

title: A novel-method of 3D-Gaussian fitting with DOM-EEMs of small sample sizes to identifying components compared with parallel factor analysis
abstract: Given that dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a complex group of compounds and its crucial role in the carbon cycle, conducting qualitative and quantitative analysis of DOM is of great importance for understanding its environmental role. Fluorescence spectroscopy combined with parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) is widely used for analysis of DOM. However, the conventional and widely used method requires large sample sizes to ensure robustness, limiting their applicability in small-sample scenarios. This study introduces a novel method to interpret fluorescence spectroscopy based on three-dimensional Gaussian fitting approach to overcome these limitations. By extending two-dimensional Gaussian fitting into the excitation-emission domain, the proposed method enables high-resolution identification of overlapping fluorescence signals even with limited samples. Using a dataset from a full-scale wastewater treatment plant, we systematically validated the method against conventional methods. The three-dimensional Gaussian fitting approach exhibited superior performance in identifying DOM components. Compared with PARAFAC, the new method identified the presence of two additional types of fluorescent components, which provided more accurate and mechanistically consistent in estimation of DOM removal rates across treatment stages. A dedicated three-dimensional R2 validation metric was developed, confirming an excellent goodness-of-fit (R2 > 0.89) across all samples. In the future, it will also be fully applicable to the processing of large samples. The three-dimensional Gaussian fitting technique offers a robust, efficient, and interpretable tool for DOM characterization in small-sample contexts, supporting improved preliminary screening, cost-effective monitoring, and process optimization in water quality management.

title: Uncovering environmental and economic hotspots of nuclear research reactors: A life cycle perspective
abstract: Nuclear research reactors provide essential services for health, industry and science, yet systematic evidence on how to operate these facilities within cleaner-production principles remains limited. This study applies an integrated Life Cycle Assessment (Environmental Footprint 3.1) and Life Cycle Costing framework to quantify environmental and economic hotspots associated with the IEA-R1 research reactor, an open-pool, light-water-moderated facility operated by IPEN in Brazil. One hour of operation at full power defines the functional unit. Long-lived infrastructure and the nuclear fuel cycle emerge as dominant contributors to environmental burdens. Infrastructure accounts for most land use (approximately 73%), water use (approximately 83%) and carcinogenic human toxicity (approximately 78%), indicating opportunities for material optimization and extended component lifetimes. Uranium enrichment, modeled with low-enriched uranium below 20% U-235, drives ionizing radiation and fossil resource depletion. Auxiliary diesel generators add combustion-related impacts, including eutrophication, photochemical oxidants, particulate matter and ozone-depleting emissions. Sensitivity analyses confirm the stability of hotspot patterns despite proxy fuel inventories, underscoring the need for more complete nuclear life-cycle datasets. The economic assessment indicates a negative net operational cost, consistent with the public-service mandate of research reactors. Overall, the integrated framework clarifies priority levers for impact prevention and resource efficiency, supporting evidence-based modernization pathways and strengthening the sustainability governance of research reactor operations.

title: High-intensity intermittent aeration with multi-stage descending rates enhances oxygen uptake to mitigate nitrogen emissions and promote humification in composting
abstract: Excessive nitrogen loss and inadequate humification are major constraints in aerobic composting. This study compared three aeration modes—continuous low (CAR-L), intermittent medium (TAR-M), and intermittent high intensity (TAR-H)—under equal total airflow with multi-stage descending rates. TAR-H created dynamic oxic-anoxic conditions, nearly doubling the cumulative oxygen uptake rate (OUR) and synergistically improving nitrogen retention and humification. It reduced cumulative NH3 and N2O emissions by 35.45% and 35.06%, respectively. Mechanistically, TAR-H upregulated thermophilic-phase nitrification genes (e.g.,amoA,hao) to curb NH3 loss, while suppressing nitrification and denitrification genes during maturation to limit N2O production. Concurrently, it enriched functional bacteria (e.g.,Streptomyces, Clostridium_sensu_stricto_1) that transformed preserved precursors into stable humic substances, raising the humification index (HIX) by 4.86%. The OUR was the central driver linking microbial succession to emission reduction and humification. Nationwide implementation of TAR-H based on livestock manure could mitigate 1.0 Mt N emissions annually, yielding $1.7 billion in societal benefits. Thus, optimizing oxygen uptake via a intermittent high-intensity aeration mode under fixed total supply synchronously enhances nitrogen conservation and humification, providing a theoretical basis for precision aeration technology.

title: EcoLLM: A lightweight ReAct-SFT framework for document-driven LCI extraction and automated LCIA in metal additive manufacturing
abstract: Life cycle assessment (LCA) relies on high-quality life cycle inventory (LCI) data, but such data are often scattered across technical reports, process descriptions, and other unstructured documents. Converting these documents into structured inventory records and linking them to background databases remains time-consuming and difficult to audit. To address these challenges in the metal additive manufacturing context, we developed EcoLLM, a lightweight and privacy-preserving framework for document-driven LCI extraction and automated LCIA. EcoLLM combines domain-adapted training data construction, tool-guided LCI extraction, semantic matching to background database flows, and openLCA-based impact calculation. To train the lightweight model for this workflow, we constructed AM-related training dialogues from synthetic process documents generated from foreground LCI records manually abstracted from real AM-LCA studies, using a semi-automated expert annotation workbench and ReAct-based supervised fine-tuning. On a 40-sample AM extraction benchmark, EcoLLM outperformed RAG-only, generic-agent, and prompt-only Qwen baselines, improving the valid JSON rate from 0.70 to 0.90 and recall from 0.64 to 0.74 relative to the prompt-only Qwen ReAct baseline. GPT-4o, included as a widely used proprietary large-scale LLM reference, achieved higher overall coverage, while EcoLLM showed comparable field-level exact match and competitive numerical correctness under a lightweight, locally deployable setting. A metal AM case study further demonstrated the practical feasibility of connecting document-grounded LCI extraction, semantic background flow linking, and openLCA-based LCIA calculation. This work could bridge the gap between unstructured data and standardized impact assessment, offering a scalable, privacy-compliant solution for accelerating sustainability analytics in vertical domains.

title: Applying a consumption-based perspective to nitrogen and phosphorus discharges in the Liao River Basin
abstract: Excessive nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) discharges threaten basin water quality, yet production-based inventories alone cannot reveal how food consumption reallocates nutrient pollution across cities through supply chains. In this study, we analyzed production-based direct discharges and consumption-based embodied discharges in trade from 1980 to 2022 by integrating six-subsystem N and P flow models with city-level environmentally extended multi-region input-output (EE-MRIO) models for 20 cities and 2 sectors in the Liao River Basin. We further identified the driving factors from EE-MRIO models using structure decomposition analysis (SDA). The results showed that N and P inputs and direct discharges in the Liao River Basin increased markedly before peaking around 2015–2016 and then decreased at different rates, with fertilizer application dominating N and P inputs and the livestock and poultry subsystem contributing the largest share of direct discharges. Spatially, N and P discharge hotspots showed clear temporal shifts along the mainstream of the Liao River, indicating substantial changes in production-based pollution pressure. The consumption-based footprint analysis further revealed strong spatial decoupling between food consumption and nutrient discharges. Based on the direction and magnitude of embodied footprint flows, cities were classified into internal-flow, external-inflow, and external-outflow patterns, showing that some consumption centers outsourced considerable N and P discharges to upstream supplying cities. SDA results indicated that production scale and final consumption mainly drove footprint increases during the rising-footprint stage, whereas changes in supply structure and final consumption contributed to footprint reductions after 2015. Ultimately, our findings reveal that traditional production-centric controls are insufficient due to the severe spatial decoupling of food supply chains. We urge policymakers to adopt differentiated, consumption-based management strategies to effectively mitigate nutrient discharges and address footprint inequalities.

title: Global accessibility of food ecosystem services under economic inequality, food production, and infrastructure shocks
abstract: Reconciling food ecosystem service (ES) supply and demand requires understanding not only food production capacity but also the transport infrastructure connecting resources to people. Economic and transport disparities cause inequalities in access to food ES, making the global food system vulnerable to disruptions. To evaluate global transport network efficiency in delivering food ES, we developed a spatial accessibility analysis method to assess the balance between food supply and demand. Our framework includes case analyses under the following scenarios: uniform transport costs, economic disparities, and regional shocks, including production disruptions and infrastructure damage caused by hazards in North America, Eastern Europe, and East Asia. Our results show that current state of transport infrastructure and food production distribution lead to unmet demand, particularly in Asia and Africa. Comparisons between equal and economic analysis show that economic differences between regions further exacerbate the ES supply-demand mismatch. Accounting for economic costs increases supply surpluses across most sub-regions, particularly in Southeast and South Asia, Africa, and Eastern Europe, while unmet demand also increases. About two-thirds of the global unmet demand is concentrated in Asia. This coexistence of surplus supply and unmet demand suggests transport bottlenecks and network inefficiencies, meaning that although food is available it cannot be effectively delivered to all the locations where it is needed. Among all scenarios analyzed, economic inequality has the greatest impact on food accessibility. Alongside food production, the structure and cost of transport are important factors in global food accessibility, even without considering trade relations and geopolitical influences.

title: From high carbon to low carbon research on the driving path of energy structure transformation under uniform and differential carbon taxes
abstract: Under the backdrop of China's "carbon neutrality" strategy, this paper constructs a general equilibrium model to compare and analyze the policy effects of uniform carbon tax and differential carbon tax. The results show that both types of policies share commonalities - they both have a negative impact on the macroeconomy and the intensity of the impact increases with the increase in tax rates. The reduction in carbon emissions increases with the tax rate and the reduction volume is positively correlated with the economic cost. At the same time, both can drive the contraction of coal consumption and the increase in the proportion of oil and natural gas, helping to transform the energy structure from the traditional high-carbon paradigm to a medium-low carbon paradigm. The heterogeneity is manifested as follows: the differential carbon tax, through differentiated tax burden design, implements tax relief for low-emission industries to buffer the GDP impact, and raises the carbon tax for high-emission industries to enhance the motivation for reducing coal consumption. This can further promote the transformation of the investment structure of fossil energy. The uniform tax system, by balancing the constraints on the cost of fossil energy, more significantly encourages the development of clean energy such as hydropower and wind power, and accelerates the deep decarbonization of the energy structure. In summary, the effects of the two types of policies are different, and it is necessary to combine the "carbon neutrality" goal to adapt and select the policy priority at different stages to achieve precise matching between policy effects and strategic goals.

title: Emissions prediction and mechanistic interpretation for sludge gasification via multi-source temporal modeling
abstract: Sludge gasification technology has emerged as a promising method for sludge treatment, offering significant advancements in resource recovery, pollution reduction and carbon mitigation. However, the generated air pollutants limit the widespread adoption of this technology. We construct a timeline-based framework using actual production data with minute-level resolution. This framework integrates historical emission concentrations, operational parameters (e.g., temperature, pH), input materials (e.g., gasifying agents, steam), as well as predetermined operational settings and inputs (e.g., steam flow rate, gasification agent pressure and fan frequency) to construct multi-source features, while constantly rolling the lookback and forecasting window to dynamically predict the SO2 concentrations, oxygen content and particulate matter. On this basis, we systematically evaluate four machine learning models and four deep learning models using the Python-based Darts time series library, and use interpretability including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP) in conjunction with process knowledge to analyze the underlying causes of SO2 fluctuations. The results suggest that model performance is closely related to the generation mechanisms of pollutants: TiDE performs optimally in predicting SO2, which has strong nonlinearity and hysteresis characteristics, while the timeline-based Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model demonstrates robust performance across multi-tasks. Additionally, the gasifier outlet temperature, pressure and steam flow rate are key factors for SO2 fluctuation, with their effects exhibiting a lag window of 5–8 min. Notably, the synergistic effect of low steam flow rate (<300 kg/h) and high outlet pressure (>4.0 kPa) contribute to a steep increase in SO2. By integrating data science with process mechanisms, this study aims to provide accurate and reliable decision support for proactive control and parameter optimization, thus enhance the environmental friendliness and economic feasibility of sludge gasification.

title: From historical analysis to future scenario simulation: How does climate change affect vegetation greenness in the Jinsha River Basin, China?
abstract: Clarifying the response relationship between vegetation greenness in mountain ecosystems and climate change is important for assessing regional vegetation-change risks and supporting sustainable land management. As a key ecological barrier in the upper Yangtze River and the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, the Jinsha River Basin (JRB) still lacks a clear understanding of how vegetation greenness responds to climate change and how it may change under future scenarios. Based on the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and meteorological data, this study used trend analysis, ridge regression, and machine learning models to construct an integrated framework of “historical diagnosis–mechanism analysis–future scenario simulation” and explored NDVI responses to climate change and potential trends under different future scenarios (SSP119, SSP245, and SSP585). The main results are as follows: From 2000 to 2025, NDVI in the JRB showed an increasing trend, with an interannual change rate of 5×10−4yr−1, and this increase was mainly concentrated in the lower reaches. NDVI responses to temperature-related factors differed: annual mean temperature (TEM) and maximum temperature (MaxTEM) were negatively correlated with NDVI changes, with relative contribution rates of 29.86% and 14.97%, respectively, whereas minimum temperature (MinTEM) was positively correlated with NDVI changes, with a contribution rate of 18.46%. Among moisture factors, precipitation (PRE) and potential evapotranspiration (EVA) contributed 10.14% and 17.48%, respectively. Under the influence of future climate change, NDVI showed a declining trend under the SSP119, SSP245, and SSP585 scenarios during 2026–2050, with interannual change rates of −1×10−4yr−1, −2×10−4yr−1, and −3×10−4yr−1, respectively. The potential risk of NDVI decline was higher under the high-emission scenario, and low-elevation areas may be sensitive regions of vegetation greenness change. Dynamic monitoring of biodiversity-sensitive areas in these regions should therefore be strengthened in basin ecological management.

title: Hierarchical 3D architecture of Ni-integrated bismuth oxyhalide embedded on boron, nitrogen co-doped reduced graphene oxide for the determination of methyl parathion in environmental media
abstract: The widespread application of pesticides in agriculture has become a pressing environmental concern, particularly due to their persistence in soil and water resources, which disrupts ecosystems, necessitating stricter environmental protection measures and underscoring the importance of enhanced environmental safeguards and food safety practices. Among the various pesticides, methyl parathion (MEPA) is a highly toxic organophosphate pesticide that demands sensitive and reliable monitoring strategies. This study reports the design and fabrication of a cutting-edge electrochemical sensor based on nickel-ion-incorporated bismuth oxychloride with boron, nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide (Ni-BOC/B,N@rGO). The phase structure of the as-prepared Ni-BOC/B,N@rGO was validated through X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR), and Raman spectroscopy. The surface morphology and elemental distribution were evaluated using Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM), and Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Furthermore, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was used to analyze the electron transfer dynamics at the electrode interface, indicating enhanced electron transfer kinetics and quicker response time relative to the bare glassy carbon electrode (GCE). To analyze the electrochemical properties, cyclic voltammetry (CV) was conducted, which showed that the nanocomposite achieved the cathodic peak current at pH 7.0, reflecting its higher catalytic activity for MEPA sensing. Under ideal conditions, the sensor achieved detection limits of 2.8 nM and 3.7 nM for MEPA, along with linear ranges of 0.01–747.18 μM and 0.01–273.49 μM at DPV and i-t, respectively, exhibiting excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. For MEPA detection in food samples and environmental samples, the Ni-BOC/B,N@rGO/GCE sensor exhibited commendable recovery rates for safety monitoring applications.

title: Natural gas purification with complete CO2 capture using ionic liquids: Process optimization and multi-criteria evaluation
abstract: Conventional amine-based natural gas purification processes are energy-intensive and environmentally burdensome. This study proposes an ionic liquid (IL)-based purification process enabling complete carbon dioxide (CO2) capture. Ten ILs were screened from eighteen candidates based on key thermodynamic, environmental, and transport properties. Process optimization was performed using Total Annualized Cost (TAC) and exergy analysis, while overall performance was evaluated via multi-criteria decision-making considering economic, environmental, and energetic indicators. Among the candidates, the N-Ethylmorpholine acetate ([NEMH][Ac]) process demonstrated the best overall performance, achieving full CO2 removal with methane (CH4) purity above 98 % and CO2 purity of 99.6 %. Compared with the conventional Monoethanolamine (MEA) process, TAC, global warming potential, toxicity, and energy consumption were reduced by 62.59 %, 81.01 %, 24.74 %, and 81.01 %. Partial least squares (PLS) regression further linked IL properties with process performance, enabling rapid IL screening in natural gas purification.

title: Reduced-energy processing of PLA/Talc biocomposites: Comparing in-mold crystallization and IR annealing
abstract: PLA is a promising bio-based alternative to fossil-based plastics, but its slow crystallization during injection molding often requires high mold temperatures, increasing cycle time and energy demand. This study evaluates two manufacturing routes for obtaining highly crystalline PLA/talc injection-molded parts: (i) high mold temperature molding at 100 °C and (ii) low mold temperature molding at 30 °C followed by infrared post-molding annealing. The comparison integrates manufacturability, crystallinity, surface quality, thermomechanical/mechanical response, and gate-to-gate specific energy consumption. Samples molded at 100 °C with a cooling time of 35 s (HM(35)) reached a crystallinity of 54.12 ± 0.65%, whereas samples molded at 30 °C (LM) showed 25.0 ± 0.23%. A 1-min IR treatment increased the crystallinity of LM-IR to approximately 54%. Under optimized annealing utilization and similar crystallinity, LM-IR reduced specific energy consumption by about 45% relative to HM(35). Ejection force measurements showed lower ejection demand during the high mold temperature molding, while surface roughness parameters including Ra, Rz, Rv, and Rp showed lower values at 100 °C. Maximum tensile strength was 48.98 ± 0.42 MPa for LM, compared to 44.66 ± 1.44 MPa for HM(35) and 43.50 ± 0.83 MPa for LM-IR. Heat deflection temperature increased from 55.0 ± 0.2 °C for LM to 145.81 ± 0.42 °C for HM(35) and 134.6 ± 1.4 °C for LM-IR. Overall, the study provides an integrated gate-to-gate comparison of two established routes for the investigated commercial PLA/talc composite and quantifies the process-property-energy trade-offs that govern route selection in similar nucleated PLA systems.

title: Comparative LCA of germanium production from coal fly ash using chlorinated distillation and solvent extraction
abstract: Germanium is increasingly important for high-tech applications, yet its supply chain is vulnerable, with production limited to a few countries. Although prior research has explored alternative techniques for extracting and recovering germanium, the literature lacks comparative life-cycle evidence that quantifies their environmental burdens and translates findings into actionable (policy) recommendations. This paper presents a cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment that compares the environmental burdens of producing 1 kg of single-crystal germanium from coal fly ash via chlorinated distillation (CD) and solvent extraction (SX). Under the study's assumptions, CD has lower potential impacts in 15 of 19 impact categories, while both routes show similar stratospheric ozone depletion potential. For SX, transportation (of fly ash and GeO2) and kerosene consumption each contribute 28–35% of the global warming, terrestrial acidification, and particulate matter formation impacts, while water leaching accounts for 67% of water consumption, and kerosene contributes 53% of cumulative energy demand. For CD, electricity consumption dominates (>50%) most impact categories, except terrestrial acidification, which is dominated (>50%) by chlorine gas used in GeCl4 purification. For SX, the most significant impact-reduction strategies are increasing organic-phase reuse (>95%), eliminating fresh kerosene input (or substituting lower-impact diluents), and up-concentrating germanium in the fly ash. For CD, cleaner production should prioritize the use of low-carbon electricity, integrating waste heat into acid-regeneration operations, and exploring chlorine substitutes in GeCl4 fractional distillation. These results show that policies seeking to advance new Ge process routes should first evaluate environmental burdens. Also, new process routes should be efficient and reduce waste.

title: The symphony of resilience: structural classification of urban agglomeration resilience via multilevel coupling coordination
abstract: As global urbanization accelerates, urban agglomerations face growing exposure to compound natural hazards and human pressures. Resilience assessment at the agglomeration scale is therefore essential for identifying structural weaknesses and informing differentiated governance. A capacity based framework is proposed that structures urban resilience around resistance, recovery, and adaptation across economic, social, engineering, and ecological subsystems. To reduce construct misalignment in ecological resilience measurement, indicators are selected to reflect the state and functioning of the natural system rather than proxies for governance performance. Cities within 19 urban agglomerations in China are used as the units of analysis. This study first uses an improved Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method to determine indicator weights and then applies the coupling coordination degree model and spatial overlay analysis to characterize the spatiotemporal patterns and structural coordination of urban resilience. The results show four main findings. First, urban resilience increases overall, yet disparities persist between coastal and inland urban agglomerations and among urban agglomerations at national, regional, and local levels. Economic and engineering subsystems contribute most to the increase, whereas ecological resilience constrains further gains. Second, within each subsystem, the balance among resistance, recovery, and adaptation varies markedly, indicating that resilience improvement does not necessarily imply balanced capacity development. Third, the coupling coordination degree between subsystems generally remains at the basic coordination level and is relatively stable. By contrast, internal coordination within subsystems is more differentiated, with ecological resilience emerging as the priority weakness. Fourth, spatial overlay yields a governance oriented classification. Most cities are classified as basic coordination with basically balanced structure. Among cities with structural imbalance, ecological subsystem imbalance is the most prevalent pattern. Overall, the framework links resilience performance with structural coordination and supports more targeted resilience improvement. It provides empirical guidance for China and other countries with similar development contexts in advancing urban resilience and building resilient cities.

title: Does artificial intelligence increase green total factor productivity in manufacturing? Based on the perspective of industrial robot sources
abstract: As an important carrier of intelligent manufacturing, the industrial robot application has gradually become the key to achieving green development. Based on the perspective of domestic- and foreign-sourced robots, this study examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on green total factor productivity (GTFP) in the manufacturing industry. The results indicate that AI has a significant positive impact on the GTFP of the manufacturing sector. Notably, foreign-sourced robots have a more pronounced effect on boosting manufacturing GTFP than domestic-sourced robots. Specifically, foreign-sourced robots primarily drive GTFP growth by fostering innovation, optimizing energy structures and enhancing employment levels. In contrast, domestic-sourced robots primarily contribute through the labor substitution effect, whereby machines replace workers to improve productivity. Further analysis reveals that the promotional effect of AI on GTFP is influenced by technological intensity and ownership structure. First, this study expands the scope of research on the economic and environmental impacts of AI. Second, this paper analyzes the differential effects of AI on GTFP from the perspectives of domestic- and foreign-sourced robots, thereby providing a basis for a comprehensive and objective assessment of the impacts of AI. Finally, this paper reveals the potential mechanisms through which domestic- and foreign-sourced robots influence GTFP.

title: Unveiling the ESG weighting system using multi-level global analysis: A machine learning approach with SHAP explainability
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics are increasingly critical for evaluating corporate sustainability and investment risk. As of today, several ESG frameworks consider different metrics, often assigning different weights to ESG pillars. However, these weights are often derived through opaque methodologies and could vary at the industry and company levels, limiting transparency and cross-company comparability. This research seeks to understand the primary drivers of ESG's weight emphasis across firms while maintaining regional and industry contextualization. In addition, interpretable models are developed using machine learning that predict ESG pillar weights based on structured economic and market variables, while considering the industry- and region-level heterogeneity among firms. The analysis dataset consisted of 1327 observations spanning 13 industrial groups and 27 countries in three regions of Asia, Europe, and North America. The study provides insights into how financial performance, industry concentration, and, to a lesser extent, regional context influences the weighting of the ESG pillars. Our findings demonstrate the need for tailored ESG frameworks that capture the firm-specific and industry-specific components while accounting for regional-level considerations.

title: Analysis of sustainable printing materials using computed tomography and tensile testing for aeronautical applications
abstract: Material extrusion is a well-established strategy for producing multiple parts for aeronautics applications. The process primarily consumes thermoplastic materials, which are a significant environmental risk. Thus, there is a need to develop sustainable printing strategies that achieve the expected benefits without compromising the environment's future. This manuscript analyzes three materials: conventional polylactic acid (PLA) and two potential PLA substitutes: recycled PLA and lightweight PLA. The specimens were then tested to determine the maximum tensile stress for two printing orientations: vertical and horizontal. The results show that PLA and recycled PLA exhibit similar behavior in tensile testing, with lower tensile strength observed in the vertical orientation. Using a lightweight PLA resulted in lower tensile stress but allowed higher strains. Computed tomography enabled a precise assessment of printing quality. Specifically, computed tomography enabled identification of how the cross-sectional area varied across the gauge section and revealed that Lw_PLA specimens exhibited significant expansion compared with their respective models. Finally, it was noted that the tensile strength calculated from computed tomography can vary by up to 8% relative to that calculated from the nominal cross-section for PLA and r-PLA. For Lw-PLA, this difference ranges from 25% to 30%.

title: Climate and anthropogenic drivers of spatiotemporal variation in ecosystem regulation service value across China (2000-2023)
abstract: Ecosystem service values (ESV) are utilized by many nations to guide investments in ecological conservation and restoration. However, the relative contributions of natural and anthropogenic factors to the spatiotemporal variations in ESV under the combined pressures of reclamation, urbanization, and ecological restoration remain poorly understood, with an increasing number of cases failing to achieve expected value realization. This paper quantifies the ecosystem regulation service value (ERSV) in China from 2000 to 2023, performing pixel-level trend analysis, identifying major contributing factors using the ARIMA time series method, and differentiating responses of ERSV to climate change, reclamation, urbanization, and ecological restoration. Our results indicate an overall upward trend in the average ERSV in China. Areas where precipitation and evapotranspiration are the primary contributing factors constitute over 65% of the land area, exhibiting distinctive zonal distribution patterns. Within regions experiencing Land Cover (LC) changes, a substantial proportion of ERSV variation remains primarily climate-driven. Climate-induced fluctuations account for over 81% of the total terrestrial area and ERSV. The gains in ERSV from ecological restoration projects reached 1236.70 billion yuan in 2023, which have compensated for and even exceeded the losses due to reclamation and urbanization. The study identifies and quantifies the impacts of natural and anthropogenic factors on changes in ERSV, while assessing the balance between ecological depletion losses and ecological restoration gains on human well-being, providing data support for the precise implementation of future ecological conservation policies.

title: A novel integrated risk assessment approach based on a two-dimensional water quality model and Bayesian networks: A case study in the Yangtze River basin
abstract: The Yangtze River Basin is an ecologically sensitive region, where sudden water pollution accidents pose significant risks to ecosystem health and public well-being. This study proposes an environmental risk assessment framework based on a two-dimensional water quality simulation-Bayesian network (2D-WQ-BN) model, with the aim of quantitatively predicting the risks associated with such pollution accidents. Decision and utility nodes are incorporated into the network to form a Bayesian influence diagram. A risk regulation computation is then established, integrating the assessments of the changes in risk levels and associated costs, and quantitatively comparing the effects of various regulatory measures. The model was applied to the risk assessment and regulation analysis of sudden water pollution accidents in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River. Populations served by the Third Water Plant and the Municipal Water Plant face a significantly greater number of acute drinking water health risks, with a risk index of 3244.0, compared to 2991.7 for those relying on the Fifth Water Plant. The core zone of the Tongling Freshwater Dolphins National Nature Reserve exhibits numerous acute aquatic ecological risks due to pollutant inputs from upstream enterprises. Sensitivity analysis identifies exposure hazard as the common primary driver, while revealing that ecological risks are more sensitive to aquatic receptor vulnerability, whereas health risks are more dependent on exposure levels. These findings are supported by uncertainty and sensitivity analyses confirming the model's high robustness and logical consistency. Risk sources H5, H8, and H10 should be prioritized as key management targets. Furthermore, the risk regulation computation reveals that measure M2 (improving the level of enterprise risk control) and M6 (enhancing the emergency response capacity of government departments) are the most effective, potentially reducing the overall risk index by 81.0 and 66.2. Regarding cost-effectiveness, the most efficient measures are M6 and M1 (reducing the number of hazardous substances in storage). The quantitative risk assessment and comparison of regulatory measures provide strong support for preventing and managing sudden water pollution accidents.

title: Between refuse and recycle: asymmetric polarization in circular economy representations
abstract: The concept of the circular economy ( CE ) has gained increasing prominence over the past decade, yet its meaning remains ambiguous and often diverges from the original vision of early CE pioneers. Understanding how this ambiguity shapes public perceptions is critical for the effective design and implementation of CE policies. Drawing on a survey of 1281 respondents in France, this study examines individuals' familiarity with CE , their spontaneous definitions, and their prioritization of circular strategies using the 5R hierarchy (refuse, reduce, reuse, repair, recycle). The results reveal a strong and asymmetric polarization of CE representations, structured around the acceptance or rejection of the refuse (sufficiency) lever. Recycling and reuse dominate spontaneous definitions, while reuse and recycling are prioritized when respondents explicitly rank CE levers. By contrast, refuse remains marginal despite its central role in strong circularity approaches. Socio-economic characteristics do not robustly explain this polarization. However, respondents whose preferences align more closely with strong circularity—consistent with the pioneers’ vision—report higher levels of pro-environmental behaviors and stronger support for CE-related public policies. These findings highlight a persistent gap between weak and strong circularity representations and suggest important implications for CE communication strategies and public policymaking.

title: Multi-objective design optimization of bio-based oriented strand boards from urban and orchard pruning residues via support vector machine and genetic algorithm
abstract: The increasing accumulation of pruning residues from urban and orchard trees represents both an environmental challenge and a valuable opportunity for sustainable material utilization. This study evaluated the feasibility of converting these residues into oriented strand board (OSB) panels and systematically investigated the effects of strand mixing ratio (MR), adhesive content (AC), and mat moisture content (MMC) on mechanical performance, bonding behavior, and dimensional stability. OSB panels were manufactured using different combinations of orchard and urban wood strands, phenol–formaldehyde resin levels, and mat moisture conditions, and their properties were evaluated in accordance with BS EN 300 standards. The results demonstrated that panels produced with a balanced strand composition and appropriately controlled processing parameters exhibited superior modulus of rupture and stiffness along both major and minor axes, higher internal bonding under dry and wet conditions, enhanced screw-holding capacity, and improved dimensional stability, reflected by lower water absorption and thickness swelling. Panels dominated by a single residue type showed inferior performance, which was attributed to increased material heterogeneity and weaker fiber–matrix interactions. Support Vector Machine (SVM) modeling successfully captured the nonlinear relationships between processing variables and panel properties, achieving high predictive accuracy across all evaluated responses (R2 = 0.86–1.00). The integration of SVM-based response surface analysis with genetic algorithm optimization and TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making identified a consistent processing window that simultaneously optimized mechanical, bonding, and physical properties. Optimal overall performance was achieved at 50% MR, 10% AC, and 12% MMC. These findings confirm that urban and orchard pruning residues can be effectively valorized as sustainable raw materials for high-performance OSB production and demonstrate that the proposed data-driven optimization framework provides a robust and industrially applicable basis for engineered wood panel design.

title: Exploring the spatiotemporal coupling mechanism of livestock carbon emissions intensity and ecological vulnerability in inner Mongolia: An ensemble learning approach
abstract: Understanding the interaction between livestock production and ecosystem stability is essential for promoting sustainable development in fragile pastoral regions. However, the spatiotemporal coupling between the two systems and their underlying driving mechanisms remain insufficiently explored. This study develops an integrated analytical framework that combines livestock carbon emission accounting, ecological vulnerability assessment, coupling analysis, and interpretable machine learning to investigate the dynamic interactions between livestock carbon emissions intensity and ecological vulnerability in Inner Mongolia from 2000 to 2020. Unlike previous studies that directly use total carbon emissions as a subsystem indicator, this study constructs a livestock carbon emission intensity indicator to capture the carbon cost per unit of economic output and the production efficiency of the livestock sector. An improved coupling coordination model that endogenously determines subsystem contribution weights is applied to reduce biases caused by subjective weighting. In addition, an ensemble learning model selection framework integrating nested cross-validation and Bayesian optimization is used to identify the optimal algorithm and interpret the underlying driving mechanisms. The results reveal that livestock carbon emission intensity and ecological vulnerability exhibit pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, with the coupled system predominantly characterized by weak to moderate negative coupling. Vegetation conditions represent the most important positive regulating factor, while adequate forage supply and increased precipitation mitigate ecological pressure associated with livestock carbon emissions. In contrast, rural population proportion acts as the most significant negative driver, intensifying human–livestock–grassland interactions and increasing coupling pressure. These findings provide new insights into the interaction between livestock production and ecological vulnerability and offer scientific support for promoting low-carbon livestock development and enhancing ecological resilience in pastoral regions.

title: A comprehensive LCA CO2 emission inventory for passenger car fleet in Europe and future trends
abstract: Europe, countries worldwide and several organizations account systematically the emissions from road transport in various applications ranging from official sectorial targets setting to territorial inventories and monitoring statistics. However, this paper argues that the ongoing shift to electrification challenges the adequacy of these activities in revealing true climatic impacts of road transport. The current focus on Tank-to-Wheel (TTW) emissions that narrows the accounting boundaries to on-road operation would benefit from additional elements that would take into consideration upstream and end-of-life emissions of vehicles and fuels, similar to the approaches adopted in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). To support efforts for more holistic emission inventorying in Europe, this paper compiles a comprehensive lifecycle CO 2 inventory for the passenger-car fleet of EU-27 countries using a fleet-based method. The inventory is “comprehensive” in the sense that it represents the entire fleet at an increased level of detail, covering all fuel types and vehicle size classes, instead of emphasizing individual vehicle performance. It is also based on actual data for fleet composition, vehicle characteristics and activity patterns. Up-to-date emission factors are used to account for the fleet emission performance across all lifecycle stages. Projections for the future are made in all elements, considering a realistic fleet electrification pathway in response to official EU CO 2 targets. In addition, to ensure consistency and comparison with TTW regulated emissions reporting practices, the inventory builds upon COPERT, which is widely used for TTW inventorying in Europe, and enriches it with lifecycle system boundaries. Results achieved with this extended inventory have practical meaning as they answer questions on how much the total greenhouse emissions of the fleet are, and how far the global picture from the TTW is, given that targets for road transport are set on TTW basis in EU. Results show that electrification can bring true net-zero CO 2 results, which can only be assessed with an LCA-equivalent method.

title: Decomposing capital-endogenized emissions: A comprehensive accounting analysis of Korea's carbon emissions
abstract: Conventional carbon accounting methods for production-based emissions (PBE) or consumption-based emissions (CBE) treat investment as an exogenous final demand category, without accounting for the fact that capital goods are emission-intensive inputs to production. Using Korea's 2020 benchmark input–output table, we construct and compare PBE, CBE, and a capital-endogenized consumption-based measure (CBEk). We further decompose CBEk into emissions induced by household consumption, government demand, investment, and imports. The results show that endogenizing capital fundamentally reshapes the sectoral distribution of emissions. Relative to conventional CBE, emissions attributed to the Construction sector decline by 64.4%, while those for capital-using sectors increase markedly, with emissions in the Dwelling sector rising by 227.4%, ICT & Communications by 21.6%, and Service by 17.4%. Applying a novel decomposition method that fully attributes emissions to final demand, including those embodied in intermediate imports, we find that household consumption-induced emissions amount to 58.5% of total emissions under CBEk. These findings underscore the importance of endogenizing capital in national carbon accounting standards and in shifting policy attention toward demand-side mitigation strategies.

title: Parametric sensitivity analysis of design and operation for a methanol synthesis process
abstract: Methanol is a key chemical molecule and energy carrier whose importance is expected to grow as a cornerstone of future energy systems and carbon recycling strategies. Its sustainable production is tightly linked to the availability of renewable hydrogen, making the efficient and flexible use of syngas a critical challenge. This work presents a reactor-level parametric assessment of the flexibility and performance of an industrial boiling water-cooled multitubular methanol synthesis reactor. A pseudo-homogeneous model was developed to evaluate the combined effects of syngas quality, expressed through the Carbon Oxide Ratio (COR) and the Stoichiometric Number (SN), and syngas quantity, represented by the Gas Hourly Space Velocity (GHSV). Results show that a favorable operating region of COR value exists in the range 0.05–0.2, with operation below this range (CO-rich feeds) leading to steep losses in methanol yield and conversion. In contrast, a slight CO 2 surplus has less impact, making CO 2 -rich operation more robust to variations in inlet feed composition. The SN most favorable region depends strongly on feed composition: values below 2 (SN ≈ 1–1.3) maximize methanol yield while reducing hydrogen demand for mixed CO/ CO 2 feeds, whereas CO 2 -rich feeds require higher SN values ( ≈ 2.5–3). GHSV critically affects performance, with lower values extending residence time and increasing yield, while higher values amplify sensitivity to feed composition. Flexibility analysis highlights that both operational and design strategies, such as reactor volume increase, can mitigate off-optimal performance. Overall, the study demonstrates that methanol synthesis reactors are highly sensitive to the balance between syngas composition and reactor load. Beyond identifying favorable steady-state operating windows, the results provide reactor-level guidelines for exploiting operational and design flexibility to improve carbon utilization and reduce renewable hydrogen demand. The proposed maps may support the preliminary design and control-oriented interpretation of methanol synthesis units into power-to-methanol schemes and renewable-based CO 2 valorization pathways.

title: Quantifying carbon emissions in multimodal passenger transport: Evidence from urban subcenter development
abstract: Polycentric urban development is a spatial governance strategy adopted by megacities to address urban sprawl and excessive agglomeration through the decentralization of population and economic activities into functionally complementary sub-centers. However, its implications for passenger transport carbon emissions remain under-explored, posing challenges for greenhouse gas mitigation. This study develops a histogram-based gradient boosting decision tree model, incorporating a bottom-up carbon emission calculation method, to predict passenger transportation carbon emissions under various development scenarios in urban economic convergence zones (urban sub-centers) outside Beijing government-designated core business districts. Taking Beijing as a case study, the research findings indicate that the development of sub-centers is projected to reduce total passenger transport carbon emissions by 0.65 million tonnes while increasing the relative share of emissions from high-carbon travel modes. Long walking times for public transport, inconvenient transfers, and fare disparities are the primary factors encouraging high-carbon travel modes. These findings suggest that to mitigate emissions from high-carbon modes, priority should be given to strengthening rapid public transport connections between the city center and sub-centers, improving the convenience of intermodal transport, and adjusting fare structures, particularly by increasing taxi fares. This study provides empirical evidence for policymakers to advance green transport strategies within the context of polycentric urban planning.

title: How policy constraints reshape systematic conservation planning: evidence from ecosystem services, biodiversity co-representation, and ecological connectivity in the Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Reconciling ecosystem service protection, biodiversity conservation, and land-use pressure remains a major challenge for sustainable watershed management. However, it remains unclear how policy-related spatial rules alter conservation portfolios relative to an unconstrained baseline. This study developed an integrated systematic conservation planning framework combining Marxan optimization, multiscale TOPSIS ranking, Pareto trade-off diagnosis, self-organizing map clustering, and circuit-theory connectivity modeling. Using the Yangtze River Basin as a case study, an unconstrained setting was compared with a policy-constrained setting in which existing nature reserves were locked in and urban land was excluded from selection. Under the 30% carbon sequestration priority scenario, the policy-constrained setting selected 655,233 km2 of priority conservation areas, compared with 572,650 km2 under the unconstrained setting, and produced a more compact portfolio around existing nature reserves. Baseline–incremental decomposition showed that existing nature reserves already represented 38.75% of key biodiversity areas (KBAs) and 45.41% of endemic bird areas, whereas newly selected areas under the policy-constrained 30% scenario contributed 25.52%–31.38% of the modeled amount of the five ecosystem services and 29.94% of composite mammal distributions. Multiscale ranking identified the Yalong, Minjiang, and Jialing River basins as stable priority regions. Pareto analysis showed that trade-off structures depended on the biodiversity feature considered: the policy-constrained setting had a higher multi-objective co-benefit index when KBAs were used as the biodiversity feature (0.142 vs. 0.101), whereas the unconstrained setting showed a more balanced structure when composite mammal distributions were used. Connectivity modeling indicated that the policy-constrained setting had lower Human Footprint Index (HFI)-based patch resistance than the unconstrained setting (115,820.6 vs. 122,037.3), but slightly higher corridor connection cost (357,268 vs. 287,526). Connectivity indices were also higher under the policy-constrained setting, with the integral index of connectivity (IIC) increasing from 0.3615 to 0.4934 and the probability of connectivity (PC) increasing from 0.5018 to 0.7181. These findings show that policy constraints reshape conservation outcomes by changing spatial configuration, ecological representation, HFI-based proxy cost, and network structure, rather than uniformly improving all conservation dimensions. The framework provides decision-support information for cleaner land-use governance and ecological redline implementation in complex human–land systems.

title: Measurement, Evaluation and Parametric Analysis of Acoustical Characteristics of Vegetative Species for Noise Control Applications
abstract: The rapid expansion of cities and transportation networks has led to elevated levels of noise pollution worldwide. The use of vegetative noise – shielding barriers is a sustainable and cost-effective approach that is increasingly needed to address this issue. The present study aims to evaluate the acoustical characteristics of various abundantly available vegetative species categorized as grasses, herbs, shrubs, climbing shrubs, and trees. A normal-incidence sound impedance tube was used to measure the Sound Absorption Characteristics (SAC) across the frequency range from 50 Hz to 6600 Hz. The study concludes that different vegetative species exhibit distinct acoustical behaviour. Experimental study was performed on three sample types: 1) leaves (L), with a highest observed Noise Reduction Coefficient (NRC) of 0.85 for the silver oak, 2) stem in combination with leaves, with a highest NRC of 0.77 for madhumalti, and 3) soil substrate and stem in combination with leaves, with a highest NRC of 0.65 for kadi patta. Majorly, species showed mid to higher absorption from 1000 Hz to 6600 Hz frequency range. The correlation parameters revealed, no significant correlation between studied parameters of morphological traits (AL, TL, leaf surface roughness, and MC) – sample parameters (mass, density and surface density) – acoustical parameters (NRC, SAA) of vegetative species. The study also reports the regression analysis (linear and base-10 logarithmically transformed values) for correlating NRC and SAA with leaf thickness, leaf area and density of samples. The paper presents the best sound absorptive vegetative species to use as noise barriers, which are abundantly available in the Indian scenario. This study will be helpful for the design and development of noise – shielding vegetative barriers for controlling environmental noise pollution and in forming policies and landscape planning.

title: China's agricultural carbon emission efficiency: A fixed-sum Malmquist index approach
abstract: China faces serious environmental challenges, with agriculture playing a key role in emission reduction. This study developed a novel approach to dynamically assess agricultural carbon emission efficiency (ACEE) under undesirable fixed-sum outputs. An algorithm was proposed to generate representative samples of equilibrium effective frontiers (EEFs) and the Malmquist productivity index (MPI), and Kernel density estimation (KDE) was used to capture the distribution and variation of the MPI samples. The methodology was applied to 30 Chinese provinces from 2015 to 2021. The results show that, except for the 2016-2017 period, agricultural carbon emission efficiency generally improved, with over half of the provinces achieving an MPI >1. Most provinces exhibited an initial decline, followed by an increase in ACEE, with several provinces showing a decline during the 2020-2021 period. Yunnan consistently performed the best, showing continuous improvement. The assessment results provide a theoretical reference for promoting low-carbon agricultural development and several policy recommendations have been proposed. To demonstrate robustness, sensitivity analyses on the sample size and repeated random sampling were conducted, together with an external consistency check by comparing MPI with an independent low-carbon performance indicator. These additional analyses confirmed the stability and reliability of the proposed approach.

title: Identifying vegetation dynamics and their drivers in China's oases using multi-source data
abstract: Oases in China, occupying merely approximately 3.02% of the country's total land area, support the overwhelming majority of the population and most economic activities in the arid regions of Northwest China. However, drastic changes in their vegetation are profoundly reshaping the ecological structure of oases and posing severe challenges to regional sustainable development. To accurately reveal the complex driving mechanisms underlying these changes, this study constructed an integrated machine learning-based attribution framework. This framework integrated multi-source data spanning 2000 to 2020, and captured the nonlinear responses of vegetation to various factors via the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model. It then quantified the explanatory power of each factor for the spatial differentiation in combination with the Geodetector model. The results show that: (1) Over the past 21 years, driven by the reshaping of land use patterns characterized by continuous cropland expansion, the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) of oases has increased steadily at a rate of 0.001/yr. (2) Attribution analysis indicates that Soil Water Content (SWC) and the Irrigated Cropland Area Ratio (IRR) are the primary drivers of NDVI growth; together, the two factors explain 65.07% of the spatial heterogeneity in NDVI, confirming that human-managed irrigation is a key force in sustaining the vitality of oasis vegetation. (3) Water and heat exert synergistic effects on vegetation growth under specific conditions. Specifically, the core threshold range promoting positive NDVI growth occurs when IRR ranges from 30% to 100%, SWC is between 15% and 39%, annual mean Air Temperature (TEMP) ranges from 10 °C to 15 °C, and annual mean Surface Net Solar Radiation (SSRD) is approximately 1830 kWh/m2. The water and heat response patterns, thresholds, and their provincial heterogeneity of China's oases revealed in this study provide a critical scientific basis for optimizing water resource allocation and delineating the sustainable development boundaries of oases in arid regions.

title: Optimizing low-carbon construction for sustainable built environment: A semantic ontology and hybrid intelligence-driven framework
abstract: Over the past four decades, China's construction industry has developed remarkably and accumulated extensive knowledge in low-carbon construction management. However, this knowledge is applied inefficiently—limited to passive representation and simplistic use, lacking a systematic and automated framework. Therefore, promoting the efficient reuse of low-carbon construction case knowledge is urgent. This study develops a semantic ontology-based framework that includes constructing a semantic ontology for standardized case representation, implementing case matching through semantic similarity computation, and adopting a Genetic Algorithm-optimized Ant Colony Optimization (GA-ACO) method for multi-objective optimization of CO2 emissions, cost, and construction difficulty. Validated by a project in Chengdu, the framework generates optimized technical solutions. Results show that the optimal recommendation reduces costs by 1.5348 million CNY, CO2 emissions by 51.3 tons, and the construction difficulty index by 1.44. This study provides a novel decision-support framework that advances the intelligent management of construction knowledge for sustainable built environment. It demonstrates significant potential in facilitating precise carbon mitigation and resource-efficient construction practices.

title: Thermal selection of microbial consortia modulates copper corrosion toward mineral stabilization
abstract: Copper corrosion can be strongly modulated by microbial activity despite the intrinsic toxicity of copper ions to most microorganisms. This study investigates the corrosion behavior of high-purity copper (Cu ≥ 99.9 wt%) exposed to thermophilic bacteria and methanogenic archaea collected from a biological methanation plant. Batch experiments were conducted at 45 °C for 15 days, using the inoculum as-is (biotic), or after three distinct treatments: 1) boiling (120 min), which did not significantly alter the overall-community-level diversity and structure; 2) double autoclaving (121 °C, 20 min), which selectively enriched thermotolerant populations, and 3) sterilization, only achieved by combining autoclaving (121 °C, 60 min), filtration (Φ = 0.22 μm), and UV exposure. Microbial communities were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing; corrosion was monitored by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Raman spectroscopy. Results reveal a time-dependent transition from microbially influenced corrosion (MIC) to microbial corrosion-inhibition (MICI). Bacterial-dominated communities transiently perturbed interfacial electrochemistry and delayed passivation but did not produce the highest cumulative copper dissolution (3,1, 3,73, 3,09 mg L −1 , for biotic, boiled, and autoclaved inoculum, respectively). Two distinct MICI pathways were identified: Cu 2 O barrier stabilization under archaeal-dominated inoculum (autoclaved), and diffusion resistance through porous phosphates precipitation in mixed bacterial-archaeal communities (biotic, boiled inoculum). Sterile conditions exhibited uninhibited chloride-driven localized corrosion and the highest copper release (7.1 mg L −1 ). Overall, the microbial community exerts a net moderating influence on copper dissolution, and thermal selection of community composition determines which MICI mechanism prevails.

title: Survival-first or cooperation-first: How nutritional status shape quorum sensing-mediated trade-offs between methane production and antibiotic resistance gene propagation during sludge digestion
abstract: Waste-activated sludge (WAS) presents a fundamental paradox: substantial energy recovery potential coupled with critical antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination risks. While anaerobic digestion (AD) offers promise for addressing both challenges, the underlying mechanisms governing the trade-off between methane production and ARG propagation under varying nutritional conditions remain poorly understood. This study investigated how C10-HSL, a key quorum sensing (QS) signaling molecule, mediates this critical balance during WAS digestion under oligotrophic versus eutrophic conditions. Under oligotrophic conditions, C10-HSL enhanced methane production by 35.3% while simultaneously reducing ARG abundance by 10.0% relative to the control by inducing a survival-first metabolic strategy with preferential energy storage and basal metabolism. Mechanistically, C10-HSL upregulated survival-associated QS genes (e.g., cviI and secY) and enhanced substrate utilization efficiency (protease activity increased 2.96-fold), while systematically downregulating resistance mechanisms including efflux pumps and ABC transporters. Conversely, under eutrophic conditions, in comparison with the control, C10-HSL achieved superior methane enhancement (12.2% increase) but at the cost of increased ARG propagation (15.9% increase) by driving a cooperation-first metabolic strategy that strengthened syntrophic metabolism via complex microbial cooperative interactions. C10-HSL activated cooperation-associated QS genes (e.g., luxS and secDF) and specialized metabolic pathways (carbohydrate metabolism increased to 8.53% while amino acid metabolism decreased), while simultaneously upregulating horizontal gene transfer systems including type IV secretion components (e.g., VirB1 and VirB4). Generally, adaptive bacteria dominated oligotrophic systems with strong negative correlations to ARG dissemination, while symbiotic bacteria dominated eutrophic systems with positive correlations to both methane production and ARG propagation.

title: Confronting the carbon responsibility mismatch in China's fixed capital: insights from the production and consumption perspectives
abstract: Fixed capital plays a dual role as both a productive input and a concealed carrier of carbon emissions, yet its cross-sectoral and cross-regional reallocations and the resulting mismatches in embodied carbon responsibility remain largely overlooked. By integrating an environmentally extended multiregional input–output model with detailed capital databases, this study constructed a sectoral production–use matrix to quantify China's fixed capital production, use, and to trace embodied carbon flows along the full supply chain. China has long been both a global net supplier of fixed capital and a major bearer of outsourced embodied carbon. Carbon responsibility mismatches occur simultaneously across sectors and regions. More than 75% of China's capital-related emissions originated from energy- and material-intensive sectors, rather than from capital-using sectors or capital-producing sectors. Although a weak decoupling emerged between capital exports and their embodied emissions, export-driven production accounted for about one-fifth of China's domestic emissions, implying additional carbon mitigation responsibility. China's proportion of imported capital use declined to 1%, whereas the share of embodied carbon in imported capital rose to 10%, indicating a potential cross-border mitigation blind spot that may be difficult to govern. This paradox rises from the global capital production system's dependence on resource-based economies, such as Russia, India, and Brazil, where slow decoupling transfers upstream emissions along global value chains to China, meaning that capital imports are characterized by strong negative decoupling. These findings underscore the need for full lifecycle, cross-sectoral governance and international cooperation to correct the responsibility mismatches in the global capital trade.

title: Extraction of Fe, Si, Mg, Ni and Co from nickel slag by sulfuric acid leaching and stepwise precipitation methods
abstract: Recovering strategic and critical metals from nickel slag eliminates pollution sources, aligning with circular economy principles and ecological development goals. This study develops an innovative hydrometallurgical approach for extracting Fe, Si, Mg, Ni and Co from nickel slag through atmospheric pressure sulfuric acid leaching followed by stepwise precipitation. The elemental leaching and precipitation behaviors were investigated, and the underlying mechanisms were explored. The results show that the dissolution of fayalite, magnetite, and sulfides facilitated the leaching of 91%–92% of Fe, Ni and Co, 70.0% of Si, and 98.6% of Mg at optimal conditions: sulfuric acid concentration of 1.5 mol/L, temperature of 90 °C, time of 30 min, and liquid-to-solid ratio of 10 mL/g. Kinetic analysis revealed that Fe, Ni and Co exhibit similar leaching behaviors, fitting a second-order kinetic model with activation energies of 47–52 kJ/mol. Stepwise processing via polymerization precipitation, hydrolytic precipitation, and evaporative crystallization successfully yielded separable products: silica gel, goethite, Ni-Co precipitate and magnesium sulfate crystals. Higher temperature and acid concentration accelerated silica gel formation. Magnesium oxide demonstrated dual functionality in pH regulation and metal (Fe, Ni and Co) exchange. The decomposition of magnesium sulfate crystals could produce recyclable magnesium oxide while generating sulfur oxides for sulfuric acid regeneration. This closed-loop system demonstrated 75.8% mass reduction of original slag while achieving simultaneous metal extraction and material recovery, providing practical guidance for nickel slag utilization.

title: Strengthening water-energy-food security through interconnected systems: A nexus perspective
abstract: Water, energy, and food systems are increasingly exposed to multifaceted pressures driven by social, economic, and environmental dynamics. Addressing these pressures demands a holistic understanding of the Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus. However, current research remains fragmented, lacking integration across these interconnected systems. Existing studies predominantly focus on resource flow analysis or assessments of individual or dual systems, with insufficient attention to the interconnections among systems within multi-policy frameworks, as well as the dynamic evolution and feedback mechanisms that characterize them. To address this gap, this study develops a comprehensive interconnections index (WEFc) that integrates three key dimensions—dependency, constraint, and synergy—to systematically quantify interconnections among WEF systems under multiple policy frameworks and to identify potential conflicts as well as feedback characteristics related to security and system interconnections. Results indicate that across 31 provinces in mainland China, the mean value of WEFc increased from 0.20 to 0.27. Spatial analysis reveals pronounced heterogeneity, with weaker interconnections observed in Northeast China and Northwest China, whereas Central China and Eastern China exhibited stronger coupling and more effective coordination. However, persistent governance fragmentation across sectors weakens coordinated responses, thereby amplifying systemic vulnerabilities and security risks—particularly within water and food systems. These heightened pressures reinforce cross-sectoral coupling and further increase the complexity of interconnections within the WEF Nexus. Accordingly, this study proposes sustainable transition pathways centered with WEFc on water-saving management, low-carbon energy transformation, and a balanced food supply-demand system. These integrated strategies help mitigate intersystem dependency, alleviate mutual constraints, and enhance synergistic efficiency, ultimately promoting the sustainable and resilient evolution of the WEF Nexus and providing scientific support for the comprehensive management of ecological environments.

title: A governance-sensitive blue economy index for ports: Benchmarking sustainability and transition readiness in Spanish ports
abstract: Ports occupy a critical role in supporting sustainability transitions within the contemporary Blue Economy, yet existing evaluation frameworks remain fragmented and not aligned with governance and transition-related challenges. This article introduces a governance-sensitive composite index designed to evaluate port performance across five core dimensions: Economic, Environmental, Social, Innovation & Technology, and Governance & Regulation. The framework consists of 26 indicators aggregated through a seven-step methodology that includes Delphi validation, min-max normalization, and weighted aggregation. The empirical application focuses on four anonymized Spanish ports representing different functional profiles across both the Mediterranean and Atlantic façades. The empirical results reveal substantial heterogeneities in sustainability performance and institutional readiness, with Blue Economy Index (BEI) scores ranging from 62.3 to 89.7. For instance, Mediterranean ports obtained the highest overall scores, driven primarily by innovation and governance dimensions, whereas lower-performing nodes exhibited greater structural weaknesses and limited adaptive capacity. To complement the static assessment, two forward-looking indicators were incorporated: the Forward Capacity Index (FCI), associated with institutional and innovation readiness, and the Blue Transition Risk Index (BTRI), designed to identify latent vulnerabilities related to sustainability alignment. The findings suggest that governance capacity and innovation dynamics play a central role in shaping long-term sustainability performance and transition preparedness in port systems. The resulting index can support benchmarking, strategic planning, and governance-sensitive sustainability evaluation within Blue Economy contexts.

title: Food waste-sludge co-fermentation liquid drives efficient partial denitrification: Kinetics, microbial community, and metabolic insights
abstract: The insufficient carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio of wastewater often constrains biological denitrification, necessitating external carbon sources. This study evaluated food waste and sewage sludge co-fermentation liquid (FWss-CoFL) as a sustainable alternative to conventional glucose in sequencing batch reactors over 120 days across a range of C/N ratios (3–6). Both achieved >95% nitrogen removal at C/N = 5. However, FWss-CoFL demonstrated superior stability under carbon-limited conditions (C/N = 3) and uniquely promoted efficient partial denitrification with exceptionally high nitrite accumulation, achieving peak nitrate-to-nitrite transformation ratio of 77.27%, 53.59%, and 72.61% at C/N 4, 5, and 6, respectively. Kinetic analysis revealed that FWss-CoFL supported a 2.4-fold higher nitrate reduction rate (31.26 vs. 12.91 mg N/(g VSS·h)) and a 1.8-fold higher nitrite accumulation rate at C/N = 5 compared to glucose. Microbial community analysis showed that FWss-CoFL enriched a functionally synergistic consortium, comprising potential partial denitrifiers (e.g., SC-I-84) and complete denitrifiers (e.g., Pseudomonas), whereas glucose favored generalist heterotrophs. Metagenomic predictions further revealed that FWss-CoFL upregulated key genes for the tricarboxylic acid cycle (e.g., citrate synthase), electron transport chain complexes, and downstream denitrification steps (nirK, nosZ), while enhancing nitrate/nitrite transporter abundance.
