Consequently, climate-vulnerable regions such as the Sahel, South Asia, and Brazil experience contrasting precipitation responses. These findings, derived from thermodynamic climate simulations, demonstrate that large-scale desert solar farms are not climate-neutral and highlight the need to integrate climate teleconnections into renewable energy planning for sustainable development.

title: Global shipping pollutant emissions from 1970 to 2022: spatiotemporal changes and exposures
abstract: Global shipping plays a crucial role in international trade but has significant environmental and social implications due to pollutant emissions. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of shipping-related pollutant emissions from 1970 to 2022 and examines population exposure disparities between the Global North and South. Using EDGAR v8.1 dataset, this research quantifies emissions of eight major pollutants (SO2, NOX, PM2.5, BC, CO, NMVOC, NH3, OC) and their exposure in coastal cities worldwide. The study employs multi-scale statistical analyses, including correlation assessments and trend decomposition, to identify long-term patterns and inequalities in pollution exposure. The findings reveal that shipping-related emissions have increased substantially over the past five decades, particularly in the Global South. Between 1970 and 2022, NOX emissions in the South surged by 270.87 t/yr, while the North exhibited a net reduction of −19.61 t/yr. Similarly, SO2 emissions in the South increased by 178.39 t/yr, whereas the North saw a decrease of −23.40 t/yr. Strong correlations exist between pollutant exposure and GDP, with a correlation coefficient of 0.79 (p = 0) for NOX,suggesting that higher-income coastal cities bear disproportionate pollution burdens. Additionally, shipping carbon emissions exhibit a robust association with population exposure, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.462 to 0.846, further highlighting the environmental risks borne by densely populated regions. This study underscores the urgent need for equitable environmental governance and targeted emission reduction policies to address pollution disparities, particularly in the Global South.

title: Energy- and oxidant-efficient VUV/H2O2 polishing via surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning
abstract: Vacuum ultraviolet/hydrogen peroxide (VUV/H2O2) advanced oxidation is a promising polishing strategy for low-total-organic-carbon (TOC) high-purity water systems. However, its practical operation is constrained by coupled trade-offs among TOC removal, residual H2O2, and energy demand, often leading to inefficient energy use and excessive oxidant consumption. This study developed a surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework for energy- and oxidant-efficient single-pass VUV/H2O2 polishing under low-TOC conditions, using methanol as a neutral low-molecular-weight model organic. A high-fidelity COMSOL multiphysics model was used to generate simulation data, and a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate replaced direct simulations, reducing evaluation time from minutes-scale COMSOL calculations to second-scale prediction and enabling scalable policy learning. Among the evaluated RL algorithms, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) achieved the best performance under a multi-objective formulation integrating TOC removal, residual H2O2, electrical energy per order (EEO), and apparent reaction kinetic performance. The optimized policy identified operating regimes characterized by low energy consumption (EEO ≤ 2.5 kWh m−3 order−1), sufficient hydraulic throughput (>79 mL min−1), and high TOC removal (>71.8 %). Experimental validation confirmed the applicability of the optimized policy, with RL predictions agreeing with measurements within 1.5–3.4 % for TOC removal. Compared with an empirical baseline under identical influent conditions, the optimized operation increased TOC removal by 18.0 percentage points, from 58.3 % to 76.3 %, while reducing EEO by 55.8 %, from 4.39 to 1.94 kWh m−3 order−1. These results demonstrate that integrating physics-based modeling, surrogate learning, and RL can support energy-efficient and residual-oxidant-aware operation of VUV/H2O2 polishing, providing a scalable pathway toward resource-efficient water treatment.

title: Comprehensive 12E assessment of hybrid nano-PCM and metal-mesh PVT-integrated hexagonal solar still for sustainable desalination
abstract: Growing global demand for renewable energy and freshwater resources integrated, long-term solutions, especially in water-constrained and off-grid areas. This work describes a novel hybrid solar system that combines a photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) unit with a hexagonal solar still (HSS), with the goal of addressing both energy and water scarcity through improved thermal energy recovery and storage that rarely explored in previous studies. A key innovation lies in the development of a hybrid nano-phase change material (HNPCM), composed of paraffin wax, graphene, Al2O3 nanoparticles, and radial metal mesh, which significantly improves thermal conductivity and latent heat storage. Six HSS configurations were developed and experimentally evaluated using combinations of sensible and latent heat storage materials such as granite, black sand, and metal sponge. The system was comprehensively assessed under a 12E framework covering energy, exergy, economic, environmental, and sustainability metrics. Results showed that the optimized PVT module (Panel 4) achieved a peak overall energy efficiency of 92.05% (combined electrical and thermal heat extraction). Furthermore, the integrated HSS system achieved a 60.22% higher freshwater yield, while the modified PV panel demonstrated a 24.09% relative improvement in electrical efficiency over the conventional system. Energy payback time was reduced to 0.266 years, and CO2 emissions mitigation reaching 1042.5 kg/year. The study demonstrates a scalable, multifunctional design suitable for decentralized applications, aligning with circular economy principles. This work contributes to the advancement of low-carbon, resource-efficient solar technologies for cleaner production in developing and climate-vulnerable regions.

title: Process design and techno-economic-assessment of the sorption enhanced methanol synthesis over zeolite 3A
abstract: The current effort towards sustainable methanol production is fostering research into the development of new small-scale processes that can adapt to the decentralized nature of most renewable electricity production sources. The production of methanol from electrolytic H 2 and C O 2 requires the development of new chemical routes that account for the many limitations present in small-scale applications. Among these, the most relevant is the low pressure (<30 bar) at which H 2 is normally delivered from electrolysis. In this context, the exploitation of sorption-enhancement may be of interest as it shifts the thermodynamic equilibrium, requiring lower synthesis pressure. This work delivers a comprehensive model of the sorption-enhanced methanol synthesis process, including both the reaction and the regeneration phase in the simulation. An economic assessment is performed to determine the levelized cost of methanol (LCMeOH) and compare it with that of a benchmark methanol plant. In every scenario analyzed, the configuration with the sorption-enhanced reactor shows better economic performance. Nevertheless, costs related to the production of hydrogen, representing 50.60% of capital expenditures and 76.40% of operational expenditures, make this solution not competitive compared to the traditional, fossil-based production process. As the electricity cost is dominant in the total process costs, the LCMeOH can be reduced by considering the self-production of electricity from photovoltaic panels, decreasing the LCMeOH by 28.71%, settling it at 1785 $ / t o n . With an increase in the operating hours. it could be possible to achieve an additional reduction by 29,54% of the levelized cost, to 1250 $ / t o n .

title: Synchronous separation and rejuvenation systems for reclaimed asphalt pavement based on a deconstruction-reconstruction strategy
abstract: High-value utilization of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) remains a critical challenge for sustainable road engineering. Traditional mechanical shearing and external rejuvenation techniques struggle to completely disrupt the strongly polar stacking structure of asphaltene micelles in aged asphalt, leading to macro-micro property mismatches and insufficient long-term durability. To overcome this bottleneck, this study proposes a synchronous separation and rejuvenation (SSR) system for RAP based on a deconstruction-reconstruction strategy. Utilizing Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) theory, a three-dimensional thermodynamic evaluation model was constructed to accurately screen a composite solvent system using trichloroethylene (TCE) as the separation phase and tire pyrolysis oil (TPO) as the rejuvenation phase. Supported by statistical analysis and thermodynamic data (apparent activation energy Ea = 43.41 kJ/mol), separation kinetics and multi-scale characterization indicate the SSR process is controlled by physicochemical desorption at the solid-liquid interface, optimizing the liquid-phase mass transfer environment. Chemical and rheological characterizations confirm that in-situ embedding of TPO during separation phase evaporation effectively blocks asphaltene secondary aggregation, disrupts the polar association network of polynuclear aromatic rings, and reduces large molecular size (LMS) components. This phase-boundary homogenization and colloidal reconstruction avoid physical phase separation risks inherent in traditional blending, providing an 82% fatigue life gain for SSR-rejuvenated asphalt compared to traditional high-shear rejuvenation (HSR) systems. This research proposes the robust SSR framework using a model composite solvent, providing theoretical support and broad applicability for screening green alternatives in high-quality RAP recycling.

title: From centralised planning to self-organisation in Industrial Symbiosis: A Simulation–Optimisation framework with incentive mechanisms
abstract: Industrial Symbiosis (IS) is a sub-field of Industrial Ecology that aims to increase resource efficiency through exchanges of waste materials within industries. IS network planning refers to the configuration of symbiotic exchanges which reveals potential economic, environmental, and social benefits of the network. While IS could be developed in both systematic-planning (top-down) and self-organising (bottom-up) approaches, existing studies predominantly focus on top-down approaches that prioritise global network optimisation. However, such centralised planning often overlooks the incentives and constraints faced by individual firms, resulting in conflicts between system-wide goals and localised interests, undermining the practical implementation of the proposed symbiotic configurations. To address the problem, this work proposes a simulation–optimisation framework which integrates dynamic self-organisation and incentive optimisation into IS network planning to increase the practical viability and stability of the desired symbiotic network. Specifically, the framework involves an Agent-Based Model that simulates dynamic network formation through decentralised firm-level decision-making, and a multi-objective optimisation based on evolutionary computation that targets system-level economic and environmental performances. Results demonstrate that a purely top-down approach may lead to economically unviable exchanges, while a purely bottom-up approach may fail to fully realise the network’s decarbonisation potential. In contrast, the proposed integrated framework enables near-optimal network design while ensuring its practical feasibility through incentive-based coordination. The proposed simulation–optimisation framework, hence, effectively aligns firm-level benefits with system-level objectives, facilitating practical implementation of IS systems with a novel incentive design mechanism.

title: Triple sustainability image for AI-enabled sustainable products
abstract: Multidimensional sustainability has become increasingly important in consumer decision-making. By leveraging AI technologies to generate benefits across the triple bottom line—people, planet, and profit—AI-enabled sustainable products, such as smart electric vehicles (SEVs), have emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional cars. However, existing research has largely emphasized environmental or green image, overlooking how multiple sustainability dimensions are combined into a product-level sustainability image. In the SEV context, product evaluation extends beyond environmental considerations alone to include social and economic considerations. Accordingly, we introduce triple sustainability image (TSI)—a novel product-level construct that captures consumers' overall sustainability image based on the combined evaluation of social, environmental, and economic dimensions. To conceptualize TSI, this research adopts a mixed-methods design. In Study 1, we conduct structured written interviews to explore U.S. consumers' sustainability perceptions of SEVs and identify the key attributes of TSI. In Study 2, we validate TSI within a two-stage SEV adoption process, using covariance-based structural equation modeling to test its effect on purchase intention. Theoretically, this research contributes to extant research by conceptualizing and validating TSI as a multidimensional construct. Empirically, the findings show that TSI significantly shapes consumers’ intention to purchase AI-enabled sustainable products, specifically SEVs. Furthermore, we identify key boundary conditions, showing that consumer age and sustainability preferences significantly moderate the decision-making process.

title: Environmental impact of the total chemical synthesis of barettin
abstract: The development of a sustainable bioeconomy depends on ensuring that novel bio-based products incur a smaller environmental footprint than the conventional counterparts they replace. Benchmarking the environmental burdens of emerging production routes against established synthetic baselines is critical to avoid "burden shifting". This study presents the first prospective attributional Life Cycle Assessment of the total chemical synthesis of barettin, a bioactive alkaloid originally isolated from the deep-sea marine sponge Geodia barretti - with promising pharmaceutical and antifouling applications. The assessment covers four main reaction steps and incorporates 32 separate inventories for intermediate molecules. Environmental performance was evaluated across sixteen impact categories and four process maturity scenarios: laboratory, scaled-up, scaled-up optimised, and a future decarbonisation scenario. The results indicate a climate change burden ranging from 1884 to 13,970 kg CO 2 equivalents per kg of barettin. Organic solvent use (specifically ethyl acetate, dichloromethane, and diethyl ether) was identified as the principal environmental hotspot, driving impacts across almost all categories. The findings demonstrate that transitioning from waste incineration to 95% solvent recycling is the most effective mitigation lever, achieving impact reductions ranging between 32% and 95% across all 16 impact categories assessed. This study establishes a critical environmental baseline against which future bio-based production routes, such as sponge cell culture or wild harvesting, can be rigorously benchmarked. It provides actionable evidence for researchers and decision-makers in the pharmaceutical and bioeconomy sectors to guide the sustainable scale-up of marine-derived metabolites.

title: A critical review of emerging technologies for direct lithium extraction from brines: Current industrial practices, challenges for sustainable process integration, and a view of current commercialization status
abstract: Lithium has seen a surge in global demand, primarily driven by the growing interest in electric vehicles as a sustainable transportation solution and by advancements in portable electronics. Traditional lithium production methods, i.e., mining and evaporitic processes, have inherent sustainability issues due to environmental risks and significant process lead times. In response, researchers have been actively investigating rapid and sustainable alternatives for extracting this critical element from brines using direct lithium extraction (DLE) processes. Many techniques have been proposed including adsorption, ion-exchange, precipitation, and solvent extraction, and recently, many of these processes have been demonstrated industrially and are approaching commercialization. This paper comprehensively reviews these DLE techniques and points out the ones that can be used synergistically for a complete lithium production treatment train. Lithium extraction technology is analyzed from a macroscopic perspective, filling a sufficient literary gap by addressing practical challenges and considerations that arise when translating scientific knowledge into real-world operations. This holistic examination provides a greater understanding of the intricacies and interconnectedness of unit operations within the extraction processes. Furthermore, technical and economic data are evaluated for ongoing industrial projects proving that commercialization is feasible. This work advances the knowledge of the ever-evolving lithium extraction process by identifying advantages, disadvantages, key challenges, and potential opportunities for the production of a sustainable lithium supply on an industrial and engineering scale.

title: Ultrafast and selective recovery of rare earths from aqueous streams using a P507-scaffolded dendritic nanosilica
abstract: The recovery of rare earth elements (REEs) is critical for supporting a circular economy, yet conventional industrial approaches, such as liquid-liquid extraction (LLE), are often unsustainable due to high solvent consumption and hazardous waste generation. Here, we report a sustainable alternative using a reusable solid-phase adsorbent to achieve rapid and selective REE recovery directly from complex industrial and environmental aqueous streams. The adsorbent is prepared by immobilizing the organophosphorus extractant P507 onto a dendritic fibrous nanosilica (DFNS) scaffold, producing a uniform, accessible layer that supports efficient metal-binding. The optimized material (DFNS-P_1.25) achieves high Dy3+ capacity (86.2 mg/g) and ultrafast uptake, achieving >95% removal within 5 min, across environmentally and industrially relevant concentrations, while exhibiting pronounced selectivity for heavy REEs over competing ions. This performance reflects the combination of rapid mass transport through open DFNS channels and the intrinsic chemisorption properties of P507. Compared to conventional LLE, this approach reduces solvent life cycle use and allows direct material reuse, offering a reusable solid-phase platform for critical metal recovery from industrial and environmental aqueous streams.

title: Numerical simulation of the stability and energy capture of a hybrid floating offshore wind and wave energy system with elliptical cylindrical wave energy converters
abstract: As floating offshore wind expands into deep-water sites, hybrid floating offshore wind and wave energy systems combining a floating wind turbine and wave energy converters are attractive because shared mooring infrastructure may lower the levelized cost of energy. Conventional axisymmetric floats, however, have limited directional sensitivity, which restricts the use of float orientation to regulate diffraction–radiation interference, drift respones, and mooring loads. This work introduces elliptical cylindrical floats as non-axisymmetric WEC floats and treats array orientation as a hydrodynamic design variable. Using an established fully coupled time-domain aero-hydro-servo-elastic and potential-flow hydrodynamic framework, this study evaluates a 5-MW braceless semi-submersible wind turbine integrated with three layouts: cylindrical floats (HFOWWS-1), radially oriented elliptical cylindrical floats (HFOWWS-2), and wave-aligned elliptical cylindrical floats (HFOWWS-3). The simulations indicate that integrating WECs modifies the local wave field, while the hydrodynamic anisotropy of elliptical cylindrical floats further affects platform responses and the distribution of idealized absorbed mechanical power. Under the considered rated actual operating conditions, HFOWWS-2 reduces platform pitch by 13.8% and decreases tower-base fatigue-equivalent loads by 15.4%, although increased drift and mooring tension are also observed. In contrast, HFOWWS-3 mitigates shielding through alignment with the wave direction and achieves a mean idealized absorbed mechanical power of 484 kW in a high-sea case. These findings provide numerical evidence that non-axisymmetric float geometry and array orientation can influence the coupled performance trade-offs of hybrid floating wind-wave systems.

title: A multi-strategy incorporated artificial bee colony algorithm for multi-AGV scheduling with downtime failure
abstract: This study aims to solve the multi-AGV scheduling problem with downtime failure (MAGVSPDF) in a matrix manufacturing workshop. Based on its characteristics, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is formulated, and a multi-strategy incorporated artificial bee colony (MSI-ABC) algorithm is proposed. In the initialization phase, a task-scale based parameter setting strategy is employed for parameter configuration, and a hybrid initialization strategy is designed to generate high-quality initial population. In the employed bee phase, four inter-vehicle based operators are developed to enhance the algorithm's exploration ability. In the onlooker bee phase, three key-vehicle based operators are developed to further enhance the algorithm's exploitation ability. In the scout bee phase, an elite-guided individual restart strategy is utilized to reactivate the population vitality. Additionally, to address downtime failure that occurs frequently during AGV task execution, a rescheduling scheme considering material recovery and task reassignment (MRTR) is investigated. Finally, MSI-ABC was compared with seven state-of-the-art algorithms on 100 real-world instances. Experimental results showed that MSI-ABC, along with QEDA, DFMO, and MRIG, achieved the best results on small-scale instances, while exhibiting significant advantages as the task size increased. Specifically, MSI-ABC obtained 71 best solutions from 80 medium and large scale instances, whereas the remaining 9 best solutions were achieved by three compared algorithms, respectively. In terms of the average relative percentage increase metric, MSI-ABC achieved 0.996%, an improvement of 45.5% compared to the result of the second-best performance algorithm QEDA with 1.828%. These results indicated the effectiveness of MSI-ABC in solving the MAGVSPDF.

title: Comparative life cycle assessment of stainless steel and single-use bioreactor units: A laboratory scale case study
abstract: In recent years, the biopharmaceutical industry has witnessed a surge in the adoption of Single-Use technologies; however, concerns about environmental sustainability have arisen due to the substantial amount of solid plastic waste generated by implementing such technologies. This study presents a comparative Life Cycle Assessment grounded in an industrially applied case study at a pharmaceutical facility in Italy, using primary operational data. The assessment evaluates two distinct laboratory scale bioreactor units reflecting the actual equipment configuration at the facility: a conventional stainless-steel bioreactor (SSB) and a single-use bioreactor (SUB). The assessment followed a cradle-to-grave approach over a 20-year operational horizon, normalising the results to the functional unit of 1 g of protein produced in a bioreactor. Five end-of-life scenarios for the single-use bioreactor were explored: landfill, incineration, incineration with energy recovery (IER), recycling and a combined recycling with IER scenario. Results across all 16 evaluated impact categories consistently show that the SSB exhibits a higher environmental burden than the SUB. In the Climate Change impact category, producing 1 g of protein in the SSB emitted 14.9 kg of CO 2 -eq., whereas the SUB emitted 8.7 kg of CO 2 -eq, assuming landfill as the base case disposal method. Electricity consumption was identified as the dominant environmental driver for both systems. The study also demonstrates that end-of-life management is not a marginal factor. The environmental profile of the SUB varied across disposal scenarios, with IER providing the most ecological benefits. These findings confirm that the disposal of plastic components emerges as a critical factor in assessing the environmental sustainability of single-use technologies.

title: Extrusion-shaped PEI@B/MC-M560 adsorbents for direct air capture: Balancing mechanical strength and CO2 adsorption efficiency
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) of CO2 represents a critical technology for achieving net-zero emissions, yet its implementation is challenged by adsorbents with high capacity and stability, mechanical robustness, and process compatibility under ultra-low CO2 concentrations. Shaping the powdery solid amine sorbents into mechanically robust and low-resistance structures is essential for their practical deployment in DAC systems. In this work, extrusion-shaped PEI@B/MC-M560 adsorbents were developed using a composite bentonite/methyl-cellulose binder system to enhance structural integrity while preserving CO2 adsorption performance. The optimized B/MC-M560 pellet retained over 90% of the mesoporosity of raw M560 powder, supported high PEI loadings (45–50 wt%), and exhibited uniform amine dispersion. Under pure CO2 testing conditions, the synthesized PEI@2.5%B/MC-M560 adsorbent achieved an intrinsic CO2 uptake of 138.8 mg/g and demonstrated excellent stability, maintaining >98% capacity after 50 cycles. For practical DAC-relevant performance (400 ppm CO2), the material reached an uptake of approximately 60 mg/g. Pelletization significantly reduced pressure drop by more than an order of magnitude, creating well-defined interparticle channels that improve hydrodynamic behavior and lower air-handling energy consumption in DAC operation. Breakthrough experiments further showed that the extrusion-shaped adsorbents maintained tunable yet stable performance under different pellet diameters, humidity levels, and temperatures, with moderate humidity enhancing CO2 uptake via PEI plasticization and bicarbonate formation. Overall, this study establishes a scalable extrusion-shaping strategy that simultaneously improves mechanical strength, CO2 capture efficiency, and flow-performance. The structure-performance insights obtained provide practical guidance for designing next-generation solid amine sorbents for industrial-scale DAC applications.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution of climatic drought and its impacts on crop production and phenology in China
abstract: Climatic drought increasingly affects agricultural systems in China, posing risks to crop production and development. This study examines the spatiotemporal evolution of drought across China and its impacts on crop production and the phenology of major grain crops. It uses a physically consistent, spatially resolved Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) framework, with potential evapotranspiration (PET) estimated by the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method based on ERA5-Land data. The resulting PET agrees closely with pan evaporation, and SPEI correlates positively with root zone soil moisture, confirming its robust drought representation. SPEI-3 analysis reveals widespread drying during 2000–2020, with declining trends in 68.53% of pixels and lower national mean values after October 2005. In the Northeast China Plain, maize, wheat, and rice all showed predominantly positive crop production–SPEI correlations, whereas rice exhibited a more spatially dispersed and heterogeneous response than maize and wheat in other regions, especially in southern China. Phenological responses were stage-dependent, with reproductive stage changes being dominated by shortening and generally showing greater spatial coherence than vegetative-stage changes; these effects intensified under more severe drought, particularly in South China. These findings demonstrate that intensifying drought has altered both crop production and crop development processes and provide guidance for adaptive management of water and crop planning.

title: Carbon emission reduction benefits analysis of recycled aggregate-based sandwich permeable bricks based on sponge effect enhancement design
abstract: This study develops recycled aggregate-based sandwich permeable bricks, which adopt a three-layer functional design consisting of high-strength permeable surface layer, ceramsite core layer and recycled aggregate base layer. Through structural design, performance experiments, and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), the sponge effect enhancement mechanism and carbon emission reduction potential of the bricks were systematically explored. The results show that while ensuring engineering performance with a 28-day flexural strength of 3.12 MPa, compared with traditional permeable bricks, the recycled aggregate-based sandwich permeable brick exhibits significant performance improvements, which demonstrates a balanced integration of infiltration, storage, retention, and drainage functions and mechanical stability. LCA quantification indicates that with the functional unit defined as 1 m2 of permeable brick over a 20-year service life, the total carbon emission reduction reaches 10.13 kgCO2. A sensitivity analysis varying the ceramsite factor by ±20% yields a net reduction ranging from 1.97 to 18.29 kgCO2, confirming a positive carbon reduction potential. Functional emission reduction driven by the sponge effect is the primary contributor, and the carbon emissions from ceramsite core layer production are effectively compensated by the functional emission reduction. Scenario analysis based on Hangzhou's road network planning, under low, medium, and high replacement rates, the total carbon emission reductions over 20 years are 0.16, 0.75, and 1.92 million tons respectively, with the annual average emission reduction accounting for 0.01%-0.13% of Hangzhou's total carbon emissions in 2022. This study realizes the high-value utilization of solid wastes such as recycled aggregates, provides a technical path for material innovation and large-scale application in the low-carbonization of municipal pavement engineering, and supports the coordinated development of Sponge Cities and low-carbon cities.

title: Recycling retired grid-scale lithium iron phosphate energy storage batteries in China: Carbon benefits, economic viability and scenario pathways
abstract: Grid-scale lithium iron phosphate (LFP) energy storage is expanding rapidly in China, yet end-of-life management of retired batteries remains insufficiently understood, particularly for centralized recycling pathways. This study evaluates the carbon mitigation potential and economic feasibility of recycling retired grid-scale LFP energy storage batteries using an integrated framework that combines retirement forecasting, material flow estimation, life-cycle mitigation accounting, and policy–technology–market scenario analysis. In the regional case of Shandong and its surrounding collection radius, the baseline effective recovery rate is estimated at 7.6%, and recoverable volumes rise rapidly after 2030. Using a literature-informed, route-specific avoided-emission factor, annual net carbon mitigation under the baseline case is estimated at 0.288 Mt CO2-eq in 2030 and 0.975 Mt CO2-eq in 2035, with sensitivity bounds ranging from 0 to 1.658 Mt CO2-eq in 2035. Economic assessment indicates that the project is only conditionally feasible, with a baseline internal rate of return of approximately 16.1%. Profitability remains highly unstable. The dynamic payback period is relatively long (about 11.3 years), and project performance is highly sensitive to recycling scale, market prices, and policy support. These findings indicate that recycling retired grid-scale LFP batteries has growing environmental value but has not yet become a robust near-term investment, highlighting the need for phased infrastructure deployment, technology upgrading, and targeted policy support.

title: Toward valorization of waste polyethylene terephthalate via iron-assisted pyrolysis: Product distribution and the critical role of iron valence
abstract: The catalytic pyrolysis of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) presents a promising route for upcycling plastic waste into valuable chemicals and fuels. This study systematically evaluated the effects of three stable iron species with distinct valence states (Fe, Fe2O3, and Fe3O4) on PET pyrolysis. Using thermogravimetry analysis and in-situ X-ray diffraction, the decomposition behavior of PET and phase evolution of the iron additives were monitored. Complementary batch pyrolysis experiments and detailed product identification revealed Fe2O3 as the suitable additive, owing to its oxidative properties and accessible Lewis acidity that efficiently drove decarboxylation and aromatization. Subsequently, based on combined online and offline product characterization, a decomposition mechanism for PET under Fe2O3-assisted pyrolysis was proposed, involving random cleavage at ester linkages followed by reactions including decarboxylation, dehydroxylation, and rearrangement. Furthermore, a machine learning approach was applied to model the yields of gas, oil, and solid residue, as well as the distribution of four key products (benzoic acid, biphenyl, CO, and H2), exhibiting strong predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.95 for all test sets), and pyrolysis temperature was identified as the most significant feature. Additionally, cyclic experiments demonstrated the satisfactory regenerability and structural stability of Fe2O3, highlighting its potential for long-term reuse. This work not only advances the fundamental understanding of metal-oxide-catalyzed PET pyrolysis but also offers insights for designing efficient, scalable plastic valorization processes.

title: Soil stabilization using in-situ polymer cross-linking driven by freeze-thaw cycles
abstract: Frequent freeze-thaw cycles (FTC) are generally considered a major cause of soil structure deterioration in cold regions. In this study, however, FTC are used constructively to promote in-situ cross-linking of a polymer within the soil, forming a stable polymer network. The mechanical performance of the polymer-modified soil under the FTC was evaluated through compressive strength and rheological tests. The interaction mechanisms between the polymer and soil particles were investigated using computed tomography, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and zeta potential tests. The results showed that after 12 FTC, the compressive strength of the modified soil (2.78% polymer content) increased by 2.10-fold (from 126.73 kPa to 393.05 kPa), and the maximum rheological shear stress increased by 6.02-fold. Under the FTC, the porosity, fractal dimension, and proportion of connected pores of the modified soil decreased, and the pore and throat radius distribution shifted toward smaller sizes. These changes were interpreted as FTC-driven cross-linking of polymer chains through hydrogen bonding and esterification, which bound soil particles together and might restrained ice crystal expansion and water migration. This work offered a practical approach for potentially sustainable soil stabilization in cold regions via turning freeze-thaw action into a beneficial engineering process.

title: Research and Pilot-Scale Application of Hydro-Jet Oscillation Enhanced Carbon Capture Technology
abstract: To address the bottleneck of efficient and low-cost CO2 capture from blast furnace flue gas, this study systematically investigates HOP gas-liquid mass transfer intensification technology. Via high-speed camera observation, laboratory experiments and Meishan hundred-cubic-meter-scale pilot, the dual-orifice jet's five-stage breakup and mass transfer mechanism are revealed, and operating parameter effects on η and KGa are clarified. The bag-breakup mode generated 323 droplets, with an average particle size of 500 ∼ 800 μm. This significantly increased the contact area between the liquid and gas phases. The oscillation frequency range of the droplets was 100 ∼ 1430 Hz, which enhanced the rate of interface renewal. 28 % DETA +2 % PZ performs best (ηmax = 90.1 %, KGamax = 2.89 kmol kPa−1·m−3·s−1). An empirical formula for 28 % DETA +2 % PZ and CO2 mass transfer was proposed. The 4.2 m-tall pilot device has a carbon capture efficiency ranging 84.18 % ∼97.48 %, and its footprint is reduced by 60 % ∼80 %. This compact design significantly cuts down manufacturing, civil engineering and space occupation costs while ensuring operational stability, providing crucial technical support and engineering references for CO2 capture in high-carbon emission industries.

title: Phenolic compounds extracted by ultrasound-assisted SUPRAS from Solanum nigrum L. fruits – Evolutions and XOD inhibitions
abstract: The current study investigates extractions of phenolic compounds from Solanum nigrum L. fruits by high-intensity ultrasound (HIU) and supramolecular solvents (SUPRAS). The HIU-SUPRAS strategy enhances phenolic yield from 738.93 ± 15.33 to 1184.33 ± 41.77 μg/mL. Moreover, those crude phenolic extracts (CPEs) exhibit stronger antioxidant activity compared with aqueous extracts (DPPH IC50: 4.34 ± 0.33 μg/mL vs. 14.43 ± 0.49 μg/mL). It is also found that CPEs possess strong inhibitory ability against xanthine oxidase (XOD). Molecular docking reveals 5 key residues around the XOD molybdopyrimidine center (Phe 914, Phe 1009, Glu 802, Arg 880, Thr 1010) contributing to ligand binding via π-π interactions and hydrogen bonding. Comprehensive studies demonstrate 21 phenolic compounds exhibiting stronger binding affinity with XOD than xanthine, of which 10 phenolic compounds are even stronger than the clinical medicine febuxostat. Notably, the XOD inhibitory effects of CPEs are increased during storage, which is attributed to compound evolutions rather than oxidations or degradations induced by HIU or SUPRAS. Metabolomics identifies 5 and 3 phenolic compounds responsible for the increased XOD inhibition activity during storage in SUPRAS extracts with and without HIU, respectively. In vitro experiments validate the results of molecular docking and suggest that up-regulations of (−)-liquiritigenin and sideroxylin during storage account for enhanced XOD inhibitions of CPEs. HIU-assisted SUPRAS is demonstrated as an efficient and green processing for functional food additives and pharmaceutical ingredients. Additionally, the quantitative and functional evolutions of phenolic compounds during storage provide valuable insights for the utilizations of Solanum nigrum L. fruits and other berries.

title: A novel design using vapor compression and blended amine for techno-economic improvement in shipboard CO2 capture processes
abstract: Shipboard CO2 capture (SCC) processes face major challenges in achieving energy-efficient and cost-effective designs and identifying their optimal operating conditions. This study proposes a novel SCC design and determines its optimal operating parameters and blended amine ratio to significantly improve techno-economic performance. Specifically, we integrate CO2 vapor compression (CVC) and lean vapor compression (LVC) with a Monoethanolamine/Piperazine (MP) blended solvent to develop an efficient CVC-LVC-MP design, which significantly reduces energy consumption and capture costs. To overcome the computational burden associated with cyclic steady-state simulations, a deep neural network (DNN) model is developed to accurately and efficiently approximate the CVC-LVC-MP simulator. Based on the DNN model, optimization problems are formulated to minimize energy consumption, while ensuring at least 90% and 95% CO2 capture rates using available onboard energy sources. Under optimal conditions, the CVC-LVC-MP design demonstrates a 15.48–46.7% reduction in heating energy and a 9.26–70.09% reduction in capture cost compared to previously reported SCC designs. Furthermore, a comprehensive performance analysis is conducted to provide operational guidelines and to demonstrate the design’s feasibility of achieving high CO2 capture rates using available onboard energy sources. These results provide valuable insights for the design and operation of the SCC process.

title: Surfactant-accelerated alkaline hydrolysis of waste PET for upcycling into MIL-53Fe catalysts toward enhanced catalytic ozonation
abstract: The rapid accumulation of plastic waste has become a major environmental challenge, driving growing interest in upcycling strategies that transform waste polymers into high-value products within a circular economy framework. Among waste plastics, polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most abundant and widely discarded materials, yet its sustainable valorization remains constrained by the energy-intensive and chemically demanding nature of conventional recycling processes. In this study, a surfactant-accelerated alkaline hydrolysis strategy using dodecyl dimethyl benzyl ammonium chloride (DDBAC, known as surfactant-1227) is developed to enable efficient PET depolymerization under mild conditions, achieving a terephthalic acid (TPA) yield of 99.6% with a purity of 99%. The recovered TPA is directly reutilized as an organic linker for the synthesis of MIL-53Fe via a solvothermal process, yielding an ozonation catalyst denoted as TS-MIL-53Fe. The TS-MIL-53Fe/O3 system exhibits markedly enhanced catalytic ozonation performance toward the degradation of acid orange 7 (AO-7), with an observed pseudo-first-order rate constant (kobs) of 1.11 min−1, 1.8 times higher than that of the conventional MIL-53Fe/O3 system. Mechanistic investigations indicate that improved electron transfer characteristics of TS-MIL-53Fe promote ozone activation at Fe sites, leading to significantly increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, particularly singlet oxygen (1O2). The catalyst also demonstrates robust stability and broad applicability for the removal of diverse organic contaminants and the treatment of complex industrial wastewater. This work presents a low-carbon and resource-efficient approach for converting waste PET into high-performance water treatment catalysts, simultaneously contributing to plastic waste valorization and advanced wastewater remediation.

title: Reusing 55-year-old lightweight ceramisites concrete in belite-rich cement clinker production: feasibility, performance and LCA assessment
abstract: The cement industry currently faces dual challenges regarding high carbon emissions and the disposal of massive construction demolished wastes. Although the reuse of recycled concrete has been widely investigated, the recycling of real service-aged concrete, particularly lightweight aggregate concrete containing ceramisites aggregates, remains scarce. The behavior of such aged LWAC powders during clinker phase reconstruction is still insufficiently understood. This study confirms the feasibility of reusing a 55-year-old lightweight ceramisites concrete (LWAC) associated with carbide slag (CS) in eco-friendly belite-rich cement clinker fabrication. The effects of recycled powder proportions and calcination temperatures (1350 °C and 1450 °C) on mineral phase evolution and microstructure were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM-EDS), and free calcium oxide (f-CaO) analysis. The optimal mixture consisting of 50% LWAC, 46% CS, and 4% recycled mortar, achieved the desired clinker minerals formation at a calcination temperature of 1450 °C. The prepared clinker contained desired contents of C2S and C3S, with favorable 7-day compressive strength development. This research provides a viable theoretical and practical basis for the zero-waste resource utilization of industrial solid wastes and construction wastes. By replacing limestone with no carbonate calcium sources, this technology can theoretically reduce process related CO2 emissions by approximately 500 kg per ton of clinker, offering a scalable technical pathway for the low carbon cement with demolishing aged construction.

title: Rapid urbanization reshapes the spatial-seasonal alignment of green environments: Unveiling the provision-persistence gap for residents across 295 Chinese cities
abstract: The actual benefits of urban greenspace depend on the alignment between spatial availability and seasonal persistence. However, current static assessments often fail to capture this critical temporal dimension, leading to a biased understanding of actual greenspace provision and persistence during rapid urbanization. To address this, we developed an integrated “spatial-seasonal” framework and the Greenspace Provision–Persistence Index (GPPI). Using 30-m Landsat time-series imagery and population data, we quantified population-weighted greenspace exposure (GSE) and greenspace duration exposure (GDE) for new and old urban areas across 295 Chinese cities from 2000 to 2020. Results indicate that while new urban areas initially showed higher spatial exposure, they experienced widespread declines (mean GSE dropped from 0.53 to 0.42). In contrast, old urban areas demonstrated a provision-driven improvement, maintaining a consistent advantage in duration exposure (186.7 days vs. 181.1 days). Notably, the GPPI revealed divergent evolutionary dynamics: although new urban areas retained higher mean values (0.65 vs. 0.58), 81% of them faced a widening provision–persistence misalignment, contrasting with the coordinated improvement observed in 78% of old urban areas. Variance partitioning analysis (VPA) further identified distinct drivers in new and old urban areas, with growing season length primarily buffering the declining trend in new urban areas (62.7% contribution), whereas physical provision served as the decisive determinant driving the coordinated improvement in old ones (65.3%). Highlighting the influence of urbanization patterns on realized greenspace exposure, we suggest differentiated governance. Future planning must prioritize the strict preservation and climate-appropriate evergreen configuration of green infrastructure in new urban areas, while focusing on stock optimization in old urban areas to support resilient, equitable environments.

title: Reinforcement learning control of pilot-scale solvent recovery for battery manufacturing: Surrogate-assisted optimization with techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment
abstract: As electric-vehicle battery manufacturing scales up, its environmental footprint grows, primarily driven by the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from using N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone in electrode fabrication. Establishing an efficient closed-loop recycling process for this solvent is therefore essential to advance a circular economy and align with emerging eco-design principles. To systematically minimize the GHG emissions of battery manufacturing, this study presents a surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the solvent recycling process, validated with data from a pilot-scale plant. The framework integrates a first-principles dynamic model developed in Aspen Plus Dynamics, a physics-constrained neural ordinary differential equation surrogate model, and an RL agent to jointly optimize reflux-ratio trajectories and batch termination under a stringent purity requirement of 99.99 wt%. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment modules translate control policies into quantitative production cost and GHG outcomes. As a result, the recycling process achieves GHG emissions of 0.222 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram of recovered solvent, compared to 8.06 kilograms for virgin production. Furthermore, the learned RL policies reduce production cost by up to 3.8% and decrease GHG emissions by up to 57%, relative to the worst-case fixed reflux ratio scenario. This pilot-validated framework provides a scalable pathway toward sustainable solvent-recovery practice in battery manufacturing, demonstrating that RL-based control can deliver both operational feasibility and environmental benefits.

title: Modeling the knowledge-innovation-sustainability nexus: Human factors and nonlinear pathways to social sustainability
abstract: Manufacturers face increasing pressure to innovate, but also to care for their workers and communities. But the human-related capabilities that support both are not well understood as an integrated system. This study develops and tests a partial least square structural equation model (PLS-SEM) based on the knowledge-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities that consider innovative organizational culture (IOCU), knowledge management and organizational learning (KMOL), and talent and human capital management (THCM) as hierarchically interdependent antecedents of social sustainability (SOSU). Data from 332 respondents in six industrial sectors support the six proposed relationships (p < 0.001). The main finding is the systematic prevalence of indirect over direct effects. The mediated effect of IOCU to SOSU was 107.7% higher than its direct effect (indirect β = 0.378 vs. direct β = 0.182). Effective knowledge management was not observed without a well-established innovative culture (P(KMOL+|IOCU−) = 0.000). Knowledge management was the strongest single predictor of high social sustainability outcomes (P(SOSU+|KMOL+) = 0.640), and non-linear modeling showed that all six relationships generated bounded returns. The return on talent management with innovative culture reached the maximum at an intermediate-to-high level of implementation (β = 0.56) and decreased thereafter. The results extend the theory of dynamic capabilities to the organizational outcome of social sustainability and provide conditional probabilities as operational diagnostic tools for managers in the manufacturing sector.

title: The impact of transportation infrastructure on carbon emissions: Nonlinear threshold, regional linkage and causal relationship analysis
abstract: Understanding how transportation infrastructure influences carbon emissions is essential for supporting China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. This study integrates interpretable machine learning, spatial analysis, and causal inference methods to examine the relationship between transportation infrastructure and carbon emissions in China from 2006 to 2019. Specifically, it quantifies the contributions of different infrastructure types, identifies nonlinear relationships and threshold effects, and examines regional linkages and conditional causal effects. Results show that Class I highways are the dominant positive contributor to carbon emissions among transportation infrastructure types, whereas waterways and airports help mitigate carbon emissions in certain regions. Transportation infrastructure exhibits nonlinear relationships and threshold effects with carbon emissions. The carbon-emission centroid shifted northwestward, while regional disparities gradually narrowed. Spatiotemporal correlation effects of different infrastructure on carbon emissions exhibit heterogeneity across regions. Class I highways have the strongest positive conditional causal effect in the Middle Yangtze River Region, whereas they exert a suppressing effect in the Southern Coastal Region. Railway mileage has a positive effect on carbon emissions in the Middle Yellow River and Northern Coastal Regions, but a negative effect in the Eastern and Southern Coastal Regions. Waterway mileage generally helps reduce carbon emissions, but positive conditional causal effects are observed in regions with well-developed waterway systems, such as the Middle Yangtze River and Eastern Coastal Regions. Airports exhibit weaker conditional causal effects on carbon emissions than other infrastructure types. These findings provide evidence for differentiated transportation infrastructure planning and region-specific carbon emission reduction strategies.

title: The three pillars of decarbonizing the EU's core economies: Sustainable industry, rule of law, and environmental policy
abstract: This study examines the challenge of reconciling industrial growth with ecological sustainability in the European Union's five largest economies: France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands (EU-5). Despite ambitious climate policies and substantial financial commitments under frameworks such as the European Green Deal, deep decarbonization remains uncertain. The study focuses on three interrelated dimensions that are central to the decarbonization trajectory of the EU-5: sustainable industrial performance, which reflects the qualitative transformation of industry; the rule of law, which captures the credibility of governance and policy implementation; and environmental policy stringency, which reflects regulatory ambition. Integrating the Green Kaldorian Framework and the Porter Hypothesis, the analysis examines how sustainable industrial performance, rule of law, and environmental policy stringency are associated with carbon dioxide emissions from 2000 to 2024, while controlling for energy transition and economic growth. Using a second-generation panel model, the findings provide new evidence on the structural, institutional, and regulatory relationships associated with decarbonization in the EU-5. The study offers policy-relevant insights for policymakers seeking to align industrial competitiveness, governance quality, and regulatory design with climate objectives. In addition, the findings have implications for SDGs 7, 8, 9, and 13.

title: Stratification enhances yet self-limits carbon sequestration through microbial necromass accumulation at reservoir sediment–water interfaces
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) includes a substantial recalcitrant fraction that constitutes a major form of long-term carbon storage in sediments, yet the processes controlling its stabilization at reservoir sediment–water interfaces (SWIs) under climate-driven stratification remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated temperate stratified reservoirs using high-resolution mass spectrometry and multi-omics to resolve how stratification reshapes DOM transformation at SWIs. During summer stratification, recalcitrant dissolved organic matter (RDOM) concentration and total dissolved organic carbon (TDOC) increased by 50.7% and 37.8%, respectively. Stratification enhanced nitrogen mineralization and suppressed ammonium oxidation at SWIs, promoting amino sugar biosynthesis and microbial necromass accumulation associated with DOM recalcitrance. The summer plateau in RDOM accumulation further suggests a necromass-associated substrate-supply constraint that self-limits continued carbon sequestration under prolonged stratification. Short-term hydrodynamic disturbances from natural events or human-induced intermittent mixing temporarily relieve this constraint and sustain DOM transformation. These findings uncover a climate-sensitive, internally regulated feedback that governs carbon sequestration efficiency at reservoir SWIs, with implications for predicting inland-water carbon storage under a warming climate.

title: Impact of sustainable product development tools through intermediaries: A multi-actor study of pathways and conditions
abstract: This study provides an empirically grounded, multi-actor investigation of how industrial impact of sustainable product development (SPD) tools forms along the pathway from academic tool development, through intermediary adoption and adaptation, to client application, and under what conditions impact unfolds over time. A multi-actor, multiple-case design, combining an embedded consultancy case with cross-sector client cases was employed, using interviews and follow-up questionnaires to explore how consultants adopt and adapt academically developed SPD tools and how clients experience and assess their application and impact. The analysis shows that adoption by consultants is enabled when tools are proven useable and time-effective in early phases, provide clear visualizations and credible traceability, and can be customized to sector language and practices. Across client cases, the application of SPD tools was perceived primarily as an enabler for innovation and competitiveness, together with increased ability to meet customer needs and improved reputation. The findings indicate a multi-layered and time-phased pattern of impact where impacts were reported most consistently at organizational level, including mindset change, cross-functional dialogue, and prioritization routines, whereas more technical and measurable outcomes emerged more selectively, with time delay, and depended on enabling conditions beyond tool use, e.g., governance and leadership, supplier capability and openness, policy and market signals. System-level change is discussed as a potential downstream pathway when SPD tool use is paired with deliberate work on enabling conditions. The study synthesizes these insights into seven multi-actor recommendations for researchers, consultants, and firms on designing, translating, and embedding SPD tools to maximize impact.

title: A field-scale model using an integrated framework for evaluating food and water dynamics in agrivoltaics in three-dimensional space
abstract: Growing pressure on food production, water resources, and renewable energy deployment has increased the need for integrated land-use strategies. Agrivoltaic systems (AVS), which co-locate solar photovoltaic (PV) installations with agricultural production, have emerged as a promising solution to improve land-use efficiency and climate resilience. However, existing modelling approaches are limited in their ability to represent the three-dimensional interactions governing food and water dynamics within AVS environments. This study developed a field-scale model (AVS-FW) using an integrated framework to represent the key factors affecting food and water dynamics in AVS in three-dimensional space. The AVS-FW used the framework to integrate the AVS-Microclimate model (simulating three-dimensional microclimatic conditions under solar panels), R-SWMS model (simulating three-dimensional soil condition and water transport), and Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) crop growth module (simulating plant growth). The AVS-FW model was demonstrated on a site in Colorado, USA, through scenario-based simulations comparing conditions with and without solar PV panels. The average actual evapotranspiration, water stored at the root depth, and biomass of lettuce with solar panels compared to without solar panels changed by −2.43% to −26.28%, 0.80% to 10.63%, and −3.17% to −34.63%, respectively. The temporal patterns of cumulative fluxes across soil domain boundaries were similar for cases with/without solar panels, but their magnitudes varied; and these were also found for total water volume in soil domain. The framework of the AVS-FW can assist decision-makers in evaluating the impacts of varied layouts (azimuth angles, inclinations, spacing, heights) and dimensions (lengths/widths) of solar PV panels on food and water dynamics in AVS.

title: Beyond Kaolinite: Unlocking the performance of diverse calcined clays as sustainable cement replacement
abstract: “Greening” cement with supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) is considered as an effective strategy to mitigate CO 2 emissions from the cement industry, with calcined clays (CCs) emerging as promising alternatives. However, the performance of such low-carbon cements highly depends on the nature of the clay utilized. Existing studies have mainly focused on kaolinitic clays which are relatively scarce in Europe, where illitic, smectitic, and mixed-layered clays predominate. The recent industrial implementation of low-carbon calcined clay cements in Europe, such as Futurecem™, further highlights the growing practical relevance of non-kaolinitic CCs. In this study, locally available non-kaolinitic calcined smectitic, illitic, and common (mix-layered) clays from Germany were investigated in comparison with a commercial metakaolin. Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) was replaced by 30 wt% or 50 wt% with CCs, their rheological behavior, flow behavior, workability retention, mechanical properties, environmental impact, and cost efficiency of the OPC/CC blends were systematically evaluated. The results demonstrate that calcined illitic and smectitic clays significantly increased water demand, impaired PCE efficiency and slump retention, even in the presence of high-range water-reducing admixtures. In contrast, the calcined common clay (CMC) exhibited a rheological behavior comparable to OPC, substantially better than the other non-kaolinitic clays. Although metakaolin exhibited superior strength development, CMC demonstrated the best balance between workability, environmental benefit, and cost effectiveness. This work highlights the critical role of specific surface area and mineralogy of CCs used in calcined clay cement blends, and demonstrates the potential of non-kaolinitic clays as viable low-carbon SCMs for sustainable cement formulations.

title: The multilayered toxic effects of cadmium on earthworms are driven by both cadmium content and soil properties: The potential mediating role of microbiota
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination poses substantial risks to soil fauna, yet the combined roles of soil properties and microbial communities in mediating Cd toxicity remain poorly understood. Here, molecular, physiological, and microbiological endpoints were integrated to evaluate multilayered Cd effects on Eisenia fetida across three contrasting soils. Bioavailability assessments showed that soil properties strongly regulated Cd mobility and earthworm accumulation, outperforming total Cd as predictors of toxicity. Cd exposure induced oxidative stress, gene dysregulation, and growth inhibition, with marked soil-dependent variation. Bulk soil microbiota (BSM) and Earthworm gut microbiota (EGM) exhibited distinct but coordinated responses: BSM experienced community disruption, diversity loss, and an increased relative abundance of taxa associated with mobile genetic elements, whereas EGM exhibited structural resilience and an enrichment of putative stress-tolerance traits. Variance decomposition revealed that Cd exposure and soil properties accounted for an average of 53.8% and 46.2% of the explained variance in toxicity-related endpoints, respectively. Structural equation modeling suggested potential indirect pathways linking soil properties and Cd exposure to earthworm growth mediated by microbial communities (standardized effects: −0.68 and −0.17). Overall, Cd toxicity arises from coupled interactions among contamination levels, soil physicochemical traits, and microbial resilience, emphasizing the need to incorporate microbial processes into soil ecotoxicological risk assessments.

title: Biostimulant-enriched anaerobic digestate as a sustainable nitrogen fertiliser for enhancing wheat growth, drought resilience and soil health
abstract: Climate change is driving farmers to adopt sustainable, eco-friendly fertilisers that enhance crop resilience. Anaerobic digestate, a nutrient-rich byproduct of biogas production, offers a promising biofertiliser option. However, its agronomic performance and interaction with biostimulants under water stress remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated the effect of substituting inorganic nitrogen (N) fertilisers with anaerobic digestate, with or without biostimulants (plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria and humic substances), on the growth and drought resilience of common wheat ( Triticum aestivum ). A long-term pot experiment comprising sixteen treatments was conducted, supplying 100 kg N/ha through varying ratios of digestate and diammonium phosphate/urea. Biostimulants were applied at standard agronomic rates– Bacillus spp. (20 L/ha), humic acid (10 L/ha), and fulvic acid (500 g/ha). A drought condition was simulated during stem elongation. Plant biometrics, soil physicochemical properties, and post-harvest microbial communities were analysed. Wheat growth was comparable across treatments, indicating the digestate's potential to replace inorganic fertilisers. Under drought conditions, treatments receiving ≥85% digestate N combined with biostimulants showed improved soil moisture retention, thereby enhancing drought tolerance. The application of digestate (40–85% N) containing biostimulants, enriched soil nutrients, optimised N and potassium uptake, and reduced phytotoxicity. Specifically, digestate-based fertilisation (100% N) with biostimulant supplementation reduced potentially pathogenic Clostridia while promoting beneficial taxa, including drought-tolerant Bacillus licheniformis and Alphaproteobacteria associated with nutrient cycling. Thus, integrating anaerobic digestate with biostimulants showed enhanced wheat drought resilience and improved soil health compared to inorganic fertilisers, supporting the sustainable recycling of waste into effective biofertilisers.

title: Novel synthesis of a sulfur-magnesium compound fertilizer from magnesium-based flue gas desulfurization byproducts
abstract: Magnesium oxide (MgO)-based wet flue gas desulfurization (FGD) technology is recognized for its high SO2-removal efficiency, simple operation, and low energy demand, yet the required post-oxidation / purification and separation steps add considerable complexity and cost. This study introduces an innovative and simplified approach that transforms unoxidized magnesium sulfite (MgSO3) gypsum into a compound fertilizer. Direct co-granulation of MgSO3 with (NH4)2HPO4 or KCl resulted in SO2 losses from the fertilizer (a 30-min cumulative loss of 2.5% or 0.6% for (NH4)2HPO4 or KCl, respectively). However, using layered granulation technology allowed production of a compound fertilizer (CF) with negligible losses (SO2 cumulative loss rate <0.01%). Upon addition to soil, sulfite in the fertilizer was transformed to sulfate with a half-time of approximately 20 d. In a pot trial with radish plants, MgSO3-CF significantly increased radish biomass by 16.7% compared to MgSO4-CF at an added S rate of 6.7 mg kg−1, while also inducing greater enhancements in leaf SPAD (12.6% and 12.1%), sucrose content (25.1% and 21.7%), and leaf sulfur content (15.1% and 19.3%) at added S rates of 6.7 and 13.3 mg kg−1. However, at a high addition rate (26.7 mg S kg−1), the biomass yield was 43.1% lower for MgSO3-CF than for MgSO4-CF, indicating sulfite toxicity may occur at elevated rates. By demonstrating the direct laboratory-scale conversion of sulfite-rich Mg-gypsum into a sulfur–magnesium compound fertilizer, this work offers a new route to reduce the post-treatment burden associated with MgO-based wet FGD byproducts while helping to address S and Mg deficiencies in acidic agricultural soils. Although further validation using real industrial residues is still needed, these findings provide an important basis for developing cleaner and more circular fertilizer-production systems.

title: The role of economic resilience in charting a path forward: Do supply chain pressures, energy crises, and oil market volatility threaten global sustainability?
abstract: The global sustainability milieu is progressively delicate and under siege, as the world faces interrelated systemic shocks and economic disruptions. Escalating market dynamics and uncertainty owing to global crises continue to erode the path to a sustainable and resilient future, which need to be immediately assessed and addressed. Thus, this study examines how global sustainability uncertainty (SUI) is determined by global economic conditions (ECI), energy uncertainty (EUI), supply chain pressures (SCP), real commodity prices (CFP), oil supply shocks (OLS), and oil inventory demand shocks (OID) using monthly data from November 2002 to December 2023. The results from the Quantile-on-Quantile Regression (QQR) and Wavelet Quantile Regression (WQR) models reveal that the EUI, ECI, and SCP depict a positive and significant impact on the SUI across the short, medium, and long run. Conversely, the influence of CFP is positive in the short and medium term but turns negative in the long run. The OLS reveals a negative influence in the short and medium term, whereas its effect becomes positive in the long run. Finally, OID exerts a negative influence in the short and long run, but a positive impact during the medium term on SUI. Similarly, the findings of the Quantile-on-Quantile Granger Causality (QQGC) approach confirm that all covariates significantly drive causality toward SUI across different quantiles. Based on these insights, the research recommends targeted policy interventions meant at shielding sustainability from numerous economic shocks, thereby fostering a cleaner and greener future for the world.

title: Measuring public acceptance resilience toward waste-to-energy incineration facilities in China: Scale development and validation based on the 4R resilience framework
abstract: Cleaner production infrastructures, such as waste-to-energy (WTE) incineration facilities, face persistent social sustainability challenges arising from volatility in public acceptance, which can disrupt construction progress, operational stability, and long-term system performance. Research largely treats public acceptance as a static attitudinal outcome, providing limited insight into how acceptance responds to disturbances and recovers over time. From a cleaner production and sustainability governance perspective, understanding the resilience of public acceptance is therefore critical for maintaining the reliable operation of environmentally beneficial but socially contested infrastructure systems. This study introduces the concept of public acceptance resilience, defined as the public's capacity to maintain or restore acceptance attitudes in the face of external disturbances. Drawing on the 4R resilience framework, a measurement scale is developed and validated through a four-stage empirical design. Study 1 generated an initial item pool through a systematic literature review and a modified Delphi process involving interdisciplinary experts. Studies 2 (n = 237) and 3 (n = 245) used exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses to establish a robust 12-item scale comprising two dimensions: stability and recoverability. Study 4 (n = 231) further confirmed the scale's nomological validity by examining its theoretical relationships with perceived risk and public trust. The resulting scale provides a reliable and operational tool for assessing the social resilience of cleaner production facilities. By enabling early detection of vulnerability and recovery capacity in public acceptance, the scale supports a shift from reactive conflict management to proactive social risk governance, contributing to the sustained operation of cleaner production and sustainable infrastructure systems.

title: Economic and environmental trade-offs in circular food systems: Toward cleaner agricultural production and responsible consumption
abstract: The study reviews the trade-offs in the economic and environmental dimensions of circular food systems in response to growing sustainability demands. This study proposes an Integrated Sustainability Assessment paradigm for agri-food supply chains that merges the Triple Bottom Line approach with Circular Economy concepts. The paradigm considers circularity as a separate analytical aspect alongside economic, environmental, and social performance, facilitating a more structured assessment of sustainability trade-offs and operational strategies within agri-food systems. Based on an extensive review of academic literature and industry practices from 2012 to 2024, sixteen Sustainability Performance Metrics were established to measure important sustainability aspects in agri-food supply chains. The research used the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process to rank these indicators according to their relative importance within the proposed evaluation framework. These indicators encompass economic, environmental, social, and circular aspects of sustainability. The results suggest that the economic dimension is the most influential (0.40), followed by the environmental (0.34), circular (0.16), and social (0.10) dimensions. The Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution was used to assess the effectiveness of the dairy supply chain, incorporating uncertainty and expert judgment into the sustainability indicators. Circular strategies such as reverse logistics, resource regeneration, and green logistics encourage cleaner farming and responsible consumption by reducing food waste and building confidence in sustainable food systems. The Integrated Sustainability Assessment model significantly supports sustainability evaluation, strategic planning, and alignment with global goals, such as SDG 12 on responsible production and consumption.

title: A novel, spatially-explicit framework to simulate ecosystem service potential for guiding ecological restoration: A Beijing case study
abstract: In highly urbanized areas, rapid expansion of construction land often undermines ecological restoration benefits. Traditional ecological restoration frameworks struggle to meet the growing demand for ecosystem services (ES) during socio-economic development. Using Beijing as a case study, this research integrates socio-economic-natural complex ecosystem theory, spatial homogeneity theory, and restoration limitation hypothesis to propose a framework for simulating ecosystem service potential. This framework provides broader spatial options and quantitative reference targets for ecological restoration. The results showed that ecosystem service value (ESV) in Beijing has generally declined over the past 20 years, though it has increased annually by 1.46% in the last five years. Topographical factors significantly influence the spatial differentiation of ecosystem services across the city. When considering comprehensive ecological benefit restoration, the potential ESV for Beijing is estimated at 311821.57 million CNY, representing a 10.25% potential growth over current levels, with a recoverable area of 11446.20 km2. The value enhancement potential of individual ecosystem services ranges from 2.28% to 25.00%, with corresponding recoverable areas ranging from 981.69 km2 to 12693.01 km2. Forests and cropland play a significant role in restoring ecosystem service value potential. The mountain forests within the ecological conservation development zones and the wetlands across the city remain key areas for restoring ecosystem service value potential. This study enhances existing spatial identification approaches and provides quantitative reference targets for ecological restoration based on ecosystem service potential, supporting sustainable urban ecological planning.

title: Beyond externalities: Evaluating the localized environmental benefits of large-scale green energy projects under environmental federalism
abstract: Under the framework of environmental federalism, local governments are often hesitant to invest in large-scale green energy projects due to potential spillover effects. Utilizing monthly multi-source remote sensing data from sources such as EDGAR and NASA, this paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of the localized environmental benefits of China’s Photovoltaic Poverty Alleviation Program. The study finds that the PPAP significantly reduced atmospheric pollutant emissions in the residential sector. Specifically, the implementation of the PPAP led to an average monthly reduction of 1.1%–1.3% in CO2, SO2, PM2.5, and NOx emissions, with every 10% increase in policy intensity yielding an additional 0.04% reduction. Mechanism analysis confirms that these localized benefits primarily originate from the terminal substitution of household energy consumption rather than a transformation of the local power generation structure. Dynamic and heterogeneity analyses further corroborate these research findings. Furthermore, we observe a U-shaped seasonal trajectory in the emission reductions of SO2 and PM2.5 and confirm that this U-shaped characteristic is driven by heating rigidity. Finally, we identify a resource misallocation within the PPAP, suggesting that social welfare objectives may have taken precedence over efficiency maximization. Our research confirms the internalization of environmental benefits from green energy projects, providing critical evidence to incentivize local government participation in the energy transition.

title: Decarbonizing Pakistan's cement sector: Multi-scope emissions inventory, drivers, and mitigation pathways
abstract: This study quantifies greenhouse gas emissions from Pakistan's cement sector over a 32-year historical period (1991–2022) and projects emissions to 2050 under 12 scenario combinations, providing the first comprehensive multi-scope inventory for this major industrial emitter. Emissions were calculated across Scopes 1, 2, and 3 following IPCC Tier 2 methodology with country-specific parameters. Total emissions increased six-fold from 7.7 Mt CO2 in 1991 to 46.2 Mt CO2 in 2022, with Scope 1 (process and fuel combustion) accounting for 89% of the total. Carbon intensity declined 17% from 1.05 to 0.87 tCO2/t cement, yet remains 6% above the global average of 0.82 tCO2/t cement when comparing all scopes. Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition revealed that economic activity drove 76.5% of emission growth, while efficiency improvements offset only 5.6%. Scenario projections showed no emission peak under medium or high demand trajectories; the Integrated pathway achieved 22% mitigation relative to Baseline by 2050, though absolute emissions continued rising. Monte Carlo analysis (n = 10,000) identified demand growth rate as the dominant uncertainty driver, explaining 94% of projection variance. Among mitigation levers, clinker-ratio reduction and thermal-efficiency improvements were the dominant supply-side abatement channels under a component-wise attribution. The findings demonstrate that achieving emission stabilization would require combining aggressive supply-side measures with demand management, as efficiency improvements alone cannot offset continued production growth.

title: Collaborative emission reduction: Spillover effects of corporate carbon information disclosure across the supply chain
abstract: Carbon information disclosure (CID), to a certain extent, signals enterprises' commitment to emission reduction. Using data from China's A-share listed companies and their supply chain partners, we empirically examine the impacts of CID on firms' own carbon emission and its supply chain spillover effects. Our findings indicate that corporate CID significantly reduces own carbon emission by fostering green technological innovation and improving energy efficiency, which is more pronounced in developed regions and for firms facing high financing constraints.
