Moreover, CID generates spillover reduction effects across the entire supply chain. The impact on upstream suppliers is particularly strong, mainly achieved through signaling effects and pressure transmission, while the effect on downstream customers operates via knowledge spillover and demonstration effects. These findings undergo various robustness tests. Furthermore, we also find that core firm size, industry, the listing status of upstream and downstream, the tightness of inter-firm transaction relationships, and relative carbon emission levels all influence the spillover effects. This study offers comprehensive empirical evidences for facilitating chain-wide carbon reduction and green supply chain management.

title: Rethinking rural small hydropower transition in China through socio-ecological archetypes: Mechanism mapping and scenario simulation
abstract: Small hydropower (SHP) is internationally recognized as a clean and renewable energy source and has made substantial contributions to local economic and social development. However, community disputes and environmental conflicts resulting from disorderly development have posed major challenges to its sustainable transition, indicating that the small hydropower green transition (SHPGT) is no longer merely a matter of technological upgrading. As a major country in SHP development, China has advocated a SHPGT mode centered on ecological protection, intelligent efficiency enhancement, and collaborative governance. Reframing the SHPGT in China as a context-dependent socio-ecological transition process, archetype-based differentiated governance can help avoid one-size-fits-all management and mismatched interventions, while responding to the development needs of the SHP sector. Therefore, grounded in socio-ecological systems (SES) theory, this study applies an “identification-deconstruction-simulation” framework that integrates qualitative archetype analysis (AA) with quantitative methods, including an improved Pythagorean Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory-Interpretive Structural Modeling (PF-DEMATEL-ISM) method and nonlinear fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM). The results show that: (1) China's SHPGT can be classified into three archetypes, namely the SHP-community collaborative co-development mode, the government-led smart operation optimization mode, and the incentive-driven resource revitalization mode. (2) The representative SHP plants corresponding to these three archetypes are Zhushuqiao, Panshitou, and Mantaicheng, respectively, and their key driving factors are mainly distributed across the resource base, actors, and governance system. (3) Scenario simulations further indicate that the optimal intervention portfolios for the three representative stations are community participation and functional expansion, government coordination combined with smart operation and maintenance and refined management, and government support together with reward and subsidy incentives, respectively. Overall, the SHPGT should shift from compliance with unified standards toward archetype-based differentiated governance. Differentiated portfolios of interventions should be implemented according to the SES conditions of different SHP plants, thereby achieving collaborative symbiosis and the comprehensive benefits of transition.

title: Analyzing the interface fusion and diffusion mechanism between new and aged bitumen during secondary regeneration based on molecular dynamics
abstract: Regenerated bitumen is a common sustainable pavement material. Given that this material inevitably ages again after service, a second regeneration (secondary regeneration) becomes necessary. However, for different regenerators, the fusion and diffusion mechanisms at the new-aged bitumen interface during secondary regeneration remain largely unknown which greatly limits the application of secondary regeneration technology. To address this bottleneck, this study established a molecular dynamics model of secondary regenerated bitumen that accounts for aging history, analyzing the effects of five regenerators from different sources on the fusion and diffusion performance of molecules at the new-aged bitumen interface during secondary regeneration. Results show that primary regeneration is synergistically dominated by the regenerator and light components, whereas secondary regeneration relies primarily on the regenerator alone. Even after aging, the degree of regeneration compatibility (Drc) between bitumen and regenerators remains higher than that with unaged light components. The Drc value of manure oil (MO) in secondary regenerated bitumen increases by 7.1% compared with primary regeneration. Moreover, the small molecular fragments generated from oxidative cleavage of MO maintain diffusion potential, causing its diffusion coefficient to increase by 56% after aging rather than decrease. These advantages make MO the most suitable regenerator for secondary regeneration of RAP. Collectively, evaluating secondary rejuvenation should prioritize stability of regenerator molecular under multiple aging cycles over initial molecular fusion efficiency. These provide theoretical and technical support for mechanistic research, regenerator selection, and engineering applications of secondary regenerated bitumen, which intends to ensure long-term recycling and material usage.

title: Valorization of raw starch from potato processing waste via enzymatic hydrolysis using novel Bacillus clarus NITTBP1 amylase under optimal strategy
abstract: Potato processing waste (PPW) from the food processing industry contributes to an environmental threat, and valorizing these starch-rich wastes contributes significantly to generating value-added products. This research explored the utilization of PPW for the conversion of raw starch to reducing sugar through novel enzyme using an optimal strategy in comparison with commercial starch (CS). The compositional and physicochemical parameters were analyzed for PPW. Bacillus clarus amylase was employed as a partially purified amylase (PPA) for hydrolysis. Statistical models provided the optimized enzymatic hydrolysis conditions as 46 °C, 0.7 U/mL, 95 min, and 59 °C, 0.9 U/mL, 109 min, for CS and PPW, with the R2 of 0.99, respectively. Experimentally validated maximum hydrolysis percentage from the optimized levels of the models were 98.853 ± 0.03% and 96.152 ± 0.05%, respectively. This optimal and sustainable enzymatic conversion of raw PPW starch into enriched products supports the industrial circular bioeconomy.

title: Deciphering the multivariable interactions of MOFs in heavy metal adsorption via explainable machine learning for sustainable and resource-efficient adsorbent development
abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) in aquatic environments seriously threaten ecosystems and human health. Although metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have shown great potential for HMs removal, adsorption performance is governed by complex interactions between material characteristics and operating conditions. However, while existing studies largely emphasize performance prediction, systematic data-driven frameworks for decoding these interactions and guiding adsorbent design remain limited. This study constructed a comprehensive dataset comprising 4289 samples, incorporating MOF characteristics, experimental conditions, and adsorption data for Cr(VI), Pb(II), Cd(II), and As(V). Large-scale data mining was performed using explainable machine learning. Key findings include: the solution volume and shaker speed must be systematically investigated as critical parameters to enable a clear mechanistic discussion of the adsorption material and reliable performance comparison. The strong synergistic or antagonistic relationships between MOF components and experimental conditions were systematically explained as decisive for adsorption behaviors, highlighting the necessity of integrated parameter optimization for efficient adsorbent development and process design. The initial concentration of pollutants and reaction time showed significant interactive effects with other factors. In contrast, 95% of feature importance results consistently indicate that organic ligands exert a stronger influence on adsorption capacity, while coordination metals more readily affect removal rate. Finally, eight representative MOF compositions were identified for different environmental scenarios. This work establishes an explainable, data-driven decision-support framework that transforms adsorption data into actionable design knowledge, supporting resource-efficient material development and sustainable environmental remediation.

title: How effective are China's green electricity certificate? A perspective from carbon lock-in
abstract: The green electricity certificate (GEC) in China has been widely acknowledged for its positive role in advancing high-quality development in the renewable energy sector over the nearly 10 years since its implementation. However, it remains to be seen whether the GEC can overcome the carbon lock-in (CLI) trap that is hindering China's decarbonization process. Using panel data from 30 provinces of China covering the period 2013 to 2022, we apply a continuous difference-in-differences (DID) model to investigate the influence of the GEC on CLI, its potential mechanisms of action, and the heterogeneity observed systematically. Empirical results indicate that the GEC can effectively mitigate CLI, a conclusion that has passed a number of robustness tests. Mechanism analysis shows that the indirect influence of the GEC on CLI is primarily achieved through optimizing the power generation structure and promoting technological innovations in renewable energy. Furthermore, the carbon unlocking effect of the GEC is more pronounced in eastern and western region, whereas it produces the opposite effect in the northeastern region. The GEC is also more effective in promoting unlocking at the industrial and behavioral dimensions. This study expands the theoretical horizons of GEC policy evaluation and provides empirical evidence and policy guidance for the optimization of China's GEC.

title: Life cycle and economic assessment of inverted p-i-n perovskite solar cells
abstract: Photovoltaic technologies hold significant potential for meeting the world's growing energy demands. Among emerging alternatives to conventional silicon-based solar cells, perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted increasing attention for their promising efficiency and cost-effectiveness. This study aims to evaluate the sustainability performance of an inverted PSC, addressing a critical gap in the integrated assessment of this emerging technology. A cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted, combined with energetic and economic analyses, evaluating energy payback time (EPBT), energy return on investment (EROI), and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). A sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the influence of key operational parameters. The results show a carbon footprint of 0.20 kg CO 2 eq./kWh and a cumulative energy demand of 4.88 MJ/kWh. The system exhibits an EPBT of 0.53 years and an EROI of 9.50, while the LCOE is estimated at 0.29 €/kWh, for a PSC production cost at 0.67 €/cm 2 . The sensitivity analysis indicates that the PCE and degradation rates are the main drivers of energetic performance, whereas the LCOE remains relatively stable. Additionally, EPBT and EROI are strongly influenced by solar irradiance and local climatic conditions. These findings highlight that, despite the relatively low manufacturing impacts, improvements in PCE, operational lifetime, and degradation rates are essential for enhancing the overall sustainability and economic viability of PSCs. The main contribution of this work lies in providing a multidimensional (environmental, energetic, and economic) baseline assessment of inverted PSCs, offering novel insights into the key parameters that will determine their future commercial competitiveness.

title: Deconstructing the carbon spillover effects of foreign direct investment: Upstream-downstream production linkages perspective
abstract: Foreign direct investment (FDI) plays a crucial role in economic growth, yet its environmental implications through production linkages remain underexplored. This paper develops a novel indicator that distinguishes FDI in the upstream (FDI_U) and downstream (FDI_D). Using global panel data covering 41 industries in 77 economies from 2000 to 2020, we examine their effects on the carbon emissions of domestic-owned enterprises. The results show that FDI_U reduces carbon emissions by 0.021%, whereas FDI_D increases emissions by 0.2649%. Mechanism analysis indicates that FDI_U improves firms’ global value chains position and forward participation, while FDI_D inhibits their backward participation. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the emission reduction effect of FDI_U is concentrated in developed and high institutional quality economies, as well as energy-intensive sectors, whereas FDI_D is consistently associated with higher emissions. In addition, both FDI_U and FDI_D generate economic benefits by increasing the value added of domestic-owned enterprises, improve economic-environmental performance by reducing carbon intensity, and promote environmental catch-up by narrowing the carbon intensity gap with foreign-owned enterprises. These findings offer policy insights for aligning FDI attraction with emission reduction.

title: Adaptation analysis of microalgae cultivation in coal mining Sunken water surface
abstract: Coal-mining subsidence water bodies are widely distributed in post-mining areas, but their potential for Chlorella cultivation and biomass recovery remains unclear. Unlike conventional wastewater-based microalgal systems, these water bodies are open or semi-enclosed semi-natural systems characterized by heterogeneous water quality, hydrological connectivity, diverse land-use patterns, and native algal communities. This study developed a screening-level framework integrating water-quality-based Alga Fit (AF) ranking, microscopy-based background community screening, laboratory Chlorella cultivation, biomass characterization, life-cycle assessment, and economic scenario analysis. Twenty sampling sites in Huainan and Huaibei, China, were investigated, covering wetland parks, aquaculture waters, floating photovoltaic waters, river-connected waters, and natural subsidence waters. Huaibei sites showed higher relative suitability than Huainan sites, with mean AF0 values of 0.462 and 0.229, respectively, and AF rankings remained stable in sensitivity analyses. Under controlled cultivation conditions, most cultures grew rapidly during the first 9 days and then tended to stabilize. The tested Huaibei floating photovoltaic water sample showed the strongest Chlorella growth response. FTIR and supplementary crude lipid extraction indicated lipid-related functional groups and crude extractable lipid contents of 16.85%–26.76%, supporting preliminary biomass utilization potential but not confirming biodiesel yield. Photosynthetic CO2 uptake was separately estimated from biomass increase, whereas LCA results showed that freeze-drying dominated energy consumption and cost. These results indicate that selected coal-mining subsidence water bodies may support Chlorella cultivation, but field validation, pollutant removal assessment, low-energy biomass processing, and ecological risk control are still required.

title: Life-cycle environmental and cost implications of longer-life road infrastructure designs: A case study of California
abstract: Most state road agencies in the U.S. design rigid pavements for a 40-year design life based on specific performance criteria for fatigue cracking, longitudinal smoothness, and sometimes other distresses. Would there be reductions in life-cycle environmental impacts and economic gains if the design lives were 60 or even 100 years? To answer this question, a comprehensive analysis was conducted on three representative case studies, each designed for 40-, 60-, and 100-year lives, with data applicable to California. The pavement structural design showed that extending the design life from 40 to 60 years necessitated only a modest 15 mm (0.05 feet) increase in concrete thickness, corresponding to an approximate 5% increase in initial construction costs. The life-cycle cost analysis indicated a 3% reduction in life-cycle agency costs, while infrastructure life-cycle global warming potential was reduced by around 24% without discounting and around 5% using time-adjusted warming potential. Fewer life cycle construction closures for maintenance, rehabilitation, and reconstruction activities also reduced road user delay costs. In contrast, increasing the design life to 100 years provided diminishing returns. The minimal additional savings are attributed to the relatively high annual discount rate (3.2%), which drastically reduces the present value of far-future savings. Consequently, a 60-year design life emerges as the most balanced and beneficial alternative, offering significant sustainability gains and cost savings for a minimal upfront investment.

title: Scaling sustainable protein production: Integrating farmer knowledge with AI to optimize black soldier fly larvae cultivation
abstract: The transition toward a circular bio-economy requires scalable technologies for organic waste upcycling and sustainable protein production. Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming has emerged as a promising approach for waste-to-resource conversion; however, its industrial expansion is constrained by biological variability and the lack of robust optimization tools suitable for decentralized production systems. This study presents a farmer-partnered Decision Support System (DSS) that applies machine learning to optimize larval biomass yield and nutritional quality, including protein and fat content, using real-world data collected across multiple farms. The proposed DSS follows a data-centric approach that integrates practitioner domain expertise with longitudinal experimental data while accounting for the biological variability inherent in organic side-streams. We evaluate cross-farm generalization compared to personalized modeling strategies and analyze how shared datasets can improve prediction reliability in heterogeneous farming environments. To support practical adoption, the system incorporates explainability and interactive visualizations that enable farmers to better understand how diet composition influences larval growth and nutrient outcomes. The results demonstrate that integrating data science with farmer knowledge can improve process consistency and resource efficiency in BSF production systems, contributing to reduced reliance on marine-derived feed inputs and supporting progress toward UN Sustainable Development Goals related to responsible production and environmental sustainability.

title: A comparative techno-economic and life cycle assessment of energy-from-waste technology integrated with carbon capture and storage
abstract: Rising urbanisation and global population growth are projected to nearly double municipal solid waste (MSW) generation by 2050. Energy-from-waste (EfW) technologies recover energy from mixed waste streams, generating electricity and heat. However, for every tonne of MSW incinerated, 0.7–1.7 tonnes of CO 2 is emitted. Integrating carbon capture and storage (CCS) into EfW (EfW + CCS) presents a promising pathway to mitigate these emissions yet remains constrained by high costs and decreased energy efficiency. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of EfW + CCS, using a combined techno-economic and life cycle assessments approach. A thermodynamic steady-state model was developed in Aspen Plus to evaluate mass and energy balances for both standalone EfW and EfW + CCS. Results show that an EfW + CCS system with 250 ktpa capacity and 80% capture rate incurs a 35% energy penalty and increases capital (CAPEX) and operating expenditure (OPEX) both by 30%. Additionally, the system results in a positive net present value, 2.7% return on investment and a levelised cost of electricity of £163/MWh, but extended payback period from 4.5 to 8.3 years compared to standalone EfW. The life cycle assessment results showed a 33% reduction in global warming potential (GWP), though monoethanolamine production and carbon capture infrastructure increased other impacts. This study suggests that the current carbon price of £49.4/t CO 2 is insufficient to incentivise CCS deployment, with a required subsidy estimated at £178/t CO 2 captured. Furthermore, ammonia use for NO x removal strongly influenced GWP and OPEX, with 60% NO x removal resulting in a reduction of 41% in GWP and increasing OPEX by 19% compared to standalone EfW.

title: A calcium-assisted route for humic-carbon enrichment in manure–straw biochar via mild hydrothermal pretreatment and low-temperature pyrolysis
abstract: Livestock manure and crop straw are abundant biowastes. Conventional pyrolysis often produces stable biochars with limited humic characteristics, whereas natural humification is slow and low-yield. Here, chicken manure and corn stover were converted through a stepwise hydrothermal–pyrolytic route to improve the recovery of extractable humic fractions in biochar. Stepwise screening identified mild hydrothermal pretreatment coupled with 300 °C pyrolysis as the baseline process window, and Ca(OH)2 as the most effective additive. Relative to the additive-free control, Ca(OH)2 increased the feedstock-normalised humic substance yield from 60.77 to 107.86 mg C g−1 and shifted the humic pool towards a humic-acid-enriched composition, with the humic acid to humic substances ratio increasing from 0.10 to 0.70. EEM–PARAFAC showed that the contribution of the most humified component increased from 14.16% to 30.83%, accompanied by the disappearance of the shortest-wavelength component. Complementary functional-group and microstructural evidence showed additive-dependent rebalancing of oxygenated functionalities and Ca-enriched surface domains, with surface Ca increasing from 1.8 to 4.1 wt%. Non-targeted UHPLC–Orbitrap MS further indicated a redistributed and more signal-concentrated detectable ionisable subpool under Ca-assisted conditions, with the number of retained molecular features decreasing from 361 to 263. Collectively, these findings suggest a Ca-associated shift in the extractable humic pool toward HA enrichment, likely involving both alkaline transformation and mineral–organic association under mild hydrothermal–pyrolytic conditions, and highlight the potential of this route for humic-fraction enrichment from waste biomass.

title: Transition to a circular economy in pearl aquaculture: Environmental impacts, consumer preferences, and willingness to pay
abstract: The transition to a circular economy in pearl aquaculture is hindered by uncertainties regarding both environmental performance and consumer acceptance of sustainability premiums in this luxury sector, yet these two dimensions have rarely been examined together. This creates a critical gap in understanding whether environmentally beneficial recycling practices can also gain support from consumers. This study integrates Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) with a Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE) to estimate consumers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for pearl products associated with recycling-based reductions in the environmental impacts of discarded pearl aquaculture cages. The LCA results show that the Full Recycling scenario substantially reduces environmental impacts compared with the Partial and No Recycling scenarios, primarily through resource substitution effects. Based on the DCE administered to 600 Japanese consumers, the analysis estimated a median premium of JPY 1,438 per pearl among experienced consumers for upgrading from No Recycling to Full Recycling. Incremental premiums were estimated at JPY 494 for upgrading from No Recycling to Partial Recycling and JPY 944 for upgrading from Partial Recycling to Full Recycling. Latent class analysis further showed that demand for recycling-based sustainability was concentrated among Eco-conscious Balancers, whereas higher-income Aesthetic Seekers placed greater weight on conventional luxury attributes such as luster and size. Together, the results quantify the environmental benefits of recycling-based circular strategies in pearl aquaculture and consumers’ stated WTP for these sustainability improvements, while economic feasibility still depends on additional cost-side evidence and credible sustainability communication.

title: Closing the global loop: A battery deposit mechanism for cross-border EV battery recycling
abstract: European Union member states have collectively invested tens of billions of euros in electric vehicle (EV) purchase incentives since 2016 to advance their circular economy ambitions, yet as these incentivised vehicles age and depreciate, they enter global second-hand markets and are exported to developing countries lacking recycling infrastructure – breaking the circular loop green policy was designed to close. Once an EV is exported beyond EU borders, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations are extinguished and producers are released from recycling cost obligations rather than triggering end-of-life management. Drawing on 21 elite semi-structured interviews with government regulators, battery recyclers, environmental advocacy organisations, and original equipment manufacturers across developed and developing countries, this study examines whether the Battery Deposit Concept can function as a viable circular economy policy instrument to address this structural gap. Findings reveal strong multi-stakeholder convergence on the feasibility of a split-incentive mechanism in which a portion of the EV purchase incentive is withheld as a refundable deposit, redeemable upon certified battery recycling anywhere in the world. The mechanism is self-enforcing, unilaterally implementable by EU governments, and enabled by the EU Battery Passport operational from 2027. Three contributions are made: among the first empirical analyses of a cross-border deposit-refund mechanism for complex, high-value products; identification of the EPR guarantee system as the institutional mechanism that financially enables circular economy leakage; and demonstration that the EU Battery Regulation 2023 creates enabling architecture for market-based cross-border circular economy policy instruments.

title: Data-driven techno-economic optimization of an integrated industrial-scale methanol plant with carbon capture: A market-driven profitability analysis
abstract: This study presents an industrially validated and verified analysis of a large-scale methanol plant integrated with carbon capture, comparing Iranian and global markets. Operational cases were evaluated using four objectives: maximizing variable income (both with and without a carbon tax), maximizing methanol production, and maximizing carbon efficiency. The first finding is the demonstration that the choice of objective function fundamentally determines economic outcomes: maximizing methanol production (a target often assumed to align with profitability) reduces profit by 13.51% (Iran) and 18.53% (global) compared to variable income maximization, while maximizing carbon efficiency (another objective function usually assumed to align with profitability) reduces profit by 11.95% (Iran) and 11.04% (global). The second finding is the identification of purge-gas recycle management as a Zero-CAPEX operational lever that enhances profitability without additional capital investment, provided a suitable objective function is selected. A surrogate-model-assisted genetic-algorithm framework, employing Box–Behnken design of experiments and both response surface methodology and Gaussian process models, was developed to overcome convergence challenges, high computational cost associated with direct optimization and enable systematic exploration of operational decision spaces. The integrated plant is approximately 1.1 times more profitable under Iranian market conditions than under global market conditions. Under current regulations (i.e., as long as reducing carbon emissions to a specified level is not mandatory and carbon taxes are low), paying carbon taxes can be more economical than increasing the carbon capture rate.

title: Solid-phase sulfidation-volatilization for detoxification and recovery of arsenic and zinc from zinc arsenate waste
abstract: Arsenic-containing zinc residues from non-ferrous smelting, particularly zinc arsenate, are hazardous and difficult to treat because conventional methods commonly suffer from incomplete arsenic removal, secondary pollution, and limited resource recovery. In this study, a solid-phase sulfidation-volatilization process was developed using coking sulfur paste (CSP), an industrial by-product, as a low-cost bifunctional reagent for reduction and sulfidation. Under oxygen-free conditions, zinc arsenate was selectively converted into volatile As2O3 and stable ZnS. Under the optimized conditions of 700 °C, S/As = 11, and 90 min, arsenic removal reached 99.73%, and the residue consisted predominantly of high-purity ZnS. The resulting As2O3-S8 condensate was further separated under reduced pressure (5 Pa) by temperature-gradient condensation in a multi-zone tube furnace with a heating zone at 200 °C, yielding high-purity As2O3 (99.87%) and S8 (99.26%). This process avoids hazardous reagents and arsenic-containing wastewater, reduces global warming potential by 65-70% relative to carbon-based roasting, and enables closed-loop sulfur circulation. By converting two hazardous wastes into three value-added products, this work provides a clean, efficient, and economically attractive route for arsenic-bearing waste treatment and resource recovery.

title: Balancing food security and sustainability: An analysis of agricultural yields and emissions in India
abstract: India has undergone a rapid agricultural transformation, resulting in increased foodgrain output and food security for the nation. However, agricultural productivity gains have increasingly been accompanied by rising agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. This paper examines the short and long-run association between rainfall, foodgrain output, and agricultural emissions. It has utilized the annual time-series data from 1971 to 2022. The ARDL bounds testing approach and FMOLS are employed for estimation, whereas the Granger causality test is used to analyze the direction of causality between the variables. Rainfall emerges as a significant determinant of agricultural output. Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions show a statistically significant positive association with foodgrain yield: a rise of 1 per cent increase in N2O emissions entails a 1.71% increase in foodgrain yield in the long run, reflecting the productivity effects of fertilizer use, whereas carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions exhibit a statistically significant negative relationship with agricultural productivity: as 1% increase in agri-CO2 emissions can cause decrease in foodgrain production by 0.29%. Methane emissions display a negative but statistically insignificant relationship with yield. The results highlight a sustainability trade-off within India's productivity-driven, input-intensive agricultural growth model, which has been accompanied by rising emission levels. The findings underscore the importance of climate-resilient strategies—such as improved fertilizer management and crop diversification—to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while supporting sustainable food security and providing empirical evidence on the productivity–emissions trade-off in Indian agriculture.

title: Microwave hydrodiffusion-gravity as a cleaner extraction route for Abies holophylla needle oil: process greenness, monoterpene enrichment and value-added bioactivity
abstract: Forest conifer biomass is a promising renewable source of high-value volatile products, but its industrial utilization requires extraction routes that reduce process burden while preserving product quality. In this study, microwave hydrodiffusion-gravity (MHG) was developed as a cleaner production-oriented strategy for extracting essential oil (EO) from fresh Abies holophylla needles. The MHG process was optimized by face-centered central composite design and kinetic modeling, then benchmarked against microwave-assisted hydrodistillation (MHD), solvent-free microwave extraction (SFME), and conventional hydrodistillation (HD) in terms of extraction yield, energy and carbon performance, process greenness, volatile composition, and value-added bioactivity. Under the optimized conditions (385 W, 35 min), MHG produced the highest EO yield (16.55 ± 0.83 mL/kg DW). Compared with HD, MHD, and SFME, MHG technology reduces energy consumption and CO2 emissions. Consistent with this, the AGREEprep analysis showed that MHG achieved the highest green score (0.62), reflecting its advantages in solvent-free operation, lower process load, reduced wastewater generation, and higher energy efficiency. GC-MS analysis further indicated that MHG favored enrichment of monoterpene hydrocarbons, particularly α-pinene and camphene. In parallel, the EO from MHG exhibited the strongest in vitro acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory activity among the reference extraction methods. Overall, the results demonstrate that MHG can simultaneously improve resource-use efficiency, reduce preparation burden, and enhance product functionality, providing a practical, cleaner extraction option for the high-value utilization of A. holophylla needles.

title: Circular economy strategies in metal production: A comparative environmental and economic analysis of primary lead and secondary lead smelting in China
abstract: As an industrial-critical metal, Pb (lead) faces rising demand, limited reserves and potential environmental risks, necessitating sustainable resource management through secondary production. This is the first study to develop a systematic life cycle assessment (LCA) framework for evaluating the environmental impacts and economic performance of primary Pb (PPb) and secondary Pb (SPb) production systems at the corporate level in China. The results show that SPb production generates only 0.51 t CO2 eq./t, representing an 72.18% reduction compared to PPb production (1.84 t CO2 eq./t). The crude Pb smelting stage constitutes the primary source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in both Pb production systems, with electricity consumption also playing a significant role. A key distinction lies in material consumption: Pb concentrate dominates in the PPb system (79.45%), while chemical reagents account for a significant share in the SPb system (11.7%). Compared to PPb production, the SPb production system offers varying degrees of advantages in terms of other environmental impact categories, e.g. resource consumption, ecosystem and human health impact. PPb shows slightly higher profitability than SPb, but SPb's higher carbon profitability (0.47 USD/kg CO2 eq.) indicates greater sustainability. Under an ideal scenario, the Pb production industry is projected to achieve a 60.92% GHG reduction rate by 2050.

title: Contributions of ecological engineering to sustainable development goals on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Ecological engineering is a key nature-based approach to ecosystem restoration and sustainable development, yet its contributions to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remain difficult to quantify because effects may vary across engineering types, regions and time. We integrated multi-source spatial datasets with propensity score matching to quantify the contributions of four ecological engineering types to Zero Hunger (SDG2), Clean Water and Sanitation (SDG6), Climate Action (SDG13) and Life on Land (SDG15) across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau from 2000 to 2020. Ecological engineering generally promoted SDG progress, with an average contribution of 1.70% relative to matched non-engineering areas. Mean effects were positive for SDG15 (+3.47%), SDG6 (+2.75%) and SDG13 (+0.76%), but slightly negative for SDG2 (−0.18%), with all SDG responses showing marked variation among engineering types. These effects were strongly heterogeneous across engineering types and space, with positive and negative contribution areas often coexisting within the same engineering category. Temporal cumulative effects also differed among SDGs. SDG13 showed persistent but moderate positive effects across engineering types, while SDG15 exhibited strong cumulative responses that varied among engineering types, including strengthening under grassland-related engineering and weakening under some protection-oriented interventions. Precipitation was the dominant natural driver of ecological engineering effectiveness, while accessibility-related factors, including distance to county centres and roads, further shaped spatial differences in SDG contributions. These findings suggest that ecological engineering in high-altitude, fragile regions should move beyond uniform restoration targets toward spatially differentiated, adaptive governance that jointly considers ecological suitability, accessibility, long-term maintenance and SDG trade-offs.

title: Towards an extended product value model for circular products
abstract: The adoption of circular products remains limited despite strong consumer support for sustainability. A key explanation is the persistent gap between consumers’ stated intentions and their actual purchasing behaviour. Existing research in the circular economy has largely focused on improving the tangible characteristics of products, while paying less attention to how consumers perceive value. This conceptual article argues that the intention–behaviour gap is partly rooted in how circular products are experienced and valued. It examines the role of intangible value dimensions, particularly trust, authenticity, and symbolic meaning, in shaping consumer decisions. To do this, it develops a synthesis of three complementary frameworks: the Golden Circle from strategy and leadership, the multidimensional framework of product value and authenticity, and the marketing mix. The resulting extended product value model shows how organisational purpose, operational practices, and product attributes interact to shape perceived value. The analysis suggests that circular products are more likely to be adopted when they are experienced as trustworthy, meaningful, and relevant, not only environmentally beneficial. The article therefore argues that firms need to move beyond a narrow focus on material sustainability and engage more directly with how value is constructed and communicated. By highlighting the role of intangible value in enabling sustainable consumption, the paper contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of persistent barriers to the adoption of circular products.

title: Ecological implications of fishery-photovoltaic systems: Altered phytoplankton dynamics and reduced microbial network stability under photovoltaic coverage
abstract: Water-surface photovoltaic systems (WSPV) have attracted increasing attention as a renewable energy solution, yet their ecological impacts in mariculture ecosystems remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the effects of PV coverage on phytoplankton community structure and microbial interactions based on a one-year field experiment in mariculture ponds with high-throughput rRNA gene sequencing and co-occurrence network analysis. Our results showed that the annual average temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, dissolved silicate, and dissolved inorganic phosphate concentrations were decreased under PV coverage, while dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) increased, especially in active mariculture ponds. These environmental shifts coincided with a substantial reduction in total phytoplankton abundance (63–75%), while α-diversity increased and composition shifted notably toward dinoflagellates in summer, including several potentially harmful algal taxa. However, in the present study, only total phytoplankton abundance and relative compositional shifts were reported, species-specific absolute abundances were not determined, leaving their trends under PV coverage unknown. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed that PV coverage triggered a restructuring of microbial interactions, resulting in phytoplankton networks that were more modular while less robust, and phytoplankton-bacteria associations that were intensified but less stable. The consistent occurrence of key bacterial families, e.g., Rhodobacteraceae and Flavobacteriaceae, likely enhanced nutrient recycling, contributing to elevated DIN. However, light limitation may decouple this bacterial-mediated regeneration from algal production, suggesting the possibility of a high-turnover, bacterially dominated nutrient loop that sustains lower phytoplankton abundance. Overall, our findings demonstrated that PV coverage can substantially modify pond environmental conditions and phytoplankton community organization, with important implications for the ecological sustainability of WSPV–mariculture systems.

title: Synergistic ionic liquid modification and MOF-based confinement of polyoxometalates for ultra-efficient oxidative desulfurization
abstract: The development of highly efficient and recyclable catalysts is crucial for the practical implementation of deep oxidative desulfurization (ODS) of fuel oils. To address the issues of aggregation and leaching of polyoxometalates (POMs) in ODS, an ionic liquid (IL)–metal–organic framework (MOF) confinement-coordinated immobilization strategy was proposed to construct a bifunctional composite catalyst, BmimPMo/MIL-101(Cr). Specifically, Bmim+ and [PMo12O40]3- form large-sized clusters through ionic interactions and are effectively confined within the MIL-101(Cr) nanocages, which not only suppresses the leaching of active components but also optimizes the interfacial microenvironment, thereby enhancing their adsorption and mass transfer performance for sulfur-containing compounds in the oil phase. The reaction conditions were systematically optimized using response surface methodology (RSM) based on a Box–Behnken design (BBD), yielding optimal conditions: 50 °C, an O/S ratio of 10, and a catalyst dosage of 2.5 g L−1. Under these mild conditions, the catalyst achieved a DBT removal efficiency of 99.76% within 80 min and exhibited excellent stability with only a 4.20% decrease in activity after eight consecutive cycles. Mechanistic studies revealed that superoxide radicals (·O2−) are the dominant reactive species, and the reaction follows a synergistic “adsorption–activation–oxidation” pathway. The kinetics conform to a pseudo-first-order model with a relatively low apparent activation energy of 15.0 kJ mol−1. Furthermore, a high desulfurization efficiency of 92.61% was maintained in real gasoline, demonstrating its promising potential for practical applications.

title: Organic matter enrichment and warming synergistically drive sediment phosphorus release in macrophyte-dominated lakes: Geochemical and microbial mechanisms
abstract: Sediment phosphorus (P) release generally intensifies with warming; yet the synergistic effects of temperature and organic matter (OM) enrichment on P dynamics remain poorly understood. In this study, we conducted long-term microcosm incubations under ambient and elevated temperatures using sediments with equivalent total P but varying OM contents. The results showed that elevated OM expanded the sedimentary mobile P (Mobile-P) pool; high-OM sediments (M-10%) contained 1.5 times more Mobile-P than low-OM sediments (M-2%). Warming and high-OM loading synergistically increased the sediment oxygen uptake rate and compressed the interfacial oxidation layer (<2 mm). Consequently, the average soluble reactive phosphorus (SRP) release flux in the M-10% treatment on day 15 was 47 times that of the M-2% treatment. This intense P release was driven by the reductive dissolution of iron-bound P (BD-P), the enzymatic hydrolysis of organic P (Org-P), and the chemical dissolution of calcium-bound P (HCl-P). Microbial analysis further revealed that high OM enrichment upregulated genes involved in Org-P hydrolysis (phoD) and iron reduction (mtrC). However, warming reshaped the dissolved organic matter (DOM) pool in the M-10% treatment, where accumulated insoluble humic acids immobilized SRP via chemical complexation with metal cations, thereby reducing the SRP flux by day 50. Nevertheless, this flux remained 21 times that of the M-2% treatment. This study elucidates the key geochemical and microbial mechanisms by which macrophyte-derived OM enrichment promotes sediment P release under warming, providing critical insights for sediment management and eutrophication control in macrophyte-dominated ecosystems.

title: Steam gasification of municipal solid waste with subsequent tar cracking for ultra-low tar, hydrogen-rich syngas production
abstract: The uptrend in municipal solid waste (MSW) generation poses a serious threat to human wellbeing and the environment, also having added economic penalties for its handling and storage. The problems associated with MSW can be addressed by employing effective waste management techniques, and if the generated wastes are utilized to produce syngas or other value-added products, this will also help to cater to the ever-increasing energy need for the modern world. In this article, a novel MSW to H2-rich syngas system has been proposed, validated with different experimental works, and analyzed through parametric variation and three-step sequential parametric optimization. A comprehensive steam gasification model has been developed that includes the formation of tar as well, and the subsequent tar cracking sub-system has been developed and integrated to the main unit, i.e., steam gasification process, to have a complete, realistic steam gasification model. The syngas produced by the steam gasification process has been mixed with the tar-cracked syngas to analyze the stage-wise syngas quality, and finally, process optimization has been performed for multiple output parameters considering a three-step optimization approach. It is observed that the model yields clean and dry H2-rich syngas having an LHV of 17.05 MJ/kg with a combined system efficiency of 83.02%, 20-35% higher than conventional setups under comparable operating trends. On the other hand, the H2 content at this condition is about 54%. However, H2 content as high as 63% is achievable from the developed model at higher steam to MSW ratio operations.

title: A straw-derived carbon-based emitter for integrated irrigation and heavy metal removal
abstract: Open burning of agricultural straw poses a serious threat to the sustainable development of agriculture. To address this challenge, this study developed an eco-friendly carbon-based emitter (CBE) using waste maize straw that integrates irrigation and heavy metal removal, providing a feasible pathway for straw resource utilization and the safe reuse of wastewater. The CBE was fabricated from discarded maize straw through a vacuum pyrolysis-molding-sintering process. The fabricated CBEs exhibited flexural strength ranging from 2.25 to 3.72 MPa, open porosity between 52.66% and 55.41%, and hydraulic flux from 42.09 to 206.78 L m−2 h−1. The optimal formulation (straw: biochar: clay = 2:4:1) with a sintering temperature of 900 °C achieved the best hydraulic performance. The CBE features a hierarchical lotus-root-like porous structure and shows high removal efficiencies for heavy-metal-contaminated irrigation water, with removal rates of 99.99%, 94.87%, and 83.73% for Cu(II), Cd(II), and Pb(II), respectively. The removal mechanisms are mainly attributed to chemical adsorption by surface oxygen-containing functional groups (–OH, –COOH) combined with pore-size sieving effects. Under multi-ion coexistence conditions, the effluent quality still meets the agricultural irrigation standards. Overall, this study demonstrates a multifunctional strategy for converting waste maize straw into structured CBE which integrates low-pressure irrigation with in-process heavy metal interception. These findings provide practical implications for straw valorization, safe wastewater reuse, and sustainable agricultural production.

title: Assessing the industrial-scale recycling feasibility of paper, board and fiber-based composites from lightweight packaging waste for high-quality applications
abstract: Despite high recycling targets, paper and board (PB), including fiber-based composites from German lightweight packaging waste (LWP), are still predominantly subjected to thermal recovery or low-quality recycling due to technical and regulatory barriers. To overcome these barriers and support the development of sustainable, high-quality recycling pathways (i.e., reutilization in applications comparable to the original product), we conducted two production trials in an operational board mill. The trials aimed to demonstrate technical recycling feasibility on an industrial scale, while generating data to support regulatory adaptation and providing primary data for a subsequent comparative life cycle assessment. Using a tailored quality assessment, we evaluated the entire process chain, including dry mechanical sorting, defibration, wet mechanical processing with an additional hygienization step, and final board production. The results indicate that PB recycling from LWP for high-quality applications is technically feasible (under investigated conditions, feedstock share 12.5 wt%), provided that specific process adaptations are implemented. Based on the assessed quality parameters, a substitution coefficient of 0.75 was derived for PB from LWP in the newly developed recycling process, indicating near-equivalent recyclability to that of conventionally collected recovered PB. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive industrial-scale quality assessment of PB recycling from LWP, with a particular focus on primary data collection and high-quality material recovery. The results support the scientific basis for the development of sustainable recycling pathways.

title: Optimal scale of sloping farmland in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area under the constraints of water-soil-carbon functional synergy: Nonlinear response and threshold effects
abstract: As an important type of cultivated land, the sustainable use of sloping farmland is crucial for ensuring regional food and ecological security. The spatially optimal allocation of sloping farmland resources requires limiting its scale to a reasonable range and further exploring the interaction effects and critical thresholds among multiple driving factors of ecological functions. Nevertheless, existing research still has a weak understanding of these aspects. This study focused on the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (TGRA) and systematically analyzed the spatial differentiation patterns of the water conservation (WC), soil conservation (SC), and carbon sequestration (CS) functions of sloping farmland, by adopting methods including the InVEST model, constraint line analysis and conditional inference tree model. It further identified the key driving factors and revealed the threshold effects of both single factors and multifactor interactions on these functions. Additionally, the optimal scale threshold of sloping farmland under the synergistic constraints of water–soil–carbon functions was quantified. The results showed that the WC and SC functions of sloping farmland were high in the central region and low in the western region, whereas the CS function was high in the central region and low in the eastern and southwestern regions. The WC, SC, and CS functions of sloping farmland were nonlinearly constrained by their corresponding key driving factors and exhibited clear critical threshold phenomena. The Normalized difference vegetation index, a typical driving factor, showed a parabolic constraint relationship with the three functions, with corresponding critical thresholds of 0.80, 0.78, and 0.73, respectively. Under the synergistic constraints of water–soil–carbon functions, the estimated optimal scale range of sloping farmland in the TGRA was determined to be 9083–10039 km2, implying that 1492–2448 km2 of sloping farmland should be prioritized for conversion into forestland. To strictly uphold the national farmland protection red line and ensure regional food security, it is necessary to promote the adjustment and conversion between forestland with a slope below 3° and sloping farmland planned for Grain-for-Green. The threshold quantification results provide a scientific basis and methodological reference for spatial optimization decision-making, sustainable utilization, and ecological protection and restoration of regional sloping farmland resources.

title: Efficiency-enhanced distributed low-carbon dispatch for multi-virtual power plants: A spatio-temporal collaborative ADMM approach
abstract: The collaborative operation of multiple Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) has emerged as a crucial pathway for integrating high-penetration renewable energy under carbon neutrality targets. However, existing multi-VPP dispatch schemes often prioritize economic profits while neglecting environmental benefits, and face challenges regarding data privacy and convergence efficiency in cross-entity transactions. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving low-carbon economic dispatch method for multi-VPP systems based on an improved Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). By introducing a dynamic carbon emission penalty mechanism and incorporating spatio-temporal collaborative over-relaxation correction with an adaptive penalty factor, the proposed algorithm resolves the conflict between transaction consistency and energy storage temporal continuity while balancing operational costs and environmental benefits. Simulation on a heterogeneous three-VPP test system demonstrates a 35.6% reduction in computation time relative to adaptive ADMM and a 21.8% reduction in solution error relative to traditional ADMM, with substantially reduced carbon-intensive grid dependence and improved renewable self-sufficiency.

title: Salt-assisted liquid-liquid extraction for valorization of hydrothermal carbonization process water
abstract: Process water from the hydrothermal carbonization of biomass (HTC-PW) is saturated with organic molecules whose presence hinders disposal. Recovering these organics from HTC-PW as value-added products could enhance process economics. While the literature is replete with the use of conventional liquid-liquid extraction (LLE) to accomplish such separation, LLE requires large solvent volumes owing to low extraction efficiencies. We compare conventional LLE to one where the equilibrium is disrupted by the addition of neutral salts, or Salt-Assisted Liquid-Liquid Extraction (SALLE). Neutral salts strengthen water's hydrogen-bonding network and reduce solute solubility, disrupting the equilibria between the HTC-PW and the extracting solvent by raising the chemical potential of the solute in the HTC-PW. In this work, we use the HTC-PW of microcrystalline cellulose, a model biomass compound, to compare the efficacy of SALLE using three solvents (ethyl acetate, hexane, and acetone) and four salts (sodium chloride, sodium sulphate, potassium chloride, and potassium sulphate) across the partition ratio (KD) and selectivity (αi,ii) of each compound. Among the four salts, Na2SO4, which has the greatest hydration energy and contributes the most entropy, exhibits the largest improvements in KD. Solute properties also influence separation. Furfural, being less polar, partitions more easily than 5-hydroxymethylfurfural. Longer-chain acids are more readily extracted than highly hydrophilic acids. Increasing salt beyond its solubility limit initially improves partitioning, but KD decreases beyond specific salt concentrations. Ethyl acetate with 4M Na2SO4 is an optimal combination identified in this work, where detected compounds in the HTC-PW fall below 200 mg/L, including polar hydrophilic carboxylic acids.

title: Climate variability and land use change drive spatiotemporal patterns of groundwater storage along the Tarim River mainstream
abstract: Groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) are important indicators for groundwater security and sustainable water governance in arid inland river systems. This study investigates long-term GWSA trends along the Tarim River mainstream during 1990–2020 using a 1-km downscaled GWSA dataset and crop-specific land-use analysis. Results show a persistent decline in GWSA at a rate of −0.451 cm/year, with greater losses in the upper and middle reaches. Spatial variation is primarily associated with cropland expansion, impervious surface growth, and regional hydroclimatic variability. Land-use change dominates the long-term pattern of groundwater depletion, whereas climate variability remains an important co-driver of seasonal and interannual groundwater fluctuations. Additional analysis based on crop-area statistics from the main administrative regions along the Tarim mainstream indicates that the expansion of high-water-demand crops, particularly cotton, grapes, and red dates, is associated with lower groundwater storage conditions. By quantifying the relative roles of climate variability and land-use change across subregions, this study provides evidence for spatially targeted and crop-sensitive groundwater governance and sustainable irrigation management in arid inland river systems.

title: Soil texture affects methane emissions in paddy fields through alterations in organic carbon partitioning and root exudation
abstract: Paddy rice systems are a major agricultural source of methane (CH4) emissions. Although soil texture is a fundamental soil property, its role in regulating CH4 emissions remains underexplored. A two-year field experiment was conducted using a split-split-plot design, with soil texture as the main plot, straw return method as the subplot, and nitrogen application as the sub-subplot, to elucidate the effects and mechanisms of soil texture on CH4 emissions. The results showed that paddy fields with different soil textures exhibited distinct CH4 emission patterns and responded differently to straw incorporation and nitrogen fertilization. When straw was incorporated, nitrogen fertilization significantly reduced CH4 emissions in silty clay loam (15.9% clay) and sandy loam (7.0% clay) by 19.20% and 43.14%, respectively, but increased emissions in silty loam (2.6% clay) by 36.84%. Therefore, this study proposed that straw return and nitrogen application strategies should be optimized based on soil texture, which would facilitate further CH4 mitigation. Soil texture was found to primarily regulate CH4 emissions by influencing organic carbon allocation and plant growth. Silty clay loam promoted the partitioning of organic carbon into mineral-associated organic carbon, whereas sandy loam favored the accumulation of particulate organic carbon. Dissolved organic carbon exhibited the strongest correlation with CH4 emissions. Root exudates were identified as a key factor in the soil-plant-microbe interaction network governing CH4 emissions in paddy fields and had the highest importance score in Random Forest models. Moreover, key differential root metabolites not only demonstrated strong predictive performance for CH4 emissions but also exhibited robust linear relationships with CH4 fluxes, and were also significantly correlated with the composition of CH4-related functional microbial communities. This work provided new insights into the mechanisms underlying CH4 emissions in paddy fields and provided both a theoretical foundation and practical management strategies for precision mitigation. These advances contributed to promoting cleaner rice production and achieving sustainable agricultural goals.

title: Sectoral value-added structure, energy consumption dynamics, international trade, and governance quality in shaping carbon emissions: Evidence from RCEP economies
abstract: The rapid economic expansion of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) economies has intensified environmental pressures and positioned the region as a significant contributor to global carbon emissions. This study, therefore, investigates the determinants of carbon emissions by integrating sectoral value-added structures, energy consumption dynamics, international trade, governance quality, and key socioeconomic factors within a unified empirical framework. Methodologically, the study uses panel data from 2000 to 2023 and employs the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR), which captures distributional heterogeneity beyond conventional mean-based models. Also, to address potential endogeneity and simultaneity concerns, additional estimations using Instrumental Variable (IV), Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS), and System-Generalized Method of Moments (System-GMM) are implemented, confirming the robustness of the empirical findings. The results revealed that energy consumption emerges as the strongest driver of emissions, with estimated elasticities ranging from 0.134 to 0.603 across the quantiles. In contrast, access to clean energy technologies consistently reduces emissions, with coefficients ranging from −0.123 to −0.249 across the distribution. Sectoral restructuring also plays an important role: manufacturing value added increases emissions, whereas service-sector expansion reduces emissions, with effects ranging from 0.248 to 0.712. Governance quality also contributes significantly to emission mitigation, with political stability and government effectiveness exerting increasingly stronger emission-reducing effects across higher quantiles. These findings suggest that emission mitigation in RCEP economies depends heavily on structural transformation and energy system transitions. The study highlights the importance of distribution-sensitive environmental strategies and demonstrates the value of quantile-based approaches for identifying heterogeneous drivers of carbon emissions in integrated regional economies.

title: Multiphysics-informed multi-objective optimization of hydrogen–carbon synergistic reduction of hematite pellets: Mechanistic insights and process decision strategies
abstract: To support deep decarbonization of the steel sector, hydrogen–carbon synergistic reduction has emerged as a key enabling technology. However, the nonlinear couplings linking process variables to reduction performance remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a physics-grounded optimization framework that integrates transient multiphysics modeling, response surface methodology, NSGA-II-based Pareto optimization, and TOPSIS–LINMAP decision-making for single hematite pellets reduced in H2–CO atmospheres. The multiphysics model incorporates multi-step reduction kinetics, coupled molecular–Knudsen diffusion, non-isothermal heat transfer, and reduction-driven pore-structure evolution. The response surfaces show that pellet radius and reducing-gas temperature dominate the reduction time, pellet radius and the H2-to-CO molar ratio govern the signed cumulative net reaction heat, and the H2-to-CO molar ratio and inlet velocity strongly affect reducing-gas utilization efficiency. A high-efficiency operating window is identified at 1250–1270 K and a moderate H2-to-CO molar ratio of 2.5–3.7, where rapid reaction kinetics and CO-assisted heat compensation are well balanced. Increasing inlet velocity enhances mass transfer but shortens gas residence time, revealing a trade-off between transport intensification and reaction sufficiency. Relative to the center-point baseline, the multiphysics-verified TOPSIS and LINMAP schemes substantially improve overall reduction performance: they shorten the time required to reach 95% reduction by approximately 37.7% and 39.3%, reduce the net heat absorption demand by approximately 65.2% and 68.7%, and improve reducing-gas utilization efficiency by approximately 65.5% and 61.0%, respectively. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, mechanism-resolved, and decision-oriented route toward cleaner and more efficient H2–CO direct reduction.

title: Fiscal investment and ecosystem service trade-offs in the upper Yangtze river basin: Limits to hydrological resilience in watershed PES governance
abstract: Payment-for-ecosystem-services programmes allocate fiscal resources on the assumption that ecological investment improves watershed ecosystem service delivery, yet the welfare returns of such investment in hydrological provisioning remain empirically unresolved. This study develops a dual-index Hydrological Resilience Index framework grounded in Budyko water balance theory to separately evaluate landscape resilience and hydrological behavior resilience across five sub-basins of the Upper Yangtze River Basin over 1991–2024, integrating Random Forest regression with TreeSHAP attribution, mediation analysis, and two-way fixed-effects panel regression to test the fiscal-to-ecosystem-service causal pathway in watershed PES design. Results reveal a structural decoupling between landscape and hydrological resilience (r = −0.172, p = 0.025), whereby vegetation expansion strengthens regulating services while reducing hydrological provisioning capacity. Climate aridity dominates hydrological behavior resilience with explanatory importance approximately 32 times greater than any fiscal variable (fiscal SHAP: 3.1 ± 0.3%), while fiscal investment shows a modest association with landscape resilience (9.0 ± 0.5%) and no statistically significant influence on hydrological resilience (p > 0.05). The fiscal-to-land cover mediation pathway is not supported, indicating a breakdown in the causal mechanism through which PES investment is assumed to improve provisioning outcomes. Upstream populations gain regulating service improvements while downstream in-basin water users experience reduced hydrological provisioning capacity relative to landscape service gains, a welfare asymmetry persisting across sub-basins over three decades. These findings demonstrate that PES schemes rewarding vegetation metrics may not reliably secure hydrological provisioning services, and support redesigning performance criteria to incorporate hydrological indicators and spatially differentiated payment structures.

title: Quantitative social life cycle assessment of plastic, bioplastic, and paper packaging systems
abstract: Social impacts in packaging supply chains remain underexplored compared to environmental and economic aspects, despite their growing relevance in sustainability decision-making. This study applies Social Life Cycle Assessment (S-LCA) to evaluate the social sustainability of three carrier bag types: low-density polyethylene (LDPE) plastic, polylactic acid (PLA) bioplastic and kraft paper. The assessment is conducted using OpenLCA by integrating primary data with the SOCA V2 database, and focuses on four stakeholder groups, including Local Communities, Society, Value Chain Actors, and Workers. Social impacts are quantified across life cycle stages and stakeholder categories. Results are expressed as “medium risk hours,” a relative indicator used for comparative hotspot identification. The results indicate that Society and Value Chain Actors face high to very high risks (>40%) across all materials, highlighting potential areas for improvements. The PLA bioplastic bag exhibits the highest social impacts during raw material production, while the kraft paper bag performs worst in manufacturing and end-of life treatment. Overall social impacts rank PLA bioplastic highest (95.79 medium risk hours), followed by kraft paper (54.45), and LDPE plastic (35.15), a ranking that challenges common assumptions about the sustainability of bioplastics and paper alternatives. This quantitative social impact analysis provides clear, data-driven insights into social risk hotspots and improvement opportunities.

title: Physically consistent design of hybrid renewable energy systems for green methanol: A chained load modeling and techno-economic approach
abstract: Green methanol is emerging as a strategic fuel for decarbonizing carbon-intensive industries; however, many existing Power-to-Methanol (PtM) assessments rely on decoupled modeling approaches that risk producing economically optimal yet physically inconsistent system configurations. This study proposes a stoichiometrically coupled chained load modeling framework to ensure strict mass and energy conservation between renewable electricity generation, hydrogen production, direct air capture (DAC), and methanol synthesis at hourly resolution. The framework is implemented in HOMER Pro and extended with Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC)-weighted stochastic Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS), Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and cross-validation using Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to enhance robustness and reproducibility. A hybrid PV-Wind-Battery configuration optimized for Yalova, Türkiye, achieves a Net Present Cost (NPC) of 889,216 USD and a Levelized Cost of Methanol (LCOM) of 0.523 USD kg−1 under fully renewable operation. Wind energy contributes 62.8% of annual generation, providing structural dominance, while solar energy ensures seasonal complementarity. Sensitivity analysis demonstrates that even under extreme capital cost escalation scenarios compared to baseline projections, the LCOM (up to 1.06 USD kg−1) remains within competitive literature ranges confirming the system's economic resilience. Additional deterministic and stochastic MCDA analyses further demonstrate that the ranking of the optimal configuration remains stable under equal-weight, environmental-priority, and Monte Carlo-based weighting scenarios, confirming the robustness of the decision framework beyond CAPEX-dominant conditions. The proposed framework eliminates non-physical operating states commonly observed in conventional black-box optimizations and confirms structural convergence across independent optimization algorithms. A simplified cradle-to-gate environmental assessment indicates a net carbon intensity of approximately −0.97 kg CO2-eq kg−1 MeOH. This result confirms that the stoichiometric capture of atmospheric CO2 exceeds the embodied emissions of the renewable infrastructure within the defined cradle-to-gate system boundary, providing a scalable framework for carbon-negative green methanol system design.

title: Interactions between curbside collection and open-access street recycling systems: Evidence from a field experiment in Chile
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of introducing a curbside recycling collection service (CRCS) on plastic recycling, primarily PET bottles, when implemented alongside open-access street recycling bins. The analysis uses objective operational records from a 91-week non-randomized field experiment conducted in two middle-income neighborhoods in Osorno, Chile. The intervention included three stages: installation of street recycling bins in both neighborhoods, introduction of CRCS in the treatment area, and subsequent reinforcement through injunctive-normative appeal brochures. Results show that CRCS increased plastic collection by 3.5 kg per withdrawal and polygon, equivalent to a 74% increase relative to the control group. During the reinforcement stage, plastic collection increased by 1.3 kg, equivalent to a 31.1% increase, although this estimate cannot be interpreted as the isolated causal effect of messaging. Street-bin use did not decline after CRCS was introduced, providing suggestive evidence of complementarity between collection systems. Non-recyclable material increased modestly during the CRCS-only stage but decreased and became statistically insignificant during the reinforcement stage. By jointly examining material recovery, system interaction, and contamination using objective longitudinal field data, this study contributes to the literature on recycling system design in middle-income urban contexts. The findings suggest that curbside collection can improve plastic recovery, provided that monitoring and communication strategies are used to preserve material quality.

title: ESG reporting and action in real estate: A case study of Australian Real Estate Investment Trusts
abstract: ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) has emerged as the latest catchphrase to define sustainability in organisational practice. However, understanding what ESG means in practice and how it applies in the real estate sector remains mute. Building rating tools have significantly influenced market adoption of sustainable building practices. This paper explored ESG reporting and prevalence of sustainability rating tool use by Australian Real Estate Investment Trusts (AREITs), through a content analysis and comparison of 10 AREITs sustainability and/or annual reports. Findings revealed a higher emphasis on the Social component of ESG, mainly focused on aspects of Community and Customer relations, surpassing the Environmental and Governance criteria in terms of number of occurrences and investments disclosed. ESG strategies were found to be interconnected, with actions mainly defined by a combination of environmental, social and governance aspects. Leading AREITs, classified as frontrunners, were characterised by more detailed disclosure of their actions, alignment with global financial standards and a strong commitment to financial disclosures related to ESG and sustainability. Sustainability rating tools were commonly used to demonstrate ESG credentials, mostly focused on performance-based tools, yet an increasing focus was dedicated to social sustainability, especially in health and wellbeing of building occupants. Findings from this research help establish AREITs reporting practices of ESG and sustainability, albeit it should be acknowledged there is some disconnect between corporate sustainability and the asset portfolio's sustainability. It also provides the property industry with a better understanding of the profile of current ESG and sustainability characteristics in real estate, enabling prioritisation and reflection in the ESG consideration requirements under the International Valuation Standards.

title: Global vulnerability of coastal blue carbon ecosystems to climate and anthropogenic impacts: A spatiotemporal perspective
abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic activities have increased the vulnerability of coastal blue carbon ecosystems, including saltmarshes, mangrove forests, and seagrass beds. However, existing vulnerability assessments are predominantly region-specific and lack a global perspective. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive global spatiotemporal vulnerability assessment of coastal blue carbon ecosystems. Ten physical, ecological, and socioeconomic indicators were integrated within a pressure–state–response (PSR) framework and weighted using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to calculate the coastal blue carbon vulnerability index (CBCVI) across 52 coastal countries at a 1 km resolution from 2000 to 2020. The results indicated that seagrass beds were the most vulnerable ecosystem and showed an increasing vulnerability trend over the study period. Mangrove forests were the second most vulnerable ecosystem, with a mildly fluctuating vulnerability, while saltmarshes were the least vulnerable. Geographically, prominent concentrations of high vulnerability areas were identified in Asia, Africa, and Oceania. Temporally, the proportion of areas with very low vulnerability decreased from 20.60% in 2005 to 17.92% in 2020, while that of areas with very high vulnerability increased from 4.88% to 7.12% during the same period. Economic development, coastal slope, and vegetation growth conditions were identified as key factors contributing to vulnerability. This groundbreaking global assessment offers scientific insights into the conservation and sustainable management of coastal blue carbon ecosystems and emphasizes the need for strengthened ecological protection, infrastructure, and land-use planning to inform evidence-based policymaking.

title: Navigating toward 2050 decarbonization: A design-constrained life cycle emission and costs assessment for sustainable marine fuel retrofits incorporating feedstock sources
abstract: This study contributes to the maritime industry's pathway toward the IMO 2050 net-zero objective through an integrated approach that links design-constrained retrofit evaluation and fuel feedstock sources with life-cycle and cost assessments. Two representative vessels, a 49 m Ro-Ro ship operating on medium range routes and an 87 m car ferry operating on longer routes, are evaluated, with propulsion configurations divided into ICE systems and electric motor systems. Retrofit scenarios include electric propulsion using lithium-ion batteries and hydrogen fuel cells, and ICE propulsion operating on methanol and ammonia, both recognized for their potential to deliver low or near-zero carbon emissions. Environmental performance is assessed through a well to wake life cycle assessment, while the cost analysis incorporates feedstock sources to evaluate long-term cost feasibility under future decarbonization pathways. The retrofit feasibility assessment shows that all alternatives except pure battery-electric propulsion are technically achievable, with battery energy density as the limiting factor. From a life cycle perspective, hybrid diesel–electric propulsion, fossil based hydrogen fuel cells, fossil based ammonia ICE, and renewable energy based methanol ICE offer viable mid-term mitigation options, while only renewable energy based ammonia and renewable energy based hydrogen enable net zero decarbonization consistent with long-term climate objectives. Integrating retrofit feasibility, environmental performance, and cost assessment, the study highlights ammonia-based ICE systems as particularly promising solutions for achieving IMO 2050 targets, offering both technical feasibility and economic robustness under time horizon and scenario of this study.

title: Risk control zoning optimization and source contribution identification of microplastics in wetland water under ecological risk threshold and uncertainty constraints
abstract: Microplastic contamination has emerged as an urgent challenge for global aquatic environments, and developing accurate and efficient integrated risk-assessment schemes remains both a priority and a bottleneck. Here, we combined ecological risk assessment, positive matrix factorization (PMF), and one and two-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate microplastic risks and their driving factors in the surface water of Baiyangdian, the largest wetland in North China, and to delineate areas requiring differentiated risk control. By integrating multiple approaches, this study promotes a shift in microplastic risk assessment from single-indicator screening to multidimensional integrated judgement, and establishes a transferable framework to support precision regional risk management. Microplastic abundance in Baiyangdian ranged from 40 to 126 items·L−1, with a mean of 63 items·L−1, indicating a high pollution level at the global scale.
