Overall, the findings show that household economic strength is a key driver of renewable energy uptake, and effective policy must prioritize long-term affordability, targeted incentives, and structural support for household-level adoption.

title: Novel hydrometallurgy separation and recovery of silicon/silver from waste crystalline silicon solar cells
abstract: The recycling of waste crystalline silicon solar cells presents a dual challenge: recovering high-value metal silver with high efficiency while also recovering high-purity silicon. This study introduces an innovative selective etching approach to achieve preferential etching of metal gates and silicon substrates at sintering points. Leveraging the characteristics of screen printing and sintering—high defect density and variations in silicon nitride coverage at sintering points—the initial stage employs silicate accumulation combined with mask etching to remove the silicon dioxide film, exposing fresh silicon surfaces and enabling a continuous self-catalyzing cycle for silicon-silver separation. Subsequent metal-catalyzed chemical etching (MCCE) enables precise etching at the sintering junctions, achieving solid-state separation of silver grids from silicon substrates without apparent damage. The catalytic corrosion method yields superior results compared to the initial thermal alkali stripping process. The overall silver recovery ratio is doubled, while the total weight loss of the silicon cell is only half of that in the previous method, simultaneously ensuring the recovery of high-purity silicon. Through response surface methodology (RSM) optimization and combined etching processes, the final silver grid can be almost completely stripped, with a minimum silver recovery efficiency of 93% in the optimal process range, silicon purity reaching 99.99%. The silicon substrate maintaining structural integrity and can be used as raw material for purification into high-purity silicon. Overall, this method highlights the potential for sustainable, low-damage silicon-silver separation, promoting the development of a circular economy in renewable energy technologies.

title: Thermodynamic-kinetic integrated analysis of heat exchanger scaling and control techniques: A case study from a potash processing plant in northwest China
abstract: The inaccurate prediction of scale formation in heat exchangers, particularly under conditions of saline-alkaline water, has been relatively overlooked. This study systematically investigates both severe scaling and technique for effective control in heat exchangers at a potash processing plant in northwest China using two types of complex water supplies: Mixi surface water (MX) and Hongliu groundwater (HL). By integrating classical nucleation theory with PHREEQC (a geochemical modeling software) simulations, a comprehensive thermodynamic–kinetic analytical framework was developed to explore the effects of supersaturation state on precipitation and surface deposition. The feasibility of non-chemical scaling mitigation strategies for MX and HL was further evaluated. The findings indicate that CaCO3 scaling is jointly governed by supersaturation evolution and kinetic constraints. Although MX and HL have similar saturation indices (SI) and initial nucleation rates under the same conditions, pronounced differences in the final precipitation and surface deposition amounts were observed due to variations in the ionic composition. Grey relational analysis (GRA) further revealed that HCO3− has a stronger impact than Ca2+ on both precipitation and deposition in real saline-alkaline water. This underscores the critical roles of carbonate species derived from bicarbonate in controlling post-nucleation crystal growth and deposition behavior. Based on these findings, an ultrasonic descaling strategy was proposed. Under representative operating conditions (80 °C, pH = 8.5), ultrasonic treatment reduced wall deposition by approximately 70 %. During 73 days of industrial operation, the retrofitted heat exchanger maintained an inlet-outlet temperature difference (ΔT) above 50 °C for approximately 57 % of the operating time, more than twice the 26 % observed for the non-retrofitted unit. Overall, this study provides both a theoretical framework and a practical solution for mitigating mineral scaling in heat exchangers operating with saline-alkaline industrial waters.

title: Synergistic SF6 abatement and desalination brine valorization for valuable resource recovery: Techno-economic and environmental assessment
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is a potent greenhouse gas with a long atmospheric lifetime, necessitating effective treatment despite substitution efforts. While thermal incineration is widely utilized, most systems overlook by-product recovery. Desalination brine discharge presents environmental challenges but offers potential as a chemical resource. In this study, four process configurations for treating 250 kg h−1 of SF6 were designed, simulated, and evaluated from economic and environmental perspectives. The baseline configuration (Case 1) based on single-stage scrubbing resulted in the highest levelized cost of SF6 destruction (LCOD) of 13.95 $ kg−1. In contrast, multistage systems (Cases 2–4) enabled selective capture and by-product recovery. Case 2 significantly reduced the LCOD to 3.25 $ kg−1 SF6 but remained dependent on purchased neutralizers. Cases 3 and 4 utilized desalination brine-derived reagents. While sensitive to fluctuations in by-product revenues, electricity costs, and taxation, they achieved negative LCOD values (−2.32 and −4.01 $ kg−1 SF6). Heat-exchange network (HEN) integration in Case 4 improved performance, reducing heating and cooling demands by 56.15% and 63.74%, respectively. Life cycle assessments showed that all configurations achieved >99.8% reductions in global warming potential relative to direct SF6 emissions (26,241.7 kg CO2 eq kg−1 SF6). With a 35% share of renewable energy, the HEN-optimized system achieved net-negative emissions while maintaining economic viability. These results demonstrate the benefits of integrated waste management for simultaneous emission reduction and economic gain, supporting the development of coupled SF6–brine treatment systems.

title: A multi-task learning model integrating physical property databases and multidimensional descriptors for predicting thermophysical properties of type III and V deep eutectic solvents and assisting screening
abstract: Organic solvents are widely recognized as environmental hazards due to their high pollution potential. In contrast, deep eutectic solvents (DESs), particularly Type III and V DESs, are promising green alternatives. Their structural tunability enables numerous possible combinations, which makes identifying DESs that meet industrial requirements challenging and necessitates systematic screening. In practice, industrial performance depends on multiple interrelated physical properties rather than a single parameter. Accordingly, we constructed a DES property database containing 10,537 data points for melting point, viscosity, density, and surface tension. Using this database and multidimensional descriptors, we developed a multi-task learning (MTL) model to predict these properties simultaneously. The model achieved high predictive accuracy, with R2 values of 0.980 for melting point, 0.971 for viscosity, 0.993 for density, and 0.963 for surface tension. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis quantified feature–property relationships, improving model interpretability and supporting DES molecular design. The MTL model was further applied to screen DESs based on composite physical properties and identify promising solvent combinations. Overall, the model enables accurate property prediction and efficient screening of DESs for industrial applications.

title: Evaluation of the carbon intensity of biomethane under Brazil's National Biofuel Policy (RenovaBio): impacts of system boundary variations
authors: Marília Ieda da Silveira Folegatti Matsuura
abstract: Biomethane from organic waste is a strategic option for decarbonizing energy systems and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. However, system-boundary definition strongly affects carbon-intensity accounting and economic incentives under Brazil's National Biofuel Policy (RenovaBio). This study compares four emission-allocation approaches for biomethane certification, considering different boundaries and avoided-emission assumptions. The results showed that carbon intensity varied strongly according to the boundary approach adopted. Scenario 1 produced the highest impacts, especially for swine manure systems and MSW landfills, with average carbon intensities of 114.45 ± 90.57 and 597.22 ± 52.01 g CO2eq MJ−1, respectively, mainly due to fugitive methane emissions. Scenario 2 resulted in more stable environmental-efficiency scores, with an average NEEA of 74.46 g CO2eq MJ−1, by assigning waste-treatment burdens to the waste-generating activity. In contrast, Scenarios 3 and 3.1 substantially increased the mitigation potential of anaerobic-digestion routes, with NEEA values ranging from 256.77 to 893.39 g CO2eq MJ−1 under avoided-emission accounting. For landfill biomethane, Scenario 3 remained unfavorable, with an average carbon intensity of 404.12 ± 192.23 g CO2eq MJ−1, whereas Scenario 3.1 improved performance to 2.10 ± 51.84 g CO2eq MJ−1 and a positive average NEEA of 84.60 ± 51.84 g CO2eq MJ−1. Overall, Scenario 2 emerges as the most balanced short-term approach for the current RenovaCalc framework, offering regulatory predictability while correctly attributing environmental responsibility to the waste-generating activity. In the longer term, Scenario 3.1 represents a promising methodological improvement, provided that robust rules for baseline definition, monitoring, verification, additionality, double-counting prevention, leakage control, and market stability are established. Aligning RenovaCalc with international carbon-intensity-based fuel policies could strengthen the competitiveness of biomethane in Brazil and support its integration into national decarbonization strategies.

title: Social acceptance of solar fuels in Germany: Evidence from a national survey on artificial photosynthesis-derived isobutanol
abstract: Innovative energy carriers, such as solar fuels, are essential for decarbonizing hard-to-abate mobility sectors and industrial processes. Social acceptance is pivotal for the implementation and scaling of solar fuels, influencing policy feasibility and market uptake. However, empirical evidence remains scarce. Conducting an online survey (N = 830), we assess acceptance levels and perceptions in Germany of a hybrid artificial photosynthesis pathway that produces solar isobutanol. Attitudes are moderately favorable, with moderate sociopolitical support and market acceptance, while community acceptance is neutral. Support for solar fuels is highest in freight transport, followed by public transport and aviation, while acceptance is lowest for private car use and industrial solvent applications. Perceived risks are associated with uncertainties for consumers, production, local implementation, and poor sustainability performance. Perceived benefits include fossil fuel substitution, sustainability, local implementation potential, consumer convenience, and consumer sustainability feelings. While the perceived benefit of fossil fuel substitution, interest in solar fuels and their perceived relevance are the main drivers of sociopolitical and market acceptance, community acceptance is limited by risks relating to production and local implementation, among other factors. Acceptance of genetically modified bacteria for fuel production emerges as a key predictor of acceptance across all dimensions. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the acceptance of solar fuel and emphasize the importance of multidimensional acceptance modeling. Based on this understanding of acceptance levels, drivers and barriers, socially accepted pathways in the production, deployment and roll-out of solar fuels can be identified and effective communication strategies developed.

title: Development of a multi-criteria indicator for product life cycle decision-making
abstract: Maximizing product value and resource efficiency has been widely regarded as a key objective throughout the product life cycle, supported by improved product designs, informed manufacturing decisions, and regenerative approaches. Despite the importance of effectively evaluating how well these objectives are achieved, there remains a lack of indicators that comprehensively characterize multi-dimensional performance at the level of individual product life cycle stages. To address this gap, this study develops a novel indicator, the Life Cycle Performance Indicator (LCPI). This indicator combines multiple dimensions (economic efficiency, pollutant release level, and workforce stability) into a single integrated measure using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to evaluate performance at each life cycle stage. The proposed indicator is applied in a case study of a diesel engine remanufactured into an LNG engine at the end of a use cycle to identify underperforming life cycle stages and support targeted improvement efforts. Scenario-based analysis under the evaluated data variation scenarios indicates that the LCPI could potentially be improved by up to 60%, demonstrating substantial opportunities for enhancing life cycle performance. This study provides decision-makers with insights to identify underperforming life cycle stages, prioritize improvement efforts, and understand trade-offs among multiple performance dimensions.

title: Timber carbon stocks in China's forest production-consumption nexus: Interregional redistribution and implications for sustainable forest resources
abstract: As China advances its national agenda for carbon neutrality and ecological civilization, understanding how timber use affects forest carbon sinks across regions is increasingly important for forest policy and governance. Using data from 31 provincial-level administrative regions from 2002 to 2020, this study constructs a timber carbon stock satellite matrix and applies a multi-regional input-output model to quantify the interregional redistribution of timber carbon stocks within China. It constructs a Forestry Carbon Sink Pressure Index to identify whether the consumption of timber-related carbon is compatible with provincial sink capacity. The results show that interprovincial timber carbon stocks expanded markedly over time and underwent a clear north-to-south reconfiguration shaped by forestry policies and industrial restructuring. Central and eastern provinces increasingly became major inflow regions. The FCSPI shows that the Bohai Rim and most of the central and eastern provinces face pressure as demand exceeds local sink capacity, while the southwestern and northeastern regions act as net ecological suppliers. This study links the constraints on forest ecosystem goods and services with the interregional trade flow of timber, provides suggestions for a reasonable coordination of timber use and carbon-sink management in China, and addresses China's climate and forestry strategy.

title: Recycling neutralization sludge into hydrotalcite for source control of acid mine drainage: From waste to value-added passivation material
abstract: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) from sulfide oxidation in mining waste rocks poses long-term environmental threats. The traditional chemical neutralization treatment method consumes a large amount of reagents and produces alkaline sludge. In this study, two hydrotalcite-like materials, Layered Double Hydroxides (LDHs) and modified LDHs (AS-LDHs), were synthesized utilizing sludge from the AMD neutralization process. They were applied to in-situ control of mining waste rocks to achieve source reduction of AMD. Results showed that acid-extractable and reducible metal fractions (Cd, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn) in waste rocks were the main pollution sources. With 1% addition and uniform mixing, LDHs exhibited optimal performance. After 28 days of reaction, the barrier rates of LDHs for Cd, Cu, Fe, Mn, and Zn reached 73.08%, 62.77%, 64.59%, 85.56%, and 58.48%, respectively, and the dominant mechanism was the adsorption of LDHs. LDHs also achieved 50% acidity barrier efficiency, enhancing the self-neutralization of carbonate minerals in waste rocks. Quantitative analysis attributed acidity removal to LDHs (46.5%), MgCO3 (43.5%), and CaCO3 (10.0%), raising waste rock pH 4.5 to 6.88 and classifying it as general industrial solid waste. This study demonstrates a sustainable “waste-treats-waste” closed-loop strategy, providing a cost-effective paradigm for at-source AMD control and solid waste resource utilization.

title: A process-informed framework for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for PPCPs by integrating machine learning and vadose-zone transport modeling
abstract: Conventional approaches for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) often simplify subsurface transport and neglect attenuation in the vadose zone, which can lead to overly conservative screening outcomes. To support more realistic and proportionate groundwater protection, this study developed a process-informed framework that integrates machine learning with HYDRUS-based vadose zone transport modeling. A global dataset covering 24 PPCPs and 584 soil and sediment samples was first used to predict the solid–liquid partition coefficient (Kd), and the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model showed the best performance. The results indicated that molecular properties and soil organic carbon were the major controls on partitioning. Vadose zone attenuation factors (AF) were then quantified by coupling HYDRUS simulations with machine learning, and the best performing model achieved an R2 of 0.90. Depth, KOC, and precipitation were identified as the dominant controls on attenuation, accounting for 76% of the total contribution. By integrating Kd, AF, and groundwater dilution factor (DF), groundwater-protective soil thresholds were derived for trimethoprim, nalidixic acid, and niflumic acid, with HC5 values of 0.06, 0.80, and 41.12 mg kg−1, respectively. Compared with conventional EPA-style calculations, explicitly accounting for vadose-zone attenuation materially changed the threshold estimates. These findings demonstrate that explicit representation of vadose-zone processes improves the realism of soil screening and supports science-based site management and groundwater risk control for emerging contaminants.

title: The role of central actors in improving the circular economy adoption in born-sustainable industries: Case of the offshore wind industry
abstract: Industries are increasingly shifting from linear to circular economy (CE) practices in response to growing resource pressures. Traditional industries, however, find this transition costly and difficult because their value creation models are long established, which creates rigidities that slow change. One way to avoid these barriers is for emerging sectors in the green transition to be born-sustainable. These sectors are designed around sustainability principles from the outset and continuously innovate to improve their environmental performance. Many of them are adopting CE practices to reduce reliance on virgin materials during manufacturing and to minimise waste at the end of life. Despite these intentions, overall CE adoption in born-sustainable industries remains limited. This study argues that the complexity of value chain structures plays a central role, since numerous stakeholders are involved and some hold more influence than others in driving progress. The research examines how central actors contribute to CE adoption in born-sustainable sectors through a case study of the offshore wind industry, supported by insights from the Solar PV and EV battery sectors. The analysis identifies regulatory bodies, asset owners and component manufacturers as central actors. It also shows that these actors need to engage in two types of collective-oriented governance collaborations, both within their industry and beyond industry boundaries. They are considered central because they can influence regulation, shape cross-industry CE initiatives, and build the collaborations needed to advance CE from a systemic perspective.

title: Enhancing early-stage hardening of autoclaved aerated concrete with high-dosage pisha sandstone through composite alkali activation and kinetic modeling
abstract: To mitigate the shortage of siliceous raw materials in autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC), this study explores the potential of replacing quartz sand with locally available, low-grade pisha sandstone (PS). Due to its high montmorillonite content, PS tends to absorb water and expand, significantly delaying the hardening of AAC green bodies. However, previous studies have mainly focused on the hydration behavior or low-replacement utilization of PS, while the hardening mechanism and process optimization of high-dosage PS-AAC systems remain poorly understood. To address this challenge, a composite alkali-activation approach using NaOH and Na2SiO3 is adopted. This method aims to sequentially activate reactive phases in both PS and fly ash (FA), thereby facilitating the co-development of mixed gel and expediting early-stage structural hardening. Under optimal composite activation conditions (1 wt% NaOH + 1 wt% Na2SiO3, 40 °C pouring temperature, and 60 °C pre-curing temperature), the PS content reaches 90-100 wt%, with t500 controlled between 1.9 h and 3.2 h, with no structural collapse observed. After autoclaving, the resulting AAC blocks exhibit compressive strength >3.9 MPa and dry density <541 kg m−3, meeting GB/T 11968-2020 A3.5/B05 grade requirements. Additionally, A mathematical hardening kinetic model is developed to predict the time required to achieve cutting hardness (t500). The model demonstrates high fitting accuracy (R2 = 0.95, MAE = 0.18 h, RMSE = 0.22 h) and can guide industrial process optimization. These findings demonstrate that mechanism-guided composite activation, combined with predictive modelling, enables industrially feasible, high-dosage PS utilization in AAC production.

title: Research on quality–energy–emission collaborative optimization framework for CO2-enhanced basic oxygen furnace steelmaking process
abstract: Complex interdependent relationships exist among smelting quality, energy consumption, and pollutant emissions in basic oxygen furnace steelmaking, making traditional processes unable to achieve multi-objective optimization. This study developed a quality–energy–emission collaborative optimization framework for a 120-t top-bottom combined blowing converter, establishing a three-phase flow heat and mass transfer mathematical model for CO2-enhanced smelting. Using multi-physics CFD coupled with Pareto optimization algorithms, the influence mechanisms of top-blown CO2 ratio and bottom-blown flow rate on dephosphorization, denitrification, energy consumption, and particulate emissions were systematically investigated. CO2's endothermic reaction characteristics effectively regulated molten bath temperature and extended the favorable dephosphorization time window, while bottom-blown CO2 significantly improved denitrification by diluting nitrogen's partial pressure. The optimized configuration (top-blown CO2 ratio, 11.4%; bottom-blown flow rate, 71.88 m3/(h·t)) achieved significant collaborative optimization: steel's phosphorus content decreased by 12.79%, nitrogen content by 11.97%; oxygen savings were 3.70 m3/t steel, with energy recovery increased by 1.91 kgce/t; the particulate generation rate decreased by 2.96 g/s·t and net CO2 emissions decreased by 13.60%. Industrial validation confirmed the effectiveness of this approach, providing theoretical support and practical solutions for steel-industry green transformation.

title: Distinct immobilization pathways of Pb and Cd in groundwater mediated by phosphate-solubilizing bacteria with hydroxyapatite
abstract: Microbially induced phosphate precipitation (MIPP) represents a sustainable approach for immobilizing heavy metals in groundwater. However, a comparative understanding of the immobilization mechanisms for different metals, particularly lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd), remains limited. This study elucidates the distinct fixation pathways of Pb2+ and Cd2+ in an MIPP system mediated by a phosphate-solubilizing bacterial consortium, using hydroxyapatite (HAP) as the phosphorus source. Our findings reveal a fundamental mechanistic divergence at the initial reaction stage. Pb2+ immobilization is predominantly driven by a HAP dissolution-reprecipitation process, facilitating its rapid conversion into highly stable, low-solubility crystalline phases such as Pb5(PO4)3Cl and PbC2O4. This efficient mineralization pathway resulted in near-complete removal (>99.6%) of Pb2+ at concentrations of 100, 300, and 500 mg/L within 48 h. In contrast, Cd2+, with its weaker affinity for phosphate, could not effectively engage in direct phosphate mineralization. Instead, its immobilization relied primarily on biosorption and complexation by bacterial cells and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), leading to the formation of multiple, less-stable phases like doped Ca8.6Cd0.7(PO4)6(OH)1.8, C4H6CdO4, and Cd(H2PO4)2. Consequently, the removal efficiencies for 50, 100, and 200 mg/L Cd2+ were significantly lower, reaching only 56.6%, 60.3%, and 38.7% after 48 h, respectively. This study demonstrates that within the MIPP framework, Pb2+ undergoes a strongly driven mineralization process yielding stable products, whereas Cd2+ follows a more passive and dispersed immobilization pathway with inferior stability. These insights, established at molecular and mineral scales, provide a critical theoretical foundation for the targeted regulation of heavy metal fixation via microbial mineralization strategies.

title: Scale effects, bundle evolution, and nonlinear thresholds of ecosystem services in the Yellow River Basin: Implications for zone-based ecological restoration
abstract: The Yellow River Basin (YRB) exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity and scale dependence in ecosystem services (ES); however, multi-scale ES relationships, bundle evolution, and nonlinear threshold mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Taking the YRB as the study area, this study evaluated carbon storage (CS), water yield (WY), habitat quality (HQ), and soil conservation (SC) from 2001 to 2022 at both raster and county scales. Their spatiotemporal dynamics, trade-offs and synergies, ES bundle evolution, dominant drivers, and nonlinear threshold responses were further analyzed. The results showed that: (1) the overall ES supply increased, with WY and SC increasing markedly by 98.60% and 43.22%, respectively, while CS showed a slight fluctuating increase and HQ declined slightly; (2) ES relationships were dominated by synergies, with CS–HQ exhibiting the most stable and continuously strengthening synergy. Its correlation increased from 0.46 to 0.56 at the raster scale and from 0.72 to 0.79 at the county scale, while the mean correlations of the three core synergistic pairs were 26.5%–48.4% higher at the county scale than at the raster scale; (3) four ES bundles were identified, namely the HQ–WY synergistic bundle (B1), multifunctional complex bundle (B2), low-function bundle (B3), and HQ–CS synergistic bundle (B4). Although the overall bundle pattern remained relatively stable, internal reorganization persisted, as indicated by the continuous expansion of B2 and contraction of B3, suggesting a shift from low-function and fragile combinations toward multifunctional and synergistic states; and (4) CS, WY, HQ, and SC were primarily controlled by vegetation, climate, human activities, and topography, respectively, with representative thresholds of normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) = 0.58 for CS, precipitation (PRE) = 511.06 mm for WY, human footprint (HF) = 15.75 for HQ, and slope (SLOP) = 3.20° for SC. These findings suggest that ecological restoration in the YRB should move beyond uniform implementation and adopt differentiated governance by zone, category, and intervention intensity according to ES bundle patterns, trade-off and synergy relationships, dominant drivers, and threshold characteristics. This study provides scale-adaptive quantitative evidence for zone-based ecological restoration and refined ES management in the YRB.

title: Exploring the green development path in western China from the perspective of spatial functional heterogeneity: An integrated application of fsQCA and machine learning
abstract: Exploring the configuration path and antecedent variable relative importance of green development level (GDL) in western China can offer realistic policy references for reconciling its economic growth with ecological security. However, the complex regional characteristics and fragile ecological environment of this region pose substantial obstacles to formulating effective strategies for high-quality green development. Building upon the theoretical foundation of national spatial function and adopting a system operation perspective, therefore, this study constructs a configuration framework that includes four dimensions of “driving-incentive-constraint-safeguard” according to the regional characteristics of three main functional zones (MFZs) in western China. This work then uses the dynamic fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) method to systematically explore the green development paths of 101 cities in these zones from 2006 to 2023. The three, four, and five feasible configuration paths for achieving the high GDL in urban, agricultural, and ecological MFZs are identified, respectively, which can be further classified into triple-dimension collaborative (A3, B3), dual-dimension supportive (A2, B1, B2, C5, C1), and single-dimension driven (A1, B4, C2, C3, C4) types. It is found that these paths have distinct multi-factor synergistic effects and regional heterogeneity, and most configuration patterns within each MFZ display significant temporal and regional variations. This work further quantifies the individual contribution of each antecedent variable for three MFZs by combining the machine learning models with Shapley Additive Explanations algorithm. The analysis reveals that the total emission reduction constraint serves as the primary determinant of GDL across all three MFZs, however, there are significant differences in the secondary key variable. This difference suggests that while unified environmental requirements can promote sustainable outcomes, their specific implementation requires policy adjustments tailored to different regions. These findings offer practical policy guidance and theoretical insights for formulating green development strategies in specific region of western China, while also provide valuable reference for developing countries pursuing harmonious coexistence between sustainable development and environment protection, particularly those facing comparable geographical constraints and developmental challenges.

title: Knowledge management and organizational sustainability performance: Dual mediating effects of knowledge auditing and supply chain learning
abstract: Drawing on the Knowledge-Based View (KBV), this study investigates how knowledge management (KM) processes drive organizational sustainability performance. Despite the recognized importance of KM, the specific mechanisms particularly the sequential roles of knowledge auditing and supply chain learning remain underexplored, especially in resource-constrained contexts like SMEs. Using PLS-SEM analysis of data from 206 manufacturing SMEs in Shanghai, this study tests a model where knowledge creation and acquisition influence sustainability performance through the dual mediating effects of knowledge auditing and supply chain learning. This “dual mediation” refers to a sequential pathway where knowledge auditing first assesses and organizes knowledge, which then enables targeted supply chain learning, ultimately enhancing organizational sustainability performance. Knowledge creation, but not acquisition, significantly fuels knowledge auditing. Knowledge auditing, in turn, is a vital catalyst for supply chain learning, which directly improves sustainability performance. The key finding is the validated sequential mediation: knowledge creation → knowledge auditing → supply chain learning → sustainability performance. This pathway provides an actionable model for SMEs to systematically convert knowledge into tangible sustainability gains, offering a clear theoretical extension of KBV into the sustainability domain and practical guidance for achieving Triple Bottom Line outcomes. This study makes three key contributions: (1) it expands KBV by empirically unveiling this specific dual-mediation pathway to sustainability; (2) it positions knowledge auditing as a critical, yet understudied, process that translates knowledge into actionable learning; and (3) it offers managers a clear blueprint: focus on internal knowledge creation and reinforce it with regular audits and supply chain learning initiatives.

title: From mismatch to reconfiguration: How environmental regulation and fiscal stimulus reshaped China's spatial carbon responsibility
abstract: China's carbon-neutrality challenge is complicated by the spatial separation between carbon-intensive production and ecosystem carbon-sink capacity. Existing studies have documented this mismatch, but usually treat it as a relatively stable pattern and assess policy effects mainly through emissions. Whether carbon responsibility has been reallocated across regions, and what has driven that change, remains less clear. Using a county-level panel spanning 2000-2023, we show that the historically negative association between carbon emissions and carbon sequestration weakens steadily over time, with developed eastern regions moving toward a positive association. The distributional evidence points to two turning points around 2006 and 2009: among top-GDP counties, emissions shares peak around 2006 and then decline while sequestration shares bottom out and rebound; among bottom-GDP counties, emissions shares rebound after 2009. Motivated by these facts, we construct a Carbon Responsibility Matching (CRM) Index that compares local carbon sequestration capacity with local carbon emissions, and examine how two policy environments reshaped spatial carbon responsibility: tightening environmental regulation under the 11th Five-Year Plan and the RMB 4 trillion stimulus. Regulation is associated with higher CRM, consistent with cleaner production adjustment together with improved ecological conditions. The stimulus is associated with lower CRM, consistent with an investment-led expansion of carbon-intensive activity supported by fiscal spending, credit growth, and construction-related land development. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that regulation is stronger where ecological capacity supports recovery, whereas stimulus impacts are more negative in regions with weaker green capability and more carbon-intensive industrial bases, and smaller where environmental governance is stronger. Overall, the results suggest that climate outcomes depend on how environmental mandates are coordinated with growth-oriented investment, underscoring the value of sink-inclusive responsibility metrics for safeguarding infrastructure programs.

title: Weak electric field accelerates aerobic granular sludge maturation via adhesion–biofilm–EPS restructuring with life-cycle trade-offs
abstract: Although aerobic granular sludge (AGS) represents a highly compact biotechnology critical for next-generation wastewater treatment, its full-scale deployment remains constrained by prolonged start-up and, more fundamentally, by the persistent tension between rapid granulation and structural stability. To overcome this bottleneck, we integrated a weak electric field (WEF) into a sequencing batch reactor to regulate microbial aggregation and systematically evaluated its mechanistic basis and life-cycle implications. Phenotypically, WEF markedly accelerated structural consolidation, achieving stable carbon removal, operationally defined as effluent chemical oxygen demand (COD) below 20 mg/L during routine monitoring, by day 25 compared with day 73 in the control. Compared with the control, the electrified system achieved 3.67-fold greater biomass retention and increased total nitrogen removal from 70.47% to 83.67%. Mechanistically, metagenomic profiling revealed that WEF did not act as a non-specific physiological stimulant, but rather as a selective ecological cue that restructured the microbial adhesion-biofilm-extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) axis. This shift was associated with elevated intracellular cyclic diguanylate monophosphate (c-di-GMP) signaling, triggering the targeted accumulation of tightly bound EPS proteins and the upregulation of genetic potential related to c-di-GMP turnover and surface sensing. This selective environment favored the robust enrichment of functional taxa, notably Candidatus Accumulibacter and Nitrospira. Crucially, the life cycle assessment indicated that, under the functional unit of 1 kg TN removed, the WEF-assisted system showed lower impacts than the control in 17 of the 18 midpoint categories, suggesting that the performance gains were sufficient to offset most electrification-related burdens. Although mineral resource scarcity increased because of electrode materials, WEF ultimately emerged, on a 1 kg TN removed basis, as a mechanistically targeted and environmentally favorable strategy for accelerating AGS maturation, supporting the energy-efficient intensification of modern water resource recovery facilities.

title: Travel-driven carbon emissions: Evidence from winter travel flow from Northeast to Hainan in China
abstract: Seasonal population travel flow refers to periodic, climate-driven relocations that shift energy demand and emissions across regions, significantly impacting carbon accounting and mitigation planning. This study develops a travel flow-induced emission assessment framework (TFIEAF) to analyze the incremental carbon emission caused by winter travel flow. A comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) of carbon emissions induced by winter travel flow from Northeast China to Hainan Province is first conducted, which is a long-distance population shift driven by climatic comfort. High-resolution travel flow data (2019–2023), regional electricity load statistics, and a time-series ARIMAX(1,1,1) forecasting model are integrated to quantify direct and indirect emissions across four domains: transportation, accommodation, energy consumption, and food Results reveal that winter travel flow contributed 2.47 Mt of incremental carbon emissions in 2020. Among the four components, accommodation and transportation account for 57.7 % and 28.8 % of the total, with air travel being the most carbon-intensive factor. Sensitivity analysis shows that no single mitigation action can independently meet China’s carbon peaking goals by 2030. A coordinated mitigation strategy across all sectors is required. The travel flow-driven emissions are generated in regions that do not host the permanent population responsible for them, thereby decoupling carbon responsibility from governance jurisdiction. This misalignment between the spatial origin of emissions and the actors accountable for mitigation introduces a blind spot in current carbon accounting frameworks. The proposed framework can be generalized to other seasonal travel flow scenarios globally, such as snowbird travel flows in North America or Europe.

title: Closed-loop supply chain recycling strategies for power batteries under blockchain traceability cost sharing
abstract: The rapid expansion of the new energy vehicle market has led to a substantial increase in retired power batteries, placing enormous operational and regulatory pressure on closed-loop supply chain recycling. As a tamper-proof and full-lifecycle tracking technology, blockchain can effectively mitigate information asymmetry in battery recycling. However, supply chain operations face severe incentive imbalance: upstream firms bear the full costs of blockchain deployment, whereas recycling benefits are shared by multiple participants, hindering sustainable recycling coordination. Existing literature predominantly focuses on blockchain supervision in forward supply chains while neglecting reverse recycling decision-making. Moreover, most relevant game models either ignore endogenous traceability costs or adopt a single leading investor setting, lacking comparative analysis of alternative blockchain leadership structures in three-echelon power battery recycling systems. To address these research gaps, this paper establishes a three-echelon Stackelberg game model with endogenized blockchain traceability investment. Four scenarios are compared, including the non-blockchain benchmark, supplier-led, manufacturer-led, and third-party recycler-led blockchain investment strategies. Backward induction is employed to derive equilibrium pricing, traceability investment levels, recycling prices, and profit distributions. Through numerical simulation and sensitivity analysis, this study identifies the optimal blockchain-leading participant and clarifies the cost threshold for profitable blockchain implementation. The findings provide theoretical support for cost-sharing contract design and standardized recycling policy formulation for power battery closed-loop supply chains.

title: Achieving the Global Methane Pledge through key pathways in inter-country production and consumption networks using feasible technologies at minimum cost
abstract: The Global Methane Pledge faces significant challenges due to the ambiguous attribution of methane emissions within complex global supply chains and the uncertain costs of mitigation technologies. To address this knowledge gap, the paper developed a multi-regional input-output model based on environmental expansion, reflecting global production and consumption networks annually during 2000-2020, covering 76 major economies and their 14 sectors. It innovatively proposed an Environmental Double Filtering Method (EDFM), which identified the key pathways of global methane emissions, and systematically estimated the emission reduction potential with feasible technologies and the lowest cost for achieving the goals of the “Global Methane Pledge”. It distinguished the methane emissions into those embedded in domestic intermediate input (DOE) and versus those in imported intermediate inputs (IME). The results reveal a highly concentrated emission structure: just 0.24% of all network linkages account for approximately 60% of global anthropogenic methane emissions. To achieve the 2030 targets, the aggregated potential reduction in optimistic case for DOE across key linkages are projected to reach 71600 kt with a cost of US$20.4 billion, for IME are projected to 4200 kt at a cost of US$0.3 billion. The analysis identifies distinct geographic and sectoral hotspots; cost burdens are primarily concentrated in Agricultural DOE (China, Brazil, Pakistan and Bangladesh) and Waste DOE (Russia, India and China), whereas significant negative abatement costs (profitable reductions) are found in Primary Energy IME (Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Canada, the United States, and Mexico). Notably, specific technological interventions, such as Alternate Wetting and Drying, manure storage covers in Chinese and Brazilian agriculture, demonstrate high feasibility. The research provides a systematic and quantitative approach for global methane reduction. These findings give a strategic roadmap for international collaboration, highlighting that focusing on a minimal set of high-impact pathways can lead to significant progress toward the Global Methane Pledge.

title: Assessing industrial-driven regional water vulnerability and targeted adaptive management: An integrated resilience-based framework
abstract: The high risk associated with industrial water use and the asymmetry of accident consequences shape decision-makers’ strong aversion to losses. However, existing water resource vulnerability (WRV) assessments often overlook decision-makers’ risk aversion and system resilience. To address this, this study develops an industrial-driven regional water vulnerability (IDRWV) framework integrating Driving Force-Pressure-State-Impact-Response-Resilience (DPSIRR) diagnosis, stochastic Deck of Cards (DoC)-CRITIC weighting, and prospect-theory-based K-means-TODIMSort classification. This framework distinguishes external response from endogenous resilience, quantifies expert cognitive divergence, and captures loss-averse vulnerability sorting. Anhui Province in China, a typical industrial-agricultural composite region, serves as the case study. Results indicate that the provincial IDRWV score increases from 0.5013 in 2012 to 0.8086 in 2023, while the number of cities reaching Level V or above rises from 1 to 13. The 2020 peak score of 0.8312 reveals the short-term effect of end-of-pipe treatment, but source reduction remains a bottleneck. Industrial wastewater environmental load ratio (q=0.6868) and total industrial wastewater discharge (q=0.6015) are the dominant drivers, indicating a shift from discharge-volume control to load-capacity mismatch management. The rigid industrial structure of heavy industrial cities along the Yangtze River causes their IDRWV improvement to lag behind, making resilience building the key to overcoming their developmental challenges. This study reveals that the key to the transformation of industrialized cities lies in establishing a water resource resilience system that aligns with industrial structures through adaptive management.

title: Automating production and innovation: How artificial intelligence technological innovation promotes green growth in China
abstract: Balancing economic growth with environmental protection is a major challenge for developing countries experiencing rapid industrialization. This study investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) technological innovation affects green growth through the dual channels of the automation of production and the automation of innovation. Using panel data of 282 Chinese cities from 2007 to 2022, we construct a city-level AI technological innovation index covering human capital, market application, and technological output. Green growth efficiency is evaluated using a super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model that incorporates undesirable outputs. The empirical results indicate that a 0.1-unit increase in the AI technological innovation index increases green growth efficiency at the city level by 0.08737 units (p < 0.01). This baseline effect remains robust after addressing endogeneity issues via an instrumental variable approach and conducting a series of robustness tests. Mechanism analysis reveals two primary transmission channels. First, through the automation of production channel, AI technological innovation enhances resource allocation and process control, thereby reducing energy waste and pollutant emissions per unit of output. Second, through the automation of innovation channel, AI improves the efficiency of green knowledge generation per unit of R&D input. These findings demonstrate that AI innovation can support cleaner production and sustainable urban transformation. This study provides new city-level evidence on the relationship between intelligent technologies and green growth, offering practical implications for policymakers seeking to align industrial automation and innovation strategies with environmental goals in emerging economies.

title: Touch performance and microfiber pollution potentials of commercial fleece fabrics
abstract: This paper aims to measure the skin touch comfort parameters and microfiber shedding potentials of commercially produced three-thread fleece (3 TF) fabrics objectively and quantitatively, which have not been presented before. Four different 3 TF fabrics – straight, double tuck, 3-butt diagonal, and 4-butt diagonal - were produced in an industrial setup using the same types of yarns, under identical knitting and finishing conditions with a cotton-polyester blend ratio of 70:30. The skin touch sensation of these fabrics was tested using the latest Fabric Touch Tester (FTT) from SDL ATLAS, initially developed by Hong Kong Research Institute of Textile and Apparel (HKRITA) and the Honk Kong Polytechnique University. To evaluate the microfiber shedding tendency of these fabrics, the material loss from the fleece fabrics during washing was determined following the BS EN ISO 4484-1:2023 and fiber shedding by mechanical abrasion was tested using an industrially practiced method known as pilling box-syringe test. Findings show that double tuck structure performs the best when the touch comfort properties and microfiber pollution potential are considered jointly. It also shows that the industrially practised pilling box-syringe method for testing fiber shedding suffers from limitations and needs further improvement.

title: Same protein, smaller footprint: Iso-nutritional life cycle assessment of demand-supply protein shifts
abstract: Animal-based protein production is causing substantive climate and nutrient pollution, particularly in livestock-intensive regions such as Flanders (Belgium), a European hotspot reliant on imported feed. A protein transition away from animal-based products can lower environmental impacts, but requires careful dietary design to retain full nutritional adequacy. Life cycle assessments (LCA) can quantify these environmental benefits, but they often rely on simplistic functional units such as kg protein, where they should instead be based on iso-nutritional properties. In this work, this is addressed by applying an LCA that accounts for essential amino acid composition, digestibility, and energy content to enable fair comparison across different protein transition pathways. The analysis compares two distinct transition pathways: demand-side dietary shifts (S1 Food-over-Feed and S2 Processing variants) and supply-side novel feed substitution (S3 Novel Feed Substitution), with a combined approach (S4 Stacked) also examined. Most environmental pressure originates in feed production and manure-linked emissions, while the most practical intervention points are located in food processing and diet composition. Replacing about one-third to one-half of pork portions with legume-based foods gives the largest environmental gains. Such a dietary change cuts greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 14-21%. By contrast, highly refined products of plant origin (e.g., protein isolates or concentrates) can increase GHG emissions due to higher processing energy demand, but offer advantages in nutritional precision, reduced land use, and formulation flexibility. In the novel feed substitution scenario (S3), replacing imported oilseeds (soybean meal from South American regions) with domestically produced alternative proteins (insect meal, microbial protein, and duckweed) reduces feed-related GHG emissions by 58–64% per kilogram of iso-nutritional protein (matched amino acid profiles and energy content) at the feed production gate. A combined strategy that includes moderate meat reduction and land-free feed substitution delivers the strongest and most balanced benefits, cutting GHG emissions by 14% and reducing acidification, eutrophication, and water use by 22–24% per kilogram of iso-nutritional protein at the food processing gate. Focusing on low-input crops, simple processing steps, and full use of by-products offers a clear pathway for livestock-intensive regions to reduce environmental pressure without compromising nutrition.

title: Ecological–social multilayer coupling network mediated by carbon sequestration service flows: Cross-layer driving mechanisms and social network–oriented synergistic optimization
abstract: Synergistically improving the matching efficiency of carbon sequestration services between protected areas (PAs) and built-up areas (BAs) was a critical pathway toward achieving carbon neutrality. However, existing studies were largely limited to static, single-layer spatial network analyses and neglected the coupling mechanisms between carbon cycling and the land surface thermal environment. Research broke through the traditional source identification paradigm and constructed a “carbon–temperature” dual-factor source identification framework. Second, a wind flow field model was introduced to dynamically characterize the pathways of carbon sequestration service flows (CSSF), and a machine learning model (LightGBM–SHAP) was applied to construct a nonlinear resistance surface. These methods jointly supported the establishment of an ecological–social multilayer coupling network (ESMLN) at the national scale of China for the first time. Furthermore, exponential random graph models (ERGM) were applied to reveal the topology and driving mechanisms of cross-layer connections within the ESMLN. Finally, the social network (SN) was used as the entry point to propose differentiated improvement pathways for carbon neutrality governance. The results showed that the carbon–temperature coupling perspective significantly improved the differentiation and balance of source identification. Ecological sources with composite characteristics of “high carbon sequestration and cooling island” were more conducive to delivering CSSF to the social system, whereas the high-temperature characteristics of social sources exerted significant resistance to CSSF reception. In terms of spatial patterns, SN and ecological network (EN) exhibited geographical supply–demand mismatches, while the cross-layer network (CLN) showed characteristics of sparse connectivity and structural fragility. In terms of network structural attributes, ecological sources occupying intermediary positions within EN were more likely to establish connections with SN, whereas highly clustered ecological sources showed weaker connections due to their geographically remote locations. In terms of planning optimization, five spatial planning scenarios were identified, and targeted optimization strategies were proposed from the perspective of SN. This study provided an innovative research paradigm for achieving carbon neutrality through ecological–social synergistic enhancement, spanning from source identification to network optimization.

title: Global wind and solar energy sustainable development potential and regional joint optimization assessment under Climate Change
abstract: Global wind and solar energy potential is vast, but their variability challenges grid stability. While regional assessments about wind and solar energy exist, global systematic evaluations on their stable development potential under climate change remain limited, especially regarding whether joint development across adjacent regions can mitigate their output volatility. This study integrates eight CMIP6 climate models to evaluate historical and future wind and solar energy supply stability for individual and hybrid systems, and explores volatility reduction via adjacent regional joint development. Results show significant, yet declining, global wind and solar energy potential with regional differences. Wind energy exhibits poor stability, with an average coefficient of variation (CV) above 1.2. Notably, wind-solar hybridization greatly enhances stability, reducing the CV to below 0.4. The results further demonstrate prominent advantages of adjacent regional joint utilization for mitigating wind and solar volatility. The average CV of wind energy density in all joint regions declines by over 0.2 with such joint development. Although solar and hybrid systems benefit less from geographical pooling, their variability also decreases. This study clarifies the regional potential of wind and solar energy for stable deployment worldwide under climate change and offers references for regional joint development.

title: Analyzing economic efficiency of global net primary production utilization within biosphere planetary boundary
abstract: Terrestrial net primary production (NPP) is a foundational ecological resource for agriculture, ecosystem services, and socio-economic development, yet rising human appropriation of NPP increasingly challenges the biosphere planetary boundary. Here, we refine the Human Appropriation of Net Primary Production (HANPP) framework by distinguishing consumptive NPP use through crop and livestock production from non-consumptive NPP-related value realization through eco-tourism. We introduce the Economic Efficiency of NPP utilization (EEN) to measure consumptive and non-consumptive economic returns per unit of directly appropriated NPP, while using HANPPluc as a complementary indicator of land-conversion pressure. Using data from 193 countries from 2010 to 2022, we quantified global NPP utilization structures, EEN, and regional differences in resource-use efficiency. Global HANPP exceeded the biosphere planetary boundary and generated approximately 5.4 trillion Int$ in annual economic benefits, excluding HANPPluc. Global EEN increased from 539.8 to 572.2 Int$ t C−1 yr−1 before declining after the COVID-19 shock to eco-tourism. Before the pandemic, eco-tourism contributed 26.2% of total NPP utilization revenue, highlighting the economic relevance of non-consumptive NPP-related value realization, although indirect ecological costs remain outside the direct HANPP accounting boundary. A hindcast validation showed low short-term projection errors, supporting the use of the model for aggregate trend assessment and scenario comparison rather than deterministic long-term forecasting. SSP1–SSP5 projections suggest divergent future HANPP and EEN trajectories, with 2100 estimates interpreted as exploratory endpoints. Under SSP1, global HANPP transgression may be gradually alleviated by 2100, and the contribution of eco-tourism to EENa may rise to 55.6%. Overall, EEN provides a bounded tool for comparing ecological resource efficiency and eco-economic structures within planetary boundaries.

title: Transitioning to a circular economy: A framework of economic analysis and measures of circularity
abstract: The transition to a circular economy (CE) is crucial for addressing the complex challenges of population growth, climate change, and the need to boost production in food, feed, fiber, and bioenergy amidst depleting natural resources. Even though circular economic systems comprise both market mechanisms and material flow systems and their feasibility and sustainability depend largely on their economic viability, the role of markets and the economics associated with their functioning have largely been ignored by the relevant literature. This paper presents a general, empirically relevant, integrated multimarket framework of analysis of the supply chain transition to a more circular system. The framework explicitly accounts for imperfectly competitive market structures at the various stages of the supply chain and for the joint production and disposability when modeling the relevant production technologies in the supply chain of interest. The framework can also be utilized to examine the market and welfare impacts of a number of changes in the demand and/or supply conditions due to increased circularity (like changes in consumer preferences, production technologies, costs and market structure), identify potential market failures and rebound effects, and inform the design of policies and strategies that can induce the system transition to a more socially desirable level of circularity.

title: Power play: A multi-criteria analysis of present and future battery technologies
abstract: Advancing electrification requires batteries that combine high performance with sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and supply-chain resilience.Post lithium-ion batteries (PLIBs) such as sodium-ion (SIB), lithium-sulfur (LSB), and solid-state batteries (SSB) are widely discussed as alternatives to today's lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet discussion of their technical and sustainability benefits and drawbacks remains fragmented.Here we present an integrated, multi-criteria assessment of twelve battery chemistries, combining cradle-to-gate life cycle, raw material criticality and material cost analyses with performance metrics, specific energy and energy density into a unified comparison.On average, PLIBs exhibit 114 % higher global warming potential and up to 461 % higher material costs than LIBs, particularly when lithium metal or specialty lithium chemicals are required.SIBs achieve 94 % lower criticality and slightly lower cost than LIBs, although their specific energy and energy density remain comparatively low.SSBs deliver the highest specific energy, outperforming LIBs, but depend on costly and less scalable materials.LSBs exploit abundant sulfur and offer high theoretical specific energy, but today's reliance on lithium foil and electrolyte-intensive designs lead to elevated cost, criticality, and carbon footprint.A sensitivity analysis demonstrates how improvements in specific energies enhance PLIB competitiveness.By linking sustainability, cost and criticality hotspots with performance, this study identifies targeted areas of improvement to guide next-generation battery development.

title: Sustainable lactic acid production from lignocellulosic biomass via circular salt recycling: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment
abstract: This study aims to develop and evaluate techno-economic-environmental performance of lignocellulosic biomass-to-lactic acid (LTL) processes integrating different fermentation, purification, and salt management technologies. We overcame significant challenges in process development by identifying the optimal combination of fermentation strategy, purification technology, and salt recycling scheme across five LTL process configurations. Among the proposed configurations, the KOH-neutralized fermentation with liquid-liquid extraction and dual recycling (K-LEDR) achieved the lowest minimum selling price (MSP) of 0.90 $/kg and global warming potential (GWP) of 0.74 kgCO2-eq/kg. The proposed LTL processes were further compared with other lactic acid (LA) production pathways utilizing corn, sugarcane, microalgae, and glycerol feedstocks, in which LTL demonstrated superior environmental performance with GWPs 68-89% lower than alternative pathways at a market-competitive price. Additionally, the industrial and social impact of LTL was investigated under governmental incentives and carbon taxation scenarios, in which combined government incentives reduced the MSP to 0.64 $/kg. A region-based analysis across major agricultural countries revealed that regional feedstock availability and energy systems significantly influence the process performance; for example, USA and Brazil for balanced economic and environmental performance, France for low-carbon LA production. Therefore, this work assists stakeholders and policymakers in the strategic planning toward economically viable and environmentally sustainable LA production from lignocellulosic biomass.

title: Agents of the circular ecosystem engaged in Preparation for Reuse (PfR) activities: a set of best practices for circularity
abstract: Preparation for Reuse (PfR) encompasses activities such as reuse, repair, refurbishment, remanufacturing, and repurposing, occupying a priority position within the waste management hierarchy by enabling the extension of the useful life of products and materials with lower additional consumption of resources and energy when compared to recycling and energy recovery. Despite its relevance, PfR remains underrepresented in public policies, monitoring instruments, and consolidated operational models, which limits its adoption on a broader scale. In this context, this article aimed to propose a set of best practices for the incorporation of PfR by organizations, thereby contributing to the transition toward a Circular Economy. To this end, this study adopts a qualitative multiple-case study research design and a systematic literature review, guided by an abductive analytical approach, systematic combining, which blends deductive and inductive elements across three interconnected phases. The results show that, although heterogeneous, these organizations share convergent patterns in operational, managerial, and institutional aspects. Based on these findings, the study systematizes best practices in a framework structured around five analytical dimensions – collection and logistics, operations and technical aspects, governance and management, financial sustainability, and social and educational practices – and in an operational flowchart that visualizes their application along the material trajectory. This framework supports the identification of bottlenecks, the prioritization of actions, and organizational self-diagnosis, helping organizations recognize which practices they already perform and which represent opportunities for development. Thus, the study contributes by providing applicable instruments that bring PfR closer to its concrete implementation as a Circular Economy strategy.

title: Hydrological connectivity regulates soil organic carbon stocks in coastal riparian wetlands within urbanized regions
abstract: Coastal riparian wetlands, including mangroves and tidal marshes, function as critical blue carbon sinks within urbanized regions, yet the effect of hydrological connectivity (HC) on soil organic carbon (SOC) storage remains poorly constrained. We addressed this knowledge gap using regional field measurements in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA). An HC index was developed at the regional scale by integrating four hydrological variables, including tidal inundation frequency, tidal hydrodynamic conditions, distance from wetland to estuary, and runoff. SOC stocks exhibited distinct spatial patterns across the GBA, and showed a clear inverted U-shaped relationship with HC, with thresholds varying between wetland types. Below the threshold, SOC sequestration was enhanced, associated with an increasing proportion of terrestrial organic carbon (OC) inputs and improving SOC stability. However, once HC exceeded the threshold, SOC stocks decreased with increasing HC, partly because of altered soil physicochemical properties, such as salinity and SOC optical properties, and SOC export, which reduced SOC storage. Based on the HC-SOC stock relationship, 32.4% of mangrove HC values and 60.8% of tidal marsh HC values have the potential to shift into the optimal HC range via hydrological regulation, where SOC stocks reach 85% of their maximum, increasing SOC stocks by 14.1% and 28.8%, respectively. Under this scenario, the regional estimation suggests a potential increase in carbon-credit value on the order of tens of millions of USD for the GBA. These findings highlight the potential to enhance SOC stocks in coastal riparian wetlands through strategic HC regulation with multiple hydrological variables, providing guidance for wetland restoration and carbon management in urbanized regions.

title: Waste heat recovery from flue gas inside MEA-based CO2 capture processes using heat pump technologies and associated environmental impact assessment
abstract: High regeneration energy severely restricts the large-scale deployment of amine-based post-combustion CO2 capture in coal-fired power plants, while heat pump technologies offer a promising route to recover underutilized low-grade flue gas waste heat and cut capture costs. This work establishes a standard monoethanolamine (MEA) CO2 capture model with an annual capture capacity of 1 million tons via Aspen Plus, and proposes an energy-saving scheme integrating absorber intercooling (AIC) with diverse heat pumps. Genetic algorithm (GA) is adopted to realize the automatic global optimization of process parameters and evaluate the energy-saving potential of different schemes. The optimized standalone AIC only achieves a marginal 1% reduction in regeneration energy to 3.81 GJ/t CO2. Among compression heat pumps (CHP), type-II absorption heat pumps (AHP II) and cascade heat pumps, CHP exhibits the best matching performance with flue gas waste heat in the MEA capture system. The CHP-AIC integrated process reduces solvent regeneration energy by 28.3% relative to the standard MEA scheme. Nevertheless, electricity-driven heat pumps induce notable environmental burdens despite remarkable heat conservation. Life cycle assessment reveals that electricity consumption triggers higher human toxicity and ecological damage, whereas thermally driven AHP II delivers superior environmental sustainability. This study systematically evaluates the energy-saving potential and environmental risks of multiple heat-integrated strategies, providing technical and theoretical support for the low-carbon upgrading of coal-fired CCUS projects.

title: Nuclear cogeneration in district heating systems: optimal pathways to decarbonization
abstract: Nuclear cogeneration—the use of nuclear plants in cogeneration mode to produce both heat and electricity—is a proven technology for decarbonized electricity generation and has already been employed in a number of district heating (DH) networks worldwide. However, despite its promises as an option for low-carbon residential and commercial space heating, expanding the use of nuclear technology requires substantial investment, whereas more established conventional low-carbon heat energy sources such as biomass and large-scale heat pumps are already available. At this juncture, the potential role of nuclear cogeneration demands thoughtful assessment. This paper aims to identify key factors influencing the optimal transition pathways to low-carbon DH systems with the potential to include nuclear cogeneration plants. We explore how nuclear cogeneration can fit into an optimized heat production mix at local scale alongside conventional low-carbon technologies. We develop scenarios to quantify the benefits of nuclear cogeneration in optimal multi-year DH network decarbonization pathways in various local-scale configurations and exogenous economic and policy conditions. Transport of heat produced is a pivotal factor in both the modeling and the economic evaluation. Our results suggest that integrating a nuclear cogeneration plant (NCP) into the set of technologies available to the DH planner could significantly reduce overall DH system costs, with larger and closer networks benefiting more from NCP availability. The economic competitiveness of nuclear cogeneration depends primarily on NCP-to-DH network distance, annual consumption of the DH network, and discount rate, rather than on carbon emissions caps or the prices of conventional fuel sources. We find that when it is cost-competitive to include nuclear cogeneration in the production mix, the NCP can largely replace conventional low-carbon heat generators and cover the bulk of district heat demand.

title: The impact of electric accumulator trade on energy efficiency in Africa: A mediation and threshold analysis
abstract: The demand for critical minerals has surged in recent years, driven by their essential role in clean energy technologies. Electric accumulators (EAs), which rely heavily on these minerals and their co-products, are central to enhancing energy stability and resilience. As African economies pursue growth amid persistent energy deficits and unreliable supply, understanding whether trade in EA technologies improves energy efficiency is increasingly important. Yet empirical evidence on this relationship and its transmission mechanisms remains limited. This paper examines the impact of trade in critical mineral-based electric accumulators (EAs) on energy efficiency across 34 African economies from 2010 to 2023, using the Shephard energy distance function and both linear and non-linear econometric approaches. Three key findings emerge. First, EA trade improves energy efficiency, with effects varying across income levels, regions, and resource dependence; gains are strongest in middle-income economies and Southern Africa, but weaken or reverse in resource-rich economies. Second, the EA–efficiency relationship operates through heterogeneous channels: electricity infrastructure reinforces trade-induced gains, whereas R&D inflows and industrial upgrading generate offsetting indirect effects. Third, the relationship is regime-dependent. Efficiency gains emerge only at higher levels of industrial upgrading, are concentrated in lower-R&D inflow environments, and reverse at high levels of renewable energy penetration, consistent with integration constraints. The findings suggest that trade in critical mineral-based technologies is most effective when embedded within coherent industrial, infrastructure, and innovation strategies tailored to structural and regional conditions.

title: An exploratory framework for flood risk assessment considering cascade effect of inundation volume in highly developed urban areas
abstract: Due to the escalating effects of global climate change and the rapid pace of urban development, urban flooding events are occurring more frequently, causing considerable economic losses and far-reaching social consequences. Evaluating flood risk is essential for effective urban flood management and the development of disaster reduction strategies. This study adopts a tracer-aided urban flood model to distinguish endogenous and exogenous flood volume, and establishes an exploratory framework for flood risk assessment considering cascade effect of inundation volume. The Haikou City's Haidian Island in Hainan Province, China was selected as the study area. Eight risk assessment indicators were chosen, and a combined weighting method that integrated the analytic hierarchy process with the entropy weight method was used to determine their individual weights. A spatial map depicting flood risk throughout the study area was created using the model's outputs. The spatial differentiation law of endogenous and exogenous flood risks was revealed. Furthermore, Comparative simulations of flood mitigation schemes demonstrated that the source-oriented regulation guided by the proposed framework delivers better flood mitigation performance. This study provides targeted technical support for refined urban flood risk management.

title: Rewiring the digital–ecological nexus: Utility tunnels and smart sustainable city performance
abstract: Smart city programs often emphasize digital efficiency, while sustainability agendas remain environmentally focused, leaving the digital–ecological nexus insufficiently measured and governed. Building on the UN smart sustainable cities (SSC) framework, this study constructs a composite SSC index that captures ecological infrastructure, technological capability, industrial transition, and institutional support. Using China’s Urban Utility Tunnel Pilot (UUTP) as a quasi-natural experiment and panel data for 270 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2021, we apply Double Machine Learning (DML) to estimate the causal effect of UUTP on SSC. The results show that UUTP significantly improves SSC performance, and the findings remain robust across alternative learners and specifications. DML-based causal mediation analysis provides evidence that UUTP affects SSC partly through Municipal Basic Service Capacity, Business Environment, and Energy Use Efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects in cities with higher green finance development, non-resource-based cities, and coastal cities. The findings advance a sociotechnical view of underground infrastructure as an enabling platform that supports service provision, market conditions, and green urban operation, and they offer policy guidance for embedding municipal infrastructure renewal into smart sustainable urban transformation in developing economies.

title: How capital supply shapes carbon emissions in China: Income-Based accounting and structural decomposition with asset lifetimes
abstract: Assigning carbon emission responsibility to primary input suppliers is essential for top-down mitigation. In China, decades of investment-led growth have created long-lived capital stocks, reshaping both the scale and structure of primary inputs. Income-based accounting of capital-enabled emissions is therefore crucial for understanding China's emission patterns. Building on an intertemporal capital service dataset constructed in this study, we develop an environmentally extended Ghosh model to quantify capital-enabled emissions across China's provinces, sectors, and asset types. We then apply structural decomposition analysis to identify the socioeconomic enablers and mechanisms through which the scale and structure of capital influence emissions. The results show that (1) capital-enabled emissions increased over time, with high totals in provinces along the Middle Yellow River, Northern Coast, and Eastern Coast, and carbon- and capital-intensive sectors were the dominant contributors; (2) economic growth was the main driver of increases in capital-enabled emissions, whereas other socioeconomic factors exerted net emission-reducing effects; (3) the net effect of capital scale reflects opposing accounting channels: the rising capital–labor ratio increased capital-enabled emissions, whereas labor-productivity gains and declining user costs provided combined offsets; and (4) changes in the sectoral distribution of capital services, rather than asset composition, accounted for nearly all of the temporal capital-structure effect. These findings show that capital-oriented mitigation priorities cannot be inferred from aggregate investment or capital growth alone but require attention to productivity, user costs, and sectoral capital allocation.

title: Region-specific strategies for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing emergy sustainability in China's apple production
abstract: China is the world's largest apple producer, yet its highly resource-dependent production model has resulted in resource misallocation and intensified environmental pressures, severely constraining sustainable apple production. Although external interventions can improve farmers' water and fertilizer management to jointly optimize yield and environmental outcomes, the spatial alignment between technological and orchard management practices and regional resource endowments remains insufficiently defined. We employed life cycle assessment (LCA) and emergy analysis to reveal spatiotemporal sustainability in China's apple production. Our main findings are as follows. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions increased 68% while emergy sustainability declined by half during 2000-2020. GHG emissions and ESI exhibited pronounced heterogeneity across major production provinces. These patterns were largely driven by fertilization intensity and orchard management practices in major apple production areas. Scenario analysis of key intervention points in apple production revealed that, by 2030, orchard area in the major apple production areas could be reduced by 26.5%, annual GHG emissions could decline by 32.8%, and ESI could increase by 67.0%.
