We propose region-specific optimization strategies for apple production, including fertilizer and horticultural management interventions tailored for the Bohai Bay production area, and integrated regional planning and optimization strategies for the Northwest Loess Plateau production area and the Yellow River Old Road production area in China. This study provides evidence that integrated scientific fertilization and orchard management practices implemented in the region both ensured apple consumption and enhanced environmental sustainability.

title: From agglomeration costs to green dividends: The U-shaped impact of digital industry agglomeration on inclusive green growth
abstract: Fostering the coordinated development of digital industry agglomeration and inclusive green growth is a crucial pathway for high-quality economic development in the digital economy era. Using panel data from prefecture-level cities for the period 2011–2024 and registered capital data from enterprises across six core digital economy sectors, this study constructs a city-level indicator of digital industry agglomeration and systematically examines its impact on inclusive green growth efficiency. The results show that digital industry agglomeration exerts a significant U-shaped nonlinear effect on inclusive green growth efficiency. Specifically, digital industry agglomeration suppresses inclusive green growth at an early stage, but its positive effect emerges and strengthens as the level of agglomeration increases. Mechanism analyses indicate that digital industry agglomeration influences inclusive green growth indirectly through three dimensions: technological innovation, employment optimisation, and livelihood inclusion. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the U-shaped effect is more significant in cities characterised by greater governmental attention to digital development and lower levels of market fragmentation. This study enriches the literature by introducing a novel interdisciplinary perspective on the relationship between the digital economy and green development and offers policy insights for optimising the spatial distribution of digital industries and deepening the integration of the digital economy with inclusive green growth.

title: Experimental and computational investigation on CO2 absorption kinetics of five piperazine-derived cyclic amines in aqueous/ether-water systems
abstract: Piperazine-derived cyclic amines represent promising solutions for efficient CO2 capture. However, fundamental understanding of their structure-activity relationships remains limited. This work combined experimental and computational approaches to elucidate the influences of cyclic structures and functional groups of piperazine-derived cyclic amines (PZ, 2MPZ, AEP, 1MPZ and 2HPZ) on their CO2 capture performance and the structure-activity relationship in both pure water and water-lean environments. Key findings reveal that substituents reduce nitrogen electron density and impose steric hindrance, impeding CO2 access to active sites. Stopped-flow measurements of the intrinsic kinetics of cyclic amines in aqueous and ether-water solvents revealed a reactivity trend: PZ > 2MPZ > AEP > 1MPZ > 2HPZ. The zwitterion mechanism demonstrates relatively good accuracy (AARD: 1.30%-2.66%) than base-catalyzed hydration (AARD: 2.62%-9.46%). DFT validates the zwitterion pathway, while MD simulations indicate that pure water solution maintains dynamic hydrogen-bond networks without outer-layer clustering. Ether addition disrupts hydrogen bonding and diminishes electron density at reactive sites, reducing absorption rates. These findings elucidate the underlying structure-activity relationships and solvation effects, providing a fundamental molecular-level understanding of the kinetic behaviors in water-lean amine systems.

title: Prediction model for adhesion characteristics between warm-mix recycled asphalt and aggregate based on machine learning
abstract: The interfacial adhesion between warm-mix recycled asphalt and aggregates is a key determinant of asphalt pavement durability. In this study, the adhesion performance between asphalt and aggregates was quantitatively evaluated based on the adhesion work derived from atomic force microscopy (AFM) force-distance curves, while microscopic information of asphalt and aggregates were obtained from Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), gel permeation chromatography (GPC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and AFM. Key features were extracted through systematic feature-preprocessing and selection procedures based on Pearson correlation analysis and distance correlation analysis. Model training and benchmarking were subsequently performed using convolutional neural networks (CNN), backpropagation neural networks (BPNN), and Elman neural networks to identify the optimal predictive architecture. Finally, L-Ra, L-Rz, J-Ra, IC=C, IC=O, RC=C, RC=O, Mw, CaO, and SiO2 were selected as the ten input variables for the model. The Elman neural network exhibits superior predictive accuracy and robustness, as demonstrated by its relative percentage error (RPE)、mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2). These findings confirm that the Elman neural network provides the most accurate and reliable prediction of asphalt-aggregate interfacial adhesion, enabling rapid estimation from routinely measurable microscopic parameters to reduce time-consuming tests and support rational design of high-RAP warm-mix recycled asphalt mixtures.

title: Synergistic effect of oxygen vacancies and metal-oxygen bonding in metal oxides for efficient As2O3 removal from coal combustion flue gas
abstract: The arsenic (mainly As2O3) emitted from coal-fired flue gas can cause deactivation of selective catalytic reduction (SCR) denitrification catalysts and pose serious risks to the global environment and human health. The oxygen vacancy (Ov) in metal oxides is considered to play an important role in the As2O3 removal. However, the action mechanisms of reactive oxygen species, metal-oxygen bonds, and O2 in the oxidation adsorption process of As2O3 are still unclear. In this work, the As2O3 removal by a single transition metal oxide was systematically investigated, followed by the extraction of theoretical descriptors that affect As2O3 removal, and the prediction and validation of the optimal arsenic removal bimetallic oxide. The results show Fe2O3 and Mn2O3 exhibit the highest adsorption ability (106.5 and 112.6 μg/g, respectively) among single metal oxides. Ov enhances metal atom instability and facilitates lattice oxygen (Ol) mobility, thus promoting As2O3 oxidative adsorption. Meanwhile, O2 can accelerate Ov formation by supplementing it and generating adsorbed oxygen (Oα), further enhancing the oxidation adsorption of arsenic. Given the important role of Ov in arsenic removal, the Ov formation energy is proposed to predict the optimal metal oxides, where NFe1Ce2 exhibits 1.39-1.72 times higher As2O3 adsorption ability than its single-component oxides. The Ce-O bond rupture increases Ov density and O2 replenishment-dissociation cycle increases surface electronic instability, which thereby promotes As2O3 oxidation, while Fe-O sites provide active centers for As2O3 fixation. Good pore structure and Ov content or formability are important factors affecting the excellent arsenic removal performance of metal oxides. This work unveils the atomic-level synergism between Ov and metal-oxygen bonds, providing a mechanistic basis for the design of next-generation arsenic removal materials.

title: An Animal-fur inspired strategy boosts electrochemical uranium extraction from seawater
abstract: Extracting uranium from seawater presents an almost inexhaustible fuel source for sustainable nuclear energy, but is hindered by its ultra-low concentration and complex ionic matrix. Inspired by the hierarchical and breathable structure of mammalian fur, which balances large surface area with efficient mass transport, we fabricated a self-supporting, integrated laser-induced graphene-amidoxime (LIG-AO) electrode that unifies conduction, adsorption, and mass transport into a hierarchical porous architecture. Via uranium extraction cell (UEC), this electrode achieved a uranium uptake of 99% within 48 h from 10 ppm simulated wastewater, and over 73% from natural seawater within 4 days—while simultaneously generating electricity—along with high selectivity and robust stability in untreated seawater under 7 days of continuous operation. More importantly, via multi-scale characterization and simulation, we illustrate the mechanisms underlying its high performance: the hair-cluster structure facilitates electrochemical pre-concentration of uranyl ions at the electrode surface, overcoming diffusion limitations caused by low concentration; topological defects introduced by laser synergistically boost the amidoxime groups' binding affinity for uranyl ions. This work demonstrates a bio-inspired strategy for designing high-performance electrochemical interfaces through structural and defect engineering, offering broad implications for resource recovery and energy technologies.

title: Long-term greenhouse gas emissions from an agricultural pond in subtropical hilly catchment: Patterns and drivers
abstract: Small water bodies like ponds are significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG), yet their dynamics and drivers in hilly agricultural landscapes remain poorly characterized. Through a six-year monthly monitoring campaign (2019–2024) in an agricultural pond from a subtropical hilly catchment, we quantified mean areal fluxes of 26.51 ± 10.43, 0.42 ± 0.37, and 0.04 ± 0.04 mmol m−2 d−1 for CO2, CH4, and N2O, respectively. Each gas exhibited distinct temporal pattern: N2O showed sharp summer pulses, CH4 peaked counterintuitively in winter, and CO2 followed a temperature-mediated seasonal cycle. Analyses revealed gas-specific drivers: N2O was strongly associated with nitrate nitrogen, CH4 with ammonium and organic substrate, and CO2 with dissolved oxygen and algal productivity. Importantly, antecedent rainfall and drought functioned as critical distal controls, creating episodic “hot moments” of N2O and CH4 emissions, whereas CO2 remained largely unresponsive to these factors. This shows GHG emissions stem not just from in-pond conditions but from the precipitation-driven hillslope-pond interactions. By resolving distal hydrometeorological factors from proximal biogeochemical controls via long-term monitoring, our study provides a refined basis for more accurately incorporating these dynamic ponds into regional GHG inventories.

title: Research on multi-agent collaborative waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) recycling strategy with government involvement
abstract: China's WEEE recycling rate remains significantly below market demand, hindering the industry's transition toward modern online recycling systems. This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game model involving recycling platforms, e-commerce platforms, and consumers under government regulation, using second-hand mobile phone recycling as a representative empirical context. Departing from traditional models that assume consumer homogeneity, we incorporate consumer heterogeneity by segmenting consumers into three distinct groups—Green Pioneers, Pragmatic Rationalists, and Traditional Conservatives—via K-Means clustering, each characterized by differentiated initial online recycling probabilities. Numerical simulations demonstrate that government intervention significantly incentivizes recycling participation and fosters inter-platform collaboration. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identifies critical thresholds for subsidy saturation and penalty-induced behavioral shifts. Robustness tests confirm the stability of evolutionary outcomes across diverse initial conditions and ±10% parameter perturbations; notably, Sobol sensitivity analysis identifies the recycling platform's unit processing revenue as the primary driver of cooperative evolution. The novelty of this work lies in integrating consumer segmentation into an evolutionary game framework, allowing for granular, segment-specific policy analysis. This study contributes to the literature by extending the standard tripartite game with consumer heterogeneity and providing actionable, data-driven policy recommendations for optimal government subsidy design and platform-level cooperation strategies. Limitations include the restriction to a single product category (mobile phones) and the reliance on cross-sectional survey data for parameter calibration, which may limit generalizability to other WEEE contexts.

title: Waste valorization by methacrylation of fish skin collagen for bioprinting of neural stem cells
abstract: The sustainability of bioinks derived from eco-friendly sources lies in their ability to utilize renewable and abundant biomaterials, thereby reducing dependence on finite resources and promoting waste valorization. Fish skin, typically discarded as a by-product of the fishing industry, presents an opportunity for repurposing into biocompatible bioinks, aligning with the principles of cleaner production. In this study, we present a method for extracting high-purity collagen from grouper fish skin, demonstrating a sustainable approach to utilizing this underutilized resource. The extracted collagen is further modified into collagen methacryloyl (ColMA), with varying degrees of methacrylation, to enhance its suitability for bioprinting applications. Rheological studies reveal the rapid gel formation of ColMA formulations upon UV-light exposure, enabling efficient utilization in additive manufacturing processes. Mechanical and physical evaluations of UV-crosslinked ColMA samples demonstrate their potential for use in Digital Light Processing (DLP) printing, facilitating the creation of complex structures with high shape fidelity. Notably, DLP-bioprinted neural stem cell–laden ColMA constructs exhibited high cell viability (above 85%) and proliferative capacity, while ColMA hydrogels also supported neurogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells under defined induction conditions, collectively highlighting the applicability of this waste-derived collagen platform for sustainable neural biofabrication and tissue-engineering applications.

title: Shifting to bio-based plastics in Austria: An assessment of options within the bioeconomy under land constraints
abstract: Bio-based plastics are promoted as a sustainable alternative to fossil-based plastics to reduce emissions, fossil fuel dependency, and environmental pollution. However, increasing bio-based plastic production can intensify land-use pressures through competition with food, feed, and bioenergy. By incorporating a detailed representation of bio-based plastics production into the mass-balanced accounting model FoodClim, we analyze an option space consisting of 432 scenarios for 2050 to explore the potential for a shift to bio-based plastics without expanding agricultural land and compromising food security in Austria. These scenarios combine assumptions for bio-based plastic demand with changes in diets, bioenergy consumption, trade patterns, and food losses. We find that a full substitution with bio-based plastics, assuming no other systemic changes, would increase the cropland embodied in domestic biomass inputs (domestic extraction and imports) into the Austrian bioeconomy by 0.29 megahectares (Mha), or 6.6%, under an ambitious plastic demand reduction scenario. In contrast, in the absence of any plastic demand reduction, this increase would rise to 0.41 Mha, or 11.2%, compared to the 2050 reference scenario. The option space reveals that 14.6% of the scenarios remain within domestic and global agricultural land limits, as defined by the 2020 baseline. These scenarios require at least shifts to less land-intensive diets, limited bioenergy demand, and improved food system efficiency, with the majority also involving a significant reduction in plastic demand. Without these systemic changes, a shift to bio-based plastics could result in land-use changes, posing risks to biodiversity and food security.

title: Crystal structure manipulation for enhanced activity of MnO2 in sunlight-mediated peracetic acid activation: Phase-dependent charge separation and activation mechanisms
abstract: MnO2 has shown promising prospects for the purification of antibiotic wastewater via sunlight-mediated peracetic acid (PAA) activation. However, the structure-activity correlative mechanism between the crystal structure of MnO2 and PAA activation has not been revealed. In this work, a series of MnO2 with different crystal phases (α-, β-, γ-, and δ-MnO2) were synthesized through microstructure engineering and applied to the degradation of chlortetracycline (CTC) via PAA activation under simulated sunlight. The degradation efficiency of MnO2 with different crystal phases for CTC was δ-MnO2 (94.23%) > α-MnO2 (89.70%) > γ-MnO2 (88.04%) > β-MnO2 (76.44%), demonstrating that δ-MnO2 exhibited the best synergistic effect with simulated sunlight in PAA activation. The identification of reactive species demonstrated that CTC degradation occurred through single electron transfer mechanism mediated by the metastable MnO2-PAA* complex formed by PAA interaction with MnO2 surfaces. Structure-activity correlation analysis revealed that variations in specific surface area and oxygen defect density among different crystalline phases governed MnO2's effectiveness in PAA activation under simulated solar irradiation. The high specific surface area of MnO2 offers abundant active sites for PAA activation, while the increased oxygen defects enhance both PAA adsorption and photogenerated charge separation efficiency. The separated charges subsequently reorganize the MnO2 surface properties and replenish the oxygen defects, enabling efficient and sustained PAA activation. This work reveals the structure-activity correlation mechanism between MnO2 crystal structure and PAA activation from the perspective of intrinsic properties.

title: Nitrogen in light-industrial biowastes: From functional characterization to thermochemical regulation strategies
abstract: Light-industrial biowastes with high nitrogen content (exceeding 2%) pose significant environmental challenges, as fuel-nitrogen released during thermochemical conversion is a major source of NOx precursors. Accurate identification of nitrogen functionalities by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is further constrained by overlapping N 1s signals, limiting precise nitrogen-regulation strategies. Here, nitrogen-containing model compounds were used to refine XPS peak assignment and an integrated strategy of hydrothermal pretreatment (HTP) and pyrolysis was proposed to better regulate nitrogen conversion. The results reveal a clear progression from nitrogen functional characterization to thermochemical regulation. Nitrogen exhibits a strong inverse correlation with lignocellulosic content, rising from 2% to 11% as lignocellulose decreased from 96% to 1%, providing a basis for biowaste classification. Refined XPS analysis enabled accurate identification for ammonium-N (401.9 ± 0.4 eV), protonated amine-N (401.4 ± 0.6 eV), amide-N (399.8 ± 0.4 eV), amine-N (399.4 ± 0.1 eV), and amino-N (399.1 ± 0.4 eV), resolving overlapping peaks near 399.8 ± 0.3 eV and 401.5 ± 0.3 eV. The corresponding thermal stability follows: pyridinic-N > pyrrolic-N > polyamide-N > ammonium-N > protonated amine-N. Guided by these characterizations, alkaline-active HTP intensifies hydrolysis and deamination of unstable nitrogen while suppressing Maillard-derived heterocyclic nitrogen, and subsequent Fe2O3-catalytic pyrolysis converts volatile nitrogen precursors into inert N2. Together, the conversion of total nitrogen into NH3–N and HCN–N were reduced by 64.2–65.6% versus conventional pyrolysis. These findings clarify nitrogen speciation and transformation in light-industrial biowastes and demonstrate an effective thermochemical pathway for coordinated source reduction and process control.

title: Fabrication of a flower-like MgIn2S4/BiOBr Z-scheme heterostructure via an in situ route for organic pollutant photodegradation
abstract: In this study, a Z-scheme heterojunction was constructed by the in-situ formation of MgIn2S4 (MIS) on BiOBr (BOB), yielding a composite with intimate interfacial contact. The optimized 10%-MIS/BOB heterojunction exhibited significantly enhanced photocatalytic activity toward the degradation of tetracycline (TC) and rhodamine B (RhB). The degradation rate constant for TC reached 0.0255 min−1, which is approximately 5.43, 2.58, and 2.11 times higher than those of pure MIS, BOB, and their physical mixture, respectively. Correspondingly, the RhB degradation rate constant was about 3.33 and 4.36 times that of BOB and MIS. Notably, the photocatalytic activity of the heterojunction was approximately 2.2 times that achieved by a simple mechanical mixture. This significant enhancement can be attributed to the strong interfacial coupling, which is proven to be crucial for boosting performance. A Z-scheme charge transfer mechanism was elucidated through radical trapping, band structure analysis, ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS), electron spin resonance (ESR) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). This pathway not only enhances charge separation but also preserves the strong redox potentials of photoinduced carriers, thereby promoting the generation of reactive species. Systematic parameter studies revealed that the heterojunction maintains high degradation efficiency over a wide pH range (3 - 11) and shows strong tolerance to common anions, except for sulfate due to competitive adsorption and radical quenching. Practical applicability was further verified in various real water matrices, where the catalyst retained robust performance. In summary, this work provides a comprehensive understanding of the interfacial charge dynamics in MIS/BOB Z-scheme photocatalysts and demonstrates their potential for efficient and stable wastewater treatment under environmentally relevant conditions.

title: A hybrid machine learning framework for enhanced day-ahead solar forecasting in large scale systems
abstract: Accurate solar power forecasting is becoming increasingly crucial for the efficient planning and operation of modern power systems as solar energy constitutes a growing share of the energy mix. This work evaluates the performance of various artificial neural network (ANN) models for day-ahead solar power forecasting. Through two case studies, it examines the impact of seasonal and weather-related variations on large-scale distributed solar generation. The analysis draws on solar power generation and weather data from the Imperial Irrigation District (IID) and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) in the United States from January 2019 to December 2022, with over 20,000 h of operational data. The bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) model demonstrated the highest accuracy in day-ahead solar power forecasting and was selected as the baseline for comparison. To further improve prediction accuracy, two ensemble approaches, namely weighted averaging and multi-input, were explored. The results show that both approaches improve forecasting performance relative to the baseline, yielding positive MAE-based skill score improvements on the order of several percent across seasons. In particular, weighted averaging provides stronger and more consistent gains in the IID case study, with skill score improvements reaching approximately 11% in favorable seasons, whereas the multi-input ensemble demonstrates more consistently favorable performance in the LADWP case study, achieving skill score improvements of up to about 13%. These findings suggest that ensemble formulations provide a practical framework for improving day-ahead solar power forecasting in large-scale distributed PV systems. The results further indicate that performance depends on regional characteristics and the structure of available meteorological inputs.

title: Prediction of breakthrough time in hydrogen purification from coke oven gas using deep learning model
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of obtaining breakthrough curves in hydrogen purification from coke oven gas (COG), this study focuses on a ternary H2/CO/CH4 system. A single-column activated carbon adsorption model for describing multicomponent dynamic adsorption behavior was established on the Aspen Adsorption platform, and its accuracy was validated with experimental data. The effects of inlet pressure, inlet temperature, and bed height on the breakthrough time of the three gas components were analyzed. To address the issue of numerical calculation iteration diverges in certain special cases with the conventional model and to improve the efficiency of breakthrough time prediction, a deep learning model was developed using inlet pressure, inlet temperature, and bed height as input variables. The optimal neural network structure was determined using the Bayesian optimization algorithm. Subsequently, model reliability and generalization validation were conducted on the established neural network. Specifically, three rounds of testing were separately performed on the two test sets, and the model's response to continuous variation of a single input variable was examined. The results showed that the average prediction errors of the six tests were 0.96%, 1.01%, 1.05%, 1.02%, 0.94%, and 1.06%, respectively, and the variation trends of the single variable followed the expected physical behavior. These findings demonstrate that the constructed neural network model possesses good stability, prediction accuracy, and generalization ability, and can effectively compensate for the problem of missing data caused by divergence in traditional simulation calculations. This provides a reliable data-driven method for rapid breakthrough time prediction and process optimization in hydrogen purification from COG.

title: Biodiversity at risk when businesses rely on narrow indicators
abstract: Businesses are major drivers of biodiversity loss and face increasing pressure to assess and disclose risks to biodiversity from their activities. Yet it remains unclear which indicators businesses rely on to measure biodiversity, and whether these indicators represent biodiversity broadly enough to support robust decision-making. We reviewed which indicators Global Fortune 500 businesses in high-impact sectors have reported using and assessed how well these indicators represent biodiversity. As of 2025, only 9% of assessed businesses had reported using biodiversity indicators. Businesses that reported indicators rarely applied more than one simultaneously, and these indicators captured only a narrow scope of biodiversity. Spatial correlations among the indicators were often weak, and sometimes negative, indicating that decisions based on avoiding high-value areas for one indicator, such as ecosystem integrity measured by Mean Species Abundance (MSA), may still degrade areas important for another, such as threatened-species importance measured by the STAR metric. We further identified ecoregions where comprehensive biodiversity assessments are especially critical because high values of multiple indicators, most notably threatened-species importance, coincide with areas projected to undergo high habitat loss by 2050. In 33 of the world's 846 terrestrial ecoregions, more than half of the aggregated value of each assessed indicator was concentrated in such high-risk areas, rising to at least 80% in 10 ecoregions. Most of these ecoregions occur in the tropics, where agricultural expansion and deforestation are the primary drivers of projected habitat loss. Composites integrating multiple indicators can reduce the risk of overlooking important values, but applying multiple individual indicators in parallel remains the most robust way to retain information on each biodiversity aspect.

title: Bridging the attitude-behavior gap in circular plastic management: Evidence from structural equation modeling at a Vietnamese higher education institution
abstract: Single-use plastic (SUP) consumption remains a critical sustainability challenge within higher education institutions (HEIs), even among environmentally aware student populations. This study aimed to investigate the determinants of SUP consumption and reuse behaviors among university students in a rapidly urbanizing emerging economy and to identify the structural barriers that prevent the translation of pro-environmental intentions into circular behaviors. A survey was administered to 608 students at Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City (VNUHCM) using a mixed-methods instrument that combined quantitative ordinal measures of consumption with attitudinal subscales derived from the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Data were analyzed using Ordinal Logistic Regression (OLR) and Path Analysis (via structural equation modeling). The results indicate that accommodation status was the primary driver of SUP consumption intensity (β = 0.32, p < 0.01), while demographic variables failed to predict reuse behavior (McFadden R2 = 0.015), suggesting systemic rather than motivational constraints on SUP consumption. Path analysis confirmed that environmental attitude strongly predicted behavioral intention (β = 0.31, p < 0.001), yet the intention-to-reuse-behavior pathway was substantially attenuated (β = 0.18, p < 0.01). The structural barrier “Lack of Alternatives” exerted a significant, direct negative effect on reuse behavior (β = −0.15, p < 0.001), indicating that institutional supply chain design is the primary obstacle to achieving circularity. These findings demonstrate that persistent SUP use in HEIs is a system design failure, not a behavioral deficit, and that effective interventions must prioritize supply-side procurement reform over awareness campaigns. The integrated TPB-structural barriers framework developed in this study offers a methodological template for diagnostic assessment of circular transition barriers in HEIs, which requires site-specific empirical validation before quantitative findings are transferred to other institutional or national contexts.

title: Evolution and mechanism of industrial carrying status in desertification reversal areas through “load-carrier” spatiotemporal interaction
abstract: Scientific assessment of the industrial carrying status in desertification reversal areas is critical for optimizing industrial layout and supporting high-quality economic development. Using Yanchi County, China as a representative case, this study develops an indicator system to evaluate industrial load and industrial carrier within a spatiotemporal “load-carrier” interaction framework. We integrate geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR), the coupling coordination degree model (CCD), spatial Markov chains, and geographically weighted random forest (GWRF) to examine spatiotemporal evolution patterns and underlying mechanisms from 2005 to 2023. Results indicate that: 1) industrial load shows a clear spatial gradient, with higher values in the northeast and lower values in the south, whereas high industrial carrier levels concentrate around the county seat and adjacent areas, remaining relatively low in central and southern zones. Industrial load and industrial carrier exhibited a predominantly synergistic growth pattern, although the strength of their synergy varied across spatiotemporal contexts. 2) The industrial carrying status improves steadily over time, exhibiting pronounced path dependence and spatial spillover effects, with transitions dominated by incremental upgrading. Low level areas tend to display a lock-in effect when embedded in low level neighborhoods, while proximity to high level areas substantially increases the likelihood of upward transitions. 3) Multiple factors jointly shape the industrial carrying status; among them, manpower resource, technological innovation capability, desertification control, transportation construction, and geographic distance emerge as the dominant determinants. The industrial carrying status evaluation methodology developed in this study enables policymakers to diagnose whether industrial carrying status is constrained by excessive load or insufficient carrier capacity, providing targeted guidance for promoting coordinated eco-economic development in desertification reversal areas.

title: Changes in perceptions of cultural ecosystem services in urban coastal park during different phases of COVID-19: Integrating the prompt engineering and aspect-based sentiment analysis with a large language model
abstract: Understanding changes in cultural ecosystem services (CES) perceptions across different COVID-19 pandemic phases is vital for human well-being. While social media big data are increasingly used for CES evaluation, few studies harness AI's intelligent advantages to process massive data and reveal changes across pre-, during, and post-COVID-19 phases. This study integrates prompt engineering and aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) into large language models (LLMs). Four LLMs are compared with three baseline models trained on different datasets using Chinese RoBERTa; the best-performing LLM (DeepSeek-V3.2-Reasoner) is selected, and a topic model is applied to analyze changes in public concern, based on social media comments from Wuyuan Bay, China. Results show that in three ABSA tasks—aspect identification, sentiment score, and sentiment polarity—LLMs outperform baselines with limited training data. When data increase to 30000, three LLMs perform slightly lower than the baseline models on the aspect identification task, but still outperform them on remaining tasks. Nine CES categories were identified, with recreation, aesthetic, social relation, and health/wellness showing higher frequencies and positive sentiment (>3.0). Across phases, perception frequencies and sentiment scores of recreation and social relation continuously increased, while aesthetic and health/wellness first increased then declined. Public concern content included four topics; parent-child leisure proportion increased continuously. Overall, compared to baselines, all prompt engineering-based LLMs demonstrated data efficiency advantages. Meanwhile, they exhibited cross-model generalizability in certain tasks. This study demonstrates the relative advantages of the method in CES evaluation and can offer recommendations for further optimizing urban coastal parks.

title: An integrated life-cycle assessment of three different propulsion pathways for medium-sized wheel loaders under Nordic quarry conditions: A case study
abstract: Non-road mobile machinery (NRMM) represents a hard-to-abate segment because of high power demand, long operating hours, and limited charging or refuelling flexibility. To address the limited evidence linking life-cycle climate performance and economic competitiveness in NRMM, this study applies an integrated life-cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic assessment (TEA) to three propulsion pathways for medium-sized wheel loaders operating under Nordic quarry conditions: diesel internal-combustion engines, battery-electric drivetrains, and hydrogen fuel-cell electric systems. Environmental performance is evaluated using a work-normalised functional unit (kg CO 2 -eq t −1 moved), while economic performance is assessed using relative-adjusted total cost of ownership (RA–TCO, € t −1 moved), complemented by net present cost and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Under the assessed Nordic electricity, energy-price, utilisation, and quarry-duty assumptions, battery-electric wheel loaders achieve the lowest life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions and RA–TCO across the four countries considered. This outcome is driven by high drivetrain efficiency, comparatively low grid-carbon intensity, and lower energy expenditure per unit of productive work. Hydrogen results are strongly dependent on the production pathway and upstream electricity supply. Renewable hydrogen can reduce life-cycle emissions relative to diesel under low-carbon electricity conditions, but remains cost-disadvantaged in the modelled cases, whereas grid-based electrolytic hydrogen can exceed diesel impacts when supplied by carbon-intensive electricity. Investment support and shared infrastructure improve battery-electric economics, while the hydrogen pathways remain more sensitive to fuel price and infrastructure utilisation. The findings indicate that battery-electric propulsion is the most robust option for the medium-sized wheel-loader application and Nordic quarry conditions evaluated in this study. The results should not be interpreted as a universal ranking for all NRMM applications, duty cycles, electricity systems, or regional markets.

title: Towards a circular water economy in Southeast Asian cities
abstract: Water supply continuity and quality are significant policy challenges in developing countries, exposing shortcomings in resourcing, infrastructure, and governance capacity. At the same time, water policy often remains embedded in a command-and-control paradigm that relies on perpetual technological innovation and infrastructure investment to offset increasingly unsustainable demand patterns and management inefficiencies. This article explores the opportunities and challenges of integrating a circular-based perspective at the urban scale to overcome exploitive and inefficient patterns of water management, focusing on Southeast Asia. Emerging from the realm of industrial production, the circular economy emphasizes waste reduction and reuse. The circular water economy can be used a means for addressing supply scarcity. While a physical circular water economy would still primarily be local or national in scale, we posit that policy coordination, knowledge exchange, and institutional learning across Southeast Asia urban areas can complement localized circular water practices by generating a community of practice. The article concludes with six practical pathways to realizing this ambition.

title: Effect of alkanolamine molecular structure on the complexation activation of steel slag: A mechanistic study
abstract: To elucidate the mechanistic influence of alkanolamines with distinct molecular structures on steel slag hydration, this study deconstructs the hydration process into discrete dissolution and precipitation stages. A combination of conductivity measurements, ICP-AES elemental analysis, and coprecipitation experiments was employed to investigate how structurally varied alkanolamines affect the dissolution–precipitation behavior of steel slag. Results show that the isopropanol groups and the number of amino groups collectively govern the selective complexation ability of alkanolamines toward different metal ions. Specifically, diamine-structured N,N,N′,N'-tetrakis (2-hydroxyethyl)ethylenediamine (THEED) exhibits the strongest complexation capacity, while triethanolamine (TEA) shows the weakest. Alkanolamines containing isopropanol groups display competitive complexation characteristics in multi-ion systems. Diethanol-isopropanolamine (DEIPA) preferentially complexes Fe3+, whereas ethanol-diisopropanolamine (EDIPA) shows a preference for Al3+. All four alkanolamines inhibit the precipitation of portlandite (CH) and ettringite (AFt). In contrast, while they have little effect on the participation of Ca2+ in C-S-H formation, they actively promote the incorporation of silicate ions, which consequently lowers its Ca/Si ratio. Owing to its strong affinity for Fe3+, THEED markedly suppresses the precipitation of ferric hydroxide (FH). The enhancement in 3-day compressive strength of steel-slag pastes by alkanolamines is primarily attributed to their ability to promote the dissolution of Ca2+ and Al3+ via complexation, without substantially inhibiting the precipitation of hydration products. Among the four alkanolamines, DEIPA and EDIPA addition results in higher early strength. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the structure-dependent complexation activation of steel slag and clarify how alkanolamine molecular structure regulates its early hydration behavior.

title: Coupling coordination between energy–environment–economy systems and human well-being under the SDGs: Evidence from the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei urban agglomeration
abstract: Against the slowdown in global Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) delivery, the disconnect between energy–environment–economy (3E) coordination and human well-being (HWB) improvement has become a key bottleneck for people-centered clean transition in urban agglomerations. Existing 3E coupling studies focus on internal synergy but rarely examine its translation into HWB gains. This study develops an SDG-oriented 3E–HWB framework, conceptualizes HWB as the end product of coordinated 3E development rather than a parallel subsystem, and applies CCD, two-dimensional development mode classification, and XGBoost–SHAP to 13 BTHUA cities from 2015 to 2022. Results show that: (1) The 3E development index and HWB outcome index increased annually by 3.45% and 3.50%; the environmental subsystem remains the primary constraint despite its largest improvement margin. (2) The internal 3E CCD and 3E–HWB outcome CCD rose steadily with spatial heterogeneity: Baoding recorded the largest increase (121.55%), Chengde remained dysfunctional, and by 2022 Beijing reached 1.0 while most Hebei cities exceeded 0.5, indicating improved conversion efficiency from 3E synergy to HWB gains. (3) The BTHUA shifted from imbalance to high-quality coordination, forming four trajectories: Leading, Leapfrogging, Breakthrough, and Potential Cities. (4) Dominant explanatory factors showed temporal and typological heterogeneity, with innovation input, resource-use efficiency, environmental constraints, and livelihood indicators exerting differentiated marginal effects across city types, while the explanatory emphasis shifted from scale expansion to efficiency- and innovation-related factors. This study extends traditional 3E research toward outcome-oriented well-being improvement and supports differentiated cleaner production policies, people-centered green transition, and coordinated regional sustainable development.

title: Study on the impact of recycled plastic introduction methods on the performance of asphalt mixtures
abstract: Each year, millions of tons of waste plastic are produced, yet the recycling rate remains low. Incorporating recycled plastics into asphalt pavement construction is a promising approach to utilizing waste plastics beneficially. Various methods exist for introducing recycled plastics into asphalt mixtures; however, most past studies have focused on laboratory-produced plastics-modified asphalt mixtures. Plant production conditions differ significantly from those in laboratory settings and may therefore affect the performance of plastic-modified asphalt mixtures. This study evaluated how plant- and laboratory-based introduction methods of recycled plastics influence asphalt mixture performance, particularly at high application rates. Recycled plastics, a blend of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and low-density polyethylene (LDPE), were introduced into plant-produced loose asphalt mixtures in the plant and laboratory, respectively. Recycled PE was added at rates of 0%, 0.75%, and 1.5% of the total asphalt mixture mass, respectively. The results showed that the introduction methods had a significant influence on asphalt mixture performance in terms of rutting and fatigue cracking resistance. The addition of 1.5% plastics resulted in a 45.5% increase in cracking resistance for laboratory-introduced mixtures, whereas a 24.4% reduction was observed for plant-introduced mixtures. The absorption of maltenes by recycled PE and the reinforcing effects of recycled plastics are believed to play key roles in performance outcomes. This study demonstrated the importance of using realistic production conditions when evaluating the performance of recycled plastics-modified asphalt mixtures.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics and influencing factors of phosphorus metabolism in China's food consumption and disposal system
abstract: Phosphorus (P) scarcity and its environmental accumulation pose dual challenges to global sustainability, particularly for populous nations undergoing rapid dietary transitions. However, the spatiotemporal evolution and socioeconomic factors associated with P flows in China's food consumption and disposal system remain insufficiently characterized. Here we integrate Substance Flow Analysis (SFA) with a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to examine P metabolism across 31 Chinese provinces (excluding Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) from 2015 to 2023. We reveal a pronounced urban-rural dichotomy: urban P input expanded by 7.47% while rural input contracted by 2.00%, accompanied by declining P loss rate from 64.36% to 55.27% and rising recovery rate from 7.15% to 12.09%. Spatial econometric analysis identifies animal-based food consumption share as the factor most strongly associated with P input, and urban sewage treatment capacity as the factor most strongly negatively associated with P discharge, both exhibiting significant spatial spillover effects, suggesting the presence of interprovincial linkages in P metabolism. Based on these findings, we propose a diagnosis-regulation-governance framework with regionally coordinated and urban-rural differentiated management pathways. This work advances understanding of P metabolism's spatial dimension and provides scientific foundations for cross-regional sustainable P strategies applicable to transitioning economies worldwide.

title: Decarbonized synthesis of feed-grade calcium phosphates via alkaline conversion of calcite-rich phosphate mining waste
abstract: An integrated alkaline–acid route was investigated to convert calcite-rich phosphate mining waste (CRWR) into feed-grade calcium phosphates while avoiding the direct CO2 evolution associated with conventional acid–carbonate neutralization. The key concept is to decouple carbonate conversion from phosphate synthesis: CaCO3 contained in CRWR is first reacted with NaOH to form a Ca(OH)2-rich solid intermediate and soluble Na2CO3, thereby transferring carbonate carbon into a recoverable carbonate salt instead of releasing it as gaseous CO2 during H3PO4 addition. Statistical optimization using Plackett–Burman screening and Central Composite Design showed that NaOH concentration and solid-to-liquid ratio were the dominant parameters controlling CaCO3 conversion. Under optimized conditions of 7.95 mol L−1 NaOH, 4.28 g CRWR per 50 mL solution, and 26 min reaction time, 88% CaCO3 conversion was achieved. Subsequent crystallization recovered 86% of the carbonate as Na2CO3, corresponding to 0.33 t CO2-equivalent stabilized per tonne of initial calcite, or approximately 0.27 t CO2-equivalent per tonne of CRWR considering its calcite content. The Ca(OH)2-rich intermediate was then neutralized with H3PO4 to synthesize phase-pure dicalcium phosphate (DCP) and monocalcium phosphate (MCP), both showing citric acid solubilities above 90% and meeting key feed-grade requirements. Thermodynamic calculations supported the spontaneous and exothermic nature of the alkaline conversion, while a preliminary techno-economic assessment indicated promising process potential. Overall, this work demonstrates a proof-of-concept cleaner-production route that combines calcite-rich waste valorization, direct CO2-emission avoidance, carbonate stabilization as Na2CO3, and feed-grade phosphate synthesis.

title: Sustainable acrolein production from gas-glycerol catalytic dehydration over low-cost and high-efficiency industrial Kaolin-based catalysts
abstract: Acrolein production from gas-glycerol presented a promising and alternative approach to the traditional fossil feedstocks. For this, a series of phosphorus-modified kaolin catalysts (P-K) with different P2O5 loadings were prepared by one-step facile and economical impregnation method. P-K30 exhibited optimal catalytic performance, achieving 98.9 % glycerol conversion and 93.1 % acrolein selectivity at 300 °C, surpassing most reported phosphorus-modified catalysts. Moreover, P-K30 maintained high activity and selectivity over 30 h of continuous reaction, demonstrating good catalytic stability. Characterizations including XRD, BET, SEM, FT-IR, NMR, Py-IR, and NH3-TPD revealed strong interactions between P2O5 and kaolin, which induced the reconstruction of aluminum coordination environments. These interactions generated [AlO4], [AlO5], [AlO6] and AlPO4 species as strong Lewis acid sites, and formed [AlO4-O-P-OH] moieties and [Si-OH-Al] bridged hydroxyls as weak Brønsted acid sites, thus constructing an efficient Lewis-Brønsted acid synergistic system that effectively suppressed side reactions. This work provided a low-cost catalytic strategy for the high-value valorization of bioglycerol and showed great promise for industrial applications.

title: Study on durability property and environmental benefit of modified asphalt containing high-volume lithium slag under different aging conditions
abstract: The recent growth in the production of new energy vehicles and smart devices resulted in the great amount of lithium slag (LS), whose traditional landfilling disposal method posed a severe challenge to the environmental concerns and heavy burden to the land resources. And the large quantity of active nano-oxides in LS provided the prospect for its application in asphalt pavement. In this study, five kinds of lithium slag modified asphalt (LSMA) were prepared to investigate the durability performance and environmental benefit. Rolling thin film oven (RTFO) test, pressurized aging vessel (PAV) test and ultraviolet (UV) aging test were applied in all samples to simulate the aging conditions. The fourier transform infrared (FTIR) test, multiple stress creep recovery (MSCR) test, temperature sweep (TS) test and linear amplitude sweep (LAS) test were conducted to evaluate the impact of anti-aging performance. The carbon emissions were assessed and compared between traditional landfilling disposal and application of LSMA. The chemical results revealed that active chemical components of LS exerted limited influence on the fundamental structure of virgin binder, facilitated the formation of network and contributed to positive functional groups. And the rheological tests indicated that LSMA enhanced the stress sensitivity, aging durability and fatigue failure cycles when compared to virgin binder. The recommended powder-binder ratio of LS was in the range from 0.8 to 1.0, which achieved desirable durability and rheological performance. The environmental assessment showed that the utilization of LS1.0 in asphalt pavements reduced lifecycle carbon emissions by approximately 62.41% when compared to traditional landfill disposal. The findings provided a sustainable solution for high-volume industrial solid waste valorization and low-carbon infrastructure development.

title: Collaborative optimization of capacity configuration and interest equilibrium for wind-photovoltaic-hydrogen-biogas multi-energy system towards negative emissions and deep sustainability
abstract: To address climate challenges, global temperature control targets become a consensus-based action guide, with negative emissions as a vital pathway to achievement. However, despite being ideal integration scenarios for bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS), multi-energy complementary systems (MECSs) remain limited to zero-carbon level in current research. To mitigate this limitation, this study integrates the probabilistic scenario generation approach, establishes an optimistic collaborative capacity configuration model, and devises a heterogeneous collaborative three-stage interest equilibrium framework for the wind-photovoltaic-hydrogen-biogas MECS, targeting negative emissions and deep sustainability. Results demonstrate that the constructed system delivers a net profit of 4.73 million CNY and an annual carbon emission reduction of 19,984 tons. Compared to the natural gas-driven MECS, these metrics represent improvements of 2.06% and 50.66%, respectively, delivering significant economic and environmental benefits. Scenario analysis validates outstanding negative emission benefits of BECCS, while comparative analysis verifies the rationality of the optimized planning. In the interest equilibrium process, the role positioning of system entities dynamically adjusts as consideration factors are progressively integrated, ultimately achieving a higher degree of alignment between each entity's interests and their overall contributions. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis of parameter volatility not only validates the sound applicability of the designed interest equilibrium model but also shows that system benefits align with carbon trading price trends, indicating promising prospects for the constructed system. This study provides practical paradigms for the implementation of similar complex energy systems, and offers theoretical references for the collaborative practice of multi-entity alliances.

title: Leveraging common ownership: Socially responsible investors and corporate green transition behavior
abstract: This paper examines whether socially responsible investors (SRI) are associated with corporate green transition through common ownership networks. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we find that SRI common ownership is positively associated with green information disclosure, green patenting activity, and the consistency between firms’ green statements and green actions, whereas the corresponding association is weaker or negative for non-SRI common ownership. We further document stronger associations when common ownership networks are broader, among non-state-owned enterprises, and under stronger external environmental regulation and analyst coverage. Mechanism-related evidence is most consistent with scaled green governance and the alleviation of financing constraints, while the competition-mitigation channel appears more conditional and less stable. Overall, the findings suggest that common ownership may be one context in which socially responsible investors are associated with more active corporate green-transition-related behavior, while the strength of this association remains context-dependent.

title: In-situ upgrading of waste passenger car tires via molten salt thermal treatment: Effects of particle size and temperature
abstract: Waste passenger car tires present significant recycling challenges due to their low thermal conductivity and high ash and sulfur contents, which frequently result in suboptimal product quality during conventional pyrolysis. To overcome the limitations of complex post-treatment processes, a molten salt thermal treatment method utilizing NaOH-Na2CO3 medium was proposed to achieve the in-situ upgrading of pyrolysis products. In this study, the effects of operating temperature (425-575 °C) and feedstock particle size (6-10 mm) on products were systematically evaluated. Experimental results indicate that the molten salt medium significantly enhanced heat transfer and catalytic cracking, which effectively fixed CO2 and led to a 19-fold surge in H2 production, peaking at 5.57 mmol/g. For the liquid-phase products, the introduction of molten salt significantly promoted the dealkylation of substituted aromatics, increasing the benzene concentration by 5.43 to 8.61 times. Furthermore, the molten salt effectively overcame the mass transfer resistance of larger particles, facilitating the extensive formation of monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Notably, at the solid-phase interface, the molten salt acted as an efficient in-situ purifying agent, reacting directly with inorganic impurities (SiO2, CaCO3) and sulfides to form highly water-soluble salts. This mechanism achieved a maximum deashing ratio of 71% and a desulfurization ratio of 36.74%, yielding a high-value pyrolytic char with a carbon content exceeding 90%. Overall, this approach demonstrates that the thermal conversion products of low-quality passenger car tires can be significantly upgraded, providing a highly efficient pathway for comprehensive resource recovery.

title: Enhanced glyphosate biodegradation by heavy metal-tolerant microbial consortium QLBS in co-contaminated environment: Kinetics and metabolic pathways
abstract: The extensive application of glyphosate has led to widespread environmental contamination, which is further exacerbated in sites co-contaminated with heavy metals. However, most reported glyphosate-degrading microorganisms or consortia are ineffective under multi-stress conditions, particularly in the presence of toxic metals that strongly inhibit microbial metabolism and degradation efficiency. Thus, a critical knowledge gap remains in developing robust microbial consortia capable of degrading glyphosate under heavy metal stress in realistic environmental matrices. In this study, we isolated a novel heavy metal-tolerant microbial consortium, QLBS, which exhibits high-efficiency degradation of glyphosate and its major product aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA). QLBS can degrade up to 98% of glyphosate (<800 mg/L) within 6 d. UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified the presence of both AMPA and sarcosine pathways in the degradation process facilitated by QLBS. Furthermore, QLBS exhibits robust colonization capabilities in slurry and soil systems, contributing to the outstanding degradation of glyphosate. 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing of glyphosate-contaminated soil following the introduction of QLBS revealed changes in microbial community structure. Significantly, QLBS displays excellent ability in the degradation of glyphosate in water/soil environments stressed by multiple heavy metals (Cr, Cd, Cu, and Pb). Overall, our findings address a crucial gap in implementing biofortification strategies aimed at removing glyphosate from environments contaminated with both heavy metals and glyphosate.

title: Sulfide-doped SnO2/CF cathode for enhancing U(VI) reduction in a self-sustaining tandem photocatalytic fuel cell for complex radioactive wastewater treatment
abstract: Photocatalytic fuel cell (PFC) had been widely used in the resource utilization treatment of wastewater. However, most PFC designs focused on the photoanodes to enhance the organic degradation or hydrogen production performance, while few PFCs focused on the cathode modification to enhance the heavy metals removal efficiency. This study firstly developed a S doped SnO2 decorated carbon felt (S-SnO2/CF) cathode to construct a self-sustaining tandem PFC (STPFC) for improving U(VI) removal efficiency. Within 90 min, the removal rates of U(VI) and ibuprofen (IBU) were respectively increased to ∼100.00% and ∼98.03%, accompany with the maximum power output density (Pmax) reached 1.535 mW cm−2, which was much higher than the other reported PFCs. S doping not only introduced a large number of active sites, enabling more U(VI) ions to be captured and reduced, and enhanced the separation efficiency of electrons/holes, increasing the number of holes available for organic degradation, but also reduced the resistance and enhanced the electron transfer efficiency, thereby increasing the power generation. The constructed STPFC also exhibited excellent adaptability and reusability. This study would supply a new way for the treatment of the complex waste water, and also provide a new approach for optimizing PFC.

title: Real-time State of Charge estimation using LSTM-GRU hybrid with Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: The worldwide drive for clean energy and green transport has rapidly increased the adoption of electric vehicles because of improved battery reliability and efficiency standards. The sustainability of this system is enabled by the Battery Management System (BMS), which ensures safe, stable battery usage. At the core of the BMS lies the accurate estimation of the battery’s internal State of Charge (SoC). We present a hybrid approach employing an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) integrated with independently developed, trained, and tested deep learning models. The proposed solution operates in real-time using data from the BMS, incorporating key parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature. Initially, EKF provided SoC estimates, which were utilised along with required parameters (voltage, current, and temperature). Furthermore, various deep learning models have been implemented, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and LSTM-GRU. Eventually, the LSTM-GRU model emerged as the most effective through empirical testing and underwent further refinement through hyperparameter tuning. The experimental results have been validated using real-time battery data collected from the BMS deployed in the E-Kart. This work is significant as it enhances the reliability and sustainability of electric vehicle batteries by enabling more accurate range prediction, reducing unexpected failures, and extending battery life under real-world conditions. The final integrated model, EKF combined with LSTM-GRU, outperformed other existing state-of-the-art models with superior accuracy, achieving MAE = 0.00056, RMSE = 0.0223, MSE = 0.0005, and MAPE = 0.00061. The validation of the proposed model has been done on the real-time battery data. Additionally, the approach accounts for the impact of battery degradation on SoC estimation by validating SoC against the State of Health (SoH), ensuring robustness under varying battery conditions.

title: Segmentation of energy-poor households using K-means clustering: Insights into energy poverty dynamics
abstract: Research on energy poverty has mostly focused on static measures, and much less is known about its persistence and how it evolves across different groups of households. In particular, evidence on the processes through which families fall into, remain in, or manage to exit energy poverty over time is still scarce. This paper adopts a trajectory-based approach to uncover dynamic patterns of energy deprivation. Using longitudinal data from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey, we construct a multidimensional energy poverty index (MEPI) and apply K-means clustering to group households according to the level, trend, and volatility of their energy poverty trajectories. We then estimate cluster-specific dynamic models using a Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) framework. The results reveal four different clusters, each with markedly different exposure, persistence and drivers of energy poverty. The effects of income and energy prices vary substantially across groups, limiting the effectiveness of uniform policy responses and calling for more targeted interventions.

title: Enhancing mechanical performance and environmental sustainability of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) biopolymers using modified bio-oils: A comparative study
abstract: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) is a promising biodegradable polymer for sustainable packaging applications; however, its inherent brittleness and limited flexibility restrict its wider use. Bio-based plasticizers have the potential to improve the performance of this material while reducing dependence on fossil-derived additives. Therefore, this study investigates the effects of different modified bio-oils on the mechanical performance and environmental sustainability of plasticized PHBV materials, with Mesamoll® included as a synthetic plasticizer reference for comparison. Mechanical performance was evaluated through tensile and Charpy impact tests, while thermal properties were analyzed using differential scanning calorimetry. In addition, a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment was performed using the Environmental Footprint (EF) v3.1 method to compare the environmental impacts of bio-based and synthetic plasticizers. The results showed that bio-based plasticizers significantly improved the processability and mechanical performance of the polymer. Among the investigated formulations, the material containing 20 wt% sunflower and soybean oil epoxidized ester achieved a tensile strength of 24.6 MPa and a strain at break of 2.2%, showing performance comparable to that of the synthetic plasticizer Mesamoll®. The addition of modified bio-oils reduced processing torque and temperature, indicating improved flowability during processing. Thermal analysis revealed changes in melting temperature and crystallinity depending on the type and concentration of plasticizer. The life cycle assessment demonstrated that bio-plasticized materials generally exhibited environmental impacts comparable to or lower than those of the synthetic reference in several impact categories. However, sunflower and soybean oil epoxidized ester showed higher impacts in categories related to fertilizer use, land occupation, and land transformation. The study demonstrates that modified bio-oils are promising alternatives to conventional plasticizers for biodegradable packaging applications. Future research should focus on optimizing bio-oil production and processing routes to further improve material performance and reduce environmental impacts, thereby supporting cleaner production and sustainable material development.

title: A fuel modification strategy for cleaner iron ore sintering: lime milk-derived calcium oxide coating of coke breeze for combustion regulation and multi-pollutant reduction
abstract: Iron ore sintering represents the largest source of air pollutants in the integrated iron and steel industry, yet a unified source-level strategy capable of simultaneously suppressing CO, CO2, SO2, and NO through fuel property management has not been established. Moreover, the effects of lime milk surface modification of coke breeze on sintering flue gas pollutant emission behavior, along with its combined influence on sintering performance, have not been systematically investigated. In this study, lime milk modification was applied to full-size (Full-CBM), coarse-size (Coarse-CBM), and fine-size (Fine-CBM) coke breeze at varying modifier dosages, and systematically evaluated through sintering pot experiments, thermogravimetric analysis, SEM-EDS characterization, and real-time flue gas monitoring. At the optimal coke breeze-to-lime milk mass ratio of 2:1, Full-CBM enhanced the maximum combustion rate and combustion characteristic index by 51.1% and 105.7% relative to the unmodified bench mark under identical thermogravimetric conditions. Sintering yield was simultaneously improved, with solid fuel consumption reduced by 2.45 kg t−1. Furthermore, CO and CO2 emissions per tonne of sinter decreased by approximately 18%, while NO and SO2 emissions per tonne of sinter declined by 37.9% and 37.4%. Emission reduction is attributed to two synergistic mechanisms. The first is condition-dependent combustion modulation: the CaO coating promotes combustion under oxygen-rich conditions but forms an O2 diffusion barrier in the oxygen-limited sintering bed, lowering the instantaneous carbon oxidation rate while a narrower combustion interval improves thermal utilization and reduces solid fuel consumption. The second is chemical fixation of fuel-bound sulfur and nitrogen through in-situ CaSO4 formation and calcium ferrite melt bonding, with the crystalline CaSO4 and calcium ferrite phases confirmed by XRD. This work provides mechanistic and process-level insights into the clean production potential of lime milk-based coke breeze modification in iron ore sintering, thereby providing a viable pathway toward meeting increasingly stringent environmental governance requirements.

title: Water-flow-driven piezo-photocatalytic activation of percarbonate for advanced water purification: Insights from N-CQDs/g-C3N4 composites
abstract: Photocatalysis is an environmentally friendly strategy for antibiotic degradation; however, its practical application is hindered by rapid charge recombination. Piezocatalysis can effectively suppress charge recombination, but it typically depends on energy-intensive ultrasonic stimulation. In this study, a water-flow-driven N-CQDs/g-C3N4 piezo–photocatalyst was developed to activate sodium percarbonate (SPC), enabling efficient degradation of oxytetracycline (OTC). The incorporation of N-CQDs enhanced both the light absorption and piezoelectric properties of g-C3N4, thereby promoting the generation of •OH radicals. Computational fluid dynamics (Fluent) simulations demonstrated that the flow-induced piezopotential significantly enhanced the degradation of OTC. Under optimal conditions (10 mg/L OTC, 0.4 g/L catalyst, 0.2 g/L SPC, 800 rpm, pH 6.42), 99% degradation was achieved within 15 min. The pseudo-first-order rate constant reached 0.3064 min−1, which was 17.02 and 2.63 times higher than that of SPC alone and the g-C3N4/SPC system, respectively. h+, •OH, and O2•- were identified as the dominant reactive species responsible for the degradation of OTC. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that piezoelectric polarization facilitated electron transfer from g-C3N4 to N-CQDs. Fukui function analysis further confirmed that •OH radicals preferentially attacked C-C, C-N, and C-O bonds in OTC. The degradation intermediates exhibited low ecotoxicity. Moreover, the catalyst retained over 89% of its activity after ten cycles, demonstrating excellent stability and reusability.

title: Multi-objective water–energy Co-optimization and risk-informed decision-making for hydro–wind–solar systems in arid regions
abstract: Hydro-wind-solar hybrid renewable energy systems provide an important pathway for coordinated clean energy production and water-resource utilization in arid regions. However, the operational value of such systems depends not only on multi-objective scheduling, but also on whether uncertain runoff forecasts and uncertain stakeholder preferences can be consistently propagated into final scheduling decisions. This study develops an integrated decision-support framework that links hydrological forecast-error simulation, multi-objective stochastic scheduling, and risk-informed group decision-making for hydro-wind-solar systems. A martingale-based forecast evolution model is used to characterize runoff forecast uncertainty and generate runoff scenario trees. These scenarios, together with wind and solar power sequences, are embedded into a multi-objective stochastic scheduling model solved by the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II. The resulting non-dominated scheduling alternatives are then evaluated through a stochastic decision matrix and uncertain criteria weights. By coupling Stochastic Multi-criteria Acceptability Analysis (SMAA) with Grey Target Decision-Making (GTDM), the proposed SMAA-GTDM decision layer ranks scheduling alternatives while quantifying the reliability of the ranking results through a decision risk metric. The framework is demonstrated through a case study in the Kashi River Basin, Northwest China. Numerical experiments show that: (1) the martingale-based model can represent the evolution of hydrological forecast uncertainty; (2) incorporating runoff forecast scenarios into the scheduling model helps characterize trade-offs between renewable energy benefits and agricultural irrigation water supply under operational constraints; (3) compared with the conventional SMAA-2 utility structure, the SMAA-GTDM decision layer provides stronger discrimination among competing scheduling alternatives and lower decision risk in the tested case; and (4) the distributional characteristics of forecast errors can affect both the stochastic scheduling results and the reliability of final decisions. The study provides a risk-informed workflow for supporting hydro-wind-solar operation in water-stressed regions, while clarifying how runoff forecast uncertainty may propagate from scenario generation to optimization and final alternative selection.

title: Achieving net-zero for artificial intelligence: Big-tech's sustainability challenges from 2030 to 2050
abstract: Today big-tech companies—the largest, most financially successful, and most influential firms developing technology platforms and products— are responsible for 40% of overall data center energy consumption, and they pose a significant risk to environmental sustainability. To mitigate this risk, many of these corporations are claiming to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2030, including major big-tech companies, such as Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft. However, carbon accounting methodologies can be misleading, due to lack of harmonized data as well as various strategies employed such as carbon offsetting. Furthermore, existing studies often examine these issues separately. AI energy-demand projections are typically reported at the aggregate data center level, while analyses of corporate sustainability claims rarely connect carbon accounting practices to company-level AI growth trajectories. As a result, the literature lacks an integrated assessment of how AI-driven energy demand, reported versus gross emissions, mitigation pathways, and offsetting costs interact for major big-tech companies over long-term net-zero timelines. In this article, we find that AI-driven energy consumption is projected to account for 40-79% of total data center energy by 2028 depending on the growth scenario, before gradually declining as AI demand saturates, and energy uses shift from the training of AI models to their deployment and use. We further show that big-tech companies’ gross market-based emissions are substantially higher than their reported figures when renewable energy credits are excluded. The annual cost of carbon offsetting across four major big-tech companies is projected to reach $9.8B-$29.4B by 2030 under plausible price scenarios. We evaluate mitigation pathways, including renewable energy transition, AI-driven efficiency, and software improvements, and show that combined adoption could reduce cumulative emissions by up to 48% relative to the baseline. Our findings highlight the urgency of reducing absolute emissions rather than relying on carbon market instruments to meet net-zero targets.

title: Spatial effects of synergistic governance of pollution reduction and carbon emission mitigation in the Yangtze River Delta: A regional synergy perspective
abstract: Pollution and carbon emissions in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) rarely remain within administrative boundaries, making isolated municipal governance insufficient for improving synergistic efficiency of pollution and carbon emission reduction (PCSE). Although regional collaboration has become an important policy tool in China's urban agglomerations, its role in shaping synergistic efficiency and cross-city spillovers remains underexamined. This study asks whether regional collaboration improves local PCSE, whether these effects spill over to spatially connected cities, and under what urban conditions they are strengthened or weakened. Using panel data for 27 YRD cities from 2008 to 2023, this study combines the Super-SBM model, social network analysis, and the Spatial Durbin Model to measure PCSE, identify collaborative network structures, and estimate direct and spatial effects. Robustness, endogeneity, heterogeneity, and mechanism tests are also conducted. The results show that PCSE presents a clear east-high and west-low spatial pattern. Regional collaboration significantly improves local PCSE and generates positive spatial spillovers. Its effects are heterogeneous: economic development strengthens both the local and spatial effects of collaboration, while industrialization and environmental pressure mainly enhance the spatial effect. The collaborative network has shifted from a Shanghai-centered single-core structure to a more diversified multi-center network, although horizontal ties among peripheral cities remain weak. Mechanism analysis further reveals a suppression effect of industrial structure upgrading. By linking PCSE with intercity collaborative networks, this study extends research from city-level efficiency evaluation to regional governance processes and provides evidence for more institutionalized, differentiated, and network-based collaborative governance.

title: Nonlinear effects of urban green space spatial morphology on urban flood resilience: Insights from explainable machine learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization and extreme rainfall highlight urban green space (UGS) as a nature-based solution for enhancing flood resilience. However, the nonlinear relationship between UGS spatial morphology and flood resilience, driven by environmental complexity and spatial heterogeneity, remains poorly understood. This study developed a three-dimensional flood resilience framework encompassing robustness, recovery, and reconstruction. Focusing on Wuhan, China, the spatiotemporal evolution of flood resilience at the block scale is evaluated from 2014 to 2024. The nonlinear correlation and threshold effects of UGS spatial morphology are explored by integrating morphological spatial pattern analysis with explainable machine learning. The findings show: (1) Urban flood resilience exhibits significant spatial differentiation, characterized by a core–periphery gradient decline, with low-resilience areas exhibiting pronounced path dependence and spatial locking. (2) With advancing urbanization, the logic behind flood resilience promotion tends to transition from dependence on topological connectivity to reliance on the water storage and regulation capacity of high-quality core green patches. (3) Low density of islet and branch exerts significant positive marginal effects on flood resilience, whereas the core density exhibits a positive scale threshold at 0.25. Surpassing this threshold and ensuring efficient connectivity are essential for systematically enhancing flood resilience. (4) Flood resilience emerges from the dynamic synergy among UGS spatial morphology, population distribution, and topography. Crucially, connectivity exhibits a non-monotonic relationship with flood resilience, where moderate connectivity may alleviate localized flooding under runoff superposition. These insights offer a blueprint for optimizing UGS spatial morphology to enhance flood resilience in high-density urban environments.

title: Absorption, accumulation, physiological responses, and mechanistic insights into tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) to polystyrene microplastics
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized for their uptake by plants and associated risks to human health through the food chain. However, the underlying mechanisms governing MP absorption and physiological impacts in crop plants remain inadequately understood. This study systematically examined for the first time the uptake, translocation, accumulation, physiological alterations, and molecular mechanisms elicited by polystyrene MPs (PS-MPs) in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.). Results showed that both sized PS-MPs were absorbed by root tissues and then translocated to aerial parts, accumulating preferentially in roots > stems > leaves. Smaller particles and higher exposure concentrations significantly enhanced internal accumulation.
