PS-MPs stress reduced root elongation, plant height, and fresh biomass, while upregulating oxidative stress markers concentration-dependently. Transcriptomic analyses showed that high concentrations of smaller-sized PS-MPs induced more differentially expressed genes, particularly those involved in key pathways such as plant hormone signal transduction, MAPK signaling pathway-plant, and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis. Metabolomic profiling verified disruptions in phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, ascorbate and aldarate metabolism, and glycerophospholipid metabolism, suggesting compromised membrane integrity and antioxidant capacity. This study advances our understanding of the physiological and molecular responses of tomato seedlings to MP stress and provides a theoretical framework for assessing the accumulation potential and ecological risks of terrestrial MP contamination in agricultural systems.

title: pH-mediated mechanisms and optimization of electrocoagulation for treating authentic Fe-rich acid mine drainage
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) containing high Fe concentrations of 1–10 g L −1 is characterized by strong acidity, complex redox cycling, and unstable mineral precipitation, making remediation more challenging than for low-Fe AMD. Here, electrocoagulation (EC) was systematically evaluated for treating authentic Fe-rich AMD collected from two pyrite mines, focusing on pH-mediated transformation pathways by electrode combinations of Fe (anode) and stainless steel (cathode). An optimal current density of 30 mA cm −2 was identified. Experimental results indicate that an initial pH 5 serves as a practical threshold for EC applicability. Below pH 5, initial metal concentration is the dominant control on purification efficiency. Solid-phase analysis revealed interconnected transformation of Fe reduction, hydrolysis, and co-precipitation. The metal removal pathway exhibits a distinct temporal evolution under experimental conditions. Mechanistically, three pH-mediated removal stages were identified, with Fe-(oxy)hydroxide precipitation, subsequent surface complexation, and co-precipitation acting as the dominant pathways for the removal of Cu, Zn, and Mn. Under high ionic strength, pH elevation was suppressed and energy efficiency decreased, limiting the effectiveness of standalone EC-based AMD treatment. An integrated neutralization-EC configuration addressed these limitations, achieving over 97.5% removal of all target metals while reducing wet sludge production by 32%. The results demonstrate that neutralization-EC is an effective and practical strategy for treating authentic Fe-rich AMD.

title: Selective oxidation of biomass-derived platform compounds to 2,5-diformylfuran through polyoxometalate heterogeneous catalysts
abstract: The selective upgrading of biomass-derived platform molecules under mild conditions remains a significant challenge in advancing the substitution of fossil resources and promoting cleaner production. 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a versatile chemical intermediate derived from carbohydrate-rich biomass, has emerged as a critical platform compound bridging renewable feedstocks and value-added products in sustainable chemistry. We report a novel electron-transfer mediator (ETM)-assisted strategy for efficient aerobic oxidation of 5-HMF to 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) under ambient pressure, achieved by anchoring (NH4)5H6PMo4V8O40 (NPMoV) on mesoporous g-C3N4 (mpg-C3N4) via hydrogen bonding. These NPMoV(n)/mpg-C3N4(n = 10, 20, 25, 30, 35 %, POM loading amount) showed high activity in activating oxygen to oxidize 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) to 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) under atmospheric pressure of O2. NPMoV(30)/mpg-C3N4 achieves 90.6 % DFF yield at 97.6 % conversion. This superior performance originates from its unique structure of BrØnsted acidic, redox, basic sites in one, as well as strong absorption of 5-HMF. Meanwhile, the direct interaction between polyanion and mpg-C3N4 enables faster electron transfer in hybrids than in NPMoV. Here mpg-C3N4 acts as an ETM, accelerating electron transfer between NPMoV and O2 while suppressing overoxidation via spatial confinement of DFF. Meanwhile, the multifunctional sites in NPMoV(30)/mpg-C3N4 allow the fructose and glucose to be converted to DFF undergoing acidic/basic catalyzing isomerization, dehydration over acidic sites, and oxidation by redox sites. The strong interaction between NPMoV and mpg-C3N4 permitted no leaching of active sites of NPMoV confirming its high stability and recyclability. This work integrates technical and economic analyses to propose a scalable strategy for the high-value utilization of biomass platform compounds.

title: Full-range performance analysis of a Carnot battery system coupled thermochemical energy storage and coal-fired power plant
abstract: The Carnot battery is a promising energy storage technology. Integrating it with coal-fired plants enables energy storage and enhances flexibility. However, existing research primarily focuses on design conditions, lacking full-range performance analysis. Furthermore, the critical impact on boiler thermal balance is rarely considered, which may lead to unrealistic results and safety risks. This study proposes a Carnot battery system integrating a coal-fired plant with Ca(OH)2/CaO thermochemical energy storage and a supercritical CO2 reverse Brayton cycle, aiming for energy storage, coal consumption reduction, and operational flexibility enhancement. An Aspen-Matlab co-simulation model is developed for full-range analysis. Two energy release strategies—Mass-Based and Time-Based—are proposed. Crucially, the system's impact on boiler thermal balance is examined and the analysis shows original boiler design causes excessively high main steam temperature and low reheat steam/flue gas temperatures under off-design conditions. A boiler retrofit scheme is proposed and subsequent analysis shows that within 20-100 MW storage capacity, cumulative coal savings reach 7.7%-17.8%, with round-trip efficiency of 31.0%-53.7%. Finally, a peak-raising strategy using hydration heat to replace extracted steam is proposed, providing up to 89.2 MW additional capacity and extending the unit's operating range to 0-125% THA. Under the design condition, the system achieves a levelized cost of storage of 0.74 RMB/kWh, and a net present value of 69.96 million RMB. This research advances practical deployment of renewable energy-storage-thermal power integration.

title: MXene sediment/AgNW-filled PVA-PAAm aerogels for efficient solar-driven seawater desalination
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers an efficient route for alleviating freshwater scarcity, but its practical performance strongly depends on the rational integration of photothermal fillers, water-transport pathways, and thermally insulating matrices. Herein, MXene sediment (MS), a byproduct generated during MXene preparation, was reutilized as a waste-derived photothermal filler and incorporated with a low loading of silver nanowires (AgNWs) into a GLYMO-crosslinked poly (vinyl alcohol)/polyacrylamide (PVA/PAAm) aerogel. The vertically aligned microchannels and superhydrophilic polymer network provided continuous water transport, while the GLYMO-reinforced organic–inorganic network improved structural robustness. In addition, the broadband absorption of MS and AgNW-assisted optical enhancement enabled a solar absorptance of approximately 95%. Under 1 sun illumination, the optimized PPAMS20@AgNWs evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of 3.21 kg m−2 h−1 and an effective-enthalpy-based solar-to-vapor efficiency of approximately 97%. It also exhibited stable repeated-operation performance over 25 cycles and good salt-resistant behavior under the tested high-salinity conditions. This work demonstrates a potential strategy for converting MS into a functional photothermal filler for solar-driven seawater desalination.

title: A novel carbon-free direct reduction process for sulfur-oxygen mixed antimony ore via low-temperature smelting based on interactive reaction
abstract: To address the issues of SO2 pollution, high energy consumption, long process flow, and severe carbon emissions in the conventional volatilization smelting process for sulfur-oxygen mixed antimony ore, this study proposes a novel carbon-free direct reduction process based on a B2O3-Al2O3-CaO-SiO2 quaternary low-melting-point slag system for low-temperature electric furnace smelting. This process utilizes the interactive reaction between Sb2S3 and Sb2O3 (Sb2S3 + 2Sb2O3 = 6Sb + 3SO2) to achieve one-step reduction of antimony through a self-reduction mechanism without consuming any carbon-based reductant, eliminating carbon emissions at the source, with the product mainly consisting of antimony matte (containing metallic antimony and Sb2S3). Thermodynamic analysis indicates that this reaction can occur spontaneously in the molten phase, and experiments confirm that it can also occur in the gas phase. By investigating the effects of slag basicity, smelting temperature, and holding time on the direct recovery rate of antimony, the optimal process parameters were determined as follows: basicity of 0.5, temperature of 1100°C, and holding time of 1 h. Under these conditions, the direct recovery rate of antimony reaches 93.95%, the mass fraction of metallic antimony in the antimony matte is 56.6 wt%, and the slag ratio is approximately 48%. Compared with conventional processes, this novel process significantly shortens the process flow, generates high-concentration SO2 that can be used for sulfuric acid production (enabling sulfur resource utilization), and substantially reduces slag generation. This work provides a new technological pathway for the carbon-free, clean, and efficient utilization of complex antimony resources.

title: A hybrid particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based framework for green diesel production under the water-energy-food nexus paradigm
authors: Mauro Antonio da Silva Sá Ravagnani
abstract: The energy transition toward renewable fuels is essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and decrease reliance on fossil resources. This manuscript presents a hybrid framework for designing a green diesel supply chain under the water-energy-food (WEF) nexus. The framework integrates data reduction techniques, simulation-based surrogate models generated from Aspen Plus simulations, and a multi-objective optimization model solved using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The surrogate models, coded as Optimized Baselined Regressors (OBR), enable efficient estimation of process performance and their integration into large-scale optimization. The OBR achieved adjusted R 2 values above 0.99, validated through 5-fold cross-validation, confirming their robustness and predictive accuracy. The case study focuses on Paraná, Brazil. A scoring and selection procedure reduces the number of municipalities from 399 to 24 representative nodes. Results show that green diesel production from soybean oil can reach about 180 m 3 per hour, equivalent to roughly half of the conventional diesel demand in the region, without violating WEF constraints. The optimal configuration results in total greenhouse gas emissions of 178.5 million t-CO 2 per year, a total annual cost of 41.5 MMUSD per year, and freshwater consumption of 79.79 hm 3 per year. The findings demonstrate that combining OBR surrogates with a PSO-based optimization model provides an effective way to balance cost, emissions, water use, and fuel output in biofuel supply chain planning. This is the first integration of PSO with OBR surrogates for simultaneous supply chain design and WEF nexus analysis in green diesel production.

title: Parametric life cycle assessment of asphalt pavements with probabilistic lifetimes and traffic
abstract: This study develops a parametric life cycle assessment (LCA) framework to evaluate the environmental impacts of asphalt pavements, integrating probabilistic lifetimes and traffic volumes. The attributional LCA method (cut-off approach) is applied to five asphalt pavement types, incorporating seven key parameters and statistical modeling based on Norwegian road data. Results indicate that binder type, asphalt plant efficiency, and transport distances are dominant contributors to environmental impacts, with stone mastic asphalt (SMA) showing the highest burden due to its polymer-modified bitumen content. By incorporating probabilistic lifetimes and traffic loads into the functional unit, the study reshapes environmental rankings, revealing that longer pavement lifetimes do not always equate to lower environmental burdens. These findings underscore the importance of real-world performance factors in LCA and provide data-driven insights for reducing the environmental impacts of road construction and maintenance.

title: Suppression effect and mechanism of expandable phosphorus-boron composite suppressant on Al dust explosion
abstract: In this study, three kinds of expandable phosphorus-boron composite suppressants (EPBS) were prepared based on ammonium polyphosphate (APP) through coupling agent modification and mechanochemical compounding technology. Through a systematic comparative study on the suppression effects of three EPBS on Al dust explosion, the formulation with the optimal suppression effect was selected. This top-performing EPBS exhibited an initial decomposition temperature of 75 °C, a unit heat absorption capacity of 698 J/g, and the physical coating layer can expand up to 520 times in volume when covering combustible media. As the concentration of EPBS increased, the maximum explosion pressure (Pmax), maximum explosion pressure rise rate ((dP/dt)max), and average flame propagation velocity (Vavg) all decreased. Additionally, the critical suppression concentration was further reduced to 400 g/m3, eliminating the phenomenon of enhanced explosion intensity (SEEP). EPBS exerted the suppression effect through chemical and physical mechanism (heat absorption, coating, barrier formation and dilution). Chemically, the decomposition products of EPBS capture key explosion radicals O and AlO through radical-scavenging reactions (HOPO + O<=>OH + PO2, HPO3+O<=>OH + PO3), thereby interrupting the chain reaction pathway of Al dust combustion in the gas phase.

title: Urban resilience and carbon decoupling: An integrated Tapio-LMDI analysis of spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms in the Yangtze river economic belt
abstract: Understanding the association between urban resilience improvements and the decoupling of urban development from carbon emissions is essential for achieving carbon neutrality and sustainable urban transition. While existing studies primarily focus on the GDP–carbon emissions nexus, the role of urban resilience as a multidimensional system in shaping decoupling remains insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study developed an integrated analytical framework linking urban resilience with carbon emission dynamics from a decoupling perspective. Using panel data for 110 prefecture-level cities in China's Yangtze River Economic Belt from 2003 to 2022, this study combines the Tapio decoupling model, spatiotemporal analysis, and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition approach. The results show that urban resilience improves steadily, whereas carbon emissions continue to increase, but at a slower pace, after 2010. Spatially, urban resilience exhibits gradual regional convergence, whereas carbon emissions remain concentrated in the downstream metropolitan areas. The resilience–emissions relationship undergoes a marked transition from a predominantly negative decoupling pattern to a decoupling-dominated structure over the study period. During 2004–2010, negative decoupling accounted for more than 70% of cities, whereas after 2012, the decoupling structure became increasingly dominant. By 2022, strong decoupling accounted for more than 80% of cities, whereas negative decoupling declined to below 5%. The decomposition results further indicate that economic development remains the primary driver of decoupling, energy intensity mainly explains short-term fluctuations, carbon intensity plays an increasingly important role in facilitating decoupling, and the population effect remains limited. By integrating urban resilience into the decoupling framework, this study extends the conventional GDP-based decoupling analysis and demonstrates that improvements in adaptive capacity, structural transformation, and resource allocation are increasingly associated with low-carbon transitions, providing empirical support for differentiated regional development strategies.

title: Can an environmental policy mix curb the financialization of heavily polluting enterprises? Evidence from green credit and fiscal policies
abstract: Corporate financialization of heavily polluting enterprises has increased in recent years, raising concerns about resource diversion from the real economy. How an environmental policy mix can curb this trend has therefore become an important policy issue. This study employs a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2008 to 2023 and applies difference-in-differences (DID) and triple-difference (DDD) models. It examines the association between green credit policy and the financialization of heavily polluting enterprises, as well as the heterogeneous role of incentive-based and penalty-based fiscal policies under different conditions. The results show that the green credit policy is associated with an average 0.0097-unit reduction in the financial asset holdings of heavily polluting enterprises. Mechanism tests suggest that this association operates through improved capital investment structure, enhanced technological innovation, and strengthened internal risk management. These results remain robust after parallel trend tests, propensity score matching combined with difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) estimation, and placebo tests. Heterogeneity tests indicate that combining green credit policy with incentive-based fiscal policy may generate misalignment in state-owned, small-scale, and labor-intensive enterprises, as well as in firms facing weaker external constraints and limited internal resource allocation flexibility. In contrast, exploratory subgroup analyses suggest that combining green credit policy with penalty-based fiscal policy may have complementary effects among firms with tighter financing constraints or higher cash holdings. These findings provide evidence for optimizing the environmental policy mix and strengthening the capacity of green credit policy in guiding financial resources toward the real economy.

title: The relationship between waste intensity and corporate cost behavior: Implications for the circular economy and resource efficiency
abstract: As waste generation grows globally, cleaner production and circular economy research increasingly seeks to understand how waste-related environmental outcomes are reflected inside firms’ cost structures. Using archival data for publicly listed Japanese firms from 2005 to 2024, this study examines the association between waste intensity and production costs, administrative costs, total operating costs, and cost stickiness. Waste intensity is positively associated with cost of goods sold (COGS) and negatively associated with selling, general, and administrative expenses (SG&A). Lower waste intensity is also associated with greater SG&A stickiness, while we find no support for an association with COGS stickiness. This pattern is consistent with persistent administrative commitments, but does not establish that lower waste intensity reflects stronger waste-reduction effort. Because COGS and SG&A have opposing associations with waste intensity and differ in baseline scale, the total operating cost analysis estimates their combined association on a common cost base, whereas the disaggregated analyses identify the underlying channels. The findings indicate a production-side inefficiency channel reflected in COGS and an administration-side commitment channel reflected in SG&A and SG&A stickiness. The study contributes to circular economy and resource-efficiency research by showing that waste-related practices should not be evaluated as producing a uniform financial effect. Managers and policymakers should therefore evaluate circular economy initiatives from a total-cost perspective that considers both production-side efficiency and persistent administrative infrastructure.

title: Surfing for sustainability: Innovation and environmental challenges in the surf industry
abstract: The surf industry, despite its strong connection to nature, faces significant environmental challenges due to the use of non-renewable materials and unsustainable production practices. This study analyzed the environmental impacts associated with the production and disposal of surfboards, neoprene wetsuits, and other surfing equipment, highlighting innovative solutions to mitigate these issues. Through an integrative literature review based on systematic protocols such as the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) method, key trends, challenges, and innovations in the sector were identified. The results show that materials such as polyurethane and petrochemical resins generate a high carbon footprint and hinder recycling efforts. Proposed solutions include the use of biomaterials, design for disassembly, and reverse logistics systems for used equipment. The analysis also revealed a growing adoption of sustainable practices, driven by technological innovations and environmental awareness. However, challenges such as high costs, inadequate infrastructure, and market resistance still limit more significant advancements. This study provides a comprehensive overview of emerging initiatives and future pathways for sustainability in the surf industry, suggesting that the sector can lead greener practices and reduce its negative environmental impacts.

title: N/S-doped carbon electrode material derived from white-rot fungus-activated poplar for high-performance supercapacitors
abstract: Wood has a regular, vertical pore structure by nature, making it a naturally porous biomass material. It can be utilized to create and manufacture supercapacitor electrodes after carbonization while maintaining its natural skeletal shape. In this study, we culture white rot fungi in a medium supplemented with sulfuric acid and ammonium nitrate to etch and activate poplar wood, thereby preparing nitrogen- and sulfur-rich wood/mycelium-based materials (CWM-N and CWM-S). The degradation of lignin by white rot fungi improves microporous and mesoporous structures of the material while also resulting in a more uniform pore size distribution. Compared to the undoped wood carbon source (CWM), the surface area of CWM-N and CWM-S increased significantly (387.8 m2/g and 346.6 m2/g). The fabricated wood-based carbon electrodes exhibited excellent electrochemical performance in a three-electrode cell (At a current density of 1.0 mA/cm2, the area- and mass-specific capacitances of the two materials were 4759.25 mF/cm2 and 3839.38 mF/cm2, 54.70 F/g and 59.07 F/g, respectively) and good cycling stability (retention rates of 97.58% and 97.64% after 10000 cycles). The results indicate that pre-treating wood with white rot fungi and doping it with S and N elements is a unique green technique for enhancing supercapacitor performance.

title: Pressure-regulated Fe-Ni/HZSM-5 catalysis promotes selective monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbon production from LDPE/biomass co-pyrolysis
abstract: Monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (MAHs), especially benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes, are important liquid fuel components and platform chemicals for producing polymers, solvents, and fine chemicals. Catalytic co-pyrolysis of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and biomass provides a promising route for the selective production of MAHs. In this study, a pressure-regulated catalytic co-pyrolysis process was developed in which LDPE and Camellia oleifera shell (COS) were converted into MAHs over Fe-Ni/HZSM-5 catalysts with different Fe loadings and reduction states. Catalytic behaviors at 0.3 and 0.8 MPa were evaluated by py-GC/MS combined with XPS, XRD, BET, Py-IR, and SEM-EDX analyses. Increasing pressure generally suppressed oxygenates and aliphatic hydrocarbons, while promoting aromatization, indicating enhanced secondary deoxygenation, cyclization, and aromatization at the metal-acid interface. Among the unreduced catalysts, Fe15Ni10-HZ50 gave the best overall performance, affording 77.04% and 83.21% MAHs at 0.3 and 0.8 MPa, respectively, with relatively low oxygenates and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). This behavior was associated with a well-matched FeOx-NiOx/acid interface, the highest acidity, and favorable pore accessibility. After H2 reduction, the catalyst surface evolved into a mixed metallic/oxidized interface, while the marked loss of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites changed the dominant catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ni10-HZ50-R performed best at 0.3 MPa, whereas Fe50Ni10-HZ50-R achieved the highest MAHs content of 86.30% at 0.8 MPa. Overall, pressure-regulated Fe-Ni/acid synergy provides an effective strategy for converting LDPE and biomass into value-added MAHs during catalytic co-pyrolysis.

title: From Kaizen to sustainability: How operational lean tools drive the Triple Bottom Line
abstract: The manufacturing industry seeks to achieve operational efficiency and sustainability through lean manufacturing; however, the literature has not fully established their relationship, as prior studies have examined them in isolation and have not modeled Kaizen (KAI) as a philosophical driver that governs another Operational Lean Tool (OLT). This study proposes a structural equation model (SEM) assuming KAI as an umbrella that enforces three OLTs, namely 5S, Gemba Walking (GEM), and Muda (MUD) identification, to obtain Sustainability (SUS), operationalized as a second-order formative construct according to the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework. The SEM was validated using data from 834 responses to a survey applied to professionals in the manufacturing industry, employing the Partial Least Squares approach in WarpPLS v.8 and the Warp3 algorithm to detect nonlinear relationships, where eight of nine hypotheses were supported. Kaizen influences all three OLTs (5S: β = 0.513; GEM: β = 0.431; MUD: β = 0.227) and had the strongest direct effect on SUS (β = 0.540); however, the GEM→SUS relationship was rejected (β = 0.013, p = 0.357) indicating that GEM improves SUS only through the waste identification (indirect effect: β = 0.154). The model explains 73.6% of the variance in SUS. Beyond validating the hierarchical logic of the Toyota Production System (TPS), this study contributes a formative second-order conceptualization of TBL sustainability as a methodological advance. Two practical implications emerge from this study: building Kaizen as an organizational culture before deploying specific tools and redesigning Gemba Walks as structured dialogues rather than observation exercises.

title: Accuracy VS. efficiency: A hybrid deep learning framework for urban wastewater forecasting based on LSTM-Transformer
abstract: Municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are energy-intensive urban infrastructures. Accurate forecasting of influent dynamics is fundamental for stable operations and for reducing energy and chemical consumption. Although deep learning provides promising solutions for intelligent environmental management, its practical deployment is often limited by suboptimal model architecture, data volume, and high computational costs, which limit its viability as a sustainable, low-carbon tool. To overcome these challenges, we developed an LSTM-Transformer hybrid model. We evaluated its performance and efficiency using data from a WWTP in Northwest China. Residual-LSTM-Transformer demonstrated robust performance, with Mean Absolute Percentage Errors across all indicators remaining below 0.08. Residual connections outperformed parallel one by up to 18.45%. Ablation experiment confirmed VMD preprocessing contributes the most to model stability, and residual connections have also been proven to improve model accuracy. Data-volume and sparse-sampling experiments indicated that at least a dataset covering approximately one year is needed to ensure the predictive performance of the data-driven model. As the sampling interval increased from 2 h to 24 h, flow and TN predictions remained relatively stable, whereas COD and TP were more sensitive to reduced monitoring frequency, especially when the interval exceeded 6 h. Additionally, Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified that solar radiation and snowfall are the key driving factors influencing flow dynamics in our case. These findings provide a theoretical foundation and technical reference for municipal wastewater management, facilitating the upgrade of water infrastructure towards high efficiency and low-carbon development.

title: How ready is the downstream? A pollutant-treatment taxonomy and public-data framework for auditing U.S. wastewater and landfill infrastructure against industrial emerging contaminants
abstract: Industrial chemistry evolves in years, but the infrastructure that handles its by-products is built over decades. Each generation of emerging contaminants (today per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, PFAS; tomorrow whatever the chemical, electronics, or battery sectors scale next) reaches sewage plants and landfills as a surprise, though these chemicals are declared in federal inventories years earlier. A framework is proposed in which contaminants are classified by how they must be removed rather than by chemical identity, only public federal data are used, and the classification follows a taxonomy of eight removal-mechanism classes. A Treatment Readiness Index (TRI-RDY) is defined at every U.S. publicly owned treatment works (POTW), the municipal plants that treat a community's sewage (17,544 plants, 270.4 million people), and at every municipal landfill; each facility's predicted contaminant load is compared with its installed removal capability. To ground the framework in numbers, an example TRI-RDY is computed for PFAS across common treatment configurations, with Monte Carlo uncertainty, a sensitivity analysis, a semiconductor-plant scenario, and a check against occurrence data. Under conventional treatment the example median TRI-RDY for regulated PFAS is 4.0, a near-certain readiness gap; it falls below one only when granular activated carbon, ion exchange, or reverse osmosis is present, as occurrence data confirm. A national inventory of treatment capability is also shown to be absent from federal data, and a strategy to build it is set out. The framework does not depend on any single regulation and transfers to any country with a public pollutant-release inventory.

title: Design of microwave-heated pavement using recycled metallic wastes for enhanced snow melting efficiency and energy utilization: Mitigate diminishing marginal effects
abstract: The extensive accumulation of metallic waste presents serious environmental challenges worldwide. This study proposes a novel, sustainable strategy for repurposing such waste by developing a Blend Doped Microwave-absorbing Asphalt Pavement (BDMAP) for efficient microwave deicing. The pavement incorporates recycled waste Mn-Zn ferrite (WMF) and waste steel shavings (WSS) into different layers to leverage their microwave interactions: the WMF enhances microwave absorption, while the WSS reflects microwave. This microwave interaction can effectively mitigate the diminishing marginal effect — a phenomenon in which the heating efficiency improvement declines as the proportion of a single metallic material increases. By mitigating this effect, microwave energy is effectively confined to the upper pavement layer, thereby substantially improving snow-melting efficiency. Laboratory tests show that the optimal BDMAP design enhances the surface heating rate by 0.92°C/s and improves energy utilization by 15.5% compared with conventional asphalt mixtures. Furthermore, per kilometer of single-lane pavement, the proposed design can consume over 240 tons of metallic waste and reduce CO2 emissions by more than 50%, while satisfying standard mechanical performance requirements. This research not only provides an effective solution for winter road maintenance but also contributes to a circular economy by transforming industrial waste into construction materials, aligning closely with sustainable infrastructure goals.

title: Life cycle assessment of battery minerals to 2040: contribution of voluntary sustainability initiatives
abstract: The expansion of electric mobility is intensifying demand for lithium, nickel, and manganese, increasing the environmental burdens of mineral extraction and processing. Voluntary sustainability initiatives (VSIs) have emerged to encourage improved environmental management, yet their long-term effectiveness remains uncertain. This study explores a proof-of-concept of how VSI-aligned operational interventions could influence the future environmental performance of battery mineral supply chains, using a scenario-based prospective environmental assessment informed by life cycle modelling. By integrating Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) with VSI-aligned process measures such as air pollution control devices (APCDs), we assess midpoint impacts including climate change, particulate matter formation, and human toxicity. Results show that systemic background decarbonization dominates reductions, while VSI-inspired interventions deliver complementary benefits, including up to ∼75% reductions in particulate matter formation for nickel beneficiation and localized process-level reductions of up to ∼90%. These findings highlight how coupling systemic and operational measures can improve resource efficiency and environmental performance in battery-mineral supply chains.

title: Soil organic carbon and pH govern the divergent trajectories of organic and inorganic sulfur under long-term fertilization
abstract: Globally, declining atmospheric sulfur (S) deposition has increased the risk of S deficiency in intensive agricultural systems, yet the long-term changes in soil S fractions and their regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we used three 30-year (1990–2019) field experiments spanning China's temperate-to-subtropical climate gradient to examine changes in soil organic S (SOS) and inorganic S (SIS) fractions under contrasting fertilization regimes. Despite consistently positive apparent S budgets, topsoil SIS declined by 30–112 mg kg−1 under most site-treatment combinations, whereas SOS remained stable or increased, indicating a decoupling between apparent S inputs and SIS retention. This divergence reflected the different controls on organic S stabilization and inorganic S retention. Linear mixed-effects models and partial least squares path analysis showed that soil organic carbon (SOC) and pH were the major regulatory factors: SOC was significantly positively correlated with SOS and its fractions, whereas pH governed SIS retention through pH-dependent sulfate adsorption and calcium-associated sulfate stabilization mechanisms. Integrated organic-mineral fertilization, namely NPKM (nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium fertilizers plus manure), emerged as a promising strategy, as it simultaneously maintained crop yields, sustained SOS accumulation, kept soil available S above the reference deficiency threshold across sites, and reduced acidification pressure compared with mineral fertilization alone. These findings demonstrate that sustainable soil S management should move beyond input replacement and instead regulate soil-internal cycling processes, particularly SOC accumulation and pH buffering, to sustain soil S fertility under declining atmospheric S deposition.

title: Reed-derived biochar immobilized sulfate-reducing bacteria for stable acid mine drainage remediation under continuous-flow conditions
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD), characterized by strong acidity, high sulfate concentrations, and heavy metal contamination, poses a significant global environmental challenge. Although sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB)-based bioremediation is a promising approach, its efficacy is often limited by bacterial washout and metabolic inhibition under dynamic flow and acidic conditions. This study developed a composite inoculant by immobilizing SRB onto reed-derived biochar (SRB@LWC) to overcome these limitations. Static experiments demonstrated that SRB@LWC achieved removal efficiencies of 85.23% for sulfate and over 99% for total iron, leveraging synergistic mechanisms including biochar adsorption, SRB-mediated sulfate reduction, and metal sulfide precipitation. Dynamic column experiments simulating realistic flow conditions revealed that SRB@LWC maintained superior stable performance for 30 days, elevating pH above 6.5, stabilizing oxidation-reduction potential near −300 mV, and achieving removal rates of 69.84% for sulfate and 94.26% for iron. In contrast, free SRB lost activity within three days. Microbial community analysis indicated that biochar facilitated the colonization and spatial stratification of the core functional genus Desulfovibrio, which reached 68.32% relative abundance. This study demonstrates that biochar-immobilized SRB offers a stable and effective strategy for in-situ AMD remediation under continuous-flow conditions.

title: Soybean-urease-induced CaCO3 precipitation for improving the engineering properties of red clay: A novel eco-friendly method
abstract: Red clay contains abundant hydrophilic clay minerals such as montmorillonite and illite, resulting in unfavorable engineering properties, including high liquid limit, high plasticity, and strong susceptibility to water-induced disintegration, which severely restricts its application as an engineering fill material. To address the limitations of conventional solid-powder inorganic cementitious stabilizers (e.g., cement and lime), such as non-uniform mixing and considerable ecological impacts, this study investigates soybean-urease-induced calcium carbonate (CaCO3) precipitation (SICP) as a novel and eco-friendly technique for red clay solidification. The effectiveness of SICP treatment was evaluated through Atterberg limits, unconfined compressive strength (UCS), direct shear, and disintegration tests, with untreated red clay (URC) used as the reference material. The influence of cementing solution content (ws) on the engineering performance of SICP-solidified red clay (SCRC) was systematically examined. Furthermore, the underlying improvement mechanisms were investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses. The results indicate that SICP treatment substantially reduced the liquid limit (wL), plastic limit (wp), plasticity index (Ip), and disintegration rate of red clay, while significantly enhancing UCS, cohesion, internal friction angle, and disintegration time. An optimum cementing solution content of ws = 25.0% was identified, at which the UCS and disintegration time increased by 106.15% and 442.86%, respectively, whereas wL, wp, and Ip decreased by 17.95%, 15.27%, and 20.33%, respectively. These findings demonstrate that SICP is an effective and sustainable alternative to conventional stabilization methods and offers considerable potential for improving the engineering performance and durability of red clay in geotechnical applications.

title: In situ polyacrylamide grafted biochar for heavy metal remediation and alleviation of phytotoxicity
abstract: Biochar exhibits notable potential for heavy metal remediation owing to economic feasibility and environmental compatibility, but pristine coconut shell biochar remains constrained by limited immobilization capability, insufficient stability, as well as narrow applicability. Polyacrylamide grafted coconut shell biochar (PAM-BC) was synthesized via in situ polymerization to overcome previous limitations. PAM-BC exhibited effective adsorption performance in aqueous solutions, with maximum capacities reaching 151.3 mg/g for Cd2+ and 174.1 mg/g for Pb2+. In a soil-plant system, PAM-BC significantly decreased bioavailable fractions of Cd2+ and Pb2+ by 56.1%/76.1%, respectively. The reduction effectively inhibited migration and accumulation of heavy metals in plant roots, stems, as well as leaves. Concurrently, the microbial community was optimized through the enrichment of beneficial functional bacteria as well as the suppression of harmful populations. The remediation performance is attributed to the unique architecture. A three dimensional network was constructed by the extension of flexible PAM chains into rigid pores, and the biochar skeleton was preserved. Abundant -NH2 and -COOH groups facilitated stable chelation with Cd2+ and Pb2+, achieving dual enhancement via physical entrapment as well as chemical fixation. Consequently, a viable pathway for biochar functionalization is proposed, and the potential of PAM-BC for heavy metal remediation across diverse scenarios is demonstrated.

title: Enzyme-immobilized metal-organic framework biosensor for target-triggered sensitive fluorescence detection of diazinon residue and accumulation in rice
abstract: Developing rapid and sensitive analytical methods for detecting diazinon residue in agricultural products is necessary for food safety surveillance. Herein, we developed a urease modified Zr-centered metal–organic framework (ZrMOF@urease) nanosensor for detecting diazinon accumulation in crops. ZrMOF@urease was synthesized through rational immobilization of urease on the scaffold of ZrMOF to achieve a robust biocatalyst with significant enhancement in enzyme activity. The efficient hydrolysis of urea by ZrMOF@urease produced ammonia, which interacted with the terminal and bridging hydroxyl groups of the Zr6 clusters. This interaction resulted in measurable fluorescence recovery. Furthermore, the presence of diazinon inhibited the enzyme-catalyzed reaction, generating variations in detectable fluorescence signals. The fluorescence sensor achieved a detection limit of 4.5 ng mL −1 against diazinon. High recovery rates from various real samples and stable bioaccumulation monitoring in rice highlighted the effectiveness and reliability of the biosensor. This enzyme-immobilized metal–organic framework (MOF) sensor not only offers valuable insights into the structure-activity relationship of enzyme-functionalized MOFs, but also promoted the application of MOF-based biosensors for rapid pesticide detection in environmental monitoring and agricultural management.

title: Biochar increases plant biomass and reshapes biomass allocation through coordinated belowground and aboveground responses
abstract: Biochar is increasingly used to improve soil function and plant production, but its influence on biomass allocation remains unresolved at the global scale. Here, we conducted a global meta-analysis using 6489 paired observations from 107 studies to quantify how biochar addition affects plant biomass, biomass partitioning, plant functional traits, and soil properties across terrestrial ecosystems. Biochar addition increased overall plant biomass accumulation by 40.1%, with significant gains in whole-plant biomass, aboveground biomass, and belowground biomass of 35.4%, 36.6%, and 48.0%, respectively. The root-to-shoot ratio also increased by 16.0%, showing that biochar addition promoted growth while shifting biomass allocation. Plant functional types showed contrasting responses to biochar addition. Herbaceous plants exhibited significant increases in total, aboveground, and belowground biomass together with a higher root-to-shoot ratio, whereas woody plants showed biomass increases but relatively stable allocation patterns. Biochar addition was also associated with improvements in soil physicochemical and biological properties, enhanced root morphology and physiology, promoted stem and leaf development, and increased photosynthetic capacity. Meta-regression further showed that biomass responses increased with mean annual temperature, mean annual precipitation, biochar pH, biochar total carbon content, and initial soil organic carbon. In contrast, application rate, experimental duration, and biochar specific surface area and initial soil pH showed nonlinear, moderator-specific responses. Our analysis further showed that repeated biochar applications were associated with substantially stronger biomass responses than single applications. These effects reveal biochar sensitivity to management and background environmental conditions. Overall, our findings demonstrate that biochar influences multiple dimensions of plant and soil functioning and highlight its important role in regulating plant productivity and soil processes across environmental conditions.

title: High−entropy perovskite−based S-scheme heterojunction with interfacial Cu0 as electron-transport highway for efficient CO2 conversion
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 methanation has emerged as a sustainable strategy for carbon resource utilization, yet achieving high selectivity toward a single product such as CH4 remains challenging due to the complexity of multielectron transfer processes. Herein, a novel S-scheme Cu−BTC/LMO−400 heterojunction was constructed by integrating La(CrFeCoCuTi)XO3 (LMO) with Cu−BTC derivatives (Cu−BTC−400), where Cu0 serves as an efficient electron-transport highway at the interface. The lattice distortion in LMO generates abundant oxygen vacancies, facilitating CO2 adsorption and activation. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) confirms the presence of an internal electric field and S-scheme charge transfer pathway, which enhances the interfacial charge transfer and promotes the separation of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. The key intermediates CHO and *CH3O identified by in situ DR−FTIR are crucial for CH4 formation during CO2 reduction. DFT calculations further reveal that the Gibbs free energy of CH4 production path is significantly lower than that for producing CO. Consequently, the optimized catalyst Cu−BTC/LMO−400 achieves a CH4 production rate of 36.60 μmol g−1 h−1 with a selectivity of 93.47% under simulated solar irradiation without any sacrificial agent. This study provides deep insights into the rational design of high entropy perovskite oxides-based photocatalysts for CO2 conversion.

title: An operational decision framework for energy–carbon trade-offs in hemp-derived biochar systems
authors: Thiago Luccas Correa dos Santos Gomes
abstract: Industrial hemp ( Cannabis sativa L.) is increasingly discussed as a multipurpose lignocellulosic feedstock for renewable energy, carbon sequestration, and circular bioeconomy strategies. However, current evidence on hemp-derived biochar remains dispersed across agronomy, thermochemical conversion, environmental assessment, techno-economic analysis, and regulatory readiness, limiting transparent decision-making for process selection and scale-up. This study develops an operational decision framework for hemp-derived biochar systems through a structured evidence synthesis and scenario-oriented classification of thermochemical pathways. Peer-reviewed literature on hemp biomass, biochar production, thermochemical conversion, integrated assessment, and regulatory constraints was screened and coded to define three decision dimensions: energy recovery, carbon retention, and operational feasibility. These dimensions were translated into carbon-oriented, balanced, and energy-oriented regimes and operationalized through an ordinal scenario-screening matrix for comparing low-, intermediate-, and high-temperature conversion pathways. The analysis indicates that thermochemical conditions, especially temperature and residence time, control the core trade-off between stable carbon retention and recoverable energy products. Lower-temperature regimes generally favor biochar yield and carbon stability, whereas higher-temperature regimes increase energy carrier production but reduce the solid carbon fraction. Intermediate regimes provide the strongest basis for multiproduct circular bioeconomy configurations. The framework does not replace life-cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, or multi-criteria decision analysis; instead, it provides an upstream operational layer for defining system objectives, selecting conversion regimes, and identifying where detailed quantitative assessment is required. By linking process parameters, energy–carbon performance, environmental applications, logistics, and regulatory constraints, the study offers a practical decision-oriented contribution to cleaner biomass valorization and hemp-based bioeconomy design. Statement of novelty This study proposes an operational decision framework for hemp-derived biochar systems by explicitly linking thermochemical process conditions with energy recovery, carbon retention, environmental applications, and feasibility constraints. Unlike conventional descriptive syntheses, the framework organizes dispersed evidence into an energy–carbon decision space and classifies conversion pathways according to their dominant functional objectives. The contribution differs from LCA, TEA, MCDA, and generic biochar assessment approaches by providing an upstream screening layer that helps define system objectives and select candidate thermochemical configurations before more detailed quantitative assessments are conducted.

title: Integrated optimization of berth allocation, crane assignment, and onshore power supply with multi-source energy dispatch for green ports
abstract: Container terminal operations generate substantial emissions from vessel auxiliary engines and grid electricity consumption. This study develops an integrated optimization framework for continuous berth allocation, quay crane (QC) and yard crane (YC) assignment, onshore power supply (OPS) allocation, and multi-source energy dispatch. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) and reformulated as a tractable mixed-integer linear program (MILP), capturing vessel heterogeneity, OPS access feasibility, renewable generation, energy storage, electricity trading, and carbon accounting. Three strategies with different integration depths are examined: centralized optimization (CO), two-stage optimization (TSO), and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based coordination. Across twelve heterogeneous vessel datasets, CO reduces total cost by 15.69% under flat pricing and 19.87% under time-of-use (TOU) pricing relative to TSO; TOU pricing further lowers total cost by up to 20.92%. CO raises direct renewable utilization to 61-65%, cuts curtailment to 5-7%, and reduces port-side carbon by 14-16 tons; the three strategies exhibit a clear quality-scalability trade-off, with ADMM bridging 3-17% of the cost gap between TSO and CO on large-scale instances. Sensitivity analyses show that integrated logistics-energy coordination is most valuable when the peak-valley price ratio exceeds 2.75:1, peak-renewable energy storage sizing delivers the lowest energy cost, and OPS coverage and vessel retrofit rate act as complementary decarbonization levers. The results provide quantitative guidance for electricity pricing, OPS deployment, and storage investment in green port planning.

title: Toward sustainable food systems: Circular economy practices and perspectives of small-scale producers in the Bega Valley
abstract: There is an increasing focus on transitioning to a circular economy within the agrifood industry for both human and planetary health. This study aimed to explore the perspectives of small-scale producers towards circularity and understand the barriers and enablers towards implementing more circular supply chains. Small agrifood producers in the Bega Valley region, a shire in regional Australia with a unique circularity focus, were recruited using purposive sampling. Guided interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim. Reflexive, thematic analysis was used to identify key themes in the data, which are interpreted through a framework of four interacting dynamics: institutional, logistical, relational, and economic. Ten interviews were completed with producers from a range of areas: horticulture and market gardening (n = 4), food and beverage manufacture (n = 4); aquaculture (n = 1); and apiary (n = 1). The results reveal that producers engaged readily in reducing, reusing, and repurposing, while engagement in more complex recycling, repairing, and recovery was more limited. This uneven adoption reflected not individual motivation but how far institutional, logistical, relational, and economic conditions aligned, and varied with producers' scale, sector, and market position. As such, circularity in regional agrifood systems is framed as a challenge of ecosystem-level governance rather than -organisational level innovation. Advancing circularity therefore requires coordinated, ecosystem-level support, including shared infrastructure, mechanisms for knowledge exchange and collaboration, financial support for small producers, and alternative local food-system and labelling models, which are likely to be applicable across other regional agrifood systems internationally.

title: Amending soil with dredged nutrient-rich lake sediment and biostimulants to enhance plant growth and phosphorus recycling
abstract: Phosphorus (P) management in agriculture remains a global challenge due to its scarcity, geopolitical constraints, and its central role in maintaining crop yields, while driving freshwater eutrophication. The reuse of dredged P-rich lake sediments offers a dual opportunity to mitigate eutrophication and recover a recyclable P resource for crop production. This study evaluated dredged lake sediment as a recyclable P fertiliser, alone and in combination with P-solubilising biostimulants (PSB), on pea ( Pisum sativum L.) grown in a 45-day laboratory experiment. Treatments comprised the application of 30 kg P ha −1 as either lake sediment or conventional superphosphate fertiliser (positive control), alongside a negative control with no P added, each applied with and without PSB. We analysed a range of plant parameters (biomass and nutrient uptake) and rhizosphere soil attributes (Olsen P, cation-exchange capacity (CEC), water-holding capacity (WHC), total carbon, and enzyme activities). Lake sediment application produced biomass and P uptake comparable to the positive control, while increasing biomass by 45% and P uptake by 106% compared to the negative control. Compared with the positive control, lake sediment increased N, K, and Mg uptake by 7%, 43%, and 17%, respectively. It also enhanced rhizosphere functioning, increasing CEC (+15%) and WHC (+22%), alongside higher enzyme activities (acid phosphatase +16%, alkaline phosphatase +118%, and β-glucosidase +10%). In contrast, Olsen P was reduced by 12% relative to the positive control. Although lake sediment combined with PSB tended to result in higher nutrient uptake, particularly of N, K, and Mg, the statistical PSB effect was context-specific and not consistently observed across treatments. We conclude that lake sediment was the primary driver of improved plant nutrition and rhizosphere functioning, while PSB showed minor additional effect on nutrient mobilisation.

title: Navigating the global expanse of offshore floating photovoltaics: Techno-ecological-economic boundaries decoded by artificial intelligence
abstract: Offshore floating photovoltaics (OFPV) offer a massive frontier for global clean energy without land competition, yet theoretical estimates ignore severe marine limitations and risks. This paper, for the first time, proposes a novel “virtual expert” framework to capture the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of marine environments for data-driven suitability assessment of global OFPV potential. Under current-stage assumptions, our analysis reveals that within Exclusive Economic Zones, stringent techno-environmental constraints curtail the initial 14,831,550 TWh/year (128.94 million km2) theoretical potential by 93.7%. This yields a realizable potential of 935,110 TWh/year across 9.04 million km2, underscoring the profound impact of technical and environmental thresholds on OFPV expansion. Regionally, Asia dominates in absolute potential, while Africa boasts the highest average suitability, with specific cyclone-exempt African nations achieving 100% “most suitable” coverage as promising early-stage deployment candidates. Constraint analysis identifies water depth as the primary physical barrier, eliminating vast high-radiance areas across Europe, the Americas, and Africa. Meanwhile, sea ice and marine protected areas impose absolute exclusions in high-latitude and ecological hotspots, whereas low-latitude deployments—notably in Asia and Oceania—demand robust tropical cyclone resilience. Furthermore, spatially resolved techno-economic assessments reveal that while unconstrained marine areas achieve an average levelized cost of energy of 9.16 US cents/kWh under standardized economic assumptions, some constrained zones nevertheless retain relatively favorable solar economics, suggesting that deep-water station-keeping and cyclone-resilient floating structures may become high-priority R&D directions for future OFPV innovation. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that OFPV deployment is inherently a highly localized spatial optimization challenge, our framework providing a macro-siting tool to assist stakeholders in balancing clean energy expansion with marine conservation and environmental risk mitigation.

title: Optimal prosumer participation in dual peer-to-peer markets using multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, fuzzy satisfaction level, and blockchain settlement
abstract: The transition toward decentralized renewable energy systems has increased the role of prosumers and energy communities in achieving cleaner, sustainable, and more flexible energy management. It is therefore essential to employ proper market trading frameworks to guarantee the economic efficiency of prosumers while preserving privacy and improving operational autonomy. Motivated by these challenges, this paper develops a multi-stage prosumer-community-centered scheduling and trading framework for energy management and transactive energy objectives. To address prosumer-centered objectives, a multi-agent twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3) algorithm is employed for scheduling prosumers' demand load, energy storage system (ESS) operation, and bid/ask prices under the decentralized training and execution (DTDE) strategy. Additionally, a flexibility-in-trading (FinT) concept is introduced for optimal peer-to-peer (P2P) market participation, evaluated by fuzzy satisfaction level-based (FSL) sensitivity analysis. At the community level, a centralized community-to-community (C2C) market is implemented to facilitate communities' net load exchanges and coordinate dual market clearing between prosumers and communities. A case study of 90 residential prosumers, divided into six energy communities, is engaged in P2P and C2C transactions consisting of real-world data. Finally, market transactions are recorded in an Ethereum-based consortium blockchain to ensure transparency and cyber-physical security. Quantitative results with scheduling errors below 10% and 12.6% in the scheduling and trading stages represent stable learning. Moreover, the proposed FinT mechanism achieves Jain's Fairness Index of 0.88 and FSL mean-score of 92.6%, illustrating effective and equitable market participation. The findings confirm that the proposed system improves operational flexibility and transaction transparency and provides a pathway toward cleaner and sustainable prosumer-centric energy communities.

title: Coordinated capacity configuration and techno-economic assessment of a grid-connected hydro–wind–solar–pumped storage complementary system for long-distance UHVDC power transmission
abstract: Against the background of the global low-carbon energy transition, long-distance power delivery from large-scale wind and photovoltaic bases to remote load centers has become an important pathway for improving renewable energy utilization. However, hydro–wind–solar–pumped storage complementary systems for ultra-high-voltage direct current power delivery still face two key challenges. The first is the difficulty of formulating stable transmission profiles. The second is the mismatch between generation-side capacity and grid-side transmission capacity. To address these challenges, this study develops a source–grid coordinated optimization framework with transmission corridor capacity treated as a rigid engineering constraint. Photovoltaic installed capacity and transmission corridor capacity are defined as the core decision variables. A multi-timescale dual-layer dispatch model is incorporated into the proposed framework. The CRITIC–GLDS multicriteria decision-making method is further integrated to identify the economically optimal scheme within the technical feasibility domain. A clean energy base in the upper reaches of the Yellow River, comprising 2320 MW of hydropower capacity and 4200 MW of pumped storage capacity, is selected as the case study. The results show that stable transmission profiles can be generated under a 95% export plan fulfillment rate constraint. The economically optimal matching relationship between transmission corridor capacity and photovoltaic installed capacity is approximately 1:2.5. The preferred configuration is identified as 18 GW photovoltaic capacity and 8 GW transmission corridor capacity. Under this configuration, the levelized cost of electricity is 256.62 RMB/MWh, the transmission corridor utilization rate is 61.78%, and the renewable energy utilization rate is 91.11%. This study provides decision support for the long-distance transmission of large-scale renewable energy bases and source–grid coordinated planning.

title: Coal to carbon quantum dots via Fenton’s reagent
abstract: Industrial scale-up of top-down synthesized carbon quantum dots (CQDs) is currently bottlenecked by the environmental hazards of harsh acidic oxidizers and a total lack of predictive process and techno-economic frameworks. This work addressis this gap by presenting a novel and environmentally friendly process for converting Wyoming Powder River Basin coal into carbon quantum dots (CQDs) by leveraging naturally occurring iron to drive an in situ Fenton reaction. XPS and FTIR characterization confirmed the formation of highly functionalized CQDs, validating the molecular models used in our kinetic analysis. A two-step sequential mechanism was developed and validated using a global basin-hopping optimization algorithm. Operating at an optimized 8-hour/90 °C regime, the process maximizes CQD yield (43%) while ensuring high photoluminescent quality. Process modeling and techno-economic analysis were performed on a potential coal-to-CQD process at pilot, intermediate, and industrial-scale production rates to establish the first commercial viability benchmarks for this green technology. It was found that pilot and intermediate-scale facilities could be built with limited capital investment. CQDs produced in these plants could be sold at prices lower than CQDs currently available commercially. Capital and operating costs at the industrial scale are significantly higher than those at the intermediate scale, but the staged deployment scheme presented here minimizes investment risk while allowing CQDs to move from niche uses as laboratory reagents into bulk commodity applications. Ultimately, these findings establish a scalable blueprint for repurposing fossil fuel resources into sustainable, high-value carbon materials.

title: Dusty plasma actuators: “Powder-phobic” walls to mitigate clogging in granular flows
abstract: Clogging is a thornier problem for many production environments run by granular flows. The cure? Purging and cleaning the pipelines continuously. Although simple and certainly effective, such mechanical operations indicate that there is no pat answer to this challenge. Yet, stopping the line jeopardizes the reliability and predictability of production environments — two pivotal concerns for many industrial sectors, such as new energy systems based on granular media. Here, we propose the use of electric forces to clear the granular material adhered to the pipeline walls. The charge injected from the electrodes is transferred to the grains that eventually repel each other and the electrodes. To that end, we used a dielectric barrier discharge setup, with fine powders settling on the surface. Experiments monitored the powder mass ejected from the surface, exploring the role of the particle size (from 15 to 80 microns) and the frequency of the electric signal (from 2 to 500 Hz). The results left no doubt about the potential of these settings. All the tests, irrespective of the frequency and particle sizes, led to clean surfaces with no trace of particles — as general trend, higher frequencies result in faster cleaning. Particle size also plays a role; it modulates the powder removal rate. Importantly, we found an operational regime for frequencies of the electric stimulus around 100 Hz in which all the powder samples were thrust efficiently (in a minimal time window) and homogeneously (within similar time windows, regardless of the particle size). Undoubtedly, the practicality of using electrical forces to prevent particles from adhering to the pipeline walls opens new avenues for designing robust and reliable pumping systems — a long-standing demand for an ample palette of engineering processes that require transporting and storing cohesive granular media.

title: Smart municipal waste management with source segregation and recovery optimization
abstract: This study develops an integrated optimization framework for designing a source-segregated municipal solid waste management network. A mixed-integer linear programming model is proposed to determine the optimal configuration of collection stations, assignment of waste generation points, installation of smart monitoring systems, and allocation of waste flows to treatment and recycling facilities within a multi-echelon municipal logistics network. The model minimizes total system cost while satisfying capacity, budget, and recycling constraints. A numerical experiment based on a representative case study of Tabuk city, Saudi Arabia, is conducted to demonstrate the applicability of the model. The results show that the optimal network opens three collection stations and allocates waste efficiently across treatment facilities, achieving a diversion rate of approximately 72% from landfill. The comparative and sensitivity analyses indicate that integrating source segregation with monitoring-enabled operational coordination, optimized infrastructure utilization, and resource recovery can significantly improve economic performance while reducing landfill dependency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that segregation participation, recycling revenue, and disposal cost are key drivers of system performance. Increased participation in source segregation leads to higher recovery rates and improved economic outcomes, while higher recycling revenues and disposal costs promote waste diversion from landfill. The findings highlight the importance of coordinated planning, economic incentives, operational coordination, and public participation in developing sustainable waste management systems. The proposed framework provides a practical decision-support tool for municipalities seeking to transition toward circular economy practices and improve resource efficiency in urban waste management.

title: Linking anisotropic chloride transport to annualised carbon intensity: A durability-informed sustainability assessment of 3D-printed UHPC
abstract: Chloride-induced corrosion significantly shortens the service life of reinforced concrete infrastructure and increases life-cycle carbon emissions through repeated maintenance interventions. In 3D-printed ultra-high-performance concrete (3DP-UHPC), build-induced anisotropy alters chloride transport behaviour, yet its long-term durability and sustainability implications remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a durability-informed comparative framework that links anisotropic chloride transport to maintenance-normalised carbon implications in 3DP-UHPC. Long-term immersion experiments were conducted to obtain depth-resolved chloride profiles for different build orientations. A time-dependent diffusion model incorporating surface chloride accumulation kinetics was used to identify orientation-dependent transport parameters, which were subsequently translated into corrosion-initiation-based service life and a parameterised carbon amplification formulation over a 50-year design horizon. Results show that corrosion initiation under a 20 mm cover condition is governed primarily by surface accumulation kinetics rather than instantaneous diffusion intensity. A stable durability hierarchy (3D-Z > MC ≈ 3D-Y > 3D-X) persists under realistic variations in corrosion threshold and cover depth. Within the adopted comparative framework, and using 3D-X as the reference condition, orientation optimisation yields up to a 38% relative reduction in the parameterised annualised carbon-intensity indicator without altering material composition or structural geometry. The findings indicate that build orientation can function as a non-material sustainability lever by regulating durability-controlled maintenance demand in chloride-exposed infrastructure.

title: Selective suppression of key hazardous asphalt VOCs by MIL-101: From risk screening to mechanistic insights
abstract: As a fundamental component of the global transportation network, asphalt pavements inevitably release complex volatile organic compounds (VOCs) throughout their entire life cycle, posing persistent threat to ecosystems and human health while hindering cleaner production in sector. Owing to the extreme compositional complexity of asphalt VOC emissions, existing studies have largely focused on total emission control, often overlooking the dominant contribution of a small number of highly toxic components to overall risk. To address this limitation, this study proposes a risk-oriented selective suppression strategy. A multidimensional evaluation framework was established to identify key hazardous components, prioritizing isoprene, p-xylene, dimethyl disulfide, and methyl vinyl ketone as primary control targets. Subsequently, a low-emission asphalt material was developed using the high-surface-area metal–organic framework MIL-101 as a modifier to enable targeted adsorption of these characteristic pollutants. Multiscale molecular simulations reveal that the abundant unsaturated metal sites and unique pore environment of MIL-101 generate deep free-energy wells and pronounced diffusion barriers, endowing the material with higher adsorption affinity and stronger intracrystalline retention for selective capture of the target pollutants. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) experiments further validate the simulation predictions, demonstrating that MIL-101 significantly reduces emissions of the risk-dominant pollutants, Overall, this work integrates risk-oriented screening with mechanism-guided material design, providing an effective pathway for cleaner production of low-emission asphalt materials and the development of more sustainable transportation infrastructure.

title: Entrepreneurial leadership and resource management efficiency as necessary conditions for SME sustainability: A moderated mediation analysis of digital readiness and financial inclusion
abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are central to employment and value creation, yet pressures from sustainability transition expose endemic financing frictions and uneven digital readiness (DR), particularly in emerging markets. This study examines how SME capabilities viz.: entrepreneurial leadership (EL) and resource management efficiency (RME) associate with triple-bottom-line (TBL) sustainability across economic (ECOS), environmental (ENVS), and social (SOCS) pillars, whether firm-level financial inclusion (FI) statistically mediates capability-to-TBL associations, and whether DR conditions these associations. Using survey data from 429 Malaysian SMEs, we apply a sequential analytics design: Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modelling to test direct, mediated, and interaction effects; followed by Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and Importance-Performance Map Analysis in the bid to identify bottlenecks and practical priorities. Results show that EL is positively associated with ECOS, ENVS, and SOCS; whereas RME is strongly positively associated with ECOS and ENVS but is not significant for SOCS. FI is TBL pillar-asymmetric: it bolsters ENVS and SOCS but exhibits a negative effect on ECOS, and the mediated effects through FI mirror the pattern. DR significantly strengthens the FI to TBL pathways, yet conditional indirect effects indicate that high DR can neutralise FI's economic drag without reliably improving ECOS. NCA sharpens the conclusion: high ECOS is unattainable without RME, while high ENVS and SOCS require EL-RME-FI jointly; DR is not a robust necessity condition. Practically, SMEs should tighten efficiency routines first, mobilise leadership for adoption, channel finance through verified upgrading milestones and invest in DR only where it improves monitoring, traceability and compliance.

title: Lignin-based aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt: Preparation, performance characterization, and sustainable applications
abstract: Under the macro-background of the global carbon neutrality strategy driving the transition of transportation infrastructure construction materials toward “bio-based green production,” the frequent occurrence of distresses such as potholes during pavement maintenance poses extreme challenges to the overall performance of repair materials. In this context, the use of aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt is regarded as an effective maintenance solution. However, its large-scale application still faces practical challenges, particularly regarding the carbon footprint associated with petroleum dependence and the fluctuating economic costs of synthetic raw materials. As a renewable resource with abundant reserves and excellent affinity with asphalt, lignin provides a strategic opportunity to break this deadlock. This study developed a “green preparation method for lignin-based aqueous epoxy emulsified asphalt.” Lignin-based aqueous epoxy resin was synthesized through simple chemical grafting of lignin with glycerol triglycidyl ether (GTE). Furthermore, the thermodynamic spontaneity and chemical bonding process of the grafting reaction were demonstrated at the molecular level using electrostatic potential (ESP) calculations and FTIR spectroscopy. Performance evaluations indicate that the construction of a three-dimensional cross-linking network within the system, when the lignin-based aqueous epoxy content reaches 12 wt%, is the physical essence behind the enhancement of macro-performance. Moreover, rheological and interfacial thermodynamic analyses confirmed that this network significantly reinforces the high-temperature rheological properties and adhesion performance of the system. At the mixture level, performance tests including high-temperature rutting, low-temperature bending, and moisture stability confirmed that the proposed material maintains robust high-temperature stability while balancing low-temperature crack resistance and resistance to hydrothermal damage. Furthermore, a simplified life cycle assessment (LCA) indicates that the incorporation of lignin-based aqueous epoxy provides a potential reduction of approximately 10% in global warming potential compared to conventional bisphenol A-based systems. This research not only achieves the transformation of industrial byproducts into green pavement toughening agents but also provides a scientific basis and technical pathway for the development of high-performance, cost-effective, and eco-friendly road maintenance materials.

title: Multiphase flow and hydrate plugging during liquid CO2 injection into water-saturated sediments: Experimental and CFD insights for geological CO2 storage
abstract: Reliable CO2 injection into geological formations is essential for large-scale carbon storage, yet hydrate formation during injection can significantly impair injectivity and flow stability. This study investigated the multiphase flow behavior of liquid CO2 injected into water-saturated sediments using a combination of laboratory experiments and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Liquid CO2 injection experiments were conducted in a horizontal one-dimensional reactor designed to simulate water-saturated sediment. Under hydrate-stable conditions at 274.15 K and 4.0 MPa, CO2 hydrate formation caused severe flow restriction and eventual plugging within the reactor, whereas stable CO2 transport was maintained at 286.15 K without persistent plugging. The addition of monoethylene glycol as a thermodynamic hydrate inhibitor mitigated hydrate formation; however, its apparent inhibition performance deviated from closed-system expectations. CO2 discharge resumed after approximately 4 h at 4.6 mol% MEG, whereas the pressure increased to approximately 10 MPa after about 8 h at 8.8 mol% MEG, owing to dynamic water/inhibitor redistribution during liquid CO2 injection. CFD simulations complemented the experiments by resolving internal phase distributions and multiphase transport processes that cannot be directly observed experimentally. The simulations revealed the formation of an inlet-side dry-out region, hydrate accumulation in the mid-section, and preferential flow pathways that control CO2 migration and injectivity. These results provide mechanistic insight into hydrate-induced flow restriction during liquid CO2 injection and highlight important considerations for hydrate mitigation in geological CO2 storage systems.

title: RSM–ANN-driven process engineering for greener polyphenol extraction from kodo millet husk and their translational efficacy against acute lung inflammation in both in vitro and in vivo models
abstract: This study establishes the first systematic translation of kodo millet husk into a biologically validated functional resource via extraction of polyphenol-rich fractions with demonstrated anti-inflammatory efficacy. A data-driven framework integrating simplex-lattice solvent optimization, response surface methodology–artificial neural network (RSM–ANN) hybrid modeling, and kinetic–thermodynamic analysis was employed to enhance extraction efficiency and functional performance, followed by validation in cellular systems and a preclinical acute respiratory distress syndrome model. Under optimized conditions, the extract yielded 35.41 μmol FAE g−1 total phenolics, 3.05 μmol QE g−1 flavonoids, and 98.34% ABTS inhibition, corresponding to ∼66% and ∼9% improvements, respectively. ANN exhibited superior capability in resolving nonlinear process interactions.
