Kinetic and thermodynamic assessments indicated a diffusion-controlled, endothermic, and entropy-driven process with low activation energy (11.57 kJ mol−1) and negative ΔG°, confirming spontaneity. HPLC-DAD-ESI-MS/MS profiling identified fifteen phenolics, dominated by hydroxycinnamic acids. Preclinical evaluation demonstrated significant attenuation of LPS-induced inflammation, including reduced cytokine levels, modulation of macrophage response, and preservation of lung architecture, with efficacy comparable to dexamethasone. Overall, this study provides a mechanistically grounded and scalable framework for the translational valorization of kodo millet husk.

title: A policy-driven and climate-adjusted Weibull framework for forecasting end-of-life photovoltaic module waste in Korea
abstract: This study quantitatively predicts the future generation of end-of-life (EoL) photovoltaic (PV) module waste in South Korea and assesses uncertainty associated with key lifetime and modeling assumptions. Separate lifetime models were developed for commercial and self-consumption PV systems using a Weibull-based framework that incorporates the contractual structures of national PV support policies and empirical evidence from module disposal cases. For commercial systems, distinct Weibull distributions were applied to installation cohorts according to policy-specific contract termination periods under the Feed-in Tariff (FIT) and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) schemes. For self-consumption systems, an Acceleration Failure Time (AFT)-Weibull model was employed, integrating region-specific climatic risk factors—temperature, precipitation, humidity, particulate matter (PM), and ozone concentration—as determinants of lifetime degradation. Annual waste generation is projected to increase sharply, peaking around 2040, with cumulative EoL PV waste estimated to reach approximately 1.7-1.9 million tons by 2050. Regional analysis reveals higher waste generation in Jeonnam, Jeonbuk, Gyeongbuk, and Chungnam provinces, primarily driven by installed capacity rather than accelerated degradation. Sensitivity analyses, including variations in climate acceleration factors and reuse rates, indicate that uncertainty mainly affects the magnitude of waste generation whereas the overall temporal pattern remains robust. These findings provide a quantitative foundation for developing PV recycling policies and planning resource recovery infrastructure in Korea.

title: Self-driven antibiotic dehalogenation via novel decoupled aluminium-carbon system: Performance, mechanism, and biodegradability assessment
abstract: The residual presence of halogenated antibiotics in aquatic environments poses threats due to the stability of carbon-halogen (C-X) bonds. Herein, we propose a self-driven purification technology comprising zero-valent aluminium (ZVAl) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) for the efficient dehalogenation of florfenicol (FLO). The physical separation of the ZVAl anode and CNTs cathode into distinct chambers facilitates the direct replacement of spent anodes and permits the facile recovery and reuse of CNTs. The ZVAl//CNTs system achieved high removal efficiency of FLO (>81.4%) over a wide pH range (3–11) and showed strong resilience to various water matrix components (NO3−, SO42−, and humic acid); other halogenated compounds such as chloramphenicol and thiamphenicol could also be effectively degraded by this system. Mechanistic investigations revealed that dehalogenation proceeds predominantly via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathways. Integrated experimental and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed that C-Cl bonds are cleaved prior to the C-F bond during FLO reduction. The ZVAl//CNTs process successfully diminished the antibacterial activity and phytotoxicity of FLO, and improved the biodegradability of effluents (BOD5/COD increased from 0.08 to 0.29). This study establishes a sustainable paradigm for dehalogenating refractory halogenated pollutants, emphasizing a strategy that fosters the circulation of carbon materials.

title: Bayesian material flow analysis and life cycle assessment reveal decarbonisation and land use trade-off in England's cement and concrete sector
abstract: Concrete is essential for modern infrastructure, but its production has significant environmental costs, including carbon emissions and land use. Comprehensive material life cycle data for cement and concrete are currently lacking, hindering assessment of its life cycle environmental impacts and strategies for mitigative action including policy decisions. This study applies Bayesian Material Flow Analysis (BaMFA) for the quantitative material flow analysis of the 2019 cement and concrete life cycle in England. Integrating the BaMFA results – estimates of material flows and stocks – into Life Cycle Assessment enables more complete assessment of the material system's potential life cycle impacts. This study has two aims. First, to establish the first quantitative material life cycle for cement and concrete in England; second, to demonstrate the potential of BaMFA in strategic material assessment. The modelled system has a global warming potential of 17.0MtCO2-eq, 2.6% of the reported 2019 UK total. Including land use (239km2a crop-eq, 0.1% of England's land area) highlights difficulties of achieving improvements concurrently across them. Priority actions for decarbonisation alongside land use reduction is clinker substitution in cement manufacturing and reduced coal use in steelmaking. Greater attention should also be paid to reducing impacts related to transport, which contributes 1.34 Mt CO2-eq and 54.5% of land use in the system, especially where interventions affect logistics and infrastructure needs. Data availability is a persistent barrier to informed policy and decision-making, including decarbonisation for net-zero, and system optimisation through modelling. BaMFA can help to estimate incomplete or absent data in any complex material systems.

title: Co-inoculation of PGPB and AMF: Impacts on common bean yield, nutrition, and selective root taxon co-occurrence
abstract: Although inoculation with plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) has shown promise for cleaner production with reduced reliance on synthetic fertilizers in common bean, field evidence regarding its combined use with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) remains quite limited. This study investigated the effects of PGPB and their co-inoculation with the AMF Rhizophagus clarus on grain yield, plant nutrition, and microorganisms associated with common bean roots. The experiment was conducted in a randomized block design with an 8 x 2 factorial scheme and four replicates, and was repeated in the same plots over two winter cropping seasons. The treatments consisted of inoculation with the PGPBs Azospirillum brasilense, Azomonas macrocytogenes, Azotobacter beijerinckii, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, Bacillus aryabhattai, Burkholderia vietnamiensis, Nitrospirillum amazonense , and an uninoculated control, combined or not with R. clarus . The results demonstrated that co-inoculation efficacy is highly context- and strain-dependent. significant increases in grain yield were achieved when R. clarus was applied alone. Furthermore, true synergistic increments were observed under co-inoculation with Bur. vietnamiensis , Az. brasilense , or Azot. beijerinckii . Significant grain biofortification was observed, with specific PGPBs enhancing nitrogen and magnesium export, while the AMF increased iron export. Conversely, the incompatibility of certain co-inoculations was evidenced by antagonistic effects, such as the reduction in yield following the co-inoculation of R. clarus + A. macrocytogenes . Finally, the analysis of the root-associated microbiome - restricted to a subset of three selected PGPB strains and their co-inoculations with R. clarus ( Az. brasilense, Bur. vietnamiensis, and N. amazonense ) - revealed that the inoculations did not alter the overall diversity but were observed in association with exclusive genera, driving specific qualitative changes in the microbial community without altering its global structure. In conclusion, under the conditions of this single cultivation site, this study demonstrates that R. clarus can benefit winter common bean by increasing yield and inducing qualitative changes in low-abundance root-associated taxa. Similarly, PGPB and their co-inoculations with AMF can benefit crop yield and nutrition, depending on the specific microbial combination.

title: From predictive accuracy to prescriptive value: A data-driven framework for sustainable multi-period electric vehicle battery recycling networks
abstract: With the accelerated expansion of global electric vehicles, the recycling of end-of-life electric vehicle batteries (EVB) is crucial to achieving a circular economy. In this study, a data-driven multi-period EVB recycling network design problem is investigated from a fourth-party logistics (4PL) perspective. The contributions involve two main aspects. First, an advanced data-driven optimization framework is proposed, wherein forecasting methods are evaluated based on the quality of the resulting decisions, thereby establishing a closed-loop linkage between prediction and optimization. Second, the 4PL concept is integrated into EVB recycling network design by jointly optimizing site selection and transportation link selection, facilitating the effective coordination of multiple third-party logistics providers, whereby network flexibility and operational efficiency are enhanced. To solve this problem, a two-stage stochastic multi-period network design model is formulated, and subsequently reformulated as a mixed-integer linear programming model using sample average approximation. To ensure computational scalability, a scenario decomposition and relaxation-based heuristic algorithm is developed, which integrates Latin hypercube sampling, Lagrangian relaxation, and the progressive hedging algorithm. Finally, numerical experiments using realistic profiles are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that the Transformer-based design achieves the lowest decision regret, with only 0.03% regret relative to the actual-demand benchmark. Compared with the GRU-based design, which performs strongly at the forecasting layer but yields 1.28% decision regret, the Transformer-based design reduces regret by approximately 97.3% and lowers the realized cost by about USD 0.62 million. These findings indicate that evaluating forecasting methods through downstream optimization outcomes can help mitigate the suboptimality caused by relying on statistical accuracy alone. Furthermore, the extended low-carbon analysis shows that carbon regulations significantly reshape the EVB recycling network. A moderate carbon tax (0.08–0.10 USD/kg) increases green 3PL adoption from 46.22% to over 53% while reducing variable emissions per EVB by approximately 1.4%, while RCR decreases only from 75.39% to 74.23%. In contrast, stringent carbon caps reduce variable emissions per EVB by about 4.4% but substantially decrease the recovery rate from 75.39% to 58.93%, highlighting a critical trade-off between decarbonization and circularity.

title: Estimating the nutrition- and environment-attributable human health burden of the Spanish food consumption vs. Spanish dietary guidelines
abstract: Current dietary patterns in Spain contribute significantly to both chronic health burden and environmental degradation, which in turn has a health impact. Using disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) as a common metric, this study aimed to quantify and compare the dietary health burden among Spanish adults (referred to as nutDALYs) and the human health burden associated with the environmental impacts of food consumption (referred to as envDALYs). We analyzed current food consumption in Spain in 2022 and compared it with scenarios reflecting adherence to the 2022 Spanish Dietary Guidelines, and alternative, more plant-forward dietary guidelines. Their effects on morbidity and mortality were quantified through dietary comparative risk assessment (for nutDALY) and life cycle assessment (for envDALY). In 2022, Spanish adult diets were associated with 945,351 nutDALYs and 331,797 envDALYs, primarily driven by low intake of whole grains, fruits and legumes, and high consumption of red meat and ultra-processed foods. Adherence to the Spanish Dietary Guidelines could reduce nutDALYs by 78–96%, with further reductions under alternative, more plant-forward guidelines. These shifts would also improve nutritional adequacy, aligning intake with WHO recommendations—except for calcium and vitamin B12 in certain plant-based scenarios. Environmentally mediated health impacts showed more nuanced changes: compared to current diets, Spanish Dietary Guidelines adoption would reduce envDALYs by 3% to 27%, while alternative, more plant-forward guidelines would reduce envDALYs by up to 33%. This study underscores the dual potential of dietary transitions through sustainable dietary guidelines to improve direct and indirect human health, offering a realistic and inclusive pathway toward sustainable food systems.

title: Carbon continuum across Eastern Himalayan forests: Elevational shifts in productivity, storage and turnover
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) that enhance carbon (C) sequestration while maintaining ecosystem resilience are central to climate-change mitigation and sustainable land management. Forests of the Eastern Himalaya, spanning steep elevational gradients, offer a unique opportunity to examine how productivity, carbon storage, and turnover together sustain these outcomes. This study quantified biomass, net primary productivity (NPP), vegetation and soil organic carbon (SOC) pools across tropical (TRF), subtropical (STRF), and temperate (TMF) forests in Mizoram, Northeast India, using intensive field-based measurements of trees, shrubs, herbs, litter, fine roots, and soils. Carbon dynamics varied significantly with elevation. The STRF exhibited the highest total biomass (286.70 Mg ha−1), vegetation C (134.75 Mg C ha−1), SOC pools (104.3 Mg C ha−1), and C sequestration rate (10.81 Mg C ha−1 yr−1), reflecting an optimal balance between productivity and carbon residence time. In contrast, TRF showed rapid C turnover with lower standing stocks (107.00 Mg C ha−1) but high fluxes, while TMF functioned as a long-term C reservoir with moderate biomass (254.10 Mg ha−1) and slow decomposition kinetics. Distinct litter and fine-root dynamics revealed complementary C cycling strategies along the elevational gradient. Collectively, these forests constitute a functional C continuum in which tropical systems act as high-exchange zones, subtropical forests as efficient C sinks, and temperate forests as stable long-term C stores. Conserving this elevational mosaic represents a robust nature-based sustainability solution that simultaneously supports climate mitigation, ecosystem resilience, and regional C balance in the Eastern Himalayan forests.

title: Synergistic enhancement of low-carbon cement-based materials and CO2 sequestration via graded carbonization and composite design of rice husk ash
abstract: To achieve solid waste recycling and carbon emission reduction in the cement industry, this study proposes a graded carbonation and functional compounding strategy that utilizes rice husk ash (RHA) as CO2-sequestration functional carrier capable of active CO2 sequestration and structural regulation. The progressively refined RHA samples (S1, S2, S3) were subjected to activation-carbonation treatment and graded compounding (Scheme A, B, C) and subsequently incorporated into an alkaline composite cementitious system at contents of 4%–20%. CO2 adsorption tests combined with the Avrami model were employed to quantitatively evaluate the CO2 capture capacity, while FTIR confirmed the coupling of physical adsorption and chemical carbonation processes. MIP, TG-DTG and SEM-EDS were used to systematically characterize the influence of the compounding schemes on the workability and mechanical performance of the system. The results demonstrate that progressive refinement from S1 to S3 transforms the pore structure of RHA from a macropore-dominated system to one enriched in micropores and mesopores, with the specific surface area increasing from 21.49 to 104.19 m2/g. FTIR and CO2 adsorption experiments confirm the concurrent enhancement of physical adsorption and chemical carbonation, with the maximum CO2 adsorption capacity increasing from 3.21 to 16.21 cm3/g. RHA-S3 exhibits a higher density of high-energy adsorption sites and enhanced adsorption kinetics. The RHA20-C group achieved the highest compressive strength of 51.11 MPa. TG-DTG analysis indicates that appropriate gradation enhances the pozzolanic reaction, promotes CH consumption, and facilitates the formation of stable carbonate phases. Pre-carbonation with CO2 further refined the pore structure and reduced the total pore volume, thereby increasing the proportion of harmless pores from 30%–34% to 34%–40%. Graded compounding counteracted structural degradation induced by macropores. The proposed system reduced carbon emissions by up to 11.16% and achieved a carbon sequestration capacity of 39.48 g CO2/kg. These findings provide a feasible pathway for the high-value utilization of solid waste and the development of low-carbon alkaline cementitious materials with integrated carbon sequestration functionality.

title: Integrated nitrogen fertilizer management strategies for sustainable subtropical vegetable production: A multi-objective approach
abstract: Optimizing nitrogen (N) management is key to high-yield, high-quality, and environmentally sustainable vegetable production. However, the long-term sustainability of integrated N management strategies considering agronomic performance, environmental impacts, and economic outcomes remains insufficiently evaluated, particularly in subtropical vegetable systems. This study combined two consecutive four-year field experiments with a multi-objective sustainability assessment framework integrating life cycle assessment (LCA) to systematically evaluate representative N management strategies in subtropical open-field pepper production. Experiment 1 assessed five N application rates, and Experiment 2, using the optimized rate, evaluated four N sources: conventional urea (CU), organic–inorganic fertilizer (OIF), stabilized fertilizer with nitrification inhibitor (NI), and controlled-release urea (CRU). In Experiment 1, the conventional N practice (FNP) with the highest N rate was the least sustainable, characterized by low N use efficiency, high environmental burdens, high social costs (including ecosystem and human health damages), and poor fruit quality. In contrast, the optimized N strategy (OPT) reduced N input while maintaining yields, improving N use efficiency and fruit quality, and decreasing environmental burdens by 43–59% and social costs by 46%. Experiment 2 further demonstrated that, compared with CU, the OIF, NI, and CRU further enhanced sustainability. Notably, NI and CRU enhanced pepper yield by 9–11%, N use efficiency by 9–17%, and improved fruit quality traits. These treatments also reduced environmental burdens by 14–52% and social costs by 31–40%, and increased net ecosystem economic benefits by 8–16%. Overall, integrating optimized N application rates with enhanced-efficiency fertilizers offers a promising strategy to achieve high yield, better quality, lower environmental burdens, and greater economic benefits in subtropical vegetable production. This study provides long-term field evidence and a comprehensive assessment framework for identifying sustainable N management strategies and supporting region-specific fertilizer management decisions.

title: Dynamic emission evolution and synergistic effect of heavy metals and primary air pollutants in China's iron and steel industry
abstract: At present, most reductions in heavy metals (HMs) emissions in the iron and steel industry (ISI) are attributable to synergistic decreases resulting from the implementation of dust removal, desulfurization, and denitrification facilities. However, the correlation between HMs and primary air pollutants (PAPs) emissions remains understudied. In this study, we systematically investigated the spatiotemporal evolutionary dynamics of HMs and PAPs emissions, as well as their synergistic effects, using an established long-time-series HMs and PAPs emission inventory based on a facility-level point source activity database. The results showed that HMs and PAPs emissions from the ISI in China were estimated at 1445.8 t and 1327.1 kt in 2023, respectively. Basic oxygen furnace and electric arc furnace processes were identified as the primary sources of HMs emissions. The Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region and the Yangtze River Delta were identified as the main areas with high levels of HMs and PAPs emissions. Spring and summer were also identified as the primary seasons associated with elevated HMs and PAPs emissions. From 2013 to 2023, emission reductions of HMs ranged from 21.2% to 81.1%, while reductions of PAPs ranged from 37.0% to 87.0%. Among the PAPs, NOx exhibited the greatest synergistic reduction potential with HMs, whereas PM demonstrated the strongest synergistic effects with HMs. End-of-pipe treatment levels (65.9%–85.7%) and energy intensity (13.5%–33.4%) were identified as the primary drivers of synergistic emission reductions. These findings provide data support for the formulation of targeted policies aimed at achieving synergistic emission reductions of HMs and PAPs in the ISI.

title: Carbon footprints of RFID labels in mass production
abstract: This study presents the first comparative carbon footprint assessment of four industrially manufactured UHF RFID label technologies under an identical design framework, addressing a critical knowledge gap in understanding the environmental impacts of emerging RFID manufacturing processes. While RFID labels have become essential for supply chain traceability, inventory management, and digital product identification, limited studies have quantified and compared the carbon footprints of different antenna fabrication technologies using primary industrial production data. In this work, cradle-to-gate carbon footprints were evaluated for four commercially relevant RFID label types manufactured using etching, printing, laser die-cutting, and embroidery processes. The assessment was based on detailed manufacturing inventories collected from industrial production lines, including material consumption, energy use, and process-specific inputs. The results demonstrate that RFID labels fabricated using laser die-cut antennas exhibited the lowest carbon footprint, indicating the environmental benefits of simplified manufacturing routes and reduced material waste. In contrast, labels produced using embroidery technology showed the highest carbon footprint under current manufacturing conditions, primarily due to the high environmental burden associated with silver-coated conductive yarns. However, embroidery-based RFID labels also displayed the greatest long-term potential for carbon reduction because of their simplified process chain, eliminating several conventional manufacturing steps. Across all technologies, antenna conductor material was identified as the dominant contributor to overall greenhouse gas emissions, with aluminium based conductors exhibiting substantially lower carbon footprints than silver-based alternatives. These findings provide new insights into the environmental performance of RFID technologies and offer practical guidance for developing more sustainable label solutions aligned with global net-zero goals.

title: Reducing the carbon footprint of asphalt production through crude oil selection guided by refining history
abstract: Asphalt production is a carbon-intensive industrial process, yet refineries lack predictive tools to link crude oil characteristics to final binder performance. This knowledge gap forces conservative, energy-intensive over-distillation, unnecessarily increasing the carbon footprint of pavement materials. Here we explore whether machine learning can decode the crude-to-binder structural evolution to enable a cleaner production pathway. Tracking two crude oils through laboratory-scale refining (crude oil, atmospheric residue, vacuum residue, asphalt binder), we combine multi-scale characterization with Random Forest analysis to identify which molecular features govern pavement performance. We identify preliminary evidence for a temperature-dependent switching mechanism: high-temperature performance is associated with peak molecular weight (Mp) and methylene-to-methyl ratio (ICH2/CH3), while fatigue resistance shows links to asphaltene content and sulfur content. These findings translate into three strategies for reducing carbon emissions: (i) pre-refining selection of crude oils with favorable molecular profiles, avoiding over-distillation of marginal crudes; (ii) targeted process control to engineer these molecular features, replacing empirical trial-and-error; and (iii) climate-tailored binder design to eliminate over-processing. Unsupervised clustering indicates that crude oil molecular fingerprints reflect final binder performance, suggesting the feasibility of crude selection. This work offers a knowledge-driven perspective that replaces energy-intensive over-processing with predictive design, contributing to low-carbon asphalt production and sustainable infrastructure.

title: Data for circularity assessment: what, where, and how?
abstract: The growing need for circular economy (CE) assessment in manufacturing enterprises is driven by increasing regulatory and market pressures. However, existing approaches provide limited support for identifying and collecting the required data to compute circularity indicators. The main contribution of this paper is a structured method that links circularity indicators to collectable data and formalizes data collection as a decision problem. CE assessment is operationalized through a four-phase, data-driven approach comprising (1) an industrial diagnosis to define objectives, scope, and relevant information systems, (2) a systematic sense-making process to translate CE assessment resources into structured data requirements, (3) a decomposition of circularity indicators into data points, referred to as c-data, and (4) a mixed-integer linear programming model to determine an efficient data collection strategy. Applied to a medical radiology system manufacturer case study, 69 target indicators are decomposed into 91 c-data points distributed across eight information systems. Building on this, the optimization model shows that accessing only a limited subset of systems can be sufficient to compute a substantial share of indicators, thereby revealing trade-offs between implementation effort and assessment coverage. In this context, three alternative data collection strategies are identified for the company. Notably, one of these strategies demonstrates that accessing just one of eight information systems makes it possible to collect 13% of eligible data points, which in turn enables the computation of 25% of CE indicators. The approach supports the transition from high-level assessment requirements to actionable data sourcing strategies and is extendable to other sustainability assessment contexts.

title: Decarbonizing manufacturing through circularity and renewable electrification: A panel threshold analysis of production-based and consumption-based emissions in the EU-27
abstract: Decarbonizing manufacturing is central to the EU's 2050 climate-neutral agenda. However, production-based and consumption-based emission perspectives are rarely contrasted, and the conditions under which circularity and renewable electrification jointly reduce emissions remain underexplored. This study examines how circular material use, renewable energy share, and resource productivity affect production- and consumption-based emissions in the EU-27 panel, 2010-2024, combining cross-sectional dependence and unit-root diagnostics, Westerlund cointegration, Augmented Mean Group and Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, Hansen panel threshold regression, Driscoll-Kraay robustness, and System GMM. The Hansen test locates a candidate breakpoint at a circular material use rate of 2.80%, with a positive coefficient below and a small negative coefficient above the threshold; the likelihood-ratio test does not reject linearity at conventional levels (p = 0.213), so this result is suggestive rather than confirmed. Per-capita income elasticity is strongly negative for production-based emission intensity (−0.97) but positive for consumption-based footprint (+0.27), consistent with carbon leakage, though the design cannot identify leakage causally. Resource productivity cointegrates negatively with emission intensity in both perspectives, while the renewable-energy channel reaches significance under Driscoll-Kraay fixed effects but not under the heterogeneous-slope estimators. Country-level decomposition shows that the pooled circularity effect is concentrated in a small number of economies rather than being uniform across the EU-27. Findings imply that the European Green Deal's 2030 circularity target exceeds the candidate threshold, and that the production-consumption asymmetry is a relevant consideration for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism design. Policy implications are framed as conditional priorities for circularity planning, infrastructure financing, and standardized emission reporting.

title: In situ Zn-substituted CuFe2O4 for enhanced peroxymonosulfate activation and antibiotic degradation in real wastewater
abstract: The persistence of antibiotic residues poses a severe threat to ecosystems and human health. While sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs) are effective for tetracycline degradation, their engineering application faces three major bottlenecks: low persulfate utilization efficiency, challenging solid-liquid separation of powdered catalysts, and metal ion leaching leading to secondary pollution. This work reports a synergistic strategy that integrates atomic-scale Zn2+ doping with macroscopic immobilization to simultaneously overcome these limitations in a CuFe2O4 platform. Theoretical and experimental analyses revealed that Zn2+, with its d10 configuration, preferentially occupies the tetrahedral sites in CuFe2O4. This doping inhibits Jahn-Teller distortion, reduces Cu ion leaching to 0.8 mg/L, and optimizes the electronic structure, significantly increasing the Cu+/Cu2+ ratio. Consequently, the rate constant for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation and tetracycline degradation reached 0.1329 min−1, which is 3 times as higher as that of the undoped sample. The optimal catalyst (Zn0.2CFO) maintained high activity across a broad pH range (3–11) and under high ionic strength. Critically, the powder separation bottleneck was overcome through sodium alginate-Ca2+ dynamic crosslinking, transforming the nano-powder into millimeter-sized granules that preserve active site accessibility. In fixed-bed reactors treating real aquaculture wastewater, the granular catalyst achieves >99.99% tetracycline removal with zero powder loss and no secondary pollution. This work demonstrates a synergistic atomic-level doping regulation and macroscopic-level structure immobilization strategy, providing a novel pathway for designing advanced oxidation catalysts with high activity, stability, and engineering practicality.

title: Bioelectrochemical enhancement for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons degradation in saline wastewater
abstract: The biological treatment and biogas recovery of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in high-salinity wastewater from coal chemical industries are often severely inhibited by salt stress, resulting in low efficiency and a lack of energy recovery. This study proposes that weak current intervention in anaerobic digestion offers an effective method for treating high-salinity PAH wastewater. Anaerobic degradation was conducted on salinity (up to 5%) wastewater containing naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene. Weak current intervention (0.8 V) significantly enhanced PAHs degradation efficiency, with the total organic carbon removal rate increasing by up to 2.5 times, a peak degradation efficiency of 1307.8 mg/(L∙d), and removal rates of naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene reaching 99.3%, 98.9%, and 94.0% in 4 days, respectively. When applied to coal chemical wastewater treatment, the chemical oxygen demand removal rate was increased to approximately threefold, with removal rates of naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene at 79.38%, 79.44%, and 81.39% in 4 days, respectively. Notably, methane and hydrogen were collected at volumes of 73.23 ± 0.50 mL and 5.94 ± 0.23 mL per cycle, respectively, corresponding to an energy recovery rate of 109.6% of the input electrical energy, excluding the energy from organic matter in wastewater. Moreover, weak current intervention enhanced microbial activity, adenosine triphosphate activity, and microbial diversity, while promoting the enrichment of salt-tolerant, halophilic, and methanogenic microorganisms. Distinct microbial community shifts were observed under weak current-assisted conditions, indicating enhanced biological adaptation to salinity stress and improved anaerobic treatment performance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying weak current-assisted anaerobic digestion to real coal chemical wastewater and highlight its potential for simultaneous pollutant removal and energy recovery in high-salinity industrial wastewater treatment.

title: Climate change impacts on designing the power system of Kenya in 2050
abstract: Africa’s economic growth in the coming decades will hinge on the strategic planning of national power systems to meet growing demand and ensure rural energy access. Renewable energy sources, particularly wind and solar, will be pivotal in the expansion and transition to a low-carbon energy system. However, the vulnerability of these renewable sources to climate change could introduce imponderability in the design of the energy mix. In this regard, this paper explores a climate-informed energy system pathway by integrating the future climate projections directly into the capacity expansion of Kenya’s power system within three scenarios towards 2050, to formulate future energy profiles under climate change. The PyPSA-Earth model is applied to calculate capacity expansion decisions of the Kenyan power system. The EC-Earth3-Veg Earth System Model projects future climate variables such as wind speed. The cooling demands with global warming are estimated based on Cooling Degree Days (CDDs) projected by the Multi-Climate Model ensemble. The capacity expansion optimization results reveal that temperature increase leads to a rise in cooling demand, resulting in capacity expansion by 12% to 52% larger than the cooling demand without global warming. The projected change in wind speed is complex, with the onshore wind speed declining and the offshore wind speed rising, which causes a jump in the share of offshore wind power, taking 9% to 19% of the total capacity. Life cycle assessment indicates that large-scale deployment of wind and solar has less 5% climate change mitigation potential, but has 35% more total system cost compared to the baseline. In Kenya, geothermal is expected to continue playing a critical role in the energy strategy. Besides solar power, offshore wind is forecasted to become an important renewable energy source for Kenya. However, climate models’ resolutions and accuracy need to be further improved for effective integration into energy system modelling.

title: Cleaner transportation through energy-oriented vehicle routing under disrupted arcs
abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) represents a challenging optimization task with direct implications for energy consumption, emissions, and sustainable transportation. In this study, we extend classical VRP formulations to account for the effects of arc disruptions, such as road closures, congestion, or infrastructure failures, on energy efficiency and service reliability. We investigated three models: the single-depot capacitated VRP, the single-depot VRP with time windows, and the VRP with simultaneous pickup and delivery, all of which were reformulated to account for disruption probabilities and arc availability. A normalized energy-impact measure, reflecting the environmental implications of routing decisions (including potential CO2 emissions), is embedded into the objective function. A Genetic Algorithm is developed to solve these models efficiently, and numerical experiments, supported by sensitivity analyses, highlight the trade-offs between resilience, energy use, and service quality. The results demonstrate that the proposed energy-oriented, disruption-aware models yield more realistic, environmentally responsible, and cleaner routing strategies than conventional VRPs. This work underscores the potential of integrating energy and disruption considerations into vehicle routing to promote sustainability in logistics and support cleaner production practices.

title: Magnetic response associated enhancement of magneto-Fenton degradation of p-Nitrophenol over amorphous FeSiB
abstract: P-Nitrophenol (p-NP) is a refractory organic pollutant that can be removed by Fenton oxidation. However, the efficiency of conventional Fenton oxidation is often limited by sluggish Fe redox cycling. Herein, an amorphous Fe93.7Si3.1B3.2 alloy (FeSiB) was employed to construct a magnetic field assisted Fenton system for efficient p-NP degradation. Under a static magnetic field of 130 mT, FeSiB achieved 95.0% p-NP removal within 15 min, with a reaction rate constant 5.6 times that under non-magnetic conditions. Comparative experiments using weakly magnetic FeCrMo and annealed FeSiB indicate that the magnetic response of FeSiB is closely associated with its magneto-Fenton enhancement, although the activity is not governed solely by bulk magnetization. Mössbauer spectroscopy reveals Fe-centered local environments with pronounced magnetic hyperfine interactions and metallic character, which may facilitate Fe redox cycling during H2O2 activation. Combined XPS, Fe-leaching, filtration, radical-quenching, fluorescence, and open-circuit potential results suggest that the enhancement arises from coupled FeSiB surface-mediated H2O2 activation, improved Fe2+ availability, dissolved Fe-assisted redox cycling, and magnetic field affected interfacial behavior. TOC and LC-MS analyses further show partial mineralization through hydroxylation, oxidative denitration, oxidation, and ring-opening reactions. This work provides guidance for designing intrinsically magnetic amorphous catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: An integrated modelling framework for feedback-driven and mass-balanced circular economy analysis
abstract: Achieving a circular economy requires not only quantifying material stocks and flows but also understanding the dynamic processes that shape them over time. While Material Flow Analysis (MFA) is widely used to track physical stocks and flows, MFA has limited capacity to represent behavioral feedback, endogenous system responses, and temporal delays. System Dynamics (SD), by contrast, is well suited to capturing feedback structures and non-linear system behavior, but it does not inherently enforce mass conservation. Despite these fundamental differences, the two approaches are often applied without a clear conceptual distinction. Here, we compare and integrate MFA and SD to develop a modelling framework that is both mass balanced and feedback driven. Using three simplified models (MFA, SD, and integrated SD-MFA), we demonstrate that the integrated approach can simultaneously preserve mass balance and represent causal relationships, feedback loops, and time delays. The combined framework offers a more robust basis for analyzing circular economy transitions, enabling the assessment of not only how materials flow through systems, but also how socio-technical dynamics influence those flows over time.

title: Mechanistic insights into coupled Fe–S–N cycling in constructed wetlands: potential contributions of cable bacteria and their community associations
abstract: Cable bacteria exhibit remarkable electron-transfer capabilities and are commonly enriched in sulfur (S)-rich environments, where they actively interact with diverse microorganisms. However, the potential link between cable bacteria-mediated S cycling and nitrogen (N) metabolism in constructed wetlands (CWs) remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, four sets of CWs with different Fe and S conditions were developed under near-natural conditions to investigate the underlying microbial mechanisms. The findings showed that cable bacteria functioned as key modular hubs within the microbial network, linking abiotic FeS2-mediated electron-transfer processes with biogeochemical S cycling. By employing long-distance electron transfer (LDET) and extracellular electron transfer (EET), cable bacteria enhanced the quinone pool capacity of N-removing bacteria. They promoted direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) within S-autotrophic denitrification (SAD) pathways and among associated microbial populations. This electron-transfer mechanism contributed to the coupled Fe–S–N cycle, resulting in a 30.89% increase in nitrogen removal efficiency compared with CWs-CK. Overall, this study provides novel insights into the synergistic interactions among S, Fe, and microbial communities, offering a mechanistic basis for optimizing SAD-based processes in CWs.

title: Is ESG always profitable? Sustainability transition and dimension-level evidence from an emerging market banking system
abstract: Banks play a central role in financing sustainability transitions by allocating credit to firms engaged in green investment, climate-risk adaptation, and cleaner production activities. Yet empirical evidence on whether ESG engagement improves bank profitability remains mixed, partly because ESG is often measured through composite indices that combine heterogeneous environmental, social, and governance dimensions. This study examines whether ESG measurement design shapes the observed ESG–profitability relationship in a regulated emerging market banking system. Using panel data from BIST-listed banking institutions in Türkiye with available Refinitiv ESG data over the 2016–2023 period, the study estimates fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors to compare composite and dimension-specific ESG specifications. ESG variables are lagged to partially reduce simultaneity concerns, while the estimates are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. The results show that the composite ESG score is not statistically associated with bank profitability, measured by return on assets (ROA). When ESG is decomposed into its individual pillars, only the social dimension exhibits a negative and statistically significant short-term association, whereas the environmental and governance dimensions remain insignificant. This pattern suggests that composite ESG scores may obscure dimension-specific financial dynamics, although limited statistical power, unequal pillar variation, measurement error, and finite-sample instability remain plausible alternative explanations. The study provides context-specific evidence that ESG measurement design matters for sustainable banking and cleaner production financing. For regulators, bank boards, and ESG reporting units, the findings are consistent with the practical value of pillar-level ESG assessment. Whether the environmental pillar translates into green credit allocation, transition finance, and long-term cleaner production investment remains a direction for future research rather than a finding directly established by this analysis.

title: Evolution path of anti-involution in photovoltaic enterprises driven by digital twin technology
abstract: In the context of the global energy transition and the “dual carbon” goals, China's photovoltaic industry is trapped in an involutionary dilemma characterized by overcapacity, homogenized competition, price wars, declining profits, and low operational efficiency. Traditional decision-making methods are inadequate for supporting dynamic and quantitative anti-involution governance. To address these challenges and optimize strategic decision-making, this paper introduces digital twin technology into the decision management of the photovoltaic industry. Based on data from 98 listed photovoltaic companies between 2020 and 2024, this study processes the indicators, calculates a comprehensive price, and constructs a baseline real-time information matrix. Three proactive anti-involution strategies are designed: price increases, Research and Development (R&D) investment, and combined strategy, along with a passive non-intervention option. A 300-day dynamic simulation matrix iteration mechanism is established, and a profit and loss evaluation model is constructed to quantify the decision effects. The research results show that while a pure price increase can improve short-term profits, it lacks sustainability. Independent R&D investment can enhance product differentiation but increases financial pressure. Within the proposed simulation framework, the combined strategy achieves the highest comprehensive profit and loss value among all tested alternatives, suggesting that the simultaneous pursuit of value-recovery pricing and R&D intensification offers a structurally superior path for balancing short-term profit recovery with long-term technological upgrade needs, subject to the model's calibration assumptions and the absence of strategic competitor retaliation. This study extends the application of digital twin technology to the field of industrial strategic decision-making and constructs a quantitative anti-involution framework, providing a reference for companies to escape low-price competition, optimize resource allocation, and achieve high-quality development.

title: Urban organisms’ metabolic laws and policy effects: A weight-physique perspective
abstract: Rapid urbanization has given rise to severe resource consumption and environmental pollution, which can be conceptualized as urban material and pollutant metabolism issues. Drawing parallels between cities and natural organisms, this study treats cities as “urban organisms” and explores how urban weight (population, GDP, built-up area) and physique (industrial structure-based functional types) shape urban metabolism, aiming to enhance the sustainability of urban material metabolism. Using 20 typical Chinese megacities as cases, we analyzed metabolic patterns from 2000 to 2020 and projected future trajectories (2025–2035) under policy intervention and no-policy scenarios. The results reveal that urban weight and metabolic scale exhibit a negative allometric growth pattern (coefficient = 0.76), analogous to natural organisms. Metabolic characteristics vary significantly across urban physique types, with material consumption structure and metabolic network functionality being most notably differentiated. Policy interventions are projected to reduce urban metabolic scale by approximately 20%, improve the metabolic network functionality of over 50% of cities, and refine the allometric growth coefficient to 0.75, bringing it closer to Kleiber's Law. This study provides a metabolic perspective on sustainable urban transitions, underscoring the necessity of tailoring governance strategies to specific urban physiques to mitigate metabolic pressures from expansion, providing evidence-based insights for sustainable urban policy-making.

title: Unveiling the role of soil in urban vegetation greenness: City-scale evidence from field sampling across green spaces in Shanghai
abstract: Urban green spaces (UGSs) provide essential ecological functions in highly urbanized landscapes, yet city-scale associations between soil conditions and vegetation greenness remain insufficiently understood due to limited field-based evidence. This study investigated Shanghai, China, by integrating long-term Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time-series data from 2000 to 2020 with field soil sampling from 183 UGS sites, covering 18 edaphic properties. Together with vegetation baseline, human activity, and climate covariates, we assessed the relative and spatially heterogeneous associations of soil conditions with vegetation greenness dynamics (VGD) and current vegetation greenness (VG). Shanghai's UGSs showed substantially stronger greening than the broader urban background, with a mean VGD of 0.074 decade−1 compared with 0.017 decade−1 citywide, and 87.98% of sampled sites exhibited positive greening trends. Park green spaces maintained higher VG and stronger VGD than roadside green spaces, while VGD and VG were significantly but only moderately associated, indicating that they represent distinct dimensions of UGS performance. Attribution analysis showed that vegetation baseline and soil properties were the dominant contributors to VGD, explaining 17% and 11% of the variance, respectively. For VG, soil emerged as the leading determinant, independently explaining 15% of spatial variation, with associations distributed across multiple edaphic dimensions rather than controlled by a single soil property. Spatial modeling further revealed scale-dependent soil associations: soil–VGD associations were strongest in intermediate and outer urban zones, whereas soil–VG associations were more outward-oriented and more frequently negative. These findings provide city-scale empirical evidence that soil conditions are associated with urban greenness patterns in spatially heterogeneous ways, highlighting the need for soil-sensitive UGS assessment and management across urban gradients.

title: Mechanistic insights into lidocaine degradation in UV/H2O2 and Fenton systems: A computational investigation of pathways, kinetics, and toxicity evolution
abstract: Lidocaine (LDC), a widely used local anesthetic, is incompletely removed during wastewater treatment and may persist in aquatic environments. In this study, density functional theory (DFT), transition state theory (TST), kinetic modeling, QSAR-based toxicity prediction, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were integrated to investigate the transformation of LDC initiated by reactive species, its degradation performance in advanced oxidation processes, and the associated risk evolution. Among ·OH, HO2·, 1O2, and O3, ·OH exhibited the highest reactivity toward LDC, with a calculated second order rate constant of 9.39 × 109 M−1 s−1 at 298 K. Kinetic simulations showed that both UV/H2O2 and Fenton oxidation performed more effectively under acidic conditions but exhibited distinct treatment characteristics. Under the selected operating conditions, Fenton oxidation provided faster initial removal, whereas UV/H2O2 achieved more sustained and extensive removal during prolonged treatment. Reaction network analysis proposed 14 plausible intermediates and transformation products formed through hydroxylation, hydrogen abstraction, demethylation, and amide bond cleavage. Transformation was not predicted to necessarily result in detoxification, as several products showed increased aquatic toxicity or bioconcentration potential. Notably, MD simulations indicated that the transformation product 2,6-dimethylphenol exhibited stronger membrane affinity than LDC and caused greater expansion and thinning of the lipid bilayer. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the transformation of pharmaceutical contaminants by reactive species and support process optimization, environmental risk assessment, and cleaner treatment process design.

title: Effect of replacement rate on longevity and methane emissions for dairy herds in New Zealand
abstract: A high replacement rate in dairy herds is desirable to accelerate genetic gain. However, higher replacement costs are incurred, and average age and maturity of the herd is decreased, which can diminish overall herd productivity and profitability, but effects on methane emissions have not been reported. This study examines the relationship between herd replacement rate, longevity and methane emissions of the New Zealand dairy herd under grazing conditions. Three herd replacement scenarios were examined, low (13%), base (17%) and high (19.5%) using a farm model to quantify the annual metabolizable energy requirements for growth, maintenance, pregnancy and milk production for the national herd. Farm income was the sale of dairy products, culled cows and surplus calves, minus processing costs. Methane emissions were calculated using dry matter requirements and were expressed as CO 2-e . An increase in the replacement rate from 13% to 19.5% resulted in a reduction of 400 days in the life expectancy of a cow. The methane emission at the low replacement rate was 7.97 kg CO 2 -e/kg fat + protein, while methane emission at the high replacement rate was 8.81 kg CO 2 -e/kg fat + protein. By increasing the lifetime of the cow producing milk, the methane burden decreased from 3.0 kg total CH 4 /kg lactational CH 4 when the cow is 3 years old, to 2.1 kg CH 4 /kg CH 4 when the cow reaches 10-years. A better alignment between profitable production and consumer needs, animal welfare and an improved environment is needed.

title: Structure-guided tuning of the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio enables low-temperature fiberization of red mud slags
abstract: Producing high-quality inorganic fibers from red mud is an effective route for its high-value utilization; however, the high-alumina, high-alkali nature of red mud gives rise to melts with limited fluidity and a strong crystallization tendency, thereby impairing fiberization performance. To enable the production of high-quality fibers from red-mud-derived slag, this study combines thermodynamic calculations, crystallization-kinetics analysis, and structural characterization by Raman spectroscopy, MAS NMR, and XPS to elucidate how the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio governs the minimum suitable fiber-forming conditions and melt structure; these findings are further validated by centrifugal fiberization experiments. The results show that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio from 0.8 to 2.8 markedly improves melt fluidity, lowering the flow temperature by 92 °C. During melting, the coexisting mineral phases evolve from Al-rich refractory phases to Ca-Mg silicate phases, substantially narrowing the temperature interval between the deformation and flow points. During cooling, the primary crystalline phase precipitating from the melt is nepheline (NaAlSiO4). With increasing SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio, the crystallization driving force (Ran) decreases by 0.177%/K, whereas the crystallization activation energy (Ec) increases by 141.1 kJ/mol, indicating a substantially reduced crystallization propensity. Moreover, the crystallization process is surface-crystallization-dominated (n = 0.9-2.3). The minimum suitable fiber-forming temperature decreases by approximately 200 °C as the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio increases, and the controlling factor shifts from crystallization-limited to fluidity-limited behavior at SiO2/Al2O3 = 1.8. Structural analysis at the minimum suitable fiber-forming temperature shows that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio raises the fractions of Q3+Q4 units and bridging oxygen, increases the proportion of [AlO5]7- species, and enhances network polymerization. Meanwhile, the tendency toward local ordering weakens, leading to a gradual improvement in the glass-forming ability of the red-mud-derived melt. Centrifugal fiberization experiments demonstrate that increasing the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio reduces the average fiber diameter by approximately 41% and the slag-shot content by 5.7 percentage points. At SiO2/Al2O3 = 1.8, the fiber properties meet the relevant national standards, supporting the synergistic improvement in fiber performance arising from the optimized melt structure and enhanced amorphous-forming ability at this composition. Collectively, these results demonstrate that tuning the SiO2/Al2O3 mass ratio to synergistically regulate network polymerization, Al coordination, and the local Si-O-Al configuration enhances the glass-forming ability of red-mud-derived melts, thereby providing a mechanistic basis for compositional redesign and process optimization toward high-quality inorganic fibers.

title: Manufacture or recycle? Strategies for green products in a closed-loop supply chain
abstract: This study develops a two-period model for a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) focused on manufacturing and recycling green products supported by government subsidies. The manufacturer produces green products in the first period and, in the second period, may supplement new production by recycling used products collected from the market. We find that the structure of optimal decisions of agents in centralized and decentralized settings is driven by the savings from recycling. The study highlights the inefficiencies in the decentralized supply chain under the wholesale price contract and proposes a two-part tariff contract to achieve coordination. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of retailer competition on the CLSC performance and we find that under competition, manufacturers produce new products in the second period irrespective of the savings from recycling. In contrast, the manufacturer in the monopolistic retailer setting refrains from manufacturing new products for higher levels of savings from recycling.

title: Driving green ethical behaviour: the sequential effects of transformational leadership, ethical climate and co-worker ethical behaviour
abstract: This study examines how owner-managers’ transformational leadership influences employee green ethical behaviour through ethical climate and co-worker ethical behaviour. Data were collected from 388 owner-managers and employees of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana. The results show that transformational leadership positively influences employee green ethical behaviour. Although ethical climate does not significantly moderate the relationship between transformational leadership and green ethical behaviour, it mediates this relationship. The findings also reveal a sequential mediation effect, where transformational leadership enhances ethical climate, which promotes co-worker ethical behaviour and, in turn, improves employee green ethical behaviour. The study highlights that green ethical behaviour is driven not only by leadership directly, but also through the combined influence of organizational norms and peer behaviour.

title: The impact of green finance on the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction: Exploring the moderating role of institutional environment and spatial spillover effects
abstract: Promoting the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction (PCCR synergy) is now a key strategy in climate-change governance. By channeling capital toward clean industries, green finance (GF) plays a key role in promoting economic growth alongside environmental improvement. Using data from 282 Chinese cities during 2007-2023, this paper examines the direct impact of GF on PCCR synergy, as well as the mechanisms and spatial spillovers involved. We demonstrate that GF substantially enhances PCCR synergy. The mechanism analysis shows that GF promotes PCCR synergy mainly by strengthening green technology innovation, promoting energy transition, and advancing industrial upgrading. In addition, regional integration strengthens this positive impact by reducing administrative barriers, whereas climate policy uncertainty weakens the effectiveness of GF by increasing investment hesitation. The heterogeneity results suggest that GF promotes PCCR synergy more strongly in resource-based cities than in non-resource-based cities. Further analysis shows that this promoting effect is most pronounced in growing and mature resource-based cities. Furthermore, we reveal a beggar-thy-neighbor phenomenon. Although GF improves local synergy, it generates negative spatial spillovers for neighboring areas through resource siphoning and pollution transfer. These findings deepen the understanding of GF-induced environmental synergy and offer policy guidance for differentiated governance and the promotion of environmental equity across regions.

title: Enhancing sustainable oil palm management through plantation age mapping and yield estimation
abstract: Improving oil palm production without further land expansion requires spatially explicit identification of both yield potential and renewal pressure. Here, we combine remote-sensing-based plantation age mapping with biophysical suitability and management adjustments to estimate oil palm yield across Malaysia. In 2020, 28.1% of stands were 9–14 years old and 26.0% were 15–24 years old, indicating mounting renewal pressure in the coming decade. Consistent with this pattern, 32.2% of cultivated area was classified as high-yield, whereas 13.8% was identified as requiring replanting. Predicted state-level production agreed well with official statistics for 2018–2022 (R2 > 0.73; error < 1.6 Mt) and reproduced the main production cores in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak. These findings show that integrating age structure, site suitability, and management constraints can identify where productivity can be sustained and where delayed renewal may threaten future supply. Its outputs are intended to support regional screening, replanting prioritization, and more efficient resource allocation; application elsewhere requires region-specific recalibration and independent local validation.

title: Doped NiFe2O4 spinel oxygen carriers for enhanced H2 production in photo-assisted chemical looping reforming with water splitting under mild conditions
abstract: Photo-assisted chemical looping reforming coupled with water splitting (PA-CLR-WS) provides a promising route for H2 production under relatively mild conditions, but its performance strongly depends on the ability of oxygen carriers (OCs) to balance redox activity, structural stability, and photo-response behavior. In this study, NiFe2O4 spinel was selected as the matrix, and a series of Co- and Cu-doped AxNi1−xFe2O4 OCs (A = Co or Cu; x = 0.10, 0.25, and 0.50) were prepared to clarify the dopant-dependent regulation of NiFe2O4 in PA-CLR-WS. The results show that the introduction of Co and Cu affects NiFe2O4 through different pathways. Low-level Co doping helps maintain the spinel structure and improves photo-generated charge separation and transport, thereby promoting H2 production during the steam reaction. In contrast, Cu doping enhances low-temperature reducibility but excessive Cu incorporation leads to stronger carrier recombination and particle agglomeration, which limits the effective utilization of photo-generated carriers and weakens the overall H2 production performance. Among the tested OCs, Co0.10Ni0.90Fe2O4 exhibited the best overall performance at 600°C under light irradiation, achieving an H2 yield of 9.5 mmol g−1 OCs with a purity of ≥98%. During 20 cycles, it maintained high H2 purity, with H2 yield fluctuating within 8.0-9.5 mmol g−1 OCs. These findings demonstrate that moderate Co introduction is more effective than Cu introduction for optimizing NiFe2O4 in the present PA-CLR-WS system and provide guidance for the compositional design of spinel OCs for low-temperature chemical looping hydrogen production.

title: Life cycle assessment of the Mekong Delta rice supply chain: emission inventory and mitigation pathways toward food security synergies
abstract: Despite growing pressure to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions in rice systems, supply chain assessments jointly addressing mitigation and food availability trade-offs within an explicit national policy framework remain limited. Vietnam's Mekong Delta, supplying approximately 10% of global rice trade while accounting for 48% of national agricultural emissions, represents a critical case study for evidence-based mitigation. We conducted an LCA drawing on 11 focus groups with rice farmers and 478 farmer and post-harvest stakeholder interviews to quantify cradle-to-market carbon intensities and evaluate mitigation scenarios and food security trade-offs under a cradle-to-dryer-gate boundary. Cradle-to-market carbon intensities were 2.96 and 2.93 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 for market-ready milled rice in the domestic and export channels, respectively, with over 97% of emissions concentrated in cultivation, dominated by methane from flooded fields and anaerobic straw decomposition, the two highest-sensitivity parameters. We established a Business-as-Usual baseline (1.84 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 dried paddy; 46.52 Mt CO 2 -eq yr −1 ) to enable scenario-based analysis across six intervention levers through single-lever, trade-off, and policy-aligned scenarios. Deep alternate wetting and drying and intensified straw removal achieved single-lever reductions of 14-26%. Trade-off analysis revealed two mitigation pathways: structural interventions, such as land transformation, achieved larger reductions but cut milled rice output by up to 18%, while efficiency-based interventions (food loss reduction, silo drying) reduced emissions while improving food availability. The integrated MI3 achieved a 31% reduction in total GHG emissions alongside a 1.75% increase in milled rice output, surpassing current policy targets and suggesting that ambitious mitigation need not reduce food availability under the modelled conditions. These findings demonstrate that mitigation and food security can be mutually reinforcing, offering actionable pathways for Vietnam's One Million Low-Emission Hectare Initiative and Nationally Determined Contributions.

title: Digital transformation and the diffusion of social sustainability practices in supply chains: Evidence from buyer–supplier dyads
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) has been widely acknowledged for its potential to promote social sustainability practice (SSP). As the world's primary manufacturing center, China has witnessed rapid adoption of DT; nevertheless, lingering social sustainability issues have exposed a significant gap in research on how such transformation drives the diffusion of SSP along supply chains. To address this research gap, this study employs fixed effects regression and difference-in-differences analysis using panel data from 2750 Chinese manufacturing firms and 186 buyer–supplier dyads from 2011 to 2021. Grounded in the knowledge diffusion perspective, the study identifies that DT exerts a positive effect on the SSP of both focal firms and their suppliers, while supplier SSP mediates the link between buyer DT and buyer SSP. Furthermore, high buyer power attenuates the reverse diffusion pathway of SSP from suppliers to buyer firms. These findings are further validated by difference-in-differences estimation. By framing DT as an enabler of SSP-related knowledge transfer and power asymmetry as a barrier to reverse knowledge flows from suppliers to buyers, this study deepens theoretical understanding and offers practical implications for industry practitioners.

title: A data mining-enhanced machine learning model considering breakpoint events for daily carbon dioxide emissions forecasting
abstract: Accurate prediction of carbon dioxide emissions is crucial for formulating emission reduction strategies in various sectors. However, major events such as the pandemic and policies can alter the underlying driving mechanisms of carbon dioxide emissions, leading to breakpoints that reduce prediction accuracy. Therefore, a data mining-enhanced machine learning model considering breakpoint events was proposed for daily carbon dioxide emission forecasting. This model integrated breakpoint detection with segment clustering to identify segments with similar underlying driving mechanisms, thereby effectively filtering out anomalous fluctuations and mitigating the adverse impacts of structural shifts caused by shocks from major events. Furthermore, an adaptive prediction framework based on complexity classification was constructed to accurately predict carbon dioxide emissions in sectors with different features. Six carbon dioxide emission sectors in China were employed to validate the effectiveness of the model. Results indicated that the proposed model achieved high prediction accuracy, with the average mean absolute percentage error of only 0.42%. Comparative analysis showed that the integration of breakpoint detection with segment clustering and the adaptive prediction framework improved the forecast accuracy by 43.75% and 60.48%, respectively. Therefore, the proposed model can serve as an effective predictive tool to support carbon reduction efforts across sectors.

title: BCT adoption for organic product deter counterfeiting: Tripartite evolutionary game with government involvement
abstract: Counterfeiting has triggered a series of food safety issues. Organic firms and governments face dilemmas in deciding whether to adopt blockchain technology (BCT) and enforce strict supervision, respectively. Based on this context, we construct a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, conventional firms, and organic firms. We analyze key factors influencing individual stability and examine the impact of organic product attractiveness on system equilibrium. The findings indicate that: (1) When organic products have high (scenario H) or extremely high (scenario E) attractiveness, the government should adopt a lenient supervision approach combined with high-level fines to maintain market order. (2) The adoption of blockchain by organic firms is most stable under conditions of extremely high organic product attractiveness (scenario E). (3) The counterfeiting strategies of conventional firms have limited applicability. Such behaviors are more likely to occur in markets markets with low organic product attractiveness (scenario L) or low-level fines. This study extends the organic agricultural supply chain literature beyond traditional operational decisions by revealing the dynamic evolutionary mechanism underlying technology adoption, counterfeit deterrence, and government regulation. Furthermore, it identifies organic product attractiveness as a novel contingency factor that reshapes the evolutionary stability of supply chain stakeholders, thereby advancing the theoretical understanding of blockchain-enabled market governance. Practically, the findings provide guidance for organic firms’ blockchain adoption decisions and government anti-counterfeiting policies.

title: Modeling sustainable development in resource-based regions: New evidence from an improved multivariate grey model
abstract: As global climate change intensifies, reducing carbon emissions has become a critical global issue. As a pivotal energy-producing province in China, Shanxi Province has high carbon emissions and therefore faces significant challenges in meeting the national “Dual Carbon” goals. To address the inherent limitations of first-order accumulation in the traditional grey model, which struggles to handle the volatility of raw data sequences effectively, this study proposes a variable-order weighted multivariate grey model integrated with grey relational analysis. This model is employed to analyze the dynamic evolutionary characteristics of carbon emissions in Shanxi Province and to simulate emission trends under various scenarios. Grey relational analysis was employed to identify key factors influencing carbon emissions, including coal consumption, thermal power installed capacity, and the value added by the secondary industry. The results indicate that by 2030, carbon emissions in Shanxi Province under the business-as-usual scenario will continue to rise to 691.13 Mt, whereas emissions will be 597.70 Mt under the low-carbon sustainable development scenario and 812.58 Mt under the fossil energy-driven scenario. Notably, Shanxi Province is projected to achieve its carbon peak target before 2030 under the low-carbon sustainable development scenario. Furthermore, the robustness of the proposed model was verified by constructing a validation framework that incorporates the three dimensions of sample input, model parameter structure, and data statistical error interference to assess the model's accuracy. Based on the research findings, relevant recommendations are provided to reduce carbon emissions in Shanxi Province.

title: Assessing the impact of green certificate market transformation on China's carbon market under a multi-market coupling framework
abstract: China's 2023 revision of its green-certificate policy marks a new phase for tradable green certificates (TGCs), but its implications for national carbon emission trading (CET) remain unclear. The reform turns TGCs into an accounting basis for renewable-electricity environmental attributes, whereas current CET compliance remains centered on direct emissions. We construct a system dynamics model coupling China's TGC, power, and CET markets to examine how this accounting reform could affect carbon-market outcomes as policy boundaries expand. A mechanism-separated scenario ladder distinguishes TGC issuance expansion, tiered industrial CET expansion, indirect-emission accounting under compensating free allocation, and bundled green-power deduction. Monthly simulations over a January 2022 to January 2035 horizon, with 2022 used for base-year initialization and the post-reform policy transition evaluated from January 2023 onward, show that TGC issuance expansion alone has limited direct carbon-market effects: the 2035 carbon price rises by 5.24% while allowance demand remains broadly stable. Scarcity is reshaped mainly by CET design: the two industrial-expansion steps raise the carbon price by 7.85% and 3.53%, and adding electricity-related indirect emissions increases gross allowance demand by 22.29% and the carbon price by 10.41%. Once this boundary is active, bundled green-power deduction credits 56.94 million MWh/month by 2035, equal to 15.33% of covered purchased electricity, reducing electricity-related allowance demand by 6.06%, total allowance demand by 1.63%, and the carbon price by 6.07%. The reform therefore functions first as renewable-attribute accounting infrastructure; its carbon-market role emerges only when explicit, double-counting-safe linkage rules convert those attributes into bounded compliance flexibility.

title: Pyrolysis temperature controls long-term stability of heavy metals in sludge-derived biochar after soil application and oxidative aging
abstract: We evaluated how pyrolysis temperature and post-application aging jointly control heavy-metal speciation and ecological risk in sewage sludge-derived biochars. Metal-enriched sludge was pyrolyzed at 300, 500, 700, and 900 °C, mixed with soil, and aerobically incubated for 300 days; metal partitioning was quantified using a modified BCR (European Community Bureau of Reference) sequential extraction. To evaluate the resistance of metal stabilization to accelerated oxidative aging, pristine materials were pretreated with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2; 1% or 5%, w/v) before 30-day soil incubation. A temperature-dependent transition in metal stabilization occurred between 500 and 700 °C, with metal partitioning shifting from oxidizable fractions (F4) to mineral-dominated residual fractions (F5) at ≥700 °C. During pyrolysis, Hg was almost completely volatilized at 300 °C, and Cd decreased markedly at ≥700 °C, indicating volatility-driven reduction in solid-phase risk. In contrast, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn, Ni, and As were largely retained and exhibited element-specific redistribution during soil incubation. Pb, Cr, Cu, and Zn showed progressive enrichment in F5, whereas Ni stabilization was mainly established during pyrolysis. Arsenic remained comparatively sensitive to oxidative alteration, displaying measurable redistribution during aging. The fraction-based modified ecological risk index values were lowest for ≥700 °C biochars and remained low after aging, indicating that high-temperature pyrolysis enhances long-term stability but requires emission control for volatilized metals.

title: One-pot Cr3+-catalyzed alkaline oxidative hydrolysis for isolation of cellulose nanocrystals from waste paper towels
abstract: A one-pot Cr3+-catalyzed alkaline oxidative hydrolysis route was developed for the isolation of cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) from post-consumer waste paper towels (WPT), a cellulose-rich sanitary waste stream that remains largely underutilized. The process was conducted under mild conditions (75.00 °C, 30.00 min, dilute catalyst loading) and avoided concentrated mineral acids and multistep pretreatment. The study aimed to evaluate whether a sanitary paper waste feedstock could be converted into structurally robust CNC through a transition-metal-catalyzed oxidative pathway while maintaining low catalyst residue in the final product. A CNC yield of 63.00 ± 2.00% was obtained based on the dry cellulose-rich input. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed retention of the cellulose backbone together with removal of non-cellulosic additives and formation of mildly oxidized surface groups, including carbonyl/carboxylate functionalities. Wide-angle X-ray scattering showed an increase in crystallinity index from 68.80 ± 0.40% for WPT to 82.20 ± 0.50% for CNC, indicating selective removal of amorphous contents. Transmission electron microscopy revealed rod-like CNC with average dimensions of 100.00 ± 20.00 nm in length and 8.00 ± 2.00 nm in width. Thermogravimetric analysis showed improved thermal stability, with a maximum degradation temperature of 372.00 °C for CNC compared with 330.00 °C for raw WPT. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed removal of calcium carbonate-rich surface additives and showed no detectable chromium on the CNC surface, while inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry confirmed that 98.80% of the introduced chromium was removed during purification. The main contribution of this work is the demonstration that pre-bleached sanitary paper waste can serve as a suitable feedstock for one-pot catalytic CNC production, yielding high-crystallinity and thermally stable nanocrystal without conventional strong-acid hydrolysis. The main limitation is that catalyst recovery, liquid-stream management, and process-level environmental assessment were not investigated in this laboratory-scale study and should be addressed in future scale-up, techno-economic, and life-cycle investigations.

title: Determining time- and region- specific electricity carbon emission factors with dynamic spatial zoning
abstract: Constructing a high-resolution electricity carbon emission factor (ECEF) accounting model is the foundation for the low-carbon transition of new-type power systems. Existing research on zoning methods for carbon emission factor accounting remains insufficient, and green Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) face the risk of distorted green electricity rights accounting when transmission channels are congested. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Time- and Region- Specific ECEF accounting model that decouples the physical base-map from the market floating-layer.
