The index is designed as a screening tool to guide, not replace, comprehensive lifecycle assessment, and its component weights should be adjusted based on specific application contexts and regional infrastructure availability. Any quantitative framework must be interpreted with attention to context (application requirements, infrastructure, waste management). We conclude with a forward-looking perspective on the interdisciplinary convergence—policy, scalable manufacturing, lifecycle thinking—needed for a truly circular polymer economy.

title: Whole process risk assessment of hazardous waste in typical non-ferrous metal production systems: a case study in China
abstract: The rapid economic expansion and industrialization have significantly increased hazardous waste (HW) generation, and the corresponding lifecycle environmental risks have evolved into a major issue requiring systematic resolution. Conventional assessments are incapable of accurately quantifying the compound risks of various HWs, resulting in challenges in implementing targeted management and control measures. This study establishes a whole process risk assessment framework for the classification and grading of HW management, considering waste attribute identification, toxic migration effect and process disposal difficulty. Focusing on 30 HW categories in non-ferrous metal industry, nine critical waste categories from copper and aluminum smelting industries were evaluated by employing the entropy weight method and analytic hierarchy process. Annual data analysis reveals that HW generation surged from 5.75 to 14.39 million tons from 2021 to 2023, primarily concentrated in aluminum and lead-zinc smelting industries. Based on waste attribute identification, fluoride is identified as the main pollutant in aluminum smelting, whereas Fe2O3, As2O3, and CdO are determined as the primary concerns in copper smelting. By evaluating toxic migration effect, the leaching toxicity of copper smelting waste (11413.05) markedly exceeds that of aluminum smelting waste (1155.96). In terms of process disposal difficulty (RDD), more attention should be paid to the copper smelting industry with the RDD value of NF32 for 7.96. Under the whole process risk assessment, 321-023-48 (NF23) is identified as the HW posing the highest risk, demonstrating an annual risk value of 17.08. The assessment quantifies risks of the HW process chain, thereby supporting targeted management and sustainable development in the non-ferrous metal industry.

title: Peak prediction and emission reduction pathways of building operational carbon emissions in Eastern China
abstract: Building operational carbon emissions constitute the largest and most persistent share of the building sector's carbon footprint, yet their peak trajectory in Eastern China remains insufficiently investigated. This study develops an integrated accounting, driving factor identification, and prediction framework. The emission factor method quantifies building operational carbon emissions in Eastern China and its four sub-regions from 2000 to 2022. An extended STIRPAT model with ridge regression identifies driving factors. A TimeGAN-GS-LSTM model projects emission trajectories under three scenarios from 2023 to 2060. Results show that: (1) Carbon emissions in Eastern China increased from 244 MtCO2 to 922 MtCO2 from 2000 to 2022, with BTH as the dominant emission core. (2) GDP per capita (GDPpc) and urbanization rate (UR) are the primary positive drivers. (3) The Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) data augmentation technique effectively alleviates overfitting under small-sample conditions and significantly enhances prediction performance, ultimately achieving an R2 value of 0.94 for Eastern China. (4) Scenario projections indicate that emissions in Eastern China will peak in 2041 under the low-carbon scenario (LCS), 2047 under the baseline scenario (BAS), and 2056 under the high-carbon scenario (HCS), with pronounced regional heterogeneity. The PRD and BTH regions peak earliest in 2036 under LCS, while YRD peaks later in 2041 due to efficiency ceilings and service sector rigidity. (5) Sensitivity analysis indicates that macroeconomic and demographic factors exert a stronger influence on peak timing than technological parameters such as energy intensity and carbon intensity. These findings provide quantitative evidence for regionally differentiated decarbonization pathways in Eastern China, emphasizing that policy instruments must be tailored to each region's dominant driving factors.

title: GONGGA-Lagrange: A novel atmospheric carbon inversion system integrating NLS-4DVar assimilation method and the Lagrangian particle dispersion model
abstract: By updating the Global ObservatioN-based system for monitoring Greenhouse GAses (GONGGA) with the Lagrangian particle dispersion model (LPDM), we developed a novel regional carbon inversion system named GONGGA-Lagrange (GONGGA-L). The system employs the nonlinear least squares four-dimensional variational (NLS-4DVar) assimilation method, enabling ensemble-based, flow-dependent prior error covariance modeling and scalable computational performance, thereby distinguishing it from conventional LPDM-based inversion systems. We evaluated GONGGA-L's performance in estimating the 2017 North American net ecosystem exchange (NEE) using Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) built upon CarbonTracker 2022 flux data and a high-resolution footprint library. The validation comprised baseline OSSEs, which compared the intrinsic performance of GONGGA-L against the established CarbonTracker-Lagrange (CT-L) system under idealized conditions, and subsequent experiments that assessed robustness under more realistic transport errors and complex observation noise. The results demonstrate that GONGGA-L effectively assimilates observations, leading to a substantial reduction in prior NEE flux errors, with annual average reductions of 21.7% for Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and 22.1% for Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). During both winter and summer, the spatial patterns of inversion increments between GONGGA-L and CT-L are generally consistent; however, GONGGA-L tends to provide more effective correction of prior errors. Sensitivity analyses indicate that GONGGA-L is robust to random observation noise and exhibits limited sensitivity to moderate systematic biases and transport errors. Parameter sensitivity tests suggest that performance is highest with ensemble sizes above ∼150 and the localization radius around 1300 km. Quantitative analysis shows that NLS-4DVar computational cost scales approximately linearly with model grid points and observation count; in a representative monthly case, GONGGA-L achieved a 4.3-fold speedup relative to CT-L. This substantial reduction in computational and memory demands positions GONGGA-L as a scalable solution for the assimilation of increasingly abundant satellite observations and has the potential to enable higher-resolution inversions.

title: Multi-criteria decision analysis for mass timber sourcing for construction in the United States
abstract: Mass timber (MT) is among the most sustainable construction materials for building structures. While U.S. building codes facilitate MT construction up to 18 stories of height, the frequent international sourcing of MT raises sustainability concerns regarding transportation emissions. Previous research relies primarily on deterministic whole building life cycle assessment (WBLCA), which lacks the mechanisms to balance environmental impacts with competing economic and logistical factors under uncertainty. To address this, we developed a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework that employs a Weighted Sum Model (WSM) to establish a deterministic baseline integrating upfront global warming impacts (GWI) (Modules A1–A4), material and transportation costs, and transportation times. To account for data ambiguity, this baseline is then expanded into a stochastic Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis (10,000 iterations) using parametric uncertainties (±40% for GWI and ±25% for costs). This framework was applied to four diverse U.S. cities, evaluating eight domestic and four international suppliers across multi-modal networks under three weighting cases (prioritizing GWI, Cost, or Time). Probabilistic results indicate that when prioritizing GWI, Canadian imports generally achieve the highest probability of optimality due to lower manufacturing emissions. Conversely, domestic U.S. manufacturers consistently emerge as optimal options when prioritizing economic costs or delivery times. These findings demonstrate that geographic proximity does not guarantee the highest sustainability, and MCDA often yields different optimal selections than WBLCA alone. Ultimately, this robust, customizable framework optimizes MT supply chain decisions and identifies areas where domestic infrastructure must improve for the local MT industry to outcompete the global marketplace.

title: Feasibility-enhanced and cluster-guided optimization for coordinated hydro-wind-photovoltaic dispatch under cross-regional power delivery
abstract: Large-scale hydro–wind–photovoltaic (HWP) bases are increasingly important for expanding clean-energy supply, yet their cross-regional operation is challenged by renewable variability and strongly coupled hydraulic and transmission constraints. This study develops a feasibility-enhanced, cluster-guided optimization framework for source–grid coordinated HWP dispatch under cross-regional power delivery (CRPD). A topology-explicit model links cascade reservoir regulation, bank-side hydropower allocation, channel-specific transmission limits, and receiving-end residual-load smoothing. A water-volume reallocation strategy (WRS) and dynamic constraint-handling strategy (DCHS) are integrated to restore terminal reservoir states and progressively guide the search toward feasible regions, while a cluster-guided optimization algorithm assigns differentiated search roles according to population structure and solution quality. A multi-level evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the framework. At the feasibility-enhancement level, WRS restored final water levels to the prescribed tolerances in all runs, and the selected DCHS reduced mean residual-load root-mean-square error (RLMSE) by 34.00%–67.16% relative to the fixed-rigid-constraint setting while increasing the mean proportion of feasible population (PFP) from 0% to 100%. At the algorithmic level, CGO ranked first in the Friedman analysis of 23 benchmark functions and retained the best average rank under a unified total function-evaluation budget. At the application level, it maintained a mean PFP of 100% across three representative HWP conditions and produced schedules that balanced residual-load smoothing, solution stability, and operational feasibility. The proposed framework therefore provides an effective means of leveraging hydropower flexibility to smooth receiving-end residual-load processes and support reliable cross-regional clean power delivery.

title: Coercive effects of land use carbon emissions on ecosystem service values and multi-scenario simulations in the mountain-river-sea transition zone: A case of the Southwest Guangxi Karst-Beibu Gulf, China
abstract: Revealing the coercive effects of land use carbon emissions (LUCE) on ecosystem service values (ESV) is a critical scientific issue for coordinating low-carbon development and ecological security in mountain-river-sea transition zone. Taking the Southwest Guangxi Karst-Beibu Gulf region as a case, this study systematically investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and response mechanisms of the coercive effects of LUCE on ESV from 2000 to 2030 through multi-scenario simulations and spatial analysis methods. The results indicate the following findings. LUCE and ESV exhibited a consistently significant negative correlation from 2000 to 2020, with the correlation coefficient intensifying from −0.350 to −0.363, indicating an overall strengthening of coercive relationships. Spatially, two typical coercion patterns characterized by High LUCE-Low ESV and Low LUCE-High ESV exhibited a significant reverse nested distribution. Specifically, the Low LUCE-High ESV pattern was stably concentrated in the interlaced areas of Karst forestlands and water bodies to form ecological buffer zones. Conversely, the High LUCE-Low ESV pattern expanded from point-like clusters around coastal ports and core urban areas toward inland river valleys along major transportation axes, resulting in the formation of coercion corridors. The region displayed a clear gradient differentiation pattern with high coercion in coastal areas, medium coercion in river valleys, and low coercion in mountainous areas. Multi-scenario simulations further demonstrate that under the guidance of ecological conservation and low-carbon development, the expansion of High LUCE-Low ESV zones slows down and coercion in local valleys is alleviated. Under the influence of economic development and high-carbon expansion, however, the coercion corridors further coalesce and expand toward inland hills and Karst fringe areas, which intensifies spatial polarization. This study provides a scientific basis for differentiated territorial spatial regulation and coordinated low-carbon optimization in the mountain-river-sea transition zone.

title: Interpretable machine learning reveals multi-scale controls on groundwater fluoride across the Shanxi rift system
abstract: Groundwater fluoride in the Shanxi Rift System displays marked spatial heterogeneity, with high-fluoride basins occurring adjacent to zones of totally low concentrations. This study investigates the factors responsible for this contrast by applying an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates supervised model comparison with posterior interpretation analyses. The modelling reveals a distinct scale dependence in fluoride controls. At the basin scale, fluoride enrichment is primarily influenced by hydrochemical conditions dominated by Ca2+ and HCO3−. At the cross-basin scale, however, the dominant control shifts to geological setting, particularly the distance to carbonate formations. Short distances correspond to higher Ca2+ and lower HCO3− conditions, resulting in hydrochemical “non-responsive intervals” in which fluoride concentrations remain low and insensitive to further changes in Ca2+ and HCO3−. This mechanism accounts for the anomalously low fluoride levels observed in the Changzhi Basin. Overall, the results demonstrate that fluoride distribution in the Shanxi Rift System is shaped by the combined effects of local hydrochemical equilibria and regional geological structure, and highlight the importance of explicitly considering spatial scale when interpreting the processes governing geogenic fluoride contamination.

title: Selective and sustainable lithium recovery via integrated electrocoagulation, ion exchange resin, and nanofiltration for high-purity Li3PO4 production
abstract: Due to the rapid growth in electric vehicle and electronic product production, the demand for lithium recovery from wastewater is increasing dramatically. Therefore, the development of cost-effective technologies has become crucial. In this study, a hybrid system based on nanofiltration (NF) and a pretreatment process consisting of a combination of electrocoagulation (EC) and ion exchange resin (IER) was investigated for the selective recovery of lithium from lithium-containing wastewater. The optimized EC and IER conditions of 6.00 V, pH 6.00, and 120 min increased boron removal to 99.5% and kept lithium loss to a minimum, creating a suitable feed for subsequent separation steps. Following pretreatment, four different NF membranes (NP030, NP010, NF270, and NF90) were tested. Lithium recoveries for NF270, NF90, NP010, and NP030 membranes (20 bar, pH 8.00) were 319.6 mg/L, 622.2 mg/L, 314.5 mg/L, and 333.2 mg/L, respectively. The optimized NF90 membrane increased the lithium concentration in the feed solution from 335 mg/L to 1054 mg/L at pH 8.00 and 40 bar pressure, achieving an approximately threefold concentration. The lithium-rich solution obtained after nanofiltration was further processed by phosphate precipitation to yield 95% pure Li3PO4. The produced Li3PO4 can be used as a lithium source for energy storage technologies such as lithium carbonate production in lithium-ion batteries. The results demonstrate that the hybrid approach using EC–IER pretreatment and the NF90 membrane offers a selective, efficient, and scalable lithium recovery method and represents a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to meet the growing industrial lithium demand.

title: From vulnerability to viability: A framework for equitable, climate-resilient EV infrastructure investment
abstract: Transportation electrification offers significant potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve public health, and promote energy justice. However, without intentional planning, electrification risks reinforcing spatial and social inequities in infrastructure access, environmental exposure, and climate vulnerability. This study introduces a multi-burden framework for prioritizing equitable and resilient EV infrastructure deployment. The approach integrates four domains of potential disadvantage: EV access, environmental exposure, socioeconomic vulnerability, and flood risk into a composite viability score (EVVS) that identifies communities where investment can most effectively address cumulative burdens, advance equitable electrification, and deliver the greatest justice-informed benefits. Each domain is assessed using publicly available indicators and summarized via Principal Component Analysis to preserve latent structure while reducing dimensionality. To avoid compensatory effects and preserve the salience of high burdens in individual domains, a Crowding-distance Pareto ranking method is used to produce a non-compensatory prioritization score. Demonstrated through a statewide case study in Connecticut, the framework delineates where intersecting social, environmental, and hazard-related burdens concentrate and where EV infrastructure investments can deliver the greatest equity and resilience gains. Results show pronounced spatial heterogeneity in burden patterns across towns. Across weighting schemes, EVVS values range from a mean of 0.49 (Pareto-based) to 0.59 (weighted schemes), with reduced variability under weighted configurations (standard deviation = 0.12). Burden domain means range from approximately 0.45 to 0.68 across the four burden components. Areas such as Windham and Litchfield County exhibiting consistently high, multi-dimensional burdens and emerging as viable locations for equitable EV infrastructure investment. More advantaged regions such as Fairfield County show lower intervention urgency. By embedding energy justice principles, the framework advances a transferable, policy-relevant approach for aligning EV infrastructure deployment with equity and climate-risk reduction goals.

title: A dynamic goal programming approach for sustainable product design: Balancing multi-dimensional sustainability objectives under uncertainty
abstract: This study develops a Dynamic Goal Programming (DGP) model for sustainable new product design that simultaneously optimizes economic, environmental, social, and material sustainability goals under real-world operational constraints. The model employs a rolling-horizon approach to handle stochastic demand and to dynamically recalibrate goal targets and objective weights across planning periods. A comprehensive Sustainability Index (SI) integrates weighted criteria including renewable energy use, hazardous material reduction, greenhouse gas emissions, customer satisfaction, and design usability. The specific contributions of this work are: (1) integration of material sustainability as a fourth optimization objective via hazardous material coefficients (hj), a dimension absent from all prior SNPD-GP studies documented in the literature; (2) a rolling-horizon DGP formulation in which goal targets, bound values, and objective weights are recalibrated at each planning period in response to updated demand and stock data; (3) direct embedding of the SI into the optimization objective rather than post-hoc evaluation, enabling sustainability metrics to govern production and material selection decisions in real time; and (4) a quantified Pareto frontier (α ∈ [0.1, 1.0]) enabling transparent managerial navigation of sustainability–profitability trade-offs, validated in the furniture manufacturing sector using 44 months of real production data. The results demonstrate that the model maintains strict economic viability (positive profit in all ten periods) while providing decision-makers with a controllable trade-off mechanism between aggregate SI (0.535 at α = 0.1 to 0.443 at α = 1.0) and total profit (42,165 TRY to 163,156 TRY on average).

title: Towards high-resolution energy performance monitoring in ceramic tile manufacturing: Coupling production and energy metering data for detailed KPI construction
abstract: Improving energy performance monitoring in ceramic tile manufacturing requires industrial datasets with sufficient granularity to distinguish productive from non-productive energy consumption and to enable efficiency assessment at the level of specific tile formats. Conventional reference datasets typically rely on monthly aggregated production and energy records, which limits their suitability for detailed operational analysis and the identification of cleaner production opportunities. This study proposes a data-driven methodology to construct a detailed industrial dataset by coupling daily production records with electrical and thermal energy metering data from five ceramic tile factories. Energy consumption is allocated to individual production records using a time-based correlation approach, and a hierarchical data curation procedure, combining interquartile range filtering, robust Huber regression, and Mahalanobis distance analysis, is applied to identify and remove non-representative observations. A consistency check at monthly scale confirms that the reconstructed energy consumption preserves the overall distributional characteristics of the reference data, while providing substantially higher operational resolution. The resulting cleaned detailed dataset enables the estimation of format-specific energy key performance indicators (KPIs) that are less affected by non-productive consumption than traditional aggregated metrics. These format-level KPIs provide a consistent basis for more detailed energy performance assessment and illustrate how routinely available industrial data can be transformed into operationally meaningful information to support cleaner production practices in the ceramic tile industry. The format-level granularity of the curated dataset enables operational comparisons that are not achievable with conventional monthly aggregated data, such as the detection of systematic differences in specific energy consumption between factories producing the same tile format under otherwise comparable conditions.

title: Highly efficient and selective recovery of rare earths from NdFeB waste via water-regulated deep eutectic solvent
abstract: The efficient recycling of rare earth elements (REEs) from waste neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets is critical for supply chain security and environmental sustainability. However, conventional recycling methods face significant challenges due to complex separation procedures, excessive reagent consumption, and the generation of substantial quantities of secondary waste. This study develops an efficient and green process for the sequential recovery of high-purity mixed REEs (primarily Nd, Pr, Ce) and iron (Fe) from waste NdFeB magnets, utilizing a water-regulated choline chloride-oxalic acid (ChCl-OA-H2O) deep eutectic solvent (DES). After calcination pretreatment selectively converts the NdFeB alloy into soluble REE2O3 and Fe2O3, Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize the leaching process. Under the identified optimized conditions (water content: 39.56%, solid/liquid ratio: 98.15 g/L, temperature: 91.06°C, time: 12.07 h), leaching efficiencies reached 97.81% for Nd and 99.23% for Fe. The DES system demonstrated excellent recyclability, maintaining >90% Nd recovery over ten cycles without significant performance loss. Mechanistic studies indicate that ChCl-OA has the dual functionality: selective precipitation of REE3+ as insoluble oxalates REE2(C2O4)3·10H2O, and complexation of Fe3+ as soluble [Fe(C2O4)3]3-. The dissolved [Fe(C2O4)3]3- is subsequently recovered from the filtrate as high-purity FeC2O4·2H2O (97.52%) via UV-Vis photoreduction. Besides, water addition strategically reduces DES viscosity, overcoming the mass transfer limitations that plague conventional DES systems. This work establishes a sustainable, closed-loop pathway for the comprehensive valorization of NdFeB waste, directly addressing the critical trade-off between recovery efficiency and environmental impact in rare earth recycling.

title: Insight into peroxymonosulfate activation by biochar-derived dissolved organic matter toward in-situ sustainable groundwater remediation: The role of active functional groups and efficient electron shuttles
abstract: Groundwater tetracycline contamination is a major environmental hazard that can be effectively remedied using advanced oxidation technology based on peroxymonosulfate (PMS). However, it typically necessitates the addition of synthetic catalysts, which results in remediation costs that are unaffordable and prevent widespread practical use. This study focuses on biochar-derived dissolved organic matter (BDOM) naturally leached from rice straw biochar as a sustainable, metal-free, and soluble electron shuttle for PMS activation under strictly anoxic groundwater conditions (DO < 0.2 mg L-1), a scenario that has rarely been explored previously. Owing to its hydrophilic, low-aromaticity nature and abundant phenolic hydroxyl, carboxyl, and amino functional groups, BDOM activates PMS via a dual-path mechanism comprising both radical and non-radical pathways. Phenolic hydroxyl groups act as the main electron donors, facilitating the generation of sulfate radicals (·SO4−), while singlet oxygen (1O2) is generated through a BDOM-mediated non-radical pathway. Both reactive species play important roles in tetracycline degradation. Both pathways are confirmed by EPR and quenching experiments, and further corroborated by DFT calculations demonstrating their thermodynamic feasibility. The system exhibits remarkable resistance to common groundwater anions, achieving a tetracycline removal efficiency of 85.7% within 120 min. Semi-continuous cyclic stability tests further reveal that BDOM possesses sustained PMS activation capacity, with the degradation efficiency decreasing only marginally from 85.7% to 80.6% after five cycles. This slight performance attenuation is attributed to the progressive oxidative transformation of phenolic hydroxyl groups into carboxylate-dominated structures. Collectively, this study highlights the potential of BDOM as a sustainable and natural substitute for traditional chemical catalysts for in-situ remediation of antibiotic-contaminated groundwater. These advantages stem from its anoxic adaptability, soluble electron-shuttling capability, and DFT-quantified dual-path mechanism.

title: Price models as the missing link between sustainable business models and Scope 3 decarbonisation: Evidence from timber transportation
abstract: Scope 3 decarbonisation requires more than corporate sustainability ambitions, reporting systems, or cleaner technologies. It also depends on the contractual and economic mechanisms through which supply-chain activities are governed. This paper examines price models as such mechanisms and investigates whether, and how, corporate Scope 3 ambitions are translated into the purchasing and contracting of timber transportation in the Swedish forest industry. Drawing on the Price Model Equaliser, the study analyses how the dominant price model structures value sharing, incentives, risks, and responsibilities between forest companies and external hauliers. Empirical data were collected through 39 semi-structured and in-depth interviews with 26 interviewees, complemented by archival material, annual reports, and participation in industry conferences. The findings reveal a clear disconnect: large forest companies articulate Scope 3 ambitions in public sustainability communication, but these ambitions are largely absent from the standardised price model used to purchase timber transportation. The current model rewards tonnes, distance, and short-term flexibility, while reinforcing cost pressure rather than incentivising lower emissions. The paper contributes to cleaner production research by showing that Scope 3 decarbonisation depends on price models that make lower-emission practices economically actionable. It contributes to sustainable supply-chain governance by conceptualising price models as micro-level contractual governance mechanisms, and to sustainable business model research by specifying the price model as a missing link between sustainability-oriented business model claims and the concrete contractual arrangements that shape behaviour in activity systems.

title: Flash Joule heating biochar for enhanced biodrying and carbon upgrading of food waste digestate
abstract: Bio-derived carbon materials generated through electrified synthesis are emerging as key platforms for sustainable carbon utilization and circular bioeconomy. In this study, biochar produced via flash Joule heating (FJH) was employed as a functional carbon additive to enhance the biodrying and carbon upgrading of food waste digestate. Owing to its highly porous structure and high electrical conductivity, the FJH-biochar substantially improved the physicochemical properties of the biodrying matrix, accelerating moisture removal and promoting organic matter decomposition. Microbial functional analyses revealed that FJH-biochar reshaped microbial community assembly, enriching carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) and enhancing tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle activity. These metabolic shifts intensified microbial energy metabolism and heat generation, facilitating efficient organic carbon mineralization while simultaneously reducing residual antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes. Integration of FJH-biochar also contributed to the production of agronomically valuable, carbon-rich end-products; the germination index reached 135% after 150 days of maturation, indicating effective detoxification. Pot experiments further confirmed the high fertilizer potential of the processed digestate, where a 10% application rate promoted robust plant root growth (120 mm). This work presents a bio-derived carbon-assisted strategy for accelerating biodrying, upgrading organic carbon content, and enabling safe agricultural utilization of organic digestate, offering a sustainable route for circular carbon management and valorization of bio-waste-derived carbon materials.

title: Using a moderately complex model to quantify the contributions of increased precipitation, reduced pumping, and water diversion to groundwater recovery in the southern Hebei Plain
abstract: Quantifying the contributions of climatic and anthropogenic factors to groundwater level changes is essential for formulating effective groundwater management strategies, especially in over-exploited regions such as the Southern Hebei Plain of the North China Plain (NCP). However, current study methodologies entail a compromise between structural complexity and result reliability, and the precise attribution of groundwater recovery to specific drivers across different cities within the Southern Hebei Plain remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify the contributions of increased precipitation, reduced groundwater pumping, and water diversion on shallow groundwater recovery in seven cities of the Southern Hebei Plain. We developed a moderately complex water balance model and employed a scenario simulation methodology, calibrating and validating the model using data from 2000 to 2021. Model performance was evaluated using Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) and Mean Relative Error (MRE), while uncertainty was analyzed by Monte Carlo simulation. The results indicate that reduced pumping and water diversion collectively accounted for 76% (30% from reduced pumping, 46% from water diversion) of regional groundwater recovery, whereas increased precipitation contributed merely 24%. Contribution rates exhibited significant spatial variability. The model demonstrated satisfactory performance for most cities (NSE > 0.58, MRE < 6.1%). The uncertainty analysis results indicate that even under conditions with certain errors in driving data and model parameters, the calculated contribution rates vary only slightly, illustrating the water balance model's significant stability in quantifying attribution. These findings demonstrate the substantial efficacy of anthropogenic management strategies and highlight the necessity of developing differentiated, zone-based groundwater management strategies adapted to local hydrogeological conditions and water use structures. The developed model provides a methodological reference for similar attribution studies and offers a scientific basis for optimizing groundwater over-exploitation management in the NCP.

title: Electrochemical mechanism and performance regulation of ultrasound-assisted electrodeposition of iron
abstract: Electrochemical ironmaking represents one of the key technological pathways for achieving a low-carbon transition in the steel industry. However, bubble attachment at electrode interfaces causes mass transfer limitations and increased energy consumption, which severely hinder its industrial application. To address this challenge, this study focuses on ultrasound-assisted electrochemical deposition of iron, employing a combination of electrochemical testing, in-situ interfacial observation, and multi-scale characterization to systematically investigate the effects of different ultrasonic power levels (0-60 W) on macroscopic performance, gas evolution behavior at interfaces, electrochemical kinetics, nucleation mechanisms, and microstructural evolution during the iron electrodeposition process. The results demonstrate that 20 W ultrasound significantly reduces cathodic hydrogen bubble detachment size, enhances bubble detachment frequency from both anode and cathode, decreases charge transfer resistance by 52.40%, and transforms the nucleation mode from progressive to instantaneous, achieving energy consumption reductions of 15.54% and 28.34% in standard and depleted Fe2+ electrolyte systems, respectively. Moderate ultrasonic power (10-20 W) promotes grain refinement, hardness improvement, and significant reduction in surface roughness, whereas excessive power (≥40 W) leads to grain coarsening and performance degradation. This study establishes 20 W as the optimal process window balancing energy efficiency, deposition rate, and coating quality, revealing the “optimization-transformation” regulatory mechanism of the ultrasound on iron electrochemical deposition. These findings provide theoretical foundations and technical guidance for developing green and efficient electrochemical iron smelting technologies.

title: Occurrence, variation and risks of viruses in aerosols during rural wastewater collection, treatment and discharge
abstract: Viral contamination of aerosols in rural decentralised wastewater systems poses distinct public health challenges that remain insufficiently characterised compared to urban infrastructures. This study employed virome analysis and qPCR to investigate the occurrence, variation, and influencing factors of aerosol viruses across rural sewage collection, treatment, and discharge processes. Results showed that multiple sewage-derived RNA viruses were detected in aerosols, with bacteriophages and plant viruses being the most prevalent (>96%). Human-associated Caliciviridae (0.04%) were detected in aerosols, whereas no human-associated or vertebrate viruses were identified in background air. Typical viruses (HEV, HAstV, and NoV-GI/II) were consistently detected across all rural wastewater collection, treatment, and discharge units. Peak concentrations of NoV-GII in aerosols and wastewater were observed in the septic tank (2761 GC/m3) and anoxic tank (673 GC/L), respectively. Aerosolized viruses showed no consistent variation patterns nor convergence with communities. Temperature and relative humidity were identified as primary environmental influence factors (P < 0.05). Quantitative microbial risk assessment revealed high theoretical disease risks from NoV-GII exposure via ingestion and inhalation, particularly wading in septic tank, where risk levels exceeded the WHO threshold by 314.2%. Comparative analysis with urban data showed studied rural wastewater aerosols contained fewer human-associated but more plant viruses, yet exhibited comparable concentrations of pathogenic viruses. This research, conducted in a typical village in northern China, clarified the warm-season characteristics and transmission risks of viruses in the aerosols of rural wastewater, and emphasized the need for future research on the specific aerosolization mechanism of viruses in rural wastewater treatment.

title: Urban resilience as a pathway from new-type urbanization to SDG 11 in Chinese urban agglomerations
abstract: In the context of accelerating global urbanization and increasing climate risks, enhancing urban resilience (UR) has become a key pathway associated with achieving Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). As a key approach to advancing high-quality urban development in China, the role of New-type Urbanization (NU) in relation to UR and its association with SDG 11 remains underexplored, especially at the urban agglomeration scale. This study constructed a comprehensive evaluation system for NU, UR, and SDG 11 across 19 urban agglomerations in China from 2003 to 2020, and further revealed the relationships among NU, UR, and SDG 11 by combining the Boosted Regression Tree (BRT) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results showed that: (1) Between 2003 and 2020, UR across China's urban agglomerations showed an overall declining trend, and NU and UR exhibited a high degree of overlap in their spatiotemporal distribution. (2) A significant U-shaped relationship exists between NU and UR, with significant variation across different types of urban agglomerations: NU shows a stronger positive association with UR in Nurtured Urban Agglomerations, whereas the relationship appears weaker or negative in Developing and Mature Urban Agglomerations. (3) In NUA, UR serves as an important bridge that partially mitigates the trade-off between NU and SDG 11, but it does not fully reverse the overall negative total effect. In DUA and MUA, the potential synergistic mediating role of UR is relatively limited. This study reveals the nonlinear effect of NU on UR and the key role of UR in shaping the synergy–trade-off relationship between NU and SDG 11. The study recommends establishing a coordinated development mechanism across urban agglomerations and implementing new-type urbanization strategies in stages, tailored to each agglomeration's development stage, to enhance their sustainable development capabilities. This provides a theoretical foundation and policy pathways for advancing resilient urban development, regional coordination, and achieving sustainable development goals.

title: Optimization of biomass pyrolysis reactor model and performance analysis of pyrolysis gas separation using Laval nozzle and absorption refrigeration cycle
abstract: With the growing demand for clean energy, biomass pyrolysis has attracted increasing attention for producing high-value carbon-neutral products, but pyrolysis gas treatment remains a key bottleneck. This study compares mixed-gas separation driven by pyrolysis gas pressure using a Laval nozzle and absorption refrigeration liquefaction. An accurate biomass pyrolysis reactor model was first developed to predict pyrolysis gas distribution. By incorporating Gibbs free energy minimization and the catalytic effect of biochar, the model reduced prediction deviation by 2.53% compared with the original thermodynamic model. Based on the separation model, Laval nozzle separation generated CO2 microdroplets with an average mass fraction of 0.175 and reduced the CO2 molar fraction in pyrolysis gas by 23.91%. The separated liquid phase reached a CO2 molar fraction above 0.925, while requiring a small footprint and showing favorable economic feasibility, making it suitable for small-scale separation. In terms of exergy destruction, the Laval nozzle showed clear advantages: when only evaporator heat exchange was considered in the absorption refrigeration cycle, its exergy destruction was only 44.28% – 55.07% of that of absorption refrigeration liquefaction. Absorption refrigeration liquefaction required additional low-quality heat. For the optimal working-fluid pair and a pyrolysis gas flow rate of 1.0 kg h−1, the maximum condensed liquid reached 0.5378 kg h−1, 3.07 times that of Laval nozzle separation, with a COP of 0.6654 and low-quality heat consumption of 0.0778 kW. However, due to phase equilibrium limitations, the CO2 purity was only 0.576 – 0.844, making it more suitable for large-scale separation.

title: Water–rock interaction mechanisms and hydrochemical dynamics during mine water rebound: Evolutionary patterns and mechanistic insights
abstract: Long-term coal mining significantly disrupts hydrogeological structures and alters hydraulic connectivity between aquifers. Following mine closure, groundwater rebound initiates multi-stage water–rock interactions with surrounding strata, driving sequential geochemical processes that are difficult to disentangle. To address this challenge, we combined field hydrochemical sampling, controlled water–rock interaction experiments, and PHREEQC inverse modeling to investigate the hydrochemical evolution during the Ordovician limestone water inrush–accumulation–rebound sequence in the North China coalfield. Results show that mine waters are dominated by Na+, Ca2+, and SO42−, with marked Na+ enrichment primarily induced by cation exchange and evaporite dissolution. These coupled reactions drive a progressive hydrochemical evolution that can be divided into three stages. The first stage is dominated by cation exchange, with rapid Na + enrichment and Ca2+-Mg2+ depletion. The second is jointly controlled by cation exchange and mineral dissolution–precipitation, and the third is a late dynamic equilibrium stage with relatively stable ion concentrations. Inverse geochemical modeling further corroborates this sequence, revealing a shift of dominant reactions along seepage pathways, where persistent evaporite dissolution in goaf zones emerges as the critical control in late-stage evolution. By integrating field hydrochemical data with laboratory simulation experiments and comparative analysis, this study establishes a conceptual model of hydrochemical evolution for Ordovician aquifers in the North China Coalfield. The findings advance mechanistic understanding of groundwater rebound in closed coal mines and provide a scientific basis for environmental risk assessment and sustainable mine-water management.

title: Unsustainable virtual water trade amplifies global inequalities in nutrient distribution and cascading nutrition risks
abstract: Virtual water trade is generally expected to improve global resource-use efficiency, but persistent transfers of water-intensive products from water-scarce to water-abundant regions may increase nutrition-related supply risks. This study integrates virtual water and micronutrient flows embedded in international food trade to assess misalignments between water endowments and nutrient redistribution. Water-scarce countries accounted for 92% of global net virtual water exports and 73% of global net nutrient exports, and production shocks in these exporters disproportionately reduce nutrient availability in nutrient-inadequate countries. Under 5% to 20% production reductions in ten high-risk exporters, nutrient availability declined by 17.8%-35.1% in nutrient-inadequate countries, compared with 0.5%-2.9% in high-adequacy countries. These findings show that food trade can externalizes water use to stressed regions and amplify uneven exposure to nutrient supply risks even when it improves aggregate water-use efficiency. The framework provides a basis for evaluating food trade in terms of resource sustainability, nutritional equity and systemic resilience.

title: Digital technology innovation and carbon productivity in China's low-carbon transition: Evidence from provincial data
abstract: Digital technology innovation is increasingly important for China's low-carbon transition and sustainable development. We construct a four-dimensional provincial composite index of digital technology innovation using a hybrid XGBoost–Entropy Weight Method approach. The index covers core digital innovation activities and the broader conditions that support digital technology development and diffusion. This study examines the relationship between digital technology innovation and carbon productivity across 31 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2022. The results show that: (1) A 1% increase in the digital technology innovation index is associated with a 0.1608% increase in carbon productivity. (2) Mechanism tests suggest that this association is linked to the fixed asset investment saving effect and the new quality productivity enhancement effect. (3) Regionally, the estimated coefficient is larger in eastern provinces than in central and western regions. (4) Temporally, a structural break occurred around 2019, after which the marginal effect weakened. This attenuation suggests a later-stage shift in this relationship and indicates that policy attention may need to move gradually from scale expansion to efficiency optimization.

title: From fossil fuel infrastructure to sustainable land use: agrivoltaics on oil and gas pipelines in Alberta, Canada
abstract: This study investigates re-purposing the 60 m wide oil and gas pipeline buffer zones for agrivoltaic applications. A case study of Alberta's oil pipelines is presented that maps them with solar irradiance to estimate available photovoltaic production. The results found that agrivoltaic electricity generation on the oil pipeline buffers would pay for themselves under 11 years, could theoretically generate between CAD $1.3 (single axis tracker for wheat) and CAD $6.6 trillion (fixed tilt for sheep grazing) in electricity over 30 years under full build-out conditions compared to oil pipelines' CAD $5.2 trillion. This could provide more than twice Canada's electricity needs, cut all electrical-related greenhouse gas emissions and provide more food (CAD $1.6 billion of wheat or CAD $1.0 billion in extra sheep meat/year), though actual utilization may be constrained by grid capacity, storage, and transmission infrastructure. The results show that oil and gas pipeline corridors can be transformed from long-term environmental liabilities into economically and environmentally productive assets that simultaneously advance climate mitigation, energy security, agricultural resilience, employment and land restoration.

title: On track but too slow? The dynamics of EU decarbonization
abstract: Despite the strong commitment of European countries to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, the extent to which key policies and drivers jointly shape emissions dynamics remains insufficiently investigated. The study suggests that the interaction among circular economy, energy transition, emissions trading systems, carbon tax, and digitalization policies creates structural constraints on CO 2 emissions in the European countries. Using annual data from 2000 to 2023, the analysis integrates exploratory causal discovery, time-varying dependence modeling, and machine learning methods to unravel system-level causal structure, dynamic connectedness, and future emission trajectories. The results indicate that resource productivity emerges as a central transmission channel within the system, linking upstream factors (material footprint) and digitalization to downstream emission outcomes. Lagged disequilibrium shocks propagate through resource use as a mediating channel. Time-varying copula models indicate significant heterogeneity and evolving dependence among key factors, highlighting the dynamic nature of policy and relationships over time. Forecasting results, based on a Support Vector Regression model under the European Union's 2030 climate policy framework, indicate a persistently declining emission trajectory, but at a pace insufficient to meet the EU's 2030 target. Sensitivity analysis suggests that this gap does not primarily reflect a policy failure, but the structural limitations in how policy interactions translate into decarbonization outcomes. These findings highlight the need to improve the effectiveness of policy instruments by strengthening resource productivity and accelerating progress toward the targets.

title: Product-grade enrichment of byproduct deuterium in PEM natural water electrolysis for hydrogen production
abstract: The abundance disproportional release of hydrogen isotopes during the hydrogen production process using proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis presents a promising avenue for deuterium recovery, offering a means to mitigate the high economic costs resulting from high energy consumption of hydrogen production. However, the underlying mechanism governing this isotope fractionation remains elusive. Here, experimental validation and density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the underlying mechanism: the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) spontaneously couples with catalytic exchange between D species and cathode feed water on the catalyst surface, which is universal across Pt/C, Pd/C, Mo2C, MoS2, and WS2 catalysts. Motivated by this finding, we designed a tailored PEM electrolysis system that leverages the cathode water-mediated hydrogen isotope exchange via bipolar water feed. As such, the system enhances H/D isotope release selectivity by 6-fold, achieving an unprecedented separation factor (α) of 21.37, far exceeding the α of 3.54 for conventional anode-only water feed systems. Leveraging above mechanism, natural water (D: 0.0146%) was efficiently upgraded to product-grade heavy water with 97.3% purity, with minimal energy penalty, as bipolar water feed introduces negligible overpotential increase. Finally, the theoretical mathematical model to predict deuterium enrichment in large-scale industrial PEM electrolysis systems, spanning ten-ton-level water electrolysis and thousand-standard-cubic-meter-level scale hydrogen production, was established, and providing a critical roadmap for future industrial implementation.

title: Thermal reactivation and CO2 carbonation of recycled concrete fines: Assessing R3 reactivity as a predictor of mechanical performance
abstract: The use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) remains one of the most effective strategies for lowering the embodied carbon of cement-based materials. Growing shortages of conventional SCMs such as fly ash and slag have increased interest in alternative sources derived from recycled concrete. This research studied the performance of thermal reactivation and/or CO2 carbonation treatment of recycled concrete fines (RCF) as a potential SCM. Thermal activation of RCF involved heat treatment at a temperature between 450 °C and 850 °C to regenerate reactive phases. Carbonation treatment of RCF was conducted under controlled CO2 pressure to achieve microstructural densification. The treated RCF was incorporated into mortar at a 20% cement replacement level. Chemical reactivity was quantified using the ASTM C1897 R3 bound-water test, and the resulting performance was compared with fly ash and slag. The results indicated that thermal activation significantly increased the reactivity of RCF, with a maximum R3 value achieved by RCF treated at 650 °C. Thermal activation of RCF also improved the CO2 uptake, with maximum CO2 uptake occurring in RCF treated at 650 °C, rising from 7.36 wt% in untreated RCF to 15.71 wt% after activation. The compressive strengths of mortars prepared using raw RCF, thermally activated RCF, carbonated RCF, and thermally activated–carbonated RCF were compared with mortars containing slag and fly ash. The results showed that mortars prepared with thermally activated and carbonated RCF showed substantial improvements in strength compared with those prepared with untreated RCF, reaching a 28-day strength of 5190 psi, comparable to the control mixture and approaching the performance of slag- and fly-ash-based systems. R3 reactivity exhibited a positive correlation with compressive strength for both carbonated and uncarbonated materials. At similar R3 values of RCF (thermally treated or untreated), mortar incorporated with carbonated RCF achieved higher strength due to pore filling and surface refinement effects. These results demonstrate that recycled concrete fines can be reactivated through controlled heating and carbonation to function as an effective SCM while simultaneously storing CO2. This approach offers a promising pathway for upgrading RCF into high performance, economically viable, low-carbon cementitious materials.

title: Unpacking the impact of digital innovation ecosystem on urban green productivity: The mediating role of network centrality
abstract: The transition to a low-carbon economy requires coordinated digital and institutional transformation to reshape urban sustainability trajectories. Drawing on the ecosystem and network embeddedness perspectives, this paper develops a digital innovation ecosystem–green innovation network–green total factor productivity (DIE–GIN–GTFP) analytical framework to investigate how the digital innovation ecosystem (DIE) influences urban green total factor productivity (GTFP). Using panel data for 259 Chinese cities during 2011–2022, this study constructs a multidimensional DIE index and employs spatial Durbin and spatial mediation models to examine direct effects, spatial spillovers, and network embeddedness mechanisms. The results show that DIE significantly enhances GTFP and generates substantial spatial spillover effects. Cities’ network embeddedness within green innovation networks (GINs), measured by degree centrality and betweenness centrality, exhibits significant mediating effects. In particular, degree centrality generates stronger regional spillovers, highlighting the importance of collaborative connectivity in digital-green transformation. The results remain stable across a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. Further analysis reveals significant regional heterogeneity: spillover-driven effects dominate in eastern China, whereas network-embedded upgrading is more prominent in central and western regions. By contrast, the effects of DIE remain insignificant in northeastern China. This study provides robust empirical evidence and advances a systematic understanding of the digital-green nexus, offering policy insights for promoting coordinated digital and green transformation.

title: Auto-optimized interpretable machine learning for terminal water quality prediction of the ultrapure water production system in the semiconductor industry: demonstration in a full-scale system
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, maintaining ultrapure water (UPW) quality at the terminal is critical for product safety. However, early prediction and warning of water quality deterioration remain challenging due to complex process interactions and limited monitoring responsiveness. This study developed interpretable machine learning models for 1-h-ahead prediction of terminal total organic carbon (TOC) and resistivity in a full-scale UPW system (48 m3/d). Six modeling approaches were evaluated, and XGBoost and Random Forest (RF) were selected as the optimal models for TOC and resistivity prediction, respectively. After hyperparameter optimization, the Optuna-XGBoost model achieved an R2 of 0.9664 for TOC prediction, while the RS-RF model achieved an R2 of 0.9670 for resistivity prediction. Model interpretation using SHAP and partial dependence analysis identified return water resistivity as a key influencing factor for both targets, suggesting that return water may act as a potential risk source. Strong nonlinear interaction effects were observed, particularly between first- and second-stage RO rejection rates for TOC prediction, and between return water resistivity and first-stage RO rejection for resistivity prediction. In addition, models were developed for RO membrane rejection rates. First-stage rejection was mainly governed by historical behavior, whereas second-stage rejection depended on influent conductivity and operational conditions. The proposed framework enables reliable 1-h-ahead prediction and early warning of water quality deterioration, supporting proactive operational strategies such as return water management and RO/VUV/mixed bed optimization. Overall, this work demonstrates the value of interpretable auto machine learning for early warning and decision support in semiconductor UPW systems.

title: A living lab approach to urban water reuse: Coupling plant growth monitoring and social acceptance in university buildings
abstract: This study presents a socio-technical assessment of treated wastewater (TWW) reuse for indoor irrigation, integrating plant growth monitoring based on projected leaf area with user acceptance analysis in a real-world educational environment. Unlike prior studies relying on hypothetical exposure, this living lab links continuous system performance with user perception under real operational conditions, addressing a key gap in the literature. Plant growth was monitored over one year using non-invasive image-based analysis, while social acceptance was assessed among 186 students through the Perception and Acceptance of Water Reuse (PAWR) index (Cronbach's α = 0.878). Four classroom environments were considered: a green classroom (GR) incorporating a nature-based solution with living plants irrigated with either TWW or drinking water (DW); a biophilic design classroom (BDR) featuring visual nature imagery; and two neutral classrooms (NR) without biophilic elements, serving as controls. TWW supported plant growth at levels comparable to DW across most species, with no adverse effects observed; only one species (Scindapsus aureus) showed significantly greater growth under TWW (p = 0.006). The overall PAWR index (3.9 ± 0.5) indicated generally high acceptance of water reuse, particularly among students with water-related academic backgrounds, while the physical classroom environment showed limited overall influence, though responses were more favourable in the GR for specific reuse applications. By integrating plant growth monitoring and behavioural analysis within a living lab setting, this study provides a transferable socio-technical framework for evaluating water reuse systems in institutional buildings, supporting freshwater conservation and evidence-based circular water strategies in higher education institutions.

title: Research on the coordination between agricultural carbon emission efficiency and food security in Hebei province based on the coupling framework of “Water-Land-Energy-Carbon”
abstract: Agricultural carbon emissions pose a persistent threat to ecological sustainability. Hebei Province, a vital grain-producing region, faces the dual challenge of low-carbon transition and food security. This study established a “Water-Land-Energy-Carbon” nexus framework to couple agricultural carbon emission efficiency (ACEE) with food security (FS). By incorporating non-CO2 gases (CH4,N2O) and indirect emissions into a comprehensive accounting model, this research develops a multi-dimensional food security evaluation system. This new paradigm surpasses simple output-based metrics by strictly accounting for resource constraints. The results indicate that: (1) ACEE exhibited a fluctuating upward trend (0.0232/year, mean 0.769), with inefficiencies linked to misalignment among water, soil, and energy systems. The Malmquist–Luenberger index remained above 1, reflecting productivity gains; (2) The multi-dimensional Food Security Index (FSI) expanded steadily from 0.181 in 1995 to 0.414 in 2023, shifting sequentially from the “Transitional Stage” into the “High Resilience Stage”; (3) The ACEE-FS coupling coordination degree (CCD) rose from 0.5009 to a peak of 0.7469, transitioning to intermediate coordination with a post-2016 “structural plateau” and a distinct policy-driven “three-regime” spatial pattern; (4) Random forest analysis identifies water-saving irrigation engineering coverage, rural per capita income, and per capita arable land area as the most significant drivers of the coupling coordination degree. Overall, the findings of this study regarding the growth in efficiency, food security, and coordination levels provide a valuable reference for green and synergistic agricultural development under “Water-Land-Energy-Carbon” collaborative management.

title: Comparative assessment of photovoltaic waste generation across European countries
abstract: During the 2000s, photovoltaic (PV) solar energy began a period of sustained development in many European countries. The lifespan of PV panels, which is 25-35 years, will present a significant challenge for waste management in all these countries in the coming years. This study examines photovoltaic deployment in the European countries with the highest solar PV capacity—Germany, Italy, Spain, France, and the Netherlands—and introduces a waste generation model to estimate photovoltaic waste streams up to 2035. This model is based on a Weibull distribution, and its specific parameters are discussed in order to improve the current estimations. These estimations are too outdated to include the latest PV installations, and they were developed without considering the significant increase in waste generation that began in 2018. The proposed model showed good agreement with the observed data for all analysed countries, with the exception of Spain, where the later development of photovoltaic technologies resulted in an outlying behaviour. The analysis considers the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. By 2035, it is estimated that 230,000 tonnes of PV waste will be generated in Germany, 100,000 in Italy, 44,000 in Spain, 30,000 in France, and lastly 5000 tonnes in the Netherlands. These findings highlight the need to boost current collection rates and drive the development of recycling techniques to improve the circularity of the sector. This would foster the recovery of significant quantities of glass, Ag, Al, Cu, and Si, as well as contribute to the supply needs of the European Union.

title: Power-demand-informed robust power coordination for series hybrid electric vehicles with prescribed-performance constraints
abstract: Reliable power-following capability is essential for series hybrid electric vehicles (SHEVs), yet practical discrepancies between actual load-side demand and source-side generation can produce source-load power mismatch, thereby degrading charge-sustaining performance. Additionally, the ability of the power coordination strategy to reconcile transient maneuverability with steady-state fuel economy is also critical for unlocking the full potential of SHEVs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a power-demand-informed robust power coordination strategy for SHEVs with prescribed-performance constraints. First, source-load power mismatch is formulated as an equivalent battery-port residual and mapped into an additive disturbance, which connects practical unmodeled powertrain uncertainties with the control-oriented model. Second, a power-demand-informed factor is constructed to adaptively blend economy-oriented and dynamic oriented engine speeds, thereby accommodating diverse driving demands. Third, an extended state observer is designed to estimate the disturbance. Then, its bounded estimation error is derived and incorporated as a robustness margin into the transformation from prescribed-performance requirements to battery power constraints. The resulting nonlinear model predictive control problem is efficiently solved with constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests are conducted to validate the performance of the proposed strategy. Compared with the baseline strategies, the proposed strategy achieves a favorable compromise among fuel economy, engine speed stability, and SoC robustness across both testing scenarios. The root mean square error of SoC is reduced by 97.778% and 97.297%, respectively, demonstrating its robustness against source-load power mismatch. The HIL test results further confirm the practical application potential of the strategy.

title: Spatiotemporal changes in offshore wind energy availability and stability in the China sea and adjacent waters under climate change
abstract: Against the backdrop of climate change, spatial heterogeneity and uncertainties in multi-model climate simulations significantly constrain the reliable assessment of offshore wind energy resources. Addressing the limitations of traditional multi-model weighted averaging methods in capturing regional variations and nonlinear relationships, this study proposes a spatially context-aware assessment framework. By integrating ERA5 reanalysis data with CMIP6 multi-model climate simulations, it systematically analyzes historical and future offshore wind energy resources in the China Seas and adjacent waters. The study employs the SKATER algorithm to identify spatially contiguous regions with similar wind-climate characteristics and constructs local models within each stratum to mitigate regional modeling biases. Results show that spatial regionalization enhances the consistency between ERA5 and CMIP6 simulations, achieving high prediction accuracy for key variables including wind speed, air temperature, and surface pressure. Joint analysis of wind power density (WPD) and wind energy stability index (SI) reveals pronounced nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous relationships, indicating that regions with high wind energy potential do not necessarily exhibit high stability. Future projections indicate weak and statistically non-significant long-term trends in regional-average WPD under all three SSP scenarios, together with a largely stable seasonal structure. However, future-period mean WPD relative to the 1995–2014 baseline exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with locally large anomalies emerging under SSP5-8.5 toward the late century. Because monthly mean wind speed is directly used in the cubic WPD formulation, submonthly wind-speed variability is not retained and absolute WPD values are systematically biased low. The reported WPD values should therefore be interpreted as relative climate-scale indicators rather than unbiased engineering estimates. This study provides methodological support for long-term, climate-scale offshore wind resource assessment and preliminary regional screening under climate change, while further hub-height and high-frequency wind analyses are required for engineering-scale wind farm planning.

title: Tribological behaviour of sustainably fabricated Al-Si-Mg composite reinforced with agro-waste through ANN approach
abstract: This study reports the development and performance evaluation of eco-friendly Al-6.6Si-0.2 Mg metal matrix composites reinforced with 7.5 wt% Coconut Shell Ash, an agricultural waste by-product promoting sustainable “waste-to-wealth” utilization. The composites were fabricated via stir casting process and subjected to a T6 heat treatment cycle comprising solution treatment at 548°C for 8 h, water quenching, and artificial ageing at 180°C for 4, 8, and 12 h. Among these, sample aged at 8h exhibited the maximum microhardness (128.98 ± 5.03 HV) and superior wear resistance, attributed to effective precipitation hardening. The presence of protective tribo layers were confirmed through sliding wear test and subsequent scanning electron microscopy analysis. Furthermore, an artificial neural network was employed to predict the specific wear rate and friction coefficient, with the 3-10-2 Levenberg–Marquardt model achieving a strong correlation (R = 0.99527). The close agreement between experimental results and artificial neural network results underscores the reliability of the model in forecasting wear performance. The novel composite demonstrates potential for lightweight, high-performance automotive components, combining enhanced mechanical properties with the sustainable reuse of bio-waste reinforcement, contributing to green manufacturing initiatives.

title: Control-oriented dynamic analysis of a PEM water electrolysis system considering balance of plant interactions
abstract: This study develops a control-oriented dynamic model of a polymer electrolyte membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) system. The model examines how balance of plant (BoP) components affect stack behavior under prescribed variable load conditions. The stack voltage response was validated using steady state polarization data and current step experiments. During steady state validation, the voltage deviation remained within 1.0% over the tested current density range. Separator level control triggered intermittent injection of low temperature deionized water into the anode recirculation loop. This injection disturbed the thermal state of the system. At low current density, the stack temperature decreased by 6.1 °C, and the cell voltage increased by about 52 mV. A rapid load increase also caused a voltage overshoot because the electrochemical response was faster than the thermal response. In the prescribed transition case, a temperature control strategy based on thermal preconditioning reduced the overshoot from 98.0 to 36.9 mV. Increasing separator capacity lengthened the oscillation period but had little effect on the overshoot magnitude. These results show that BoP control actions and design parameters can influence PEMWE transients through changes in stack inlet and thermal conditions. Since experimental validation was limited to stack voltage, results related to the BoP should be interpreted as simulation based trends for the selected system configuration.

title: Unlocking a decarbonized future: Institutional barriers and governance innovations in China's circular economy transition for the built environment
abstract: China's deep decarbonization of the built environment is hindered by institutional lock-ins in the circular economy transition. Applying Scott's three pillars of institutions and using document analysis, semi-structured interviews, and comparative case studies, this research diagnoses how fragmented regulations, cost-driven industry norms, and cognitive biases mutually reinforce stagnation. Successful projects demonstrate that alignment across pillars enables circular practices, while failures stem from misalignment. To break institutional lock-ins, governance innovations must shift green standards from voluntary to mandatory, embed circularity into financial and performance metrics, and establish multi-stakeholder platforms. These findings contribute a dynamic institutional explanation and contextualize transition barriers within China's strong state–strong market configuration, offering pathways for coordinated policy, market, and cultural change toward a low-carbon circular built environment.

title: Integrated process development and comparative assessment of CO2-to-sustainable aviation fuel production via thermochemical and electrochemical pathways
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive comparative assessment of two CO2 production routes from green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide: (i) thermochemical reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) and (ii) electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR). Both pathways are integrated with downstream Fischer–Tropsch (FT) synthesis for SAF production. Techno-economic analysis of the two processes estimates the minimum fuel selling price (MFSP) of SAF to be $9.48/kg and $9.01/kg for the RWGS and CO2RR pathways, respectively. For the RWGS pathway, the integration of the endothermic RWGS reaction with the highly exothermic FT synthesis results in a thermodynamic mismatch, which poses challenges for energy efficiency and operational complexity. In contrast, the CO2RR pathway benefits from the elimination of the RWGS reaction, leading to advantages in both cost and energy consumption. Nevertheless, its relatively low CO2 conversion results in larger and more energy-intensive carbon capture units. Despite this drawback, the CO2RR pathway remains economically more feasible. From an environmental perspective, however, its performance is lower because of the high amine make-up demand associated with its low CO2 conversion. The global warming potential (GWP) of the RWGS pathway is estimated at −3.28 kg CO2 eq per kg SAF, while that of the CO2RR pathway is −2.72 kg CO2 eq per kg SAF. The results quantify the trade-offs between thermochemical and electrochemical pathways in terms of efficiency, capital intensity, operational flexibility, and carbon performance. The study provides a systematic basis for selecting optimal power-to-liquid conversion technologies under future renewable energy systems.

title: Cost-saving and decarbonization-oriented coordinated optimization for copper metallurgy integrated energy system under material–energy–carbon coupling constraints
abstract: As energy-intensive industries move toward deep decarbonization, copper metallurgy remains constrained by tightly coupled multi-energy flows, limited process flexibility, and high carbon intensity. These characteristics hinder the coordinated regulation of production and energy systems and complicate the simultaneous pursuit of economic and low-carbon operation. This study develops an economic low-carbon coordinated optimization framework for a copper metallurgy integrated energy system (CMIES). A unified CMIES model is established to capture the coupling of electricity, heat, gas, material, and carbon flows, and a decoupling mechanism based on anode copper storage is introduced to separate continuous smelting from flexible electrolytic refining, thereby releasing process-side scheduling flexibility. On this basis, a bi-objective optimization model is formulated to minimize total operating cost and total carbon emissions. To obtain implementable operating strategies, the solution framework combines NSGA-II for Pareto search, hypervolume (HV) and spacing for solution-quality evaluation, and knee-point identification and TOPSIS for preference-based decision-making. Case studies show that the proposed flexible scheduling mechanism reduces total operating cost by 7.36%, while carbon capture and storage (CCS) reduces carbon emissions by more than 50%. When process flexibility and CCS are jointly coordinated, the system achieves a balanced improvement in economic and environmental performance. This study provides a practical pathway for low-carbon operation and decision support in energy-intensive process industries.

title: Bridging microextraction and fiber coalescence for rare-earth enrichment
abstract: Efficient enrichment of rare-earth ions from dilute aqueous solutions remains challenging for conventional solvent extraction, as high aqueous-to-organic ratios limit interfacial mass transfer and slow phase disengagement. Herein, we report an integrated microextraction and fiber-induced phase separation (MEFS) system for continuous-flow rare-earth enrichment. Microscale biphasic dispersion in the micromixer and tubular extractor accelerates interfacial mass transfer, while the downstream fiber separator promotes droplet coalescence and phase disengagement, enabling stable recirculation of a low-volume organic phase. Using Nd3+ as a model ion, the MEFS system achieved a 16.7-fold increase in the apparent extraction rate constant compared with batch extraction while enabling rapid phase disengagement within seconds. At an aqueous-to-organic volume ratio of 100:1, the system delivered an average Nd3+ extraction efficiency of approximately 95% from a 100 ppm feed and enriched the circulating organic phase to 18.9 g/L. Its applicability was further demonstrated across different mixer configurations, acidic organophosphorus extractants, and representative light and heavy rare-earth ions. These results suggest that coupling microextraction with fiber-induced phase separation provides an effective continuous-flow strategy for rare-earth enrichment under high-ratio solvent extraction conditions.

title: CarbonTimer: Overcoming data scarcity in carbon price forecasting with a large time series model
abstract: Data scarcity and high volatility in China's carbon emissions trading system pose persistent challenges to accurate price prediction. Addressing the challenge of carbon price forecasting under small-sample conditions, we introduce CarbonTimer which is built on a large time series model Timer and fine-tuned on specific carbon market data via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). This approach enables CarbonTimer to possess both the general temporal feature extraction capabilities of a large model and a dedicated focus on carbon price forecasting, thereby effectively overcoming the limitations of few-shot learning. Through an integrated feature selection mechanism, the model demonstrates significant potential in multi-task collaborative forecasting. Extensive evaluation on real-world datasets from the Guangdong and Hubei carbon markets validates CarbonTimer's outstanding performance: compared to the state-of-the-art benchmark model Qwen2, it achieves an average reduction of 29.5% in mean squared error for single-step predictions. For multi-step forecasting, the mean squared error of CarbonTimer is on average over 40% lower than that of LSTM models. Furthermore, equipped with a feature selection mechanism and a multi-task collaborative forecasting framework, CarbonTimer is capable of capturing the dynamic correlations between carbon prices and key financial indices, demonstrating considerable application potential in handling core forecasting tasks.

title: One sphere, multiple functions: mineralized cellulose nanocrystal–calcium carbonate microspheres enhance polylactic acid mulch with improved crystallization, fertilizer release, and soil degradation
abstract: Bio-based polylactic acid (PLA) is increasingly explored as an alternative to petroleum-based mulches, yet simultaneously achieving mechanical durability, enhanced soil degradability, fertilizer loading, and controlled release within a single mulch film remains highly challenging. Here, multifunctional bio-based PLA mulch films were developed using a mineralized carboxylated cellulose nanocrystal–calcium carbonate microsphere reinforcement strategy. These microspheres functioned as both heterogeneous nucleating agents and urea carriers within the PLA film.
