With the addition of 5 wt% microspheres, the crystallization half-time was reduced to 6.95 min, and the crystallinity increased to 37.8%. The uniformly dispersed microspheres promoted tensile strength and elongation at break by 21.6% and 169.0%, respectively. Soil degradability was also improved due to the enhanced hydrophilicity introduced by the microspheres, with PLCNs-5% showing a weight loss of 7.9% after 150 days of soil burial. In addition, the hierarchical porosity of the microspheres enabled sustained urea release over 120 h and promoted soybean seedling growth, as demonstrated by improved root development and biomass accumulation after 30 days. This “one sphere, multiple functions” strategy provides a sustainable approach for developing next-generation mulch films.

title: Optimization of energy transition pathways in the lime industry: A superstructure approach
abstract: Lime manufacturing is a hard-to-abate industry, owing to high-temperature heat requirements and process-related CO2 emissions from limestone calcination. Although numerous mitigation technologies have been proposed, existing studies generally evaluate individual options or rely on predefined economic scenarios, providing limited guidance for technology selection under uncertain future energy and carbon prices. This study presents a systematic techno-economic assessment of multiple decarbonization options, including fuel switching, electrification, and CO2 capture (CC) with storage or utilization. A unified superstructure model is coupled with scenario analysis and a parameter sweep of key energy and CO2 prices to assess robustness under market volatility. Results show that the fuel switching alone achieves only 18% CO2 emission reduction, making CC implementation inevitable for deep decarbonization. Implementing CC enables up to 78% emission reduction for fossil-based routes and net-negative emissions down to −0.22 tCO2/tlime for biomass-based configurations, at the expense of an energy penalty of 1.4–6.2 GJ/tlime. Current economic conditions favor unabated and bioenergy-based production (€147–176/tlime vs. €257–380/tlime with CC), whereas CC becomes competitive only under high CO2 pricing, achieving cost reductions up to 45% compared to the base case. Electrification and hydrogen-based production require very low-cost (≤€62/MWh) low-carbon energy to become competitive, whereas CCU remains constrained by its high energy demand (12.2 GJ/tlime). Finally, oxycombustion appears as the most promising decarbonization pathway, as it consistently provides the best trade-off between energy penalty, CO2 emissions, total cost, and robustness to market fluctuations, outperforming amine-based capture across all pricing scenarios.

title: Promoting green transportation: A systematic assessment of carbon emission efficiency and decoupling status in China’s urban rail transit agglomerations
abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s carbon neutrality goals, optimizing the carbon emission efficiency of urban rail transit is imperative. This study constructs a systematic framework to analyze the spatio-temporal evolution of eight major urban agglomerations, providing a basis for evidence-based regional governance. We integrate a top-down accounting approach with the Tapio model to assess decoupling status, while employing the super-epsilon-based measure model and global Malmquist–Luenberger index to evaluate static and dynamic efficiency. Furthermore, a novel grey model-sand cat swarm optimization-gated recurrent unit hybrid prediction model, GM-SCSO-GRU, is developed to predict future carbon trajectories across different city clusters under multiple scenarios. The results reveal significant regional disparities, with carbon emissions in eastern coastal agglomerations being substantially higher than those in inland and northeastern regions. Most cities exhibit expansionary negative decoupling, indicating that urban rail transit network expansion currently outpaces carbon control efforts. Notably, the efficiency evolution across agglomerations shows distinct recovery paths. While the Harbin–Changchun agglomeration displays a V-shaped trend, other regions primarily exhibit W-shaped fluctuations. The GM-SCSO-GRU model demonstrates superior accuracy and stability, predicting that while total emissions will continue to grow across all clusters, growth rates will diverge significantly due to varying industrial structures and technological levels. These findings underscore the necessity for differentiated emission reduction strategies and collaborative green governance to advance sustainable development in China’s urban rail transit systems.

title: Optimization of anaerobic digestion conditions for methane production from waste activated sludge and elucidation of process mechanisms based on a calibrated ADM1
abstract: Nowadays, the anaerobic digestion (AD) process still encounters significant challenges of low bioconversion efficiency for biogas production from waste activated sludge (WAS). Mathematical models serve as a useful and cost-effective tool to optimize the operation of the AD. In this study, Anaerobic Digestion Model No 1 (ADM1) was calibrated and used to obtain optimal operational conditions for methane production from the AD of WAS. Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) identified pH, solids retention time (SRT), and organic loading rate (OLR) as the critical operational parameters affecting methane production under mesophilic AD conditions. The ADM1 was calibrated for major model component fractions and parameters, improving methane production simulation with the Theil's inequality coefficient (TIC) of 0.069 – 0.102. Using this calibrated ADM1, optimal conditions for methane production were obtained as SRT = 30 d, pH = 7.2 ± 0.1, and OLR = 1.56 g TS·L−1·d−1. Both lab-scale and pilot-scale semi-continuous AD experiments confirmed the optimization results, with 68.7 – 93.4% improvement of methane production under the optimal conditions over other conditions. Based on partial least-squares path modeling (PLS-PM) analysis and Gibbs free energy (ΔG) calculations, the calibrated ADM1 contributed to a deeper comprehension of the AD process mechanisms. Especially, the calculations of ΔG confirmed the better stability of the AD under the above optimal conditions, a desirable feature. This study provides a robust model-based tool for mechanistic understanding of the AD of WAS, which can inform future AD process optimization strategies. By advancing such predictive capabilities, this work supports broader adoption of AD technology in sludge treatment, delivering both economic and environmental benefits.

title: Coupling iron-carbon micro-electrolysis ceramsite with constructed wetlands for sustainable rural wastewater treatment: Long-term performance, underlying mechanisms and potential risks
abstract: To overcome passivation, poor electron transfer and instability of conventional iron-carbon powders in constructed wetlands (CWs), this study developed iron-carbon micro-electrolysis ceramsite (ICMEC) as a functional substrate and evaluated its long-term purification effect for high-concentration rural sewage and the microorganism response. The results revealed that ICMEC significantly enhanced total nitrogen and total phosphorus removal, achieving efficiencies of 67.8-75.1% and 65.1-77.8%, respectively, which were 25.4% and 33.6% higher than those of the control. Sustained Fe2+ and H2 release enabled micro-electrolysis, driving iron- and hydrogen-based autotrophic denitrification and enhancing coupled nitrification-denitrification. Additionally, the microbial community structure was significantly reshaped, enriching nitrifying bacteria (e.g., Nitrosomonas and Nitrosospira) and denitrifying bacteria (e.g., Thauera, Hydrogenophaga, Azospira), alongside iron oxidation/reduction bacteria, collectively enhancing electron transfer and energy metabolism. Meanwhile, ICMEC provided abundant biofilm attachment sites, increasing extracellular polymeric substances content by 1.33 times, which brought potential biological clogging risk. This study revealed the deep coupling mechanism of physical, chemical and biological processes of ICMEC in CWs, providing a basis for the design of next generation engineered CWs substrates.

title: Towards a circular economy for EV batteries in India: Spatiotemporal foresight of end-of-life material flows and reverse logistics stress (2030–2050)
abstract: India's electric vehicle transition will generate a battery end-of-life challenge whose magnitude, timing, and spatial concentration remain unquantified at the resolution required for planning. This study develops a spatiotemporal foresight framework projecting EV battery end-of-life flows across 742 Indian districts from 2015 to 2050, identifying where circular infrastructure gaps pose the greatest reverse-logistics risk. Annual EV registration records from VAHAN (2015–2025), disaggregated by vehicle category and district, are converted into active stock via Weibull survival analysis and forward-projected using Prophet-based forecasting. Retirements are translated into end-of-life energy and mass flows using class-specific battery capacities and chemistry proxies (LFP, NMC, Lead-Acid). National end-of-life battery volumes increase from 14 to 15 GWh in 2030 to 135–136 GWh by 2050, corresponding to approximately 1.05 million tonnes. Four-wheelers dominate the waste stream despite lower fleet penetration, contributing 50.3% of cumulative end-of-life battery mass by 2050 - driven by battery capacity rather than fleet size. Spatial analysis confirms statistically significant clustering of reverse-logistics pressure (Global Moran's I = 0.360, p = 0.001), indicating infrastructure gaps are geographically concentrated and regionally systematic. A novel Reverse Logistics Stress Index, combining district-level end-of-life volumes with recycler accessibility, identifies priority intervention zones where high waste generation coincides with poor circular infrastructure access. Integrating this index with Local Moran's I cluster typologies yields a spatially differentiated planning framework distinguishing regions requiring recycling hubs, satellite collection points, and phased infrastructure expansion. Findings provide district-resolution evidence supporting Extended Producer Responsibility enforcement and circular infrastructure investment under India's Battery Waste Management Rules.

title: A cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment of United States’ grain and pulse carbon footprint using Bayesian machine learning and global uncertainty analysis
abstract: As the world's population approaches 10 billion, ensuring food security while mitigating carbon emissions poses a significant global challenge. Yet despite the United States' dominance in global grain and pulse supply, few studies have conducted a unified, cradle-to-grave carbon intensity assessment spanning both crop types. This study fills this gap by quantifying cradle-to-grave carbon intensity for nine major U.S grain and pulse crops from 2000 to 2023, evaluating emissions across input production, farm operation, processing, transportation, and waste-disposal stages. To capture nonlinear relationships that conventional LCA methods cannot recover, the Bayesian Additive Regression Tree (BART) is integrated into the LCA framework and benchmarked against five alternative models. A four-layer uncertainty framework that combines Bayesian posterior inference, Monte Carlo simulation, scenario analysis, and Sobol global sensitivity indices systematically decomposes sources of uncertainty. Grain exhibits a higher mean carbon intensity (0.720 kg CO2e/kg), 36.4% higher than pulses (0.528 kg CO2e/kg), with this relative ordering persisting across all temporal sub-periods and production scenarios. Food waste rate and nitrogen application are the two dominant drivers of variation in carbon intensity, jointly accounting for 84.9% of the total variance. ARIMA forecasts near-stabilization in both crop systems through 2030, indicating that incremental efficiency gains are insufficient to meet IPCC agricultural mitigation targets without coordinated multi-stage interventions.

title: Techno-economic design of integrated infrastructure for CO2 transportation to sequestration and utilisation sites
abstract: Efficient CO 2 transport pathways are essential for reducing emissions and completing carbon capture and utilisation (CCU), carbon capture and sequestration (CCS), and carbon dioxide removal (CDR) chains. This study presents a techno-economic assessment of integrated CO 2 infrastructure for two key emitters in Finland, a pulp and paper mill and a cement plant, covering capture, conditioning, multimodal transport, and end use. Utilisation in the form of e-methanol synthesis is assumed in Oulu, Finland and Spain, while offshore and onshore sequestration are considered in Norway and Iceland. Aspen HYSYS was used for modelling and costs are presented as levelised costs of utilisation/sequestration for 2030-2050. Results indicate that shipping is the cheapest transportation option for long routes. Among sequestration scenarios, rail transport to port followed by shipping to Norway for offshore injection is the cheapest option. Despite higher injection costs in Norway (15-16.8 €/tCO 2 ) compared to mineralisation in basaltic rocks in Iceland (7.9-10.2 €/tCO 2 ), the shorter distance results in lower overall costs. For utilisation, shipping CO 2 to Spain for solar photovoltaics-based e-methanol synthesis results in lower costs than pipeline transport within Finland for wind power-based production, highlighting the stronger impact of electricity costs over transport costs. Overall, hybrid pipeline–shipping systems offer cost-efficient and flexible CO 2 transport solutions for future carbon management strategies in Northern Europe.

title: Influencing factors and hierarchical pathways of structural quality in concrete modular integrated construction: A dematel–ism case study in Hong Kong
abstract: Concrete Modular Integrated Construction (C-MiC) is increasingly promoted as an industrialised approach that may support cleaner production, yet structural quality remains an implementation constraint. Cross-stage relationships and hierarchical pathways remain insufficiently understood. Using expert judgements and routine project records from Hong Kong's Tonkin Street C-MiC project, this study develops an exploratory framework to identify and structure factors affecting C-MiC structural quality. A targeted literature review and semi-structured expert interviews identified 31 candidate factors; Relative Importance Index screening retained 16. DEMATEL, interpretive structural modelling and robustness analyses were used to examine influence relationships and threshold-based hierarchical pathways. The results showed that perceived importance did not necessarily coincide with DEMATEL prominence, net-influence role or ISM level. Lack of professional construction management personnel (CF12) emerged as a prominent management-related net-influence factor, whereas lack of professional quality inspection personnel (CF13) acted mainly as an inspection-control factor. At the selected ISM threshold (λ = 0.180), the analysis identified inadequate fixation measures for protruding rebars (CF14) as a localised technical precursor, complex mould assembly and disassembly (CF7) as an outcome-related factor, and insufficient accuracy of installation surveying and setting-out (CF16) as a threshold-isolated installation-control factor. The post-intervention means of the four quality indicators were 3.66–39.79 percentage points higher than their pre-intervention means, with Cohen's d values ranging from 0.73 to 4.40. The findings support role-sensitive defect prevention and targeted quality control, with implications for process-level cleaner production in comparable C-MiC contexts.

title: Eco-Construction from the sea: assessment of mollusk shells by-products as sustainable building materials
abstract: This paper describes the development of novel bio-composite mortars made by reusing waste from the fish canning industry, namely mussel, clam, and oyster shells, as recycled aggregates to achieve a complete (100%) replacement of conventional sand. For each shell type, different granulometric fractions (0.00–1.00 mm, 1.00–2.00 mm, 2.00–4.00 mm, and a calibrated 0.00–4.00 mm blend) were investigated. Several waste-based cement mixes were tested and compared with conventional OPC mortar. Chemical-physical properties and the functional and engineering performance of the new bio-composite mortars were evaluated to explore their potential for construction applications. Main results indicated a strong dependence of mortar performance on both shell type and particle size distribution. In particular, oyster- and clam-shell mortars significantly improved the mechanical properties, achieving increases of up to 120% in flexural strength and 60% in compressive strength compared with the reference mortar, whereas mussel-shell formulations generally exhibited lower mechanical performance; opposite behaviours were observed for the mussel shell. Nevertheless, developed mixes were analysed in light of EN 998-1 and EN 998-2, for plastering and masonry application respectively, demonstrating potentials for uses in construction, including ordinary and lightweight structures and plasters. In addition, with an average 30% reduction in bulk density and a 40% increase in energy behaviour, the bio-composite mortars resulted particularly suitable for improved energy-saving applications. Finally, accelerated aging tests based on salt (4% NaCl) crystallization and exposure to high thermal loads (up to 800 °C), permitted to simulate exposure to prolonged stress and preliminary investigate the evolution of degradation phenomena, suggesting long life span. In conclusion, the use of sole bio-waste aggregate offers a sustainable alternative to conventional landfill disposal of the waste and makes these mortars promising candidates for Minimum Environmental Criteria certification, in line with the European Green Deal and Circular Economy principles.

title: Efficiency measures recommended for industrial facilities: Environmental and economic perspectives
abstract: This study analyzes common industrial Energy Efficiency Measures (EEMs) recommended by University-based Assistance Programs in the United States, evaluating both their financial and environmental performance in manufacturing facilities across Nebraska, and compares them to EEMs from a national US database. Specifically, the research quantifies the payback periods and net cost per metric ton of CO2-equivalent (MTCO2-eq) reduced, providing a framework to prioritize measures based on both economic feasibility and climate impact considering site-to-site variability. The US database showed that the eleven common EEMs studied all generally yielded positive economic benefits. An analysis of site-specific EEM data highlighted common reasons for variability in benefits, including facility size, operating hours, and process energy intensity. Key findings indicate that measures such as adding insulation to hot pipes and buildings, installing High-Volume, Low-Speed (HVLS) fans, and implementing boiler economizers offer the most attractive combination of short payback periods and low cost per MTCO2-eq avoided. Lighting upgrades, occupancy sensors, and compressed air leak detection also present cost-effective opportunities for immediate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) reductions. Conversely, certain motor replacements are less economically favorable, particularly if implemented before the equipment reaches the end of its efficient life. The study provides actionable insights for facility managers and policymakers, highlighting which EEMs are most attractive under different operational and financial conditions, thereby supporting strategic, cost-effective decarbonization in the industrial sector and reinforcing the role of targeted, data-driven EEM selection in advancing long-term sustainability goals.

title: Proof-of-concept investigation of an integrated multi-effect and forced-circulation adsorption water treatment system
abstract: Water scarcity and increasing environmental concerns have intensified interest in developing energy-efficient water treatment and resource recovery technologies. Adsorption water treatment has demonstrated high water recovery as an effective concentration step for mature landfill leachate, contributing to both freshwater production and valuable resource recovery. However, despite its high water recovery potential, adsorption water treatment yields relatively low freshwater production and requires a large footprint compared with other treatment processes, limiting its large-scale applicability. To overcome these constraints, the present study proposes a proof-of-concept of a multi-effect and forced-circulation adsorption water treatment system. The proposed system integrates adsorption water treatment with a multi-effect evaporator to enhance freshwater yield and a forced-circulation separator to ensure stable concentration and crystallization under high-concentration conditions. A thermodynamic model was developed based on systematic adsorption isotherms and kinetic studies of silica gel and applied to pilot-scale system design. Experimental validation under various operating conditions yielded a maximum relative error below 7.5%. The system achieved a maximum specific daily water production of 33 m3/t·d at 65 °C hot water temperature and 4 bar motive steam pressure (152 °C), approximately four times that of the conventional adsorption water treatment system. By integrating medium-grade waste heat (100–400 °C), the specific energy consumption and footprint were reduced by approximately 55.1% and 38.4%, respectively, compared with conventional adsorption water treatment. The findings suggest that the proposed multi-effect and forced-circulation adsorption water treatment system has the potential to improve the energy efficiency and productivity of adsorption-based water treatment systems. wastewater reuse.

title: In-situ hydrogen generation via water-gas shift reaction over Ni-Fe3O4/USY: A sustainable pathway for efficient polypropylene hydrogenolysis
abstract: The escalating crisis of global plastic pollution underscores an urgent need for truly sustainable and closed-loop technological solutions. While chemical recycling presents a promising route, its current reliance on fossil-derived hydrogen fundamentally undermines the process's environmental rationale. Herein, an innovative cascade catalytic system is introduced that directly addresses this challenge by employing the water-gas shift reaction (WGSR) as an in-situ hydrogen source. This integrated strategy enables the efficient conversion of polypropylene (PP) waste into high-value liquid fuels (C5-C22). The process is driven by a rationally designed bifunctional catalyst, Ni-Fe3O4/USY. The reducible Fe3O4 continuously generates active hydrogen species through the WGSR, while Ni finely tunes the redox properties required for CO activation. Concurrently, the acidic sites of the USY zeolite facilitate the selective cleavage of C-C bonds in the polymer chain. The results show that the well-designed tandem reaction achieves >99% conversion of post-consumer PP waste and a remarkably high liquid fuel yield of 83.2% under relatively mild conditions (340 °C). This study establishes a green and intensified pathway for plastic valorization, fundamentally circumventing the dependency on external fossil-based hydrogen and paving the way for more sustainable chemical recycling paradigms.

title: Single-step fast decomposition of high-strength organophosphorus in industrial aqueous waste using DC water plasma
abstract: The treatment of high strength organophosphorus in aqueous waste from industrial activities has long posed a significant challenge for wastewater treatment. Water plasma is a novel alternative for aqueous waste treatment, with high capability and high energy efficiency. This study demonstrates the single-step direct treatment of high-strength organophosphorus in aqueous wastes using water plasma, using triethyl phosphate as a model. The conversion of phosphorus in water plasma is systematically studied for the first time. High decomposition rates exceeding 90% are achieved at triethyl phosphate concentrations up to 67 g/L, with up to 2% of carbon converted to by-products within the liquid effluent. High energy efficiencies of up to 22 g/kWh are achieved. The fast decomposition and mineralization are achieved by the high-intensity plasma arc with temperatures exceeding 10,000 K, while the quenching effect resulting from rapid cooling in the downstream region inhibits the formation of unwanted reduced by-products. Phosphorus in the aqueous wastes can be recovered as solid products and mixed acid in liquid effluent, while carbon is primarily converted to CO and CO2 as gas products, simultaneously producing hydrogen. The comparison with other studies highlights the high capability and high energy efficiency of the water plasma system.

title: Decision-making in electrification transformation under dual-subsidy policy: Insights from digital investment and cost threshold analysis
abstract: In the context of the global automotive industry's shift, particularly in China, the US, and the EU, government subsidies are key to driving electrification and intelligence. This paper builds a three-stage game model with a government, a monopolistic automaker, and consumers to examine how purchase-subsidy and/or digital-investment-subsidy strategies affect automakers' electrification decisions. It analyzes interactions among factors such as electric vehicle (EV) production costs, market competition intensity, and digital investment efficiency. Findings: (1) A dual threshold in decisions, shaped by cost and competition, exists, with weak competition offering a transformation window. (2) The path is not always gradual; a leapfrog shift from gasoline vehicles (GVs) to EVs can occur under certain conditions. (3) Demand-side (purchase) and supply-side (digital investment) subsidies differ fundamentally. Purchase subsidies mainly shift the decision threshold, while high digital subsidies alter the decision structure. Both may cause transformation inertia later by boosting the hybrid production model's profitability. This study provides a theoretical reference for understanding how different subsidy instruments influence staged electrification decisions under varying cost and competition conditions.

title: Sustainability assessment of concrete pavement overlays reinforced with hybrid recycled and manufactured steel fibers
abstract: The lack of a comprehensive quantitative sustainability assessment for using recycled steel fibers (RSF) as reinforcement in concrete, either alone or in combination with manufactured steel fibers (MSF), has hindered their wider adoption. This paper addresses this gap through a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) and a life cycle cost analysis (LCCA). A comparative LCA was performed to quantify embodied energy and greenhouse gas emissions associated with concrete pavement overlays incorporating RSF, MSF, and their hybrid combinations, while the LCCA evaluated their economic implications. The functional unit was defined as a 1 km long and 3.5 m wide single-lane asphalt highway rehabilitated with a concrete overlay. The overlay thickness for different combinations of RSF and MSF was determined using the bonded concrete overlay on asphalt mechanistic-empirical design procedure (BCOA-ME). The findings indicate that concrete overlays reinforced with RSF offer substantial sustainability benefits over other steel-fiber reinforced concrete (SFRC) mixtures, exhibiting 32% lower embodied energy and 6.6% reduced CO2 emission compared to concrete with straight MSF. Additionally, the hybrid combination of RSF and hooked end MSF demonstrates superior sustainability than concrete containing only hooked end or straight MSF, or a hybrid combination of hooked end and straight MSF, achieving an 18% reduction in CO2 emissions and a 28% reduction in energy consumption compared to concrete with hooked end MSF. The LCCA results further reveal that overlays reinforced with a hybrid combination of RSF and hooked end MSF are the most cost-effective, reducing costs by 47% compared to concrete with straight MSF, followed by concrete incorporating RSF alone with a 36% cost reduction. Overall, the use of RSF alone or in combination with hooked end MSF in concrete presents notable environmental and economic benefits.

title: From waste to thermal regulator: Upcycling preservative-treated wood into multifunctional composite phase change materials for sustainable thermal management
abstract: Meeting the growing global demand for sustainable thermal energy is a critical challenge in the transition toward a low-carbon future. Meanwhile, the continuous accumulation of heavy metal-containing preservative-treated wood waste presents persistent environmental and health risks. Here, we present an interfacial engineering strategy in which polydopamine is employed to regulate the structural framework and functional properties of copper-based preservative-treated wood biochar, enabling integrated thermal energy storage and conversion under solar irradiation and electrical stimulation. By pyrolysis and polydopamine-mediated modification, a hierarchical copper–biochar–polydopamine architecture is constructed, promoting efficient thermal transport and energy conversion. The resulting composite phase change materials (PCMs) exhibits the latent heat of 108.3 J g−1 and an excellent thermal conductivity of 0.689 W m−1 K−1. Owing to the synergistic contributions, efficient dual-mode energy conversion was achieved, with photothermal and electrothermal efficiencies reaching 92.93% and 86.58%, respectively. Beyond material-level performance, building-scale simulations further demonstrate that floor heating systems incorporating this PCM enable effective temperature regulation. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and low-carbon pathway for transforming preservative-treated wood into interfacially engineered composites for thermal management, offering a sustainable strategy for thermal energy storage, conversion, and management in functional energy materials.

title: Compound environmental exposures and age-stratified vulnerability: Nationwide evidence from U.S. county-level mortality among older adults
abstract: Population aging is accelerating while environmental stressors intensify, yet how combined exposures shape older-adult mortality remains insufficiently understood. Existing evidence has examined heat, fine particulate matter, or greenness separately, or has assessed environmental mixtures without simultaneously incorporating population-weighted exposure assessment and nonlinear interaction. Older adults are also often treated as a homogeneous group, obscuring age-related physiological differences. We analyzed U.S. counties (2010–2020) using age-specific annual all-cause mortality rates and 1-km population-weighted summer temperature, PM2.5, and NDVI, applying a data-driven three-year exposure window and interpretable machine-learning model, and partial dependence plots to assess nonlinear thresholds and interactions across ages 60–69, 70–79, and 80+. Results suggest that older-adult mortality predictions were structured by clear exposure thresholds and interaction-like patterns among environmental factors. Heat exposure showed a distinct threshold: when temperature increased from 28 to 29 °C, mortality increased by 0.002 absolute rate units in the overall older-adult population while the increase doubled in aged 80+ group. Air pollution effects strengthened sharply with age: increasing PM2.5 from 5 to 10 μg/m3 raised mortality by about 0.0006 in 60-69 age group, but by nearly 0.003 in 80+ age group. Greenness measured by NDVI displayed a J-shaped association. For younger-old adults, NDVI rising to 0.2 was associated with nearly 0.001 lower model-predicted mortality, whereas higher county-level NDVI was associated with higher predicted mortality and steeper heat- and PM2.5-related gradients. Among the 80+ age group, counties with higher NDVI showed higher model-predicted mortality under concurrent heat and pollution, with joint differences reaching 0.016 and 0.013, suggesting limited buffering. Beyond exposures, income, transit access, and activity-supportive greening emerged as protective factors, providing actionable reference for age-targeted climate adaptation to protect older adults.

title: Green in situ construction of a macadamia waste-derived biochar/UiO-66-NH2 hybrid for high-efficiency removal of congo red and methyl orange from wastewater
abstract: The effective elimination of azo dyes from wastewater remains a significant challenge. In this study, a sustainable biochar–MOF hybrid (BC/UiO-66-NH2) derived from macadamia biomass was uniquely engineered through a green in situ synthesis strategy using ethanol and formic acid as environmentally benign solvents instead of conventional DMF, integrating waste-derived hierarchical biochar with amino-functionalized UiO-66-NH2. To overcome the limitations of conventional sorbents, this composite was developed to improve stability and uptake performance for Congo Red (CR) and Methyl Orange (MO). Optimal uptake performance was achieved at pH 3, 10 mg sorbent mass, achieving elimination efficiencies of 95.42 % for CR and 92.98 % for MO. Equilibrium profiles were well illustrated by the Langmuir model, yielding maximum uptake abilities of 1298.03 mg g−1 for CR and 1219.48 mg g−1 for MO. The composite also retained high adsorption efficiency after multiple ethanol-assisted regeneration cycles, confirming its structural robustness and reusability. When applied to real textile wastewater collected from a dyeing village in Bac Ninh, removal efficiencies remained high at 82.32 % for CR and 77.76 % for MO despite the occurrence of competing ions and complex organic constituents. Nevertheless, the optimum adsorption performance was obtained under acidic conditions (pH 3), whereas the real wastewater exhibited an initial alkaline pH 9, indicating that pH adjustment may be required for maximum efficiency. Furthermore, the present findings are based on batch-scale experiments, and additional continuous-flow and pilot-scale studies are necessary to further evaluate the practical applicability of the proposed adsorbent.

title: Green finance and the efficiency of energy transition policies: An integrated MCDA and SHAP approach for OECD countries
abstract: This study examines how green finance strategies influence energy transition performance in 31 OECD countries. It combines a structured, literature-based indicator framework with WSM, TOPSIS, SMAA robustness analysis, and interpretable machine learning via Random Forest, XGBoost, and SHAP, and double machine learning for orthogonalized effect estimation. The results reveal significant differences among countries, with Denmark ranking as the top performer and several others constrained by fossil fuel dependence and structural barriers. The XGBoost model predicts the SMAA-based country ranking with an R² value of 0.447. SHAP analysis identifies real GDP per capita, renewable energy public RD&D, and green patents as the three strongest predictors of transition performance rankings, followed by environmentally related tax revenues and energy productivity. Double machine learning shows that environmental tax revenues carry a robust orthogonalized effect on the transition rank, stable across nuisance learners and control sets. The 31 OECD countries fall into three strategic profiles: 8 renewable-dominant, 8 intermediate-transition, and 15 fossil-dominant. These findings demonstrate that effective green finance strategies require coherence among fiscal instruments, innovation support, energy productivity, and country-specific structural conditions. The study provides a comparative framework for designing differentiated policy strategies aligned with national transition capacities.

title: Structural and operational optimization of cold storage system for enhanced energy efficiency, rapid cold release and economic benefits
abstract: The increasing global energy demand and the accelerated integration of renewable energy have intensified the need for efficient and flexible building cooling technologies with low carbon impact. Ice cold storage systems (ICSS) offer a promising solution for demand-side energy management; however, their practical application is still constrained by limited heat transfer efficiency, insufficient cold energy conversion efficiency and restricted operational flexibility. In this study, a pilot-scale ICSS incorporating an internal cycle gas disturbance strategy was developed and investigated. Results indicate that the internal cycle gas disturbance significantly improves system performance by enhancing heat transfer coefficients and accelerating the rate of cold energy storage and release. Under optimal conditions (−3°C, 30 m3/h), the coefficient of performance (COP) of the chiller and the overall system increased by 9.27% and 7.42%, respectively, while favorable cold storage and discharge efficiency was achieved. Simulations further demonstrated that the proposed system outperforms conventional air-conditioning systems, reducing annual operational costs by a factor of 2.16 to 3.91, with payback periods of less than 2.77 years achieved across all representative regions under the optimal cold supply mode. Overall, the developed ICSS provides an energy-efficient and economically viable approach for cold energy storage. The results obtained under pilot-scale conditions demonstrate its engineering applicability and provide valuable insights into the scale-up and practical implementation of ice cold storage systems for building cooling applications.

title: Average photon energy based solar spectrum reconstruction for building-oriented TMY databases
abstract: With the transition of solar energy utilization toward a spectrum-regulation paradigm, solar spectral irradiance distribution (SID) has become increasingly important for building energy and photovoltaic (PV) applications. However, conventional typical meteorological year (TMY) databases generally lack spectral information, limiting their use in advanced energy analyses. To address this challenge, this study proposes a decoupled shape-intensity data-driven framework for high-fidelity solar spectrum reconstruction and TMY database enhancement featuring three core innovations. First, a shape-intensity decoupling mechanism is proposed, in which average photon energy (APE) characterizes spectral morphology while global horizontal irradiance (GHI) independently determines spectral intensity, enabling high-resolution spectral reconstruction from low-dimensional meteorological inputs. Second, an APE-GHI dual-variable spectral representation paradigm is established, providing a lightweight and data-driven alternative to conventional radiative transfer models. Third, this study pioneers the quantitative spectral enhancement and diagnostic analysis of mainstream TMY databases, revealing systematic spectral discrepancies among different data sources and climatic regions. The Random Forest model (RF) achieves an R2 of 0.949 with an RMSE of 0.009 eV for APE prediction while the reconstructed spectra exhibit an average error of 0.0177 W·m−2·nm−1 under diverse atmospheric conditions. Furthermore, the proposed multi-input prediction strategy maintains an R2 above 0.866 even without irradiance input, demonstrating adequate adaptability in data-scarce scenarios. This study provides a low-cost and scalable framework for enriching building-oriented TMY databases with dynamic spectral information, supporting advanced photovoltaic evaluation and spectrally responsive energy analyses.

title: Developing a phased implementation strategy for greenhouse gas mitigation in Korea's cement industry with the MESSAGEix model
abstract: The cement industry is difficult to decarbonize because fuel-combustion emissions and process emissions from limestone calcination occur simultaneously. This study develops a Korea-specific MESSAGEix-based bottom-up optimization model that integrates energy and material flows in the cement production system. Scenario analysis is conducted to distinguish reductions in total greenhouse gas emissions from reductions in clinker-specific emission intensity and to quantify the phase-specific roles and deployment timing of product and material substitution, process technology substitution, and CO2 capture and storage (CCS) through 2050. The results indicate that expanding blended cement and increasing supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) content in Portland cement can provide immediate mitigation and cost-saving potential by reducing clinker demand. Advanced kiln and raw mill technologies become increasingly important for lowering clinker-specific emission intensity in the medium term. In the long term, low-temperature calcination and CCS are required to manage residual process emissions under a 2050 carbon-neutrality constraint. These findings suggest that Korea's cement sector decarbonization requires a sequential portfolio strategy combining near-term reduction in clinker demand, mid-term process innovation, and long-term residual-emission management.

title: Interfacial electron redistribution stabilizes Cu-centered redox cycling for efficient Fenton-like catalysis
abstract: Efficient degradation of organic pollutants via Fenton-like catalysis remains a challenge due to the instability of the redox cycle under prolonged operation. Herein, we construct an interface-engineered FeCu layered double hydroxide/g-C3N4 heterostructure (FeCu-LDH/g-C3N4) to establish an internal electron-supply pathway for stabilizing Cu-centered redox cycling. Spectroscopic analyses, together with DFT calculations, support interface-induced electron redistribution, which favors electron depletion in the g-C3N4 framework and preferential electron enrichment at Cu sites, promoting partial Cu2+ reduction to Cu+, while Fe3+ remains largely stable as a structural and electronic modulator. Benefiting from this site-selective electronic regulation, FeCu-LDH/g-C3N4 exhibits markedly accelerated H2O2 activation and achieves near-complete Rhodamine B degradation within 20 min, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant 4.6 times that of pristine FeCu-LDH. Active-site substitution confirms Cu as the primary redox center, while ROS quenching and electron paramagnetic resonance analyses identify 1O2 as the dominant oxidative species, accompanied by •OH and O2•-. The catalyst further shows robust recyclability, broad pH adaptability, and strong tolerance to humic substances and common ions. This work demonstrates a Cu-site-selective interfacial electron-regulation strategy for designing stable and efficient Fenton-like catalysts.

title: Supply chain carbon penalties of U.S. carbon capture deployment: An EEIO-based assessment of net abatement performance
abstract: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is increasingly viewed as an essential option for decarbonizing emissions-intensive sectors, yet its net abatement value depends not only on captured emissions at host facilities but also on the economy-wide effects induced by deployment spending. Existing studies rarely integrate output propagation, supply-chain emissions added, emissions removed, and net performance indicators within a single U.S.-wide high-resolution framework. This study addresses that gap by developing an environmentally extended input-output model to quantify the economy-wide production impacts, supply chain carbon penalties, and net performance of CCS deployment in the United States. Annualized capital and operating expenditures for CCS were represented as an exogenous final-demand shock and mapped into the 402-sector USEEIO v2.5 framework, while emissions were evaluated using sector-specific capture fractions. For the modeled 90% capture scenario in electricity, lime and gypsum products, cement, and iron and steel, gross CO 2 removal reached 1.14 Gt, supply-chain activity added 0.08 Gt CO 2 , and net abatement remained substantial at 1.06 Gt CO 2 . The corresponding emission penalty ratio was around 67 kg CO 2 added per ton removed, and the net abatement cost was 73 $/tCO 2 . Scenario analysis showed that a 20% reduction in total CCS cost lowered the emission penalty ratio by 19% and the net abatement cost by 20%, whereas a 90% reduction in electricity-sector CO 2 intensity lowered the penalty ratio by 59% while producing only a marginal reduction in net abatement cost. These results indicate that CCS can deliver substantial net abatement, with cost reductions primarily improving economic performance and electricity-sector decarbonization providing greater leverage for reducing the upstream carbon penalty. Because the analysis uses a static national EEIO structure, it does not resolve regional heterogeneity, facility-level technological differences, or endogenous changes in economic and production relationships over time.

title: Annual energy use and economic performance of rice-based cropping systems: A three-year field study in Southwest China
abstract: Rice-based cropping systems are central to food security in Southwest China, yet integrated energy–economic assessments across diverse rotations remain scarce, particularly for rice-green manure and rice-vegetable systems. A three-year field experiment (2022–2025) was conducted in a typical rice-growing region of Southwest China to compare four upland–paddy rotations, namely wheat-rice (RW), rapeseed-rice (RR), green vegetables-rice (RG), and Vicia villosa var.-rice (RV), against a fallow–rice (RF) control, using an integrated energy input–output and cost–benefit framework. Results showed that RG recorded the highest annual energy input (51,754 MJ ha−1), dominated by nitrogen fertilizer, while RV had the lowest (31,345 MJ ha−1) without chemical fertilizer, corresponding to 84% and 12% increases over RF. Energy use efficiency (EUE) diverged even more markedly: RV achieved the highest annual EUE (25.37), with a dry-season EUE of 130.75, whereas RG had the lowest (8.14) despite the highest grain-equivalent yield (22,547 kg ha−1). Economic assessment revealed a clear efficiency–profitability trade-off. RG generated the highest net returns (5924 USD ha−1, benefit–cost ratio 1.11); RR and RW were intermediate (0.82 and 0.64); and RV yielded the lowest (1274 USD ha−1), as green manure provides no direct commodity income. The systems were thus classified into three patterns: high input, high output and low efficiency (RG); balanced (RW and RR); and low input, high efficiency and low return (RV). These findings provide quantitative evidence for region-specific strategies. RG with enhanced nutrient management is recommended for peri-urban areas, RR and RW for major grain-producing regions, and RV with ecological compensation for ecologically sensitive zones, thereby supporting the green transformation of rice-based agriculture.

title: Toward circular biochar systems from waste-derived precursors: multi-analytical and multivariate insights into adsorption and heterogeneous Fenton-like oxidation performance
abstract: Understanding how waste-derived resources can be transformed into functional materials is essential for advancing circular economy strategies and sustainable water treatment technologies. In this work, a combined multi-analytical and multivariate framework is developed to elucidate how waste-derived precursor type, pyrolysis temperature, and iron functionalization collectively control adsorption and heterogeneous Fenton-like oxidation in biochar-based systems. Biochars were produced from 4 waste-derived precursors: spent coffee grounds, olive pomace, olive pomace stones, and sewage sludge, at three pyrolysis temperatures (450, 550, and 650 °C), generating 12 pristine materials and, after iron functionalization, a total of 24 materials. This design enables a systematic evaluation of waste-to-resource pathways and the decoupling of compositional and structural effects. Advanced characterization was combined with I-optimal response surface methodology (RSM) and principal component analysis (PCA) to provide complementary information: RSM was used to optimize material and process variables, whereas PCA was applied to interpret structure-property-performance relationships and identify the main descriptors controlling adsorption and heterogeneous Fenton-like oxidation. Equilibrium adsorption data were better described by the Freundlich model (R 2 ≥ 0.97), indicating that surface heterogeneity was a dominant factor, while Langmuir-derived Qmax values were used only as comparative capacity indicators. Lignocellulosic biochars were governed by surface area and aromaticity, whereas sewage-sludge-derived biochars showed enhanced affinity due to their mineral-rich matrices and oxygenated functionalities. Iron functionalization significantly improved performance, with Fe-SSBC450 showing the highest Langmuir-derived adsorption capacity (Qmax = 6.57 mg g −1 ) and oxidation efficiency (∼76% phenol removal). Oxidation proceeded via • OH-driven mechanisms following pseudo-second-order kinetics. This work demonstrates how waste-derived precursors can be valorised into high-value materials for environmental remediation, supporting circular economy strategies through resource-efficient water purification.

title: Towards cleaner rare earth metal production: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of direct Nd2O3 pyroelectroreduction in low-temperature chloride-based molten salt
abstract: Industrial neodymium metal production is currently dominated by high-temperature fluoride-based molten salt electrolysis, a process plagued by high energy demand, aggressive corrosion, fluoride waste generation, and significant greenhouse gas emissions. This work evaluates a cleaner alternative using a chloride electrolyte, in which Neodymium metal (Nd) is produced in a LiCl-KCl eutectic at 450°C. The analyzed route incorporates Neodymium (III) oxide (Nd2O3) pellets, a novel approach that enables stable electroreduction, reduces material losses, enhances current efficiency, and simplifies solid handling compared to conventional dissolved feedstocks. We compare this method against the established LiF-NdF3 process operating near 1000°C. Capital and operating expenditures were evaluated using validated cost-scaling correlations, an electrowinning-specific CapEx model, and experimentally supported process assumptions, with a novel density-based correction factor introduced to reconcile discrepancies and improve prediction accuracy. Our results demonstrate that the chloride-based pellet process operates with substantially lower energy input, reduced anode consumption, and lower CapEx and OpEx across all evaluated production scales.

title: A decision-support framework for structuring and assessing photovoltaic panel recycling costs in emerging economies
abstract: The rapid expansion of solar energy systems has intensified concerns about the sustainable management of photovoltaic panels at the end of its life cycle, particularly recycling and resource recovery. Despite the growing volume of end-of-life solar equipment, significant uncertainties persist regarding recycling costs, especially in emerging economies, where structured economic assessment approaches remain limited. This study proposes a structured decision-support framework to support the assessment and management of recycling costs associated with end-of-life photovoltaic panels. A Systematic Literature Review was conducted to identify cost components related to photovoltaic recycling, which were then structured using the Function Analysis System Technique. Expert evaluation was used to validate cost relevance and structure. The Fuzzy Delphi method and Mean Rank Position were applied to reach consensus on cost relevance, while the Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis method was used to assign weights to cost categories. The resulting framework consolidates consensual cost components into weighted functional clusters, providing a structured basis for economic assessment and supporting decision-making in photovoltaic panel recycling initiatives. The proposed framework contributes to resource conservation and circular economy strategies by supporting managers, investors, and policymakers in structuring and comparing the cost dimensions associated with photovoltaic panel recycling in emerging economies.

title: Global perspectives on the curricular integration of nature-based solutions in hydrology and water resources management education
abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are strongly advocated in international environmental discourse and policy agendas for climate risk management. However, a critical knowledge gap remains regarding the extent to which NbS concepts are systematically integrated into higher education curricula, despite the role of universities as institutional settings for developing and disseminating knowledge relevant to NbS. In this study, we examined the degree of curricular integration of NbS within university study programs in water resources management (WRM) and hydrology at the undergraduate, master's, and doctoral levels across 25 countries in 8 geographic regions. Data were collected through a structured survey, and curricula analysis was conducted, in which the proportion of NbS content within each course was categorized into Major (core focus), Moderate (partial coverage), Minor (peripheral inclusion), or NA (no explicit content). Our findings reveal significant regional and disciplinary contrasts. Countries with research-active disciplines, such as engineering and environmental science, and those with formal NbS policy frameworks, such as in the EU, show earlier or more extensive NbS curricular integration. Contrary to the interdisciplinary nature of NbS, we find that NbS are predominantly, yet sporadically, embedded in civil and environmental engineering and natural sciences, with minimal contributions from other disciplines, such as social sciences. Moreover, NbS concept remains insufficiently represented at the undergraduate level as 45.9% of the courses contain Minor content and 33.9% have no explicit NbS content, which represents a missed opportunity for NbS exposure during foundational professional study and training. More substantive NbS content appears in master's and doctoral programs, suggesting that NbS remains a specialized, research-oriented topic rather than foundational curriculum content. Faculty-led NbS teaching initiatives, identified through the survey, though encouraging, reveal a misalignment between high NbS research activity and their low curricular integration, where 31–41% of lecturers in courses with NA and Minor NbS integration do publish NbS-related research. Without explicit NbS framing in WRM and hydrology curricula, study programs may remain confined to specific disciplinary silos, potentially limiting students' overall engagement with NbS concepts. These findings collectively suggest that advancing comprehensive NbS integration in higher education may require deliberate and coordinated curricular reform across institutional levels, highlighting the importance of a whole-institution approach that systematically integrates NbS into curriculum, governance structures, and campus infrastructure.

title: Decision-making for enhancing thermal resilience: Identifying and prioritising intervention domains across social, economic, ecological, and technological systems
abstract: The compounding effects of climate change and urbanisation have intensified heatwave frequency and the urban heat island effect, posing growing risks to thermal comfort and public health. Enhancing thermal resilience requires coordinated interventions across social, economic, ecological, and technological systems. However, existing studies remain limited in clearly identifying key intervention domains and in understanding how these domains interact within an integrated systems perspective. Therefore, the overarching aim of this research is to identify key thermal resilience interventions, examine expert-perceived interrelationships among them, and develop an expert-informed decision-support analytical framework for interpreting and prioritising interventions. Focus groups with experts from China and the UK were conducted using a modified Problem Tree Analysis approach to elicit intervention-related problems, perceived causes and effects. A subsequent web-based survey was used to assess the perceived influence relationships among the identified intervention domains. These relationships were analysed using the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory-based Analytic Network Process (DANP) method. The results reveal distinct expert-perceived influence structures among intervention domains across Social-Economic-Ecological-Technological (SEET) system dimensions, while also highlighting the central role of policy development and planning and economic feasibility in shaping the implementation of intervention domains. The key contribution of this study is the development of an expert-informed decision-support analytical framework that systematically captures cross-dimensional influence relationships and supports the prioritisation of thermal resilience interventions. The findings provide an expert-informed analytical basis for supporting context-sensitive decision-making in urban heat adaptation under climate change.

title: Pressure-aware multi-modal CO2 transport planning for industrial decarbonization: A case study of Germany's steel sector to 2050
abstract: Multi-modal CO 2 transport networks involve coupled decisions on operating pressure, mode-switching equipment, and infrastructure deployment timing, yet existing optimization studies typically treat the associated compression, liquefaction, and heat exchange as post-processing assumptions. This study develops a pressure-aware mixed-integer linear programming framework for multi-modal CO 2 transport planning that couples mode selection with pressure-state-dependent conditioning, allowing pressure regimes and mode transitions to be optimized jointly. The framework integrates phased deployment across three time horizons (2030, 2040, 2050) under three decarbonization pathways, carbon pricing for uncaptured emissions, and selective reuse of existing pipelines within a single optimization. Seven mode-pressure variants are considered, with mode-transition costs derived from a 49-transition simulation matrix. The framework is applied to twelve major German steel emitters connected to the Northern Lights offshore storage site via three candidate ports. The cost-optimal network shifts from truck-and-rail logistics in the early, low-volume stage to a dense-phase pipeline backbone as captured volumes grow. Unit transport costs remain within 15–18 €/tCO 2 across the scenarios. The marginal cost of expanding transport and conditioning capacity stabilizes at 13–14 €/tCO 2 from 2040 onward. These figures indicate that transport is not the binding economic constraint on scaling up capture ambition, rather than that CCUS as a whole is inexpensive. Existing pipeline reuse is found to be capacity- and stage-dependent: sufficiently large reused assets can reduce new-build requirements. The framework offers a transferable approach for cleaner industrial logistics design, supporting the transition to low-carbon hard-to-abate sectors in Europe and beyond.

title: Interface interaction between yeast and β-glucan drives soil aggregate stabilization: molecular mechanisms and bioremediation functions
abstract: Soil aggregates formed during microbial-mediated soil remediation contribute critically to consolidating soil particles, enhancing soil stability, and improving soil permeability. However, the molecular-scale interaction mechanisms among microorganisms, their extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), and soil minerals during aggregate formation remain unclear. This study systematically elucidates the molecular mechanism underlying soil aggregate formation in a model yeast-EPS (β-glucan)-mineral system specifically designed to address soil structure degradation in the Loess Plateau. By integrating multi-scale experimental approaches with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate that β-glucan mediates stable adhesion between yeast cells and soil-driven SiO2 particles primarily through van der Waals forces, thereby facilitating the assembly of a three-dimensional “microorganism–EPS–mineral” composite architecture. The co-application of yeast and β-glucan increased the proportion of macroaggregates (>0.25 mm) to 22.58%, compared to only 2.49% in the unamended control. Notably, owing to yeast's intrinsic dormancy response under environmental stress, the aggregates exhibited remarkable resilience against aging and repeated freeze-thaw cycles. This bioengineered system significantly improved soil functions. Total organic carbon (TOC) content increased from 2.57 g/kg to 20.90 g/kg, while total dissolved solids (TDS) remained stably below 2.5 g/kg through yeast metabolic regulation. Furthermore, the soil erodibility factor and fractal dimension analysis confirmed that the β-glucan/yeast/loess aggregate significantly enhanced soil structural integrity and markedly reduced erosion susceptibility. Our findings underscore the promise of biologically driven remediation strategies for restoring degraded soils in the Loess Plateau and provide mechanistic insights that may inform future studies on complex interfacial interactions among microorganisms, organic polymers, and mineral surfaces.

title: Uncovering the burden shifting of data center cooling: System-level water-energy-carbon optimization for urban infrastructure
abstract: The rapid growth of data centers (DCs), driven by artificial intelligence and cloud computing, presents a critical resource challenge for urban infrastructure planning across the water-energy-carbon nexus. Traditional energy models often treat DC integration merely as an isolated electrical load, failing to capture weather-dependent cooling demands and the resulting "burden-shifting" between direct on-site water consumption and the indirect water footprint of the regional grid. To bridge this gap, this study introduces a multi-scale mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) optimization framework for urban capacity expansion planning that explicitly integrates hourly climate data with the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) of distinct DC cooling architectures. Applied to a representative urban microgrid, the model simulates a multi-year horizon at an hourly resolution to evaluate two contrasting DC cooling strategies: evaporative cooling and closed-loop air chillers. Our results reveal a critical trade-off: optimizing exclusively for zero on-site water use via air chillers inadvertently shifts the resource burden upstream to the regional electrical grid, demanding substantial increases in low-carbon generation, energy storage, and total infrastructure costs. Ultimately, moving beyond facility-specific metrics to evaluate holistic, system-wide Pareto trade-offs is essential for developing sustainable urban energy strategies.

title: Fewer children, higher carbon intensity? Exploring household carbon emission intensity in low-fertility contexts
abstract: Low fertility and global warming have become pressing global concerns. However, systematic research on how low fertility and regional disparities affect household carbon emission intensity remains limited. To address this gap, we adopt a micro level household structure perspective and utilize CFPS panel data for 2014-2022 to analyze the temporal dynamics of household carbon emission intensity across China's eight major economic zones. On this basis, a bidirectional fixed-effects model, along with mediation and moderation analyses, is employed to explore the impact of low fertility on household carbon emission intensity and to further identify its transmission channels. Results show that, in terms of temporal trends, low fertility and household carbon emission intensity display a synchronous relationship, with notable stage-specific and regional differences. In terms of empirical results, low fertility raises household carbon emission intensity, with the effect being especially pronounced in regions with very low-fertility. The results further indicate that scale effects and neighborhood effects are key channels influencing the relationship between the two, while environmental awareness and internet use play moderating roles. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that families without intergenerational care, households with a first-born girl, developmental consumption and those in the Northeast and Northern coastal regions all exert an amplifying effect on household carbon emission intensity. Therefore, it is essential to align the consumption patterns of low-fertility households with national and regional carbon emissions, offering valuable policy insights for the integrated optimization of population and low-carbon strategies.

title: Machine learning prediction and analysis for LFL of C0-C2 combustible gases and blends under wide operating conditions
abstract: The safe deployment of low- and zero-carbon fuels requires reliable prediction of lower flammability limits (LFLs) over broad temperature, pressure, and composition ranges. This need is increasingly important for hydrogen, ammonia, alcohols, ethers, and C0-C2 combustible-gas blends used in storage, transport, and energy-conversion systems. However, conventional LFL prediction methods tend to be inaccurate for gases with a reference Lewis-number factor below unity (Leref < 1), particularly hydrogen and hydrogen-rich mixtures. They are also difficult to apply efficiently to multi-component blends under variable operating conditions because direct extinction-limit calculations require repeated flame simulations and boundary tracking. A C0–C2 reaction mechanism with 110 species and 682 reactions was developed. In addition, an enhanced counterflow premixed flame model was introduced, incorporating flame stretch, radiative heat loss, and an Leref-based stability correction, which significantly reduced prediction errors for combustible gases with Leref < 1. Sensitivity analysis and symbolic regression over 250–500 K and 0.05–2 MPa show that increasing temperature consistently lowers LFL, whereas pressure effects are nonlinear and gas dependent. To reduce the computational burden of blend prediction, eight machine learning algorithms were benchmarked, and the optimal model was coupled with the Le Chatelier's principle as a rapid surrogate for multi-component LFL estimation. Validation against 793 experimental data points confirms that the proposed framework can accurately predict multi-component LFLs while greatly reducing the need for direct flame simulations. The trained model provides predictions within seconds, offering a practical tool for large-scale parametric screening, safety-boundary assessment and cleaner utilization of low-carbon combustible-gas blends in storage, transport, and energy-conversion applications.

title: Resilience and reconfiguration: A CPD-STERGM analysis of structural breaks in the BRI LIB trade network
abstract: Amid the global energy transition, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are a key commodity underpinning clean energy and electrified transport. The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), centered on intergovernmental dialogue and coordinated infrastructure, fundamentally reshapes how trade ties form among participating countries. Understanding this network's resilience requires identifying structural breaks in the mechanisms governing trade tie formation and dissolution. This study identifies the timing of these breaks in the BRI LIB trade network from 2017 to 2022 to examine how geographic, institutional, and technological factors drive trade tie dynamics across distinct evolutionary phases. Using trade data from 56 BRI countries, this study integrates Change Point Detection with the Separable Temporal Exponential Random Graph Model (CPD-STERGM) to estimate phase-specific mechanisms of tie formation and dissolution. Four breakpoints are detected at October 2017, January 2019, January 2020, and April 2022. The network evolved through five phases, exhibiting a pronounced “core-transit-periphery” stratification. Driving mechanisms shifted from “hard” factors like geographic proximity to “soft” factors including common language and bilateral investment treaties. Consequently, this study proposes a differentiated supply chain governance framework encompassing emergency response mechanisms, logistics hub upgrading, and institutional coordination via the mutual recognition of standards and investment protection. This offers actionable policy insights to enhance LIB supply chain resilience within the BRI.

title: Green efficiency under heterogeneous technologies: Evidence from Indian manufacturing industry
abstract: The manufacturing industry is central to India's economic growth, but it also accounts for substantial energy use and CO2 emissions. An understanding of green efficiency under heterogeneous technologies is crucial for designing differentiated industrial decarbonisation strategies. This study evaluates the green efficiency of 21 manufacturing industries in India from 2010 to 11 to 2022-23 using an input-oriented window data envelopment analysis model within a metafrontier framework. Labour, capital, and energy are used as inputs, gross sales are used as the desirable output, and CO2 emissions are treated as the undesirable output. A non-linear path in green efficiency is observed, indicating a broad transitional adjustment process accompanied by technical inefficiencies. Significant industry heterogeneity is observed, with technology-intensive industries remaining closest to the frontier, while labour- and capital-intensive industries exhibit persistent inefficiencies and technology gaps. Policy recommendations are proposed to facilitate cluster-specific strategies for improving green efficiency.

title: Understanding consumer reactions and corporate reputation in corporate sustainability crises: The role of blame, harm, and CSR relevance
abstract: This study investigates how consumers' behavioral responses vary across different types of corporate sustainability crises characterized by differences in potential harm, attribution of blame, and relevance to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). We also examine the moderating role of pre-crisis corporate reputation in shaping these responses. An experimental full factorial design is employed based on a representative sample of U.S. adults (N = 680). Situational Crisis Communication Theory (SCCT) posits that stakeholders' attributions of responsibility are influenced by an organization's crisis history, stakeholder relationships, and reputation. Extending SCCT, the findings indicate that when a firm's pre-crisis reputation is low, consumers' behavioral responses are not significantly influenced by the crisis's potential for harm, CSR relevance, or attribution of blame. In contrast, when pre-crisis reputation is high, both potential harm and attribution of blame exert a significant effect on consumer behavior, whereas CSR relevance does not. This study makes a novel contribution by examining a comprehensive set of sustainability-related crisis types, including industry-wide collective crises, product-harm crises, and CSR-related tensions. Theoretical and managerial implications are discussed.

title: Modified lignosulfonate-assisted in situ synthesis of Co3Mo3N/CoMo2S4 heterojunction electrocatalyst with strong interfacial interactions for efficient overall water splitting
abstract: The high cost of precious metals has driven the pursuit of efficient and stable non-precious metal electrocatalysts, which remains a central challenge for electrocatalytic water splitting. Herein, aminated sodium lignosulfonate served as a biomacromolecular skeleton for the construction of a novel bifunctional electrocatalyst, CoMo@NSLA, via a hydrothermal-pyrolysis approach. This approach enabled the in situ formation of Co3Mo3N particles and CoMo2S4 nanosheets on the derived carbon matrix. CoMo@NSLA showed high HER and OER efficiency in alkaline media, with overpotentials as low as 102 and 251 mV at 10 mA cm−2. The assembled CoMo@NSLA-based electrolyzer exhibited a low operating voltage of 1.61 V at 10 mA cm−2 and maintained 94 % performance over 30 h, demonstrating excellent durability. As confirmed by experimental and theoretical analyses, the superior performance originated from its porous architecture, high surface area, as well as strong interfacial interaction within the Co3Mo3N/CoMo2S4 heterojunction. Specifically, interfacial charge transfer induced electronic reconfiguration that activated Mo sites and optimized the d-band center. This synergistically regulated the adsorption/desorption of reaction intermediates, thereby enhancing the kinetics of HER and OER. This work achieves the high-value utilization of lignosulfonate and paves a new route toward high-performance electrocatalysts based on biomass-carbon-supported bimetallic nitride/sulfide composites.

title: Regulating interface charge separation to unlock photocatalytic non-radical pathways: Construction of BiOCl/COF S-scheme heterojunction for efficient antibiotic remediation
abstract: The inefficiency of charge separation and the unselective nature of radical-based pathways severely limit the practical application of photocatalysis for water purification. Herein, a BiOCl/COF (BOC/COF) S-scheme heterojunction was successfully constructed via ultrasonic assistance. Remarkably, the optimized S-scheme heterojunction significantly enhanced photo-generated carrier separation efficiency, which effectively promoted ROS generation and improved the removal rate of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) (degradation rate: 91.6%). The research has found that non-radical pathways collectively accounted for 89.11% of the degradation activity, endowing the system with high selectivity. It is worth noting that the BC-20 membrane can efficiently eliminate TC in a continuous-flow wastewater treatment system. Furthermore, BC-20 can degrade TC in an enlarged reactor under natural sunlight irradiation. The three possible degradation pathways were analyzed through Fukui function and LC-MS. The toxicity of the TC solution after being treated with the BOC/COF S-scheme was evaluated using mung beans as a crop model. Through (in-situ) characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the S-scheme charge transfer mechanism and interfacial electric field (IEF) driving efficient 1O2 production were systematically elucidated. These findings not only deciphered the interface engineering-mediated non-radical generation mechanism in BOC/COF S-scheme photocatalysis but also advanced its practical application in aquatic environmental remediation.

title: Investigating the regulatory effects of surfactants to design high-performance and eco-friendly soybean oil-based emulsions for the manufacturing industry
abstract: To address the critical challenges associated with vegetable oil-based emulsions in the ultra-precision machining of TC4 titanium alloy-namely, insufficient stability, limited lubrication performance, and environmental compatibility concerns-the regulatory regulation mechanism of surfactant charge characteristics and molecular configuration on the multiscale properties of emulsions was systematically investigated. The results revealed that the anionic surfactant (SDBS) significantly enhanced interfacial mass transfer and oil droplet replenishment through the formation of a low-viscosity, small-droplet-size emulsion system, thereby inducing a stable mixed lubrication film at the friction interface. In addition, its strong adsorption behavior, in conjunction with ultrasonic cavitation effects, promoted the in-situ generation of a dense TiO2 passivation layer on the TC4 surface. This dual composite structure, consisting of an adsorption layer and a passivation film, endowed the system with remarkable corrosion resistance. Regarding machining performance, the SDBS emulsion facilitated efficient swarf removal and suppressed interfacial adhesion by virtue of its superior wetting and spreading capability and high oil film load-bearing capacity, while also minimizing the wear and blunting of diamond abrasives. Compared with the T80 and CTAC systems, the SDBS system reduced tool wear rates by 35.12% and 31.05%, respectively, and increased material removal rates by 25.14% and 20.11%. Furthermore, this system exhibited satisfactory antibacterial activity and low biotoxicity, demonstrating notable eco-friendly characteristics. Collectively, these findings provide a systematic theoretical and experimental foundation for the design of plant oil-based emulsions tailored for green and high-efficiency manufacturing processes.

title: Sustainable salt recovery from DMF-containing industrial brines through integrated nanofiltration and space-confined catalytic ozonation
abstract: Industrial waste brines containing trace refractory organics remain difficult to purify and reuse, limiting sustainable salt recovery. In this study, an integrated process combining nanofiltration (NF) and ceramic-membrane-enabled space-confined catalytic ozonation was developed for the treatment of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)-containing industrial brines. NF achieved 96.27% SO42− rejection with minimal chloride loss, while the subsequent catalytic ozonation step, optimized at an initial pH of 12.41, an O3 flow rate of 384 mL min−1, and a catalyst dosage of 14.25 g, reached 96.7% TOC removal. Radical quenching experiments indicated that hydroxyl radicals played a dominant role in the confined oxidation process. For real industrial brine, although the TOC of NF permeate fluctuated between 130 and 195 mg L−1, the catalytic ozonation step consistently reduced the final TOC to 3–10 mg L−1, meeting the organic-content requirement for downstream chlor-alkali use. Electrolysis tests further showed that the refined brine supported stable cell operation under the tested conditions. These results demonstrate that the integrated NF and space-confined catalytic ozonation process is effective for sulfate control, deep organic removal, and subsequent brine reuse, providing a feasible route for sustainable salt recovery from DMF-containing industrial brines.

title: Life cycle assessment of growing media: a baseline dataset for European horticulture
abstract: Growing media underpin a substantial and growing share of European food and ornamental production, with 116 million cubic metres used globally per year. Their environmental footprint has become a focus of regulatory and commercial attention, but comparative assessments to date have been fragmented in scope and rely on outdated data, limiting their value for research and industry. This study presents a Life Cycle Assessment of twelve constituents and thirty mixes (covering seven applications) representative of European horticulture.
