The study follows a cradle-to-gate scope, including use-phase emissions for all organic materials. Climate change impact and single score (weighted impact of 16 categories) are presented per functional unit (1 m 3 ) at the constituent and mix levels. Wood fibre (15 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 ) and expanded perlite (33 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 ) had the lowest climate change impact; white peat (219 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 ), green compost (249 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 ), and black peat (390 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 ) had the highest. Single score results show a reversal in ranking for white peat (7.7 mPt/m 3 ) and coir constituents (9.0 to 10.5 mPt/m 3 ), emphasising the need for multi-indicator assessments to minimise the risk of shifting environmental burdens. Green compost presents a high climate change impact and single score result (21.3 mPt/m 3 ), but substantial uncertainty of this estimate highlights the need for further inventory data improvement. Mix-level results indicate that substantial carbon savings can be achieved by strategic formulation of mixes in the sectors of fruiting vegetables, potted plants and ornamentals, and tree nurseries. Assessment at the application level is identified as the next methodological priority to define strategies for efficient use of growing media resources.

title: Cradle to grave life cycle assessment of retreaded truck tyres: an industrial case study in Italy
abstract: The transition to climate-neutrality by 2050 requires decarbonizing mobility and among the different materials used in this sector there is the urgent need to decarbonize tyres. Despite the problems related to the recycling of tyres, retreading is a technology already available on the market that, prolonging the useful service life of tyres, allows considerable environmental advantages. However, its diffusion is still limited and concentrated in the truck sector with a decreasing trend in the last decade. This study presents for the first time a cradle to grave Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) that compares the environmental performance of two product systems, i.e. retreaded truck tyres and virgin truck tyres. The study is based on primary data, when available, and on secondary data or estimations, when necessary. The results show that retreading allows a considerable reduction in the environmental impact of tyres: up to 50 % in the climate change impact category, 52 % in the fossil fuels consumption, 49 % in the consumption of natural resources, 55 % in the water use, 37 % in the PM 10 emission and 10 % in the PM 2.5 emissions. Moreover, retreading allows for a reduction up to 46 % in the use of natural rubber (EU is 100 % import-reliant on this material). These findings highlight the urgent need for policies that can promote the diffusion of retreading on a larger scale in case of truck tyres and that support the creation of a dedicated supply chain for the retreading of car tyres.

title: Delay-consistent adaptive incentive governance for circular beverage packaging systems: distinguishing structural and algorithmic limits in PET and returnable glass recovery in Mexico
abstract: Mexico's 2030 target of 80% PET-container recovery under the ANNEP agreement remains 16 percentage points above the current national recovery rate, with returnable glass already operating near its infrastructure asymptote. Whether adaptive incentive governance can close this gap depends on distinguishing the mechanism sources of policy performance: the adaptive feedback timing itself, the average incentive intensity at which policies operate, or the underlying behavioral response of the recovery system. This paper investigates the distinction using a delay-consistent adaptive proportional–integral controller embedded in a system-dynamics closed-loop supply chain calibrated against four independent empirical sources for the Mexican beverage-container context. Four policies are compared in a 216-cell balanced factorial design: a no-incentive baseline, a constant deposit-refund, an adaptive proportional–integral controller, and a quarterly threshold rule. A new stratified matched-budget identification experiment decomposes policy performance into three analytically distinct levels — algorithmic effects, operating-point effects, and structural constraints — by comparing the adaptive controller against an equivalent-intensity fixed benchmark across baseline, demand-dip, and demand-whiplash regimes. The matched-budget analysis indicates that the adaptive controller and the equivalent-intensity fixed policy converge to essentially identical steady-state return rates (approximately 0.759) under all three demand regimes; the previously observed adaptive advantage is attributable to operating-point effects rather than to feedback timing. This identification supports interpreting the 2.1-percentage-point gap between the observed ceiling and the 0.78 composite target as structural rather than algorithmic in origin: the ceiling reflects the saturating Michaelis–Menten behavioral response of the recovery system, not a limitation of the control algorithm. Closing this gap requires policy instruments capable of expanding the behavioral elasticity envelope itself — reverse-vending densification, extended producer responsibility, informal-sector formalization, and consumer information campaigns — rather than stronger deposit-refund incentives alone. • Matched-budget identification experiment isolates algorithmic from operating-point effects in deposit-refund governance. • Adaptive controller and equivalent-intensity fixed policy converge to identical return rates across three demand regimes. • The 0.759 composite return-rate ceiling is structural, not algorithmic — reflecting behavioral elasticity limits. • Structural ceiling stops recovery 2.1 percentage points below Mexico's 0.78 composite target under current elasticities. • Closing the gap requires elasticity-envelope expansion, not stronger deposit-refund incentives.

title: Evaluating and advancing large language models for soil and water conservation tasks: Case study of the black soil region
abstract: Soil and water conservation (SWC) has accumulated decades of vast but fragmented knowledge, limiting efficient use. Although large language models (LLMs) excel across professional domains, their SWC competence remains uncharacterized. We developed SWC-KC (SWC-Knowledge and Computation) to quantify LLM capability boundaries and test whether supervised fine-tuning (SFT) transfers to SWC. For the black soil region, we organized knowledge and computation tasks by Bloom's six cognitive levels, curated evaluation and fine-tuning datasets from authoritative corpora, benchmarked eight mainstream Chinese and international models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o-mini), and LoRA-fine-tuned two open-source 14B models (Qwen3-14B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B). All models attained 40%–60% knowledge-task accuracy. Reasoning models excelled only with formulas provided (DeepSeek-R1 highest, 73.70%); without formulas all performed poorly (≤17.37%), leaving applicability to more complex engineering scenarios unverified. Computational errors decomposed into formula selection and execution, diverging sharply across question types; knowledge errors concentrated in short-answer questions and tracked subtask. Quality gains were costly, reasoning models added 9.34 accuracy percentage points on average but extended response time over 25-fold, task type dominating this trade-off. SFT raised knowledge accuracy by over 20 percentage points but barely improved computation. Deployment should match models to latency and error cost, routing high-stakes computation through human-in-the-loop workflows combining retrieval-supplied pathways, tool execution, and expert review. Fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool invocation, and structured prompting can combine into hybrid pathways targeting distinct bottlenecks. Overall, this first SWC-specific LLM evaluation framework shows that SFT closes knowledge gaps but not reasoning bottlenecks under the tested settings, offering a transferable paradigm for other environmental disciplines.

title: A polymer-modified bentonite stabilizer for cadmium- and arsenic-contaminated soils: Simultaneous microbial diversity enhancement, nutrient enrichment, and plant growth promotion
abstract: Mining activities have led to significant cadmium (Cd) and arsenic (As) contamination in agricultural soil. Due to their divergent chemical behaviors, simultaneously stabilizing both metals remains a critical challenge. In this study, we synthesized a chitosan (CS)-grafted polymerized iron-pillared bentonite (CS@Fe@Bt) to integrate CS's chelating sites with the redox-active surfaces of Fe-oxide pillars. Soil culture experiments demonstrate that the 2% addition of CS@Fe@Bt reduced bioavailable Cd and As by 83.61% and 74.81% in mining-contaminated soils, respectively. Such balanced stabilization performance points toward the synergistic effect of the CS amino groups and polymerized iron pillars. The characterization test results obtained from X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) suggested that the stabilization pathways are driven by site-specific interactions: Cd is probably sequestered through coordination complexation with -NH2/-OH groups and pH-induced precipitation, while As is likely immobilized via oxidation of As(III) to As(V) followed by Fe-O-As ligand exchange. Concurrently, adding 1% CS@Fe@Bt enhanced soil nutrient availability, with available nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) increasing by 5.03%, 2.87%, and 5.32%, respectively. Furthermore, significant increases in bacterial richness and total organic carbon were observed, indicating favorable shifts in the soil microenvironment and carbon pool. Pot experiments revealed that 1% CS@Fe@Bt reduced Cd and As levels in stems and leaves of the pak choi by 15.11% and 55.98% in mining-contaminated soils; 2% CS@Fe@Bt increased the plant height and fresh weight by 13.63% and 91.68% respectively, suggesting that CS@Fe@Bt effectively mitigated heavy metal toxicity to plants. In summary, CS@Fe@Bt effectively mitigated concurrent Cd and As contamination while improving soil nutrient availability and promoting plant growth. Further long-term field trials are required to evaluate the long-term stability of immobilized heavy metals under variable environmental stresses.

title: Release of multilayered constraints drives metabolic and regulatory evolutionary strategies for polyethylene biodegradation
abstract: Despite advances in identifying polyethylene (PE) biodegradation enzymes, the routes by which different bacteria enhance PE degradation remain poorly understood. This study began with a simple observation: two taxonomically distinct bacterial strains, subjected to the same selective pressure, both enhanced their PE degradation capacity—yet through fundamentally different molecular routes. Pursuing this divergence through integrated multi-omics revealed that PE degradation is governed not by a single rate-limiting enzyme or path, but by a multilayered network of constraints spanning genomic, enzymatic, metabolic, and functional layers. Different strains are limited at different layers, and the release of these constraints—through mutagenesis and selection—gives rise to distinct evolutionary strategies that converge on a common phenotype. The two strategies documented here, global metabolic remodeling and targeted regulatory enhancement, represent two instances of this principle. This multilayered framework extends the enzyme-centric view of PE biodegradation, providing insight into how complex microbial functions can be enhanced through the release of constraints distributed across multiple layers of biological organization.

title: Estimating consumption-based electricity carbon emission intensity from public data: A cleaner production framework for the Tokyo Metropolitan Area
abstract: This study develops a reproducible framework to estimate synthetic 30-min electricity-related CO 2 emissions intensity (CEI) across 14 zones in the Tokyo Metropolitan Area (TMA), addressing gaps in urban emission accounting for decarbonization planning. The primary contribution is an economic dispatch-based electricity carbon emission (ED-CE) model implemented under both Monthly and Intra-day demand allocation approaches using publicly available data. The ED-CE model combines a merit-order dispatch algorithm with a neighbor-priority allocation approach in which surplus electricity is redistributed to the closest zones based on geographical proximity. The Intra-day approach incorporates synthetic half-hourly demand profiles to represent short-term electricity consumption variability. To assess robustness, a network-constrained electricity carbon emission (NC-CE) model is implemented using power-flow information. Results show that while system-level CEI estimates are consistent across ED-CE and NC-CE, spatial patterns are more sensitive to allocation assumptions under ED-CE, whereas NC-CE produces comparatively smoother spatial variability due to power flow constraints and flow-traced emission attribution. In addition, a sensitivity analysis using random surplus allocation indicates that major emission hotspots are generally robust, although absolute zonal magnitudes remain uncertain. The results reveal spatial and temporal heterogeneity in electricity-related emissions and annual emissions (33.2 MtCO 2 /year), increasing 37.0 MtCO 2 /year under the Intra-day approach, while suburban regions show lower or redistributed emissions under intra-day allocation. Southern Ibaraki maintains the lowest CEI (0.26 kgCO 2 /kWh) across all model configurations, indicating a robust low-carbon supply pattern. Industrial and commercial emissions exceed Tokyo Cap-and-Trade value due to differing boundaries and methods, while electricity CEI shows temporal variability from renewables.

title: Electricity-carbon traceability settlement model based on contract and power flow distribution under the new-type power system
abstract: The collaborative operation of electricity and carbon markets is critical for both addressing global climate change and advancing the low-carbon energy transition. However, existing frameworks suffer from ambiguous carbon responsibility allocation and inefficient transmission of environmental benefits. To address these issues, this paper proposes a settlement model for electricity-carbon traceability based on contract transactions and power flow distribution in the new-type power system. First, by coupling contract fulfillment with power flow tracing, the model establishes an electricity traceability framework that covers the entire transaction chain from trading and contract execution to deviation adjustment. Then, the model quantifies the life-cycle carbon intensities of thermal, wind, and photovoltaic generation units using life cycle assessment, replacing traditional average emission factors. Finally, the model apportions deviation electricity through power-flow tracing and settles the corresponding carbon emissions and green certificates for each user. Simulations on the IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate that the proposed model improves electricity-carbon traceability and settlement accuracy, while maintaining real-time balance between system-wide carbon emissions and load-side indirect emissions. Sensitivity analysis further validates the robustness of this model under different renewable energy penetration rates and renewable portfolio standard weight. Overall, this research offers a practical electricity-carbon collaborative management solution for the new-type power system, with implications for deeper integration of electricity and carbon markets.

title: Regulating CoOx/Ni inverse structure to enhance magnetocatalytic purification of VOCs emitted from intermittent sources
abstract: Catalytic oxidation is widely employed in volatile organic compounds (VOCs) degradation. The continuous optimization of catalytic oxidation technology encompasses the materials design and heat sources innovations. Herein, we found that adjusting the temperature and H2 treatment could regulate inverse structure of CoOx/Ni foam (CoOx/NF) monolithic catalysts, resulting in enhancement of oxygen vacancies generation. This promotional effect could be further amplified by electromagnetic induction heating (EMIH), which was probably ascribed to the acceleration of charge transfer across the inverse interface induced by alternating magnetic field. Consequently, CoOx/NF-300R, as an inverse catalyst synthesized under optimized conditions, could exhibit superior activity for catalytic oxidation of VOCs including benzene, toluene and o-xylene. The demanded temperature for removal of toluene in EMIH mode was reduced by approximately 50°C compared to that in traditional heating mode. Furthermore, the VOCs catalytic oxidation system composed of CoOx/NF-300R and electromagnetic induction could meet the requirements for rapid and efficient purification of multi-species and intermittent pollution sources.

title: Towards eco-friendly biofuel design: Atmospheric transformation and divergent ecological risk assessment of dimethylbutanol isomers
abstract: Branched saturated higher alcohols such as 3,3-dimethyl-1-butanol (3,3DM1ButOH) and 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol (3,3DM2ButOH) are promising oxygenated biofuel additives, yet their atmospheric transformation pathways and associated ecological risks remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrate density functional theory with multi-structural canonical variational transition state theory including small-curvature tunneling to elucidate the ·OH-initiated oxidation mechanisms and kinetics of both isomers over atmospherically relevant conditions. Four distinct H-abstraction channels are identified for each alcohol, with reactivity governed by hydroxyl position: the β-secondary H in 3,3DM1ButOH and the α-carbinol H in 3,3DM2ButOH dominate abstraction. At 298 K, computed total rate coefficients—5.29 × 10−12 cm3 molecule−1 s−1 (3,3DM1ButOH) and 1.07 × 10−11 cm3 molecule−1 s−1 (3,3DM2ButOH)—agree well with experimental data and reveal that 3,3DM2ButOH reacts nearly twice as fast due to its activated α-hydrogen. Subsequent peroxy radical (RO2·) chemistry is mapped under varying NOx regimes: RO2· + NO dominates in polluted environments, yielding multifunctional carbonyls (e.g., aldehydes, enols, ketones) and organic peroxynitrite (ROONO), while RO2· + HO2· and RO2· + RO2· pathways under low-NOx conditions produce hydroperoxides (ROOH) and dimeric products. Critically, environmental risk assessment using EPA-based toxicity models reveals divergent hazard trajectories: H-shift-driven autoxidation channels amplify developmental and aquatic toxicity, whereas radical termination via RO2· + HO2·/RO2· yields readily biodegradable, low-toxicity products. The RO2· + NO route exhibits mixed risk outcomes. Overall, low-NOx conditions mitigate integrated ecological risk despite comparable degradation rates. These findings bridge atmospheric chemical mechanisms with ecological risk assessment, providing a scientific foundation for the development of eco-friendlier biofuel additives with reduced environmental hazards.

title: Data-driven multi-ion synergistic regulation for cleaner copper electrorefining: Enhancing energy and resource efficiency
abstract: With intensified ore grade fluctuations, impurity interference in copper electrorefining has become a critical bottleneck hindering green and sustainable manufacturing. Traditional empirical diversion strategies fail to adapt to dynamic multi-ion fluctuations, leading to energy waste and quality risks. This study proposes a data-driven multi-ion synergistic regulation strategy assisted by a digital decision tool. By elucidating the coupling mechanisms among Cu, As, Sb, Bi, and Ni, this study established precise electrolyte concentration reference ranges and differentiated diversion logic for eight operational scenarios. Industrial validation confirms effective resolution of ion accumulation imbalance. Specifically, the fluctuation range of copper concentration was narrowed by 34.2 %, the arsenic over-limit rate dropped from 37.1 % to 25.6 %, and the nickel concentration decreased from 15.17 g/L to 10.64 g/L. Notably, the average cell voltage was reduced by 7.3 %, and the current efficiency was increased from 89.99 % to 90.90 %, yielding an additional output of 31,350 tons of cathode copper. The impurity content of cathode copper is significantly reduced, and the electricity consumption is cut by 28.5 kWh/ton of copper. Annual benefits include $ 1.028 million in electricity cost savings, $ 87,000 in environmental cost reduction, $ 504,000 in nickel resource revenue, and $ 4.138 million in additional processing income from increased production. This work provides a scalable, green, and intelligent paradigm for upgrading hydrometallurgical processes.

title: Techno-economic and risk-adjusted assessment of PV–wind–hydrogen hybrid energy systems in Morocco: Towards cost-effective low-carbon electricity supply
abstract: Hybrid renewable-energy systems integrating hydrogen storage offer a potential solution for reliable low-carbon electricity supply in regions with variable renewable resources. This study presents a TRNSYS-18-based techno-economic optimization and risk-adjusted assessment of a standalone hybrid renewable-energy system designed to supply a representative residential district in Dakhla, Morocco. Three configurations were evaluated under identical hourly operating conditions: wind–fuel cell–natural gas engine-generator (S1), photovoltaic–wind–fuel cell–natural gas engine-generator (S2), and photovoltaic–fuel cell–natural gas engine-generator (S3). The optimization considered capital, replacement, operation and maintenance, engineering, and fuel costs while enforcing a loss-of-power-supply probability below 0.5%. The results reveal a trade-off between economic performance and operational resilience. S3 achieved the lowest conventional baseline levelized cost of electricity, at 0.0362 USD/kWh, whereas S2 provided the strongest operational performance, with a renewable fraction of 70.25%, an NGG contribution of only 15.99%, and the most stable hydrogen-storage profile. S2 also avoided approximately 148.5 ktCO2 over the 20-year project lifetime. A financial de-risking package combining concessional debt, sovereign guarantees, standardized power-purchase agreements, streamlined permitting, and partial currency indexation reduced the post-tax weighted-average cost of capital from 9.6% to 6.6%. The corresponding post-de-risking adjusted LCOE values were 0.026, 0.032, and 0.027 USD/kWh for S1, S2, and S3, respectively. The framework demonstrates that financing conditions substantially influence HRES competitiveness and provides decision support for balancing cost minimization, renewable integration, and operational reliability in Morocco and comparable coastal regions.

title: Structuring co-creation for circular ecosystem emergence: The minimum viable circular ecosystem framework
abstract: Circular economy transitions require coordinated action among multiple interdependent actors across value chains. While research on circular ecosystems has expanded rapidly, two interrelated gaps persist: existing frameworks remain largely conceptual and provide limited process-level guidance for orchestrators, and the field lacks a theoretical account of how circular ecosystem emergence unfolds through co-creation; what orchestration activities are required at each stage and through what mechanisms they shape alignment and value creation outcomes. This study addresses both gaps by developing the Minimum Viable Circular Ecosystem (MVCE) framework through a design science research approach combining a literature synthesis, fifteen semi-structured expert interviews, and three multi-actor workshops conducted in the context of emerging reusable packaging ecosystems. The MVCE framework conceptualises circular ecosystem emergence as an iterative co-creation process unfolding through four interrelated phases: visioning, ecosystem framing, experimentation and learning, and structuring and governance, each operationalised through a dedicated boundary tool supporting collective sensemaking, ecosystem configuration, hypothesis-driven experimentation, and collaborative governance. While prior ecosystem frameworks address individual functions such as actor mapping, readiness assessment, or governance design in isolation, to our knowledge, prior frameworks have not integrated all four functions within a single co-creation process architecture operationalised through complementary boundary tools. The study advances four theoretical contributions: a theoretically grounded process framework for circular ecosystem emergence; the operationalisation of distributed orchestration through boundary objects; an account of value co-creation at the ecosystem emergence level; and a nascent design theory for circular ecosystem orchestration. Together, these contributions advance understanding of how circular ecosystems can be deliberately designed, aligned, and validated through structured co-creation.

title: Can digital transportation contribute to mitigating environmental pollution? Evidence from the Chinese Context
abstract: Digital transportation plays a crucial role in affecting environmental pollution. However, there remains limited research on the mechanism of digital transportation's impacts on environmental pollution. By acknowledging this research gap, this study examines the mechanism through designing and testing six research hypotheses. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) is employed to validate these hypotheses. The panel data used for analysis are from 30 Chinese provinces spanning the period from 2014 to 2023. The main findings include: (1) Digital transportation exerts total pollution emissions as it leads to population expansion; (2) Digital transportation contributes to the reduction of environmental pollution by three typical pathways: curbing excessive economic growth, stimulating technological innovation, and promoting the application of data flow; (3) The two pollution-reduction pathways of stimulating technological innovation and promoting the application of data flow are more influential in Western provinces, whereas curbing economic growth constitutes an effective pollution-reduction pathway only in Eastern and Central provinces. The findings suggest that region-specific policy strategies are needed to promote environmental sustainability during the development of digital transportation, across the dimensions of technological innovation and effective utilization of traffic data resources. This study provides valuable insights into mitigating environmental pollution through developing digital transportation.

title: AI-driven multi-objective decision framework for flare gas valorization pathway selection: Regional comparative analysis for Iran and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq
abstract: Flare gas valorization remains a major challenge in the oil and gas industry due to resource losses, greenhouse gas emissions, and the complexity of selecting appropriate utilization pathways under varying operational conditions. This study develops an AI-assisted, physics-grounded, and multi-criteria decision framework for intelligent selection of flare gas recovery technologies across diverse regional and operational scenarios. Six major pathways, including power generation, gas sweetening and sulfur recovery, gas reinjection, hydrogen production, methanol production, and mini-LNG, are evaluated using integrated techno-economic, environmental, feasibility, and risk criteria. A total of 300 representative scenarios were generated using Latin Hypercube Sampling for Iran-like, Iraq-like, and global conditions. The resulting dataset was used to train and compare four machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron, and Stacking Ensemble. The results demonstrate that gas reinjection and sulfur recovery are the dominant pathways under baseline conditions, accounting for 55.3% and 37.3% of optimal selections, respectively. Random Forest and Stacking Ensemble achieved the best classification performance with an accuracy of 86.7%. Sensitivity analysis revealed that environmental prioritization can alter pathway selection in 63.3% of scenarios, highlighting the importance of decision priorities in flare gas management. The proposed framework provides a transferable decision-support tool for region-specific flare gas valorization strategies and supports cleaner production by enabling region-specific low-emission flare gas utilization strategies.

title: Natural sciences for post-growth in practice: low-tech iron oxide reduction under a concentrated light flux using urine-derived ammonia and hydrogen as reducers
abstract: A telling example of the green growth sociotechnical imaginary in natural sciences is the future of ‘green’ steel production, envisaged to grow based on a hypothetical massive deployment of low-carbon electricity. In this article, we show how a post-growth, low-tech framework can open up new innovation pathways towards sustainable futures of ironmaking. The low-tech processes that we envision aim at converting iron oxide into iron using readily available and renewable sources of reducing agents and energy: ammonia and hydrogen from urine, and concentrated sunlight. In our study, a solar concentrator simulator and synthetic urea were used as models to assess two ways of generating ammonia from urea for iron oxide reduction: i) the pyrolysis of solid urea inside the reduction reactor under concentrated light flux, and ii) the biocatalysed hydrolysis of urea by addition of urease-rich plant seeds – like soybeans or watermelon seeds – to an aqueous solution of urea mimicking urine. During the reduction of iron oxide, in situ mass spectrometry confirmed the decomposition of ammonia into hydrogen in presence of iron species. X-ray diffraction analysis of the resulting samples showed that the reduction yield successfully reached 90–98%. The global level of production of iron of such a process would be limited by urine production; estimates are provided and discussed. Parting from the green growth imaginary, our interdisciplinary work aims at reintegrating chemical processes into natural cycles, independent from both electricity and fossil fuels, and also at participating in opening up research to more diverse visions of the future.

title: A low-energy natural carbonation pathway for fully recycled self-compacting concrete: mechanical performance and life-cycle carbon assessment
abstract: Decarbonizing concrete production while closing the construction-and-demolition-waste loop remains a central challenge for cleaner production in the built environment. This study develops a low-energy natural carbonation pathway in which recycled powder (RP), recycled fine aggregate (RFA), and recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) are CO2-mineralized under ambient conditions and then used to produce fully recycled self-compacting concrete (CFR-SCC), with RP partially replacing cement and carbonated RFA and RCA fully replacing natural aggregates. Natural carbonation reaches a degree comparable to accelerated carbonation within 28, 28, and 42 days for RP, RFA, and RCA, respectively, without direct chamber electricity, thermal input, or external concentrated CO2 supply. Although increasing replacement ratios generally reduce workability and mechanical performance, with RFA exerting a stronger adverse effect than RCA, carbonation treatment refines aggregate porosity and the interfacial transition zone through a dense surface CaCO3 layer, confirmed by X-CT and SEM, raising cube compressive and splitting tensile strengths by up to 13% and 7%. A code-based uniaxial stress-strain model calibrated for CFR-SCC reproduces the measured compressive behaviour with good accuracy. A cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment, with 1 m3 of C40 concrete as the functional unit, shows that CFR-SCC incorporating naturally carbonated recycled constituents lowers production-stage carbon emissions by approximately 17% relative to conventional concrete, of which 72% originates from cement replacement by RP and 28% from CO2 sequestration; natural carbonation further reduces emissions by about 5% compared with accelerated carbonation. The present study establishes an integrated framework that connects multi-constituent natural carbonation with fresh and mechanical performance, microstructural evolution, constitutive modelling, and cradle-to-gate carbon assessment, thereby supporting the cleaner production of fully recycled concrete.

title: Quantitative sustainability assessment of bioactive ingredients lipophilization
abstract: Bioactive compounds exhibit diverse biological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-microbial, photoprotective, and anti-aging effects, making them highly attractive ingredients in cosmetic formulations. However, despite their multifunctional potential, the practical application of many natural compounds is often limited by poor chemical stability, low aqueous or lipid solubility, and poor compatibility with formulation matrices. This work critically evaluates the sustainability of recent lipophilization (bio)catalytic strategies for the functional upgrading of bioactive compounds for cosmetic applications, especially those with antioxidant properties, with particular emphasis on reaction media design and materials efficiency. The analysis covers processes carried out in volatile organic solvents (VOSs), ionic liquids (ILs), deep eutectic solvents (DESs) and solvent-free media, including self-DES and “2-in-1” systems. Representative case studies are compared using a “gate-to-gate” sustainability assessment (comprising product synthesis and purification), or a strictly upstream analysis when the workup has not been addressed. A quantitative assessment was enabled by selected Green Metrics, CHEM21 solvent selection guide and the Modified Green Star Area. Results unveil the following rank of median Environmental factor values: organic solvents (72.6) > ILs (32.7) > DESs (7.0) > Solvent-free (4.6). These data underscore that non-reusable solvents are the main source of waste and carbon emissions, with product workup identifying as a critical bottleneck. Although product purity is vital for the cosmetic industry, this step is often neglected, creating a major gap in successful industrial scalability. To address this, solvent-free systems are crucial, as they facilitate the streamlined utilization of products with minimal environmental and health impacts.

title: Unravelling the atmospheric occurrence and partitioning of emerging PAH derivatives from the coking industry: Mechanistic insights into 9,10-anthraquinone formation
abstract: A typical coking plant (TCP) emits substantial quantities of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). However, the atmospheric behavior and formation mechanisms of their emerging derivatives remain unclear. Herein, we integrate field observations with theoretical analysis to elucidate their atmospheric occurrence and key formation pathways. Oxygenated PAHs in TCP were the dominant pollutants in PM2.5, with 9,10-anthraquinone being the predominant derivative, whereas heterocyclic and alkylated PAHs were the predominantly gaseous pollutants. The cold drum process was identified as the critical emission source, and pollution levels showed a negative correlation with distance from the TCP. Increased aromatic rings and carbonyl/quinone groups facilitated on-site accumulation. Partitioning model comparisons demonstrated that the D-E model and the steady-state N-S model outperformed traditional equilibrium models, highlighting soot-phase adsorption and non-equilibrium effects as the key mechanisms governing partitioning. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations confirmed that site-dependent kinetic advantages of ·OH-initiated oxidation and O2-addition are consistent with the high field concentrations and toxicity of 9,10-anthraquinone. Notably, NO acted as a crucial reactant, significantly promoting 9,10-anthraquinone formation. Therefore, future TCP management should prioritize the synergistic control of NO and parent PAHs. This study offers critical insights into the environmental behavior and control of emerging PAH derivatives.

title: Does repair improve environmental performance? Integrating temporal dynamics into environmental assessment of circular strategies
abstract: Growing electronic waste and rising demand for critical materials have intensified interest in circular economy strategies that keep products, components and materials in use for longer. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is the most widely used method for assessing environmental impacts, but it is a static methodology and does not inherently incorporate the timing of circular interventions. This is particularly relevant for time-sensitive products exposed to component failure, technological obsolescence or performance decline, where repair benefits can depend on when failure occurs during the product's service life. This study develops a time-explicit, LCIA-derived threshold metric to assess whether repair or replacement is environmentally preferable under different component-failure scenarios. The metric is demonstrated through a mobile device case study comparing replacement with battery, display and printed wiring board repair across selected LCIA impact categories. The results show that repair is not uniformly preferable: the threshold between repair and replacement depends on the environmental burden of the failed component repair, failure timing and the impact category assessed. Components with higher repair-to-product burden ratios reach the replacement-preferable threshold earlier in the product's service life, while lower ratios extend the range of service life in which repair remains environmentally preferable. The findings demonstrate that environmental assessments of circular strategies can produce oversimplified conclusions when failure timing is not represented explicitly. The proposed metric provides a transparent approach for incorporating temporal dynamics into repair-versus-replacement assessment for consumer electronics and may be extended to other time-sensitive product categories, such as electric mobility components and renewable energy technologies.

title: Blockchain enabled closed-loop supply chain for EV batteries with environmental tax and reward penalty policy
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created an urgent challenge. How to manage the growing number of retired batteries? If improperly discarded, these batteries pose serious environmental risks, but when recycled or reused they provide valuable raw materials and enable new energy storage applications. This study proposes a blockchain-enabled closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) model involving manufacturers, retailers, and echelon utilization firms. Blockchain ensures traceability and transparency, while government policies such as an environmental tax on new battery production and a reward-penalty for collection provide incentives for sustainable practices. A Stackelberg game framework is applied to analyze six decision-making scenarios. To demonstrate the practical relevance, a case analysis of the Tata Nexon EV Max battery is conducted. Results indicate that the scenario combining blockchain adoption, cost-sharing contracts, and echelon utilization (CBMRU) delivers the highest profitability, consumer trust, and environmental benefits. A sensitivity analysis further shows that blockchain cost, consumer responsiveness to transparency, and tax intensity significantly influence outcomes. Overall, this research integrates blockchain and government policy tools into a unified game-theoretic model. The findings highlight that coordinated adoption of digital traceability, cost-sharing, and effective recycling policies can build a profitable, transparent, and environmentally sustainable EV battery recycling system.

title: You can't improve what you don't measure: empirical evidence from Australian businesses around industrial decarbonisation
abstract: Industrial decarbonisation is central to achieving Net Zero emissions in manufacturing, and its success depends not only on technological implementation but also on firms’ ability to measure performance. Despite growing attention to sustainability reporting, little focus has been placed on measuring decarbonisation performance at firm level. To address this gap, this study develops a framework for assessing decarbonisation performance integrating Triple Bottom Line of sustainability, followed by an exploratory investigation among 217 Australian manufacturing firms in measuring their decarbonisation performance. Findings reveal significant gaps and uneven trends in current decarbonisation performance measurement practices. Of 49 indicators examined, 17 were not reported by respondents as being measured, mainly those related to pollution control, carbon pricing, and cost competitiveness. Moreover, the indicators not reported as being measured comprised 10 of the 25 economic indicators (40%), 5 of the 20 environmental indicators (25.0%), and 2 of the 4 social indicators (50%). In the investigated sample, larger firms omitted 51% of indicators compared to 36.7% in Small- and Medium-sized Enterprises. Sectoral analysis also showed comparatively high proportions of indicators not reported as being measured across food (65.3%), beverages (65.3%), wood (57.1%), chemicals (67.3%), machinery (63.2%), textiles (67.3%) and other industries including pulp & paper, fabricated metal products, and transport equipment (63.2%). This study finds that manufacturing firms do not comprehensively measure decarbonisation performance yet. Furthermore, noticeable differences were observed across firms, indicating uneven levels of engagement toward decarbonisation performance measurement practices. The findings suggest implications for policy and managerial practice, calling for a paradigm shift that embeds decarbonisation measurement within business strategy.

title: Towards sustainable land-use systems: Multiscale water-wetland-food trade-offs and governance pathways in China
abstract: Sustainable land-use systems require balancing water security, wetland conservation and food production under increasing pressures from agricultural intensification, urban expansion and climate change. This study develops an integrated water-wetland-food framework to assess ecosystem service trade-offs, synergies and governance pathways in China from 2000 to 2020. Water yield, flood regulation, leisure and recreation, and grain yield are quantified using multi-source spatial data and ecosystem service models. Trade-offs and synergies are examined across provincial, city, county and pixel scales, and interpretable machine learning and structural equation modelling to identify the key predictors, nonlinear responses, and structural pathways of individual ecosystem services. Results show that China's water-wetland-food system was spatially heterogeneous but temporally stable. Low-synergy areas covered nearly 80% of the country, while strong trade-off zones accounted for 30-50% across scales. Persistent conflicts were concentrated in major grain-producing regions, especially between wetland regulation or recreation services and agricultural production, whereas wetland-rich Yangtze River and coastal regions showed stronger multifunctional synergies. Scale aggregation amplified apparent synergies but concealed local conflict hotspots, indicating that coarse administrative assessments may underestimate ecological risks in intensive land-use regions. Climate conditions mainly controlled water and wetland services, while land-use intensity and vegetation conditions shaped grain production. Four functional governance zones were identified to support differentiated strategies, including water-resource constraints, wetland protection, high-standard farmland management, nature-based solutions and ecological compensation. This framework provides spatially explicit evidence for improving resource efficiency, ecological conservation and food security in sustainable land-use systems.

title: Experimental quantification of the competitive adsorption characteristics and flow dynamics of CO2/CH4/N2 mixtures in a coal seam
abstract: The injection of CO2 and/or N2 into coal seams represents an effective strategy for enhancing coalbed methane (CBM) recovery while achieving carbon sequestration. Understanding the competitive adsorption dynamics and flow kinetics among these gases is essential for optimizing engineering efficiency. In this work, well-designed experiments were conducted to quantify the competitive adsorption characteristics and flow dynamics of binary and ternary CO2/CH4/N2 mixtures in coal seams. Key parameters including concentration, flow rate, adsorption amount, effective diffusion coefficient, length of adsorption zone, and separation factor were evaluated. A novel concept, i.e., the competitive adsorption coefficient (CAC) is proposed to quantitatively analyze the competitive adsorption characteristics of binary and ternary gas mixtures in coal beds, enabling temporal quantification of competitive intensity. Due to differences in adsorption capacity, the outlet flow rate exhibits a “clumping” phenomenon. The CAC values for the ternary mixture follow N2 (0.909 × 10−4 Scm3·g/s2) > CH4 > CO2 (0.132 × 10−4 Scm3·g/s2), reflecting N2's high mobility and weak adsorption versus CO2's deep penetration and prolonged retention. The separation factor correlates positively with adsorption capacity, with CO2/CH4 reaching 6.95, higher than that (0.76) of N2/CH4. Competitive displacement in enhanced coalbed methane recovery is not an instantaneous equilibrium process but a time-dependent, diffusion-controlled transport phenomenon. The Bohart-Adams model further indicates the adsorption rate hierarchy: kS2-CO2 > kS1-CO2 > kT1-CO2. These microscopic kinetic insights provide a theoretical basis for designing efficient CBM recovery and secure CO2 storage strategies.

title: Cl−-mediated low-dose peroxymonosulfate activation for non-radical degradation of chloramphenicol
abstract: Peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation has been widely investigated using homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts, whereas the role of naturally occurring chloride in redirecting PMS oxidation chemistry under catalyst-free conditions, particularly in chloride-rich and high-salinity waters, remains poorly understood. This study constructed a Cl−-mediated PMS activation system (Cl−/TW/PMS) with tap water (TW) as the base medium, and then evaluated its ability to degrade chloramphenicol (CAP). Under optimized conditions of pH = 7.76, T = 30 °C, [PMS] = 0.07 g/L (low dosage) and [Cl−] = 400 mM, the Cl−/TW/PMS system achieved 97% CAP degradation efficiency within 60 min. Combining quenching experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical analysis and DFT calculations, mechanistic investigations demonstrated that background chloride fundamentally redirected PMS activation from conventional radical oxidation to a free-chlorine (ClO−)-dominated non-radical pathway. The process exhibited high tolerance towards common water constituents, including HCO3−, SO42− and humic acid. Toxicity prediction and E. coli growth assays consistently demonstrated a reduction in overall biological toxicity after treatment. Furthermore, validation across multiple real water matrices confirmed the robustness and applicability of CAP degradation. Notably, the presence of intrinsic chloride in saline waters can effectively activate PMS to facilitate catalyst-free CAP oxidation. This sheds light on the underlying mechanisms and demonstrates the potential of this chloride-enabled strategy for degrading antibiotics in highly saline aquatic environments.

title: Hydrothermal carbonization-induced ash chemistry reconstruction for mitigating slagging and refractory corrosion during co-gasification of biomass and coal
abstract: Co-gasification of biomass and coal serves as a crucial pathway for achieving carbon neutrality and efficient energy utilization. Nevertheless, the industrial scalability of this technology remains perennially challenged by accelerated slagging and severe refractory degradation, primarily driven by the high concentrations of alkali metals and chlorine in biomass feedstocks. This study proposes hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) pretreatment as an effective strategy to regulate the ash chemistry of biomass, and systematically evaluates its impact on slag rheological behavior and the corrosion resistance of high-chromium refractories. The results demonstrate that HTC pretreatment induces substantial de-alkalization and aluminum enrichment, achieving a K-removal efficiency of 67.1% and the near-total elimination of Cl. This promotes the transformation of ash minerals into a high-melting-point Al-Ca-Si system, thereby elevating the ash flow temperature by 180 °C. The extensive removal of network modifiers by HTC lowers the NBO/T of the SH-CS50 co-gasification slag from 0.571 to 0.186 in the SH-HTC50 system, shifting the slag dynamics from short slag to long slag. HTC facilitates the formation of an in situ passivation barrier at the interface, restricting the penetration depth of alkali vapors to within 50 μm. Simultaneously, liquid-phase corrosion is mitigated to a depth of less than 80 μm through a combination of high-viscosity rheological retardation and a dense protective layer. An NBO/T < 0.25 is identified as the critical threshold for inhibiting deep slag penetration and preserving the structural integrity of linings. This study provides both fundamental insights and practical guidance for enhancing the durability of refractories and promoting the long-term stable operation of industrial gasifiers in co-gasification systems.

title: Can highway-based photovoltaic power support electric road systems for heavy-duty trucks? Evidence from large-scale GPS data in China
abstract: Integrating roadside photovoltaic (PV) systems into electric road systems (ERS) presents a promising strategy for decarbonizing heavy-duty trucks (HDTs). Current literature, however, lacks high-resolution and nationwide evidence evaluating whether the highway-based PV generation can adequately meet HDT electricity demand, and how this supply-demand balance varies spatially. To bridge this gap, this study evaluates the spatial alignment between HDT electricity demand and highway PV generation potential across China. Using trajectory data from approximately 2.7 million HDTs, we estimate segment-level electricity demand and compare it with a conservative PV deployment scenario: assuming the PV panels are installed along 5-m-wide slopes on both sides of highways. Under this configuration, the total HDT electricity demand and PV potential during the study period reach 18.12 TWh and 9.97 TWh, respectively. Moreover, notable spatial mismatches were identified, with power-deficit segments accounting for 50.5% of total highway mileage but representing 90.5% of national HDT electricity demand, predominantly concentrate along the major freight corridors in Eastern and Northern China. Furthermore, the findings highlight a structural imbalance, where the high-demand regions face the most severe shortfalls, whereas the resource-abundant areas in the Northwest, Southwest, and South China consistently exhibit surpluses. Northwest China alone, particularly, contributes approximately 2.0 TWh of PV potential. Extreme deficits (supply-demand ratios <0.25) are widespread, while most surpluses are moderate (supply-demand ratios of 1-5). Notably, Xizang (Tibet) emerges as the only region to achieve complete network-wide self-sufficiency. These findings offer valuable insights for planning and optimizing the deployment of ERS across China's highway network.

title: Modeling and numerical study of hydrogen permeation characteristics coupled with agglomerate sub-model of catalyst layer in PEM water electrolyzers
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is a promising technology for renewable hydrogen production; however, hydrogen permeation remains a critical safety challenge. This study develops a three-dimensional hydrogen permeation model by coupling a macroscopic two-phase flow framework with an agglomerate catalyst layer (CL) sub-model, enabling explicit consideration of CL microstructure in hydrogen transport. The coupled framework links CL composition and microstructure to local hydrogen transport resistance, dissolved hydrogen accumulation, and ultimately membrane crossover through the coupled effects of liquid water, ionomer coverage, and catalyst agglomeration. Hydrogen permeation exhibits three distinct regimes with increasing current density. Initially, H2 in O2 vol% decreases rapidly due to oxygen dilution. Subsequently, hydrogen crossover approaches a quasi-steady state owing to the combined effects of cathode CL transport resistance and electro-osmotic drag (EOD). At high current densities, enhanced dissolved hydrogen accumulation in the cathode CL increases the concentration gradient across the membrane, accelerating hydrogen permeation. The cathodic CL composition is identified as the dominant factor governing hydrogen permeation, because variations in Pt loading, ionomer content, and Pt/C ratio simultaneously modify the local hydrogen transport resistance and dissolved hydrogen concentration within the agglomerate CL. Membrane thinning improves electrochemical performance but inevitably increases hydrogen crossover by shortening transport pathways. The coupled model provides mechanistic insights into how CL microstructure regulates hydrogen permeation and offers guidance for designing safer and more efficient PEMWE systems.

title: A government-anchored graph learning framework for predicting embodied carbon of construction materials in data-scarce regions
abstract: Embodied carbon assessment of construction materials is critical for achieving carbon neutrality, yet countries such as South Korea lack product-level life cycle inventory (LCI) databases despite having category-level government evaluation coefficients. This study proposes a government-anchored graph learning framework that combines cross-regional graph features with Korean government calibration coefficients to predict the carbon intensity of 39,372 Korean construction materials. A heterogeneous graph integrating 52,486 processes from five international LCI databases is constructed through cross-lingual semantic matching. A region-adaptive Graph Attention Network with gated feature bypass and domain adaptation transfers carbon knowledge from data-rich regions to the unlabeled Korean domain, while conformal prediction provides distribution-free prediction intervals with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. The model achieves R2 = 0.735 on the labeled test set (5-fold CV: 0.734 ± 0.027), and per-category calibration anchored to Korean Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) evaluation coefficients (KEITI) yields Spearman ρ = 0.878 (p < 0.001) against 18 Korean construction materials with a median absolute error of 24.5% and 66.7% of predictions within ±50% of government reference values. The calibration extends Korean government category-level coefficients to 39,372 product-level predictions. A counterfactual analysis separates the two roles: the KEITI anchors—not the choice of predictor—supply the absolute, region-specific scale and are the primary source of Korean-side accuracy, but government coefficients exist for only 11 of the 20 unified categories; the GNN supplies coverage and generalization, degrading gracefully on the 72.3% of Korean products that have no confident cross-database match, where retrieval-based alternatives collapse (R2 ≈ 0). A QR code-based feedback system with Bayesian corrections further improves EPD compliance from 66.7% to 83.3% with 33 field observations. The framework offers a practical complementary system for carbon-informed material selection in data-scarce markets where category-level government data exists but product-level assessments are unavailable.

title: Methanol vehicles with low PN23 emissions may still exhibit a potential SubPN23 particle burden
abstract: Particle number (PN) emissions from vehicle exhaust have increasingly become a target of pollutant control. However, current exhaust emission regulations mainly specify measurement procedures and limits for PN23 (particles with a diameter larger or equal to 23 nm), while no definitive PN10 (particles with a diameter larger or equal to 10 nm) emission limit has yet been established, particularly for hybrid and alternative-fuel vehicles. To address this gap, three vehicle categories of China 6 including the methanol-fueled internal combustion engine vehicle, methanol-fueled hybrid electric vehicle, and gasoline-fueled hybrid electric vehicle were tested to characterize their instantaneous and cycle-integrated PN10 and PN23 emissions. The results showed that the methanol-fueled internal combustion engine vehicle exhibited a relatively high fraction of SubPN23 (particles between 10 and 23 nm), with a maximum emission factor of 1.1 × 1011#/km. Within the tested vehicle fleet, hybrid powertrains showed potential to reduce the relative contribution of SubPN23, with the lowest SubPN23 fraction accounting for 14.39% of PN10 emissions under the investigated operating conditions. The instantaneous PN10 and PN23 emission factors exhibited coincident peaks, which occurred primarily during acceleration and rapid deceleration events, irrespective of vehicle category. These PN peaks generally occurred after fluctuations in the air–fuel ratio, suggesting that transient combustion instability may contribute to particle formation. The findings indicate that the use of fuels generally regarded as cleaner does not necessarily reduce emissions across all particle-size ranges and may, under certain operating conditions, increase the relative contribution of more harmful ultrafine particles.

title: Integrated digital framework for wastewater treatment performance and sustainability assessment in low-income countries
abstract: Modelling and simulation are widely used to optimise biological wastewater treatment processes, while life cycle assessment (LCA) is well established for evaluating environmental impacts. However, integrated modelling-LCA approaches have largely been developed for data-rich and well-resourced settings, limiting their practical application in developing countries where reliable operational data, technical capacity, and resources are often constrained. Moreover, few studies have demonstrated such integrated approaches using field-measured data and validated their recommendations through full-scale implementation. To address these gaps, an integrated digital framework linking metabolic activated sludge model (META-ASM) with LCA was developed and applied to optimise the Santa Catarina wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) in Cape Verde. The framework integrates systematic data collection and reconciliation, field-data-driven dynamic simulation, scenario-based optimisation, sensitivity analysis, and sustainability assessment. Model predictions were evaluated against observed plant performance, and operational and structural scenarios were sequentially assessed to identify improvements across individual treatment units. The recommended operational strategies were subsequently implemented at full scale, with field monitoring confirming reductions in effluent total chemical oxygen demand (COD Tot ), total suspended solids (TSS), total phosphorus (P Tot ), and total nitrogen (N Tot ) of 51.4%, 58.7%, 44.4%, and 21.5%, respectively, compared with baseline operation. LCA further demonstrated reductions of approximately 30% in human toxicity, freshwater ecotoxicity, and marine ecotoxicity, and 36% in eutrophication potential. Beyond improving treatment and environmental performance, the framework incorporates practical data-management tools, capacity building, and context-specific operational considerations. This field-validated, data-adaptive approach provides a scalable and transferable pathway for applying digital process modelling and sustainability assessment to WWTP optimisation in resource-constrained developing country contexts.

title: Carbon dot-modified CdS/Sporomusa ovata biohybrids for light-driven CO2 reduction to acetate
abstract: Carbon dioxide valorization is central to cleaner production and circular carbon utilization, yet its selective conversion into value-added chemicals under mild conditions remains technically challenging. Semiconductor-microbe biohybrid systems provide a solar-driven route that couples abiotic light harvesting with microbial carbon fixation, but their performance is often constrained by inefficient interfacial electron delivery and limited photosensitizer stability. Here, carbon dots (CDs) were coupled with CdS to construct a CdS/CDs/Sporomusa ovata biohybrid for light-driven CO2 reduction to acetate. The CDs broadened the visible-light response of CdS, improved the separation and lifetime of photogenerated charge carriers, and provided an electron-buffering interface that promoted electron availability to S. ovata. Under visible-light irradiation, the optimized CdS/CDs2/S. ovata hybrid yielded 1725 ± 84 mg L−1 acetate during continuous illumination, which increased to 2582 ± 116 mg L−1 under a simulated 12 h light/12 h dark cycle. The apparent quantum yield (AQY) for acetate production was calculated to be 11.37 ± 0.55%. Isotope tracking (13C-labeling) verified that the synthesized acetate originated exclusively from CO2/bicarbonate reduction. Transcriptomic analysis revealed the upregulation of genes associated with membrane-bound flavoproteins, cytochromes, hydrogenases, and the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, indicating enhanced electron uptake, reducing-equivalent regeneration and acetogenic carbon fixation. This work demonstrates that carbon-based interfacial engineering effectively stabilizes CdS-driven microbial photosynthesis, offering a mechanistic framework for advancing resource-efficient CO2-to-chemical technologies.

title: Trade-offs and coordinated management of water-energy-ecology-food nexus: A Stackelberg game-based bi-level decentralized stochastic programming method
abstract: Decision preferences at different hierarchical levels and multiple uncertainties pose substantial challenges to the coordinated management of the water-energy-ecology-food (WEEF) nexus. This study develops a Stackelberg game-based bi-level decentralized stochastic programming (SGBDSP) for planning WEEF nexus, which has advantages in making tradeoffs between different stakeholders in a two-level hierarchical framework and quantifying the joint risks of correlated random parameters. Then, the SGBDSP-WEEF model is formulated for the Jiziwan region in the Yellow River basin, where coupling coordination degree model is used to assess the coordination of the agricultural, energy and ecological subsystems, in order to identify coordinated strategies for regional sustainable development. Major findings are: (i) with the transition from conventional to clean energy, water consumption and carbon emissions of energy production would reduce by 30.87% and 40.38%, respectively; (ii) the highest water deficit would occur under L-L-L scenario (11.48 × 109 m3), unconventional water would alleviate water scarcity, but a 20.3% water shortage rate would remain; transferred water would further decrease the deficit by 1.73 × 109 m3, demonstrating the importance of diversified water supplies for regional water security and coordinated management of WEEF nexus; (iii) compared with 2024, as the utilization of unconventional and transferred water resources increased, the total water allocation would increase by 6.38%, while conventional water allocation would decrease by approximately 3.25 × 109 m3 by the end of the planning period (2036-2040); (iv) the highest coordination degree among agriculture, energy and ecosystems would be achieved under scenario 8 (with high water resource availability and agricultural water-demand uncertainty), reaching 0.90 (high-quality coordination). The results provide decision support for balancing trade-offs among different sectors and formulating coordinated strategies within the nexus system.

title: Nonlinear climatic controls and land-use modulations of net ecosystem productivity: Implications for regional carbon management
abstract: Under intensifying climate change and carbon neutrality goals, diagnosing the spatial heterogeneity and response complexity of terrestrial carbon sinks is critical for precise carbon-cycle modeling. However, the context-dependent and nonlinear responses of net ecosystem productivity (NEP) in topographically complex regions remain unclear. Taking the Yimeng Mountain Area as a representative case, this research developed an integrated framework to diagnose regional NEP dynamics, biophysical responses, and land-use-related effects. The results revealed a persistent enhancement in regional NEP from 2001 to 2020, with a mean of 205.21 g C m−2 a−1. Linear screening did not identify a single dominant linear factor across 67.01% of the area, highlighting spatial complexity and pervasive non-linearity of NEP responses in heterogeneous landscapes. Interpretable machine learning further identified potential evapotranspiration (PET) and soil moisture (SM) as key model-derived predictors, with clear thresholds: SM showed a transition from negative to positive ALE responses at approximately 0.21 m3 m−3, whereas PET shifted from positive to negative ALE effects at approximately 1480 mm. Furthermore, climatic sensitivities differed among land-use contexts: croplands showed earlier PET-related transitions, forests showed stronger precipitation-related responses, and grasslands were more closely linked to soil moisture, precipitation, and temperature. Attribution analysis indicated that the residual component accounted for an average of 16.06% in joint-promoting areas and 44.07% in joint-suppressing areas. This study presents a diagnostic framework for linking multiple dimensions of ecosystem carbon sequestration and provides spatially explicit, land-use-specific insights to support carbon-oriented environmental impact assessment and land-use planning.

title: Environmental impact of manufacturing and use of ceramic matrix composites for aerospace propulsion applications
abstract: Ceramic Matrix Composites (CMCs) have emerged as promising materials with exceptional mechanical properties, making them appealing for aerospace applications. Notable contenders among various CMC formulations, including Al 2 O 3 /SiO 2 , Al 2 O 3 /B4C, and SiC/SiC, show great potential for replacing traditional materials in the production of aircraft components, such as turbine blades. However, environmental evidence to support such substitution remains limited, and no consistent basis exists for comparing CMCs with established materials across their full life cycle. This paper presents a cradle-to-grave Life Cycle Assessment that compares five candidate blade materials under a common functional unit and a single blade geometry, so that differences in impact are attributable to the material and its manufacturing route. The study covers Al 2 O 3 /SiO 2 manufactured by sol-gel infiltration, Al 2 O 3 /B 4 C manufactured by sintering, and SiC/SiC manufactured by chemical vapour infiltration, pyrolysis of a preceramic polymer, or melt infiltration, alongside the nickel superalloys Inconel 625 and Hastelloy X manufactured by powder metallurgy. An aircraft turbine blade is selected as the case study, with material quantities defined from the blade design criteria and impacts assessed across the manufacturing, use, and end-of-life phases. Variation in the underlying inventory and operational assumptions is examined to test how firmly the comparison holds and which parameters drive it. The results provide a quantified basis for material and process selection in turbine blade design, identifying the life cycle stages and manufacturing parameters that govern the environmental performance of each option.

title: Hidden health burdens: The spatiotemporal trade-offs of China's passenger vehicle electrification
abstract: Passenger vehicle electrification is central to transport decarbonization, but its PM2.5-related health benefits depend on the timing of grid cleaning and the spatial transfer of electricity-generation emissions. This study develops a dynamic spatiotemporal framework for 30 provinces in China from 2023 to 2060, coupling fleet turnover, electricity-related emission transfer, reduced complexity air quality modelling, and PM2.5-related mortality assessment. We compare alternative electrification timelines with different power mix and end-of-pipe control scenarios. The results show that faster electrification consistently increases cumulative greenhouse gas mitigation, but health outcomes are conditional on grid cleaning. When electrification progresses faster than power-sector decarbonization and pollutant controls, additional electricity demand can shift emissions from roads to power generation and create short-to medium-term health burdens in some provinces. These burdens may persist for more than 16 years under some modelled scenarios. Snapshot year assessments can therefore obscure transitional health losses that are visible only in annual or cumulative transition analysis. The spatial pattern of health impacts is also uneven: provinces with cleaner electricity supply can gain health co-benefits earlier, whereas coal-dependent or electricity-supplying provinces may face delayed benefits or temporary health losses. These findings suggest that passenger vehicle electrification policies should be coordinated with power sector decarbonization, strict pollutant controls, and regional electricity-supply responsibilities.

title: Solid waste-derived biochar: An effective additive for enhancing CO2 absorption, suppressing NH3 slip, and saving energy in mild-temperature ammonia solutions
abstract: Ammonia-based CO2 capture is a promising technology due to the high absorption capacity and low regeneration energy consumption. However, its large-scale application is hindered by slow CO2 absorption rate, high ammonia loss, and large refrigeration investment (particularly in Chilled ammonia process (CAP)). To address these challenges, a low-cost functional additive was prepared by converting textile dyeing sludge and corncob into gradient porous biochar. Under optimal conditions, the addition of biochar produced at 800 °C (SC800) increased CO2 uptake by 3.88% to 5.82% and decreased ammonia slip by 46.52% to 79.54% compared with the ammonia solution alone. The optimal operation temperature of the modified absorption system was elevated to 25 °C, which could potentially reduce the energy consumption by 0.010–0.138 GJ/t CO2 captured compared to CAP. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation indicated that the biochar promoted diffusion and mass transport of CO2 and NH3 molecules within the pore channels. Correlation analysis revealed that biochars with higher mesopore volume and quaternary nitrogen content, together with lower pyrrolic nitrogen content, exhibited better performance on CO2 absorption enhancement and NH3 slip inhibition. The absorption–desorption cycling experiments further demonstrated the potential of SC800 for practical CO2 capture applications, with only a 5.16% decreased in CO2 uptake and an 11.60% increase in NH3 slip after 5 cycles. Furthermore, the resulting mixture of biochar and fine NH4HCO3 crystals showed potential as a nitrogen-stabilized fertilizer. This work provides a sustainable route for converting solid wastes into high-value additives for more efficient and flexible ammonia-based CO2 capture.

title: Shifting carbon-water coupling: spatiotemporal strengthening of positive water use efficiency responses to greening in China
abstract: Large-scale ecological restoration in China has profoundly altered carbon-water coupling dynamics, necessitating a precise assessment of ecosystem adaptive changes. To address this, we developed a spatial response model integrated with multi-scenario land surface model simulations to quantify the spatiotemporal sensitivity and response of water use efficiency (WUE) to Leaf Area Index (LAI) and its underlying drivers. Our results revealed that high sensitivity of WUE to LAI was predominantly observed in arid and semi-arid regions, exhibiting a decreasing trend as aridity diminished. This sensitivity was most pronounced in grasslands (0.27 ± 0.08 gCm−2mm−1). Since 2000, WUE has exhibited a sustained positive response to vegetation greening. The spatial extent of this positive response has expanded by 14.81% compared to the pre-2000 period. However, significant spatial heterogeneity persists; specifically, the enhancement of the positive response was most pronounced in forest ecosystems, whereas the change in response was comparatively modest in grassland ecosystems. Concurrently, the response threshold of WUE to LAI shifted from 1.05 ± 0.13 10−3m2m−2 to 1.21 ± 0.10 10−3m2m−2. Attribution analysis revealed that among LAI components driven by CO2 concentration, climate change, and land cover change, the component driven by CO2 concentration exerted the most significant effect on WUE. The increase in WUE was primarily driven by enhanced carbon uptake, which exceeded the concurrent changes in evapotranspiration. Furthermore, ecological restoration projects were found to facilitate the positive response of WUE to LAI. The spatiotemporal response results of WUE to greening are critical for determining whether carbon-water coupling acts synergistically or competitively across distinct environmental gradients. Therefore, incorporating the response of carbon-water coupling into ecological restoration and environmental assessment frameworks is essential for ensuring the sustainability of ecological restoration efforts and regional water security.

title: Pulsed electric field pretreatment enhances anaerobic digestion of cashew apple bagasse by increasing methane yield and energy recovery
abstract: To avoid the high energy demand and inhibitory compounds associated with conventional methods, pulsed electric field (PEF) pretreatment was investigated as a low-energy strategy to enhance the anaerobic digestion (AD) of cashew apple bagasse, a lignocellulosic residue with limited biodegradability. Two stirred tank reactors (4.3 L) were operated for 42 days under mesophilic conditions (36 °C) with a hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 25.8 days: a control reactor fed with untreated bagasse and a PEF reactor initially fed with PEF-pretreated biomass. During the semi-continuous phase, both reactors were subsequently fed with untreated bagasse. PEF processing promoted complete cell disintegration (Z = 1) and induced structural modifications, as indicated by Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), thereby enhancing substrate accessibility by disrupting the fibers' physical barriers and significantly increasing the available surface area for AD. As a result, cumulative biogas production in the PEF reactor increased by 37.67% compared to the control (75.47 L vs. 54.82 L), while methane yield increased by 22.01%, reaching 235.23 L CH 4 per kg of volatile solids. The methane concentration in the biogas remained similar (∼70%) in both reactors, suggesting that PEF primarily enhanced hydrolysis efficiency rather than altering methanogenic pathways. Dynamic volatile fatty acids (VFA) monitoring showed PEF accelerated intermediate consumption, especially of butyric acid. The system maintained low propionic/acetic acid ratios (≤0.37), ensuring stability without toxicity and enhancing methanogenic activity. Despite the additional energy input required for PEF pretreatment (22.52 kJ per kg), the overall energy balance remained positive, resulting in higher net electricity (70.55 kWh per t) and heat (634.91 MJ per t) generation. Greenhouse gas mitigation increased to 38.27 kg CO 2 -eq per t of biomass in the PEF scenario. A preliminary techno-economic assessment estimated that PEF integration could double annual cash flow and reduce the estimated payback period from 6.7 to 3.3 years under the evaluated assumptions. A univariate sensitivity analysis (±30%) shows that both configurations are sensitive to changes in heat prices, but the PEF scenario offers greater economic stability, with a payback period of 5.1 years even under a 30% drop in thermal energy prices. These results indicate that PEF is an effective pretreatment for improving methane production, energy recovery, and the sustainability of AD of cashew apple bagasse.

title: Verification-aware sustainable sourcing under carbon border costs, digital product passports, and greenwashing risk
abstract: Carbon border charges and product-level sustainability records make the credibility of supplier information an operational concern. This study develops a verification-aware sourcing framework in which a buyer updates supplier beliefs, allocates orders subject to capacity and service considerations, and assigns a common verification budget to audits and Digital Product Passport (DPP) records. A conceptual network value function links multi-tier operational considerations to a tractable supplier-allocation problem, while the simulation focuses on the reduced supplier-allocation layer. The analysis identifies the value of more informative signals and a truthful-reporting region. Under convex costs, concave detection, and Slater feasibility, it also provides globally sufficient Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) tests for an interior audit–DPP mix or a single-tool boundary solution. A redesigned computational study uses 100 paired stochastic replications, equal verification expenditure, common random numbers, ablations, and sensitivity analysis. In the baseline, integrated verification lowers mean loss, true emissions, disclosure bias, and high-opacity sourcing. The mechanism test shows, however, that most of this advantage is conditional on verification being coupled with supplier remediation and development. The information-only advantage is small. Period-level tail loss and cumulative tail loss are reported separately. The results provide internally reproducible mechanism evidence in a synthetic, reduced-form setting; empirical generalization requires sector-specific calibration and richer regulatory mapping.

title: Climate stress and transboundary water governance: Evidence from global water conflict and cooperation networks
abstract: Climate change can intensify conflict over shared water resources while also creating incentives for cooperation. This study examines how chronic climate stress and acute climate shocks are associated with divergent transboundary water outcomes and how governance capacity conditions these relationships. We construct annual cooperation and conflict networks among 149 riparian states from 1995 to 2023 using global treaty and water-event data and estimate temporal exponential random graph models.
