The results show that chronic water-supply stress is positively associated with conflict, whereas drought and flood shocks are positively associated with cooperation. Stronger governance capacity is associated with less conflict and more cooperation and strengthens the positive relationship between acute shocks and cooperation. Governance-capacity gaps reduce both cooperative and observable conflict ties, suggesting institutional disconnection; however, these gaps amplify the positive relationship between chronic stress and conflict. Both networks also exhibit strong temporal dependence. These findings demonstrate that climate stress does not have uniform implications for transboundary water interactions, as its consequences depend on the type of stress and the level and compatibility of governance capacity. The study provides empirical evidence for developing climate-responsive institutions, strengthening governance capacity, and promoting cross-border coordination under SDG 6.5.2.

title: Unlocking the main and interactive impacts of driving factors on urban eco-environmental quality from the perspective of local climate zones
abstract: Urbanization is a major driver of environmental change, exacerbating climate-related impacts and contributing to the degradation in the urban eco-environmental quality (UEQ). Although numerous studies have assessed UEQ and its drivers, most existing studies have focused on the macro scale, with limited exploration of the driving factors of UEQ at meso- and micro-scales, particularly from different local climate zones (LCZ), hindering the development of targeted UEQ improvement strategies for different LCZ types. Here, we integrate the LCZ framework with the XGBoost machine learning algorithm and SHAP to identify and interpret key factors shaping UEQ in Taipei, China. The results indicate that vegetation structural parameters and landscape pattern indices consistently exert strong influences on UEQ across different LCZ types. SHAP dependence plots further reveals significant and positive contributions from fractional vegetation cover, largest patch index, vegetation height, elevation, and building height. Conversely, floor area ratio and building density (BD) show negative impacts on UEQ, and both exhibit a threshold effect. Specifically, BD enhances UEQ below 0.4 but diminishes it beyond this value. Moreover, the interaction effects among the key indicators indicate that the combined influence of fractional vegetation cover, largest patch index and vegetation height contributes the most significantly to the improvement of UEQ. These findings offer practical guidance for designing LCZ-specific urban planning strategies to improve UEQ in cities facing climate and environmental challenges.

title: Sustainable food supply chains under multi-resource boundaries: Cross-basin resource mismatches and environmental inequities associated with physical water transfers and agricultural trade
abstract: Modern anthropogenic interventions have fundamentally reconfigured food supply chains. While large-scale physical water transfers are engineered to alleviate regional water scarcity, agricultural trade embodied in food systems often induces reverse flows, creating a profound socio-ecological paradox. However, how these interconnected physical and virtual water flows trigger cross-basin multi-resource mismatches and spatial inequities remains largely unclear. Taking the Yangtze and Yellow River Basins in China as the study area, we develop a telecoupling analytical framework to evaluate the sustainability of food supply chains under water-land-food-carbon (WLFC) constraints from 2000 to 2023. By integrating network analysis, environmental footprint accounting, and the XGBoost-SHAP model, we systematically identify resource mismatches, trade-offs and synergies, spatial spillovers, and nonlinear driving mechanisms across the dual basins. The results capture a progressive increase in the sustainability of food supply chains in the Yangtze and Yellow River Basins, with average annual growth rates of 2.10% and 2.23%, respectively. However, their transition pathways differ markedly. The Yangtze River Basin shows relatively coordinated improvement, driven by increases in grain production (2.98%) and water productivity (1.79%), whereas the Yellow River Basin faces a structural mismatch between agricultural expansion (3.7%) and rigid water constraints (0.9%). Cross-basin analysis further reveals that agricultural trade generates 9.73 billion m3 of virtual water flows and 1.37 million tons CO2e of embodied greenhouse gas emissions in 2023, intensifying spatial inequities and responsibility mismatches between the two basins. Furthermore, the XGBoost-SHAP model demonstrates that socio-economic factors contribute 70%-91% to the sustainability of food supply chains, exhibiting significant non-linear threshold effects. These findings demonstrate that building sustainable food supply chains under changing environments requires a paradigm shift from localized infrastructure management to telecoupling multi-resource governance.

title: Environmental and Economic Life Cycle Assessment of low-tech digesters coupled with gasification technology implemented in a small-scale dairy farm
abstract: Improving organic waste management while strengthening the circular bioeconomy and providing clean energy remains a key challenge for small-scale farms in low- and middle-income countries. This study assessed the potential environmental and economic impacts of low-tech digesters coupled with gasification technology in a small-scale farm producing dairy products in Colombia, using the Life Cycle Assessment and the Life Cycle Costing tools. Three scenarios were considered: i) a baseline scenario based on conventional waste management and fossil energy use, ii) a scenario with a low-tech digester, and iii) a scenario with a digester coupled with a gasifier. The selected functional unit was 1 kg of produced cheese. The system boundaries (i.e. cradle to grave) included the emissions associated with waste management, the construction and operation of the low-tech digester and gasifier, and the use of fuels, synthetic fertilisers and/or digestate in agriculture. The results showed that adopting low-tech digesters to co-digest cattle manure with waste generated from dairy processing (i.e. cheese whey) reduced the environmental impacts associated with eutrophication, climate change and fossil resource scarcity (up to 17% reduction compared to the baseline scenario). Moreover, coupling the digester with gasification further increased bioenergy production and completely replaced fossil fuel consumption. From an economic point of view, the synergies between low-tech digesters and gasification technology reduced the total costs associated with cheese production by 56% compared to the baseline scenario. Overall, the study demonstrated the potential of decentralised, low-tech bioenergy solutions to support circular bioeconomy and sustainability in small-scale dairy farms in low-income countries.

title: Optimization of multi-product and multi-period natural gas logistics network under multimodal transport
abstract: The natural gas logistics network plays a vital role in modern energy systems. Its effective coordination and optimization are essential for reducing costs, improving transportation efficiency, enhancing supply flexibility, and promoting emission reduction. However, the coexistence and conversion among multiple product types, such as liquefied natural gas (LNG), pipeline natural gas (PNG), and compressed natural gas (CNG), introduce complex multimodal transportation scenarios, posing significant challenges to the integrated optimization of the logistics network. To address this, the present study develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model tailored for a multi-product, multi-period natural gas logistics network under multimodal transportation modes. The proposed model covers the entire supply chain, from resource extraction to end-user consumption, while accounting for key operational constraints in production, transportation, storage, and sales. It aims to optimize operational strategies across time periods to maximize net profit. To demonstrate the model's practical applicability, a coastal city cluster in China is used as a case study, identifying optimal strategies in infrastructure construction, production scheduling, LNG procurement, product conversion, transport routing, and peak-shaving system deployment. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted to explore the impacts of product type, gas field extraction strategy, user supply method, and LNG sales price on overall system performance. Results show that the MILP-based model effectively integrates multiple decision dimensions and offers valuable support for enhancing energy efficiency and promoting more sustainable practices within natural gas supply chains.

title: An integrated machine learning and MATLAB/Simulink framework for enhanced photovoltaic power forecasting and grid integration
abstract: The rapid integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into modern power grids requires energy forecasting approaches that are both statistically accurate and physically consistent. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines machine–learning–based prediction with physics-based validation in MATLAB/Simulink. The key contribution is a two-layer validation workflow in which data-driven ensemble forecasts are evaluated against a grid-connected PV simulation model to assess their physical feasibility under realistic operating conditions. The proposed framework employs a stacking ensemble that integrates complementary tree-based and neural-network-based learners and is evaluated across multiple datasets, including reanalysis-based meteorological data and field-measured PV outputs. Results show that the stacking ensemble achieves an RMSE of 0.022, MAE of 0.011, and R2 of 0.996 on the reanalysis-based dataset (MERRA-2). On real-world (Northern Hemisphere) PV data, the model achieves an RMSE of 4.7211 W, MAE of 3.5061 W, and R2 of 0.5612, while independent meteorological data (NSRDB) yield an RMSE of 0.0554 W, MAE of 0.0297 W, and R2 of 0.9815, demonstrating competitive performance across different operating conditions. Statistical comparisons indicate that the ensemble achieves significant improvements in MAE relative to benchmark models in selected datasets while remaining competitive on RMSE. To enhance interpretability, LIME-based analysis is used to quantify the influence of meteorological features, and ablation studies are conducted to assess the contribution and robustness of the ensemble architecture. Physics-based validation using a 10-kW grid-connected Simulink model demonstrates that the predicted power trajectories are consistent with converter dynamics and operational constraints, with an average deviation of approximately 3% and an RMSE of 0.182 kW between the machine-learning predictions and simulation outputs. Additional validation using reanalysis data from Tamil Nadu indicates promising generalization, although evaluation remains limited to specific sites and conditions. Long-term forecasting that incorporates degradation effects is also explored to extend the framework for planning applications. Overall, the proposed approach provides a structured pathway for integrating data-driven forecasting with engineering validation, enabling more reliable renewable energy integration, improved energy management, and resource-efficient grid operations that support the transition toward cleaner electricity production.

title: A predictive cruise eco-driving control strategy for connected autonomous vehicles through successive signalized intersections in mixed urban traffic flow
abstract: Connected autonomous vehicles can use vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication for energy-efficient driving. However, in urban mixed traffic involving both autonomous and human-driven vehicles, driver uncertainty and the spatio-temporal coupling of consecutive traffic signals significantly increase the complexity of eco-driving control. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hierarchical green-wave speed-based predictive eco-driving strategy for connected autonomous vehicles at successive signalized intersections, enabled by cloud-to-vehicle coordination. The upper cloud layer performs green-wave speed planning in the distance domain using direct projection algorithms to handle spatio-temporal constraints across multiple intersections. The lower vehicle layer integrates an Informer network-based speed prediction model to mitigate disturbances from surrounding traffic and refine the planned trajectory in real time. Furthermore, a speed-tracking controller based on the Pontryagin maximum principle and a binary search method is designed to achieve smooth, energy-efficient tracking performance. Simulation experiments on a Speedgoat platform demonstrate the feasibility and superior energy-saving performance of the proposed control strategy under mixed-traffic conditions.

title: Multi-stage low-carbon planning of hydrogen-based multi-energy microgrids with multiple hydrogen pathways and hybrid uncertainties
abstract: Driven by the dual forces of carbon reduction policies and hydrogen energy development, hydrogen-based multi-energy microgrids (H-MEMGs) are emerging as a promising solution for enhancing sustainability and facilitating hydrogen integration. However, existing planning methods predominantly focus on an idealized future dominated by green hydrogen while overlooking the practical need for a balanced selection of diverse hydrogen production technologies in real-world applications. Moreover, they fail to comprehensively address uncertainties across multiple planning stages, particularly the distinct impacts of short-term operational variability and long-term policy evolution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-stage low-carbon planning framework for H-MEMGs considering multiple hydrogen production technologies and hybrid uncertainty risks. The proposed framework enables the endogenous selection and capacity expansion of gray hydrogen, blue hydrogen, and green hydrogen technologies across multiple planning stages, while coordinating renewable generation and energy storage resources. To address uncertainties with different temporal characteristics, a Wasserstein-based distributionally robust joint chance constraint is employed to capture short-term renewable generation uncertainty, and information gap decision theory is integrated to quantify the robustness of planning decisions against long-term decarbonization pathway deviations. Furthermore, a tailored bilinear Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to efficiently solve the resulting mixed-integer optimization problem. Numerical case studies demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reduce carbon emissions by approximately 26.9% compared with the carbon-unconstrained benchmark, while enabling adaptive hydrogen production technology selection under evolving carbon emission restrictions. Compared with fixed hydrogen production pathways, the proposed framework achieves a maximum cost saving of 14.2%, thereby establishing a better trade-off between economic efficiency and emission reduction. Additionally, it enhances the robustness and adaptability of planning decisions by proactively managing uncertainties across different time scales. The results also show that the proposed algorithm significantly improves computational efficiency, reducing the computation time by 39.3% for the small-scale case while ensuring stable solutions for larger-scale planning instances.

title: Organic vs. conventional wine production: a comparative multi-year environmental LCA study in central Italy
abstract: Comparative assessments of organic and conventional wine have reported divergent results and are largely based on single production years. This study evaluates and compares the environmental impacts of a 0.75 L bottle of conventional and of organic wine over three consecutive years. Using Life Cycle Assessment, the analysis covers all phases from raw material production to the farm gate. Primary data were collected from an Italian winery for 2022–2024, years with different climatic conditions, levels of field operations and grape yields. On average, the organic bottle shows higher impacts than the conventional one in 14 out of 18 impact categories considered. Differences are modest but systematic and mainly reflect more field operations, higher diesel use and lower yields in the organic vineyard. In both systems, glass bottle production is the dominant hotspot in most of the impact categories. Organic viticulture shows a clear advantage in terrestrial ecotoxicity, due to the absence of specific synthetic fungicides. For marine ecotoxicity and human non-carcinogenic toxicity, differences are marginal, indicating broadly comparable performance. The comparison further shows that the gap between systems varies with climatic conditions, input profiles and yields, with rainier years associated with more field operations but not necessarily with higher impacts when management is adjusted. Overall, neither production system is environmentally superior across all impact categories. Organic management improves toxicity-related indicators but performs worse in climate- and resource-related categories, while conventional management shows the opposite pattern, highlighting the value of multi-year, multi-indicator LCAs to capture trade-offs in viticulture.

title: Construction of a promising self-sedimenting industrial chassis strain EGMS of Euglena gracilis with high paramylon yield via EMS mutagenesis combined with dark-heterotrophic screening
abstract: The commercial production of paramylon, a high-value β-1,3-glucan from Euglena gracilis, is hindered by the growth-production trade-off and high harvesting costs. Here, we established a high-paramylon-yield mutant, E. gracilis mutant sedimentation (EGMS), via EMS mutagenesis coupled with label-free “dark-heterotrophic” morphological screening. Under heterotrophic conditions, EGMS exhibited enhanced biomass accumulation under non-starvation conditions, achieving a 39.70% higher specific growth rate and a maximum dry cell weight of 1.62 g/L, alongside consistently elevated paramylon content. Uniquely, increased intracellular granule accumulation and cellular structural remodeling were associated with a transition toward a spherical morphology with enhanced sedimentation properties. This self-sedimenting trait increased harvesting efficiency by 118.9%, potentially alleviating downstream processing challenges. The proposed “Push-and-Pull” model was associated with enhanced carbohydrate metabolism, paramylon biosynthesis-related transcriptional changes, and reduced lipid-associated pathways. Crucially, multi-omics analysis suggested a “dual-blockade” mechanism involving reduced lipid-associated metabolism: MYB-related transcriptional changes were associated with reduced expression of fatty acid synthesis-related genes, while additional lipid-associated regulatory changes were observed. Strong suppression of sulfur assimilation-associated genes (Cysteine synthase K, CysK, −21.87-fold) suggested altered sulfur metabolism associated with lipid regulation. Collectively, EGMS represents a metabolically remodeled and promising industrial chassis that improves both production and harvesting characteristics, offering a potential platform for efficient paramylon biomanufacturing.

title: Comprehensiveness or equalization? Rethinking urban-rural integration through a dual-dimension framework and its sustainable development implications in Northeast China
abstract: Urban-rural integration (URI) is critical for improving urban-rural relations and advancing regional sustainable development. However, defining and assessing URI remain challenging, and its sustainable development implications, particularly regarding specific sustainable development goals (SDGs), remain insufficiently articulated. This study distinguishes Urban-Rural Comprehensive Development (URCD) and Urban-Rural Equalized Development (URED) as two analytically distinct dimensions of URI, operationalized through the production, living, and ecological functions of urban-rural systems. Across prefecture-level cities in Northeast China (2000–2020), it examines their spatiotemporal evolution, barrier factors and interactions, and differentiated SDG profiles. The results reveal that: (1) URI exhibited a consistent upward trend, yet URCD and URED followed divergent trajectories — URCD rose from a level well below URED, increasing by 89%, while URED grew by only 0.99% — producing a characteristic V-shaped gap. Functional contributions followed the order EF > LF > PF across both dimensions. Spatially, core cities led in comprehensive prosperity but lagged in equalization, while peripheral cities displayed the opposite pattern. (2) Barrier factors constraining URI comprised enhancing, attenuating, and volatilizing types, with enhancing and attenuating factors counterbalancing each other and volatilizing factors modulating their dynamics. Factor interactions were predominantly bivariate-enhancing. URCD constraints exhibited pronounced functional differentiation, whereas URED constraints remained diffusely distributed across all functions. (3) SDG decomposition yielded contrasting structural profiles across both URI dimensions — divergent, with economic targets exceeding ecological and governance targets, under URCD and balanced but level-limited under URED — with synergistic intensity declining under both. These findings offer a dual-dimension perspective for understanding urban-rural integration and its sustainable development implications in analogous regions.

title: A thermodynamic framework linking phase assemblage to mix design optimization in mineral admixture-modified magnesium oxychloride cement
abstract: Magnesium oxychloride cement (MOC) has attracted considerable attention owing to its low CO2 footprint. However, the coupled effects of mix proportion and the type and dosage of mineral admixtures (MAs) on the phase assemblage and performance of MOC remain unclear. Moreover, owing to the lack of an internally consistent thermodynamic database for MgO-MgCl2-H2O-MA systems, these coupled effects have not been systematically elucidated from a thermodynamic perspective. To address this gap, we develop a self-consistent thermodynamic database and integrate it into a thermodynamic framework for predicting phase assemblages in hardened MOC pastes. The predictions are validated against literature-reported and newly obtained XRD data. Results show that active MAs, including silica fume, fly ash, slag, metakaolin, and carbide slag, chemically interact with MOC and promote M-(A-)S-H formation, whereas C-(A-)S-H formation is not observed within the investigated compositional range. In contrast, inert MAs (CaCO3 and CaSO4·2H2O) mainly act as microstructural densifiers without altering the hydration products. Coupling the predicted phase assemblages with the gel-space ratio captures the overall trend in literature-reported compressive strength. Further analysis of composite modification combining silica fume with chemical modifiers (citric acid, H3PO4, KH2PO4, and FeSO4) indicates that such modifiers do not introduce new solid phases. By integrating the calculated gel-space ratio with reported trends in water resistance and setting time, the analysis suggests a potentially favorable design range of nα-MgO/nMgCl2 = 9-12, ∼30 wt% MA, and ∼1 wt% chemical modifier. The framework provides mechanistic insights into MOC phase evolution and qualitative guidance for performance-oriented mix design.

title: Emission forecasting based spatial-temporal carbon response: A multi-agent attention-enhanced deep learning framework
abstract: As a major contributor to carbon emissions, the decarbonization of power systems has garnered significant societal attention. Nodal carbon intensity (NCI), a critical factor in carbon-oriented demand response, has traditionally been determined through ex-post calculations. However, this ex-post approach introduces latency in low-carbon dispatch. To address this, this paper presents a proactive ex-ante spatial-temporal carbon response framework. At its core, we develop a novel deep learning-based hierarchical design, enhanced by a dual-stage attention mechanism and a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent cooperation system, to accurately forecast day-ahead NCI. This design effectively mitigates the impact of renewable energy uncertainty and enhances predictive resilience. On the demand side, the framework proposes a spatial-temporal carbon scheduling model that integrates geographically dispatchable loads (GDLs), including mobile energy storage systems (MESSs) and distributed data centers (DDCs). Leveraging high-accuracy day-ahead NCI predictions, the framework can effectively reduce system emissions by quickly responding to carbon intensity fluctuations. The proposed framework is tested on the modified IEEE 33-bus system. According to the simulation results, the impacts of proposed framework on dispatching latency and emission outcomes are analyzed. The results demonstrate that under a one-hour reduction in carbon scheduling latency, the proposed model and methodology can achieve over 30% emission reduction. This research breaks through the limitations of passive carbon accounting, advancing toward proactive carbon management. It offers an intelligent solution that accelerates the transition to cleaner power systems while directly supporting sustainable production goals.

title: Multi-objective evaluation of CO2-ECBM operating conditions in deep low-permeability coal reservoirs: Trade-offs among CH4 recovery, CO2 storage, and permeability preservation
abstract: CO2-enhanced coalbed methane recovery (CO2-ECBM) can couple methane production with CO2 storage, but its application in deep low-permeability coal reservoirs is constrained by trade-offs among CH4 recovery, CO2 storage, and permeability preservation. This study adopts a multicomponent dual-porosity numerical framework coupling CH4–CO2 competitive adsorption, diffusion-controlled matrix–fracture transfer, gas–water flow, and effective-stress- and adsorption-strain-dependent permeability evolution. A multi-objective evaluation framework integrating CH4 production enhancement, cumulative CO2 storage, simulation-period CO2 retention efficiency, incremental CH4 production per unit CO2 stored, and profile-averaged permeability retention was established using hierarchical weighting, TOPSIS, and weight-sensitivity analysis. The results show that, under the base CO2-ECBM case, cumulative CH4 production increased by 30.4% relative to primary CBM recovery, while 4.03 × 106 m3 of CO2 was retained with an efficiency of 98.8%. Increasing injection pressure or rate enhanced absolute CH4 recovery and CO2 storage, but produced diminishing marginal gains and, at higher intensities, lower CO2 retention efficiency and poorer permeability preservation. Multi-objective ranking identified 16 MPa as a robust preferred pressure within the tested range, whereas 50–60 t/d formed a competitive preferred rate interval, with 60 t/d ranking first under the baseline weights. Model reliability was further assessed against published permeability experiments, yielding a mean absolute percentage deviation of 4.93% and an RMSE of 0.048. These results support coordinated and adaptive CO2-ECBM operation that balances recovery, storage, and reservoir flow-capacity preservation rather than maximizing injection intensity alone.

title: Recycling Ti6Al4V machining chips into powder for aerospace additive manufacturing: Environmental impacts and market dynamics
abstract: Titanium's high specific strength and corrosion resistance make it critical in aerospace applications, yet its soaring powder costs cast a shadow over the surging demand fueled by the rise of additive manufacturing. A market-oriented environmental impact assessment is presented for a novel method for recycling Ti6Al4V machining chips into atomization electrode feedstock. The recycled alternatives demonstrated similar properties to commercial variants, both in powder form and in parts printed using Laser Powder Bed Fusion and Composite Extrusion Modeling. Environmental analysis revealed substantial gains, largely driven by reduced reliance on energy-intensive titanium sponge production. Substituting the Ti6Al4V sleeve, essential for electrode fabrication, with a stainless steel variant decreased CO2-eq by 33.2%. The sponge market dominance of China, Japan, and Russia, with their fossil-dependent electricity generation, prevented leveraging a green energy mix, as evidenced by a modest 14% decline in the greenhouse effect associated with electrode fabrication despite a fivefold increase in renewable energy share. Assuming 60% scrap integration in the Ti6Al4V sleeve, the chip-based electrode's cumulative energy demand and CO2-eq decreased by 66.6% and 70.8%, respectively, compared to the commercial electrode with a similar scrap-to-sponge ratio. The process could save between 31.31MJ and 131.04 MJ per 1 kg of remelted ingot, considering material losses in the titanium value chain. Short-term market disruption from the developed process is unlikely, but the additive manufacturing expansion would drive long-term shifts in scrap and sponge demand. Amid a titanium market badly shaken by the Russia-Ukraine war, this study reveals a path to greener, cheaper titanium powder production; an insight for decision-makers striving for resilience in aerospace and additive manufacturing.

title: Systematic assessment of EHC-ccSCR systems for ultra-low NOx emissions: A strategy for sustainable heavy-duty transportation
abstract: Low exhaust temperature during sustained low-load operation remains a major obstacle to maintaining high aftertreatment efficiency in heavy-duty diesel engines. However, existing EHC studies have focused primarily on cold-start warm-up, while its capability for sustained thermal compensation during prolonged low-load operation, together with its coupled effects on dual-SCR reductant utilization, multi-pollutant emissions, and electrical energy consumption, has not been systematically evaluated. To address these gaps, this study experimentally evaluates an electrically heated catalyst coupled with close-coupled selective catalytic reduction (EHC-ccSCR) system as an active thermal management (ATM) strategy under the World Harmonized Stationary Cycle (WHSC) and Low Load Cycle (LLC), representing steady-state and transient low-temperature operating conditions, respectively. The results show that EHC-assisted ATM provides rapid front-stage thermal activation and promotes downstream thermal propagation, thereby extending the effective urea dosing window and enhancing the coordinated utilization of the dual-SCR system. Under WHSC, 240 s of EHC activation suppressed the initial NOx breakthrough and reduced NOx specific emissions to 19.23 mg/kWh. Under LLC, the dynamic ATM strategy increased downstream SCR urea consumption by 60.4%, indicating a shift from front-stage-dominated NOx conversion to dual-stage SCR coordination, and reduced NOx specific emissions by 95.5% to 53.38 mg/kWh. The elevated DOC temperature also improved CH4 conversion, whereas slight increases in N2O and PN10/PN23 emissions revealed secondary-emission trade-offs associated with intensified thermal and reductant management. Overall, the proposed EHC-assisted ATM strategy effectively mitigates low-temperature aftertreatment deactivation and provides an experimental basis for energy-aware, multi-pollutant emission control under future heavy-duty emission regulations.

title: The moderating role of climate governance in the transition risk–bank stability nexus amid hard-to-abate financing
abstract: The rapid pace of change towards a low-carbon economy is increasing the level of transition risk (TR) for banks, given their significant lending exposure to hard-to-abate sectors. These exposures increase their susceptibility to asset revaluation and rising credit defaults, which can ultimately undermine their bank stability (BS). In this vein, grounded within the Natural Resource-Based View (NRBV) and Dynamic Capability theory, this study conceptualizes climate governance (ClimGOV) as a strategic “adaptive capability” that enables banks to perceive, interpret, and adapt to these climate-related disruptions through enhanced oversight, risk management, and alignment with long-term climatic conditions. Accordingly, the study examines the moderating role of ClimGOV in mitigating the adverse impact of TR associated with hard-to-abate financing (particularly in the sectors of metal, cement, and chemical) on BS. The study uses an unbalanced panel dataset of the NIFTY Bank index from 2012 to 2023. These banks are highly liquid and systemically important institutions that collectively account for nearly 69.85% (approximately 70%) of scheduled banks' total assets, reflecting their dominant position in the banking sector. The empirical analysis, conducted using the Panel Corrected Standard Error (PCSE) estimator, reveals that strong ClimGOV has a significant positive effect on BS by reducing TR associated with hard-to-abate financing. Furthermore, the effect is more pronounced among smaller, highly capitalized, and banks with a commitment to Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG13: Climate Action), highlighting the heterogeneous nature of ClimGOV effectiveness. These findings are further confirmed through robustness checks, which employ Instrumental Variables Two-Stage Least Squares (IV 2SLS) to address concerns about endogeneity, followed by alternative proxy variables and a method, i.e., Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS). The study concludes by stating the theoretical, managerial, and policy implications of the results.

title: Spain's realistic potential for ocean alkalinity enhancement: Carbon dioxide removal through industrial integration
abstract: A common challenge for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) approaches, including those falling under ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE), is the need to develop new global industries and supply chains to underpin their sustainable scale-up. To facilitate roll-out, OAE approaches could be incorporated into existing industries, notably by: i) partially substituting silica sand in existing beach nourishment projects with (ultra)mafic (e.g., olivine-rich) sand for carbon dioxide drawdown through coastal enhanced weathering; ii) using the spare capacity of the cement industry to produce slaked lime for ocean liming; and iii) producing sodium hydroxide from waste desalination brines through electrochemical brine splitting. Here, the gross CDR capacities of these OAE approaches were examined for Spain by considering spare capacities, technical constraints, and engineering restrictions and challenges. Prospective life cycle assessment (pLCA) revealed their net-negativity and their sensitivity to future climate scenarios and particularly technology maturity. Spain's gross/net CDR capacity via OAE amounted to 13.52/8.27, 38.35/26.50, and 40.54/38.13 Mt CO 2 yr −1 in 2030, 2040, and 2050, respectively. Future decarbonisation and improved technology readiness levels and spare capacities drive this increase. Therefore, technological maturity and decarbonised economies, particularly decarbonised energy, are needed for CDR technologies to achieve their full potential. Finally, we considered how complex social, regulatory, and governance factors may impinge on the feasibility of these three OAE approaches. Regulatory clarity and innovation, governance frameworks, and social acceptance are needed, which also requires robust efforts to consult and engage communities. Overall, OAE could underpin national long-term strategies and form an essential part of climate-neutrality strategies.

title: Deciphering the enhanced effect of graphene aerogel and nitrogen-doped graphene aerogel on anaerobic digestion of food waste: microbial community structure, metabolic pathways, and electron transfer
abstract: Graphene (G) and graphene oxide (GO) have been explored as promising additives to enhance anaerobic digestion (AD) of food waste (FW). And the graphene aerogel (GA) and nitrogen-doped graphene aerogel (NGA) produced by reducing graphene oxide exhibit superior capacitance and electrical conductivity. This study systematically investigated the impacts of (G, GO, GA, and NGA) on methane production during the AD of FW. Results demonstrated that cumulative methane production was enhanced by 12.48%, 9.32%, 2.83%, and 6.99% upon addition of NGA, GA, GO, and G, respectively. Graphene-based materials also altered bacterial and archaeal community composition. GA, GO, and G were associated with enrichment of the acetoclastic methanogen Methanosaeta during the early stage, whereas NGA consistently favored the hydrogenotrophic methanogen Methanobacterium, whose relative abundance on day 15 was approximately 4.3-fold that of the control group. PICRUSt2-based predictions indicated that NGA was associated with higher predicted functional potential related to hydrogenotrophic and methylotrophic methanogenesis and to the biosynthesis of quinones, riboflavin, and type IV pili. GA was mainly associated with predicted functions related to ubiquinone and c-type cytochromes. These results suggested that GA and NGA could enhance methane production, potentially through distinct shifts in methanogenic communities and predicted electron-transfer-related functions. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that both NGA and GA effectively augment methane production during AD of FW, offering mechanistic insights and theoretical foundations for optimizing AD performance.

title: From AI competencies to energy-saving value: A capability–behavior–performance model
abstract: Although firms increasingly deploy artificial intelligence (AI) in energy management, limited evidence explains how AI competencies are associated with environmental and economic outcomes. Drawing on the core competence view and dynamic capability theory, we develop a capability–behavior–performance model. The model links AI competencies to three energy-saving dynamic capabilities: opportunity sensing, opportunity seizing, and resource reconfiguration. These capabilities are associated with energy-saving innovation behavior, which is further associated with environmental and economic performance. PLS-SEM analysis of two-wave survey data from 414 firms in Guangdong Province, China, supported all proposed relationships. The three capabilities significantly mediated the association between AI competencies and energy-saving innovation behavior, while a significant direct association remained. Environmental performance was also positively associated with economic performance. These findings clarify the capability-based pathways linking AI competencies to energy-saving value.

title: Hierarchical energy management strategy for hybrid electric air-ground vehicles considering engine start-stop response characteristics
abstract: Low-carbon transportation is a critical global issue in addressing climate change, and air-ground vehicles, as an emerging carrier for urban air mobility, offer an important pathway toward sustainable mobility. Hybrid electric air-ground vehicles with dual turboshaft engines exhibit significant potential for cost and emission reduction owing to their high power-to-weight ratio and wide operating range. However, in existing studies, the two turboshaft engines are typically of identical power rating, leaving room for improvement in energy efficiency between ground and aerial modes. Moreover, the start–stop delay characteristics further complicate power allocation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a differentiated dual-turboshaft hybrid configuration, in which engines of distinct specifications are assigned more clearly defined roles across the two modes, and develops a hierarchical energy management strategy. The upper layer employs an LSTM-Attention-LSTM model for short-term power demand prediction. The lower layer targets the hybrid action problem in which discrete start-stop commands coexist with continuous power allocation, and introduces an improved deep reinforcement learning TD3 algorithm that reformulates the discrete action into a continuous form. A dual-policy network selection mechanism combined with softmax-weighted fusion is incorporated to suppress policy oscillation near the start-stop boundary. Simulation results show that the proposed DP-STD3 strategy triggers only two engine start-stop events, with fuel consumption deviating by merely 1.05% from the globally optimal DP strategy and decreasing by 1.73% compared with the DDQN strategy, while delivering smoother power output, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: Intelligent identification method for gas well string leakage based on time-series data and time-frequency fusion BiLSTM model
abstract: Accurate and timely detection of string leakage in ultra-deep gas wells is vital for operational safety. Current methods largely depend on instrumental measurements, with limited intelligent approaches based on multi-source time-frequency data. Based on wellbore multiphase flow theory and considering temperature-pressure coupling effects, this study establishes a high-fidelity dynamic dataset (leak depth: 500-7500 m; size: 0.1-30 mm). A time-frequency dual-stream gated attention network is proposed, integrating parallel multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to capture local anomalies and frequency-domain signatures. Bidirectional Long Short-term Memory (BiLSTM) with adaptive multi-head attention highlights transient signals, while gated residual units remove feature redundancy, addressing the issue of leak signal decoupling and quantitative inversion in a complex noise environment. The model achieves highly accurate and robust regression predictions, with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)≈30 m and Mean Absolute Error (MAE)≈0.09 mm for location and size, respectively (location: R2 > 0.99; size: R2 > 0.99). Through feature Integrated Gradients analysis, annulus head pressure is identified as the dominant feature (20 %-30 % contribution). The Gated Residual Network (GRN) module effectively filters nonlinear redundant information, reducing MAE by 24 %-58 % compared to Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Residual Network (ResNet). Furthermore, the time-frequency design lowers MAE by 70 %-84 % in location and 79 %-85 % in size compared to mainstream sequential models (e.g., TCN, Transformer). Under feature scarcity (1-2 features) or limited data (20 % samples), performance remains robust (location R2 > 0.99; size R2 > 0.97), outperforming single models by 47 %-79 % in MAE. Additionally, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) proves effective as a cost-efficient localization solution in resource-constrained scenarios (R2 > 0.995).

title: Sustainable plant-oil rejuvenation of aged SBS-modified asphalt: Balancing initial recovery and secondary-aging durability
abstract: The rejuvenation of aged styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS)-modified asphalt is difficult because matrix oxidation, light-fraction loss, SBS degradation and polymer-phase destabilization occur together. This study compared eight plant-oil rejuvenators, each at a dosage of 10 wt%, for the rejuvenation of aged SBS-modified asphalt. Physical, rheological, interfacial, spectroscopic and microscopic tests were performed at the initial state and after thermo-oxidative and ultraviolet aging. The plant-oil rejuvenators improved the initial state, with penetration increasing by 14.1-200.0%, ductility by 61.1-738.9%, and viscosity at 135 °C decreasing from 13,300 mPa s to 2481–3188 mPa s. However, normalized ductility recovery reached only 3.8-45.4% of the aging-induced loss, showing that apparent softening did not equal toughness or SBS-network recovery. At 64 °C, service aging increased the complex modulus from 21.74 kPa to 206.75 kPa, while the plant-oil rejuvenators restored flowability initially but underwent secondary-aging re-hardening. Low-temperature results showed that stiffness-controlled and relaxation-controlled critical temperatures shifted from −22.77 °C and −21.48 °C to −13.16 °C and −11.50 °C after aging, with ultraviolet aging causing stronger cumulative deterioration than thermo-oxidative aging. Interfacial results showed strong correlations between bond strength ratio and 24 h water-conditioned cohesive-dominated area fraction under thermo-oxidative and ultraviolet aging, with R2 values of 0.845 and 0.811. Chemical and microscopic evidence linked carbonyl index changes to rheological re-hardening more consistently than sulfoxide index changes and indicated local redistribution of the polymer-rich phase rather than continuous-network reconstruction. The selection framework showed that waste soybean oil had the most balanced profile, tall oil provided rapid Initial recovery and interfacial improvement but required attention to rutting-related stability and aged-state retention, castor oil acted mainly as an interfacial functional component, algal oil showed low-temperature-oriented potential, and soybean, corn, and peanut oils showed moderate profiles requiring service-condition-dependent stabilization. These findings support durability-informed plant-oil selection for sustainable asphalt recycling.

title: Rubberized Engineered/Strain-Hardening Geopolymer Composites (EGC/SHGC) with low fiber content to enhance strength and ductility efficiencies
abstract: Traditional waste tire disposal methods, such as landfilling and incineration, pose serious threats to the ecological environment. In response, this study developed sustainable Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC) by incorporating crumb rubber (CR) as both waste-derived aggregates and matrix crack-resistance regulators, while using only 0.8% PE fibers to balance mechanical performance and sustainability efficiency. The results showed that although the incorporation of CR reduced the compressive strength of EGC, it significantly improved tensile ductility, reaching a maximum of 7.94% at fly ash (FA)/ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) = 7/3. In addition, increasing GGBS ratios was found to enhance the compressive strength of EGC but reduce its tensile ductility. A Weibull-based probabilistic model developed to describe the over-satuatrated cracking behavior and crack width evolution showed excellent agreement with the experimental results, demonstrating its capability for predicting the maximum crack width. Furthermore, compared with existing rubberized Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) and EGC systems, the developed rubberized EGC achieved the lowest embodied energy, embodied carbon, and material cost per Strength-Ductility Index, with minimum values of 745.2 MJ/m3/MPa, 86.1 kg CO2/m3/MPa, and 974.9 CNY/m3/MPa, respectively, while showing a high ductility efficiency of up to 9.9. These findings offer a viable strategy for upcycling waste tires into sustainable high-performance construction materials.

title: Are environmental standards unsustainable? A discussion through the regulatory uncertainty of double materiality
abstract: Although environmental standards are intended to support ecological transition, the regulatory uncertainty surrounding their implementation may paradoxically reinforce the neoliberal logics of the very financial capitalism they claim to challenge. This article examines to what extent, and through which mechanisms, the uncertainty associated with double materiality transforms environmental reporting mechanisms into (counter-)performative tools. We analyse 812 CSR reports issued between 2016 and 2022 by the largest French listed firms (SBF120). Using a structured content analysis, we identify four reporting profiles and show a marked phase of instability between 2017 and 2019, during which time dominant firms in the field test and recombine registers of legitimation while concrete requirements remain unclear. Our results suggest that uncertainty is not merely an obstacle to compliance, but can become a strategic lever through which dominant actors reappropriate the (critical) language embedded in emerging sustainability standards, prioritise communication over action, and produce symbolic reports. In this sense, double materiality risks operating as a counter-performative standard, enabling reporting to be deployed as an instrument of legitimation that renews and reinforces neoliberal logics, potentially to the benefit of the most polluting firms. We thus expand the debate on the political role of quantification mechanisms and underscore the need to rethink the institutional and political conditions under which double materiality can become a genuine lever for environmental change rather than a language that fuels the capitalist machine.

title: Machine learning-based integration of plant growth regulators and overcompensation enhances microalgal protein production from wastewater
abstract: Photoautotrophic wastewater valorization represents a sustainable route for carbon-neutral nutrient upcycling into bioproducts. However, its practical implementation is often constrained by wastewater-induced growth inhibition. Besides, the distribution of metabolic flux across competing pathways may further restrict nutrient allocation towards target product. In this study, we propose a combined strategy integrating plant growth regulators (PGRs) with a nitrogen overcompensation strategy to enhance microalgal performance during potato starch wastewater treatment. Gibberellic acid (GA 3 ) and naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) both alleviated wastewater inhibition and enhanced nutrient recovery in Chlorella pyrenoidosa , achieving up to 79.9% total nitrogen removal. Notably, supplementation with 10 mg L −1 GA 3 resulted in a 26.2% increase in biomass compared to controls. The random forest model identified candidate high-response concentrations of approximately 10.5 ± 1 mg L −1 for GA 3 and 10.2 ± 1 mg L −1 for NAA and suggested declining biomass responses at higher NAA concentrations, whereas GA 3 showed a broader model-predicted growth-promoting range. Under the nitrogen starvation–repletion condition, PGR-supplemented cultures achieved maximum biomass and protein concentrations of up to 1.58 g L −1 and 594.82 mg L −1 , respectively, together with over 90% removal of COD, total phosphorus, and ammonium. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that GA 3 induced significant upregulation of genes involved in photosynthetic apparatus function, ribosomal biogenesis, and transmembrane transport processes compared to NAA. This work establishes a strategy that integrates PGRs with nitrogen overcompensation to overcome wastewater-induced stress. The proposed approach provides a practical strategy for improving microalgal productivity and nutrient recovery from high-strength wastewater, advancing the development of carbon-neutral biorefinery systems.

title: Sludge-derived biochar-activated peroxymonosulfate as a waste-to-resource pretreatment for sustainable membrane fouling control: Adsorption-oxidation interplay and thermodynamic insights
abstract: Pretreatment strategies that integrate membrane fouling control with waste valorization offer a promising route to sustainable water reuse. In this study, municipal sewage sludge was converted into unmodified sludge-derived biochar (SBC) and employed as a waste-derived activator of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for membrane fouling control. Compared with commercial biochar, SBC exhibited superior catalytic and adsorption performance owing to its hierarchical porous structure, abundant defects, and naturally embedded Fe/Ca species, which provided interfacial regulation functions. Under a fixed PMS dose, however, the SBC/PMS system showed a dose-dependent, non-monotonic fouling response. At low SBC dosages, limited reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation caused fouling evolution to be dominated by adsorption, promoting compact and cross-linked gel layers and increasing the specific filtration resistance (SFR). As the SBC dosage increased, the naturally embedded Fe species sustained PMS activation and ROS generation, while Fe3+/Ca2+ facilitated bridging among oxidized foulant fragments. This coupled oxidation-reorganization process transformed compact adsorption complexes into porous and more hydrophilic flocs, reducing SFR by 86.6%. Multiscale analyses integrating XDLVO and Flory-Huggins thermodynamic frameworks further revealed that increasing SBC dosage shifted membrane-foulant interactions from attraction to repulsion and reduced the chemical potential difference across the fouling layer. These changes weakened foulant adhesion and reduced bound-water capacity, yielding water loss rate of 92.0% and thereby markedly mitigating fouling. Overall, membrane fouling evolution in the SBC/PMS system was governed by the dose-dependent interplay of adsorption, catalytic oxidation, and Fe/Ca-mediated foulant restructuring. This study offers a sustainable, cleaner-production pathway with the potential to mitigate the carbon footprint of water treatment by synergizing sewage sludge valorization with membrane fouling control.

title: Synergetic activation of slag by sodium sulphate and magnesium oxide: Strength, hydration, and microstructure
abstract: Sodium sulphate-activated slag has been recognised as an eco-friendly binder, although it faces issues of slow setting and strength development. In this study, magnesium oxide (MgO) is introduced as a co-activator alongside sodium sulphate (SST) to tackle these challenges. The results demonstrate that SST-MgO-activated slag (SSTMS) pastes exhibit favourable fresh and mechanical properties, with the fastest setting time of around 12 h and compressive strength of up to 55 MPa at 28 days. During hydration, MgO partially dissolves and primarily provides an alkaline environment to initiate slag dissolution. Afterwards, SST actively participates in the alkali-activation process by reacting with Ca 2+ and Al(OH) 4 - ions released from slag to form ettringite at early ages. This not only promotes self-alkalinisation for accelerating slag dissolution, but also enhances strength through the pore-filling and bridging effects of ettringite. However, the competition for aluminium sources between ettringite and C-A-S-H gel results in some retardation of the initial gel polymerisation. As the pore solution alkalinity exceeds a level aborting ettringite precipitation, the hydration of SSTMS paste gradually resembles that of MgO-incorporated alkali-activated slag (AAS) paste. The excess Al(OH) 4 - ions then tend to react with Mg 2+ ions, leading to the generation of hydrotalcite at a later stage. Overall, understanding the hydration mechanism for the SSTMS system provides a theoretical basis for optimising its mechanical performance. The SSTMS paste, as a weakly AAS system, offers favourable long-term compressive strength and improved operational safety compared to conventional AAS systems.

title: Taxonomy of circular economy practices aimed at preventing and reducing food waste in retail
abstract: Food loss and waste (FLW) in food retail poses critical challenges at the intersection of environmental sustainability and circular economy (CE) transitions. Despite growing scholarly attention, approaches to preventing and reducing FLW remain fragmented, with uneven adoption across institutional contexts. This study develops a systematic taxonomy of CE practices and applies it in a comparative analysis of Brazil and Spain, two countries with contrasting institutional contexts for circular economy implementation. A systematic literature review identified 233 practices, which were consolidated into a taxonomy of 33 CE practices organized into five hierarchical categories based on value preservation: food surplus prevention, avoidable waste prevention, reuse, recycling, and recovery. An Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) assessed specialists' perceptions of the strategic importance and implementation of each practice. The findings indicate that, although CE practices were consistently perceived as highly important in both countries, their implementation differed substantially. Higher implementation levels in Spain were associated with a more consolidated regulatory environment, technological infrastructure, and coordinated governance, whereas wider implementation gaps in Brazil were linked to technological limitations and institutional fragmentation. This study contributes by systematizing retail-oriented CE practices into an integrated taxonomy, operationalizing the distinction between food surplus prevention and avoidable waste prevention, and showing how institutional conditions shape the adoption of CE practices. The findings provide practical guidance for retailers in prioritizing circular interventions and inform policymakers on institutional actions needed to accelerate food waste prevention and support progress toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12.3.

title: Chemical-biological suitability of biochar for peat, lime and fertilizer replacement in horticultural substrates
abstract: Growing media in horticulture face sustainability challenges due to extensive use of non-renewable and single-use materials. Peat is an excellent bulk material but is under pressure for environmental and economic reasons. Existing peat replacements include wood fibers, coir and bark products. Potential peat replacements include biochars, composts and plant fibers, but their composition is highly variable depending on feedstock and production processes. The chemical and biological properties of biochars may therefore limit their potential use as bulk material in horticultural substrates. Insight is needed into the fit between biochar type in terms of feedstock and their use in horticulture, i.e., as peat replacement in growing media. More than 150 samples, including 75 biochar samples and more than 75 samples of peat, coir and feedstock materials to produce biochar, were scored based on eight chemical or biological characteristics. Suitability of biochars and their feedstocks for use in growing media blends was assessed using the Peat, Lime and Fertilizer replacement Index. Defining subcategories of feedstock and production process, assessed per batch, further refined the suitability assessment by reflecting the range of variability within the same type of material. Wood-based, fiber-based and bark-based biochars, organic spent growing media and straw-like plant fibers received the highest scores for the Peat, Lime and Fertilizer replacement Index, indicating high potential for use in horticultural substrates. Digestate-based or manure-based biochars and other nutrient-rich subcategories received low scores, with the inorganic C content and electrical conductivity being major bottlenecks for most nutrient-rich materials. The high acid buffering capacity of manure-based materials due to high content of inorganic C limits their application as peat replacement but indicates their potential to replace fossil lime and fertilizers when applied in a sufficiently low dose. In conclusion, different biochars should be selected according to their specific functional properties and intended role in growing media, rather than being considered interchangeable peat substitutes.

title: Environmental performance of bamboo winding composite pipe (BWCP): A life cycle assessment compared to conventional pipe materials
abstract: Bamboo winding composite pipe (BWCP) is an emerging bio-based alternative for pipeline infrastructure. This study evaluates the environmental performance of BWCP through a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment and compares it with PVC, HDPE, reinforced concrete (RC), and ductile iron (DI) pipes under unified buried-pipeline functional conditions. The functional unit is defined as a 1-m pipe with an inner diameter of 1.4 m, a ring stiffness of 9.43 kN/m2, and a design service life exceeding 50 years. Environmental impacts are assessed using the ReCiPe (H) Midpoint and Endpoint methods, with sensitivity analyses conducted for functional-unit conversion and end-of-life assumptions. Results show that BWCP has the lowest total environmental impact among the five pipe materials, with a single score of 31.6 Pt. This is 67%, 26%, 17%, and 58% lower than those of PVC, HDPE, RC, and DI pipes, respectively. BWCP also reduces global warming potential by 62%, 43%, and 27% compared with PVC, HDPE, and DI pipes. The production stage is the dominant contributor to BWCP impacts, mainly due to resin production and curing electricity. Process-improvement scenarios show that reducing resin consumption and curing electricity can further decrease the total impact by about 12%. These results indicate that BWCP is a promising low-impact alternative for buried pipeline applications.

title: Carbon subsidies and blockchain adoption feasibility in closed-loop supply chains: emission-based versus investment-based schemes
abstract: Blockchain-enabled traceability can improve the credibility of low-carbon supply chains, but adoption remains costly and sensitive to subsidy design. This study examines a manufacturer's blockchain adoption in a manufacturer-led closed-loop supply chain when consumers value low-carbon attributes but discount unverifiable claims. The analysis uses a Stackelberg model with six scenarios: no subsidy, emission-based subsidy, and investment-based subsidy, each with and without blockchain. Closed-form equilibria are derived, and adoption feasibility is characterized by an adoption-dominance interval over the abatement-cost parameter and a blockchain-cost threshold for the high-abatement-cost region. The analysis also considers verification effectiveness, fixed implementation costs, welfare-compatible thresholds, fiscal efficiency, and budget-neutral comparison. Analytical results show that blockchain adoption, when privately profitable, raises the manufacturer's optimal emission-reduction intensity and that higher verification effectiveness expands the adoption region. The numerical analysis shows that, under budget-neutral matching, the investment-based scheme expands the adoption-dominance interval more than the emission-based scheme, with the advantage increasing from 8% to 44% as the emission-based subsidy intensity increases from 0.10 to 0.40, while the difference in the blockchain-cost threshold remains small. At the highest subsidy intensity, increasing verification effectiveness from 0.2 to 1.0 raises the blockchain-cost threshold by factors of approximately 7.3 and 7.5 under the emission-based and investment-based schemes, respectively. The welfare-compatible adoption interval is also approximately 3.3–3.9 times as long as the privately optimal interval. Fiscal-efficiency rankings vary with subsidy intensity, with the fiscal-efficiency ratio of the investment-based scheme to the emission-based scheme falling to 0.390 at an emission-based subsidy intensity of 0.40.

title: Carbon footprints of Asian seaweed cultivation under methane decay
abstract: Dietary transition is an attractive pathway to mitigate climate change. Cultivated seaweed, as a blue food, offers an alternative to land fertilizer-intensive vegetables and thus has the potential to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. However, seaweed's climate burden that is complicated by methane decay has seldom been quantified, particularly in Asian economies, where 97% of global seaweed was produced in 2022. This study used life cycle assessment (LCA) to quantify the carbon footprint (CF) of five seaweed species (Saccharina, Undaria, Eucheumatoids, Gracilaria, and Pyropia) cultivated in six major Asian producer countries (South Korea, Japan, China, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Malaysia). Across economies, the CF of Saccharina (91–154 kgCO2e t−1) and Undaria (103–189 kgCO2e t−1) are comparable and exceed those of Eucheumatoids (28–43 kgCO2e t−1) and Gracilaria (33–107 kgCO2e t−1), but fall below that of Pyropia (176–258 kgCO2e t−1). Philippine Eucheumatoids have the lowest CF (i.e., 28 kgCO2e t−1), and Pyropia show no clear climate advantage over some land vegetables. Concrete anchors contribute 41–61% to the CF of Saccharina and Undaria cultivations. Replacing concrete-to-wood anchors and extending rope lifespan are effective ways to reduce climate burdens by 53–66%. Given methane decay, the underestimated CF of seaweed at the 100-year horizon overstates the climate advantage of seaweeds compared to vegetables. This study quantifies the CF of major Asian seaweeds and highlights their time-dependent climate performance relative to land vegetables.

title: Decentralized carbon-aware hierarchical coordination of multi-layer power networks through locational marginal carbon intensity propagation
abstract: This paper presents a carbon-aware hierarchical dispatch approach for the joint scheduling of transmission, distribution, and microgrid systems. The framework considers operation of complex multi-layer power networks, wherein independent optimization of each layer can give rise to infeasible and inconsequential boundary exchanges, contradictory carbon calculation, and suboptimal use of distributed flexibility. The problem is cast as a three-level optimization. At the transmission level, generation scheduling and locational carbon intensity for the bulk power system are established. At the distribution level, dispatch choices synchronize distributed generation and responsive demand. At the level of microgrid, local energy management is carried out subject to explicit carbon budget constraints. To address the tightly coupled integer nonlinear optimization problem in a decentralized way, a tri-level alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with adaptive penalty updating is designed. As a dynamic variable, the carbon emission intensity coordinates the layers to ensure emissions are tracked consistently. For distribution network constraints, SOCR is employed. Simulation studies are conducted on an integrated transmission–distribution–microgrid test system. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework, relative to uncoordinated operation with the same carbon constraints, reduces operating costs from 501,840 to 468,940 USD/day through effective coordination of multi-layer resources. Compared to a coordinated baseline without carbon constraints, the carbon-aware framework increases operating costs by approximately 13.7% (412,480 → 468,940 USD/day) while achieving substantial emissions reductions from 8240 to 4630 tCO2/day (43.8% reduction). Wind curtailment is reduced from 285 to 142 MWh, and microgrid carbon budget violations are eliminated. The proposed method yields a result close to the convex relaxation of the centralized MISOCP solution (which serves as a practical benchmark within our modeling framework) with cost and emission gaps of 0.36% and 0.70%, respectively, and computation time is reduced from 8420 s to 598 s. These findings demonstrate that the architecture can effectively enable coordinated low-carbon dispatch across multi-layer power systems at a quantifiable economic cost that is justified by significant environmental benefits.

title: Reconceptualizing water environmental capacity as a network-driven property: A spatially cascading framework for basin-scale phosphorus management
abstract: Excessive phosphorus loading triggers eutrophication, yet basin-scale pollution mitigation efforts are constrained by conventional water environmental capacity (WEC) estimation approaches that neglect the spatiotemporal dynamics and the cascading transfer of WEC within river networks. This study proposes a spatially cascading WEC framework for basin-scale total phosphorus (TP) management. The framework reconceptualizes WEC as a dynamic, network-driven property by decomposing it into four distinct components: base (BWEC), transferred (TWEC), available (AWEC), and surplus (SWEC) components. By integrating SWAT-simulated hydrological and water quality processes with river network topological features, the framework enables dynamic and explicit quantification of capacity generation, inheritance, and redistribution across entire dendritic river networks. Applied to the Yong River Basin in China (2010–2021), the framework revealed significant spatiotemporal variability of WEC across 162 sub-basins. Both BWEC and AWEC showed strong intra-annual variability (CV up to 1.21 and 0.81, respectively), with 51.6 ± 10.9% of basin-aggregated BWEC concentrated in monsoon months. Further results showed that upstream cascading transport contributed up to 99.1% of available WEC in downstream reaches of the Yong River Basin, confirming the pronounced longitudinal cascading buildup of available capacity. By balancing cascading AWEC against pollutant loads, the framework identified a required annual TP load reduction of 13.0–26.2% at the basin scale, with spatially refined targets allocated to 162 individual sub-basins. This study elucidates the cascading network nature of WEC, improves methodological support for basin-scale pollution governance, and provides a transferable paradigm for rational pollutant load allocation across different river systems.

title: Technoeconomic analysis of catalytic alcoholysis of fusel oil for the synthesis of methyl glycolate
abstract: Polyglycolic acid production generates a stream of fusel oil with close boiling points, which makes the recycling extremely challenging. Due to a lack of effective treatment technologies, enterprises currently sell this by-product at low prices. The growing stockpiles have become an increasing burden and a hidden concern for the enterprises. To address this, fixed bed experiments of catalytic alcoholysis of fusel oil over three catalysts for the synthesis of methyl glycolate were conducted, achieving stable continuous operation for 500 h without significant catalyst deactivation. The effects of reaction type, pressure, and temperature on product distribution were investigated. Cu-Si catalyst exhibited the best reaction performance. At 433 K and 2.8 MPa, the conversion of high boiling point components in the alcoholysis reaction could be stabilized at 88 %, with a 93 % selectivity. Based on the experimental results, a catalytic alcoholysis process model was developed and integrated into the existing polyglycolic acid production process, which enables a 5 % increase in methyl glycolate and a 142 % increase in ethylene glycol with existing facilities, with a specific energy demand of 46.84 kg of fuel oil for per ton of products. Economic evaluation of the catalytic alcoholysis technology was studied, for a 70,000-ton-per-year PGA production facility, it can achieve an annual profit increase of over USD 6.32 million, validating significant commercial potential.

title: Macro-micro coordinated optimization for energy consumption forecasting: A Bi-level dual-fractional neural ODE grey model
abstract: Under the “dual-carbon” strategy, accurately forecasting China's energy consumption is a key prerequisite for policy evaluation and pathway planning. Existing energy forecasting studies mostly focus on aggregate quantities or single-level structures, and often fail to adequately describe the hierarchical relationships between the macro-level and micro-level. To address this gap, this paper proposes a bi-level dual-fractional neural ODE grey model (BDF-NODE-GM). At the model-structure level, the upper level models the aggregate evolution trend of clean and non-clean energy, while the lower level captures the dynamic evolution of five representative energy types. The two levels are coordinated through a bi-level programming framework. Methodologically, fractional accumulation and fractional derivatives are embedded into a neural ODE framework, enabling collaborative modeling of grey-system prior constraints and neural dynamical systems. Building on this design, we further develop a collaborative bi-level solution mechanism. Specifically, we adopt independent training for the two levels and introduce one-way parameter transfer from the lower level to the upper level, thereby achieving stable optimization of high-dimensional coupled parameters. Then, the proposed model is applied to China's energy consumption data from 2000 to 2023 for model fitting, and scenario forecasts are generated for 2024-2030. The model is validated through four types of experiments: cross-validation, ablation experiment, multi-model comparison, and parameter sensitivity analysis. The results show that new model outperforms competing models across multiple evaluation metrics, with fitting and forecasting MAPE of 1.0407% and 1.3707%, respectively. Finally, the forecasting results indicate that, during 2024-2030, clean and non-clean energy consumption will grow at average annual rates of 5.8% and 1.7%, respectively. However, no coal-consumption peak inflection point is observed within the model's forecast horizon, indicating that the system remains in the incremental substitution stage.

title: Who bears the burden? Tracing carbon emission responsibilities and flows across socioeconomic strata for sustainable development
abstract: Urban transport decarbonization is not only about how much CO2 is emitted, but also where emissions accumulate on the road network and which neighborhoods’ commuting demand gives rise to them. Existing studies often map emissions, quantify inequality, or assign responsibility separately, leaving the responsibility–burden mismatch unresolved at the scale where congestion and route choice operate. We bridge this gap in Shanghai using mobile phone signaling data, a stochastic multi-path assignment model, and COPERT to reconstruct dynamic road-link CO2 emissions from private-car commuting. The inventory shows a Pareto-like concentration: about 20% of road segments account for roughly 80% of emissions. We then use hierarchical Theil decomposition and network-based source tracing to compare local-burden shares—emissions released on road links within each housing-price-based neighborhood stratum—with source-attributed responsibility—the same emissions reassigned to the neighborhood origins of the commuting flows that generated them. Within-district variation explains 91% of overall inequality, indicating that the dominant disparity lies below the district scale. Local burden peaks in the middle-price strata, whereas the highest-price SES-6 stratum rises from 13.59% of local burden to 16.21% of source-attributed responsibility. The tracing matrix further shows strong same-stratum attribution, especially at both ends of the socioeconomic spectrum, revealing a partially segregated carbon-flow geography rather than a simple one-way transfer from higher- to lower-price neighborhoods. By linking road-level emission concentration, multiscale inequality, and source tracing, the framework provides an auditable basis for spatially differentiated and equity-sensitive urban transport decarbonization

title: Economic viability of thermal flexibilization of agricultural anaerobic digesters under intermittent Power-to-Gas plant operation
abstract: Power-to-Gas systems in biogas plants complement volatile renewable energy systems by converting surplus electricity into an energy carrier suitable for long-term storage. Heat integration and sales support the economic performance especially for catalytic high-temperature technologies, but thermal storage is required to assure supply to the anaerobic degradation process in intermittent operation. This can be achieved by thermally flexibilizing the digesters avoiding additional heat storage. This study evaluates such thermal flexibilization in Power-to-Gas applications by comparing its total costs with various conventional constant-temperature alternatives. Detailed simulations of typical agricultural biogas facilities and intermittent Power-to-Gas plant operation provided data for the techno-economic assessment. The results indicate that thermal flexibilization is viable between 4,000 and 8,000 annual full-load hours of Power-to-Gas system operation. The relative economic improvement over the closest constant-temperature alternative is at least 5.7% and 6.6% for manure- and energy-crop-based biogas plants, respectively, even at low methane prices. If the influence of temperature on biogas production is neglected, thermal flexibilization becomes non-viable at 8,000 annual full-load hours. While savings in internal methane consumption alone are sufficient for a competitive thermal flexibilization in energy-crop-based biogas plants, manure-intensive facilities may require additional measures in the absence of waste-heat revenues, with necessity depending on Power-to-Gas plant configuration. In future intermittently operated catalytic Power-to-Gas plants, conventional waste-heat integration can reduce synthetic methane production costs by 8% and 5% for manure- and energy-crop-based biogas plants, respectively. Thermal flexibilization can provide further cost reductions of 2% and 1%, respectively.

title: Environmental regulation and municipal public finances: Evidence from Brazil’s National Solid Waste Policy
abstract: This study investigates the effect of Brazil’s National Solid Waste Policy (Política Nacional de Resíduos Sólidos – PNRS) on municipal expenditure on solid waste management. Despite the rapid diffusion of such environmental mandates across developing countries, rigorous causal evidence on their fiscal consequences for local governments remains scarce. Using data from the National Sanitation Information System covering 3292 municipalities over the period 2002–2019, we employ a difference-in-differences estimator to account for the staggered adoption of Municipal Integrated Solid Waste Management Plans (ISWMPs), the legally required instrument for municipal compliance with the PNRS. Our results show that the PNRS implementation increases municipal per capita waste management expenditure by R$ 11.77 annually (2019 values), representing a 9.3% increase relative to the control group. The analysis reveals substantial regional heterogeneity, with the policy’s effects being more pronounced in municipalities with greater pre-existing institutional and financial capacity. Fourteen robustness tests confirm the consistency of our main findings. However, we do not find statistically robust evidence of improvements in health outcomes, including infant mortality and hospitalisations due to intestinal infections. These results provide the first rigorous causal evidence of the PNRS’s compliance costs, filling a gap in the literature that has documented waste-management costs predominantly in high-income countries without identifying their causal fiscal effects in developing federations.

title: Agro-environmental synergy efficiency in 329 Chinese cities: Spatiotemporal patterns, dynamic decomposition, and structural drivers
abstract: Under the dual pressures of climate change and food security, achieving agricultural production while reducing carbon emission pressure and enhancing ecological carbon sequestration capacity represents a major challenge for agricultural green transformation.
