Agro-Environmental Synergy Efficiency (AESE) is used to evaluate the overall synergistic performance of agricultural production systems under the joint effects of production objectives and environmental constraints. Based on panel data from 329 prefecture-level cities in China during 2000–2022, this study develops an integrated analytical framework incorporating carbon emission downscaling, carbon sink estimation, efficiency measurement, and driving mechanism identification. The Environmental Kuznets Curve Downscaling Model (EKCDM) is used to estimate agricultural carbon emissions at the city level, while remote-sensing land-cover data are applied to estimate ecological carbon sinks. The Slacks-Based Measure Directional Distance Function (SBM-DDF) is then employed to measure static AESE Score, and a Global Malmquist-Luenberger (GML) index is constructed to characterize dynamic changes in AESE Growth Index (AGI). The Geographical Detector method is further used to identify the driving factors. The results show that 75 cities remained at relatively low efficiency levels for an extended period. AESE improved gradually during the study period, with the cumulative AGI increasing by approximately 2.91%. This improvement was mainly driven by growth in the green efficiency change index (GEC), while the dominant drivers of AESE Score shifted from differences in agricultural economic development and basic conditions toward disparities in social governance and human capital. These findings provide city-level empirical evidence for the formulation of differentiated policies for agricultural green transformation.

title: Improving the utilization rate of renewable energy in food industrial parks with electric heavy-duty trucks: A novel pricing-theory and energy consumption quota-driven electricity dispatch allocation mechanism
abstract: As a typical integrated energy system, the food industrial park (FIP) is characterized by high energy consumption. At present, existing scheduling methods for FIPs are subject to limitations in addressing diversified load types, real-time supply–demand fluctuations, and coordination with mobile energy storage, making it difficult for improving the utilization rate of renewable energy in FIP. Therefore, a pricing-theory and energy consumption quota-driven electricity dispatch and allocation mechanism is proposed to the utilization level of renewable energy in FIPs. First, a pricing theory and marginal analysis-driven zoned dynamic priority scheduling strategy is developed, in which optimal electricity allocation is achieved through a simulated market auction mechanism. Second, an energy consumption quotas-based electricity allocation strategy for electric heavy-duty trucks is proposed, through which electric heavy-duty trucks within the park are transformed into flexible and responsive mobile micro-energy nodes. On this basis, an improved multi-objective tetragonula carbonaria optimization algorithm is proposed to address the high-dimensional and nonlinear characteristics of the FIP scheduling model. The solution performance of the algorithm is comprehensively enhanced through three mechanisms: scout bee-guided initialization, dynamic role assignment, and adaptive temperature regulation. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategies enable the operational cost of the FIP to be reduced by 26.48%, carbon emissions to be decreased by 17.2%, and the profits of electric heavy-duty truck owners to be increased, while the vehicle-to-grid response rate is improved to 62.0%. Overall, the utilization level of renewable energy and operational flexibility of the FIP are significantly enhanced.

title: Sustainable reuse of floral waste for incense stick production: Formulation optimization, emission profiling, and microstructural assessment
abstract: The global increase in floral waste from religious, cultural, and commercial use presents major environmental challenges due to poor disposal. In India, this issue is more severe, with urban temples and ceremonies generating large amounts of organic waste. Recognizing the untapped potential of this biodegradable material, the present study proposes a sustainable reuse pathway by converting floral waste into incense sticks. Five distinct formulations were developed by varying the proportions of flower powder, sawdust, coal dust, and jigat as a natural binder. These samples: 1 to 5 (as described in Table 3) underwent comprehensive evaluation based on moisture content, burning time, essential oil absorption, particulate emissions (PM10 and PM2.5) emissions, ash pH, and microstructural behavior using FESEM and EDS. However, existing studies predominantly focus on qualitative feasibility, leaving a critical knowledge gap regarding how filler-specific microstructures govern solid-state combustion kinetics, particulate emission factors (EF), and bulk chemical safety. Addressing this gap, the results revealed that Sample-3 (Table 3), composed of floral powder and sawdust, exhibited the lowest particulate emissions, indicating lower emission potential and improved relative combustion cleanliness under the tested conditions. Sample-1 (Table 3) demonstrated effective fragrance retention and consistent burn profile due to its high floral content. Elemental analyses (EDS/XRF) were conducted. While EDS spot analysis confirmed a primary C + O composition, a more robust, quantitative XRF analysis of the bulk raw materials revealed that the coal powder contained 0.0293 mass% Lead Oxide (PbO), a toxic heavy metal not detected in the floral or sawdust fillers. This provides a chemical basis, in addition to the emission results, for recommending the substitution of coal. Comparative analysis revealed that performance was highly dependent on formulation. The coal-free Sample 3 (Table 3) significantly outperformed the commercial control in terms of PM10 emissions factor (0.97 vs. 1.22 mg/stick), while Sample 1 (Table 3) was comparable. However, formulations containing coal dust resulted in higher emission factors than the commercial product. Thus, Sample 3 emerges as a promising low-emission alternative under the evaluated parameters. Grounded in the principles of Cleaner Production and the Circular Economy, this study develops and tests a conceptual model linking waste material properties (e.g., porosity, carbon content) to formulation, combustion performance, and emission profiles. Specifically, it demonstrates how the physicochemical properties of floral waste and additives influence combustion efficiency, emission reduction, and potential community adoption. Future studies should explore real-world factors like ventilation, large-scale production, and user feedback. Recommendations include replacing coal dust with cleaner binders, establish community floral waste collection, and move toward pilot-scale production. This supports waste management and advances circular economy through eco-friendly, culturally meaningful incense products.

title: Exergy loss distribution and guided optimization of cold storage packed bed for liquid air energy storage
abstract: Cold storage packed bed filled with solid particles is widely used in liquid air energy storage (LAES) systems. Its exergy efficiency has a significant effect on the system performance. During operation, the packed bed experiences charging, storage and discharging processes, which lead to exergy loss because of convection, conduction and environmental heat dissipation. It is not clear how the exergy loss distributes in the above processes, thus limiting exergy efficiency optimization. To address the above issues, this study develops an exergy loss distribution model for the cold storage packed bed in a commercial-scale LAES system (50 MW/200 MWh). It is found that convective exergy loss is dominant, accounting for 71.92% of the total exergy loss, which is closely related to parameters of solid particles. Thus, thermophysical properties of solid particles are studied and an exergy efficiency map is established, where the optimized properties are identified at an average thermal conductivity of 0.73 W/(m·K) and an average volumetric heat capacity of 0.91 MJ/(m3·K). Under this condition, convective exergy loss is concentrated in the middle region of the packed bed, corresponding to 25%-75% of the bed height. Therefore, particle diameters are optimized with smaller particles (0.01 m) arranged in this middle region and larger particles (0.02 m) in the top and bottom regions. Finally, exergy efficiency of the cold storage packed bed is significantly improved from 95.1% to 96.3%. These results provide direct guidance for performance improvement of the cold storage packed bed in the LAES applications.

title: Life-cycle modeling of integrated agro-industrial and urban waste biorefineries in Brazil
abstract: The shift toward a low-carbon circular economy requires transforming conventional wastewater and solid waste treatment systems into integrated biorefineries capable of recovering value-added products. Participatory approaches address the complexity of this transition by leveraging stakeholder expertise to guide the selection of feedstocks, technologies, and products suitable for integration into biorefinery systems. This study proposes a novel conceptual biorefinery design developed through participatory workshops and the collaborative process mapping of 33 Brazilian research initiatives focused on agro-industrial and urban-source wastewater and waste streams. The analysis reveals a multi-product landscape dominated by low-value energy outputs, primarily generating biogas, methane, hydrogen, and syngas, followed by medium-value-added products, including volatile fatty acids, fertilizers, and biochar. Conversely, high-value bioproducts (polyhydroxyalkanoates, lactic acid, acetic acid, γ-valerolactone, mycelium-based materials) were identified less frequently. Based on this analysis, seven conceptual integrated biorefinery scenarios originating from local agro-industrial sectors and urban environmental services were proposed by combining: (i) feedstock-based integration, clustering by-products originating from the same production chain and functionally similar wastes from different sources within defined sectors; (ii) technological integration, emphasizing mass/energy integration and process intensification; and (iii) product integration, utilizing a value-oriented cascading logic and zero-waste principles. Finally, although no quantitative Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was performed, the study presents preliminary LCA modeling for a multifunctional scenario, with decision-support criteria and thresholds for constructing integrated biorefinery scenarios, providing practical guidelines for future multi-product life cycle modeling of these conceptual configurations through a scenario-based application of a five-step LCA decision framework.

title: In-situ CO2 injection driven redirection of early reaction pathways for Pb solidification in gold tailings using solid waste based binder
abstract: Long-term immobilization of Pb in tailings is essential for their safe disposal and resource utilization. Previous studies have demonstrated that CO2-assisted stabilization can improve heavy metal immobilization; however, existing studies have mainly focused on macroscopic leaching behavior and carbonation products, while the role of CO2 in affecting the early reaction pathway and molecular-level mechanism of heavy metal immobilization remains unclear. Therefore, clarifying how CO2 alters Pb transformation pathways during the initial hydration stage is critical for achieving stable and sustainable tailings solidification. In this study, a solid waste-based binder composed of steel slag, coal gasification slag, and phosphogypsum was used to immobilize Pb in gold tailings. CO2 was introduced directly into the fresh slurry during mixing to regulate the early hydration environment. Time-resolved leaching and BCR extraction, multiscale characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics combined with well-tempered metadynamics were used to resolve the Pb immobilization pathway. In-situ CO2 injection reduced Pb leaching throughout curing. At 7 d, the Pb leaching concentration of the CO2-treated specimen was 6.94 μg/L, compared with 9.83 μg/L for the control. The stable F4 fraction increased from 65.32% at 1 d to 97.49% at 180 d in the CO2-treated system, exceeding the corresponding final value of 88.47% in the control. Without CO2, early Pb immobilization was dominated by Pb-OOH coordination and Pb(OH)2 precipitation. With CO2 injection, HCO3− primarily modified the Ca-associated local environment and reduced the free-energy barrier for Pb-OSi coordination, promoting the earlier formation of Pb-containing silicate structures. Pb subsequently passed through a transient Fe-O-Pb-associated environment before becoming structurally locked within a highly polymerized silicate gel network. CO2 injection also enhanced silicate polymerization, refined the pore structure, and increased the unconfined compressive strength from 1.44 MPa at 1 d to 8.21 MPa at 180 d, compared with 0.84 and 6.33 MPa for the control, respectively. These findings demonstrate that CO2 primarily acts as an early reaction-pathway regulator under the investigated conditions, enabling earlier and more stable Pb immobilization while improving the mechanical performance of the solidified tailings.

title: Improving ferrous bioavailability with Fe3O4/CNTs carriers to bolster multi-pathway nitrogen removal by anammox consortia
abstract: Iron, particularly ferrous ions (Fe2+), plays a critical role in the metabolic processes of anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) bacteria (AnAOB). However, iron in anammox systems is predominantly present as ferric ions (Fe3+) with low solubility, notwithstanding the physiological preference of AnAOB for soluble Fe2+. Magnetite decorated carbon nanotube (Fe3O4/CNTs) composite carriers were successfully synthesized in this study, through which a sustained and stable release of Fe2+ was achieved. Experimental results demonstrated that the enrichment of AnAOB was significantly promoted by Fe-C composite carriers, leading to enhanced nitrogen removal performance and augmented resistance to shock loading in the reactor. Compared to the group supplemented with Fe3O4 alone, the relative abundance of AnAOB and the nitrogen removal efficiency in the experimental group were increased by 39% and 18%, respectively. Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses further revealed that the expression levels of genes associated with nitrogen metabolism (e.g., hzs, hdh, nirKS, and narGHI) were significantly up-regulated by the introduction of Fe3O4/CNTs. Concurrently, multi-pathway Fe-N coupling processes, specifically encompassing dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) and nitrate-dependent Fe(Ⅱ) oxidation (NDFO), were facilitated by this intervention, thereby constructing a more sophisticated and efficient nitrogen transformation network. This study reveals that Fe3O4/CNTs drive the remodeling of iron nitrogen metabolic networks within anammox consortia by augmenting iron bioavailability, implying the pivotal role of such metabolic synergies in reinforcing functional resilience and bolstering the technical feasibility of advanced anammox processes for large scale engineering applications.

title: Green technological innovation and urban–rural inequality: Nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous evidence from the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: Green technological innovation (GTI) is an important driving force for cleaner production and sustainable transition, yet its innovation resources and transition benefits are not necessarily evenly distributed between urban and rural areas or among cities. Using 2011–2021 data from 41 cities in the Yangtze River Delta, this study constructs a GTI indicator system comprising support, development, and spatial diffusion dimensions, and measures urban–rural income inequality using the Theil index. Integrating CatBoost–SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), the two-way fixed-effects spatial Durbin model, and its restricted cubic spline extension, this study identifies the predictive contributions, average spatial associations, and stage-dependent nonlinear associations of multidimensional GTI. Results show that urban–rural income inequality declined by 43.1% during the study period, while significant spatial dependence persisted, with a baseline spatial autoregressive parameter of ρ = 0.587 and higher inequality concentrated in some peripheral cities. Local GTI features and neighbouring-city GTI exposure jointly account for 64.84% of the total mean absolute SHAP contribution. GPA is the most important feature and, together with science and technology expenditure intensity (STE) and photovoltaic deployment intensity (PV), shows that increases from relatively low levels are associated with declines in urban–rural income inequality, followed by weakening marginal associations. Contribution transitions occur at 6.36–9.90 applications/100 km2 for GPA, 1.94% for STE, and 0.382–1.322 (×104) for PV. Among the spatial-lag features, neighbouring-city energy-conservation and environmental-protection expenditure intensity and GPA exposure show contribution transitions at approximately 2.99% and 10.18 applications/100 km2, respectively. Local and neighbouring-city stage-dependent patterns are not always aligned, with PV showing the most pronounced divergence. These findings indicate that improving green innovation capacity and sharing green-transition benefits are interrelated but not equivalent, supporting differentiated governance that accounts for development stage and spatial context. The integrated framework provides city-scale evidence of multidimensional, stage-dependent, and spatially heterogeneous associations between the cleaner production transition and urban–rural inequality.

title: GIS-based multi-criteria assessment of CO2 storage suitability in deep saline aquifers: A case study of the southern Songliao Basin
abstract: The IPCC AR6 confirms that human activities are the unequivocal cause of global warming, driven mainly by the sharp increase in atmospheric CO2. As natural carbon sinks are losing their capacity to absorb CO2, CO2 storage has become a critical strategy to stabilize global temperatures. Deep saline aquifers, with the largest theoretical storage capacity, are the most promising option for large-scale CO2 storage. However, safety, efficiency, and economics depend on site-specific geology, making systematic site-suitability assessment essential. Existing assessment methods often rely on deterministic zoning and insufficiently quantify uncertainties associated with evaluation criteria and model parameters. To address this limitation, this study focuses on the central depression of the Songliao Basin, integrating GIS spatial analysis with multicriteria decision-making methods. The framework integrates AHP for indicator weighting, FCE for multi-source suitability fusion, and Monte Carlo simulation for uncertainty quantification. The proposed approach generates continuous suitability maps and separately quantifies uncertainties arising from fuzzy membership assignments and weighting schemes. The results indicate that most of the study area exhibits moderate to high storage suitability, with highly suitable regions mainly concentrated in the HGT and CLS units. The estimated regional CO2 storage capacity is approximately 5.55 × 109 t under baseline conditions and increases to 1.28 × 1010 t under a high-efficiency storage scenario. Comparison with existing CCUS project locations further demonstrates the practical applicability of the assessment results. This study provides a transferable methodology for uncertainty-aware CO2 storage suitability assessment in complex geological settings and supports safe storage deployment for climate mitigation.

title: Optimizing textile supply chains for a sustainable transition to a circular economy
abstract: The continuous rise in living standards has led to a significant increase in textile consumption, creating major challenges in textile waste management and recycling. Although existing research has largely focused on technological innovations, limited attention has been given to integrated optimization approaches that simultaneously address economic, social, and environmental dimensions. To bridge this gap, this study develops a generic Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) model for strategic and tactical planning in multi-echelon direct and reverse textile supply chains. The proposed framework is sector-specific to the textile industry but designed to be region-independent and adaptable to different geographical contexts. The model explicitly incorporates recovery and recycling processes for both pre- and post-consumer products, aiming to minimize total system costs while reducing environmental impacts. To manage computational complexity and embed sustainability-driven criteria, two hybrid Genetic Algorithm heuristics are developed and combined with the ELECTRE III multi-criteria decision analysis method and an exact Branch-and-Cut procedure. Computational experiments conducted on representative instances demonstrate that GA-Hybrid 1 achieves solutions within 1.05% of the optimal cost, with emission deviations below 2%, while significantly reducing computation time compared to CPLEX for medium and large-scale instances. Additionally, GA-Hybrid 2 generates diverse Pareto-optimal trade-offs, with cost increases ranging from 0.1% to 26% and emission reductions reaching nearly 19%, thereby providing decision-makers with a structured spectrum of cost-emission compromises. These results confirm the practical relevance and scalability of the proposed generic framework for supporting collaborative and sustainable textile supply chain design. Beyond managerial implications, the study contributes to the advancement of large-scale multi-criteria optimization and life-cycle-oriented sustainability assessment in circular supply chain systems.

title: Life cycle optimization of an off-grid waste-to-energy-renewable-methanol coupled system considering economic-environmental trade-offs
abstract: Integrating waste-to-energy (WtE) with variable renewable energy and power-to-methanol technologies offers a promising pathway for waste valorization and low carbon fuel production. This study develops a high-fidelity life-cycle optimization (LCO) framework for an off-grid WtE-renewable-methanol coupled system by integrating Aspen Plus simulation, mixed-integer linear programming, and 18 midpoint indicators from ReCiPe 2016 (H). The framework jointly optimizes capacity allocation and representative daily dispatch for four regions in China under four weighting scenarios. Results show that the LCO framework captures region-specific configuration pathways and weighting-driven structural shifts in energy supply and buffering layers. The optimized systems achieve life-cycle emissions of 0.539-0.801 kg CO2 eq./kg MeOH and levelized costs of 438.2-644.6 $/t MeOH. Regional resource endowments strongly shape system design, with Inner Mongolia being wind dominated and most cost competitive, Guangdong relying on photovoltaic generation with higher flexibility needs, Xinjiang requiring stronger thermal and carbon buffering despite abundant resources, and Jiangsu exhibiting greater capacity redundancy under moderate resource conditions. Increasing environmental weightings reduces reliance on photovoltaic generation and electrochemical storage while favoring wind power, WtE, and thermal or material storage. Notably, the climate-priority scenario reduces climate impacts but aggravates toxicity, resource depletion, and air pollution, revealing environmental burden shifting, whereas the environment-priority scenario delivers the most balanced performance. These results highlight LCO as a robust decision-support tool for regional green methanol system planning.

title: Spatially explicit assessment of seawater intrusion in urbanized coastal aquifers using an integrated geophysical-hydrochemical approach
abstract: Seawater intrusion (SWI) poses a persistent threat to coastal groundwater sustainability, compromising freshwater resources and ecosystem health. An integrated assessment framework was developed to enable high-resolution, spatially explicit SWI mapping, overcoming the limitations of sparse monitoring networks and the interpretative ambiguity of standalone geophysical methods. Combining area-wide electrical resistivity tomography (25 profiles), dense vertical electrical sounding (340 points), and co-located hydrochemical sampling (46 sites) in the urbanized coastal zone of Northern Jiaozhou Bay, China, we established quantitative relationships between groundwater salinity and resistivity-derived parameters. These were synthesized into a novel Hierarchical Weighting Model for SWI (HWMSWI) to generate continuous SWI severity maps. Results from the HWMSWI framework show that over 47% of the area is severely affected by saline groundwater, with freshwater confined to elevated bedrock zones. Critically, surface water networks were spatially associated with inland seawater migration, consistent with prior process-level evidence, suggesting that they may function as conduits and highlighting a potentially overlooked salinization pathway in urbanized coasts. The HWMSWI framework provides a data-efficient tool for spatially explicit SWI assessment. Transferable as a workflow and weighting logic, the framework requires site-specific calibration of its empirical relationships and thresholds. It supports targeted monitoring and mitigation strategies that align with cleaner production principles by optimizing resource use and preventing further groundwater quality degradation in vulnerable coastal zones worldwide.

title: Smart carbon capture: Leveraging LSTM networks for hourly CO2 flow prediction in an industrial stack of a CO2 recovery plant
abstract: Efficient performance prediction of CO2 stack gas recovery plants is crucial for optimizing greenhouse gas mitigation strategies. This study introduces a novel Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network model for the real-time forecasting of CO2 product flow in an industrial amine-based Carbon Dioxide Recovery (CDR) plant-addressing a significant gap in the application of deep sequential learning to real-world carbon capture operations. Using a high-dimensional, real-world dataset of 4582 hourly records spanning 54 operational parameters from a plant in Iran, a Pearson correlation-based feature selection method was engineered to identify and retain the 39 most influential process variables. The optimized LSTM architecture-configured with two layers, 200 neurons per layer, and the ADAM optimizer-was trained on 4125 data points and validated on 457 subsequent hours. The model demonstrated strong predictive accuracy, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 88.9 kg/h, root mean squared error (RMSE) of 115.97 kg/h, and a determination coefficient (R2) of 0.87. Key findings confirm the model's capability to capture temporal dynamics under normal operating conditions, though performance diminishes during unscheduled plant failures. This work establishes a practical, data-driven LSTM framework for real-time monitoring and predictive control of CO2 recovery systems, offering a scalable tool for digital twin integration and operational optimization in industrial carbon capture.

title: Environmental labeling in food services: Which strategy is the most effective?
abstract: Food prepared outside the home accounts for a significant portion of food-related greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. However, consumers have little information about the GHG emissions associated with their food choices. Environmental labels and information schemes (ELIS) could be a lever for steering these choices toward environmentally sustainable options. This experimental study examines the effectiveness of six types of ELIS formats (1 informative, 1 contextual, 2 interpretive, and 2 mixed) featured on restaurant menu cards. A hypothetical choice task experiment was designed to assess consumers' response to two successive choice tasks: without information and with general information (control) or with one of the 6 ELIS signaling the environmental sustainability of either separate dish options or a set table d'hôte. 2808 Canadian respondents were randomly assigned to one of the 14 experimental groups (2 contexts × 7 information conditions). All ELIS formats significantly increased the likelihood of choosing a meal with a lower environmental impact, although individual-level choice changes remained only partially explained. Mixed formats, combining visual elements and numerical data, were the most effective, in terms of shifting choices toward meals with a lower environmental impact and in terms of reduction in GHG emissions. By comparing six ELIS formats within a single experimental framework, this study provides novel empirical evidence on the relative effectiveness of environmental labeling strategies in food service settings. These results suggest that mixed formats could be integrated as tools in public policy or food service differentiation strategies to promote more environmentally sustainable eating. However, future research in real-world conditions is needed to confirm these effects.

title: Integration of geothermal energy in RO desalination plant: Flexible design meeting variable water demand with cleaning and maintenance schedule
abstract: Desalination technologies are being used to meet the world's growing demand for freshwater but are extremely energy intensive whether it is a thermal or a membrane based process. As global fossil fuel-based energy supplies have been going through a turmoil in recent years due to war in several parts of the world, consideration of alternative and renewable energy sources for desalination is extremely important. In this work, potential for low-enthalpy geothermal resources to provide a part of the required energy in a 3-stage Reverse Osmosis (RO) desalination plant to supply freshwater to a population of 40,000 people in the city of El Masdar in UAE is investigated. As the demand for freshwater changes throughout the day and throughout the year, the plant is flexibly designed with storage tanks and also using disconnected pressure vessels (PVs) to be cleaned and serviced (schedule maintenance) throughout the year without the need for shutting down the plant at any time. To prevent the use of enormous storage tanks, RO plant operates to produce minimum excess water at the end of every month allowing cleaning of storage tanks at least once in each month. ASPEN HYSYS software is used to design the Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) plant, which produces 1 MW of electricity using the geothermal field in El-Masdar city with 10% efficiency, which is then used to supply part of the RO plant's electrical demand. The investigation indicates that integrating low-enthalpy geothermal energy in RO plant can decrease dependence on fossil fuels by offsetting the external power required to operate the RO system. The findings showed that geothermal energy can provide considerable offsets of fossil fuel, reaching 28.87% of the required external energy during peak water-demand months and 55% during low water-demand months.

title: Farmers' income increase and environmental win-win: How China's digital industry cluster policies balance economic development with ecological efficiency
abstract: Amid global efforts to achieve both economic revitalization and environmental sustainability, China's implementation of the Digital Industry Cluster Policy (DICP) presents a novel pathway for integrating digital transformation with rural development. However, it remains unclear whether such industrial policies, though not directly targeting agriculture, can generate inclusive economic benefits for farmers while enhancing agricultural ecological efficiency. This study investigates the dual impact of DICP using a multi-period difference-in-differences spatial Durbin model (DID-SDM) based on panel data from 273 counties between 2007 and 2023. Empirical results reveal that the policy significantly increases farmers' income and improves ecological efficiency, with total effects of 0.600 and 0.230, respectively. Mechanism analysis identifies non-agricultural employment and agricultural digitalization as key mediators, while spatial analysis uncovers heterogeneous, distance-decaying spillover patterns across the two outcomes: positive income spillovers attenuate with distance and turn negative beyond approximately 500 km, indicating a spatial redistribution of resources from distant regions toward policy-targeted areas, whereas ecological spillovers decay toward zero within roughly 400 km without turning negative. These findings advance theoretical understanding by integrating Lewis's dual economy theory and the Environmental Kuznets Curve into a unified spatial framework, offering actionable insights for aligning digital policy design with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially in balancing growth with green transformation at the local level.

title: Zero-residue valorization of chrysotile asbestos tailings via oxygen-free NaOH roasting: Stepwise recovery of SiO2 and MgO with chromium stabilization
abstract: Chrysotile asbestos tailings contain abundant silicon and magnesium resources. Existing extraction processes mainly focus on the efficient recovery of silicon and magnesium, yet they often cause the oxidation of Cr(III) to Cr(VI) and the co-dissolution of metal impurities, reducing product purity and producing secondary residues. Herein, this study developed a stepwise clean separation process via oxygen-free NaOH roasting-water leaching. Under an oxygen-free atmosphere, the oxidation of Cr(III) to highly toxic Cr(VI) is effectively suppressed during alkali roasting. Meanwhile, silicate minerals react with NaOH to form soluble sodium silicates (Na4SiO4 and Na2MgSiO4) and insoluble periclase. During water leaching, sodium silicates dissolve while Cr(III) and Fe(III) species reprecipitate as hydroxides under strong alkaline conditions, enabling selective silicon extraction. Under optimized conditions (750 °C, 60 min, Na2O/SiO2 molar ratio of 2.25, liquid-to-solid ratio of 8 mL/g), the SiO2 leaching efficiency reaches 93.59% with an ultra-high filtrate purity of 99.96%, while the leaching efficiencies of Cr and Fe are 4.74% and 0.09%, respectively. The magnesium-rich residue is subsequently subjected to selective acid leaching, achieving 85.55% Mg2+ recovery with 98.96% purity, and leaving an iron-rich residue suitable for ironmaking feedstock. These results demonstrate that atmosphere control can suppress Cr(III) oxidation while maintaining efficient silicate activation, thereby integrating Cr stabilization with the stepwise selective recovery of SiO2 and MgO. This work provides a new route for the full-component and zero-residue valorization of chrysotile asbestos tailings.

title: Optimization of filter bag structure for metal dust removal system based on multi-physical field simulation of high-temperature flue gas
abstract: High-temperature flue gas from aluminum smelting carries ultrafine metal dust featuring high chemical reactivity and explosion risk, which imposes critical challenges to the efficient and safe operation of pulse-jet baghouse systems. This study develops a gas-solid two-phase multi-physics coupled model incorporating high-temperature corrections for non-spherical particle dynamics and full-mode heat-mass transfer. The independent and coupled effects of pipeline velocity, dust concentration, and flue gas temperature on comprehensive performance are systematically investigated via computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The global optimal operating condition is identified using entropy weight-grey relational analysis (EW-GRA). Furthermore, a hybrid multi-objective optimization framework integrating orthogonal test, response surface methodology (RSM), and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) with an elite retention strategy is developed for filter bag structural parameter optimization. Results show the influence ranking: flue gas temperature > dust concentration > pipeline velocity. The globally optimal operating condition is determined as a pipeline flow velocity of 24 m/s, dust concentration of 500 mg/m3, and flue gas temperature of 523 K, while the optimal filter bag configuration is length 1405 mm, diameter 580 mm, and thickness 3.5 mm. Post-optimization, dust removal efficiency reaches 99.02% (＋1.22%), system pressure loss drops to 1228 Pa (−12.41%), and velocity standard deviation and bag temperature difference decrease by 91.54% and 81.89%, respectively. This work provides theoretical support and quantitative technical guidelines for the design and operational optimization of high-temperature dust removal systems in the aluminum smelting industry.

title: Beyond compliance: How sustainability assurance achieves value creation under resource scarcity
abstract: Sustainability assurance serves as a critical measure to alleviate resource and environmental constraints. However, how it facilitates value creation remains underexplored. Compared to the extensive literature on financial auditing, scholarly work dedicated to sustainability assurance is notably sparse. Using a sample of A-share listed companies from 2014 to 2025, this paper examines how sustainability assurance achieves value creation under resource scarcity. The results show that: (1) Sustainability assurance plays a significant role in promoting corporate value creation and serves as a vital tool for resource allocation. (2) Investor confidence partially mediates the relationship between sustainability assurance and corporate value creation, and financing constraints positively moderate this relationship. (3) Further analysis finds that if sustainability assurance entities are certified public accounting (CPA) firms, or sustainability assurance and financial statement auditing are conducted by the same entity, the effect of sustainability assurance on corporate value creation is more pronounced, and sustainability assurance plays a more significant role in promoting corporate value creation among high-risk enterprises. This paper offers policy insights and empirical support for enhancing sustainability assurance, boosting investor confidence, alleviating financing constraints, and achieving corporate value creation.

title: Multidimensional energy poverty assessment and behavioral scenarios: An interpretable analytics approach
abstract: Energy poverty is a multidimensional socioeconomic and sustainability challenge that extends beyond affordability to include inadequate thermal comfort, limited access to energy services, and adverse health and well-being effects. This study examines how multidimensional energy-poverty assessment can be integrated with interpretable analytics to identify household vulnerability drivers and explore the model-based implications of changes in selected behavioral practices. The framework is applied to pilot survey data from households in Portugal and Denmark. An adapted multidimensional energy poverty index (MEPI) is constructed using four dimensions: heating and cooling comfort, financial strain, access to energy-efficient appliances, and health and well-being. The resulting MEPI-based classification is then linked to socioeconomic, behavioral, dwelling-related, and policy-related predictors through recursive feature elimination with cross-validation, logistic regression, and the Shapley additive explanations. Robustness is examined through regularized-model comparisons, repeated cross-validation, calibration assessment, and country-held-out validation. Energy-saving beliefs, power-saving practices, and selected resource-efficient behaviors are associated with lower predicted energy-poverty vulnerability, whereas larger household size and reported policy or subsidy support are associated with higher predicted risk. The latter may reflect support being targeted towards households already experiencing vulnerability. Exploratory scenarios indicate that hypothetical increases in several negatively associated behavioral practices correspond to lower model-predicted energy-poverty prevalence, although the uncertainty intervals are wide and the results noncausal. The study contributes an integrated workflow for multidimensional identification, transparent driver analysis, and exploratory behavioral scenario assessment. Despite the limited pilot sample, the framework supports the development of policy hypotheses for testing in larger and more representative datasets.

title: Forecasting Sustainable Development Goals scores through the vulnerability–resilience framework: A global income group analysis
abstract: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for integrated, forward-looking analysis that goes beyond retrospective monitoring to examine the structural conditions shaping future trajectories. This study proposes a framework that combines vulnerability-resilience diagnostics with time-series forecasting and scenario-based simulation to analyze SDG Index dynamics across four World Bank income groups from 2000 to 2024 and project trajectories to 2030. Composite Vulnerability and Resilience Indices are constructed from 98 normalized SDG sub-indicators, with the Resilience Index decomposed into hard (physical and infrastructure capacity) and soft (institutional, social, and innovation capacity) sub-dimensions. Both indices show strong correlations with the overall SDG Index (−0.961 and +0.994, respectively) with robustness confirmed across five alternative weighting methods. Forecast performance is evaluated using rolling-origin walk-forward cross-validation. ARIMAX is retained as the primary structural model, while Holt and Linear Regression-Holt smoothing serve as complementary trend benchmarks. Under the ARIMAX business-as-usual baseline, projected 2030 scores range from approximately 78.4 for high-income to 49.4 for low-income countries, with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests confirming that all income-group distributions remain statistically distinct throughout the projection period. Elasticity analysis shows that the vulnerability-resilience framework accounts for more than 99 percent of within-group SDG variation. Scenario-based sensitivity analysis shows that vulnerability reduction yields the largest modeled SDG gains across all income groups, with marginal SDG gains of approximately 0.22 points per 1% reduction for upper-middle-income countries and 0.15 points per 1% reduction for lower-middle-income countries. For low-income countries, positive gains from both vulnerability reduction and resilience improvement support a dual-intervention approach. These findings support differentiated, income-group-specific policy recommendations grounded directly in the empirical results.

title: International trade redistributes global nitrous oxide emissions and responsibility patterns
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance, yet existing assessments remain dominated by production-based accounting (PBA), obscuring the role of consumption in global supply chains and potentially masking emission outsourcing and apparent mitigation. Therefore, we develop a long-term consumption-based assessment of global N2O emissions from 1995 to 2020 that jointly tracks trade-embodied emission flows, production–consumption responsibility asymmetries, decoupling patterns, and their underlying structural drivers. This integrated framework enables us to examine how changing global supply chains reshape the spatial distribution of N2O emissions, mitigation responsibility, and the balance between efficiency improvements and consumption-driven emission growth. N2O emissions increased by 25.8%, while trade-embodied emissions grew faster, reaching 36.9% of total emissions in 2020. Embodied N2O flows exhibited a dual restructuring: the traditional South-to-North responsibility asymmetry persisted, while South-South transfers expanded rapidly and became increasingly concentrated around major emerging-economy corridors, particularly the Brazil–China linkage. Divergences between PBA and CBA indicate a growing spatial separation between where emissions are generated and where the associated consumption occurs. Meanwhile, reductions in emission intensity failed to offset demand growth. These findings call for a shift in N2O governance from territorial emission control toward global consumption responsibility, linking nitrogen mitigation to trade justice and environmental equity.

title: Structural vulnerability and operational adaptation: Insights from ecological network analysis of China's chromium supply chain security
abstract: The key mineral chromium is a core feedstock for stainless steel production and irreplaceable in modern industry. China is the world's largest importer and consumer of chromium, with a 99% import dependence on chromite. Global chromium market fluctuations can have a strong impact on China's domestic supply chain. Currently, rising geopolitical tensions and U.S.-China trade frictions have further amplified supply chain security risks, making it critical to evaluate China's chromium supply chain security. Therefore, this research applies ecological network analysis (ENA) to assess the structural and operational dynamics of China's chromium supply chain from 2000 to 2023 to provide policy-relevant evidence for maintaining supply stability and strengthening supply chain security. The research results show that: (1) Structurally, China's chromium supply chain exhibits high sensitivity to policy shifts in core chromium-associated countries. The ENA system of China's chromium supply chain is dominated by competitive inter-compartment relationships, with persistently weakening indirect effects, low complexity, and limited internal connectivity, driving rising systemic vulnerability. (2) Operationally, the expansion of China's chromium supply chain has contributed to an enhancement in its overall stability. Over time, there has been an improvement and stabilization in the alignment between resource availability and the system's capacity. (3) Scenario analysis shows that supply and demand contractions alter inter-compartment competitive dynamics and reduce system synergy, and that balancing supply and demand does not always yield positive system outcomes. Based on these findings, this paper proposes policy recommendations including: implementing precise and balanced supply, elevating the strategic status of secondary chromium, promoting collaborative governance across the industrial chain, and advancing follow-up research on the chromium supply chain.

title: Coupling effect of stress and dry-wet cycles on self-healing performance of geopolymer cutoff wall backfills incorporating microcapsules
abstract: Cutoff walls are widely used to prevent lateral migration of contaminated groundwater in geoenvironmental applications. The change in hydraulic conductivity (kw) due to dry-wet cycles (DWC) has been recognized as a long-term performance concern for cutoff walls. Most existing laboratory methods are unable to maintain stress effects during continuous DWC processes, which limits accurately assessing kw of cutoff wall backfills. This work developed an experimental apparatus to reproduce the coupling effect of stress and DWC on the microcapsule self-healing cutoff wall backfill (MSHCWB). Supplementary crack closure observations under unstressed condition were also conducted. The microstructural characteristics were measured by X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Computed Tomography (CT). MSHCWB exhibited promising self-healing capability, achieving over 50% crack width reduction and up to 236.71% improvement in crack closure rate after 28 days of healing. Under the axial stress of 150 kPa, the kw of MSHCWB containing 8% microcapsules remained below 1 × 10−9 m/s after ten DWC. The microcapsule structure, whether single-walled or double-walled, had little effect on the kw under higher axial stress. The axial stress reduced the pore space and decreased the seepage path to enhance impermeability, while higher stress level also positively contributed to microcapsule rupture and the self-healing process. The empirical function of kw with respect to the cycle number and axial stress was further proposed. The axial stress substantially influences the variation magnitude of kw during the DWC, which requires consideration in cutoff wall design.

title: Synergistic water regulation and byproduct confinement in non-woven fabric-encapsulated Al@MgH2 for controlled hydrogen generation via parallel and sequential reactor designs
abstract: Active Al-based composite hydrolysis for hydrogen production holds broad application prospects in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, key challenges such as controllability of hydrogen production, byproduct recovery, and hydrogen purity still need to be addressed. This study tackles these issues by designing a non-woven fabric-encapsulated hydrogen production unit and two hydrolysis reactors. This unit consists of a non-woven fabric envelope and an internal Al@30 % MgH2 block. The regular pore structure of the non-woven fabric regulates water mass transfer and confines byproducts. This leads to effective control of hydrogen production, enhanced solution utilization, and one-step byproduct recovery. The parallel and sequential hydrogen production reactors were designed according to the hydrolysis characteristics of the encapsulated unit. The flow paths of the reaction solution were controlled accordingly. Under low solution flow rate conditions, the parallel reactor achieved a stable hydrogen generation rate (sHGR) of 1.36 mL s−1 over 3573 s. The measured total hydrogen generation was 4579 mL. In contrast, the sequential reactor maintained a sHGR of 0.84 mL s−1 over 5177 s. The measured total hydrogen generation was 4448 mL. Purity tests confirmed that the hydrogen purity exceeded 99.2 %. This study combines physical encapsulation, solution injection strategy, and reactor design. This integrated approach overcomes the explosive reaction of active powders, achieves tunable hydrolysis kinetics, and provides a practical pathway from laboratory to application.

title: The impact of international technology investment on carbon emissions: Global evidence
abstract: Despite international technology investment emerging as a key feature of the globalizing world, its impact on global carbon emissions has yet to attract attention. Using a compiled dataset of international technology investment deals, this study examines the spatiotemporal patterns of international technology investment and the corresponding carbon-emission-reduction performance from 1998 to 2023. Our findings demonstrate that an increase in international technology investment transactions contributes to reductions in carbon emissions globally, in both the home and host countries. However, in a subsample analysis, we found that the carbon-emission-reduction performance of international technology investment is closely related to the level of national development. Although transactions in advanced economies have achieved greater reductions in carbon emissions, those in non-advanced economies have not yet optimized their carbon emissions, since the emission-increasing scale effect of production expansion outweighs and dominates the energy-saving technique effect in non-advanced economies. Further research shows that technology investments from advanced economies into non-advanced economies weaken host countries’ emission-reduction performance. In contrast, transactions from non-advanced to advanced economies enhance the host countries' abatement results but weaken mitigation efforts in their home countries. This result tentatively suggests that advanced economies hold a relatively advantageous position in cross-border carbon governance associated with technology investment. Based on the analyses in this paper, we emphasize the need for advanced economies to assume greater responsibility in global environmental governance, while suggesting that non-advanced economies consider adopting environmental taxation frameworks.

title: Coastal bird migration exposure as a spatial constraint for wind energy and airports in eastern China
abstract: Bird migration creates collision risks for wind farms and airports, yet many regions lack radar and bird strike data for infrastructure planning. Using eBird checklist data, distance to coast, and weekly reanalysis climate variables, we developed a screening level assessment of migration exposure for eastern China's lowlands, a key segment of the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. Migration intensity was aggregated to 25 km grid cells and weekly periods for spring and autumn 2021–2025. Distance to coast (0–300 km) captured a weak but temporally consistent decline in exposure inland, with negative slopes across all ten migration seasons. At the 25 km weekly resolution used here, the selected weekly climate metrics explained little of the week-to-week variation in the eBird based migration exposure index. We summarized this coastal gradient into simple high- (0–100 km), medium- (100–200 km), and low-exposure (200–300 km) belts for screening-level mapping, providing a transparent migration-exposure map for planners. This distance-based zonation does not provide operational forecasts or calibrated collision-risk estimates but offers a practical, within region screening framework for identifying relative exposure patterns where high-resolution migration and strike datasets are unavailable. By steering new projects away from the highest-exposure coastal belts where feasible, the approach supports cleaner production by helping avoid costly ecological conflicts, retrofits, and operational constraints.

title: Computer-aided ionic liquid design integrated with process parallel computing for enhanced C4 hydrocarbon separation
abstract: The molecular solvent-based extractive distillation used for the separation of 1,3-butadiene from C4 hydrocarbons continues to be challenging due to the presence of multiple azeotropes and close-boiling mixtures. Ionic liquids (ILs) are regarded as promising alternatives, but due to the time-consuming nature of process optimization, only a limited number of IL processes can be evaluated, so ILs with outstanding thermodynamic abilities may still underperform in practical applications. To address this contradiction, this work proposes a novel method integrating computer-aided ILs design with process parallel optimization. It solves a multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model using a sequential strategy, first maximizing the separation selectivity to identify 10 preferred IL structures, and then rapidly minimizing their process costs. The optimization time based on rigorous process models is significantly reduced from 11.32 h in serial mode to 3.83 h in parallel mode. The [MMIM][TFA] exhibits the best process performance, reducing the total annual cost by 44.34% compared to the conventional NMP-water process. Notably, the ranking of thermodynamic selectivity ([HMIM][TFA] ranks highest) is inconsistent with the ranking of the process costs, highlighting that solely pursuing thermodynamic abilities may lead to suboptimal designs at the process level. Furthermore, quantum chemical calculations reveal that the superior separation performance of [MMIM][TFA] for binary C4 mixtures is mainly governed by the combined effect of its stronger electrostatic interactions and dispersion interactions, compared with NMP. This method framework provides an integrated solution for the green separation, spanning from the molecular to the process scale.

title: Robust deployment optimization of flue gas enhanced oil recovery systems under oilfield production uncertainty
abstract: Effective deployment of flue gas enhanced oil recovery (EOR) systems requires coordinated decisions under changing techno-economic conditions and uncertain oilfield production. This study develops an integrated framework for optimizing the deployment of flue gas EOR systems by combining flue gas composition characterization, dynamic forecasting of techno-economic parameters, and two-stage robust optimization. A column-and-constraint generation (CCG) algorithm is employed to solve the model. The results indicate that (1) the proposed model coordinates facility and capacity planning with flue gas allocation, producing deployment plans that remain feasible under worst-case realizations of oilfield production; (2) the CCG algorithm achieves faster convergence and greater computational efficiency than Benders decomposition (BD) while retaining a verifiable optimality guarantee, demonstrating its suitability for larger deployment problems; and (3) compared with conventional CO2-EOR, flue gas EOR reduces the total system cost by approximately 48.3%, while its compression-related cost is 59.0% lower than the capture-related cost of the benchmark system. These findings provide a quantitative and methodological basis for the robust and economically efficient deployment of flue gas EOR systems under uncertain operating conditions.

title: Additive-free microwave co-pyrolysis of polyethylene and sewage sludge for cleaner waste valorization and energy recovery
abstract: This study evaluated the additive-free microwave co-pyrolysis of commercial polyethylene packaging bag waste (PEB) and municipal sewage sludge (SS), without externally added microwave absorbers or commercial catalysts. In this study, conventional pyrolysis (CP) and microwave pyrolysis (MWP) of PEB and PEB + SS were systematically compared at 400-800 °C in terms of product distribution, gas and liquid composition, char functional groups, and energy extraction. For PEB, MWP resulted in a markedly different apparent low-temperature conversion behavior compared with CP. At 400 °C, the liquid-tar yield reached 71.3% under MWP, whereas CP retained 92.6% solid residue. After SS addition, MWP-PEB + SS showed a more pronounced redistribution of products than CP-PEB + SS. The observed increase in liquid yield and the changes in gas composition suggest that the polar organic matter, retained water, and inorganic constituents in SS may contribute to microwave-assisted conversion and product regulation, thereby facilitating PEB-SS conversion. At 800 °C, MWP-PEB + SS achieved a liquid tar yield of 60.3% with an HHV of 21.95 MJ/kg. Meanwhile, the gas composition shifted from hydrocarbon-rich products toward H2/CO-enriched gas, which was consistent with possible reforming-related pathways. Energy extraction analysis further demonstrated that MWP-PEB + SS at 800 °C was the most favorable microwave co-pyrolysis condition, achieving a product energy recovery efficiency of 64.02%, with liquid tar serving as the dominant energy carrier. Overall, this study indicates that SS may reduce the dependence on external microwave absorbers and commercial catalysts by providing intrinsic microwave-responsive and reaction-regulating components. This additive-free strategy may simplify solid-residue management and provide a cleaner-production-oriented route for converting mixed solid wastes into energy-dense liquid products and H2/CO-enriched gas.

title: A Bayesian Network-based non-deterministic optimization model for planning climate-resilient and low-carbon power systems: A case study of Nova Scotia, Canada
abstract: Extreme events such as hurricanes pose challenges to clean power system planning. Existing studies rarely jointly manage the interactive relationships among uncertain climate, socioeconomic, and environmental risks. To address this gap, this study develops a Bayesian Network-based non-deterministic optimization model that integrates multidimensional risk management with system optimization to support long-term climate-resilient and low-carbon power system planning. The model enables robust decision-making under multiple risks while balancing trade-offs among system resilience, economic costs, and emission mitigation. A case study of Nova Scotia, Canada (2026–2045) demonstrates its applicability in hurricane-prone regions. To evaluate hurricane impacts on system reliability, a system performance loss index (SPL) is developed. Results show that high-intensity hurricanes could increase SPL to 10.69–22.70%, causing 25,847.54–54,891.40 GWh of unavailable supply and C$ 208.22–776.78 million in economic losses. SPL may also rise five-fold to 17.81–37.81% with increased hurricane frequencies. Low-fragility natural gas generation will supply ∼30% of electricity, with its capacity losses roughly one-third of wind generation. Energy storage-based planning would strengthen system resilience and reduce additional emissions of ∼3.42 Mt but comes with high electricity costs, reaching 0.21–6.87 C$/kWh and increasing by 20–50% under high hurricane frequency. In comparison, diversified generation and grid hardening strategies would maintain stable costs within 0.064–0.081 C$/kWh. Therefore, transitioning to a diversified mix of natural gas and renewables with underground lines, supported by cost-feasible storage measures, would offer a balanced climate-resilient strategy. This study provides quantitative insights into climate adaptation-mitigation linkages and identifies cost-effective management plans.

title: Human preference and vegetation features enhance soil carbon sequestration in urban green spaces: implications from soil oxidizable carbon fractionation
abstract: Urban areas drive >70% of global energy CO2 emissions, positioning urban green spaces as critical yet underoptimized nature-based climate solutions. However, coupled effects of human preferences (a proxy for management probability and public use patterns) and multi-layer vegetation on soil organic carbon (SOC) stability remain poorly understood, hindering evidence-based low-carbon urban management. We surveyed 370 subtropical urban forest plots to disentangle drivers of four soil oxidizable carbon fractions: very labile, labile, less labile, and non-labile, covering human preference metrics, vegetation traits, soil nutrients, aggregation and water-holding capacity (total 63 parameters). Redundancy analysis, variation partitioning and partial least squares structural equation modeling revealed: (1) Tall, large-diameter, and low density trees combined with sparse-short herb layers significantly elevated less & non-labile fractions and improved the soil carbon stability, a vegetation structure strongly aligned with high-human-preference areas subject to intensive management near roads; (2) Soil total nitrogen (explaining 28.9% of SOC fraction variation) and glomalin-related soil protein were the dominant direct regulators of carbon accrual, while soil aggregate stability and water-holding capacity acted as core mediators linking vegetation/human factors to SOC dynamics; (3) Human preference mainly exerted indirect effects on SOC and its fractions via regulating soil nutrient availability, physical structure and water-holding capacities. We propose a preference-stratified management framework, and recommend "tall open-canopy trees + sparse herb" configuration at high human preferred regions reconciling recreational demands with long-term carbon sequestration. Our findings highlights that integrating appropriate vegetation and human preferences can enhance soil carbon sequestration—a nature-based pathway toward low-carbon urban transition.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and drivers of vegetation greenness and resilience in China's open-pit coal mines over the past four decades
abstract: Open-pit mining and reclamation directly reshape land surfaces, making vegetation a sensitive remote sensing indicator of ecological dynamics in mining areas. However, most existing assessments focus on vegetation greenness, even though greening does not necessarily imply enhanced resilience. In mining areas, non-stationarity and signal mixing hinder large-scale, long-term assessment of vegetation resilience. Here, we combined VegDecouple with critical slowing down theory to extract vegetation disturbance signals and quantify vegetation resilience. Using Landsat-derived annual maximum NDVI data from 1987 to 2025, we extracted the steady-state NDVI component, NDVIss, to represent vegetation greenness and investigated the spatiotemporal patterns of vegetation greenness and resilience across 329 open-pit coal mines in China, identified their trajectory types, and evaluated the effects of climatic and anthropogenic drivers using mixed-effects models. The results showed that (1) vegetation greenness exhibited a three-stage trajectory, with slow growth during 1987–2005, degradation during 2006–2016, and recovery after 2017, and was generally higher in northeastern China and lower in central China; (2) vegetation resilience fluctuated during 1993–2007, declined during 2007–2014, and increased after 2014, without a clear macrogeographic gradient; (3) four greenness–resilience trajectory types were identified, among which greening with resilience enhancement was dominant nationally and most concentrated in the Shendong coal base; and (4) mixed-effects models revealed divergent driver responses. NDVIss was mainly associated with the long-term climate background, particularly mean precipitation, and with recovery age, whereas vegetation resilience was primarily associated with annual temperature anomaly, mean precipitation, and annual net solar radiation anomaly. Sensitivity analyses using alternative water indicators further suggested that NDVIss was more closely related to persistent water availability and soil moisture in the upper 0–7 cm layer, whereas vegetation resilience was more sensitive to water deficits captured by SPEI over 3 and 6 months than to total annual precipitation. This study advances the understanding of long-term vegetation greenness and resilience dynamics in China's open-pit coal mines and provides a remote sensing perspective for assessing ecological change in mining areas.

title: Acid mine drainage as a lixiviant for rare earth element recovery from ion-adsorption clay mine tailings: leaching behavior, mechanistic interpretation, and machine-learning-assisted analysis
abstract: This study evaluates a mine-internal waste-to-waste strategy in which raw acid mine drainage (AMD) generated at an ion-adsorption rare earth mine is reused as an on-site lixiviant to recover residual rare earth elements (REEs), including yttrium (Y) and scandium (Sc), from associated mine tailings. One-factor-at-a-time screening identified favorable laboratory conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio [S/L] = 1:50, 50 °C, 135 rpm, and 3 h), under which the reported calculations gave REE extraction efficiencies of approximately 70-92%. Solution and surface analyses documented REE release and iron enrichment of the leached residue, while XGBoost-SHAP provided internally evaluated predictive associations that require external validation. The findings support laboratory-scale technical feasibility for integrated management of two mine-derived waste streams, rather than establishing AMD itself as an unconventional REE resource or demonstrating a net environmental or economic benefit. The analytical scope focused on REEs and did not provide a complete mass balance for coexisting Fe, Al, Mn, Pb, As, Th, and U. Scale-up therefore requires assessment of seasonal AMD variability, acid-neutralization demand, downstream REE separation, treatment of the co-contaminated pregnant leach solution, and the long-term stability and leachability of the Fe-rich residue.

title: Climate change, ecosystem service value loss, and adaptive policy evaluation: Evidence from Chinese cities
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens regional ecosystem service value (ESV), while mismatches between ecological pressures and adaptive policy capacity may constrain sustainable development. This study combines climate-grid data, land-cover-derived ESV accounts, and panel data for 281 Chinese prefecture-level cities (2000–2020) to estimate associations between long-term climate normals and ESV. We then analyze 21,930 ecological policy documents using the Qwen2.5 large language model to characterize policy scope, depth, and speed, and use a two-dimensional framework to describe policy–ecology coordination. Results show that higher temperature normals are associated with lower ESV, with larger estimated losses in warmer regions, whereas higher precipitation normals are associated with higher ESV. The cumulative ESV loss associated with observed long-term climate changes exceeds 30 billion yuan; hydrological regulation accounts for the largest estimated loss (7.47 billion yuan). Policy–ecology coordination displays an east–central–west gradient, but the policy scores are text-based indicators and the coordination analysis is descriptive rather than causal. Effective adaptation therefore requires policy design to be aligned with local ecological conditions and implementation capacity.

title: Photovoltaic-induced heterogeneity drives plant–soil feedback divergence and microhabitat differentiation in a typical steppe
abstract: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) power stations is profoundly altering grassland ecosystems, yet the mechanisms that link plant community responses to belowground ecological processes remain unclear. Here, three microhabitats in a typical steppe PV station located in Inner Mongolia: under-panel, between-panel, and control microhabitats were investigated. The results showed that PV-induced microhabitat heterogeneity reshaped plant-derived inputs to the soil and microbial activity, thereby generating different aboveground and belowground feedbacks that reinforced the heterogeneity. The under-panel community exhibited low diversity but high aboveground biomass dominated by a few species (e.g., Carex lanceolata), whereas between-panel plots maintained higher plant diversity with moderate biomass. These differences affected the belowground ecological processes. Under the panels, greater litter accumulation but reduced rhizosphere carbon inputs were accompanied by lower soil organic carbon and total nitrogen, higher NO3−-N, a higher microbial biomass C to N ratio, and enrichment of RB41, exhibiting a more conservative microbial strategy. In contrast, between-panel plots were characterized by higher peroxidase activity and NH4+-N, together with enrichment of Humicola and Hygrocybe and greater predicted potential for organic matter transformation and nutrient mineralization. Together, these findings show that PV-induced heterogeneity creates functional trade-offs among productivity, biodiversity maintenance, and belowground nutrient processes within a single power station. Therefore, increases in vegetation biomass or cover alone should not be interpreted as evidence of ecological improvement, because they may coincide with biodiversity loss and altered soil C–N cycling. PV development should balance energy production with biodiversity conservation and long-term ecosystem functioning.

title: Subcritical extraction enhances the milk thistle value chain by improving economic and nutritional-functional performance with limited environmental trade-offs
abstract: The industrial production of Silybum marianum has expanded rapidly in recent years. However, its conventional processing chain, mainly based on mechanical pressing followed by silymarin extraction, still faces challenges in resource utilization and value enhancement. In this study, three oil extraction pathways, including solvent extraction (SE), mechanical pressing (PE), and subcritical butane extraction (SBE), were evaluated by integrating life-cycle environmental assessment, economic analysis, and nutritional-functional evaluation. PE exhibited the lowest environmental impacts among the three pathways, whereas SBE achieved higher economic value and nutritional-functional performance under the baseline weighting scheme due to its higher oil recovery and favorable product characteristics. Compared with PE, the transition to SBE increased the full-chain carbon footprint by approximately 12.7%, while increasing economic value by about 76.6% under realistic commercialization conditions. Under the expanded refined-oil commercialization scenario, SBE showed an approximately 86.8% higher modeled economic value than PE. These results indicate that SBE can improve the value generation potential of the milk thistle processing chain while maintaining an acceptable environmental burden. This study provides insights into the selection of extraction technologies for sustainable and high-value utilization of milk thistle resources.

title: Life cycle analysis on United States titanium dioxide and titanium metal products based on global titanium supply chain datasets
abstract: Complexity of global supply chain of titanium makes accurate analysis on the life cycle of titanium products challenging. To address this need, life cycle inventory datasets for titanium dioxide and titanium metal powder are collected using trade databases published by the United States International Trade Commission and the World Bank. Then, leveraging those global supply chain datasets of raw and intermediate titanium feedstocks for the final titanium products, the greenhouse gas emissions for titanium metal powder and titanium dioxide produced in the United States are assessed using the R&D Greenhouse gases, Regulated Emissions, and Energy use in Technologies (R&D GREET) database. The potential changes in greenhouse gas emissions intensity of titanium dioxide and metal powder produced in the United States are estimated for multiple scenarios, assuming changes in the domestic production share of titanium feedstocks and types of energy and material resources used for final titanium products. The results show that increasing domestic production of titanium sponge metal or titanium slag can achieve about 2-7% (current) and 5-15% (2035 projection) reduction in the greenhouse gas emissions intensity of titanium metal powder. However, more emissions reduction (about 19% for titanium metal powder and about 30% for titanium dioxide) is expected by replacing fossil fuel energy sources (e.g., coal) with lower emitting sources (such as nuclear or renewable electricity) for chlorination or by replacing the average grid electricity with nuclear or renewable energy to produce key material inputs (e.g., sodium hydroxide) required for the chlorination process.

title: Multi-objective optimization for sizing of residential hybrid renewable systems with battery storage: Balancing economic, environmental, and energy autonomy perspectives
abstract: The expansion of residential prosumer systems has increased the need for sustainable sizing models that incorporate local generation and storage. This study proposes a multi-objective model for the optimal sizing of residential hybrid renewable energy systems, evaluated from economic, environmental, and energy autonomy perspectives. The approach combines Response Surface Methodology and Normal Boundary Intersection to model and optimize three objective functions: Net Present Value, equivalent CO2 emissions, and Self-sufficiency. A post-Pareto selection method is used to identify an optimal solution from each Pareto front. A case study is developed across the nine capitals of the Brazilian Northeast region, considering the current regulatory changes to the net-metering system established by Law 14,300/2022. This study advances the literature by explicitly integrating economic, environmental (accounting for life-cycle emissions of renewable technologies), and energy self-sufficiency objectives in the optimal sizing of residential photovoltaic/wind/battery systems under a real regulatory transition. The main results indicate that, despite the regulatory change, investments remain viable, particularly when based on photovoltaic energy. The selected solutions achieved self-sufficiency levels of 54.7% to 68.1% and life-cycle emissions of 6894 to 8655 kgCO2eq. The results also indicate the benefit of small-scale wind energy over increasing battery bank capacity, as it enables greater self-sufficiency with a lower environmental impact. Despite this, the use of wind energy remains limited to regions with favorable wind regimes; however, these areas still represent a considerable portion of a country with continental dimensions such as Brazil. Formulating public policies and incentives tailored to each region's specificities can ensure greater integration of distributed generation without negatively affecting energy distributors or consumers who do not use this technology, thereby providing a more sustainable model in the long term.

title: Synergetic high selectively Uranium(VI) adsorption via molecularly engineered tetradentate Schiff base functionalized chitosan/carboxymethyl cellulose bio-composite: From molecular design to life cycle assessment
abstract: The extraction of uranium has been an important solution for resolving the radioactive contamination in water resources and the nuclear fuel shortage. Developing effective eco-friendly bio-adsorbents is urgently needed. A composite biomaterial was designed by combining chitosan (CS) and carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) (CS/CMC), which is further functionalized by a novel unsymmetrical O-phenylenediamine tetradentate Schiff base ligand (LOph) (3-bromo-2-((E)-((2-(((E)-2-chloro-6-hydroxybenzylidene)amino)phenyl)-imino)-methyl)phenol) (CS/CMC-LOph). CS/CMC-LOph composite showed a strong binding affinity to U(VI) and was able to adsorb 782.4 mg/g of uranyl ions at pH 5, 318 K, and 300 ppm. From an environmental perspective (1 ppm), the CS/CMC-LOph achieved significant adsorption, with a removal rate of 99.6% and a uranium residual concentration of 3.1 ppb after 24 h, which is below the WHO standards (15 ppb). In simulated real seawater, the material removes 98.7% of uranium with a Kd of 378663.3 mL/g. The thermodynamic study confirms that the process is endothermic and spontaneous. DFT calculations demonstrate a binding energy of −54.75 kcal/mol for U(VI) with the LOph, which is significantly stronger than those of chitosan and CMC. The CS/CMC-LOph demonstrated good recyclability with a removal capacity of 81.6% after six cycles. An LCA study has been conducted to assess the environmental impact of manufacturing 1 kg of CS/CMC-LOph. The minimum total cost of reusability and use of sustainable technologies proved to be effective in water treatment, uranium separation, and recovery.

title: Bioconversion of nuisance macroalgal biomass into fish production: Implications for low-input and circular aquaculture
abstract: Excess macroalgal blooms represent a persistent waste-management challenge in coastal aquaculture systems. Therefore, developing low-input, resource-efficient strategies that prevent waste accumulation while recovering value from nuisance biomass is a key objective of cleaner production. Here, we evaluate trophic bioconversion as a resource-recovery pathway by testing whether an herbivorous fish can convert nuisance macroalgal biomass (Ulva prolifera) into marketable seafood while mitigating water-quality risks associated with algal decomposition.
