Back-substitution into the mathematical model showed that the maximum relative error of the compromise solution was 2.39%, while the errors in system net efficiency, levelized cost of electricity and CO2 emission intensity were all below 0.2%. Relative to the baseline case, the optimized case increased net efficiency from 41.20% to 54.25%, reduced LCOE from 0.135 to 0.118 $/kWh and lowered CO2 emission intensity from 15.54 to 11.81 gCO2/kWh. Advanced exergy analysis further showed that system exergy efficiency increased from 38.72% to 50.98%, total exergy destruction decreased by 28.40 MW, and the main gains came from lower irreversibility in coal gasification and SOFC conversion. Some losses were transferred to the waste heat boiler (WHB) and the expansion/compression loop. The results indicate that surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization becomes a reliable basis for IGFC/CCS engineering diagnosis only when it is checked by mathematical-model back-substitution and advanced exergy diagnosis.

title: Thermodynamically driven arsenic mobilization via concurrent microbial Fe(III)/As(V) reduction pathways mediated by redox-active shuttles
abstract: Iron-bearing minerals are the primary arsenic carriers in subsurface environments, where microbially mediated concurrent Fe(III)/As(V) reduction serves as a widespread dual-pathway process driving arsenic release. Arsenic mobility and toxicity depend intrinsically on its redox speciation, so understanding this process is critical for accurate risk assessment. However, the specific kinetic and thermodynamic rules governing this process remain poorly understood, particularly when mediated by prevalent redox-active shuttles such as natural organic matter (NOM). Here, we systematically investigated arsenic mobilization from iron-bearing clay minerals using a representative Fe(III)/As(V)-reducing bacterium and a suite of electron shuttles (ESs) spanning redox potentials (Eh) from −3 to −500 mV. Our findings demonstrate that ESs within an optimal redox potential window (−137 to −225 mV) markedly accelerate arsenic mobilization, enhancing average release rates of As(V) and newly formed As(III) by up to 3.10-fold and 2.02-fold, respectively. Conversely, ESs outside this window provided only a limited and kinetically delayed enhancement. Linear free energy relationships (LFERs) reveal that the Eh is significantly correlated with reaction kinetics (R2 > 0.87), identifying redox potential as a key thermodynamic regulator governing arsenic mobilization and structural iron reduction. These dynamics are governed by a synchronized “push-pull” mechanism: microbial As(V) reduction creates a concentration-driven “pull”, while ES-mediated acceleration of structural iron reduction provides a structural “push” that facilitates desorption. This mechanistic coupling underscores the intricate interplay between arsenic valence transformation and mineral structural evolution. These results elucidate the thermodynamic constraints on arsenic mobilization and provide a mechanistic basis for risk assessment in complex subsurface systems.

title: Sustainable collaborative planning of green hydrogen refueling networks in urban agglomerations: A three-stage framework integrating geospatially explicit screening, fuzzy MCDM, and stochastic optimization
abstract: Urban agglomerations, as strategic units for transportation decarbonization, face systemic challenges in their hydrogen refueling station (HRS) networks, including misalignment of wind-solar resources, highly heterogeneous hydrogen demand, and isolated station operations. Existing research, limited to single-station static planning, struggles to support green hydrogen transportation systems, thereby impeding sustainable urban mobility development. This study proposes a three-stage collaborative planning framework: Geospatial analysis, fuzzy MCDM, and stochastic optimization addressing site selection, optimization, configuration, and scheduling for HRSs. A combination method based on spatial analysis realizes coupling of wind-solar resources and transportation demand. A hybrid decision model quantifies expert’ fuzzy cognition and uncovers causal networks of indicators. Seasonal scenarios are generated through gaussian kernel density estimation and LHS, with NSGA-III solving the economic-environmental objective collaborative model for dynamic multi-station hydrogen synergy. Empirical results from a wind-solar-rich urban agglomerations (Urumqi-Changji-Shihezi) identify eight optimal sites. The results show that with a total annual cost of 366.24 million CNY, the lifecycle carbon emissions are 4766.5 tons, achieving carbon reductions of 28.36% and 40.28% compared to gray and black hydrogen, respectively. Collaborative scheduling reduces the system’s supply-demand gap by an average of 87%, significantly enhancing network resilience. The wind-solar hybrid configuration reduces costs by 25.3% and carbon emissions by 50.6% compared to single-energy solutions. This study provides a reusable collaborative HRSs planning paradigm for wind-solar resource-rich regions and enhances hydrogen infrastructure planning theory from the perspectives of spatial adaptation and dynamic coordination, offering valuable insights for the sustainable development of green transportation networks in global urban agglomerations.

title: Mass transfer, phase transition processes and mechanisms of transcritical-CO2 in rapid leakage from offshore saline aquifer storage: A visualization study
abstract: Geological storage of CO2 in saline aquifers is a critical strategy for major global economies to achieve carbon neutrality. With the transitions from pilot-scale demonstrations to large-scale implementation, ensuring its safety and effectiveness has become a primary focus. The phase transition and thermodynamic characteristics of CO2 leakage are the theoretical basis for leakage prevention and control. Herein, we used visual PVT-cell to record the entire process of CO2 from stable storage to complete leakage in brine. Subsequently, we developed a multiphysics coupled numerical model, and integrated with experimental observations to elucidate the coupled mechanisms of convection, phase transition, interfacial mass transfer, and heat transfer during leakage. The results reveal that rapid depressurization at the moment of leakage triggers a transcritical-phase-transition of CO2, forming a mist-like layer through heterogeneous nucleation at the interface, with structural trapping dominating the initial leakage. When the pressure drops to about 9.0 MPa, the CO2 phase undergoes a rapid density reconstruction, accompanied by waterfall-flow due to the critical opalescence principle. Meanwhile, jellyfish-flow emerges in the saline, indicating the destabilization of solubility trapping. In the later stage of leakage, due to the loss of temperature induced by phase transition, extensive CO2 hydrates generate, which temporarily hinders the leakage of CO2 but lead to concentration accumulation. Hydrates decompose driven by geothermal heat, leading to rapid leakage dominated by CO2 in solubility trapping. Therefore, the timing of hydrate formation is the bottom line for storage safety monitoring. This paper fills the gap in visual research on the entire process of CO2 leakage and provides a reliable research framework for multiphysics coupled solubility trapping.

title: New strategy for enhanced degradation of regulated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar pitch by long chain alkene modification
abstract: The presence of toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar pitch (CTP) restricts its sustainable application and poses severe environmental risks. This study developed an alkylation method by using 1-tetradecene to modify CTP, aiming to reduce hazardous compound content while comprehensively evaluating sample toxicity through chemical and biological indicators. The modification achieved 92.73% reduction rate for the 16 priority PAHs regulated by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in real CTP and decreased PAHs emissions in CTP fumes by 97.47%. In exploratory experiments, the four model PAHs, phenanthrene, anthracene, fluoranthene, and pyrene, were reduced by 99.97%, surpassing all previously reported literature. Comprehensive evaluations using cytotoxicity, toxicity calculations, and ecological indicators confirmed a significant decline in overall toxicity. The study successfully explained the molecular mechanism of the alkylation reaction and clarified why the long-chain alkene prevented cellular carcinogenicity. The study supplied a crucial theoretical foundation for the safe utilization of CTP in road construction. Furthermore, extending this method to waste plastic pyrolysis products established a sustainable framework for resource recycling and waste treatment.

title: Characteristics of microplastic release from self-heating food packaging and its health risks to human population
abstract: While existing research on microplastics (MPs) migration has predominantly focused on microwave-heated plastic containers and short-term exposure within liquid media, the exposure characteristics and human health risks associated with the emerging scenario of self-heating foods remain poorly understood. To address this research gap, this study pioneeringly established a MP migration simulation framework based on realistic self-heating dynamics. Integrating nationwide survey data from 916 consumers, we developed a novel behavior-based exposure risk assessment model. Crucially, we introduced an innovative consumption-weighted frequency parameter to explicitly capture real-world dietary patterns within the exposure modeling framework. By quantitatively evaluating the estimated daily intake (EDI) of MPs across both the general population and sensitive demographics, this work provides compelling empirical evidence and a robust methodological foundation for evaluating packaging-derived MP risks in self-heating foods. The results showed that high temperature, long contact time, and high-fat, acidic media significantly exacerbated the migration and release of MPs. Under 100 °C conditions, the MP concentration in the olive oil simulant was 5.7 times that under 40 °C conditions, while the acidic environment (3% acetic acid) led to a 2- to 5-fold increase in MP release compared to that under deionized water (DI). In the sensitive population, the EDI value of self-heating rice for children aged 0–7 was as high as 1221 ± 592 particles/(kg·d). Self-heating noodle soup exhibited the highest MP contamination risk, self-heating rice showed a moderately high risk. The MP exposure risk from self-heating foods warrants further attention, especially for sensitive groups such as children.

title: Extracellular ROS fingerprinting guides mixed-gas ARTP optimization for lipid-oriented breeding of Chlorella sorokiniana
abstract: Atmospheric room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis has been increasingly applied for non-transgenic strain improvement in microalgae, yet its optimization remains largely empirical due to unclear roles of specific reactive oxygen species (ROS). This study quantitatively profiled extracellular ROS species (1O2, O2•-, •OH, H2O2) under low-voltage ARTP conditions using air, argon, and mixed gas at 40–130 V and 1 A. These profiles were further linked to intracellular redox dynamics and triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation in Chlorella sorokiniana. Electron paramagnetic resonance and colorimetric assays revealed that 1O2 was suppressed at higher voltages and under argon-rich plasma conditions, whereas •OH and H2O2 peaked under moderate mixed-gas treatment (air:argon = 1:2). Over a 43-day cultivation, intracellular ROS exhibited multi-phase trajectories, coupled with glutathione buffering, Ca2+ signaling, and enhanced activities of lipogenic enzymes. Linear mixed model analysis revealed that TAG accumulation was significantly positively correlated with O2•- (β = 38.98) and negatively correlated with 1O2 (β = −20.75), but not with •OH or H2O2. ROS–TAG coupling was strongest at mid-culture, after which sustained oxidative stress appeared to impose physiological burdens and shifted metabolic trajectories. Under optimized ARTP conditions, the selected mutants achieved a lipid productivity of 1.39 × 10−5 kg L−1 d−1, 2.36-fold that of the wild type (5.90 × 10−6 kg L−1 d−1), while reducing resource intensity per unit lipid by 57.6%, equivalent to ∼154 kg CO2 eq per kg lipid saved. Collectively, these results suggest that ARTP-induced mutagenesis is governed by selective redox regulation rather than by absolute oxidative intensity alone. The proposed ROS-speciation framework provides a more rational and resource-efficient strategy for replacing empirical screening in the development of sustainable microalgal cell-factories for lipid production.

title: Service-life-informed carbon footprint assessment of 3D-printed residual mud concrete considering mechanical and durability uncertainties
abstract: This study develops a 3D printed concrete (3DPC) incorporating modified residual mud powder (MRMP) as a supplementary cementitious material, and proposes a life cycle assessment (LCA) method that accounts for mechanical performance, durability, and their variability. MRMP replaced 20% of cement, and the resulting 3DPC-MRMP reached a maximum compressive strength of 37.3 MPa in the printing direction. MRMP reduced the chloride diffusion coefficient (Dcl-) in cast specimens to approximately 50% of that of the cement mixture. However, in 3D printed specimens, 3DPC-MRMP showed a slightly higher Dcl- than 3DPC-C, indicating that transport behavior was governed mainly by the weak interlayer regions rather than by matrix densification. A Monte Carlo simulation was used to predict the service life of a 3D printed beam under chloride exposure, and the annualized environmental burden was calculated based on the service life. The 3DPC-MRMP beam had a service life 1.1 years shorter than that of 3DPC-C, but still achieved reductions across four damage categories, including a 16.5% reduction in climate change impact. A sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the influence of 3DPC material variability on reliability, service-life assessment, and the resulting service-life-informed LCA outcomes. Life cycle cost (LCC) analysis further confirmed the economic advantages of 3DPC-MRMP. This study suggests that MRMP is a promising sustainable supplementary cementitious material and provides a methodological framework for assessing the performance of 3DPC and life cycle environmental impacts of 3DPC.

title: From plant auxin to antibiotic resistance genes dissemination: Comparative insights into indole-3-acetic acid-enhanced horizontal gene transfer and underlying mechanisms between soil microbiomes and pure cultures
abstract: The spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in plant-soil systems threatens human health. Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), an auxin secreted by plants and microorganisms, can be released into the soil during plant growth. However, little is known about whether IAA affects the spread of ARGs in soil microbiomes, which possess broad-host-range plasmids that potentially affect ARGs transmission more substantially than pure bacterial cultures. Here, we systematically investigated contributions of environmental-level IAA on the horizontal transfer of ARGs and the underlying mechanisms in soil microbiomes and pure cultures. Our results demonstrated that IAA enhanced both conjugative and transformative transfer of ARGs in soil microbial communities, in contrast to the limited effects in pure cultures. Integrated phenotypic, genotypic, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses revealed that the enhanced ARGs transmission in the soil microbial community was affiliated with over-produced reactive oxygen species (ROS), increased cell membrane permeability, enhanced biofilm formation, activated quorum sensing, and promoted bacterial competence. Different biofilm formation capacities and ROS-induced stress responses resulted in different ARGs transfer frequencies in soil microbiomes and pure cultures. Our study highlights IAA's important role in ARGs dissemination in microbiomes of plant-soil systems and underscores the need to evaluate the potential risks of IAA application in agriculture.

title: Carbon balance in the Brazilian tropical dairy farming system
abstract: The expected increase in the global population is projected to raise the demand for milk and dairy products by 2050, highlighting the need to improve production efficiency while mitigating environmental impacts. This study evaluated the carbon balance of Brazilian tropical dairy farming systems by integrating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and removals into a single farm-scale assessment, focusing on two milk production levels during lactation: high (HPS, ≥8500 kg milk cow −1 year −1 ) and medium production potential (MPS, <8500 kg milk cow −1 year −1 ). Emissions and removals were estimated following the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and the Livestock Environmental Assessment and Performance Partnership guidelines. Compared with MPS, HPS showed larger areas, herd sizes, and milk production, reflecting greater productive efficiency associated with more effective management. Consequently, HPS exhibited lower GHG emission intensity from enteric fermentation, manure management, and feed, resulting in a lower overall emission intensity. In contrast, MPS attained higher GHG removal intensity, mainly through soil carbon sequestration associated with land-use change and tree biomass. Despite this greater removal capacity, the higher emission intensity of MPS resulted in a less favorable overall carbon balance than HPS. Both systems therefore contribute to low-carbon dairy development through complementary pathways: HPS primarily by reducing emissions per unit of product, and MPS primarily by enhancing carbon removals. Integrating emission-reduction strategies with practices that enhance carbon sequestration is required to advance low-carbon milk production and support the sector's mitigation goals.

title: Comparative analysis of energy consumption, CO2 emissions, and production costs for conventional and emerging ironmaking routes
abstract: A comprehensive assessment of energy consumption (EC), CO2 emissions (CE) and production costs (C) across different ironmaking routes is essential for supporting governments and enterprises in formulating effective low-carbon transition strategies. However, existing studies have largely concentrated on the conventional blast furnace ironmaking route (BFI), while systematic assessments of emerging ironmaking routes and comparative analyses of key parameters across different routes remain limited. In this study, a life cycle assessment (LCA) is employed to evaluate the EC, CE and C of four ironmaking routes: the BFI, coal gasification-based hydrogen ironmaking route (CG-HI), water electrolysis-based hydrogen ironmaking route (WE-HI), and acidic electrolysis ironmaking route (AEI). The results indicate that producing 1 tonne of contained Fe in iron product requires 15.5, 14.8, 13.9 and 27.0 GJ of energy for the four routes, respectively. The corresponding CE are 1.41, 1.30, 3.27 and 4.49 t, while the C are 2500, 2670, 4530 and 6080 CNY, respectively. In addition, sensitivity analysis is employed to examine the effects of electricity structure, energy structure, material structure and TRL correction coefficient on the EC, CE and C of the four ironmaking routes. The results suggest that increasing the share of renewable electricity in the power grid will significantly enhance the low-carbon potential of the WE-HI and AEI.

title: Aggregate gains and crop-driven trade-offs in the carbon and nitrogen footprints of China's interprovincial trade in rice, wheat and maize
abstract: China's grain production and consumption are spatially mismatched, but the joint carbon–nitrogen consequences of interprovincial trade bridging this mismatch remain unclear. We applied a carbon–nitrogen footprint framework to evaluate rice, wheat and maize bilateral trade among 31 Chinese provinces for ten selected observation years between 2000 and 2022. Local self-supply counterfactual scenario was used as an analytical baseline. Interprovincial trade reduced national production-stage greenhouse gas emissions and reactive nitrogen losses in all observation years. In 2022, reductions reached 35.7 Mt CO2-eq and 1.17 Mt N-eq, or 9.7% and 16.3% of local self-supply burdens, and remained positive in uncertainty analyses. All three crops contributed positively, with maize providing the largest share of both benefits—48.3% of the GHG reduction and 66.8% of the reactive-N reduction. Provincial outcomes diverged: seven provinces had opposing greenhouse gas and nitrogen effects in 2022, with rice-exporting provinces showing higher greenhouse gas but lower nitrogen burdens relative to local self-supply, and maize- or wheat-exporting provinces showing the reverse. China's interprovincial trade in rice, wheat and maize delivers aggregate gains while revealing crop-driven provincial trade-offs.

title: Use of incineration bottom ash for geopolymer electrolytes in structural supercapacitors
abstract: The development of structural energy storage materials is constrained by the inherent trade-off between mechanical strength and ionic conductivity. This study develops a sustainable structural supercapacitor by utilizing municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) bottom ash as a functional foaming agent in a geopolymer electrolyte. The incorporation of IBA resulted in a reduction in compressive strength owing to increased porosity and coarser pore structure as revealed by micro-CT test. Electrochemical characterization revealed that the incorporation of IBA improved ionic transport by reducing the equivalent series resistance by 60.7%, while maintaining a compressive strength of 40 MPa. Microstructural analysis via FTIR and TG revealed an increased silicate polymerization and reduced gel-bound water with the addition of IBA. Finally, a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment revealed that incorporating IBA reduced the overall environmental impact, with the alkali activator (i.e., sodium silicate) identified as the primary contributor of the environmental footprint. This work successfully transforms industrial waste into a functional component, presenting a scalable and promising pathway for developing sustainable energy-storage infrastructures.

title: Mitigating thermal degradation of cement paste at elevated temperatures via ultra-fine magnesite tailings incorporation
abstract: Ordinary Portland cement paste undergoes substantial dehydration and phase decomposition at elevated temperatures, resulting in microstructural damage and strength loss. In this study, ultra-fine magnesite tailings (UMT) were incorporated into cement paste at replacement levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, and 30% to delay the onset of severe thermal degradation of hardened pastes. The mechanical and physical properties, as well as phase evolution and microstructural changes, were investigated after exposure to 105, 300, 500, 700, and 900 °C. The results indicate that, due to high-temperature curing effects, the residual compressive strength of the cement paste at 300 °C was 114.8% of its corresponding value at 20 °C, after which it began to decrease. However, with the addition of UMT, the residual compressive strength of the paste continued to increase from 105 to 500 °C. When 20% UMT was added, the residual compressive strength at 700 °C remained at 101.9% (76.43 MPa). 1H LF NMR, XCT, and MIP suggested that the incorporation of UMT at high temperatures limited the loss of interlayer water and gel water in the C–S–H gel, as well as the development of cracks, thereby optimizing the pore structure. SEM, TGA, XRD, FTIR, and 29Si MAS NMR results further demonstrated that UMT may formed new crystal structures with hydration products at lower temperatures, enhancing stability at higher temperatures. This study provides a low-carbon method to improve the high-temperature resistance of cement paste and offers an efficient, value-added approach to the accumulation and management of magnesite tailings.

title: Explainable machine learning reveals spatially heterogeneous BOD–COD relationships in a large river basin to inform targeted monitoring strategies
abstract: Accurate monitoring of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is essential for assessing river health, but its measurement is labor-intensive and time-consuming. In contrast, chemical oxygen demand (COD) is routinely and automatically monitored in China's national network, yet it does not fully capture ecological stress. To address this limitation, we developed a machine learning framework to predict hard-to-measure BOD dynamics using frequently measured COD together with other environmental variables. Monthly observations from 135 monitoring sites across the Yellow River Basin during 2016–2022 were integrated with water quality parameters, catchment attributes, and anthropogenic emission indicators to construct a stacking model. The ensemble combined five base learners, including random forest, svmRadial, xgbTree, Cubist, and gbm. The stacking model achieved satisfactory predictive performance, with an R2 of 0.78, representing an improvement of approximately 5.4% to 15% compared with the individual base models. SHAP analysis identified COD as the dominant predictor of BOD, exerting a strong positive effect. The strength of the BOD–COD coupling varied spatially, being stronger in urbanized watersheds with intensive domestic emissions and weaker in relatively natural, less-disturbed basins. Structural equation modeling further indicated that the spatial heterogeneity of human activities amplifies regional differentiation in the BOD-COD relationship, a pattern likely mediated by basin-specific dissolved organic matter characteristics. These findings support a differentiated monitoring strategy, whereby model predictions can complement BOD measurements in human-impacted basins, while higher sampling density is warranted in natural systems. Overall, the proposed framework enables optimized resource allocation and targeted monitoring of organic pollution in large, heterogeneous river basins.

title: Governance mechanisms for Low-value recyclable waste recycling under dual information asymmetry and residents’ perceived value
abstract: The recycling of Low-value recyclable waste (LVRW) suffers from low economic value, high collection costs, and weak resident participation, resulting in sustained reliance on government subsidies. However, asymmetric information on recyclers’ ability and effort leads to subsidy misallocation and reduced incentive efficiency. This study develops a principal–agent based dynamic model with residents’ perceived value and compares three regimes: no subsidy, recycler-only subsidy, and dual subsidies for recyclers and residents. Results show that no subsidy yields a low-efficiency equilibrium. Recycler-only subsidy raises effort and output but concentrates benefits among high-ability recyclers. Dual subsidies achieve more stable and balanced growth in recycling performance and social welfare. As a vital transmission channel, perceived value leads to varied subsidy incentives under behavioral feedback. The findings inform more efficient subsidy design for LVRW recycling systems.

title: Integration of multispectral imaging and explainable AI for alfalfa seed priming optimization under saline-alkali stress
abstract: Soil salinization poses an increasingly severe threat to sustainable agriculture globally, while conventional seed priming optimization remains time- and resource-intensive, limiting its widespread adoption. This study developed an innovative smart seed priming framework that seamlessly combined multispectral imaging technology with explainable machine learning algorithms to optimize alfalfa seed priming under saline-alkali stress (75 mM Na 2 SO 4 ). Through systematic evaluation of six distinct priming agents (gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), ascorbic acid (AsA), melatonin (MT), salicylic acid (SA), spermidine (Spd), and sodium sulfate (Na 2 SO 4 ), our sophisticated stacking ensemble model demonstrated exceptional performance in both priming parameter classification (accuracy: 0.812-0.920, ROC-AUC: 0.941-0.994) and effect prediction (accuracy: 0.820-0.950, ROC-AUC: 0.928-0.960). Comprehensive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified critical spectral features across multiple analytical scales: the parameter model highlighted wavelengths at 570 nm and 970 nm as key indicators of moisture content and flavonoid compositional changes; for priming effects assessment, wavelengths at 850 nm (associated with storage materials) and 490 nm exhibited significant negative synergistic effects specifically on the ‘first’ category of MT priming; detailed individual seed analysis revealed complex nonlinear relationships between priming agent concentration, treatment duration, and corresponding spectral variations. The developed smart seed priming framework enabled rapid and efficient non-destructive optimization of seed priming, significantly accelerating priming technology development processes and advancing sustainable agricultural practices by providing personalized priming solutions under various stress conditions, particularly in regions affected by soil salinization.

title: Assessing energy security and sustainable development goal 7 performance in EU - A meta four-parallel two-stage undesirable dynamic DDF model
abstract: Amid escalating geopolitical uncertainty and accelerating low-carbon transition pressures, energy security has become a critical issue affecting sustainable development and the achievement of SDG7. This research integrates APERC's four dimensions of energy security with Parallel DEA, Dynamic Network DEA, and meta-frontier analysis to develop a meta four-parallel two-stage undesirable dynamic directional distance function (DDF) model. The proposed framework helps evaluate the efficiency performances of energy security and energy sustainability in 26 EU countries during 2018-2022 under geopolitical shocks and energy transition pressures. The empirical results reveal significant technological heterogeneity between Eastern and Western European countries. Eastern European countries exhibit comparatively smaller technology gaps relative to the meta-frontier. Accessibility and acceptability are the major sources of inefficiency in many EU countries. Malmquist productivity decomposition indicates a clear temporal shift in the sources of productivity change. While efficiency improvement and technological progress mainly drove productivity improvement in 2020, technological regress gradually became the dominant source of productivity deterioration after 2021. This pattern may reflect the challenges that geopolitical shocks and energy transition pressures pose for the technological frontier of EU energy systems. The primary contribution of this study lies in integrating meta-frontier analysis, parallel structure decomposition, dynamic network linkages, and undesirable DDF measurement into a unified analytical framework that simultaneously captures technological heterogeneity, multi-stage structures, and intertemporal dynamic relationships. The findings provide important policy implications for improving EU energy resilience and renewable energy governance under geopolitical uncertainty.

title: A remote sensing–GIS decision-support framework for mapping woody biochar potential and logistics-constrained application suitability on degraded rural land
abstract: Land degradation represents a major environmental challenge affecting soil productivity, ecosystem services, and climate regulation. Biochar application gained increasing attention as a potential response because it can improve soil properties while contributing to carbon dioxide removal. However, its large-scale deployment for restoration purposes remains constrained by the lack of spatially explicit assessments integrating biomass availability, production potential, logistical constraints, and land restoration needs. This study develops a remote sensing–GIS decision-support framework to assess whether the valorization of residual woody biomass could support degraded rural areas restoration. The framework objectives are to estimate biomass residue availability, biochar production potential, and logistics-constrained biochar application suitability on degraded rural land of the Veneto Region (Italy). Approximately 169,200 ha of degraded rural land were identified across the region, while useable residual biomass was estimated at about 10.2 million t yr −1 , corresponding to a theoretical biochar production potential of approximately 3.1 million t yr −1 . Despite this, spatial and logistical constraints strongly limited its effective deployment, with about 2% of degraded land treated even under the most viable scenario. Lower biochar application rates combined with short transportation distances provided the greatest territorial coverage. These findings demonstrate that biomass abundance alone does not determine restoration potential; rather, effective biochar deployment depends on the spatial alignment of biomass supply, production infrastructure, transportation feasibility, and restoration demand. The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for identifying where biomass valorization can realistically contribute to land restoration and complement with circular bioeconomy and restoration measures into regional planning.

title: Complexation-assisted regulatory mechanism: Insights into microscale interactions and macroscale oxidation kinetics
abstract: Abstract The formation of antibiotic-metal complexes (AMCs) via organic pollutant-metal ion binding is ubiquitous in transition metal-based Fenton-like processes. However, the regulatory mechanisms of binding interactions on oxidative degradation remain underexplored. In this study, tetracycline (TET) was selected as a model organic pollutant, and the impact of TET-Cu(II) micro-complexation on macroscale degradation in the Cu(II)/H 2 O 2 system was systematically elucidated, integrating in-situ spectroscopy, ex-situ characterization, hydrogen nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR), electrochemistry, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) techniques. Results suggested that Cu(II) rapidly formed a TET-Cu(II) complex with TET’s dimethylamino, amino, and hydroxyl groups at a 1:1 ratio, with a complexation constant of 98036.7 L⋅mol − 1 , which had been confirmed to significantly promoted the macroscopic degradation of TET. Additionally, the bound TET was proved degraded preferentially over free TET, and the dissociation rates significantly exceeded binding rates during oxidation via time-resolved fluorescence scan analysis. The binding interaction promoted the formation of an TET ± -Cu(II)-OOH⁻ intermediate, which further enhanced Cu(II)/Cu(I) cycling and accelerated the generation of the dominant reactive species (hydroxyl radicals (•OH)), while O 2 inhibited reactions by consuming Cu(I) to generate superoxide radicals (•O 2 ⁻). Based on the Benesi-Hildebrand equation, the bound fractions of both TET and Cu(II) were accurately calculated, indicating that the bound TET in the system accounted for more than 90%. Furthermore, the binding model was constructed to accurately predict the degradation rate constants ( k obs ), with an R 2 of 0.96 against experimental values. This study uncovered the intrinsic link between microscale complexation and macroscale degradation, providing theoretical support for efficient composite pollution treatment.

title: Sustainability assessment of China's nitrogen-phosphorus cycling system under future carbon neutrality transition scenarios
abstract: Achieving sustainable management of the nitrogen–phosphorus (N–P) cycling system is essential for advancing multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, yet its long-term sustainability under carbon neutrality transition pathways remains insufficiently understood. This study develops a multi-dimensional assessment framework integrating resource, environmental, trade, and network perspectives to evaluate the sustainability of China's N–P cycling system. Using a material flow analysis–based model combined with multi-indicator evaluation and scenario analysis, we examine historical evolution from 1980 to 2020 and project future trend under alternative socioeconomic and carbon neutrality transition scenarios, and quantifies potential improvements achievable through different management strategies. Results indicate that China's N–P cycling system has experienced a persistent decline in overall sustainability over the past four decades, by approximately 55%, driven primarily by intensifying resource inputs, environmental pressures, and increasing trade dependence, although recent policy interventions have partially reversed this trend, drove a recovery of the index to 1.66 by 2020. Scenario projections further show that a clean energy transition without coordinated resource management may intensify pressure on phosphorus resources and weaken system sustainability. In contrast, integrated management strategies across production, consumption, and trade sectors can significantly enhance N and P sustainability, achieving 5.8-fold and 2-fold improvements over the BAU scenario. Consequently, strengthening the implementation of relevant measures to balance food security, resource efficiency, and clean energy transitions is imperative to ensure the sustainable development of the cycling system.

title: Six decades of afforestation reshape deep soil microbial networks on the Loess Plateau: Implications for environmental assessment and ecological restoration policy in the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Large-scale afforestation programs, including the ‘Grain for Green’ program implemented in the Yellow River Basin, are central to combating land degradation, yet their long-term belowground effects remain difficult to assess. This study evaluated the 60-year effects of Caragana korshinskii afforestation on the Loess Plateau using 0-10 m soil profiles, soil physicochemical analyses, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and molecular ecological network analysis. The deep-profile design allowed us to identify where restoration signals were strongest and where afforestation effects attenuated along loess deposits. Long-term afforestation was associated with lower deep-layer soil water content, a decline in soil pH from 9.08 to 8.72, and a 23% increase in surface dissolved organic carbon. Bacterial diversity followed a U-shaped trajectory, recovering to exceed cropland levels after six decades. Microbial co-occurrence networks were more connected and showed higher topological robustness under targeted node removal than the cropland network (0.655 ± 0.011 vs. 0.563 ± 0.006). Soil pH was the environmental variable most strongly associated with this network shift; here, it is interpreted as an integrative proxy for vegetation-mediated changes in root activity, carbon inputs, nitrate redistribution, and hydrology rather than as an independent causal driver. These findings indicate that the gradual moderation of alkalinity co-varied with subsurface microbial reorganization. Together with soil water, DOC, and nitrate, pH provides a practical indicator set for assessing belowground restoration progress in the alkaline loess-derived soils examined.

title: Large-scale solar parks reshape ground arthropod assembly in the Tengger desert
abstract: The photovoltaic desertification control model effectively suppresses aeolian activity while promoting vegetation recovery and soil improvement, yet its impact on the diversity and function of ground arthropods remains unclear. This study was conducted at the Jiuduntan Photovoltaic Demonstration Park, located on the southern edge of the Tengger Desert. We sampled ground arthropods using pitfall trapping in the solar park (SP), the adjacent straw checkerboard barrier (SCB) and natural sand dune (SD) areas. Vegetation and soil factors were examined to identify the primary factors associated with ground arthropod community assembly. We found that: (1) The solar parks boosted shrub density, cover, and herb richness but reduced shrub richness, herb cover, and biomass versus straw checkerboard barrier and natural sand dune areas. Soil water content and hardness declined markedly in the solar parks, with nutrients unchanged. (2) Community structure of ground arthropods differed significantly across the natural sand dune, straw checkerboard barrier, and solar park areas. A sequential decline in both total abundance and species richness was observed along the gradient from natural sand dune to solar park, with a concomitant increase in evenness index. (3) The solar park elicited divergent responses from arthropods: beetles and ants declined significantly in both abundance and richness, whereas other insects increased and spiders remained unchanged. (4) Ground arthropod assemblages across different areas were primarily shaped by shrub cover, soil water content, and soil hardness, with beetles demonstrating greater environmental sensitivity than spiders. In short, photovoltaic desertification control rapidly promotes vegetation recovery and alters the physical environment, such as soil moisture and hardness, thereby driving the assembly changes of ground arthropods.

title: Enhancing rapid removal of iron from recycled aluminium based on reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance by an immersion rotational segregation process
abstract: Recycling of aluminum scrap is a crucial pathway for carbon reduction in the aluminum industry, as its carbon emissions represent only 3%-5% of those from primary aluminum production. However, a great challenge is to further remove trace iron content to a certain range in order to meet the requirements of multi grade high-end aluminum alloys. Herein, a novel immersion rotational segregation process (IRSP) is proposed to remove trace iron content in short time, which effectively reduces interfacial mass transfer resistance due to boundary layer thinning. Kilogram-scale experiments show that a single-stage process achieves a 60% iron removal efficiency within 3 min. By employing a two-stage treatment, the Fe content is successfully reduced from 0.8 wt% to below 0.15 wt%, meeting the stringent purity standards for high-quality aluminum alloy raw materials. This rapid purification is driven by intense shear forces that induce complex fluid interactions within high-speed shear zone and vortex zones, compressing the concentration boundary layer to 0.31 mm and significantly reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance. Furthermore, 100-kg scale-up experiments were performed to validate the industrial viability of the process, achieving an iron removal efficiency exceeding 70% within 20 min. This method provides a efficient pathway for the high-value upcycling of aluminium scrap, significantly reducing reliance on primary aluminum consumption and contributing to substantial carbon emission reductions in the global aluminum industry.

title: A two-condenser DHW heat pump for flexible heating: Assessing carbon savings using hourly grid emissions
abstract: Current building decarbonization policies often prioritize on-site renewable energy generation, an approach that is frequently unfeasible for block residential buildings with limited space for photovoltaic (PV) installations, as it is the case of many buildings in Spain. As national electricity grids become increasingly renewable, utilizing hourly grid CO2 emission profiles rather than annual average provides more realistic results. In 2024, annual average CO2 emissions in the Spanish grid was 0.096 kg CO2/kWh, while hourly CO2 emission factors calculated month by month ranged from 0.047 kg CO2/kWh to 0.180 kg CO2/kWh. This article presents an innovative heat pump with two condensers that improves its COP and controls usage times in order to reduce CO2 emissions associated with consumption. This new design is a solution that allows to pursue the flexibility of the systems, one of the key points of European regulations. Then the performance of the unit with two condensers is compared to a conventional one-condenser unit, results show that while standard annual-average assessments estimate a CO2 emission reduction of up to 18%, applying an hourly evaluation reveals CO2 emission savings exceeding 35%. This work highlights the problems with the current evaluation of heat pumps and the need to evaluate their associated CO2 emissions more accurately, either through the use of electricity obtained from the grid or even by the use of on-site photovoltaic panels.

title: Innovative synergy coefficient revealed the negative PM2.5–O3 synergistic pollution in China over the past decade
abstract: Over the past decade (2015-2024), China has implemented stringent policies to tackle PM2.5 pollution. However, this period has also witnessed the rise of O3 pollution as an increasingly pressing issue. This changing pollution pattern has been accompanied by more frequent synergistic PM2.5-O3 pollution episodes in China. Joint exposure to PM2.5 and O3 may impose greater health risks than exposure to either pollutant alone. This study developed an innovative Synergy Coefficient (SC) to quantify long-term synergistic trends using data from 1180 environmental monitoring stations across 328 cities in China from 2015 to 2024. Negative synergy emerged as the dominant relationship at 83% of stations, indicating generally divergent trends between PM2.5 and O3. The most pronounced negative SC values occurred in autumn and winter, while positive SC values reached a higher proportion during summer, particularly within the middle temperate zone and southern subtropical zone. Temperature played an increasingly important role in O3 variation over the study period, whereas the key factors affecting PM2.5 remained relatively stable. Natural factors primarily modulated SC values in the northern subtropical zone, warm temperate zone, and middle subtropical zone, whereas the southern subtropical zone exhibited a more pronounced sensitivity to anthropogenic drivers. The SC quantified the evolving synergy between PM2.5 and O3 variations. This coefficient provides a consistent basis for evaluating long-term progress in coordinated air quality control and supports simultaneous reductions in PM2.5 and O3 while respecting the unique environmental context of each climate zone.

title: Distributionally robust optimal scheduling of urban multi-energy wastewater treatment plants under multiple uncertainties
abstract: Urban wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are evolving from electricity-intensive facilities into multi-energy systems, which makes coordinated operation considerably more complex. This paper proposes a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) coordinated scheduling framework for urban multi-energy WWTPs under multiple uncertainties. First, a coordinated scheduling model of WWTPs that jointly considers electricity, heat, water, and biogas is developed, which incorporates wastewater multistage utilization, blower start-stop control, and carbon trading. Then, a combined 1-norm and ∞-norm ambiguity set is constructed to characterize multiple uncertainties in the photovoltaic (PV) power output and effluent flow, based on which a two-stage DRO model is formulated. The resulting model is solved using a column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm that iteratively solves a master problem and a two-layer subproblem. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves operation economy, enhances internal energy utilization, and reduces carbon emissions. The results further show that the DRO method effectively balances economic performance and operational robustness. Besides, simultaneously accounting for uncertainties in PV power output and effluent flow reduces the total cost of the WWTPs by 1.24% and 0.49%, compared with the cases considering only PV power output and effluent flow uncertainties respectively.

title: Greenhouse gas and economic assessments of biochar-based composite panels from forest residues
abstract: Among other threats to forests across the western U.S., large-scale outbreaks of mountain pine beetle have generated extensive volumes of low-value forest residues that increase wildfire risk while remaining underutilized as a carbon resource. Converting these residues into high-value biochar products offers a pathway for carbon stabilization and value creation, yet most existing markets for biochar remain relatively low value. This study represents the first system-level assessment of biochar-based composite panels that jointly evaluates life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and techno-economic performance for biochar-based panel products at industrial scale. The modeled system integrates distributed biochar production using portable pyrolysis units with centralized panel manufacturing that uses kraft lignin as a renewable binder. In addition to a base-case (BC) configuration representing conventional biochar-lignin composite panel production, five alternative scenarios are modeled in which panels undergo secondary pyrolysis treatments at different temperatures and processing conditions associated with potential adsorption, structural, or fire-resistant applications. Cradle-to-gate GHG emissions range from 311 to 565 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . In addition, an illustrative 100-year carbon retention scenario based on assumed long-term biochar stability results in net GHG balances ranging from −343 to −750 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . Minimum selling price values range from 548 to 1101 US$/m 3 depending on panel type and processing conditions. The BC panel configuration falls toward the higher end of conventional particleboard and MDF price benchmarks, while the estimated MSPs of pyrolyzed panel configurations fall within or below the price ranges of selected benchmark materials used in water remediation and fire-resistant composite applications. These comparisons provide market-price context for the modeled MSPs but do not establish functional equivalence or commercial competitiveness, which require experimental validation.

title: Morphology-aware bidirectional state-space model for power prediction in CNC milling
abstract: Accurate power prediction in CNC milling is essential for process-level power assessment, low-carbon process planning, and power-aware scheduling. However, existing data-driven predictors often degrade around trajectory transitions, as they rely on one-way temporal histories and insufficiently represent geometry-induced load variation. This paper proposes a morphology-aware bidirectional state-space model (MA-BiSSM) for CNC milling power prediction. A bidirectional scanning policy exploits historical states and pre-known planned-trajectory context within a machining window, improving prediction around entry, cornering, and exit regions. A material-removal morphology module encodes a Z-map-derived two-dimensional material-removal map together with a removal-height gate, conditioning the cutting-related correction on geometry-induced load variation. Experiments on real CNC milling monitoring data evaluate the prediction of the X-, Y-, and Z-axis powers and spindle power. Compared with the best result among all competing models for each metric, MA-BiSSM reduces RMSE, MAE, Abs Sum Error, and normalized absolute error (NAE) by approximately 33.0%, 19.1%, 15.3%, and 19.1%, respectively (LSTM for RMSE, MAE, and NAE; Mamba for Abs Sum Error). Ablation studies confirm that bidirectional temporal modeling and material-removal morphology conditioning provide complementary gains in transient accuracy and long-horizon power-profile consistency. The resulting power-profile estimates can support comparison of alternative toolpaths and process-parameter settings, peak-load identification, and energy-aware process planning for cleaner machining.

title: Economic and environmental assessment of waste-derived aviation fuels using agent-based modeling under carbon pricing
abstract: Limited attention has been given to how environmental performance and economic incentives jointly shape aviation fuel adoption under evolving policy conditions. Most existing Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) studies rely on aggregated optimization models that assume equilibrium conditions, overlooking decentralized decision-making and actor heterogeneity. This study addresses this gap by framing the adoption of SAF as a complex adaptive system, where diverse flight agents respond to economic and regulatory incentives, producing fleet-level outcomes through decentralized operational decisions. An integrated framework is developed, combining life cycle assessment (LCA), techno-economic data, and agent-based modeling (ABM), simulating fuel selection at the individual flight level. By integrating environmental assessment with economic optimization, the model allows analysis at both flight and fleet levels. Results show that a 50% pyrolysis bio-oil blend consistently minimizes total operational cost under carbon pricing, reducing fleet-level costs from USD 9.38 billion for operating on 100% conventional jet fuel baseline to USD 4.7 billion while achieving significant lifecycle emissions reductions. The framework enables testing of alternative policy instruments, such as carbon pricing and blending mandates, providing practical insight into the aviation decarbonization pathway. Future research will incorporate endogenous supply–demand interactions, dynamic fuel pricing, infrastructure and resource constraints, and stochastic decision-making to better capture evolving SAF markets and improve the framework's applicability.

title: Bi-objective pareto low-carbon automatic demand response of energy-intensive enterprises accommodating users’ electricity consumption habits and behaviors
abstract: With the advancement of technology and social development, the carbon emissions caused by enterprises’ electricity consumption have become increasingly severe, intensifying the urgency of environmental governance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Low-Carbon Automatic Demand Response (ADR) method for energy-intensive enterprises, which is based on time scale classification and a multi-objective optimization framework. Firstly, considering the influence of historical data on future electricity planning, a method was proposed to classify and average the historical data on a time scale to extract typical days, in order to extract representative electricity consumption patterns. On this basis, a multi-objective optimization model for Low-carbon ADR in energy-intensive enterprises is constructed. This model relies on historical electricity consumption data, electricity price data, and carbon factor data. By establishing electricity cost targets and carbon emission targets while taking into account constraints such as power balance, upper and lower limits of electricity consumption, and comfort level, it formulates comprehensive electricity plans for energy-intensive enterprises. By introducing 10 multi-objective optimization algorithms, simulation analyses were conducted in the different scenarios that before and after classification of 210 days of historical data according to the time scale, as well as in the typical-day scenarios of electricity consumption behavior extracted based on 210 days of historical data, ultimately generating diverse electricity consumption strategies. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively assist energy-intensive enterprises in participating in ADR, ensuring production needs and comfort satisfaction while achieving a coordinated reduction in electricity costs and carbon emissions.

title: Organic copper substitution mitigates feed-derived copper emissions by enhancing bioefficacy and redox–microbiota homeostasis in Eriocheir sinensis
abstract: Copper supplementation is essential in aquaculture for maintaining growth and physiological functions but poses significant environmental risks due to poor bioavailability and excessive discharge from inorganic copper sources such as copper sulfate (CuSO4·5H2O). This study evaluated hydroxy copper methionine (HCM), a highly bioavailable organic copper complex, as a sustainable nutritional alternative in the diet of Eriocheir sinensis using an integrated multi-omics approach combining transcriptomics and 16S rRNA sequencing. Over an 8-week feeding trial, dietary HCM (8, 18, 28, and 38 mg/kg) was compared with conventional CuSO4·5H2O (18, 28, and 38 mg/kg) in terms of copper retention, growth performance, antioxidant activity, intestinal microbiota modulation, and estimated unretained copper. Supplementation with 18 mg/kg HCM achieved copper retention and growth performance comparable to those of 28 mg/kg CuSO4·5H2O. HCM significantly enhanced antioxidant capacity, as indicated by increased Cu-Zn SOD activity, T-AOC, and GSH levels; upregulated antioxidant genes (gst, Cu-Zn sod) and copper homeostasis-related genes (Ctr1, mt1); and modulated lipid metabolism-related genes (acox1, me2). Transcriptomic analysis showed enrichment of glutathione metabolism and peroxisomal pathways. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed a marked restructuring of the intestinal microbiota, characterized by selective enrichment of Bacteroides, which was positively associated with antioxidant and immune indices. Mass-balance modeling projected that replacing 28 mg/kg CuSO4·5H2O with 18 mg/kg HCM could reduce annual copper additive input by 19,398–22,250 kg and reduce projected unretained copper discharge by 8,588–9,851 kg at the baseline FCR of 2.5. These findings support HCM as a nutritionally effective and environmentally responsible alternative for cleaner and more sustainable crustacean farming.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and determinants of the marginal abatement cost of agricultural nonpoint-source pollution in China
abstract: Agricultural nonpoint-source pollution control depends not only on the scale of pollution emissions but also on regional differences in the opportunity costs of abatement. Identifying the marginal economic cost of additional pollution abatement across regions is essential for assessing abatement potential, optimizing the allocation of abatement resources, and balancing food security with agricultural environmental protection. However, the spatiotemporal evolution and formation mechanisms of the marginal abatement cost (MAC) of agricultural nonpoint-source pollution remain insufficiently explored. Using panel data for 30 provinces in China from 2000 to 2023, this study estimates the MAC of agricultural nonpoint-source pollution using a slacks-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs and examines its spatiotemporal evolution, regional disparities, and determinants by combining Dagum Gini decomposition, kernel density estimation, and a two-way fixed-effects model. The results show that: (1) The MAC exhibited an overall fluctuating upward trend during 2000-2023, accompanied by pronounced spatial disparities, while pollution load and MAC showed a clear spatial mismatch; (2) The overall Gini coefficient also followed a fluctuating upward trend, with between-region disparities constituting the primary source of overall inequality. The MAC distribution generally shifted toward higher values, with a relatively concentrated distribution in Central China, more pronounced stratification in Eastern China, and some degree of divergence in Western China in certain years; (3) Agricultural industrial agglomeration, rural labor quality, and agricultural technology level all exhibited U-shaped relationships with MAC. Fiscal support for agriculture had an overall negative effect, whereas the crop disaster rate had an overall positive effect. Moreover, the effects of agricultural technology and crop disasters displayed pronounced heterogeneity across grain production functional zones and geographical regions. This study reveals the spatial disparities and formation mechanisms of the incremental abatement costs of agricultural nonpoint-source pollution, providing a basis for identifying low-cost abatement opportunities, formulating differentiated abatement targets, and optimizing the allocation of fiscal and technological resources, thereby contributing to a better balance among food security, farmers’ incomes, and agricultural environmental protection.

title: Chemical upcycling method for complete binder replacement from recycled asphalt shingle (RAS) binder using renewable chemistry
abstract: Renewable fatty amines can react with asphaltenes in recycled asphalt shingles (RAS) to convert them into maltenes in a process of true chemical rejuvenation. During this reaction the asphaltenes are preferentially converted to Aromatics 3 as shown by the saturates, aromatics, resins-Asphaltene Determinator (SAR-ADTM) data. Size exclusion chromatography data likewise shows a significant drop in the associated asphaltene molecular species. Chemical rejuvenation experiments were performed on an air blown asphalt, extracted binder from RAS, and on a synthetic RAS binder produced by laboratory aging the air blown asphalt. By controlling the process conditions, a minimum of softening produces a chemically rejuvenated asphalt with properties similar to a virgin air blown asphalt, additional softening produces a paving grade binder, and significant softening can be performed to generate a liquid product. Roofing grade and paving grade chemically rejuvenated RAS binders have significantly enhanced low temperature relaxation properties indicated by low values for the critical temperature of the m-value (Tc(m)). Dynamic shear rheometer Black space diagrams confirm that the chemical rejuvenation process improves the ductile behavior by shifting the phase angle to higher values relative to dilution with the same fatty amine. This process is repeatable as it was reapplied successfully after re-aging the chemically rejuvenated binder—thus providing circularity. According to binder-level characterization, high-quality asphalt binders produced from this novel method potentially allows for oxidized and aged binders to replace 100% of virgin binder, thus opening the door for perpetual roofing and paving asphalts. Reaction products produced from extracted RAS asphaltenes, that were separated by heptane precipitation, and coco amine were analyzed by SAR-AD which showed transformation of asphaltenes into Aromatics and Resins. Proton NMR, FTIR, and GCMS data gave evidence of alkyl groups and alkyl amines being grafted onto the aromatic structure of asphaltenes.

title: Power production and emergy-based sustainability in port areas
abstract: Port activities represent an outstanding sector in Blue Economy, with a contribution of approximately 11% to the Gross Value Added of the Blue Economy in the European Union. In addition, Blue Economy guidelines for Trans-European Transport Network — TEN-T — consider the deployment of structures and facilities enforcing clean On-Shore Power Supply — OPS — for ships at berth, and sustainable marine transport and port activities. This paper presents a comprehensive emergy-based sustainability assessment on the improvement of port areas with power supply systems based on Oscillating Water Column technology — OWC — to be used as specific OPS facilities, grid supply or ultimate storage systems. Emergy evaluation accounts for materials, machinery and workers, as well as their direct and indirect CO 2 emissions and embodied energy — eMergy —. Emergy-based indexes are calculated to appropriately quantify the degree of sustainability and renewability of a marine project, its dependence on social investments and the pressure on local ecosystems. A case study of OWC power facility commissioning in a port terminal project is presented for a better focusing. Without loss of generality, results show that the implementation of OWC power facility into the port system improves the overall sustainability, renewability, emergy-based indicators, as well as a reduction in CO 2 emissions, even if breakwater construction and port activities are not sustainable solely, involving non-renewable resources and fluxes from the environment and society. Moreover, the emergy budget allows to analyse the evolution of sustainability during the operational phase due to delays in construction and operational stops, showing that emergy accounting is a valuable tool for long-term management and planning of port infrastructure regarding sustainability.

title: Synergistic evaluation of pollutants and carbon emissions in typical spent lithium-ion batteries recycling processes
abstract: Existing lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) recycling processes disproportionately focus on pollution control and fail to achieve whole-process carbon reduction. Therefore, system-level identification of the critical stages driving carbon emissions in LIBs recycling processes and the development of feasible synergistic strategies for pollution and carbon mitigation are urgently needed. In this study, a carbon–pollution synergistic framework based on the Tapio decoupling method is established for 15 typical LIBs recycling processes and multiple synergistic pathways are explored. The comprehensive environmental impact (CEI) assessment demonstrates that the recycling process with the lowest pollutant environmental impact depends on the LIBs type. Direct recycling has the lowest CEI for LiFePO4 (LFP), whereas pyrometallurgy has the lowest CEI for LiNixCoyMn1−x−yO2 (NCM), LiNixCoyAl1−x−yO2, LiCoO2 (LCO) and LiMn2O4 (LMO). Global warming potential (GWP) quantifies carbon emissions of LIBs recycling processes, which are primarily driven by energy consumption, especially during the direct recycling of LCO and LMO. High CEI does not necessarily coincide with high GWP because the dominant drivers of pollutant impacts and carbon emissions differ amongst recycling processes. The synergistic assessment identifies direct recycling of LFP and NCM and pyrometallurgy of LCO and LMO as synergistic processes, with LCO pyrometallurgy achieving a Balanced Synergy index of 0.86. After exploring various potential pathways, the GWP of LIBs recycling is reduced by approximately 34% by 2050 under balanced synergy scenario. This research provides a quantifiable synergistic assessment of LIBs recycling and offers new insights to guide sustainable LIBs recycling technology selection.

title: Uncovering the heterogeneous effects of China's Organic-Substitute-Chemical-Fertilizer policy: The role of local conditions in shaping distinct policy responses
abstract: China's Organic-Substitute-Chemical-Fertilizer (OSCF) policy aims to reduce chemical fertilizer dependence, yet its county-level effectiveness may vary with local production, capacity, and implementation conditions. Using panel data for 2726 counties from 2012 to 2022, we estimate the average and heterogeneous effects of OSCF on chemical fertilizer application intensity with double machine learning and SHAP-based interpretation. The policy is associated with a statistically significant average reduction in standardized chemical fertilizer application intensity, with an average treatment effect of −0.0469 that remains stable across robustness checks. Cross-county heterogeneity is expressed mainly in response magnitude. The estimated reduction is 0.0291 larger in high- than low-target-relevance counties and 0.0338 larger in non-grain-oriented than grain-dominant counties. Gross Output Value of Agriculture and Gross Regional Product rank highest in feature importance, followed by broadband access, non-food cropping, and village committees. Among representative fitted county profiles, the high Gross Output Value of Agriculture profile has a fitted response 0.0256 closer to zero than the low profile, whereas the high Gross Regional Product profile is 0.0335 more negative than the low profile. Contributions of key conditions vary across observed levels. Descriptive joint profiles also show configuration-specific differences, with high target relevance combined with high broadband access having a fitted response about 0.041 more negative than the low-low profile. These results motivate differentiated county screening that begins with policy-scope relevance and then assesses production feasibility, farmer/local adaptive capacity, and policy transmission and implementation capacity to identify where local assessment and policy-addressable support should focus.

title: Mechanical harvesting of cyanobacterial blooms shifts greenhouse gas potential to post-harvest sludge in a hypereutrophic lake
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms are increasingly managed through large-scale mechanical harvesting, but greenhouse gas (GHG) production from moisture-rich cyanobacterial sludge (CS) remains poorly constrained. We conducted two controlled experiments using natural cyanobacterial biomass and harvested CS from Lake Dianchi, a hypereutrophic lake in southwestern China, to assess GHG accumulation in bloom-affected lake water and post-harvest CS. In the biomass-gradient experiment simulating natural cyanobacterial concentrations, dissolved CH4, CO2 and N2O increased significantly with cyanobacterial biomass (p < 0.001). Maximum GHG concentrations in the highest-biomass treatment were 1.91-, 2.95-, and 1.94-fold higher than those in the lowest-biomass treatment, respectively. Dissolved GHG concentrations were positively associated with chlorophyll a (Chl-a) and turbidity, but negatively associated with dissolved oxygen (DO) and pH, indicating that bloom biomass accumulation and associated physicochemical shifts promoted GHG accumulation in lake water. In the moisture-manipulation experiment with harvested CS, CH4 release increased significantly with sludge moisture, reaching 2.3-fold higher levels at 93.17% moisture than at 78.21%, whereas N2O peaked at lower moisture levels. Sludge decomposition shifted archaeal communities toward methanogen dominance, with Methanosarcina and Methanobacterium becoming predominant. Structural equation modeling indicated that moisture-driven GHG responses were associated with shifts in sludge organic and nitrogen pools, particularly the coupled variation of dissolved total nitrogen (DTN), volatile solids and protein. These findings demonstrate that mechanical harvesting transfers part of the bloom-derived GHG production potential to post-harvest CS, where high moisture favors CH4 accumulation. Post-harvest CS handling, including rapid dewatering, shorter wet storage, and low-carbon treatment, should therefore be integrated into lower-carbon bloom management.

title: Experimental investigation of phosphorus and potassium recovery from chicken manure incineration ash (CMIA) using a mixed nitric acid–oxalic acid system
abstract: Traditional acid leaching of chicken manure incineration ash (CMIA) often shows poor selectivity and may generate phosphogypsum. To address these limitations, this study developed a nitric–oxalic acid process for recovering phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) from CMIA with a high Ca/P ratio. The influence of thermal-treatment temperature on the transformation of P-bearing phases in chicken manure was investigated. At 1073 K, thermal treatment promoted the transformation of operationally defined organic P into crystalline calcium phosphate (Ca-P) phases. The leaching behavior under different mixed acid conditions was systematically studied. Under optimal mixed acid conditions, P and K leaching efficiencies reached 91.24% and 94.45%, respectively. Kinetic fitting, the apparent activation energy of 10.81 kJ/mol, and particle-size dependence were consistent with a mixed-control process involving an appreciable diffusion-related contribution. Under these conditions, XRD identified hydrated calcium oxalate phases in the residue, while FTIR and SEM-EDS corroborated oxalate groups and Ca-C-O-rich deposits. Thermodynamic calculations indicated that concurrent Ca precipitation during Ca-P dissolution was feasible. The process produced a nitrate-containing, P- and K-rich leachate. A 35-day cherry-radish pot experiment provided preliminary evidence of its fertilizer application potential, while commercial formulation and storage stability require further validation. Because no sulfate reagent was introduced, the process may help reduce phosphogypsum generation at the source.

title: Basin-scale coupling between water-resource protection priority areas and urban–agricultural–ecological configuration typologies: Evidence from the Dongting Lake Basin, China
abstract: Climate change, urbanization, and intensified resource development are increasing pressure on freshwater systems and creating a need for spatially differentiated basin-scale protection. This study develops an integrated evaluation-configuration-diagnosis framework for the Dongting Lake Basin (DLB) from 2000 to 2023. A Water Resource Protection Importance Index (WRPI) and multiscale sensitivity analysis were used to identify stable high-demand areas. Class-level aggregation indices (CLUMPY) characterized the aggregation of urban, agricultural, and ecological spaces and identified stable spatial configurations. Spatial overlay delineated coupled priority areas, while an obstacle-degree model diagnosed municipal-level constraint structures. Stable high-demand areas were concentrated in the southern and southwestern basin, and their core distribution remained consistent across grid scales. In the urban-agricultural-ecological sequence, Low-Low-Low (LLL) and Low-High-High (LHH) were the dominant stable configurations, accounting for 40.99% and 31.62% of the total stable-configuration area, respectively. Overall, 90.96% of stable high-demand areas overlapped with stable configuration units, with LLL and LHH jointly accounting for 71.08% of the total overlap. The WRPI obstacle structure remained stable over time and was dominated by constraints related to Water Resource Conditions and Water Resource Development Potential, although their relative importance varied among municipalities and configuration contexts. Integrating municipal obstacle structures with stable configurations connected basin-scale priority assessment with specific spatial implementation contexts. The framework supports spatially targeted and differentiated water-resource governance in the DLB and provides a transferable workflow for other large basins.

title: A transformer-MPA-KEA integrated framework for adaptive remediation trains in contaminated sites: Multi-objective collaborative trade-offs and knowledge-enhanced decision constraints
abstract: Remediation technology decision-making is a crucial aspect of risk management at contaminated sites, as its rationality directly influences contaminant reduction efficiency, economic performance, and the sustainability of subsequent site management. In practice, remediation is not merely a one-time technology screening task, the preferred remediation technology may evolve throughout the remediation process. Recent advancements in machine learning and deep learning offer a foundation for capturing the complex relationships between diverse site information and remediation technologies. However, most artificial intelligence studies still treat remediation technology selection as a static classification task, thereby limiting their capacity to update remediation train decisions during the remediation process. To address this limitation, this study established a structured knowledge graph integrating 690 contaminated site cases with an independent remediation technology database. Based on this foundation, a Transformer-MPA-KEA framework was developed for adaptive remediation train decision-making. By integrating MPA and KEA, the framework generated stage-specific technology priorities and provided perspective-level contributions and feature-technology associations for interpreting the decision results. Model interpretation indicated that contaminant properties, engineering-economic constraints, and hydrogeological conditions contributed most to the model outputs. In a case study of a contaminated site, groundwater monitoring of benzene facilitated a staged transition from pump-and-treat (P&T) to in-situ chemical oxidation (ISCO), followed by monitored natural attenuation (MNA). Overall, the proposed framework provides a data-driven approach for monitoring-informed, stage-wise remediation technology decision support.

title: A framework for assessing the carbon-water-energy nexus of cropping systems, applied to tobacco production
abstract: Carbon, water, and energy use are tightly interconnected in crop production, and integrated carbon-water-energy assessments have been used to evaluate these interactions. However, less attention has been paid to whether the three subsystems develop in a coordinated manner, which subsystem constrains nexus performance, and which variables are most strongly associated with its spatiotemporal variation. This study integrates carbon footprint (CF), water footprint (WF), and emergy input (EM) accounting with a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, elasticity-based sensitivity analysis, and a random forest model to diagnose the carbon-water-energy nexus of cropping systems. The framework was applied to tobacco production in 17 Chinese provinces from 2004 to 2021. Producing 1 kg of dry tobacco leaf emitted on average 5.9 kg CO2-eq, consumed 1.6 m3 of water, and required 6.4 × 1012 sej of emergy inputs. The curing stage accounted for 70% of CF and 36% of EM, while green water dominated WF. The national CCD mean increased from 0.77 in 2004 to 0.80 in 2010, declined to 0.66 in 2015, and recovered to 0.78 in 2021. Northern provinces were generally better coordinated than southeastern provinces. The water subsystem was the main internal constraint, while curing-energy consumption and nitrogen fertilizer input showed the strongest predictive associations with CCD. Site-specific irrigation optimization, targeted nitrogen management, and clean-energy transition in curing are critical to enhancing the sustainability of tobacco production. The framework can be adapted to other crops when crop-specific inventories and parameters are available, and expanded to broader ecological indicators.

title: Pyruvic acid-based reactive deep eutectic solvents enable in-situ lignin stabilization for enhanced biomass valorization
abstract: Lignin condensation during biomass pretreatment severely limits both cellulose accessibility and lignin valorization, posing a fundamental challenge to lignocellulosic biorefineries. Herein, a pyruvic acid-based reactive deep eutectic solvent (PA-DES) composed of choline chloride and pyruvic acid was developed, in which PA serves as not only the hydrogen bond donor but also a reactive agent potentially contributing to lignin regulation. Kamlet–Taft analysis revealed favorable solvent properties for biomass fractionation, enabling superior delignification (up to 98.66%) compared with conventional lactic acid-based DES (LA-DES). Consequently, near-complete enzymatic hydrolysis was achieved at a low enzyme loading (5 FPU/g glucan) after alkaline washing.
