Notably, PA-DES produced lignin with structural characteristics consistent with a lower extent of condensation relative to lignin produced with LA-DES under the conditions investigated, despite the acidic pretreatment environment. Structural analyses suggest that PA may have contributed to lignin structural regulation and may have limited condensation while simultaneously introducing carboxyl functionalities during pretreatment, yielding lignin with a carboxyl group content of 0.78 mmol/g. The resulting lignin could be directly utilized as a functional adsorbent without additional post-modification, exhibiting a maximum methylene blue adsorption capacity of 331.64 mg/g. Furthermore, a solvent-property-guided regeneration strategy enabled repeated reuse of recovered PA-DES after component replenishment while maintaining high pretreatment performance. Overall, this work demonstrates that reactive DES design can simultaneously enable biomass fractionation and lignin functionalization, providing an effective strategy for integrated lignocellulosic valorization.

title: Life cycle assessment of dairy sludge-based biodiesel production process via acid catalytic and thermal transesterification reactions
abstract: Second-generation biodiesel is recognized as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels because it avoids competition with food resources and reduces the production costs of edible oil-based feedstocks. However, its sustainability depends on the production process, necessitating quantitative evaluation through life cycle assessment (LCA). Despite its importance, LCA studies of biodiesel derived from dairy sludge remain limited, with most focusing on catalyst-based processes and few evaluating thermal approaches. This study conducted a comprehensive LCA comparing acid-catalyzed and thermal conversion scenarios for biodiesel production from dairy sludge. Results show that the catalytic biodiesel production, due to its lower yield of 66.4% compared to 75.8% for thermal biodiesel production, required higher solvent consumption per functional unit, resulting in greater environmental burdens across most impact categories. Specifically, the global warming potential for catalytic route was 254.7 kg CO2-eq/kg BD, which was 5.5% higher than thermal route (240.8 kg CO2-eq/kg BD). Sensitivity analysis indicated that lipid yield, biodiesel yield, and chloroform consumption were the key influencing parameters, with variation ranges of approximately ±10%, ±6%, and ±4%, respectively. These results demonstrate that improvements in process yield as well as the management of solvent usage have a significant impact on overall environmental performance. In addition, the chloroform recovery analysis showed a strong negative correlation between recovery rate and all environmental impact categories, indicating that an increase in recovery rate can effectively reduce environmental burdens. This study provides baseline data for dairy sludge-based biodiesel production and contributes to research directions for sustainable biodiesel production.

title: Crystal-water-mediated construction of inorganic framework of magnesium chlorocarbonate for AsIII mineralization via structure reconstruction
abstract: Mineralization performance of traditional magnesium-based materials is limited by mass transfer, causing the reactions to be confined primarily to the external surface. Meanwhile, the synthesis of inorganic framework materials with ordered internal channels remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a convenient synthesis using only urea and MgCl2·6H2O to construct a magnesium-based inorganic framework, Mg2(CO3)Cl(OH)·3H2O (denoted Tunnel-Mg). The structure consists of interconnected MgO6 octahedra bridged by carbonate groups, forming 15-membered puckered rings and continuous axial tunnels. Weakly confined water molecules and chloride ions occupy these channels, maintaining charge balance and framework stability. Time-resolved crystallization and hydration-control experiments reveal that Tunnel-Mg forms through rapid phase-selective nucleation within a balanced hydration environment, where crystal water promotes precursor reorganization and retained chloride stabilizes the open-channel structure. By virtue of its channel structure and labile chloride ions, Tunnel-Mg achieves a maximum AsIII uptake capacity of 384.48 mg g−1 in arsenic-contaminated water. Experimental results demonstrate that AsIII species trigger the migration of tunnel-confined guest species and induce structural reconstruction, transforming the pristine nanorods into Mg–O/Mg–OH-rich nanosheets. XANES/EXAFS analysis and DFT calculations reveal that AsIII is stabilized primarily via inner-sphere bidentate binuclear As–O–Mg coordination on reconstruction-derived Mg–OH sites. Furthermore, Tunnel-Mg can be integrated with paper pulp to form a macroscopic flow-through filter while retaining effective AsIII removal. This work highlights labile channel ions as structural regulators of framework reconstruction, offering a design principle for magnesium-based mineralization materials with accessible internal reactivity.

title: Nonlinear threshold effects of land use mixture on ecosystem health and zoned governance in China's land border regions
abstract: China's land border regions represent a convergence of biodiversity hotspots, ecological fragility, and socioeconomic underdevelopment, rendering them particularly susceptible to land-use change. Although these regions are experiencing intensifying land-use mixing (LUM) alongside a gradual decline in ecosystem health (EH), most existing research has centred on urban settings, leaving the nonlinear threshold dynamics between LUM and EH in border contexts largely unexamined. Focusing on the 60-km inland buffer zone along China's land borders, this study integrates econometric and machine-learning approaches to characterize the spatiotemporal patterns, spatial associations, and nonlinear threshold characteristics linking LUM and EH between 2000 and 2025. The results showed that LUM increased gradually over the study period, whereas EH declined slightly, with both exhibiting pronounced spatial heterogeneity. The differences between LUM and EH were primarily attributable to interregional variation, and the two showed a significant negative spatial correlation overall. No universal LUM–EH threshold was identified at the national scale, whereas pronounced nonlinear relationships and region-specific thresholds emerged at the regional scale. Higher thresholds emerged in the southwestern border region and Tibet, whereas lower thresholds characterized the northeastern, northern, and northwestern border regions. The predictive contributions of LUM factors to EH and their interactions changed markedly across the threshold. Before the threshold, natural ecological land types, including forestland, grassland, and unused land, showed greater predictive contributions. Beyond the threshold, the contributions of farmland and construction land increased, accompanied by a shift in land-use relationships from relatively simple coupling to the coexistence of multi-type synergies and trade-offs. These findings provide a scientific basis for ecological security governance in China's land border regions and offer a transferable analytical framework for balancing land development with ecological conservation in border regions worldwide, in support of the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Hydrophilic headgroup engineering of oleochemical-derived branched nonionic surfactants for bio-based aircraft hard-surface cleaners
abstract: High-performance bio-based surfactants derived from renewable oleochemical feedstocks are indispensable for aircraft hard-surface cleaning. However, traditional branched surfactants exhibit inherent drawbacks such as complex synthetic routes and narrow feedstock sources. Additionally, the structure-activity relationships (SARs) of novel oleochemical-based branched nonionic surfactants and their synergistic effects with anionic surfactants remain poorly understood. To address these knowledge gaps, we systematically explored the SARs of three oleochemical-based surfactants (DMOEn, 12-HMEEn, and 9/10-HMEEn) by correlating their molecular architectures with surface activity and application performance. The stability, synergism, and optimal formulations of mixtures prepared by mixing these nonionic surfactants with linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) were also evaluated, along with the performance of optimized formulations. The results revealed a clear SARs for these surfactants: Y-shaped congeners with smaller hydrophilic headgroups exhibited superior surface tension reduction capacity, whereas X-shaped surfactants with larger hydrophilic moieties possessed higher reduction efficiency owing to a lower critical micelle concentration (CMC). Moreover, symmetric hydrophobic alkyl chains and terminal ester moieties in the hydrophobic chains modulated surface activity by altering molecular aggregation and interfacial adsorption. All mixtures exhibited excellent stability, and strong synergistic effects were observed between nonionic and anionic surfactants. The optimal formulations were determined to be 6#, 42#, 86# (LAS-based) and 31#, 66#, 112# (SDS-based). These optimized formulations exhibit characteristic branched surfactant properties, including exceptional wettability, low foaming and rapid defoaming, and deliver excellent hard-surface cleaning efficiency that is comparable to both commercial XP70-based formulations and FMEE-derived bio-based reference systems. This work elucidates the SARs of oleochemical-based branched nonionic surfactants, lays a theoretical foundation for their performance optimization, and provides a potentially sustainable high-efficiency formulation for aircraft hard-surface cleaning.

title: A DPP-enabled decision support system for end-of-life strategy recommendation
abstract: The transition towards a circular economy requires reliable lifecycle information to support end-of-life (EoL) decision-making. Using a sample luminaire, this study proposes a decision-support component designed to enhance Digital Product Passport (DPP) functionality by integrating lifecycle data, condition monitoring, predictive analytics, and stakeholder priorities for end-of-life strategy selection. Guided by Axiomatic Design principles, a prototype platform was developed and demonstrated for the representative lighting fixture. The system combines product information, sensor-derived condition indicators, remaining useful life estimation, anomaly detection, and multi-criteria user preferences to generate probabilistic recommendations for alternative EoL strategies. An interactive dashboard was implemented to provide an intuitive user interface and support transparency and usability. Industrial evaluation with domain experts confirmed the conceptual validity and practical relevance of the approach while highlighting challenges related to data governance, interoperability, cybersecurity, and business model integration. The findings demonstrate the potential of intelligent DPP-enabled systems to support circular decision-making and sustainable lifecycle management.

title: The policy triad: Designing the interactions of incentive, constraint, and enabling instruments on ecosystem value realization
abstract: The translation of ecological assets into sustainable economic value remains a core challenge in environmental governance. Although gross ecosystem product (GEP) accounting offers a standardized metric for ecosystem outputs, the patterns through which policy portfolios are associated with GEP variation—including their relative contributions, non-linear thresholds, and interaction effects—are not well quantified. This study develops and empirically examines an integrative “Incentive-Constraint-Enabling” (ICE) framework to characterize the heterogeneous associations between six environmental policy instruments and GEP variation across Chinese provinces. Applying a machine-learning approach (XGBoost-SHAP) to data from 2014 to 2023, we identify three predictive patterns. First, the policy portfolio is associated with substantial variation in GEP and exhibits nonlinear contribution patterns, including diminishing marginal contributions of green finance at higher intensity levels and differentiated contribution patterns of constraint-based instruments across policy ranges. Second, we identify differentiated contribution patterns across ecosystem service dimensions: incentive-based instruments show stronger predictive contributions to material supply, constraint-based instruments are more closely associated with regulatory services, and enabling instruments exhibit stronger contributions to cultural services. Third, both policy effectiveness and their interactions are recalibrated by regional socio-ecological contexts, with identical combinations producing synergies in some regions but antagonisms in others. These insights contribute to precision environmental governance by highlighting the importance of calibrating policy intensity and bundling instruments into context-sensitive portfolios that reflect differences in ecosystem service objectives and regional conditions.

title: Novel and efficient removal of impurities from spent silicon contact mass via an in situ copper-catalyzed leaching process
abstract: As spent silicon contact mass (SCM) continues to accumulate, recovering silicon from this waste stream has become increasingly important for resource sustainability and waste management. In this study, we developed a novel in situ copper-catalyzed leaching strategy that exploits the copper naturally present in SCM to promote impurity dissolution in an oxidative acid-leaching system, thereby facilitating the efficient removal of impurities and the recovery of both silicon and copper. Compared with conventional leaching processes, the proposed approach substantially enhanced impurity removal. Under optimized conditions, the leaching efficiencies of iron, aluminum, and calcium reached 99.33%, 97.54%, and 99.59%, respectively, while the purity of the recovered silicon and the copper recovery efficiency reached 99.76% and 98.82%, respectively. The leaching kinetics of iron were analyzed using the shrinking-core and homogeneous-reaction models. The homogeneous-reaction model provided a better fit to the experimental data. When combined with activation-energy analysis, the rate equation, and its criterion number, these kinetic results provided further insight into the mechanism governing iron dissolution. Overall, this study demonstrates an environmentally sustainable strategy for the efficient removal of impurities and high-value recovery of resources from SCM. The proposed process offers a promising route for hazardous-waste valorization and supports cleaner production within a circular economy.

title: The politics of forest biomass co-firing in Indonesia: Explaining policy implementation through the Actor–Network–Interest (ANI) framework
abstract: Biomass co-firing in coal-fired power plants has been promoted as a transitional strategy for increasing the share of renewable energy in Indonesia's electricity sector to support the national goal of net-zero emission. This paper analyses actor's behaviour to shed light on why the implementation of biomass co-firing policy has yet to reach the target level required to achieve national targets. To do so, this paper develops a novel Actor–Network–Interest (ANI) Framework that predicts actors' implementation behaviour based on the interaction between their structural positions within policy networks and the consistency of their formal and informal interests. It employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, combining Social Network Analysis (SNA) of 65 actors with in-depth interviews and qualitative stakeholder analysis. SNA was used to identify influential actors through degree and betweenness centrality, while qualitative analysis explored the formal and informal interests underlying actors' policy responses. The results reveal a cross-sectoral network dominated by actors from the energy and forestry sectors, with limited participation from market and civil society organisations. Perhutani and PLN Energi Primer Indonesia (PLN EPI) occupy the most central positions due to their strategic roles in biomass supply and electricity system integration. The interaction between network position and interest finds three dominant implementation patterns: 1) selective–pragmatic, 2) administrative–selective, and 3) compliant–administrative. These findings support the explanatory and predictive value of the proposed framework. At the same time, brokerage functions remain weak, indicating limited capacity to coordinate interests across sectors. Consequently, biomass co-firing has been implemented largely as an incremental adjustment compatible with existing coal-based electricity systems rather than as a transformative energy transition strategy. The findings highlight the importance of stronger brokerage mechanisms, better-aligned incentives, and more effective cross-sectoral coordination to accelerate renewable energy transitions.

title: Multidimensional contributions to the water-energy-food nexus: Interpretable evidence from cities in China's Yellow river region
abstract: River basins are critical to resource security and sustainable development. Using panel data for 54 prefecture-level cities in provinces traversed by the Yellow River from 2006 to 2020, this study evaluates water–energy–food (WEF) coordination and examines its associated factors. An entropy-weighted coupling coordination model is combined with a CNN–BiLSTM–Attention model and SHAP analysis to capture nonlinear and heterogeneous contribution patterns, while a two-way fixed-effects model serves as a linear benchmark. The proposed model achieves a held-out evaluation R2 of 0.726 and an RMSE of 0.088. Green expansion contributes the largest share to model predictions (29.23%), followed by growth (24.35%), carbon reduction (23.99%), and pollution reduction (22.43%). Ecological conditions, industrial structure upgrading, and digital development emerge as key factors. Digital development and green finance are generally associated with higher WEF coordination, whereas pollution emissions and intensive industrial activities are associated with constraints under specific conditions. The results support differentiated, place-based resource governance for the sampled cities.

title: Voyage-based optimisation of biofuel bunkering strategies using real ship data
abstract: Maritime decarbonisation requires operationally realistic strategies that account for fuel availability and evolving regulatory constraints. This study presents a data-driven framework for optimising biofuel bunkering strategies for a real-world bulk carrier by integrating historical voyage data, port-specific biofuel availability, lifecycle emissions, and regulatory performance metrics. Historical voyage data are used to reconstruct routes and estimate energy demand. Candidate biofuels derived from different feedstocks, including FAME, HVO, and biodiesel blends (B24 and B30), are evaluated using a multi-objective optimisation model (NSGA-III) considering: (i) the overall WTW GHG emission intensity, (ii) lost cargo volume, and (iii) annual FuelEU compliance margin. Results show that fuel type primarily governs WTW emissions, while feedstock availability influences high-biofuel-share pathways, and port-level biofuel availability dominates optimal bunkering strategies. Waste-based biofuels achieve the lowest WTW emission intensities (≤16 gCO 2 eq/MJ), outperforming animal fat-derived (20-22 gCO 2 eq/MJ), crop-based biofuels (44-51 gCO 2 eq/MJ), and biodiesel blends (>70 gCO 2 eq/MJ). Cargo volume loss remains minimal (<1%) across all scenarios. Regulatory analysis indicates that crop-based biofuels become non-compliant with FuelEU GHG intensity targets by 2045. The proposed framework enables actionable, voyage-specific decarbonisation strategies and highlights the critical role of fuel type, feedstock selection, port-level fuel availability and biofuel supply development.

title: City-scale dynamic mining zoning for source-based damage reduction and efficient coal resource utilization in high-groundwater-table coal–farmland overlapped areas
abstract: In high-groundwater-table coal–farmland overlapped areas, the superposition of temporal groundwater-level fluctuations and mining-induced subsidence exposes permanent basic farmland to long-term dynamic risks. However, existing mining spatially partitioned subsidence control technology generally adopts static groundwater levels as the design baseline, resulting in conservative risk assessment and constrained resource utilization efficiency. To address this issue, a city-scale mining suitability zoning method incorporating groundwater dynamics was proposed in this study. Taking Yongcheng City, China, as a case study, groundwater monitoring data from 2019 to 2024 were used, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model was employed to achieve quarterly dynamic updating of groundwater levels. Furthermore, a dynamic groundwater threshold was established under the dual constraints of crop yield reduction and soil salinization, and was coupled with subsidence responses under different mining methods to develop a dynamic zoning determination system. The results indicate that the study area exhibits a city-scale spatial pattern characterized by restricted mining in the sensitive western area, conditionally suitable mining in the central area, and natural mining in the eastern area. Compared with conventional mining design, the proposed dynamic subsidence-control design increases the suitable mining area by 74.24% relative to the conventional design, while maintaining the productive function of permanent basic farmland. At the pre-mining planning stage, 103.65 km2 of stably releasable overlying coal resource space and 299.74 km2 of conditionally releasable space requiring dynamic regulation can be identified within the coal–farmland overlapped area. This study provides a city-scale decision-making pathway for alleviating the conflict between coal resource extraction and permanent basic farmland protection in high-groundwater-table regions and for achieving efficient utilization of underlying coal resources.

title: Tax coal or subsidize clean capacity? A differential game of incumbent utilities’ energy transition
abstract: Electricity decarbonization requires both replacement investment and decisions about the remaining life of coal assets. This paper develops a Stackelberg differential-game benchmark with an incumbent utility that builds clean capacity and retires coal, and an independent clean developer. Binding organizational constraints make construction and closure substitutes; binding finance can instead make them complements when retirement releases net funds. Annual numerical experiments compare five policy classes using a common post-window continuation rule, incumbent-value limits and explicit capacity-gap ceilings. In the normalized China-scale baseline, the highest-welfare unconditional candidate found within the tested policy class coincides with clean support alone. Retirement-linked support combined with an early coal charge raises welfare by 1.07% relative to that benchmark and induces 0.0317 TW of accelerated retirement without an aggregate capacity gap. Freezing the same realized support and charge paths removes almost all accelerated retirement, identifying a behavioral contribution from the link. The advantage is conditional: it disappears under zero continuation values, and declining clean-capacity credits can reverse fixed-policy rankings. Wider support bounds also change the preferred instrument mix. The results identify how shared adjustment resources and dependable replacement capacity condition policy choice; the numerical rates are unestimated policy experiments for an existing portfolio, rather than national forecasts.

title: Spatial distribution and influencing factors of data center water usage effectiveness in China
abstract: This study evaluates the direct water consumption of data centers using water-side cooling systems in China. A WUE calculation framework is developed by coupling cooling-tower water loss with cooling-system COP. Long-term meteorological data are used to extract representative typical days, which are then used to simulate annual and seasonal WUE patterns across major Chinese cities. The results show a clear spatial pattern: WUE is generally lower in northern and western China and higher in southern and eastern China. For closed-circuit cooling towers, WUE is mostly below 1.0 L/kWh in Northeast China, Northwest China, and the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau, but approaches or exceeds 2.0 L/kWh in hot and humid cities in South China. Among the eight national data center hub regions, the wet-cooling operation ratio is 27.3% in Inner Mongolia, 36.6% in Ningxia, and 52.4% in Gansu, while it reaches 100% in the Pearl River Delta. The results indicate that climate conditions and cooling-control strategies strongly affect water use. In the model, a 7 °C wet-bulb threshold is used for closed-tower dry-wet switching and for identifying open-tower natural-cooling availability, while open-tower air-to-water-ratio modes are classified using seasonal mean dry-bulb temperature.

title: Global coal mining carbon emissions: Spatiotemporal evolution patterns, driving mechanisms and China's decoupling path under carbon neutrality
abstract: Global climate governance faced a critical window to achieve the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C target. As a key part of coal's full-life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions, coal mining emissions became a core focus for global methane mitigation and the coal sector's low-carbon transition However, long-term spatiotemporal patterns, nonlinear drivers, and mine-level empirical evidence remain unclear. This study developed a novel multi-scale analytical framework that bridges global macro-level patterns and mine-level micro-level heterogeneity by integrating 44-year global panel data (1981–2024) with mine-level data from 12,568 Chinese mines. This cross-scale integration, combined with phased random forest–SHAP modeling, IPCC Tier 2 estimation, operation-level emission tracing, and LMDI decomposition, enables consistent empirical analysis across scales—from global spatiotemporal evolution to mine-specific technological mechanisms. Results show global coal mining emissions experienced three phases: moderate growth (1981–1999), rapid expansion (2000–2013), and decelerated growth (2014–2024), with an inverted-V marginal emission intensity. High-emission areas concentrated in East Asia, South Asia, central-western Europe, and central-eastern North America, with an eastward shift of the emission center. Six major coal-producing countries formed four evolutionary patterns. The emission driving effect also displayed an inverted V-shape, peaking during 2000–2012 and weakening markedly after 2014, with obvious cross-country heterogeneity. China's coal mining achieved decoupling: output increased by 2.78% while methane emissions decreased by 8.84%. Mine-level results revealed large intensity differences across methods, gas grades, and scales; heading operations were the main bottleneck, and mining depth had a nonlinear threshold effect. LMDI decomposition showed structural optimization contributed 78.7% to the emission intensity decline and technological progress 21.3%. This study clarifies the spatiotemporal dynamics and drivers of global coal mining emissions, reveals China's decoupling pathways, and supports low-carbon transition and methane mitigation.

title: Decarbonizing Canadian commercial aviation: Efficiency gains, sustainable aviation fuel, and structural limits to emissions reduction
abstract: Commercial aviation is a difficult-to-abate sector in which traffic growth can offset improvements in operational and fuel efficiency. This study evaluates the decarbonization trajectory of Canadian commercial aviation from 2015 to 2025, examining whether efficiency gains have been sufficient to counteract activity-driven emissions growth and represent a persistent structural improvement. This study analyzes eight open-government analytical datasets, supplemented by two external benchmark sources. Kaya–Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition quantifies the contributions of activity, stage length, load factor, and fuel intensity to CO 2 emissions, while trend and structural-break analyses assess changes in emissions intensity. Complementary analyses examine airport recovery, an exploratory association between occurrence-based turbofan representation and aviation incidents, and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) scenarios. Annual CO 2 intensity declined significantly over the non-pandemic period, and fuel-intensity improvements avoided approximately 2.9 Mt CO 2 between 2015 and 2019. However, activity growth added approximately 5.3 Mt CO 2 , outweighing these gains. Monthly analysis identifies a major structural disruption at the onset of COVID-19 followed by a subsequent recovery regime. Airport recovery was heterogeneous, while the safety analysis identified an exploratory negative association between occurrence-based turbofan share and incident counts. Under the SAF uptake and traffic-growth scenarios evaluated, fuel substitution alone does not fully offset projected activity-driven emissions growth through 2030. Overall, efficiency improvements have reduced Canadian aviation carbon intensity but remain insufficient to achieve sustained reductions in absolute emissions under continued traffic growth, highlighting the need to evaluate accelerated SAF deployment alongside additional mitigation measures. When the observed fuel-efficiency trend and the 5% SAF blend are evaluated jointly, however, projected 2030 emissions fall to approximately 19.8 Mt—below the 2025 level of about 20.1 Mt—so that the two levers together offset essentially the entire traffic-driven increment.

title: Incremental learning-based dynamic multiobjective optimization algorithm for disassembly line balancing
abstract: Disassembly line balancing is a key operational problem in remanufacturing and circular manufacturing systems. In practical disassembly lines, task processing times are not stationary because component corrosion, wear and deformation, together with robot performance degradation, continuously change operation durations and resource availability. These physical-state variations make the Pareto-optimal solution set and Pareto front migrate across environments. Existing dynamic multiobjective evolutionary algorithms commonly reuse raw historical populations, rebuild archives or reconstruct learning models after environmental changes, which may cause redundant knowledge accumulation, negative transfer, high repeated learning cost and catastrophic forgetting. To address these issues, this paper proposes an incremental learning-based dynamic multiobjective optimization algorithm, termed IL-DMOEA, for physical-state-driven dynamic disassembly line balancing. The algorithm integrates physical-state modeling, density-based historical knowledge clustering, environment-similarity matching, prototype memory construction, knowledge incremental update, memory retention, prototype-driven initialization and evolutionary search into one unified method chain. Historical nondominated solutions are first organized into transferable cluster-level knowledge, and this knowledge is then compressed into compact prototype memory units that can be locally updated when new environments arrive. Computational experiments on 12 dynamic disassembly instances under high-, medium- and low-similarity environments show that IL-DMOEA obtains competitive or superior mean inverted generational distance, mean hypervolume and average running time results compared with representative dynamic multiobjective and disassembly line balancing algorithms. The results indicate that prototype-memory-based incremental learning can improve both solution quality and response efficiency in long-term dynamic disassembly optimization.

title: Identification of descriptors for thiophene desulfurization and heavy metal immobilization over K-modified calcium-based materials
abstract: Inhibiting the emission of sulfurous species and heavy metals is essential for the clean utilization of carbon-containing resources in the co-pyrolysis of sludge and low-rank coal. Although calcium-based materials show promise for pollutant control, existing materials suffer from limited multifunctionality and low utilization efficiency. Herein, a theoretical investigation based on density functional theory (DFT) calculations was conducted to elucidate thiophene desulfurization mechanisms and heavy metal adsorption energies on CaCO3 and K2Ca(CO3)2, while ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations were performed to evaluate the structural stability of the optimized catalyst. The KCa-terminal of K2Ca(CO3)2 exhibits optimal bifunctional performance. Density of states analysis reveals that K incorporation enhances the electronic activity of p orbitals, and there exists a positive correlation between the p-band center to the Fermi level and both desulfurization and immobilization performance. Microscopic dynamic analysis identifies 873−923 K as the optimal desulfurization temperature. Furthermore, machine learning-based feature correlation analysis identifies eight key descriptors governing heavy metal adsorption energy, which are integrated into a unified expression to quantitatively elucidate the contributions of geometric structure and electronic properties. This work establishes a theoretical insight into the rational design of efficient bifunctional materials.

title: Mass and functionality based exergy analysis of different rapeseed protein production routes
abstract: Rapeseed proteins are among the outstanding plant-based proteins due to their favorable interfacial functionality. This study evaluates the resource use of the most common rapeseed protein production routes – acidic precipitation, ultrafiltration and wet mild fractionation – using an exergy-based approach. The exergy consumption is normalized based on both product mass and protein functionality. Mass-based assessment indicates that the routes producing dry rapeseed protein concentrate exhibit relatively low exergy efficiencies (12.3 – 20.7%), mainly due to production of a single useful stream and dilute processing conditions that intensify the drying-related exergy demand. Wet mild fractionation shows the highest exergy efficiency at 47.3%, by distributing resource inputs across two useful products, oleosome cream and proteins. When evaluated based on protein functionality, however, ultrafiltration-based recovery of proteins from rapeseed meal and acid precipitation from cold-pressed cake emerge as the least exergy-intensive options to produce rapeseed protein-based emulsifiers. Therefore, the study shows that the resource use efficiency of a process is strongly dependent on the chosen evaluation criterion and highlights the importance of functionality-oriented valorisation of useful streams to enhance the efficiency of resources use.

title: Automated detection of morphologically diverse microplastics using ensemble deep learning
abstract: Microplastics in water emerge as hazardous materials that contaminate the environment and adversely impact public health. Current approaches for detecting and characterizing microplastics are manual and inefficient in time, cost, and labor. Recent advances in deep learning-based computer vision approaches have enhanced efficiency, while they suffer from low accuracy for various types of microplastics. This paper presents a size-adaptive ensemble deep learning approach, aiming to overcome the challenge of morphological diversity and automate the detection of microplastics. The approach employs two specialized YOLOv8 models, including a high-resolution model for small particles (e.g., pellets) and a standard-resolution model for large particles (e.g., fibers, films, fragments). The presented approach was implemented and evaluated using a dataset including 1,600 images. The results show that the approach improved detection accuracy (17.5% increase in mAP50, 32.1% increase in mAP50-95) compared with traditional unified deep learning models. This research advances the ability to automatically detect various microplastics based on computer vision and deep learning.

title: Reaction and microstructural insights into UHPC with carbonated steel slag at different substitution ratios
abstract: Basic oxygen furnace (BOF) slag, a major type of steel slag generated during steelmaking, offers significant potential as a low-carbon cement replacement. Carbonation pretreatment has been developed to enhance both the filler effect and the pozzolanic reactivity of steel slag powder (SSP), enabling partial replacement of cement with carbonated SSP (CSSP) in ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC). However, the reaction mechanisms governing CSSP in UHPC remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the phase assemblage, calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) characteristics, and microstructure of UHPC substituted with CSSP were investigated. The results revealed that the optimal mechanical performance was achieved at a 30 % replacement level, with the compressive strength being 10.0 % higher than that of the untreated SSP mixture. At moderate CSSP contents, carbonation-derived calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) acted synergistically as both a micro filler and nucleation site. Consequently, UHPC substituted with CSSP exhibited a higher degree of hydration (DoH), an increased mean chain length (MCL) of C-S-H, and higher pore fractal dimensions than UHPC with untreated SSP. However, at 40-50 % CSSP substitution levels, cement clinker dilution becomes dominant and outweighs the compensatory physical filler effect and chemical contribution of CaCO 3 . Although additional carbonate ions can promote the formation of AFm-type carbonate phases, the reduced availability of reactive clinker limits CH generation and decreases the Ca/Si ratio of the C-S-H gel. Consequently, C-S-H formation becomes insufficient, leading to limited pore refinement, increased pore irregularity, and a less dense UHPC matrix.

title: Is Metro-based logistics always greener? A carbon emission break-even analysis under the trend of electrification and multi-dimensional spatiotemporal constraints
abstract: Metro-based Underground Logistics Systems (M-ULS), which leverage spare capacity in urban rail transit networks, have been widely regarded as a promising solution for alleviating urban congestion and reducing carbon emissions. However, as battery electric trucks (ET) rapidly proliferate and regional electricity grids progressively decarbonize, the traditional binary comparison of “metro versus diesel trucks” is no longer a sufficient basis for claiming M-ULS environmental superiority. Two questions remain unresolved: whether M-ULS retains meaningful emission advantages over electric trucks under realistic urban operating conditions, and how road congestion, ambient temperature, and metro stop-start dynamics jointly shape this comparison. This study develops a refined carbon accounting model that compares M-ULS with both electric trucks and conventional diesel trucks (DT) within a unified framework. The model incorporates a BPR (Bureau of Public Roads) function-based congestion coefficient and powertrain-specific temperature correction factors. These are applied symmetrically to all road-based segments, including M-ULS drayage, under a consistent well-to-wheel boundary. The model also derives a marginal energy consumption formula for metro operations, capturing microscopic stop-start characteristics. Under the baseline scenario (a single shipment of 55 t over a 40 km O-D (Origin-Destination) distance), M-ULS reduces carbon emissions by 69.8% compared to DT and by 24.2% compared to ET. These advantages are conditional. The emission edge inverts when last-mile drayage exceeds a critical distance of 9.6 km, and reduction rates above 20% require trunk distances beyond roughly 19 km together with drayage shares kept below 15% of total distance. A network-distance analysis of Shenzhen shows that about 79% of freight endpoints lie within a 3 km drayage radius of metro stations, indicating that these boundary conditions are largely attainable in practice. The study further reveals distinctive climate robustness. Under severe congestion and large temperature deviations, whether severe cold or intense heat, the emission reduction dividend of M-ULS relative to electric trucks is maximized. These findings delineate clear spatiotemporal boundaries for M-ULS applicability and provide quantitative evidence for tiered, zone-specific green logistics strategies.

title: Thermally treated oyster shells elevate biofilm viability and nutrient removal in sediment microbial fuel cells
abstract: Sediment microbial fuel cells (SMFC) effectively treat benthic pollutants and simultaneously generate bioelectricity. This study evaluates novel application of thermally treated oyster shell (COS) at 600°C to promote biofilm viability and benthic nutrient removal for 375 days. Sustaining microbial biomass adhesion and viability on anode surface is essential for long-term SMFC operation, which relies on sediment microbial metabolism. In CLSM imaging, green fluorescence in COS-10g and COS-20g reflect high biovolumes of viable microbial biomass, correlated with increased COS dosing. FESEM shows that COS-10g and COS-20g produce the thickest and most densely packed biofilms on anode surfaces. Maximum viable biofilm thickness is 40 μm, with biovolumes of 242,698 and 140,610 pixels and viabilities of 91.2% and 85.8% for COS-10g and COS-20g, linked to Ca2+ elution from COS. High biofilm viability improves mass electron transport by reducing charge transfer resistance to 193 Ω (COS-10g) and 84 Ω (COS-20g), coinciding with higher biofilm viability at higher COS dosing. SMFC enhances PO4-P removal across all COS cases, reducing PO4-P from 1.92 to 0.30 mg/L in COS-10g, while control cases remain up to 1.8 mg/L, highlighting the synergistic effect of SMFC and COS addition. COS addition with SMFC operation does not result in pH elevation that would deteriorate sediment microbial activity, maintaining sediment pH between 6.392 and 6.503 throughout operation. COS-10g shows the highest sediment ORP of −94.2 mV, reflecting notable biofilm viability for microbial oxidation in sediment. Valorizing thermally treated COS waste improves SMFC by boosting microbial biomass and nutrient removal for bioelectricity generation.

title: Systematic power decarbonization strategies for sustainable steel manufacturing: an integrated modeling framework combining process regulation and technology integration
abstract: Achieving an economically feasible low-carbon transition is critical for the steel industry. Electricity serves as a central energy carrier in steel manufacturing, making power decarbonization important to the low-carbon development of this sector. However, existing studies often underrepresent the system-wide propagation effects arising from the coupling between production and power systems, which can bias estimates of decarbonization benefits and associated trade-offs. This study develops an integrated modeling framework to quantify the emission and economic contributions of electricity and to evaluate plant-level power decarbonization strategies based on parameter regulation and low-carbon technology deployment. For the case plant, emissions of the BF-BOF process are 1548.14 kg-CO2/t-CS, of which electricity-related emissions account for 24.79% (383.82 kg-CO2/t-CS). Energy costs account for 12.08% of the total cost (2739.08 CNY/t-CS). Adjustments to raw-material quality, production organization, and technical parameters can synergistically achieve carbon and cost reduction of the power and production system. Under the specified electricity price, emission factor, and substitution ratio, contractual green-power procurement reduces emissions and may achieve cost parity without carbon-market revenue. The plant-gate CCU scenarios yield substantial emission reductions, but the economics depend on carbon prices, capture costs, and downstream CO2 utilization revenues. The scrap-EAF route supplied with green electricity can reduce emissions to 35.51 kg-CO2/t-CS, though it relies on stable supply of cost-competitive scrap steel. The DRI-based routes remain sensitive to costs and emissions associated with hydrogen production, indicating the necessity of low-cost green hydrogen supply and supportive market conditions.

title: From data-driven analysis to system development: A framework for developing an ease-of-disassembly evaluation system based on experimental data and multi-source text
abstract: Existing ease-of-disassembly evaluation systems are increasingly challenged by the high integration and multi-layered structural characteristics of electronic products, such as smartphones and tablets. Many existing approaches rely heavily on expert judgement and outcome-oriented metrics, whilst lacking sufficient support from disassembly process data, which limits their interpretability and applicability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a systematic, data-driven framework for developing ease-of-disassembly evaluation systems for electronic products. A candidate indicator pool is first constructed by integrating multi-source text data from academic literature, policy documents, and industry forums. Standardized disassembly experiments are then conducted to collect process data and identify representative disassembly scenarios. Based on these data sources, a three-pathway indicator screening strategy integrating data analysis, scenario cases, and mechanism-based judgement is developed to establish a multi-level ease-of-disassembly indicator system. Subsequently, indicator quantification rules and a subjective–objective hybrid weighting method are employed to construct a computable and interpretable evaluation model. The proposed framework is instantiated and validated through a smartphone case study. Four representative smartphone models are evaluated, and the results demonstrate that the proposed system can effectively distinguish ease-of-disassembly performance, identify disassembly bottlenecks, and support targeted design improvements. A comparative analysis with the time-based eDiM method further shows that the proposed approach provides stronger capability in bottleneck diagnosis, causal explanation, and improvement guidance. The proposed framework provides a practical and extensible basis for supporting disassembly-oriented product design and sustainable end-of-life management of electronic products.

title: Feasibility study of stabilizing soft soil in the Jianghan Plain using one-part alkali-activated materials developed by iron and steel slags
abstract: The stabilization of soft soil subgrade is essential for infrastructure development in lacustrine regions; however, conventional cement stabilization faces challenges related to limited applicability and high carbon emissions. This study developed a one-part alkali-activated material (OPAAM) using alkali-fused steel slag (AFSS) and granulated blast furnace slag (GBFS) for stabilizing soft soil from the Jianghan Plain, China. Response surface methodology, multi-objective particle swarm optimization, and entropy-weighted TOPSIS were used to optimize strength, workability, CO2eq, and cost. The optimized OPAAM was prepared with a precursor blend containing 29.0 wt% AFSS and 71.0 wt% GBFS, with sodium silicate and borax externally added at 9.1 wt% and 3.4 wt%, respectively, based on the total precursor mass. At this proportion, OPAAM reduces CO2eq by 82% compared with cement. Soft soil stabilized with 16 wt% OPAAM achieved a 28 d compressive strength of 3.9 MPa, exceeding that of the 20 wt% cement-stabilized control, while reducing CO2eq and cost by 85.6% and 17.6%, respectively. Microstructural analyses showed that C-(N-)A-S-H gel and hydrotalcite were the main hydration products of OPAAM, which filled pores and bound soft soil particles and served as the primary source of strength in the stabilized soft soil. Heavy metals leaching concentrations of OPAAM stabilized soft soil remain far below regulatory limits, confirming its environmental safety. This study provides theoretical and practical insights into the production and application of low-carbon soft soil stabilizers.

title: When does Remanufacturing versus new product manufacture pay off? Derivation of a commercial ReMan formula and decision logic based on empirical ratio analyses across multi company production data
abstract: Remanufacturing (ReMan) is an ecologically and economically promising production approach and business model for enabling a circular economy and conserving resources. However, its adoption across industrial sectors remains limited due to a lack of knowledge and guidance on the product characteristics and cost factors that support a profitable ReMan business. Therefore, this study derives a commercial ReMan formula linking those production cost metrics that significantly influence profitability with corresponding product characteristics. The formula is based on a ratio analysis of product characteristics and commercial data from successful ReMan cases (n=355) covering various product categories from two mechanical engineering companies. Our results show that the economic efficiency of ReMan business is primarily driven by increasing net and material costs, increasing weight, and greater product complexity including part count. In contrast, assembly costs, testing costs, logistics costs, overhead surcharges, and the expected CO2e-surcharge savings of ReMan products exert only a marginal impact on cost-effectiveness. Based on the findings, a ReMan formula and decision logic are developed, incorporating four identified key commercial metrics: (1) the value of reusable ReMan components, (2) repurchase price of the used product, (3) costs of disassembly, cleaning, and inspection of the used product, and (4) the price delta between new and remanufactured product. Future research could extend the derived ReMan formula by investigating absolute cost thresholds for critical ReMan activities, such as disassembly, cleaning, and inspection, to identify economic barriers limiting ReMan adoption, particularly in consumer goods markets and further industrial sectors.

title: Dual regulation of CO2 hydrate formation by clay mineral and kinetic promoter: mechanistic insights for marine sequestration
abstract: Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration is recognized as a promising strategy to mitigate global warming due to its large storage potential and long-term stability. However, the role of clay minerals widely distributed in marine sediments in regulating hydrate formation remains poorly understood, hindering field-scale deployment. In this study, low-field nuclear magnetic resonance was used to investigate the effects of typical clay minerals (montmorillonite, illite, and kaolinite) on the kinetics and spatial evolution of CO2 hydrate formation. The results demonstrate that, despite the presence of sodium dodecyl sulfate as a kinetic promoter, clay minerals generally exhibit an inhibitory effect. This inhibition arises from two synergistic mechanisms: clay-induced reduction in water activity limits the availability of free water molecules, while adsorption and electrostatic interactions between clay particles and the promoter modify the zeta potential and Derjaguin–Landau–Verwey–Overbeek interaction energy, increasing foam viscosity, suppressing local drainage, and narrowing Plateau–Gibbs channels, thereby weakening the promoting effect of the promoter. Among them, montmorillonite exhibits the strongest inhibition due to its large specific surface area and interlayer swelling, resulting in a 7.98% reduction in sequestration efficiency compared with the seawater system (70.57%). Considering clay-induced inhibition, the global and northern South China Sea hydrate-based CO2 sequestration storage capacities were evaluated, indicating a reduction of at least 2520 Gt CO2 globally and ∼23.43% locally. These findings provide pore-scale insights into clay–hydrate interactions and guidance for hydrate-based CO2 sequestration site selection.

title: When is carbonation-cured concrete actually cleaner? A systematic review, a net-benefit condition framework, and a proposed minimum reporting set for CO2 mineralization in cement-based products
abstract: Cement manufacture releases 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO 2 , most of it from the irreducible calcination of limestone. Accelerated carbonation curing mineralizes captured CO 2 inside cement-based products. Whether it delivers a net climate benefit, and under what conditions, cannot presently be answered from the published life-cycle assessment (LCA) literature. A reproducible PRISMA 2020 search (713 records), confirmed against Web of Science, identified seventeen studies declaring a functional unit, a cradle-to-gate boundary and a non-carbonated comparator. Their outcomes cannot be pooled: five functional-unit bases, seventeen comparators, baselines spanning 280–540 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 , and results reported in structurally different forms. That incommensurability is the first finding. In most of the set the benefit tracks avoided Portland clinker rather than mineralized CO 2 : every reduction above 10% involves clinker being substituted or eliminated, and one study reports 5–8 kg CO 2 -eq per tonne of cement for each 1% of clinker replaced. Across matched comparisons the isolated effect of carbonation spans both signs — from a 3.1–11.3% net increase once process electricity is charged to reductions of 37%. Varying only the CO 2 recovery route for one product returns 68%, 77% and 71%. Of twenty-five papers reporting an environmental result, eight omit a functional unit or system boundary. A net-benefit condition model accounts for the spread, and a five-field minimum reporting set mapped to EN 15804, ISO 21930 and ISO 14025 is proposed so future LCAs can be synthesized.

title: Does memory of hydrological processes and atmospheric dryness influence forest fire intensity: A case study in the western Himalayas
abstract: Forest fires in the Western Himalayas are characterised by high-intensity energy releases, resulting in influencing forest functionality. In contrast, fire management remains largely reactive due to limited understanding about the climatic and ecological drivers of forest fires in the region. The current study was attempted to identify the relationships between climatic and ecological drivers with fire intensity by integrating a 13-year (2012–2024) spatially thinned fire dataset with multi-seasonal hydroclimatic, vegetation, and terrain variables across different Himalayan forests in Himachal Pradesh, India. These variables were modelled for fire radiative power using structural equation modelling (SEM) and random forest bench marking. The findings indicate a significant hydrological memory effect, whereby antecedent winter precipitation (AWP) influenced pre-monsoon fuel moisture and was indirectly associated with fire intensity, whereas spring rainfall had a non-significant impact. Vapour pressure deficit (VPD) exhibited the strongest direct association with fire intensity (β = 0.15), while multi-group SEM revealed ecosystem-specific responses. AWP showed a significant positive effect on vegetation moisture across all forest ecosystems, whereas VPD showed a significant negative effect. In dry deciduous forests, vegetation moisture (β = −0.185) and distance to housing (β = −0.140) also significantly affected fire intensity. Gradient hydroclimatic perturbation analysis (±10% and ±20%) indicated that fire intensity was more sensitive to changes in VPD and vegetation moisture than to changes in AWP. Overall, AWP and VPD were associated with vegetation moisture and fire intensity, providing a mechanistic understanding of the hydroclimatic pathways across Himalayan Forest ecosystems.

title: When circularity gains diverge from social-equity outcomes: A justice-oriented agent-based scenario-comparison model with an Amsterdam case study
abstract: This study develops a justice-oriented agent-based model (ABM) to examine how everyday circular-economy (CE) practices, spatial access to CE infrastructure and labor-market assumptions jointly shape distributive urban outcomes. Using Amsterdam as an illustrative case, the model represents household sorting, bulky-item drop-off and repair behavior under uneven access to sorting containers, recycling centers, repair cafés and waste-burden locations. Four CE policy scenarios are compared through replicated simulations, plausibility checks and extended sensitivity screening. The results show that CE-active scenarios generate circular activity relative to the Linear reference, while mean local CE activation and flow-based citywide CE throughput do not always follow the same pattern. Under the model's assumed negative reduced-form CE–unemployment coupling, CE-active scenarios also produce lower simulated unemployment. This conditional result reflects the specified labor-market mechanism and does not imply that CE policies generally cause unemployment to fall. Spatial-advantage inequality is higher in CE-active scenarios when scenario-specific opportunity activation interacts with uneven access and burden layers, while accumulated-resource inequality does not automatically decline under stronger CE support. The main contribution is a transparent scenario-analysis testbed that connects household heterogeneity, spatial opportunity, behavioral mechanisms and distributional consequences, helping to explore when aggregate circularity gains may diverge from justice-oriented urban outcomes.

title: Cleaner peri-urban agricultural transitions under nitrogen-related water constraints: A teacher-validated evaluation of land-use alternatives in Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands
abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. This study develops a teacher-validated framework for evaluating cleaner peri-urban agricultural land-use alternatives, using Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands, as a living-lab case. We combine the InVEST Nutrient Delivery Ratio (NDR) model as a process-based teacher model with deep surrogate models and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to generate and screen alternative crop-pattern configurations under explicit feasibility constraints. Candidate Pareto solutions are then materialised and re-evaluated with the teacher model, which separates rapid screening from final environmental interpretation. The framework is designed around an explicit scale mismatch: land-use decisions are taken on individual parcels and governance blocks, whereas nitrogen impacts accumulate over the whole planning domain. Under the available data regime, the governance-aligned graph surrogate outperforms pixel-level emulation and provides acceptable screening fidelity on the 32 × 32 intervention grid. Teacher validation shows that the best alternatives lower domain-integrated subsurface nitrogen export by up to 998.55 kg N yr −1 (ΔN = −998.55 kg N yr −1 ), equivalent to about 10.8% of the baseline, at an intervention footprint of about 2392 ha. Screening reliability is further quantified through rank association, top- K precision and Pareto overlap. The contribution of the study is to link cleaner peri-urban agricultural transition, nitrogen-related environmental management and land-use alternative appraisal in a single reproducible framework for comparing productive configurations under water-quality constraints. More broadly, the study shows how rapid alternative exploration and teacher-validated environmental evidence can be combined to support cleaner and more sustainable peri-urban land-use transitions.

title: Dynamic responses of Rhodobacter capsulatus to light and oxygen cultivated on H2 and CO2: Effects on the productivity of biomass, protein, pigments, coenzyme Q10, and antioxidant capacity
abstract: Hydrogenotrophic autotrophic growth of purple non-sulphur bacteria, on H2 and CO2, provides a route to produce proteins and high-value chemicals such as pigments and coenzyme Q10 while avoiding inputs derived from fossil fuels and agriculture. While heterotrophic production of these compounds is established, production under hydrogenotrophic conditions and systematic research on the influence of light and oxygen on these compounds remains underexplored. In this study, Rhodobacter capsulatus was cultivated in a bioreactor under photohydrogenotrophic (with light), chemohydrogenotrophic (with O2), and mixohydrogenotrophic (with both light and O2) conditions. The study focused on volumetric productivity and biomass composition (proteins, pigments, coenzyme Q10, and antioxidant capacity). Highest productivities of biomass (1.20 ± 0.35 gTSS L−1 d−1) and protein (0.65 ± 0.14 g protein L−1 d−1) were achieved mixohydrogenotrophically. Photohydrogenotrophic conditions exhibited the highest bacteriochlorophyll (27.0 ± 1.8 mg gTSS−1) and carotenoid (7.5 ± 0.4 mg gTSS−1) content, which was dependent on biomass concentration in the reactor. The elevated pigment content also resulted in the highest antioxidant capacity of the biomass. In contrast, chemohydrogenotrophy resulted in the lowest volumetric productivity (0.61 gTSS L−1 d−1) and reduction of pigment content, although coenzyme Q10 concentration remained similar to mixohydrogenotrophic conditions (2.3 to 2.6 mg gTSS−1). These findings demonstrate that the hydrogenotrophic metabolism of Rb. capsulatus can be strategically tuned to prioritise volumetric productivity or high-value compounds for microbial food or feed applications.

title: Spatiotemporal variability of pavement material costs: Implications for maintenance strategies and economic-environmental sustainability
abstract: Traditional pavement management often fails to account for the spatiotemporal variability of material and energy costs, compromising both budgetary accuracy and long-term sustainability. To bridge the gap, this study introduces a dynamic optimization framework that integrates spatiotemporal cost predictions into multi-year maintenance planning. Using provincial-level monthly cost data from China, five time series models were developed and validated for key pavement materials and energy, with prediction uncertainty quantified via residual bootstrapping. An exhaustive search over a five-year decision period within a 10-year life-cycle analysis then identifies strategies that minimize total life-cycle cost, encompassing agency cost, user cost, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Results show significant spatiotemporal variability in historical costs, which was effectively captured by province-specific models, achieving in-sample and out-of-sample mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) both within 10%. Maintenance optimization under dynamic cost scenarios alters optimal strategies across provinces, affecting treatment timing, frequency, and intensity due to shifting trade-offs among agency, user, and environmental costs. A life-cycle impact analysis reveals substantial economic and environmental variability. At the national average, total life-cycle costs under dynamic forecasts range from 16.9% below to 9.0% above static baselines, with agency costs exhibiting even greater fluctuation. While mean dynamic forecasts for user costs and GHG emissions align closely with static results, their percentile projections show large deviations, highlighting a high sensitivity to extreme cost pathways. The findings of this study are expected to substantially enhance the realism and accuracy of pavement management strategies under spatiotemporally dynamic economic and environmental conditions.

title: Two-stage robust optimization of shared energy storage system in multi-community energy systems considering electric vehicle flexibility
abstract: The variability of renewable energy and the increasing integration of electric vehicles (EVs) pose significant challenges to the planning and operation of multi-community energy systems. Shared energy storage systems (SESS) have emerged as an effective solution to enhance flexibility and improve system performance. In this study, a multi-community SESS planning and operation optimization framework considering EV participation is developed to determine the optimal storage configuration and operational strategies. First, an electric vehicle cluster (EVC) dispatchable capacity model is constructed to capture EV users’ willingness to participate in scheduling and aggregate the dispatchable capacity of EVC. Then, based on EVC dispatchable capacity, a two-stage robust optimization model is formulated to optimize multi-community SESS planning and system operation under renewable uncertainty. Case studies show that compared with benchmark strategies, the proposed method reduces SESS investment costs by 7.7% and decreases peak grid electricity purchase by 31.56%. In addition, system performance remains stable under renewable fluctuations. The results highlight the potential of SESS combined with EV flexibility for improving the economic performance and resilience of future community energy systems.

title: Predicting staggered carbon peaking in the logistics industry: Evidence from China's new international land-sea trade corridor
abstract: Under China's carbon peaking target, logistics-related emissions require close examination because the sector links regional production and consumption and remains energy-intensive. This study establishes a framework covering emission accounting, influencing factor identification, scenario forecasting, and staggered peaking assessment. Focusing on 12 provinces in China's New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, we trace logistics-related carbon emissions from 1997 to 2021 and project their trajectories for 2022-2040 under business-as-usual, low-carbon, and high-development pathways. By linking regional forecasts with provincial peak timing, the framework extends carbon-peaking analysis beyond a single aggregate turning point. The results show that: (1) Regional logistics emissions rose from 29.56 million tonnes (Mt) in 1997 to 205.46 Mt in 2021, an increase of about 5.95 times; Sichuan, Yunnan, and Xinjiang were the largest emitters in 2021. (2) Ten potential determinants are examined, among which population scale and urbanization are the dominant forces increasing emissions, whereas energy intensity remains a major barrier to mitigation. (3) The regional peak is projected at 229.11 Mt in 2032 under the low-carbon scenario, but is postponed to 2037 and 2038 under the business-as-usual and high-development scenarios, reaching 258.68 Mt and 284.33 Mt, respectively. Nine provinces peak before 2030 under the low-carbon scenario, whereas staggered peaking is less distinct under the other scenarios. (4) Provinces are grouped according to the stability of their peaking outcomes across scenarios, and tailored mitigation strategies are suggested. The framework supports differentiated mitigation in regional logistics systems and can be adapted for use in other countries and regions.

title: Advancing NO2 exposure assessment with hourly seamless retrievals from geostationary satellites
abstract: Although nitrogen dioxide (NO2) poses significant public health risks, conventional polar-orbiting satellites fail to capture its rapid diurnal variability due to limited temporal resolution. To bridge this gap, we constructed a seamless, all-day NO2 dataset at hourly intervals for East-Central China spanning 2017–2023. Our approach integrates infrared observations from the geostationary Himawari-8/9 satellite with ground-based measurements and environmental variables, employing a Random Forest model enhanced by spatiotemporal optimizations. The retrieved concentrations show high agreement with in-situ measurements (sample-based validation: R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 7.30 μg/m3; station-based validation: R2 = 0.78, RMSE = 10.27 μg/m3) and stable performance throughout the day. This high-resolution monitoring captures clear diurnal cycles, characterized by morning and evening peaks versus mid-afternoon minima, and tracks a substantial regional reduction in NO2 levels during the study period (from 24.13 ± 7.65 μg/m3 to 18.22 ± 5.69 μg/m3), attributing to stringent emission controls. However, population exposure analysis reveals persistent challenges: while compliance with the 40 μg/m3 guideline has largely been achieved, over 36% of the population remained exposed to levels above the 25 μg/m3 threshold in 2023, with more widespread exceedances of the stricter 10 μg/m3 standard. In summary, by overcoming the spatiotemporal limitations of previous satellite products, our dataset provides essential support for refined air quality management and health risk assessments.

title: The role of intermediate product innovation in the low-carbon transformation of traditional manufacturing
abstract: Intermediate products connect upstream technologies and materials to downstream production processes. Innovation embodied in these inputs may therefore spread across production networks and contribute to the low-carbon transformation of traditional manufacturing (LCTTM). This study examines the effect of intermediate product innovation (IPI) on LCTTM under domestic and international circulation. We combine patent- and R&D-based knowledge measures with input–output linkages to construct indicators of IPI, using provincial panel data for China from 2006 to 2020 and panel data for 30 countries from 2001 to 2014. The results show that IPI promotes LCTTM, and the main finding is robust to alternative specifications and tests for endogeneity. The effect is stronger in capital-intensive industries, coastal provinces, key regions involved in the Belt and Road Initiative, non-EU countries, and trade-surplus economies. The mechanism results differ between domestic and international circulation. IPI is associated with a larger share of relatively less carbon-intensive fuels and a greater share of output from less energy-intensive industries in the international sample. In the domestic sample, however, changes in energy composition are not statistically evident. One possible explanation is that the effect initially operates through production-efficiency improvements, while the development of low-carbon value chains may temporarily raise the output share of energy-intensive upstream sectors. IPI also increases green and low-carbon technological innovation in both samples. Further analysis shows that intra-provincial and inter-provincial IPI each contribute to LCTTM, but their interaction is negative, indicating competition rather than complementarity across provinces. At the international level, the evidence is stronger for domestically generated IPI, while innovation originating within and outside traditional manufacturing is positively associated with LCTTM when examined separately. These findings show how innovation embodied in intermediate inputs can affect manufacturing decarbonization through regional and sectoral production linkages.

title: Cadmium bioavailability during flooding–drainage in paddy soils: Spatiotemporal associations with dissolved organic matter transformation and iron speciation
abstract: The mechanism underlying the coupled regulation of Cadmium (Cd) activity by Iron (Fe) oxides and dissolved organic matter (DOM) in farmland soils during flooding followed by drainage remains unclear. This study addressed this issue by combining spatial sampling (n = 94) and time-series experiments to elucidate the Fe–DOM–Cd interaction mechanism using the diffusive gradients in thin films (DGT) technique. Regional surveys showed that 83.6% of soils in the study area were acidic, with an average total Cd content of 0.5 mg kg−1, indicating a substantial Cd pollution risk. Examination of soil properties revealed that the initial release fraction of Cd was dominated by organic-bound components and that Fe oxides could indirectly inhibit Cd activity. This study further selected two soils (AH and HS, respectively collected from Anhua and Heshan districts of Hunan Province, China) with similar total contents of Fe, Cd, and organic matter to investigate the differential mechanisms underlying Cd activity regulation during flooding and drainage periods. HS soil consistently contained higher amorphous Fe content than AH soil, and its labile Fe content was 18.3 times that of AH soil after 1 d of flooding. The increase in labile and amorphous Fe in HS soil coincided with a marked decrease in Cd availability after 5 d of flooding, whereas the corresponding decrease in AH soil was substantially delayed. DOM characteristics considerably differed between flooding and drainage periods. AH soil DOM showed higher aromaticity and humification, while HS soil DOM exhibited a cyclic transformation from protein-like substances to humus and back to protein-like substances. Parallel factor analysis identified two major fluorescent components, namely, terrestrial humus (C1) and tryptophan-like substances (C2). During HS soil flooding, C1 proportion increased from 26% to 88%, while during the early AH soil flooding stage, it exceeded 85%. The concurrent increase in labile Fe and DOM humification was associated with the stronger decline in Cd availability in HS soil, suggesting a potential coupled influence of Fe transformation and DOM evolution on Cd dynamics. Overall, this study provides a theoretical reference for Cd risk regulation in contaminated paddy fields.

title: Digitalization systematically shifts the balance between green narratives and substantive green performance in China
abstract: Digital transformation can reduce information friction and in turn promote green innovation. This study, however, shows a more complex pattern. Digitalization not only enables firms to innovate more effectively, but also changes how they produce, communicate, and refine green messages, making visible green claims more likely to run ahead of verifiable green outcomes. Based on a firm-level panel of Chinese listed companies from 2013 to 2024, this study finds that a one-standard-deviation increase in digital transformation is associated with an approximately 7% increase in the green innovation bubble. This implies that digital transformation widens the gap between green patent applications and authorizations. The study also finds that the alleviation of financing constraints is consistent with this relationship, as the evidence suggests that additional financial resources may initially support visible green narratives rather than being converted simultaneously into verifiable technological substance. Moreover, the narrative–substance discrepancy is not uniform across regions. The digitalization-related bubble effect is strongest in low-to-moderate digital financial inclusion cities, but becomes substantially weaker in the most advanced digital-finance ecosystems, which is consistent with stronger screening and discipline at higher levels of financial digitalization. The findings indicate that governance in a digitalization-driven green transition should move beyond expanding visibility and pay greater attention to limiting narrative lead, ensuring that green signals do not systematically run ahead of green substance.

title: High-temperature thermal treatment for the whitening of secondary aluminum dross towards high-value utilization: Overcoming carbon-iron coloration and regulating mineral phase reconstruction
abstract: Although the high alumina content in secondary aluminum dross (SAD) presents excellent resource recovery potential, its conversion into high-value materials is severely restricted by low whiteness caused by iron and carbon. However, the coupled roles of residual carbon and iron during high temperature mineral phase reconstruction remain insufficiently understood, while existing whitening strategies mainly rely on the removal of chromogenic impurities rather than controlling iron valence states and its incorporation into newly formed mineral phases. In this study, coloration mechanisms and phase reconstruction behaviors during calcination are investigated using a pure reagent simulated system and real SAD. Results indicate that residual carbon creates a localized reducing atmosphere, forcing the reduction of Fe(III) into highly chromogenic Fe(II), which is subsequently irreversibly incorporated into complex silicate or aluminosilicate lattices. To disrupt this pathway, rather than using conventional subtractive iron-removal methods, a novel “phase reconstruction and solid-solution inhibition” strategy is proposed via a two-step aerobic thermal treatment coupled with MgO regulation. This strategy exploits the thermodynamic stability zone of Fe2O3 at medium temperatures to preferentially eliminate carbon sources, and this avoids high temperature iron reduction and lattice fixation. Additionally, introducing MgO promotes the formation of high whiteness magnesium aluminum spinel and competitively consumes silicon based chromogenic carriers. Under optimal conditions of two-step calcination in air with 3% MgO, product whiteness increases from 23.9% to 54.1%, alongside the deep denitrification of hazardous AlN, dechlorination and highly efficient fluorine immobilization. This study elucidates the evolution mechanisms of chromogenic impurities, providing an innovative, acid- and chlorine-free theoretical foundation for the safe disposal and utilization of SAD.

title: Assessing cross-regional carbon responsibility through ecosystem service flows: A dual-factor ecological compensation framework for China
abstract: Carbon sequestration services play a critical role in climate regulation and global carbon-cycle stability. However, the spatial mismatch between carbon sequestration supply and demand generates cross-regional ecological externalities and uneven environmental responsibilities, posing significant challenges for sustainable governance. Existing government-led vertical ecological compensation mechanisms often fail to capture interregional ecological linkages and differentiated responsibility relationships. Using Chinese counties as analytical units, this study develops an integrated framework that combines ecosystem service flow analysis with responsibility allocation and ecological compensation design. Specifically, a resistance-adjusted comparative ecological radiation force model (R-CERF) is employed to quantify ecological linkages between carbon-surplus and carbon-deficit regions under spatial heterogeneity, while SHAP-based explainable machine learning is used to identify the major drivers of carbon supply-demand patterns.
