This study develops an open-data pre-feasibility screen for three contrasting pathways: anaerobic digestion of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW), palm oil mill effluent (POME) biogas/compressed biomethane (bio-CNG), and livestock biogas. All 11 Southeast Asian countries represented in harmonized World Bank What a Waste 3.0 and the FAOSTAT database maintained by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) were assessed. A nested OFMSW analysis used the 12 Southeast Asian city records available in the World Bank city dataset. Pathway-specific indicators were normalized within the regional sample and combined using literature-informed weights. Data completeness was excluded from the implementation score and reported separately as weighted observed-evidence confidence. Robustness was tested with resource-led, balanced, and readiness-led scenarios, leave-one-indicator-out tests, and 10,000 constrained random-weight simulations. Indonesia ranked first for POME (88.6) and livestock biogas (87.8), whereas Indonesia (67.2) and Viet Nam (59.4) formed a weight-sensitive OFMSW pair. Ho Chi Minh City ranked first among cities (79.3) and remained first in 99.24% of simulations. Median Spearman correlations between primary and simulated rankings were 0.973 for country OFMSW, 1.000 for POME, 0.991 for livestock, and 0.972 for cities. The results identify where project-level techno-economic and life-cycle assessments, logistics analysis, market assessment, and stakeholder studies should begin; they do not constitute feasibility or investment verdicts.

title: Hydrothermal water–CO2 co-processing of immature kerogen: operating-window optimization, light-hydrocarbon selectivity and molecular pathways
abstract: Hot pressurized water can convert immature oil shale into light liquid hydrocarbons, but under severe conditions, the liquids are cracked into gas or condensed into heavy residue. This study shows that adding CO2 to the hydrothermal conversion of immature kerogen, the insoluble organic matter of oil shale, shifts the products from permanent gases toward liquid oil, and it identifies the operating conditions under which this occurs. Hydrothermal experiments on Type I kerogen-bearing shale from the Chang 7 Member, Ordos Basin, were combined with a statistically designed response surface and with reactive molecular dynamics simulations of a kerogen model built from spectroscopic data. A light-component enrichment index, which combines the number of detected liquid compounds with their light fraction, reached a broad plateau near 400–410 °C and was largely insensitive to the initial CO2 pressure, whereas CO2 strongly suppressed the formation of hydrogen, carbon monoxide and methane. At the validated condition, adding CO2 raised the oil yield by about 40% relative to water alone. The simulations show water acting as a recyclable hydrogen-transfer medium that stabilizes cracked fragments, nitrogen released mainly via ring cleavage to form hydrogen cyanide, and sulfur retained in organic structures. These results define a practical window for steering immature kerogen toward light liquid products while limiting over-gasification.

title: Multi-dimensional interactive industrial carbon-neutrality pathways for megacities under economic, policy, and technological constraints: Insights from coupled models of Long-Term Energy Alternatives Planning, System Dynamics and Technology Readiness Level
abstract: The challenge of industrial decarbonization in megacities lies in the gap between carbon-neutrality targets and implementable pathways constrained by multi-dimensional interactive factors from technology maturity, policy timing, and the carbon intensity of energy supply. To address this challenge, a novel loosely coupled model using Long-term Energy Alternatives Planning-System, Dynamics-Technology and Readiness Level (LEAP-TRL-SD) model was developed to design implementable industrial carbon-neutrality pathways by integrating economic growth, policy feedback, and maturity-constrained technology deployment, achieving an accuracy of 95.6%. The LEAP model was employed to simulate industry restructuring–driven changes in energy demand and energy carriers, SD was applied to represent dynamic interactions among economic development, policy intervention, and technological progress, and TRL was used to constrain technology deployment timing. Application to Beijing indicated that the optimal scenario reduced carbon emissions from a peak of 161.8 million tons (Mt) to 7.3 Mt. Approximately 81.7% of this reduction was derived from renewable energy-based electricity (83.4%), heat (13%), and hydrogen (3.6%). Sensitivity analysis further identified GDP growth rate as the dominant driver, with a ±10% change leading to an 11.01% deviation in energy demand. This was followed by renewable energy substitution ratio (±6.2–6.6%), process optimization technologies (±3.1%), and policy intensity (±0.32%). By 2050, Beijing's carbon neutrality pathway sustains a 2.8-fold economic growth while reducing emissions to 7.3 Mt, with high-tech service sectors expanding to 50% of industry and average technological decarbonization efficiency rising by 28.5%. The LEAP–TRL–SD model provided a quantitative and practical tool for designing phased, implementable industrial decarbonization strategies under multi-dimensional interactive real-world economic, technological, and policy constraints.

title: Retraction notice to “How can sustainable entrepreneurial enterprises escape the “green prison” in the context of environmental dynamism? — An Ecological Niche Enhancement Perspective” [J. Clean. Prod. 479, (2024), 144086]

title: Engine exhaust waste heat recovery and utilization: synergistic optimization of Cu-based ternary catalysts for hydrogen-rich fuel production from green methanol cracking
abstract: Valorizing engine-exhaust waste heat through conversion into reusable chemical energy can improve energy utilization and reduce thermal-energy losses. Green-methanol cracking offers a potential route for such waste-heat recovery while producing hydrogen-rich fuel. This study develops a data-driven framework for selecting Cu-based ternary catalysts for hydrogen-rich fuel production by green-methanol cracking using engine-exhaust waste heat. Sixteen Cu–Zn–X and Cu–Ni–X catalysts were evaluated at 220–340 °C and three methanol feed rates, and their composition–operation–performance relationships were examined through multi-criteria decision analysis, interpretable machine learning, and robustness testing. Catalyst preference depended strongly on the evaluation objective. In the application-oriented TOPSIS analysis, Cu3Ni1Mn1/Al2O3 delivered the strongest cross-condition performance, ranking first under 13 of 21 operating conditions. By contrast, Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 provided the best balance in the Pareto-based evaluation and machine-learning-assisted recommendation. At 0.7 mL min−1 and 340 °C, Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 achieved 94.3% methanol conversion and an apparent H2-yield index of 64.0%. Interpretable models identified temperature and feed rate as the principal determinants of conversion and product distribution, while promoter composition controlled catalyst-specific responses. XRD, H2-TPR, XPS, physisorption, and microscopy analyses associated the balanced performance of Cu3Zn1Co1/Al2O3 with dispersed Cu–Co–Zn interfacial structures, favorable reducibility, and hierarchical morphology. The proposed workflow provides an experimentally grounded approach to catalyst screening and operating-condition selection for waste-heat-driven methanol cracking.

title: Stakeholder-anchored multi-criteria deployment of island hybrid renewable energy systems for lifecycle carbon reduction: A weight-robustness analysis
abstract: Choosing a low-carbon configuration for an island hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) is a multi-criteria decision on which stakeholders disagree. This study ranks fourteen genetic-algorithm-sized HRES configurations for Crete on five composite criteria: economic, environmental, social, political and technological. The environmental criterion is the share of the grid's lifecycle carbon footprint a configuration avoids. Criterion weights are derived from a 100-respondent stakeholder survey by a Random Forest with its Shapley-value attribution (TreeSHAP) and by the model-free CRiteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) ranks the configurations. The novelty is a diagnostic protocol that tests whether, and where, the recommendation depends on the weights: an equal-weights null, whole-simplex sampling, direct-rating and class-balanced weights, seven further aggregation methods, index-coefficient perturbation and a decision boundary. The marine-augmented configuration with battery storage (S14) ranks first under all three survey-based weightings and equal weights and, under the adopted inventory, avoids 79.15% of the grid's lifecycle carbon footprint, against 71.64% for the best shore-only option. This agreement stems mainly from the decision matrix, where S14 weakly dominates ten of thirteen alternatives. It leads in 67.0% of uniformly sampled weight vectors and under all seven further methods, but in only 57–77% of joint index-coefficient perturbations. Entropy weights, a higher political weight or a 20% higher policy premium for wind make a wind-rich alternative first. S14 is therefore the most frequent, not an invariant, first choice, conditional on policy judgements open to stakeholder deliberation.

title: Rotational grazing modulates the soil–plant–animal carbon cycling pump in an alpine ranch on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
abstract: Alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP) store substantial carbon, yet how grazing management regulates carbon transfer across the soil–plant–animal continuum remains poorly resolved. Based on a 5-year (2010–2014) experiment, we compared continuous grazing (CG) and rotational grazing (RG) at two intensities (8 and 16 sheep ha−1) and quantified carbon transfer across plant, livestock, soil, and ecosystem subsystems. At 8 sheep ha−1, RG increased gross primary production by 24.6%, plant to soil carbon by 37.2%, and livestock product carbon by 20.8%, while reducing livestock emissions by 12.0% relative to CG. These benefits were larger at lower intensity. The higher intensity suppressed productivity and respiratory fluxes but elevated emissions. Variation partitioning analysis showed that grazing intensity × climate interactions explained most variation in carbon fixation and respiration fluxes, whereas grazing system × intensity interactions governed trophic carbon transfers. Structural equation modelling revealed that grazing system exerted an indirect positive effect on ecosystem carbon transfer through improved soil physicochemical properties, grazing intensity an indirect negative effect via reduced aboveground biomass, and climate a direct negative effect. Against a dominant climatic forcing, rotational grazing at 8 sheep ha−1 acts as a secondary but actionable modulator of the carbon cycling pump, providing a low-cost strategy to partially buffer climatic pressure while sustaining livestock production on the QXP.

title: Simultaneous dark fermentation and microbial fuel cell for co-production of hydrogen and electricity from typical garden waste using two co-culture systems
abstract: Dark fermentation (DF) faces inherent drawbacks of low hydrogen yield and soluble microbial product accumulation. To address these limitations, the single-stage dark fermentation and microbial fuel cell (sDFMFC) system was constructed to evaluate its performance for lignocellulose treatment and co-production of hydrogen and electricity using four typical fallen leaves (poplar, ginkgo, oak, and pine) as substrates under continuous flow (HRT = 8 h). Two model co-culture systems (fermentative bacterium + electroactive bacterium) were employed in the experiment: Escherichia coli + Shewanella oneidensis and Enterobacter aerogenes + Shewanella oneidensis. The results showed that the E. aerogenes + S. oneidensis system exhibited superior hydrogen production (43.04 mL-H2/g-removedCOD) and total energy recovery efficiency (19.64%), but lower power density (91.13 mW/m3). In contrast, the E. coli + S. oneidensis system achieved higher power density (180.5 mW/m3) and higher COD removal (42.5%), but lower hydrogen yield. Notably, hydrogen accounted for more than 99.9% of the total energy recovery; electricity was negligible. Furthermore, substrate fermentability was the key factor governing overall performance. Poplar leaves showed the best performance for combined hydrogen and electricity production, while pine needles performed the poorest due to high lignin content and the presence of inhibitors. This study confirms the feasibility of continuous-flow sDFMFC for treating garden waste and reveals the metabolic pathway differences between two co-culture systems, providing a reference for cascaded valorization of lignocellulosic waste.

title: Bio-fiber envelopes for digital twin-enabled thermal management: Decoupling cold-chain from high-global warming potential insulations
abstract: Global cold-chain logistics relies heavily on energy-intensive and hard-to-recycle materials that offer excellent thermal insulation, but are often made using highly polluting materials and are vulnerable to punctures. Here, we developed mycelium-bound bio-fiber envelopes (BFEs) obtained by growing Ganoderma lucidum mycelium on discarded lignocellulosic cardboard, rice husk, and oats. The hyphal fiber network bonds the waste substrates into a mechanically robust (yield strength = 0.72 MPa), thermally insulating (thermal conductivity = 0.05 W/m.K), hydrophobic (contact angle = 121.4°), fire-resistant, and fully biodegradable composite in tropical ambient outdoor climate. The BFE delivers thermal insulation comparable to foams, while achieving 6× lower carbon emissions and 4.2× lower energy demand than other cold-chain materials. To overcome the issue of performance uncertainty, a digital twin framework is integrated for real-time monitoring. Combining bio-based materials with digital tracking can reduce risks and make them reliable for demanding applications such as cold-chain logistics. Unlike prior mycelium composites, which are typically characterized in isolation from real-time performance monitoring, this work couples a living bio-based insulation material with a physics-based digital twin, turning biological variability into a bounded and monitored quantity and offering a practical route to qualify bio-based materials for regulated cold-chain logistics. This study is limited to prototype-scale envelopes and to a digital twin validated on a bounded set of payloads, geometries, and ambient profiles, and wider qualification is the subject of ongoing work.

title: Environmental footprint of remediation in two contaminated steel plant sites: Integrating life cycle assessment with post-remediation carbon-budget scenarios
abstract: Remediation of contaminated industrial sites can create substantial immediate environmental burdens, whereas post-remediation ecological redevelopment can provide delayed carbon uptake. However, the extent to which ecological redevelopment can repay the upfront carbon debt from engineering-intensive remediation remains poorly characterized, particularly for large steel plant brownfields. To address this gap, we integrated life cycle assessment (LCA) with a project-scale net ecosystem carbon budget (NECB) framework for two former steel plant sites in China, one in Beijing (Site 1) and the other in Zhejiang (Site 2). The LCA used 1 m3 of remediated soil as the functional unit within a harmonized core boundary covering material and energy inputs, transportation, remediation operations, and waste treatment, with site/project records for foreground inventories and Ecoinvent 3.1.0 for background data. Remediation generated 21,226 t CO2-eq at Site 1 and 73,849 t CO2-eq at Site 2, with the difference largely reflecting remediation scale. At the technology level, environmental impacts varied substantially and were driven by energy use, transportation, and technology-specific material inputs. Under the reference structural scenario, assuming afforestation of 70% of the site area, locally plausible forest types compensated 37.3–39.6% of the initial carbon debt at Site 1 after 100 years, while a theoretical evergreen broad-leaved forest upper bound reached 60.2%. The corresponding compensation at Site 2 was 11.9–20.0%, and none of the simulated forest types fully repaid the project carbon debt within 100 years. The projected compensation was strongly influenced by land availability and assumptions governing forest productivity-heterotrophic respiration coupling, whereas afforestation-establishment emissions had only a minor effect. Afforestation can therefore provide partial, long-term compensation for remediation-stage carbon debt but cannot substitute for direct emission reductions during remediation. Integrating remediation-stage environmental assessment with post-remediation carbon accounting provides a life cycle-oriented basis for coordinating lower-carbon remediation with ecological redevelopment of industrial brownfields.

title: MICP versus MIPP for Cd immobilization: kinetics, products, leaching stability and conversion feasibility
abstract: Microbially induced carbonate/phosphate precipitation (MICP/MIPP) are prevalent techniques for heavy metal (HM) remediation. However, systematic comparative studies on their functional strains, mineralization efficiency, precipitate stability, and integrated application potential are still scarce. Here, the MICP-functional strain Sporosarcina sp. DF-C31 and MIPP-functional strain Burkholderia orbicola PSB4 were employed to investigate their cadmium (Cd2+) mineralization performance. The MICP system achieved 98.98% Cd2+ removal efficiency within 36 h and generated stable calcite precipitate within 72 h, while MIPP immobilized 98.39% of Cd2+ within 168 h and yielded highly crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) within 120 h. The MICP precipitates consisted of a Ca1-xCdxCO3 solid solution, and the MIPP precipitates were composed of Ca10-xCdx(PO4)6(OH)2. Multiple characterization techniques collectively demonstrated that Cd immobilization proceeded via Ca-site substitution and lattice incorporation in both systems. Specifically, MIPP adopted a pathway of surface adsorption followed by lattice migration, while MICP operates via coprecipitation-mediated entrapment. In two-month acid leaching tests, Cd2+ release from MICP precipitates increased significantly under aggressive low-pH conditions. For MICP precipitates, Cd2+ release rates reached 23.86% and 1.70% at pH 2 and pH 4, respectively. In contrast, MIPP precipitates showed only a moderate increase to 10.18% and 0.55%. The sequential MICP-to-MIPP phase conversion process was further evaluated. At an initial Cd concentration of 50 mg/L, HAP formation was negligible at 30 °C and only partial (35.98% conversion) at 50 °C. The corresponding Cd removal efficiencies remained unchanged and increased by 1.1%, respectively. Overall, this integrated strategy provides a condition-dependent remediation approach, where the stability enhancement is critically dependent on the extent of HAP conversion.

title: Waste lignin-derived carbon nanotube fibers: Isotope tracing mechanisms and structural optimization
abstract: Biomass-derived carbon, particularly from waste streams such as lignin, offers a sustainable feedstock for carbon nanotube (CNT) synthesis. However, the complex pyrolysis pathways obscure its influence on CNT growth mechanisms. Here, lignin-based CNTs were investigated using isotope labeling and tailored catalysts in a floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition (FCCVD) system to elucidate high-temperature transformation processes and regional growth characteristics. Catalyst composition critically modulated CNT structure and properties: iron catalysts achieved the highest yield (116 mg h−1), while Fe-Co-Ni ternary catalysts produced highly graphitized CNTs (IG/ID = 7) with elevated electrical conductivity (8.5 × 104 S m−1). Isotopic analysis confirmed that lignin contributed 83% of the carbon, with methanol accounting for 17%. Life cycle assessment further demonstrated a lower global warming potential than ethanol-derived CNTs, underscoring the sustainability and circular-economy relevance of lignin as a carbon source. These findings provide mechanistic insight and practical guidance for the controllable synthesis of high-performance biomass-derived CNTs.

title: Enhancing robustness and reliability of underwater RGB-based water quality retrieval under inland cross-water and cross-seasonal conditions
abstract: To address cross-domain generalization challenges and depth-related optical variations in water quality retrieval, this study proposes FMC-ConvNeXt, a five-module framework for underwater RGB imagery. Built on ConvNeXt, it combines spectral-attenuation attention with data-driven components to improve adaptability under cross-water and cross-seasonal shifts. Datasets covering different inland water types and seasons were constructed in Handan, China, and evaluated using complementary image-level and sampling-point-isolated protocols. Evaluation covered overall performance, module contributions and configuration dependence, cross-domain adaptation, unseen-sampling-point generalization, uncertainty reliability, and robustness to simulated optical perturbations and reservoir depth variations. Under image-level supervision, FMC-ConvNeXt achieved R2 values of 0.9334 and 0.9561 for turbidity and suspended solids, respectively, in the Summer Target Domain. Fine-tuning with 20% target samples reduced RMSE to 2.082 and 0.858 NTU. Under moderate to severe spectral distortion, RMSE and MAE in the Winter Target Domain remained at 0.3757 and 0.2424 NTU. Uncertainty calibration reduced regression ECE in the Summer Target Domain from 0.1561 to 0.0728, with uncertainty significantly associated with absolute error. Reservoir evaluation yielded R2 = 0.6387, while image luminance and texture responses decreased with depth. Ablation results showed configuration dependent rather than linearly additive module contributions. Under sampling-point isolation, turbidity R2 values were 0.8208, 0.5047, and 0.3550 in the Source Domain, Summer Target Domain, and Winter Target Domain, respectively. Overall, FMC-ConvNeXt improved Turb and SS retrieval and retained predictive capability under controlled perturbations and field conditions, supporting ROV assisted high frequency screening, repeated inspection, confirmatory sampling, pollution anomaly identification, and cleaner-production-related water management.

title: CO2 emission drivers in Ecuador's service sector: An input–output subsystem structural decomposition analysis for climate policy
abstract: The expansion of service activities reshapes production systems and transfers emission burdens across the economy. Previous structural decomposition applications to input–output subsystems have generally aggregated internal and external intersectoral mechanisms, obscuring the channels through which services induce emissions beyond their boundaries. This study applies a six-component input–output subsystem decomposition: net own, internal feedback, internal spillover, scale, external feedback and external spillover, and further decomposes their changes into twelve effects, distinguishing technological and demand effects across linkage components and demand and emission-intensity effects in the scale component. The framework is applied to analyse CO 2 emission drivers in Ecuador's service sector between 2007 and 2018. The results show that the demand effect contributed 5892 kt CO 2 to emission growth, partially offset by the technological effect (−1606 kt) and the emission-intensity effect (−1731 kt). The disaggregated framework reveals that the external spillover component—representing emissions induced in non-service sectors by service-sector demand for inputs—increased from 25.2% to 27.2% of total subsystem emissions, a distinction that would be obscured if internal and external spillover effects were aggregated. These findings illustrate how service-sector expansion can be associated with substantial emissions beyond service-sector boundaries through intersectoral linkages and underscore the need for mitigation policies that account for emission transfers along supply chains rather than targeting direct sectoral emissions alone.

title: Trajectories of carbon storage and productivity dynamics during post-fire forest recovery in severely burned areas of Daxing'an Mountains
abstract: The forest recovery cycle in heavily burned areas is protracted, and carbon sink-oriented restoration strategies remain unclear. This study examines severely burned sites in the Daxing'an Mountains. Planted Larix gmelinii forests (3300 and 4400 trees hm−2) were compared with naturally regenerated Betula platyphylla forests. The standard tree method was used to examine temporal patterns of forest carbon stock (FCS) and stand productivity (SP). Thinning was actually implemented in birch stands and simulated in high-density larch plantations. RDA and path analysis identified primary drivers. Results showed that plantation FCS remained significantly higher than natural forest FCS 35 years post-fire, with the highest value (30.99 t hm−2) in the 3300 trees hm−2 plantation. SP exhibited an initial increase followed by decline. Specifically, natural forest SP peaked earlier and decreased, whereas plantation SP continued increasing for 20 years post-fire before declining. Plantation SP remained higher than natural regeneration for over 20 years post-fire. Thinning increased SP within 5 years, but the effect weakened after 10 years. FCS increased by 105.54% in birch and 60.02% in high-density larch within 10 years after thinning. RDA and path analysis indicated stand density as the primary driver of FCS and SP, and growing-season temperature as the key climatic factor. These results demonstrate that plantations enhance carbon sequestration more than natural regeneration over the medium to long term. Meanwhile, thinning effects exhibited distinct temporal sensitivity. Subsequent management should employ intermittent density regulation to sustainably promote forest recovery.

title: Toward a sustainable and resilient EU energy transition: Prospective life cycle assessment of material stocks and supply-chain alternatives
abstract: The rapid expansion of clean-energy technologies is central to global decarbonization but intensifies reliance on critical raw materials, raising environmental and supply chain concerns that intensify toward mid-century. This study applies a prospective life cycle assessment (2000-2050) with temporal modeling of installed-capacity stocks and comprehensive uncertainty analysis, quantifying environmental burdens across six key technologies: solar photovoltaics, onshore and offshore wind, and three battery chemistries. The assessment compares business as usual (BAU) and regional supply chains aligned with the Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA). This study captures the temporal evolution of installed-capacity stocks, supply chain variability, and the environmental trade-offs associated with alternative sourcing strategies. Results show mineral depletion reaching 1.99 × 10 9 kg Cu-eq in 2050, with NMC622 alone contributing over 70%, whereas solar PV and wind account for less than 2% owing to their lower material intensity. Within NMC622, nickel (43%) and copper (37%) dominate the depletion profile, followed by graphite and aluminum. Carcinogenic toxicity reaches 5.06 × 10 9 kg 1,4-DCB-eq, and embodied climate-change burdens reach 2.55 × 10 9 kg CO 2 -eq. China accounts for approximately half of the cradle-to-gate climate-change impact under BAU, dropping below 0.1% under diversified sourcing. Alternative sourcing reduces material depletion by approximately 3%, redistributing environmental pressures to EU and allied regions. Overall environmental burdens remain largely unchanged, indicating that supply diversification alone is insufficient. A resilient and sustainable energy transition will therefore require coordinated advances across multiple fronts, including low-impact battery chemistries, cleaner refining, and high-efficiency material recovery.

title: A dual-calcium regulation strategy for variable-temperature adaptive red mud-based binders: Hydration optimization, resource efficiency and sustainability assessment
abstract: With the increasing demand for industrial solid waste valorization, the development of cementitious materials that adaptability to harsh service conditions has become an important direction for sustainable construction materials, CaO-CaO2 composite synergistic regulation system was developed in this study. LT-DSC, FTIR, TG-DTG, and MIP were employed to characterize the hydration and microstructural evolution. In addition, multi-objective optimization was conducted using the NSGA-II coupled with the TOPSIS. The effects of CaO-CaO2 dosages on mechanical properties, variable-temperature thermal behavior, hydration product formation, and pore structure evolution were systematically investigated, and conduct economic feasibility and resource efficiency evaluation. The results demonstrated that the dual-calcium system enhanced the adaptability of the material to variable-temperature curing. When CaO–CaO2 completely replaced the alkaline activator, the strength retention ratio reached 72.07%. The incorporation of CaO2 reduced the freezing temperature of the paste and decreased the amount of freezable water, resulting in reductions of 8.67% and 31.78% in the freezing temperature and melting enthalpy at the final setting stage, respectively. CaO(4%)-CaO2(2.5%), CaO(7%)-CaO2(2.5%), CaO(8.2%)-CaO2(3.5%) were identified as optimal formulations for cost efficiency, variable-temperature mechanical performance, and multi-objective balance, respectively. This study elucidates the synergistic regulation mechanism of the CaO–CaO2 composite system on the variable-temperature hydration behavior of strong-alkali-free red mud-based cementitious materials and provides a theoretical basis for the resource utilization of industrial solid wastes in cold regions.

title: Design and multi-dimensional evaluation of bio-fermentation equipment for the circular economy in agriculture
abstract: The transition toward a circular economy in agro-industrial systems requires energy-efficient and sustainable technologies for organic waste processing. This study evaluates high-density polyethylene (HDPE) as an alternative to structural steel (St3/S235JR) for drum-type biofermenter construction. Three drum scales (L = 3, 6, and 12 m) were analyzed using multiphysics modeling (Ansys Workbench, 2023 R2), dynamic heat–mass transfer simulation (MATLAB), full-scale prototype testing, and techno-economic assessment based on life cycle costing and discounted cash flow analysis. Results demonstrate that HDPE construction reduces structural mass by 59–70% (from 8945 kg to 3670 kg for the large drum, steady-state heat losses by up to 6.6 times, and drive power requirements by 47–51% (from 30.4 kW to 16 kW for the large drum), while maximum deformations (0.42 mm) remain within GOST/ISO permissible limits. A cradle-to-gate LCA indicated a significant reduction in GWP by up to 66.6% for smaller drums. Economic viability was achieved exclusively for large-scale installations (12 m drum): the HDPE configuration showed 7.3% lower capital expenditures, 11.3% reduced operating costs, a discounted payback period of 1.5 years, net present value of USD 57.5 k, and internal rate of return of 79%. Small and medium configurations exhibited negative NPV under current market conditions, highlighting critical economies of scale. The HDPE biofermenter reached a stable thermophilic regime (63.4 °C) within 48 h with a temperature uniformity coefficient of variation below 7%, outperforming traditional windrow composting. These findings confirm that polymer-based biofermenters are technically feasible and economically attractive for industrial-scale organic waste valorization. The integrated Ansys–MATLAB modeling framework provides a scalable digital twin tool for equipment optimization in circular bioeconomy applications.

title: Nanoscale surface on internal runner of thin-walled micro-grooved channel produced by a novel combined jet polishing process using three developed devices
abstract: Adhered powder and spherical particles usually appear on the internal runners of parts produced by additive manufacturing. These defects must be removed to prevent them from detaching and entering moving components. Nevertheless, conventional polishing methods cannot effectively remove these defects when the groove size is less than 0.5 mm. To overcome this challenge, a novel approach was developed to achieve a nanoscale surface on the internal runners of thin-walled micro-grooved channel using three developed devices. Micro-grooves with a minimum size of 0.22 mm are located in a channel with a thickness of 0.7 mm fabricated by a custom metallic three-dimensional printer. Air abrasive jet polishing (AAJP) was carried out using silicon carbide (SiC) abrasives by a custom-made polisher. After AAJP using a traditional circular nozzle, surface roughness Ra values were 36.99, 1.79, and 5.46 μm on the side, top, and bottom surfaces of a groove, respectively. Ra increased by 39% on the side surface after AAJP compared to the pristine surface of the laser powder bed fusion, and this phenomenon is firstly discovered. To address this, a novel multi-lobed nozzle was designed. AAJP and ultrasonic-assisted immersed jet polishing (UAIJP) were conducted using the new lobed nozzle on two self-made polishers. The novel UAIJP slurry consisted of SiC and ceria hybrid abrasives, hydrogen peroxide, and sodium bicarbonate. The Ra values were 15.83, 0.79, 3.16 μm and 0.86, 0.07, 0.26 μm on the side, top, and bottom surfaces after AAJP and UAIJP, respectively. After AAJP, Ra values were reduced by 57%, 56%, and 42% on the side, top, and bottom surfaces, respectively, compared to the circular nozzle; after UAIJP, the reductions reached 99%, 96%, and 98%, respectively. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) calculations reveal that surface defects are preferentially removed by abrasive particles. The structure of the lobed nozzle suppresses the central straight-through airflow, causing radial turbulent disturbances and reducing the radial ineffective collision rate of abrasives from 50.96% for the conventional circular nozzle to 41.84%. Meanwhile, the modulation effect of the flow field in the lobed nozzle forces more abrasives to enter the micro-grooves, increasing the radial collision frequency rate of abrasives on the side surface from 45.65% to 51.82%. The lobed nozzle broadens the collision angle of abrasives from near 0° for the circular nozzle to 60°, promoting more abrasives to impact defects at an optimal impact angle of 18.43°, calculated from the Finnie erosion model. Our findings provide new outcomes to fabricate nanoscale surface on the internal runner of thin-walled micro-grooved channel of Ti6Al4V via AAJP and UAIJP using a multi-lobed nozzle by three developed setups.

title: Local fiscal science and technology expenditure, air quality, and house prices: Evidence from Chinese metropolitan areas
abstract: Local fiscal science and technology (S&T) expenditure is an underexamined form of urban fiscal effort. Whether it is associated with cleaner air and whether environmental improvement is reflected in housing values remain unclear, particularly across metropolitan hierarchies. We analyse panel data for 151 prefecture-level cities across 27 nationally designated Chinese metropolitan areas over 2008–2020. Treating local government expenditure on science and technology as a fiscal input, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models that control for industrial composition and socioeconomic covariates. We also conduct exploratory subgroup analyses of core and non-core cities and use 1000 bootstrap replications to assess the indirect association operating through PM2.5. Fiscal S&T expenditure is negatively associated with PM2.5 in the full sample and both city groups. Its total association with housing prices is positive in the full sample and non-core cities but not significant in core cities. Bootstrap confidence intervals for the indirect association include zero in the full sample (estimate: 0.0024) and core cities. The indirect association was positive and supported by bootstrap results in the non-core-city sample (0.0034; 95% confidence interval: 0.0002–0.0071), equivalent to a 10% increase in S&T expenditure being associated with approximately 0.03% higher housing prices via PM2.5. This study provides city-level evidence on the associations among government expenditure on science and technology, air quality, and housing prices.

title: Oil–dependent control of methane hydrate kinetics and slurry rheology by a kinetic hydrate inhibitor in oil–water systems
abstract: Gas hydrate blockage remains a major flow-assurance challenge in gas condensate pipelines, where the coexistence of condensate oil and water creates non-emulsified or weakly dispersed oil–water environments that affect hydrate formation and slurry flow behavior. Although kinetic hydrate inhibitors (KHIs) are widely used to delay hydrate nucleation, their influence on post-nucleation hydrate aggregation and slurry rheology in non-emulsified condensate oil–water systems remains insufficiently understood. In this study, methane hydrate formation kinetics and slurry rheological behavior were investigated in systems containing the tested KHI and model condensate oil (n-hexane) at different oil volume fractions. The results show that, at 20 vol% n-hexane, the tested KHI significantly prolongs the early warning period for hydrate nucleation, whereas at 80 vol% n-hexane, it extends the low-risk growth period, with no transition to the high-risk agglomeration stage observed within the 720 min post-nucleation observation window. In this high-oil system, a relatively high water conversion rate is accompanied by low final slurry viscosity. Rheological measurements further reveal that the resulting hydrate slurry exhibits shear-thinning behavior, yield stress, thixotropy, and a transition from elasticity-dominated to viscosity-dominated behavior. The yield stress increases with shut-in duration and depends strongly on shear history, indicating potential restart risk. These results demonstrate that the dominant role of the tested KHI shifts from nucleation delay under low-oil conditions to post-nucleation aggregation control and slurry flowability maintenance under high-oil conditions. This study provides experimental evidence for evaluating KHI performance from a coupled kinetic–rheological perspective in non-emulsified condensate oil–water systems.

title: Carbon-associated nitrite partitioning between DNRA and denitrification in relation to N2O emissions during thermophilic composting
abstract: Despite growing recognition that thermophilic composting is a major hotspot for nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, the metabolic mechanisms governing N2O production during the thermophilic phase remain poorly understood. This knowledge gap hampers mechanistic interpretation of thermophilic N2O emission pulses and constrains the development of targeted strategies for greenhouse gas mitigation. By integrating additive-based regulation with process monitoring, metagenomic analysis, kinetic analysis and path modeling, this study revealed how intensified carbon turnover regulates the partitioning of NO2−-N between dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) and denitrification during thermophilic composting. Kinetic fitting showed a closer association of nitrite than nitrate with N2O formation. Under thermophilic conditions, intensive organic matter degradation and oxygen consumption may increase electron-donor availability, a pattern consistent with greater DNRA-related functional potential relative to N2O-producing denitrification in NO2−-N utilization. Consistent with this interpretation, the Bacillus subtilis-inoculated treatment and biochar-amended treatment showed higher DNRA-related NO2−-N reduction potential and lower N2O -producing denitrification potential, accompanied by cumulative N2O emission reductions of 84.15% and 76.35%, respectively, relative to the control. These findings suggest that carbon-driven competition between DNRA and denitrification may be an important mechanism associated with N2O mitigation during thermophilic composting.

title: Machine learning-driven intelligent optimization of layered double hydroxides-peroxymonosulfate system for antibiotic degradation: Interactive effect analysis and precise prediction
abstract: Traditional single-factor analysis based on the control variable method requires extensive experimental data to explore interactions among multiple parameters, which substantially increases experimental complexity in nonlinear catalytic systems. Herein, a closed-loop framework integrating data integration, machine learning modeling, and experimental validation was proposed to rapidly and accurately predict optimal operational parameters for the elimination of recalcitrant pollutants in water. By collecting and preprocessing literature-derived and experimental data on antibiotic degradation in layered double hydroxides–peroxymonosulfate (LDH-PMS) systems, a multi-dimensional database was constructed for the first time and evaluated using six representative machine learning models. Feature importance analysis, partial dependence plots, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interaction analysis identified reaction time, LDH dosage, and PMS dosage as the dominant driving factors, while revealing their threshold behaviors and nonlinear interactions. Model reliability was demonstrated by the strong agreement between predicted and experimental results (R2 > 0.900). Notably, experiments conducted under model-guided conditions achieved significantly higher median removal efficiencies (93-98%) than those obtained without model guidance (73-94%). This study provides a data-driven framework for rational experimental design and highlights the potential of machine learning-assisted strategies for optimizing advanced oxidation processes in environmental remediation.

title: Administrative challenges and efficiency in integrating education for sustainable development in Jordanian universities: A mixed-methods analysis
abstract: Universities are increasingly expected to translate Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) commitments into institutional practice, yet the administrative conditions shaping this process remain underexamined in Middle Eastern higher education. This study examines administrative challenges and efficiency in integrating ESD within Jordanian universities. Using an exploratory sequential mixed methods design, the study conducted 22 semi-structured interviews with deans, heads of departments, lecturers, and students, followed by a survey of 113 academic staff. The qualitative phase identified four major challenges: curriculum integration, educational practices, resources and support, and stakeholder engagement. The quantitative phase showed that existing administrative practices address ESD challenges only moderately overall (M = 3.47). Operational Procedures recorded the highest level of practice (M = 3.68), indicating relative progress in visible sustainability-related operations, while Faculty Members recorded the lowest level (M = 3.24), highlighting weaknesses in staff development and pedagogical readiness. The findings show uneven ESD integration, with operational progress ahead of curriculum reform, research support, faculty capacity, stakeholder participation, and governance coordination. The study argues that administrative efficiency is the institutional capacity to connect sustainability-related decisions, resources, people, and learning processes across the university.

title: Rare earth elements as emerging tracers for sustainable urban water management: Insights from weekly monitoring of a typical river in Beijing
abstract: Urban rivers are critical components of sustainable water management in megacities, yet strong temporal variability complicates the identification of pollution sources and anthropogenic impacts. This study employed weekly monitoring in a densely populated urban river in Beijing over an entire hydrological year to investigate the temporal dynamics, sources, and anthropogenic signatures of dissolved rare earth elements (REEs). Total REE concentrations ranged from 34.96 to 350.24 ng/L. Although several concentration peaks occurred during the monitoring period, no systematic wet season versus dry season differences were observed. The river consistently exhibited medium REE enrichment, while positive Gd anomalies (δGd: 7.28 ∼ 248.43) persisted throughout the monitoring period. Anthropogenic Gd accounted for more than 98% of dissolved Gd, and δGd was positively correlated with Cl−, indicating a persistent wastewater-related contribution and similar transport pathways. In contrast, La, Sm, and Eu anomalies showed greater temporal variability, suggesting additional and less persistent urban inputs. Temporal variations in dissolved REEs were primarily controlled by reclaimed water inputs rather than by precipitation driven dilution or natural weathering processes. Overall, the weekly year-round observations captured both the persistence of anthropogenic Gd and the temporal variability of other anthropogenic REE signatures, providing improved constraints on wastewater inputs in reclaimed water fed urban rivers.

title: Monetizing flare gas through liquid blue hydrogen: Integrated production, liquefaction, and value recovery pathway
abstract: Gas flaring leads to significant greenhouse gas emissions and valuable hydrocarbon losses, posing major environmental and sustainability challenges. This study offers a promising pathway to decarbonize otherwise wasted flare gas into hydrogen, a clean and high-energy carrier, while reducing significant environmental impact. However, current hydrogen production and liquefaction studies are still under studied in terms of integration of production and liquefaction in one framework. In addition, the utilization of flare gas as a feedstock has not been fully explored for liquid hydrogen production, and previous studies rely on complex cryogenic schemes with multiple cryogenic heat exchangers and expanders, increasing system irreversibility and capital cost. This study proposes a fully integrated process for producing liquid blue hydrogen from flare gas and evaluates its performance using energy, exergy, economic, environmental and sustainability analyses. Hydrogen is generated via steam methane reforming (SMR) with CO2 capture and liquefied using nitrogen and helium Brayton cycles. The design achieves complete liquefaction using only two cryogenic multi-stream heat exchangers, thereby simplifying the overall process configuration and reducing the number of equipment required for liquefaction. This overall simplified configuration may potentially reduce exergy destruction and lower capital requirements by minimizing the number of equipment and liquefaction process stages. Optimization results demonstrate a liquefaction SEC of 9.353 kWh/kg H2, corresponding to 21% lower value than the arithmetic mean of the conceptual integrated hydrogen liquefaction with production processes, indicating potential energy savings. The system achieves overall energy and exergy efficiencies of 73.87% and 26.85%, respectively. The proposed model is compared against published research data in all aspects of the 4 E analysis to ensure thermodynamic consistency and reliability. The proposed study establishes a new process configuration and scalable pathway for flare gas valorization into cost-effective liquid hydrogen, supporting net-zero flaring objectives and sustainable hydrogen supply chains.

title: Policy instruments reshaping production profitability: NPV optimization under carbon policy scenarios for an offshore oilfield in the South China Sea
abstract: As carbon regulation expands across China’s industrial sectors, offshore oil and gas operations must incorporate carbon constraints into production decisions to support low-carbon and cleaner production. However, conventional net present value (NPV) optimization often relies on static carbon estimates, with insufficient consideration of changes in emissions and carbon costs induced by production reallocation. This study develops a carbon-accounting and decision-support workflow that couples reservoir numerical simulation with surface equipment modeling. For each production strategy, the workflow evaluates production performance, equipment energy consumption, and carbon emissions, which are then incorporated into an NPV model that accounts for carbon policy instruments. A random-forest sensitivity analysis identifies oil price and production allocation as the two leading factors affecting NPV variability, with normalized importance scores of 48.0% and 24.2%, respectively. Optimization across 32 carbon policy scenarios shows that combining multiple incentive-based policies does not necessarily improve NPV and may reduce it by up to 13.35%. In contrast, a phased policy pathway sustains NPV growth while reducing CO2 emission intensity by 11.1%. Beyond this specific case study, the framework is generalizable to other offshore fields through recalibration. The proposed workflow supports carbon-constrained production planning by linking reservoir performance, surface-equipment energy consumption, carbon accounting, and economic optimization. These findings provide practical decision support for offshore oilfield operators and policy implications for designing coordinated carbon-market instruments.

title: Liquid hydrogen from waste biogas: an integrated process for deep-eutectic-solvent upgrading, steam reforming, and cryogenic liquefaction with energy–exergy–economic optimization
abstract: Renewable liquid hydrogen (LH 2 ) from biogas remains energy- and capital-intensive, and existing studies treat hydrogen production and liquefaction as independent subsystems, leaving a unified energy–exergy–economic (3E) framework across the full biogas-to-LH 2 chain lacking. To address this, a steady-state Aspen Plus V12 flowsheet linking anaerobic co-digestion of food waste and manure, choline-chloride/urea deep-eutectic-solvent (DES) upgrading, dual-stage SMR with water–gas shift, and liquid-nitrogen-precooled helium liquefaction was optimized by a structured parametric search over the reformer temperature (300–1000°C), steam-to-biomethane ratio (12.7–0.16), and refrigeration conditions against a base case. Optimizing the reformer near 700°C with a moderate steam-to-biomethane ratio lowered the SMR-SEC from 10.76 to 5.15 kW kg −1 H 2 (≈52%), with hydrogen output plateauing near 52.8 kg h −1 (biomethane-to-steam 0.16–0.50). Integrated liquefaction raised the COP from 0.210 to 0.225, reduced the LH 2 -SEC from 7.15 to 6.85 kW kg −1 , cut total exergy destruction by ≈ 237 kW, and raised the liquefaction exergy efficiency from 61% to 70%. The total capital cost fell from $53.47 to $23.41 million (−56.2%), total annualized and operating costs by 50.9% and 38.5%, and the levelized hydrogen cost from $32.96 to $16.18 kg −1 , raising the internal rate of return from 17% to 25% and shortening payback from 7.05 to 5.3 years. Liquefaction (∼one-third of capital cost) enabled transport at ≈$0.1 kg −1 per 100 km versus ≈$1 kg −1 for compressed hydrogen. Integrated 3E optimization thus makes renewable biogas-derived LH 2 technically and economically credible.

title: Preparation of MSCF via MPAM: A thermally stable modified material for the ecological backfilling of mine waste rock
abstract: In this study, a bentonite–polymer composite modifier (MPAM) was synthesized from sodium bentonite (NaB), cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTMAB), acrylamide (AM), and polyacrylamide (PAM). PAM in the original SCF formulation was subsequently replaced with MPAM to produce the modified backfill material MSCF. The compressive strength, water retention, and thermal stability of SCF and MSCF were compared. Thermal analysis, cone calorimetry, CT, and COMSOL simulation were then used to examine how MSCF regulates pore structure and forms an interlayer composite network. The results indicate that, under identical conditions, MSCF consistently exhibits higher strength; simultaneously, MSCF demonstrates superior water retention capacity and thermal stability. As the MSCF content increases, the heat release, smoke generation and CO2 emission of the coal gangue composite system are all significantly suppressed, internal pore connectivity is reduced, and the tendency for long-term heat accumulation is weakened. The improvement in the comprehensive performance of MSCF is primarily attributed to the uniform dispersion and stable incorporation of MPAM-modified bentonite layers within the polymer network, resulting in a denser interlayer composite network structure. MSCF achieves synergistic optimisation of the mechanical performance and thermal safety of backfill materials, while showing low raw-material cost potential; however, its laboratory-scale material-plus-energy cost remains higher than that of SCF, indicating that further process optimisation and scale-up are required to realise its economic advantage. MSCF shows potential for the safe backfilling and resource utilisation of coal gangue.

title: Cleaner production of ceramic fracturing proppants from bauxite tailings and oil-based drilling cuttings: process optimization, resource substitution and hazardous-element risk reduction
abstract: Cleaner production of oilfield and alumina-industry residues requires routes that convert hazardous and bulk solid wastes into functional products while reducing subsequent environmental risk. Here, oil-based drilling cuttings (OBDC) and bauxite tailings (BT) were co-sintered as solid-waste-derived aluminosilicate precursors for ceramic fracturing proppants. The study integrates raw-material complementarity, process optimization, proppant performance, pH-dependent leaching and hazardous-element fraction transformation to evaluate whether the proposed route can deliver both product utility and environmental-risk reduction. Single-factor experiments showed that sintering temperature, sintering time and OBDC dosage jointly controlled liquid-phase formation, quartz consumption, transient cordierite formation/dissolution and mullite crystallization. A processing window centered on 1280 °C, 60 min and 20 wt% OBDC produced a mullite-rich interlocking ceramic framework; response surface analysis and validation further supported an optimized condition of approximately 1339.42 °C, 53 min and 19 wt% OBDC for preparing the final ceramic proppant. Validation produced CP with an 8.6% breakage ratio at 52 MPa, a bulk density of 1.30 g cm−3 and 4.0% acid solubility; the breakage and acid-solubility values satisfy the respective 9% and 7% limits in SY/T 5108-2014. Environmental assessment identified Na, As, Mn, Ni and Sb as target risk elements. Sintering sharply reduced OPTI values under standard and pH-dependent leaching scenarios, while BCR/RAC results showed strong stabilization of Mn, Sb and Na and more element-specific behavior for As and Ni. XRD, FTIR, SEM–EDS/mapping and XPS evidence linked this risk reduction to mullite/aluminosilicate skeleton formation, glass-phase encapsulation, Fe/Al/Ca−associated binding, Na redistribution in the glassy network and densification-induced diffusion limitation. The work establishes a cleaner-production route that couples complete waste-derived mineral substitution with standard-compliant proppant performance and multi-element risk reduction.

title: Feasibility of the frass recirculation method during Hermetia illucens larvae treatment of organic waste streams
abstract: Waste treatment with black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) is a promising technology connecting biowaste management with feed and fertilizer production. The frass fertilizer produced in the bioconversion process is typically unstable and requires post-processing. Recirculating this material as part of the larvae's rearing substrate was recently proposed as a novel methodology for increasing waste bioconversion efficiency and enhancing the quality of downstream products (larval biomass and fertilizer). This study investigated the impact of frass recirculation during the bioconversion of various biowaste streams, considering process efficiency and product quality aspects. The type of biowaste used as feedstock affected the impact that frass recirculation had on the efficiency of the bioconversion process; however, the general trend was that the yield of larval biomass and frass fertilizer per unit of waste increased with recirculation. This improvement was larger for substrates that were more nutritionally balanced, such as chicken feed and food waste. While there was a tendency of protein accumulation and fat reduction in the larval biomass when recirculating frass, the resulting frass quality mostly remained unaltered in relation to the concentration of plant nutrients. Notably, frass' maturity and stability degrees increased significantly, as indicated by parameters such as pH, electrical conductivity, C/N ratio, microbial respiration and seed germination index. Frass recirculation holds great promise in relation to eliminating the need for external inputs such as drying agents for wet substrates, while positively changing the quality of downstream products. Future research should address the long-term frass recirculation effects on process efficiency and product quality.

title: Navigating the green gap: Environmental justice and the challenge of inclusive sustainability education in Chinese universities
abstract: The pursuit of sustainability in higher education has gained global momentum, yet universities increasingly prioritize quantifiable outcomes over the social and equity dimensions of sustainability. Despite widespread institutional commitments to both sustainability and diversity, the intersection between these agendas remains underexplored, particularly regarding how underrepresented students experience campus sustainability education. This study addresses this gap by investigating inequities in student participation, benefit, and influence within campus sustainability initiatives in Chinese higher education. Informed by environmental justice theory, it explores how underrepresented students navigate sustainability education amid China's top-down "Ecological Civilization" and "green campus" policies. Through semi-structured interviews with 24 students, three core tensions emerge: performative inclusion versus meaningful partnership; hidden economic, temporal, and cultural costs of participation; and epistemic dissonance between technocratic sustainability narratives and students' community based environmental knowledge. The findings reveal a "green gap" that manifests as a tripartite justice crisis: procedural, distributive, and recognitional. Beyond critique, the study presents student envisioned pathways toward equitable transformation, including co-governance structures, barrier free program design, and integration of pluralistic knowledge systems into sustainability curricula. This research offers a student centered, empirically grounded roadmap for embedding equity into campus sustainability practice, challenging universities to move beyond tokenism and reposition underrepresented students as co authors of just institutional change.

title: Multi-scale risk assessment of non-point source pollution in a mountainous city based on transport processes
abstract: Existing ANPS pollution risk assessments have been conducted at multiple spatial scales; however, cross-scale risk evolution and driving mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. From the full “Input–Transport–Output” pollutant process, this study develops an integrated multi-scale model for ANPS pollution risk identification. Chongqing Municipality is selected as the study area, and analyses are conducted at three spatial levels: district–county, township, and village. Risk level transition analysis is introduced to quantify structural transition during scale refinement. Combined with spatial autocorrelation, hotspot analysis, and a multi-scale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model, the scale dependence of risk patterns and their driving mechanisms is systematically revealed. Results show that the district–county scale captures the overall pollution background, with high and extremely high-risk zones accounting for 58.87%, but tends to obscure local hotspots. The township scale represents a critical level of structural transition, where the proportion of unchanged risk increases from 23.3% to 49.6%, and the mean risk change decreases from 1.23 to 0.58. At the village scale, a clear local amplification effect emerges, with high-risk zones forming point-like clusters that enable precise identification of critical source zones. MGWR results indicate significant scale-dependent effects of natural and socioeconomic factors. Precipitation and cropland proportion show stable positive impacts, whereas GDP and population exhibit scale-varying effects. This framework provides a reliable basis for multi-scale ANPS risk identification and supports hierarchical control and refined management in mountainous cities.

title: Enhanced-robustness HTO control strategy for safety in alkaline electrolyzer operation
abstract: Alkaline water electrolysis systems are widely used to integrate renewable energy fluctuations and hydrogen production. Due to the high dynamics and intermittency of wind and solar energy, achieving stable and safe dynamic control in such systems remains a challenge. This paper proposes a robustness-enhanced hydrogen to oxygen (HTO) concentration control strategy to improve system safety and operational flexibility. Unlike previous studies employing optimal operation curve tracking controllers, this work proposes a feedforward-feedback composite structure integrated with the Active Disturbance Rejection Control algorithm to enhance control robustness under uncertain conditions through real-time disturbance estimation and compensation. To address the inherent lag in HTO response, an inertial compensation component is incorporated into the Extended State Observer to improve dynamic response speed. Additionally, a Pareto-based pressure feedforward module is developed to balance HTO concentration and electrolysis efficiency and determine a compromise pressure schedule. Validation under five typical dynamic conditions, including load, pressure, and temperature fluctuations, demonstrates that the proposed method reduces HTO control errors by 15% to 80% compared to the optimal operation curve tracking controller, significantly lowering the probability of threshold violations. Monte Carlo simulation-based probabilistic robustness analysis further indicates a 0.8% reduction in the variation range of electrolysis efficiency. Furthermore, measured data confirm that the proposed method achieves renewable energy utilization efficiencies of 96.9% (wind) and 89.6% (photovoltaic) while ensuring fast and disturbance-resistant HTO responses. These results highlight the robustness and efficiency of the proposed method. This study contributes to enhancing the safety margins of green hydrogen production systems and ensuring the secure operation of renewable energy integration.

title: The green push: How does China's carbon-emissions trading drive corporate green transformation?
abstract: China's carbon-emissions trading (CET) scheme is a key market-based instrument for achieving carbon neutrality, yet its impact on corporate green transition remains hard to assess. This study develops a multidimensional Corporate Green Transformation Index (CGTI) using Word2Vec and textual analysis of annual reports from firms listed on China's A-share market. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design over 2008-2024, we find that CET coverage raises the CGTI by about 0.017, or 7% of its sample mean, consistent with the Porter Hypothesis. We further find mediating effects through upgraded human capital and increased research-and-development investment, which account for about 6.5% and 2.7% of the total effect, respectively. The estimated effect is 0.0231 for non-state-owned firms against 0.0124 for state-owned firms, and 0.0285 and 0.0304 for firms in central and western China against 0.0151 for those in the east. The response is also stronger among medium-sized firms, firms with poorer disclosure quality, and firms facing intense competition, whereas polluting industries show no significant pooled response. These results indicate that even a modest carbon price can steer firms toward broader green transformation, and that complementing the national carbon market with support for skills and innovation would strengthen its effect.

title: Defect-mediated electric-field coupling enables low-threshold methane hydrate dissociation toward cleaner gas recovery
abstract: Methane hydrate is an important unconventional natural gas resource, but its dissociation is commonly constrained by slow kinetics and inefficient heat delivery during conventional thermal stimulation. Electric fields provide a potential route for reducing the dependence on intensive thermal input, yet the molecular mechanism by which field energy couples with intrinsic hydrate defects remains unclear. Here, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate methane hydrate dissociation under direct-current, terahertz sinusoidal, and terahertz bidirectional pulsed electric fields in the presence of water and methane vacancies. Water vacancies were found to dominate hydrate destabilization by disrupting the hydrogen-bond network and forming structural vulnerability gradients, whereas methane vacancies mainly perturbed the guest sublattice. Terahertz pulsed fields induced the fastest cage collapse, whereas weak direct-current fields produced the largest relative defect-induced gain within the sampled parameter space, indicating that field mode and framework integrity jointly govern hydrate dissociation. Monte Carlo-calibrated targeting analysis confirmed preferential field activation near water-vacancy sites, while a dual-index percolation model linked critical dissociation boundaries to hydrogen-bond and cage-network connectivity losses. These findings reveal vacancy-mediated electric-field coupling as a molecular mechanism for low-threshold methane hydrate dissociation and provide molecular-level insight for developing less thermally intensive hydrate dissociation strategies.

title: Breaking the cycle: Corruption, innovation, and sustainability in emerging economies
abstract: Increasingly high expectations for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) sustainability have become an important issue for companies operating in an unpredictable institutional context. This problem is especially critical for post-Soviet countries that have not yet been able to strengthen their institutions due to corruption. However, the role of corruption in the innovation-sustainability relationship remains underexplored. Although, according to the "sand-the-wheel" approach, corruption negatively affects business performance through inefficiency and uncertainty, the "grease-the-wheel" approach suggests that this negative impact may be reversed if corruption helps business activities in an inefficient bureaucratic environment. Based on the Institutional Theory, the Agency Theory, the Transaction Cost Economics, and the Resource-Based View, this study explores the effect of a weak institutional environment on firm performance, the impact of corruption on the worsening of the principal-agent problem, informal payments made to decrease transaction costs, and firm innovation capacity that helps to become sustainable. For this purpose, firm-level data from the World Bank Enterprise Survey of 2023-2024 were obtained, and a stratified random sampling method was used with a particular regression estimation technique. It was found that corruption had a statistically significant negative influence on firms' sustainability efforts, supporting the "sand-the-wheel" concept. However, corruption also had a positive influence on firms' innovation capacity - thus, a "grease-the-wheel" effect can be assumed in the post-Soviet context, characterized by an inefficient bureaucratic system and a weak institutional environment. Innovation, in turn, positively influences firms' sustainability efforts.

title: Sustainable development performance shortfalls and corporate ESG greenwashing
abstract: Amidst the rising strategic importance of ESG disclosure and concerns about greenwashing, a key unresolved question is under what performance conditions firms become more prone to such behavior. This study investigates the relationship between corporate sustainable development performance shortfalls and ESG greenwashing by developing and testing a contingency framework. Methodologically, we develop ESG-BERTopic, a deep learning framework for constructing a text-based measure of corporate ESG greenwashing based on the relative emphasis on future-oriented commitments in corporate reports. Analyzing a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms (2008–2024), we find that sustainable development performance shortfalls are associated with higher levels of corporate ESG greenwashing. This association is stronger in firms with more slack resources and weaker in firms with higher institutional ownership. Further analysis based on rating-based ESG greenwashing also shows a positive association with performance shortfalls. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that this association is statistically significant only among non-high-tech firms in heavily polluting industries. By linking shortfalls against an integrated sustainability aspiration to corporate ESG greenwashing, the study extends research on performance feedback and clarifies the moderating roles of slack resources and institutional ownership. The findings inform the review of ESG commitments by linking disclosure assessment to firms’ performance context, the implementation basis of proposed initiatives, and evidence of subsequent progress.

title: The rationality gap and information bridging:Explaining farmers’ abandonment of sustainable agricultural practices
abstract: The rice-green manure rotation system (RGRS) shows great potential in producing nutrient-enhanced rice and improving paddy field ecosystem. To clarify the behavioral mechanism of farmers' sustainable adoption of RGRS, this study systematically examined the tripartite rationality framework and its role in shaping sustainable behavior using a sample of 934 farmers, while revealing the moderating effect of digital information access. The main findings include: first, only 11.2% of farmers maintained continuous adoption throughout the observation window, while 27.1% never adopted RGRS and 61.7% adopted it only on a sporadic basis; second, farmers give priority to maximizing economic benefits while pursuing the satisfaction brought by ecological rationality; Third, although the current explanatory power of health rationality for sustainable behavior is weak, its role is expected to be significantly enhanced in the long term; fourth, economic rationality and the ecological rationality are mutually exclusive, healthy rationality strengthens ecological rationality while suppressing economic rationality; fifth, digital information access can stimulate sustainable behavior by alleviating the contradictions among the triple rationality and strengthening coordination. Under the assumption that newly expanded areas share similar agroecological and institutional conditions with existing cultivation zones, the potential diffusion area could increase by approximately 49% relative to the current base. This expansion would generate substantial economic, ecological and health benefits. These insights hold particular significance for policymakers seeking to enhance the scalability of RGRS through targeted information interventions that strategically align farmers’ rational motivations with sustainable agricultural objectives.

title: Corrigendum to “Structural and operational optimization of cold storage system for enhanced energy efficiency, rapid cold release and economic benefits” [J. Clean. Prod. 575, (2026), 149203]

title: A process-level framework for reconciling corporate GHG inventories and product carbon footprints
abstract: Corporate greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories and product carbon footprints (PCFs) are important tools for climate governance and decision making for cleaner production but are typically developed as separate reporting systems which result in redundant data handling processes, inconsistent emission factors and allocation practices as well as weak traceability between corporate totals and product-level accounts, particularly for shared utilities or value-chain emissions. This study proposes a process-level framework that reconciles corporate GHG inventories and PCFs through explicit accounting rules. The methodology involves a common activity-data backbone, process-level canonical emissions layer and hierarchy in which corporate totals result from aggregation while PCFs are derived by allocating the same process-level emissions. The framework formalizes a reconciliation identity in which corporate gross emissions equal the sum of product-attributed emissions, boundary-excluded emissions, and non-functionally linked emissions, preventing double-counting and improving transparency. The proposed framework is demonstrated by using an illustrative example and a case study of a chemical manufacturing facility. Based on the results, corporate and product-level emissions can be computed consistently from the same dataset and maintain traceability across all results. Product carbon footprints are predominantly driven by intensity of process energy and the input materials while the reconciliation structure allows definite identification of emission factors and allocation impacts. Sensitivity analysis is conducted to examine the impact of different allocation methods on the PCF of individual product. The sensitivity analysis shows that individual PCFs are sensitive to the selected allocation basis, whereas aggregate corporate-PCF accounting closure remains unchanged under normalized allocation. The proposed framework builds the reconciliation directly into the accounting structure instead of using post-processing adjustments, thereby improving consistency between the two reporting outputs. This framework facilitates more consistent reporting, better data governance, and enhances support for cleaner production and decarbonization decisions for the corporation.

title: Evaluating fiber harvesting modules as subsurface stormwater retrofits: Hydrologic, life-cycle environmental, economic, and decision-analytic evidence from contrasting urban contexts
abstract: Urban stormwater retrofits face a growing mismatch between hydrological demand and available surface space. The fiber harvesting module (FHM), a buried mineral-fiber system designed to create subsurface storage–release capacity, has been deployed at scale and incorporated into technical standards in China, yet systematic evidence remains limited. This study assessed FHM as a standalone retrofit and as a hybrid component with bioretention cells (BC) or green roofs across two contrasting catchments in Tianjin, China. Six configurations were compared under 15 design storms using SWMM, life cycle assessment, life cycle costing, marginal cost analysis and stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis. FHM-based systems reduced runoff by up to 93.2% and maintained greater stability as storm severity increased. FHM also achieved the lowest life-cycle environmental burden, with aggregated impacts 89–90% lower than conventional drainage, and consistently produced the lowest external cost. BC-FHM hybrid further outperformed standalone BC in runoff control, life-cycle environmental impact and cost. Decision analysis revealed that FHM and BC-FHM competed under different stakeholder priorities in the factory catchment, whereas FHM remained robustly preferred in the park catchment. These findings suggest that subsurface modular regulation can expand the stormwater retrofit design space, shifting selection from facility-based comparison toward context-specific combinations of surface ecology, subsurface capacity, and life-cycle efficiency.

title: Spatio-temporal evolution and driving mechanism of the level of coordinated transitional development between fossil fuel energy and clean energy in Chinese Cities: Insights from geospatial explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: Against the background of global warming, the coordinated transitional development between fossil fuel energy (FFE) and clean energy (CE) has become a core issue in China's energy transition. Most existing studies have analyzed energy transition at the national or provincial scale from a single dimension, overlooking city-level spatial heterogeneity and the need for an integrated FFE-CE perspective. Taking 291 Chinese cities as research objects, this study applies the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model to measure the level of coordinated transitional development during 2011–2021 and constructs a geospatial explainable artificial intelligence (GeoXAI) framework integrating XGBoost and the GeoShapley algorithm to analyze the spatially heterogeneous contributions of predictor variables to CCD predictions at national, regional, and city levels. The results show that: (1) CCD increased across all 291 cities during 2011–2021, with significant spatiotemporal differentiation. (2) CCD exhibited significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Global Moran's I > 0.6, Z > 2.58, p < 0.001), with High-High clusters concentrated in the eastern coastal region and Low-Low clusters emerging at the central-western border. (3) The XGBoost model achieved high prediction performance (test-set R2 = 0.9481, MAE = 0.0142, RMSE = 0.0206), and nuclear power plant accessibility (NPPA) was the most important factor at all scales, contributing 37.33% of total GeoShapley importance nationally and up to 42.79% in the Eastern Region. (4) Factor interactions were markedly stronger in the Western Region than those at other scales, with the NPPA-Temperature interaction reaching 8.62 × 10−4. The findings of this study not only provide scientific guidance for the formulation of multi-scale energy coordinated transition policies, but also promote the implementation of the “Dual Carbon” goals in China.

title: Optimizing rural sewage management systems: A spatial configuration typology approach with multivariate factor analysis
abstract: A scientific and applicable evaluation system for rural domestic sewage is a key prerequisite for efficient treatment.
