However, the selection of rural sewage treatment process still mainly refers to the urban sewage treatment process and relies on human judgment, lacking the multi-dimensional objective decision-making basis matching the spatial characteristics of the village. This study provides a rural domestic sewage treatment model and process decision-making system integrating village objective spatial pattern analysis and expert experience evaluation. Through the verification and analysis of 233 natural villages in Dengkou County, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, it is found that the residential density of villages in this county is mainly decentralized (43.25%), and the terrain type is mainly flat dam (85.85%). The treatment model is dominated by centralized (61.05%) and resource utilization (23.23%), which is consistent with the regional characteristics of the Yellow River Basin and the high degree of agricultural intensification. Combined with the decision tree and AHP-TOPSIS model, this study proposes the optimal sewage treatment process for different emission standards, and its comprehensiveness and applicability are better than the existing local processes. Partial least squares regression analysis was used to evaluate the influencing factors of treatment mode selection, and the results showed that population size (0.92) and gross domestic product (0.76) had a significant positive impact on the choice of treatment mode. By coupling objective spatial pattern analysis with expert experience evaluation, this study provides a replicable decision-making framework for rural sewage treatment technology screening while offering methodological support for relevant policy formulation.

title: Active suppression of wind-induced coal particle migration via flow optimization and fluid-structure interaction using gondola fairings
abstract: Coal particle migration induced by aerodynamic effects causes safety and environmental hazard during railway transportation. Apart from the existing particle isolation strategies from airflow, the optimization of flow driving forces could theoretically suppress particle migration. Guided by fluid-structure interaction, this study proposes semi-enclosed aerodynamic fairings above gondola carriages to intercept and redirect incoming airflow, thereby achieving flow optimization along coal accumulation surfaces. Discrete Phase Model with Computational Fluid Dynamics coupling simulations (DPM-CFD coupling) and streamline analyses in ANSYS-Fluent were adopted to compare the suppression effects of various fairing configurations, and the aerodynamic load effect and operation energy consumption were evaluated with the optimal fairing design during open-line and tunnel operations. Relevant results show that, despite the non-uniform and unsteady distribution along the coal accumulation surfaces, the fairings substantially weakened the horizontal airflow speed. The upward-closed fairing reduced the sweeping effect during the particle start-up process and established a more favorable flow direction and spatial relationship between vortices and structures. Under standard double-track tunnel operation conditions with train speed of 80 km/h, the fairing application achieved net mass reduction of 64.81% for one carriage during tunnel entry, and 42.81% migrated mass reduction under reality condition could be realized. The fairings increased the overall frontal area and, by enclosing and shielding the coal accumulation surface, reduced the sweep velocity over it. The flow optimization was realized by the enhanced fluid-structure interaction, which will also induce extra aerodynamic load on structures and drag energy consumption.

title: Crop growth and radiation use efficiency in urban agrivoltaic rooftop greenhouse environments: analysis of the vegetative phase of tomato, lettuce and common bean
abstract: Rooftop agrivoltaic greenhouses integrate food and photovoltaic (PV) energy production by co-locating crops and PV panels, although the shared use of solar radiation may limit crop productivity. Understanding crop growth dynamics and radiation use efficiency (RUE) under these conditions is essential to characterize system performance. To characterize inter- and intra-specific variability in plant responses, three sequential experiments were conducted comparing a conventional rooftop greenhouse (RTGctrl) and an agrivoltaic one (RTGapv) equipped with semitransparent PV panels. Three horticultural species (tomato, lettuce, and common bean) were evaluated during the vegetative phase across three experiments. Growth, morphological, and physiological traits were quantified through biweekly phenotyping to estimate relative growth rate (RGR), its physiological components, and RUE. Agroclimatic conditions were similar between greenhouses except for radiation, which decreased in RTGapv by 17.2%, 41.0%, and 47.9% in cumulated solar daily light integral (DLI). Supplementary LED lighting increased DLI in RTGapv to values 4.8% higher in Exp2 and 17.5% lower in Exp3 than RTGctrl. Seasonal differences explained most phenotypic variation in plant growth (70% of total dry biomass variance), whereas inter-specific variability was the main determinant of RUE (41.5%). RUE ranged from 0.44 to 7.92 g MJ −1 PAR, with tomato showing the highest values. Plants grown in the agrivoltaic greenhouse compartment exhibited lower RGR (14-45%) and RUE (16-69%) under suboptimal light (Exp1), whereas no differences between greenhouse compartments were observed in Exp2 and Exp3. These findings highlight the importance of adequate light availability and support further evaluation of RUE across crop genetic diversity under rooftop agrivoltaic conditions.

title: Cooling effects of urban blue-green spaces across China's climate zones: A dual-perspective and multi-factor analysis
abstract: Quantifying the cooling effects of urban blue-green spaces (UBGS) and identifying their driving factors are essential for optimizing blue-green infrastructure and mitigating urban thermal stress. This study investigated 950 UBGS samples across 30 major Chinese cities representing five distinct climate zones (BWk, BSk, Dwa, Cfa, and Cwa). Using remote sensing, GIS analysis, and Boosted Regression Tree (BRT) modeling, we quantified six cooling indicators, including cooling temperature (CT), distance (CD), area (CA), efficiency (CE), intensity (CI), and gradient (CG) from both maximum-value and cumulative-value perspectives. The primary findings are as follows: (1) Cooling effects exhibited pronounced climatic differentiation. The BWk zone showed superior performance in CT, CD, CI, and CG, while the BSk zone showed moderate performance, the Dwa zone exhibited balanced and favorable performance with the largest CA, the Cwa zone exhibited generally weak cooling performance, and Cfa demonstrated the highest CE. (2) Four distinct cooling typologies were identified: High-Intensity Cooling (large area, complex morphology), Marginal Cooling (high impervious coverage), Optimal Synergistic (strong aggregation, complex water geometry), and Extensive Radiation (high fragmentation). (3) Scale and composition characteristics showed the highest relative importance for CT, CD, CA, and CE, whereas landscape patterns ranked first in CI and CG, highlighting a functional differentiation in thermal regulation. Patch area (AREA) and green-space patch density (PD_GR) emerged as universal high-importance factors, frequently exhibiting non-linear threshold effects (e.g., CT enhancement when patch area is within the 0–300 ha range). Based on these insights, differentiated climate-adaptive planning strategies are proposed. These findings provide a robust scientific basis for cross-climatic urban thermal management and the enhancement of human settlement quality.

title: An AI-agent-enabled geospatial decision support system for urban multi-geohazard susceptibility screening
abstract: Urban multi-geohazard susceptibility screening requires reproducible tools that can identify where multiple geohazard signals co-occur and where field verification should be prioritized. However, assessment remains constrained by noisy historical samples, subjective hazard weighting, and susceptibility-signal dilution under linear aggregation. This study develops an AI-agent-enabled decision support system for urban multi-geohazard susceptibility screening. The Sample Enhancement Algorithm constructed training datasets for four XGBoost models, which achieved held-out accuracies of 0.894–0.954 and areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.959–0.990. AI agents then generated analytic hierarchy process and fuzzy analytic hierarchy process judgments under a structured Expert Skill Protocol; all model-method combinations retained their modal hazard order in 10/10 runs, with a maximum weight coefficient of variation of 2.10%. Label-conditioned Shapley additive explanations provided internal objective weights whose relative ranking remained stable across nine prespecified scenarios and two balancing methods. A Bayesian-inspired rule fused the subjective and internal objective weights, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution–Grey Relational Analysis aggregated the fused weights. Compared with weighted summation, this approach upgraded 24.8% of 811,806 grid cells, including 53,456 from High to Very High and 96,668 from Medium to High susceptibility. Independent evaluation using 16 unique collapse-landslide chain events from 2024 showed that the approach captured 31.3% of events within the highest-ranked 20% of the study area, compared with 18.8% under weighted summation. The framework provides an auditable susceptibility-screening workflow for prioritizing field verification in data-limited urban environments.

title: How farm size reshapes straw management structure? Evidence from household surveys in five Chinese provinces
abstract: Expanding farm size is often regarded as a key driver of the green and low-carbon transition in agriculture. However, unlike green technologies such as substituting chemical fertilizers and pesticides, crop straw management is a matter of allocating post-harvest byproducts across multiple pathways, and the direction in which farm-size expansion affects this process remains unclear. Based on 3675 household-crop-year observations from Jiangsu, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jilin, and Hebei provinces in China in 2018 and 2022, this study classifies straw management into four pathways: disposal, returning-to-field, household self-use, and selling. Using a Seemingly Unrelated Regression model, this study estimates the effects of crop-level farm size on crop straw management. The results indicate that farm size is not associated with the disposal share although the burning component alone rises with farm size; it is associated with higher returning-to-field and selling shares and a lower household self-use share. A decomposition into absolute quantities shows that all four pathways expand with farm size. The compositional movement therefore reflects differences in how fast each pathway grows and in how likely larger farms are to use it, rather than a physical transfer of straw between them. The returning-to-field response is concentrated in Sichuan and among rapeseed and soybean growers. The scale association also varies across terrain, household income, and educational attainment. The study suggests that farm size is an important prerequisite, but not a sufficient condition, for resource-oriented straw utilization. Only when mechanized services and collection, storage, and transportation systems are in place can scale advantages be translated into cleaner utilization pathways.

title: Regulation-conditioned market potential and value-added implications of wood fibre insulation in new residential construction in Finland, Germany, and the United Kingdom
abstract: The European forest sector faces increasing pressure to generate higher value added (VA) while operating under constrained harvesting levels and tightening climate targets. At the same time, substantial volumes of woodworking byproducts are allocated to energy production despite their suitability for higher-value material applications. This study investigates the regulation-conditioned market potential and VA implications of expanding wood fibre insulation (WFI) in new residential construction in Finland, Germany, and the United Kingdom (UK). A bottom-up assessment combines building-scale insulation demand, national construction volumes, regulatory boundary conditions, and harmonized sectoral VA metrics to compare alternative biomass allocation pathways. On a dry-matter (DM) basis, loose-fill WFI generated approximately five to seven times higher gross VA per tonne than bioenergy utilization, while board-type WFI consistently provided the highest returns. Resource analysis indicates that residues currently allocated to energy are sufficient to meet the modelled WFI demand in Finland and Germany, whereas the UK exhibits a tighter feedstock balance under the highest deployment scenario. However, realized market potential remains constrained by regulatory thresholds, construction systems, and supply-chain structures rather than resource availability alone. The findings suggest that reallocating suitable woodworking byproducts from energy to material use could increase forest-sector VA and extend the residence time of biogenic carbon in building products, although the overall climate implications depend on replacement-energy pathways and broader substitution effects.

title: How can composite policy potential energy drive county green innovation? A quasi-natural experiment of fiscal decentralization-performance evaluation synergy
abstract: Green innovation is crucial for reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, but its success relies on effectively motivating local governments to guide and support green innovation activities, addressing the dual externalities involved. This study constructs a compound quasi-natural experiment by combining China's “Province-Managing-County” fiscal reform with the 2013 performance evaluation reform. Using an unbalanced panel of Chinese counties from 2000 to 2019 and a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) approach, we examine the impact of this institutional complementarity on county-level green innovation. The results show that the institutional complementarity significantly promotes green innovation. These findings remain robust under placebo tests and PSM-DID estimations. Mechanism analyses show that institutional complementarity promotes green innovation by reshaping local government behavior through increasing local governments' environmental attention, expanding public investment, and intensifying promotion-based competition among officials. Moreover, the effects are more pronounced in counties with higher environmental assessment pressure, tighter financing constraints, and greater fiscal pressure. To maximize the impact of institutional complementarity, fiscal, assessment, and related policy tools should be integrated into a complementary and reinforcing framework.

title: A high-performance integrated PV water-electricity cogeneration device via enhanced steam circulation and dropwise condensation
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) water-electricity cogeneration offers a compelling pathway to simultaneously address water scarcity and rising energy demand. However, current systems are typically constrained by inefficient steam transport and suboptimal condensation heat transfer, limiting overall performance. Here, we present an integrated PV water-electricity cogeneration (IPVWC) device that overcomes these limitations through a rationally designed dual-enhancement strategy: a dedicated steam circulation module coupled with an amphiphilic hybrid copper condenser that enables rapid steam transport and efficient dropwise condensation. Comprehensive COMSOL Multiphysics simulations were performed to elucidate the entire transport chain from capillary wick evaporation to steam flow dynamics and condensation and to guide the optimization of device architecture. Concurrently, a theoretical framework describing droplet nucleation, growth, and departure on the condenser surface was established to inform surface design. At an illumination of 1 kW/m2, the optimized IPVWC device achieves a significant PV temperature reduction of 24.61°C while maintaining a continuous water production rate of 0.58 L/m2·h with the hybrid copper condenser, a chamber thickness of 5 mm and a nominal fan outlet velocity of 0.5 m/s. This work provides a viable design paradigm for next-generation integrated water-energy systems with strong potential for sustainable desalination applications.

title: Structural modeling of community acceptance for treated wastewater across diverse reuse applications
abstract: Water scarcity in arid regions has intensified the need for alternative water sources, with treated wastewater reuse emerging as a viable solution. However, its successful implementation depends largely on public acceptance, which varies across reuse applications and socio-demographic groups. This study investigates the determinants of community acceptance of treated greywater (GW) and mixed wastewater (MW) through a pioneering application of Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), focusing on the complex interplay between socio-demographic factors and reuse applications, including non-body contact (NBC), body contact (BC), and non-edible plants (NEP) domains. Survey data collected in the Dammam Metropolitan Area, Saudi Arabia, were analyzed using Confirmatory Factor Analysis and path modeling in SPSS and AMOS. The results indicate a gender-sensitive acceptance structure with satisfactory measurement reliability, validity, and model fit, confirming the hierarchical interdependencies among the investigated factors. NBC applications achieved the highest acceptance level (regression estimates 0.98–1.03), followed by NEP irrigation (0.75–0.96), while BC uses (0.47–0.91) faced greater resistance due to health and cultural concerns. Education level and awareness of wastewater treatment costs emerged as important predictors of acceptance, particularly among women, as well as younger and urban respondents. The study recommends prioritizing NBC and agricultural reuse applications, strengthening public trust, implementing targeted awareness campaigns, and infrastructure expansion. The study contributes to the literature by developing a multi-domain, theory-informed framework that integrates behavioral and socio-cultural factors to explain community acceptance of treated wastewater reuse. These insights align with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and the UN Sustainable Development Goals on water security, highlighting the untapped potential of wastewater reuse in arid regions. The findings provide a basis for a phased and context-sensitive policy strategy to enhance wastewater reuse adoption in water-scarce environments.

title: Mixing and sequencing matter: How policy instruments shape rural human settlements improvement under the “Motivation–Capacity–Trigger” governance framework
abstract: Governments worldwide have adopted diverse policy instruments to improve rural human settlements (RHS), yet how these instruments interact, combine, and should be prioritized remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM), this study develops an integrated framework encompassing motivation-enhancing, capacity-building, and trigger-based policy instruments. Using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces during 2005–2023, we combine NCA, fsQCA, and Geodetector approaches to examine the effectiveness of RHS policy instruments. The results show sustained improvements in both RHS performance and policy instrument intensity, accompanied by clear spatial stratified heterogeneity (SSH). Several instruments exhibit degree-based necessity under NCA, but no single policy instrument is universally indispensable across cases and performance levels. Consistently, fsQCA identifies no single condition as necessary in kind. Instead, nine antecedent conditions jointly generate seven effective pathways, which can be grouped into four configuration types, highlighting the prominent roles of economic incentives, social demonstration, technical–human support, infrastructure construction, and evaluation feedback. Policy implementation priorities vary across configurations, indicating that additional policy effort should be tailored to the existing policy mix rather than follow a uniform sequence. Spatially, eastern–central and western China exhibit distinct configurational pathways and implementation priorities, demonstrating that SSH extends from RHS outcomes to the policy mechanisms through which high performance is achieved. Overall, RHS improvement depends less on any universally indispensable instrument than on the context-specific combination, complementarity, and prioritization of policy instruments.

title: Carry-over release of microplastics and additives from PBAT mulch film residues affects soil-maize-microbiota system
abstract: Although biodegradable mulch films (BDMs) are promoted as sustainable alternatives to polyethylene films, their degradation may generate microplastics (MPs) and release chemical additives. In this study, commercial poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate)-based BDM (PBAT-BDM) residues were evaluated as a polymer additive system in a two-year carry-over greenhouse maize experiment. PBAT-BDM fragments were incorporated into soil at 0%, 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1% (w/w), and maize was grown for two consecutive cycles (P1 and P2) in the same continuously irrigated, residue-amended soil. During degradation, PBAT-BDMs developed progressive surface cracking, increased hydrophilicity, decreased C/O ratios, and generated more PBAT-derived MPs. Ultraviolet absorbers (e.g., UV-234 and UV-360) and organophosphate esters (e.g., AO168=O and TNPP) were also released and showed compound-specific dissipation and organ-dependent accumulation in maize. Increasing PBAT-BDM amendment levels altered soil physicochemical properties, reduced chlorophyll content, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities, particularly in P2, indicating carry-over physiological stress after prolonged exposure. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed shifts in the microbial community composition, including changes in the relative abundances of Pseudomonadota, Bacteroidota, Bacillota, and Actinomycetota. Structural equation modeling suggested that additive uptake disrupted antioxidant defense and contributed to maize biomass reduction. These findings indicate that commercial PBAT-BDM residues should be assessed as integrated sources of MPs and additives, rather than as biodegradable polymer matrices alone. They provide a scientific basis for managing the combined pollution risks of biodegradable plastics and their additives in agricultural environments.

title: Techno-economic analysis of a sequential bioprocessing facility for sustainable dairy feed production
abstract: An alternative feed supply from upcycling of food wastes in agri-food system would make dairy farms more independent from feed price oscillation. A techno-economic analysis of the sustainable dairy feed production facility via sequential fermentation of crop residue and fresh fruit/vegetable (FFV) discards was conducted. The facility has a 10-year lifetime with an annual capacity of producing 82,787 metric tons (MT) of fermented feed for dairy cattle from 18,081 MT of wheat straw, 43,396 MT of FFV discards, and 12,151 MT of alfalfa hay. The facility was profitable when sale price of the fermented feed was $90 MT−1 (the minimum selling price was $83.2 MT−1), FFV tipping fee was $67 MT−1, at an annual inflation rate of 2.0%. This condition created annual net cash flow of $1,687,450 (year 1) to $656,262 (year 10), a payback period of 3.96 years, and annualized return on investment (ROI) of 10.6%. At 5% discount rate, the net present value (NPV) of the investment was $3,436,129 with an internal rate of return (IRR) of 18% and discounted payback period of 4.63 years. Sensitivity analysis showed that the sale price of the fermented feed was the greatest determinant of the facility's profitability followed by FFV landfill tipping fee, cost of alfalfa hay. Cost of wheat straw, equipment and labor force had relatively less impact on profitability of the facility. Process capacity analysis suggested that the facility needs to be operated at least 20% of its full capacity to be profitable. This study theoretically demonstrated the economic feasibility of a proposed sequential bioprocessing facility as a method of producing sustainable dairy feed in the agricultural industry.

title: Can cropland yield and production resilience be reconciled? Evidence from a symbiotic framework in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain, China
abstract: Unraveling the complex interplay between yield and resilience is crucial for sustainable cropland development and food security. However, existing resilience assessments have largely relied on subjective indicator-based approaches and have paid limited attention to the dynamic interactions between yield and resilience. Therefore, this study quantified the spatiotemporal evolution of cropland production resilience in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain (HHHP) from a recovery dynamics perspective and developed a symbiotic framework to characterize its interaction with yield. Subsequently, the Lotka-Volterra and multiscale geographically and temporally weighted regression models were employed to characterize symbiotic states and their influencing factors. Results indicate that cropland production resilience in the HHHP exhibited a spatial pattern of increases in the central region but declines in the northern and southern regions, with approximately 47% of cities showing resilience growth. The yield-resilience symbiosis shifted from a competition-dominated to an antagonism-dominated regime, accompanied by a directional transition from resilience-favoring to yield-favoring pathways and an increasing prevalence of high-gain states. In contrast, mutualism remained scarce and was more susceptible to degradation. The impacts of individual driving factors on this symbiosis exhibited significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Agricultural inputs and technological progress showed predominantly positive influences, while climatic influences were relatively localized, whereas socioeconomic and cropland utilization factors exhibited bidirectional influences. Notably, in the absence of targeted interventions, the yield-resilience symbiosis still faces long-term risks of lock-in in competition and antagonism. These findings provide new insights into reconciling cropland yield and production resilience, supporting sustainable agricultural management.

title: Electro-regulated microbial interface drive sulfur cycling for enhancing anaerobic reduction of nitro-compounds: insights into electron distribution and metabolic response
abstract: In sulfate-containing anaerobic systems, electron competition between nitroaromatic compound reduction and sulfate reduction severely limits pollutant removal efficiency. In this study, an electro-assisted anaerobic system was constructed to elucidate electro-regulated electron distribution driving sulfur cycling for enhanced nitrobenzene reduction (NB). The results demonstrated that NB removal efficiency highly increased to approximately 99%, along with enhanced sulfate reduction at cathode potentials ≤ −700 mV. At the cathode, conductive pili and electroactive proteins facilitated electron uptake, while propionate metabolism supported NADH-related reducing processes, thereby promoting NB and sulfate reduction. At the anode, sulfide was oxidized (S2−→S0→SO42−), providing electrons that facilitated NB reduction. Elemental sulfur (S0), as a key intermediate in the oxidation pathway, functions as an electron relay to establish a dynamic electron transfer bridge between anodic and cathodic bio-interfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed favorable interfacial configurations between sulfur and heme proteins, suggesting its potential involvement in extracellular electron transfer. Electro-regulation was associated with sulfur redox transformation and changes in electron utilization, while the responses of sulfur-transforming microorganisms and NB degraders suggested a potential shift from electron competition toward more cooperative electron utilization under electro-regulated conditions. This study proposes the mechanism underlying electro-regulated enhancement of anaerobic nitroaromatic compound transformation from the perspective of electron distribution coupled with sulfur cycling, providing a novel strategy for the efficient treatment of wastewater co-contaminated with sulfate and nitro-compounds.

title: Experimental study on the degradation of inorganic nitrogen via biochar loaded with magnetic particles nZVI-LDH in the Erhai plateau lake, SW China
abstract: In plateau lake watersheds, the simultaneous removal of surplus NH4+ and NO3− is critical for mitigating soil nutrient surplus and aquatic eutrophication. Accordingly, this study synthesized a composite material, nZVI-LDH@Biochar (nZVI-LDH-BC), to facilitate the deep adsorption and redox degradation of NH4+ and NO3−. Specifically, removal rates reached 89.93% for NH4+ and 99.24% for NO3− under optimal conditions, with N2-N proportions of 90.18 wt% and 94.36 wt% in the degradation products, respectively. Moreover, the material achieved near-complete removal of both NH4+ and NO3− when applied to natural water from the Erhai Lake watershed. The recyclability of nZVI-LDH-BC is enhanced by its magnetic properties. It maintained 87.44% (NH4+) and 92.79% (NO3−) of its original removal capacity after 5 successive cycles. Batch degradation experiments, density functional theory calculations, intercalated ion concentration measurements, and scavenging experiments elucidated the degradation mechanisms of NH4+ and NO3−. ·OH and ·O2− consistently dominated the redox pathways for both NH4+ and NO3−, contributing 35.96%/23.69% directly to NH4+ removal and 11.02%/7.44% indirectly to NO3− removal. This study provides a fresh perspective on the development of materials for water pollution control.

title: Economic vs. green complexity: Distinguishing their roles in monetary policy and energy vulnerability
abstract: It is essential to understand the effect of monetary policy and green complexity on energy vulnerability. We analyze the distinct roles of Green Complexity Index (GCI) and the Economic Complexity Index (ECI) in 28 middle-income countries from 2000 to 2019 and find that GCI exerts a non-linear, inverted U-shaped impact on energy vulnerability, acting as a structural catalyst for energy transition only after reaching specific technological thresholds. In contrast, ECI demonstrates a direct, linear, and positive influence without such non-linear moderations. We further find that expansionary monetary policy consistently exerts a negative impact on energy vulnerability across the conditional distribution and that this mitigating effect of monetary policy is significantly amplified as the level of GCI increases, identifying GCI as a sophisticated moderator of monetary transmission. This positive moderation is most pronounced in high-vulnerability economies; in these contexts, increased GCI capacity effectively doubles the marginal efficacy of monetary policy in curbing energy vulnerability. We conclude that prioritizing targeted green industrial strategies—integrated with strategic monetary policy—provides a substantially more effective lever for enhancing energy resilience than pursuing either general broad-based industrial growth or the reliance on traditional economic complexity (ECI) alone.

title: Investigating the hydrogen-based reduction of industrial BF-grade iron ore pellets: Reduction behavior and microstructural insights towards sustainable ironmaking
abstract: Conventional carbon-based ironmaking processes are a major source of global CO 2 emissions, which can be significantly mitigated by hydrogen-based direct reduction (H 2 -DR). Significant industrial and research efforts are underway to adapt processes for hydrogen utilization. However, a fundamental understanding of the complex interplay between reduction kinetics, microstructural evolution, and structural integrity remains elusive. This gap is particularly important for understanding how abundant, lower-cost BF-grade pellets behave compared with premium DR-grade pellets. This study investigates the hydrogen reduction of industrial BF-grade iron ore pellets at 700–1000 °C. Thermogravimetric analysis and multiscale microstructural characterization linked phase transformations, pore evolution, and metallic iron morphology to global reduction behavior. Results show that increasing temperature from 700 °C to 1000 °C accelerates reduction kinetics, decreasing the time to reach 93% metallization by 77%. This acceleration is accompanied by significant, temperature-dependent microstructural evolution. At lower temperatures, a stable, fine-pored structure is formed, while temperatures above 900 °C lead to significant pore coarsening and severe cracking. Microstructural analysis confirms a topochemical reduction pattern. A critical challenge emerges at 700 °C, where complete core metallization is impeded by the formation of a dense iron layer around unreduced FeO particles. At higher temperatures (≥800 °C), metallization is more pervasive throughout the pellet. The study highlights the interplay between temperature, kinetics, and microstructure during the hydrogen reduction of BF-grade pellets, providing insights crucial for optimizing H 2 -DR processes for a wider range of raw materials.

title: Evaluation and further development of the VERA multi-farm approach to test emission mitigation measures for floor systems in naturally ventilated dairy barns
abstract: Emissions from dairy barns should be reduced, given their environmental and climatic impacts. To assess potential mitigation measures comparative measurements are required. In order to achieve comparable results, the VERA test protocol was developed. Should the preferred case-control approach not be implementable, the multi-farm approach may be used as an alternative. However, recent studies have highlighted the question of whether increased variances between the calculated emissions of the barns prevent clear conclusions. The aim of this study is to evaluate the suitability of the multi-farm approach of the VERA test protocol for detecting emission mitigation effects of different floor systems under practical dairy barn conditions. The primary focus was the performance of the study design, rather than an assessment of the mitigation effect. To validate the method 4 b were equipped with a reduction measure and examined in terms of their methane (CH 4 ) and ammonia (NH 3 ) emissions. The concentrations of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), CH 4 and NH 3 were measured using a Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer. Annual emissions were calculated by conducting measurements across seasons. The determined average annual emissions of the investigated dairy barns were 2.3 – 13.7 kg NH 3 -N and 180.6 – 356.5 kg CH 4 per animal place and year. The wide ranges of the estimated emissions indicate that the multi-farm approach presents statistical challenges due to individual barn variations. The analysis could be improved by including more barns.

title: AI to the rescue: A novel approach to measure plate leftovers
abstract: Assessment of household food waste has mainly relied on surveys, diaries, or waste bin composition analyses, each challenged by representativeness, completeness, validity, and/or measurement error. Photographing food waste is a promising alternative but manual coding requires time and effort. We demonstrate how recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to analyze photographed leftovers. Based on 469 photos of leftover dinner plates, we use GPT4o to obtain a reliable estimate of the type and quantity of visible remnants on plates. Based on our prompt development, we provide insights on how to use AI. We validate our findings, and assess the impact of measurement error by respondents, with 93 pictures collected by experts. The use of this novel approach severely reduces the effort associated with photo coding, while maintaining high precision and allowing for easy up-scaling.

title: Efficient separation and recovery of tellurium, germanium, and gallium from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass by sustainable vacuum distillation strategy
abstract: Tellurium (Te), germanium (Ge), and gallium (Ga) are critical strategic metals. They are widely used in photovoltaic devices, infrared optical systems, semiconductors, and advanced defense technologies. Waste chalcogenide glass represents an important secondary resource for these valuable elements. However, its clean and efficient recycling remains challenging due to the complex occurrence states of Te, Ge, and Ga and the limitations of conventional recovery processes. In this study, a two-stage vacuum distillation strategy was proposed for the selective separation and recovery of Te, Ge, and Ga from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass. The feasibility of the process was first evaluated based on saturated vapor pressure, maximum evaporation speed, separation coefficient and evaporation characteristics analyses. Two process routes were then designed and experimentally validated: high-temperature followed by low-temperature vacuum distillation (HTLT vacuum distillation), and low-temperature followed by high-temperature vacuum distillation (LTHT vacuum distillation). The results indicated that the HTLT vacuum distillation process yielded three products: the tellurium product contained 98.53 % Te, the germanium product contained 57.61 % Ge, and the gallium product contained 44.81 % Ga. The LTHT vacuum distillation process yielded three products: the tellurium product contained 95.69 % Te, the germanium product contained 34.73 % Ge, and the gallium product contained 27.31 % Ga. The proposed process features a short flowsheet, high adaptability to different raw material compositions, and environmental compatibility. This work provides a clean technical route for the separation and recovery of strategic metals from crystallized waste chalcogenide glass.

title: Supply chain digital innovation and the clean energy transition: Evidence from urban China
abstract: The clean energy transition (CET) depends on technological substitution and on the capacity to coordinate information and resources. This study evaluates whether exposure to China's 2018 Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Policy (SCIAPP) is associated with changes in urban CET. We use a balanced panel of 279 prefecture-level cities observed from 2008 to 2021 and a difference-in-differences design with city and year fixed effects and city-clustered standard errors. In the controlled specification, SCIAPP exposure is associated with a 0.032-log-point increase in the CET index (95% CI: 0.008–0.056), equivalent to approximately 3.27%. Adding province-specific linear trends yields a smaller estimate of 0.024 (95% CI: 0.007–0.042). Mechanism-proxy regressions are consistent with greater ESG-oriented fund allocation and forecasting performance as well as a lower energy-loss rate. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect is more significant in cities outside the Yangtze River Economic Belt and in areas with higher levels of market segmentation. Key limitations concern external validity beyond Chinese prefecture-level cities. Policy design should strengthen ESG-oriented green-finance allocation, forecasting and information capabilities, and operational-loss monitoring, while tailoring implementation to local market conditions and institutional capacity.

title: Territory, cleaner production practices and firm performance: evidence from the Spanish wine industry
abstract: The transition towards environmentally responsible production systems is reshaping strategic priorities across the global wine industry, requiring wineries to reconcile ecological objectives with economic competitiveness. The interaction between cleaner production practices and territorial governance structures remains only partially understood in geographically embedded agri-food industries. The analysis investigates the relationship between formal environmental sustainability practices and firm performance in the Spanish wine industry, with particular attention to the role of territory, identified through Protected Designations of Origin (PDOs). Drawing from a dataset comprising 318 Spanish wineries observed between 2014 and 2022, the study analyses whether environmental sustainability engagement and place-based dynamics are associated with differences in economic performance and adoption patterns. Sustainability engagement is identified through the variable certification, which captures externally verified certifications and other formal, observable signals of environmental sustainability practices, while economic performance is measured through return on assets (ROA), return on sales (ROS) and labour productivity indicators. Empirical evidence reveals that wineries with formal environmental sustainability practices displayed significantly higher economic performance in the post-adoption window than those without practices, with average ROA values of 5.3% compared with 2.1% of non-engaged wineries ( p < 0.001). Firm size was significantly associated with formal sustainability engagement (χ 2 = 7.507; p = 0.023). In addition, adoption differed significantly across PDO territorial structures (χ 2 = 14.383; p = 0.006), highlighting the relevance of institutional and geographical embeddedness in sustainability transitions. The study contributes empirical evidence on the business case for sustainability in agri-food systems and advances a territorial perspective on cleaner production practices in the wine industry.

title: Upcycling spent coffee grounds into deprotonated carboxyl-rich dissolved organic matter for functional gypsum-based thick coatings
abstract: Enhancing the mechanical strength of composites with agricultural waste has long been a bottleneck in advancing environmental sustainability. This study successfully introduces a circular economy strategy by incorporating spent coffee ground-derived dissolved organic matter (SDOM) into gypsum-based thick coatings, where interfacial complexation and retarding effects are proposed to govern the molecular structural development. The objective of this study is to convert spent coffee grounds (SCGs) into dissolved organic matter with high water solubility (>90%), enriched with deprotonated carboxyl functional groups through solid-to-solute (STS) technology. The resulting SDOM is incorporated into commercial gypsum matrices. FTIR and mechanical evaluations suggest that the deprotonated carboxyl groups in SDOM undergo coordinate complexation and hydrogen bonding with the calcium ions and hydroxyl groups of the gypsum components. This chemical interaction is expected to exert a regulatory retarding effect that promotes uniform dispersion, mitigates stress concentration, and facilitates a more complete matrix hydration. Consequently, the composite yields high-strength thick coatings with robust complexed carbonyl (C=O) coordination structures. Taguchi orthogonal design and analysis of variance (ANOVA) identified the SDOM solution concentration as the most influential factor affecting mechanical strength. Under optimal conditions, the maximum bending strength of SDOM-incorporated thick coatings reached 30.11 MPa, representing a 1.65-fold increase compared with pure gypsum (control). Moreover, SCG-derived SDOM enriched with hydrophilic deprotonated carboxyl functional groups facilitates uniform dispersion in water-based gypsum, enabling the composite thick coatings to exhibit superior surface thermal barrier capability and storability. The findings provide a transformative demonstration for the green building and waste-upcycling industries, contributing to the realization of environmental sustainability goals.

title: Temperature–humidity operating windows for mitigating degradation and enhancing passive shutdown recovery of a PEMFC stack under long-term WHVC operation using in situ water balance analysis
abstract: This study experimentally investigated the effects of operating temperature and inlet relative humidity (RH) on initial electrochemical performance, irreversible voltage degradation, internal water balance, and passive shutdown recovery of a three-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell stack under the World Harmonized Vehicle Cycle (WHVC). Nine temperature–humidity conditions (50–70 °C and 50–90% RH) were evaluated using three 50-h WHVC blocks per case, each followed by a 15-h passive shutdown, corresponding to 150 h of WHVC operation and 195 h per case. The highest initial performance was achieved at 60 °C/90% RH, whereas the lowest voltage degradation rate and highest mean shutdown recovery rate were obtained at 50 °C/90% RH. At 1.1 A/cm2, the voltage degradation rate ranged from 143.4 μV/h at 50 °C/90% RH to 1318.2 μV/h at 70 °C/50% RH. In situ water-balance analysis showed higher calculated water accumulation and lower outlet vapor flow rates at 50 °C/90% RH, whereas 70 °C/50% RH exhibited limited calculated water accumulation and high outlet vapor flow rates. The relationship between mean total water accumulation fraction and irreversible voltage degradation became stronger under load, with R2 increasing from 0.503 at 0.5 A/cm2 to 0.828 at 0.8 A/cm2. The mean shutdown recovery rate was 67.61% at 50 °C/90% RH and 18.13% at 70 °C/50% RH. Within the tested matrix, lower-temperature, high-RH conditions provided a more suitable operating window for limiting irreversible degradation and maintaining voltage recovery under WHVC operation.

title: Self-assembled biofilm consortia resist volatile fatty acid inhibition: Mechanisms underlying robust anaerobic digestion at high organic loading rates
abstract: High organic loading rate (OLR) often induce volatile fatty acids (VFAs) inhibition, destabilizing anaerobic digestion. To address this, an anaerobic fixed-bed biofilm reactor was operated under a stepwise increased OLR from 0.9 to 16.3 kg COD/m3/d. Results demonstrated that elevated VFAs stress triggered protein-driven self-assembly, fostering a robust biofilm consortium dominated by Methanothrix. A distinct niche partition emerged: suspended flocs, enriched with fermentative bacteria (e.g., Escherichia-Shigella), acted as a microbial seed bank for rapid substrate hydrolysis, while the biofilm, hosting specialized syntrophs like Anaerotignum, ensured stable methanogenesis. Functional gene profiling revealed the enrichment of norank_Geobacteraceae and c-di-GMP signaling pathways, suggesting potential direct interspecies electron transfer and enhanced structural integrity. Despite effluent VFAs peaks of 2000 mg COD/L, the system maintained a COD removal efficiency of 73%. This resilience was attributed to the functional redundancy between flocs and biofilm, which mitigated hydraulic washout and metabolic imbalances. This study elucidates the mechanistic underpinnings of microbial self-assembly into biofilms conferring robust resistance to VFAs inhibition, providing a viable technological paradigm for full-scale high-rate anaerobic digestion of concentrated wastewaters.

title: Carbon intensity–cost trajectories and policy implications for sustainable aviation fuels under electricity and hydrogen transitions
abstract: Existing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) assessments show that pathway carbon intensity and production cost vary across technologies, feedstocks, regions, and background energy systems. Yet static pathway rankings reveal little about how these differences translate into policy outcomes as electricity and hydrogen systems evolve. We use a scenario-consistent prospective life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis framework to trace how region- and scenario-specific electricity and hydrogen trajectories alter pathway carbon intensity and production cost. A carbon-intensity-based policy-mapping layer then translates these trajectories into compliance windows, credit balances, and break-even credit prices relative to the used-cooking-oil reference pathway. The analysis covers seven pathways, four regions, four transition scenarios, and 2025–2050, while forward-projecting only electricity- and hydrogen-related emission factors and prices to isolate this background-energy channel. Power-to-liquid with direct air capture shows the largest carbon-intensity and cost response, whereas the Fischer–Tropsch pathways remain comparatively stable. Under the assumed central carbon-intensity benchmark trajectory, only 17.9% of pathway–region–scenario cases remain compliant in 2050. At a fixed credit price of 200 USD/t CO2, power-to-liquid with direct air capture has positive median 2050 credit balances in EU-15, the USA, and Japan but a deficit in China. Break-even credit prices vary substantially across regions and years, indicating different incentives required for cost parity. These results show that regional energy-system changes propagate through pathway-specific environmental and economic responses and interact with policy parameters to shape modeled SAF compliance and incentive outcomes that cannot be inferred from static pathway rankings alone.

title: When is it valuable to be green? Impact of green practices on firm resilience
abstract: Against the global green transition, green practices have become imperative for manufacturing firms, yet their divergent impacts on firm resilience remain underexplained. Existing sustainable operations management literature overemphasizes green practice effectiveness but neglects the heterogeneity of practice types (substantive vs. symbolic) and the strategic value of adoption timing, lacking a contingent framework to interpret their boundary conditions. Using 2012-2023 data from Chinese listed manufacturers and the Awareness-Motivation-Capability (AMC) framework, this study explores how substantive (Sub) and symbolic (Sym) green practice adoption timing affect firm resilience. We find that Sub exhibit a first-mover advantage: earlier adoption of substantive practices is positively associated with firm resilience. Managerial myopia weakens the advantage, while customer concentration strengthens it. In contrast, Sym do not exhibit a clear first-mover advantage individually; however, their association with firm resilience becomes positive conditionally, at higher levels of managerial myopia or asymmetric cost management. The results provide clear guidance for firms to select green practices and optimize adoption timing, and help green initiatives effectively improve resilience against market fluctuations.

title: Acetate-rich short-chain fatty acid production from waste activated sludge via in situ sulfate-mediated anaerobic fermentation
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation of waste activated sludge (WAS) is a promising route for recovering short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), but its performance is often constrained by limited substrate accessibility, unfavorable electron partitioning, and methanogenic SCFA consumption. This study investigated direct Na2SO4 supplementation as an in situ fermentation-stage strategy for enhancing acetate-rich SCFA production. At the preferred dosage of 4500 mg Na2SO4/L, peak SCFA production increased from 211.7 to 298.8 mg COD/g VSS, while acetate selectivity increased from 64% to >90%. Sulfate supplementation promoted EPS restructuring and soluble organic matter release, as indicated by EPS redistribution, a zeta-potential shift toward neutrality, and elevated SCOD and NH4+-N release. In parallel, sulfate transformation was supported by dose-dependent sulfide accumulation and supplementary sulfur-speciation evidence showing sulfate depletion, minor sulfite accumulation, and HS−-dominated dissolved sulfide under the final alkaline conditions. Gas-phase measurements further indicated a lower estimated reactor-level H2 partial pressure and suppressed CH4 production under sulfate supplementation, providing an experimentally constrained basis for interpreting sulfate-associated electron dissipation and reduced methanogenic consumption. Metagenomic and enzyme analyses revealed enrichment of sulfate-reducing populations (Desulfovibrio, Desulfomicrobium) and sulfate-reduction genes (dsrA/B, +3.2-fold; aprB, +2.08-fold), enhanced SCFA-forming functions, and reduced methanogenesis-related functional potential (mcrA gene abundance reduced to 52.2% of the control). These shifts suggest that direct sulfate addition enhances acetate-rich SCFA accumulation through coupled improvement of substrate accessibility, sulfate-associated electron partitioning, and attenuation of methanogenesis-related SCFA consumption. This work provides a fermentation-stage sulfur-regulation strategy for producing acetate-rich internal carbon sources from WAS.

title: Synergistic reinforcement and heavy metal stabilization of lithium slag-feldspar powder composites via microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation
abstract: The continued accumulation of lithium slag (LS) and low-activity feldspar powder (FP) causes high disposal costs and persistent heavy metals (HMs) leaching hazards. Large-scale synergistic treatment methods for these wastes are still critically lacking. This study utilized microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) for the synergistic solidification of the LS-FP micro-graded system. The micro-graded skeleton was constructed through particle micro-grinding and subsequent size classification. Response surface methodology (RSM) optimized the process parameters, and the mechanical responses and HMs stabilization mechanisms were systematically investigated. Maximum CaCO3 precipitation of 15.3% was obtained at 1.25 mol/L and 12 grouting cycles, while the RSM-optimized parameters (80% LS, 0.76 mol/L, and 10 grouting cycles) produced a UCS of 0.84 MPa and a peak shear strength exceeding the untreated control by 60.57% (348.6 kPa). The lateral ultimate strain exhibited a 45.4% decrease, pointing to a distinct improvement in deformation and spalling resistance. Multi-scale microstructural characterizations indicate that CaCO3 precipitates provide physical entrapment through pore filling and co-precipitation, the micro-gradation and interlocking of LS–FP particles form a load-bearing framework, and the C-(A)-S-H gel network generated by the pozzolanic reaction of reactive aluminosilicate phases provides particle cementation and interlayer adsorption. The interplay of these three components creates the physicochemical basis for mechanical reinforcement and HMs stabilization. Leaching inhibition rates of 18.5% and 44.1% were recorded for Be(II) and Tl(I), respectively. Overall, the proposed approach offers a sustainable avenue for the synergistic recycling of LS and FP, subject to further field-scale validation.

title: From exploitation-driven accumulation to mutualistic coordination: Evolutionary transitions of urban metabolic networks in 20 representative cities based on a process-structure-function framework
abstract: Rapid urbanization has imposed unprecedented resource and environmental pressures on Chinese cities. To identify keystone sectors in urban metabolism and reveal how sector-system interactions evolve with increasing material flows, we constructed an eight-sector urban material metabolic network for 20 representative Chinese cities by integrating material flow analysis with ecological network analysis. Ecological relationships, the Mixed-trophic impact (MTI) index, and ecological benefit were quantified within a process-structure-function framework and linked to total material flow. The results show that exploitation/control relationships dominated in all cities, typically accounting for 50-65% of interactions. The proportions of mutualistic relationships ranged from 14% to 33% and exceeded 25% in certain years in half of the cities. Mining was the keystone sector in all cities except Shenzhen, where energy conversion dominated, accounting for more than 35% of the total MTI. The MTI share of mining remained above 22% throughout the study period and reached 89%. Manufacturing generated the lowest ecological benefit across all city types except Shenzhen, and its ecological benefit declined in 75% of the cities. In leading-development cities, waste treatment produced the highest ecological benefit, generally exceeding 1.0, whereas mining produced the highest ecological benefit at other development stages. As metabolic scale increased, systems shifted from dominance by exploitation/control relationships toward stronger competition and ultimately to dominance by mutualistic relationships. The MTI share of mining rose from 40-60% to 80-90%, while total ecological benefit declined and stabilized at 5.3-5.9. These findings reveal an “accumulation-efficiency-coordination” trajectory and provide measurable indicators for identifying sustainable development pathways, cross-stage benchmarking, and improving resource efficiency across different urban types.

title: Sustainable recovery of silver wires from crystalline silicon solar cells
abstract: Silver is a valuable metal in end-of-life crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules, yet recycling mainly relies on acid leaching, which converts metallic Ag into Ag+ and generates acidic wastewater. Although molten salt Ag-recovery methods avoid acid use, they cannot effectively control Si-substrate corrosion loss, and the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here, NaOH-KOH molten salt etching of Al-BSF solar cells was investigated to elucidate the mechanisms of Ag wires recovery and Si-substrate loss. The molten salt etched the SiNx passivation layer and weakened Ag/SiNx interfacial adhesion, allowing Ag wires to detach without ionic dissolution. Thermodynamic calculations showed that Si3N4 and exposed Si reacted with NaOH-KOH molten salt to form Na2SiO3 and K2SiO3. Experimental results showed that the Si-substrate loss ratio was only 2.62 % at 230 °C for 100 s. At 230 °C for 150 s, Ag recovery reached 94.34 %, and the SiNx passivation layer was effectively removed, maximum Ag recovery was 97.11 %. Regarding the mechanism of Si-substrate loss, the exposed Si substrate undergoes alkaline molten salt etching after SiNx removal, during which OH− promotes conversion of Si into soluble Na/K silicates, causing localized Si-substrate loss and pitting. These findings clarify the mechanisms of acid-free, low-loss precious-metal recovery from crystalline silicon photovoltaic materials.

title: Decoding the ecological–economic transition in Beijing city through culturomics and co-expression networks: from trade-off to synergy
abstract: The synergistic advancement of economic development and ecological quality in a city is central to sustainable development. While the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis posits an initial trade-off followed by a turning point toward synergy, high-resolution quantitative evidence identifying these inflection points and their potential underlying dynamics in specific city contexts remains scarce. In this exploratory study, we investigated the relationship between ecological and economic activities of Beijing (2005–2024) by applying culturomics and word co-expression network (WCN) analysis to longitudinal textual data from the Beijing Daily. The results indicated that negative ecological words (NEs) and environmental pollution indicators in Beijing followed an inverted U-shaped EKC, with a potential peak occurring around 2015 at a per capita gross domestic product (GDP) of approximately 16,666 USD. Media discourse exhibited a fundamental structural transition, shifting from non-ecologically friendly economic activities toward ecologically friendly terms, with ecological activities gaining a systemic advantage (Revealed comparative advantage [RCA] > 1) by 2018. The synergy-to-tradeoff ratio of the ecological-economic co-expression network increased to 1.20, coinciding with a 63% increase in non-negative ecological terms and a 40% decrease in negative terms within the core lexicon, as well as reductions in pollutant levels. City sustainability was characterized by a dynamic balance, in which overall synergistic transformation was punctuated by transient periods of synchronized decline in both ecology and economy, reflecting the system's “adaptive sustainability”. Ultimately, this study provides a replicable, data-driven framework for diagnosing city sustainability transitions and highlights the pivotal role of policy intervention in restructuring the trajectory of city development.

title: Methodological framework for planning and evaluating circular economy projects in socio-environmental vulnerable territories
authors: Rita de Cássia de Oliveira Sebastião
abstract: The transition to a circular economy requires context-sensitive projects that integrate resource circularity with socioenvironmental inclusion, particularly in vulnerable territories where infrastructure and institutional support are uneven. However, practical and reproducible frameworks that guide both the planning and evaluation of community-based circular economy projects across their life cycle remain limited. This study proposes a structured methodological framework aligned with cleaner production principles that integrates participatory planning with a multidimensional impact assessment. The framework operationalizes 24 indicators grouped into six analytical dimensions and uses an explicit 1-5 scoring rubric supported by traceable evidence sources. Because the 6D/24I framework is conceived as a formative, multidimensional evaluation architecture rather than a reflective measurement scale, classical psychometric validation techniques, such as internal consistency coefficients or factor analysis, are not conceptually appropriate. The indicators do not represent interchangeable manifestations of a single latent construct; instead, each captures a substantively distinct dimension of project performance. In formative models, low inter-item correlation does not indicate measurement weakness, but dimensional independence. The framework is therefore designed as a structured multi-criteria diagnostic system rather than a latent-variable measurement instrument. Robustness is assessed through evidence traceability, explicit scoring rubrics, triangulation of qualitative and quantitative sources, and sensitivity analysis of weighting schemes. The framework was applied to four socioenvironmental projects in Brazil that reuse glass waste in distinct intervention modes: sustainable materials development, ecojewelry production, eco-brick manufacturing in quilombola communities, and socioenvironmental entrepreneurship in basic education schools. An additional ex post application to an externally developed project (Acelera Rio Doce), assessed by evaluators who were not involved in either the author team or the project, was used to examine the framework's operational usability beyond the author-led cases; this application is interpreted as an external methodological illustration rather than formal validation of inter-rater or cross-context reproducibility. Cross-case application revealed differentiated performance profiles across dimensions and highlighted boundary conditions for implementation, including institutional arrangements, infrastructure availability, and the maturity of local governance networks. The study contributes a transparent and evidence-traceable assessment architecture for practitioners and researchers, providing a structured basis for criterion-referenced diagnosis and offering design principles that are potentially transferable to comparable Global South contexts when enabling conditions are considered.

title: An integrative design framework for campus souvenirs: Fostering product attachment and sustainable use
abstract: Campus souvenirs carry emotional and cultural value, yet many fail to support sustained, meaningful use. This study developed the positive experience-driven design (PEDD) framework as an integrative approach to campus souvenir design, exploring how product attachment may be directed toward continued and meaningful use rather than passive retention. Using qualitative user research, we identified users' experiential motivations and psychological needs, translated these insights into design opportunities through structured tools, and evaluated the resulting concepts through prototype-based feedback. The findings provide preliminary qualitative evidence that the framework may support concept generation and refinement, while participatory and meaningful experiences were associated with product attachment, and participants reported intentions for continued engagement with the product. By clarifying how experience-driven design may shape product attachment toward sustainable usage, this study contributes an integrative perspective to research on product attachment and subjective well-being and provides practical guidance for campus souvenir design.

title: 3D spherical Fe-Mn-N co-doped porous carbon catalyst for peroxymonosulfate activation toward 2,4,6 trichlorophenol degradation: Performance and singlet-oxygen-dominated mechanism
abstract: Powdered metal-carbon catalysts for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation suffer from difficult solid-liquid separation, poor hydraulic stability, and severe metal leaching, restricting their continuous-flow wastewater treatment applications. Herein, a millimeter-scale 3D spherical Fe-Mn-N co-doped porous carbon catalyst (DCN4@FS0.3-SA) was fabricated via a low-cost, eco-friendly route using delignified balsa sawdust, steel blast furnace ferromanganese sludge (FS), melamine, and sodium alginate. Delignification pretreatment optimized the biomass pore framework, while FS supplied Fe/Mn bimetallic active species, and melamine enabled uniform nitrogen doping. The optimal catalyst possessed a well-developed hierarchical micro-mesoporous network, uniformly dispersed Fe-Mn oxide/nitride nanoparticles, high graphitization, and abundant surface defects. Under optimal conditions, the DCN4@FS0.3-SA/PMS system achieved 99.5% removal efficiency and 62.4% mineralization of 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (TCP) within 50 min with the kobs of 0.098 min−1. Batch and continuous-flow filtration tests verified its favorable hydraulic adaptability and recyclability, with thermal regeneration effectively restoring deactivated activity. Results revealed 1O2 as the dominant reactive species, accompanied by SO4•−, HO•, and O2•− via synergistic Fe-Mn redox cycling and N-doped carbon-mediated electron transfer. Three parallel TCP degradation pathways were proposed based on mass spectrometry intermediates, and toxicity evaluation confirmed that complete ring-opening mineralization drastically reduced aquatic ecological risks. This work provides a sustainable strategy for co-valorizing biomass and metallurgical solid wastes to develop separable spherical catalysts for refractory halogenated phenolic wastewater remediation.

title: Exploring sustainable food procurement strategy – the case of farmed fish
abstract: Sustainable food procurement faces complex challenges, including balancing environmental goals with economic constraints, ensuring consistent supply, and meeting consumer expectations. This study explores how Sweden's major grocery retailers (ICA, Coop, and Axfood) approach the procurement of locally produced fish amid growing concerns about food system vulnerabilities. Focusing on consumer preferences, branding, and sustainability commitments, the study uses a qualitative case study design based on interviews with procurement managers and secondary data from annual and sustainability reports. Guided by frameworks on product branding and sustainable food procurement strategy, the analysis reveals a gap between sustainability ambitions and actual procurement practices. Despite strong sustainability messaging, Swedish fish remains underrepresented due to high prices, limited availability, and unpredictable demand. Consumers show interest in local, sustainable fish but tend to buy familiar, accessible options like salmon and cod. Nevertheless, retailers are taking steps through supplier collaboration, cost management, and gradual product integration. The findings offer insights into how branding and sustainability commitments shape procurement strategies and highlight key barriers and opportunities for strengthening local sourcing.

title: Life cycle assessment of heat pipe grinding wheels for cleaner machining of aerospace superalloys
abstract: Global carbon-neutral commitments are compelling aerospace manufacturers to reconcile high-performance machining with environmental sustainability. Grinding nickel-based superalloys conventionally demands flood cooling to prevent thermal damage, creating substantial carbon footprints from energy-intensive coolant systems and hazardous waste treatment. This study introduces a heat-pipe grinding wheel (HPGW) combined with minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) as a tool-enabled cleaner grinding route. Orthogonal experiments were conducted to compare the thermal performance of the HPGW and conventional grinding wheel (CGW), followed by a stage-wise life cycle assessment covering wheel manufacturing and one-pass grinding. At vs 55 m/s, vw 120 mm/min, ap 0.2 mm, the CGW-MQL route causes workpiece burn at 696 °C, while the HPGW-MQL limits it to 494 °C without burn. This result establishes the feasibility of replacing the CGW–flood route with the HPGW–MQL route. In the manufacturing stage, the HPGW reduces steel use by 52.3%, lowering the fossil global warming potential (GWP) from 40.0 to 27.7 kg CO2-eq, despite higher electricity. In the grinding stage, the fossil GWP for CGW-flood route decreases from 0.184 to 0.0434 kg CO2-eq per pass for HPGW-MQL, corresponding to a 76.4% reduction, compared the CGW-flood cooling route. This route eliminates waste treatment requirements and achieves consistent improvements across acidification, toxicity, and resource scarcity indicators. Tool-structure-enabled process-route substitution offers a feasible pathway to prevent grinding burn in difficult-to-machine materials while reducing grinding-stage environmental burdens, enabling machining decisions to be evaluated more comprehensively from a system-level environmental perspective.

title: Prolonged (80-day) exposure to waste drilling fluids alters the structure and trophic networks of marine plankton communities in a microcosm study
abstract: The ecological risks associated with the direct discharge of waste drilling fluids (WDFs) into the ocean must be systematically assessed. Through an 80-day microcosm experiment, we assessed main pollution characteristics and seawater quality after introducing WDF water extracts at three concentrations and examined the prolonged dynamic effects of continuous exposure on natural plankton communities. WDF input altered key water quality parameters, increased Cr and As, and caused Cr and Hg in the HIGH group to exceed GB 3097-1997 Class I seawater standards. Chlorophyll a (Chl a) and dissolved oxygen (DO) levels and the pH decreased, whereas turbidity increased. WDF input also changed phytoplankton and zooplankton species compositions, increased spatial differentiation within communities, and generated dose-dependent effects. Phytoplankton responded more quickly than zooplankton, and toxicity verification experiments confirmed that phytoplankton were more sensitive. RDA indicated that Cr and Hg were the primary variables that explained changes in the community structure of phytoplankton and zooplankton, respectively. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed decreases in the total network and subnetwork topologies and the connectivity and abundance of key taxonomic groups, suggesting general network degradation. Based on the random forest model and Spearman's correlation analyses, cross-trophic interactions dominated the total network responses, followed by the phytoplankton subnetwork. These results indicate that the central mechanism underlying WDF ecological risk is weakening planktonic interactions via direct interspecies interference and impaired phytoplankton supply. These findings provide a systematic foundation and theoretical support for establishing an ecological risk assessment system for WDFs and promoting their eco-friendly use and emission management.

title: Circularity of different plastic product sectors in Germany: Product interaction with surrounding infrastructure
abstract: Circular Economy potential has often been classified based on individual aspects such as recyclability of materials. This fails to capture the complex interaction between products and the surrounding infrastructure, which stems from country-, product- and material-specific regulations and market conditions. Therefore, this study assesses the circularity of different product categories in Germany resulting from this interaction using a Material Flow Analysis and the Material Circularity Indicator. Different levers are discussed: i) applied polymer types, ii) product design, iii) waste collection systems and iv) product-specific regulations. The results show large differences in circularity of different product categories and reveal untapped Circular Economy potentials. They indicate that most applied polymers are technically recyclable, but circularity is limited by product design from a product perspective and waste collection systems and missing regulations for recyclate use from an infrastructure perspective. A successful Circular Economy implementation requires for both perspectives to be considered.

title: Longevity index for small electrical and electronic appliances: Qualitative assessment of reliability and durability
abstract: The growing concern over electronic waste and the need to extend product lifespans have highlighted longevity as a key aspect of sustainable product design. This research presents a longevity index as a practical tool for manufacturers and stakeholders to assess, communicate and improve the longevity of small electrical and electronic equipment (sEEE). The main novelty of the study lies in the integration of reliability and durability into a single operational index specifically developed for sEEE, combining technical, repairability, maintenance and warranty-related indicators through a transparent scoring and weighting system. The proposed methodology combines qualitative and quantitative elements to evaluate product longevity in a structured and comparable manner. The index was developed for application to different products within the sEEE category and implemented through an Excel-based tool that guides data collection and automatically calculates the final score. A controlled case-study application involving two products from the same category and three evaluators was conducted to examine the practical application of the method, its ability to differentiate between comparable products and inter-evaluator variability. A sensitivity analysis was also performed to assess the stability of the product scores and ranking under variations in the factor weights. As a decision-support tool, the longevity index contributes to circular economy objectives by providing structured information to support sustainable product choices.

title: Carbon emission efficiency of China's manufacturing industry and choice of precise carbon reduction paths——Analysis perspective based on the potential cost framework
abstract: Targeted decarbonization in manufacturing requires more than identifying efficiency losses; it also requires assessing each energy source's technical abatement potential, marginal abatement cost, and implementation priority. Using a balanced panel of 29 manufacturing subsectors in China from 2010 to 2024, this study estimates carbon emission efficiency with slacks-based measure directional distance function (SBM-DDF) models under meta-frontier and group-frontier technologies. It then uses undesirable-output slacks to quantify the abatement potential for coal, oil, and natural gas and combines these estimates with marginal abatement costs derived from parametric linear programming to construct a potential-Boston matrix. The results show that the manufacturing sector's meta-frontier efficiency increased from 0.520 to 0.641, although substantial room for improvement remains. For the medium- and high-emission groups, group-frontier efficiency was markedly higher than meta-frontier efficiency, indicating the need for both within-group catch-up and technological upgrading toward the meta-frontier. The high-emission group had the greatest abatement potential and the lowest average marginal abatement cost, whereas abating emissions associated with natural gas was generally more costly than abating those associated with coal or oil. The potential-Boston matrix classifies the 29 subsectors into four decarbonization pathways: phased advancement (13), comprehensive advancement (2), steady maintenance (12), and priority-focused mitigation (2). The proposed framework uses the meta-frontier to define long-term targets and group frontiers to set near-term catch-up benchmarks, translating efficiency, potential, and cost estimates into industry-energy priorities. Technology retrofits, fuel substitution, carbon pricing, transition finance, and regulatory measures can then be tailored to limit output losses while prioritizing high-potential, low-cost abatement opportunities.

title: Eco-fiscal sustainability of plain afforestation: From ecological value creation to value realization
abstract: Afforestation projects can enhance ecosystem services (ESs) but may leave persistent fiscal commitments for land leasing and forest maintenance after project construction. Existing ES and Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) assessments have largely focused on ecological value creation, with limited attention to whether and under what conditions this value can be converted into funding for long-term operation. This study develops an eco-fiscal sustainability framework integrating spatial restructuring, GEP accounting, life-cycle cost analysis, future projection, ecological value realization (EVR), and uncertainty analysis, using the Plain Afforestation Project in Xiji Town, Beijing, as a case study. From 2010 to 2023, afforestation transformed the landscape from cropland dominance to a forest–cropland mosaic, while GEP increased by 26.6% to CNY 839.5 million and regulating services accounted for 92.02% of total GEP. Assuming no further afforestation, total GEP is projected to increase to CNY 916.2–939.8 million by 2080, mainly through forest development within the afforestation area, whereas annual fiscal costs generally decline as construction expenditure ends and maintenance requirements decrease. However, cumulative cost coverage depends strongly on EVR: under the 2030 baseline activation scenario, and given the specified cost pathway and GEP uncertainty, the 10% and 20% EVR scenarios do not achieve cumulative cost coverage by 2080, whereas all 3000 simulations under the 30% scenario reach non-negative cumulative net cash flow before 2080.
