These findings show that eco-fiscal sustainability depends not only on ecological value creation but, more critically, on the capacity to convert realizable ecological value into stable funding, providing a framework for the long-term management of post-construction peri-urban plain afforestation.

title: Dietary transitions for urban water sustainability in arid regions: A planetary health case study from Ürümqi, China
abstract: We develop an integrated domestic water-conservation framework combining dynamic water pricing with healthy-diet interventions to jointly manage physical and virtual water use. (Virtual water refers to the total interregional flow, through trade, of water consumed in the production of traded products.) Relative to the baseline diet, healthy, vegetarian and meat-based diets reduced annual per-capita food water footprints (The water footprint quantifies the total water use associated with consumption by an individual, region or country.) by 166.11, 208.42 and 167.97 m3, respectively, and industrial water footprints by 14.95, 22.05 and 15.17 m3 through supply-chain linkages, while direct domestic water use remained largely unchanged. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual per-capita shower water use by 10.58–15.88 m3 and total domestic water use by 42.32–83.58 m3. Acceptance differed between interventions: 41.67% supported water-price regulation, mainly influenced by consumption habits, whereas 53.57% accepted dietary adjustment, with willingness more strongly associated with ethnicity and income. After accounting for acceptance rates, the three dietary scenarios reduced city-wide annual food water footprints by 370, 464 and 374 million m3 and industrial water footprints by 33, 49 and 34 million m3, respectively. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual urban water use by 73–145 million m3, including 18–27 million m3 of shower water. Water pricing therefore primarily affects direct domestic use, whereas dietary adjustment propagates upstream through supply chains, generating broader water-footprint effects. This framework advances domestic water conservation towards coordinated social–ecological governance of physical and virtual water, offering a transferable pathway for water-scarce cities.

title: From past trends to future costs: The influence of economic parameter selection on building life cycle costs in Belgium
abstract: While upfront investment costs remain a key decision parameter in building design due to budget constraints, life cycle costs have become increasingly important for evaluating financial feasibility due to rising energy, material, and maintenance costs. Estimating life cycle costs requires assumptions on price evolution and discount rates, which are particularly uncertain given the long service life of a building. Accurately estimating life cycle costs therefore requires reliable economic parameters. This study analyses the historical evolution of key economic parameters in the Belgian context. A long-term dataset is constructed and analysed across multiple observation periods. Derived rates are used to assess how variations in parameter values influence the life cycle cost of a case study building. The results show that parameter values vary significantly depending on the selected observation period. Energy and material cost growth rates exhibit the highest variability, while labour costs show a more stable trend. The discount rate is identified as one of the most influential parameters, with low values leading to higher life cycle costs. The findings highlight the importance of transparent and context-specific parameter selection. Based on the analysis, a 50-year observation period is proposed as a reference to estimate LCC parameter values, supplemented by a sensitivity analysis using shorter periods to assess the influence of alternative economic conditions. For Belgium, this corresponds to a recommended real annual discount rate of 4,20% and real material, labour, and energy growth rates of 0,74%, 0,50% and 2,00% respectively.

title: Ranking green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) framework: Empirical evidence from Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry
abstract: The petrochemical industry faces increasing pressure to decarbonize due to its high energy intensity, carbon emissions, and environmental footprint. This study evaluates and ranks green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework to identify the highest-ranked mechanisms for supporting the sustainable transition of Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry. A two-stage multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework integrating the Analytic Network Process (ANP) and fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was employed to assess six alternatives comprising four green finance instruments and two finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms against three ESG dimensions and fifteen industry-specific sub-criteria. The results show that the Environmental dimension carries the highest priority, followed by Governance and Social, highlighting the importance of measurable environmental outcomes supported by robust governance structures. Among the evaluated alternatives, green tax policies ranked first, followed by green credit mechanisms and investor risk mitigation instruments. The findings suggest that progressive environmental taxation, preferential green lending, and blended-finance mechanisms are better positioned to support industrial decarbonization while limiting abrupt cost pressures during the transition. Furthermore, the effectiveness of green bonds and emission trading systems depends on transparent governance, regulatory compliance, and credible sustainability reporting frameworks. This study provides policy insights for aligning industrial finance with Saudi Vision 2030, the Saudi Green Initiative, and the Kingdom's 2060 net-zero target, while offering a practical decision-support framework for prioritizing sustainable finance in energy-intensive industries.

title: Sustainable production of ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage particles from molten steel slag
abstract: Steel slag (SS), a high-volume byproduct (150 kg/ton steel) with severe disposal burdens, poses critical environmental challenges. To transform this waste into value, we propose the novel TERSEG protocol–a sustainable valorization route that, for the first time, simultaneously enables ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage (TES) particle production from molten SS via centrifugal granulation and recovers its >1400 °C waste heat. By modifying molten SS with blast furnace slag (BFS) to drastically reduce its viscosity by ∼90% (to 0.23 Pa s at 1500 °C), we overcome prior barriers to granulation. The engineered particles (1-3 mm) exhibit exceptional thermal stability (<1% mass loss over 10 cycles at 400-1000 °C), good sphericity (axis ratio of 1.5), and low porosity (<4%), making them ideal TES materials. This approach recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional materials. The TES particle production scalability is demonstrated via an empirical correlation validated across broad operational conditions. This approach pioneers a sustainable valorization route that simultaneously recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional TES materials. This work provides a circular economy strategy for the steel industry, diverting slag from landfills, reducing industrial CO2 footprint, and advancing net-zero goals.

title: Unlocking the carbon reduction potential of building integrated photovoltaics beyond rooftops in an urban core considering inter building shading
abstract: Building integrated photovoltaics have substantial potential for large scale deployment in existing urban areas under climate change mitigation. However, conventional assessments often neglect inter building shading and differences among façades. This may overestimate solar resources and carbon emission reduction potential. This study develops a three-dimensional assessment framework for the urban core of Fuzhou. The framework integrates solar radiation modelling, dynamic technical and economic evaluation, and future operational carbon emission reduction. The results show that the mean shading ratio of urban building surfaces was 28.04%, and technically useable solar energy reached 3.56 × 1010 kWh. This resource could generate 5.69 × 109 kWh of annual alternating current electricity, covering about 10.11% of Fuzhou's citywide annual electricity consumption and avoiding about 3.60 × 106 tCO2 of operational carbon emissions. The technical and economic evaluation further identified rooftop deployment as the most robust option, with west façades more favorable than south façades. Long term scenario analysis also showed that technology improvement produced greater carbon reduction gains than expansion of installable area. By 2060, under the fast pathways, technology improvement and urban expansion increased the annual carbon emission reduction potential to 8.77 × 106 and 5.69 × 106 tCO2, respectively. These results show that photovoltaic deployment on building surfaces beyond rooftops offers considerable carbon emission reduction potential and can be incorporated into future urban planning to support climate change mitigation.

title: Solvothermal carbonization of waste activated sludge using deep eutectic solvents: A solvent-directed route to tunable biochar properties
abstract: The disposal of waste activated sludge (WAS) poses a persistent environmental challenge. While hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) enables sludge valorization without pre-drying, the resulting hydrochar often exhibits low carbon content, high nitrogen levels and inferior fuel properties. This study aimed to determine whether the acidity/basicity and composition of preformed DES-based media could redirect the carbonization pathways of WAS compared with conventional aqueous HTC. Unlike previous DES-assisted HTC systems, in which low-dose DESs are added to water-dominated media, the preformed DES-based media replaced the conventional bulk aqueous medium. Acidic DES showed characteristics consistent with enhanced dehydration, decarboxylation, and condensation characteristics, producing a biochar with substantially higher carbon content (21.97% vs. 9.60% for HTC), low H/C (1.57) and O/C (0.41) atomic ratios, relatively enhanced aromatic character, reduced hydrophilicity, and higher thermal stability (dominant combustion peak at 445.1 °C). In contrast, alkaline DES was associated with enhanced hydrolysis and solubilization, yielding a carbon-depleted, highly hydrophilic residue. Neutral DES exhibits intermediate behavior, producing an oxygen-enriched surface. Overall, DES chemistry produced distinct transformation pathways and tunable biochar properties relative to conventional HTC, providing insights into solvent-mediated regulation of sludge-derived carbon materials.

title: Reconfiguring urban mining: Orchestrating multi-actor E-waste supply chains for circular value recovery through an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling framework
abstract: The accelerating generation of e-waste in developing economies presents both an environmental challenge and an opportunity for circular value recovery through urban mining, yet fragmented coordination among heterogeneous formal and informal actors limits the realization of this potential. This study addresses the gap between causal diagnosis and dynamic simulation by proposing an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) framework for reconfiguring multi-actor e-waste supply chains toward enhanced circular value recovery. The framework was operationalized through ten expert panelists who validated fifteen coordination factors. DEMATEL identified causal structures and systemic influence, BWM established strategic priorities, and ABM translated these findings into agent-level behavioral rules and environmental conditions across six orchestration scenarios. The DEMATEL analysis revealed regulatory and institutional factors as primary causal drivers, with regulatory enforcement exerting the strongest systemic influence. The BWM analysis confirmed regulatory enforcement as the most strategically important factor. The ABM simulation demonstrated that combined orchestration achieved a 134.81% improvement in recovered material and a 100% collection rate, while economic incentives provided the best overall multi-metric performance. The constant recovery rate across all scenarios confirmed that improvements were driven by increased formal participation and collection throughput rather than technological efficiency, underscoring systemic coordination failures as the primary barrier to circular value recovery. The priority-causal matrix identified regulatory factors and formal-informal integration as priority intervention points offering both high causal influence and strategic importance. These findings are conditional on expert-elicited parameters and should be interpreted as exploratory simulation evidence rather than externally validated prediction. This study provides a methodological foundation for bridging causal diagnosis, strategic prioritization, and dynamic simulation in circular supply chain research, offering practical guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to unlock the value of the urban mine in developing economy contexts.

title: Evaluating Critical Raw Materials in the energy sector through an energy criticality index
abstract: The deployment of clean energy technologies to meet global decarbonization targets is driving an increase in the demand for Critical Raw Materials: for the energy sector alone, reaching net-zero emissions by 2050 requires up to a sixfold increase of these materials. Despite the growing need of evaluating material criticality of energy technologies, existing methods also based on life cycle thinking approach currently lacks a universally accepted framework that considers different aspects of “criticality.” To address this gap, the study proposes the Energy Criticality Index (ECI), a novel index developed within the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework designed particularly for the energy sector. ECI integrates supply risk, economic importance, geological reserves, import reliance and recyclability into a single dimensionless parameter. To demonstrate its applicability, two hydrogen energy technologies at different stages of technological maturity are tested: a lab-scale alkaline electrolyser cell and an industrial-scale proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell. The application to the two case studies shows that the ECI redistributes criticality: for the alkaline electrolyser, fluorspar (39%) and gallium (20%) emerge as primary hotspots, replacing the rare earth elements dominated profile (92%) of the SH2E (Sustainability assessment of Harmonized Hydrogen Energy systems) method, a criticality index used as benchmark for the same case study. For the fuel cell, gallium (44%) and tantalum (33%) are identified as dominant contributors despite their negligible mass. The index advances the state of the art by substituting annual consumption with geological reserves, introducing a vector magnitude formulation, combining supply risk and normalised economic importance. The same approach is replicable across different technologies for which a life cycle inventory is available.

title: Impact of slurry additives on nitrogen emissions, grass agronomy and soil microbial communities following slurry landspreading
abstract: This study assessed the effects of specific slurry additives on nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, grass herbage yield and N uptake and soil microbial communities. The experimental work was conducted on two soil types: i) a moderately to poorly drained fine loam and ii) an imperfectly drained clay loam over two growing seasons. Cattle slurry was applied in three split applications at both sites simulating trailing shoe application method and the treatments were control (no treatment), unamended slurry, slurry + sulphuric acid, slurry + biochar, slurry + gypsum and urea + urease inhibitor N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) (NBPT-urea). Nitrous oxide was measured during the growing period using the static chambers and dry matter yield was measured at every harvest. Ammonia (NH3) was also quantified at one of the sites, therefore NH3 responses are site-specific. Ammonia was measured within the first week of slurry application using dynamic chambers coupled with a photoacoustic gas analyser. Soil samples were collected after the end of the experiment for microbial analysis at both sites. The acidified slurry increased grass yield by more than one tonne ha−1, increased plant N recovery by 21 to 24 kg N ha−1, suggesting improved nitrogen conservation may have contributed to these agronomic benefits, and increased fungal abundance however, it also increased N2O on one occasion. The other slurry amendments did not have significant effect on N2O. The cumulative N2O emissions from the moderately drained soil were significantly lower than the imperfectly drained soil. None of the amendments significantly reduced NH3 emissions in the moderately to poorly drained soil, while biochar increased NH3 during a single application timing.

title: Hofstede cultural dimensions and sustainable development goals disclosure: Evidence from Europe
abstract: This study examines whether national culture is associated with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) disclosure among 1650 firms in 21 EU countries over 2019–2024 (9900 firm-year observations). SDG disclosure is measured as a provider-coded indicator of disclosure breadth: the share of the 17 SDGs that Refinitiv/LSEG codes as addressed in firms' reporting, while culture is captured using Hofstede's six dimensions. Pooled OLS with year and industry fixed effects is complemented by firm- and country-clustered inference, wild-cluster-bootstrap tests and multiple robustness analyses. Indulgence shows the most consistent positive association with SDG disclosure and is the only dimension that remains significant under country-clustered inference after a Holm adjustment for testing six dimensions, although not under the wild-cluster bootstrap. Masculinity is negatively associated and uncertainty avoidance positively associated under firm- and country-clustered inference, but neither survives the wild-cluster bootstrap. Power distance, individualism and long-term orientation show weaker, specification-sensitive associations. Disclosure is also highly persistent over time. The evidence is therefore suggestive rather than robust, and is consistent with persistent cultural heterogeneity in SDG disclosure under increasingly common European reporting pressures. The findings also show the importance of matching statistical inference to the country level at which cultural variables vary and caution against treating disclosure breadth as equivalent to sustainability performance.

title: Temporal feature augmentation for transient fuel consumption prediction of heavy-duty trucks: Toward sustainable road freight and cleaner operations
abstract: Transient operations substantially increase fuel consumption in heavy-duty trucks, while conventional static models fail to capture these short-term dynamics. Existing data-driven models either treat the engine-vehicle system as memoryless or rely on black-box sequence models that sacrifice interpretability. This study introduces a physics-informed, model-agnostic Temporal Feature Augmentation (TFA) framework that encodes unobserved internal states, such as turbocharger spool state, manifold filling, and thermal inertia, into compact and interpretable derivative-based proxy features computed causally from standard onboard measurements without additional hardware. TFA enriches the feature space by incorporating instantaneous temporal derivatives of measurable engine and air-path states, including the excess air coefficient λ, intake pressure, and pre-turbine pressure and temperature, which serve as compact proxies for unobserved transient dynamics. Validated on standardized CHTC-TT (1800 s) and extensive real-world cycles (5350 s) using five algorithms (RF, XGBoost, SVM, RNN, LSTM), TFA consistently enhances prediction accuracy and cross-cycle robustness: the best model achieves R2 = 0.996 and reduces RMSE by 23.4% relative to static-feature baselines. Feature-importance analysis confirms that temporal-derivative features effectively proxy load transients. The proposed framework supports eco-driving assistance, fleet fuel monitoring, and data-driven quantification of fuel-saving opportunities, contributing to low-carbon, cleaner production operations in commercial road freight.

title: Utilization of carbonyl-modified carbon nanotubes for selective removal of perfluorinated sulfonates from surface water
abstract: The simultaneous treatment addressing large-scale, low-concentration PFAS in natural waters is still a challenge due to the persistence of perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) compared to perfluorocarboxylic acid (PFCA). This study presents a breakthrough treatment for PFAS wastewater based on carbonyl multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) for selective PFSA capture. The developed MWCNTs near-completely removed perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and its substitute 6:2 chlorinated polyfluorinated ether sulfonate (F53-B) from 50 mL of surface water within 5 min from six mixed PFAS solutions with different chain lengths and functional groups, with maximum adsorption capacities of 407.3 mg g−1 and 611.9 mg g−1, respectively. The material characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that this outstanding performance arises from three synergistic mechanisms: a specific interaction between carbonyl groups and C-F bonds, enhanced electrostatic attraction, and π-π stacking interactions. These interactions enable preferential PFSA even in complex matrices containing humic acid and competing anions. The material maintains excellent stability, with complete F53-B removal sustained over five of adsorption cycles. Notably, the F53-B eluted from MWCNTs was near-completely defluorinated in UV254/sulfite system, effectively mitigating secondary pollution risks. This study provides a new approach to address the key challenges of PFSA and PFCA pollution in natural water, providing reference for the rapid separation of PFSA and the subsequent harmless treatment of residual PFCA, which protect water ecology and water resources security.

title: Continuous score-based optimization of pressure sensor placement for burst detection in water distribution networks
abstract: Pipe bursts in water distribution networks (WDNs) can cause substantial water loss and service disruption, making reliable pressure monitoring essential. However, existing event-driven methods for optimal pressure sensor placement (OSP) commonly rely on a single predefined detection threshold to distinguish burst-induced pressure residuals from background noise. This can lead to unstable optimization outcomes, multiple equivalent layouts, and degraded performance under varying noise conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a continuous score-based placement optimization (CSPO) method. Compared with commonly used threshold-based binary placement optimization (TBPO), CSPO uses a sigmoid function to map pressure residuals to continuous scores and optimizes the continuous detection score (CDS). This preserves hydraulic response magnitudes and provides a more discriminative objective for sensor placement. Results from the Hanoi and C-Town networks show that CSPO produces more stable and consistent layouts than TBPO while requiring fewer simulated burst events. It also reduces solution multiplicity and yields a single Pareto-optimal layout for each sensor count, providing a clearer basis for deployment decisions. Under cross-evaluation across multiple background noise conditions, CSPO maintains robust performance, with the mean relative performance index generally above 0.98 and the coefficient of variation below 0.02. Further results from L-Town, with pressure data and an expert-guided reference layout, show that CSPO provides a more balanced layout than the TBPO variants across threshold-based detection standards. Overall, CSPO provides a robust and practical method for pressure sensor placement, supporting the design of reliable and effective monitoring systems in WDNs.

title: Examining associations of urban green-space greenness and net primary productivity with water quality using interpretable machine learning
abstract: Urban green spaces (UGSs) are widely used to support urban water-quality improvement, and vegetation cover in many cities is becoming greener. Existing the UGS-water-quality studies have mainly focused on landscape composition and configuration, whereas the associations of the UGS greenness and net primary productivity (NPP) with water quality remain insufficiently evaluated. We analysed monitoring records of chemical oxygen demand (COD), total phosphorus (TP), ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N), and dissolved oxygen (DO) at 44 sites in the Xi'an City during wet and dry seasons and combined these observations with multi-source remote-sensing and socioeconomic data. Redundancy analysis (RDA), Geodetector, and XGBoost-PSO-SHAP-LOWESS were integrated to compare linear, spatially stratified, and nonlinear predictive associations across spatial supports and to identify approximate turning regions. The results revealed that: (1) across the monitoring network, NH3-N concentrations ranged from 0.118 to 1.802 mg/L; higher urban concentrations were spatially consistent with potential anthropogenic inputs, while water-quality indicators differed between wet and dry seasons; (2) The XGBoost-SHAP provided feature-level nonlinear interpretation complementary to RDA and Geodetector; (3) The UGS greenness and NPP were associated with water-quality variation, but meteorological and socioeconomic variables were often equally or more influential, and the direction of association differed among indicators; and (4) The SHAP-LOWESS curves indicated approximate turning regions for selected greenness and NPP indicators rather than precise causal thresholds. These findings support season- and context-specific UGS planning while emphasizing the exploratory nature of the inferred associations.

title: Sustainable artificial stone production using recycled glass waste and determining aesthetic performance
abstract: Waste generation and waste management have become critical components of environmental sustainability and successful waste management is crucial for protecting human health, conserving natural resources. The increasing generation of glass waste has created an urgent need for sustainable recycling strategies and alternative utilization methods. In this study, artificial stone composites were produced using soda-lime glass waste with different particle sizes and unsaturated polyester resin. The waste glass was first crushed and milled, and then sieved to obtain different particle size fractions. Based on the average particle size, the glass particles were classified into three groups: fine (150 μm), medium (300 μm), and coarse (600 μm). The aim of the research was to evaluate the effects of particle size on the physical, mechanical, and surface properties of artificial stones and to investigate their resistance to environmental aging conditions, including freeze–thaw, thermal shock, and salt crystallisation cycles. For this purpose, weight, porosity, water absorption, colour, and gloss were measured before and after the ageing cycles, and the changes between the two measurements were evaluated. The results indicate that particle size distribution plays a critical role in determining the microstructure and durability of artificial stones. Samples containing mixed and medium particle sizes exhibited improved particle packing and lower porosity due to better resin penetration. In contrast, coarse particle samples showed higher porosity and weaker interfacial bonding. Among the aging mechanisms, thermal shock produced the most significant deterioration, generating internal stresses at the resin–particle interface and resulting in higher weight losses. Freeze–thaw and salt crystallisation cycles mainly caused surface degradation, particularly in terms of gloss reduction. Interestingly, thermal shock led to an apparent increase in gloss in some samples due to resin redistribution and surface smoothing, although this did not correspond to improved structural integrity. The outputs of the result demonstrated that glass waste can be effectively reused in artificial stone production.

title: An interpretable decision-making model for identifying socio-environmental transition intervals in rural wastewater management pathway planning
abstract: In rural wastewater management, inappropriate pathway selection can lock settlements into over-engineered centralized facilities or underperforming decentralized systems, generating avoidable capital waste, inefficient resource use, and long-term operation burdens. This study develops an interpretable transition-interval identification framework to support cleaner production-oriented rural wastewater pathway planning. Using village-level data from 353 settlements in Guangdong Province, China, the framework combines class balancing, Random Forest classification, SHAP response mapping, rule extraction, administratively grouped cross-validation and spatial autocorrelation analysis to translate nonlinear model behavior into transparent screening rules between decentralized resource-recovery and centralized engineering pathways. Within Guangdong, five-fold administratively grouped cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.766 ± 0.146. Direct application of the frozen Guangdong model to 8595 Shandong villages yielded an AUC of 0.525, whereas Shandong-local redevelopment under nested administratively grouped cross-validation produced a mean fold-specific AUC of 0.585 ± 0.144 for the best-performing candidate model. Two prominent empirical transition intervals were identified: a permanent population of 1000–1600 residents, representing the principal scale-related transition interval, and an NH3-N pollution intensity of 3.1-3.2 kg·person−1·yr−1, representing the primary pollution-related refinement. Settlement compactness and topographic slope showed additional context-dependent associations with model-predicted pathway preference. Spatial autocorrelation analysis revealed pronounced geographic clustering of observed pathway choices (Moran's I = 0.885), with centralized engineering pathways clustering in high-density coastal plains and decentralized resource-recovery pathways prevailing in mountainous settlements. The resulting boundary system provides county-level planners with a data-derivable screening tool based on routinely available village indicators, helping reduce infrastructure-context mismatch and improve resource-efficient wastewater investment before detailed project-level design.

title: How does corporate ESG shape urban economic resilience?
abstract: Enhancing urban economic resilience is critical amid global uncertainty. Using panel data from 260 Chinese cities over 2009–2021, we construct an Urban Corporate Aggregated ESG (UESG) index by aggregating firm-level ESG ratings using firm-size weights. We examine the association between UESG and urban economic resilience and explore potential mediating channels. The results show that higher UESG is significantly associated with greater urban economic resilience. Mediation estimates are consistent with partial mediation involving external openness, green total factor productivity, and industrial structure, with estimated mediation proportions of 8.74%, 6.89%, and 11.74%, respectively. Subgroup analyses identify statistically significant positive associations in eastern regions, tier-2 cities, and non-resource-based cities. These findings link aggregate corporate ESG performance to urban economic resilience and inform discussions of urban sustainability policies suited to local conditions.

title: Synergistic Pt single atoms and nanoparticles boost atomic-hydrogen spillover at Cu2O interface for highly selective nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3RR) to ammonia (NH3) holds promise for wastewater remediation and sustainable NH3 production. However, its efficiency is often curtailed by competing hydrogen evolution (HER) and insufficient active hydrogen (*H) supply on Cu-based catalysts. We designed an electrocatalyst (PtCSA/Cu2O/NF) that features coexisting clustered platinum nanoparticles (PtC) and platinum single atoms (PtSA) anchored on Cu2O/NF to overcome these limitations via a synergistic hydrogen-spillover network. Under the potential of −0.39 V vs. RHE, this catalyst achieves complete nitrate (NO3−) removal (100%) and high ammonia (NH4+) selectivity (98.7%). In-situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support a plausible three-stage PtC/PtSA-assisted hydrogen spillover mechanism: PtC facilitates H2O dissociation to generate *H; coexisting PtSA may regulate *H adsorption and lower the barrier for hydrogen transfer; and Cu sites consume *H to promote NO3− reduction, accelerate the Cu(I)/Cu(0) redox cycle, and suppress hydrogen evolution. Furthermore, a 100% nitrogen recovery as ammonium sulfate has been achieved from nitrate-contaminated water in an integrated flow-through device. This work establishes an energy-efficient strategy for simultaneous nitrate remediation, resource recovery as green ammonia, and restoration of the disrupted anthropogenic nitrogen cycle in wastewater treatment.

title: Digital economy-driven resilience enhancement in the global food supply chain
abstract: The global food system is undergoing significant changes due to the digital economy, but the specific impact of this on the resilience of the food supply chain remains unclear. This study examines the impact of the digital economy on the resilience of food supply chains in 106 countries between 2013 and 2023. The findings show that although the digital economy is growing internationally, its development is still unequal, especially in terms of digital market and digital governance. Food trade networks are becoming more interconnected; trade in plant-based foods is more geographically diverse, while trade in animal-based foods is more closely linked. Resilience patterns reveal significant disparities, with high-income countries continuing to have a distinct edge. For animal-based food supply chains, digital technology is the main source of resilience (35.6% of total feature importance); for plant-based food supply chains, on the other hand, GDP is the most important factor (54.2%). The degree to which different digital economy factors affect resilience is determined by threshold effects. Critical levels usually fall between 36 and 74 on the digital economy index, depending on the food type and digital dimension. These results highlight the necessity of category-specific approaches to help create more resilient and sustainable global food supply chains.

title: Predictive energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles integrating operating condition recognition and condition-matched speed prediction
abstract: The substantial differences between land and water operating conditions, abrupt power-demand variations, and multi-objective optimization conflicts pose significant challenges to real-time energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles. This study proposes a coordinated predictive energy management strategy integrating online operating-condition recognition and speed prediction to improve power response, fuel economy, and battery safety. A switchable hybrid powertrain operates in series mode on land and parallel mode on water. Representative operating conditions are identified offline using kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) and K-means++ clustering, and the resulting labels are used to train a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for online recognition. A dual-path condition-dependent adaptation mechanism is established: discrete condition labels select the corresponding condition-matched variational mode decomposition–radial basis function (VMD-RBF) speed predictors, while continuous distances to cluster centers adaptively adjust the power-response and fuel-economy weights of the predictive equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS). Real-vehicle tests show that the proposed strategy reduces the mean 0–100 km/h acceleration time on land by 14.9% compared with the conventional predictive strategy, avoids the engine-overload shutdown observed in six of ten rule-based tests, and reduces the mean 0–60 km/h acceleration time on water by 9.2% compared with the rule-based strategy. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for coordinated energy management across amphibious operating domains.

title: Assessing the circular transition progress across Pakistan's textile supply chain: Empirical evidence from the field
abstract: Textile manufacturing constitutes one of the most resource-intensive industries, which faces growing pressure to shift from traditional, linear production to a circular economy (CE). Although extensive literature exists on circular business models (CBM), most studies focus on Global North country contexts, leaving a limited understanding of how firms in emerging economies implement circular practices across supply chains. The study addresses this gap and applies a novel circularity evaluation framework that integrates the Resource-Based View and the Socio-technical Transition Theory. The framework examines patterns in circular practice adoption and differences in circularity performance. Using a qualitative multiple-case study of 26 large textile firms, the research collected primary data through key informant interviews and field observations. The analysis combines thematic analysis, pattern matching, and multi-value Qualitative Comparative Analysis (mvQCA) and descriptive statistics to map R-strategies across supply chain stages and cluster firms by circular performance. Findings reveal a strong emphasis on internal operations and end-of-life solutions, characterized by lower-value strategies, e.g., recycling and recovery. Consequently, the industry exhibits uncoordinated patterns of circular practices that only partially close material loops, driven primarily by customer demand, transnational governance, and competitive pressures. Export-oriented firms show stronger performance, revealing industry polarisation. Overall, systemic CE implementation remains absent across the fragmented supply chain, constrained by limited strategic knowledge, and the lack of a national regulatory roadmap. The study's findings further hint to a need for stronger policy and management engagement towards green procurement, industrial symbiosis, reverse logistics, closer cooperation with international buyers, and inclusive national policies.

title: A physics-guided grey-box residual framework for cleaner production and energy-efficiency optimization in aluminum electrolysis
abstract: Aluminum electrolysis production is a typical high-energy-consuming continuous industrial process, and its energy consumption prediction and optimization are of great significance to industrial energy systems. To address the issues of existing data-driven models being unable to characterize the complex coupled effects within electrolytic cells, lacking sufficient analysis of spatial topological heterogeneity, and failing to provide reliable decision support, this paper proposes an integrated learning framework that combines physics-guided prediction, calibrated uncertainty assessment, and constraint-screened counterfactual optimization. A physics-enhanced feature set integrating temporal, spatial, thermal, and electrical information was constructed, and XGBoost was used as the baseline predictor. To improve predictive accuracy while retaining physical interpretability, a two-stage residual framework based on a calibrated first-order Faraday-law energy anchor was introduced. The anchor was combined with a topology-aware residual learner to capture higher-order process deviations. The 86-feature physics-guided XGBoost baseline achieved a test-set R2 of 0.821, and the enhanced Faraday-topology residual model improved this value to 0.865 with RMSE reduced to 77.9 kWh/t. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was used to identify the main influencing factors. A risk-aware prediction module and a constraint-screened counterfactual recommendation strategy were further developed for high-energy-consumption conditions. Under joint operating-feasibility, local-trust-region, and abnormal-sample-screening constraints, the optimization strategy yielded an average expected energy-saving potential of 63.0 kWh/t for 159 high-energy-consumption samples. These results suggest that physics-guided feature construction, structured residual learning, and uncertainty-informed constraint screening can improve prediction accuracy, interpretability, and decision support for aluminum electrolysis.

title: Root-associated microbial community dynamics in tobacco following topping: implications for nicotine degradation
abstract: Agricultural topping is followed by rapid nicotine synthesis in tobacco roots, which may pose environmental risks due to nicotine accumulation in soil. Microbial degradation offers a promising remediation strategy, but the temporal associations between nicotine accumulation and root-associated microbiomes remain unclear. Here, we integrated multi-omics analysis and experimental validation to characterize the post-topping temporal dynamics of tobacco root-associated microbiomes and their potential roles in nicotine degradation. Amplicon sequencing revealed distinct temporal shifts in bacterial communities in bulk soil and rhizosphere (explaining 2.84% of bacterial variance), as well as the fungal community in the root endosphere following topping. Notably, this included enrichment of key nicotine-degrading microorganisms such as Paenarthrobacter , Streptomyces , Arthrobacter , Ensifer , and Nocardioides . Metabolomic profiling showed increased levels of nicotine, its biosynthetic precursor (putrescine), and microbial degradation products (6-hydroxynicotinine and 6-hydroxy-N-methylmyosmine) following topping. Integrated microbiome-metabolome analysis highlighted strong correlations between rhizosphere bacteria and nicotine-related alkaloids, particularly with nicotine-degrading genera such as Paenarthrobacter , Streptomyces , Arthrobacter , Ensifer , and Nocardioides . High-throughput cultivation yielded 221 and 197 nicotine-utilizing bacteria from rhizosphere and root, respectively. Functional validation of five representative strains demonstrated exceptional degradation efficiency, notably in Ensifer sp. A4 and Pseudomonas sp. B11. Given the absence of matched untopped controls in the field sampling scheme, our findings should be interpreted as temporal post-topping associations rather than causal evidence of topping effects. This study provides novel insights into the ecological patterns and temporal dynamics of tobacco root-associated microbiomes following topping, highlighting the potential role of specific microbes in nicotine degradation.

title: Supporting circular economy decisions in hospitality SMEs: A multi-criteria approach to strategy prioritization
abstract: Circular economy (CE) research has mainly focused on manufacturing and product-based sectors, while its application to service industries remains less understood. In services, circularity cannot be reduced to material loops, as it involves customer participation, organizational capabilities, service routines, and stakeholder coordination. Existing studies have widely examined CE practices, drivers, and barriers, but provide fewer tools for translating these elements into decision criteria, understood here as conditions used to compare the relative actionability of alternative circular strategies. This study develops and applies a multi-criteria decision support approach to Italian hospitality SMEs. Circular practices are classified into circular strategy options, while CE drivers and barriers are operationalized as economic-financial, technological-operational, stakeholder-related, and governance criteria that may facilitate or constrain implementation. By combining survey data collected from hospitality firms, expert-derived criteria weights, and stochastic multi-criteria acceptability analysis, the results indicate that reduction-oriented strategies show the most favourable average position across the four ranking methods, while asset renewal and life extension occupy comparatively favourable positions. Rethink, repurpose, and reuse have very similar expected ranks and cannot be meaningfully ordered. The study frames CE adoption in services as a prioritization process guided by predefined criteria and offers insights for resource efficiency, waste prevention, and cleaner service operations.

title: Proteus mirabilis reshapes the gut microenvironment and enhances protein degradation and nitrogen conversion in Hermetia illucens larvae via enzyme-mediated ammonia accumulation
abstract: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) can efficiently convert high-nitrogen organic wastes such as food waste and livestock manure, and their gut symbiotic microbiota serve as the core regulator of protein degradation and nitrogen cycling. A urease-producing Proteus mirabilis strain was isolated from BSFL. In vitro assays confirmed its extracellular urease, serine protease, and phenylalanine deaminase activities, which enable ammonia production through both urea hydrolysis and amino acid deamination. In vitro co-culture assays revealed that this strain inhibits the dominant gut bacterium Klebsiella through a dual mechanism: ammonia accumulation elevates the microenvironmental pH and exerts ammonia induced cytotoxicity. Klebsiella metabolically produces acids, which can alter the microenvironment, induce protein flocculation and precipitation, and impede substrate hydrolysis. In contrast, ammonia production by Proteus mirabilis neutralizes acidity and alleviates this protein precipitation bottleneck. In vivo inoculation combined with metagenomic analysis confirmed that colonization by Proteus mirabilis reshaped the gut microbial community structure, reduced Klebsiella abundance, and enhanced the activity of metabolic pathways associated with protein degradation. Thus, Proteus mirabilis suppresses Klebsiella populations through its multiple ammonia-producing functions, modulates local gut microenvironment pH, improves protein digestion capacity in BSFL fed with high-protein organic waste, and enhances organic nitrogen conversion efficiency. These findings provide theoretical support for the application of functional microorganisms to enhance insect-mediated bioconversion of organic solid waste.

title: Green conversion of wild plant biomass into agricultural biostimulants: Fermentation dynamics and microbial associations
abstract: Despite growing interest in Agricultural Jiaosu (AJ) as a sustainable biostimulant, the use of wild plant feedstocks remains underexplored, and the underlying fermentation dynamics are poorly understood. Here, we employed Humulus scandens (HS) and Portulaca oleracea (PO) to produce AJ through a 90-day natural fermentation, systematically analyzing the multi-scale dynamics of physicochemical parameters, metabolites, microbial communities, and functions. Both AJs exhibited typical fermentation features (rapid pH decline to 3.6–3.7, organic matter degradation 40.8%–68.8%, organic acids accumulation >5 g/L and mineral release with phosphorus activation >8-fold). However, from day 15 onward, the two systems diverged along distinct temporal trajectories: HS-AJ progressively enriched amino acids and salicylic acid (903.14 μg/L), while PO-AJ accumulated high levels of oxalic acid (1846.6 mg/L) and citric acid, accompanied by a sharp drop in soluble calcium. Correspondingly, microbial communities shifted from Proteobacteria to Firmicutes (shift of ∼60%) with different assembly drivers, methionine and auxin in HS-AJ versus organic acids in PO-AJ. Functional predictions and PLSR analysis further revealed that phosphorus, salicylic acid, and lactic acid were positively associated with seedling growth rate, whereas oxalic acid and electrical conductivity correlated with seedling robustness. These divergent metabolic and microbial trajectories culminated in distinct agronomic outcomes: optimal dilutions were 100-fold for HS-AJ and 400-fold for PO-AJ, enhancing seedling vigor index by 42.3% and 17.6%, respectively, achieved comparable effects to the nutrient solution. Together, this study elucidates the cascade from feedstock chemistry to microbial function and agronomic performance (feedstock-microbe-metabolite-effect), providing a quantitative basis for the rational design of plant-derived biostimulants.

title: A framework for developing an emissions reduction roadmap for new residential buildings in urban Uganda: A demonstrative case study of detached bungalows
abstract: Considering the remaining global emissions budget is essential when regulating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the building sector, especially for emerging economies where the building stock is still undergoing rapid expansion. This study demonstrates a framework for developing an emissions reduction roadmap for detached bungalows in urban Uganda. A planetary boundary-based top-down benchmark for Uganda's housing emissions is derived. A hybrid life cycle GHG emissions assessment is conducted for a bungalow over 50 years. Context-specific emissions targets and reduction pathways are derived, forming the roadmap. The framework explores how a 71.6% emissions reduction requirement could be achieved over a 20-year period to remain below the 2°C warming threshold at an 83% risk-avoidance level. The demonstrative findings suggest that significant emissions reductions could be achieved by lowering embodied GHG emissions through sufficiency-oriented building design and low emissions-intensive construction materials and methods. Regulating dwelling stock growth and designing for optimal occupancy densities are identified as potentially important for achieving meaningful reductions. The framework highlights the importance of improving and scaling up Uganda's traditional earthen and bio-based materials to support reductions in embodied emissions. It further demonstrates the value of expressing assessment results using both floor area-based and per capita-based functional units to better account for house size in sufficiency-oriented design. The demonstrative application also highlights the importance of developing context-specific material life cycle inventory data and integrating emissions reduction strategies into Uganda's building policies to support refinement and implementation of the proposed reduction roadmap.

title: Estimating the economic and environmental impacts of critical infrastructure failure in the global natural gas industry: A case study of Nord Stream pipeline
abstract: Geopolitical tension is becoming an increasingly significant risk that threatens the safe operation of critical energy infrastructure. However, existing studies pay little attention to how infrastructure failures spill over into global gas supply chains, causing economic, environmental, and distributional effects. Drawing on granular infrastructure data, this study builds a large-scale linear optimization model to quantify the economic and environmental implications of the Nord Stream pipeline failure. First, we simulate how the global natural gas supply chain reconfigured across production, liquefaction, trade, regasification, and consumption. Then, we estimate the economic spillovers and life-cycle climate impacts resulting from this reconfiguration and its components. Finally, we compare the estimated economic impact of Nord Stream pipeline failure with other key infrastructure disruptions. Our major findings are: (1) By reshaping the supply chain, the Nord Stream failure increases the theoretical lowest global costs by 2.80 billion dollars, primarily through production misallocations. Europe bears only 20.7%, highlighting massive spillovers. (2) The Nord Stream failure results in winners and losers, with Norway benefiting most economically. (3) Economic impacts vary drastically across key infrastructures, ranging from $0.02 billion (Pyeongtaek regasification) to $25.8 billion (Groningen field). (4) Environmentally, the disruption reduces the global carbon footprint by 28.31 million tons CO2 eq, because the shift to more expensive but cleaner gas.

title: Limits to achieving high circularity in PET bottle systems: Trade-offs, policy needs, and the role of multi-route recycling
abstract: Plastic beverage bottles remain a major environmental challenge, while most circular economy (CE) studies focus on isolated recycling pathways and rarely evaluate operational interactions among multiple recycling destinations. This study proposes a multi-route PET bottle CE network integrating bottle-to-bottle recycling with bottle-to-fiber, bottle-to-sheet, bottle-to-filament, and disposal pathways under operational, market, regulatory, and collection constraints. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is combined with Taguchi-based scenario analysis and the L p -metric method to evaluate economic, energy, circularity, and manpower performance under different decision-prioritization conditions. Results show that decision-prioritization directly reshapes recycling-route allocation, where circularity-oriented strategies improve material circulation but increase cost and energy burden (over 20%) nonlinearly, particularly beyond 60% circularity. Collection rate remains the strongest driver of circularity performance, while open-loop routes complement bottle-to-bottle recycling by absorbing material flows that are economically or operationally constrained. Restricting market acceptance of bottle-to-filament recycling—the outlet receiving the largest allocation in the examined case—reduced circularity by up to 55%, demonstrating how a route-specific demand shock can alter recycling-route allocation and redirect recyclable material toward disposal. Furthermore, mandatory r P E T -content regulation alone cannot significantly expand bottle-to-bottle recycling, while combining it with tax relief improves closed-loop recycling performance by 129–200%. The findings indicate that transitioning toward high-circularity PET bottle systems depends on operational maturity, collection stability, market acceptance, and flexible interaction between closed-loop and open-loop recycling pathways.

title: A life cycle assessment of scale-environment trade-offs for distillery waste recycling in China's Baijiu industry
abstract: The sustainable valorization of Baijiu distiller's grains is often constrained by variations in processing scale. This study evaluated six circular pathways across four treatment scenarios by integrating process simulation, life cycle assessment, multi-scenario analysis, and system dynamics. Pathway performance exhibited clear scale dependence. For large-scale agglomeration processing, Route 2 (aerobic composting with nutrient return) performed best, ranking first in the large-enterprise and agglomeration scenarios, with a coefficient of variation below 12% and top selection in over 70% of Monte Carlo simulations. For small-to medium-scale independent processing, Route 5 (enhanced fermentation for rejuvenated liquor production) proved to be the most economical. The break-even capacity for on-site treatment was 30,899 t/yr in 2025; technological learning alone would raise this threshold by 22.4% by 2045. Policy simulations indicate that a carbon tax is the most effective instrument, elevating the viable threshold to 61,277–62,006 t/yr, above the large-enterprise benchmark of 52,000 t/yr; operational subsidies remain the pragmatic near-term choice. Route 6 (anaerobic digestion with nutrient return) exhibits a carbon-benefit trade-off: each 10% increase in biogas capture efficiency raises profits by approximately 2.8 USD/t and reduces life cycle GHG emissions by approximately 99 kg CO2-eq/t. All six pathways reduce global warming potential by 60-85% and 35-75% relative to landfilling and incineration, respectively. Overall, technological design outweighs processing scale in driving emission reduction, underscoring the need to match technology to scale.

title: Extended oxygenation control of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized sewage
abstract: Load fluctuations are a primary factor disrupting biofilm integrity and microbial growth in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized rural sewage. This disruption can trigger the migration of loosely attached biomass into the treated effluent, thereby impairing treatment performance. To overcome this limitation, this study explored the formation of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations and proposed an extended oxygenation (EO) strategy to regulate microbial biomass transformation. The incorporation of an EO layer enabled stable removal efficiencies of 92.7% for organic matter and 82.1% for total nitrogen (TN), with the EO layer contributing 13.2% to TN removal. In the EO layer, the biofilm extracellular polymeric substances contained a higher abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups, enabling them to intercept endogenous biomass migrating with the water flow. By utilizing the intercepted biomass, denitrifying bacteria, represented by Dechloromonas and Zoogloea, were enriched within the EO layer. Metagenomic analysis revealed that the abundance of functional genes related to reactive oxygen species synthesis and quorum sensing in microorganisms within the EO layer increased significantly. These genes regulated substance transport as well as polysaccharide and lipid metabolism, thereby compensating for the suppression of metabolic activity during substrate deprivation. The EO strategy enables microorganisms to intercept and transform endogenous contaminants into energy and material sources, thereby, ensuring their survival and pollutant removal functions under substrate deprivation and oxidative stress. This study provides valuable insights into enhancing the efficiency and stability of biofilter processes under load fluctuations.

title: AI-driven granular LCA for apparel: Quantifying product-specific GHG emissions for sustainable design and circularity
abstract: Product-specific Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) for apparel is hindered by generalized data, failing to quantify unique environmental burdens crucial for sustainable production and consumption. This study addresses this challenge by proposing and validating an automated methodology using a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to extract product-specific details (e.g., fabric composition) from unstructured User-Generated Content (UGC) on consumer-to-consumer (C2C) platforms and subsequently calculate corresponding product-specific greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The study seeks to demonstrate the significance of AI-enabled product-specific information as a tool for deriving insights into sustainable production, cleaner manufacturing, and resource efficiency. Applying this framework to 3500 apparel listings from a major C2C marketplace, our VLM demonstrated high accuracy in extracting physical attributes like garment size (92.3%) and fabric composition (81.6%). The subsequent LCA quantified an average emission of 11.9 kg-CO 2 eq/item. More importantly, by analyzing the product-related parameters required for these computations, we attempted to extract and structure data on product attributes and user behavior from unstructured UGC, enabling more effective estimation of product-specific GHG emissions. Although challenges remain in precisely inferring complex user behaviors from unstructured data, the successful granularization of material composition highlights the significant impact of material selection, providing actionable insights for sustainable eco-design and circularity. Ultimately, by significantly enhancing information transparency across the value chain, our work directly aligns with emerging global policies like the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP), fostering data-driven decision-making for cleaner production goals.

title: Three-dimensional heterogeneity andpersistence of petroleum contaminants in a deep vadose zone
abstract: Petroleum contamination in deep vadose zones at legacy pipeline leaks is often hidden, develops over decades, and can create delayed groundwater risk. However, its three-dimensional (3D) architecture, environmental associations, and long-term trajectories remain poorly quantified. Here, we investigated a representative legacy refined-oil pipeline leak site where a leakage incident occurred in 2009. We collected 374 vadose-zone soil samples across depth and combined pollution indices with 3D geostatistical interpolation to delineate the spatial patterns of benzene, ethylbenzene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH). All three contaminants exhibited pronounced 3D heterogeneity, including a persistent enrichment zone at 60-75 m and laterally localized hotspots. Machine-learning analysis revealed pollutant-specific associations: benzene with moisture and soil properties, ethylbenzene with spatial position and soil properties, and TPH with spatial position and hydraulic and pore-structure variables. Feature importance reflects relative predictive contributions rather than causal controls, supported by the good performance of the representative models. HYDRUS simulations, initiated from the sampling date, indicated that benzene remains highly mobile, with its maximum concentration reaching 10.795 mg/kg after 10 years, exceeding the screening value (4 mg/kg). Although concentrations decline over 18-30 years, benzene continues migrating downward toward the underlying aquifer. Collectively, our findings show that the deep vadose zone functions as an active regulatory compartment characterized by long-term retention and delayed release, rather than a passive barrier. This study provides quantitative evidence to support groundwater risk assessment, depth-targeted monitoring, and long-term management of legacy petroleum-contaminated sites.

title: Corrigendum to “Waste heat recovery from flue gas inside MEA-based CO2 capture processes using heat pump technologies and associated environmental impact Assessment” [J. Clean. Prod. 573, 149046, (2026)]
abstract: exclude

title: Joint decision-making for contract duration and benefit sharing in energy performance contract: A China-based shared-savings building retrofit case
abstract: Energy Performance Contract (EPC) is a pivotal market mechanism for building energy efficiency retrofits. However, challenges persist in coordinating contract duration and benefit allocation between building owners and energy service companies (ESCOs), weakening investment incentives and contractual adaptability. This study develops an integrated decision-making framework coupling contract duration determination with benefit allocation design. The framework applies a fuzzy real options model to define a flexible contract-duration domain under technological, policy, and investment uncertainty. A Stackelberg game is used to simulate the realistic leader-follower bargaining, while a modified Shapley value model refines benefit allocation by incorporating risk bearing, capital input, task complexity, and cooperation level. Application to a China-based shared-savings EPC retrofit case yielded an 8-year contract and a 71.2% ESCO benefit share, compared with the observed 7.5 years and 60.0%, respectively. A 20% increase in initial investment raised the optimized ESCO share to 81.9%, whereas a separate 20% reduction in annual energy-saving benefits raised it to 88.9%; both changes extended the duration to 10 years. The ESCO share remained within 71.0-71.3% across variations in the Stackelberg-Shapley combination weight, but ranged from 64.30% to 72.84% under alternative contribution-factor weighting structures. These results indicate that less favorable project economics require adjustments to both contractual terms under the case assumptions, while allocation outcomes depend more on contribution-weighting priorities than on the combination weight within the tested settings. Although case-specific, these findings provide a quantitative basis for coordinating investment recovery and benefit allocation, informing EPC contract design to balance between cooperation efficiency and benefit equity in building energy efficiency improvements and cleaner production.

title: Cryogenic boil-off sustainable inventory system for liquid hydrogen under insulation investment and uncertainty
abstract: Liquid hydrogen (LH2) is a central energy carrier for hard to abate sectors, but its cryogenic supply chain suffers an unavoidable evaporative loss known as boil-off (BOG) that existing operations research and hydrogen engineering literatures both treat as an exogenous efficiency loss rather than an economic decision. This paper closes that gap by reconceptualizing boil-off as endogenous, investment dependent deterioration within a sustainable economic order quantity framework whose total cost per unit time objective couples a convexly insulation-reducible boil-off rate, carbon taxed liquefaction and reliquefaction emissions, and freshness sensitive demand. Joint convexity in cycle length and insulation investment is established, first-order optimality conditions are derived, and the calibrated boil-off function is validated against published LH2 storage benchmarks spanning the industry regime of 0.1–0.5% per day. Three extensions strengthen the analysis, which are a stochastic model with random demand and heat ingress that endogenizes safety stock, a differential evolution metaheuristic, validated across 30 seeds, that confirms global optimality, and a Sobol variance-based sensitivity analysis. For a calibrated mid-sized depot, jointly optimising insulation cuts total cost by ∼1.1%, nearly halves annual boil-off losses (49%), and lowers emissions. Under uncertainty the depot rationally shortens cycles and carries a safety buffer at a value of the stochastic solution of ∼31% of expected cost, while demand scale and unit liquefaction cost jointly explain ∼97% of cost variance. The framework transfers deteriorating-inventory theory to the green hydrogen economy, giving managers a defensible basis for coordinating cryogenic storage, replenishment, and decarbonization decisions.

title: Developing a tailored reactive rejuvenation approach for aged phosphogypsum-loaded asphalt: from performance evaluation to chemical mechanism analysis
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG) is an industrial by-product that can be used as a substitute for mineral filler in asphalt mixtures, providing an effective approach for resource utilization. However, the expansion of PG upon wetting weakens the asphalt–aggregate interface, compromising the long-term stability of PG asphalt mixtures. Although PMDI modification improves the engineering performance of these mixtures, PMDI-modified PG asphalt mixtures remain susceptible to thermal-oxidative aging, and conventional physical rejuvenation methods are insufficient to fully restore their performance. In this study, a reactive rejuvenation strategy combining waste cooking oil (WCO) and PMDI was proposed to recover the performance of aged PG asphalt mastic containing PMDI (PGam). The physical properties, rheological behavior, chemical structure, and interfacial adhesion were evaluated to clarify the rejuvenation mechanism. The results showed that WCO can effectively improve the flexibility and fatigue resistance of aged PGam but deteriorate its high-temperature deformation resistance, whereas the incorporation of PMDI compensated for this deficiency while maintaining favorable fatigue resistance. Compared with WCO-rejuvenated PGam, reactive rejuvenated PGam increased the pull-off strength by 167.2 kPa before water immersion and 397.8 kPa after immersion, while improving the fracture energy retention rate by 10.0%, demonstrating enhanced moisture resistance. Furthermore, WCO mainly acted through physical rejuvenation, whereas PMDI enhanced the chemical activity of the aged asphalt phase, strengthened the interactions among asphalt components and the interfacial bonding between the asphalt phase and PG particles, thereby promoting the recovery of the rheological properties and interfacial adhesion performance of rejuvenated PGam. Overall, the proposed reactive rejuvenation method provides a promising approach for performance recovery and high-value utilization of aged PG asphalt materials.

title: Embodied carbon and energy evaluation of reinforced concrete, precast concrete, and steel hybrid systems in multistory buildings
abstract: Reducing the embodied environmental impacts of building structures is crucial for sustainable construction. In this study, a consistent life cycle assessment involving identical geometries, loads, and design assumptions was performed to compare reinforced concrete, precast concrete, and structural steel systems in a nine-story office building. A comprehensive 27-option hybrid matrix was developed by combining the validated column, beam, and slab quantities across the three systems. This enabled the systematic exploration of realistic hybrid configurations while preserving structural feasibility. The results revealed that slab type predominantly governs embodied carbon, beam type determines embodied energy, and column type balances these impacts. Steel systems reduce embodied carbon by about 50% but have higher embodied energy, whereas precast concrete offers intermediate performance. Hybrid systems, particularly those that combine steel columns, reinforced concrete beams, and precast concrete slabs, achieve up to 70% embodied carbon reduction and lower embodied energy than reinforced concrete baselines. These findings indicate that targeted member-level hybridization can substantially reduce embodied impacts and maintain structural feasibility, providing practical guidance for low-carbon multistory building design.

title: Deep eutectic solvent processing of seagrass biomass from beach wrack for sustainable polypropylene composites in large format additive manufacturing
abstract: Seagrass-rich beach wrack collected from the Bay of Cádiz (Spain) was valorized as a reinforcement for polypropylene (PP) composites manufactured by large-format additive manufacturing by fused granular fabrication (LFAM-FGF). Two delignification approaches were investigated with NaOH (SG-NaOH) and a deep eutectic solvent (DES) based on lactic acid and choline chloride (SG-DES). While SG-NaOH achieved greater lignin removal, SG-DES yielded a cellulose-rich material with higher crystallinity and a distinctive nanofibrillar morphology. When incorporated into PP at 15 wt%, untreated seagrass (SG-UT) and SG-NaOH resulted in a marked reduction in tensile strength and ductility. In contrast, composites reinforced with SG-DES exhibited a significant increase in Young's modulus while maintaining tensile strength comparable to neat PP and preserving high elongation at break. Thus, despite its lower delignification efficiency, the DES treatment produced the most effective reinforcement among the investigated formulations, highlighting that extensive lignin removal is not necessarily required to achieve high composite performance. In addition, all seagrass-filled formulations showed improved dimensional stability during LFAM-FGF printing, effectively suppressing the warping commonly observed in neat PP, enabling the fabrication of large-scale demonstrator parts which maintained their structural integrity after more than one year of outdoor exposure.

title: Upcycling whey permeate into a clean-label bio-preservative via fermentation: Metabolomic insights and application in sponge cake
abstract: Whey permeate (WP), a major cheese-processing byproduct, causes severe environmental pollution upon untreated discharge and is vastly underexploited for value-added applications. Breakthrough valorization technologies are urgently needed to reduce environmental impact and improve profitability. To address this, a waste-to-biocontrol cleaner production strategy was developed by upcycling WP into a fermentation-derived biopreservative with potential relevance to clean-label product development via Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LW11 fermentation. Results revealed that 0.5% sodium acetate likely acted as a crucial fermentation adjunct, maximizing the antifungal efficacy of the fermented WP (FWP). Untargeted metabolomics suggested that the high-lactose, nitrogen-starved WP matrix might trigger a global stress response in lactic acid bacteria, potentially redirecting metabolic fluxes toward the potent accumulation of organic acids (e.g., butyric acid) and phenolic compounds (e.g., coumarinic acid, 2-hydroxycinnamic acid, and 3-hydroxybenzoic acid), thereby likely establishing a robust multi-target antifungal network. Furthermore, the freeze-dried FWP was evaluated in a real sponge cake system. Correlation analysis revealed a complex trade-off between microbiological stability and sensory acceptance. The effect of FWP on sponge cake exhibited a significant concentration-dependent pattern: 0.1% FWP improved sensory texture but exerted limited antimicrobial activity; 0.5% FWP achieved a balance between antimicrobial efficacy (comparable to potassium sorbate) and product quality. However, 1.0% FWP induced adverse effects, including altered water distribution, elevated baking loss, excessive browning, and increased instrumental hardness, which significantly compromised overall sensory preference. This study provides proof-of-concept evidence for the potential valorization of dairy WP into an FWP-based biopreservative for bakery applications.

title: Reversal from historical gains to future losses of tropical ecosystem resilience under climate change
abstract: Understanding the dynamic evolution and driving mechanisms of tropical terrestrial ecosystem resilience represents a critical scientific priority for safeguarding global biodiversity and ecological security. This study systematically integrated remote sensing observations, TRENDY dynamic vegetation model ensembles, and Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) climate projections, using the lag-1 autocorrelation method to quantitatively assess the spatio-temporal characteristics of the resilience of tropical ecosystems in history (1982-2018) and future (2015-2100). Random forest and PCMCI causal analysis were used to explore the response mechanism of resilience to environmental changes and its time-lag effect. The results showed that: (1) Tropical ecosystem resilience exhibited a significant strengthening trend during the historical period (1982-2018; p < 0.01), with shrublands (representing unmanaged grass-shrub mosaics and natural grasslands) displaying the most rapid resilience gain among the four vegetation categories, followed by forests, croplands, and pastures. (2) Attribution analysis identifies climate change (44.0%) as the dominant driver over CO2 (34.9%) and LUCC (21.1%). Random-forest and SHAP analysis identified temperature, radiation, and precipitation as the dominant hydrothermal controls, accounting for 22.86%, 43.42%, and 17.04% of the tropical area, respectively, while root-zone and surface soil moisture exerted broadly positive effects, particularly in Africa. (3) PCMCI causal analysis demonstrates both precipitation and root zone moisture have a positive time-lag effect on resilience, while vapor pressure shows a negative lag effect. (4) Future projections (2015-2100) reveal that tropical ecosystem resilience shows a significant declining trend (p < 0.01) under SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585 scenarios—reversing the historical strengthening pattern and indicating increased vulnerability to critical transitions—while SSP370 diverges from this pattern with a slight resilience gain. Collectively, this study establishes a transferable framework for integrating observations, process-based models, climate projections, machine learning, and causal discovery to diagnose and project ecosystem resilience across the global tropics. The results provide a scientific basis for incorporating resilience-based indicators into global ecosystem monitoring, early-warning systems, climate adaptation, and biodiversity conservation planning.

title: Hydrogen-enhanced pulverized coal combustion under ultra-low load for deep peak regulation: A stability-constrained techno-economic assessment
abstract: The transition toward carbon neutrality is transforming coal-fired power plants from baseload suppliers into flexible resources for deep peak regulation. However, ultra-low-load operation of pulverized-coal boilers remains constrained by flame instability, degraded heat-transfer performance, and costly auxiliary stabilization. This study proposes a hydrogen-enhanced pulverized-coal combustion pathway and develops a techno-economic and environmental framework informed by combustion-stability boundaries for a 600 MWe supercritical unit. The framework integrates on-site alkaline water electrolysis using surplus zero- or negative-price renewable electricity, combustion-limit analysis, boiler heat-transfer modeling, full-chain economics, and carbon pricing. A key novel effort of the present study lies in embedding quantifiable combustion-stability boundaries into the techno-economic model, allowing hydrogen demand and minimum load to be evaluated under safety, performance, and economic constraints. Results show that hydrogen addition lowers coal ignition temperature and ignition energy, extending the calculated combustion stable boundary from 30% of full load to 5% of full load; the 5% load case represents a theoretical boundary close to, or already at, practical safety limits and subject to plant-specific constraints. Moderate hydrogen co-firing improves furnace temperature uniformity and heat flux distribution, maintaining boiler efficiency at about 85% at the condition of 10% of full load. The Performance Index (PI)-Economic Index (EI) evaluation identifies 20% – 30% load as the practical range, with the case of 20% of full load showing the best overall PI-EI performance. With an annual financial internal rate of return of 8%, the investment payback period is approximately 11 years. Assuming about 42 TWh, equivalent to 60% of estimated 2024 curtailed wind and solar electricity in China, is fed to on-site electrolyzers, the resulting hydrogen could support about 81% of the considered coal-fired capacity at 20% load, reducing annual CO2 emissions by 8.76 MtCO2 and standard coal consumption by 3.35 Mtce.

title: Target dependent cleaner production screening of recycling pathways for end of life electric vehicle lithium ion batteries using an interpretable machine learning framework
