abstract: Which recycling route is preferred when the decision target, proxy boundary, functional-unit scaling, and model-use domain change? This study developed an auditable, time-indexed scenario-screening framework for end-of-life electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries. The deterministic grid contains 1008 designed combinations representing structured scenarios rather than plant observations. A prespecified 168-row subset of 84 paired physical configurations supported machine-learning (ML) evaluation. Six targets include process energy; operational energy-related CO2 burden limited to grid electricity and direct diesel/natural-gas combustion; a spend-proxy-credit-adjusted screening balance; and three mapped economic indicators. The adjusted balance subtracts spend-normalized recovered-material proxies from the narrower operational burden and serves as a screening indicator within this partial boundary. Pack values provide a cross-model mass-intensity sensitivity; a full pack-level life-cycle inventory lies outside the analysis. All 12 target-basis tasks used five-fold physical-configuration-grouped evaluation. For each task, grouped and route-held-out learners were selected separately by minimum mean root-mean-square error (RMSE). For adjusted balance, grouped RMSE and coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.0816/0.99990 (cell) and 0.4561/0.99481 (pack); the corresponding lowest task-level route-held-out RMSEs were 7.0693 and 6.1501. Dependence-aware uncertainty analyses of the carbon-dioxide-equivalent (CO2e) indicators selected hydrometallurgical recycling for operational burden and direct recycling for fully credited adjusted balance under the specified screening assumptions. Removing the active-cathode spend proxy shifted the lower adjusted balance to hydrometallurgical recycling. Route preference changed across targets. The framework supports conditional screening and evidence prioritization within represented route families. Full life-cycle climate assessment requires complete inventories and verified substitution evidence. Application to a new route requires foreground data and revalidation.

title: Continuous removal of autotoxic substances through low–temperature co-thermal of biomass–continuous cropping soil: synergistic mechanism of iron minerals and organic matter
abstract: The continuous input of autotoxic substances in soil with continuous cropping obstacles makes it difficult for traditional measures such as chemical oxidation, microbial degradation, and crop rotation to balance immediate removal and long–term self purification. Although biomass contaminated soil co-thermal remediation can remove existing pollutants during the heat treatment process, there is still a lack of systematic understanding on whether the newly generated autotoxic substances and the synergistic mechanism between iron minerals and biomass–derived organic matter (OM) can be continuously removed after the soil returns to farmland after remediation. This study focuses on cucumber continuous cropping soil and corn stover, and conducts co-thermal at 200 ∼ 500 °C to investigate the sustained abiotic decay behavior of co-thermal products on p–hydroxybenzoic acid (p–HBA), benzoic acid (BA), ferulic acid (FA), and cinnamic acid (CNA). Low-temperature co-pyrolysis outperformed high-temperature co-pyrolysis and soil-only pyrolysis. S7B1–200 removed 97.41%, 97.90%, 72.52%, and 96.09% of p-HBA, BA, FA, and CNA, respectively, within 26 h. Mechanistically, biomass-derived OM compensated for the heat loss of the original OM in the soil and interacts with iron minerals, reshaping the Fe(II)/Fe(III)–OM electron cycling coupling system. Low temperature preserves high activity Fe(II) and low crystalline iron phases, while high temperature leads to an increase in crystallinity and a decrease in OM content of iron minerals. Surface Fe(II) under oxic conditions drives the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as O2•–, 1O2, and •OH, while the reducing OM promotes the dynamic cycling of Fe(II)/Fe(III). The structural state Fe(II) provides slow–release electrons. Fe(II), reducible OM, and electron shuttle structures in locally hypoxic pores promote proton coupled electron transfer to facilitate •H generation. Semiquantitative evaluation based on selective quenching inhibition rate showed that the apparent contributions of •H, O2•–, and 1O2 were 47.66%, 29.75%, and 22.59%, respectively. These results suggest that oxidative and reducing species may collectively govern the degradation of autotoxic substances, rather than a single •H pathway. This study proposes and supports a dual pathway mechanism of iron mineral OM synergistic driving sustained abiotic decay under low–temperature co-thermal, providing theoretical basis and technical path for straw resource utilization and long–term, low intervention remediation of continuous cropping obstacle soils.

title: Bio-based gelatin supramolecular microcup arrays via molecular engineering towards sustainable electrophoretic displays
abstract: Electrophoretic displays (EPDs) offer a low-power, paper-like readability under ambient light, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by slow response times and their processing needs to be more sustainable. Here, we present a molecular engineering strategy that transforms brittle biopolymer gelatin into a high-performance supramolecular platform for sustainable, flexible EPDs. Incorporation of a phosphonate-silane hybrid component (OP-KH), disrupts the native hydrogen-bonding network of gelatin and concurrently establishes ionic phosphinate-ammonium salt bridges, yielding a homogeneous, mechanically flexible, and optically transparent film. At optimal 5 wt% loading (GEL-5), the supramolecular gelatin film achieves a well-balanced profile of properties compared to pure gelatin (GEL), including a high transparency (∼90%), increased mechanical flexibility, and particularly the raised dielectric constant (20.28 vs 3.44, at 1 kHz) and a rapid white to black state switching time (800 ms vs 1730 ms, at 30 V). Leveraging these attributes, we demonstrate facile fabrication of highly uniform, freestanding film of hexagonal microcup arrays via simple water-based solution casting against a soft PDMS mold. A fully functional EPD device assembled with this film of microcups successfully displays switchable patterns, validating the practical viability of this bio-derived platform. This work establishes a sustainable paradigm that valorizes renewable biopolymers, contributing to cleaner production pathways for flexible electronics.

title: Upcycling agricultural biomass waste into sustainable carbon dots with dual-color emission for optical security applications
abstract: Upcycling agricultural biomass waste into value-added functional materials represents a promising pathway toward sustainable development. Herein, carbon quantum dots (CQDs) were fabricated from xylan that a major hemicellulose component of agricultural residues with via hydrothermal carbonization, followed by surface functional modification with histidine and tea polyphenols. The obtained X-CQDs, NX-CQDs, NX/His-CQDs, and NX/TP-CQDs exhibited well-dispersed nanoscale morphologies with average sizes of 6.44-10.13 nm. Structural analyses confirmed disordered carbon domains with abundant oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface groups. Photoluminescence was strongly temperature-dependent, and 180 °C was identified as the optimal hydrothermal temperature for achieving enhanced fluorescence emission. Compared with native xylan-derived CQDs, those derived from Nano-xylan showed enhanced UV-vis absorption, stronger fluorescence, and prolonged lifetime, indicating that precursor nanostructuring promoted more stable emissive centers. Fluorescence quantum yields reached 3.92%, 8.35%, 11.76%, and 9.18% for X-CQDs, NX-CQDs, NX/His-CQDs, and NX/TP-CQDs, respectively. Histidine modification enhanced blue emission, while tea polyphenol-assisted surface regulation induced red-shifted green emission. The CQD-based waterborne inks enabled invisible QR-code printing, handwriting encryption, and multi-substrate anti-counterfeiting under UV irradiation, offering a sustainable strategy for converting agricultural biomass into fluorescent security materials.

title: Quantitative evolution of unfixed dyes, clearing mechanism, and universality of low-pollution sulfonated polymer-assisted reduction-free clearing of disperse-dyed polyester fabrics
abstract: Eco-friendly reduction-free clearing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional reduction clearing for dyed polyester fabrics (PEFs). However, the quantitative variation of unfixed dyes during washing and underlying clearing mechanism of reduction-free clearing remains insufficiently clarified. Herein, in a reduction-free clearing system assisted with a commercial sulfonated polymer-based clearing agent, the unfixed dye evolution on the PEFs and in the residual rinse liquors at the various clearing steps were quantitatively evaluated; the aqueous dispersibility of washed dyes and the intermolecular interaction between various components were systematically analyzed to clarify the underlying clearing mechanism; PEFs dyed with high-energy, medium-energy, and low-energy blue disperse dyes, respectively, were used as model fabrics to verify the universality of reduction-free clearing. The optimal reduction-free clearing process achieved efficient removal of unfixed dyes as well as improved the color fastness of PEFs dyed with versatile disperse dyes, which could be attributed to stronger intermolecular interaction between the disperse dyes and sulfonated polymer than that between the dyes and polyester as well as the dis-agglomeration of dye aggregates into colloidally-stable dye particles, preventing them from re-depositing onto the PEFs. Compared with the reduction clearing, the reduction-free clearing process provided comparable color fastness with negligible fiber damage and significantly reduced organic pollutants and wastewater color, revealing it as an eco-friendly technology for polyester dyeing production. This work provides insights to the unfixed dye evolution and dye removal mechanism of sulfonated polymer-based reduction-free clearing, which may guide its optimization and industrial application for PEFs.

title: Life cycle assessment for disposal of polypropylene food packaging plastic waste
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) food packaging represents a substantial portion of short-lived plastic waste, imposing considerable environmental challenges at the end-of-life phase. This study employs an attributional life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate the environmental performance of three end-of-life treatment options for post-consumer polypropylene food packaging waste: landfilling, incineration, and mechanical recycling. The analysis utilises a functional unit of 1 kg of post-consumer polypropylene waste, with system limits confined to collection, transportation, treatment activities, and direct emissions. Life cycle inventory data were modelled in OpenLCA with Ecoinvent v3.x datasets, and environmental consequences were assessed employing the Environmental Footprint (EF) 3.0 midpoint technique across categories of climate change, acidification, eutrophication, particulate matter production, and ozone depletion. The findings indicate a consistent environmental hierarchy of mechanical recycling < landfilling < incineration across all evaluated impact categories. Mechanical recycling demonstrated the minimal climate change impact (1.829 kg CO2-eq kg−1 PP waste), realising an estimated 20% decrease relative to landfill disposal and significantly reduced emissions compared to incineration (2.449 kg CO2-eq kg−1). Comparable decreases were noted in acidification, eutrophication, and particulate matter generation, chiefly attributable to the mitigation of combustion-related emissions and enhanced material value retention within the technosphere. Sensitivity study further validated that elevated recycling rates are the primary determinant affecting environmental performance. The findings indicate that, from the standpoint of cleaner manufacturing and a circular economy, mechanical recycling is the most effective means of minimising the environmental impact of polypropylene packaging systems. The study illustrates the policy significance of incorporating recycling targets, Extended Producer Responsibility, and design-for-circularity initiatives into packaging waste regulation, facilitating the shift from linear disposal systems to regenerative material flows.

title: A model-driven simulation and requalification-decision framework for reuse of shelf-life-expired carbon-fibre prepregs in composite manufacturing
abstract: Circular composite manufacturing needs decision support that turns the uncertain condition of a recovered feedstock into production decisions. Shelf-life-expired carbon-fibre prepreg is a demanding case: each batch must be accepted, re-qualified under an adjusted process window, or rejected before it enters the line, and the information behind that decision is spread across organisations. This paper presents a model-based proof of concept of a simulation and requalification-decision framework. It couples an out-life degradation state model, a requalification and process-window decision layer, a mass-conserving material-flow model of eight unit operations and a first-time-right quality-risk module, and specifies the traceability service through which four partners share the records the decision needs. It is demonstrated on an Italian pilot reusing expired prepreg for drone components. The operational series and the out-life calibration data are synthetic, unit costs are illustrative and no part-level mechanical property was measured; 30 measured coupon-level requalification tests benchmark the out-life layer. Per 1000 kg of expired feedstock the reference case returns 149 kg of moulded output, 125 kg of it conforming, with the moulding conversion carried as a disclosed band of 0.21–0.79 (149–560 kg). For a proportional conversion, ratio results hold across that band: expired feedstock yields 84.0% of a virgin control, a value set by the admission rate, and a first-time-right cap reduces scrap by 40% for a 9% output loss under the stated parameters. In the measured tests, void content ordered the usability labels across four resin systems. Rising energy prices favour reuse in a directional screen.

title: Game equilibrium analysis of deposit refund systems and green design investment: A multi-stage Stackelberg model for E-waste recycling
abstract: Waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) recycling is increasingly important because of resource losses and environmental risks. Although Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) assigns post-consumer responsibility to producers, insufficient consumer-return incentives remain a key challenge in WEEE recovery. This study develops a manufacturer-led multi-stage Stackelberg game for a closed-loop WEEE supply chain and compares three scenarios: a benchmark recycling model, a market-driven deposit-refund system (DRS) model, and a DRS–green design model. The results show that DRS can stimulate consumer returns, but deposit levels must be coordinated with product pricing because excessive upfront payments may suppress market demand. Green design reduces recovery and refurbishment costs, lowers the manufacturer's reliance on high deposit incentives, and improves manufacturer and recycling-platform performance under feasible parameter conditions. Consumer environmental awareness and deposit responsiveness further reshape equilibrium pricing, recycling service fees, and collection quantities. These findings clarify how economic incentives and design-oriented circular strategies jointly affect WEEE closed-loop supply chain performance and provide implications for firms and policymakers seeking more effective WEEE recovery mechanisms.

title: Interpretable prediction of boiler NOx under load-ramping conditions using an attention-based spatio-temporal graph convolutional network
abstract: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy requires coal-fired power plants to operate more frequently under load-ramping conditions, posing significant challenges to the effective control of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions. Accurate prediction of NOx concentration during load ramping is therefore essential for low-NOx optimization of boiler operation. Under such transient conditions, boiler operating parameters exhibit complex spatial and temporal correlations that strongly influence NOx formation. However, these spatio-temporal correlations have not been comprehensively captured by existing NOx prediction models, limiting their prediction accuracy under transient operating conditions. To address this issue, an attention-based spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (AST-GCN) is proposed for boiler NOx prediction. The AST-GCN employs spatio-temporal graph convolution modules to capture the dependencies among boiler operating parameters and their temporal evolution, while spatial and temporal attention mechanisms dynamically quantify the contributions of different operating parameters and historical time steps to NOx prediction, thereby enhancing model interpretability. Applied to a 600 MW boiler, the AST-GCN achieves an MAE of 7.67 mg/Nm3, an RMSE of 9.53 mg/Nm3, and a MAPE of 2.51%. Compared with the best-performing benchmark model, the MAE is reduced by 39.22%, demonstrating the superior prediction accuracy of the proposed model. Temporal attention analysis reveals that NOx prediction relies more strongly on historical operating states during load ramping, highlighting the importance of incorporating temporal operating information under transient conditions. Spatial attention analysis further identifies the operating parameters that contribute most strongly to NOx prediction, providing interpretable information for parameter prioritization in low-NOx operational optimization.

title: Beating waste into value: Energy demand and technology of packaging paper production using post-consumer textiles
abstract: The increasing volume of post-consumer textile waste creates the necessity to develop alternative recycling pathways, beyond fibre-to-fibre applications. In this study, cellulose-rich textile waste (predominantly cotton) was mechanically processed, and the associated energy input was quantified. Textile fibres were refined at different levels of specific beating energy (SBE), fibre characteristics were investigated, and the resulting suspension was blended with industrial paper stock. Paper handsheets were produced, and the key properties were analysed. This study demonstrates that increasing SBE enhances tensile strength, short-span compression strength (SCT), density, and elastic modulus, while bending stiffness is comparatively less affected despite the associated densification and reduction in sheet thickness. Under realistic assumptions, the cumulative energy demand required to achieve industrially relevant fibre properties through refining was recorded at 748 kWh·t −1 at comparable dewatering resistance (Schopper-Riegler). This energy demand is well comparable to that of typical virgin fibre feedstocks utilised in packaging paper, such as mechanical pulp. A modelling approach demonstrated that the tensile index of fibre blends can be accurately predicted from the tensile properties of the pure components using a simple rule of mixtures approach. Furthermore, the tensile index was shown to be a suitable predictor of SCT. By combining these predictive models with the established energy benchmarks, this study provides a robust, data-driven roadmap for the industrial integration of textile waste into packaging paper production.

title: Major olive mill aqueous effluents as industrial sources of hydroxytyrosol, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol and tyrosol for circular valorisation
abstract: The selective recovery of valuable chemicals from waste streams is a central objective of Green Chemistry, particularly when waste prevention and the use of renewable feedstocks can be combined. In two-phase olive oil extraction systems, several aqueous effluents are generated that are commonly treated as waste despite their significant organic and phenolic content. In this work, four industrial effluents—olive washing water (OWW), hopper drip water (HDW), vertical centrifuge water (VCW) and oil decanting water (ODW)—were systematically characterised in six olive oil mills over two consecutive production seasons to evaluate their potential as sources of bioactive phenolic compounds. HDW exhibited the highest phenolic concentration, reaching up to 3.5 g/L, together with elevated sugar contents, identifying it as the most promising stream for the recovery of hydroxytyrosol (HT) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol (DHPG). VCW, although more diluted, was generated in the largest volumes and contained substantial amounts of both compounds, while ODW showed an unusual predominance of DHPG over HT, enabling selective recovery. An industrial chromatographic process was optimised to maximise phenolic retention and HT purity in the most concentrated streams. Based on national production data, the valorisation of these effluents could enable the recovery of up to 80 t/year of HT and 56 t/year of DHPG. Overall, this study highlights the potential of phenolic recovery to support waste valorisation strategies and facilitate subsequent wastewater management within a circular-economy framework.

title: Consumer willingness to pay and farmers’ adoption intentions for pesticide-reducing technologies in European orchards
abstract: Reducing synthetic pesticide use remains an EU sustainability objective, yet uptake of pesticide-reducing technologies remains limited in high-input orchard systems. This study examines whether information on consumer willingness to pay (WTP) for products with reduced pesticides is associated with farmers' adoption intentions. We focus on four pesticide-reducing innovations: smart mapping variable rate (VRA) application systems, robotic weeders, bio-based solutions with low sulphur and copper formulations, and cover crops. Evidence is drawn from a structured survey experiment involving 354 olive and vine growers across five European Union countries. Using a within-subject design with randomised presentation order and a Cheap Talk script to mitigate hypothetical bias, we compare farmers' adoption intentions before and after exposure to estimated consumer WTP premiums for wine and olive oil produced with reduced pesticide use. Non-parametric tests and multinomial logit models indicate that consumer WTP information is positively associated with both partial and full adoption intentions across all four technologies, with stronger associations for smart mapping VRA and robotic weeders than for bio-solutions and cover crops. Farm structure and behavioural factors, including perceived costs, subjective norms, and perceived effectiveness of existing pest management practices, exhibited technology-specific associations with adoption intentions. Although the study design does not permit causal inference, the findings suggest that consumer-driven market signals could complement existing policy approaches to support the transition towards more sustainable agricultural production.

title: Village and farm ponds differ in contaminant retention and mobility: Implications for sustainable management of rural agricultural landscapes
abstract: Pond systems are small but functionally important components of rural agricultural landscapes, where they intercept wastewater and runoff, and influence local environmental quality. However, village ponds (VPs) and farm ponds (FPs) may differ substantially in their contaminant inputs, retention behavior, and management needs. To address this gap, we conducted a cross-regional survey spanning 15 provinces and one municipality in China, focusing on the densely populated region southeast of the Hu Huanyong Line, which contains more than 93% of China's population. Paired water and sediment samples were analyzed to quantify representative emerging contaminants (ECs) at the molecular level. In addition, complementary positive matrix factorization (PMF), partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM), and a Toxicological Prioritization Index incorporating water-sediment partitioning (ToxPi-Kd) were utilized to explore the source-related chemical patterns, environmental and socioeconomic associations, and screening-level contaminant priorities. In general, VPs were more strongly associated with domestic-activity and pharmaceutical-related mixed wastewater inputs, whereas FPs showed more prominent pesticide and field-runoff patterns. Incorporating the apparent field-based water-sediment distribution coefficient (Kd) into the prioritization framework further highlighted contaminants with stronger relative sediment enrichment. Overall, these first-hand data indicate that VPs and FPs should not be treated as a single category in rural landscapes. Pond-type-specific consideration of possible input pathways and water-sediment partitioning can support more sustainable pond management and environmental quality protection.

title: Enhancing sustainability in greenhouse agriculture through chemical analysis–driven characterization of boiler biogas fuel strategies
abstract: Greenhouses can enhance sustainability and productivity by integrating renewable energy and CO 2 enrichment, which improves photosynthesis and reduces environmental impact. However, existing studies on biogas and methane combustion have not addressed how combustion-derived CO 2 can be strategically managed to meet the coupled thermal and photosynthetic demands of greenhouse crops. In this context, the present study is the first to conduct a parametric analysis of biogas utilization for greenhouse applications, offering a proposed adaptive fuel management strategy hypothesized to support both environmental and economic benefits. To achieve this, a counterflow flame configuration is employed to investigate the combustion characteristics of a greenhouse boiler operating with various methane–biogas fuel mixtures. The detailed Gas Research Institute Mechanism (GRI-Mech 3.0), comprising 53 species and 325 reactions, is utilized to model the reaction kinetics. Detailed thermophysical and transport properties based on fundamental thermodynamics are integrated to accurately capture flame structure and species transport. The model was validated against experimental methane/air flame data, demonstrating good agreement and confirming its predictive accuracy. The effects of (1) CO 2 enrichment, (2) operating pressure, and (3) strain rate on flame temperature and species concentrations (CO 2 , CO, NO, and NO 2 ) are systematically investigated. Findings demonstrate the potential of biogas as a sustainable fuel under characterized conditions: Biogas substitution lowers peak in-flame NO x and CO concentrations while increasing peak CO 2 concentration, highlighting its potential for CO 2 enrichment. A pressure-sensitivity analysis (1–10 atm) and a proposed adaptive diurnal fuel-switching strategy are also presented. Practical guidelines are proposed to support greenhouse growers in enhancing thermal efficiency and environmental performance.

title: Mine planning for responsible resource development: Integrated economic and sustainability-aware block valuation for open-pit to underground transition
abstract: Mine planning involves high-stakes decisions under geological, economic, operational, and sustainability-related uncertainties. Conventional optimization frameworks rely on simplified block economic value (BEV) models that omit geomechanical variability, metallurgical responses, multi-element contributions, and environmental and social externalities. This paper introduces the Comprehensive Net Block Value (CNBV) framework, which extends conventional block economic valuation through a comprehensive representation of block value. CNBV extends the conventional BEV formulation through five value-modifying modules: (i) a Rock Cost Index (RCI) for cost scaling based on material properties; (ii) an Extra Substance Impact Coefficient (ESIC) capturing recovery penalties from undesirable material content; (iii) penalty functions for deleterious elements under different mining and processing pathways; (iv) generalized by-product and co-product contributions; and (v) monetized environmental and social costs. The framework is applied to the transition from open-pit to block caving by extending the model of Badakhshan et al. (2024) and demonstrated on a large-scale copper deposit. The CNBV model identifies an optimal transition at 725 m, with a 22-year mine life, extracting 510 Mt at 0.50% grade, a stripping ratio of 1.22, and an NPV of USD 6.80 billion. In contrast, the BEV model suggests a deeper transition at 887.5 m, a higher stripping ratio of 1.64, a lower grade of 0.46%, and a higher NPV of USD 7.51 billion. The 162.5 m difference demonstrates the influence of incorporating additional value-modifying factors into block valuation. Sensitivity analysis shows that cost scaling and multi-element contributions most influence NPV, while environmental and social costs gain importance under stricter regulations.

title: One-pot maleic-acid-pretreated lignocellulose nanofibrils for UV-shielding and high-haze films
abstract: Lignocellulose nanofibrils (LCNFs) combine the mechanical advantages of nanocellulose with the optical functionality of residual lignin, but the compact lignocellulosic matrix restricts efficient nanofibrillation and controlled film-property regulation. Herein, a one-pot maleic acid pretreatment coupled with high-pressure microfluidization was used to produce carboxyl-rich LCNFs and high-haze, UV-shielding films from birch wood. Pretreatment simultaneously deconstructed the matrix and introduced surface carboxyl groups, yielding LCNFs with a carboxyl content of 0.331 mmol g−1. The resulting enhancement in fiber hydration and interfibrillar electrostatic repulsion promoted the formation of stable dispersions. Residual lignin showed a relative β-O-4 abundance of 54.4%, suggesting the preservation of a comparatively uncondensed framework with the potential to support interfacial binding during film consolidation. The MA = 60%, 60 min film combined a tensile strength of 53.24 MPa with a haze of 80.23%, UV-A blocking of 88.16%, and nearly complete UV-B and UV-C blocking. These optical properties were attributed to UV absorption by aromatic lignin structures and diffuse light scattering within the heterogeneous fibrillar network. Consistent with this optical performance, the films also delayed the photodegradation of representative photosensitive compounds. This work establishes a process–structure–property framework for producing biomass-derived films with strong UV shielding and high haze.

title: Sustainable electro-osmotic dewatering and stabilization of Cu- or Zn-contaminated dredged sludge with sodium alginate and calcium chloride
abstract: High-water-content dredged sludge contaminated with heavy metals is difficult to reuse because dewatering, mechanical upgrading and contaminant control must be considered together. This study evaluated sodium alginate (SA)- and SA/CaCl2-assisted electro-osmosis as a laboratory-scale process for the dewatering, strengthening and stabilization of Cu- or Zn-contaminated sludge. Eight treatment conditions, each represented by one electro-osmotic model test, were evaluated through electrical response, drainage, water content, bearing capacity, leaching behavior and microstructure. Because the C and Z series differed simultaneously in contaminant species, initial concentration and potential gradient, additive effects were interpreted primarily from comparisons within each series. In Z2 (1.0% SA), the five-zone mean water content decreased from 45.00% to 22.47% after 36 h, i.e., by 22.53 percentage points (50.07% relative reduction), and the mean bearing capacity was 11.5 times that of Z0; its quasi-steady energy coefficient was 0.169 W h/mL. CaCl2 increased early current but did not produce a proportional increase in drainage, particularly in Z3. SEM showed particle aggregation and surface deposits, but their bonding states and phase compositions were not identified. Leaching tests indicated that metal retention was conditional and pH-sensitive. Overall, SA-assisted electro-osmosis showed potential for simultaneously improving dewatering and mechanical performance of heavy-metal-contaminated dredged sludge, while the effects of CaCl2 depended on the treatment condition. The results also suggest that additive dosage and delivery strategy should be further optimized with consideration of energy consumption, metal retention and collected-water management.

title: Regional carbon price dispersion and national market linkages in China
abstract: China's national emissions trading system began trading alongside regional pilots in July 2021. This study distinguishes cross-pilot dispersion from short-run transmission and long-run relations with the national allowance price. CSMAR daily summaries from August 2013 to September 2026 are aggregated into weekly volume-weighted prices without price filling. The fixed Beijing–Shanghai–Guangdong–Hubei sample contains 423 common weeks. The July-only model estimates an SD level change of −0.271 and a subsequent positive trend change whose precision depends on HAC bandwidth and multiplicity adjustment. Reopening is therefore imprecisely estimated, not ruled out. Both phases depend on composition: adding Shenzhen leaves the level contraction but changes the SD and mean-gap trends to negative; omitting Beijing weakens the initial contraction, omitting Hubei attenuates reopening, and omitting Guangdong strengthens it. The February–July specification reallocates the estimated changes across milestones separated by only four common observations. None of 40 directional return tests rejects after Holm correction, although the national-to-Hubei one-week association is positive before correction. Guangdong supports cointegration in a 54-week uninterrupted calendar segment but not in its longer auxiliary trading-week segment. Hubei and Shenzhen also provide qualified long-run evidence. These findings indicate heterogeneous and sample-dependent linkages, rather than a uniform convergence-and-reversal process or an absence of integration. All segmented estimates are temporal associations: they cannot distinguish national trading from the preceding regulation and power-sector handover, post-pandemic domestic shocks, local pilot reforms, or compliance-cycle trading, and they identify neither a causal launch effect nor firm-level cleaner-production gains.

title: Greenhouse gas emission regime transitions in four middle eastern countries: A system dynamics-informed causal loop analysis
abstract: Greenhouse gas emission trajectories in the Middle East are characterized by complex, nonlinear dynamics that challenge conventional climate policy frameworks. This study combines sequential regime transition detection with a system dynamics perspective to identify greenhouse gas emission regime transitions and examine the conceptual feedback structures associated with observed CO2 and CH4 emission trajectories across four strategically important Middle Eastern countries: Iran, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and Turkey. The novelty of this work lies in integrating sequential regime transition detection with system dynamics-informed causal loop analysis, providing the first multi-country identification of statistically robust CO2 and CH4 regime transitions in the region and revealing exclusively positive methane regime transitions across all countries. This integration allows the study to link statistically detected transition timing with theoretically grounded causal mechanisms, revealing why transitions occur rather than only when they occur. This combined perspective provides insights that neither statistical regime detection nor qualitative system-dynamics analysis could produce independently. Emission time series were normalized using a multiplicative detrending approach to isolate structural deviations from long-term trends. Regime transitions were identified using sequential regime transition detection, complemented by conceptual causal loop diagrams (CLDs) to represent the feedback structures associated with the observed transition patterns. The analysis revealed three distinct development pathways. Iran exhibited sustained positive CO2 regime transitions, with mean emissions increasing from 3.68 to 7.26 tCO2 capita−1 following the 1999 transition, while Turkey exhibited sustained positive CH4 regime transitions, with emissions increasing from 30.13 % to 143.51 % relative to 1990 levels after the 2011 transition. Saudi Arabia maintained a persistently high-emission regime despite a modest decline in CO2 emissions. In contrast, the UAE exhibited a negative CO2 regime transition, with mean emissions decreasing from 45.45 to 24.27 tCO2 capita−1 during a period of economic diversification and energy policy reform. Conceptual causal loop analysis highlighted three feedback structures: reinforcing economic-energy coupling loops, balancing policy intervention loops, and resource-technology feedbacks, providing a systems-based interpretation of the observed transition patterns. Consistently positive CH4 regime transitions across all four countries suggest persistent challenges for regional methane mitigation. Overall, the findings indicate that addressing threshold-driven emission dynamics may require policy interventions that account for system feedbacks and nonlinear transitions rather than relying solely on linear policy instruments.

title: Legal-institutional inertia in circular electrification: Evidence from Swedish heavy-duty and off-road machinery
abstract: Electrifying heavy-duty and off-road machinery can cut operational emissions, but cleaner-production gains depend on circular battery and component flows, interoperable charging and useable data. Transition research explains policy mixes and socio-technical lock-in but often treats law as an external context. We ask which legal domains enable or obstruct circular electrification, how they create system inertia, and which legal design principles can reduce it. The study combines 29 semi-structured expert interviews in Sweden with hybrid thematic analysis and targeted doctrinal analysis of relevant EU and Swedish law. Eight connected domains emerge, spanning regulatory direction, permitting producer responsibility and product–waste status, standards, data governance, finance, contracts and procurement, and regulatory experimentation. Across them, ambiguity, fragmented authority and legacy-rule misfit increase coordination and transaction costs, delay decisions, shift risk to early movers and favour incumbent-led reconfiguration over more disruptive circular models. The central contribution is to specify legal-institutional inertia as a cross-domain regime mechanism that selects both transition pathway and actors. Connecting the multi-level perspective with institutional environmental governance and product-chain management, the paper derives a coordinated policy mix based on stable long-term direction, modular implementation, interoperability, proportional responsibility and experiments linked to scaling. Cleaner production policy must therefore align legal interfaces across the product chain, not only remove isolated barriers.

title: Operationalizing No Net Loss of biodiversity in tropical mining: A ten-step decision framework
abstract: The expansion of mining into tropical regions rich in strategic minerals and biodiversity creates a recurring implementation challenge: how to implement credible No Net Loss of biodiversity (NNL) outcomes where baseline data are limited, ecological trajectories are uncertain, offset options are constrained, and governance capacity is uneven. The Impact Mitigation Hierarchy has emerged as an important framework for structuring NNL commitments through avoidance, minimization, repair, and offsets. Yet, despite growing commitments from governments, industry, and financial institutions, translating NNL into operational practice remains particularly difficult in tropical mining contexts. In response, this White Paper provides decision-oriented guidance for implementing NNL, organized along the Mitigation Hierarchy. We identify key operational barriers, including data scarcity, fragile governance, ecological constraints, and uncertainty in demonstrating equivalence, additionality, and permanence. Building on these challenges, we develop a ten-step operational framework that links baseline design, counterfactual modelling, avoidance and minimization, rehabilitation, advanced offset timing, biodiversity metrics, long-term monitoring, and adaptive governance to support more credible, feasible, and transparent implementation of NNL. By translating NNL principles into an operational decision framework spanning the entire Mitigation Hierarchy, this White Paper provides practical guidance for implementing scientifically robust, transparent, and adaptive biodiversity management in tropical mining landscapes, thereby strengthening the credibility of No Net Loss assessments and supporting more effective conservation outcomes.

title: Centralized versus conventional anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge: An environmental and economic assessment
abstract: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. This work develops a modelling framework to compare centralized HSAD and decentralized LSAD through a coupled life cycle assessment (LCA) and economic analysis approach, supporting case-specific decision-making for sludge management under defined local boundary conditions. Four different sub-scenarios were modeled for both HSAD (S1.1-S1.4) and LSAD (S2.1-S2.4), forecasting different biogas uses, alternative sludge transportation routes, digestate valorization pathways, and ammonia extraction. The sub-scenarios were compared with the respective baselines (S1.0 for HSAD and S2.0 for LSAD), corresponding to full-scale Italian plant configurations. Under the investigated full-scale conditions, HSAD showed lower environmental impacts than conventional LSAD when transport distances were limited, due to higher credits generated by biogas and the avoided mineral fertilizer use in agriculture. However, input sludge/digestate transportation is a dominant driver of both environmental and economic impacts. Moreover, biogas upgrading to biomethane is environmentally preferable to electricity generation, but economically unfavourable at current market conditions. Overall, centralized HSAD can represent a favorable solution under regional-scale planning when logistics, digestate valorization, and gate-fee conditions are suitable, whereas optimized LSAD with dynamic sludge thickening can achieve comparable performance. Although the specific results are related to an Italian case study, this work provides a useful tool for decision-making among alternative sludge management solutions when local boundary conditions (sludge characteristics, transportation distances, HSAD/LSAD plant availability) are specified.

title: Assessment of carbon emissions and life cycle cost in railway infrastructure: comparison between steel slag ballast and natural aggregate
authors: Kathleen Dall Bello de Souza Risson
abstract: This paper evaluates the use of steel slag aggregates (SSA) as ballast for railways, from environmental and financial perspectives. The environmental assessment employs the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology framework to compare steel slag ballast (SSB) with natural aggregate ballast. The study focuses on the Global Warming Potential (GWP) impact category (also known as carbon footprint), measured in kg of CO 2 equivalent. The study considers a functional unit of 1 km of railway track over an 8-year reference service period, from a case study in the Southeast region of Brazil. The CO 2 uptake through the natural carbonation of the SSA was obtained through thermogravimetric analysis, resulting in an estimated uptake of 17.7 kg CO 2 /t SSA under the conditions considered, a value that was incorporated into the assessment. In addition to the environmental assessment, a Life Cycle Cost (LCC) analysis was conducted to evaluate the economic performance of the railway ballast alternatives over their life cycle. Within the defined system boundaries, the results showed that the railway with steel slag ballast showed a lower GWP than conventional ballast, primarily due to the estimated CO 2 uptake during natural carbonation. For the same 8-year reference service period, we calculated −4.82E+04 kgCO 2 e for the SSB (thus absorbing CO 2 ) and 1.30E+04 kgCO 2 e for the conventional ballast. A sensitivity analysis indicated that the SSB maintains its environmental advantage even with transportation distances of up to 470 km. From a financial standpoint, the LCC of the railway with SSB was 32% lower than that of conventional ballast. The study confirms the potential of SSB as an environmental and financial alternative for railway ballast, given the premises adopted in this research.

title: Exploring the potential and limits of non-profit-maximising business models in transformative change: Insights from Italian fashion small and medium enterprises
abstract: Transformative change in production and consumption systems is required to address intertwined socio-ecological crises. While businesses are key actors in this process, the relationship between organisational transformation and broader change remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how non-profit-maximising business models seek to contribute to transformative change and the constraints they face by analysing three Italian small and medium fashion enterprises. Drawing on sufficiency- and degrowth-oriented scholarship, we develop an extended business model canvas that conceptualises business models as potential boundary-spanning interfaces and uses selected business model dimensions to trace connections between organisational practices, value chain interactions, and broader structural conditions. Our findings show that firms implement a range of sustainability-oriented organisational changes, including durable and circular product strategies, reduced production volumes, territorially embedded supply chains, and initiatives promoting sufficient consumption and fair labour practices. These changes are accompanied by relational dynamics with consumers, suppliers, and networks, through which firms seek to influence production and consumption patterns and cultural norms beyond their organisational boundaries. However, these contributions remain partial and contingent. Bottom-up, market-based strategies face structural limitations, including constrained market power, rebound effects, and limited engagement with policy and collective actors. As a result, whether firm-level transformations contribute to broader socio-economic outcomes remains uncertain. Business-led initiatives may play a role in transformative change but are unlikely to be sufficient in isolation. We suggest that broader policy interventions and collective action to phase out unsustainable practices and define market limits are critical to address the structural drivers of socio-ecological unsustainability.

title: From risk governance to management efficiency: Trade-offs and synergies in the “Health-Failure-Management” of Urban Sewage Recycling System
abstract: Urban Sewage Recycling System (USRS) face operational risks and resource misallocation during rapid urbanization. Their sustainable operation depends on the trade-offs and synergies among health (HE), failure consequences (FA), and management (MA). This study developed evaluation systems for HE, FA, and MA, applying AHP-CRITIC game-theoretic weighting and fuzzy mathematics for sub-district quantification. Geographically Weighted Regression revealed synergies between HE-FA (64.1%) and MA-FA (71.7%), indicating that areas with high failure consequences require stronger health and management. In contrast, a trade-off relationship characterized HE and MA (67.1%), reflecting a reverse regulatory mechanism between infrastructure condition and management input. A dual mechanism identifying “relationship imbalance” and “weak constraint capacity” pinpointed 18 priority sub-districts for intervention. The evaluation model developed here has potential transferability, providing a transferable template for optimizing resource allocation and supporting refined USRS management in other cities.

title: Shifting from unilateral defense to collaborative governance by decoding spatially asymmetric risks of transboundary forest and grassland fires
abstract: Wildfire spread is not constrained by administrative borders, yet its assessment and management remain largely organized within national jurisdictions. This mismatch limits understanding of how connected fuels, seasonal fire conditions, and differences in management capacity jointly shape asymmetric risks across borders. We developed an integrated spatial–seasonal and explainable machine-learning framework to assess MODIS-detectable fire activity along the China–Russia, China–Mongolia, China–North Korea, and China–Kazakhstan borders from 2001 to 2024. MODIS Collection 6.1 active-fire records were integrated with vegetation, topographic, accessibility, socioeconomic, and land-cover variables. Spatial point-pattern analysis and Optimized Hot Spot Analysis were used to identify clustering scales and significant concentrations of historical fire activity, while seasonal association analysis, XGBoost, and SHAP were used to characterize seasonal fire regimes, model relative fire susceptibility, and interpret nonlinear predictor associations. Model robustness was evaluated using conventional random splitting and nested 100-km spatial block cross-validation, complemented by block-size sensitivity analysis, empirical spatial-dependence diagnostics, and MODIS observation-quality screening of background samples. The results reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity and asymmetric cross-border patterns of fire activity and susceptibility. The China–Russia border had the highest fire activity and the broadest clustering extent, with significant clustering persisting throughout the evaluated range up to approximately 200 km and forming a continuous high-susceptibility corridor. The China–Mongolia border showed a distinct spring–autumn bimodal pattern associated with continuous grassland fuels and seasonal dryness, whereas the China–North Korea border exhibited a narrow April peak linked to low vegetation moisture before green-up. In contrast, fire activity along the China–Kazakhstan border was concentrated in summer, while high relative susceptibility was spatially confined to lower-elevation valleys and foothill corridors. SHAP analysis showed that predicted fire susceptibility was associated with nonlinear interactions among vegetation moisture, fuel condition, topography, accessibility, and socioeconomic context. Socioeconomic indicators generally correlated negatively with predicted fire susceptibility, though the strength and form of these relationships varied across border regions depending on local fuel, terrain, and seasonal conditions. Nested spatial block validation yielded more conservative performance estimates than random splitting; nevertheless, sensitivity tests across multiple block sizes and MODIS background-observation filters confirmed that regional discrimination patterns remained robust. These findings suggest that transboundary fire governance should move beyond uniform unilateral defense toward spatially differentiated coordination, including corridor-scale monitoring along the China–Russia and China–Mongolia borders, valley-focused preparedness along the China–Kazakhstan border, and targeted spring management along the China–North Korea border.

title: Annual economic and environmental assessment of an optimized PVT/ASHP–WSHP system incorporating ASHP frosting–defrosting and WSHP start–stop models
abstract: Frosting and frequent defrosting degrade air-source heat pump (ASHP) performance in cold, humid conditions, while nighttime thermal storage can destabilize the heat source of water-source heat pumps (WSHPs). This study proposes a photovoltaic–thermal (PVT)/ASHP–WSHP cascade hybrid energy system for retrofitting an existing building in Tianjin, China. A dynamic model incorporating ASHP frosting–defrosting and WSHP start-up transients is developed to evaluate a hybrid series–parallel PVT heat-supplementation strategy. System capacity is subsequently optimized using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II), followed by techno-economic and environmental assessments. Results show that staggered off-peak WSHP start-up extends stable operating time by approximately 11.4%, while PVT heat supplementation improves system COP by approximately 10% under low-temperature, high-irradiance conditions and remains effective at lower irradiance in hybrid mode. Compared with the ASHP–TESS reference, the optimized system reduces net annual operating costs by 28.44%, with a simple payback period of 6.27 years under the assumed tariff, subsidy, and cost conditions. Removing PVT subsidies and electricity export revenue extends the payback period to 11.66 years, while all 200 Monte Carlo scenarios retain positive savings within the assumed uncertainty ranges. These findings provide a methodological basis for the integrated design and optimization of hybrid heat-pump systems, supporting informed building retrofit decisions that balance technical performance, economic feasibility, and environmental impacts.

title: Bioinspired multiscale leaf-vein sensor with rigid island/soft matrix architecture for multimodal sensing
abstract: Inspired by the multiscale architecture of natural leaf venation, we developed a bioinspired electronic skin sensor, denoted LPCP, that integrates pressure, temperature, humidity, and NH3 sensing in a single platform. A polypyrrole (PPy)-coated leaf-vein framework was constructed by in situ vapor-phase polymerization and combined with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), forming a skin-inspired rigid-island/soft-matrix architecture. The hierarchical framework provides conductive pathways, while the PVA/CNC matrix reinforces the spaces between veins. LPCP exhibited main-vein conductivity of 7.81 S m−1, resolved temperature changes of 0.1 °C, and responded to NH3 over 10–100 ppm. The humidity response followed two fitted regimes, with sensitivities of −0.686 and −2.019% (% RH)−1 over relative humidity (RH) ranges of 20–55% and 55–85%, respectively. Conductivity changed by less than 2% after four months of storage. Temperature and humidity responses remained stable under the tested pressures, and handwriting classification achieved an accuracy of 95.3%. Integration with wireless acquisition and a robotic hand demonstrated contact-temperature sensing and signal display. This work presents a leaf-vein-based material architecture for flexible multimodal sensing and human–machine interaction.

title: Cleaner and resource-efficient copper recovery in industrial electrowinning through explainable safe reinforcement learning
abstract: Industrial copper electrowinning for electrolyte purification must coordinate copper recovery, arsenic retention in solution, electricity use, profitability, and process safety across operating configurations. This study develops an explainable safe reinforcement learning framework for constrained multi-objective optimization (ESRL-CMO). Using 1978 plant records, nine condition-specific ExtraTrees models predict outlet copper and arsenic concentrations and system voltage. Shapley-based and partial dependence analyses inform process interpretation, while a preference-conditioned policy trained by proximal policy optimization with Lagrangian constraints coordinates four objectives and five constraints within the surrogate environment. Training is performed offline, and candidate recommendations are intended for operator review. Random-holdout R2 values were 0.83-0.90; a separate chronological evaluation identified sensitivity to changing production regimes. ESRL-CMO achieved higher hypervolume and lower Spacing than the reference vector guided evolutionary algorithm (RVEA) under all three configurations. Under Condition 2, predicted batch electricity consumption was 43.1% lower than Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) at inlet copper concentrations of 50-55 g/L. With batch electricity consumption capped at 2579 kWh, predicted net profit was 90.3% higher than historical operation. In simulated feed-disturbance tests, fixed-policy re-inference retained feasibility rates of 0.990-1.000 and reduced electricity consumption by 5.1-6.9% relative to static NSGA-II recommendations. The framework supports lower energy demand, reduced copper losses to arsenic-bearing residues, and safer electrochemical production.

title: Environmental, circularity, and criticality assessment of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries: Implications for management strategies in Mexico
abstract: Mexico's rapid growth in battery electric vehicle (BEV) adoption has not been accompanied by a regulatory framework for the end-of-life management of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), creating environmental risks and limiting the recovery of strategic materials. This study evaluates four end-of-life management strategies for BEV LIBs in Mexico (controlled disposal, hydrometallurgical recycling, pyrometallurgical recycling, and repurposing) using an integrated framework that combines Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI), and a criticality-weighted extension (MCI-c). The proposed MCI-c incorporates material criticality into the circularity assessment, allowing resource recovery to be evaluated not only in terms of material recirculation but also considering the strategic importance of recovered materials. Repurposing achieved the best overall environmental and circularity performance, while hydrometallurgical recycling consistently outperformed pyrometallurgical recycling among recycling alternatives. Incorporating criticality into the assessment altered the prioritization of management strategies under increasing lithium criticality, demonstrating that criticality can influence end-of-life management priorities. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental performance, material circularity, and criticality into the evaluation of end-of-life LIBs management strategies. For Mexico, they support the development of a dedicated regulatory framework that prioritizes higher-value recovery strategies and incorporates criticality into end-of-life decision-making. More broadly, the proposed framework provides a practical approach for evaluating end-of-life LIBs management in countries facing similar challenges in battery circularity and critical material supply.

title: A standardized energy performance certification framework for underground metro stations: Methodology development, seven-grade energy rating and energy-saving retrofit potential
abstract: With the expansion of global metro networks, improving energy efficiency in underground metro stations (UMSs) has become a critical sustainability priority. Existing research on energy modelling and energy-saving strategies establishes a solid foundation for UMS energy performance analysis. Nevertheless, the complex operating conditions and unique energy consumption profiles of UMSs have created a critical gap in systematic, standardized Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) methodologies, hindering the low-carbon transition of UMSs. This study addresses this gap by proposing a dedicated quantitative EPC methodological framework integrating standards, on-site measurements and calibrated simulations to establish baseline, benchmark and leading models. Following a comparative evaluation of rating approaches, a seven-grade energy use intensity rating system is adopted as the core rating scheme, supported by basic, prescribed and optional assessment items for comprehensive evaluation. Feasibility of the framework is demonstrated via a case study in Beijing, China: the station's annual energy use intensity is 238.43 kWh/(m2·a) (Grade E), failing benchmark requirements with cooling and lighting as primary energy consumers. Three priority energy efficiency measures upgrade the grade to D individually, with indoor air temperature elevation showing the largest energy-saving potential; simultaneous implementation reduces energy use intensity to 164.69 kWh/(m2·a), matching the leading value and achieving 882.93 MWh annual energy saving. The proposed framework provides a methodological reference for standardized UMS energy rating, supporting benchmarking, compliance assessment and energy-saving retrofit practice for urban rail transit energy management.

title: Between symbols and substance: Voluntary impact reporting of funds
abstract: Impact investing has emerged as a prominent investment approach to addressing social and environmental challenges while generating financial returns. Given its dual mandate to generate impact and financial returns, impact investing faces heightened pressures on its legitimacy, making transparent impact reporting essential to counter allegations of impact-washing and to safeguard the credibility of the approach. Despite the growing relevance of impact reporting, little is known about the underlying motivations and reporting strategies of fund managers who voluntarily publish impact reports. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the paper investigates the motivations and reporting strategies behind voluntary impact reporting by fund managers using a sequential exploratory design. First, 13 semi-structured interviews with impact-reporting professionals were analyzed following Grounded Theory principles. Second, a qualitative content analysis of 141 publicly available impact reports was conducted to analyze how reporting strategies are implemented in practice. The findings of the interviews reveal that fund managers’ motivations are driven by a need to show the alignment of profit with purpose, move beyond institutional compliance, and foster impact reflexivity. These motivations are operationalized through six reporting strategies: rationalization, contextualization, verification, institutionalization, participation, and transformation, which cluster around the dimensions of justification, integration, and adaptation. The content analysis assesses the potential for more substantive forms of legitimation in individual reporting elements. The paper contributes to legitimacy theory in the context of reporting by demonstrating that reporting strategies are interdependent and to practice by offering practitioners and standard setters a starting point for critically reflecting on the design of impact reporting.

title: Uncertainty-aware probabilistic dynamics and trust-guided model-based hierarchical reinforcement learning for combustion performance improvement and carbon emission reduction
abstract: Achieving simultaneous thermal efficiency enhancement and emission reduction requires addressing highly nonlinear, multivariable, and time-delayed combustion dynamics while ensuring operational safety. This study proposes an uncertainty-aware model-based hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous combustion–emission control. A probabilistic dynamic surrogate model is developed to characterize the coupled temporal evolution of combustion temperature, flame height, flame volume, and carbon emissions, while providing calibrated uncertainty estimates through mixture Student's t-distributions. Based on this surrogate environment, a trust-guided counterfactual planning mechanism evaluates candidate sub-goals using both predicted performance and uncertainty, enabling risk-aware exploration without direct interaction with the physical system. The hierarchical architecture integrates a strategic manager, five tactical workers, and a meta-supervisor to coordinate long-horizon decarbonization with fine-grained combustion control. Validation across progressive curriculum stages demonstrates stable learning behavior under coupled combustion–emission dynamics. The probabilistic surrogate achieves high predictive fidelity, providing a consistent environment for policy learning. Under uncertainty-aware hierarchical control, the system reduces the overall control penalty from initial fluctuations of approximately −1810 to a stable range of −200 to −300. The trust-guided mechanism rejects an average of 40.5% of high-risk candidate goals and successfully identifies over 84,290 potential constraint violations. In addition, combustion-temperature uncertainty is reduced by approximately 37% under high-load conditions. Compared with deterministic baselines, the proposed framework maintains median tracking errors below 10−3, while effectively suppressing large control deviations, demonstrating improved robustness and safety for industrial decarbonization-oriented control tasks.

title: From laboratory evidence to field-realized N2O mitigation by biochar: a global meta-analysis and mechanistic synthesis
abstract: Biochar can reduce soil nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, but the extent to which laboratory-observed mitigation is realized under field conditions and the mechanisms underlying field responses remain uncertain. We analyzed 874 paired N2O comparisons (450 laboratory incubations and 424 field studies) contrasting soils with and without biochar amendment to quantify field-realized N2O mitigation relative to laboratory estimates, elucidate the mechanisms underlying field responses, and identify the key determinants of field mitigation. Biochar reduced N2O emissions by 11% in field studies (95% CI, −27% to 10%), compared with 31% in laboratory incubations (95% CI, −41% to −19%). Weaker pH buffering, more dynamic nitrogen availability and reduced substrate limitation under field conditions may weaken nitrifier suppression and constrain complete denitrification, limiting the expression of biochar-induced mitigation in the field. We further identify practical strategies, including maintaining biochar alkalinity during aging and integrating biochar application with optimized nitrogen management, to improve field-scale mitigation performance.

title: Chemical upcycling of waste PET into reactive soil binders toward cleaner soil stabilization
abstract: Cement-based binders are widely used for soil stabilization because of their high reinforcement efficiency, but their energy-intensive production and associated CO2 emissions motivate the development of lower-impact alternatives. Meanwhile, the growing accumulation of plastic waste has encouraged its utilization as a low-cost additive in civil engineering and construction materials. However, direct incorporation of plastic waste into asphalt, concrete, and soil composites typically relies on passive physical reinforcement, resulting in weak interfacial bonding with the surrounding matrix and inefficient stress transfer. Here, we convert post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles into reactive soil binders through aminolysis depolymerization into amino(oligoterephthalamides), which are subsequently crosslinked with epoxide compounds to form covalent interparticle networks. Comparison of different PET-derived binder states establishes that neither chemical functionality nor cationic character alone is sufficient: only the non-protonated aminolysis product, which forms a paste-like phase spatially retained at soil interparticle contacts, yields an effective load-bearing network upon in situ crosslinking. At ca. 6 wt% total PET-derived binder content, the optimized composites achieved 616 ± 26 kPa compressive strength at 20% moisture content and up to 8792 ± 731 kPa in the dry state, corresponding to ca. 12- and 25-fold improvements over untreated soil, respectively. Microstructural analysis revealed that reinforcement arises from multiscale polymer bridges spanning soil particles. Water immersion tests showed retention of ca. 70% compressive strength after 24 h of water exposure. Spatial retention followed by covalent network formation thus provides a design principle for converting waste PET into functional soil binders. A preliminary screening assessment indicates that reagent production, rather than process energy, dominates the environmental burden of the present route, identifying reagent intensity as the key target for further optimization.

title: Environmental and economic assessment of olefin synthesis from waste as an emerging alternative to conventional light olefin production routes
abstract: Light olefins such as ethylene and propylene are essential petrochemical intermediates but remain highly energy- and carbon-intensive to produce using conventional fossil-based technologies. We conduct the life-cycle environmental and economic assessment (LCA/LCC) of seven olefin production pathways, such as coal-based, natural gas-based, shale gas-based, crude oil-based, bio-based, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis, to understand trade-offs and identify decarbonisation opportunities. A cradle-to-gate LCA employs nine EF 3.1 midpoint indicators, using foreground data from industrial sources, Aspen Plus V14 modelling, and ecoinvent v3.10 inventories. Results show that coal-based olefin production exhibits the highest environmental burdens, particularly for climate change, freshwater ecotoxicity, eutrophication, and water use. Natural gas-based and crude oil-based routes perform better across non-climate categories but remain carbon-intensive. Bio-based olefin production route provides partial climate benefits but is penalised by large land and water requirements. In contrast, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis achieve net-negative greenhouse gas emissions due to biogenic carbon uptake and integrated CO 2 capture. Sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis further reduces energy demand via in-situ water removal and process intensification, yielding lower GHG emissions (47%), reduced water use by 64%, and improved selectivity compared with conventional waste-to-olefin routes. However, higher impacts persist in ozone depletion and ionising radiation categories, driven by upstream electricity supply chains. Economic analysis indicates that gasification and CO 2 management dominate overall costs, while the sorption-enhanced synthesis adds only a modest incremental cost to waste-to-olefin pathways. Total life cycle costing for waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis falls within EUR 2130 to 3550 t −1 olefin, including environmental cost, competitive with emerging green olefin pathways. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining waste feedstocks, CO 2 capture, and sorption-enhanced process intensification offers a promising pathway for low-carbon, resource-efficient olefin production, especially within future decarbonised energy systems.

title: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of microalgae-derived sustainable aviation fuel with in-situ light hydrocarbon by-product reforming
abstract: Hydrogen supply is a major, underexplored lever for the cost and carbon intensity (CI) of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA), whereas most prior techno-economic and life-cycle studies treat external hydrogen sourcing as fixed. This study presents the first integrated assessment that combines in-situ C3-C4 by-product steam reforming (PSR) with external grey, blue, and green hydrogen for microalgae-derived HEFA SAF. A flowsheet simulation model, validated against published HEFA yield and reforming data, was developed for 812 kg h−1 of natural Chlorella vulgaris oil and coupled with techno-economic analysis, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, pinch analysis, exergy analysis, and life cycle assessment (LCA) across five scenarios (no reforming; propane-only reforming; full C3-C4 reforming with grey, blue, or green hydrogen). In-situ PSR reduced external hydrogen procurement by 17.8-29.5% without requiring additional feedstock, supplying up to 34.2% of total hydrogen demand. Minimum selling price (MSP) ranged from $1.479 L-1 (propane-only reforming) to $1.928 L-1 (green hydrogen), while CORSIA carbon intensity decreased from 65.0 to 39.4 gCO2e MJ−1. All scenarios met the CORSIA eligibility threshold, and the blue- and green-hydrogen cases also met the ReFuelEU Aviation 2030 comparison threshold of 44.5 gCO2e MJ−1. Blue hydrogen with full reforming was the lowest-cost route to this threshold, while Monte Carlo analysis identified algae oil price, not hydrogen strategy, as the dominant driver of MSP. The resulting MSP-CI frontier provides a practical, quantitative basis for selecting hydrogen strategies for algae-HEFA SAF under combined cost and carbon constraints.

title: Solar direct air capture synergized by spectral splitting and heat recovery
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) is a critical negative emission technology, yet its high energy demand remains a major bottleneck. This study proposes and evaluates a novel solar-driven DAC system synergistically integrating spectral-splitting (SS) and heat pump (HP) technologies to address this challenge. The SS module decouples photoelectric and photothermal conversion, enhancing photovoltaic conversion efficiency (PCE) by reducing cell temperature while simultaneously harvesting high-grade thermal energy from the infrared spectrum for sorbent regeneration. Theoretical models for SS, DAC, and HP were established to analyze four different integrated configurations. Key findings indicate that the SS module improves PCE by 1.07–3.58% and achieves a maximum photothermal efficiency of 33.9%, resulting in an overall solar utilization efficiency of up to 60.7%. The integration of an HP significantly reduces system energy demand; the standalone temperature swing adsorption (TSA) configuration requires 0.60 GJ/tCO2 electricity and 7.54 GJ/tCO2 heat, whereas the HP-assisted TSA configuration reduces total energy input to as low as 1.08 GJ/tCO2 of electricity only. Furthermore, the system attains a maximum CO2 productivity of 2.69 kg/m2/day at an 80 °C desorption temperature using a 1.6 eV bandgap SS material. An economic analysis reveals that the temperature swing adsorption configuration achieves the lowest levelized cost of DAC (LCOD) of $195/tCO2. By enabling in-situ electricity and heat cogeneration from a single solar input, the proposed system advances the state of the art in two key respects. It substantially improves solar energy utilization efficiency while simultaneously elevating the net carbon removal efficiency to as high as 96.2%, owing to the near-zero carbon footprint of the all-solar energy supply. This work demonstrates that the synergy of spectral splitting and heat pump technologies offers an economically viable and environmentally effective pathway for solar-driven direct air capture, contributing a more sustainable option to the portfolio of negative emission technologies.

title: Sustainable recycling of polymer-bonded magnets through continuous hydrolysis for a circular economy
abstract: The treatment of magnets containing rare earth elements (REEs) has garnered considerable attention due to their critical role in various industries and their importance in clean technologies. Polymer-bonded magnets (PBMs), composed of Nd-Fe-B (neodymium-iron-boron) magnetic particles embedded in a polymer matrix, are pivotal in many applications but present challenges in recycling. Recycling PBMs can be achieved through hydrolysis, facilitating the separation of magnetic particles from the polymer matrix. This study aims to introduce a hydrothermal process for recycling PBMs and evaluate the environmental impacts of this innovative technology using life cycle assessment. The findings of this study underscore that critical areas of concern include electricity consumption and the use of acid and alkali. Notably, substituting chemicals with high-temperature condition significantly reduces the environmental impacts of the process. The study demonstrates that recycling PBMs and producing secondary PBMs through the hydrothermal route reduces potential environmental impact by about 80% in CO2 eq. compared to the virgin PBMs production process and the conventional treatment of PBMs at end-of-life stage. Furthermore, this research advocates for optimizing the process design to mitigate the impacts of chemicals and energy consumption while effectively preserving magnetic properties.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and production–emission decoupling of the carbon footprints of China's staple crops
abstract: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions during staple-crop production while ensuring food supply requires effective production–emission decoupling and mitigation strategies. We quantified the selected cradle-to-farm gate carbon footprints of rice, wheat, and maize in China from 2006 to 2021 using a source-specific GHG inventory. We further evaluated production–emission decoupling and probabilistically ranked competing mitigation pathways using Tapio decoupling, Monte Carlo, and sensitivity analyses. Grain production and GHG emissions increased by 43.89% and 15.84%, respectively, indicating weak decoupling (Tapio elasticity = 0.36). Production increased by 10.53% while emissions reduced by 0.45% during 2015–2021, indicating strong absolute decoupling. Yield-scaled carbon footprints decreased for all three crops, although the area-scaled carbon footprint of wheat increased by 16.09%. For rice, methane (CH4) emissions were predominant during the cultivation stage, whereas nitrogen-based emissions dominated wheat and maize. Under the baseline M0 specification, fertilizer-production decarbonization had the highest dominance probability for wheat (60.84%) and maize (60.58%), whereas cultivation-stage CH4 mitigation ranked highest for rice (78.55%). These rankings were stable across alternative Monte Carlo distributions, dependence structures, and year-specific source shares; however, under the upper nitrous oxide emission-factor inventory, nitrogen-use efficiency improvement became the highest-ranked pathway for wheat and maize. Thus, crop-specific mitigation rankings were robust to alternative Monte Carlo specifications but remained sensitive to influential inventory assumptions, particularly for wheat and maize.

title: Challenges in national waste data collection for supply chain biorefinery modelling: A geospatial assessment of agricultural residues, OFMSW, and used cooking oil in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa
abstract: Reliable spatially resolved biomass data are essential for biorefinery planning, supply chain optimisation, and evidence-based policy development.
