However, such data remain scarce across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) due to fragmented waste management systems, informal collection practices, limited monitoring infrastructure, and inconsistent reporting mechanisms. Consequently, the region's biomass resources remain underutilised despite increasing global demand for renewable fuels and low-carbon products. This study develops a geospatially enabled framework to quantify and map biomass resources in Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa. Three major feedstocks were assessed: lignocellulosic agricultural residues (AW), the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW), and used cooking oil (UCO). Agricultural residue quantities were estimated using residue-to-product ratios and crop production statistics, while OFMSW and UCO generation were derived from population, waste generation, edible oil consumption, and production datasets. Proportional allocation methods, growth models, and Geographic Information System (GIS) tools were applied to generate spatially resolved datasets at state, county, and provincial levels. The novelty of this work lies in the development of an integrated and openly available geospatial biomass dataset for three major SSA economies. The results indicate substantial biomass availability, with AW estimated at 240 million tons/year in Nigeria, 85 million tons/year in South Africa, and 35 million tons/year in Kenya. OFMSW generation was estimated at 16.2, 7.6, and 4.8 million tons/year, respectively, while UCO availability reached 582,795, 215,000, and 226,626 tons/year. The resulting datasets provide a valuable evidence base for biorefinery siting, biomass supply chain optimisation, investment planning, and policy development across SSA.

title: Decoupling hydrological and economic drivers of global rainwater harvesting performance using explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: Decentralized rainwater harvesting (RWH) is critical for urban water resilience, yet current research remains fragmented, relying on site-specific case studies that limit the identification of transferable physical and economic patterns across heterogeneous urban contexts. Here, we present a unified, data-driven framework that harmonizes 3879 RWH cases across 179 cities into a globally consistent dataset. We developed predictive models for key economic and water-saving performance indicators, including benefit-cost ratio (BCR), Net Present Value (NPV), payback period (PBP), and water-saving efficiency (WSE). The predictive framework employs a Bayesian-optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) integrated with interpretability algorithms. Model robustness was evaluated using random-split, study-isolated, and geographic extrapolation tests. Across the four targets, R2 values ranged from 0.928 to 0.960 under random split and 0.656–0.868 under study-isolated validation. Geographic transferability was scale-dependent: city-level extrapolation retained R2 values of 0.740–0.892, whereas country-level extrapolation declined markedly to 0.323–0.511. SHAP-based interpretation revealed nonlinear feature interactions and indicator-specific contribution patterns, with catchment fraction identified as a key predictor reflecting the influence of system scale matching between contributing area and harvesting capacity within the compiled dataset. These results support the framework as an interpretable screening and scenario-comparison tool within the climatic, socioeconomic, and system domains represented by the compiled dataset, while indicating that applications to substantially different national contexts require local calibration and additional validation.

title: A sector-national-global cross-scale assessment for China's building carbon gap and its cascading effects on global decarbonization
abstract: China's first National Natural Disaster Risk Census discloses a total building stock of 128 billion square meters, providing a nationwide benchmark for building-stock assessment. This study developed a cross-scale analytical framework to assess the implications of this stock benchmark update for China's building sector, national carbon neutrality, and global decarbonization. The framework follows a three-stage logic—demand reconfiguration, carbon budget gap identification, and impact quantification—and is operationalized through the Building Carbon Demands Integration Model (BCDIM), which couples building stock turnover, LCA-based emission accounting, and socio-technical transition pathways to quantify embodied and operational carbon demands for urban/rural residential and public buildings. Under equity-based allocation of global 2°C/1.5°C carbon budgets, the post-disclosure carbon-budget gaps are 2.47 times (2°C) and 1.50 times (1.5°C) the pre-disclosure estimates, reflecting the combined influence of stock revision and broader building coverage. Closing the gap now requires faster decarbonization and annual mitigation efforts 3.88 times (2°C) and 1.76 times (1.5°C) the pre-disclosure estimates. The study also reveals that the additional national and global mitigation requirements estimated after disclosure are greater in the earlier period. These findings redefine China's building sector as a linchpin in both national and global mitigation, and demonstrate that empirically grounded stock data are essential for aligning sectoral decarbonization pathways with global temperature targets.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of water consumption induced by cooling and electricity use of data centers in China
abstract: Data centers consume water through on-site cooling and electricity use, yet their water consumption dynamics remain under-investigated. This study develops a bottom-up accounting framework to quantify direct cooling water consumption and indirect electricity-related water consumption of data centers in China over 2016-2024. A spatiotemporal inventory of data centers has been compiled with information on data center location, capacity, starting year of operation, power usage effectiveness, cooling type, etc. Our results reveal an overall rise in national data center water consumption from 229 Mm3 to 478 Mm3, with hotspots distributed across eastern regions as well as emerging western regions. Decoupling analysis demonstrates that data center expansion and water consumption have transitioned toward decoupling recently. Decomposition identifies scale expansion as the primary water consumption driver historically, partially offset by declining water consumption intensity. Long-term scenario projections to 2050 highlight divergent future water trajectories. Stringent efficiency upgrades together with scale control can deliver major water consumption reductions, whereas unconstrained data center growth would lead to water demand growth that efficiency gains alone cannot fully mitigate. This work provides empirical evidence for integrating water resource into data center planning to advance sustainable data center development and water resource management.

title: Aspects of sustainable plant and project management in the Polish tanning industry
abstract: The article aims to characterize the Polish tanning industry in terms of the integration of sustainable development and Sustainable Development Goals into plant management and project management. Information obtained from 20 Polish tanneries that participated in the survey research was analyzed. The majority of them (n = 17, i.e. 85%) declared that they take into account the principles of sustainable development in their plant management and operations, while just under half of the companies (n = 8, i.e. 40%) declare that their strategic goals are consistent with at least one and up to 16 SDGs. Five of the 20 plants (25%) also declared project-based activities, usually involving the implementation of production and technology projects. Among the five plants implementing projects, four declared that they take SDGs into account in project planning. In addition, the same four tanneries declared that they follow the principle of the sustainable development triad during project implementation, that their projects are designed to achieve sustainable results, and that sustainable and lasting outcomes are pursued at project closure. The study provides exploratory evidence on the incorporation of sustainable development principles into plant and project management in Polish tanneries and may offer useful insights for companies with a similar business profile.

title: Simulation-based assessment of groundwater rebound in solar versus diesel irrigation pumping: A coupled life-cycle framework
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) irrigation pumping is commonly compared with diesel under fixed water demand assumptions and carbon focused indicators, an approach that may overlook groundwater rebound when lower marginal pumping costs influence abstraction. This study develops a coupled computational framework integrating crop water demand, pumping hydraulics, life-cycle assessment, techno economic performance, endogenous abstraction, aquifer feedback, and groundwater governance. The analysis is intentionally non-site-specific: a synthetic 20-ha arid, groundwater dependent reference scheme and a generic season weighted crop coefficient are used to demonstrate the method rather than to represent a named location or crop. The framework was benchmarked against 20 reconstructed cases from four cited studies: 17 cases reproduced reported targets within 1% (median deviation 0.26%), while three field-season hydraulic cross checks differed by 3.7–14.8% where synchronized discharge-head observations were unavailable. An independent LCA benchmark reproduced the implied foreground greenhouse-gas contribution within 0.62%, providing a traceability check rather than independent ReCiPe validation. Under the synthetic reference scenario, weakly governed access combined with the assumed abstraction elasticity increased modeled PV abstraction by 33.6% relative to the fixed demand baseline and increased aquifer decline entering year 25 by approximately 7.0 m. Specific PV climate impact per cubic metre varied little across governance scenarios, demonstrating that a favorable normalized carbon metric may coexist with increasing groundwater pressure. A governance elasticity diagnostic surface was therefore developed to identify combinations of behavioral response and governance consistent with an externally specified groundwater criterion. The results demonstrate the methodological importance of coupling technology level life-cycle performance with endogenous water abstraction while explicitly separating implementation verification, field cross checking, and future site-specific validation.

title: Positively charged softwood fibers prepared via PFI refining-assisted cationization as green additives for improved retention, drainage and strength of low-grade straw pulp
abstract: Reed pulp fibers are characterized by short fibers, high negative charge, a high content of fines and parenchyma cells, so that a substantial quantity of chemical additives to compensate for the consequent low fiber retention rate and challenging water filtration issues. However, such high additive dosages escalate production costs and intensify wastewater treatment burdens. This study aimed to develop a bio-based multifunctional retention and drainage aid by mechanically refining softwood kraft pulp fibers using a PFI mill, followed by etherification with 3-chloro-2-hydroxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride in an alkaline aqueous system. PFI refining promoted external fibrillation, increased active hydroxyl content from 95.84 to 151.81 mgKOH/g, and decreased crystallinity from 75.00% to 69.42%. Following cationization, the fibers exhibited a zeta potential of +32.80 mV and a charge density of 69.33 μeq/g. The cationic fibers were blended with reed pulp for papermaking, the drainage rate was enhanced to 4.23 mL/s, with reduced the filtrate turbidity and absorbance to 3.40 NTU and 0.008, respectively. These improvements are attributed to electrostatic adsorption and physical entanglement between the cationic fibers and reed pulp fibers. At the optimal ratio (reed pulp:CF 53.8 °SR = 2:1), the burst, tensile, and tear indices reached 2.264 kPa m2/g, 33.367 N m/g, and 7.96 mN m2/g, corresponding to increases of 92%, 152%, and 143%, respectively, compared with pure reed pulp sheets. PFI-pretreated cationic fibers enhance retention, drainage, and strength, thereby providing a bio-based strategy for the utilization of agricultural residue pulp.

title: Elastic cellulose aerogel with compression-regulated thermal coupling for climate-adaptive radiative cooling and building energy saving
abstract: Passive radiative cooling offers an energy-efficient approach to reducing building cooling demand, whereas the conductive pathway between the radiative surface and the building envelope is typically treated as fixed. Here, a directionally freeze-cast biomass-derived elastic cellulose aerogel (ECA) is developed to integrate radiative cooling with mechanically regulated thermal coupling. The anisotropic lamellar architecture enables reversible radial compression, allowing the finite-layer thermal resistance to be adjusted primarily through thickness reduction and compression-induced changes in structural contact. The selected longitudinal surface exhibits a solar-weighted reflectance of 94.46 % in the released state and 97.15 % after compression, while the atmospheric-transmittance-weighted infrared emissivity over 5-25 μm increases from approximately 0.87 to 0.93. Comparative steady-state measurements show that the temperature difference across the ECA decreases from approximately 3.45 °C to 0.617 °C as the normalized thickness h/h0 decreases from 1.0 to 0.2, demonstrating substantially enhanced through-thickness thermal coupling upon compression. Outdoor comparative measurements under identical PE-enclosed boundary conditions further reveal distinct thermal responses between the released and compressed states. Building-scale simulations across 34 provincial-level regions in China, evaluated using an ideal hourly supervisory benchmark, indicate that selecting between weakly and strongly coupled states can reduce annual heating and cooling thermal loads relative to fixed operating states under diverse climatic conditions. This work demonstrates a mechanically adaptive radiative material that extends passive radiative cooling from a fixed thermal interface toward climate-responsive building-envelope thermal management with building energy-saving potential.

title: Upcycling industrial sulfur for sustainable pavement materials: Cleaner production processes and multi-scale phase evolution mechanisms
abstract: Sulfur extended asphalt (SEA) emerges as a highly promising cleaner production technology designed to upcycle industrial sulfur by-products, thereby fundamentally reducing reliance on non-renewable fossil-derived asphalt, preventing large-scale industrial waste accumulation, and maximizing resource efficiency. However, its widespread engineering deployment is constrained by post-mixing phase instabilities and time-dependent physical hardening. Herein, a comprehensive multi-scale investigation details the chemical, morphological, and thermo-rheological evolution of SEA binders across sulfur dosages of 0–30% and static ambient curing periods up to 60 days. Spectral and molecular analyses confirm that covalent sulfur grafting reaches thermodynamic equilibrium during high-temperature shear mixing (140 °C), building initial structural cohesion. Post-mixing room-temperature curing functions strictly as a physical phase rearrangement process. While low sulfur additions promote resin synthesis, excess unreacted sulfur initially persists as a soft amorphous plasticizer before kinetically precipitating into rigid crystal networks during static storage. This phase transition drives a non-monotonic thermal response and a critical rheological stiffening threshold at 5% sulfur. Synthesizing these multi-scale findings, a coupled “three-state sulfur” mechanism (interlinking chemical, amorphous, and recrystallized sulfur) is established to elucidate binder performance evolution. From a holistic cleaner production perspective, this framework identifies an optimal balance point near 20% sulfur. This optimized formulation achieves an ideal trade-off between maximizing sustainable resource efficiency via high-volume fossil fuel substitution, providing a mechanistic basis to support wide-temperature pavement durability, and strictly maintaining zero-emission environmental safety, thereby advancing SEA as a robust material for circular economy infrastructure.

title: Cleaner waste plastic-to-oil conversion through automatic control: Yield, resource intensity and the feedstock limit on batch consistency
abstract:
Introduction
Batch pyrolysis can recover landfill waste plastic as fuel oil, but small and medium-scale reactors are typically operated without any measurement of reaction progress, and it is not known how much of the resource cost per unit of oil is set by the way the reactor is operated, or what limits batch-to-batch consistency.
Materials and methods
This study addresses that gap in simulation. A five-state surrogate model of a fixed-bed batch reactor fired by liquefied petroleum gas was calibrated against published laboratory oil yields for predominantly low-density polyethylene waste at 350–500 °C; one output coefficient was fitted to four points, with a leave-one-out error of 5.22 wt%. Four strategies were compared over 400 Monte Carlo batches each, with feedstock ash drawn between 8.78 and 26.21 wt%: a fixed valve profile, PID temperature control, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) driving a conversion-based switch, and EKF-based model predictive control.
Results and discussion
Within the model, closed-loop control raised mean oil yield from 29.54 to 38.38–40.40 wt% and, per unit of oil, lowered burner input by 24–27% and a carbon-dioxide surrogate index by 21–24%, while raising a sulfur-dioxide surrogate index by 18–35%. All three closed-loop strategies reached a yield standard deviation of 1.20–1.22 wt%, close to the 1.18 wt% contributed by feedstock ash alone, and could not be distinguished from one another; a fixed-time switch reproduced the EKF-based switch.
Conclusions
Feedstock preparation, rather than controller sophistication, therefore set the limit on reproducibility in this system. These are simulation results, not experimental measurements: the gas indices are surrogates rather than predicted emissions, the controller ranking changed under perturbed kinetics, and confirmation on a physical reactor is still required.

title: A framework for deep shale gas development supporting net-zero emissions and multi-energy supply
abstract: Deep shale gas formations contain vast natural gas and geothermal energy resources and are critical to achieving carbon neutrality. However, current exploitation strategies often address hydrocarbon production, carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration, and geothermal recovery independently, missing opportunities for integration. In this study, we propose a unified technical and modeling framework called CO2 Storage with Enhanced Gas Recovery and Geothermal Extraction (CS-EGRGE), which simultaneously enables shale gas extraction, geothermal energy utilization, and CO2 storage in deep shale formations. A coupled adsorption-thermo-hydro-mechanical-diffusion (ATHMD) model was developed and validated using laboratory displacement experiments and field-scale wellbore data. Numerical simulations were performed for a representative Luzhou shale gas block (300m × 400m×80m) over an 80-year operation cycle. The results indicate that the system can cumulatively produce 2.73 × 108 m3 of shale gas, extract 2.54×107kWh of geothermal energy, and store 4.3×105t of CO2. The China scenario yields a slightly positive undiscounted balance of $0.26 million but an NPV of -$7.69 million at an 8% discount rate, whereas the corresponding NPVs for the United States and European Union scenarios are $3.47 million and $16.36 million, respectively. This study develops a coupled multiphysics simulation model to support the design and evaluation of an integrated technical framework for deep shale gas development, geothermal energy utilization, and CO2 storage, contributing to sustainable resource exploitation and carbon emission mitigation.

title: Enhancing microbially induced corrosion prediction accuracy in sewer pipes using generative adversarial network (GAN)-based data augmentation under scarce experimental data conditions
abstract: Microbially induced corrosion (MIC) is a major cause of deterioration in concrete sewer infrastructure. However, its prediction remains challenging as it relies on time consuming and resource intensive experiments to capture the gradual evolution of microbial communities and corrosion mechanisms. Limited experimental data constrain the accurate assessment of corrosion, often leading to overfitting and poor generalization even when data-driven machine-learning (ML) models are employed. This study proposes a hybrid data-driven framework that integrates limited experimental data with synthetically generated data produced using Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CT-GANs). The CT-GAN model was trained and validated using laboratory corrosion-chamber observations and subsequently employed to generate synthetic datasets. Statistical evaluation (Kolmogorov Smirnov (KS_Stat) statistics, KS p-values, Wasserstein distances, and overlap coefficient) showed high similarity between original and synthetic datasets with high overlap (>0.97). This indicates that CT-GAN retains the statistical structure of the original measurements, confirming the high fidelity of the generated datasets. ML prediction models were trained using both the original and synthetic datasets to estimate concrete corrosion loss. CT-GAN-based augmentation improved predictive performance across all evaluated ML models, with XGBoost achieving the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.9818, MAE = 0.092 mm, RMSE = 0.136 mm, and MAPE = 15.49%). Additionally, the synthetic dataset reproduced the experimental mean corrosion loss within ±3% across all H2S concentrations. The findings further revealed a non-linear corrosion response to H2S concentration, with mean corrosion loss peaking at 1.86 mm at 25 ppm H2S before declining to 1.57 mm at 50 ppm, reflecting temperature-dependent microbial sulfur oxidation. While corrosion at 100% humidity reached 2.56 mm at 25 ppm H2S, highlighting the dominant role of moisture availability. Outcomes demonstrate that GAN-based synthetic data augmentation increases data representation of the measured parameters, enhancing the robustness of corrosion-prediction models. Outcomes demonstrate that GAN-based synthetic data augmentation improves the predictive performance of the evaluated corrosion-prediction models. Consequently, this approach provides a reliable tool for predictive maintenance and asset management in contexts where long-term monitoring is limited. However, its applicability is limited to the variables and experimental conditions represented in the original dataset; incorporating concrete material and field-scale operational parameters would further strengthen its operational applicability.

title: The environmental paradox of innovation: Assessing the nexus between patents, R&D, scientific publications and trademarks with CO2-equivalent emissions
abstract: While innovation is widely championed as a solution to climate change, its aggregate impact on greenhouse gas emissions remains complex and often ambiguous. This study investigates the long-run effects of multidimensional innovation indicators—scientific publications, patents, trademarks, and R&D expenditure—on CO2-equivalent (CO2-e) emissions across 66 countries from 1996 to 2022. Employing the Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) technique, the results challenge the conventional wisdom that innovation automatically ensures environmental sustainability. The findings reveal that, without specific environmental orientation, different innovation dimensions exhibit heterogeneous long-run effects on CO2-e emissions, driven largely by scale effects. Interestingly, scientific publications yield minor emission reductions of 0.94% to 1.10%, while R&D expenditure shows a 1.29% reduction in emissions in the baseline model. In contrast, trademarks demonstrate a significant positive association with emissions in the pooled estimates, increasing emissions by 2.56% to 3.28%. The two-stage transmission channel analysis indicates a mitigating pathway through human capital, which exert a significant offsetting effect on the emission-increasing pathway of innovation. Country-specific estimates further highlight heterogeneity: Human capital is associated with emission reduction across all income groups, and the environmental impact of innovation indicators varies significantly by income level. High-income nations leverage human capital to decouple growth from emissions, while upper-middle-income economies face a steep pollution trade-off. To facilitate a cleaner production transition, policy must shift from promoting innovation quantity to steering its quality linking R&D and commercialization with human capital development.

title: Transpiration-inspired water-regulated metallization of wood: Toward green design of multifunctional wood with tunable mechanical, thermal, and electromagnetic properties
abstract: Metallic wood is a promising wood-based functional material for thermal management, structural applications, and electromagnetic regulation. However, conventional metallization methods typically rely on vacuum, pressure, or chemical assistance, resulting in high energy consumption and limited scalability. Here, a sustainable water-regulated metallization strategy was proposed to fabricate metallized wood with vertically aligned metallic networks and tunable multifunctional performance. The water-containing wood was first rapidly heated at 200 °C for a few minutes and then cooled in a 70 °C molten alloy bath, where the transient negative pressure generated by steam condensation enabled spontaneous alloy impregnation without external pressure or chemical reagents. A strong positive correlation between total vapor generation and alloy loading capacity (rs = 0.95, P < 0.01) confirmed the decisive role of water vapor in regulating infiltration efficiency. The alloy was primarily confined within vessel networks, forming continuous longitudinal conductive pathways while preserving cell wall integrity. This led to porosity reduction of up to 21.43%, accompanied by increases in bulk density (684.8%) and apparent density (375.2%), resulting in enhancements in compressive strength (37.6%) and thermal conductivity (605.8%). Strong positive correlations were observed between alloy loading capacity and compressive strength and thermal conductivity (rs = 0.97 and 0.98, P < 0.01). In addition, the interconnected conductive network and improved impedance matching enabled excellent electromagnetic wave absorption, with a minimum reflection loss of −46.8 dB and an effective bandwidth of 3.99 GHz at an optimized thickness of 4.8 mm. This work provides a scalable and energy-efficient pathway for converting natural porous biomass into high-performance multifunctional materials, offering a sustainable alternative for advanced material design in cleaner production systems.

title: Future environmental impacts of EU permanent magnet demand: a combined prospective MFA-LCA assessment
abstract: Advancing climate change necessitates a transformation of the mobility and energy sector towards low-carbon technologies. Rare earth element-containing permanent magnets (PMs), a key component in efficient electric machines, are currently produced in only a few countries and not efficiently recycled, motivating efforts to diversify supply by establishing domestic recycling routes. This study inspects the projected environmental impacts of PM value chains, thereby providing context to transitioning from a geographically concentrated, linear value chain towards a circular value chain in the European Union. Combining material flow analysis (MFA) and prospective life cycle assessment (LCA), the emissions from 2025 to 2100 are estimated under alternative production and recycling scenarios. Results show that i) future impacts of PM production will increasingly depend on the footprint of the material, ii) guaranteeing high magnetic performance during the use phase is key to achieving environmental benefits of circular value chains, iii) end-of-life products can become a relevant source for PM materials if recycling technologies and value chains are developed, and iv) recycling material substitution rates strongly influence overall results. The article showcases how to meaningfully combine LCA and MFA in dynamic system studies and demonstrates the cumulative environmental benefits of diversifying PM supply. Findings support ongoing EU efforts to strengthen domestic critical raw material supply and circular economy strategies.

title: Descriptor-resolved machine learning reveals response patterns and molecular interaction differences in MOF-based removal of hazardous aromatic pollutants
abstract: High adsorption capacities reported for MOF-based systems may reflect specific combinations of material, pollutant, and operating descriptors rather than transferable material performance. Here, a descriptor-resolved framework integrating literature-derived adsorption records, interpretable machine learning, sensitivity analysis, and representative molecular calculations was developed to distinguish response structure within the represented data domain from cross-publication transferability. The XGBoost model using CMAES-derived hyperparameters achieved a pooled out-of-fold R2 of 0.953 under record-level validation, whereas performance decreased markedly to R2 = −0.221 under publication-grouped validation. Despite this decline, the global descriptor-contribution hierarchy remained highly stable across the two validation schemes (ρ = 0.985), with initial concentration and adsorbent dosage ranking highest. Because both variables are mathematically linked to adsorption capacity, targeted feature-removal analysis was further performed. After simultaneously excluding them, the model retained an out-of-fold R2 of 0.854, while adsorption time, particle size, specific surface area, pore size, and pKa emerged as the highest-contributing descriptors. Representative paired response maps from the reduced model further revealed localized and non-monotonic associations among operating, material, and pollutant descriptors within the sampled domain. Molecular calculations showed that linker functionalization did not uniformly strengthen pollutant binding; instead, interaction stability depended on pollutant identity, aromatic contact, polar interaction, molecular orientation, and local linker chemistry. Overall, the framework distinguishes comparatively stable descriptor-response patterns from the more limited transferability of absolute adsorption-capacity predictions, providing a more rigorous basis for interpreting heterogeneous MOF adsorption evidence and prioritizing response patterns for independent experimental validation.

title: Macroeconomic impacts of regional low-carbon power trade in Northeast Asia: a linked CGE–power-system analysis
abstract: China, Korea, and Japan face different low-carbon resource endowments and abatement costs, creating scope for regional power cooperation but also uneven national impacts. We examine these effects using an iteratively soft-linked hourly power-system and multi-region CGE framework across scenarios with and without electricity trade and regional emissions trading. Interconnection reallocates low-carbon generation across the three countries, with China emerging as the main exporter, Korea as an importer and transit hub, and Japan as a terminal importer. Electricity trade has a negligible effect on three-country aggregate real income under either carbon-pricing regime, but its national incidence depends on policy design: Korea's cumulative real-GDI effect rises from about +0.1 percentage points under fragmented pricing to about +1.0 percentage point under the regional ETS, while Japan remains slightly negative and China close to zero. Regional carbon-market coordination also reduces the three-country cumulative real-income loss from about 1.4% to 0.9% and shifts mitigation burdens across countries, as national carbon prices of about 1.6 and 1.1 thousand USD/tCO2 in Korea and Japan converge toward a common level near 0.2 thousand USD/tCO2. Overall, the results show that the economic consequences of regional power trade depend not only on physical interconnection, but also on countries' network positions, relative abatement costs, and policy design.

title: A dynamic scheduling method in cloud manufacturing with green efficiency ratio guidance and energy-efficiency variation-based rescheduling triggering via deep reinforcement learning
abstract: As manufacturing increasingly shifts toward industrial cloudification and green development, distributed cloud manufacturing faces challenges in dynamic scheduling and green performance optimization under uncertain disturbances. To address these challenges, this study develops a green dynamic scheduling method for distributed cloud manufacturing workshops. First, a green efficiency ratio (GER) is developed to integrate multidimensional performance outputs and resource consumption without explicit subjective weighting. A manufacturing energy-efficiency variation-based rescheduling mechanism is then introduced to determine whether rescheduling is necessary after machine failures. Finally, a deep reinforcement learning-based global dispatching method generates scheduling decisions under dynamic conditions. A virtual simulation case of cylinder barrels from XCMG Group is conducted for validation. The proposed method increases GER by 8.43%, 9.44%, 21.47%, and 65.66% over NSGA-III, NSGA-II, PSO, and ACO, respectively. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving overall green performance and production efficiency under dynamic manufacturing conditions.

title: Contextual analysis of Black Soldier Fly farming as a sustainable organic waste treatment system in Bangladesh: Comparative case studies
abstract: Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming has emerged globally as a promising approach to transform organic waste into high-value protein and soil-enhancing frass. However, its novelty faces context-dependent constraints that limit sustainability and broader diffusion, often leading to discontinuation or stagnation. This study aims to explain how interconnected contextual factors affected the implementation and operational processes of BSF farming in practice, thereby hindering its sustainability as an organic waste treatment system. This study selected 10 cases for a comparative case study, comprising discontinued, stagnant, and operational statuses, from six climatic subregions of Bangladesh, established in urban, rural, and peri-urban locations. This study employed multiple qualitative methods for data collection, including participant observation and semi-structured interviews. Following an inductive approach and thematic content analysis, this study identified several limiting and supportive factors across social, economic, environmental, institutional, knowledge, spatial, and temporal aspects that are intertwined with the persistence of BSF farming in the context. Overall, adaptive operations were more frequent, but greater economic uncertainty was evident in cases that discontinued or stagnated. This study found that operational farms demonstrate “multinetwork resilience” to overcome most limiting factors with supportive ones, as evidenced by flexible spatial strategies, experiential knowledge competence, temporal adjustments, and institutional engagement, whereas discontinued farms were overwhelmed. Stagnating farms represented a “persistent niche,” achieving internal viability through partial adaptation but lacking the viable networks and institutional engagement needed to scale production. This study claims that the sustainability of BSF farming emerges from iterative learning and context-specific adjustments. Wider diffusion will require context-sensitive models that appreciate locally led knowledge advancements, incorporate socio-technical and spatio-temporal competencies, accommodate cumulative economic processes and affordability, and are legitimized through multi-level collaborations.

title: A nonlinear convex optimization framework for carbon-conscious, energy-efficient inventory systems with service and manufacturing innovation-driven demand
abstract: Emerging or fringe technologies are innovative tools not yet fully integrated into mainstream practices. They focus on energy efficiency, service quality, and environmentally friendly designs that influence consumer choices. Gaining a sustainable competitive advantage depends on improving service quality and innovation, often through advanced inventory systems that manage carbon emissions. For organizations with seasonal fluctuations, flexible inventory management is vital. This paper explores strategies for optimizing seasonal inventory by considering energy efficiency, service quality, innovation-driven demand, and carbon emissions. An analytical model shows how these factors affect demand, validated by numerical examples and sensitivity analyses. The framework determines the cost-minimizing replenishment cycle and quantifies the cost implications of each sustainability and competitiveness lever. Results show that a 20% improvement in the service factor and in the innovation index raises the minimum inventory cost by 8.20% and 1.98%, respectively, while reducing the optimal cycle time by 0.32% and 0.97%, whereas improvements in energy efficiency and carbon-emission performance reduce the total cost. Carbon taxation on production, storage, and transportation raises inventory costs by 1.40%, quantifying the price of regulatory compliance and guiding managers on which levers to prioritize.

title: Clean procurement reduces the supply-chain phosphorus burden of rooftop photovoltaics under manufacturing-capacity constraints
abstract: Rooftop-photovoltaic deployment reduces emissions from electricity generation, but producing its equipment also creates environmental burdens. Existing deployment and life-cycle assessments quantify potential benefits and burdens; procurement decisions additionally require estimates of reductions attainable under limits on qualifying supply, purchasing coverage and budgets. This study links a fixed deployable portfolio across 367 Chinese cities to a prospective life-cycle inventory and a city-building-type procurement-route allocation model. The analysis focuses on characterised phosphorus releases within a ten-control-variable environmental assessment and distinguishes deployment-associated carbon benefits from supply-chain burdens allocated to production regions for accounting purposes. For each procurement route, phosphorus intensity per kWh is held constant across cities and building types, allowing the effects of procurement and siting to be distinguished. A generation-mix sensitivity screen gives PV-to-reference phosphorus ratios of 5.30–5.89 across the specified cases. With both lever efficacies set to 0.85 and full addressability, unrestricted combined procurement provides an 85 % technical benchmark. Supply, coverage and budget constraints reduce the nominal generation-weighted improvement to 27.55 %; expanded qualifying supply raises it to 41.57 %. Paired joint-parameter scenarios yield median reductions of 20.56 % and 32.97 %, with 5th–95th percentile ranges of 15.60–26.21 % and 21.88–41.21 %, respectively. The scenarios show that supply expansion can shift the limiting condition towards purchasing coverage, while concurrent constraints remain important. Clean procurement can therefore improve the environmental performance of a fixed rooftop-PV deployment portfolio, provided qualifying manufacturing and material supply expands alongside procurement standards.
